title: The Pomegranate Orchard

indexNotes.about: Sefer Pardes Rimonim ("Orchard of Pomegranates") by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (the Ramak). Translation of the full table of contents (simanei ha-sefer) from the Koretz 1780 edition. The work is divided into 32 gates (she'arim), each with a symbolic title and a stated count of chapters (perakim).
indexNotes.translatorNotes: Translator's notes. Sefirotic and technical terms are transliterated (Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut; heikhalot, etc.). "Rashbi" = Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai; "the Tikkunim" = Tikkunei Zohar; "Sefer Yetzirah" is abbreviated S"Y in the original. A handful of scribal oddities in this printing are flagged inline in brackets.
indexNotes.colophon: Colophon. Up to here we have brought the matter of the chapters and the gates; their number altogether is two hundred and eighty-seven (287), with their mnemonics.
indexNotes.transliteration:
Words. The names of the sefirot and other technical terms are transliterated (Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut; heikhalot). Transliterated Hebrew and Aramaic words are set in italics (tikkun, havayah, nefesh); names are not: the sefirot and their titles, persons, places, angels, books and divine names (Keter, Rashbi, Metatron, Sefer Yetzirah, Elohim), the letters (Alef, Heh), strings of letters (YHVH), and words at home in English (Torah, Kabbalah, Sabbath, shofar). Hebrew words are transliterated for reading, without diacritics: ch = ח; kh = כ without a dagesh; tz = צ; k = כ and ק; sh = ש; s = ס and שׂ; v = ו, and ב without a dagesh; f = פ without a dagesh. An apostrophe marks א or ע where it is sounded between vowels (ma'amar, Yeri'ah).

Letters. When a Hebrew letter is spoken of as a letter, its name is spelled out and capitalised: Alef, Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Heh, Vav, Zayin, Chet, Tet, Yod, Kaf, Lamed, Mem, Nun, Samekh, Ayin, Peh, Tzadi, Kof, Resh, Shin, Tav. A group of letters taken as a unit is hyphenated (the three mothers, Alef-Mem-Shin); a list takes commas. Where Ayin, “Nothing” (אין), could be taken for the letter Ayin (ע), it is glossed once.

Letter strings. Divine names, permutations of the Name and ciphers quoted as strings of letters are given one capital per letter, the letters spaced: A = א; B = ב; G = ג; D = ד; H = ה; V = ו; Z = ז; Ch = ח; Ṭ = ט; Y = י; K = כ; L = ל; M = מ; N = נ; S = ס; Ā = ע; P = פ; Tz = צ; Q = ק; R = ר; Sh = ש; T = ת. Ṭ, Ā and Q keep ט, ע and ק apart from ת, א and כ; in words they are written t, an apostrophe and k. Thus מצפץ is M Tz P Tz and אדני is A D N Y. The Tetragrammaton is written YHVH, and spaced (Y H V H) where it is set beside its permutations. Acronyms that are read as words keep their vowels: KaChaB (Keter, Chokhmah, Binah), ABYA (the four worlds).

Vowel points. The vowel points (Gate 28) are called by their Hebrew names, transliterated. The marks, shown on the letter Bet (ב), with their names:

Cordovero uses the names of the Zohar and the Tikkunim, which do not always match today's. Marked *: the modern name differs (shofar holekh = munach, shofar mehupakh = mahpakh, ma'arikh = merkha, tircha = tipcha). Marked ?: the identification is uncertain (pazer gadol shown as pazer; telisha and tirtza shown as the large and small telisha; trei ta'amei shown as merkha kefulah). Azla and kadma have the same form; sheva ga'ya and ga'ya sheva differ in order, not in form.

introduction: Thus says the young one, Moses, son of my lord and father, the honored Rabbi Jacob Cordovero. When I saw that the days of my youth had passed and gone by in pursuit of every craving, and were spent without hope, it came to pass, when my Maker brought me to my twentieth year and yellow hair had sprouted, that my Maker roused me as a man is roused from his sleep. And I said to my soul: How long will you turn this way and that, O wayward daughter? How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine from you. How long will your wicked thoughts lodge within you, while you forget YHVH your Maker, who formed you from the womb? Now arise, call upon your God, keep watch at His doors day by day, and repair the altar of YHVH that was thrown down.

And when she heard the sound of the call, she was stirred, and said: Let me rise now and go about the city, in the markets and in the streets, to seek for myself a rest that will be good for me. And I heard the voice of one speaking: a watcher and a holy one came down from heaven, my teacher and master, the divine kabbalist, the sage, our honored Rabbi Solomon Alkabetz ha-Levi, may the Compassionate One guard and redeem him. He brought me into the halls of his palaces and taught me, and said to me: My son, let your heart hold fast to my words; incline your ear and hear the words of the wise. And he set me at the doors of wisdom and understanding, sweeter than honey and the honeycomb, which murmur and chirp in the depths of the hidden things of the Torah; and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness. I kept watch at the doors of his house of study and heard his discourse, and he roused me to learn the ways of the Zohar and the keys for opening its gates. And he pressed me, and I was occupied with it for days, and I was astonished, and said: How good and how pleasant it is that this should be my occupation! For how many days will I be a son to this wisdom! In her love I will be ravished always; her breasts will satisfy me at every time and every moment, until she is not forgotten from my mouth.

And when I came to fulfil my vows, I set before me all the books of the divine Rashbi, peace be upon him, and contemplated them. And my heart was like one who goes in the heart of the sea, like one who lies on the top of a mast, bewildered and confused in the depths of the many inquiries. And I said: I will take the scribe's inkhorn that is at my waist and set out all the inquiries, each flock by itself, until I put a space for my intellect between flock and flock; and when my heart grows firm in one inquiry, I will turn to another. And I saw, and behold, my counsel was right, and made straight by YHVH from heaven. And I spread out a scroll of a book before me, that it might be a remembrance for me and might teach its matters and their order. I called it Pardes Rimmonim [The Orchard of Pomegranates], for known reasons.

First, because this wisdom, the wisdom of Kabbalah, is referred to by the term PaRDeS [Orchard], as is known. Second, because this scroll will be for me a restorer of the soul, in which to find bliss in this world and in the world to come, and with which to sustain all my years; and it is an orchard that I planted, to revel in it. And it is of pomegranates, because its gates are its plantings and its chapters are its pomegranates; and in them new insights are arranged, this one beside that one and that one beside this one, not one and not two, but full as a pomegranate. Therefore we named it Pardes Rimmonim.

And we saw fit to divide the scroll into thirty-two parts, and we named them gates, because they are gates for entering into the inwardness of the Torah and its secrets. And we further divided the gates into chapters, some short and some long, according to the measure of the inquiry in each chapter. And we entreat the inquirer not to enter these gates of ours unless the keys and the ways of the gates have been handed down to him, for, God forbid, harm would reach him and not benefit. But one into whose hand keys have been handed, in a measure that lets him open our gates, we are assured that in these gates of ours many, many keys to this wisdom will be opened for him. And let the inquirer not expect from us the explanation of matters twice, for that would lengthen our labor. Therefore let him not move on from a chapter until he knows it; for what he needs from it for his understanding we will not repeat, but will rely on what we have already written in the previous chapter. Likewise let him not lift his feet from one gate to another until he understands it properly; and then he will go his way securely and will not fear. Even so, we will not withhold our hand from explaining, as in "as we have written in such-and-such a place" or "as we will explain in such-and-such a place." And these are the names of the gates, each by its standard, in letters:

gates.title: Ten and Not Nine
gates.description: We named it "Ten and Not Nine" because in it is explained how there came to be a consensus in the received tradition of our sages, elders, and prophets that the sefirot are ten — not nine, and not eleven. Its chapters number ten.
chapters: Explanation of the mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, "Ten sefirot of beli mah (without essence), the number ten," etc.
The same mishnah explained in another way, with further passages from the Tikkunim and the Zohar.
Explanation of the aforementioned mishnah, and the passage "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey" (Song of Songs) from the Ra'aya Mehemna.
Explanation that Tiferet tips the balance between Gevurah and Netzach, and between Chesed and Hod, on the basis of reasoning (sevara).
Explanation of the second mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah: "ten and not nine, ten and not eleven."
Explanation of the passage of the Ra'aya Mehemna on the commandment to give the half-shekel.
To save the student from the error of thinking the sefirot are eleven or more on the basis of supposed expertise and the like.
On the necessity of the sefirot from rational inquiry and from Scripture.
An inquiry whether one who denies the sefirot is called a heretic or not.
On the attestation of the ten names within the ten sefirot from the scriptural verses.

gates.title: The Reason for the Emanation
gates.description: We named it "The Reason for the Emanation" because in it is explained the reason why the sefirot were ten — no fewer and no more — and the reason for the existence of emanation itself. Its chapters number seven.
chapters: Explanation of one reason given by R. Azriel, R. Yehudah Chayyat's objection to it, and the resolution of his objections.
Explanation of another reason given by R. Yehudah Chayyat, and the reason of R. Menachem Recanati, and our objection to both — and likewise to R. Azriel.

Explanation of the recognition that our tradition holds them to be ten, from several places in the Talmud and from other compelling proofs; and there, the matter that "the world was created with ten utterances (ma'amarot)."
Explanation likewise of the ten utterances corresponding to the ten sefirot.
Explanation of the passage "these ten Kingships (Malkhuyot) correspond to whom?" in tractate Rosh Hashanah.
Explanation of the reason for emanation and the number ten.
An inquiry whether another emanation like this is possible or not; and there the secret of the reason for emanation and the order of the worlds is revealed.

gates.title: Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter
gates.description: We named it "Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter" because in it is explained whether the Ein Sof is Keter, as many have thought, and whether Keter is counted among the sefirot or not, as R. Shem Tov ibn Shem Tov supposed. Its chapters are eight.
chapters: Explanation of the view of those who say the Ein Sof is Keter, and the refutation of their view from reasoning.
The refutation of their view, and its necessity from many places in the words of the Zohar.
Explanation of R. Shem Tov ibn Shem Tov's view that Keter is not counted among the sefirot, and its refutation from reasoning and from proofs in the words of Rashbi in the Zohar.
Explanation and tikkun of the mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah that seemingly teaches in accordance with R. Shem Tov's view; we offered another interpretation of it.
Explanation of the aforementioned mishnah in the manner that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained it.

The tikkun of the passage of the Idra, "after the beginning was found" (achar de-sharuta ishtekach), which seemingly accords with R. Shem Tov; we cited another commentator's interpretation and our objection to him.
A lengthy explanation of the aforementioned passage.

Explanation of the matter of Da'at and its secret, with an interpretation of a fine passage of Rashbi from the Tikkunim: "In the beginning — two, Chokhmah and Binah; the third, the fear of the Lord; the beginning of Da'at."

gates.title: Self and Vessels
gates.description: We named it "Self and Vessels" because in it we inquire whether the ten sefirot are the very Self (atzmut) of the Godhead, as many have thought, or whether they are His vessels — like a craftsman's tools for working — and not His Self. Its chapters number ten.
chapters: Citation of the words of R. Menachem Recanati, whose view is that they are vessels.
Citation of the words of R. David, whose view is that they are Self.
Our objection to both — to those who say "Self" and to those who say "vessels."
Explanation of our own view: that the sefirot are both Self and vessels.

Explanation of the necessity of our view from the Zohar, with an explanation of part of the passage "Elijah [opened and said]: Master of the worlds, You are One and not in [the sense of] number," etc., in the Tikkunim.
Explanation of the rest of that passage, which, because of its length, we divided into two chapters.
A further proof from a passage of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar: "a point that does not stand in light," etc., concerning the measuring line (kav ha-midah).
A further proof from a passage of Rashbi in the Zohar, Ra'aya Mehemna: "and to whom will you liken Me."
Explanation of the unification of the Ein Sof within the ten sefirot, and whether the act of emanating the sefirot constitutes any novelty or change in the Emanator or not.
Citation of a passage of Rashbi that clarifies all the facets of the inquiry pursued in the previous chapters.

gates.title: The Order of the Emanation
gates.description: We named it "The Order of the Emanation" because in it is explained, regarding emanation, who was emanated by whom and who preceded whom, since the opinions on this are many. Its chapters number six.
chapters: Explanation of the view of the Geonim who say the sefirot were emanated in their order, and the necessity for their intention from Scripture and from reasoning.
Explanation of the passage "open for me" (pitchi li) of Rashbi from the Tikkunim; and there the reason is explained why Yesod sometimes precedes Netzach and Hod.
Explanation of the commentators' view on the order of emanation, and the raising of objections against them.

Explanation that the beings cannot be revealed through Keter, nor through Chokhmah; and there the passage in the Idra de-Nazir is explained — "it is taught: the Ancient of Ancients, the Concealed of the Concealed," the opening of the Idra — and likewise the passage "before the creation of the world, He and His name alone existed."

Explanation of the emanation of the first three sefirot and several aspects of emanation — how many times each sefirah emanated to another in kinds of revelation — and the four arrays of the sefirot in Chokhmah, Binah, Tiferet, and Malkhut; and one passage of the Zohar, "You made them all with wisdom."
Explanation of the order of emanation of the remaining sefirot, and the reconciliation of all the views.

gates.title: The Order of Their Standing
gates.description: We named it "The Order of Their Standing" because in it is explained the order of standing of the emanated sefirot according to their place — not spatial place, God forbid, for they are not spatial, but the place of rank and precedence — since opinions are many. Its chapters number eight.
chapters: Explanation of the order of their standing according to all the commentators' views — that is, the form of the Tree — and the principal proof among them from the words of Rashbi.
Explanation of the author of Me'irat Einayim, who reverses the views for us, and our objection to him.
Explanation of the order of the worlds from the first point to the last; and there the matter of the seven earths from the Zohar is explained.
Explanation of the order of the sefirot from cause to effect (me-illah le-alul) truly and without doubt, and the order by which the sefirot are ten.

Explanation of how the sefirot are distinguished so as to be ten, given that they are spiritual — for the spiritual is not divisible into parts — and the connection of the sefirot among themselves and with the Emanator.
Explanation that the sefirot in their standing are one above the other up to ten, and that their standing is three to the right, three to the left, and four in the center — and all is one.
To explain the matter of the Ein Sof, which has no end, and its expansion through all the grades down to the last point; and the matter of the sefirot, that each is included in its fellow.
To save the student from error in the matter of ha-edut [the term is uncertain in this printing — perhaps "the sefirot" or "the grades"] and their Emanator.

gates.title: Channels
gates.description: We named it "Channels" because in it is explained the matter of the channels that extend from one sefirah to another — how many they are, what they are, and what they serve. Its chapters number five.
chapters: What the matter of the channels is, what is meant by saying "the channels were broken," how many they are, and their form.
Explanation of the channels belonging to Keter and Chokhmah down to Hod.
Refutation of two channels the commentators posited — from Netzach to Malkhut and from Hod to Malkhut; and there the passage from the beginning of Parashat Noach is explained.
Explanation of the two channels in Yesod, one impure and one pure.
Explanation of the matter of the channels according to their varying aspects.

gates.title: Essence and Governance
gates.description: We named it "Essence and Governance" because in it is explained the essence (mahut) apprehended in the sefirot — not actual essence, God forbid — together with matters of judgment (din) and compassion (rachamim), and the governance of the King of the king of kings through them. Its chapters number twenty-six.
chapters: On the sefirot and their union in a single, equal action, despite being divided in their essence — this one judgment, that one compassion; and there the reason for the existence of the ten is explained.

Explanation of the term "sefirot" as applied to the emanated entities, and their agreement upon a single action; and there, the whole existence of the totality of the sefirot as apprehended — their being composed of ten, of seven, of five, of four, and of three.
Explanation of the essence apprehended in Keter, and its being composed of ten; and an explanation of the 620 (tar"kh) pillars of light; and there, part of the prayer of R. Nechunya ben ha-Kanah.
Explanation of the 620 pillars of light in explaining R. Nechunya ben ha-Kanah's words; and there, part of the matters of permutation (tziruf), in its secret.
Explanation of whether Chokhmah is judgment or compassion; and there we cite the words of all the commentators on this and raise objections against them.

Explanation of whether Binah is judgment or compassion, according to the Zohar; and there a passage from the Zohar on Song of Songs is explained, "by the mouth of Elijah it was decreed," etc., and a passage from Parashat Mishpatim, "when Gevurah expands."

On the necessity of determining whether Binah is judgment or compassion; and a passage from Parashat Acharei Mot, "have we not learned, Elokim is in every place," etc. — with its wording cited and notes upon it alone.
The tikkun of the passage and its explanation up to its midpoint, from within which great matters in the aforementioned inquiry are explained.
The completion of the tikkun of that passage, with the bulk of its benefit for the aforementioned inquiry.
On the existence of judgment (din) — whence its coming-to-be first arises, and what its root and source are; and there we cite the words of [Sefer ha-]Orah and raise objections against it.
On the connection of the sefirot and their union with one another, despite some being judgment and others compassion.
Explanation of "sorrow in the inner chambers" (atzivu be-vatei gavai); and there we cite the words of Sefer Otzar ha-Kavod and Sefer Sha'arei Tzedek and raise objections against them.

On the first three sefirot being reckoned as one; the tikkun of what is found in the Tikkunim concerning the exile of the upper and lower Shekhinah; and there, three aspects of the union of the sefirot, and a passage from the Tikkunim concerning "an offering to the Lord."
The tikkun of the passage "eat, friends" (ichlu re'im) in Parashat Vayikra; and the explanation and tikkun of the passage "when [Yod and] Heh join" (kad mitchabberan) in Parashat Lech Lecha.

Explanation of what the Zohar interprets — that one should not engage with the first three sefirot — and the reason for our engaging with them, with the explanation of several passages on this matter.
Explanation of the essence apprehended by us in Chesed from its actions, and the reason for the 72 bridges within it; and an explanation of what is apprehended of Gevurah.

Explanation of the essence apprehended by us from Tiferet; and there, an explanation of the union of Chokhmah with Binah and their coupling (zivug) together, the reason for the matter and what it intends — a lengthy explanation.

Explanation of the union of Tiferet with Malkhut; and there it is explained that their supernal union occurs only through an arousal from below (hit'orerut tachton); and an explanation of a passage from the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit.
Explanation of what the arousal is and whence it derives; and an explanation of a passage from the Zohar, Parashat Noach, "at the time that the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned."
Explanation of the reason for the need for arousal, what the arousal toward Chokhmah and Binah is, and the matter of the Shekhinah among the lower ones being "a need on high" (tzorekh gavoha).
Explanation of the embrace — "His left hand beneath my head," etc. — in the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut, and likewise the matter of the kiss (neshikah).
Explanation of the union proper — its enjoyment, its nature, and what derives from it; and there, the matter of the coming-to-be of souls.
Explanation of the aspects of Malkhut in relation to the limbs of the male, their union in three places, and the union of Chokhmah and Binah in three places.

Explanation of the essence apprehended in the three attributes Netzach, Hod, and Yesod; and of "pleasantness" (no'am) in relation to Netzach and Hod — that within the erasable name they have but one name, as explained in the Zohar.

Explanation that emanation establishes itself upon three lines — the line of Chesed, the line of Din, the line of Rachamim; an explanation of the passage of Parashat Vayechi, "and it was, as the musician played"; and there it is explained that Keter is the secret of Chesed and Rachamim with no admixture of Din at all, in the verse "with wisdom, with understanding, and with knowledge."
Explanation of the essence apprehended in Malkhut, its receiving from all the sefirot, through whom it receives, and its manifestation after the exile (galut).

gates.title: Arbiters
gates.description: We named it "Arbiters" because its inquiry concerns who tips the balance between Netzach and Hod, between Gedulah and Gevurah, and between Chokhmah and Binah — what arbitration is and what it serves. Its chapters number six.
chapters: Explanation of the need for arbitration; and there it is explained that it belongs to the attribute of Chesed to bestow upon the wicked and the good; and a passage from the Zohar, Parashat Terumah, is explained: "and in His goodness" — not "from His goodness."
On arbitration and its function; and there, the matter of "those who dispute for the sake of Heaven" and the dispute of Korach.

On the number of the arbiters; the arbitration of Tiferet between Gedulah and Gevurah is explained; and there, the mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, "three mothers, Aleph-Mem-Shin," and the matter of arbitration in the secret of the four elements — fire, water, air, and earth.
Explanation of the arbitration of Yesod between Netzach and Hod; and there, the passage "for each part there was a counterpart (ben zug)."

Explanation of whether there is arbitration between Chokhmah and Binah, and who the arbiter is; and there, the passage of the Ra'aya Mehemna, "and I am in the midst of the exile"; and there it is refuted that one should say Binah tips the balance between Chokhmah and Keter, as many have interpreted.
Refutation that Keter tips the balance between Chokhmah and Binah, and that Chokhmah tips the balance between Keter and Binah; and the agreement reached as to the arbiter.

gates.title: Colors
gates.description: We named it "Colors" because in it is explained what is intended by the term "color" in the sefirot, and what colors are attributed to the sefirot according to the Zohar. Its chapters number five.
chapters: Explanation of what is intended by colors in the sefirot; and there, an explanation that through the lower actions the upper sefirot are changed, or the reverse.
Explanation of the colors of the first three sefirot, each alone; and there, the matter of darkness in Keter.
Explanation of the colors of the six extremities (vav ketzavot); and there, the seven kinds of gold.
Explanation of the colors of Malkhut.
Explanation of the colors in general — where they are attributed; and there, the explanation of a passage from the Tikkunim, "...these are the heads of the patriarchs (rashei avot)."

gates.title: Tzachtzachot
gates.description: We named it "Tzachtzachot" (the Dazzling Lights) because in it is explained the matter of the ten tzachtzachot that are upon Keter, well-known in the words of the Kabbalists, and likewise the matter of "clear light" (or tzach), "refined light" (or metzuchtzach), and "primordial light" (or kadmon). Its chapters number seven.
chapters: Citation of a responsum to our teacher Rav Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, on the matter of the three tzachtzachot, whose mnemonic is "Kamatz" (קמ"ץ — kadmon, metzuchtzach, tzach).
Explanation of his words, due to their great obscurity.
Emendation of the matter of the three tzachot upon Keter, with additional explanation.
Citation of the wording of Rav Chamai Gaon on the tzachtzachot, with the interpretation of our teacher R. Aharon upon it.
Explanation of a passage from the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, "Ein Sof does not stand," from within which the tzachtzachot and their concealment are explained.
Explanation of the tzachtzachot in the passage of Parashat Noach, "Rabbi Shimon said: I raised my hands in prayer," etc.; and the inquiry is further explained at length.
On the order of the three concealed ones — kadmon, tzach, metzuchtzach — and that they are within Keter just as they are above Keter, and likewise in Tiferet.

gates.title: Paths
gates.description: We named it "Paths" because in it is explained the matter of the thirty-two paths of Chokhmah, in their generality and particularity, and the names assigned to them. Its chapters number six.
chapters: On the number of the paths; the first mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, "with thirty-two paths," etc., is explained; and a passage from the Zohar, Parashat Terumah, on the verse "the heavens declare," from which the matter of sefar, sefer, sippur (number, book, telling) is explained.
On the paths in the verses of the account of Creation, their names, and the explanation of the Geonim's words on each one.
In which eight of the paths are explained.
In which a further eight paths are explained.
In which a further eight of the paths are explained.
In which a further eight of the paths are explained — being four times eight, which are thirty-two; and because of the length of their explanation we divided them into four chapters.

gates.title: Gates
gates.description: We named it "Gates" because in it is explained the matter of the fifty gates of Binah and their cause there. Its chapters number seven.
chapters: In revealing the words of Rashbi on the fifty gates, which correspond to the fifty times the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned in the Torah; the counting of the verses, and the resolution of their apparent redundancy according to the commentators.
Citation of a passage of Rashbi from the Zohar, Parashat Yitro, "that Jubilee" (ha-hu yovla), and what we noted on it, from within which the redundancy of the verses is explained.

Explanation of five preliminaries for understanding the passage: (i) the matter of days and years; (ii) the meaning of shemittin, yovlin, years, months, sabbaths, days, hours; (iii) the matter of the exile in Egypt and its rest; (iv) the purification of Israel from the husks (kelipot) when they left Egypt; (v) the distinction between "Jubilee" (yovla) and "from the side of the Jubilee" (mi-sitra de-yovla).
Explanation of the passage itself and the resolution of its wording.
Explanation of the count of the gates: seven times seven, amounting to forty-nine.
Explanation of the count of the gates: five times ten, amounting to a full fifty.
A reconciliation of the two divisions of the two preceding chapters.

gates.title: The Gate of Manifestations
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Manifestations" because in it is explained the multiplicity of manifestations in the sefirot, despite their being, in themselves, ten alone; and likewise certain known manifestations of the sefirot. Its chapters number four.
chapters: On the manifestations themselves, their cause, their necessity, and their recognition from the words of Rashbi.

With additional explanation of the sefirot in their manifestations and aspects; the second mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, "ten sefirot," etc., "twenty-two letters," etc., is explained; and a passage from the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, on the verse "and the one thousand seven hundred [and seventy-five]."

Explanation of known manifestations explained in the Zohar — a manifestation of Binah, of Tiferet, and of Malkhut; and a passage from the Zohar, "and it shall be on that day, living waters shall go out," concerning the child (yenuka), etc.
On the necessity of the manifestations of Malkhut; and a passage from Sefer ha-Bahir, "the earth was created before the heavens."

gates.title: From Below to Above
gates.description: We named it "From Below to Above" because in it is explained the matter, well-known in Rashbi's words in the Tikkunim, that the sefirot are ten from above to below and ten from below to above. Its chapters number five.
chapters: Explanation of the manifestations of "ten from above to below" and "ten from below to above," and the matter of "their end is fixed in their beginning" (na'utz sofan be-techillatan) — a fine explanation.
Explanation that "from above to below" befalls not only the ten sefirot in their totality, but also some of them relative to others.

Explanation of the essence apprehended in "returning light" (or chozer) or "the reversing light" (mit'hapekh), and its cause; and there, the mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, "male in Aleph-Mem-Shin, female in Aleph-Shin-Mem."

Explanation of the reversing light from a passage of Sefer ha-Bahir, "from above to below we know," etc.; and there it is explained that this matter is found not only in some sefirot but even within a single sefirah.

Explanation of the name filled with yods (milui yudin) in Keter and the filling with alephs (milui alefin); and that even within a single sefirah the secret of returning light is found, even from one part of it to another.

gates.title: ABYA
gates.description: We named it "ABYA" because it is an acronym for Atzilut (Nearness), Beriah (Creation), Yetzirah (Formation), Asiyah (Action/Making); and in it is explained the matter well-known in the Tikkunim — ten sefirot of Atzilut, ten of Beriah, ten of Yetzirah, ten of Asiyah. Its chapters number nine.
chapters: Explanation of the terms Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah and their relation to one another, in both the plain and the inner sense.
In which the portion of Atzilut is explained, and that the names which may not be erased pertain only to the light of Atzilut.
On the portion of Beriah; and there, the matter of the Throne — called by the Kabbalists "the Throne of Glory" (kisei ha-kavod) and in the Zohar kursaya.
On the portion of Yetzirah; and there, the matter of Metatron and "Mitatron," and the passage "and this was formerly in Israel."

Explanation of a passage from Parashat Noach, "the gate of the inner court," etc.; and there, the union through Yesod on the Sabbath, or through Metatron on weekdays; and there it is explained that there is no withdrawal of providence in the world being sustained through the Prince of the World (sar ha-olam).

Explanation of the benefit of the Shekhinah coming through the righteous one (tzaddik) in this world and its union with him; and there, the matter of Yetzirah — a further completion of the interpretation of the passage.
Explanation of the portion of Asiyah; and there, the subjugation of the husks as they draw near to holiness.
Citation of passages from which the four portions together, or three together, are explained; and there, the matter of "sun, stand still in Gibeon."
Emendation of the passages that contradict one another in this inquiry; and there, the matter of inscription (reshimah), engraving (chakikah), hewing (chatzivah), and making (asiyah).

gates.title: The Thigh of Jacob
gates.description: We named it "The Thigh of Jacob" because in it is explained the matter mentioned in the Zohar concerning the sefirah Netzach, which was blemished through the episode of Jacob — "and a man wrestled with him... the sun rose for him and he was limping," etc. Its chapters number four.
chapters: Citation of the words of Rashbi on the aforementioned inquiry, with a note on his words in order to understand its secret.
Preliminaries for interpreting the passage: (i) that the husks do not enter within Atzilut, God forbid; (ii) explanation of Netzach toward the left and Hod toward the right.
In parsing the wording of the passage word by word, with an explanation of the blemish of that attribute and its tikkun.
To reconcile the passages that seemingly contradict one another in this; and there, the passage of Parashat [Teru]mah, "an expansion expands, of good," etc.

gates.title: The Diminishment of the Moon
gates.description: We named it "The Diminishment of the Moon" because in it is explained the diminishing of the supernal Moon, and the existence of the emanation of Tiferet and Malkhut. Its chapters number six.
chapters: Citation of the passage from Tractate Chullin, "Rabbi Shimon said," with all the commentators' views on the matter cited there.

Citation of two passages that dispute one another, both together disputing the passage of the previous chapter: the passage of Song of Songs, "and God created the two luminaries," etc., and the passage of the Ra'aya Meheimna, "and on your new moons" — without notes on the passage itself.
Explanation of the emanation of Malkhut from Tiferet at the beginning of its emanation; and there, a passage from Sefer ha-Bahir, "the light preceded the world."
Explanation that the "sawing apart" (nesirah) of Adam and Eve is not the diminishment, as many have thought; and there, a passage from Parashat Acharei Mot, "she conceived... in love."
Explanation of the diminishment of the Moon, from within which the preceding passages are explained; and there, the first passage of the first chapter.

Explanation and tikkun of the two passages of the second chapter; and there, further, the diminishment, the reason for it, the matter of the accusation (kitrug) within Atzilut, the matter of Malkhut's union — through whom — and who will be with it after its ascent on high.

gates.title: The Four-Letter Name
gates.description: We named it "The Four-Letter Name" because in it is explained the four-letter name, which the Kabbalists hold to be the proper name (shem ha-etzem), whose sanctity is distinct from that of the other names. Its chapters number four.
chapters: Explanation of the superiority of the four-letter name over the other names, for three reasons; and there, the matter of pronouncing the name as written, in the Temple.

Explanation that the four-letter name comprises all of Atzilut; and there, the name in its progressive ascent — Yod; Yod-Heh; Yod-Heh-Vav; Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh — comprising Atzilut; the name filled with yods, with alephs, with hehs, and in the very forms of the letters; and there, the matter of the four arrays of the four letters.
On the filling (milui) of the letters of the four-letter name with yods, alephs, and hehs, and in the very forms of the letters; and there, the matter of the four arrays of the four letters.
Explanation of the four-letter name in each and every sefirah, and their distinction according to their vocalization; and there, a fine passage from the Tikkunim, "Come and see: nine times."

gates.title: The Gate of Names
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Names" because in it is explained the remainder of the names that may not be erased. Its chapters number thirteen.
chapters: The difference between the four-letter name in Tiferet and the four-letter name that is the proper name; and there, four-letter names for each sefirah, one name for them all, and the names that may not be erased; the name Ehyeh in Keter and the four-letter name in Tiferet, with Keter ascending over Tiferet; and there we cite the words of Sha'arei Orah, explain them, and object to them.
Explanation of the name Ehyeh in Keter; and there, a passage from the Zohar, Parashat Acharei Mot, "Said... if it pleases my Father."
Explanation of the name Yah in Chokhmah; and there, the matter of the Shin-Dalet of "Shaddai" and the Tzadi-Bet of "Tzeva'ot," which may be erased, etc.

Explanation of the four-letter name with the vocalization of "Elohim"; and there, the two sheaths of the name — one Heh for judgment, one Heh for compassion — and why the judgment-sheath is in Binah and the compassion-sheath in Malkhut.
Explanation of the name El in Chesed; and there, the matter of "the great, the mighty God."
Explanation of the name itself; and there, a passage from Song of Songs, "the second chamber, El," etc.
Explanation of the name Elohim in Gevurah; and there, a passage of Song of Songs, "the third chamber, Elohim," etc.
Explanation of the name Elohim in Binah as well; and there, a passage of Bereshit, "at the time that the Enclosure," etc.

Explanation of the name Elohim in Malkhut as well; and there, a passage from Parashat Bereshit close to the preceding, "Rabbi Shimon said: 'By the word of the Lord the heavens were made and all their host'."
Explanation of the four-letter name in Tiferet; and there, a passage from the Tikkunim, "the head of the sword is Yod."
On the forms of the letters of the four-letter name; and there, a passage from Parashat Mishpatim, "Come and see, I saw it in a dream."
Explanation of the name Tzeva'ot in Netzach and Hod; and there, the necessity that there is no single name "Elohim Tzeva'ot" or "YHVH Tzeva'ot," contrary to the reason the commentators wrote.
Explanation of the name El Chai in Yesod, the name Shaddai in Yesod, in Malkhut, and in Metatron, and likewise the name Adonai in Malkhut.

gates.title: Particulars of Names
gates.description: We named it "Particulars of Names" because in it is explained the names assigned to the sefirot — the 72-name, the 42-name, the 22-name, the 12-name, the four-letter name, and the twelve havayot. Its chapters number sixteen.
chapters: Introducing the matter of the names and their spirituality; and there we cite the words of Sefer Or ha-Sekhel on the cycling (gilgul) of the four-letter name with the alphabet; and there, an explanation of the four-letter name.
Citation of the words of the author of Ma'arakhot Elohim Chayyim on the cycling of the name with the alphabet, and what we noted upon them.
Explanation of Araritha (אררית"א) and the name A H V Y (אה"וי); and there, the matter of "one, unique, unified" (echad, yachid, meyuchad); and there, the Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael.

Explanation of the four-letter name in the first three sefirot; and there, the matter of "the strong hand," "the great hand," "the lifted hand," "the faint hand" (yad chazakah, yad gedolah, yad ramah, yad kehah).
Explanation of the 72-name — its citation, vocalization, and derivation from the verses; and there, the 72-name in Chesed and the 216 ( R Y V ) letters in Gevurah.
Citation of a passage from Sefer ha-Bahir on the twelve boundaries (gevulin) included within the 72-name, with some explanation of it.
Explanation of the twelve diagonal boundaries (gevulei alakhson) in the body and in the world, and why they are called diagonal boundaries.
Explanation of Teli, Galgal, and Lev expounded in Sefer Yetzirah — its matter in the plain and the hidden sense; and there, the twelve boundaries in Binah, twelve in Tiferet, and twelve in Malkhut.

With additional explanation of the aforementioned twelve boundaries; and there, the 12-name and its vocalization, issuing from "may He bless you, may He shine, may He lift up" (yevarekhekha, ya'er, yisa); and there, a proper diagram for understanding the boundaries, and the sources of the 22-name, the twenty-four four-letter names, and the names of the twelve boundaries.
The completion of the explanation of the passage of Sefer ha-Bahir cited in chapter six.

Explanation of the 216 havayot that are sources for the 72 names according to the author of [Sefer] ha-Orah; the four [forms of] Ehyeh; and the 72 havayot issuing from the four-letter name filled with yods, according to Rashbi in the Tikkunim — the source of the 72-name.
The 42-name and its vocalization; the 42-name issuing from "Bereshit" and from the verse "for all the strong hand"; and the names formed from the initials of [the prayer of] 42.
The order of combining the 42-name from the verse "Bereshit," some particulars of the interpretation found in Rashbi's words, and the explanation of its sources.
Explanation of the combination of the 22-name from the verse of the Priestly Blessing, and the interpretation of the name of Hod, the name of Netzach, and the name of Yesod.
Explanation of the twelve havayot permuted from the four-letter name.
Explanation of their matter and function in the twelve months, the twelve constellations, their cycling and connection; and there, the name of Malkhut.

gates.title: The Gate of Titles
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Titles" because in it is explained the matter of the titles (kinnuyim), the reason for their multiplicity, what they are and their essence; and further, the matter of the human being as a chariot (merkavah) for the sefirot. Its chapters number four.
chapters: Explanation of the matter in saying "eye," "hand," "foot," "ear" with respect to the Godhead — from which aspect each is attributed and in what manner.
Citation of the words of Sefer ha-Orah on revealing the reason for the multiplicity of titles according to the multitude of aspects.

The matter of the chariot; and there, an explanation of the chariot of David, the chariot of Joseph, the chariot of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and the chariot of Moses our teacher, and their differences from one another.
Explanation of a passage from Sefer ha-Bahir indicating that the patriarchs pushed Malkhut away and did not wish to be a chariot for it.

gates.title: Glossary of Titles
gates.description: We named it "Glossary of Titles" — a sufficient treatment for explaining most of what is found in the Book of the Zohar, for these are the principal ones. Its chapters number twenty-three. [The printing lists twenty-two chapters, one per letter Alef through Tav; the stated count of twenty-three appears to be a discrepancy in this edition. Each chapter contains a dictionary-like listing of the Zohar's titles starting with that letter.]
chapters: Entries for Alef
Entries for Bet
Entries for Gimel
Entries for Dalet
Entries for Heh
Entries for Vav
Entries for Zayin
Entries for Chet
Entries for Tet
Entries for Yod
Entries for Kaf
Entries for Lamed
Entries for Mem
Entries for Nun
Entries for Samekh
Entries for Ayin
Entries for Peh
Entries for Tzadi
Entries for Kof
Entries for Resh
Entries for Shin
Entries for Tav

gates.title: Palaces
gates.description: We named it "Palaces" because in it is explained the matter of the seven holy palaces as found in the Zohar; and there too we explain part of the matter of the angels. Its chapters number fifteen.
chapters: Explanation of the first palace.
Explanation of the second palace.
Explanation of the third palace.
Explanation of the fourth palace.
Explanation of the fifth palace.
Explanation of the sixth palace.
Explanation of the seventh palace.
Explanation of the seven dwellings (medorin), which are seemingly the seven palaces, as explained in Rashbi's words in Parashat Terumah.
Explanation of whether the palaces belong to Atzilut, Beriah, or Yetzirah, and the necessity of the agreement reached from Rashbi's words.
On the distinction between souls, angels, and beasts, their superiority one over another, and their nature.
With additional explanation on the creation of the angels, their benefit, the reason for the need that arises concerning them, and the matter of "and God happened upon Balaam."

In noting that, since the rank of the righteous is above that of the angels, what then is the rank of Elijah and Enoch, who were righteous men yet became angels; and there, their matter from many passages; and there, the matter of Enoch.

Explanation of the matter of Elijah — what his rank was and by what merit he ascended to be a ministering angel; and there, why Moses our teacher and the patriarchs did not merit that rank, despite being among the choicest of created entities.
On Elijah and his status before he ascended to that grade, and whether he was an angel beforehand or not.
Explanation of the embodiment of the angels to be seen by human beings; it is explained that the angels have no knowledge in this world, and that the angels' principal sustenance is from Chesed.

gates.title: The Gate of Substitutes
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Substitutes" because in it is explained the matter of the husks, which are evil substituted [temurat] for good, and their existence, whence they come. Its chapters number seven.
chapters: Explanation of the coming-to-be of the husks — whence it was — through fitting analogies, and the words of Rashbi from the Zohar.
Explanation of the path of the ascent of souls and the descent of angels without passing through the husks, so as not to be embodied in the impure air (avir tamei).
Explanation of the benefit of the husk for the concealed things; and there we explain the benefit of the evil inclination in the human being and its necessity, whence it derives.
Explanation of the ten husks, their names, and their functions, one by one, to establish their reckoning.
Explanation of the matter of Lilith, Machalat the daughter of Ishmael, the "skin-serpent" (tanin or), and the twelve impure boundaries of the husk.
That the husks do not enter into Atzilut; if so, what is the matter of their blemish that is referred to in connection with the sefirot.
Explanation that some of Rashbi's passages suggest the husks are ten, some suggest they are three, and some places suggest they are four.

gates.title: The Gate of the Substitute Palaces
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of the Substitute Palaces" because, just as holiness has palaces, so the husks have palaces, and they are seven. Its chapters number eight.
chapters: Explanation of the first palace.
Explanation of the second palace.
Explanation of the third palace.
Explanation of the fourth palace.
Explanation of the fifth palace.
Explanation of the sixth palace.
Explanation of the seventh palace.
Explanation of the three divisions of the air with respect to the powers of the husks.

gates.title: The Gate of Letters
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Letters" because in it is explained the matter of the twenty-two letters in general and in particular. Its chapters number twenty-seven. [The printed index omits the entry for the letter Dalet and passes from "chapter 7" (Heh) to "chapter 9" (Vav), although it states the count as twenty-seven. In the body, chapter 7 treats Dalet and chapter 8 treats Heh; the Dalet entry is supplied here in brackets and Heh is numbered 8, so that the list matches the chapters.]
chapters: Explanation of the sanctity of the Torah and the four divisions among those who study it — all of them holy — and within them, the Divine Name.
Explanation of the spirituality of the letters and their recognition.
Explanation of the spirituality of the letters in the sefirah in general, and their divisions corresponding to the lamps of the menorah.
Explanation of the letter Alef.
Explanation of the letter Bet.
Explanation of the letter Gimel.
[Explanation of the letter Dalet.]
Explanation of the letter Heh.
Explanation of the letter Vav.
Explanation of the letter Zayin.
Explanation of the letter Chet.
Explanation of the letter Tet.
Explanation of the letter Yod.
Explanation of the letter Kaf.
Explanation of the letter Lamed.
Explanation of the letter Mem.
Explanation of the letter Nun.
Explanation of the letter Samekh.
Explanation of the letter Ayin.
Explanation of the letter Peh.
Explanation of the letter Tzadi.
Explanation of the letter Kuf.
Explanation of the letter Resh.
Explanation of the letter Shin.
Explanation of the letter Tav.
Explanation of the final letters MaNTzPaKh (מנצפ"ך).
Explanation of the existence of the source from which the twenty-two letters were emanated, and the matter of their existence in the secret of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah.

gates.title: The Gate of Vowel-Points
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Vowel-Points" because in it is explained the matter of the vowel-points (nekudot) and their secret. Its chapters number six.
chapters: On the existence of the vowel-points, their spirituality, and their division, despite their being equal.
Explanation of cholam, shuruk, and chirik with a Yod.
Explanation of the "servants" of the preceding three — namely kibbutz (pursing of the lips), chataf-kamatz, and chirik without a Yod.
Explanation of tzere and segol.
Explanation of kamatz and patach, chataf-segol, and kamatz, patach, and sheva alone.
Explanation of the source from which the vowel-points were emanated, and the matter of their illumination within the letters.

gates.title: The Gate of Cantillation Marks
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Cantillation Marks" because in it is explained the matter of the cantillation marks (te'amim) and their secret. Its chapters number five.
chapters: Explanation of zarka, makaf, shofar holekh, segolta.
Explanation of pazer gadol, yerach ben yomo, karnei farah, ga'aya, telisha, tirtza.
Explanation of azla, geresh, pesek, revia, kadma, zakef katan, zakef gadol.
Explanation of all the remaining cantillation marks.

Explanation of the source from which the cantillation marks in general were emanated, the matter of their illumination within the vowel-points, and the secret of their movement in pronunciation (havarah).

gates.title: The Gate of Permutation
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Permutation" because in it is explained the matter of tziruf (permutation), which has three parts — permutation (tziruf), substitution (temurah), and gematria — whose secret is explained in this gate. Its chapters number eight.
chapters: Explanation of the operation of permutation with simple letters.
Explanation of the operation of permutation with the doubled letters (otiyot kefulot).
Explanation of the secret of permutation in its concealment.
Explanation of the operation of permuting the vowel-points.
Explanation of substitution (temurah) in the twenty-two alphabets (alfa-betot) and the 231 ( R L A ) gates, front and back.
On arranging the four circles to generate the 231 gates and the twenty-two alphabets; and there, their secret and their concealment.

On the surpassing excellence of the alphabet that ascends and descends, and likewise the [computation underlying the names] 72 and 42; and the passage of Parashat Terumah, "there, of forty-two letters."
On gematria and the kinds of number, and the secret of initial letters (rashei tevot), final letters (sofei tevot), and middle letters (tokhei tevot), with further hints at it.

gates.title: The Gate of the Soul
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of the Soul" because in it is explained the matter of the soul in all its particulars and generalities. Its chapters number eleven.
chapters: Explanation of the place of emanation of the three parts — nefesh, ruach, neshamah — from the supernal roots, and their being included of twenty-four.

Why the ruach and the nefesh do not return to their foundation, which is the supernal roots, but remain — the ruach in the lower Garden of Eden and the nefesh in this world — as explained from Rashbi's words.

Explanation that there are people who have a nefesh but no ruach, and all the more so no neshamah; some who also have a ruach; and some who also have a neshamah; and there, the matter of the two angels that accompany a person, and from which place they were emanated; and likewise the matter of the evil inclination and the good inclination.
Explanation of the matter of the "image" (tzelem) and its coming-to-be from the roots, what the tzelem and its accidents are upon its ascent, and all its matters.
Explanation of the benefit of the soul in its coming into this world.

Further explanation on the matter of the garments (levushim); and the matter of Israel — after their pollution (zuhama) ceased, why they did not enter the Garden of Eden; and the matter of the first Adam; and the matter of those who did not die, what their rank is.
On the matter of the covering of the regretful sinner (ha-choteh ha-toheh), explained in the Zohar: the interpretation of "we have learned: good deeds," etc.
Explanation of the portions (netachim) of the human being and his limbs in the way of secret.
The existence of the bond and union of the soul with the body, and the secret of its coming to this world.
On the blemishing of the nefesh itself, and the rank of the masters of repentance (ba'alei teshuvah).
On its blemishing within the supernal roots.

gates.title: The Gate of Intention
gates.description: We named it "The Gate of Intention" because in it is explained the benefit of intention (kavanah) and the secret of intention within the supernal roots, without sin and without transgression. Its chapters number three.
chapters: Explanation of the benefit of intention, and the secret of how the one who directs intention causes the effluence (shefa) to flow through his channel.
Explanation of the harm caused by one who does not know and direct intention, and the proper order for the one who directs intention according to the known and rectified order.
Explanation of the matter of intention in the divine havayot, names, and titles.

text: The First Gate, called "Ten and not Nine":

It is known and well established that, in the matter of the number of the sefirot, all who engage in this concealed wisdom have agreed unanimously that they are ten, and on this matter there is no dispute whatsoever.

Now this is one of the matters concerning which a covenant was sealed in the wisdom of the sefirot. And we possess the Sefer Yetzirah, which is attributed to Abraham our father, peace be upon him; some attribute it to Rabbi Akiva, but this is not agreed upon.

Now the words of this book are deep and lofty, and they are hidden from the discerning eye of those who contemplate; and even though many varied commentaries have been written upon it, in all its parts we still require instruction. Yet we shall expound its words as far as is possible for our poor and limited intellect. These are its words: "Ten sefirot of belimah: the number of ten digits, five opposite five, and the covenant of the Unique One set balanced in the middle, in the word of the tongue and in the word of the [male] member [ma'or]." Thus far its words.

Although it occurred to us not to explain this mishnah — for its depths and secrets are concealed from us, being certainly above our intellect, and no one can descend to the depth of its language except Rashbi, peace be upon him, and Rabbi Akiva, peace be upon him, whose stature flesh-and-blood does not attain — nevertheless, because of the obligation incumbent upon us, we shall expound it forcefully. And what there is to scrutinize in it: First, his statement "ten sefirot of belimah, a number" — for in truth "a number" (mispar) is superfluous, since it would have been fitting to say "ten sefirot of belimah corresponding to digits": why "a number"? Second, his statement "five" — what does he need it for? Third, according to his words they amount to eleven, for they are five opposite five, and the covenant which is in the middle makes eleven. Fourth, his saying "by the word of the tongue and by the word of the member" makes it appear that there are two arbiters (makhri'in), and why are there two? Fifth, what is his intent in explaining to us whether they correspond to the digits, for seemingly this is not relevant to the topic he is treating? Sixth, now that he has set out to explain [the sefirot] by way of the bodily limbs, it would have been fitting for him to explain all the limbs in which the sefirot are hinted at, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 4, God willing. We shall say that the author of this book intended in this chapter to hide the whole wisdom of the sefirot and yet to establish it compellingly. He said that they are ten sefirot; and because he said "ten" — from which some notion of limit and corporeality might follow, since they are divided by number — he said that they are "belimah," meaning two words, "beli mah" [without what], the intent being "without essence" (mahut). For although we did not guard the utterance of our mouth in saying "ten," the true belief is that they are "beli mah," without essence. The intent is that they have no essence graspable by human beings, since they are unbounded and not apprehensible, being devoid of limit and corporeality; and that which is incorporeal can be apprehended only in the heart of the enlightened among the people of Israel, by way of vision, as in prophecy. The reason for the number ten, given that they are "beli mah," will be explained in the coming Gates, God willing. He said "a number of ten," etc., lest, out of the great difficulty posed by the limitation of our knowledge, we come to say that there exists nothing but the simple One; therefore he said that they are truly a number. And the term "sefirot" is an expression of number (mispar), for number applies to them, even though they are "beli mah." The proof of this is their very name, that they are "sefirot," an expression of number, as we have explained. And to establish that they are a number, and that their number is ten, he said "a number of ten digits." And the verse says (Psalms 8:4): "When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers."
Now from the verse it is established that the creation of the heavens and their hosts is by means of the "digits," which are a title for the sefirot of the supreme King.

Now the digits are ten; thus it emerges that the sefirot by which the world was created are ten — five against five. He found difficulty in that the verse says (Isaiah 48:13): "My hand also founded the earth, and My right hand spanned the heavens." Here it emerges that the heavens are the work of God's hand, which is five digits, and these are only five sefirot and not ten. To this he said "five against five": since the heavens are the work of God's hand and the earth is the work of God's hand, it appears that certainly the two together are ten — and this is "five against five": five on the right and five on the left, the right for the making of the heavens and the left for the making of the earth. "And the singular covenant set in the middle." He found difficulty in that this is not compelling, for one might say that they are five, or that they are twenty. The reason is that the digits are twenty — ten on the hands and ten on the feet, totaling twenty — [and one might say the same of the sefirot]. Should you say that the ten of the feet are a shadow and likeness of the ten of the hands, so that there are never more than ten sefirot — the hint being that the ten sefirot of Beriah are a shadow and garment to the ten sefirot of Atzilut, as we shall explain in the Gate of ABYA, God willing — then by the same logic we might say that there are never more than five, the five on the left being a shadow to the five on the right, so that there are never more than five sefirot; or the argument returns and we might say they are twenty. To this he establishes both at once by saying "and the singular covenant," etc. The sum of the matter is that, since between the five and the five we find a union and a covenant that unites them, the five on the right and the five on the left are one thing and one matter, whose total is ten sefirot — which is not what we find between the ten on the hands and the ten on the feet, which appear to be two arrays, each of ten, one a shadow and garment to the other. And the arbiter between the five and the five is the "tongue," which tips the balance between the digits of the hands, and the "covenant of the member" tips the balance between the ten of the feet. And regarding the sefirot in this matter — that they are five against five — the commentators gave two explanations. The first: that they arranged the sefirot into two arrays. The first array is Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah — these are five — and they said these are to govern the upper [worlds]. And Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and Malkhut are the second array, to govern the lower [worlds]. And although their statement "to govern the upper" and "to govern the lower" is not agreed upon by us, in the matter of the division of the sefirot they aimed correctly. For such is the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in several places, and especially regarding the tefillin: that the four passages of the head are Chokhmah and Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah; and in the arm they are Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod — thus they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Va'etchanan (folio 264a). And although these matters require vigorous study — for he wrote elsewhere that the four passages are the four letters [of the name] — nevertheless we derive from the totality of his words that the sefirot are divided into two arrays, as the commentators said. Likewise, regarding the chariots within the sefirot, they explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 3, and in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 111) that the "face of a man" upon the Throne is Chokhmah — "koach mah" (the power of "mah"), equal in numerical value to "Adam" — and the eagle is Binah, the lion is Chesed, and the ox is Gevurah; this is the upper chariot. And beneath it a second chariot: the "face of a man" is Tiferet; Netzach, Hod, Yesod are lion, ox, eagle — this is the second chariot. And the supernal Keter includes all above, and Malkhut includes all below. Thus he divided the sefirot into two arrays, as mentioned. And besides these there are many further proofs, but we shall not elaborate, so as not to stray from our purpose.

Now according to this explanation we shall expound this mishnah, namely that Tiferet is the "singular covenant" that ascends higher and higher in the secret of Da'at, binding the upper to the lower by its ascent into the first three sefirot, its arbitration among the "arms" (Chesed and Gevurah), and its emanating into the Netzachs [Netzach and Hod], Yesod, and Malkhut. Thus "the singular covenant, by the word of the tongue and by the word of the member, is set in the middle" — meaning, in the middle of the upper ten digits, the arbiter is Tiferet, which is called "the word of the tongue," as I shall explain. He said "the singular covenant," for a covenant (brit) involves cutting and severing, and through the cutting of that thing the bond of the covenant is made — this is the meaning of "brit." Some read "union" (yichud) and some read "singular" (yachid), and both amount to the same place. The preferable reading is "union" (yichud), for through the covenant comes the union, which is the bond of the matter, its strengthening, and its unification. Some wish to interpret "the word of the tongue" as referring to Binah, but according to our approach it is to be interpreted as Tiferet. Even though "the tongue" is a title for Binah and not for Tiferet, he did not say "the tongue" but "the word of the tongue" — which is the voice and speech that issues from the tongue, that is, by means of the tongue.

Now the voice includes water, fire, and air, as is well known, and these are the three aspects of Tiferet — for it is the air [spirit] that is the arbiter between the water and the fire of Chesed and Gevurah.

Now he did not intend the bodily limb, the tongue, for from that it would be difficult, since then they would be eleven, counting the arbiter. Rather, the arbiter is the voice, which is Tiferet, in the secret of its ascent to Binah, which is the tongue — which is the shofar from which the voice issues, including water, fire, and air. And this is the aspect of Tiferet that ascends among the first three sefirot, and tips the balance between Gedulah and Gevurah — which indicates the binding of the five upper to the five lower, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, God willing. And "the word of the member" is the covenant of circumcision (brit milah); and the meaning of "member" [ma'or] is like "ke-ma'ar ish ve-loyot" (1 Kings 7:36), as the Sages explained (Yoma 54a): "ke-ma'ar," like the joining of a man with his consort (loyah), who is the female. And the intent is to the union which is between the ten digits of the feet, by means of the member that unites them. This explanation is compelling: that "the word of the tongue" unites the ten digits of the hands, and "the word of the member" unites the ten digits of the feet — from what they explained in chapter six [of Sefer Yetzirah], whose words are: "He sealed for him a covenant between the ten digits of his feet, which is the covenant of circumcision, and between the ten digits of his hands, which is the covenant of the tongue." Thus far its words.
Now this mishnah has been explained according to the interpretation that the commentators gave concerning "five against five."

We shall further explain this mishnah according to another interpretation that the commentators gave of "five against five," which is more fitting and acceptable, and is also agreed upon in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in many places. The matter is: five on the right and five on the left. The five on the right are five sefirot whose inclination is mostly toward the side of Chesed, which is the right — namely Keter, Chokhmah, Gedulah, Netzach, Tiferet; and the five on the left are five sefirot whose inclination is mostly toward the side of Din [judgment], which is the left — namely Binah, Gevurah, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And although Tiferet is principally the middle line, its root is Chesed, as is known that it inclines toward Chesed, and its leaning is to the right. And Binah is related to Din in its aspect, for it is called "the worker of mighty deeds (gevurot)," since from it judgments are aroused, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 6. Likewise Hod, of which it is said (Daniel 10:8): "and my splendor (hodi) was turned within me to destruction [mashchit]"; "all the day [I am] faint (davah)" (Lamentations 1:13) — the same letters as "Hod." Yesod, too, has its principal inclination toward the side of Gevurah. So too Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, folio 29b) concerning "the ninth, with joy," etc., whose words are: "And the Tzaddik [Yesod] takes from the left, and the central pillar [Tiferet] takes from the right."

And he further explained there (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 125, belonging to the aforementioned passage) regarding this very matter, whose words are: "The Tzaddik [Yesod] takes to the left, which is Isaac — 'ketz chai,' 'Chai Olamim' (Life of Worlds) — bound to the left," etc. And although the passage in its place requires broad explanation and fine study, from the totality of his words it emerges for us that Yesod's principal inclination is toward the left, the opposite of Tiferet. And it is possible that this is the reason for the two arbiters, besides other reasons there are for the matter, as we shall explain in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 4, God willing. Malkhut, too, is principally Din, for it is well known by name among all the Kabbalists that it is called "the lenient attribute of judgment" (middat ha-din ha-rafah). And although in some places [sources] seemingly dispute this, these matters are well-founded foundations, like firmly planted nails, and the ruling is a true ruling.
Now these sefirot, in their order, are two hands: the right hand is Keter, Chokhmah, Gedulah, Netzach, Tiferet; and the five on the left are the left hand: Binah, Gevurah, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut.

Now Tiferet is the "covenant of the tongue," which is the arbiter between Din and the Chasadim, as is known, and it is itself among the count of the ten. Likewise the "covenant of the member" — although its root is in Yesod — according to this also hints at Tiferet, for "body and covenant we reckon as one," as is explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim many times.
Now it emerges, according to this, that between [the] ten and [the] ten there is no arbitration, as there is arbitration between five and five, as explained above in chapter 1.
Now this mishnah has been explained — a second interpretation — according to what the commentators explained regarding "five against five."

We shall further explain this mishnah — a third interpretation, by another approach to "five against five" — according to what seems right to us; and let him who chooses, choose for himself. Namely, his saying "five against five" does not refer to the aforementioned digits; for he moved from the matter of the ten to explain to us the arbitration between Din and Chesed, the order of the arbitration, and the matter of those that require arbitration. Therefore he said that they are "five against five": that Tiferet tips the balance between Chokhmah and Binah in the secret of Da'at, when it ascends to Keter, as we shall elaborate in the Gate of Arbiters, God willing. Thus [we have] two, one against one: Chokhmah against Binah, for this [Chokhmah] is the root of Chesed and this [Binah] is the root of Gevurah. Furthermore, Tiferet tips the balance between Gedulah and Gevurah, as is known; and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30, folio 75) on the verse "And there was evening and there was morning" as follows: "'And God called the firmament Heaven' — 'And God (Elohim) called' is the supernal Mother (Ima); 'the firmament Heaven' is the central pillar, which is between right and left and includes both; this is the meaning of 'and there was evening and there was morning' — and these are the 'evening' of Isaac and the 'morning' of Abraham." Thus far his words.

And although from the plain sense of the words of this passage there is a proof for our intent, nevertheless, since it has come to hand, let us say a small matter concerning it, and let it not depart without lodging [due attention]. There are points to scrutinize in it: First, his saying "And God called — this is the Mother": have we not heard before now that every [occurrence of] "Elohim" in the account of Creation hints at Binah? Second, what is his intent in saying "Mother (Ima)" and not "Binah," which is its more well-known name? Third, his saying "the central pillar, which is between right and left" — since he said "the central pillar," did we not know that the intent is that it is in the middle of the right and the left, which are Gedulah and Gevurah, that he needed to elaborate, "which is," etc.? Fourth, now that he set out to explain "which is between right and left," let him say "Tiferet, which is," etc., and be silent about "the central pillar," which appears redundant. Fifth, his saying "which is between right and left and includes both" is redundant, for "includes both" is the same as "between right and left." Sixth, his saying "this is the meaning of 'and there was evening and there was morning'" — for seemingly there is no proof at all for his intent from the verse. We shall say that Rashbi, peace be upon him, found difficulty in the verse "And God called the firmament Heaven": for the firmament (raki'a) is Tiferet, and Heaven (shamayim) is also Tiferet — so what is the verse's intent in saying "And God called the firmament Heaven," which makes it appear that "firmament" and "Heaven" are not one thing? To this he answered, "Elohim — this is the supernal Mother." The explanation, as if to say: you already know that every "Elohim" in [the account of] Creation is in Binah, and this "Elohim" is in Binah by the aspect of its relation to the lower [beings] — that it is the one which emanates, that is, which brings forth the emanated [beings] — and from there it is called "Mother"; and this is what he said, "this is the supernal Mother." "The firmament Heaven — this is the [central] pillar," etc. The explanation: Tiferet has two manifestations. The one is from the side of Chokhmah, and it is a more refined manifestation, in that it is the secret of the line of Rachamim [compassion], which is emanated from Keter and spread to Chokhmah, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. And this is the manifestation to which Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is a chariot, as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, folio 29a), whose words are: "And Jacob is certainly the form of the central pillar from the outer side. But was not Moses there too? Rather, [Moses] was from the inner side, and this [Jacob] from the outer side — this one from the body, and this one from the soul." Thus far his words.

Now this manifestation — which is its aspect with respect to Rachamim, without the compounding of Chesed and Din with it — is called "soul" (nishmata) relative to the manifestation that is newly produced from the blending and compounding; and this "soul" is called "firmament" (raki'a). And we may say, by way of permutation, "raka yod" (the Yod was spread out), for it is the manifestation that was spread out and extended from Keter by means of the Yod, which is Chokhmah. And this manifestation he indicated by his expression "the central pillar" — meaning the central pillar and line, which has no admixture of Chesed and Din at all, but is between the two; and this is what he said, "which is between right and left." And by means of Binah this firmament was rectified, and it was clothed in the totality of fire and water, which is called "Heaven" (shamayim) — and this is "He established the heavens through understanding (tevunah)" (Proverbs 3:19). And the aspect that includes this manifestation is Binah, called "Mother" (Ima), which is the existence of the letter Heh — which is three Vavs, which are the three lines, Chesed, Din, and Rachamim — as we shall explain in the Gate of Manifestations, God willing. Therefore he said "and includes both" — meaning, from the side of the Mother it includes the right and the left, which is the garment that is clothed upon, and crowns, the more refined manifestation. And there is a proof for this from the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (folio 84a), whose words are, on the verse "Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Zion, etc., upon the diadem [atarah] with which his mother crowned [ittrah] him" [Song of Songs 3:11]: "What is 'with the diadem'? Rabbi Yitzchak said: as it is written, 'And Saul and his men were encircling (otrim) David' [1 Samuel 23:26] — because he is crowned with white, with red, with green, with all colors, all of which are included in it and encircle it. Rabbi Yehudah said: 'with the diadem with which his mother crowned him' — what is the diadem? As it is written, 'Israel, in whom I will be glorified (etpa'er)' [Isaiah 49:3], and it is written, 'and the house of My glory (tiferet) I will glorify (afa'er)' [Isaiah 60:7]." Thus far his words.

And he explained "King Solomon" [as] the King to whom the peace (shalom) belongs — that is, Tiferet — and Yesod, "peace is his." And the diadem is the manifestation called "Heaven" (shamayim), which surrounds his simple manifestation called "firmament" (raki'a), emanated from Chokhmah. And this is "with the diadem with which his mother crowned him," which is the "Elohim" mentioned in the matter before us. Therefore he said above, "this is the Mother," which is Binah, the mother of the children. And "atarah" (diadem) is an expression of encircling and enveloping, as in "And Saul and his men were encircling David," that is, surrounding. And he explained that this crowning is in three colors: white, from the side of Chesed; red, from the side of Gevurah; and green, compounded of the two, which is the blend blended by the "man in between" (the mediator), Tiferet. And lest we err to say that the white and the red are not in the manifestation of Tiferet, but only the green, he said "all of them are included in it and encircle it." The explanation: "King Solomon," which is the spiritual aspect from the side of Chokhmah — also called "King Solomon," as I shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, God willing — is surrounded by the three colors, and they truly encircle it. And it is white with respect to its aspect toward Chesed, red with respect to its aspect toward Gevurah, and green with respect to the aspect of both in the equilibrium of the blend; and all of them surround it and crown it. And Rabbi Yehudah explained "with the diadem" in another way, adding to Rabbi Yitzchak and saying that it is not only this, but the diadem is the totality of all six extremities (ketzavot) — for with respect to this aspect the title "Tiferet" is apt, since it is from the term "pe'orot" (boughs), and like "pa'arei ha-migba'ot" (the adornments of the caps) (Ezekiel 39:28), meaning branches — that is, that it branches out into six extremities, and the six extremities are its branches. And this is what is said: "Israel, in whom I will be glorified (etpa'er)." And the explanation: Binah says of Tiferet, which is called "Israel," that in it she glories and branches out into boughs.

And he further brought a proof from the verse "and the house of My glory I will glorify (afa'er)," for she branches out and glories in her boughs. And he means: the "house" of Tiferet above is Binah, for there too is its dwelling (Shekhinah), since it "reaches from end to end" [Exodus 26:28] — from the [one] end of the heavens, which is Binah, to the [other] end of the heavens, which is Malkhut. And just as Malkhut is a "house" for Tiferet, so too is Binah; and this is "the house of My glory I will glorify." The explanation: she branches out together with the boughs of Tiferet, which belong to its measure. Or he means that Malkhut is the "house" for Tiferet. And Binah says "the house of My glory," which is the glory (tiferet) from my side — for from the side of Binah, it [Tiferet] also includes the boughs for its house, which is Malkhut — "I will glorify and branch out," in the secret that she includes six boughs from its side, that it is clothed six within six; and this is "with the diadem," which is this crowning and clothing.
