And because, when His exaltedness is revealed to created entities in Keter, created entities still have no power to apprehend Him, so exalted is that emanated one, He had to emanate Chokhmah, and so from Chokhmah to Binah, down to Malkhut, for there the exaltedness of the King is apprehended. And the parable for this is a ray of the sun entering a house through an aperture, to light the inner side of the house. Because it is so bright, no one in the house can bear it, and their eyes grow dim from looking at the sun, for it is great and dazzles exceedingly; so that they have had to make there a very large lantern, for the light to shine through to its far side, so that those standing in the house receive the benefit of the light and not its harm. And because the light of the sun is so bright in its strength and might, even though the light has been sweetened a little and hidden and concealed a little, those standing in the house, their sight being weak, still need a second screen, and after the second a third, up to ten. And now, when a man comes into the house to enjoy the light that shines through the lantern, and asks why the number of these lanterns is thus and so and not otherwise, we shall blunt his teeth and tell him that it is out of great foolishness that he asks about this. For since the purpose of the screens is to set the light right, so that it is sweetened to the eyes of those who see, then if the screens were fewer, the eyes of those who see would be darkened by the abundance of its light, and it would do harm; and if they were more, the light would be darkened further, and the sweetness of its light would not reach those who see, and "those who look through the apertures would be darkened." And that is not what is intended. What is intended is to set the light right, so that they may enjoy it as bright as it can be, but not in such a way that it is harmful by excess of brightness: rather a bright light, a sweet light, a fragrant light. And a compelling proof for this reason is found in a passage of the Zohar that we shall copy in the Gate of Self and Vessels, with the help of God: it is the passage "To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" etc. And there we showed, from the explicit words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that the principal purpose of the Emanation is "so that they might know Him," etc.: for through the sefirot His greatness is revealed to us. And it is not as we have seen with the investigators, men of darkness and confusion: for because they remove the predicates, the providence of the divinity is hidden from their eyes, and they thought that they had apprehended Him while their heart was far from Him. For they err about the truth of the Ein Sof, blessed be He [holding that because of His great greatness and exaltedness He does not watch over those below], and so they deny His providence and most of His dealings and actions in this world. "Not like these is the portion of Jacob, for He is the former of all." And the matter of His predicates — His sitting and His rising and His walking and His speaking and everything of the kind — is understood by those who know this wisdom, and will be explained at length in the coming Gates, with the help of God.

Now that God has granted us, in the preceding chapters, to set out a seemly and acceptable account of the reason for the Emanation and to ground it in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, we wish in this chapter to treat the matter at greater length and breadth, with the help of God, in such a way that the eyes of the inquirer are enlightened on this matter. And before we come to explain it we shall ask one question, over which some of the investigators of this wisdom have been perplexed: namely, whether the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, has the ability to emanate ten sefirot other than these, or not, God forbid.

Now it is fitting that we investigate: if He is able — since it is the attribute of His goodness to pour effluence upon what is other than Himself — why did He not emanate even a thousand thousand thousands, since this lies within the possibility of His ability, and emanate ten sefirot many times over, and many worlds, in the way that He brought this world into existence? At first sight this question would startle the eyes of the discerning and leave him astounded. But the truth is that this question is a question of great foolishness, and it is out of great folly that the questioner asked it. And the reason is this: we say to the one who asks this question that his question cannot escape three alternatives. Either he is asking that the second sefirot be equal to the true, emanated sefirot: that is, a Keter equal to Keter, a Chokhmah equal to Chokhmah, a Binah equal to Binah, and so with all of them. Or that they be greater than these, that is, subtler than these. Or that they be lesser than these and [more] revealed. Now none of these three aspects is possible. For the sefirot are subtle with the utmost subtlety — that is, spiritual with the utmost spirituality — free of body and of the corporeal and its accidents, as we have explained and as we shall explain in the Gate of Gates. And since it is true that they are not bodies, they cannot be distinct from the Emanator, and come under the count of ten, except by way of cause and effect: that is, the Emanator is cause to the emanated, and there you have a difference between Him and those He emanated — besides other differences which we have no business explaining now.

Now Keter is distinct from Chokhmah in that Chokhmah is the effect of Keter and Keter is the cause of Chokhmah; and this is how they are distinct from one another down to the lowest grade. For apart from this they have no distinction by which to come under the number ten, since what is not a body is not divided into parts, as we shall explain at length in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, with God's help. So when the questioner says that there should be ten other sefirot equal to these, we answer him that it is impossible. For if a Keter is equal to Keter, there cannot be two Keters: by what would they be distinct, so as to be two? Hence from the one, unique Emanator only one emanated being can be emanated. Two is impossible, because there is nothing to distinguish them: both are effects of the First Cause. Otherwise they are not spiritual; and if they are spiritual, they cannot be two. It is therefore necessary that only one emanated being be emanated from the Emanator. And in the same way we answer about a Chokhmah beside Chokhmah, and so for all the sefirot, until we prove conclusively that there can be no ten sefirot but these. And let it not be asked: "If so, God forbid, the Emanator has no power to emanate two equal Keters as His effects, which would be distinct from one another although equal." This is foolishness. For this is not due to any lack or weakness of ability, God forbid, either in the Emanator or in the emanated. On the contrary, it is to their praise. For in order to be distinct they would have to descend to the lowliness of body, which is divided into parts, and that is not fitting. For the greatness of the master is known from the greatness of the servant, and it belongs to his perfection to make what is other than himself perfect. Nor should it be asked: "On the contrary, we would [then] know and recognize His superiority — that He, who is without body, should make it corporeal, and that from being simple and incorporeal, as is known, He should bring body and corporeality into existence. So let Him emanate two Keters, and let them be corporeal." To this we answer you that He has indeed created many of this kind, namely the angels, which in truth are corporeal, although their corporeality is subtle, like the corporeality of fire and subtler still, as is explained in the Gate of the Palaces. Nor should it be asked that He impress into the spiritual [a nature] that, although it is subtle and spiritual, it should be divided into parts. For that would be a lessening of the spiritual, whose principal perfection lies in its oneness and its being undivided. And the parable for this: a questioner would not ask, "Does a king have the power to be a servant? And since he does not have the servant's ability, the servant turns out to be more praiseworthy than he." On the contrary: he certainly does; but if he did so, it would be a debasement and a lessening of the crown of kingship, and the honor of a king is to keep himself far from every kind of servants' service. So it is with the Emanator and the emanated: it is to the Emanator's praise to impress into the emanated the power of His seal, that they be simple, not composite, and far from corporeality and from all its accidents.

Thus we have proved that it is impossible for them to be equal. And now we say that to ask that they be greater than these is likewise no right question, and there is no truth in his words. For there is no difference between the Emanator and the emanated except the difference between cause and effect; and as near to the Emanator as it is possible for an emanated being to be, so near has Keter been brought — to the point that there is no room left to say that there could be an emanated being between Keter and the Emanator: there is only the fact that the one is cause and the other effect. And this is what necessitates its descent from the rank of the Emanator — a descent that is nonetheless great without end, for it is dark before its Emanator, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. And there is no room to ask why the Ein Sof did not emanate Keter exactly equal to Himself, since power is not lacking. For the truth is that the emanated cannot be equal to the Emanator; and this is not because of any lack in the Emanator, but because of the nature of the emanated. For once it is emanated, it is the effect of its cause, and its cause is above it, with a certain priority in several respects, since no effect can attain to its cause. It therefore follows of necessity, from its being emanated and an effect, that it descends from before its Master by the difference that lies between cause and effect. And what causes it this lack is that it is emanated and an effect, and the First Cause is prior to it. With this the question whether that [other] Keter could be greater than this Keter is also removed, since this Keter is the greatest that is possible under the law of the emanated. And to say that it should be less than this is likewise impossible; for there already is something less than it, which is Chokhmah, and whatever would rise above Chokhmah is Keter. That is: since Chokhmah is the effect of Keter, and descends from Keter only by what lies between cause and effect, one cannot ask for another emanated being between Chokhmah and Keter. For this emanated being cannot be equal to Keter, nor equal to Chokhmah, for the reason we have explained; and between Keter and Chokhmah it is impossible, because Keter and Chokhmah are cause and effect, and there is no gap between them that could admit an effect prior to Chokhmah and posterior to Keter — unless Chokhmah were to descend to the place of Binah, that is, the third effect; and then these would simply be Chokhmah and Binah. And with this all the questions are removed altogether.

And now, by what we have raised here, we shall explain the matter of the three aspects in each sefirah, on which we shall speak at length in the coming Gates, with the help of God. They are these: each and every sefirah has three aspects — first, its aspect relative to what is emanated from it; second, relative to itself; third, relative to its emanator. And the point is that in Keter itself, since it is emanated from the Emanator, who emanates and is not emanated — of whom it is certainly forbidden to speak at length, and may God forgive us for having spoken of Him at such length until now — [we say no more]. And so, in Chokhmah, which is emanated from Keter, there must be an aspect that is level [mishtaveh, with its emanator] — that is, a nearness that is united with its emanator, which is Keter, such that there is no distinction between them at all. After that it descends within itself and becomes distinct, from itself to itself, until it comes to be the cause of Binah, which is its effect.

And within it itself there must be the aspect of cause to effect, so that it rises from aspect to aspect, ever higher. And to illustrate this: the aspect that is level with Keter is the cause of the aspect of its own self, and the aspect of its own self is the cause of the one that is level with Binah [and likewise in each and every aspect there will be these same three aspects — from Asis Rimonim]. And between every two aspects three further aspects are necessary: namely, the aspect that makes the first aspect level with Keter, the aspect itself, and the aspect that makes it level with its own self. And let us draw a bodily figure from which the intellect may rise to the spiritual: as though we were to draw a rosh tor [a wedge], that is, this elongated triangle.

Now this triangle slopes downward, and it widens toward its top. It is a parable for the emanated: the nearer they come to their source, the more exalted and the wider they are — not a width of limit and body, but a width of subtlety and spirituality.

And when the inquirer looks well, he will find that the top of Keter is wide, and that it slopes and goes on narrowing until its width comes to be level with the width of Chokhmah. And even at the place where Keter and Chokhmah are level there is a great difference; for this is necessitated by that which pours forth [mashpi'a], sloping [meshuppa] downward, whose descent has no resting-place. For the farther it moves from the upper face, the more the emanated is revealed and is caused by its cause, which is above it. And this is "cause and effect," for one who has the eyes of intellect and whom YHVH has graced with knowledge. And this is the secret of "each one includes ten," and the secret of the descent of the grades within the very self of the sefirah. For the Keter-within-Keter is the side that draws near to the Emanator, and the Malkhut-within-Keter is the side that draws near to Chokhmah, and the Keter-within-Chokhmah is the effect of the Malkhut-within-Keter. And all this can be seen from the figure we have drawn. For the narrow part of Keter is the cause of the wide part of Chokhmah; and so the Keter-within-Chokhmah is the side that draws near to Keter, and the Malkhut-within-Chokhmah is the side that draws near to Binah, and the Keter-within-Binah is the effect of the Malkhut-within-Chokhmah. And on this model it must likewise be said that each and every part itself includes ten sefirot, because the light has no resting-place but keeps moving away and descending; and each and every point, each and every part, is the cause of the point below it and the effect of the point above it. And He saw in His wisdom that unless Keter itself descended ten degrees, Chokhmah could not be emanated from it at all. Likewise, had Chokhmah not descended ten degrees, it would not have been possible for Binah to be emanated from it. And so with all the sefirot, and so with all the parts and the points. And the same rule and the same reason hold for ABYA [Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah]: for in Atzilut there is ABYA, and in Beriah there is ABYA, and in Yetzirah ABYA, and in Asiyah ABYA. For ABYA is the sum of all that is distinct from the First Necessary One, the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, from Keter down to the central point at the navel of the earth; and they are the kinds of their descent, in four grades. And each one of them, in turn, when we come to divide them, we divide into four grades, and each and every grade into four grades; except that the four of Atzilut are so subtle that the Asiyah-within-Atzilut is the cause and origin of the Atzilut-within-Beriah, and likewise the Asiyah-within-Beriah is the cause and origin of the Atzilut-within-Yetzirah, and so in this order with all the grades and all the parts — so that existence turns out to be like a jointed lampstand, [its parts] united and embracing one another, as explained. And having raised this, I wish by means of it to address the question of the number ten that we asked in the preceding chapters. It is known that every effect is encompassed by its cause, and the cause encompasses the effect, as we shall explain at length in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, with God's help. And now let us draw a bodily figure, namely a circle within a circle, like this:

— so that no gap comes between these spheres. And now, if the questioner should ask why this draftsman did not draw yet more circles inside these circles, surely we shall blunt his teeth and tell him that he "has gathered the wind in his fists." For there can be no further addition to the number of circles, since they descend one from another by [no more than] a point, and there cannot possibly exist another circle within the great circle that encompasses them all within it.

Now from the bodily figure let us raise our intellect to the spiritual matter that we are explaining. It is known that the sefirot descend one from another by the difference that lies between cause and effect; and therefore they are one within another, the effect encompassed by the cause, like these circles, where the larger encompasses the one smaller than it, which is the effect. Thus Keter encompasses Chokhmah and is its cause, and Chokhmah descends from Keter by the measure of what lies between cause and effect; and Chokhmah is the cause of Binah, so that Binah descends one grade from Chokhmah and two grades from Keter, being the effect of that [Chokhmah] which is the effect of it [Keter]. And in this way the grades descend down to Malkhut.

And Malkhut is the end of Atzilut and the beginning of Beriah, and it is to Beriah as the Ein Sof is to Atzilut; and the last grade in Beriah is to Yetzirah as Malkhut is to Beriah. And this is their order, until they come to the spheres by way of degrees that are concealed and hidden from us, and revealed to those versed in the account of Creation and the account of the Chariot.

And there is no difference between Malkhut and Beriah except the difference between cause and effect. And with the descent from the last grade of Atzilut there had necessarily to be the beginning of Beriah, which is the grade that is united with Atzilut as the effect is united with its cause; and so from Beriah to Yetzirah, and so from Yetzirah to Asiyah, down to the spheres.

As for the order of the spheres, the astronomers, dim of sight, imagined that each sphere is adjacent to the next, so that no gap comes between them. But this is not the view of the masters of the Torah, who see by the everlasting light; rather, between one firmament and the next is a journey of five hundred years. And although there is this air between them, the matter nevertheless shows the evenness of the creation and its necessity, and that there could not be less than this between sphere and sphere — until the matter comes down to the element of fire; and the element of fire is united with the element of air, and the element of air is united with the element of water, and the element of water is united with the element of earth, one above the other, with no gap between them. And now, who gives a man a mouth to ask, "Let there be so many grades more, or so many fewer," or "Why did He not create the world larger than this, or smaller?" For all this is great foolishness to those who know the order of the grades. And the constitution of the world is in the most excellent way possible, in the order of the grades from the highest that can exist to the lowest that can exist, whether in limit, in finitude or in corporeality. And indeed, were the order of the sefirot not between Him and the world, the world, on account of its lowliness, could not be governed by the Ein Sof — unless the world were to rise to the spiritual grades, which are the sefirot; and for that He has already emanated the sefirot. And the intent is nothing other than to reveal the Emanation and the divinity, and not to conceal it. And it is revealed through the descent of the grades to the lowest aspect, where they now are. For even this thick, coarse earth, down to its navel, has grade after grade, to seven earths, as we shall explain something of this in [the Gate of] the Order of Their Standing, with the help of God. This is the reverse of the view of the foolish astronomers, who imagined they could give the measure of the earth and said that a line of twenty-two thousand mil would encircle it round about, and that, were the earth bored through, [the bore] would pass through to its underside through a thickness of seven thousand three hundred and thirty-three and a third mil. And they walk on in darkness.

On this matter we have a received teaching and a weighty precedent, as we shall write in the name of the Zohar in the Gate mentioned. And to return to our subject: had the world been created without intermediaries — apart from the fact that this is impossible, for the reason we have explained —

— this would be a concealment of the divinity. For when we came to know His greatness from His governance, would we not believe that, in truth, He is exalted above His world [only] by what lies between a cause and its cause [that is, by one step of cause and effect]? Therefore, so as not to conceal His divinity, He emanated the grades in the way I have explained. For now, when we look upon Keter, may it be blessed and exalted, and then raise above it its cause, the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings — how greatly is His name magnified in the eyes of all His created entities!

And so this glorious chapter is complete, and this Gate is concluded. And since YHVH has blessed us thus far, and helped us in all the way that we have gone, we are journeying to the place that we know: namely, to investigate whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, with the help of Heaven.
The Third Gate: To Know Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter:

What is intended in this Gate is to discuss the matter of the perplexity that has fallen among the Kabbalists, [in coming] to know whether the Ein Sof is the Keter itself or other than it. And this is its name, by which they call it: "Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter."
Chapter One:

Many of the Kabbalists among the people of our nation have been perplexed with a great perplexity, and have fallen into the pit of error, and thought that the supernal Keter is the Ein Sof, and that it is in the number of the ten. And [there are] some of them who said that, since we have ten grades, what need is there for a further emanation? — but rather that the matter of the Emanator with the emanated [beings] is [the] ten. And they [thought to] support themselves from the mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, which said "ten and not nine, ten and not eleven"; and they said that [its] saying "and not eleven" [means] to say that we should not add further upon ten — but [rather] that the ten are precisely [the count], [including] the Emanator, who is the Ein Sof, the supernal Keter. This is their way — and may their Master forgive them, for this is a matter of cutting [the shoots] and separation; and one who looks at what I explained concerning that mishnah, in the First Gate, ch.6, will see that, on the contrary, from there [comes] a proof to the opposite.

Now this view is rejected for several reasons. If you wish, [argue] from Scripture; if you wish, [argue] from reason. The [argument from] reason is: that since the Emanator is distinguished from His emanated [beings] in several matters — first, that the emanated [beings] fall under time, and He does not fall under time. And I do not wish to say "time" according to what appears from the plain sense of our words, but the intent is that there was already a time when they were not emanated, as [for instance] before the Emanation. And this is one of the things impossible in the Ein Sof — that there was [ever] an existence in which He did not exist; rather, He is necessarily existent, and He brought time into existence, and not that He is possessed of time, God forbid. And in this matter is understood [the saying] "first, yet there is no beginning to its beginning" — for although we say "first," and every expression "first" indicates that it has a beginning (for it is true that He is first to all that come after Him) — yet the expression "first" indicates the beginning of time. And therefore it said that He is first, and even so there is no beginning to His beginning; and the expression "first" is only to negate that no other preceded Him. And this is what is said in the Tikkunim, "I am first and I am last." And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Ani (I) is Ayin (Nothing), which is the supernal Keter. And "I" (ani) is Malkhut, which is the end of the Emanation — "its end embedded in its beginning and its beginning in its end" — for Ayin [Nothing] is Alef = supernal Keter, Yod = Chokhmah, final Nun = Binah, with the extension of the Vav, which is [the] Nun, [i.e.] Yod upon Vav; and the final Nun itself is Malkhut, in truth. It is found [that] Ayin includes the whole Emanation. And this [is] "I am first" — the secret of the extension and spreading of the Emanation from above to below; and "I am last" is the existence of the returning light, reversing from below to above. And by this is understood the matter of "first and last": for Keter is truly called "first," because it is first to all that come "in the beginning," which is [the emanated and below]; but above it, in the Ein Sof, the expression "first" does not apply. And this is "and before One, what can you count?" — the meaning [being]: Keter is called "one," which is the beginning of the count, which is the number of the ten, in which the whole count is included, and the count's foundation is above, as we explained in the preceding Gate. And it said that "before One" — which is that [which is] prior to it, namely the Ein Sof — "what can you count?", for there applies there neither number, nor speech, nor any necessity at all. And of Him it is said (Job 37:20), "shall it be counted to Him when I speak?" — for number does not apply there. And with this premise is understood the verse (Isaiah 43) in which all the literalists were perplexed: "You are My witnesses, says YHVH, and My servant whom I have chosen, that you may know and believe Me and understand that I am He: before Me no God was formed, and after Me there shall be none." And the explanation: "that I am He" — namely Keter, for it is Keter that is truly called "He" (Hu); and to indicate its concealment, the word "Hu" [is] a pronoun for the hidden [third person]. And therefore it said that it is also called "I" (Ani), to indicate that it is the beginning of the Emanation and the end of the Emanation, in the secret of "I am first and I am last," as explained. And it said "before Me no God was formed" — and the word "formed" (notzar) [is] according to its plain sense, whose meaning is "was not emanated"; for the expression "formation" (yetzirah) too serves [to denote] the Emanation, just as the expression "creation" (beri'ah) serves, namely "In the beginning [God] created." And it said: "before Me none was emanated" — for it [Keter] is the head [first] of those that come within the category of the emanated; and it is the end of the whole Emanation, and this is what is said "and after Me there shall be none." And this indicates the strength of the greatness of the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, which indicates His endurance — that He does not fall under time, but, on the contrary, He brought time into existence, and the existence of His non-being cannot be depicted in any manner in the world. And this is one of His many superiorities over His emanated [beings]: that all of them fall under [contingent] existence, [in] that there was already a time when the Ein Sof was without them, as before the Emanation. And many have thought to say that Keter was prior to all — that is, that, although there was no Emanation, it was in existence, and it is a garment to the Emanator forever. And the holders of this view are masters of the shields [formidable scholars]; and the principal necessity that compelled them to this matter is their saying, of blessed memory, in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, "before the world was created, He and His name alone existed" — the meaning [being] that "He and His name" are the Ein Sof and Keter; and they necessitated from this that Keter is prior, and that it is unified with the Emanator and a garment to Him. But this matter is not fitting to be believed. Rather, that the whole Emanation was emanated at one time, and Keter too is among the emanated [beings], as is necessitated from several passages, some of which we shall copy in the Gates, with God's help — and in particular in the Gate of Self and Vessels, and in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, and the Gate of Tzachtzachot, with God's help. It is found that the Emanator is exalted above His emanated [beings] — for His emanated [beings], their non-being preceded them; which is not so [with] the Emanator, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. And behold, [this is] a first distinction. Further, the Emanator is distinguished from the emanated [beings] in that their life depends on another — namely, on the Emanator who gives them life; and He is the source and the light and the effluence to all His emanated [beings] — they are found, all of them, to need Him; whereas the Ein Sof, blessed be He, needs nothing other than Himself, but is the source of life, and life is found from Him, until He is the life of [all] life. And therefore, in some places, Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim, called Him by the expression "a light that does not subsist in [another] light," etc. — since He does not depend on life and effluence from the side of another, but is the source of light to all the other luminaries. And this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 132b) and in the Zohar [on] Bereshit (22): "Rabbi Shimon opened further and said: 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me.' He said: Companions, hear ancient words that I wish to reveal... What is [the meaning of] what it said, 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me'? Rather, this is the Cause above all the upper ones, that [One] called the Cause of Causes, the Cause [from] among these causes, [such] that none of these causes does any deed until it takes permission from the one above it, as we established above regarding 'let us make man' — 'let us make,' surely, was said of two, [in] that this one said to the one above it... And the one above it does nothing until it takes counsel from its fellow. But the one called the Cause over all the causes, above which there is none and below which there is none equal to it — this is what is written, 'And to whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal? says the Holy One.' He said: 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me,' that takes counsel from Him, in the manner of the one that said, 'And God said, let us make man.'" Thus far [the Zohar's] words.

Now [Rashbi], peace be upon him, intended, in this holy passage, to exalt this superiority — that the Ein Sof is exalted above His emanated [beings], [in] that they need to take counsel, the lower from the upper, for it [the lower] needs effluence from its cause that emanates upon it; and therefore it says "let us make man" — as if to say, "you emanate, and I will act, and man is found made by the two of us"; and the upper one still needs to be emanated [upon] from its cause, for it too does not have the ability [on its own]. But the Ein Sof, blessed be He, does not need to say to another "let us make," but [says] "I, I am He, and there is no god with Me" — that is, "in assistance with Me" — neither a lower one, for it has none below it equal to it, nor an upper one, for there is no upper one other than it, for it is above all the existents. And it said "the Cause over all the upper ones, the Cause [from] among these causes" — [Rashbi] intended to explain to us that the reason it is called the Cause of Causes is for two reasons. The first: from the expression "ascent" (aliyah), and the intent is that it is above all the upper ones — and the intent is not an ascent of place, God forbid, for nothing enters into [the category of] place in the Emanation, all the more so in the Emanator, but the meaning [is] the existence of an ascent of degree, and spirituality, and ability. And the second meaning is from the expression "cause" (illah) and "reason" (sibbah) — that it is a cause and a reason to all the causes that are in existence.

Now a second distinction has been explained, by which the Ein Sof, the Emanator, blessed be He, is distinguished from the emanated [beings]. Further, a third distinction, and it is: that all the emanated [beings] have a name among the holy names, which delimits them, by which that sefirah and that emanated [being] is called — like Ehyeh in Keter, and Yah in Chokhmah, and so for all the rest of the sefirot, as we explained in the First Gate explicitly. And likewise the four-letter name includes the whole Emanation, as is explained in the Zohar, and we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. This is not so [with] the Ein Sof, the Emanator, blessed be He, who has no name and [vowel-]point by which we can designate Him, nor attribute that would delimit Him; and we have not found for Him a name to designate Him except "the Necessarily Existent." And the explanation: that He is necessary in His existence, because the world is impossible, ever, without a conductor who gives effluence and life to all the existents; and for this reason His existence is necessary. And because there is no name that would delimit Him, therefore we designate Him "the Necessarily Existent," and this name the philosophers attributed to Him. Further, they attributed to Him the name Ein Sof (Without End), and the reason [is] because He has no end and terminus. For the thing delimited by a name has an end; and the divinity, because it has no end, has no name that would delimit it, and therefore we designate it by [the name] Ein Sof.

And further [there is] another explanation: because the inquiry into Him has no end — for it is not in the manner of the other inquiries, which have an end and a settling upon a single conclusion; but the inquiry into the divinity is without end, and therefore there is none who knows in Him any essence at all, except by means of the sefirot, which reveal somewhat of His greatness — [and] only from His sefirot and upward; [but] from there [upward] there is no apprehension, on account of the depth of what is apprehended; and therefore they designated Him Ein Sof. Further, they attributed to Him "Cause of Causes," and the intent is that the causes — from which other [things] are caused — are [themselves] caused [by] Him; and therefore He is called "the Cause of [the] causes," since He is a first cause to all the causes in the world: for although they are causes to other caused [things], even so they are all caused [by] Him. And there are [those] who said that the supernal Keter too is called "the Cause of Causes," since it is a cause to all the other causes, which are caused [by] it; which is not so from it [Keter] and below — [in] that Chokhmah is not a cause to all the caused causes, for Keter is the [one] that causes and is not caused [by] Chokhmah, but on the contrary Chokhmah is caused [by] it. And likewise, for this reason, they said that Keter is called "the Cause of Causes," [in] that it is the cause of the causes that are effects of it. However, the Ein Sof is called "the Cause of all causes" and "the Cause over the causes," with the addition of "all," to indicate, concerning the Ein Sof, that it is the cause of all causes — even Keter; which is not so [with] Keter, of which the expression "all causes" does not [rightly] apply (and likewise it lacks the "all"), since there is already a cause and reason of which it is the caused [one] — [in] that Keter is caused [by] the Ein Sof, and the Ein Sof is its cause; and likewise [the expression with "all"] would not be attributed thus to Keter. And these three names — namely, Ein Sof, and "the Cause of all causes," and "the Cause over all causes" — Rashbi attributed to the Emanator, blessed be He, in his books many times; and he likewise attributed to Him other names, such as "the Concealed of the Concealed," and likewise "the Ancient of Ancients," and many like these similar to them; and when the inquirer examines them closely, he will find that they all indicate the concealment, as we explained — that He has no name, nor havayah, nor title that would delimit Him. And behold, [this is] a third distinction, by which the Emanator is distinguished from the emanated [beings] — apart from several other distinctions, such as the removal of measure, and limit, and the predicates, and the changes, for all is in His sefirot; and we shall not prolong [discussion] of them. And let us say that, since the Emanator is exalted and distinguished from His emanated [beings] [to] the utmost of distinction, and is distanced [to] the utmost of distance, then reason gives that it is not fitting for the Emanator to enter into the number of the emanated [beings], God forbid, as those thought who said that He is the Keter. And now let us come to prove [it] from the proofs.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, established from reason that Keter is not the Ein Sof, now we shall come, in this chapter, to nullify this view from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who enlightens the eyes of Israel in this wisdom; and we have from his words several proofs. First, he said in the book of the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 6), and these are his words: "But the name YHVH is a chariot to its Master, to the supernal Keter. And therefore, 'there is none holy like YHVH' — the Cause over all, concealed and stored away in Keter; and from it His light spread upon YHVH, which is Yod = Chokhmah, Heh = Binah, Vav including six sefirot, Heh = Malkhut" — thus far [his words], for our matter. And this is its explanation: YHVH, which is a hint at nine sefirot, as he expounds and goes on, is a chariot to its Master, [namely] Keter; and the reason he said "its Master" is because it [Keter] is a father to the whole Emanation, and the whole Emanation is a throne to it. And it said "there is none holy like [koh]" — [this] will be understood with what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in another place, where he said that "there is none holy like koh" [refers] to Keter. And he said that this is the Kaf of "koh," which is the Kaf of Keter; and the reason for the Kaf is that it is two Yods, in the secret of "ten, ten the spoon" (asarah asarah ha-kaf); and this is what he said, "and therefore there is none holy [like koh]" — the meaning [being]: because YHVH is a chariot to Keter — [in] that the four-letter name [has a] Yod at the head [beginning], and Adonai [has a] Yod at the end — they are two Yods, in the secret of direct light and returning light, which is the Kaf of Keter — as this matter will be explained at length in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light, with God's help. And because these two lights are a chariot to Keter, which is the cause of the lights [coming] from the side of the Cause of Causes, the Ein Sof, blessed be He, stored away within it — and from it the light spread by means of Keter, in order that there be direct light and returning light — therefore it is called the Kaf of Keter, which is two Yods. And let the inquirer not hope from us the explanation of this matter, for its principal place is in the aforementioned Gate. Thus far the explanation of the passage, in brief.

Now he said explicitly, "the Cause over all, concealed and stored away in Keter" — indicating that the Ein Sof is not the Keter. Further, he wrote in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 124), and these are his words: "It is called YHVH from the side of the supernal Keter, which is closed like a clenched fist (kometz) — [such] that none knows what soul there is within. And the one that is within is enclosed in thought; the Cause of Causes we call it." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that he said at the beginning of his words, above, that in Malkhut is the four-letter name without [vowel-]point; and according to her nourishment, so is her vocalization. And now he said "from the side of Keter" — the meaning [being]: when she [Malkhut] is nourished from it [Keter], she is called by the name YHVH, which is [the four-letter name] with the vocalization of kametz (kometz); and the reason [is] "like a kometz that is closed" — the meaning [being]: like [the One that] is enclosed in thought, the meaning [being] that even thought is forbidden in [respect of] Him; and He is called by us "the Cause of Causes" — but not that this name delimits Him, for there is no name that would delimit Him, as we explained in the preceding chapter. And the main part of this passage, with all that follows it, is explained at length in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name.
Behold, he explained to us explicitly that the Cause of Causes is stored away and concealed in Keter, and that the Ein Sof is not the Keter itself.

And further, explicitly, in the Tikkunim in another place (Tikkun 70, folio 130), these are his words: "The supernal Keter, although it is primordial light, clear light, refined light, is dark before the Cause of Causes." And the main part of the passage will be explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot, blessed be God.

Behold, he indicated explicitly that Keter is not the Ein Sof, in his saying that Keter is dark — that is, that its light does not shine at all [by comparison], that it has no power before the Cause of Causes, which is its Emanator. Further, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, folio 112), these are his words: "A unique Lord, ruling over them all, wondrous and covered in Keter." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that above this passage he spoke of the matter of the spiritual life-forces and chariot in the sefirot, and afterward he said that the Ein Sof — who is called "a unique Lord," as is explained in Sefer Yetzirah — is wondrous and covered in Keter. And the intent is that His divinity is revealed only by means of the sheath of His light and His garment, which is Keter, and by means of it He rides in the rest of the sefirot.

Behold, he indicated explicitly that Keter is not the Ein Sof. Further, in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Pinchas, folio 243), these are his words: "Because the Cause of Causes is wondrous and covered in this Keter and spread out in the name YHVH. On Sabbaths and festivals there is no dominion to Samael and the Serpent, nor to all his appointed [forces]; and there is no dominion to Gehinnom — the evil female of Samael and the Serpent — nor to his hosts: all of them are concealed before the hosts of the King, in the manner that the nations of the world will be concealed when the Messiah is revealed; this is what is written, 'and they shall come into the caves of the rocks and into the clefts of the crags.'" And its explanation is clear; and from it, it appears with clarity that one cannot say that Keter is the Ein Sof — [the Ra'aya Mehemna] indicates this in saying "the Cause of Causes is wondrous and covered in this Keter." It appears from his words that Keter is a palace for the Cause of Causes.

Now we have several clear proofs and faithful witnesses that Keter is not the Ein Sof, apart from several other proofs besides — and we have not copied them, because we need to copy them in the coming Gates, such as the passage of Elijah, "You are One," etc., which we shall copy in the Gate of Self and Vessels, ch.5; and some of them we have not seen [fit] to copy at all, on account of the length. Even so, by these proofs the view of those who say that Keter is the Ein Sof is nullified.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, striven to establish, of necessity, that the Ein Sof is not the Keter, but [that] each of them is a matter in its own right — that is, this [one is] Emanator and this [one] emanated — we have seen [fit], in this chapter, to nullify another view, close to the view of the earlier Kabbalists, namely the view of Rabbi Shem Tov in Sefer ha-Emunot, Gate 4, ch.1, who first counted the sefirot and said that Keter is the first sefirah, [and] afterward said that Keter is not in the category of the sefirot. And this is the form of his language, in utmost brevity: "All the Kabbalists agreed to count these ten sefirot — the first, supernal Keter; the second, Chokhmah, etc.; however, the most wondrous and the deepest in the wisdom agreed that, in truth, the supernal Keter is not to be counted in the category of the ten, for it is like the Ein Sof; and just as the Cause of all causes is not to be counted at all, so it is not fitting to count the supernal Keter, for there is no beginning and no terminus and end in it, and it is the All. And Rashbi warned about this in several places, and to this he directed [his words] in Sefer Yetzirah, 'ten and not eleven.' And you already know that it is agreed among the sages of the Mishnah that Elijah the prophet is revealed to all the worthy; and there is a tradition, to some of the later [authorities] of blessed memory, that he was revealed to the great Rabbi Abraham, the pious Av Beit Din, of blessed memory, and from him the great Rabbi Ra'avad, his son-in-law, received [it], and the pious Rabbi Isaac, whose tradition is choice flour, [penetrating] very deep into the wisdom of Kabbalah. And he too explained 'ten and not eleven' — that Keter is not to be brought into the count; and the one that completes the count is the supernal Da'at, which the verse hinted at (Proverbs 3:20), 'by His knowledge the depths were cleaved.' And of it [Sefer] ha-Bahir said that it is the holy palace. And the principal [reference] of the unique name written in the books of the Prophets, they directed [it] in the letters of the Name, by means of Tiferet, to this [Da'at], for it is a palace to the supernal root." Thus far [his words].

And he prolonged much further according to this view. And in another place he wrote that, for this reason, Sefer Yetzirah called Chokhmah "the depth of beginning," for it is the beginning, etc. This is the view of Rabbi Shem Tov, who wished to say that Keter is not in the count of the sefirot — though he admitted, regarding the matter, that the Ein Sof is not the Keter, as is proved from his language in which he said, "and just as the Cause of all causes is not to be counted at all, so it is not fitting to count the supernal Keter" — [thereby] indicating that the Cause of all causes is not the Keter, but [rather] Keter is emanated from it. And before we enter into the demolition of this view, it is fitting that we know who brought them into this error; and we say that they were driven to this view on account of three things. First, the passage "By ten utterances the world was created" (Avot 5:1), which we copied in the preceding Gate, in ch.3; and there we strove with the matter and established that from that passage there is no proof for his words at all. And the second: that they saw [that] in Sefer Yetzirah [the author] began to count from the mishnah of the depths from Chokhmah, in his saying "the depth of beginning and the depth of end," which are Chokhmah and Binah — so that it appears that it [Chokhmah] is first to the Emanation, and Keter is not in the count of the sefirot; and likewise in his saying "one: the spirit of the living God," etc., "two: spirit from spirit" — they said that "one: the spirit of the living God" is Chokhmah, and "spirit from spirit" is Binah, etc. — [so that] it appears that the count of the ten sefirot begins from Chokhmah. And the third: that they found a great tree on which to hang, namely the divine Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Idra, [where] these are his words: "The place where the beginning is found is from the Holy Ancient One, which is illumined from the mazal," etc., as we shall copy, with God's help.

Now, since the beginning of the Emanation is from Chokhmah, which is illumined from Keter, it appears explicitly that Keter is not in the category of the count of the ten sefirot; therefore they pressed themselves to seek the completion of the count of the ten, and sought Da'at. But in truth they did not seek what is right. For the matter of this view is rejected — if you wish, [argue] from Scripture; and if you wish, [argue] from reason. A proof from reason: because [Keter] cannot escape [being one] of two things — either it is emanated, or it is not emanated. If it is emanated, then, since it is an effect of the First Cause, why should it not enter into the count of the sefirot? For who diminished the honor of the Emanation [so much] that Keter, because it is like the Ein Sof and is great and praiseworthy, should not enter into the count of the sefirot? — for the sefirot (namely Chokhmah and Binah) are also like the Ein Sof in their power and their excellence, and even so we did not restrain ourselves from counting them among the ten. And behold, since Keter is a cause to Chokhmah, and Chokhmah a cause to Binah, and the three of them are surely emanated — then as Chokhmah [stands] to Binah, so Keter [stands] to Chokhmah; and just as Chokhmah is counted in the count of the sefirot together with Binah, so Keter should be counted together with Chokhmah. If so, what is the reason that we should elevate Keter above all the rest of the emanated [beings]? And further, that which he said — that it is like the Ein Sof — is no excellence at all, since it is impossible for it to be exactly equal to the Emanator, for, being an effect of Him, it necessarily descended from the degree of its cause; and after we have exalted the Cause of all causes as much as is possible in [what is] without end, it is not fitting to exalt Keter so much, for it is not at the degree of its Emanator, since it is emanated and an effect of a First Cause, as explained. And as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in saying "it is dark before the Cause of Causes" — he indicated that it is not at the degree of the Ein Sof, God forbid; and if so, why is it "like the Ein Sof"? For the definition of the Ein Sof is a predicate by which nothing is [truly] predicated at all, except [of] the Emanator. And since it [Keter] is in the category of the emanated [beings] and is not like the Ein Sof, then why should it not come into the count of the sefirot? — for it is only of the count of the emanated [beings]; and why should we count some of them and leave out some? This is not fitting. And if you say that it is not emanated — this is impossible to believe, unless we say that it is the Cause of all causes and there is none besides it; for if not so, it is a duality, God forbid, [for us] to say that there is one thing besides the Cause of all causes that was not emanated from it. And if we say that it is emanated as well, but [that] it is not like the rest of the emanated [beings] because it preceded them by a long time — this is impossible, for there cannot be priority over Chokhmah except the priority of cause and effect; for it is impossible to separate and distinguish between every emanated [being] and emanated [being] except like the distinction of cause and effect; and so too the distinction between Chokhmah and Binah. And just as we bring into the count of the emanated [beings] Chokhmah together with Binah, so we also bring in Keter together with Chokhmah. And since, from reason, it is necessitated that Keter is in the count of the ten, it is likewise necessitated from the proof from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 118), [where] these are his words: "And these limbs are all in the sefirot: the head [is] Keter; the brain, Chokhmah; Binah [is] the heart, and in it 'the heart understands'; the two arms, Chesed and Gevurah; the body, the central pillar; the two thighs, Netzach and Hod; Yesod [is] the member (amah); the Shekhinah [is] its sign (ot)." Thus far [his words].
And although there is somewhat in it to rouse [discussion], even so it is not of [what is] relevant to us.

Now he counted ten sefirot against the limbs, and counted the supernal Keter [as] the head, and did not count Da'at at all — thus the supernal Keter is in the category of the sefirot. Further, in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 3): "And I heard the sound of their wings, in ten kinds of praise. In a simple song, which is Yod — Keter; a doubled song, which is  Y H  — Chokhmah and Binah; a tripled [song] in  Y H V  — which is ChaGaT [Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferet]; a quadrupled [song] in  Y H V H  — which is  N H Y M  [Netzach-Hod-Yesod-Malkhut]." Thus far [his words].

Behold, he counted ten sefirot in ten letters, and did not count Da'at at all, but [rather] Keter. And there is no reason to say that this Keter that he counted is Da'at — for if so, he should have begun from Chokhmah, which is the beginning of the Emanation according to their view; and further, [because] all agree that this one's name is Keter and this one's name is Da'at, and they differ only [as to] which of them comes into the count of the ten.

And further, a proof from the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (folio 31), [where] these are his words: "And therefore 'Bereshit' — Bet [+] reshit — is Chokhmah, as Yonatan rendered 'Bereshit' [as] 'with wisdom' (be-chokhmeta), because it is second to the count. And it is called 'reshit' (beginning); [yet] this supernal Keter, [being] concealed, is first; and because it does not enter into the count, the second is [called] 'reshit' — therefore, Bet [+] reshit." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that he found a difficulty in the word "Bereshit," for the Bet is large, and it hints at Chokhmah, as is known, and the word "reshit" too hints at Chokhmah — it is found, then, that Chokhmah is hinted at in this word twice, improperly; and this he intended in saying "Bereshit — Bet [+] reshit — is Chokhmah," the meaning [being] that both hint at Chokhmah: the Bet, as is well known that it is Bet, and "reshit" in his saying "reshit," which is Chokhmah. And because, from this difficulty, I might have said that "Bereshit" in its entirety hints at Chokhmah — that is, that there is no hint at Chokhmah for the word "reshit" unless it comes with a Bet, namely "Bereshit" — [therefore] he established that the word "reshit" alone is the hint at Chokhmah; and a proof of this [is] from the Targum of Yonatan, who rendered "be-chokhmeta" and did not say "chokhmeta" — as it appears that the Bet always hints at Chokhmah, apart from the word "reshit," which is also a hint at Chokhmah, as Yonatan rendered "be-chokhmeta," the Bet [being] a servile [prefix].

Now from the Targum of Yonatan it is necessitated that it is always a doubling, for "reshit" is "chokhmeta" and the Bet too hints at Chokhmah. And he answered to the matter of the doubling: because the word "reshit" indicates "beginning," and it would appear that Chokhmah is the beginning of the Emanation and its first [point] — and this is not so, for Keter is the beginning of the Emanation; therefore [the word] came with the letter Bet at its beginning, as if to say: although it is called "reshit," even so it is second, by the count of the sefirot, and Keter is the first. And this is what is said, "because it is second to the count" — the meaning [being]: Chokhmah is second to the count of the sefirot. "And it is called reshit" — the meaning [being]: and why is it called "reshit," which is, in truth, the place of error, [given] that Keter is the first and the prior? (And therefore he needed to say "Bet," as he concludes at the end of his words.) To this he said, "this supernal Keter, [being] concealed, is first" — the meaning [being]: because he found a difficulty [in] that, since in truth it [Chokhmah] is second and not first, then why is it called "reshit," [when] it is not first, since Keter precedes it? And to this he said that Keter is wholly concealed, and it is not fitting that it be called "reshit"; for the meaning of "reshit" is the beginning of revelation, and the beginning of revelation is in Chokhmah, not in Keter, as will be explained, with God's help. Therefore Chokhmah is called "reshit," and not Keter. And although it is not fitting for Keter to be called "reshit," even so it is first to the Emanation and enters into the count of the Emanation — and this is what is said, "it is first." "And because it does not enter into the count" [the meaning being: into the category of the revealed], as explained, "the second is [called] reshit" — the meaning [being]: it [Chokhmah] is the second, although it is called "reshit," for the reason we explained. "Therefore, Bet [+] reshit" — the meaning [being]: and therefore the word "reshit" came doubled, to tell you [that] Chokhmah is called "reshit," and [that] although it is "reshit" it is second — and this is the Bet at the head of the word. Thus far the explanation of the passage.

Now he has indicated to us explicitly that Keter is in the count of the ten sefirot, and that there is no doubt in it, even though Chokhmah is called "reshit." And we have yet very many good proofs, the like of these and these; and we shall not trouble ourselves with copying them here, since we are obliged to copy them in the coming Gates, with God's help.
Now we have established explicitly that Keter is of the count of the sefirot. (See in [the commentary] Pelach ha-Rimmon.)

Since, in the preceding chapter, we established that Keter is in the count of the sefirot, it remains for us to explain the matter of the passages that, on their face, oppose this view — namely, those from which the commentators drew a necessity for their view. First, from Sefer Yetzirah, which said in the mishnah of the depths, [where] these are its words: "Ten sefirot of belimah; their measure is ten, which have no end: the depth of beginning and the depth of end, the depth of good and the depth of evil, the depth of above and the depth of below, the depth of east and the depth of west, the depth of north and the depth of south. And a unique Lord, God, faithful King, ruling over them all from His holy abode for ever and ever." Thus far [its words].

And they said that, since the depth of beginning is Chokhmah and the depth of end is Binah, as they explained, then it is necessitated that the count of the sefirot is specifically from Chokhmah and below, and that Keter is not in the count of the sefirot, and [that] the "depth of above" mentioned in the mishnah is Da'at.

And further, they added to bring a proof from another mishnah like this one in Sefer Yetzirah, [where] these are its words: "Ten sefirot of belimah. One: the spirit of the living God, blessed and praised be the name of the Life of the worlds — voice, and spirit, and speech; and this is the holy spirit. Two: spirit from spirit; He hewed and engraved in it twenty-two letters — three mothers, and seven doubles, and twelve simples — and a [single] spirit [is] in each one of them. Three: water from spirit; He engraved and hewed in them formlessness and void, mire and clay; He engraved them like a kind of garden-bed, and set them up like a kind of wall, and covered them like a kind of ceiling. Four: fire from water; He engraved and hewed in it the throne of glory, and the ophanim, and the seraphim, and the holy living-creatures, and the ministering angels; and from the three of them He founded His abode, as it is said (Psalms 104:4), 'who makes His angels [of] winds, His ministers a flaming fire.' Five: He sealed [the] height; He chose three letters from the simples and fixed them in His great name,  Y H V, and sealed with them six extremities; He turned upward and sealed it with  Y H V. Six: He sealed [the] depth-below; He turned downward and sealed it with  Y V H. Seven: He sealed [the] east; He turned before Him and sealed it with  H Y V. Eight: He sealed [the] west; He turned behind Him and sealed it with  H V Y. Nine: He sealed [the] south; He turned to His right and sealed it with  V Y H. Ten: He sealed [the] north; He turned to His left and sealed it with  V H Y. These [are] ten sefirot of belimah: the spirit of the living God; and spirit; and water; and fire; and height-above, and below, east, west, north, south." Thus far [its words].

Behold, it appears explicitly that [the author] took the way of the other mishnah, and said: "one: the spirit of the living God," which is Chokhmah; and "two: spirit," which is Binah; "three: water from spirit," which is Chesed; "four: fire," which is Gevurah; and "height" is necessarily Da'at — thus necessarily the count of the sefirot is only from Chokhmah. This is the view of Rabbi Shem Tov, and his [argument from] necessity. And now we are surely obliged to explain these mishnayot, so that all may be rectified, blessed be God. First our occupation will be with the mishnah of the depths, and from there the matter of the preceding mishnah will be explained. And on this mishnah Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote, "I do not understand this clause." Thus far [his words].

And in truth, the difficulty of this mishnah is not so [great] — unless we say that the order was difficult for him. And even so, the humility of the pious one [Ramban], peace be upon him, appears from this: that he chose to say "I do not understand" rather than to demolish the reasoning of his received tradition on account of the difficulty of a single mishnah — because he wished to suspect his [own] view, and not to demolish the boundary of the early [authorities]. And even so, we see no difficulty in this mishnah at all. And this is its explanation: "Ten sefirot of belimah" — the meaning: this word is divided into two, that is, "beli mah," and the meaning of "mah" [what] is "essence" (mahut); and the intent is that the ten sefirot are without essence, since their essence is not apprehended by us. And even if we say "this is judgment and this is compassion" and the like, all is apprehended by us [only] from their action, but from their very selves they are belimah. Further, it is from the expression "muzzling," as it is written (Psalms 32:9), "with bit (beli) to muzzle" — that it is fitting for a person to muzzle his mouth and not multiply his words about their essence and their matter, on account of the shortness of the apprehender and the depth of what is apprehended. Or it is from the expression of hiding and concealment, like "with [adornment] to muzzle," namely the covering of the adornment and its hiding.

Now the sefirot are called belimah — that is, the sefirot of concealment, [in] that they are concealed. And these three explanations rise to one place: that the intent is to indicate their concealment and the shortness of [their] apprehension, and that it is not fitting to prolong speech about them on account of their concealment. And it said "their measure is ten"; and because from this it would follow that they have a limit, God forbid, [therefore] it said "which have no end." And although this is a thing and its opposite — that we set a limit in it and afterward say that they have no limit — it has already been explained in the preceding chapters that, in respect of the aspect that they have toward the Emanator, they have no limit, but in respect of their aspect and their action that proceed toward us, they have a limit to their action, according to our reception, [in] that we are possessors of limit. And this is the great power of our Fashioner: without limit, He limits and contracts (tzimtzum) it for the benefit of the lower [beings], who are possessors of limit and end. And at this matter let not the eye of the enlightened be alarmed, for it is not far[-fetched]: for the heavens and the heavens of heavens cannot contain Him, [how much more] blessed be He — and even so, for the love of Israel, He would contract His Shekhinah between the two staves of the Ark, as our Sages of blessed memory explained. "The depth of beginning and the depth of end" are Chokhmah and Binah — for Chokhmah is called "beginning," as is explained in the preceding chapter, and Binah is called "end," for there [is] the end and the conclusion of the things, in the secret of the Jubilee; and this [is] the beginning of the concealment and this [is] its end, in the secret of the transmigration and the Jubilee, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And the reason it said "depth" for each one [is] to indicate that, although "beginning" and "end" and "east" and the rest of the boundaries indicate the limit, even so they are deep — "deep, deep, who can find it?" — and the apprehension of them is precluded, because they are without limit, as explained. And "good" and "evil" are Gedulah and Gevurah, and are called "good" and "evil" because Chesed performs the action of good and reward, and Gevurah performs the action of judgment and punishment; and even so, the expression "evil" is not precise. And after he explained these four depths, he returned to explain six depths, which are the six extremities — namely, the depth of above and the depth of below, east, west, north, south. And this is the reason for the delaying of Keter until here, to [associate it with] the [account of the] extremities — although it is not [properly] associated in [respect of] the matter of the order of the sefirot; for close to this matter the commentators need to explain, according to their view, that "above" (rom) is Da'at — because Da'at is above Gedulah and Gevurah and below Chokhmah and Binah, as is proved by the verses (Exodus 31:3), "and I filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of work," etc.; and further it is written (Proverbs 24:3-4), "by wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established, and by knowledge the chambers are filled" — thus Da'at precedes Chesed and Gevurah. And if so, why did they delay it until after "the depth of evil" and "the depth of good"? Rather, what have they to say [but] that the reason is on account of the order of the extremities? — if so, for us too the delaying of Keter is on account of the order of the extremities.

And further he said "the depth of above and the depth of below": namely, the supernal Keter, which is exalted above all the Emanation; and the depth of below, namely Malkhut, which is beneath all the Emanation. And the depth of east [is] Tiferet. And the depth of west is Yesod, in which all the powers are mingled — the power of judgment, and the power of Chesed, and the power of compassion — and therefore it is called "west" (ma'arav). Or he means [by] the depth of below, Yesod, which is beneath all the Emanation, [since] Malkhut's place is above, were it not for the accusation, as will be explained in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon, with God's help; and the depth of west [would then be] Malkhut, in which all the powers are mingled.

And further, [Yesod] is always opposite the east. And east and west [are] Tiferet and Malkhut. And the depth of north and the depth of south are Netzach and Hod — for Netzach's inclination is toward Chesed, namely south, and Hod's inclination is toward Gevurah, namely north; and therefore north and south rightly [apply] to them. And "a unique Lord" is the Ein Sof, who is not in the count of the sefirot, God forbid — the opposite of that view which we nullified in chapter 1 and chapter 2 of this Gate. And as for the reason he said "[God] (El), [faithful] King (melekh ne'eman)" — we may say that [their] initials [are] AMeN [Alef-Mem-Nun]; and AMeN equals 91, like the count of [the combined name]  Y A H D V N H Y  [the interweaving of YHVH and Adonai]. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained many times. And some of the masters of the wisdom attributed this name [Amen] to the Ein Sof — not because the Ein Sof receives a name, God forbid, but because this name indicates the union and the joining to the sefirot that [occurs] by means of Tiferet and Malkhut, from below to above and from above to below. For the four-letter name includes all the sefirot from above to below, and Adonai includes the ten sefirot from below to above. And this is [the] Yod at the head [beginning], and this is [the] Yod at the end, as we shall expand the explanation in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light, with God's help. Therefore they attributed this name to it, to indicate that this union, hinted at in the [combined] name  Y A H D V N H Y, is by means of it. And this is [why] he designated it here "[God] (El), [faithful] King (melekh ne'eman)."

And further: the word "El" (God) indicates the necessity of His existence; and "melekh" (King) indicates the existence of His providence and His kingship in the lowly world and in all the worlds; and "ne'eman" (faithful) indicates His eternity and His endurance — that He is faithful [in] that He shall not be moved, God forbid. And this whole matter necessitates the Ein Sof, as we explained somewhat in chapter 1. And it said "ruling over them all" — the meaning: from above to below and from below to above.

And the matter of "ruling over them all" [is] to indicate the Self that spreads within the vessels, as we shall expand the explanation in the Gate of Self and Vessels, with God's help. "From His holy abode" — this is Keter, where its [the Ein Sof's] concealment is, as was explained in chapter 2 from [the words of] Rashbi, peace be upon him. "For ever and ever" (ad adei ad) — the meaning: three attributes called "ad," [namely] Binah, Yesod, Malkhut, which include the whole Emanation in general. For Binah includes the first three; and Tiferet and Yesod are all one, for "body and covenant we reckon as one"; and this is the Vav, which includes the six extremities; and Malkhut is itself. Thus, in the matter of "ve-AD ADei AD," the whole Emanation is included. Or it is possible to say "ve-ad adei ad" [means]: although the beings have spread for ever and ever, even so He rules over them all, whether they grow distant or whether they draw near. Thus far the explanation of the mishnah. And we have answered the matter of its beginning with Chokhmah — for its intent is not, God forbid, that Keter does not enter into the count of the sefirot, but [that] the "depth of above" is Keter; and if it did not count it in its order, first to all the sefirot, it is on account of the order of the extremities. And in this manner is the way, and this is the reason, for the mishnah of the seals that we wrote at the beginning of [this] chapter. And it is found that these mishnayot are no necessity at all to overturn the premises that are our received tradition.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, explained the aforementioned mishnah in the way that the commentators explained it — "to show the peoples and the princes its beauty," and [to show] that there is no necessity from it for the words of the commentators at all, even according to their way — now we have seen [fit] to write [in] it what is [further] expounded. And it is written in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 14), [where] these are his words: "Ehyeh is  Y H V, and it is the sum of six sides, with which He sealed six sides; and they are  Y H V,  H V Y,  V H Y,  V Y H,  H Y V,  Y V H.  Y H V  — He took it [to] the right, which is Chesed, and sealed Chokhmah with it; and with it, 'one who wishes to become wise, let him turn south.'  H V Y  — He took [to] the left, which is Gevurah, and sealed wealth with it; and with it, 'one who wishes to become rich, let him turn north.'  V H Y  — He turned to the east and took the central pillar and sealed 'children' (banai).  V Y H  — He took it [to] the right thigh and looked with it upward and sealed 'life' (chayei) with it.  H Y V  — He took it [to] the left thigh and looked downward and sealed 'sustenance' (mezonei) with it; He looked upward toward Chokhmah and bound [it] to the right thigh and sealed 'life' with it, because of Chokhmah it is said, 'wisdom gives life to its possessors'; He looked upward toward the supernal Imma and bound [it] to the left thigh and sealed 'sustenance' with it.  Y V H  — He turned to the west, to the Tzaddik, which is the mixing (eruv), where all the powers are mingled; and it was included in eighteen (ch"y) letters, which are  Y H V,  H V Y,  V H Y,  V Y H,  H Y V,  Y V H  — these are the eighteen (ch"y) letters by which He is called 'Living (ch"y) of worlds,' and the Tzaddik by them is called 'Life (ch"y) of worlds.'" Thus far [his words].

And in truth, at this explanation the enlightened one will be astonished — for the six extremities mentioned are literally six extremities, as is its custom throughout the Zohar; for the six extremities are always the six days of construction, and there are no "extremities" except in the place of construction. And this matter — how good and how pleasant! But the matter of "one," and "two," and "three," and "four" is difficult for them, for there is, on its face, no way to explain them. Further, we have seen, regarding the matter of the mishnah of the depths, that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in this manner — these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 120b), in this matter, [in] the book "These are the generations of Adam" and in the matter of "and you shall envision" — [where] these are his words: "These four letters are clothed in these four colors: Yod in a white color, Heh in a red color, Vav in a green color, Heh in a black color. This name is the one that embroiders colors in every place, and it is the one that depicts the lines of the forehead, in this manner: YHVH; and these [are] the four traced [lines] of the lines, which are the depth of above, and the depth of below, and the depth of east, and the depth of west." Thus far [his words].

Now he indicated that the four depths of the mishnah — which are above, below, east, and west — are four colors, which are white, red, green, black. And in truth, according to what is customary, white and red [are] Chesed and Gevurah. But he did not explain so in the mishnah of the seals, as is proved above; rather, [there] above and below are Netzach and Hod — and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in other places, regarding the verse (Ezekiel 1:27), "from the appearance of His loins and upward" and "from the appearance of His loins and downward," that they are Netzach and Hod. And therefore we may [be] press[ed] to explain that the "depth of above" and "depth of below" mentioned are also Netzach and Hod, and that they too are red and white — although these are not their intrinsic colors, even so they are included in these colors, for this one's inclination is toward the right and this one's toward the left; and with this, the matter of Yod and Heh — which are the letters clothed in these two colors — is also related to them, as he explained. And he said, "these four letters are clothed in these four colors: Yod in a white color, Heh in a red color" — in the manner that we said in the preceding passage, in the explanation of the mishnah of the seals, where he said, "He looked upward toward Chokhmah and bound [it] to the right thigh," and likewise Hod, with which Binah is bound — and it is found that the Yod is in Netzach and the Heh is in Hod, [pointing] to this matter. And now the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the two places, in the two mishnayot, are found according to his way; and from within it there came forth for us a great light regarding the matter under discussion before us. First, he said "one: the spirit of the living God" — it is Keter; and so it is necessitated from what he said, "blessed and praised be His name." And these are his words also in Sefer ha-Bahir, in the sefirah of Keter, where he said: "And what are the utterances? The first — the supernal Keter, blessed and praised be His name." As it appears that he attributed "blessed and praised be His name" [as] relating to this sefirah. And the matter is that, although the word "blessed" (barukh) is found hinted at in various places, its principal hint is in Keter. And so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 116b), [where] these are his words: "For 'in Yah, YHVH, is the rock of worlds'; and it is the Bet of 'barukh' (blessed). And the sign: 'barukh' in the initials of [its] letters — Resh [=] head (rosh), Vav [=] source (makor), Kaf [=] all (kol): the blessings (berakhot), [in] that this is the head and the source of all the blessings. And therefore Bet — it is Chokhmah and indicates Keter, which is the head and the wellspring of all blessings; and therefore Bet is two, by the count." Thus far [his words].

And its principal place [is] there, in the matter of the Bet of Avgitatz; and he said that it is a head, that it is the name  B Y H R Y R V N  (Bihariron). The meaning: "for in Yah, YHVH, is the rock of worlds." And he said that the letter Bet of "ba-Yah" (in-Yah) means "barukh." And the matter is that "barukh" [signifies] the head and source of all blessings, namely Keter, which is the source of all the blessings. And therefore the word "ba-Yah" came [with] a Bet at its head, to indicate that it [Chokhmah] is second (namely Chokhmah), emanated from the source of the blessings, which is Keter, the first sefirah. And now let us say that the meaning of "blessed and praised be His name" [is]: it is Keter; it is "blessed" (barukh), whose meaning is the head and source of all the blessings, and it blesses and emanates to Chokhmah, which is the name of Keter. For the definition of "name" means a garment and covering, as will be explained in the Glossary of Titles, with God's help; and the garment and covering of Keter is Chokhmah. And the meaning of "one: the spirit of the living God": the meaning [of] "one" [is] that it is a soul and a vital spirit to Chokhmah, which is "the living God" (Elohim Chayim); and it is called so, because from Chokhmah the source of life flows. And Keter is called "one," for so he hinted: "one," "one and one" — they are the first three, as is explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in many places. "Blessed and praised be the name of the Life of the worlds" — I have already explained that this is expounded of Keter; and it is called "the Life of the worlds" because Keter is the life of all the existents, since it is the source of all the blessings entirely. "Voice, and spirit, and speech," etc. — the meaning, in the matter that it is called "the Life of the worlds": the meaning [of] "the worlds" [is] the worlds standing concealed in Chokhmah, where its [Keter's] effluence is; for the worlds revealed from Chokhmah and below, although they are nourished by means of Keter, [it is] by means of intermediaries; but when these worlds are in Chokhmah, then in truth they are nourished from it — from Keter specifically. And this is "voice, and spirit, and speech" — the meaning [of] the worlds of which Keter is called their life. And this is what he said, "voice," namely Tiferet, which includes the six extremities; "and spirit" is "a voice that is not heard," which is the still small voice, namely Binah, which is a spirit that has no sound, but [is] "a voice that is not heard," as explained, namely Binah; "and speech" is Malkhut.
