And this is "the holy spirit" — the meaning [being] that the sum of these three is [the place] where they are nourished from Keter; and then it is called "blessed" and the source of blessings and "the Life of the worlds," namely these three letters, which are Heh-Vav-Heh concealed in the Yod. "Two: spirit from spirit; He hewed and engraved in it" — the meaning [of] "in it" [is]: with it, namely, by the power of Chokhmah He engraved and emanated effluence, so that the letters would be depicted in Binah, namely the twenty-two letters. Or we may say "in it" literally, in its plain sense; and the reason [is] that the matter in which the supernal forms were depicted is the thirty-two paths, and they were the matter and the thickening of the earth in which the twenty-two letters were cast — namely the three mothers, which are Alef-Mem-Shin, which are KaChaB [Keter-Chokhmah-Binah], or we may say Ch[okhmah]-B[inah]-and-Da'at. And according to all the explanations, Alef-Mem-Shin — its matter is the letters Yod-Heh-Vav, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light. And it is known that the manifestation of the Vav in Keter is the secret of Da'at, as this will be explained, with God's help. And now "in it" — in Chokhmah, literally — is the existence of the depiction of Ch[okhmah]-B[inah]-and-Da'at; and therefore the creation of the world was in ChaBaD, namely the thirty-two paths of Chokhmah; and all is one, unified. "Seven doubles" are the seven sefirot of construction, which are double, composite of judgment and compassion, the hint at which is in BeGeD KeFeReT, which receive dagesh — namely judgment — and rafe — namely compassion. "And twelve simples" are the twelve diagonal boundaries, which will be explained at length in the Gate of Particulars of Names, with God's help.

And the matter of three and seven and twelve will be explained yet further in the Gate of Manifestations, with God's help. "And a spirit [is] in each one" — the meaning: when He emanated the letters, there was emanated from the very self of Chokhmah a spirit and a soul to each one of them, namely the vocalization, which is a soul to the letters — the letters [being] in Binah and the vocalization from Chokhmah. And in the sefirot, "a spirit in each one of them" [is] the Self that spreads within the vessels, for such was the existence of their emanation, as will be explained from the passage of the Zohar in the Gate of Self and Vessels, in ch.7. "Three: water from spirit" is Binah, which is third. [The meaning [of] "water" (literally) — as is written in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation, ch.4 — [is] in the matter of the third utterance, which is "let the waters be gathered," [and] is in Binah. And the reason it is called "water" is because they are thicker than the spirit, and they receive the depiction more; and likewise it [Binah] receives more the depiction of the existents, and there they are revealed more than in Chokhmah.] "He engraved in them formlessness and void, and mire and clay," which are the existence of the four letters that are in Binah: formlessness (tohu) [is] Yod, void (bohu) [is] Heh, Vav [is] mire (refesh), Heh [is] clay (tit). And in [Genesis] Rabbah it explained: what is "bohu"? — a thing that clothes the tohu. And it said [that] tohu is "a green line that encircles the world," which is Binah — and not Binah itself, but the Yod that is in Binah, which has a hylic manifestation that is not revealed in itself — that is, that the intellect judges in it all judgments, in the manner of the hyle (prime matter), and it bears them, on account of its great distance from [human] knowledge [to apprehend]; but "bohu," which is the Heh, clothes the Yod, namely Heh, a house and a palace to the Yod, like this:

And it is "bohu" that gives depiction to the tohu and reveals the matters concealed in it. "Mire" (refesh) is a greater thickness, indicating greater revelation; and this is "mire," which is the Vav, which is Tiferet, which is the revelation of Binah, although it is still concealed in it. And "clay" (tit) is [a still] greater thickness and revelation, namely Malkhut, which is the final Heh.

Now the existence of their emanation in Binah is from the power of Chokhmah. "He engraved them like a kind of garden-bed," etc. — here he included the existence of the six extremities: namely, "like a kind of garden-bed" is the below; "and set them up like a kind of wall" is the girding of the four walls of the wall — west, east, north, south; "covered them like a kind of ceiling" is the above — to indicate that, in the existence of the Vav stated in the word "mire" (refesh), as I explained there, the six extremities mentioned are included, and they are in the power of Binah. "Four: fire from water," etc. — it is Malkhut; and by means of it the rest of the worlds were created, for by means of the first three all the Emanation was made and emanated, and in particular by means of Binah. And he placed Malkhut first [with the word "clay"], before the existence of the [other] extremities, because they were already hinted at in their existence within Binah. And because he mentioned their emanation from Binah, he mentioned the rest of the existence of the worlds, namely the throne of glory and the seraphim, etc. And Malkhut is called "fire" because it is the lower Gevurah; and he said "from water," [in] that it is Malkhut from Binah, and so [is] their inclination: Binah, the upper Heh, its inclination is toward the right, and Malkhut, the lower Heh, its inclination is toward the left, and they are the right hand and the left hand, as is proved in the Tikkunim, and as will be explained in the Glossary of Titles, with God's help. And the secret of the throne of glory is Beriah, as we shall explain in the Gate of ABYA. "And from the three of them He founded His abode" — the meaning: from these three aspects, which are spirit, water, fire, are the foundation and the abode of the Shekhinah, as is proved by the verses. "Five: He sealed [the] height," etc. — namely Netzach, namely above. And he placed it first for [several] reasons: either because its principal sealing was by means of Chokhmah, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, as we set down earlier; and likewise the sealing of the below, which is Hod, was by means of Binah, and therefore he placed it first; or for the sake of the order of the extremities. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, was compelled, in the passage of the Tikkunim, to explain that the sealing of above and below was by means of Chokhmah and Binah, because with them were sealed "life" (chayei) and "sustenance" (mezonei); and we hold that "children, life, and sustenance" depend not on merit (zekhut) — namely Chesed — but on mazal — namely Keter; and not Keter specifically, but the first three. And so it is proved in the Zohar in Parashat Vayera, on the verse "behold, I [will] add to your days" — that it did not say "I am adding" (mosif), speaking in the present[, addressed] to [the listener's] presence, but "I will add" (yosif), speaking of the hidden [third person], which is Binah. Therefore, surely, the mazal — although it is principally Keter — is in partnership with the first [three]; and therefore, in order to seal "life" and "sustenance" in Netzach and Hod, it was necessitated [that it be] by means of Chokhmah and Binah. And by this is understood the doubled language of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the passage [mentioned above]. "Seven: He sealed [the] east," etc.; "Eight: He sealed [the] west," etc. — namely Tiferet and Yesod, as explained in the preceding chapter, and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. And north and south [are] according to their plain sense, which are GaG [Gedulah-Gevurah]. And after we have included the explanation of the mishnah of the seals, let us explain the mishnah of the depths; and this is its explanation, in this manner, and not exactly like it: "the depth of beginning and the depth of end" are Keter and Malkhut, in the secret of "I am first and I am last," which we explained in chapter 1. "The depth of good and the depth of evil" are Chokhmah and Binah, for this is the source of compassion and Chesed, as is known, and this is the source of judgment and punishment; and according to all the explanations, "evil" is not precise. And "the depth of above and the depth of below," etc., are the six extremities, as I explained above. And we have gained, by the way, that these six extremities are literally the six sides mentioned, and [are] hinted at in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in several places; and there is nothing twisted or crooked in them, and "each man comes to his place in peace." And their proof from these mishnayot is nullified, [in] that "the pendants that were leaning [on it] are washed away." And in the way that he explained in the Tikkunim, he likewise explained in the Ra'aya Mehemna, in the completion of the ten tikkunim of the table; and we have not seen [fit] to copy it here, so as not to be lengthy.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, striven in the explanation of the mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah and to nullify the proofs of Rabbi Shem Tov and the rest of the commentators who say that Keter does not enter into the count of the sefirot, we shall now come, in this chapter as well, to nullify his proof from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (in the Idra of Ha'azinu, folio 289b), [where] these are his words: "The place where the beginning is found is from the Holy Ancient One, which is illumined from the mazal — it is the illumination of Chokhmah, which spreads to thirty-two directions; and they came forth from that enclosed brain, from the illumination that is in it. And what the Holy Ancient One illumines first (a variant: in Chokhmah) — this it is; and the beginning was from what was revealed; and it was made into three heads, and one head includes them. And these three spread out in Zeir Anpin, and from these all is illumined. This Chokhmah was engraved, and it brought forth one river that flows and issues to water the garden; and it entered the head of Zeir Anpin, and was made into one brain; and from there it is drawn and flows into the whole body, and waters all those plantings; this is what is written, 'and a river issues from Eden [to water the garden,' etc. Again,] this Chokhmah was engraved and was drawn, and entered the head of Zeir Anpin, and was made into another brain. That illumination which was drawn from it — these two drawings were engraved and joined as one by means of [one] drawing of the depth of the well, of which it is written, 'by His knowledge the depths were cleaved'; and it entered the head of Zeir Anpin and was made into another brain; and from there it is drawn and enters within the body, and fills all those chambers and halls of the body; this is what is written, 'and by knowledge the chambers are filled.' And these are illumined from the illumination of that supernal, enclosed brain that is illumined by the mazal of the Holy Ancient One; and all are suspended this from that, and bound this to that and that to that — until it is recognized that all is one, and all is the Ancient One, and nothing is separated from it. These three lights illumine three others, which are called the fathers; and these fathers illumine the sons; and all is illumined from one place." Thus far [his words].

And regarding this passage, there has come to us a certain treatise (kuntres) from one of the accepted sages of this generation, and he explained in it an interpretation at length, with proofs from passages of the Zohar. And since, afterward, he returned and explained the construal of the language of the passage and its explanation without [bringing] proofs to his premises, we have seen [fit] to copy here that [shorter] interpretation, so that the examiner may be wary of it — for we shall not need to be lengthy, since most of our premises are explained in these Gates. And these are his words: "'The place where the beginning is found' — the place of the beginning of the Emanation, which is found and emanated from the Holy Ancient One, the Ein Sof, which illumines by way of Keter, called 'mazal' — and the reason you will find in the long explanation. 'It is the illumination of Chokhmah' — it is the light of Chokhmah, the wisdom of God, whose light spreads in the thirty-two paths. 'And they came forth,' etc. — that the spreading of this light comes and issues from Keter, called the supernal Keter, enclosed and sealed, and does not fall under thought. 'And what the Holy Ancient One illumines,' etc. — and what the Ein Sof illumines first. 'This it is' — that is, Chokhmah. 'And the beginning was from what was revealed,' etc. — and the beginning of the revelation of the Emanation from the Ein Sof is this [Chokhmah], for Keter is not apprehended even in thought. 'And it was made into three heads' — this Emanation that comes from the Ein Sof was made [into] three heads, [which] are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. 'And one head includes them' — for although they have [their separate] place, the true union is only in [all] three of them. 'And these three spread out in Zeir Anpin' — the three mentioned spread their emanation down to the last [sefirah], called Zeir Anpin; and the matter, [see the long explanation]. 'And from these all is illumined' — all of them receive these light and effluence, and they have none besides them. 'This Chokhmah was engraved' — the meaning of what he said above, 'and three heads were made': for we found only two, and the third — how was it emanated? He said, 'it was engraved,' etc. — this [Chokhmah] was opened and there was emanated from it [the third]. 'An illumination that flows and issues' — it is Binah; and the reason it is called so, [see the long explanation]. 'These two' — they are Chokhmah and Binah, which were emanated and drawn from Keter, [and which] open and draw themselves together in one drawing into the depth of Tiferet, into all those chambers and halls; and the matter of the drawing of this light from Chokhmah and Binah, [see the long explanation]. 'And these illumine with illumination' — these chambers all illumine with the light of that attribute, which is Keter, the mazal of the Holy Ancient One. 'And all are suspended this from that' — and all the sefirot are bound this to that, until the Emanation that comes from the Ein Sof is recognized and known and apprehended; and this matter is a great secret among the secrets of the Kabbalah, and the matter you will understand, [see the long explanation]. 'And all is one' — and all is unified, this unifying with that. 'And all is the Ancient One' — and all of them are unified in it like a flame bound to a coal. 'These three lights' — they are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. 'Illumine three others' — they are Chesed, Pachad, Tiferet, which, below them, are unified each one opposite [the upper] one: Chesed in Chokhmah, and Pachad in Binah, and Tiferet ascends by way of the middle line and is unified in Keter; and the reason, [see the long explanation]. 'And these fathers illumine the sons' — they are Netzach, Hod, Yesod; and [the reason] he called these 'fathers' and these 'sons,' [see the long explanation]. 'And all is illumined from the place of the beginning' — he now returned and included all that he said above, and concluded with that with which he began: all the sefirot receive their light from the place of the beginning of the Emanation." Thus far the short interpretation. And in every place where "T B H" (Tav-Bet-Heh) is written [in his text], its initials [mean] "you will find it in the long explanation," since there he brought a passage or passages from the Zohar as proof for that matter; and these passages neither raise nor lower [anything] in the explanation of the passage at all. And what there is to object to him is this: that he explained "the Holy Ancient One" [as] the Ein Sof — and this does not appear [correct], for even Keter, most of the time, Rashbi, peace be upon him, designates by the name "Ancient of Ancients" (Atika de-Atikin); how much more, then, would he now designate the Ein Sof by the name "Holy Ancient One"?

And further, that it is impossible for the intent of "the Holy Ancient One" to be the Ein Sof, because he [Rashbi] said that the Holy Ancient One is illumined and receives its light from the mazal — and therefore he said "is illumined" (de-itnehir) in the passive form, and did not say "illumines" (de-anhir) or "illumines" (de-nahir), which is an active verb; and so it is written in all the versions, and so it was written in the version of this commentator [too] — and even so, he pressed to explain it [in] the active form, [in] that he said "the Holy Ancient One, the Ein Sof, which illumines by way of Keter, called mazal." Thus far [his words].

And further, his saying is difficult: "and what the Holy Ancient One illumines first — this it is." And he explained: "that which the Ein Sof illumines first is this," that is, Chokhmah. And it is difficult — for, granted, "'and the beginning was from what was revealed,' etc." is fine, for although it [Chokhmah] is second to the Emanation, even so it is first to the revelation; but "'and what the Holy Ancient One illumines,' etc." appears [to mean] that this is literally the beginning of its illumination — and this is not so, for Keter is the beginning of illumination and Emanation according to all the explanations, even according to the words of Rabbi Shem Tov; for, certainly, they differ only [in] that he says it is not fitting that Keter enter into the count, but he admits that it is the beginning of the illumination of the Ein Sof.

And further, the doubled language "and the beginning" does not settle with his interpretation at all. Further, his saying "and it was made into three heads" — for, granted, if he were speaking of the existence of the Emanation in general, it would be fine for him to say that this Emanation was made [into] three heads, which are Keter-Chokhmah-Binah; but the intent of the passage was only to say that the existence of the beginning of the revelation is Chokhmah — if so, why did he say "it was made into three heads"? For which one was made into three heads? — since the particulars of the heads he mentioned above, [where] he said "which is illumined from the mazal," namely Keter, "it is the illumination of Chokhmah," namely Chokhmah: it is not applicable to it [Chokhmah] [to say] "it was made into three heads." Further, he said "and one head includes," etc. — he explained: that although they have [their separate] place, the true union is only in [all] three of them. And it is difficult — for if the intent were to say that the three of them are reckoned as one, he should not have said "and one head," which implies one sefirah that includes them, but [rather] "and they are included in one," the intent [being] that the three of them are reckoned as one. Further, he said "and these three spread out in Zeir Anpin," and explained: the three mentioned spread their emanation down to the last [sefirah], etc. — and this is very strained, for the nature of the language does not indicate that his occupation here is with the matter of the existence of the Emanation; and likewise it would not have been fitting for him to say "and they spread out in Zeir Anpin," which implies that Zeir Anpin is already emanated, whereas according to his interpretation he is still occupied with the beginning of the Emanation, before the whole structure was emanated. And there are yet very many matters with superfluous language, whose matter is not explained according to his interpretation; and so as not to be lengthy, it is not my wish to object to all his words — and with a little examination the difficulty of his understanding in the interpretation will be apprehended. And now it is fitting that we come to the interpretation of the passage in a manner that a settled explanation may be explained, and the proofs of Rabbi Shem Tov nullified, with God's help.

Before we enter into the explanation of this passage, we must preface one premise briefly — and its explanation will be at length in the book Or Yakar, in the commentary on the Idra, with God's help. And the matter is that, although ten sefirot are emanated, and they are garments to the light of the providence of His governance, as we shall explain in the Gate of Self and Vessels, with God's help — even so, He clothes Himself in Keter, and there is the palace of His providence and His light; and it [Keter] is what cleaves and unites with the Emanator [to] the utmost [degree of] cleaving and union, to the point that it is forbidden to prolong speech about this matter.

Now, by means of Keter, the concealment of His existence is a first concealment. And accordingly, the concealment of Keter was necessitated, to the point that its manifestation is not literally revealed in the rest of the sefirot, nor will it be revealed in them; and just as they do not include the existence of the Emanator, so they do not include Keter — except that Keter pours its effluence, by the power of the Emanator, into the sefirot, by means of Da'at, as will be explained, with God's help. And on account of the great concealment of Keter, we do not call it "the beginning of the Emanation," because it is not the beginning of the Emanation that is revealed to us — but [rather] Chokhmah; and from Chokhmah and below are the totality of the sefirot, [counted] from ten, by means of the Da'at that completes [the count]. And not that Da'at is a sefirah — rather, it is an aspect that completes the totality of the sefirot, [enabling] them to include ten from Chokhmah and below, as we shall expand the explanation in the aforementioned book. And we know that this matter alarms the heart of beginners in the wisdom of Kabbalah, and the things do not settle for them until they come to the place that we have appointed for this inquiry — and then the gates of light will be opened.

Now the emanation of Keter is called Arikh Anpin (the Long Face), and it is the first concealment to the Emanator. The second concealment is Zeir Anpin (the Small Face), and it includes all eight sefirot, which are from Chokhmah to Yesod; and this is the secret of the second concealment to the Emanator. The third concealment is called Nukva de-Zeir Anpin (the Female of Zeir Anpin), and it is Malkhut. And the secret of these three concealments is explained in the Idra, at the passing of Rashbi, peace be upon him, as the explanation will be expanded for us there. And even so, let these matters be [set] before the examiner; and let him not rebel against them, but let him kiss his lips and say, "if it is a received tradition, we shall receive [it]" — for the place of their explanation we have appointed to the aforementioned book, with God's help.

And further, we must preface a premise that we received from our teacher and master, Rabbi Solomon — may his light shine — that each and every sefirah is examined in three aspects: the first aspect, in respect of what it receives; the second, in respect of its own self; the third, in respect of what it emanates. The example of this [is] in Chokhmah, which is the matter under discussion before us: it has a first aspect, in respect of which it is equalized to Keter — [and] in this aspect it receives and is illumined from it; and this aspect is its subtlety and its spirituality, higher in degree than the aspect of its own self, since the supernal Keter is joined to it. And it has a second aspect, which is the aspect of its own self, which is its [particular] character — which is the light that illumines in its own self, without any other sefirah besides it being joined to it. And it has a third aspect, which is the aspect in which it is equalized to Binah, in order to emanate to it from its effluence.

Now this aspect is not subtle and spiritual like the first two aspects, for the reason that the lower attribute, which is below it, is joined to it. And not specifically Binah — rather, the same applies to Chesed and the rest of the sefirot that draw sustenance from it.

And further, we must preface, regarding the matter of this passage in general: that this passage was expounded in Parashat Ha'azinu, at the time of the passing of Rashbi, peace be upon him, after he had expansively spoken of the matter of Keter and its concealment, and that upon it depends all that is principal in the Emanation. Afterward he began to speak of the manifestation of the Emanation that is revealed, and said that, from the side that Keter is not revealed, therefore the beginning of all the limbs of the Holy Ancient One — their beginning is Chokhmah; and the matter of the three brains, which are opposite the three supernal [sefirot], because Keter is concealed, as he explained there. He said, in the totality of this passage, that the existence of the three brains included in the Chokhmah that is in Keter are three sefirot; and its two aspects [those of Chokhmah] come in the place of the two sefirot, which are Keter and Binah, and the aspect of Da'at that is in Chokhmah is found in the place of Keter itself, as he explains and goes on. And since he came to explain the matter of the three brains that are in Arikh Anpin, by the way he indicated to us the order of the drawing-of-sustenance of the grades — that is, the three fathers, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, draw sustenance from the three brains; for the first of them — that is, the matter of Da'at, as will be explained, and it is in the place of Keter — and from there [is] their sustenance, that is, from these three aspects. And from the three fathers [is] the sustenance of the three branches, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod. And now the matter of the sustenance of the sefirot, three from three, is understood, although Keter is concealed. And now we shall come to the explanation of the language of the passage, with God's help. "The place where the beginning is found" — the meaning: the place of the revelation of the Emanation and its being found by us; that is, although the beginning of the Emanation is from the supernal Keter, which is Arikh Anpin, even so it is concealed and is not revealed on account of its great concealment, and the beginning of the revelation of the Emanation is from Zeir Anpin, whose beginning is Chokhmah; and it is called "the beginning" (shiruta) because it is the beginning of the revelation. And he said that its emanation and its existence, in [terms of] existence, is from Arikh Anpin, which is Keter. And this is what he said, "the place where the beginning is found" — the meaning: the place where Chokhmah is emanated and found and revealed is from the Holy Ancient One, that is, Keter, Arikh Anpin, called the Holy Ancient One. And the expression "Ancient One" (Atika) indicates priority, as he indicated in the verse (Daniel 7:9), "and the Ancient of Days." And it is called "Holy" (Kadisha), for there is the source of all the holinesses; or he means that "holy" (kadosh) means "separate" and "elevated," and it is holy [i.e., separate] in respect of Zeir Anpin, which is emanated in revelation.

And further, because there are two elders — this elder, who has acquired wisdom, and there is, in the Other Side [Sitra Achra], a worthless elder (zaken ashmai), as is known, in the secret of Laban the Aramean — therefore he called it "the holy elder," the meaning [being]: in the secret of holiness, and in its joy no stranger may mingle. "Which is illumined from the mazal" — the meaning: that this "beginning" of which he spoke does not illumine from the side of Keter itself, for it is concealed [to] the utmost concealment, but [rather] from the side of a revealed aspect within it, which is the secret of the beard (dikna) of the Holy Ancient One, the beard of Arikh Anpin, and it is called "mazal." And it is the secret of the aspect of Binah that is in Keter, as will be explained in the aforementioned book. And this aspect in Keter is called by the name "mazal" to indicate the emanating aspect within the supernal Keter — that it emanates by it into Zeir Anpin; for that aspect is called "mazal," from the expression "water shall flow (yizal) from his buckets" (Numbers 24:7), and "and flowing [streams] (nozlim) from Lebanon" (Song of Songs 4:15). And the intent now [is]: although Keter was emanated, the beginning of the revelation of the Emanation is in Chokhmah, in the aspect of its reception from the supernal Keter. And it is found, accordingly, that the aspect of the beard that is in Keter emanates into the first aspect of Zeir Anpin, which is Chokhmah; and this is what is meant in his saying "which is illumined from the mazal." And so [is] the way — for the last aspect of this [sefirah] emanates into the first [aspect of the next], and the first aspect of Chokhmah is the beginning of the revelation. "It is the illumination of Chokhmah, which spread to the thirty-two directions" — before its interpretation, we must preface that there are two Chokhmahs, and of them it is said (Proverbs 1:20), "wisdoms (chokhmot) cry aloud outside"; and as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Idra: and they are the concealed Chokhmah that is in Keter — and it is the brain of Arikh Anpin, and this is called "the enclosed brain" (mocha stima'ah), which does not open even to Binah, and whose paths are not known; and this is called "the brain that rests on its dregs," which does not spread at all, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained there. However, the brain of Zeir Anpin is the emanated Chokhmah; it spreads and is revealed from the side of its paths, which spread from it to Binah; and not that it is literally revealed, but that it is not concealed like the concealment of the supernal Chokhmah that is in Keter. And we have expanded the explanation of this matter in the commentary on the Idra in the aforementioned book.

Now the emanation of the revealed Chokhmah is from the concealed Chokhmah. And now, in this, he said that the aforementioned "beginning" is Chokhmah; and because there are two Chokhmahs, as I explained, he said [it is] that revealed Chokhmah which spreads to thirty-two — unlike the concealed Chokhmah, as explained. And he said "and they came forth from that brain" — the meaning: that this Chokhmah and its thirty-two paths are emanated and found from the concealed Chokhmah that is in Keter, which is the brain of the Holy Ancient One, the brain of Arikh Anpin. And he was compelled to say so, lest we err [and] say that this Chokhmah is emanated from Keter itself — for if so, it would be found that Keter itself is revealed, and this is not so, as he expanded there [regarding] its concealment; therefore he said that its source and its emanation is from the Chokhmah that is in Keter. And some read "from that enclosed [brain]" (mehahu stima'ah), the intent [being] upon the enclosed Chokhmah that is in Keter; and even so, the more correct [reading is] "from that brain" (mehahu mocha), and the intent [is] the brain of Arikh Anpin. And it is possible that the true reading is "from that enclosed brain" (mehahu mocha stima'ah), and it is all one matter. And the secret of "from the illumination that is in it" — the intent [is] upon the Chesed that is within the Chokhmah that is within Keter; and this matter is explained and necessitated in the Idra, as we shall explain in the book Or Yakar, in Gate 7, sign 15. "And what the Holy Ancient One illumines," etc. — two [things] were difficult for him, according to his words. One: since the emanation of Chokhmah is not from Keter, as explained, but from the aspect of the concealed Chokhmah — if so, what [does] he mean [by] "the beginning is found from the Holy Ancient One," as explained above? And to this he answered, "and what the Holy Ancient One illumines," etc., "this it is" — the meaning: that all [of] Keter itself [that] is revealed is only this; and since Keter has no other revelation than Chokhmah, it is fitting that we attribute its emanation to it. Again, a second [thing] was difficult for him: why did he say that Chokhmah is the "beginning," since in truth Keter and all its tikkunim are the beginning to all the emanated [beings]? And he answered that the intent in his saying "beginning" is not the beginning of the emanated [beings], but the beginning of the revealed [ones]; and Keter is not revealed; and this is what he said, "and the beginning was from what was revealed," the meaning [being] this Chokhmah, as explained. "And it was made into three heads" — the intent [is] upon three aspects, of which the one opposite Keter is Da'at, the second opposite Chokhmah, the third opposite Binah; and they are three brains, for the brain is always in Chokhmah, as is proved in the Zohar, and therefore the brain was made [into] three heads in three cavities, as is proved there in the Idra. "And one head includes" — the meaning: that the three of them are in Chokhmah, [corresponding] to its three aspects, included together; and it is called "the skull" (gulgalta), as explained. "And these three spread out in Zeir Anpin" — it is the totality of the Emanation down to Malkhut; and in respect of Arikh Anpin and its adornments and its tikkunim, the whole is called Zeir Anpin.

And the matter of its spreading in Zeir Anpin he explains further on. "And from these all is illumined" — the meaning: three lines, which are GaGaT [Gedulah-Gevurah-Tiferet], and likewise  N H Y  [Netzach-Hod-Yesod], and they are Chesed, Din, [and] compassion, as he concludes. And the matter is that their sustenance is not literally from Keter, on account of its great concealment, except by means of this aspect, which is the brain of Zeir Anpin, as explained. And they are three roots: Chokhmah, a root to Chesed; Da'at, a root to compassion; Binah, a root to Din. "This Chokhmah was engraved," etc. — the intent [is] to explain the order of the three brains in Zeir Anpin, [namely] their being three heads that are included as one, as explained. And he said that the Chokhmah that includes three heads itself was revealed and engraved and emanated Binah from within the third aspect; and therefore he said, regarding this aspect, "and it brought forth" (ve-afik), which was not said so regarding all the rest of the aspects. "And it brought forth one river" — the meaning: Binah, which is the river, and it "issues from Eden," which is Chokhmah; and the matter of "issues" is the expression "brought forth" (afik) that he stated, [in] that it is its emanation, "to water the garden," which are the seven plantings, which are the seven days of construction, as was explained. "And it entered the head of Zeir Anpin" — that is, the first brain, from below to above, in Zeir Anpin. "And there it was made into one brain; and from there it is drawn and flows into the whole body" — he means the spreading of Binah from the head of Zeir [Anpin] into the six sefirot that are in Zeir Anpin — that is, that it is drawn from the head to water the body. And the intent is that, from Chokhmah itself, they are engraved in its manifestation, and afterward, from its place, it is drawn to water the body — that is, into the plantings of the garden, which are the six extremities, [together] with Tiferet, called "body," in which is the Vav that is in the name; for Zeir Anpin is Tiferet, as we shall expand its explanation in the book Or Yakar. And he said that from there — from the head of Zeir Anpin that is in Tiferet, which is the totality of the three supernal [sefirot] that are in it — Binah is drawn to water the rest of the plantings, which are the six extremities that are in it, that is, the "body," as explained. "Again, this Chokhmah was engraved," etc. — it is the aspect of Chokhmah itself; and he did not say "and it brought forth," because no new emanation [occurs], but [only] a drawing, which is the spreading of its light from the head of Zeir Anpin — that is, the aspect of the skull (gulgalta), which includes [all] three, upon Zeir Anpin — and in it a second brain was made. "That illumination which was drawn" — it is possible that it refers above and returns to Chokhmah; and the more correct [reading is] that it is drawn below, and he means: that illumination which is drawn from it [as] these two drawings — that is, Chokhmah, which includes Binah, and Chokhmah in the manifestation of Chokhmah. "Were engraved" — the meaning: these two aspects were engraved into the aspect of themselves, which is Chokhmah and Binah literally; and this "engraving" is not like the engraving mentioned above, for above [it] was revealed in order to spread into Zeir Anpin, and here they were engraved into the aspect of themselves, as explained.

And the matter of this engraving and this becoming-visible is in order to unite, in order to emanate a third brain, as we shall explain, with God's help. "And they joined as one by means of one drawing," etc. — since, to explain this language, one must explain the matter of Da'at, which is a very honored and lengthy matter, and whose explanation is fine, therefore we have seen [fit] to devote to it a chapter in its own right.
In which the matter of Da'at will be explained, with the help of the One who graciously grants knowledge (chonen ha-da'at).

Da'at is what is called Tiferet, in respect of its supernal manifestation — it is a choice and fair manifestation. And the matter is that Keter is principally the line of Rachamim, although it includes all three lines — the line of Chesed, the line of Rachamim, and the line of Din. And the examiner cannot grasp this matter until the Gate of Essence and Governance, in which this matter will be explained at length, with God's help.
Now, from Keter is emanated the whole line of Rachamim, which is Tiferet and Yesod and Malkhut, as will be explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, with God's help.

Now Tiferet has a concealed and choice manifestation in Keter, and that manifestation includes the six extremities; and so it was explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pinchas (folio 220b), on the verse "all that your hand finds [to do, do with your might]," etc., "for there is no doing, nor reckoning, nor wisdom, nor knowledge [in Sheol]," etc.: and they explained, "'and knowledge' (da'at) — this is the secret of the six sides that are suspended in Thought, and they are called the world of that Thought." Thus far [their words].

The meaning: that Da'at is the secret of the concealment of the six extremities above, in Thought — the meaning: the root of the six extremities, which are six sefirot, the six days included in the Vav of the name, whose root is concealed in the supernal source. And he said that it is called "the world of that Thought" — the meaning: "world" (olam) is the circuit (hekef), that is, the six days, which are the days of the circuit; and these, because they are the supernal circuit, are called "the world of that Thought," that is, Keter and Chokhmah — for both this and that are present in [respect of] the matter of Da'at. Further, in [Sefer] ha-Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, folio 47), these are his words: "Because the soul (neshamah) is the soul of life — Binah, which takes from Chokhmah; the vital soul (nefesh) — Malkhut, [called] Tevunah; the spirit (ruach) — Tiferet, and it is Da'at, [which] includes both; of it is said, 'and by knowledge the chambers are filled.'" Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that the soul (neshamah) is from Binah, and is called "the soul of life" because it receives from Chokhmah, which is the source of life (Ecclesiastes 7:12) — and it is written, "wisdom gives life to its possessors" — and this is what he said, "which takes from Chokhmah." "The vital soul (nefesh) — Malkhut, [called] Tevunah" — the meaning: that Malkhut, from the side of Binah, is called Tevunah; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in another place, and it will be explained in the Glossary of Titles (under the entry "Tevunah"). And he intended to say this because, from the side of this aspect, it [Malkhut] is unified with Binah by means of Tiferet; and from this side it is called "nefesh," [in] that it is unified with the soul (neshamah) by means of the spirit (ruach), [namely] Tiferet, which is Da'at. And it is possible that he intended [it] because Da'at always indicates union, as will be explained; and he said that this "spirit" (ruach) is the union of Binah and Malkhut, and therefore it is called Da'at, which includes both; of it is said, "and by knowledge the chambers are filled" — and it is a great secret. And here he intended to explain to us the union of Tiferet with Binah, and he necessitated [it] from this matter: that the "chambers" are in Binah, and the chambers are the six extremities concealed in Binah, and they are a root to the six extremities, the six sefirot of construction; and they are a house and a palace and a body to Da'at, since Da'at is a soul to them — because Da'at is the manifestation of the six extremities from Chokhmah and above; and just as Chokhmah is male opposite Binah, and Binah is a palace to Chokhmah, so the six extremities — chambers ascending to a thousand thousands of thousands — are a palace to Da'at, and Da'at is a root to them, and it is a source and a root and a soul to them. And however it be, we have learned that the manifestation of Tiferet is called Da'at, and it includes the six sides. Further, this matter was somewhat explained in the Ra'aya Mehemna, [where] these are his words: "And because the teru'ah is in Da'at, and it is the central pillar." Thus far. He indicated explicitly that Da'at is Tiferet — but [it must be] certainly that it is its supernal manifestation, as we have proved from the rest of the passages. Further, in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Teitzei, folio 280b), these are his words: "'in a vision (mar'eh) I make Myself known to him' — 'in a vision': the supernal Imma makes herself known, in Da'at [which is] BeN-YaH; 'in a dream I speak with him' — the last Heh." Thus far [his words].

And he said "Da'at, BeN-YaH" to indicate that it is the concealed manifestation that lies in the bosom of father and mother, which are YaH [Yod-Heh]. And because it spreads principally within Binah, as explained — "and by knowledge the chambers are filled" — therefore the permutation of Binah is BeN-YaH. And after we have been roused to the matter of Da'at['s] being the concealed manifestation of Tiferet, let us further preface that it is among the properties of Da'at to unite Chokhmah and Binah. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, folio 95b), [where] these are his words: "'Bereshit' — Bet [means] two: Chokhmah and Binah. The third — 'the fear of YHVH [is] the beginning of knowledge (reshit da'at)'; and in this Da'at it is said, 'and the man knew (yada) Eve his wife,' for there is no coupling except through Da'at, which is the central pillar; and just as it is the central pillar — the union of Abba and Imma — so below, the Tzaddik [is] the union of the central pillar and the lower Shekhinah. And of body and covenant (guf u-vrit) it is said, 'for YHVH is a God of knowledges (de'ot),' and the two of them are testimony (edut), for there is no testimony [valid with] fewer than the two of them; and this is between (variant: and this 'son' (ben) is the union of Abba and Imma) Abba and Imma." Thus far [his words].

And this is its explanation. The intent of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in this passage is to explain that the word "Bereshit" includes three sefirot, which are Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at. And the explanation, how: that the Bet hints at two, which are Chokhmah and Binah, which are male and female, coupling by means of Da'at, as he concludes; and this is what he said, "Bet [means] two," etc. "The third — the fear of YHVH," etc. — the intent is that the letters "reshit" that remain from "Bereshit" are Da'at; and it is called "reshit" (beginning), as it is written (Proverbs 1:7), "the fear of YHVH is the beginning of knowledge (reshit da'at)"; and the intent of the verse, according to the way of the plain sense of the text, is [that] "the fear of YHVH" is a beginning to knowledge and prior to it. However, according to the interpretation of Rashbi, peace be upon him, the intent [is]: "the fear of YHVH," which is Binah — its "reshit," that which is prior to it, is Da'at; for Da'at is a beginning to "the fear of YHVH," as they said, of blessed memory (Avot 2[:5]), "an empty person (bur) does not fear sin." "And in this Da'at," etc. — it was difficult for him that we should say that Da'at, which is Tiferet according to the truth, would be prior to Binah; and he brought a proof and wished to necessitate the matter, and said, "and in this Da'at," etc. It has already been explained that Adam ha-Rishon is Chokhmah, as was explained in the Glossary of Titles, under the entry "what is his name and what is his son's name," and Eve [is] in the place of Binah, and therefore she is called (Genesis 3:20) "the mother of all living." And he said that in this Da'at it is said (Genesis 4:1), "and the man knew (yada)," for "knew" (yada) is from the expression "Da'at" (knowledge), [in] that "there is no coupling except through Da'at." Lest we say that the meaning of "and the man knew" means the knowledge of coupling [i.e., carnal knowledge] — but [rather] this coupling was not by means of an intermediary, [therefore] to this he said "there is no coupling except through Da'at," the meaning [being]: since the expression "Da'at" is an expression of coupling, then the coupling must necessarily be by means of an intermediary, like the covenant that unites a man and his wife; and since there is no coupling except through Da'at, it is found that the coupling of Chokhmah and Binah is by means of Tiferet, called Da'at. And lest we err [and] say that, [while] it is true that the coupling and the union [are] by means of Tiferet and the secret of Da'at, even so, who compels us to say that Da'at is above Binah? — for this was the central point upon which the wheel of this whole passage turns, from its beginning to its end — to this he said, "and just as the central pillar," etc. And one must be precise: that according to the plain sense of the words it implies that his intent is to learn from Tiferet [about] Yesod, and this is the opposite of [what] reason [would expect] — for Yesod is known in the [other] Gates [as to] its action in the matter of coupling, whereas Tiferet has [only] now been newly [introduced] to us in this passage; and how can one learn the explicit from the obscure, and teach [from] that which [itself] is being taught? Rather, certainly, his intent is to necessitate that Tiferet is above Binah; and he said: just as we find union by means of Tiferet, so we find union by means of Yesod; and just as Yesod is above Malkhut, which is the female that is unified with Tiferet, the male, by its means — and it [Yesod] stands between the two of them — so, necessarily, we [must] judge regarding the matter of Tiferet, that it is certainly above Binah, [standing] between Binah and Chokhmah. And this is what he said, "just as it is the central pillar — the union of Abba and Imma," as explained, from the necessity of the verse "and the man knew"; so we find union by means of the Tzaddik, [namely] of Tiferet and Malkhut. And just as Yesod is between Tiferet and Malkhut and above Malkhut, so [there is] a necessity regarding Da'at, which is Tiferet in its concealed manifestation, that it is above Binah, in order to unite it with its husband, who is Chokhmah. And it is found, accordingly, that Da'at is a beginning to Binah, as explained. And now, by this, the word "reshit" rightly [applies] to Tiferet, that is, in its manifestation as Da'at. And he said "and the lower Shekhinah" to indicate her manifestation after the accusation, [in] that she is below Yesod — [whereas] after her ascent, then she will be above Yesod; and the matter of her union then, we shall explain in the Gate of the Diminishment, with God's help. "And of body and covenant it is said, 'for YHVH is a God of knowledges'" — the meaning: he wished to prove that the union of Chokhmah and Binah exists by means of Tiferet. For [were] we to say that their union is not at all by means of it, it would be found that Tiferet is never above Binah; to this he said "body and covenant," that is, Tiferet and Yesod, and he intended to call them by the name "body and covenant" to show that, just as it [Yesod] is concealed and hidden within the body, therefore there is power in the body to unite above — as he explained in the Tikkunim, that there is no true union except by means of Yesod, and if not, it is nakedness (ervah); therefore he said "body and covenant — of them it is said, 'for YHVH is a God of knowledges (de'ot)'" — two, that is, the Da'at of Yesod and the Da'at of Tiferet. He indicated that the action of Tiferet and of Yesod is equal in [respect of] the union. And likewise, by permutation, "de'ot" (knowledges) is "edut" (testimony); and there is no testimony [valid with] fewer than two; and therefore they are necessarily two, that is, Tiferet and Yesod. And since we have necessitated that they are two witnesses [who] unite, then it is necessitated that "this is between Abba and Imma," that is, the supernal Da'at, [namely] Tiferet — for Yesod['s] union is below, [and] the reverse is not applicable; and likewise, to say that it is below the two of them is not applicable to say, as he proved; and therefore he said "and this is between Abba and Imma," literally between the two of them. Or it is possible to explain in another way [regarding] "body and covenant": that he intended to necessitate that Yesod is always above Malkhut, as he said "body and covenant," as is well known that the extension of the body is the covenant — [as] in the words of the divine [Rashbi] in many places, "body and covenant we reckon as one," etc. — to indicate that, even when the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, and she [Malkhut] shall ascend to her elevated place, and Yesod shall be the tenth [below her] — even so, Yesod will, in respect of the coupling, have free passage and ascend to between the two of them, as is proved from the matter of "body and covenant," the covenant [being] between a man and his wife; and as this matter will be explained in the Gate of the Diminishment, with God's help. "And of them it is said (1 Samuel 2:3), 'for YHVH is a God of knowledges'" — he intended to necessitate this matter from his saying "for YHVH is a God of knowledges"; and they expounded (the Sages of blessed memory, Berakhot 33b), "great is knowledge (de'ah), which was placed between two letters" — which are two names. And if it were true that Yesod is the tenth [below Malkhut] and unites [the partners for] the coupling from the place of its dwelling [below], then there would be no "knowledge between two names," for one of the two "knowledges" would be below, and there is no name below it; but on the contrary, great is the name that is between the two "knowledges" — rather, what have you to say [but] that it ascends there to the union, as explained. And he further said "and the two of them [are] testimony," etc. — the meaning: the permutation [of] "de'ot" is "edut" (testimony), and there is no testimony [valid with] fewer than two — and especially in the matter of capital cases (dinei nefashot), where it is required that the two of them come and testify as one, and if not, their testimony is not combined; and this is what he said, "and there is no testimony," etc. "And this is between Abba and Imma" — the meaning: since we have necessitated that Yesod is always [present] for the union between the two unifying sefirot, then from there we learn regarding Tiferet, that it is always [present] for the union, [as] Da'at between Abba and Imma, literally between the two of them, above Binah; and therefore it is called "reshit," [in] that it is a beginning to "the fear of YHVH," which is Binah, as explained.

And after the matter of Da'at has been explained as is fitting, and its union between Abba and Imma, let us come to explain the rest of the passage [from the Idra] that we are explaining. For Chokhmah and Binah, which are "the two drawings that were engraved," as I explained in the preceding chapter, are joined — the meaning: coupled — by means of "one drawing from the depth of the well," which is Da'at, drawn from Keter, called "the depth of the well"; and it is the supernal aspect that is in Chokhmah. And in order to draw Da'at to the third brain, they [Chokhmah and Binah] must be united by means of the drawing of the depth of the well. And the reason Keter is called "the depth of the well" is as if to say: the well itself is Binah, which is called "a well," as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, with God's help; and from it living waters flow by means of Chokhmah, which are its walls that deepen [it]; and its depth, which is its bottom, from within which the water flows, is Keter. And by means of Da'at, which is emanated from Keter and drawn from it to between the two of them, in Chokhmah itself, they are united and receive one from another. And by means of Da'at, these two deeps are cleaved — this one receives and this one emanates — and there is emanated between the two of them the concealed manifestation of Da'at, and it is drawn to the head of Zeir Anpin and is made into a third brain, as he explains and goes on. "And from there it is drawn and enters within the body" — this Da'at spreads within the six extremities; for Da'at is the six supernal [sefirot], and "body" [is] the six lower [sefirot]; and the lower [ones] are literally a body to the upper [ones], and the upper [ones] are a soul to the six lower sefirot. And there it "fills the chambers and the halls," as explained; and the matter of "chambers and halls," this is not the place of its explanation. "And these are illumined" — the meaning: these two aspects, which are Chokhmah and Binah, are illumined by the power of the first, primordial Chokhmah, which is its aspect in Keter; and this is what he said, "from the illumination of that supernal, enclosed brain," etc. — the meaning: the aspect of Chokhmah that is in Keter, which is the supernal brain and the third brain that is in Arikh Anpin. "Which is illumined by the mazal" — the meaning: that that supernal Chokhmah within Keter itself illumines, in its aspect called "mazal," which is in the Holy Ancient One, which is the enclosed Chokhmah, as explained in the preceding chapter. "And all are suspended this from that," etc. — the meaning: these aspects are suspended in the secret of their aspect in Keter, Arikh Anpin; and likewise in [respect of] the matter of [drawing] sustenance, for the life of the lower [ones] is suspended in the upper [ones]. "Until it is recognized [that all is one]" — by this their unity is recognized, and they correspond [like] the loops. And although we say "Arikh Anpin" and "Zeir Anpin," even so all is one, since there is nothing above except aspects of the manifestation of what is below. "And all is the Ancient One" — the meaning: these three aspects are the three supernal [sefirot], [all] three of which are in Arikh Anpin, and from it they are drawn, and all is one, and nothing is separated from it, God forbid. "These three lights illumine three others" — the meaning: these three brains, which are three supernal aspects, emanate into GaGaT [Gedulah-Gevurah-Tiferet]; for so [is] the way of their sustenance: Gedulah from the side of Chokhmah literally, Gevurah from the side of Binah literally, Tiferet — in the secret of Da'at — from the side of the supernal aspect, [namely] Keter. And these three are called "fathers," and Netzach-Hod-Yesod are like sons in respect of them; for all that is in these is in those — except that these are "fathers" and these are "sons," these are "appointers" and these are "agents," as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in many places. "And all is illumined from one place" — that is, Keter itself, in which these three aspects are concealed, in the secret of "primordial light, clear light, refined light," as will be explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot, with God's help. And the reason he did not mention Malkhut is because it is a female, and Zeir Anpin includes everything; and he came only to teach us that there are three lines drawn from three aspects — the line of Chesed from the aspect of Chokhmah, the line of Din from the aspect of Binah, the line of Rachamim from the aspect of Da'at and Keter, as I explained above. But Malkhut includes these three aspects, and there is nothing to say about it in respect of this inquiry. And with this, the explanation of the passage is completed. And by the way, we have learned the matter of Da'at — that its matter is not as Rabbi Shem Tov thought, who supposed [it possible] to make it a sefirah in its own right; and the matter is not so, but [rather] it is the concealed manifestation of Tiferet, as I explained at the beginning of [this] chapter. And just as it is not fitting to count [as separate sefirot] the [other] manifestations on their own — and the several other manifestations that the sefirot have, besides Tiferet, as will be explained in the Gate of Manifestations, with God's help — so it is not fitting to count Da'at as a sefirah in its own right at all. And by the way, it has been explained that his saying "the place where the beginning is found" does not [mean] that there is the beginning of the Emanation and the count of the sefirot, as he [Rabbi Shem Tov] thought, God forbid; rather, Keter is in the count of the sefirot. However, the intent in his saying "the place where the beginning [is found]" [is]: the beginning of the revelation and the apprehension — in the manner that [the Zohar] explains it most of the time: "the beginning that stands to be questioned" [in reference] to Binah, and likewise "the beginning that stands to be questioned and to be answered" [in reference] to Chesed; and all [of this is] in [respect of] the matter of the revelation, and as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the last passage that we copied in ch.3.
And with this, this glorious Gate is concluded; and from God we ask forgiveness and pardon and atonement, for the general and for the particular. Amen.
The Fourth Gate is the Gate of Self and Vessels.

This Gate's name attests to it: it is to explain, regarding the matter of the sefirot, whether they are the very Self [atzmut] of the Emanator, or [whether] they are His vessels, like vessels to the craftsman. And this is a great perplexity that fell among the later Kabbalists — that is, among the later authors, such as Rabbi Menachem Recanati and Rabbi David. And with this matter will our occupation be in this Gate, with God's help.
Chapter One.

The intent in this chapter is to copy the view of Rabbi Menachem Recanati regarding the sefirot — whether they are Self or vessels — briefly, so far as is possible, although in the book Ta'amei ha-Mitzvot he prolonged the matter much. And we shall abridge his words and copy his principal proofs, and not all of them, for they are not of [what is] needed by us. And these are his words: "It is a truth in which there is no stammering [doubt], that in the Creator, blessed be He, neither multiplicity nor change can be predicated. If so, it is difficult: if the sefirot are the Self of divinity, how can it be predicated of them that they perform judgment and compassion, the right side and the left side — for all this indicates change? Second: that in the Creator, blessed be He, limit cannot be predicated — and this is a truth in which there is no doubt; if so, how, in the Sefer Heikhalot, did they speak of limit in the Creator, blessed be He, in their saying 'from His right to His left, sixteen myriad parasangs; the measure of His stature, two hundred thirty-six thousand myriad parasangs' — all this surely indicates limit, and cannot be predicated [of Him]. And further, that in the Creator number cannot be predicated; if so, how do we say 'ten'? And further, that what is not a body is not divisible; if so, how do we say 'this is judgment and this is compassion and this tips the balance between them,' etc. — for all this indicates corporeality."

"Know that, in truth, the Creator, blessed be He, has no change at all, and none of the attributes of corporeality can be predicated of Him, God forbid; and all that they measured in the book of the Merkavah, they did not say of the Creator literally, but of the sefirot. And if you say: but it is known that the power of the Emanator is in the emanated, and if so, [then] from the [same] reason for which it cannot be predicated of the Emanator, it likewise cannot be predicated of the emanated — if so, how do we say that they are in the sefirot? — there is to say: Know that what we speak of the sefirot, we do not say of the Creator; rather, the sefirot are like the vessels of the craftsman, with which he performs his work — to draw a distinction many times over. And the sefirot are equal to a thing and its opposite. And to bring the matter near to the intellect, the sages compared it to the will of the soul, which is equal to all the delights and to all the thoughts that spread from it; and although they are many, their root is only one, and the soul does not change — rather, the change is in the body, which brings the thought of the soul into actuality. And therefore there is to say that they are things equal to a thing and its opposite, for if we did not say so, there would not be in them the power for every thing. And therefore they compared them to the will of the soul; and just as the soul is clothed by the body, so the Creator, blessed be He — from His great light these vessels sparkled, and the sages called them 'sefirot'; and the spreading of the First Cause into these vessels is called Emanation." Thus far [his words].

And he brought a passage [as] a proof for his words; and since it is not of the matter, we have not copied it. And let us return to his words: "And the sefirot do not delimit Him; rather, they receive the effluence from Him first, more than all the rest of the created [entities]; and God forbid that there be in them body or corporeality — rather, they are kinds of light, like the light that issues from the eye, which is not apprehended or grasped, for it is nothing; but [only] the thing apprehended, after the light, is grasped in the depiction of the heart's thoughts, and that form is depicted by the power of the attribute. And behold, I add for you, with many proofs from the words of our Sages of blessed memory, that all that they spoke of the sefirot is not fitting to say of Him, blessed be He. And I found in the wondrous Zohar (Naso, folio 137b), these are its words: 'Thus it is taught: it is not enough for the wicked that they do not turn the attribute of judgment into the attribute of compassion, but that they [even] turn the attribute of compassion into the attribute of judgment? And how do they turn [it]? — but is it not written, "I, YHVH, have not changed"? Rather: at every time that the Ancient of Ancients, the white head, is revealed, the desire of desires [ra'ava de-ra'avin] is revealed, [and] great compassion is found in all. And at the time it is not revealed, all the judgments of Zeir Anpin are ready; and, as it were, compassion performs judgment — that Ancient One of all. For it is taught: when the Ancient of Ancients, the desire of desires, is revealed, all the lamps that are called by this name are illumined, and compassion is found in all. And at the time the Concealed of the Concealed is not revealed, and these lamps are not illumined, judgments are roused and judgment is performed. Who caused this judgment? — the desire of desires that is not revealed. And therefore the wicked turn compassion into judgment.' Thus far the Zohar. And 'do not make yourself as one dozing' in your reading of this — for if you are precise in the passage, you will find that it proves that the sefirot are not literally the Self of the Creator; for if not so, what did it answer, 'Rather, at every time that the Ancient of Ancients,' etc.? — since, in the end, it said, 'and at the time it is not revealed.' Rather, it appears that the judgment is [present] in the hiding of His face, blessed be He, from a sefirah, and then it would be consumed of itself. A parable [of] a king who commanded one of his servants, 'When you see a man swift in his work, you shall surely endow him from your threshing-floor and your winepress,' and commanded another, 'When you see a lazy man, strike him' — and behold, the king neither does evil nor does good to either of them; rather, all is by his command. So He, blessed be He, emanates into the attributes to perform actions, and He does not change His actions. Further, in the Zohar (there, folio 136), these are his words: 'In the cavities of the skull, three cavities are found, in which a brain dwells, and a thin membrane that covers them — but not a hard, enclosing membrane like the Ancient of Days; and therefore this brain spreads and issues to thirty-two tracks; this is what is written, "and a river issues from Eden." And it is taught: in the three cavities of the skull a brain dwells; from one cavity there bursts and spreads one wellspring to four directions, and there issues from that brain that dwells in this cavity thirty-two tracks, spirits of wisdom. From the second cavity there bursts and spreads another wellspring, and fifty gates are opened; from these fifty gates are bound the fifty days of the Torah, and the fifty years of the Jubilee, [and] the fifty thousand generations that the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to return the spirit to him and to make it dwell in him. From the third cavity there issue a thousand thousands [of] chambers and halls, upon which Da'at dwells, and dwells in them; and this cavity sets its dwelling between this cavity and that cavity, and all those chambers are filled from two sides; this is what is written, "and by knowledge the chambers are filled." And these three cavities spread out in the whole body, to this side and to that side; and in them the whole body is bound, and the body is bound in them on all its sides; and in the whole body they spread and are found,' etc., until: 'and in this are suspended the right and the left, light and darkness, compassion and judgment; and all the right and the left are suspended in this and not in the Ancient One.' Thus far [his words]."

And we have seen [fit] to abridge it, and not to copy the interpretation of Rabbi Menachem, of blessed memory, upon it — for he did not delve into it at all, but [gave only] the surface of the passage, and the rest of the passage neither raises nor lowers [anything]. And let us return to his words: "Contemplate this matter greatly, and turn it over in your thought, and you will see that he removed the attributes [predicates] from Him, blessed be He, in that he said 'in this they are suspended, and not in the Ancient One'; for of the Creator, blessed be He, one cannot say 'light' or 'darkness' or any of the opposites, which are attributed only to the attributes [sefirot]; and if we say that the attributes are the Self of divinity, how did he say 'and not in the Ancient One'? — Behold, we have in this matter two proofs. Further, a third proof, in the Zohar (Bamidbar, folio 120), in this language: 'Rabbi Elazar asked Rabbi Shimon his father; he said to him: a sign for the coupling of union — whence [is it]? He said to him: My son, although we have established matters for each and every side, and they were scattered — here a matter and there a matter — take this sign in your hand, and so it is: like the circuit of the altar, as we have learned, "he comes to the southeast corner, [then] the northeast, [then] the northwest, [then] the southwest," etc.' And we must explain the question and the answer; and with this our intent will be explained, with God's help. 'A sign for the coupling' — the meaning: how shall a person emanate to the head of the Tzaddik, and which attribute receives before its fellow, [and] how is the order of the union. And Rabbi Shimon answered that a person must first unite the east, which is Tiferet, with the south, which is Chesed — for it is the attribute of compassion; but not so much as the Chesed, because the attribute of judgment is emanated there, which is north, as it is said (Jeremiah 1:14), 'from the north the evil shall break forth'; and afterward one needs also the east with the north, for it receives from both of them; afterward one must join the wife to her husband by way of the attribute of judgment, which receives first, from the north by way of the east; and afterward one must unite her with the south, by way of the attribute of compassion, so that she shall not separate from the supernal waters and become the harsh attribute of judgment. And because the Shekhinah receives last, therefore they said that the Shekhinah is in the west — that is, for there the effluence and the blessing, the attribute of judgment and [the attribute] of compassion, are mingled; and then the blessings are found above and below. And I found a support for this order in the matter of the union [in] what is written (Song of Songs 4:16), 'awake, O north, and come, O south,' etc.; and see how it explained here that the garden, which is likened to the Shekhinah, receives first from the north and afterward from the south, as it is said, 'awake, O north, and come, O south, [that] my garden [may breathe out]' — the meaning: to draw the blessing to the dry garden and to water it from the waters of repentance and compassion. And all this effluence and this drawing comes entirely from the Creator, blessed be He, by the spreading of the Cause of Causes into the attributes, which is called 'the union,' and it is the Emanation, as I explained above. And so that you may be expert in the corners [directions], he said, 'take a sign,' etc. And it appears to me that from here we may say that the extremities are not joined to Him, blessed be He — for if so, they would not need the effluence and the blessing, if He, blessed be He, and the sefirot were one Self, as we explained above. And since the emanated is not separated from the Emanator, we have to say that it was not of the Creator that they said that there is in Him neither joining nor separation, but [only] of the attributes." Further, Rabbi Menachem brought proofs from the prayer of Rabbi Nechunya; and since they are not such [strong] proofs, I have not written them; and likewise from the Sefer ha-Bahir.

Now we have completed what was in our mind to copy from the words of Rabbi Menachem; and likewise Rabbi Yehudah Chayyat copied his words at length in his book Minchat Yehudah, and added to him a little — small, not great — and said that, although the law is according to the words of Rabbi Menachem, even so, that which he necessitated from the matter of the parasangs stated in the book of the Merkavah — the intent is not literal parasangs, in a quantitative sense, God forbid, but [rather] the expression is derived from the expression (Daniel 5:28) "your kingdom is divided (peres)," and the intent [is] sparks spreading from Him to every side. And Rabbi Yehudah took issue with Rabbi Menachem regarding the interpretation of the passage of the union as well, [and] likewise regarding what he wrote in the likeness of "the light that issues," etc.; and Rabbi Yehudah set forth another parable, and said: like the likeness of the spark of the sun's light and its light, which is not the very self of the sun but a property in it — so the Emanation is a property in the Emanator, and is not the Self of the Emanator. Thus far have the words of the one who says that the sefirot are vessels reached, in brief.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, written the view of the one who says that the sefirot are vessels — namely Rabbi Menachem, and Rabbi Yehudah followed after him — our intent in this chapter is to copy the view of Rabbi David, in the book Magen David, who held that they are the very Self of divinity. And because the objections that we brought from Rabbi Menachem in the preceding chapter were difficult for him, he resolved [them] and said: "Know that the variation of the names, or the number of the sefirot, does not necessitate multiplicity in the Creator, blessed be He, God forbid. For the one who said, by the name Ehyeh, that it indicates perfect compassion, and by the name Elohim, that it indicates justice and judgment, and likewise in the significations of the rest of the sefirot and their titles — this is nothing but the variation of the aspects, in [their] being joined to differing actions. That is, when you examine the Self of divinity from the side that it indicates perfect compassion — that is, that it performs the action of compassion — you call it by the name Ehyeh; and when you examine it from the side that it indicates judgment and justice — that is, that it performs the [acts of] justice — you call it by the name Elohim. And likewise in the sefirot and in the rest of the names: that there is here nothing but one Self, in the utmost of unity and simplicity, which, according to the variation of the aspects in it, in [their] being joined to its differing actions, is called by many names, and it is said of it that it is ten sefirot. And let it not carry you away [to think] that this necessitates multiplicity in the Creator, blessed be He — for these are said by way of the analogy of His Self, blessed be He, to His created [entities]." Thus far [his words].

And afterward he aimed to necessitate this with philosophical proofs, and we have not copied them, on account of the smallness of their usefulness. And he brought a proof that the sefirot are the Self of divinity from the Zohar (Ha'azinu, folio 297), [where] these are its words: "'For I call upon the name of YHVH' — what is 'for I call upon the name of YHVH'? Rabbi Shimon said: behold it is written, 'ascribe greatness to our God,' etc. 'Ascribe greatness' — this is Gedulah. 'The Rock, His work is perfect' — this is Gevurah. 'For all His ways are judgment' — this is Tiferet. 'A God of faithfulness' — this is Netzach. 'And without iniquity' — this is Hod. 'Righteous' — this is Yesod. 'And upright' — this is Malkhut. He is all the holy name of the Holy One, blessed be He. And therefore 'for I call upon the name of YHVH,' etc. Rabbi Chiya said: from this verse I have learned supernal wisdom, and so it is; but the end of the verse binds the bond of faith, in what is written, 'He' (Hu), as it is said, 'righteous and upright is He' — that is to say, He is all, He is one without separation. For lest you say [that] all these are many, it returned and said 'He' — they all ascend and are bound and unified in one. And all is 'He': He was, and He is, and He will be; and He is one — blessed be His name forever and unto the ages of ages." Thus far [its words].

Here you have a clear proof for what we have said. For he said that the end of the verse, in the word "He" (Hu), binds all the sefirot together in a firm bond — to show that, although the sefirot are many in number, ten, from the side of the aspect toward His actions, even so we may say that they are "He," that is, [that] they are the very Self of the Name, blessed be He, who is unique in the utmost of unity, to the point that it is said of Him "He." And therefore he said, "lest you say [that] they are many" — that is, lest you say that all these sefirot are many, and if so, how is it possible that they be one thing — therefore he answered him, [in] that the verse said "He" after it mentioned the ten sefirot, to indicate that they are unified in His Self, blessed be He, and the multiplicity is in [their] being joined to the recipients, in differing aspects. And this is a great proof. And it is impossible to make it known to you without my explaining to you the intent of the Zohar: for at first it mentioned the attributes in particular, and afterward included them under one name.

Now, "for the name of YHVH" hints at the first three. "Ascribe greatness to our God" — Chesed is called Gedulah. "The Rock, His work is perfect" — this hints at the Fear of Isaac, which is mighty and strong. "For all His ways are judgment" — hints at Tiferet, etc. And after the hint [to] the whole spreading, he returned and included it in complete union in the word "He" — that is to say, these sefirot, which are ten in respect of the recipients, are thus literally "He," that is, the Self of divinity, simple in the utmost. Further, he brought a proof from a mishnah in Sefer Yetzirah, from the matter of the depths, which we explained above in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter. And he said that, after it mentioned all the sefirot, it said that the Name is unique in them; and if so, they are the Self of divinity literally. Further, he brought a proof from another mishnah, "ten sefirot of belimah: their end is fixed in their beginning and their beginning in their end," etc., "that a unique Lord, and He has no second. And before one, what do you count?" — that is to say, [although] the sefirot are ten in respect of differing aspects, even so the end is fixed in the beginning, for the head is the end and the end is the head, from the side of the abundance of their unity in the Self of the Creator; and YHVH, blessed be He, is unique in them, and there is no duality there, God forbid, to the point that no number or multiplicity may be attributed to Him, God forbid — and this is their saying, "before one, what do you count?" — for one cannot say [anything] except that He is one, one in the utmost of unity. Further, a proof (from Midrash Rabbah, Shemot, ch.3) on the verse "and they say to me, what is His name?" Rabbi Abba bar Memel said: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "My name you wish to know? — according to My deeds I am called. Sometimes I am called by El Shaddai, by Tzeva'ot, by Elohim, by Adonai," etc. "When I judge the creatures, I am called Elohim," etc.

Behold, this Midrash is literally a necessitation for what we have said: that YHVH, blessed be He, is one, and if we take Him in respect of His actions in the created [entities], thus is He called by His differing names. Further, he brought a proof from the Zohar (Bereshit, folio 19b), on the verse "I went down into the garden of nuts": "And the whole world is like this kind [of thing], above and below — from the head of the secret of the supernal point to the end of all the grades, all of it is [one], this within that and that within that, until it is found that this is a husk to that and that to that. The primordial point is an inner illumination that has no measure [by which] to know its purity and subtlety and clarity, until it spread a spreading; and that spreading of that point became one palace, for that point to be clothed [in it] — an illumination that is not known, for the abundance of its purity. The palace, which is a garment to that enclosed point, is an illumination that has no measure; and even so, it is not [so] subtle and pure as that primordial point, concealed and stored away. That palace spread a spreading [of] primordial light; and that spreading is a garment to that palace, [which is itself] subtle and pure, more inward. From here onward, this spreads in that and is clothed in that, until it is found that this is a garment to that and that to that — this [is] kernel [mocha, the 'brain' of the nut] and that [is] husk. And although this is a garment, it becomes kernel to another grade.
