We saw fit not to be lengthy in the precise [parsing] of the language of the passage, but rather to explain it with a strong hand, because there is no comprehension in it at all; and by our way the whole will be explained, God willing. "A light that does not subsist in [another] light"—meaning, the Ein Sof, the King of the kings of kings, who is a light shining to all the lights; and yet He does not subsist in the light of the sefirot, but rather rules over them, and is not revealed within them, for in His existence He is the Necessarily Existent, abiding in Himself as before His spreading forth in the sefirot. Or he means: that it would be fitting that the Ein Sof, by reason of the abundance of His concealment, be called "darkness"; and since Malkhut, too, is called "darkness," yet the two are not equal—for the darkness of the Ein Sof is by reason of the utmost brilliance, which is not apprehended nor revealed, and by reason of the abundance of His concealment He is called "darkness"; whereas Malkhut is called "darkness" by reason of the absence of light.

And behold, by reason that he called the Ein Sof "light," which is not fitting—for it is not apprehended that it should be called "light," but he was compelled to call it "light" to indicate that it is the source of all the lights, and the whole Emanation are sparks of light shining from it, and therefore he designated it by the name "light"—afterward he made amends for this: that even though he called it "light," it is not an apprehended light, but a concealed light that is not fit to be designated by the name "light," except "a light that does not subsist in [another] light," but rather is concealed in the utmost concealment. Or he means "a light," etc.—the Ein Sof, who is a radiance shining to all the luminaries and exalted above all the lights: for the other lights receive light from another and are suspended upon lights other than themselves; but the Ein Sof, blessed be He, is a light that does not receive and has no need of another. And the meaning of "engraved" is "incised." And this is because it is already well known that the sefirot are subtler when they are in their source than after their spreading forth, as will be explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. And now, since he wished to say "and brought forth," which is the beginning of the Emanation and the revelation and the thickening, he had to say "engraved"—the intent being to say [it is] the beginning of the thickening of the light to be revealed; all this by way of parable, to our human intellect and our limited understanding. And he said "and issued forth" (nafik), which is an intransitive verb, and he did not say "and brought forth" (apik), because these sparks are the Self that spreads forth within the sefirot, as will be explained; and since this is the existence of His Self, therefore he said "and issued forth," whose meaning is that it issued forth of itself, and did not bring forth another; for the spreading-forth of His Self and its revelation is by means of itself, not by means of another. "The spark of all sparks"—meaning, the light of the luminaries, a soul to the souls, which is the Self of the Godhead, namely the ten sefirot, a soul to the sefirot the vessels, as explained in the preceding chapters. "And struck within the desire of desires"—the intent is the Keter, when it is concealed in the Ein Sof; then it is called "the desire of desires."

And behold, it struck within it to be revealed, and the spark was concealed within the Keter, as is fitting, because it is a soul to it. And this is what he said, "and was concealed within it and not known"—the intent is that neither the Keter nor the spark, which is a soul to it, was revealed, by reason of the abundance of concealment. "At the time when this desire wished to expand"—meaning, the Keter is called "desire"; and the reason he called it "desire" and did not call it "the desire of desires" as above is because it is already emanated and stands to emanate—for it has a revelation greater and greater than when it was concealed in the Ein Sof—and therefore it is called "desire" alone, indicating the revelation. "Wished to expand"—the intent is that the Keter wished to be revealed and to emanate an expansion, which is Chokhmah, together with the sefirot that were concealed within the Keter. "This spark issued forth"—it is a simple matter that, before the emanation of the sefirot, He had to emanate the soul; for the soul is the cause of the sefirot, and it is the one that enlarges and gives life to them, as explained above and as will be explained, God willing. And so it was necessitated to order the matter, to emanate the soul, which is the spark—namely the light that shines and sparkles within the sefirot; and afterward Chokhmah, which is the sefirah itself, the vessel, would be revealed and emanated; and afterward the spark and the soul would enter into the midst of Chokhmah. And this is why he first said "this spark issued forth and was concealed within that desire," which is the light of the soul concealed within the Keter, which is "the desire." "In a manner that is seen and not seen," etc.—meaning, while it was in the Keter it was wholly concealed; and above, in the Keter, by reason of the abundance of concealment, he said "and not known." But now, after the spreading-forth into the existence of Chokhmah, the light and the soul sparkle within it, because it has more revelation—as is known, that it is called "being"—he said "in a manner that is seen and not seen." And he was precise in saying "in a manner" (ke-gavna) and did not say "in the manner" (be-gavna, with a Bet), because even "manner" is not aptly [said] except [as] "seen and not seen"—meaning, an apprehended existence, yet not a sufficient apprehension; rather, "and did not abide so as to subsist in that manner"—meaning, the colors are the actions, and the action of Chokhmah is not apprehended, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 3, God willing. "When this desire expanded"—meaning, above he said "when it wished," that is, when it wished to expand and be revealed and had not yet expanded, and then there was the existence of the soul of Chokhmah; and now he said "when it expanded," that is, that Chokhmah itself was literally emanated. "This spark struck," etc.—meaning, the soul of Chokhmah struck within it and emanated it and entered into it, for so is the way of the soul within the sefirot. And he said "color and not color," and did not say "seen and not seen" as he said above; the reason is that above it was within the Keter and was more concealed, and therefore he said "seen," etc.; but now that it is literally within Chokhmah, he said "color and not color," which is more revealed—namely, an apprehended color; and that a person cannot judge which color it is, because the essence of Chokhmah is not apprehended at all. "And issued forth in its colors"—the intent is that there were emanated in Chokhmah all the rest of the sefirot, which were concealed within the Keter; and likewise there were emanated there also the rest of the souls of the sefirot, included in the spark, which is the soul of Chokhmah; and they are called "colors" because there is nothing in the lantern to show its colors except by means of the light that shines and makes its colors shine toward its surface; therefore the colors are attributed to the soul, namely the spark and the light.

And the matter of how the sefirot were included in the Keter and were emanated to Chokhmah, etc., will be explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. "And ascended and descended and stood, in [its] ascent, within the desire and the expansion"—meaning, the soul is concealed within the Ein Sof, that is, His Self; and it pierces and descends down to the order of the sefirot. For one may not say that what is in Chokhmah is not what is in Keter, and what is in Keter is not what is in Chokhmah, God forbid; rather all is one thing, like the likeness of the ray of the sun shining through the lanterns: for although the light shining through one lantern is red, and that shining through another is green, with all this we shall not deny that the two lights are one unified light, and the change follows from the change of the lanterns. And so for the matter of the soul, that all is one unified light, and even if it is changed, it is by reason of the sefirot. And accordingly the soul "ascends and descends and stands, in [its] ascent," for the two of them are crowned as one, and all is unified in the Ein Sof. And although we say that the light is one and unified, we shall not deny that the light shining through the Keter is the first grade, and the light is revealed there [at] the utmost height; and as the light descends from before the presence of the Ein Sof, so it descends wondrously according to the descent of the grades, from cause to effect. And with all this, the reason for the changing is by reason of the screens and the lanterns that thicken the light and darken it, and it is accidental to them, not intrinsic; and from this no blemish whatever follows to the light, just as no blemish is attributed to the ray of the sun even though its light is darkened by reason of the lanterns. And this is what he said, "and ascended and descended and stood, in [its] ascent," which is the Ein Sof; "within the desire" is the Keter; "and the expansion" is Chokhmah; and the intent is that the light is united in a complete union, as explained. "The desire struck its expansion"—for Chokhmah, by the power of Keter, emanated Binah together with the rest of the sefirot; and this is "the desire struck," which is the Keter; "its expansion" is Chokhmah. "In an enclosure that is not known"—meaning, in the first aspect of Chokhmah together with Keter; and from there [comes] the union of Keter with Chokhmah, to give it power to emanate Binah; and that aspect is concealed, as is fitting to the Keter; and from within that aspect the Keter was united with Chokhmah, so that Chokhmah might emanate, from its power, Binah; and this matter will be explained at length in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. "And brought forth subtle lights, included as one"—the intent is Binah, which includes seven sefirot; and then, while they are there, they are like the horns of locusts—until the Holy One blessed be He transplanted them, etc. And this is what he said, "subtle"—that they are not in revelation and thickness as when they are emanated below, but rather are in great subtlety. And he said "included as one"—the intent is Binah, which includes them, as we said; and the whole principal [function] of Binah is the inclusion of the six extremities; and by them it is called Heh, which is the five bars of the Tabernacle, which are from Chesed downward, included in the five lights that are in the account of creation, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Fifty Gates, chapter 7, God willing. "When they wished to issue forth"—meaning, although he said above that they were already emanated, we have already explained that they cannot be emanated unless their soul and their sparkling light are emanated to them first; but he wished to complete the matter of the emanation of the sefirot, [and] afterward he returned and said that when they wished to be revealed, they were revealed by means of the soul, which is called "spark." "In which are lights"—it is the soul fitting to Binah, which includes the souls of the rest of the sefirot, just as it includes the sefirot themselves as well, as we explained. "It struck against that expansion and was distanced," etc.—the intent is that by the power of the soul the sefirot were emanated, subtle lights, in the manner we explained above, for they were like the horns of locusts. "And were heard as one"—the intent is that until now the lights were not revealed in revelation at all; and even now that they are revealed, it is not an intrinsic revelation but a partial revelation: somewhat of hearing without sight; and this is what he said, "and were heard as one." And his saying "as one" means united as one in the existence of Binah, and in it the sefirot appear at the beginning of their revelation, as we shall explain the law and its reason in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. "Then this spark showed its colors in them"—that is, the spark of the soul; and here he said "showed" and not above, and the reason is that in Binah is "the grade that stands to be asked of," as is known, and therefore "it showed its colors in them," which is not so above; and this is what he said above, "and were heard," to indicate that in Binah is the beginning of the revelation, as we explained. And the reason for "its colors" is not that the spark, namely the soul that spreads forth, possesses colors—for we already premised above that the soul is simple, etc.—but rather, by means of the revealed light the colors appear in the sefirot, as in the parable of the lantern, which possesses known colors, and those colors are revealed only by means of the ray of the sun shining through it, and then, by means of the light, the colors are seen. And so is the matter with the sefirah: it was not able to show the peoples and the princes its power except by means of the soul that gives it life and gives it power to act—like the likeness of the body, which has no action except by means of the soul, even though the soul is simple, as explained; and the intent is that the soul reveals the colors of Binah. And the measure of the phrase is thus: "it showed its colors in them"—I mean, it shows in them, in the sefirot themselves, their colors. And the reason he said "its colors" in the singular and did not say "their colors" is because they are included in Binah in a unified oneness, as explained. "And they were all colored as one," etc.—meaning, there are no colors except in Binah when it is revealed in itself; and "they were colored" afterward, below, by means of revelations; and since from there downward are the colors, namely the actions, therefore, close to their revelation, he said "they were colored." "White"—Chesed, and Netzach, which branches from it, for it too is white, but not like it. "Red"—Gevurah and Hod, both of which are red, in the secret of judgment. "Green"—Tiferet and Yesod, which are between the two colors, white and red. "And black"—it is Malkhut; and it is named thus by way of the "darkness" we explained above. And all this will be explained in the Gate of Colors, God willing. "And it tarried within it twelve months"—it is already well known that we reckon the molad of BaHaRaD for the conjunction before the creation of the world (see Tur, Orach Chayim, §427).

And behold, it had to be a full month, and there is no month without a year; therefore there had to be, before the emanation of the structure, some [span of] time—not "time," God forbid, but a priority in the manner of the other priorities, which are a priority of rank, like the priority of the cause over the effect. And therefore there had to be, before the emanation of the six days of the structure, [a state in which] they were crowned in Binah, in the secret of six and six: six for compassion, and six for judgment. And this is what is called "tarrying." And these are the twelve boundaries that are likewise in Binah, which are the twelve havayot that are in Tiferet after its emanation in its place, as will be explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapters 6, 7, and 8, God willing.

And behold, with this there may be understood a great doubt that falls upon the account of creation, namely their saying that there was no creation on the seventh day—and why, since the creation of the Sabbath day itself was already [accomplished], for the day itself requires creation; for so it is said in the Zohar: "six days the Lord made"—it says "six," and not "in six," implying that the six themselves the Lord made, which is the creation of heaven and earth, which are the six that include the six extremities; and accordingly, the creation of the Sabbath itself was already [accomplished]; and if so, how did He "rest" and "cease" on the seventh day? Rather, surely the Sabbath preceded the world; and were it not for the Sabbath, which gives power to the six days, they would have no power to act, because all six days, which are the six extremities, receive power from the central point, which is the sustaining of the hollow of the extremities, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Fifty Gates, chapter 5, God willing.

And behold, the six days had to tarry in the Sabbath to receive their sustenance from it; and if so, the Emanation was only six days, for the Sabbath preceded the world. And likewise the matter of this world: after six days will be the Sabbath; and just as the days of the week draw sustenance from the Sabbath and enter into it, this is "and it tarried there twelve months," which are a year—namely Tiferet, which includes six extremities, and it draws sustenance [of] judgment and compassion; and so it is found, six for judgment and six for compassion, which are the twelve months. And this is the choicest of the explanations that arise in this matter. "And were transplanted in another place"—the intent is their emanation to their places, as is known, that they were like the horns of locusts, and the Holy One blessed be He transplanted them.

And the matter of the reason for the transplanting and the planting will be explained at length in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. "And this spark ascends and descends"—the intent is the soul that is unified within them, and ascends up to the uttermost height, and descends down to the uttermost depth, as I explained. "And this is called the Botzina de-Kardinuta"—the meaning of "Botzina de-Kardinuta" in all the Zohar is "brimstone," and the intent is the Keter; for the supernal light, which is the Ein Sof, cleaves to the Keter and is held within it, like a lamp of brimstone in which the light is held most firmly. And some read kadrinuta, and its meaning is "blackness," by reason of the abundance of its concealment. And we have another way in this matter, and it is explained in the Sefer Or Yakar, God willing. And now, accordingly, the light that spreads forth from within the Ein Sof, which is concealed in the supernal Keter, spreads forth from there and descends and shines by way of the sefirot, of which it is the soul. And because the source of the light and the Self is from the Keter, therefore the whole Self is called Botzina de-Kardinuta, because its root and the source of the light is related to the Keter. And so Rashbi—may peace be upon him—explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 6): "The Cause over all, concealed and stored away in the Keter; and from it His light spreads forth by way of YHVH"—that is, Yod, Chokhmah; Heh, Binah; Vav, including six sefirot; Heh, Malkhut. End of his words. And we have already explained it with a strong hand in the third Gate, chapter 2, God willing.

And behold, our whole matter appears from within it: that the light of the Self that spreads forth within the sefirot has its source [in] the Keter, by means of the Ein Sof concealed within it. If so, it is fitting that this light be called by the name Botzina de-Kardinuta, which is a name of the Keter; for by means of this light the Keter is so called, because it shines like a lamp, etc. "This [light] arrayed and struck within all the plantings of lights, and says to it, 'Grow!'"—meaning, by means of this light, which overflows and shines within the sefirot, it enlarges them and gives them measure and weight according to the will of the Emanator, namely His Self that spreads forth. And to this the Sefer Yetzirah directed [its words] (cited above in the third Gate, chapter 4), saying, "their measure is ten, which have no end," etc.—that it is in His power to enlarge them without end, and to bound them with a limit, in the manner explained above in the preceding Gates. And concerning the matter of the soul he said, "and the Lord is one," etc.—who is unified in the source, for the soul and the source are all one. "Ruling over the sefirot, all of them, and forever and ever"—the intent is that, if He wishes, He would expand them up to the Ein Sof, without end; and the intent is in the increase of the revelation of His light within them. And the measure of the language of the said passage [is thus]: "This [light] arrayed and struck," which is the Emanation; "within all the plantings," which are the sefirot; "lights," which are the souls and the Self that spreads forth—meaning, He emanates within the sefirot lights and Self. "Then it brought forth the wellsprings of that [supernal] expansion," etc.—meaning, then, after the emanation and the tikkun of the order of the sefirot, each one according to its rank, then Chokhmah—which is the expansion mentioned above—arrays the source of the lights, I mean the effluence from the Keter, and it is in its power to add or to diminish. The matter is that the absence of the light and its departure, or its providence and its descent by way of the sefirot, is in Chokhmah—as in the matter of (Psalms 10:1) "Why, O Lord, do You stand afar off?"—in the manner of the light likened in the parable of the stories, which I explained, God willing. And therefore Chokhmah is the one that brings forth the sources and the light of the sefirot, in order to give them life and to enlarge them by that effluence of light; and it is in its power to conceal the light, so that it does not shine as is fitting, and then judgment comes to be. And this is what he said, "then it brought forth the wellsprings," etc., "by this Botzina de-Kardinuta"—meaning, by means of the light of the Self that spreads forth from the supernal Keter, as explained. "He who gives light, gives light"—meaning, by means of it the Ein Sof, who is designated, in concealment, [as] "He who gives light, gives light," so as not to designate Him by a name, gives light. Or he means: by means of the Botzina de-Kardinuta there is light and effluence to every possessor of light, and it shines, because there is no light to a sefirah except by means of the Botzina de-Kardinuta, which is the source of light to all the lights. "And it ascends and descends and expands in all directions"—meaning, by means of the light it enlarges the sefirot and gives them measure in every direction, as he concludes; though this light is unified in its source, as explained; and therefore it is called the Measuring Line—meaning, a line in the manner of the attributes, which are in a line; and it is the Measuring Line that gives measure to all the Emanation. And it is literally the Botzina de-Kardinuta, as we explained; except that the aspect of the light itself is called Botzina de-Kardinuta, and in the aspect of the attributes, [in] measuring them according to His will, which is the Self of the Emanator, it is called the Measuring Line. And this is what he said, "by this Botzina de-Kardinuta," which is the light, as explained, "when it expanded in all directions," that is, that it gives measure to every side of the sides of the Emanation, then it is called the Measuring Line. "And the measure abides above and below"—meaning, in the aspect of its giving measure to all the attributes, it is called the Measuring Line, and in the aspect of its Self, it is called Botzina de-Kardinuta; for that is its aspect in relation to before its spreading forth in the sefirot, to illumine and to measure. And this is what he said, "and the Measuring Line is the Botzina de-Kardinuta"—meaning, this Measuring Line is itself the Botzina de-Kardinuta, the Enclosure of all enclosures—that is, its aspect before it spread forth to measure and to give measure to the sefirot. "A shining measure that arrayed beauty for all—that beauty which issues from the first simplicity"—meaning, the Botzina de-Kardinuta and the Measuring Line are two aspects unified in the utmost union; for the matter of its aspect before its spreading forth, that is, the departure of the light into the source, and the aspect of its measure, are all together—namely, "a shining measure," which is the light that spreads forth and gives beauty to all the attributes, in the manner of the parable of the light to the lanterns, as explained. "Which issues from the first simplicity"—if so, its being a measure to the attributes, and its being a lamp (botzina)—that is, "which issues from the first simplicity"—are all one, unified. "It arrayed them by it," etc.—meaning, the Botzina de-Kardinuta is the one that arrays the attributes by the Self, namely the Measuring Line. "Whoever merits this," etc.—as is well known, that the one who discerns the courses of the Self within the sefirot, that is the lovely rank, above which there is no rank; and of such a one, and the like of him, it is said, "He saw his world in his lifetime, [and] recognizes his Maker." And of him it is said (Psalms 91:14), "I will set him on high, because he has known My name"; and of this it is said (1 Chronicles 28:9), "Know the God of your father, and serve Him." And let not the one who studies think that the departure of this light of the Self that spreads forth, to its source, or its spreading forth, indicates change in the Emanator, God forbid; for change is not aptly [predicated] of such a matter, just as change is not aptly [predicated] of the removal of providence from the world, even according to the way of Rabbi David and the rest of those who speak on this matter; for the change in the attributes is by reason that they are not prepared to receive the Self—not by reason of change, God forbid.

And behold, the explanation of this passage is completed, according as it was poured forth upon us from Heaven. And it is not hidden from us that this passage requires a wider explanation, and an intellect that is not now within the human compass—how much more so that the absence of [such] existence could explain it; but with all this we have done what was incumbent upon us, and from within it we have learned the existence of the sefirot and the Self that spreads forth within them, as has been explained, and it will yet be explained at length, God willing. And blessed is YHVH, the God of Israel, who has not let a redeemer cease for us, and has enlightened our eyes in this passage—which is in the apprehension of a thing agreed upon in the mouths of all the Kabbalists when they say "the effluence that overflows." And from within them the give-and-take has been clarified: that the effluence is the revelation of the soul of the sefirot and of the Self of the Emanator within the sefirot; and then His light descends and pierces down to the abyss, for the sefirot will answer [with] the light to Creation, and Creation to Formation, and Formation to Action, and Action to the heavens, and the heavens will answer the earth, and the earth will answer Israel; and "abundant good to the house of Jacob" in their cleaving to their God, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4), "And you who cleave to YHVH your God are alive, all of you, this day." For the cause of life is by reason of the cleaving. And he means by saying "alive, all of you"—that you all draw sustenance from the Living, Eternal One; and therefore "alive, all of you."

After we have compelled, from the passage in the preceding chapter, the matter of the Self and the vessels, there is yet a clear proof to bring, in a third passage of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—in the book of the Ra'aya Mehemna (portion Bo, fol. 42b). And these are his words: "And to whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" (Isaiah 40:25)—for before the Holy One blessed be He created any image in the world and formed any form, He was alone, without form and without likeness. And whoever apprehends Him as He was before creation—when He is beyond any image—it is forbidden to make for Him a form or image in the world, neither by the letter Yod nor by the letter Heh, nor even by the holy name, nor by any letter or vowel-point in the world. And this is [the meaning of] "for you saw no likeness"—of anything that has in it a likeness or image you saw nothing. But after He made this image of the Chariot of the supernal Adam, He descended there and was called by that image "YHVH," so that they might apprehend Him by each and every attribute among His attributes; and He was called "El, Elohim, Shaddai, Tzeva'ot, Ehyeh," so that they might apprehend Him by each and every attribute—how the world is governed by lovingkindness and by judgment, according to the deeds of human beings. For were His light not to spread forth over all creatures, how would they apprehend Him, and how would "the whole earth is full of His glory" be fulfilled? Woe to him who likens Him to any attribute—even to any of these attributes that are His own—how much more so to human beings, whose foundation is in the dust, who perish and pass away. Rather, His likeness is according to His dominion over that attribute, and indeed over all creatures, and above that attribute; and when He withdraws from it, He has no attribute, and no likeness, and no form—like the likeness of the waters of the sea, for the waters that issue from it have no graspable [shape] at all, and no form; but by the spreading-forth of the waters of the sea over a vessel, which is the earth, a likeness is made, and we can make there a reckoning. Thus: the source of the sea is one. A spring issues from it, according to its spreading-forth into that vessel, in a circle, which is the Yod—behold, the source is one, and the spring that issues from it is two. Afterward He made a great vessel, like one who digs a great pit and it is filled with the water that issues from the spring—behold, that great vessel is called "sea," and it is the third vessel. And that great vessel is divided into seven vessels, like long vessels; thus the water spread from the sea into seven streams. Behold, the source, and the spring, and the sea, and the seven streams—these are ten. And if the Craftsman should break those vessels that He fashioned, behold, the water returns to the source, and the broken vessels remain dry, without water. Thus the Cause of causes made ten sefirot, and called Keter "source," and in it there is no end to the welling of the light; and therefore He called Himself Ein Sof, and He has no likeness or form, and there is no vessel there to grasp Him, to know Him by any knowledge at all; and therefore it is written, "Into what is too wondrous for you do not inquire, and into what is covered from you do not search." Afterward He made a small vessel, and this is the Yod, and it was filled from Him, and He called it "a welling spring of wisdom," and He called Himself "wise" by it, and He called that vessel "Chokhmah." And afterward He made a great vessel and called it "sea," and called it "Binah," and He called Himself "understanding." By it [He is] "wise of Himself and understanding of Himself." For Chokhmah is not called wisdom of itself, but only on account of that Wise One who fills it from His welling; and it is not called Binah of itself, but only on account of that Understanding One who fills it from Himself. For were He to withdraw from it, it would remain dry; this is [the meaning of] "the waters have failed from the sea, and the river is parched and dry" (Isaiah 19:5). Afterward, "and He smote it into seven streams" (Isaiah 11:15), and made it into seven precious vessels, and called them Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And He called Himself "Great" in Gedulah, and "Pious" in Chesed, and "Mighty" in Gevurah, and "Glorious" in Tiferet; and in Netzach, "the Master, victor of battles," and He is the Victory of victories; and in Hod He called His name "the Majesty of our Maker"; and in Yesod He called His name "Righteous," and Yesod—all the vessels and all the worlds rest upon it; and in Malkhut He called His name "King." And "His are the greatness, and the might, and the glory (Tiferet), and the victory (Netzach), and the majesty (Hod), for all that is in heaven [and earth]"—which is the Righteous One; "His is the kingship"—which is Malkhut. All is in His authority: to diminish in the vessels, and to add to them welling, and to diminish according to His desire in it; and there is no other god above Him to add to it or to diminish from it. End of his words, as relevant to our intent. And now, may the repose of the holy Rashbi—may peace be upon him—be exalted, for he has enlightened our eyes with the pleasantness of his sayings and the sweetness of his tongue; he was lengthy in explaining to us all the details upon which we were lengthy in chapter 4. And although our intent is explained from within his words, with all this we shall set our eyes upon this passage, to explain some of the doublings of the language and to expound the depth of his words, God willing. "Before He created," etc.—meaning, before the Ein Sof, blessed be He, was revealed in this pure and holy Emanation of His, the existence of His simple Godhead was united in the Self of His Godhead alone, and He had neither name nor letter nor vowel-point, since the existence of the names is in the Emanation; and if so, since there was no Emanation, there was neither name nor figure. And the meaning of "form and figure" is an attribute that should be designated to Him; for the Emanation is an attribute and a concealed form, apprehended by the prophets—peace be upon them—by means of the intermediaries; but then, before His Emanation, there was neither name nor figure nor attribute at all, but rather the Ein Sof united in the Self of His Godhead, as explained. "And whoever apprehends Him before creation"—meaning, the Ein Sof, blessed be He, has two aspects: whether we consider Him in relation to His Godhead before the Emanation, which is His aspect revealed to His own Self and not to another; or His apprehended aspect, which is His aspect toward the emanated ones. And now he said "and whoever apprehends Him"—the intent is that one who wishes to engage in His existence, in the knowledge of His Godhead above the emanated ones—which is the first aspect—must take care not to depict in Him any name or letter or vowel-point. And this is what he said, "and whoever apprehends Him before creation"—meaning, to engage with Him before the emanation of the created entities and the emanated ones, namely His first aspect, which is "beyond image"—meaning, that He is above the emanated ones, that is, His aspect concealed from them. He said that it is forbidden to make for Him a form and image, etc.—meaning, that it is not fitting to bound Him by a letter or a vowel-point, to say "His attribute is thus," [since] He has no attributes above. And therefore He is not designated by letters, for the letters and the attributes are all one. And the matter is that the letters are emanated forms that bound the corporeal letters to the spiritual; and how would it be apt to ascribe emanated forms to the aspect of the Ein Sof before the Emanation? And therefore neither name nor vowel-point is apt of the Ein Sof; and even in Keter, letters are not applicable in the aspect of its own self, but only in the aspect of its tikkun—that is, what it includes of nine sefirot; and therefore it is called by the name Ehyeh and by the name YHVH: from the side of Chokhmah it is called by the name YHVH, and from the side of Binah by the name Ehyeh, for the name Ehyeh is female to the name YHVH. And this matter will be explained in the coming Gates, God willing, and in the Sefer Or Yakar, in the commentary on the Idra. "And not even by the holy name," etc. And at first glance this is difficult, in view of what is expounded in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, which said that before the world was created the Holy One blessed be He and His name alone existed—from which it appears that the four-letter name preceded [the world] as [old as] His own pre-eternity. But this is no question, for the four-letter name is the existence of the sefirot, and it is a coming-to-be in the coming-to-be of the sefirot; but in the Ein Sof neither name nor vowel-point is applicable.

And the matter of the passage will be explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 4, God willing. "Of anything that has in it a likeness," etc.—meaning, of all the sefirot that receive likeness and image upon His spreading-forth within the vessels, as will be explained; and this is the second aspect of the Emanator, which is His aspect toward His sefirot, namely His Self that spreads forth within them; and this aspect receives likeness by means of the sefirot, like the likeness of the soul that receives form and likeness by means of the body. And he said that even that existence is not fitting to ascribe to His aspect concealed from all His emanated ones, for there is no apprehension of it, and no name, at all. And the measure of the language, "of anything that has in it a likeness," etc., means [the likeness] that is the bounding of the sefirot, even though it is not [literally] a bound. "You saw" nothing in the Ein Sof; and even though no prophet or seer can reach Keter, how much more so the Ein Sof above. The intent is that they reached, in the grades of Chokhmah, to know the simplicity of the Ein Sof in itself, in the understanding of the intellect, and they discerned that above, in the First Cause, it is impossible to depict by any figure His spreading-forth within the sefirot, because He is not apprehended by another, as I explained. "But after He made," etc.—the intent is, after He emanated the pure and holy Emanation, that is, the figure of Adam, by way of parable, as explained above in chapter 6 in the passage of Elijah. "He descended there"—meaning, that is His spreading-forth within the sefirot. "And was called," etc.—meaning, just as the sefirot are [named], so the light that spreads forth within them is called. "So that they might apprehend Him"—meaning, therefore He spreads forth within them; and the reason is that the whole Emanation itself is only to reveal His Godhead to the lowly, as explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation. "By each and every attribute," etc.—meaning, He spread forth according to His attributes, so that the inhabitants of the world might recognize Him according to His existence in each and every attribute, and His action by means of it. "For were He not to spread forth," etc.—the intent is that, were the grades not to descend to this limit, with the soul, which is the Self, spreading forth within them, they would not recognize the Maker, as explained in the said Gate. "And how would the whole earth is full of His glory be fulfilled?"—this is a second reason that His spreading-forth within all His emanated ones was necessitated: for were He not spreading forth within them, how would "the whole earth is full of His glory" be fulfilled? And this matter will be explained at length in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, God willing. "Like the likeness of the waters of the sea"—meaning, just as the waters that gather into the vessels, whether long or round or square, will be in the likeness of the vessels, and that likeness and form belongs to the water only while it is there—not intrinsically but accidentally—so the Self that spreads forth into the midst of the sefirot: the changes and the attributes do not belong to it intrinsically but accidentally, like the likeness of the spreading-forth of the soul within the body; and the judgment and the compassion are intrinsic to the sefirot, which are called vessels, and accidental to the sefirot which are called Self. And the matter is by means of the sefirot; and after His withdrawal from the sefirot, no attribute belongs to Him. "Into what is too wondrous for you do not inquire," etc.—it is already well known that the attribute of Keter is not apprehended even by the sefirot at all, and therefore it is expounded concerning this sefirah, "into what is too wondrous," etc. "He made a small vessel"—the intent is to the smallness of the apprehension in it, and therefore it is called "small"; but in the matter of its existence it is greater than the one below it, for it is a cause to all that is beneath it. "And He called it a welling spring of wisdom"—meaning, to His spreading-forth which is within the sefirot He called "spring," etc. "And that vessel"—meaning, the sefirah, which is the vessel, He called "Chokhmah," etc. "By it [He is] wise of Himself and understanding of Himself." The intent is to explain to us how He is wise with a wisdom that is His own, and not with a wisdom outside Himself—even though they are vessels—since they are wisdom and understanding only by means of the Self that spreads forth within them, and that Self is the principal Chokhmah and Binah; and accordingly it is found that He is wise with a wisdom that He Himself is the Chokhmah, and understanding with an understanding that He Himself is the Binah, and Chokhmah and Binah are vessels in which His wisdom and His understanding clothe themselves. "And He called Himself Great in Gedulah," etc.—His intent is to explain to us that, although in Him, may He be blessed, the descriptions are not ascribed, since He is utterly simple, without descriptions, with all this, from the side of His uniting with the sefirot and spreading forth within them, the descriptions were necessitated for Him. And this is "and He called Himself," etc.—meaning, He called Himself "Great" by means of His spreading-forth within Gedulah, etc.; and so for the rest of the sefirot. "To add to the vessels or to diminish in them"—in the manner explained in the preceding chapter, that the spreading-forth that is within them is what enlarges them, and brings them into a limit, and expands them forever and ever, for they are His vessels, and all is according to His will; which is not so in His Self, the King of the kings of kings, for there is none who overflows to Him, and He overflows to them all. Thus far has reached the force of the words of Moses our Teacher—peace be upon him—with Rashbi—may peace be upon him—and his companions, in a manner direct toward them and revealed to their eyes, as he explained in the Introduction of the Tikkunim, that He grants permission to the heads of the academies that are in the Garden of Eden to gather to them and to engage with them in this wisdom.

And behold, it has been explained from within these passages that the sefirot are the Self of the Creator, and that He is the soul that spreads forth within the sefirot, which are vessels; and behold, in this manner the Ein Sof is called "a soul to the souls," for He is a soul to the sefirot, which are souls to the rest of the effects beneath them; and they are subtle, the utmost of subtlety, until the intellect cannot liken them to anything in the world, by reason of the abundance of their subtlety and their eminence.

After we have agreed, in the matter of the sefirot, that they are Self and vessels, and the matter has been well explained—that the descriptions in the Ein Sof are not literally in Him, but by means of His sefirot, as we explained in the preceding chapters—we have gained a fine and pleasant resolution to the great perplexity in which all the philosophers, and most of the later sages of Israel who engage in the externals, were perplexed. And it is that which Rambam, of blessed memory, asked in the Sefer ha-Madda, in Hilkhot Teshuvah, chapter 5, and these are his words: "Perhaps you will say: but does not the Holy One blessed be He know all that will be before it comes to be? Did He know that this one would be righteous or wicked, or did He not know? If He knew that he would be righteous, it is impossible that he should not be righteous; and if you say that He knew he would be righteous and [yet] it is possible that he should be wicked, then He did not know the matter in its fullness." End of his words.

And behold, according to this question, it is impossible to say that the foreknowledge is above and the free will is in the hand of the human being, for the one contradicts the other. And now we have from this no difficulty at all, neither root [nor branch]. And the matter is that they posited foreknowledge in the Creator, and said that He knows, wills, and is able; for although in the rest of the descriptions they are not to be ascribed to Him, these we are compelled [to ascribe]. And so some of the Kabbalists wrote. But I say that, since we said above that the Creator is wise by means of the attribute of Chokhmah and not by a wisdom outside Himself—as we expanded the explanation in the preceding chapters—so we say that Keter is called "Will," and the Creator wills by means of it; and we shall yet be lengthy in this in the Gate of Tzachtzachot, chapter 6, God willing. And likewise the Creator is able by means of Binah, for it is called "Power," as is known. And He knows by means of Da'at, for the attribute of Da'at is the Creator's knowledge—I mean, that He knows by means of it; and from within it, in the manner we explained above. And so it is proven that this Da'at is His knowledge and His foreknowledge, for so says the verse (Proverbs 3:20), "by His knowledge the depths were split." And it will not be difficult for us [to say] that, accordingly, He and His knowledge are not [literally] one—just as it is not difficult for us that He and Chokhmah are not [literally] one, as was explained above. And now, behold, it is known that the Da'at is Tiferet, as we explained in the third Gate, chapter 8; and it is known that the free will of the human being is from the side of Malkhut, for from it downward are the two ways, and "sin crouches at the door," and it is what is called "free will"; and so it is called "the House of Choice," as is known. And now we say that there is a distinction in the foreknowledge before a person sins—even though he is destined to sin—and after he has sinned: for before he sinned, the knowledge of that sin was in Da'at, but it was not making a blemish or impression above, because he had not yet blemished, nor empowered the outer [forces]. And so too in this manner regarding the supernal foreknowledge with respect to charity and the rest of the commandments: for although it is known above, the commandment does not overflow and does not illumine until he performs it; and this is [the meaning of] (Genesis 22:12) "now I know that you fear God." And the intent is that, although the foreknowledge was above, with all this Tiferet and Malkhut were not uniting and overflowing from the side of that knowledge, for it was in potential; but after it came into actuality and the commandment was performed, behold, the knowledge was in actuality, and Tiferet united with Malkhut by means of it. And this is "now I know," which is a term of knowledge and of joining, like "and the man knew," etc. (Genesis 4:1). And likewise regarding the transgression: that supernal foreknowledge which was in Da'at made no impression, because the Holy One blessed be He judges only [a man] as he is there; but after he has sinned, it makes an impression and a blemish above. And now, after we have known this distinction, we shall further know that Tiferet is the attribute of compassion, and Malkhut the attribute of judgment.

And behold, from the side of Tiferet there is the four-letter name in direct [order], thus:  Y H V H; and this name is called "male," for the male is in the secret of compassion—because this name strengthens compassion over judgment, that is, the Yod, which is Chokhmah, over the Heh, which is Binah; this is compassion and that is judgment. And likewise the Vav over the Heh, that is, Tiferet (Vav) strengthens over Malkhut, which is Heh. And the Yod and the Vav are Abba and Son, compassion; and the two Hehs are Imma and her daughter—or bride and her mother-in-law—which are from the side of judgment. And Malkhut is the Name in reverse, thus:  H V H Y; and this is [when] the females rule, and it is judgment. And all this has been explained at length in the Tikkunim, and it will yet be explained in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light. And now we say that, just as it is not far-fetched that judgment should prevail over compassion—even though the Ein Sof Himself judges His creatures by means of them—and likewise that it is not far-fetched that Malkhut should sometimes prevail over Tiferet, even though the Ein Sof clothes Himself in them—so it is not far-fetched that Malkhut, which is the free will, should prevail over Tiferet, which is the foreknowledge and the Da'at. And all the more so, since that foreknowledge makes no impression, as we explained; for after an impression has been made, repentance is needed, which is Binah, which is higher.

And behold, the free will will prevail over the foreknowledge in other commandments that a person performs, and he will not sin. And by this may be understood what they said, of blessed memory (in tractate Avodah Zarah, fol. 4[b]), "Israel were not fit for that deed," etc.; and likewise David was not fit for that deed—that is, by means of their making the free will prevail over the foreknowledge. Further, we have gained much doubled good concerning the matter that was difficult for the commentators in the explanation of Rabbi Menachem. According to his view, since the sefirot are subject to change and limit—even though it is not literally a limit, but in the manner explained in the preceding Gates—if so, how is it possible that the Ein Sof, though removed from this matter to the utmost remove, should join with them and accompany those subject to changes? And in truth this is more and more difficult upon the view of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—who explained above that the very Self of the Godhead literally spreads forth within the sefirot: how is it possible to say that two opposite things were united, since the Ein Sof is devoid of descriptions and opposites and changes and limit, and the sefirot possess these matters—and how is it possible to say that the Ein Sof and the sefirot are all one thing? So much so that some of the commentators said that the matter of His binding and union in the sefirot is concealed and exalted, just as there is concealed from us also the existence of the union and binding of the soul with the body—even though the body is coarse and thick, possessing the corporeal cravings and the rest of the things ascribed to it, while the soul is devoid of the natures of the body and its accidents, and is a subtle and spiritual being; if so, how is it possible that they should be united? Rather, surely they are united, and their manner is exalted and concealed from the eye of the created entities, and the eyes of the sages have grown dim from comprehending this matter. And if the soul that is within us is thus, then how shall we have any engagement with the hidden things? This is the sum of their view in the matter. But for us this answer is not sufficient, for the existence of the binding of the soul with the body is explained for us, and it is among the simple matters of this wisdom, as will be explained in the Gate of the Soul; for there is a great affinity of the soul with the body, such that their union and binding is no wonder. And so we say in the matter of the sefirot and the Ein Sof, blessed be He. For the Ein Sof has attributes; and if they are not attributes in relation to Himself, they are attributes in relation to the created entities. For it is known that He is wise of Himself and great of Himself; and yet, to guide the created entities, He had to display His action to another. And since this is so, He had to emanate an Emanation, and to bring it about in such a way that the greatness and the Chesed would act in this world; and moreover He had to [arrange] that the governance be by means of Him specifically, not by means of another. And if so, in His love for the creation He had to emanate a vessel for His work, such that that Chesed would be united with His piety, and the Gevurah with His might, and His judgment with His being a Judge. And therefore it is found that all the matters of Chesed are ascribed to the Chesed which is the Self; and the Chesed which is the Self, in order to perform its action, needs the Chesed which is the vessel; and the Chesed which is the vessel needs the Chesed which is the Self; and they are united in the utmost union. And it is "like that locust whose garment is of its own [body]"—for the garment without it is a dumb stone, and it, without a garment, has no means for its actions. And so it is with the matter of the sefirot.

And behold, just as the questioner will not ask, and will not wonder, at the choice speaking creature [the human] that accompanies the garments, which are lacking in perfection, of base worth, of worn-out rags—because he sees that a person is ascribed to those garments, so that even the abstinent do not wholly remove themselves from them, as in the matter of "bread to eat and clothing to wear" that Jacob our father—peace be upon him—requested (Genesis 28:20), though he was the choicest of the secluded contemplatives of his generation, to the point that he drove sleep from his eyes for twenty years—so it should be no wonder, in the supernal matters, that they should be a need of the Godhead, and a union of the Godhead with them; for they are a supernal need, for the governance of the lowly. Even though it is true that the Emanation was not for a need that He had of them, God forbid, but only a benefaction that His attribute freely bestowed, to do good to another, and not that He was compelled—but only by will and love; and this matter, too, will be explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, God willing. And it remains incumbent upon us to explain a mighty question that falls under the category of the inquiry with which we have engaged in this Gate, and it is this: that, if it is true—as it is, beyond doubt—that the Creator, the King of the kings of kings, has no change at all, and does not change from matter to matter; and likewise He is not subject to composition, God forbid, for He is simple, and His simplicity is not like the simplicity of the angels, the separate intelligences, for they are contingently existent, and there was a time when they did not exist, as is proven in the words of the Sages, of blessed memory (in Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 3), and especially in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, where he hinted that the angels were created on the second day—and if so, they are contingently existent; and from this side is their composition, for they are composed of privation and existence—which is not so with God, who is one, simple, the utmost of simplicity, necessarily existent, and His existence neither lacks nor exceeds; and were the cessation of all created entities to be imagined, no deficiency would reach Him on that account, God forbid; and were their multiplication imagined, He would not be multiplied on that account, God forbid; and were the cessation of all created entities imagined, they would perish and He would stand. And since these premises are true, and fit to be like nails driven into the heart of the believers, how can we restrain ourselves before the modest ones, the masters of [divine] service, who say that the sefirot are His Self, and that they are emanated from some time—be it much or little? According to their view, there was already a time when they were not in existence; if so, they are contingently existent, and behold, from this side they are composite, like the composition of the angels—and this is contrary to the true faith. And it is true that one can answer this in the manner in which some of the commentators wished to answer, and they said that the coming-to-be and the Emanation is not from the side of the Emanator, for the Emanation itself was concealed in His Self, in the best, most subtle, and most excellent potential of the Agent; but now they were revealed and went forth from potential to actuality, and this is a coming-to-be in relation to the created entities, and not in relation to the Emanator. And this matter will suffice to say that the Emanation is no coming-to-be in relation to the Emanator, who is the Self of the simple Ein Sof. But as for the existence of the Emanation itself, namely the sefirot, which are His Self as I explained, surely we shall not deny that, even though they were concealed, with all this this existence of theirs—which is the existence of their spreading-forth—did not exist. If so, we say that this existence of theirs is contingent; and since it is contingent—for it is possible that it should be and possible that it should not be—even we say that they are not like the existence of God at all, for God is necessarily existent. And now, to repair and settle this matter, let us set forth a fine parable, ascribed to the Emanation, and it is: that a person should depict in his mind a great fire, in the utmost [degree], and from the abundance of the brilliance of its light and the intensity of its heat—if some formed thing should be depicted within that fire, would it not be scorched and perish in an instant?

And behold, He brought into being within it, and brought about by means of it, by the abundance of His power, by His will, a sphere that conceals the fire from all its sides, so that the light should not be revealed at all; and even though that sphere is not of the very self of the fire, nonetheless the light that shines in the sphere and governs it is the bright light prior to the existence of the sphere, and its existence did not change, except that its light was somewhat withheld from what it had been, by reason of the sphere; and there is no change to the light and to the heat, but only to the sphere. Further, He saw in His wisdom that if, within the first sphere, there should come to be a being that arises in His will to come to be, it would not be able to subsist, and the intent would not go forth into actuality, by reason of the abundance of the brilliance of the light and the heat of the fire. Therefore He had to bring into being a sphere within the sphere, so that each and every one of them should conceal the light and the brilliance of the great fire, which warms and illumines toward the surface of the spheres, inward—until the spheres reached the number of ten. And afterward He further brought into being within them spheres, from ten to ten, all of them spheres, garments, and screens to the light and the heat that comes from the roots of the great fire, and chains down by way of the spheres and clothes itself in them, until the inner Creation—which is the middle one, and which is in truth the most external—is able to bear a light, and a sweet heat, equal to its temperament, that will benefit it and not harm it.

And behold, all this is not by reason of the light and the heat, but by reason of the weakness of that Creation, which cannot bear the light and the heat that flows from the fire without intermediaries. And we shall not say that by means of the intermediaries the light and the heat changed, in relation to the heat and light [themselves]; for the first heat and light is the last, and in relation to the existence of the light and the heat themselves, it never changed. And the change is in relation to those spheres and screens, which change and descend, and by reason of which the brilliance of the light does not reach them as at its source.

And behold, the light and the heat that spreads forth within the spheres did not come to be with the coming-to-be of the spheres; rather, on the contrary, it preceded them, as the great fire—which is the source of the light and the heat—precedes [them]; and only the spheres and the vessels that thicken its light came to be, in relation to themselves, not in relation to the light and the heat, whose power then is its power now. And on the contrary, beforehand its light reached a more revealed and more excellent manifestation than this, except that the spheres clothed it and concealed it. And now, behold, the great fire is the Ein Sof, the King of the kings of kings; and it is the thing signified, here, in the parable of the great fire, by the likeness of some of the properties [of fire], as the commentators were lengthy. And the spheres are the sefirot, the vessels. And the light and the heat that spreads forth within them is His Self [may He be exalted, the concealed One that spreads forth within the sefirot—from Asis Rimonim], which is a soul to the soul, and gives life to the sefirot, and enlarges them and strengthens them, and gives them the power to stand and to serve.

And behold, the light and the heat did not come to be and did not change, except in relation to the renewed vessels. But in relation to the light itself, there is no coming-to-be and no change, for the soul existed beforehand. But in relation to the vessels, He brought into being for them a place in His Self, so that by means of them the living [vessels] might bear the power of His Godhead. Thus far has reached the parable and the thing signified.

And behold, this inquiry has been explained with a fine explanation. And to be lengthy in this is iniquity and guilt; and our intent is only for the honor of the Omnipresent, to establish faith in the heart of the discerning. And when they look upon these our words with good consideration, in this parable, there will be understood and discerned from within it several things sweeter than honey; and the brevity is fine; and may God forgive.

Behold, the intent in this chapter is only to cite a passage of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—that reveals the matter of the attributes in all the facets of the inquiry with which we have engaged in the preceding chapters; and from within it some of the passages that Rabbi David brought to compel his view will be explained. And these are the words of [Rashbi] in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Pinchas, fol. 257b), [on] the thirteenth commandment, the recitation of the Shema: And one must know that He is called "wise" in all kinds of wisdom, and "understanding" in all kinds of understanding, and "pious" in all kinds of pieties, and "mighty" in all kinds of mighty deeds, and "counselor" in all kinds of counsels, and "righteous" in all kinds of righteousness, and "king" in all kinds of kingship—up to the Ein Sof (another reading: up to Keter)—and up to that which has no investigating. And in these grades, by one He is called "compassionate" and by one "judge"; and so in several grades, up to the Ein Sof. If so, is there a change between "compassionate" and "judge"? Rather, before He created the world, He was called by all these grades on account of the creatures that were destined to be created; for were there no creatures of the world, why would He be called "compassionate," "judge"? Rather, on account of the creatures that were destined [to be]. And therefore all the names are His titles, after His deeds. In like manner He created the soul in His image, which is called after its actions in each and every limb of the body, which is called "a small world" [microcosm]. And just as the Master of the world is governed in all creatures and in each and every generation according to their deeds, so the soul [is named] according to its deeds in each and every limb: that limb in which it performs a commandment, the soul is called, in relation to it, "pity," and "lovingkindness," "favor," and "compassion"; and that limb in which it performs a transgression, the soul is called, in relation to it, "judgment," and "fury," and "irritation." But outside the body, toward whom would there be pity or cruelty? So too the Master of the world, before He created the world and created His creatures—toward whom would He be called "compassionate" and "gracious," or "judge"? Rather, all His names are titles, and [yet] not titles; and He is called by them only on account of the creatures of the world. And therefore, when the masters of the generation are good, He is called toward them "YHVH," in the attribute of compassion; and when the generation are guilty, He is called "Adonai," in the attribute of judgment—to each generation and to each human being according to his measure. But not that He has a [fixed] attribute or a known name. In like manner to the sefirot: for each sefirah has a known name, and has an attribute and a bound and a border; and by these names the Master of the world spreads forth, and reigns in them, and is called by them, and is covered in them, and dwells in them, like a soul in all the limbs of the body. And just as the Master of the worlds has no known name and no known place, but rather His dominion is on every side, so too the soul has no known name and no known place in the whole body, but its dominion is on every side, and there is no limb empty of it. And therefore one may not mark it in one place; for were one [to do so], its dominion would be lacking in the rest of the limbs. Nor [may one] call it by one name, or by two, or by three—to say of it that it is "Chokhmah," and "Binah," and that it has "Da'at," and no more; for were one to do so, behold, it would be lacking from the rest of the grades. How much more so the Master of the world, whom one may not mark in a known place, nor call by known names, nor make Him two by them, nor make Him three by them—like the grade of the Chariot, of which it is said "they shall make threefold the holiness to You"; for all His grades and Chariots, all of them are threefold, like the Patriarchs, who are the Chariot—for they are the likeness of lion, ox, eagle, and they are a Chariot to "Adam," of whom it is said, "and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man"; and from the side of the female they rule over "Adam," and the female is a Chariot to them; and therefore it is said of it, "they shall make threefold the holiness to You." In like manner the letters, which are the faces of the living creatures, are threefold, thus:  Y H V,  H V Y,  V H Y—the fourth Heh: "they shall make threefold the holiness to You," it [the fourth] is the completion of them all, to complete by them the name YHVH. But the Master of all—one may not make Him threefold by names or by letters; rather, He is called by all the names, and He has no known name, and each and every name testifies of Him: that He is Lord over all the worlds, the name Adonai testifies of Him. And there is none who knows that there is a person who inherits three hundred and ten worlds—this is [the meaning of] "to endow those who love Me with substance (yesh)," according to his grade, which is called "substance from nothing," and this is the supernal Chokhmah. And there is a person who inherits only one world, according to his grade, as we have established, "each and every righteous one has a world of his own"; and so every human being of Israel inherits worlds according to his grade above. But the Master of the world—one may not mark for Him worlds in number, but rather He is Lord over all worlds, and Adonai testifies of Him. So too YHVH: from it depend all the beings [havayot], and it and all its havayot testify of the Master of the world, that He was before all the beings, and He is within every being, and He is after every being; and this is the secret of the havayot testifying of Him: "was, is, and will be." Judgment, in the reversal of the letters, is Adonai; and therefore the Sages, of blessed memory, said, "the law of the kingdom is law." The name El testifies of the Master of all, that there is no capacity in any name and havayah and grade—how much more so in the rest of the creatures lesser than it—this is [the meaning of] "and all the inhabitants of the earth are reckoned as nothing, and according to His will He acts in the host of heaven," etc. Elohim testifies of His Godhead, that He is Elohim, and the God of gods, and He is God over all, and there is no god above Him. Tzeva'ot testifies, as it is said, "and according to His will He acts in the host of heaven." Shaddai testifies of Him, that when He said to His world "Enough!" it stood within its border and its bound, and did not spread forth further—and so too to the water, and the wind, and the fire. And so too every name and havayah testifies of Him: that when He was one, before He created the world, why would He need to be called by these names, or by the rest of the titles, such as "compassionate," "gracious," "long-suffering," etc., "judge," "powerful," "mighty"? And by many of all these names and titles He is called, on account of all the worlds and their creatures, to show His dominion over them. So too the soul: in relation to its dominion over all the limbs of the body, it is likened to Him—not that it is comparable to Him in itself, for He created it, and there is no god above Him who created Him.

And further, the soul has several changes and accidents and causes that are ascribed to it, which is not so for the Master of all; and therefore it is likened to Him in its dominion over all the limbs of the body, but not in any other matter. End of his words.

And from within it are explained all the parts and sides of the inquiry expounded in this Gate. And now it is our wish to be lengthy in its explanation and in the details of his words, by reason of the abundance of its usefulness.

And further, from within it will be explained most of what we explained in the preceding chapters. And the meaning of "wise in all kinds of wisdom" is because there are many aspects to Chokhmah and Binah, and they are "kinds of wisdom" according to the change and multiplicity of the aspects; and within them all the Ein Sof spreads forth, in order to perform all the actions, for the attributes have no power to perform an action apart from Him. And he said "up to the Ein Sof." The meaning is that all His actions are not like the actions of the attributes themselves, because the actions of the attributes have a limit and an end, according to the apprehension of each and every attribute in the Self that spreads forth into the sefirot; but the Self that spreads forth into the sefirot has no end to its actions. And the reason he did not mention Keter at all is because in Keter there is no attribute and no action at all, and it is only a throne and a palace to the Ein Sof, by means of which the Emanation and the Self spread forth within the vessels.

And behold, Keter is a source and a cause to the vessels, and the Ein Sof is a source [and] cause to the Self; and the two of them spread forth as one, the Emanator clothing Himself in the emanated. And for this reason the first emanated [Keter] has no action at all, and the beginning of action is from Chokhmah. "And counselor in all kinds of counsels"—that is, in Netzach and Hod, which are "kidneys that counsel," and by means of the overflowing of the counsel in the supernal court—that is, in the partnership of Tiferet with them, for the principal counsel is from it. And his saying "that He is called," that is, to ascribe the attributes to the Self of the Ein Sof. And this is "and in these grades by one He is called," etc.—that is, that the Self of the Ein Sof is so called by means of the attributes, as will be explained. "By one He is called compassionate"—and the intent is "compassionate" from the side of the right, and "judge" from the side of the left, that is, the change from judgment to compassion and from compassion to judgment. And therefore he raised the difficulty, how there could be the change. And by this two things are difficult: one, that He has descriptions; the second, that He is subject to changes. And if you say that this is in the aspect of the created entities—

behold, it is difficult that, before the creation of the created entities, He was not called "compassionate" and "judge"—and it is a very strained reading to say that titles came to be in Him with the coming-to-be of human beings. And therefore he answered that the titles and the attributes and the changes are forever from the side of human beings, who are acted upon by Him by means of the attributes; and also before the creation of the created entities He was called by these titles, after the names of the attributes concealed within Him—like the concealment of the flame in the coal, and like the concealment of the fire in the flint—as we shall explain in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. And He was called "compassionate" and "judge" after [the fact] that, in the emanating and spreading-forth of the attributes by means of them, He performs the compassion and the judgment. And this is [the meaning of] "Rather, before He created the world," etc., "for were there no creatures," etc. He compelled [the point] that the descriptions are not from His side but from the side of the created entities—[both] the matter of the descriptions themselves, and likewise the changes; for the titles are "judge" and "compassionate" and the like, and likewise the changes from judgment to compassion and from compassion to judgment; and behold, this matter is necessarily from the side of the created entities, not from His side—meaning, from the side of His aspect before the spreading-forth of the Emanation; for otherwise, how would "compassionate" and "judge" be apt of Him—toward whom would He be compassionate, and whom would He judge? Rather, what have you to say? That it is applicable only from the side of the spreading-forth of the Emanation and the creation of the created entities. And this is what he said, "for were there no creatures in the world, why would He be called," etc. "And therefore all the names," etc.—meaning, granted, we have compelled [the point] with respect to the titles "compassionate" and "gracious," which are actions going forth to another, acted from Him toward another; but with respect to "wise" and "understanding" and the rest of the names and titles, which stand alone in themselves and do not go forth to another, we have no compelling [argument], and we might forever say that they are in Himself, and that He is, after all, a possessor of descriptions and changes. And to this he answered "and therefore"—meaning, since we are compelled to say of some of them that, by means of His uniting with the attributes to act upon human beings, they are those descriptions, even we shall say so of all the rest of the titles and names, for some of them disclose [the nature of] the others. And this is what he said, "and therefore all the names," etc.: though they stand alone, they are titles to Him after the [His] actions. And it is possible that the intent in saying "after His deeds" is His sefirot, which are His works, and that by means of His sefirot are His titles. And the matter is that, before the spreading-forth of the attributes, He was wise in His Self, and His wisdom was in the apprehension of His Self, for He and His wisdom are all one Self; but His wisdom spread forth into the vessel of Chokhmah, to make another wise, and likewise in Binah; and forever, that which spreads forth in Chokhmah and Binah is His Self, which is the source of Chokhmah and Binah. "In like manner He created the soul"—behold, the parable of the soul that we set forth in chapter 4, and it is a fitting parable, that the soul has no corporeal actions—to say, from this aspect it sees and from this aspect it hears—and yet, in conjunction with the body, it acts in the action of the body according to the preparedness of its limbs: there is a limb in which it sees, and a limb in which it hears. And so is the matter with the Ein Sof, who is a soul to the souls: in His conjunction with the attributes, the attributes perform those changes by His power, just as the body acts by the power of the soul. And this is what he said, "He created the soul in His image, which is called after its actions," as explained: that the names of the corporeal actions are ascribed to the soul, because, by means of its conjunction with the body, the actions are performed, as explained. "That limb in which it performs a commandment," etc.—this whole matter is to ascribe the judgment and the compassion to the soul, as in the matter of the Ein Sof. And this is because the human being includes, in his creation, all the existents, all of them, from the first point to the end of Creation and Formation and Action, as it is written (Isaiah 43:7), "I created it, I formed it, indeed I made it"; and corresponding to the Ein Sof, who spreads forth and illumines and gives life from the beginning of all to the end, so is the soul in the body. And therefore, by means of the body it has actions, and outside the body it has no actions, as in the matter of the Ein Sof, as explained. And therefore there is no parable more fitting than the parable of the soul. And this is what he said, "So too the Master of the world," etc., "titles and not titles"—meaning, they are titles from the side of [His] conjunction with the attributes, and they are not titles from His own side, for in Him there is no attribute, and no description, and no action. "And by these names," etc.—meaning, they are ten sefirot, ten names; for the names are the sefirot, and the sefirot are the names. "He spreads forth"—that is, the spreading-forth of His Self within the names and the sefirot. "And reigns in them"—for they have no action except from His side, for He reigns in them according to His will, and by means of Him is their action. "And is called by them"—for by this He is called by them; but not that the names are apt of Him from His own side, but rather from the side that He reigns in them, as explained. "And is covered in them"—for the Emanation is by reason of the revelation of the Emanator; and likewise "and is called by them," for He has no name and place by which to call Him or to utter Him, except by means of His actions, and this is the cause of His revelation; and likewise they are the cause of His concealment and His covering, so that His Godhead should be revealed only to the fitting; and these are screens dividing between Him and the lower ones. And this is [the point] that the revelation is the cause of the concealment, and the concealment is the cause of the revelation. "And dwells in them," etc.—that is, that the sefirot and the names, the emanated ones, are a garment to the Emanator, as is known. "And therefore one may not mark it," etc., "how much more so the Master of the world," etc.—to say that He is revealed in Keter and in Chokhmah and the like, for if so, He would diminish His dominion and His actions. And this is what he said, "for were one to do so, behold it would be lacking from the rest of the grades; how much more so the Master of the world," etc. And it is difficult, for in several places in the Zohar it is implied that, when His providence withdraws from the attributes, the world perishes and is consumed in an instant; and according to his words, behold, at the time of His withdrawal He is "lacking His dominion." And one cannot say that "to be lacking His dominion" and "to withdraw His providence" forever is what we said is not fitting, but that for a time it is possible that He withdraws His providence—because, if so, after all, at that time a deficiency would be necessitated, God forbid. For when He withdraws His providence from Malkhut, by reason that it performs judgment, then He would not be called "King," and the Godhead would be found lacking the title of kingship; and this is not fitting, for He has no change, neither addition nor diminution, in His titles and His attributes—from the reason and the great principle that they are ten and not nine, ten and not eleven.
