And from this reason it is forbidden for us to add to the sefirot or to diminish from them, because they are the limbs of a supernal form; and with the addition of the limbs one is found adding to their soul, and likewise when one diminishes one of them, God forbid. Rather, surely this is no answer. And the principal answer is as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 3: that the kinds of effluence are three. And the first is the perpetual [effluence], which neither lacks nor exceeds, and it is the Self that spreads forth, which gives life to the attribute; for even though that attribute should clothe itself in harsh judgment, its perpetual effluence is never lacking—for otherwise, even in judgment it would not be acting, but would be like a vessel in which no one delights, and it would be as though it were not, God forbid; rather, by reason of its soul that overflows in it perpetually, it performs everything. But the intensification that intensifies upon this matter, in order to raise the attribute, and enlarge it, and equalize it to the supernal one, and the like—this is what sometimes withdraws, God forbid; and this is what is explained in the said Gate, in the matter of the three kinds of effluence. Which is not so in the attributes, for there is an attribute whose light spreads forth up to such-and-such a place, and there is [one] up to such-and-such a place—as he concludes, that there is a fourfold Chariot and there is a threefold Chariot. But in the Ein Sof it is not so; rather, "in all is He," and as he explains, "He is called by all the names," because they all draw from Him and have no existence apart from Him; and yet the names do not belong to Him. And this is what he said, "and He has no known name." Or he means that He has no special name, but rather He spreads forth in them all, as he concludes. "That there is a person who inherits," etc.—the intent is to the soul, which is not comparable to the Ein Sof, God forbid; for above there is a soul that inherits three hundred and ten (yesh) worlds, which is Chokhmah—that is, the soul that merited to ascend to that grade; and there is a soul that merits only [the level] corresponding to the Righteous One, Foundation of the world, and has only one world, that is, in the secret of the inclusion of the attributes. For in relation to each and every part of the inclusion of Yesod, the soul has three hundred and ten (yesh) inclusions and aspects.

And behold, the soul has a reckoning of three hundred and ten (yesh) worlds in which it spreads forth; but the Ein Sof is called "Adonai," meaning Lord over all the existence of worlds, up to the Ein Sof. And this is the import of the name Adnut [lordship]. And the four-letter name indicates that He was [hayah] before every being [havayah], meaning that He is the essence of the beings [havayot] and the cause prior to them, like the priority of the cause to the effect. "And He is within every being"—He is the cause of every being, and its subsistence, and its life, and without Him it has no existence; and He is the soul of the beings and their subsistence. "And He is after every being"—that is, that He is their end, at the time when He will gather His spirit and His soul to Himself. It is found that He is the soul of all the beings, and He is their subsistence, and He is the end of all the beings. And this is the secret of "the havayot testifying of Him: was," etc.—meaning, the name of four letters includes "was, is, and will be" (hayah, hoveh, ve-yihyeh), for these three words are formed from the letters of the Name; and this is the secret of the composite twelve-letter [name], which we shall explain in the Gate of Particulars of Names, in chapter 9. "El testifies," etc.—that is, that the word "El" is a term of power and strength, as in "and the mighty of the land he took" (Ezekiel 17:13), and "Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains" (Psalms 36:7), and many others like them. "Elohim testifies," etc. And because He is God over all the emanated ones, He is called "Elohim," which is close to a plural form; and this is what he was precise about in his language, saying "that He is Elohim and the God of gods." "Tzeva'ot testifies," etc.—meaning, that He is called "Tzeva'ot" because He is a prince over all hosts (tzeva'ot), to do with them according to His will, as it is written (Daniel 4:32), "and according to His will," etc. "Shaddai," etc.—indicates that He said to the world "Enough!" (dai), that is, to the lower world, the foundation of the earth, and so too to the rest of the elements. And he is lengthy in all this to teach that all the names are only from the side of the actions that flow from Him for the need of the created entities. But from the side of the aspect of His Self, there is no need for names at all; and there is not in Him any name among the holy names, how much more so titles, which literally indicate actions, as he sets forth and proceeds. Thus far has our understanding reached in this delightful inquiry, according as it was poured forth upon us from Heaven. And of the One exalted above all blessing and praise we ask forgiveness and atonement for opening the doors of our lips, for all is for His honor and for the honor of His name. And this Gate is herewith concluded. And after the Lord has helped us up to here, we journey onward to the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, with the help of Heaven.
The Fifth Gate: The Order of the Emanation

The intent in this Gate is to explain in what manner these sefirot were emanated, and the matter of their emanation according to their divisions. And the order of their standing will be explained in a separate Gate, with the help of Heaven.
Chapter One:

After we have pursued the matter of the order of the emanation of the sefirot—as a reader pursues [a path] in the mountains—we found that Rav Sherira Gaon wrote the order of their emanation, and Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov copied his language in the Sefer ha-Emunot, Gate 4, chapter 11. And these are his words: The first emanation, Keter, etc. The second emanation, Avir [air], which is Chokhmah, etc. The third emanation, Mada [knowledge]—and the mnemonic is "discerning, and he shall know them" (Hosea 14:10)—which is Tevunah [understanding], etc. The fourth emanation is the right arm—and the mnemonic is "long-suffering and abundant in lovingkindness" (Psalms 145:8)—and it is Chesed. The fifth emanation, the left arm—and the mnemonic is "Yours is an arm with might" (ibid. 89:14). The sixth emanation, the central pillar—and the mnemonic is "behold, You delight in truth in the inward parts," etc. (ibid. 51:8). The seventh emanation, the everlasting covenant—and the mnemonic is "righteousness calls it to its foot" (Isaiah 41:2), meaning that Malkhut is called "righteousness" [tzedek], receiving from the Righteous One [tzaddik], Foundation of the world. The eighth emanation, the right thigh—and the mnemonic is "pleasures in Your right hand forever (netzach)" (Psalms 16:11). The ninth emanation, the left thigh—and the mnemonic is "His footstool" (Lamentations 2:1). The tenth emanation, the daughter-voice [bat kol]—and the mnemonic is "all glorious is the king's daughter within" (Psalms 45:14). This is the sum of the secret of the ten crowns that the heads of the academies received, etc. End of his words.

And he was very lengthy, and we have abbreviated, by reason of [the maxim] "a person should always teach his students by a short way." But what appears from the explanation of his words is that they were emanated one after another, in order; and this he was precise about in saying "the first emanation, the second, and the third." And so it is proven from several places where we have seen Rashbi—may peace be upon him—counting the order of the sefirot as KaChaB, ChaGaT, NeHiYaM. And so it is proven from the verse (Job 28[:12]), "but Chokhmah—from where is it found?"—he disclosed in [this] explanation that Chokhmah is emanated and found from "Nothing," which is Keter. And afterward it says, "and where is the place of Binah?"—meaning, Alef-Yod (A Y), that is, Chokhmah, which is Yod, in partnership with Keter, which is Alef, is the place and the existence of Binah—indicating the order of these three. And likewise King David, peace be upon him, said (I Chronicles 29[:11]), "Yours, O YHVH, is the greatness, and the might, and the glory, and the victory (netzach), and the majesty (hod), for all (kol)"—which is Yesod, that "grasps in heaven and on earth," and so the Targum renders—and afterward it says "Yours, O YHVH, is the kingship," that is, Malkhut.

Behold, he has proven the order of the emanation. And so it is necessitated that the order of their emanation is one after another, and no more. For it is impossible to say that two were emanated [at once], since each one is a cause to its fellow; if so, it is necessitated that the cause precede the effect. And therefore they were emanated one after another; for were it not so, one sefirah would be found a cause to two—and this is impossible, for then they would be equal, meaning that, since both are effects of one cause, the two effects are equal; and since they are equal, then by what would they be distinguished? For that which is not a body is not divided into parts. If so, of necessity they are effects one from another, and there are not two effects [emanated] together equally. And surely the words of the Gaon are correct, and they accord with the words of Rashbi in the flow of his language in the Zohar, in his numberings in the order of one after another; and never does a Tanna omit to put Chokhmah before Keter, nor Binah before Chokhmah, and so the rest—indicating their union one with another. And both the Gaon and the Tanna agree and are correct with the verses we explained above, indicating the truth of the matter. And in addition to this, the reasonings and the true premises are agreed upon even according to the words of the investigators. And if so, we have proven clearly that the order of the sefirot is thus: the first emanation, Keter; and from Keter was emanated, etc.; and Malkhut is the end of the emanation. And what is to be examined closely in the language of the Gaon is what he wrote, "the seventh emanation, the everlasting covenant," etc., the intent being upon Yesod. And it is known that Yesod is ninth, below Netzach and Hod, according to what is agreed in most of the verses explicitly, and especially in what we wrote, that he said "and the victory and the majesty, for all (kol)"—first Netzach and Hod, and afterward Yesod, that is, "for all (kol)," as explained. And likewise most of the sayings of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—in the Tikkunim and in the Zohar, as we have already copied in the preceding Gates some sayings indicating this matter. But while we were gathering lilies and roses in the field of the divine Chokhmah and Kabbalah from Rashbi—may peace be upon him—the Lord brought before us a saying in which he took this way, and by it all will be rectified, with the help of Heaven; and we shall set it as a separate chapter, to give space between one chapter and another.

And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 102b): "Open for me" (Song of Songs 5:2) on the first day, which is the right, of which it is said "You open Your hand," etc. (Psalms 145:16)—"Your hands" (yadeikha) [is read] "Your Yods" (yodeikha), this is the Yod, which is to the right. "My sister" on the second day, where the Heh is. "My dove" on the third day, where the Vav is. "For my head is filled with dew" (SoS 5:2) on the fourth day, which is the combination of Yod-Heh-Vav, which is the reckoning of [the word] tal [dew, = 39]; and this is body and covenant, which are reckoned as one in [their] reckoning, which is Vav, ascending to one (echad). The upper Vav is the central pillar; the lower Vav is the Righteous One. The Alef shows concerning the two of them that they are one. "My locks"—these are the six extremities, which are the Heh, six segments included within the two thighs, which are the fifth day and the sixth day, of which it is said "his thighs are pillars of marble (shesh)" (SoS 5:15). "The drops of the night"—this is the lower Shekhinah, the combination of Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh. And why is she called "night"? Because she is the night of the Sabbath; a night of watching she surely is, unto YHVH. End [of quotation].

And behold, in this saying he indicated explicitly that Yesod is adjacent to Tiferet, above Netzach and Hod; and this is surely a very strained reading, and the opposite of his great [view] in most of the sayings. And we shall explain his language, and from within it all will be rectified, blessed be He. "Open for me," etc.—above this saying he explained that Tiferet is the husband of the Shekhinah, who is the beloved knocking at the door of the one he longs for; and he said that he comes including six extremities, which are the six days of Creation. And now he explains the matter of his being included within them, and his explanation is in the verse. And he said that the intent of "open for me" is in Chesed, which is the right, and it is the first day, as is well known. And because, at first glance, the opening has no relation to Chesed—but rather, on the contrary, there is the place of the closing-up and the sealing, in the manner of the kametz, which is in Chesed (and it is a full verse, "and the priest shall take a handful" [ve-kamatz])—therefore he necessitated the matter by the verse "You open Your hand"; and the word "Your hands" means "Your Yods," that is, the Yod indicates that the existence of the opening is in the place of the Yod, that is, in Chesed, in the secret of Chokhmah, which sets its dwelling upon it, as the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra, fol. 25): "one who wishes to become wise should turn southward."

And the matter of "and the priest shall take a handful" will be explained in the Gate of Vowel-Points. "My sister on the second day"—meaning Gevurah, which is the second day, as is well known. And because it was difficult for him that the word "my sister" does not indicate the existence of Gevurah at all, therefore he explained and said "where the Heh is," meaning that in Gevurah is the dwelling of Binah, which is the first Heh of the name. And because the existence of Tiferet is by means of Binah—in the manner explained, "He established the heavens by understanding" (Proverbs 3:19)—and from there Malkhut is called "Heh," as will be explained, blessed be He, therefore he said that, since the dwelling of Binah, which is Heh, is in Gevurah, and from there Malkhut is Heh, and from there "He established the heavens by Binah," if so, it is found that from the side of Gevurah, in the secret of Binah, Tiferet and Malkhut are siblings; and therefore from the side of Gevurah he called her "his sister."

And behold, now the word "my sister" is related in the secret of Gevurah. "My dove on the third day, where the Vav is"—meaning, she is called "dove" from the side of Tiferet itself, which is the third day, as is known. And to understand the relation of "my dove" to Tiferet, we need [to refer] to what he explained in another place (Tikkun 6, fol. 23): and these are his words: "The supernal Imma nests in the Throne, in the three upper sefirot. The central pillar includes six sefirot, [which] nest in Metatron. The lower Imma nests in the Ophan, of which it is said (Ezekiel 1:15), 'and behold, one Ophan upon the earth.'"

"And further, the Shekhinah, from the side of the Throne, is called nesher [eagle]; and from the side of na'ar [the youth], yonah [dove]; and from the side of the Ophan, tzippor [bird]." End [of quotation], as relevant to our matter. And we shall not trouble ourselves with the explanation of this saying, for it will be explained at length in the Gate of ABYA. And what comes out for us from his words, toward his intent, is that the Shekhinah is called "dove" from the side of na'ar, since Tiferet, including six extremities, dwells there. And for this reason he said, in the case before us, "my dove," from the side of the third day, which is Tiferet; and he said "where the Vav is," the intent being to explain that it includes six extremities, for it is what is signified by the Vav. And it is possible to say that the reason he said, in [the case of] Gedulah, "where the Yod is," and in Gevurah "where the Heh is," and in Tiferet "where the Vav is," is a preparation toward his intent below, upon the verse that said (SoS 5:2), "for my head is filled with dew (tal)," which is the fourth day, that is, Yesod—for the matter of tal is the combination of Yod-Heh-Vav—to indicate that he was compelled to count Yesod adjacent to ChaGaT, which are [the gematria] tal; and this is because Yesod is filled with the effluence of tal, which is  Y H V  [=] ChaGaT. "Filled with dew on the fourth day," the intent being upon Yesod, as we explained. "The combination of Yod-Heh-Vav," the intent being that there the effluence of the three Patriarchs—which are the three letters  Y H V—is made to overflow; and it is also called kol [all] because it includes all. And therefore he said "which is the combination," meaning the combination of the three letters, which are the three Patriarchs. "And this is body and covenant, which are reckoned," etc. It was difficult for him [what] was difficult for us in the words of Rav Sherira, of blessed memory: that he should have said first Netzach and Hod, and afterward Yesod; and why did he change the order? To this he answered that, since body and covenant—which are Tiferet and Yesod—are reckoned as one, it is fitting to mention it [Yesod] right after Tiferet. And the intent is that, when Tiferet was emanated, Yesod was concealed within it, and Yesod was somewhat revealed in a delightful manifestation; and for this reason the term "seventh emanation" applies to it. And [the term] that it is ninth or tenth applies to it because there the emanation arrived, and it was the end of all, and it was revealed after Netzach and Hod with an intrinsic revelation that reveals it in itself, and not in the subtle manifestation such as it is in Tiferet. And this is as he sets forth and proceeds: "one in reckoning," etc., "ascending to one." The intent is that Tiferet is Vav, and Yesod is the extension of the Vav; if so, the two of them together are Vav, and they ascend to one, for they are one body. And afterward he explained yet another proof, that they are two Vavs, an upper and a lower: the Vav in its full spelling [Vav-Alef-Vav] is two Vavs with an Alef in the middle. The intent is to unite them, that they are one and all one matter. And we said "to unite them"—the intent is that two attributes do not unite unless there comes to be between them a distinct existence that unites them, meaning an intermediate aspect between the two of them, by means of which aspect they unite; and this intermediate aspect is of them intrinsically: not of the upper one, since it is revealed from it, and not of the lower one, since it is concealed from it; rather it is the aspect that mediates between the two of them, and this aspect is called Alef, because in it is the power of union, to unite these two attributes. And of this aspect we have a proof from the Sefer ha-Zohar, portion Acharei (fol. 74b), in the matter of  A V Y,  V Y,  H V Y, where it says there, in the matter that the Vav was removed and the head of [the word] tzaddik—let it be examined in its place, and it will be explained for us in the Sefer Or Yakar. And let us return to the matter of the saying: that, by reason of the two reasons he stated, it is not fitting to separate Yesod from Tiferet; therefore it is fitting that Tiferet should be the third day, and Yesod after it, the fourth day. "My locks," etc.—meaning, that there are extremities that are in Netzach and Hod. And he explained them in another place in the Zohar (Vayechi, fol. 241), and said there "Netzach of netzachim, Hod of hodot." And the intent is upon three aspects, in each one of which the middle is the true Netzach, and the two outermost are called netzachim—they are the two aspects of the extremities: the aspect that Netzach has from the side of Chesed, which is in relation to what it receives from it; and the third aspect, which is in relation to what it overflows. And these two aspects are not in Netzach itself, but are aspects subordinate to it; and Netzach itself is the middle aspect, and the outermost ones are Netzach by accident, not intrinsically, like the middle one. And likewise, in this manner, in Hod. And we have already explained the matter of these three aspects in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 7—let it be examined there. "Of which it is said, his thighs are pillars of marble (shesh)." It was difficult for him: just as there is Netzach of netzachim, Hod of hodot, there is also Chesed of chesadim, Gevurah of gevurot, as he explained in the Zohar, portion Vayetzei (fol. 155a), in the matter of the twelve tribes of Israel and "all their backs were inward"; and if so, accordingly, it would be found that there are already six extremities in Gedulah and Gevurah. To this he said that the extremities that are in Netzach and Hod are more well-attested in the verse, in his saying "his thighs are pillars of marble (shesh)" [shesh = six]. "The drops of the night, this is the Shekhinah," etc.—for she includes all that is above, as is known. "And why is she called night?"—the intent is not to ask why she is called "night," for it is clear that she is the attribute of night, and "night" is forever a title for Din, as explained in the Glossary of Titles. Rather, the intent of the question is, since the import of the verse is that now "the voice of her beloved knocks" at the door of her house to embrace the one he longs for, as it appears that he has not yet coupled with her—and we hold, according to the Zohar, that she is called "night" only after her receiving from the male and her union with him. And these are his words in the Zohar, portion Bo (fol. 38b): "We have learned, it is written, 'if there shall be a maiden, a virgin' (Deuteronomy 22:23)—[but] na'ar [youth, masc.] is written. What is the reason? Because as long as she has not received the male she is called na'ar; once she has received the male she is called na'arah. So too, [she is called] leil [night] before she has received the male; and even though 'watching' (shimurim) is written of it, the male was destined to join with her. And at the time when the male joined with her, it is written (Exodus 12:42), 'this is the night (laylah) of watching unto YHVH'—'watching,' male and female; and therefore it is written 'this is the night.' And after male and female are found [together], there is none to praise but the male." End [of quotation].

And at first glance this matter appears [to be] the opposite of reason; for it would have been fitting that, while she has not [yet] received the male, she should be called "leil," indicating the feminine, and when she has received the male she should be called "laylah," indicating the masculine; and likewise na'ar [and] na'arah. But the matter will be understood by what the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin, fol. 22): "a woman makes a covenant only with the one who made her a vessel." And the matter of making the female into a vessel is by means of the male; and the letter that indicates the matter of making the vessel is the Heh; and therefore, when she has received the male, she is called "laylah," with a Heh, a hint at her being made a vessel, as a female to receive by means of her husband. And then, with the male having joined with her, her husband having made her a vessel, she is called "laylah." And the matter is that the Heh that is in Malkhut is a hint at three Vavs, which are chesed, din, and rachamim. And there is a great distinction between the upper Heh and the lower Heh: for the three Vavs that are in the lower Heh are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and the three Vavs that are in the upper Heh are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. And the union of Tiferet with Malkhut is by means of the holy member, which is Yesod, and the two testicles of the male, which are Netzach and Hod.

And behold, while she has not [yet] received the male—who is the one who sends to her the gift, to adorn herself with these three Vavs, so that there may be in her a dwelling upon her at the time of coupling—she is called "leil," or "na'ar," or "tzedek," and the like, indicating that she has not yet received upon herself the light of the male, and that she lacks the adornment, which is the Heh, which is three Vavs. But when she has received upon herself the member of the male, then these three lights illumine in her—which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod—and there are figured in her beautiful adornments, which are the form of the Heh, which is three Vavs, like this: ה. And the intent is not that, when she has received the male upon her, the union of coupling itself is effected; rather, the preparation and readying toward the coupling is the matter of "receiving the male upon her" mentioned here—that is, the betrothal and engagement, in that she has received upon herself the name of the husband. And this is her receiving, before the coupling, from the right and from the left, in the secret of "his left hand is under my head" (SoS 2:6), as we shall explain at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance and in the Gate of Particulars of Names. And then, with the figuring of the form of the Heh—that is, the three Vavs—she is surely made a vessel, that is, a receptacle to receive the three sefirot themselves, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, which dwell in her at the time of coupling literally, in the existence of the Heh, which is the existence of the three Vavs that are in it, as explained. And now, accordingly, it was difficult for him: he should have said "my locks, the drops of leil," as we said, that he has not yet coupled with her. To this he rectified and said "she is the night of the Sabbath, a night of watching"—the intent being that it is the night of the Sabbath, which is the time of her conjugal due, and a night of watching, the intent being that she is kept for her husband, for YHVH; and if so, since she is at "the door of hope," it is fitting that she be called "laylah," since her time has already arrived and she is adorned—for the word "laylah" is not a hint at union itself and intrinsic union. Rather, "laylah" means "leil Heh," that is, the leil that is Malkhut in the secret of the intensity of Din has already become "laylah," the meaning being that the male has illumined her and adorned her in the secret of the Heh, which is chesed, din, rachamim, white, red, green—the secret of the three Vavs mentioned above. And in truth, this is not union but adornment; for upon these three colors he explained, in the matter of the rainbow, in portion Noach (9:16), "and I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant"—"and I will see it" [the rainbow], like a bride adorning herself for her husband with colors, and then "to remember the covenant," which is the union. Behold, [it is stated] explicitly that the existence of the light of the Heh, which is three colors, and these three Vavs, are only adornment. And even though he said "once she has received the male upon her she is called na'arah," this is because these colors are not hers except from the side of the male, as explained, and not because there is then literally complete union; for if so, it would be fitting that she be called by the name of the male, or by a word that intrinsically indicates the male, not "laylah" and "na'arah," for in truth the Heh is principally in the female. Rather, surely, as explained, the principal union is not in this matter, and its principal [mode] is one, which is called "laylah," which is the adornment; and her being called "laylah" is the hint at her adornments, while she sits and awaits her bridegroom—when will he come to the chamber to unite. And this is what he said: "a night of watching," it is "surely unto YHVH"—meaning, that her being called "laylah" means "leil," the one who waits for her husband, who is not lacking the adornment but [only] awaits her husband.

And the matter of the verse "a night of watching, it is unto YHVH"—"this is the night, unto YHVH." The meaning of "a night of watching," etc., is the matter of her sitting and awaiting—for this is the import of "watching"—"this is the night," etc. And it is found that "laylah," with a Heh, and "a night of watching, it is unto YHVH," are all one matter. And this is what the verse explained: "a night of watching, it is unto YHVH"; "this is the night," etc. And his saying "the drops of the night"—the intent is that all these limbs, which are the days, are filled with effluence and abundant good, which is the drop of seed fitting for the night; and afterward, "open for me," etc. End [of quotation].

And behold, our intent in this saying is completed, and it has been explained in it that it is already fitting that Yesod be after Tiferet, prior to Netzach and Hod—and this by accident, not by nature, for its customary [place] is ninth. And the reason for the change of practice in this saying, Rashbi—peace be upon him—explained in his language, in saying "body and covenant are reckoned as one"; and since the intent of the verse is the matter of union and coupling, therefore he united Tiferet and Yesod, which are body and covenant, that unite together toward the coupling. And we may already examine somewhat from this in the words of the Gaon, in his saying "the seventh emanation, the everlasting covenant, and the mnemonic is 'righteousness calls it to its foot.'" And was it hidden from the Gaon that Yesod is called "yesod," and it is a full verse, "and the Righteous One is the foundation of the world"? Rather, the intent is to explain the union of Malkhut with Yesod—she being the one called "tzedek" [righteousness], grasped at the foot of Yesod, in that she joins to Tiferet; and therefore he gave it precedence, to indicate its manifestation prior to the netzachim. And to its manifestation after the netzachim he directed in his saying "the sixth emanation, the central pillar, and the mnemonic is 'behold, You delight in truth in the inward parts.'" And was the verse "You give truth to Jacob" hidden from the Gaon, for it is the most well-attested? Rather, [it was] to explain to us how it [Tiferet] is united with the inward parts [tuchot], which are Netzach and Hod: and the intent of the verse is "behold, truth"—which is Tiferet—"You delight in," pours forth delight and satiety, "in the inward parts (batuchot)," which are Netzach and Hod. And great is the power of the Gaon, who intended to explain to us two matters in one utterance. And behold, the matter of the precedence has been explained, and we shall speak further in the coming chapters. And the sum of the matters is that the emanation is emanated one after another: for Keter emanated Chokhmah, and Chokhmah emanated, etc., up to the emanation of Malkhut. And it is a correct view, agreed upon from the verses, and from reason, and from the words of the holy Tanna, Rashbi, and from the words of the Gaon.

The intent in this chapter is to explain another view, contradicting this. And it is the Kabbalah of my teacher and master, the pious one, our honored teacher Rabbi Yosef Karo—may God preserve and keep him. And these are his words: "Behold, I have come to make known to you the truth of the matter and the secret of secrets—these [things] to know: that when the desire of desires [ra'ava de-ra'avin], the Ancient of Ancients, the Ein Sof, arose to create worlds, there struck forth from Him one striking, and there shone one shining, which includes three. And as the Rabbis said, 'and one point, it includes three'—length, and breadth, and depth. And so that shining was one, and included within it were three—these are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. Afterward, each one of these three struck forth from itself one shining that includes two. Chokhmah struck forth from itself one shining that includes two, which is Chesed and Netzach; and with Chokhmah itself it was three. And Binah, too, struck forth from itself one shining that includes two, which is Gevurah [and] Hod; and with Binah itself it was three. And Keter struck forth from itself one shining that includes three, which are Tiferet, Yesod, Malkhut—because, since it is closer to the Ein Sof and resembles it (for it too is very concealed, after the manner of the Ein Sof), therefore in the shining that it brought forth there were included three, after the manner of the Ein Sof. And now, since Keter, Chokhmah, Binah were one shining, and Malkhut goes forth from Keter and Abraham from Chokhmah, it was as though both went forth from one place. And for this reason Abraham said of her (Genesis 20:12), 'and indeed she is truly my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother'; and behold, these ten sefirot were completed for them." End of his words—[in keeping with] the description of his righteousness and his piety. And the sum of his words is that Chokhmah emanated Chesed-Netzach [ChaN], Binah emanated Gevurah-Hod [GaH], and Keter [emanated] Tiferet-Yesod-Malkhut [T Y M].

And behold, this matter is necessitated from reason. For since Chesed is by its nature lovingkindness, how is it possible that Gevurah should be emanated from it, Gevurah being Din and a strong fire? And likewise, how is it possible that, Gevurah being Din and a strong fire, it should be a cause to Tiferet, which is compassion? This is impossible—to say that the action of the effect is the opposite of the action of the cause. Rather, of necessity we say that Chokhmah, whose foundation is Chesed, is a cause to ChaN [Chesed-Netzach], whose actions are lovingkindness in their root, which is Chesed. And likewise GaH [Gevurah-Hod], which are Din, their foundation is Binah, from which the [powers of] Din are aroused, as we shall explain at length in the matters of these inquiries in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And therefore it is expounded in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer: "by ten utterances the world was created, and they are included within three—within Chokhmah, and within Tevunah, and within Da'at." He indicated that, although they are ten, they are included within three—which are Chokhmah, root of the line of Chesed; Tevunah, root of the line of Din; and Da'at, root of the line of Rachamim. And the reason he said "Da'at" and not "Keter," we shall explain at length in the said Gate. All this indicates the strength of my teacher's view, that it is correct and true. But it is somewhat difficult, for in the Zohar it is expounded: "the waters departed [from] darkness"; and a proof (Genesis 25:19), "Abraham begot Isaac"—meaning that Gevurah is an effect of Chesed; and this is a very strained reading, and at first glance the opposite of reason. And likewise they also expounded in the Sefer ha-Bahir, "the waters conceived and gave birth to gloom," indicating that the cause and the source of Gevurah, which is the gloom, was Chesed, which is the waters. And how difficult this matter is to settle, for it is the opposite of reason, as we explained—for how is it possible that Din should be an effect of Chesed?

And further, Rashbi—peace be upon him—explained the opposite of this, in saying that the [powers of] Din are aroused from the side of Binah, as we shall explain in the said Gate—indicating that the cause of Gevurah is Binah, and from there [come the] judgments, and it is its cause. And besides these two views that we have set forth concerning the emanation, there is yet a third view, which is the view of Rashbi—peace be upon him—and it is explained in many places: that Keter emanated Chokhmah, and Chokhmah emanated Binah, and Binah emanated the whole structure together. And this was explained from the saying that we copied in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter 7. And so it is agreed in several places, that the plantings of the Emanation were in Binah, and from there they were planted below, to the place of their emanation. And in this way he proceeded also several times, in several places. And at first glance it appears that this view is the one agreed upon in most of the words of Rashbi—peace be upon him. And to necessitate this view there is no need, for it is very well-attested. And now, to whom shall we flee for help, and who will arbitrate for us between the three views, all three of which are the words of Rashbi—peace be upon him? And upon which of them all shall we lean, to say, "this is the straight way, let us walk in it"? And when these views have pressed upon us, we say: we have no way to exempt ourselves from rectifying these views according to their measure, until there remains for us no doubt, neither small nor great. And of God we ask the help.

Before the emanation of the emanated ones, the simple Ein Sof was in the utmost simplicity, concealed in the utmost concealment. And His Godhead was not revealed to another, by reason of the absence of the beings, by means of which there is some revelation of the loftiness of His unity. And the sefirot were in their potential, concealed in Him, in His potential, in a subtle and concealed manifestation, as befits His unity. And let not the heart of a person wonder at our saying that they were concealed in Him, and let him not hasten to reply, "if so, it is found that the sefirot already existed in Him—there is necessitated from this multiplicity and change." For this is not among the questions of the wise, but rather an enticement of the intellect. And the reason is that, even though we say that the sefirot were concealed in Him, our intent in this matter is not to say that the sefirot were literally as they are now; rather, they were unified in His unity, in true and strong union. And we shall set forth a fine parable: to the flint stone, from which fire is brought forth by the striking of iron, and from the fire there goes forth lightning. And now, in truth, it is not correct [to say] that that fire was literally within the stone, and that the stone was divided into a multiplicity of parts according to the parts of the sparks scattered from it—this, surely, the intellect of the discerning will not judge. Rather, on the contrary, that fire was concealed within the stone and unified in it in true and strong union, in such a way that there is no division or separation at all between the stone and the fire within it. So is the matter with the Self of the simple Godhead: before the spreading-forth to govern the lower ones, the sefirot were unified in His Self and bound to Him in a mighty and strong bond, until [the term] "existence of the sefirot" would scarcely apply to it at all—but rather the true union. And this union, and the subtlety mentioned, is the source of the sefirot concealed within Him, which are called the supernal Tzachtzachot, from which yet other tzachtzachot were emanated, to which the term "tzachtzachot" does not yet even apply, as will be explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot, with the help of Heaven. And when it arose in His simple Will to reveal His Godhead and to do good with His concealed attributes to another, He brought forth the privation into being, and emanated from His simple light a first sefirah, which is called Keter. And this sefirah, by reason of the abundance of its subtlety, is not revealed at all, even after its emanation—how much more so that the beings should be by means of it. For, by reason of the abundance of its adherence to its source, [the term] "Something" (yesh) does not even apply to it, but only "Nothing" (ayin). And even the name "Nothing" does not apply to its simplicity, except in its conjunction with Chokhmah and Binah. And the reason is that "Nothing" applies only to a thing whose existence is in some measure apprehended as necessitated, and one asks concerning this apprehension, "what is it?", and they reply, "nothing"—to indicate that it is a thing not [fully] apprehended, but the intellect has already apprehended it and necessitated it, to the point that one asks concerning it "what is its matter?", and the reply is "nothing." But Keter, by reason of the smallness of the apprehension in it—for the lower ones have no apprehension of it at all—the word "Nothing" is not necessitated of it in its aspect toward the Emanator, but only in its aspect toward the ones emanated from it, which is its partnership with Chokhmah and Binah; [in that aspect] it is called "Nothing." And so "Nothing" (ayin) hints: Alef = Keter, Yod = Chokhmah, Nun = Binah, as is explained in the words of Rashbi—peace be upon him—in many places, and as is explained in the Glossary of Titles, blessed be He. [Its subtlety reaches so far] that it is even called, in some places, "Ein Sof," by way of accident; and likewise it is called "the Cause of causes," by way of accident; and likewise several titles that indicate concealment. And Chokhmah, in relation to it, is called "Something" (yesh). And this is its saying "Something from Nothing," meaning Chokhmah from Keter. And even though Chokhmah was emanated, it is still the utmost of subtlety, and the beings cannot be revealed by means of it, for, by reason of the abundance of its subtlety, they call it by the name "Thought"—for, just as Thought is privation and not [an actualized] being, so Chokhmah is subtle, and the beings toward [actual] governance are [there] in privation—even though it is not like the subtlety of Keter, since it is called "Something." And although we said that it is called "Something," the intent in "Something" is not literally apprehended somethingness, complete somethingness, God forbid; rather, the intent in the word "Something" is in the distinction between "Nothing" and "Something"—not complete somethingness, but as the negation of "Nothing," and not affirming "Something" at all. And even the word "Something" does not apply to Chokhmah in respect of its aspect toward Keter, except in respect of its aspect toward Binah and its conjunction with it; for thus is "Something" (yesh) explained: Yod = Chokhmah, Shin = Binah, as is explained in the Glossary of Titles. And therefore, even though the two sefirot were emanated, by reason of the abundance of their nearness to their source, the being cannot come to be.

And the intent in this matter is not that the sefirot could not be emanated at all, for they were already being emanated, all of them in Keter, and all of them in Chokhmah. But the matter is a concealed secret, and it is not our way to exaggerate matters, God forbid, but [only] to reveal them. And the matter is that compassion is near the source, because it is not so subject to changes; and the more [a thing] draws near to the source, the more [it is] compassion. And [this is] not by reason of the subtlety, as many have thought—that the spreading-forth was the cause of the Din; for this, to us, is a rejected view, as will be explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. Rather, the reason is that "in the light of the King's face is life"; and the more the sefirot draw near to the Emanator, the more the Din is diminished from the sefirah that is the root of Din, and it is so refined that all becomes light and life, the Will of the Benefactor; and the decrees of Din do not act, and are nullified, and its powers do not go forth into actuality to act, by reason of the nearness of the emanated ones to the Emanator. And the powers of Din were rising in thought, and not [being] actualized. And this is the secret of "and these are the kings," etc., "and he died, and there reigned," etc. (Genesis 36). And the principal governance is from the side of the masters of Din, as the Sages, of blessed memory, explained: "He saw that the world could not endure; He associated with it the attribute of compassion." But, with all this, the principal governance is by Din, except that He associated with it the attribute of compassion, a mere association. And therefore, when the first two grades existed—which are Keter [and] Chokhmah—the powers of Din were not revealed at all. And from this we shall know the reason that the line of Din journeys last. For it would have been fitting that Binah be second—for, just as Gedulah is first and Gevurah second, and Tiferet, the arbiter, is third, so too [among] the supernal roots it would have been fitting that their emanation be thus: first the emanation of Chokhmah, root of Chesed; and second the emanation of Binah, root of Din; third Keter, root of compassion, the arbiter line. But, by reason of the abundance of their nearness to the source, it is impossible for Din to decree its decrees and to judge its judgments, for "in the light of the King's face is life"; and therefore the emanation had to be drawn out, and the root of Din was not emanated until the third grade, as we shall explain.

And this matter is explained in the Zohar, in the Idra de-Nazir (fol. 128a). These are its words: "It is taught: the Ancient of Ancients, the Concealed of the Concealed, before He had prepared the tikkunin of the King and the crownings [itturei] of the diadems [itrin], beginning and conclusion there was not. And He was engraving and measuring within Himself, and He spread before Himself one hanging [parsa], and on it He engraved [and measured] kings; but their tikkunin were not established. This is [the meaning of] 'and these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before there reigned a king over the children of Israel' (Genesis 36:31)—the first king, [corresponding] to the first of 'the children of Israel.' And all those engraved [ones] were called by names, and were not established, until He set them aside and stored them away. And after a time, He withdrew into that hanging and was arrayed in His tikkunin. And it is taught: when it arose in [His] desire to create the Torah and He brought it forth, immediately it said before Him, 'whoever wishes to be arrayed and to be made, let him first array His tikkunin'—the Concealed of the two thousand years." End [of quotation].

And the meaning of "the Ancient of Ancients" is the supernal Keter. And it is called "the Elder of elders." And the intent is that it is prior to the prior ones. For Keter is "elder" in relation to Chokhmah and Binah, which are "elders"; and this is "the Ancient of Ancients"—even in relation to the elders, which are Chokhmah and Binah, it is elder and concealed, to indicate its subtlety, for it is an elder concealed and exalted above the concealed supernal ones. "The Concealed of the Concealed"—meaning, concealed from the concealed ones. The intent is that, even from those sefirot that are in concealment, it is concealed. "Before He had prepared"—meaning, before the revelation of the tikkunim of the great King, which is Keter, which had already been emanated, except that it was not revealed; and its concealed sefirot and its matters are called "the crownings of the diadems," for they are a diadem to the diadems of all the sefirot. And the intent is: before the revelation of the tikkunin of the King and the crownings of the diadems. "Beginning and conclusion there was not." The meaning is: Chesed and Din were not in the world. For Chesed is called "beginning," as they said, "we begin with merit first"; and therefore Chokhmah is called "beginning," and in it is the beginning of the revelation of the line of Chesed. And "conclusion" is called Binah, for it is the line of Din, as is known. And these are the beginning of the beings and their privation: for in Chokhmah is the beginning of their existence, and in Binah is the completion of their circuit, in the secret of the Jubilee, where the beings return upon their being completed, to complete the circuit of seven years seven times. And therefore he said that "beginning and conclusion there was not." And one should not say that the line of Rachamim, which is the middle, did not exist at all, for it already existed somewhat, being the emanation of Keter, which is the Ancient itself. And therefore we say [that only] "beginning and conclusion," which are the two extremities, "there was not." "And He was engraving and measuring within Himself." The meaning is: the sefirot and the extremities, in the secret of the aspect of Din, were being emanated within the existence of Keter, and there they were being engraved, and were not [being] established—for the world could not be governed by means of them, because of the Din that was not [yet] revealed, as explained. And when He saw the subtlety of the beings and the smallness of the Din, He emanated Chokhmah and began to incise within it the beings, and to bring them forth to the revelation of Din in their existence. And this is what he said: "and He spread before Himself one hanging," that is, Chokhmah, which is a veil and a screen that conceals Keter and closes it off. "And on it He engraved the measure of kings." And "their tikkunin" [tikkunohi] are the powers of Din—not His external powers, meaning the very master of Din, but the matters of Gevurah and its judgments, and the worlds that are in it, which are called "the measure of kings," that is, the kings of Edom, as he sets forth and proceeds. "And their tikkunin"—that is, the tikkun and the emanation and its revelation—"were not established." The meaning is that it was not yet possible for the Din to be emanated and to be revealed, by reason of its nearness to its source.
And behold, in Chokhmah it is in great subtlety and near the Emanator, and therefore the secret of compassion prevails.

And further, the secret of the emanation from the side of the [powers of] Din "was not established." This is [the meaning of] "and these are the kings who reigned"—meaning, the powers of Din that arose in thought to be emanated were not emanated and were not revealed, by reason of the subtlety of Chokhmah; and therefore it is said of them "and he died," that is, concealment. And so Rashbi explained in the Idra further on, and said that the intent is not that they were nullified, God forbid, but that they were concealed, until the emanation was emanated, and from there these worlds were revealed in the fitting place, after the manner of the sefirot—for they were being revealed in Keter, and afterward in Chokhmah, but the emanation was not rectified there, until they were emanated to their place and to their line, as is fitting.

And the matter of "and he died, and he died" is the concealment of the world of Din and its line, which were not able to be revealed by reason of its intensity. And his saying "before there reigned a king over the children of Israel": the meaning is "the first king" [is Binah], and "the children of Israel," the first—that is, "Israel," the first—is Tiferet. And this is because the verse said "before there reigned a king over the children of Israel," meaning: before Binah, which is "king," should reign and be emanated, and before Israel, which is Tiferet. And this is the existence of the revelation of those worlds in Chokhmah. And it said "in the land of Edom," the intent being "in the place of Din"; for there He was incising the world before Himself—that is, the line of Din—and the worlds were being concealed, not revealed, because Binah, where the beginning of Din is, had not yet been emanated. "Until He set them aside and stored them away." The meaning is that they did not literally die—which would imply that they were nullified—but rather "He stored them away," that is, He concealed them, as he explained there, in the [matter of the] tikkunim of Zeir Anpin. And they were concealed, after the manner of the sefirot themselves, which are concealed in Chokhmah, as we shall explain. "And after a time He withdrew into that hanging." The meaning is that the cause of the revelation is the cause of the concealment, and the cause of the concealment is the cause of the revelation. And the matter is that, in the concealment of the strong light and its being clothed in a garment, it is revealed.

And behold, the light is concealed, and in truth it is revealed; for if it were not concealed, it would not be revealed—like the likeness of one who comes to gaze at the ray of the sun: by reason of the revelation of the ray of the sun is its concealment, for a person cannot gaze at it by reason of the abundance of its brilliance; and when he conceals it and gazes at it through screens, then he attains to gaze at it with his eye and it does not harm him. And so is the matter with the emanation: that it conceals itself and clothes itself in order to be revealed. And this is what he said, "and after a time"—meaning, after this incising, as we shall explain—then "He withdrew into that hanging." The meaning is: the supernal Keter withdrew, with Chokhmah, and emanated Binah; and there it was rectified, for from there is the beginning of the revelation of Din, as is known, for from Binah the [powers of] Din are aroused, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with the help of Heaven. "And it is taught: when it arose in [His] desire." He brought this baraita to support what is expounded. "It arose in desire"—that is, Keter. "To create the Torah"—that is, Chokhmah, which is the supernal Torah, prior by two thousand years, etc. And the intent is that by means of it shall be the governance and the line of Din. "And He brought it forth immediately," etc.—meaning, that He emanated it to the existence of Chokhmah, outside of Keter; "and it said before Him," that is, a parable to the existence of the worlds and the line of Din, which were not revealed in Chokhmah, and were dying and being concealed. And this is the matter of its saying [this] before its Emanator—like the matter of the hanging that he mentioned at the beginning of the discourse. "Whoever wishes to be rectified and to be made," etc. The meaning is that it is impossible for the concealed ones and the beings to be revealed unless Keter, which was not [yet] ready, be revealed further, as explained above. And afterward, when there was revealed yet a third grade—that is, in Binah—then it would be possible for the beings and the line of Din to come into being as is fitting. And he called Keter "the Concealed of the two thousand years." The meaning is: Keter is concealed from Chokhmah and from Binah, which are the two thousand years. For every sefirah includes ten, ascending to a hundred; and ten times ten are a hundred, and ten times a hundred are a thousand. It is found that Keter is concealed by [the] two thousand years. And he called it "concealed" because, at such a time, it was concealed even from the two thousand years—for so he called it above, "the Ancient of Ancients, the Concealed of the Concealed," as explained. And then, after Keter had rectified itself in what would be revealed and made ready by means of Binah, then it was possible for the beings to be revealed and emanated. And with the preface of this saying, the matter of the return of the sefirot at the Jubilee, in the fiftieth year, to Binah will be understood—and why they do not return to Keter, which is a subtler existence, more excellent and more exalted. And the reason is that in Binah they are there in the revealed existence of the sefirot; but from Binah upward, if they ascend, they are concealed as in their priority. And there is no advantage [such] that they should be nullified, God forbid; for there is no revelation of the sefirot except from Binah downward, where the line of Din is in force. And with this saying will be understood what is expounded in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer—and these are its words: "Before the world was created, the Holy One blessed be He and His name alone existed. And it arose in [His] thought to create the world. And He was incising the world before Himself. A parable to a king who wished to build a palace: if he does not incise in the ground its foundations and its exits, he does not begin to build. So too the Holy One blessed be He was incising the world before Himself, and it did not stand until He created repentance." End of his words.

The meaning of "before the world was created": the intent is, before Binah was emanated—for she is called "world," as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles—the Holy One, blessed be He, and His name alone existed. Now many explain it [thus]: "the Holy One, blessed be He" is the Ein Sof, and "His name" is Keter. But to us this is very strained, for the word "the Holy One, blessed be He" does not properly apply to the Ein Sof, since the word "blessed" [implies one who] is a recipient of effluence. And even if we explain that its meaning is "the source of the blessings," we have already explained, in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 5, that the source of blessing is Keter according to the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him. Therefore we say that "the Holy One, blessed be He" is Keter, and "His name" is Chokhmah.
And the notion of "name" [referring] to Chokhmah is not strange, for the meaning of "name" everywhere is a garment, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles (under the entry "name").

And behold, the garment of Keter is Chokhmah. And if we explain it according to their way: "the Holy One, blessed be He" is the Ein Sof, and "His name" is Keter; and "it arose in thought" is Chokhmah; "to create the world" means the emanation of the beings as the line of Din, which are the world in truth, and after their name Binah is called "world."

And behold, the beings and the line of Din arose in thought and were engraved within her [Chokhmah], after the manner of the hanging "upon which He was engraving," etc.; and this is [the meaning of] "He was incising the world before Himself." Yet it did not endure, by reason of the subtlety—like the matter of the death of the kings that we explained above—for by reason of the great subtlety of Chokhmah and her nearness to her source, no being there is revealed and no Din is revealed, "for in the light of the King's face is life." [This continues] until He emanated Binah, for there is the revelation of the matters; and this is what it said, "until He created repentance."

And behold, there has emerged for us from this that the existence of the beings and their revelation is by means of Binah; and he was precise in calling her "repentance" (teshuvah), for there is the "returning" (teshuvah) of the circuit and its return after the Jubilee.

The intent in this chapter is to explain further the matter of the three first ones in their emanation. And it is this: that the principal governance of the lower ones is only by means of the six extremities—namely Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod—and these are the streams that judge the world for good and for ill, according to the will of their Possessor.

And behold, these six extremities are a likeness to the Tree, which requires planting and transplanting. The intent is that there is needed, first, a concealed manifestation by which the watering of this Tree shall take place; and these are its roots, fixed and planted within Binah; and thence "the river issuing from Eden" waters the garden of delights, so that it may bear fruit after its kind "whose seed is in it" upon the lower earth, which is Malkhut. It emerges that these extremities—that which was designated by us in the preceding chapter by the name "the beings" and by the name "the root of Din"—[have] three necessary manifestations: the manifestation of planting, which are the roots; the manifestation of transplanting, which are the branches of the Tree; and the manifestation of the fruits [the sefirot], which are below, the place where the actions are emanated.

And behold, since the matter of the existence of the Emanation requires these three things: when it arose in His will that their planting be in Keter, it would not endure; and likewise in Chokhmah, by reason of their nearness to their source, as explained—and the beings within them were [held] in the power of the simple compassion, and Din was not seen in them as the governance requires, as explained. Therefore, when the extremities reached Binah, there was their first planting, and there [was] the existence of their root, so that from there their effluence might flow to them by means of the concealed roots within Binah. And their root that is in Binah is from their root that is in Chokhmah, and their root that is in Chokhmah is from their root that is in Keter. And there in Binah [is] the first manifestation for the extremities, in a manifestation revealed to Din and to compassion. For in Chokhmah, although their manifestation is there too—as he testified in saying "and He was engraving," etc., that He incises within her, in the hanging, [which] indicated that their manifestation is in Chokhmah, as we shall explain—yet in Binah there was revealed a manifestation revealed to Din and to compassion, after the matter that "[compassion] and judgments are aroused from her," as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And afterward, from Binah they were transplanted to their own place—that is, the second manifestation for the extremities, which is their very place, where they are the six extremities, all of them shining and effecting their action. And they are like the substance of the Tree that draws sustenance from its roots: so the sefirot draw sustenance from their roots concealed in Binah, and this is the second manifestation for all the extremities. Afterward the Tree bears its fruits, which are the actions of the sefirot effected by means of Malkhut, as is known.

And the matter of these six extremities: they are doubled—six for Din and six for compassion. And these are the twelve havayot within Tiferet, which are the twelve boundaries that are the officers of the Teli, the sphere, and the heart [Teli, galgal, lev], whose sign is TaGaL. And they are "world, year, soul"—sign: OSheN—for these three are Binah, Tiferet, Malkhut, in which are the three manifestations of the extremities; and therefore the boundaries were depicted in these three places, as we shall expand on at length in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapters 7, 8, 9, [and] 10. And now that we have called attention [to the fact] that the extremities could not be revealed by means of Keter and Chokhmah, let us proceed to explain the order of their emanation until their arrival at Binah; and afterward we shall explain, in a separate chapter, their emanation from Binah downward.

Behold, when it arose before Him to emanate Keter, at the time of its emanation there were within it the ten sefirot, this one within that and that within this, each concealed within its fellow, and all of them within Keter. However, the seven sefirot were not [the ones] revealed within Keter; rather, the [ones] that were principally revealed within it were Chokhmah and Binah. It emerges that in Keter [there is] a point that includes three points revealed within it, which were made from three lights that are concealed roots—namely, primordial light, clear light, [and] refined light—as we shall expand on in the Gate of Tzachtzachot.
And behold, within these three points the sefirot were concealed, as we shall explain in chapter 6, with God's help.

And behold, Keter emanated Chokhmah and emanated into her all the sefirot, which are included within three points; and they are three aspects within Chokhmah, corresponding to the three first ones, which are the three brains that we explained from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 7, with the help of Heaven.
And behold, Chokhmah emanated Binah, and within her [are] three points in which the whole Emanation is included, and they too correspond to the three first ones.

And behold, it was not at the time of the emanation of Chokhmah or of Binah that the sefirot were emanated within her; rather, in the matter of the emanation of each and every sefirah of these three first ones there were six aspects. The first aspect: the concealed aspect, prior to its revelation, [hidden] in the sefirah that emanates it; and it is so concealed that it is well-nigh absent. The second aspect: it is a revealed [aspect] that is revealed and seen within the sefirah that emanates it. The third aspect: revealed in itself at its fitting place—and this is the [proper] manifestation of the sefirah. The fourth aspect: to place within it the power whereby the upper sefirah is able to emanate the sefirot within it and to receive all the rest of the sefirot. The fifth aspect: it is to place within it the power whereby it is able to emanate the sefirot concealed within it to their revealed manifestation in its own self. The sixth aspect: revealed at their fitting place. And the matter is thus: at first the Ein Sof emanated Keter, and Keter was concealed and unrevealed—"air that is not grasped." Afterward the Ein Sof struck within it and emanated it [as] a revealed aspect. Third, He struck within it and emanated it at its fitting place. Fourth, afterward He struck within it and emanated within it the power that it might be able to receive the sefirot. Fifth, He emanated within it the power that the sefirot might be seen within it. Sixth, He emanated within it the power that it might be able to emanate the sefirot to their fitting place—that is, in Chokhmah, [Keter being] revealed relative to itself. And in the manner of these six aspects pertaining to Keter from the side of the Ein Sof, so [is] the manner of Chokhmah from the side of Keter—except that the last three aspects of Keter are the first three of Chokhmah. How so? The first [of Chokhmah] is revealed in Keter: yet not a revelation that is evident, but only [in that] its manifestation is there—this, then, is the fourth that he stated regarding Keter, that He placed within it the power that it might receive the sefirot, which are the manifestation of the sefirot in concealment. And the second of Chokhmah, which is revealed in itself within Keter, is the fifth of Keter, which is that He placed within it the power that the sefirot might be seen within it. And the third of Chokhmah, which is revealed at its own place, is the sixth of Keter—that is to say, [that] the Ein Sof emanated within it the power that it might be able to emanate the sefirot to their fitting place. Further, the fourth pertaining to Chokhmah—which is that He placed within her the power that she might receive the sefirot in her own self—is the first aspect of Binah, which is the manifestation of her emanation in Chokhmah in concealment. The fifth pertaining to Chokhmah—which is that He placed within her the power to reveal the manifestation of the sefirot in Chokhmah itself—is the second [pertaining] to Binah, that there was revealed within Chokhmah a somewhat-apparent revelation. The sixth pertaining to Chokhmah—which is that He placed within her the power to emanate the sefirah to its fitting place—is the third [pertaining] to Binah, that she was emanated to her place. Further, the fourth pertaining to Binah, which is the first [in this reckoning], is to place within her the power that she might receive the extremities—and this is the first manifestation for them, the first aspect. Further, the fifth pertaining to Binah is to place within her the power that the manifestation of the extremities might be seen in her, an apparent revelation—and these are the "roots" explained above. Further, the sixth pertaining to Binah, which is to place within her the power that she might be able to emanate the extremities to their own place. Thus the emanation of the three first ones has been stated.

And the matter of these aspects [is] like "nails firmly planted," in which there is no doubt at all, for we have derived them from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, concerning the Emanation. And we know that when the one who delves descends to the depth of Rashbi's words by means of these our words, his soul will bless us.

And behold, the manifestation that the extremities have, in the manner of complete concealment within Keter and within Chokhmah, is that which is designated by the "incising" mentioned in the passage in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer; and likewise the matter of the "engraving" and "incising" mentioned in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And the intent in their saying "He was incising the world," and likewise the matter of "He was engraving, and they were not established," is not that He was literally observing whether it were possible to be established—that is, for the line of Din to be revealed there, God forbid—for there is no doubt before Him, nor any lack of knowledge. Rather, it is the manifestation of the sources of the sefirot concealed in Keter and in Chokhmah, as above.

And behold, the matter of these four arrays—which are Chokhmah, Binah, Tiferet, and Malkhut—the four letters of the name come as a hint at them, in that within each and every one of them are included all ten sefirot, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name.

And behold, the fifth array, which is Keter—the thorn of the Yod—by reason of its great subtlety is not mentioned in the name. And the four arrays, which are Chokhmah, Binah, Tiferet, [and] Malkhut, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in [the] portion [of] Bereshit, each one separately, in a place of its own, many times. And Rabbi Abba mentioned all four of them together in [the] portion [of] Tazria (folio 43), and these are his words: Rabbi Abba said: "How manifold are Your works, O YHVH" (Psalms 104:24)—how many are the works of the holy King! And they are all enclosed in Chokhmah. This is [the meaning of] what is written, "All of them in wisdom You made." They are all included in Chokhmah, and they do not issue forth except by known tracks toward Binah; and from there all was made and all was rectified, as it is said, "and by understanding it is established." And concerning this, "all of them in Chokhmah"; "You made"—in Binah. "The earth is full"—"the earth," this is the Assembly of Israel, for from there she is filled from all, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 1), "all the streams go to the sea," etc. "Your possessions"—for she brings them forth afterward. This is [the meaning of] "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created"—"with Heh He created them"; and therefore, "the earth is full of Your possessions." Thus far his words.

And behold, this passage lacks nothing of what we require. He said, "and they are all enclosed in Chokhmah." The meaning: although it appears that they are in Chokhmah—since her "making" is with her—nonetheless they are not revealed in Chokhmah; rather, in Chokhmah they are enclosed and concealed [in] the utmost concealment. And he established the matter by saying "this is what is written," etc.—the meaning [being]: by this [reading] the verse is understood that said, "All of them in wisdom You made," and afterward "the earth is full." Now there is a difficulty in it: for "the earth" is certainly Malkhut, and "Chokhmah" means Chokhmah literally; and if so, how is it possible that the existence of the beings is [drawn] from Chokhmah to Malkhut, with no difference of aspect between them but a single grade? For Chokhmah is the first cause of the beings and Malkhut the fourth effect, and there are two grades between them apart from Chokhmah and Malkhut—and how did Scripture mention them together with respect to the beings? Rather, what have you to say? That "he split the verse with a sharp knife." And the meaning of "all of them in Chokhmah" is not that they are in Chokhmah intrinsically, but [that they are] included within her—and this is what it says, "and they are all included in Chokhmah." And he was precise [in deriving this] from the expression "all of them," which is an expression of inclusion; and therefore there is no escaping that they go out by means of the paths to the outside—that is, to Binah, where [is] the cascade of the paths, and where they rest from their running. And this is what it says, "and they do not issue forth except by known tracks toward Binah." The meaning: perforce their issuing is from Chokhmah to Binah. And if so, Binah is the second array for the extremities, which are the beings. "And from there all was made," etc.—it was difficult for him, for there is no [logical] necessity in that [alone], since it is already possible that their making be in Chokhmah while they pass through Binah merely in passing, and that they effect there no abiding, real action at all. Therefore he said that it is not so, but "from there all was made and all was rectified," etc.—and thus their making and their tikkun were principally by means of Binah. And for this he brought a proof from the verse, "and by understanding it is established." The meaning: and by Binah—which is also called "understanding" (tevunah), as explained in the Glossary of Titles—by her the sefirot and the beings and the deeds are established and set firm.

And behold, accordingly, the word "You made" perforce does not refer back to Chokhmah, but [is] a matter on its own—namely, the "making" of Binah, in [the production of] their beings and their establishment by means of her. And this is what it says, "and concerning this, all of them in Chokhmah"—the meaning [being]: all of them are included in Chokhmah; and here they split the verse. "You made"—this is the making of Binah and the tikkun of the beings and their revelation in her. "The earth is full," etc.—it was difficult for him, for he had established that the making is in Binah on the grounds that it is impossible that the beings be emanated from Chokhmah to Malkhut, that is, from the [one] extreme to the [other] extreme; and on the strength of this he said that "You made" refers back to Binah. And now, even accordingly there is a difficulty, for between Binah and Malkhut there is likewise a second grade—namely, "year," which is Tiferet, that is, the place of their transplanting, as explained above. And to this he replied that [as for] "the earth is full," the word "the earth" is Malkhut in [the] aspect of her receiving from Tiferet. And this is what it says, "this is the Assembly of Israel." The meaning of "this": as he said, it is impossible to escape [the conclusion] that "the earth" is called Malkhut in her aspect of receiving from Tiferet—for this is the [assembly that] gathers and is gathered from "Israel," which is Tiferet. And likewise "the earth" receives from "the heaven," and "heaven and earth" are Tiferet and Malkhut, as is known. It emerges that her aspect called "earth" and her aspect called "the Assembly of Israel" are all one thing, and both [are] in the secret of her receiving from Tiferet. And how much more so now, when it says "the earth is full"—for the "fullness" of the earth is the streams that are emanated into her, which are the extremities issuing from Binah: branches that receive from their roots and bring forth in Malkhut "the fruit of His deeds." And this is what it says, "for from there"—that is, the aforementioned Binah—"she is filled from all"; the meaning [being]: from all the streams, which are the third array. And he established the matter from the verse, "all the streams go to the sea, yet the sea is not full." It appears that the filling of the sea is by means of the streams, which are the extremities included in the great stream, which is the stream [of] Tiferet. And since it said "the earth is full," certainly the intent is that she was filled by means of that which fills her, which is Tiferet—for it includes the third array, that is, the sefirah itself and the extremities.

And behold, now there are found in this verse four divisions, [which] are the four arrays. The first array is Chokhmah, and there the beings are concealed [in] the utmost concealment—and this is what it says, "all of them in Chokhmah." And the second array, which is the array of the roots, is Binah, and it is hinted at in the verse by the word "You made"; and one should not wonder at the matter of "making" [being attributed] to Binah, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles (under the entry "making"). And the third array is the array of Tiferet, and it is hinted at by the word "is full," according to the way we have explained. And the fourth array is the array of Malkhut, hinted at by "the earth," and her [role] is to bring the matters forth into their realization below. And this is what it says, "for she brings them forth afterward." And the meaning of "afterward" [is] after these grades mentioned above; for now it is well [understood that] "she brings them forth afterward." But according to what had entered our minds—[namely] that [it ran] from Chokhmah to Malkhut—the explanation of the verse was difficult, since the array of Malkhut is not [immediately] after the array of Chokhmah. But now that he has explained that in the verse three arrays were mentioned—which are "in Chokhmah" and "in Binah" and the extremities, that is, Tiferet—this is [the meaning of] "Malkhut brings them forth afterward," that is, after Chokhmah and Binah and Tiferet in their order. This is [the meaning of] "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth." And the meaning of "the generations of the heaven and the earth," which are Tiferet and Malkhut, [is] that the generations cannot be in the earth except by means of the heaven, which is the male that emanates into the female. "With Heh He created them." The meaning: although we say that Tiferet and Malkhut begot and brought into being the generations and the beings, our intent is not that the two of them together brought them into being equally, [such] that the two of them together would constitute a single array. Rather, the intent is that Tiferet, with its extremities, displays the actions and emanates them to Malkhut, and they are one array; and Malkhut displays them below, and she is another array. And this is what Scripture says, "when they were created—with Heh He created them," for the creating was with Heh alone. And therefore Tiferet came in concealment in the verse, and it did not mention Tiferet in the verse; for it would have been fitting to say, "and heaven and earth are full of Your possessions." Why did it conceal "the heaven" by the word "the earth is full," as we have explained? Rather, certainly it wished to guard, lest we fall into error and say that heaven and earth brought the beings into being together, the two of them in a single union, [such] that the two of them would be found to be a single array, and there would be only three arrays. For this [reason] it said, "the earth is full of Your possessions," for Malkhut is the fourth array, like Tiferet and the extremities themselves; and that which fills the earth, which is Tiferet and the extremities, is the third array on its own. Thus far has reached the explanation of the passage. And from it we have learned the matter of these four arrays; and these four arrays have ever so many proofs, far clearer than these. But since each of the four is, on its own, in a passage of its own—one here and one there—we have not seen [fit] to be lengthy with proofs, [confining ourselves] only to [this] short, lovely, and sweet passage.
