After we have occupied ourselves in the preceding chapter with the matter of the emanation of the three first ones, and have said that the three of them were included in a single point, which is Keter—now we say that what we said, that all the sefirot were included within them, is according to this order: that in the supernal Keter were Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut, which are related to the middle line, the line of Rachamim; and in the point [of] the very root of Chokhmah were included Gedulah and Netzach, which are related to the right line, the line of Chesed; and in Binah were included Gevurah [and] Hod, which are related to the line of Din, on the left side. This matter is necessitated [by reason of] the secret of the actions, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with the help of Heaven, and as explained above in chapter 3 in the words of my teacher, may God preserve and keep him. And afterward, when the will arose before Him to emanate Chokhmah by the power of Keter—behold, when He had emanated her, He thereafter emanated within her and emanated first Binah, and afterward Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut, [though] not in a revealed manifestation like the revelation of Binah. And although we said "Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut," nonetheless Yesod does not yet rise in name at all, but only [as] the double-faced [du-partzufin].

And behold, the beginning of the revelation of the double-faced is in Chokhmah alone. And on this account it is found that the matter of the double-faced—although their root is from Keter—does not rise in name with respect to the matter of their emanation except in Chokhmah alone, since there they were [first] revealed, because they had a first journey from Keter to Chokhmah. Thus in Chokhmah there are now four grades in the emanation. The first is Binah, and she is revealed in her [Chokhmah], because even in Keter she came in [one] point [one of the three included within it—from Asis Rimonim], all the more so now. And the second is the emanation of the double-faced, and they are revealed, but not like Binah, since in Keter they were concealed, and now there was revealed only a slight revelation. And the third is the emanation of Chesed and Netzach, and they are concealed, for they have not yet journeyed from their place. And the fourth is the emanation of Gevurah and Hod, which have no revealed manifestation at all, since even their source—which is Binah—was as yet concealed in Chokhmah and had not been emanated. Afterward Chokhmah emanated Binah, by the power of Keter, by the power of the Ein Sof. And at the time of Binah's revelation there was emanated within her own self the secret of the concealed line of Din, for so it is fitting, [since] they are from her own self and she is their root. And immediately upon the emanation of Binah, Chokhmah emanated within her, by her [own] power, Chesed and Netzach, and by the power of Keter, the double-faced. It emerges that Binah has emanated within her three kinds of emanation: the first, her being revealed; and the principal [part] of the double-faced—which the supernal Keter emanated in Chokhmah, and Chokhmah, by the power of Keter, emanated them in Binah—it emerges that Keter Himself emanated them, and from Him they were, as explained.

And behold, this emanation [of the double-faced] is more revealed than the rest of the emanation within Binah, for it has a second journey: first they journeyed from Keter to Chokhmah, and afterward from Chokhmah to Binah. And the second emanation is the line of Chesed, which are Gedulah [and] Netzach; and this is more revealed than the line of Din, but not so much as the line of Rachamim, since it has only the first journey, which is from Chokhmah to Binah. But the line of Din is still set in its root, which is in Binah herself, and has not journeyed hither and thither—although it was revealed by means of the [general] revelation, [in] that its root was somewhat revealed. And with this premise the reason is settled why there is no Din except from Binah [downward], and not from Binah upward: because Binah is the root of Din, and even within Binah it has no revelation, all the more so from Binah upward. And also with this premise is understood the reason why Tiferet and Malkhut ascend as far as Keter, as is proven in the Tikkunim—which is not the case for Chesed and Netzach, which never ascend from Chokhmah upward, since their root is in Chokhmah. And it is now found that Tiferet and Malkhut ascend as far as Binah, and there they have a source and a revealed root; further, they ascend into Chokhmah, and there they have a revealed source and a root present—though not like their root in Binah, which is more concealed; further, they ascend as far as Keter, for there is their concealed root. And Chesed and Netzach ascend as far as Binah, and there they have a revealed root; further, they ascend into Chokhmah, and there they have a root more concealed than their root in Binah; and from Chokhmah upward they have no ascent, since they have no root above but [only] the root of their root, which is a root in Chokhmah—and although they are included in this root as well, [it is] in great concealment. And Gevurah and Hod ascend as far as Binah alone, and there is their root; and from there upward they have no root except the root of their root, which is the root of Binah, and they are there in great subtlety, as explained. And this is the reason that Din is from Binah downward. And likewise this is the matter of "and these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom," which Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained—[as] explained [in chapter 4]. And although we said that they have no ascent from there upward, [it is] not, God forbid, that they have no ascent at all—for "who has touched this and remained clean?" Rather, the intent is [that] a single attribute, or two attributes, have no ascent; but when all three lines unite to ascend, each and every line to its root, then they are exalted even as far as the Ein Sof, as explained in the preceding chapter concerning the three points. And likewise, even regarding a single attribute, it may be that Keter descends upon Gevurah, and the like. And let us return to our matter. Behold, after all the extremities had been emanated in Binah in the order stated—behold, by the power of Chokhmah, Binah emanated the Chesed within her, together with the Netzach that is included in her with Chesed. And the reason He gave Chesed precedence over Gevurah is that "one opens with [the argument for] acquittal first"; and therefore He was compelled to give Chesed precedence. And to emanate Tiferet in its [usual] way is impossible, since Tiferet is the arbiter between the extremities—and if there is no dispute, why an arbiter? Therefore He was compelled to emanate Chesed first. And afterward Binah, by the power of her own self, emanated Gevurah and Hod included within Gevurah—for Netzach is a branch of Chesed and Hod a branch of Gevurah. And afterward Binah emanated, by the power of Keter, the double-faced, to be arbiters between the right, the line of Chesed, and the left, the line of Din. And since the precedence of the double-faced precedes, in their emanation, Gedulah and Gevurah—as is proven above, that they are prior, [in] that their emanation is from Keter—therefore they have a manifestation [ranking] above Chesed and Gevurah. And this is the reason that, most of the time, we count Tiferet as the seventh from below upward, to indicate that it is above Chesed and Gevurah, in the secret of this supernal aspect [of it], which is prior to Gedulah and Gevurah, and which is its concealed aspect, [that] in the secret of its concealment in Binah. But from the side of its emanation below, it is the fifth from below upward, which indicates its being below Gedulah and Gevurah in the order of its emanation. And likewise this matter [applies] to Yesod, as we explained above in chapters 1 and 2.

And behold, it is now found that three sefirot were emanated: Chesed from the side of Chokhmah, Gevurah from the side of Binah, [and] Tiferet from the side of Keter—and all by means of Binah. And there is now no room for the disputant to dissent and to say that seven were emanated together from Binah; for so it is, that within each and every one of the three patriarchs one branch was emanated. And thus the words of the Gaon are likewise correct, that they were emanated in [sequential] order, for so the matter was, [in] that each and every one precedes its fellow, as we have explained; and thus the words of my teacher, may God preserve and keep him, are [also] correct. Afterward Chesed revealed Netzach by the power of Chokhmah; and afterward Gevurah revealed Hod by the power of Binah; and afterward Tiferet revealed the Yesod concealed within it by the power of Keter. And it will indeed be found, in truth, that Yesod, with respect to its aspect, [together] with Tiferet, is prior to Netzach and Hod—even though it is posterior, for the reason we explained regarding Tiferet.

And behold, afterward—through our many iniquities—the moon was diminished and was banished from her place, and descended to be the tenth, below Yesod, and Yesod became the ninth, as we shall expand on this matter in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon.

And behold, this exposition is hereby set in order and settled according to its proper measure, and all the views are brought to completion together with the view that obligates [the conclusion] that they were emanated one after another in [sequential] order, as we have explained. For first Keter was emanated; and afterward Chokhmah was emanated from Keter; and from Chokhmah, Binah was emanated; and from Binah, Chesed was emanated—for so it was, [in] that, although its root is in Chokhmah, it was emanated by means of Binah. And afterward Gevurah was emanated from Chesed—for, although its root is from Binah, we do not deny that by way of Chesed it was revealed to its place, and [that] it passed through her [Chesed] in a manner of passage, by way of a parable to the human intellect. And thus he was precise [in] the language of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Bereshit, folio 32b), who said, "the waters departed and begot darkness"—the meaning [being]: they conceived darkness, for there was a conception, [in] that they conceived from the darkness, after the manner of [the son] that is emanated from the male into the belly of the female, and the female conceives from him—and his root is not from the female but from the male, who deposited him in the belly of the female. And likewise Chesed conceived from Gevurah, and the root of Gevurah was emanated into it from Binah. And likewise Tiferet was emanated, by the power of Keter, from Binah, by way of Chesed and by way of Gevurah, to its fitting place; and afterward Netzach was emanated from Chesed, by way of the grades, to its fitting place; and afterward Hod was emanated from Gevurah; and afterward Yesod from Tiferet, in the manner of the sefirot mentioned; and afterward Malkhut, by means of the diminishment. And thus the words of Rashbi, who obligated [the conclusion] that they were emanated sevenfold from within Binah, are explained—for so it was, [in] that there the seven sefirot were found together, and from within her they were emanated below, as explained above concerning the three kinds of emanation within Binah. And thus the words of my teacher, may God preserve and keep him, are explained [with] sufficient explanation; and this is the foundation of our intent regarding the order of the Emanation. [This is so] even though we have no need of the reason why from Keter three were emanated, and from Chokhmah two, and from Binah two—since the matter of the double-faced has already been explained, that the two of them are one, and "they were two halves of one body," and Yesod within them unites them, and "body and covenant are reckoned as one"; and by means of one of these two reasons all is set in order.

And further, [the reason is] that the secret of the line of Rachamim, which is the arbiter between the right and the left, [has] its principal arbitration between Gedulah and Gevurah—in the secret of the element of air and the element of earth, both of which together tip the balance between fire and water, as we shall explain in the Gate of Arbiters; let it be examined in its place. Nonetheless, we do require that reason for the matter of Da'at, which is the root of compassion, in the matter of "and they were all included in wisdom, understanding, and knowledge [Chokhmah, Tevunah, and Da'at]," which we wrote above in chapter 3; and the matter will be explained at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance.
And behold, with this the chapter is concluded, and this gate is completed—by the grace of the One who graciously grants knowledge to man.
The Sixth Gate: The Order of Their Standing:

The intent in this gate is [to treat] what we have seen—[namely] that the later Kabbalists depict for themselves figures concerning the sefirot, this one saying thus and that one saying thus; and in truth not one of the views is fully satisfactory. And in this gate we shall explain the figure of most of the views, and we shall reveal the way that a person should choose for himself.
Chapter One:

Concerning the figure of the sefirot—that is to say, the order of their standing—the views concerning it are many, and the Kabbalists have depicted for themselves figures on large parchments (yeri'ot) and called them an "ilan" [Tree]. There is one who wished to depict them in the figure of an Alef. How so? They divided the head into three parts: the [first] to the supernal Keter, and the right side of the head [of the] Alef [to] Chokhmah, and the left to Binah. And the line that is below the Yod—which is the Vav of the Alef—its right "head" he called Chesed, and its left "head" Gevurah, and the middle Tiferet. And from the appearance of its loins downward: that which corresponds to the right [is] Netzach, and that which corresponds to the left [is] Hod, and that which is between the two [is] Yesod, and the lower thorn [is] Malkhut. And this is its figure:

Behold, they intended to depict the figure of the supernal Man in the figure of an Alef, to hint that the whole of it is a perfect union: although we say "ten sefirot"—which indicates separate things—the whole of it is a perfect union, and this he indicated by the likeness of an Alef. And there is some support for this view in the words of Rashbi in Sefer ha-Tikkunim (Tikkun 55), and these are his words: "Come and see: this skull is [the letter] Alef, like this; it has four sides, [and] in them YHVH is one and His name is one—there is none else besides Him," etc. Thus far [his words].
And although his words and his figure are not exactly as above,

nonetheless, from it [it] appears that the intent of the Name—which is ten sefirot, as is known—is hinted at in the figure of the Alef, to hint at ten sefirot unified [in] a perfect unity, an equal unity. And this is what it says, "in them YHVH is one and His name is one"—the meaning [being] to indicate that He and His name are unified, although His name indicates ten sefirot. And behold, the existence of the Alef indicates the union.

And the matter of the ten digits and the ten digits—its place is not here, and it will be explained in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 8. And others depicted the figure of the ten sefirot in the figure of an Alef, like this:

And it is true that the first figure is the most acceptable, for it is close to the tradition [Kabbalah] in the hand of most of the Kabbalists, as we shall explain. And the intent of these Kabbalists is not to say that this is literally the secret of their standing—for in this figure there are no channels, nor right and left intrinsically (that is to say, Chesed and Din)—but rather their intent is to indicate the complete union: just as the Alef means "one," so the ten sefirot are a perfect unity. And he further intended by this to make the figure of a patach at its [upper] thorn, above Keter, to hint that Keter is not a first cause, God forbid, but [that] above it [is] the sole Lord who rules over all of them and emanates effluence upon them; and one patach below, at Malkhut, to hint that the intent of all this is for the governance of the lower ones, and that it [Malkhut] is a passage for the effluence emanated from the First Cause to His created entities, as we have explained in the preceding gates. Further, another figure Rabbi Moshe de León wrote in the Sefer ha-Shem that he composed, and he said that it depends on the view of Sefer ha-Bahir; and some Kabbalists followed this way, and in particular because they wished to rely on it [to support] the matter of "their end is embedded in their beginning"—for the end, which is Malkhut, is embedded in the beginning, which is Keter. And its figure is like this:

And their view concerning this figure, in the matter of "their end is embedded in their beginning," is not settled at all, as the one who delves will see with his intellect; rather, the matter of "their end is embedded in their beginning" is a great secret explained in the Tikkunim in the words of Rashbi, and we shall explain it in the Gate "From Below to Above". Further, there are those who wrote a figure close to the agreement of the Kabbalists, and it is like this:

And Rabbi Moshe de León likewise copied it in the Sefer ha-Shem, and wrote: "And this view does not arise well according to the Kabbalah." But Rabbi Shem Tov ben Rabbi Shem Tov annotated upon it in the margin, [and] these are his words: "In my humble opinion, this view does not conflict with the other views, and it is very deep. And he counted ten sefirot from the known Keter, whose name is like the name of its master—it is the supernal Keter, the sole Lord; and this is called in Sefer Yetzirah 'He sealed the height' (with Yod) [with  Y H V], and it is called Keter like it, for it encompasses all the sefirot. And this is the secret of Thought emanated from the supernal Keter—[namely] Chokhmah, that is to say, the more revealed [one]; and it, by the power of the Ein Sof, brings forth the actions, [so as] to act in the likeness of the female, [and] therefore it is on the left. And Binah is called thus [because] she is between the two; in the secret of the Da'at stored away in her [which] is the emanation of the known Keter, in the secret of [the] supernal Keter. And this is the secret of the three names that the Name revealed to Moses at the bush; and the second, in the second name, is entirely the likeness of the female. Concerning this [there is] a very deep secret." Thus far [his words].

And behold, he intended to give a reason for Binah's being in the middle, [and] for Chokhmah's being on the left. And the beginning of his words may be understood somewhat by the reasoning of the view that is his, which we wrote in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 3. But in truth, [to engage in] length concerning this reasoning—that Chokhmah is on the left, and Keter on the right, and Binah in the middle—is a vain exercise, for it is a strange and rejected reasoning; for they hold that Chokhmah is Din, and Binah tips the balance between Chokhmah and Keter. And this view is null, as we shall expound at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 5. And the correct view, the received [one], agreed upon in the mouth of all the Kabbalists, is this; and Rabbi Moshe de León wrote it in the Sefer ha-Shem, [and] these are his words: "And there is another view, comely and very acceptable, surpassing them all, and it is true: that the three upper ones are like a segolta." And it is this:

And [these are] the gracious words of a wise man, for it is fine sifted flour. And this way was adopted by Rabbi Yehudah Chayyat in his book, and he gave a sign for the matter: "segolta, segol, segol"—for the three first ones [are] a segolta, the three second ones a segol, and the three third ones a segol, and Malkhut receives from all of them, below all of them. However, concerning Malkhut he wrote things that are forbidden to hear—and may his Master forgive him. And this figure is likewise agreed upon and necessitated from the words of Rashbi in many places. And in the interpretation of the points [vowels] he holds that the three first ones are a segolta, the segolta's hint being among them; and likewise he holds that the segol [signifies] the three patriarchs, and at times he holds that they are Netzach-Hod-Yesod [N H Y]—[which] indicates that this view is agreed upon and necessitated. He further explained, in another place—and it is a great proof for this view—[and] these are his words, in Sefer Ra'aya Mehemna (Beha'alotekha, folio 153): "And Chokhmah, Chesed, [and] Netzach shall be on the right, for on their account David said, 'The right hand of YHVH does valiantly, the right hand of YHVH is exalted, the right hand of YHVH does valiantly.' And three on the left shall be bound together, which are Binah, Gevurah, [and] Hod. And three grades of the middle—Keter, Tiferet, [and] Yesod—which bind [the] right and [the] left." Thus far [his words].

Behold, he explained explicitly that Chokhmah, Chesed, [and] Netzach are on the right, and Binah, Gevurah, [and Hod] are on the left, and Keter, Tiferet, [and] Yesod [are] in the middle. And according to their order known to us, it is necessitated that they be in the manner that we depicted above. And the being of Malkhut beneath Yesod is necessitated, for she receives from him, and he is the "best man" between her and her husband, and it is necessitated that she be beneath him.

And further, [it is necessitated] because she is the gate of entry, as is necessitated from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, [in] places too many to number. This matter was further explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 112), [and] these are its words: "And the nine sefirot are arranged in threes upon the central pillar, like this: Chokhmah-Chesed-Netzach, Keter-Tiferet-Yesod, Binah-Gevurah-Hod; Malkhut is the tenth to them and the fourth to them." Thus far [its words].

And the intent is clear: that the sefirot are arranged three [by] three. And once we have known this matter, of necessity their order is: Keter, Tiferet, Yesod in the middle—because Tiferet and Yesod are intermediaries and arbiters between Din and compassion, as we shall explain in the Gate of Arbiters. And therefore their depiction in this figure that we depicted above was required. It was further explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, folio 101b), [and] these are its words: "Keter over Chokhmah and Binah is a segolta—a cholam over a tzeirei. A segol is a dot beneath the tzeirei. Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet below. Netzach, Hod, Yesod in the middle is a shuruk; and so, when Tiferet is in the middle, it is a shalshelet." Thus far [its words], for our matter.

And behold, he said that Keter [is] over Chokhmah and Binah in the figure of a segolta. And he said that Tiferet [is] below Gedulah and Gevurah, and this is a segol. [It is] true that at times it [Tiferet] will be exactly between Gedulah and Gevurah, and then it will be in the figure of a shalshelet—and this is what it says, "when Tiferet is in the middle, it is a shalshelet." And likewise Yesod [is] between Netzach and Hod, and they are a shuruk, which are three dots in one row—although they are not diagonal, as is its norm. Thus far. Thus, from these passages, the figure that most of the commentators depicted for the sefirot is necessitated; and it is a correct reasoning, and there is no doubt in it.

After we have stood, in the preceding chapter, to set up the matter of the Emanation in the figure upon which all the Kabbalists, or most of them, have agreed, and we have necessitated it by means of some passages from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim—we have seen [fit] to copy here the reasoning of the author of Me'irat Einayim, [showing] that from these passages there is a refutation of his words, [for] he is opposed to all the Kabbalists. And these are his words, in [the] portion [of] Terumah. First he wrote, in the name of Rabbi Shem Tov, one figure, and it accords with the agreed-upon figure and does not conflict with the figure that we necessitated in the preceding chapter, except in the three first ones; and this is its figure:

And although the order of these three first ones is the reasoning of the author of Me'irat Einayim and the view of Rabbi Todros ha-Levi in Sefer ha-Ma'arekhet—and Rabbi Moshe de León likewise wrote something of this reasoning—

Behold, from the passages that we necessitated in the preceding figure, in the preceding chapter, there is found an explicit refutation of their words, and there is no need to be lengthy. He further wrote in Sefer Me'irat Einayim, in the aforementioned portion, [and] these are his words: "Behold, I depict for you the figure of the ten sefirot in their correct, true positioning, for [the one] to whom the Name, may He be blessed, has given eyes to see and a heart to understand; and I have not seen one in a thousand among all the Kabbalists who perceived this matter, apart from my teacher, from whom I received [it]." And this is it:

And whoever says of this form that it is reversed—he is of a perverse generation; and if the speaker's intent is good, his mind is reversed. He seeks to see the hinder parts, whereas we [see] the face, for it is said, "I have set YHVH always before me," etc. And although the sefirot are nothing but holy spirit—spiritual thoughts, unified one to another [in] a true union, and all unified in the Ein Sof, in [literally] the Ein Sof—and above there is neither right nor left, but rather these incline rightward, to acquittal, and therefore [the right] is called right and compassion, and these incline leftward, to liability, and therefore [the left] is called left and Din—nonetheless, behold, David, peace be upon him, said, "I have set YHVH always before me," etc. (Psalms 16:8). And over and above all this, our Sages of blessed memory said (Yoma, folio 53): when a person takes three steps [back], he gives "peace" to his left first, because the Shekhinah is opposite him; and thus he bows to the right of the Shekhinah, and afterward gives "peace" to his right, which is the left of the Shekhinah. Thus far [his words].

And we have several responses to him. First, regarding what he said—that he [the opponent] seeks to see the hinder parts, whereas we [see] the face: even according to him there is no substance in this reasoning, for so it is fitting not to gaze upon the face, as it is written (Exodus 33:23), "and you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen." And even [as for] the hinder parts—how many "hinder parts of hinder parts" are [the ones] that are seen!—all the more so [is it not fitting] to gaze upon the awesome face (see in Tikkun 69, folio 111, in what was said concerning "you shall not be able to see My face"). And this is the opposite of the correct view.

And further, [the truth is] that the matter is the opposite of his view, for the face is in this order: right opposite right, and left opposite left. And [there is] a proof from the matter of the tefillin: for the first portion, Kadesh—which is Chokhmah—is at the right of the reader and the left of the one laying [the tefillin]; and the portion Ve-haya im shamoa—which is Gevurah—is at the right of the one laying [them] and the left of the reader. But according to his view it should be the opposite, for the one laying [them] lays [them] right opposite right and left opposite left, and the reader, who is opposite him, would have the left toward the right and the right toward the left. And there is no [valid] response from [the fact that] Ve-haya ki yevi'akha—which is Binah—and Shema—which is Gedulah—are in [direct] correspondence: Shema, Gedulah, at the right of the one laying [them], and Ve-haya ki yevi'akha at his left. This is no response at all; for, on the contrary, Chokhmah and Gevurah are the principal [proof] for this matter, for several reasons: for it is fitting to arrange Chokhmah to the right, since it is the rightmost, the head of all the sefirot, and Gevurah [is] the principal leftmost, [tending] to liability. And why should we reverse these, which are principal, on account of two [others] that are [only] the root of the right and the left?

And further, [the proof holds] because Shema, too, [is] at the right of the reader in the aspect of Ve-haya im shamoa; and likewise Ve-haya ki yevi'akha [is] at the left of the reader in the aspect of Kadesh. And this is a compelling proof—what it is impossible to say of Kadesh and Ve-haya im shamoa—that, with respect to the aspect of all of them, Kadesh is always at the left of the one laying [them] and the right of the reader, and Ve-haya im shamoa at the right of the one laying [them] and the left of the reader. And this is certainly a refutation of the words of the author of Sefer Me'irat Einayim.

And [there is] a further proof from the ascent of the altar, for there [is] the foundation of the union, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Bamidbar, folio 120); and we have copied [its] language in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter 1, and in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 21.

And behold, the ascent of it [the altar] was by the ramp, and the ramp was on the south of the altar; and when [the priest] was ascending, he would turn to the southeast corner, which is the right of the one ascending. And were it true as the words of Sefer Me'irat Einayim, it would be fitting that he turn to his left, for there [would be] the right opposite him; and it would be fitting that the ramp be on the north of the altar, so that in his ascent by the ramp he would turn to the left of the one ascending—that is, the right that is opposite [him]—and turn to the northeast corner, in this order, etc. Rather, what have you to say? That [as for] this figure, there is no doubt that it is reversed, and the true figure is the figure agreed upon in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, [namely] that the right [corresponds] to the right and the left to the left. And therefore they expounded, "every turn that you turn shall be only to the right"—and this is the literal right of a person, [such] that "a left opposite him" and "a right opposite him" have no place there. And likewise they expounded concerning Abraham our father, peace be upon him, that all his turnings were to [the side of] Chesed. A further response to what he wished to derive support [for] from the verse "I have set YHVH always before me": it is no proof, for David, peace be upon him, would say so on account of the fear of the Name [being] before his face all the day, and he would think as if the Shekhinah were opposite him perpetually, and he [were] like a servant before the King, so as not to waver from his service, neither little nor much. And [as for] what he wished to derive support [for] from the matter of the three steps—shall we, then, set aside all the rest of the matters of the [Temple] service and bring a proof from a single detail, [namely] the matter of the steps?

Furthermore, there is no proof at all; for [though] you raise an objection against me from the view of Rava, who said "his right" [means] the right of the Holy One, blessed be He, [and] "his left" the left of the Holy One, blessed be He—I [can] support myself from the view of Abaye, who reckoned "his right" [as] his own right and "his left" his own left literally, [so as] to reckon that the matter of the steps is like the intent of the other commandments and deeds. Until Rava taught him that the meaning of "his right" is, that is to say, the right of the Holy One, blessed be He, [and] "his left" the left of the Holy One, blessed be He—the opposite of the other things. And the reason is that now, when one comes to take leave, he comes to teach a person not to think that his words are for naught and in vain, God forbid, but rather that he should be assured that his words were heard—like a person who speaks with the King in the inner chamber and takes leave of the King in peace and love. Or it is possible [that it is] to show a person his faith: that even though he unified the supernal worlds by the "hinder parts" that are seen, nonetheless the Holy One, blessed be He, hearkened to him by the "awesome face." Therefore, when he comes to take leave, he gives peace to the right of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is his [own] left. And in this manner we can explain the verse "I have set YHVH always before me," etc. Or it is possible that we should say that the matter of the peace[-giving] in this is for the [angel] who receives the prayer and makes it into crowns for his Master—even though he said "the right of the Holy One" and "his left." So too they said (in tractate Berakhot, fol. 7): Rabbi Ishmael said, "I saw Aktariel Yah YHVH Tzeva'ot," etc.—and he is the one who receives the prayers, and he is not the King of Glory; for if so, he would not have said "I saw" literally, God forbid. And as is known, Aktariel is a prince on high and not a god. And nevertheless there is no difficulty [in] his saying "Yah YHVH Tzeva'ot," for the angels are called by the name of their Master, by the Glory that hovers over them. And so it says concerning Abraham (Genesis 18:3), "And he said, my Lord [Adonai], do not pass on," and the Sages, of blessed memory, explained that he said [it] to the greatest of them—and the intent is the Glory that hovers over and clothes itself in them, which is the Shekhinah. And so [it is] in the matter of Aktariel, for concerning the Glory that clothes itself in him it says "Yah YHVH Tzeva'ot." And so [it is] in the matter of "He who makes peace," that he gives peace to the right opposite him and to the left opposite him because the Glory hovers over him and clothes itself in him; and there a literal left and a literal right apply. And this secret depends on the knowledge of the matter of the angels; it will be explained in the Gate of the Palaces.

Furthermore, another response, namely: in that it is well known that man—his forms, his structure, his limbs, his arteries, and his sinews—is the likeness of a supernal reflection. And man is a supernal shadow that became corporealized and thickened in this world, and he is the likeness of a supernal reflection appearing in this world. If so, it is fitting that his right [correspond] to the right of the supernal things and his left to the left of the supernal things—like the matter of the shadow, whose right is opposite the right of its root. And this matter is a root and a fundamental principle in faith and in piety.

Furthermore, that in truth there is above neither right nor left, but all is right and all is left. And a great proof [is] from the matter of the Tablets, which were one of the supernal branches whose spirituality became corporealized and thickened for the honor of Israel; and the Sages, of blessed memory, testified concerning them (Shekalim, fol. 16) that the Ten Commandments were visible in them from every side and from every direction and from every corner. And if in [something] corporealized [it is] so—that there is in it neither right nor left, but all is right and all is left—how much more so, and a fortiori, in the subtlety of the spiritual that is elevated above every cause, may it be praised and exalted. And if we decree right and left, it is in the aspect of merit and liability, as in the matter of what they said, "these incline to the left, to liability, and these incline to the right, to merit." And it is known that the matter of merit and liability is in our terms, not in the terms of the spiritual [realm]—rather in the terms of its actions toward its created entities. If so, His right is our right and His left is our left, and there is no distinction between this and that.

And the matter of the steps is according to one of the ways we explained. And we find ourselves learning that the principal, correct figure in this is according to what we drew in the previous chapter and established from the views of Rashbi, peace be upon him: three to the right, three to the left, three in the middle, and Malkhut receiving from them all. This is what emerges from the words of most of the Kabbalists. And there is yet [another] vision, and we shall explain it in the coming chapters, with the help of the Rock and His salvation.

After we have occupied ourselves in the previous chapters with the investigation of the figure of the standing of the pure and holy Emanation, and the figure agreed upon in the mouth of all the Kabbalists has emerged by our consensus—it is our wish to disclose to the ear of the discerning, concerning this figure, what its essence and its matter are and what the intent of its depiction is. And before everything, it is necessary to preface: although we say "right" and "left," there is there neither right nor left in their place, [and] neither back nor face. Rather, the matter of the sefirot is as we shall explain.

And behold, it is known that every cause encompasses what it causes, and every cause encompasses its effect, and the effect is encompassed by its cause—just as the point of the earth is in the middle of the firmament, and the firmament surrounds the earth, and the firmament is the cause of all the things that are beneath the heavens, by the will of the Maker; as is well known among the investigators, that the motion of the spheres is the cause of the compounding of the elements. And Rambam, of blessed memory, explained [this] in the fourth [chapter] of Hilkhot Yesodei ha-Torah, and said that the motion of the spheres necessitates the compounding of the elements in the lower world. And likewise the diurnal sphere encompasses all the spheres and is their cause, to the point that it turns them [in] the opposite of their [own] motion—which is from west to east—and it turns them from east to west, by the will of their Maker. And above all, encompassing all, is the sphere of the Intellect. And so [it is] with the ascent of the grades, for each and every one encompasses all the grades that are below it. And this appears [to be] of necessity, and in particular when one examines the chapters of the Account of Creation, he will rejoice and be glad, and the love of this premise of ours will be the more steeped in his heart. And there is a proof for this from the dictum of Resh Lakish (in Chagigah, fol. 12), and these are [the] words: Rabbi Yehudah said, there are two firmaments, for it is said, "Behold, to YHVH your God belong the heavens and the heaven of heavens." Resh Lakish said [there are] seven, and these are they: Vilon [Curtain], Raki'a, Shechakim, Zevul, Ma'on, Makhon, Aravot. Vilon serves no purpose except [that] it enters at morning and goes out at evening and renews each day the work of creation, for it is said, "who stretches out the heavens like a curtain [dok]." Raki'a—[the firmament] in which are the sun and moon, stars and constellations, fixed [in it], for it is said, "And God set them in the firmament of the heavens." Shechakim—[the firmament] in which millstones stand and grind manna for the righteous, for it is said, "And He commanded the skies [shechakim] above," etc., "and He rained down upon them manna to eat." Zevul—in which are [the heavenly] Jerusalem and the Temple, and an altar is built, and Michael the great prince stands and offers an offering upon it, for it is said, "I have surely built You a house of habitation [zevul], a place for You to dwell in forever." And whence [do we know] that it is called heaven? For it is written, "Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious habitation [zevul]." Ma'on—in which are companies of ministering angels who recite song by night and are silent by day, for the sake of the honor of Israel, for it is said, "By day YHVH commands His lovingkindness," etc., and what is the reason, etc.—thus far [the passage], to our purpose.

And behold, to say that these seven firmaments are the seven firmaments [i.e., spheres] that the astronomers counted is impossible—for he said that in one of these seven are the sun and moon, stars and constellations; and if these seven firmaments were the seven [spheres] that the astronomers counted, it would have been fitting that he count eight: seven for the seven planets, and one for the constellations. And such is not his intent, for he said that the sun and moon, stars and constellations are in one of the seven firmaments, whose name is Raki'a. And to explain that the Sages, of blessed memory, dispute with the astronomers—holding that the sun and moon, stars and constellations are fixed in a single sphere alone—[that too] is impossible. And therefore the sages of Israel do not dispute with the sages of the [other] nations except [on the question of] whether the sphere is fixed and the constellation revolves, or the constellation is fixed and the sphere revolves; but as to the number of the spheres they do not dispute.

Furthermore, the sages of Israel did retract and concede to the sages of the nations that the constellation is fixed and the sphere revolves; but as to the number of the spheres they do not dispute. And since the constellation is fixed and the sphere revolves, a multiplicity of spheres is necessitated according to the number of the constellations, which differ in their courses—and this is compelling. And the correct reason for this is that the totality of all the nine spheres is in one firmament. And likewise all the rest of the firmaments are supernal worlds, and in each one of them are many, many firmaments. And the sages who speak on the matter of the Account of Creation have already said that the number of the firmaments is like the count of [the word] "the heavens" [ha-shamayim] mentioned in the verse (Ezekiel 1:1), "the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God"—and their number is nine hundred and fifty-five; for the closed Mem of "ha-shamayim" amounts to six hundred, it being the second letter of the doubles [the final Mem]; and they are all included in a short number, [whether] seven firmaments, or nine, or five—for all of them have support and corroboration; and there is no place to elaborate.

And behold, when he said "the sun and moon, stars and constellations," he there included the totality of all the firmaments that the astronomers counted. And this is no wonder, for the astronomers counted similarly [in another case]: they said that the sphere of the moon is one, whereas they [also] said explicitly that they are three; and likewise all the spheres, their number is eighteen, as Rambam explained in the third [chapter] of Hilkhot Yesodei ha-Torah. And so [Resh Lakish] included them all in one firmament—and this reasoning is sufficient and correct by way of the plain sense. But in truth he counted in these firmaments none but spiritual matters, as is explained in the Zohar and the Ra'aya Mehemna; and so he designates those spiritual things by the term "firmaments," since they all encompass the world and the spheres. And so [it is with] everything, for the higher the grades ascend, the [more] they surround the grades within them. And so, in this manner, [is] the matter of the sefirot: for they are all within Ein Sof, the King who reigns; and within Keter, Chokhmah; and within Chokhmah, Binah; and within Binah, Chesed; and within Chesed, Gevurah; and within Gevurah, Tiferet; and within Tiferet, Netzach; and within Netzach, Hod; and within Hod, Yesod; and within Yesod, Malkhut. And within Malkhut, Beriah; and within Beriah, Yetzirah; and within Yetzirah, Asiyah. And in them are included the matter of the Account of Creation and the Account of the Chariot. Thus the chariots are found within Malkhut. And the Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the chapters of the Chariot [matters] concerning the chariots and the thrones. And within those things that are in the chapters of the Chariot [are] those things that are in the chapters of the Account of Creation; and within those things that are in the chapters of the Account of Creation, the spheres; and within the spheres, the earth; and within the earth, at its navel, are seven earths. And concerning this matter of seven earths we were astonished by this very existence, to the point that it arose in our mind to say that the matter of the seven earths stated in the Account of Creation and in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is the matter of the climes that the astronomers divided. Until God, in His compassion, favored us and brought to our hand many dicta that refute this view and concur that there are literally seven earths within the earth. And these are the words of the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 9b): Rabbi Yehudah opened: "And God said, let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters." Come and see: at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created seven firmaments above, [and] created seven earths below; seven seas, seven rivers, seven days, seven weeks, seven years, seven times, [and] seven thousand years that the world is to be. The Holy One, blessed be He, [is] in the seventh of all. Seven skies [another reading: firmaments] above, and all is one. And in each and every one [are] ministers, stars, and constellations that serve in each and every firmament; and in all of them are those chariots, these upon these, to receive upon themselves the yoke of the kingship of their Master. And in all the firmaments there are chariots and ministers differing one from another, these upon these: some of them with six wings and some of them with four wings; some of them with four faces, some of them with two faces, some of them with one; some of them flaming fire, some of them water, some of them spirit—as it is written, "He makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire." And all these firmaments [are] these upon these, like the layers of an onion, these below and these above. Each and every firmament goes and trembles from the fear of their Master; by His mouth they journey and by His mouth they stand. And higher than all of them [is] the Holy One, blessed be He, who carries them all by His strength and His might. In like manner [are] the seven earths below, and they are all inhabited—except that these are higher and these are lower. And the land of Israel is higher than all of them, and Jerusalem [is] higher than all the inhabited world. And our companions, the dwellers of the south, saw in the books of the ancients and in the Book of Adam that thus He divides all those earths, [such] that all of them are found below in like manner to those firmaments above, these upon these and these upon these. And between each and every earth [is] a firmament that separates between this and that; and therefore all the earths are distinguished by names, and between them are the Garden of Eden and Gehinnom; and among them are creatures differing one from another, in like manner to those chariots above—some of them with two faces, some with four, some with one, and the appearance of these is not like [that of] those. And should you say: behold, all the inhabitants of the world came forth from Adam—and did Adam descend to all those earths and beget children? And how many wives did he have? Rather, Adam was found only in this world, the highest of all, which is called Tevel (the earth-realm humans inhabit), as it is written, "playing in His Tevel [His earth]." And this Tevel is joined to the firmament above and is bound to the supernal name, as it is written, "and He shall judge Tevel in righteousness"—"in righteousness" indeed. And therefore the children of Adam are found in this higher [earth] that is called Tevel, and they are higher than all, in like manner to that which is above. What is the reason? Just as above, over all the firmaments there is a firmament higher than all, and above [it] is found the Throne of the Holy One, blessed be He—as it is said, "like the appearance of a sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne, and upon the likeness of the throne a likeness like the appearance of a man upon it above"—so too here, in this Tevel is found the King of all; and what is He? Adam [a man]—that which is not found in all the lower [earths]. And those lower ones, whence do they come? Rather, from the residue of the earth and the aid of the firmament above, creatures come forth differing one from another. Some of them [are] in their garments [clothed], some of them in husks like those worms that are found in the earth, some of them in red, black, and white husks, and some of them of all colors. Thus are all the creatures of this kind. And they do not endure in [continued] existence except [for] ten years or more. And in the Book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder it is explained further: that the whole inhabited world revolves in a circle like a ball, these below and these above; and all those creatures differ [according to] the difference of the air [climate] in each and every place, and they stand in their existence like other human beings. And therefore there is a place in the inhabited world where, when it is light for these, it is dark for those: for these [it is] day and for those night; and there is a place where it is all day, and no night is found in it except [for] one brief hour. And this which is stated in the books of the ancients and in the Book of Adam the First, thus it is. For so it is written, "I praise You, for I am awesomely wondrous; wondrous are Your works," and it is written, "How manifold are Your works, O YHVH." And concerning this, all is well; and this secret has been delivered to the masters of wisdom and not to dividers of boundaries, because it is a deep secret of the Torah. In like manner [there is something] in the sea, in which there are many creatures differing one from another, as it is written, "This [is] the sea, great and broad of hands," "there ships go," etc. And all depends one upon the other and is bound one to the other, and all [is] in like manner to that which is above; and in all the worlds [there is] nothing ruling over them all except Adam, and the Holy One, blessed be He, [is] above him. Rabbi Nehorai the Elder set out upon the Great Sea, and the sea raged, and all those who were in the ship perished. And a miracle was wrought for him, and he descended by known tracks into the heart of the sea, and came out beneath the sea to one inhabited [land]; and he saw [some] of those creatures, all of them small, and they were reciting a prayer, and he did not know what they were saying. A miracle was wrought for him and he ascended. He said: Happy are the righteous who toil in the Torah and know the enclosed things of the supernal secrets! Woe to those who dispute their words and do not believe! From that day on, when he would come to the study-house and they recited words of Torah, he would weep. They said to him: And why do you weep? He said to them: Because I transgressed against the faithfulness of the words of the Rabbis, and I fear the judgment of that world. Thus far [the passage].

And we know that these things are difficult for the human intellect and terrifying [to] the heart of those who examine [them]. And it is not fitting for one who believes in their tradition to doubt them; for not in vain did the Zohar adduce that Rabbi Nehorai doubted [it], even though he was [one] of the great ones of Israel and of the transmitters of the [oral] tradition, as is evident from the Midrashim and from the Gemara—whether we wish to say that he was Rabbi Meir, who is Rabbi Nehorai, as is explained in tractate [Eruvin] (fol. 13), or whether we say that he was other than him, as is evident from the words of this passage, that he was prior to Rashbi, peace be upon him, or in his time, and was a man of renown and distinguished in his generation. And so it is evident in Midrash Ruth from the Zohar, and likewise in Sefer ha-Bahir. And despite the abundance of his piety and his wisdom, he doubted it and was punished in the matter of the loss of the ship, and saw with his [own] eye [some] of the matter; and therefore those who remain shall hear and fear and shall sin no more presumptuously.

And behold, from the words of the passage it is understood how they themselves were not expert in this matter with clarity; as is evident from his proofs from the Book of Adam the First and from the Book of Rav Hamnuna, it appears that the words were faint in their hearts and not settled, as the examiner will see and read. And the matters are compelling of themselves, by the power of the true tradition, and there is no [room] to question. And even though there results from this, for the examiner, a doubt or doubts—as happens to us—it is fitting to conceal them and hide them, since they have at present no resolution, so that no one of those slack in [the study of] the words of the Sages, of blessed memory, will come and gibe from his words. And therefore let us hope [that] the compassion of God will favor us with the knowledge of this in truth, without error in the heart. And at present there is nothing to convey to another at all except the strength of the faith transmitted in this from this passage. And [as for] the rest, our eyes are toward YHVH our God, until He favors us and brings forth our judgment to light; and therefore we shall not bring ourselves into the explanation of the passage, neither much nor little. And however it be, behold, it is compelling from this passage that at the navel of the earth there are seven earths, this within that, in the manner of the spheres; and in this manner we ascend from the point of the earth up to the First Cause, the Ein Sof, blessed be He, and all the things are within it. And with this we can understand what they said, "He is the place of the world, and the world is not His place." And "the glory of God is to hide a matter," and this matter does not necessitate, God forbid, a place for His glory, may He be exalted—even though there are those who say that permission has already been given to ascribe place, [that is,] rank. And even from this we flee; rather, [we say] that His glory fills the whole earth. For even of the ninth sphere they said that from it upward place ceases, and it is without place—how much more so, higher and higher. And what we say here concerning the matter of a sefirah within the sefirot—and in these matters—the intent is not that the plain sense of the things is so, God forbid, for this is a criminal iniquity and is a fire that consumes unto destruction; for one who believes in things like these, God forbid, corporealizes the Godhead, and this is the opposite of the perfect faith that He is not a body nor a force in a body. And likewise all the Emanation, since it is close to Him, is divested of body and its accidents; for each one nearer [is] nearer than its fellow, [more] sanctified than its fellow. And what we say [as] "this above that" is priority of rank, not priority of place, as we shall explain. And let the examiner set these words of ours before his eyes, and let him not be among those who think evil, and let him not think that He is one who occupies place; for on the contrary, He is the place of the world and has no place, and He brought forth the place in which every occupier of place came to be. And before the creation of the occupiers of place, He had to create the place in which the occupiers of place would be created. And the investigators have already agreed that from the ninth sphere upward there is no place, and the tenth sphere of the Intellect, which is the holy [one], abides without place and is a place for the occupiers of place that are below it. And let this suffice for us, to be shown to the examiner; and to his God let him return, and let him keep lovingkindness and justice; and one must beware of error, for in these matters the unwittingness of study mounts up to [the level of] willful sin. And we trust in our Maker that one will not come, through our words, to error, God forbid. For concerning the like of this it is said (Ecclesiastes 12:9), "and he weighed and investigated and set in order many parables"; and they expounded in the Gemara (Eruvin, fol. 21), "the Torah was like a basket that has no handles"—although this is expounded in the Gemara concerning the safeguards of the Torah, nonetheless it hints also at our intent: that the Torah was like a basket that has no handles, until [Solomon] set in order the parables, by corporealizing the subtle matters, and from there the spiritual is understood. And how many matters like these are in Sefer ha-Bahir; and how many of the dicta of the Sages, of blessed memory, [serve] to corporealize the matter of the Godhead, in order to make [it] understood and to break [it for] the ear. And therefore the examiner must be cautious and guard himself.

In this chapter it would have been fitting to explain the order of the sefirot from cause to effect, in truth, without cavil, and likewise the order of the sefirot as to their being ten. But it is included in the coming chapters, with God's help, and from them we shall find well explained the order of the sefirot from cause to effect without cavil and the order of the sefirot as to their being ten; and [as for] turning the bag inside out, why should I [do so]?

After eras and eras have passed for us concerning this figure that [the previous chapters] furnished us, God illumined the eyes of our intellect in it, and God brought before us holy ones speaking, and we rejoiced in them as over all wealth, since we found in them a support and a stay. Firstly, the author of Sefer Me'irat Einayim—and this is the form of his words: This is the figure of the standing of the ten sefirot, without essence or change, may His name be blessed and exalted; and this is what the verse said (Job 26:7), "He suspends the earth over nothingness [belimah]." And do not say it is not [so], for it is so; and when you count from your right to your left you will find ten, and you will see that Keter is a house for them all and the source of them all. It turns out that what is prior in the Emanation is great and encompasses all, and what is posterior in the Emanation is small and encompassed by all and includes them all; and this is like the layers of an onion. And just as this lower earth is small and is in the middle of all the created entities, like a mustard-seed in a ring, and behold it includes all the elements and is in the middle of all, like the heart in the body of a man—so, as it were, [is] the Diadem.

And therefore it is called the land of the living, and the heart. And look and see that the Diadem includes the Righteous One [Yesod] and all the supernal ones, unified with them and encompassed by them all and receiving from them all. And so [too] the Righteous One, and so Hod, and so Netzach, and so Gevurah, and so Chesed, and so Binah—each includes all, and they are unified one in another, and each one includes them all, and they are all unified in it; and all is unified in Ein Sof, in the Cause of causes. Thus far [his] words. And it is a proof compelling [to] our view, letter by letter, word by word.

And further, we have a proof and a stay in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 165a), and these are [the] words: Rabbi Yossi said: There are nine firmaments, and the Shekhinah is the tenth. For should you say [that] because it is written "ten" [the sefirot are counted] apart from the Shekhinah—if so, the Shekhinah would be the eleventh, standing over ten. Rather, certainly they are nine, and they are the nine days that are between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, and Yom Kippur is the tenth. In like manner [is] the Mishkan, which is ten curtains. Ten firmaments [are] a secret of secrets that was not delivered except to those who know wisdom. And all is in the secrets of the holy Lamp [Botzina Kadisha], who reveals the secret of each and every firmament and those ministers who serve in each and every one. Seven firmaments are above, and seven firmaments are below, in like manner to that which is above. There are seven firmaments in which are stars and constellations to govern this world, each according to its way, as is required for it. In all of them the seventh is preeminent—except the eighth, which conducts them all and stands over them all, as it is written, "extol Him who rides upon the Aravot." Who is "He who rides upon the Aravot," and what is Aravot? Rather, this Aravot is the seventh firmament. Why is it called Aravot? Because it includes fire and water together, from the side of the south and from the side of the north, and it is mixed [me'orav] of the two sides. Thus far [the passage], to our purpose. And the explanation of the passage: above the [present] matter, Rabbi Chiya expounded on the explanation of the verse "And you shall make the Mishkan [of] ten curtains," etc.; and Rabbi Yossi found difficulty in the verse that said "And you shall make the Mishkan [of] ten curtains"—and it is known that the Mishkan is the Shekhinah, Malkhut. If so, how did he say that one should make ten curtains, which are the ten sefirot, over the Mishkan, which is Malkhut? It turns out, accordingly, that the sefirot are eleven—and this is the opposite of the truth, that they are ten and not nine, ten and not eleven, as is explained in [the] gate "Ten and Not Nine." For this [reason] he said that the ten curtains do not necessitate ten sefirot apart from the Shekhinah; rather, "there are nine firmaments." [That is to say,] nine sefirot alone are over the Shekhinah, and the Shekhinah is the tenth. And he adopted the wording "nine" and did not say "there are ten firmaments and the Shekhinah is one of them"—which would be more precise, [namely] that the Shekhinah too is called a firmament, as is explained from his words. The reason [is] that the place of the error and the mistake was because he said "And [you shall make] the Mishkan," which is the Shekhinah, "[of] ten curtains," as [if] it appears that ten sefirot are over Malkhut. And to guard ourselves from this corruption [of understanding], he said, against the error, "nine firmaments," and the Shekhinah, which is the Mishkan, is the tenth to the firmaments—and that is what he said, "and the Shekhinah is the tenth." "For should you say [that] because it is written 'ten,'" etc.: that is, that should you wish to say that, from the fact that the verse said "And you shall make the Mishkan [of] ten curtains" and did not say "nine curtains," it appears that they are ten apart from the Shekhinah, God forbid—if so, you will be saying that they are eleven, and the mishnah in Sefer Yetzirah said "ten and not eleven." And therefore he did not wish to say [otherwise], but [rather], "if so, the Shekhinah is the eleventh." And in his mentioning the words "the eleventh," who does not know the mishnah that said "ten and not eleven," and "one who adds to ten is not of the [proper] number"? Rather, certainly they are nine, etc. And it is not Rabbi Yossi's intent to say that Yom Kippur is Malkhut and the ten days of repentance are from above downward—for it is already explained in the Zohar and the Tikkunim and in several places that Yom Kippur is in Binah, and the testimony to this [is] the five afflictions; and it is a foretaste of the World to Come, as the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot, fol. 17a), "In the World to Come there is no eating or drinking," etc. Rather, Rabbi Yossi's intent is only to tell us that the sefirot are ten, in the likeness of those days, which are only ten. And if the sefirot were eleven, the days would be eleven. And just as the days are nine and Yom Kippur is the tenth, so it is fitting concerning the matter of the sefirot, for the Mishkan itself [is] the tenth. And the matter [is] that the ten days of repentance are days that are in repentance, which is Binah; and behold, the Yod is repentance itself—that is to say, the supernal grade within it—and it is included in [the] ten days, which are the ten sefirot, and it is of the [number of the] days. So [too] the matter of the Mishkan itself: it is the tenth curtain and the tenth sefirah. And the intent of the verse in saying "And you shall make the Mishkan," etc., the intent [is] that you shall make the existence of the Mishkan such that it include ten sefirot, which are ten curtains, and the whole ten, that is the Mishkan—not that the Mishkan is one and the curtains ten by themselves, as you might have thought, for if so they would amount to eleven; rather, the Mishkan, that is the totality of the ten curtains. And that is what Rabbi Yossi said, "in like manner [is] the Mishkan, which is ten curtains"—[that] is to say, the Mishkan is the gathering of the ten curtains, which is what we say, [that] Malkhut includes ten, as we explained in the previous gates and shall explain in [the] gate "Essence and Governance," blessed be He. "A secret of secrets," etc.: he extolled the wisdom and its excellence. "Who reveals the secret in each and every firmament, and those ministers," etc.: the intent [is] that in each attribute [there are] several angels appointed over the matter of the action of that attribute, and the angels receive the power of the action from the supernal roots by means of ministers that draw near to their source—they are those whom we shall explain in [the] Gate of the Holy Palaces. And from those near to the roots, who sit first in the palace of the King, [there] chain down many thousands and myriads of myriads, from grade to grade and from cause to effect, until they reach this world. And this matter has been explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, [in] places too many to number. And these angels mentioned are called ministers to those supernal firmaments, which are the sefirot. And that is the intent of Rabbi Yossi here, in his saying "seven firmaments are above"—the explanation [being]: seven sefirot alone are the principal ministers for the governance of the world; and therefore the building of the world [is] seven days, with the Sabbath day, since the principal governance [is] with these seven. And just as above there are seven conductors, so in the lower firmaments the conductors of the world are seven—that is, the seven planets. And he said that above six firmaments is a seventh firmament, more excellent than the six that are below it, and it is called Aravot, from the language of "mixing" [erev], for in it two attributes are mixed—that is, its blending between judgment and lovingkindness; and Aravot is Tiferet, which mixes them. And he called it "seventh," even though it is fifth below Gedulah and Gevurah, for the reason we explained in [the] Gate of the Order of the Emanation, in chapter six. And he said that there is an eighth firmament riding over all, that is, Binah, which is the mother crouching over the young.

And behold, the explanation of the passage is concluded, and from it we have learned the matter of the Emanation—that they are in the likeness of the spheres that surround this world, this within that, like the layers of an onion; and for this reason he called them firmaments, and their governance [is] like the governance of the lower firmaments, and they are spheres encompassing all that is within them, like a mustard-seed in a ring. And blessed is God, who made His lovingkindness wondrous to us in a besieged city, and we found ourselves corroboration and a stay from the words of the Zohar—[they are] all of them according to Rashbi, as is known—and there is no doubt in this matter.

After we elaborated, in the previous chapter, on the figure of the Emanation and its standing, and established it and confirmed it and upheld it as is fitting—it is fitting to see that this figure is found to demolish the whole edifice that we built in the previous chapters concerning the matter of the figure of the Emanation, [namely] that they are three rights and three lefts and three middle [ones]. And accordingly, this is not [consonant] with its [other] figure, for they are all one within another and there is in them neither right nor left. Now, [since] this and that are the words of Rashbi, it is not fitting to say that his words contradict one another, some of them against others. And likewise the author of Sefer Me'irat Einayim, who wrote that figure that we wrote above in chapter two, and afterward wrote this figure and retracted within the span of an utterance—and he said above that one who denies the first figure is [of] a generation of perversities, etc.—and this is very strained. And to resolve this matter, let us say: a question was asked among the investigators concerning the angels, which they designated by the name "separate intellects," and they said: since they are simple, spiritual, and far from all the accidents of body, if so, by what are they distinguished into the number ten? And Rambam, peace be upon him, wrote the matter of this question in the second [chapter] of Hilkhot Yesodei ha-Torah, and these are [his] words: "And by what are the forms distinguished one from another, seeing that they are not bodies?" And he answered: because they are not equal in existence, but each one of them is below the rank of its fellow, and it exists from its [fellow's] power, this above that, and all exist from the power of the Holy One, blessed be He. Thus far [his] words.

And the intent [is] that he there elaborated on the negation of body and its accidents in [the case of] the angels, and it was difficult for him: since they are far from the accidents of body, and since existents equal in existence are not distinguished one from another except by the accidents of body, and since the angels have no accidents of body—if so, by what are they distinguished, [such] that they are ten grades, as he himself counted? And he answered: because they are not equal in their existence. The explanation [is] that it is true [that] those equal in their existence are not distinguished except by the accidents of body; and the angels, which are distinguished even though they have no accidents of body—the reason is because they are not equal in their existence, but [are] effects one of another, and each one of them is below the rank of its fellow, etc. And the master Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov, in Sefer ha-Emunot, Gate 4, chapters one, two, [and] three, established with clear proofs that their view is not correct. And these are [his] words: Behold, according to their view, there is nothing between the Cause of causes and them except that this one is a cause to the effects [proceeding] from it; and we have no power to know a single thing of [any] difference between the First Cause and the last of them, etc., except [the relation] from cause to effect—that is to say, they are all unified in a complete unity, for there is among them neither conjunction nor separation, and they have no place at all, for they are not body nor a force in body, but [are] separate intellect[s]; but the cause is above what it causes and the cause is above its effect, and it turns out that the First Cause is a cause to them all, and the first effect is a cause to all the effects that are below it, and they are above the lower ones.

And further, the master refuted this view concerning the angels, because it is compelling from the words of the Sages, of blessed memory, that the angels were created on the second day or on the fifth day, according to what the Sages, of blessed memory, disputed in this (in Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 3); and he said that if the angels were [as] the unity of the [divine] Name, how is it possible to say that they were created after the creation of heaven and earth? And it is impossible, just as it is impossible to say that they preceded the First Cause.
And further, how does the language of "creation" [rightly] apply to them?

And further, he established [the point] from Parashat Vayera, from the vision of Abraham, who saw them in the likeness of men, and he established there that it cannot rightly be said that it was in a prophetic vision. Thus far his objections.

And behold, he established, on the basis of these questions, that they [the angels] are subtle beings, corporealizing themselves in a subtle and pure body; and for this he adduced [proofs] from the words of the Sages, of blessed memory, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Palaces, with God's help. And now we ourselves ask concerning the matter of the sefirot, exactly like their question: since we elaborated, in the previous gates, on the matter of the sefirot and their distancing from body and its accidents—if so, by what are they distinguished, if they are equal in their existence? And we shall answer according to their answer, that their distinction is in that they are not equal in their existence: for Keter exists from Ein Sof, and not so Chokhmah, whose existence is from Keter; and not so Binah, which exists from Chokhmah; and not so Chesed, whose existence is from Binah; and not so Gevurah, whose existence is from Chesed; and not so Tiferet, whose existence is from Gevurah; and not so Netzach, whose existence is from Tiferet; and not so Hod, whose existence is from Netzach; and not so Yesod, whose existence is from Hod; and not so Malkhut, whose existence is from Yesod. And behold, now they are distinguished one from another, in that each one is a cause to its fellow. And now, concerning the sefirot, what Rabbi Shem Tov found difficult in the words of Rambam will not be difficult for us, because the sefirot preceded the creation of heaven and earth and do not fall under time, but on the contrary, they are a root to time. For the six sefirot are a root to the six days, and the seventh is the Sabbath day, as will be explained in the Glossary of Titles, with God's help. And concerning them the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 3), "this teaches that an order of times existed before this." And it will also not be difficult for us [to explain] that they appeared to the prophets, for the prophets never apprehended the very sefirot themselves at all; and even to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, it was said (Exodus 33:23), "and you shall see My back," etc. And what we say, that the prophecy of Moses our teacher was in Tiferet and [that] of the other prophets in Malkhut—and likewise what we say, that Netzach and Hod are the two prophets of truth—the intent in all this is not that they apprehended the sefirot literally, but [rather] that from there [is] their nourishment; but their intellection was in the palaces. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Palaces, in chapter two, in the second palace, with God's help. Since his difficulties will not be difficult for us, if so, when we ask: since the sefirot are belimah, as we explained in the previous gates, [then] by what are they distinguished?—we too shall say that they are distinguished in that the one is a cause to its fellow, as if we should mean that there is no distinction between Keter and its Emanator except that the Emanator is a cause to the emanated. And beyond this they are unified [in] the utmost union; but between Ein Sof and Keter, by reason of Keter['s] being emanated and not Emanator, and Ein Sof Emanator and not emanated, there is much distinction, as explained above in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter and in the Gate of Self and Vessels. And this is clear, that Keter is emanated and Ein Sof the Emanator [is] not emanated. But by reason of their descent, the sefirot do not descend from it except in the manner [of relation] that [obtains] between Emanator and emanated and that [obtains] between cause and effect; and likewise Chokhmah descends from Keter, and Binah from Chokhmah, and likewise the other sefirot, like the descent of the effect from the cause. And the matter [is] that Malkhut apprehends Yesod, but not to the measure that it apprehends itself. And Yesod apprehends itself, and apprehends Malkhut with [a] more complete [apprehension] than Malkhut apprehends itself. And likewise it does not apprehend Hod to the measure that it apprehends itself. And Hod apprehends itself more than Yesod apprehended [it]. And likewise it apprehends Malkhut with [a] greater apprehension than Yesod apprehends [it], and how much more so Malkhut itself. And likewise Netzach—its knowledge of itself will be more elevated than Hod apprehends [it]. And likewise Yesod apprehends [it] more than Hod apprehends [it], and how much more so Yesod [apprehends] itself. And likewise it apprehends Malkhut more than Yesod apprehends [it], and how much more so Malkhut itself. And in this manner, too, the apprehension of Yesod in Hod will be more elevated than the apprehension of Malkhut in Hod; and likewise the apprehension of Hod in Netzach will be more elevated than the apprehension of Yesod [in it]; and likewise their apprehensions, one over another, will be elevated, up to the first grade.

And this matter [is] a great principle in [the realm of] existence, as we shall expand the explanation in Sefer Or Yakar, with God's help. And we know that it will be difficult in the eyes of the examiner that, accordingly, it turns out that Chokhmah is not unified with the Emanator, and likewise Binah with Keter—since that which is an effect from it, this is its cause, and the bond of the effect [is] with its cause, not with the cause of its cause, intrinsically. We shall answer to this: that it is true [that] the questioner has aimed well and is right in his ruling that they are not unified from this side; but they are unified from another side, each one in them all and all in each one, by [virtue of] the aspect of their inclusion from [the number] ten.

And behold, accordingly, Keter has with Gevurah ten unifications, namely: the Keter-within-Keter with the Keter-within-Gevurah, and the Chokhmah-within-Keter with the Chokhmah-within-Gevurah, and in this manner the other grades; and so for all the sefirot. And since it has been explained that, by way of inclusion, the sefirot ascend in their manifestations without end—as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter two, with God's help—therefore [the matter] will ascend in unification without end. And this is by [reference to] the [relative] measure of their unification and their bond [as] the emanated [sefirot] themselves. But in the Emanator they are unified in two respects: the one, by [reference to] their bond with their concealed root above, as is explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot; and the second, in the aspect of the light of the Self that spreads within the grades, which is the Self of the Godhead, not divided into these parts except by means of the sefirot, as explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels. And the Self that spreads is unified in its source, like the ray of the sun unified in the sun, and in the likeness of the soul unified in its powers that spread through the body. And the sefirah itself is unified in the Self that spreads [in the] utmost union, just as the soul is unified with the body, for reasons that we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul.

And behold, after the matter of their bond and the matter of their unification and the matter of their distinction have been explained—that they are in the likeness of cause and effect, cause and what it causes—the Emanation is found [to be] a jointed lampstand, [its parts] unified and bound [in] the utmost union, bond, and longing. And concerning this matter a covenant was cut for those who occupy themselves with the wisdom of the Pardes. And this was the claim of Elisha, [namely] that through this he became Acher [the Other].
