And this was the sin of Adam the First, who came to dismantle the tent and was found dismantling on the Sabbath, and therefore he was [held] liable. And one who contemplates this matter, [this] occupation, must beware lest he do according to their pattern; and therefore let the examiner occupy himself with this chapter, and in it he will find rest for his soul, and his soul will abide in well-being, and he will dwell secure with none to make him afraid.

After the matter of the bond of the sefirot among themselves and their bond with the Emanator has been explained in the previous chapter—when the examiner contemplates it with good diligence, he will find good taste and knowledge and the compelling [force] of the matter of itself, and the truth will show its way. And he will find, accordingly, [that] the sefirot—when we come to liken them and to depict them, by way of likeness, to the human intellect—[one] will be compelled to believe that they are one above another. For Ein Sof the Emanator is the Cause of all causes and the Source of all causes, and the first effect from it is Keter; and Keter [is] a cause and a cause to Chokhmah, by the power of the Emanator that overflows from its light upon it; and Chokhmah is a cause and a cause to Binah, by the power of the Emanator, by means of Keter, in [its] emanating the light of the Emanator by means of the first emanated [one], Keter, upon it. And so for all the rest of the Emanation: for Binah [is] a cause to Chesed, and Chesed a cause to Gevurah, and Gevurah a cause to Tiferet, and Tiferet a cause to Netzach, and Netzach a cause to Hod, and Hod a cause to Yesod, and Yesod a cause to Malkhut. Behold, they are ten grades, ordered one above another, thus: Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And of what is fitting to know [is] that, apart from this order, they have another order. And the reason for this [is] that each sefirah has two causes: the one, its cause—that after the preceding [one] was emanated, it was emanated. The example of this [is] that even though the true cause of Netzach is Chesed, nonetheless, because of the order of its emanation, its cause is none but Tiferet, as we elaborated concerning the matter of their emanation in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, in chapter six.

And behold, they have two aspects to their cause and their source: the one, the order that we explained above, one upon another up to the ten; the second, the order of their effluence and their source, according to their division. There is [one] whose aspect is lovingkindness [Chesed], and it must incline to the line of Chesed; and there is [one] whose aspect is judgment [Din], and it must incline to the line of Din; and there is [one] whose aspect is compassion [Rachamim], and it must incline to the line of Rachamim, and it aligns itself between these two lines, toward the mean.

And behold, the matter of these their aspects is their subsistence and their effluence that is poured out upon them. And it turns out, accordingly, that they have two aspects to their causes: the first aspect, the cause of the order, as explained; the second aspect is the nourishment and the effluence and the subsistence. And even though, from the side of the aspect [pertaining] to the order of the emanation, their order [being] one above another is compelling—when we look to the side of their nourishment, which is the cause of their subsistence, they are found [to be] in another arrangement; for we see [that] Keter emanates into Chokhmah and into Binah—if so, it is compelled from this that it is the cause of both of them. And from another side it is compelled that Chokhmah is the cause of Binah and Keter the cause of Chokhmah—if so, it is compelled that [they] be ordered in the likeness of a segolta, thus:

Keter; and one channel, which indicates the preceding cause—and their order is Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. And from the side of Keter's emanating into Binah, it is necessitated that there be a channel from Keter to Binah; and the matter of the channels will be explained in a gate of its own. And from the side of Chokhmah's emanating into Chesed, and Binah into Gevurah, it is compelled that Chesed be beneath Chokhmah and Gevurah beneath Binah—which indicates that Chokhmah is the cause of Chesed and Binah the cause of Gevurah. And from the side of Tiferet's drawing sustenance from Keter and from Chesed and from Gevurah, it is compelled that it be opposite it, indicating that its cause is Keter. And from the side of its drawing sustenance from Chesed and from Gevurah, it is compelled that it be between the two of them, to indicate that it is caused by both of them. And from the side of its being sixth in the Emanation, it is compelled that it be drawn somewhat below the two of them, as we have depicted. And from the side of Netzach's being seventh in the Emanation, it is compelled that it draw sustenance from Tiferet. And from the side of its drawing sustenance from Chesed, it is compelled that it be beneath Chesed. And so Hod, in this way, [is] beneath Gevurah. And Yesod is compelled to be beneath Tiferet, for from there is its principal nourishment, and it is its cause from the side of the pouring-forth [of effluence]. And from the side of its drawing sustenance from Netzach and Hod, it is likewise compelled that it be between the two of them. And from the side of its being ninth to them all, it is compelled that it be drawn downward, to beneath them all, as we have depicted.
And Malkhut, from the side of its being tenth, below Yesod, is drawn below Yesod.

And behold, after the matter of the agreement of the figures upon one matter has been explained, it is fitting to explain this matter that is found in the Zohar many times: "ascending and descending" [salka ve-nachta].

And behold, the matter of ascent and descent indicates corporeality, and this does not properly apply at all; and with this premise all will be explained. Namely: since the matter of their being one above another does not intend the existence of place, God forbid, as we have explained, but rather the matter of rank and priority from cause to effect, as explained above at length—

behold, the matter of ascent and descent likewise will be in this way. As, for example, Malkhut: before she was driven down to the tenth grade, she was in the seventh grade, beneath Tiferet, in her rank and her subtlety, so much so that she was a cause to Netzach and Hod and Yesod. And when iniquity caused [it] and she was driven from her place, she descended, and her lights were coarsened and darkened, until she does not have the capacity to be a cause to Netzach and Hod; rather, on the contrary, she is their effect and needs them and receives light and effluence from them—and this is the matter of her descent. And so the matter of her ascent: that she be refined so much that she return to Tiferet, and Tiferet be her cause, and she be a cause to all that is beneath Tiferet, owing to the abundance of her brilliance and her light. And likewise, in this way, when we say that one attribute among the attributes ascends to another attribute higher than it, the intent is this matter: that because of the effluence that that higher attribute poured into the lower attribute, it was refined until it ascends from grade to grade, until it becomes a cause to the other attributes that are beneath the attribute that overflows upon it—and this is called that that attribute "ascended" to the other. And therefore it is explained in the Zohar many times, and in particular in the Commandments [Pikkudin], the commandment "to bless" (in Parashat Ekev, fol. 271a), etc., that it is impossible for any attribute to ascend to another attribute unless it first receives from it abundant effluence in its [own] place, so that, by the measure of the abundance of the effluence, so will it be raised from grade to grade. And there are times when the effluence is not so intensified, and it does not ascend as far as the attribute that overflows upon it, but to another attribute that is beneath it, and from there it receives from it—like Malkhut, who at times ascends as far as Yesod alone, to receive effluence from her husband, Tiferet; and this indicates that Malkhut was refined until she ascended from being tenth to the ninth, and was not refined so much as to be literally seventh, near to Tiferet; rather, from that grade she receives from him. And this is the matter of ascent and descent mentioned in the Zohar concerning the attributes; and this is enough of a remark on this matter. And with this the interpretation of all the matters has been explained, and [that] the figure agreed upon in the mouth of all the Kabbalists is the truest—and not that there is a literal figure there, God forbid, nor a place of their standing, nor face nor back, nor right nor left, except from the side of Din or of Rachamim, according to their nourishment, each and every one according to its pouring-forth and its nourishment. And indeed, the key to all these matters is that being a cause or an effect [and the grades' being one beneath another — from Asis Rimonim] is in the two ways explained above; and with this it is clear that sometimes this depiction will obtain and sometimes another, all according to the pouring-forth [of effluence]—though it is true that this is the customary and the constant one.

After we have already roused ourselves, as much as is needed, concerning the matter of the order of their standing in the preceding chapters, there remains an obligation upon us, in the matter of this inquiry, to save the inquirer from error. For perhaps he will be in doubt and say: since it is true that the sefirot have a number, as explained in the preceding gates, and the number necessitated in them is ten—if so, when we come to their matter we shall say that the place of the end of Malkhut is the beginning of Yesod (that is to say, in the way of spirituality, from effect to cause), and the place of the end of Yesod is the beginning of Hod; for what is Hod is not Yesod, and what is Yesod is not Hod, and what is Hod is not Netzach—for they are distinct, [by] what [lies] between cause and effect; and behold, the effect is not the cause, and the cause is not the effect.

And behold, accordingly it turns out that, even though they are unified [in] a complete union, nonetheless they are, in this respect, distinct, as explained above. And now, behold, Keter is the effect of the Ein Sof, and the Ein Sof is its cause; if so, what is Keter is not the Ein Sof, and what is the Ein Sof is not Keter—and behold, it turns out that the Ein Sof has a limit, God forbid, [namely] what is not Keter; for the place of the end of Keter is the beginning of the Ein Sof. And on the face of it, this question is the place of the error to which a person is brought [when he comes] to contemplate this; and it is an error and a great confusion. And the laying to rest of this doubt is clear, and there is no place for this question at all. And the reason is that the power of the cause is in the effect, and the effect is not bereft of its cause. That is to say: when we say "this is Keter," we do not on that account necessitate that it is not the Ein Sof, God forbid. For on the contrary, there is no place for the effect apart from the cause; and behold, the effect draws sustenance from it, and its being is its cause—in the likeness of the soul within the body. For you cannot object that what is body is not soul, and what is soul is not body; for this claim does not properly apply, for two reasons. One: because the soul is certainly the cause of the body, and there is no body without a soul, and what is body is the soul—for the soul gives life to the body, and the body is nourished from the soul, and it is impossible to depict that the soul be annulled from a part of the body unless it return to dust. But the living body is certainly a garment to the soul; and therefore it is compelled that what is body be soul, for it is the cause of the body, and a living body cannot be brought into existence without a soul. However, our saying "a soul without a body" does apply properly, for there is indeed a place for a soul without a body, since the soul is not the effect of the body. And so are the matters with the Ein Sof and those that are its effects: for it is not possible to bring into existence an effect without a cause, and what is an effect—certainly the power of the cause is within it. However, a cause without an effect does apply properly; for the cause has an aspect in its own right, from the side of what does not need the effects, and it has an aspect that spreads forth and shines in the effects and gives life to them. And in this way we shall understand the matter of the sefirot themselves: for on account of this reason it is compelled that the power of Keter be in Chokhmah, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Chokhmah in Binah, for the cause of Binah is Chokhmah, and it is its vitality; and so the power of Binah is in Chesed, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Chesed in Gevurah, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality. And with this will be understood what is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 167), that the five times "water" in the Account of Creation are on the second day, in Gevurah—and since Gevurah is the power of fire, how is it possible that the power of water be in it? Rather, [it is] in this way. And so the power of Gevurah in Tiferet, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Tiferet in Netzach, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Netzach in Hod, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Hod in Yesod, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Yesod in Malkhut, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality. And it turns out, accordingly, that Malkhut is Yesod, and Yesod is Hod, and Hod is Netzach, and Netzach is Tiferet, and Tiferet is Gevurah, and Gevurah is Gedulah, and Gedulah is Binah, and Binah is Chokhmah, and Chokhmah is Keter, and Keter is the Ein Sof. And not this alone, but [it] spreads forth in them all, so that it cannot properly be said "this is Malkhut and not the Ein Sof," God forbid; rather, Malkhut too has within it the power of the Ein Sof. And not this alone, but in this way is the vitality of the sefirot, and the vitality of the chariots, and the vitality of the angels, and the vitality of all the work of creation, from the first point to the last. And this is "and You give life to them all" (Nehemiah 9:6), and the Sages, of blessed memory, explained: "and You bring them all into being." And so they explained "and You give life to them all"—and it is all one matter. For since He brought them into being and brought them into existence from Nothing, it is compelled that they be poured upon from Him, and that all draw their vitality from Him; and since He gives life to them, it turns out that He brings them into existence and brings them into being at every time and at every moment and at every hour.

And behold, bringing-into-being and giving-life are all one matter for them. And by this matter will be understood "and in His goodness He renews every day, continually, the work of creation"—which is the effluence that overflows to give them life and to make them stand and to set them in their [proper] character. And if, God forbid, the withdrawal of His effluence from them should arise in the mind, in a moment they would perish. And they are but renewed, in the secret of the renewal of His light; and it is the effluence of a river that does not cease but is renewed, like the waters of the river, which at every moment are renewed. And let us return to our matter: for the Ein Sof, the King of kings of kings, rules over them all; for His Self pierces and descends by way of the sefirot and between the sefirot, and within the chariots and between the chariots, and within the angels and between the angels, and within the spheres and between the spheres, and within the elements and between the lowly elements, and within the earth and between the earth and its offspring, and unto the last point that is in the abysses—"the whole earth is full of His glory." And this is what Rashbi intended in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 3b), in his saying: "And the Cause over all shines in the ten sefirot of Atzilut and in the ten of Beriah, and shines in the ten classes of angels and in the ten spheres of the firmament, and does not change in any place." Thus far [his] words.

And he was precise in his saying "and does not change," to guard lest we say that, since He spreads forth in this measure, it turns out that He changes according to the change of the garments, God forbid; for this he said "and does not change in any place." And the rest of the words of the passage will be explained in the Gate of ABYA.

And behold, when the inquirer sets his intellect upon the rightness of the concealment of the King of kings of kings, we shall set him further upon the matter of the sefirot, of which we said above that Keter is in Chokhmah and Chokhmah in Binah, etc. There is yet [another] chosen order for them, namely: that the power of Malkhut is in Yesod, and the power of Yesod in Hod, and the power of Hod in Netzach, and the power of Netzach in Tiferet, and the power of Tiferet in Gevurah, and the power of Gevurah in Gedulah, and the power of Gedulah in Binah, and the power of Binah in Chokhmah, and the power of Chokhmah in Keter—which we cannot say [in the case of Keter, namely] that the power of Keter is in the Ein Sof. And the intent is not to say that it is not in the Ein Sof, God forbid, as will be explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot, with God's help; rather, in the way in which we necessitate this order in the sefirot, we do not necessitate that the power of Keter is in the Ein Sof. And the matter is that the matter of "the Shekhinah among the lower ones is a need on high" has already been explained, and we shall expand the explanation of it in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with God's help. And the matter is that Keter needs Chokhmah, for from the side of its shining to Chokhmah, the Ein Sof shines in it; it turns out that in this aspect Chokhmah is a cause to Keter, and the power of Chokhmah is in Keter. And in this way for all the sefirot. And it turns out [that] the power of Malkhut is in Yesod, because [Malkhut] is its cause in the respect that Yesod needs it in order to receive from Hod, which is above it; and so the power of Yesod in Hod, because Hod needs it in order to receive from Netzach, which is above it; and so the power of Hod in Netzach, because [Netzach] needs it in order to receive from Tiferet, which is above it; and so the power of Netzach in Tiferet, because Tiferet needs it in order to receive from Gevurah, which is above it; and so the power of Tiferet in Gevurah, because Gevurah needs it in order to receive from Gedulah, which is above it; and so the power of Gevurah in Gedulah, because Gedulah needs it in order to receive from Binah, which is above it; and so the power of Gedulah in Binah, because Binah needs it in order to receive from Chokhmah, which is above it; and so the power of Binah in Chokhmah, because Chokhmah needs it in order to receive from Keter, which is above it; and so the power of Chokhmah in Keter, because Keter needs it in order to receive from the Ein Sof, which is above it. And we cannot say that the power of Keter is in the Ein Sof, for He needs nothing other than Himself, and all need Him, and He is the source of all, and all draw from Him; He is the cause of Himself, and there is no cause prior to Him, God forbid. And concerning the matter of these two inclusions in the sefirot—which are from below upward and from above downward—[it is] explained many times in the Zohar, and in particular in Parashat Vayetze (fol. 158), on the matter of the tribes, where Rabbi Chizkiyah said: "'The mountains of spices'—who are the 'spices'? These are the six sons of Leah, who include six others; and they are twelve, and they are six, because each one is included in its fellow." Thus far [his] words.

And in the way that we have explained, it is clear—only that the inclusion is in one of two modes: either the upper ones in the lower ones, or the lower ones in the upper ones. This matter is further explained in the Zohar on the Song of Songs, on the verse "seven and seven pipes," and there he explained the inclusion from below upward, as is explained; and we shall not copy its language here, because it needs a broad explanation, and it is explained by us in its place. This matter is further explained there on the verse (Song of Songs 1:2) "Let him kiss me," etc. And with this will be understood the matter of "that the right is included in the left and the left in the right," which comes in the Zohar many times; and it is a key to several gates.
And behold, this chapter is concluded and this Gate is completed, as we were shown from Heaven; and praise [be] to God, blessed be He, who has helped us. Amen.
The Seventh Gate: The Gate of Channels:

The intent in this Gate is to explain the matter of the channels, concerning which the commentators have agreed that they are between each and every sefirah, [and] by means of which the sefirot draw their effluence one from another. And so we shall explain what their matter is, and the intent in them, and their figure, and their number.
Chapter One:

Before anything [else], we say that the term "channel" [tzinor] is derived from the language of "Deep calls unto deep at the sound of Your channels [tzinorekha]" (Psalms 42:8). And the meaning of tzinor is a pipe made [as] a way by which water comes from place to place. And the Kabbalists applied this [term] to the way of the effluence that is poured from attribute to attribute. And many times the Kabbalists designated the stopping of the effluence by the expression "the breaking of the channels," and likewise "the ruin of the channels," and the like; and these things are not as their plain sense. And the matter is that every sefirah that receives from its fellow, at the time of its will to receive, certainly an arousal must ascend from it to the upper one, so that by means of its arousal the upper one will be aroused and pour effluence into it; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in many places. And the proof of the matter is from the verse (Genesis 2:6) "And a mist went up from the earth," and afterward "and watered," etc. And we have set this matter apart, to explain it with sufficient explanation in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with God's help. And since the matter is so, therefore when a sefirah wishes to receive from the sefirah above it, the lower attribute must shine toward it a shining face, so that by the light of its face, gazing upon the light of the [upper] sefirah, it will arouse it, and abundant effluence will be poured into it, and its face will shine from the light of the upper sefirah. And not from all the faces together is it aroused to receive, but particular faces opposite particular faces, according to the will of their Emanator. And as the faces opposite the faces multiply, the channels multiply, as we shall explain in the coming chapters. And the general rule is that the light that is aroused from this one to that one and from that one to this one, by means of which the effluence is poured forth, is called a channel. And the parable for this is the sight of the eye, of which most of the natural philosophers said that a subtle light goes out from the eye and strikes the thing seen, and draws in that light, and from within it apprehends the thing seen. It turns out, according to their view, that the light that is aroused from the eye to draw in the sight would be called a channel, by way of parable: for just as the channel is a passage for the water, and by means of it the water is drawn to the place where it is wanted, so the light that goes out from the eye is a channel for the sight, to draw by means of it the thing seen into the eye. And so is the matter in the sefirot: the light that goes out from the lower one to the upper one, and from the upper one to the lower one, is designated by the name "channel," because by means of it the effluence is drawn from the upper sefirah to the lower sefirah. And just as, when a person hides his eyes from seeing, that channel is stopped and the eye does not draw in the sight—and this matter would be designated the breaking of the channel and its stopping—so in the matter of the sefirot: when, through the multitude of iniquities, the faces turn aside, and that light is not aroused, and the sefirah does not draw the effluence from its fellow, this is designated by the name "the breaking of the channels and their stopping." And now, with this matter, how much sweeter than honey is the parable of the stories that we set forth in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter four.

And behold, this matter is explained in the Zohar in many places, and in particular in Parashat Vayikra (fol. 15), and these are its words: "For it is taught: at the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, looks upon the world and sees that the deeds of human beings below are worthy, the Holy Ancient One is revealed in Zeir Anpin, and all those holy crowns gaze face to face, enclosed, and all of them are blessed. Why are they blessed? Because they gaze one upon another in a straight way, not turning aside to the right or to the left. This is what is written: 'their faces behold [one another] straight.' And all of them are blessed and water one another, until all the worlds are blessed and all the worlds are found as one; and then it is called 'YHVH is one and His name is one.' And when the sins of the world multiply, the Holy Ancient One is enclosed, and they do not look face to face. And then judgments are aroused in the world, and thrones are cast down, and the Ancient of Days is enclosed and is not revealed. This is what is written: 'I beheld until thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of Days sat,' etc.—for those supernal crowns that water all the others do not stand in their subsistence (in our Zohar the reading is le-okmei be-kiyyumaihu, 'to sustain [them] in their subsistence') (lo, 'not'). And who are they? The Patriarchs. 'And the Ancient of Days sat'—and was not revealed. And then the wicked of the world overturn compassion into judgment." Thus far [its] words.

From within it the matter of the channels and their tikkun is explicitly explained: that it is at the time when the Emanator wills to pour forth [effluence]; and then the Holy Ancient One—which is Keter, Arikh Anpin—pours light and effluence to all the sefirot, and the faces, which are the matter of the sefirot, are set straight opposite them, and the effluence multiplies. However, when the faces turn aside to the right and to the left through the iniquity of the generation, then the channels are ruined and no effluence is poured forth. And there are many [passages] like this passage in the Zohar that reveal this matter, and there is no need to go on at length, for they are recognizable as words of truth. And now that the essence of the channel and what is meant by it have been explained, we shall further explain the number of the channels upon which the commentators have agreed. And the number of the channels: three are drawn from Keter—one to Chokhmah, and one to Binah, and one to Tiferet. A further three (a variant reads: four) are drawn from Chokhmah—one to Binah, and one to Chesed (a variant reads: and one to Gevurah), and one to Tiferet. A further two (a variant reads: three) are drawn from Binah—(a variant reads: one to Chesed), one to Gevurah, and one to Tiferet. A further three from Gedulah—one to Gevurah, one to Tiferet, one to Netzach. A further two are drawn from Gevurah—one to Tiferet, and one to Hod. A further three are drawn from Tiferet—one to Netzach, and one to Hod, and one to Yesod. A further two are drawn from Netzach—one to Hod, and one to Yesod; and, in the view of some, one to Malkhut. A further one channel is drawn from Hod to Yesod; and, in the view of some, one to Malkhut. A further one is drawn from Yesod to Malkhut. Their total is found [to be] twenty-two, as the number of "By you [bekha = 22] shall Israel bless, saying" (Genesis 48:20). And it is our wish to depict their figure here, so that understanding them will be easy in the eyes of the discerning; and this is their figure:

<small>(Says the editor: We have depicted this figure, the one agreed upon according to the view of the author—namely, four from Chokhmah and three from Binah—for so he depicted and explained in his Sefer Or Ne'erav, part six, chapter two. But in this composition he wrote the view of the commentators, and omitted two channels—one from Chokhmah to Gevurah and one from Binah to Gedulah—and added two channels, one from Netzach to Malkhut and one from Hod to Malkhut. And it is not agreed upon, as he explained in chapter three and proved from the Zohar, Parashat Noach):</small>

Since in the preceding chapter we have planted the Tree of Life for the knowledge of good, and [shown] how the deeps [call]—"deep calls unto deep at the sound of the channels"—it is fitting for the inquirer to take care in working it and in keeping it, so that we shall not need to depict it again in the coming chapters, God willing. And now we shall explain what these callings serve.
And behold, from Keter three channels go out:

The first channel [is] to Chokhmah. From this channel is the beginning of the spreading-forth of the supernal world; and they are the shining face from which the whole world was illumined by the glory of its emanation, and from there all the sefirot were revealed. And they called its name "the Concealed Channel," since there is none more concealed than it; for the joining of Chokhmah to Keter—it is not known how and in what way—so much so that, almost, by way of that channel Chokhmah at times draws sustenance in effluence from the Ein Sof by means of Keter; for there is the hiding-place of the Cause of causes. And this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 52, fol. 84), and these are his words, on the verse "YHVH Adonai is my strength [cheili]," etc.: "What is 'my strength' [cheili]? The might of all, from above. Cheili—the strength of Yod [cheil yod]; and this is Abba, whose might, whose welling, is the Ein Sof (a variant reads: a welling that has no end)." Thus far [his] words.

And because the inquirer might imagine to reject this proof of ours by saying that at times Keter is called Ein Sof, we have seen fit to explain the passage, so that from within it it will be compelled that "Ein Sof" is the very Ein Sof. And this is its explanation. "What is cheili?"—the reason being that above he explained all the rest of the verse, and now he asked of the word cheili, what its meaning is. And he answered, "the might of all, from above," and the intent is the Ein Sof. And because to the Ein Sof neither name nor word properly applies, for this he said that the meaning of cheili is from the language of power, and the intent is [that] the Ein Sof is the one who gives power and strength and might to all the sefirot. And because this matter might already apply properly to Keter—for Keter too gives power and strength to all that is below it—therefore he lengthened his language and said "the might of all, from above," meaning: the one who gives power to all, and who is above all, there being none above Him; and that is the Ein Sof. And because, since cheili means the supernal power, I might have said that the meaning of cheili is the strength of Keter, for this he said "the strength of Yod," that is, Chokhmah, which is called Yod, as is known. And what he said, "and this is Abba," follows along with the rest of the explanation of the passage, and there is no [need] to go on at length. And they said that to this channel, which is from Keter to Chokhmah, the right strap of the head-tefillin hints—that is, with the hint of the housing [bayit] being to Keter—and from this channel went forth "living waters, flowing from Lebanon" to Chokhmah.

The second channel goes out from Keter to Binah. From this channel Binah receives effluence [of] abundant good from Keter. And they said that from it the perfumed wine spreads forth to Binah, and Binah brings it out from potential to actuality; and the perfumed wine spreads forth as far as the altar, in order to set right the dish of the pot gone rancid on account of the transgressions of Israel, and there, on account of [our] iniquities, they pour it out as a libation. For here "libation-wine" [yein nesekh] does not apply, for there is no touch of a gentile here. And they meant, in their saying "to set right the dish gone rancid," something like what was explained in the Zohar (perhaps he means Zohar, Balak, fol. 189a-b; see there) concerning Isaac: that there was mixed in his wine the wine of Esau, poured out [in order] to bless him; and Jacob brought him of the spiced wine, of the good wine, as it is written (Genesis 27:25), "and he brought him wine"—and then the power of compassion was added to him. And likewise, from this channel compassion is poured to Binah, to suckle the power of the milk to the children, so that our eyes be "washed in milk," and they grow quiet and rest, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter six. And then, as they are washed in milk, the red eyes are whitened; and this is by the power of this channel, which pours the power of the milk from the supernal whiteness. And this channel is concealed. And they said that it is the left strap of the head-tefillin.

The third channel goes out from Keter to Tiferet; and from there is the way of its ascent to Keter, to receive effluence and abundant good to pour forth to the four flocks of sheep that are beneath it, and they are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And by way of this channel it ascends to join Father and Mother in the secret of their union, by means of Da'at, as explained above in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter. And by means of the effluence poured upon it from Keter by way of this channel, it has the power to incline toward Chesed; for because it draws sustenance from Chesed and Gevurah, it stands between the two of them, even; and when effluence is poured upon it from the supernal whiteness, then it inclines toward Chesed. And this channel is called "the middle line," together with its continuation as far as Malkhut. And the commentators explained that this channel is what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, sought to know, and He answered him, "for no man shall see Me and live" (Exodus 33:20). And these are words of [mere] prophesying, for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, never asked about this.

A further three channels are drawn from Chokhmah. The first, to Binah: it is that by which the thirty-two paths are drawn from Chokhmah to Binah—and they are the twenty-two letters and the ten utterances, which are concealed in Chokhmah, "koach mah" (the power of "mah"), and Binah brings them out from potential to actuality; so the commentators explained. And it is possible that this is the channel by which was the spreading-forth from Chokhmah to Binah in the sefirot themselves, at the beginning of the Emanation, as explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, with God's help. And by way of this channel Chokhmah is concealed within Binah, as is explained in the Zohar in many places.

The second channel is drawn from Chokhmah to Chesed. By way of this channel the effluence of lovingkindness [chesed] is drawn to Gedulah from Chokhmah. And by way of this channel the seventy-two bridges are drawn to Chesed, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter sixteen. And the seventy-two bridges are in Chokhmah—"koach mah"—in potential, and in Chesed in actuality. And so "Chokhmah" amounts to seventy-three, which are the seventy-two bridges with Chesed hovering over them. And likewise, by means of this channel is drawn "the good oil upon the head, running down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron," as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, under the entry "oil"—that the principal [source] of the oil is from Keter, by means of Chokhmah, to the priest, the man of Chesed. And because its root is in Keter, therefore shemen ["oil"] in atbash amounts to Bet-Yod-Tet [21], which is Ehyeh, and it is a holy name. And likewise, by way of this channel the [effluence of] Chokhmah descends to Chesed, as they, of blessed memory, said: "One who wishes to become wise should turn south"; and through this the Yod of the name is at times designated in Chesed, as is customary in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim.

The third channel is drawn from Chokhmah to Tiferet; and this we have found only with the author of the parchment (Yeri'ah) [a particular chart of the Tree]. And possibly the reason is that Tiferet is the son of Chokhmah and Binah, and behold, it is compelled that the power of the father be in the power of the son, and likewise the power of the mother; for "there are three partners in a person." And possibly by way of this channel is the matter of "Israel arose in thought." And for this matter there is disclosure from many places in the Zohar and in the Idra, as will be explained in Sefer Or Yakar, with God's help.

A further two channels are drawn from Binah. The first, to Gevurah. And the commentators explained that it is to quiet the judgment of Gevurah and the power of the husks. And it is known that Binah pours into Gevurah in two modes. The one is judgment and might [gevurah]—for Binah is called "the worker of mighty deeds (gevurot)," and "from its side judgments are aroused," as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And this is specifically when it pours through this channel alone, which is from its own self. However, when it receives through the channel that it has from Keter and pours through this channel into Gevurah, then the effluence is to quiet the judgment and the might. And in this way is drawn the weakening of the husks, which are the officers of the judges, from outside; and when the judgment is annulled, their power is annulled, since they do not effect their action.
The second channel [is] from Binah to Tiferet.

Behold, this channel will be explained in the way that we explained above concerning the third channel, which is drawn from Chokhmah to Tiferet. And by way of this channel Tiferet ascends to Binah. And by way of this channel Binah established Tiferet, as in the matter of "He established the heavens by understanding" (Proverbs 3:19), as will be explained in the Gate of Manifestations, and was explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine."

A further three channels go out from Chesed. And the first of them, to Gevurah. And likewise from Gevurah the power of the fire of Gevurah goes out to Chesed, to dry the moisture of the water of Chesed; and the power of the water of Chesed [goes out] to quench the fire of Gevurah—for so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. And with this will be understood a matter in which one thing opposes another: that the south is hot and dry, and the north cold and moist—and it would have been fitting to be the reverse. And what is explained on this is set forth in the Gate of Essence and Governance, in chapter eleven, and in the Glossary of Titles, in the name of Rashbi, peace be upon him. Many have explained that between [the ends of] this channel is Tiferet, which is what combines them. But by what we have explained it is better settled: that apart from Tiferet they have a channel together; and this agrees best with most of the words of the Zohar. And by means of this channel Chesed is included in Gevurah and Gevurah in Chesed, without the joining of Tiferet, as is explained in the Zohar and explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. The second channel goes out from Chesed to Tiferet. And they said that from this channel thirty-five princes are drawn to Tiferet, and Tiferet brings them out from potential to actuality; and they are those who incline rightward, toward merit—so the commentators explained. And likewise, by means of this channel are also drawn seventy-two powers that are joined to the seventy-two names, as is known—which are the 216 lights: seventy-two of the right, seventy-two of the left, seventy-two of the middle. And Tiferet is what brings them out from potential to actuality and tips them toward the right. And likewise, by means of this channel is the matter of the arbitration, in combination with that of Gevurah.

The third channel goes out from Gedulah to Netzach; from there is the principal nourishment of Netzach, from Chesed. And the secret [is] "pleasantness at Your right hand forever [netzach]" (Psalms 16:11). For it is the emissary of Gedulah, and the principal action of Netzach is in lovingkindness [chesed]. And just as in Chesed there are seventy-two powers for the name of seventy-two, so there are in Netzach as well. For the three Patriarchs are the three Vavs—va-yissa, va-yavo, va-yet (Exodus 14)—and likewise they are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and in them too is the name of seventy-two. So Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim.

A further two channels are drawn from Gevurah. The first, to Tiferet. And the commentators explained that from there are drawn thirty-five princes who incline leftward, toward the scale-pan of liability, and Tiferet brings them out to actuality. And likewise, from within this channel are drawn seventy-two powers that are joined to the seventy-two names, as is known—which are the 216 lights, and seventy-two of them are of the left; and by means of this channel and that of Chesed, it is the arbiter between them, as we have explained. And further, by means of the aid of these channels, of Chesed and of Gevurah, he is united with his bride, in the secret of (Song of Songs 2:6) "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me," and as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And we have already written a little of this in the preceding gates.

The second channel goes out from Gevurah to Hod, and by means of it is the principal nourishment of Hod from Din, as we explained above in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine." And the commentators explained that by means of this channel the negative commandments are drawn from Gevurah to Hod, and in Hod is their explication; and likewise the positive commandments from Chesed to Netzach, by means of the channel that it has from it. And it is possible that Gedulah and Gevurah are the principal powers of the positive commandments and the negative commandments, and by means of Netzach and Hod they are revealed, just as the other actions that are in Chesed and in Gevurah are revealed by their means.

A further three channels are drawn from Tiferet. The first, to Netzach; and by means of it [Netzach] draws a little sustenance from the redness of Gevurah, for the sake of the blending, as is explained at length in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," in chapter four. And there is one who did not write this channel, nor the one going out from it to Hod. And this is a void opinion; and this [channel] is agreed upon, as we have explained.

The second channel goes out from Tiferet to Hod, to sweeten its judgment a little. And this is on account of its inclining—the whiteness toward the redness—as is explained in the said Gate and will be explained in the Gate of Colors. And by means of the two said channels the dew pours forth and descends from the heavens, [which is] Tiferet; then they [Netzach and Hod] "grind manna for the righteous"—Yesod and Malkhut, Tzaddik and Tzedek. And it will be explained in the Glossary of Titles, under the entry "Shechakim."

The third channel goes out from Tiferet to Yesod. And by means of it Yesod receives abundant good, to unite the groom with his bride; for by means of it her sustenance descends, and it is the best man. It turns out that this channel has two actions. The one: the sustenance that overflows to the woman by means of the intermediary, and likewise the sustenance of Yesod itself. And the second action: that it is the way of her ascent to be united with her husband, after she has been adorned "as a bride adorns herself with her jewels."

A further two channels go out from Netzach. The first, to Hod. And the commentators explained that by means of this channel they are united to ascend (to the heavens). And it is possible that by means of this channel is the grinding of the manna, in a slight evenness of blending, before its coming to Yesod. And by means of this channel, and likewise the channel that is from Chesed to Gevurah, and likewise the channel that is from Chokhmah to Binah, is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, in the secret of their inclining to the right and to the left. For Tiferet is in Netzach and Malkhut in Hod: YHVH in Netzach, Adonai in Hod; and by means of Yesod the two of them are united together, and  Y A H D V N H Y  is made. And so they are in Chesed and Gevurah—the male to the right and the female to the left: YHVH in Chesed, Adonai in Gevurah; and the two of them are united in Tiferet. And so they are in Chokhmah and Binah—the male to the right and the female to the left: YHVH in Chokhmah, Adonai in Binah; and the two of them are united in Keter—and not literally Keter, but in the secret of Da'at, which is the union of Chokhmah and Binah.

And behold, it turns out that these three channels—that from Chokhmah to Binah, and that between Gedulah and Gevurah, and that between Netzach and Hod—are for [set] times; that is to say, for the times of the union of Tiferet with Malkhut.
And the matter of these unifications is explained in the Tikkunim [Tikkun 18, fol. 33a].

The second channel goes out from Netzach to Yesod. For by means of this channel and the one opposite it is the blending and the arbitration by which Yesod tips the balance between Netzach and Hod. And by means of these two channels is the power of the seed, and by their means it is ripened—as is known, that Yesod is the member, and Netzach and Hod are the two testicles of the male.

The third channel goes out from Netzach to Malkhut. And by means of it "a thread of lovingkindness [chesed] was drawn over Esther," and by means of it she receives effluence from Chesed before the coupling. And likewise by means of Hod—for she needs to receive effluence from two places, from the right and from the left, in the secret of (Song of Songs 2:6) "His left hand is under my head," etc. And it will be explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with God's help, in chapter twenty-one.

A further two channels go out from Hod. The first, to Yesod; and its rule has been explained above. And the second, to Malkhut. And the author of the parchment explained that from this channel the primordial serpent cast filth into Eve. And his words are words of dreams, like one prophesying a vain vision; for "who set a drunkard among the Nazirites?"—as we shall explain, that the husk has no entry into holiness at all, as will be explained in the Gate of Substitutes. And what it might have been possible to say [is] that by means of this channel judgment is poured from Hod to Malkhut; but all this is without foundation [yesod], as we shall explain in the coming chapter.

And what is fitting to know [is] that what the commentators said concerning the two channels—one from Netzach to Malkhut and the second from Hod to Malkhut—is not tenable at all. For it is clear that Malkhut receives effluence only by means of Yesod, as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 59b), and these are its words: "Rabbi Elazar said: 'These' [eleh] in every place invalidates the former ones. We have learned, etc. What is written above, in the portion of Bereshit? 'And a river issues from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divides,' etc. That river that flows and issues [nagid ve-nafik] and enters the garden and waters it with the watering from above, and gives it rest [naycha], and it yields fruit and makes seeds grow—and it is then rest for all. And this is rest for the garden, and this one makes rest in it, as it is said, 'for in it He rested,' and it is written, 'and He rested on the seventh day.' And this is the secret of the matter: this one makes generations, and no other. Come and see: [in like manner] Noah below was the holy covenant, a pattern of that above, and therefore he is called 'a man of the ground.' And we have learned a secret: for Noah needed the ark [tevah], to be joined with it and to sustain the seed of all, as it is written, 'to keep seed alive.' Who is the ark? This is the Ark of the Covenant. And Noah and the ark below were thus, after the pattern of above. Of Noah, 'covenant' is written, as it is written, 'and I will establish My covenant with you,' etc. And until the covenant was established in him he did not enter the ark, as it is written, 'and I will establish My covenant with you, and you shall come into the ark.' And then the ark was the Ark of the Covenant. Ark and Noah—all after the manner of above. And because this covenant above makes generations, in like manner Noah below makes generations. On account of this it is written, 'These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man.' So it is, certainly, after the manner of above. And therefore it is written, 'and the righteous one is the foundation of the world,' and the earth is sustained upon this; for he is the pillar upon which the world stands. And who is he? This is the Righteous One [Tzaddik]. And Noah is called 'righteous' below. And the secret of all: 'Noah walked with God'—precisely; that he never separated from Him, and [so as] to be on earth after the manner of above: 'a righteous man'—the foundation of the world; 'covenant of peace'—the peace of the world; 'a man of the ground'—certainly. And therefore, 'and Noah found favor in the eyes of YHVH.'" Thus far [its] words.

What there is to be precise about in this passage is: First, his saying "that river that flows and issues"—what need is there for the word "flows" [nagid]? For his saying "issues" [nafik]—which is the language of the verse, which says "and a river issues from Eden"—suffices.

And further: he ought to have [said] "issues, and afterward flows"; for such is the way—that first it issues, and afterward it is drawn onward. And we can resolve [this by saying] that he adopted the language of the verse, "a river of fire flowed and issued from before Him" (Daniel 7:10). And nonetheless, according to our way it will be made more precise.

And further, on the verse too there is a difficulty: why did it not say "a river … issued from before Him"? Or let it say "issued and flowed"; what is "flowed and issued," not in order? Second: what he said, "and waters it with the watering from above"—certainly it is the watering from above! For such is the way of a river: it is drawn from above downward and waters the lower ones from the effluence of the upper ones. And why did he go on at length about what teaches us nothing, since it is obvious? Third: his saying "and gives it rest," etc., and afterward he said "and it is then rest for the garden," etc., according to one reading—or, according to another reading, "and it is then rest for all," etc. One must see why he did not state, in the first clause, two aspects, as he stated in the latter clause—as appears from the sense of the language, where he says "and it is then rest for the garden, and the garden is rest in it," or, according to the other reading, "and this is rest for the garden, and this one makes rest in it." But in the first clause he said only "and gives it rest," alone. Fourth: his saying "and it yields fruit and makes seeds grow" appears a needless doubling. Fifth: his saying "Who is the ark? This is the Ark of the Covenant"—why did he adopt the language "the Ark of the Covenant," and not say "Who is the ark? This is Malkhut," which would be preferable? Sixth: here it is implied that the ark by itself is the Ark of the Covenant, whereas further on he concludes that when Noah is within the ark, the two of them in union are called the Ark of the Covenant. Seventh: his saying "'a righteous man'—so it is, certainly," etc., up to "for he is the pillar upon which the world stands," etc.—it all appears a lengthening upon what was already expounded at the beginning. Eighth: his saying "And who is he? This is the Righteous One." Now with what was he occupied until now, that he asks "who is he"? Are we not dealing with the Righteous One? And to resolve all this, it seems [right] to explain that for Rabbi Elazar there was a difficulty in the verse, in its saying "These are the generations." And his difficulty was: always, "And these" adds to the former ones; "These" invalidates the former ones—and this "These," what does it invalidate? For one cannot say that it invalidates the whole work of creation, for it would not be pleasing to their Master that one say so. And he said, "We have learned, etc. What is written above, in the portion of Bereshit?"—because it was difficult for him [that] we should say that it invalidates the generations of formlessness [tohu] and void [bohu] and darkness, which are the husks. Therefore he said, "What is written above, in the portion of Bereshit?"—as one who is precise and says that it is not fitting to explain that it refers back to formlessness and void and does not refer back to the whole portion of Bereshit that adjoins it. "And a river issues from Eden to water," etc.—"that river that flows and issues," etc. He said "flows" because Eden is Binah, and the river is Tiferet, and the garden is Malkhut; and because it does not water the garden as [soon as] it issues from its mother's womb—for it must be drawn a journey of five hundred years, that is, the five sefirot, until it arrives to water the garden—therefore he was compelled to use the language "flows," that is, meaning: it is drawn through all those grades until it arrives at the garden. And he reversed the order in saying "flows" and afterward "issues," because it was difficult for him that it would have been fitting for the verse to be silent about the word "issues" and say "a river from Eden waters the garden," since the word "issues" is not precise—for it issues and is drawn [onward]; or let it say "and a river issues from Eden and comes to water the garden," for now the language of each one would be precise, that is, [that it is] drawn. And at the resolution of this he aimed in saying "flows and issues"; namely, that the verse comes to inform us of a novel matter: that we should not err and say that when Tiferet waters Malkhut it does not literally water [her] from the effluence of Binah, but changes it from its nature and waters Malkhut according to her measure below. For this he said that it is not so; rather, Tiferet pours into Malkhut that effluence according to its nature in Binah, as though Malkhut herself were receiving from Binah itself, with no intermediary at all. And this is what it says: "issues from Eden to water the garden." And therefore it did not say "and comes," because the matter of the drawing-forth does not intrinsically pertain here, since it is not changed from its character on account of the drawing-forth—as though the garden, which is Malkhut, literally receives it from the source, which is Binah, and Tiferet and Yesod serve for this matter of watering only the service of a passage. And this he taught us by his language "flows and issues"—the intent [being]: as is the manner of its issuing from Binah, so is the manner of its being drawn forth. And the measure of the language is thus: it flows in the manner in which it issues, and in the manner in which it issues it enters the garden—as though she herself were receiving from Binah with no intermediary. And this is what he says: "and waters it with the watering from above." The intent is that the effluence that comes to her by means of the river is as though she were drawing sustenance and receiving from Binah itself with no intermediary—"the watering from above," literally; and the intermediaries serve for this matter only the service of a mere channel, although it is not so with regard to other matters and to another effluence. "And gives it rest"—the intent is that Yesod makes rest for Malkhut by this effluence, and no benefit is drawn from it to Yesod; because this effluence is to set Malkhut right and to adorn her, alone. For this effluence is like the first rainfall [revi'ah] upon the earth, which is for the preparing of the ground, to plough and to sow, and not to make what is sown grow. And therefore he said "and gives it rest"—meaning that this benefit is for Malkhut alone. But after this tikkun he pours into her the effluence that is fit to beget, which is the coupling after the tikkun and the adornment of the bride. And then the effluence is to make fruit, which are the souls that are poured forth from above in the secret of the union of the groom and his bride. And this is "and it yields fruit"—for the souls are the fruit of the Tree; and this is the matter of the second rainfall, which is to make the existence of the seeds sprout. "And makes seeds grow"—this is the matter of the third rainfall, which is the effluence poured forth to make grow and to make splendid the plantings and the seeds, which are the souls; and this is "and makes seeds grow." And they are a parable for marital relations in the last three months, of which it is explained in the Gemara (Niddah, fol. 31a) that they are good for the child and for the mother—namely, that the child comes forth vigorous. And from our flesh we behold God: for so it is above—when the effluence increases upon the plantings, the plantings multiply and grow. And the witness to this is the matter of the soul that comes in the waning of the moon or in its fullness, expounded in the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 98). "And it is then rest for all"—meaning: when the effluence is in these two times, which are the second and the third rainfall, then by this benefit and rest are drawn to all: to Tiferet and Yesod, which are the secret of the river and the secret of the male, and to Malkhut, which is the secret of the female, as is known. For in the coupling there is rest for the male and rest for the female, in the secret of "the Shekhinah among the lower ones is a need on high." "And this is rest for the garden, and this one makes rest in it." He aimed to explain that, although we say "and this is rest for all," the intent is not that it is rest for them equally. Rather, the rest of the Shekhinah is drawn from the river itself; and this is what he says, "and this is rest for the garden"—by means of the said river there is benefit and repose for the Shekhinah. But it is not the rest of the river, [in the sense] that the Shekhinah makes repose for him; rather, it is drawn to him from above on her account. And this is what he says, "and this one makes rest in it"—meaning, the river makes repose, respite and ease in her; and not that she makes the repose for him. Rather, he makes his rest there, and the rest is drawn to him from above on her account, through the river's coupling, until abundant effluence is drawn to him from above. And it is a parable of a weary man who stops to rest in some place: it is not the place that makes rest for him, but he makes his rest there. "As it is said, 'for in it He rested,'" etc. Neither of the verses is specific to his proof, for each of them admits of being explained in two ways. Either we say [that] "for in it He rested" means: [she] rested in Yesod, and not [in] Malkhut; or we say [that] "in it" means: in the garden, which is Malkhut, Yesod rested and reposed. And so the verse "and He rested on the seventh day"—we can explain it in these two ways: the one, meaning that Yesod rested in Malkhut, which is the Sabbath day; or it means that Malkhut rested on the seventh day, which is Yesod—for of both of them the name "seventh day" is correctly predicated, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, under the entry "Sabbath" and under the entry "days." And he aimed to explain from these two verses the two aspects—the rest of Malkhut and the rest of Yesod—for from the superfluity of the verses we expound one thus and one thus; for if you do not say so, why are [both] needed? Rather, [it is] as we have explained. And because on the face of it one [sense] is implied—namely, that Malkhut rested and reposed in Yesod, which on the face of it is the more accepted—therefore he took up first the second verse and said "for in it He rested," that is, the additional verse, which comes to teach us the resting of Yesod in Malkhut; for the resting of Malkhut in Yesod is the first verse, which is "and He rested on the seventh day." And this is what he aimed at in reversing the order of the verses—as if he said: Know that Yesod rested and reposed in Malkhut, for it is written "for in it He rested." What will you say—that this is the resting of Malkhut in Yesod? For this he said, "and He rested on the seventh day," meaning the resting of Malkhut in Yesod—behold, it is [already] written; for they are two verses: the first for the resting of Malkhut in Yesod, and the second for the resting of Yesod in Malkhut. This is the way according to this reading, and it is the more correct reading. And there are books that read, above: "and makes seeds grow, and it is then rest for the garden, and the garden is rest in it, as it is written, 'for in it He rested,'" etc. And it is possible to settle it [thus]: that the intent, with regard to the union, is the two aspects in Malkhut—her manifestation that is united with her husband, which ascends to be united, and her manifestation that remains in its place, in the secret of the manifestations.

And behold, the manifestation that ascends—its rest is in her husband himself, who is united with it. And her lower manifestation has rest, but not in her husband himself, for he is not united with it but with the upper manifestation alone. And of these two aspects he spoke. Of the aspect that remains, which is the lower aspect, he said "and it is then rest for the garden"—meaning: repose and contentment are drawn to the garden, but not that her rest is with him himself. And of the second aspect he said "and the garden is rest in it," that is, in him himself—which is the manifestation that ascends to be united. And he brought proof for this matter from the two verses. First, "for in it He rested," that is, in him himself, in the secret of the aspect that is united with her husband above. And the second, "and He rested on the seventh day," which means that He poured forth rest upon the seventh day; but it is not evident from it that [it is] in him himself, as [in] the first verse, which said "for in it He rested," that is, in him himself. And therefore he put first the verse "for in it He rested," because from it it is compelled that "and He rested on the seventh day" is not in him himself—since it did not say "in it" in that verse. "The secret of the matter," etc.—meaning, the sum of the secret of the whole matter is that there is none who gives contentment to Malkhut but Yesod, in the secret of the river from its beginning to its end, that is, the Vav, which is the river, as is well known. And by this the word "These" will be understood: for the intent is not "these are generations, and not others"—for there are no others besides them—but this is its explanation: "These are the generations of Noah"—Noah is the master of generations, and none other. And the word "These," which invalidates, does not invalidate generations; rather, it invalidates [another] master of generations—for there is no master of generations but Yesod. And this is what is meant by "the secret of the matter," etc. "Come and see: in like manner, Noah below was the holy covenant." Now he comes to explain "Noah, Noah," which means two rests, as explained above. And to indicate that the intent is Yesod, which is what is hinted at in Noah, he said "Noah was the holy covenant"—meaning: Noah was the chariot for Yesod, which is kayyama kaddisha, whose meaning is "holy covenant." "And therefore he is called 'a man of the ground'"—meaning, husband [ba'al] of the ground; the intent is: husband of Malkhut, who is called "ground." "And we have learned a secret: for Noah," etc. He wished to prove that Yesod has no place into which to pour except Malkhut—lest we say that it is true that Malkhut does not receive from any but Yesod, yet it is still possible that Yesod pours into something other than Malkhut. For this he said, "we have learned a secret," etc., "Noah needed the ark," etc.—the intent being that just as Malkhut needs Yesod, so Yesod needs Malkhut; as he goes on to explain, that there is no subsistence for the generations of Yesod except by means of Malkhut, as he concludes. "Who is the ark? This is the Ark of the Covenant," etc. It was difficult for him, for the correlation of the ark, which is Malkhut, is correlated only with the aspect of Yesod, which is Noah. For [it is] like the head-tefillin, which is the male, and the female correlated with it is the hand-tefillin; and so day in relation to night, and so the sun in relation to the moon, and so the etrog with the species that are in the lulav. And therefore it would be fitting, since Noah is Yesod, that his wife be Malkhut, and she is a correlative aspect. But that Noah, who is a human being, should be correlated with an ark of gopher wood—this is certainly not correlative. For this he said that, on the contrary, the aspect of Malkhut in respect of Yesod is found only in the ark. And the proof is from the Ark where the Torah is: Scripture called it "the Ark of the Covenant"—meaning that Malkhut is called "ark" [aron] and "ark" [tevah] in respect of her joining to Yesod, and this is "the Ark of the Covenant." And now, since Noah is Yesod, that which is correlated with Yesod, which is Noah, is none but the ark. And this is what he says: "And Noah and the ark below were thus, after the pattern of above"—meaning, they are correlated, even though Noah is a human being and this is an ark of wood. And he proved the matter from Scripture, in his saying "Of Noah, 'covenant' is written"—meaning, Scripture testified to his being a chariot for Yesod, as [in] "and I will establish My covenant with you," etc. "And until the covenant was established in him," etc.—meaning: after he proved that Noah is Yesod, he wished to prove also that the ark is Malkhut; and this is what he says, "and until the covenant was established in him"—meaning: since we see that he did not merit to enter the ark until he was at the grade of covenant, it appears that the ark is Malkhut, and he did not merit to enter within Malkhut until he was "covenant," which is Yesod. And this is what Scripture says: "and I will establish My covenant with you, and you shall come into the ark"—meaning: when I establish My covenant with you, that is, that he be a chariot for Yesod, then he will merit to enter within the ark, which is Malkhut. "And then the ark was the Ark of the Covenant"—meaning: when Noah, who is called "covenant," is within the ark, then the ark is called the Ark of the Covenant. And [so] the matter of the ark and Noah is settled—their being correlated with one another in a complete relation. And this is what he says: "Ark and Noah—all after the manner of above," etc.—meaning: just as Noah did not enter the ark until he was "covenant," it appears that Malkhut has no effluence or receiving except from Yesod. And since, in order to keep seed alive, he needed to enter the ark, it appears that Yesod has no place apart from Malkhut. And the intent in this is to explain to us what Scripture said, "These," which invalidated the former ones: that there is none who pours into Malkhut but Yesod, and Yesod has no recipient but Malkhut. And this is "Ark and Noah—all after the manner of above," as explained: that there is no livelihood or subsistence or generations for Noah except by means of the ark, and there is no existence for the ark except through Noah. "Noah was a righteous man—so it is, certainly, after the manner," etc. It was difficult for him: according to what he has now explained—that the intent of Scripture in the matter of "These are the generations of Noah: Noah" is Yesod, which makes generations, and it invalidated [any other], for no other makes generations; and it said twice "Noah, Noah," which are two rests, rest for Malkhut and rest for Yesod—if so, it is difficult, for the verse is superfluous in saying "a righteous man." And he explained that the aspect of his being called "righteous" is not the same as the aspect of his being called "Noah." For he is called "Noah" on account of the generations and the souls, as explained at the beginning of our discussion; but he is called "righteous" from his aspect of being the subsistence of Malkhut—that is to say, from the aspect of Yesod's pouring into Malkhut the effluence without which she has no subsistence. And this is what he says: "So it is, certainly, after the manner of above"—the intent being that just as Yesod has yet another aspect besides the generations, so [too] Noah, who was a chariot for him, [was so] in this aspect as well. And this is what he said, "after the manner of above"—meaning, in all the supernal aspects. "And therefore it is written, 'and the righteous one is the foundation of the world.'" Meaning: he comes to explain that the aspect of Yesod in which it is called "righteous" is on account of Malkhut's having no existence without him—not in the aspect of the souls, but in the aspect of the sustenance and the effluence and the subsistence of Malkhut. And he proved the matter from the verse "and the righteous one is the foundation of the world"; and the intent is that he is the foundation [yesod] of Malkhut, which is the lower world, and she has no existence without him—like a foundation, which is the place of the building and makes it stand, and without which it has no standing or footing. And this is what he says: "and the earth is sustained upon this; for he," etc.—meaning: the existence of the intrinsic subsistence is only by means of Yesod. "And who is he? This is the Righteous One"—meaning: and what is the name and the title that delimits and defines this aspect? You must say: "This is the Righteous One"—[the name] hints at this aspect, as it is written, "and the righteous one is the foundation of the world." If so, it appears of necessity that the word "righteous" hints at the aspect of the subsistence of Malkhut; and this is what Scripture aimed at in saying "a righteous man"—the intent being that he had the aspect of subsistence as well; that in respect of this aspect too he was a chariot for Yesod. And this is what he says: "And Noah is called 'righteous' below"—meaning that he was a chariot for him in this aspect as well. "And the secret of all," etc.—meaning: he proved the matter from Scripture, which said "Noah walked." And if it should arise in the mind that Noah was a chariot for Yesod only in respect of the generations alone, why did Scripture say "with God," etc.—whose intent is that his walking was always with the Shekhinah, who is called "God" [Elohim]? For the aspect of the generations is only from time to time. Rather, certainly [it is] as we have said. "'With God,' etc.—that he never separated from Him"—meaning that the Shekhinah is always with Yesod in union. It appears that he was a chariot also in respect of the perpetual effluence that is poured forth for sustenance. And therefore it is fitting that she not be separated from him, for she has no existence without him. "And [so as] to be on earth after the manner of above"—meaning, in all the aspects that are in Yesod, as explained. "'A righteous man'—the foundation of the world; 'covenant of peace,'" etc. It was difficult for him: granted that it should say "righteous," as we have said—what does "man" come for? For "man" is the very same as "righteous," that is, "husband," as in the saying "the man of God," which means husband of the Shekhinah. For this he resolved that "man" is another aspect besides these two; namely, that Yesod is called "man" when the Shekhinah is clothed in the force of judgment, when she is a sword of war; and Yesod pours into her and sets the blood of war in peace—then he is called "man." And this is what he says, "covenant of peace"—meaning, Yesod is called "covenant of peace"; and his being called "covenant of peace" is in this aspect: that he brings peace to the world, which exists in the force of the judgment that is poured forth from Malkhut reddened with judgment. And this is what he says, "the peace of the world"—in this aspect Noah is called "man." And this is what he says of Noah himself: "'a man of the ground'—certainly"; the intent being that he is "man" and pours forth peace and compassion when Malkhut is called "ground" [adamah]—the intent being: when she is red [adumah], from the side of the force of the redness of judgment. And it is an aspect new beyond the two preceding ones. "And therefore, 'and Noah found favor,'" etc.—meaning: because Noah was a chariot for Yesod from the side of all these aspects, it was said, of the rank of his chariot-hood, "and Noah found favor"—which was not said of any other. For how many others there were who were a chariot for Yesod, and "found favor" was not said of them! Rather, certainly the reason is that he included all the aspects that Yesod has with Malkhut, which is not so with the others. Thus far the explanation of the passage. And the general rule that emerges from the passage is that Yesod pours into Malkhut, and Malkhut does not receive from any other. And by this the view of those who say that there are two channels from Netzach and Hod to Malkhut is annulled; rather, it is impossible for any sefirah among the sefirot to pour into Malkhut except by means of Yesod. Further, Scripture said (Isaiah 57), "and none understands that because of the evil the righteous one is gathered in"—meaning, gathered in from pouring forth. It appears that all the effluence depends on Yesod, which is the Righteous One; for if not so, how did it say that the righteous one alone "is gathered in"? And so they expounded of the Assembly of Israel, which is Malkhut, that she is likened to a dove, etc. And so it is said (Isaiah 57:1), "The righteous one has lost," etc.—he has lost the Lady [Matronita]. And the like. All this indicates that there is none who pours into Malkhut but Yesod. And it is indeed true that we find that Netzach pours into Malkhut, and likewise Hod; and likewise, above, in the matter of the thread of lovingkindness from the side of Chesed, and the scarlet thread from the side of Gevurah. The intent is not that they have other channels; rather, the intent is that all is by means of Yesod, which is the passage for all sustenance and effluence that is poured into Malkhut. And just as we insist upon this of her, so we insist in the matter of Yesod, that he has no place into which to pour but her, as is proved from the passage mentioned above.

A further channel is drawn from Yesod to Malkhut; for it is the course of the great river that issues from the Edens [delights] of Binah to water the garden. And by means of this channel he takes hold of Malkhut, to couple her with her husband above; and by way of this channel she was driven out, through iniquities. And concerning this channel we have seen in the Ta'amei ha-Mitzvot of Ibn Farchi, in the negative commandment not to drink libation-wine [yein nesekh], and these are his words there: "There are two orifices in the supernal Covenant. From the one he pours to the Shekhinah, and that effluence which goes out is called 'sweet waters'; and from there go out many reasons [te'amim, 'flavors'] of Torah, which are called 'water,' as it is said (Isaiah 55:1), 'Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the water'—and 'water' is nothing but Torah. And the second orifice pours to the powers of impurity, and it is called 'libation-wine,'" etc. Thus far his words, in brief.
Behold, from his language it is implied that these words of his are words of received tradition [kabbalah]. And the matters prove themselves of their own accord, for "from my flesh I behold God."

And behold, in a human being there are two orifices: the one to pour into his female, to beget in his likeness, and the second to expel the foul matter and the residue. Further, we have found a companion for him in a book whose author's name is not known to us—it is a commentary on the Song of Songs and a commentary on Parashat Terumah, and its language in some places is Aramaic—and these are its words, in the explanation of the letters, on the letter Ayin: "And now we have to show, in the secret of Ayin—their source—what the image is; thus it hints: secrets hinted and concealed were engraved. Beneath the chariot of the Holy King is the secret of the holy covenant of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is called 'the righteous one, the foundation of the world'; and it is the wellspring that pours into the holy well, which is the Lady.

"And those two heads of the Ayin are the secret of these two orifices that are in the mouth of the member. And they are two wellsprings: the holy wellspring of the right is the nourishment of the Lady, and from there draw nourishment the prophets and the pious and the blameless and the righteous, who delight in the Garden of Eden. And the second wellspring is the nourishment of the bands of impurity and of the angels that accuse in the world; and from there is the nourishment of Balaam the wicked; and from there comes the good [fortune] of the wicked, who prosper in their ways in this world. And concerning this it is written (Job 38:13), 'and the wicked are shaken out of it'—with a large Ayin—for their nourishment is from the second head of the Ayin." Thus far [its] words.

And his words are clear, being a support for the tradition of Ibn Farchi that I wrote above, who said that in Yesod there are two channels, one holy and one for the dross, the smeltings of gold. He further wrote these very things in the explanation of the letter Tzadi: "The Tzadi has two heads, which hints at the attribute of the Righteous One [tzaddik]; and those are two holy wellsprings. One pours and draws from there to the Lady, and from there the upper and the lower ones are blessed—'for there YHVH commanded the blessing,' etc. And this is the wellspring from which the holy angels were created, and many holy souls were created. And the second wellspring pours to His left side (of the Holy One, blessed be He), and from there is the nourishment of the strange woman and the adulterous woman. And if Israel are worthy, that wellspring is enclosed and the holy wellspring of the right is opened; and if not, that wellspring is opened which pours [to] the strange woman—the powers of impurity that sit outside the supernal academy, which are called 'others' [acherim]," etc. "And from the second wellspring—from there go out [draw nourishment] demons and spirits and night-spirits [lilin] and harmful spirits and the wicked, from the left side," etc. Thus far [its] words.

And his words are clear and agree with our matter.
