And there is some proof for this in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 74a), and these are its words: "Rabbi Yehudah said: At the time when the righteous multiply in the world, the Assembly of Israel sends up good fragrances and is blessed by the Holy King, and her face shines. And at the time when the wicked multiply in the world, as it were, the Assembly of Israel does not send up fragrance, and she tastes of the bitter Other Side [Sitra Achra]. Then it is written, 'He cast down from heaven to earth the beauty [tiferet] of Israel,' and her face is darkened." Thus far [its] words.

And the intent is that when there are in this world righteous and pious ones, then by means of their good deeds the Shekhinah draws effluence from above through their merit; and they are the female waters [mayin nukvin] that she pours forth in order to receive the male waters [mayin dekhurin], as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with God's help. And so is the matter with regard to the effluence and the blessing. And this is what it says, "sends up fragrances"—meaning, she sends up the fragrance of the deeds of the righteous, as in the matter of (Genesis 27:27) "See, the fragrance of my son is as the fragrance of a field"—for he smelled in him that it was from the supernal field. And when there are no righteous in this world, the effluence does not descend, and Malkhut seeks the waters of lovingkindness [chesed] and there are none. And then the power of judgment is aroused through the claims of the husks, and they are poured upon by way of that evil channel; and then she tastes [what is] more bitter than death. And this is "and she tastes of the Other Side," etc.—meaning, she tastes bitterness from the place of gall, from impurity. And accordingly it is compelled that there be in Yesod two channels: one for blessing, from the side of the right, and one for bitterness, from the side of the left, by which dross is poured to her, from the side of the smeltings of gold, and she receives bitter dross. And one who has eyes of intellect and is of the reapers of the field will understand, by this premise, the matter of the sin of the son of the Israelite woman (Leviticus 24), which is closed in the Zohar, and they revealed it to those who know; and we shall not explain, because "it is the glory of God to hide a matter." And the matter will be understood when you are precise about the language of the Zohar in Parashat Emor (fol. 106a), which said there, "the last Heh was the female," etc. And with this he was covering over his mother, and he cursed himself, God forbid. "But we will bless Yah." And the reason for there being in the Righteous One these two orifices is that the Righteous One was the governor who poured forth to the upper and the lower, to the inner and to the outer ones, and on him hung the sustenance of all created entities, those of the right and those of the left, before the diminishment; and also whenever Malkhut ascends to her place, to the height [ha-Ramatah], to her husband, for there is her house—sitting at the head of the corner, as will be explained in the Gate of the Diminishment [of the Moon]—then it is compelled that the Righteous One be the one who feeds the world; and then the created entities are poured upon by means of these two orifices: the one for the sustenance, to the sons of the palace, and the second, the residue, to the dogs. And if the questioner should ask, "Who has put residue among the holy things?"—this will be explained in the Gate of Substitutes. And in these matters brevity is fitting, out of regard for the honor of the Omnipresent.

After we have, in the preceding chapters, summed up the tradition of the channels as it is found in the mouth of all the Kabbalists, early and late, we shall now broaden the explanation and explain the matter of these channels according to their aspect, and according to what is understood by us from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, after the whole of the Glossary of Titles, with their explanation, has passed through our mind—as their aspect and their division and their matter will be explained. And after looking into the matter of the bond of the sefirot according to Rashbi, as will be explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance—and there it is explained that they are bound by means of their equivalents; that is to say, that Keter is united with the nine sefirot by means of the portion of Keter that is in all the sefirot, and Chokhmah by means of the portion of Chokhmah that is in all the sefirot, and Binah by means of the portion of Binah that is in all the sefirot. And after the intellect has been well strengthened in this premise, by the power of inquiry and correct discernment, as will be explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, the inquirer will discern with his intellect that the channels vary according to the aspects, by the thousands and the myriads, just as the inclusions of the sefirot have no number. And the example of this: when the faces turn, and the face of Keter shines upon Chokhmah with the shining face that is in it from the side of its own self, Keter, then it is compelled that Chokhmah show opposite it a face correlative to the face of Keter [which is the Keter-within-Chokhmah]; and then they are united and bound in a mighty union and bond, by means of the shining of the faces and the drawing-forth of the light, in the likeness of the light that goes out from the eye, as explained above at the beginning of chapter one. And this is a superior union, by means of which Chokhmah receives the names [effluence] of Keter and its very aspect, because their union and their channel are by means of Keter itself, pouring and receiving; and this is the most superior union among all the unions. And then three aspects are distinguished between them, besides the three aspects mentioned above, as explained. And these aspects are: the aspect of the Keter that pours, and the aspect of the Keter that receives, and the aspect of the middle channel between them, which raises the light and pours it—behold, their union is complete. And at times they are united by means of the aspects of Chokhmah. The example of this: that Keter reveals the face of Chokhmah that it has, in order to pour into Chokhmah; and then Chokhmah reveals its face, the face of Chokhmah that it has; and then they are united in a mighty union by means of the faces that are equal, for good; and there comes to be between them the channel that befits them, according to the aspect of their union.

And behold, this union is superior, but not as the first. For in the first, of which we said that the union is by means of Keter, Chokhmah receives from Keter effluence as befits Keter—for from Keter to Keter all is poured—and it receives a concealed effluence according to the measure of the one that pours and the one that receives. But with Chokhmah, even though it receives a superior effluence, nonetheless it is not as the first, for this is the effluence of Chokhmah, since from Chokhmah to Chokhmah it went forth. And in this way the inquirer shall judge for all the unions that this sefirah has with the one above it. And from the union of this sefirah will be understood their union one with another, one with them all and them all with one; and so for all the sefirot. And now, according to this way, when we wish to pour forth compassion in the secret of the compassion of Keter, we unite Chokhmah with Keter in the aspect of Keter, and Binah with Keter in the aspect of Keter, and Chesed with Chokhmah in the aspect of Keter, and Gevurah with Binah in the aspect of Keter. And let no man's heart fail him at our saying that Binah receives from Keter in the aspect of the Keter that is in it and pours into Gevurah in the aspect of the Keter that is in it; for it is known that their inclusion of ten ascends without limit and without end. And it turns out, accordingly, [that there are] how many faces to the awesome faces, and how many backs to the backs that are seen. And when it receives, it receives in the aspect of the Keter-within-Keter-within-Binah; and when it pours, it pours in the aspect of the Keter-within-Malkhut-within-Binah. And so for all the sefirot. For in this way the aspects will be; and accordingly the pouring-forth is found [to be] the pouring-forth of Keter, from Keter to Keter, down to the last grade among the grades, and the compassion [is] simple compassion, in the manner that befits Keter.

And further, it is fitting that Keter be united in all the sefirot through the Keter that is in them, at that same moment; and so Chokhmah, and so for all the sefirot. And then the effluence is an effluence bright and radiant, as the radiance of those that shine. And when, God forbid, judgment is poured forth, then the sefirot receive from one another by means of the aspect of Gevurah that is in each one of them; and then the judgment is poured forth with force, "and God hastens to do it," and does not delay the day of its coming. And according to this way we may infer to the other actions. And with this premise it will be understood, manifestly, [that there is] a compelling necessity for the governance—as for the actions—of union, in the agreement of all the sefirot, in the binding of limb to limb and aspect to aspect, until their agreeing together upon that action; and they are all clothed in the likeness of that action and are transformed according to the aspect of their action. And by this the channels vary in their aspect by the thousands and the myriads; for they are always united according to their bond and their union, which is the union of all the aspects and all the divisions in complete equality—and so the channels, for the aspects and the channels are all one thing. And it has been reported to us that there exists a book whose name is Sefer ha-Tzinorot (the Book of the Channels), which speaks of the matter of the channels specifically and counts six hundred thousand channels. And for our iniquities we have not merited it; and they say that it is found among our brethren in the city of Fez, may their Rock and Redeemer preserve them. And it is our wish now to divide the matter of the divisions by which it is possible for the sefirot to receive one from another: whether from Keter to Keter down to Malkhut, or from Chokhmah to Chokhmah down to Malkhut, or from Binah to Binah down to Malkhut; and so for all the sefirot—from Chesed to Chesed, and from Gevurah to Gevurah, and from Tiferet to Tiferet, and from Netzach to Netzach, and from Hod to Hod, and from Yesod to Yesod, and from Malkhut to Malkhut. And by this all the sefirot are found to be in agreement upon one action, in the secret of the channels, all included and in agreement upon that action. And not only this, from sefirah to sefirah, but even within a sefirah itself, in the secret of its pouring into its parts, it will be likewise in this way—for example, from Keter to Keter, and all within Keter. And the inclusions of the ten sefirot that are in Keter are found all opened and shining with the light of Keter, or with the light of Chokhmah, or with the light of Binah, and so with the other lights that are in the sefirot; and so for the parts of the other sefirot—that the sefirah of Chokhmah be opened entirely in [the light of] Keter, or entirely in the light of Chokhmah, or entirely in the light of Binah, and so with the other lights of the sefirot.

And behold, there are yet [further] aspects. The example of this: if Keter pours, through the Keter that is in it, into the Chokhmah-within-Chokhmah, and from the Chokhmah-within-Chokhmah into the Binah-within-Binah, and from the Binah-within-Binah into the Chesed-within-Chesed, and so for all the sefirot in this way—there are many kinds of divisions, which it is impossible to grasp except by a corporeal depiction: that we depict before us ten circles, and in each and every circle ten faces, which are the ten aspects of the ten sefirot that are in each one of the ten sefirot; and the faces revolve, face opposite face, as their rule requires. For example: the face of the Malkhut-within-Keter with the face of the Keter-within-Chokhmah, and so the Keter in them all with the Malkhut-within-Keter—for then the effluence is of another kind; and afterward we turn the face of the Yesod-within-Keter to the face of the Keter in them all—the effluence will be of [yet] another kind. And so for all the ten faces of Keter: there are ten kinds of effluence and ten kinds of channels, for according to the change of the effluence the channels change. And now, if we turn Chokhmah alone ten times, for each one of the ten faces of Keter, without the faces of the remaining sefirot changing or turning, the number of the kinds of effluence will amount to one hundred.

And the matter of these divisions cannot be set down in writing; and if a person wishes to accustom himself to them, let him occupy himself with the figure depicted before him, and conduct himself in it with inquiry for many days, until YHVH enlightens the eyes of his intellect. For the power of the pen fails to prolong these matters further—unless this matter be passed on from mouth to mouth, or the discerning one delve into them with his intellect by means of this figure.

And behold, with this the Gate is concluded; and blessed is the true Helper, to whom wisdom belongs. And in these matters we fear error and trust in pardon; for of such as this it is said (Proverbs 5:19), "in her love you shall err [tishgeh] always"—these are matters which a person does not grasp except through difficulty.

<small>(Says the editor: These ten circles, in which the ten sefirot are depicted—let the inquirer picture [them] as though the circles were revolving in their rotation, and then he will understand the intent of the author, peace be upon him. And the matter is: when the inquirer examines the facing of the sefirot—for example, the aspect of the Chokhmah-within-Chokhmah to the aspect of the Chokhmah-within-Keter, or the aspect of the Binah-within-Binah to the aspect of the Binah-within-Chokhmah or within Keter—then he must imagine and think as though the circle revolves and the Chokhmah-within-Chokhmah, in the circle of Chokhmah, stands opposite the Chokhmah that is in the circle of Keter; and so all of them. Then he will understand and discern the intent of the author, and will know it in truth, with the help of the God of knowledges, YHVH. Thus far [his] words):</small>
The Eighth Gate: Essence and Governance.

After we occupied ourselves in the preceding Gate with the matter of the channels in all the particulars of their parts, we have seen fit to explain in this Gate the matter of the sefirot in their essence as it is apprehended by us—whether lovingkindness [Chesed], or judgment [Din], or compassion [Rachamim]—and something of the way of their governance, as far as is apprehended by us.
Chapter One:

Most of the Kabbalists have agreed that the sefirot are a power that includes many opposites. And the parable for this is the will of the soul: for it turns to many actions, even if they are almost opposite—such as love and hatred, and irritation and laughter, and the other opposite actions like these. And so is the matter in the sefirot, which have in them judgment and compassion: at times [a sefirah] clothes itself in judgment, and at times in compassion. And just as it is in the hand of a person to receive and to bestow—and each of these two actions divides into two: whether receiving good or receiving evil, whether bestowing good or bestowing evil—and likewise many [other] actions; and it is a small limb in a person, conducting itself according to the will of the soul: so is the matter of the sefirot. There is in each and every sefirah the power to effect a thousand thousands of thousands of differing actions, each and every one according to its matter and its power and its apprehension and its knowledge and its imprint [teva], which the Emanator impressed in it. And we know that this premise which we have set forth will be difficult for the inquirer, and he will say: if so, one sefirah would have sufficed—why did He emanate ten, since the one is a power that includes many opposites, and by it He could effect all the actions? And to this we answer that they were needed for the reason explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation, in chapter six: that for a human being to apprehend the concealed—that is to say, the Godhead—this revelation was needed, up to ten revelations, one below another, so that by this means the created entities might apprehend a little of the knowledge of the exaltedness of the Emanator.

And further: even though we say that there is in each sefirah a power that includes many opposites, nonetheless there are still many things such that what this one pours forth, that one does not pour forth—as they, of blessed memory, said (Mo'ed Katan, fol. 28): "Children, life, and sustenance—the matter does not depend on merit, but the matter depends on mazal." And the meaning is: "merit" is Chesed, and "mazal" is Keter. And the intent is that, although most of the kindnesses and the good things are drawn from Chesed, and its name proves it, nonetheless children, life, and sustenance are not in the hand of this attribute; rather, their principal [source] is in Keter, for it is the supernal mazal. And even though the commentators explained otherwise and said that "merit" is Gevurah, nonetheless [it is] in accordance with these words of ours [that] it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 10, fol. 24), and as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, under the entry "merit." And in this way we shall explain that Binah receives those who return; therefore it is called Repentance [Teshuvah]. And it is there that forgiveness and atonement principally depend, by the power of the supernal Keter that overflows upon it. And in this way vengeance is in Gevurah; and so various actions are assigned to the sefirot, and what is assigned to this one is not assigned to that one. And what was said above, that it is a power that includes many opposites, will be in this way: that in the action that is drawn from it, it must effect many opposites—like the eye, whose action is sight, yet it includes opposites: evil sight or good sight, little sight or much sight. And so is the matter in the sefirot. The example of this: one who returns to YHVH with all his power and with all his intent, like the repentance of King David, peace be upon him, and all the other penitents who returned to YHVH with all that is possible within the bounds of repentance—these, certainly, their repentance is superior and is most accepted, to raise their soul to the choice grade of penitents. And when the sinner does not return to YHVH in this grade, then his repentance is accepted, but his soul will not ascend to that choice grade to which the repentance of King David, peace be upon him, ascended. And likewise one who returns and mortifies his soul with a slight mortification; and there is one who confesses his sin only; and likewise one who does not return until the crushing of the soul. And such things, which exist in parts of parts, the knowledge of human beings cannot take in—only the divine knowledge and power, which belong to Him, may He be blessed and exalted, in the sefirot. And all these divisions are for good, and to reward with good reward in the World to Come. And there is likewise, in this way, [the power] to punish one who did not afflict himself on Yom Kippur with the five afflictions that depend on Yom Kippur, which is Binah, certainly. For it is not fitting to punish one who ate to his fill as one who ate an olive's bulk or two olives' bulk; and one who ate and drank is not equal to one who had marital relations; and likewise one who had marital relations is not equal to one who anointed himself. And such are the distinctions that actually occur, which human knowledge cannot take in, still less judge—only the divine power.

And the matter of the negative commandments and the positive is that they are divided and dependent upon all ten sefirot. And although all of them in their generality are the 248 positive commandments in Chesed and the 365 negative commandments in Gevurah, nonetheless their particulars are in the ten sefirot, as we have said. And their punishment, or their reward, or their claim in judgment, or the tikkun of the ruin that the sinner has ruined, depends upon the sefirah at which the commandment hints. And its particulars and its laws and its reward and its punishment, in general and in particular, are [by] the power that includes many opposites, of which we have spoken. For if it were a power fitted to the sefirah and belonging to it, then if it does good it would not punish, and if it punishes it would not do good; and if it increases reward for one it would not lessen [it] for others, and if it lessens [it] for one it would not increase [it] for others. Rather, certainly, it is compelled that they be a power that includes opposites, to judge the sinner or to reward the doer, whether little or much. And all these actions are by the will of the Emanator, who pours His providence upon them and by means of His sefirot, as we explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels. And in this way is the governance in the world. And the question does not arise, to say: let all the commandments be in one power, and the judging itself in that power—for several reasons, [among them] the reasons that I explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation and that we explained above.

And further: because it is not the commandments that necessitated the sefirot, but the sefirot that necessitated the commandments. For in our doing the commandment we unite the power that hints at the commandment, which is a branch of the sefirah, with its root; and this is the will of our Maker, that we unite His sefirot—for by their light we see light, for in them is His Self—and it is the glory of the kingship of the [King of the] world that we set right His palaces and His thrones as is fitting, so that His Shekhinah may be among us. And in some of the commandments there is power to remove the spirit of impurity from the earth, "and the idols shall be utterly cut off"; and this is the glory of the King of the world, that we contend with those who rise up against Him. And concerning this the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin, fol. 111): "'and opened her mouth without measure [chok]'—[this is] one who has not fulfilled even one statute [chok]," which is one commandment: even though he has not transgressed a negative commandment, nonetheless he has no portion in His attributes, may He be blessed, since he has not set right or united there any attribute so that he might cleave to it. We can further answer, on that reason, in another manner, more seemly and acceptable: that the matter of the sefirot is the revelation of His powers, which are His effects and are included in His Self, as will be explained further in the Gate of Tzachtzachot; and this is for the sake of the governance. And lovingkindness and compassion and might and victory and thanksgiving and righteousness and kingship—all of them are attributes included in Him and concealed in His Self. And no multiplicity befalls the Emanator by this, God forbid, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, and we shall also explain in the Gate of Tzachtzachot, in chapters three [and] four. And now, will the questioner ask why a person has made, in his garment, sleeves, or leggings, or sheaths for the digits? No. For we shall answer him that, since this is the garment for the body, and the body is the cause of the garment, it is compelled that the garment be correlated with the body in all its parts and in all its limbs. And since the sefirot are the revelation of His attributes, and are a garment to them, as we explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels, in chapter four—if so, the question does not arise, "why thus and not thus," as we have said.

And behold, in this way it has been explained how the question does not arise concerning the human body—why its limbs are thus and not thus, and why its hairs are thus, and all such things. For the body is a garment to the soul, and the soul reveals its actions by means of it—so much so that when [a person] sins and is defiled, that sin is depicted in the soul and afterward in the body, as the prophet testified in his reproofs (Isaiah 3), "The look of their faces testifies against them," etc. And so it says in the Zohar that at a time when there is pestilence in the city, God forbid, it is fitting for every person to cover his forehead, so that the Angel of Death not recognize his iniquities engraved on his forehead. And so the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit, fol. 30b): "Whoever eats meat and drinks wine on the eve of the Ninth of Av—his iniquities are engraved upon his bones, as it is said, 'and their iniquities were upon their bones.'" And all this is for the reason that the soul shows its actions in them, and the stains that are in it, it shows in the body.

And behold, it is known that the soul includes ten, as we explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter five, and as will be explained in the Gate of the Soul. And since the soul includes all the upper worlds, it is compelled that its garment be the mold and form of the soul, which is the form of the upper worlds. And this is what Scripture says (Job 19:26): "and from my flesh I behold God." If so, it turns out, accordingly, that it is compelled that its limbs be in this structure, and [with] these joints and these veins, which are the channels of the effluence that is poured to the limbs. And all these limbs [matters] are verified of themselves and need no proof; and they will be explained at length in the Gate of the Soul, in part two.
And behold, with this we have added instruction on the matter of the reason for the Emanation, in addition to what we explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation, with the help of Heaven.

After we set out in the preceding chapter the matter of the sefirot, and explained that they are a power that includes many opposites, we can say that this is the reason for their being called sefirot—from the term "sapphire stone" [even sappir]. For just as the sapphire has no particular color, but includes all the colors that are seen in it, so the sefirah includes all the opposites, as we have explained. And although each one has a known color, as we shall explain in the Gate of Colors, nonetheless in this aspect they are called sefirot, as we have explained. And they are also called sefirot from the term "telling" [sippur]; and so explained Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov in Sefer ha-Emunot, Gate 4, chapter 4, and these are his words: "In the Bahir I found: Why are they called sefirot? Because 'the heavens tell [mesapperim] the glory of God' (Psalms 19:2).

And the intent is that, just as speech and writing, by their delimiting, make plain—so as to be perceptible—the things concealed within the thought of the wise man, so the heavens indicate the Lord, blessed be He; for so the sefirot are what reveal the concealed thoughts and the forms that are separate from any body, [of which there is] no grasp and no depiction at all." Thus far his words; and [these are] the gracious words of a wise man. For the sefirot tell of, and set a limit to, what is not limited—though not literally a limit, God forbid, as we explained in the preceding gates. And there are those who explained [it] from the term "number" [mispar], for number is among the things that are limited. And although they are not limited relative to their simple root, they are limited relative to their action toward us, as we explained above (in Gate 2, chapter 1). And other commentators explained [it] from the term "telling" [sippur]; and the intent is that telling and speaking of them is permitted, which is not so of the Ein Sof. And there are those who explained [it] from the term "border" [sefar], as in "a city that is near the border," which is a term of boundary and limit; and the intent is that they set a limit to what is no limit at all—and the intent is not that they literally set a limit, but as we have explained. And what it is fitting to explain is that what we said in the preceding chapter—that the governance, and the reward and the punishment, are by means of a particular attribute—does not mean that He effects lovingkindness for them by means of the attribute of Chesed alone, God forbid; for if so, this is separation and cutting, God forbid. For once it is possible for the action to be by means of one of the sefirot, it turns out that it is possible for a sefirah to be separate, in its parts, by itself; and this is not of the truth. Rather, it is not fitting to picture action and governance in any sefirah by itself, since no sefirah acts by means of its own manifestation alone; rather, the governance is by means of all of them. And when we say that the action is by means of some sefirah, the intent is that when lovingkindness prevails in the sefirah, Malkhut receives their effluence, and then all of them are, in her, Chasadim [lovingkindnesses], and all of them agree toward the side of Chesed. And likewise Gevurah: when judgment and the Gevurot prevail in the sefirah, Malkhut receives their effluence, and then all of them are, in her, Gevurot, and all of them agree toward the side of Gevurah. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the book of the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 40a), and these are his words: "When this stone wishes to execute judgment upon Amalek, or upon the Other Side, and likewise upon the guilty, she takes from Gevurah, and all the sefirot are included in her, and in her they are all called Gevurot. And when she wishes to do favor and lovingkindness in the world, she takes from Chesed, and all the sefirot are included in her, and they are called Chasadim. And when she wishes to have compassion on the world, she takes from the central pillar, and all the sefirot are included in her, and they are called Rachamim [compassions]." Thus far [his] words.

Behold, he explained explicitly how the sefirot all agree toward the sefirah that prevails, and all by means of the last attribute, which governs the world, for in her is the principal governance. And what it is fitting to examine closely in this matter is that it is impossible that Chesed should agree toward the side of Gevurah, and likewise Gevurah toward the side of Chesed, since they are two opposites—this one judgment and that one lovingkindness. And how is it possible to say that what is lovingkindness should effect the power of judgment, and that what is judgment should effect the power of lovingkindness? And we answer that this matter is impossible except in that each one of them includes ten; and you will find that there is in Chesed the power of Gevurah, and there is in Gevurah the power of Chesed, and so for all the sefirot. And by means of this equality they are unified and become equal, as we shall explain in this Gate. And we need to explain the matter of "each one includes ten," so that the inquirer should not think that each one includes ten in the plain sense—that is, that there is in Chesed a recognizable part that is Gevurah, and likewise in Gevurah a recognizable part that is Chesed. For if so, God forbid, the sefirot turn out to be divided into parts and separated from one another; and what we had in mind to set right by our saying "each one includes ten" is spoiled by what follows from it, for [then] even each one is divided into ten parts. Rather, the intent is that no one can say "this is a part of Chesed" that does not include ten, nor of any part among the parts of the other sefirot that all the ten are not included in it; and likewise ten from ten, without end and without limit—everything includes ten upon ten, and ten from ten. And should you say: if so—that each one includes all of them—it now turns out, accordingly, that there is no difference among the sefirot, and all of them are equal; and if so, how do we say that this one is Gevurah and this one Chesed, and so for all of them? Since in Chesed there are ten and in Gevurah ten, all of them turn out equal, for good or for ill, God forbid. To this we answer with a premise that Rambam explained concerning the elements, in chapter 4 of the Laws of the Foundations of the Torah, and these are his words: "Every single body—of man and beast and wild animal and bird and fish and plant and metal and stone—its matter is joined together from fire and air and water and earth. And the four of them are mixed together, and each one of them is changed at the time of the mixing, until what is joined together from the four of them is found to be unlike any one of them when it is alone. And there is not in the mixture of them even one part that is fire by itself, or water by itself, or earth by itself, or air by itself; rather, all have been changed and have become another body. And every body that is joined together from the four of them—there are found in it cold and heat, moist and dry, as one. There are among them bodies in which the element of fire is strong, such as, etc.; and there are among them bodies in which the element of water is strong, etc. And in this way one body is found hotter than another hot body, and one body drier than another dry body; and [there are] bodies in which the cold alone is seen, and bodies in which the moist alone is seen, and bodies in which the cold and the dry are seen as one, equally, etc., or the heat and the dry as one, equally, etc." Thus far his words, for our matter.

And behold, by this premise a person can contemplate the sefirot: that the principal [thing] is the power of Gevurah, in which judgment is seen and not lovingkindness, and the power of Chesed, in which lovingkindness prevails and not judgment. And we needed all this so as not to make a separation, God forbid, as we have explained. And when this principle is fixed in the heart of the discerning, it will not be far from him to know how Chesed, when Gevurah prevails, can itself also effect Gevurah, since in Chesed too there is the power of Gevurah; and so for all the sefirot and in all the blendings. However, the matter of this agreement is, intrinsically, by means of the Diadem, which governs the world, for in her this blending is made. For in their own place it is impossible: for if we say that the agreement and the blending are in their place above, it turns out, God forbid, that nine sefirot are lacking, for all of them are Gevurot or Chasadim. Rather, perforce we say that in their place they are [in] their [own] blending, which their Emanator set in them. It is true that its being drawn to effect that action is by means of the Gevurot that are in them, or by means of the Chasadim that are in each and every sefirah, as we explained in the Gate of Channels, chapter 5. But that they should be turned to judgment and Gevurah, or to lovingkindness, altogether—this is impossible except by means of Malkhut specifically. And of this Rashbi, peace be upon him, was exact in his wording, in the passage that we copied, in that he said "and all the sefirot are included in her, and they are called Chasadim," etc.—meaning that first they are included in the stone, which is Malkhut, and then they are called Chasadim or Gevurot or Rachamim altogether. And the hint to their each including ten is in the way that Rashbi said in the book of the Tikkunim (Tikkun 47, fol. 81b), and these are his words: "For there is no sefirah that does not include ten, each one in its own dominion." Thus far [his] words. And it is clear. And he was exact in saying "in its own dominion"—meaning, even while its dominion, its [own] action, prevails in it, in the way that we have explained.

And now, after we have explained the matter of their including ten, we wish to explain the matter of the revelation of the ten in each and every one, for it is a wondrous rank. And the matter is that—besides their including ten in the way that we have explained, and this inclusion never falls short and never exceeds, just as it is impossible for the sefirot to be eleven, or nine, so too with regard to the inclusion—there is, however, a matter more important than this, which is not found in them except when there is abundant good: namely, that [the ten] be revealed in them, and each one of them be included in all of them; as if to say that all the ten sefirot that are in it appear, by reason of its having received from ten and its shining in ten. That is to say, Keter includes ten by reason of its being unified with ten. How so? It shines in the nine, and the nine shine in it, and they shine toward the face of Keter; so that ten shine in it. And so in Chokhmah, and so in Binah. How so? Binah pours forth effluence into the seven lower ones—here are seven that are included in her, and she is included in them; and the two upper ones shine in her and are included in her—here are nine; and further, her own face itself shines in her—here are ten. And so for all the sefirot. And by this, ten sefirot appear in all of them; and this is a manifestation choicer than the inclusion expounded above. And this manifestation is found more commonly in Malkhut, as we explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine." And the inquirer must keep his eyes open to this manifestation, which is not like the preceding manifestation. And this manifestation will at times be partial—that is, they will be included only in seven, which are the seven sefirot of the Structure; and this inclusion will not be of the importance and rank that it has when it is of ten, as we shall explain in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 5. And one should not wonder and say that a separation is seen in this, since only seven appear in it, and not ten. The reason is that, since all the ten are included in it, and [only] on account of the scantness of the light do they not all appear, but are concealed and do not act, it is not called separation. For such is the way of the sefirot: although they include ten, they act only from the one that prevails, and nonetheless it is not called separation, since all of them are included in it. And for all that, the one that prevails is the principal one—if in Chesed, Chesed; if in Gevurah, Gevurah. And so is the matter with these inclusions: because they received only from the seven, they were included only in seven. And now, accordingly, when we count in them ten times ten, which are a hundred, we mean this important inclusion. And when we count ten times a hundred, we mean to say that even those ten were shining in ten others; and so the number rises from ten to ten without end, and according as the number grows, it indicates the abundance of the inclusion. And likewise, at times we count seven times seven, indicating the seven days of the Structure, which were included in themselves; and so their number rises from seven to seven, by sevens—such as seven times seven, forty-nine, or forty-nine times forty-nine. And at times we compound the two numbers and say that the seven lower ones were included in ten; and now they come to seven times ten, which are seventy, or seven hundred—all according to the strengthening of the inclusion, as we have explained. And there is another aspect, namely that we say that the ten sefirot include seven; and the number and the inclusion rise in the manner of the preceding number. However, it indicates compassion more, since in this aspect the first three themselves were revealed, which is not so in the preceding aspects, in which they were revealed only in the lower ones; and it is clear. And all these aspects and their inclusion—their explanation has come in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim and in the commentators; and since the matters are scattered, one here and one there, and it would be burdensome for us to bring their proof, we have written them in brief; and they are agreed upon of themselves. Further, the sefirot include ten in another aspect, and these are the manifestations of the sefirot themselves. And the matter is that in Keter all the sefirot were revealed at the time of the Emanation, as we explained in the Gate of the Emanation; and on this account their manifestation must be there, as we shall explain the matter of the manifestations in the Gate of Manifestations.

And behold, these nine are spiritual beings, subtler than their own self that is revealed below, so that they are sources and a channel through which the life-force is poured to their lower manifestation. And when they were emanated in Chokhmah, there too the manifestation of eight sefirot remained; and the supernal Keter—its manifestation was emanated in her, so that they should not be nine, God forbid. And further, this was necessary because by means of it the Emanation was emanated. So in Chokhmah there is a manifestation of ten, but not like the manifestation that is within Keter, because in Keter they are in subtlety.

And further, the nine above were a source for the nine lower ones, which is not so in Chokhmah, for the eight are a source for the eight lower ones; but Keter, on the contrary—its principal source is the manifestation of the upper sefirah, which was completed above her in [its] manifestation, and it is a branch and has need of it. And likewise seven were emanated in Binah—here are seven—and they are sources for the seven lower ones, and they are not like the sources that are in Chokhmah. And further, in Chokhmah there were eight, a source for eight, and in Binah seven, a source for seven; and the two upper ones are emanated there to complete [them].

And further, because by means of them was the principal [part] of the Emanation, for by their power the seven were emanated in her; and therefore their manifestation remained there. And in this way for all the sefirot, for all of them are in all of them. And this is another matter, which is the manifestation of the sefirah itself in the sefirah. And so all the sefirot turn out to have aspects corresponding to all of them. And Malkhut differs from all of them, for she has a literal source in each one of the sefirot, since she is the last of them all. And this is the reason that her manifestation remained in all the grades of the sefirot, for she descended by way of the grades of the ladder, as was explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 10b), and these are its words: "When she was taken from Keter, she was called 'diadem of splendor' [ateret tiferet], etc.; when she was taken from the supernal Chokhmah, which is 'beginning' [reshit], she was called after its name; and when she was taken from Binah, she was called after its name, Tevunah; and when she was taken from Chesed, she was called," etc. And in this way he explained there in the Tikkunim, to show her name according to her aspects, by way of the grades of the ladder by which she descended; and according to the sources—to show her ascent to that aspect—she is called after its name, as we shall explain in the explanation of the passage in its place, if God decrees life. Further, the sefirot have another inclusion, of three—namely the three lines: the line of Chesed, the line of Din, the line of Rachamim—and in this aspect [each] includes three. And at times [each] includes four—namely Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Malkhut, which are the four legs of the Chariot; and they are literally the four letters of the name, for Yod is in Chesed and Heh in Gevurah, as is explained in the Tikkunim many times; and they are also the face of a man, the face of a lion, the face of an ox, the face of an eagle, as the matter will be explained in the Gate of Titles. And at times they include five, which are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod; and the reason is that thus far the Emanation reached, for Malkhut and Yesod are included in Tiferet. And when we consider the aforementioned five with respect to their being included in ten, they come to fifty. And likewise, when we consider them with respect to each one's including five, they come to twenty-five.

And further, at times they include six, which are the six extremities that are included in Tiferet; and then each and every one is designated by the name Vav [six]. And they are three upper Vavs—Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet—and they are [those of] va-yissa, va-yavo, va-yet (Exodus 14:19–21): Vav, Vav, Vav; and they are eighteen. And they are likewise in Netzach and Hod and Yesod, and they are another eighteen; their sum is thirty-six. And when they include ten, they come to sixty. And these inclusions and their order are explained in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim many times; and we have abridged the matter in this chapter so that it be set in order before the eyes of the inquirer, for wherever there is need of it.

After we have occupied ourselves in the preceding chapters with the matter of the inclusion of the sefirot and their bearing on the governance, we shall add further explanation of the essence apprehended in them by the Kabbalists—a tradition from one man's mouth to another's, back to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, from the mouth of the Almighty [Gevurah]. The first sefirah is the first emanated, and it is the supernal Keter, in which, relative to the emanated that are below it, there is no lack at all and no deficiency at all; rather, it is simple compassion, without any admixture of judgment at all. If so, how is it possible for it to include ten? For the inclusion indicates that there is in it a side of Gevurah, which is judgment; and we say that it is simple, without any admixture of judgment at all. And it is possible to answer this in several ways. The first is that it need not be that it includes Gevurah in the aspect of judgment; rather, it includes Gevurah in the aspect of the wealth that is under the hand of Gevurah, as the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra, fol. 25b): "One who wishes to become wealthy should turn north"; and its matter corresponds to Gevurah, for there is the gold. And likewise [there are] such matters as these, which are compassion and are of the action of Gevurah—like the rains, which are from the side of Gevurah and are compassion for the world. And likewise a person's being mighty [gibbor], conquering his inclination: that might [gevurah] is from the side of complete compassion, in that he was not delivered into the hand of his inclination—by the power of Gevurah, which made him prevail over his enemy. And so they explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 114b), and these are its words: "In the fifth month, there is given in it the might of Gevurah, to prevail over the evil inclination from the side of the left, so that it not rule over him," etc.; see there. And although this is expounded there for another matter, nonetheless it emerges for us from his words that a person's prevailing over his inclination is from the side of Gevurah.

And further, they have other actions, such and such, good and pleasant. And from the side of the aspect of Gevurah in these actions, Keter includes it. And when Gevurah is aroused, Keter pours forth effluence by the side of Gevurah that it has; and even if it pours forth the action of compassion—such as the effluence of wealth, or of prevailing, below—from the supernal Keter that effluence will strengthen Gevurah, so that there be in it strength and firmness of power to act. And although this matter belongs to Keter accidentally, for its principal pouring-forth was for compassion, nonetheless in Gevurah "kind found its kind," and by it Gevurah was aroused to act. Further, it is possible to answer in another way: that it is true that Keter effects only compassion—this is its power; although it includes Gevurah, nonetheless it has the power to nullify that Gevurah and to subdue it to compassion. And not on this account is its including ten to be denied. As is the matter with the elements: not because a given body shows heat alone, or cold alone, shall we be obliged [to say] that it is simple and is not composed of the four elements at all. Rather, we shall say that it is composed of the four elements, and because of the prevalence of the element of water that is in it the other elements do not act in it, and the cold alone is seen in it. And so is the matter when heat is seen in it: its cause is the prevalence of the fire, as Rambam, peace be upon him, explained in his words that we copied in the preceding chapter. And in this way with the sefirah of Keter: although there be in it the power of Gevurah, its judgment does not act, as happens with the elements, which we explained. Further, we can resolve [it] in another way, and it is nearer to the truth and is the principal one. And the matter is well known: that in the simple Ein Sof it is necessary that there be a manifestation of the ten sefirot, as we shall explain in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. And now, why should it not be difficult for us that, accordingly, the simple God turns out to be composite, with a great composition such as this—of ten sefirot, among which are Gevurah, the power of judgment, and Gedulah, the power of lovingkindness? And in truth there is no composition greater than this. And such is not the rule of the cardinal faith that is fixed in the heart of the believers; for the cardinal principle of the faith is to believe that the Ein Sof is one, simple with the utmost simplicity, without any composition. Rather, certainly, the answer to this question is at its side: for, God forbid, our intent in saying that the manifestation of the sefirot is in the Ein Sof is not that their manifestation above is in the way that their manifestation is below. Rather, above they are simple with the utmost simplicity, and unified in the very roots with the utmost union, and they are subtle [and] spiritual with the utmost subtlety, so that neither multiplicity nor change, neither judgment nor compassion, is attributed to them; and we shall speak of them at length in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. And now, since Keter is the first emanated, there is nothing between it and the Emanator except that this one is cause and this one is its effect. And according to the measure that we were obliged to go far in the matter of the sefirot that are in the Ein Sof, in that same way we are obliged to go far in the matter of the sefirot that are in Keter. For according to their descent from before Him, so the things and the actions are revealed; and according to their nearness to their source, so they are concealed and hidden. And therefore, although Keter includes ten, the intent is not that the ten effect judgment and compassion as is their action in their [own] place; rather, they are concealed sources. And in this way is the manifestation of the emanation of judgment, for those who ask whence judgment came forth, as we shall explain in this Gate explicitly. This is what is given to the human intellect to answer to the question. However, the tradition compels us that Keter is the utmost of compassion, as it is written (Daniel 7:9), "And the Ancient of Days sat; His garment was white as snow." And its effluence is nothing but simple compassion; and "He sits upon a throne of sparks of fire, to subdue them"; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Idra (of Naso, fol. 128b). However, judgment is effected in the hiding of its face, God forbid, and the departure of its effluence from the sefirot; then judgment acts of itself. For the arousal of the line of Din prevails over the line of Rachamim, and the Gevurah that is in each and every attribute prevails, and by means of it judgment acts. However, the Gevurah that is in Keter is the reverse—[it is] to subdue judgment; and it is "the forehead of the King," for when the forehead of the will is revealed, the judgments are nullified, as Rashbi explained in the Idra (there, fol. 129a); and we shall explain [it] there, with God's help, in the book Or Yakar. However, a mighty difficulty follows from this: for the actions of judgment turn out to be effected by means of nine sefirot alone, and this is not fitting. And we answer that the departure and the hiding of the face of Keter from the attributes, so that judgment may act—this is called partnership, in that Keter is a partner to judgment. And so Rashbi explained there in the Idra. And this is the explanation of the passage that Rabbi Menachem Recanati explained, as we copied in the Gate of Self and Vessels, in chapter 2: "And YHVH rained upon Sodom," etc. And likewise the matter of the parable of the stories that we explained there in chapter 4. And there is no strain in our saying that the departure and the hiding of its face is called partnership with judgment; for we are compelled to say something close to this matter of the Ein Sof: for if He were spreading forth in all the sefirot, there would be no judgment at all; and it is impossible to say that judgment is not effected by Him, for if so, punishment turns out not to be by Him, God forbid, and this is the removal of providence. Rather, the hiding of His face and the removal of His providence from His sefirot is His partnership with judgment. And one may object: if so—that He removes His providence and His Self from the attributes—then it turns out that the sefirot have actions apart from Him, for they effect judgment upon the departure of His providence. Therefore we answer that certainly there are different aspects to His providence in the sefirot.

Behold, when the matter is complete compassion, and the heavens are pure before Him, He is revealed in His attributes with a revelation of [His] Self, so that all of them are unified with the utmost union. However, when the heavens are clothed in blackness, His providence departs from the sefirot—yet not altogether; rather, He reveals the light in them by means of an intermediary, by means of Binah, in the six extremities, from the side of Gevurah; and the effluence and the providence are scant, so that judgment is effected. And this is the secret of "From afar YHVH appeared to me" (Jeremiah 31:2), and likewise "Why, YHVH, do You stand afar off" (Psalms 10:1)—for the light is not revealed as is fitting; and this is "You conceal [Yourself] in times of trouble." And this is the cause of judgment and its coming-to-be, according to the truth. And its tikkun [is by means of repentance], in the secret of the revelation of providence and the shining of the Ein Sof by means of Keter in the sefirot. And this is the secret of the effluence and the compassion that are poured forth, by means of which judgment is set right, and "eyes washed in milk," as will be explained, with God's help, in the coming chapters. Further, concerning the manifestation of this sefirah: although it is concealed with the utmost concealment—so that, on account of its great concealment, Chokhmah is called the beginning of the revelation, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 3—nonetheless our sages and our elders, who received from our prophets, revealed to us that there are in this sefirah 620 pillars of light, as the number of [the word] keter. And the first to reveal this matter is Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah, in his lovely prayer, and these are his words there: "I call You by six hundred and twenty pillars of light, which are the head of Your speech, which are a tikkun for the height of Your rank; and from them the life-force is drawn into all the sefirot; and they stand one beside another, as a soul within the body; and they are full within and without and on the outside—YHVH YHVH YHVH; and they are engraved in the likeness of male and female, and are reversed into Tiferet and kingship in the permutation [tziruf] of the height of their stature; and to their subtlety there is no end; and they are parts that are not divided at all; and they are exalted in reading and combining and reckoning. There goes forth the wellspring of the flame, which is beyond searching out and beyond number, from the light that is concealed, with the increase of the darkness that is hidden; and it is the manifestation known to all the discerning, in thirteen kinds of substitution [temurah], which are revealed and concealed, laid upon Keter literally:  M Tz P Tz  M Tz P Tz  T K  G S P Y  P S Ṭ P Ṭ  T G L  T V M Y  P G Sh  S Ch Q  P T Y A  Ṭ H G  S Ch Q  K T K V M Y  Ṭ B T  Z P Ṭ  P V B Z  P S N T Tz  P Ṭ D Tz." Thus far his words. And its explanation: "I call You by six hundred and twenty"—"calling" [keri'ah] is a term of the pouring-forth of effluence, as in "Deep calls to deep at the voice of Your channels" (Psalms 42:8), and as in "And one called to another and said" (Isaiah 6:3), which the Targum renders "and they receive one from another." And so "I call You," etc., means: I shall draw forth Your effluence in six hundred, etc. "Which are the head of Your speech" means the beginning of the revelation of the Ein Sof, although they are not apprehended by us. And since speech is a figure for revelation—because above, in the Ein Sof, on account of His great concealment, speech of Him is forbidden—therefore he said that the 620 are "the head of Your speech," meaning the first of the emanated things that enter into speech. Or "I call You by six," etc., means: I call You and title You by the name "620 pillars of light"; for it is known that in the Ein Sof there is no name that would limit Him, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 1, with Heaven's help.

And behold, the name of the Ein Sof is the Emanation, all of it as a whole: just as a name indicates the matter that is titled by that name, so the whole Emanation indicates the Ein Sof. And just as a name is like a handhold upon the thing spoken of—as if to say that there is no possibility of speaking of so-and-so unless we title him by such-and-such a name, and by means of that name we have a place to speak of that thing—so with the Ein Sof there is no place to speak of Him except from the side of the aspect of the Emanation and its revelation, and it is the place of a handhold upon Him. Therefore he said "which are the head of Your speech": it is the place of beginning and the head of speech concerning the Ein Sof; for from there and upward there is no place for speech, and the beginning of speech is from the 620, from Keter and downward. "Which are a tikkun for the height of Your rank." Meaning: it was already explained in the Idra de-Nazir—and we copied its words in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 4—that the Emanation is a tikkun for the Emanator. Since there is no intellection of the Emanator except by means of the emanated, His tikkun is therefore the Emanation, and His revelation is His beauty; since His delight is in revelation, revelation is beauty and rank for Him. Or "which are a tikkun" means that these pillars are the beauty and the adornment and the tikkun of Keter, which is the height of the rank of the Ein Sof according to what is revealed to us. "And from them the life-force is drawn." Meaning: from these pillars are drawn the light and the effluence that is the life-force of all the sefirot; for the light of the Ein Sof is what gives life and nourishment to all the emanated, and the emanated take pleasure in the radiance and the light of the Emanator, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, chapter 8. And as it appears, these pillars are channels and sources for the sefirot, which draw light from the Ein Sof. "And they stand one beside another, as a soul within the body." Meaning: these pillars in Keter are in this order—that they are one beside another, and they are one within another, as a soul within the body; so they are found in the matters of their order, one within another. They are found one beside another, and they are found to be as a soul within the body, one within another, like the order of the sefirot that we explained in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, in chapter 4 and in chapter 7. And he said "one beside another" because, relative to the sefirot, they are one beside another, as we see that the middle points are sefirot (see Asis Rimonim); so they are found one beside another. And according to the truth, when we come to consider them in themselves, they are one within another, like the soul within the body—this one a cause to that, and that one an effect of this—like the relation of the sefirot themselves, which are distinct as cause and effect are distinct; such is the difference in the relation of these pillars. "And they are full within and without and on the outside." Meaning: each and every pillar has in it three kinds of effluence, which are "within" and "without" and "on the outside." That is: they are full "within," namely the pillar's own self and the aspect of itself; and "without" is the aspect of its cause, namely the light received by it from above; and "on the outside" is with respect to its aspect that pours forth. And they are now three aspects. The first is its intrinsic aspect, which is the essence of the pillar in itself. And the second is its aspect from the side of its receiving, which is, according to the truth, "without" its self, although it is more excellent than its self. The third is "on the outside," which is its aspect with respect to what it pours forth to another; and it is, according to the truth, called "outer," because it goes outward from its grade and from its interior, which is the aspect of its self.

And behold, these three aspects are: the first, with respect to the cause that it has; and the second, with respect to itself, which is the effect of the one above it; and the third, with respect to its effect, which is below it. And this is "within," which is the aspect of itself; and "without," the aspect of its cause; and "on the outside," the aspect of its effect; and they are three kinds of effluence. And the light that pours forth upon each and every one of the pillars is "YHVH YHVH YHVH." Meaning: it is already known that the four-letter name includes all the ten sefirot, and it will be explained in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. And it is known that each and every pillar includes ten sefirot, since there is no branch at all in the sefirot that does not include ten. And therefore, since there are three aspects in each and every pillar, they turn out to be three times ten sefirot, for each aspect includes ten; and they are three names of the four-letter name, which are YHVH YHVH YHVH. "And they are engraved in the likeness of male and female." Meaning: these names are their engraving and their depiction—that is, their emanation—in the likeness of male and female. And the matter is that the aspect that is with respect to what it receives, namely the aspect called above "without," is the aspect of a male, pouring forth effluence to the aspect of its self, which is called above "within." If so, there turn out to be two names, the upper one male and the second female—one that pours forth effluence and one that receives it. And likewise the aspect of itself is a male, pouring forth effluence to its aspect that receives the effluence, which is the one titled above "on the outside." And therefore there turn out to be three names, three aspects, whose matter and whose engraving is in the likeness of male and female. "And are reversed into Tiferet and kingship," etc. Meaning: the first aspect, which is the one titled "without" above, and the second aspect, which is the one titled "within"—we said that they are males; and the last, which is "on the outside," is female. He said that they are reversed into Tiferet and kingship, that is, male and female. For the last, outer aspect of this pillar pours forth effluence into the first [aspect], which is the "without," of the lower pillar. So the aspects turn out to have been reversed: what is male was reversed into female, and what was female was reversed into male; for the last aspect is male to the first [aspect] of the pillar that is beneath it, which receives from it. "In the permutation of the height of their stature; and to their subtlety there is no end." Meaning: the reversal; and it is when they are all joined [yitztarfu] according to the order of the height of their stature, in that they are one above another. The last aspect of the upper one of them turns out to be male to the first aspect of the second, which is below it; and this is when we consider them with respect to their joining together [tzirufam] and with respect to the height of their stature, one on top of another, as has been explained. "And to their subtlety there is no end." Meaning: although we have spoken of all these parts in them, the intent is not, God forbid, that there is in them a body that is divided, at all; for, on the contrary, they are subtle and spiritual with the utmost spirituality, on account of their nearness to their source, so that to their subtlety there is no end. And although we distinguish divisions and aspects in them, it is not that they are divided parts, God forbid; rather, they are parts that are not divided except with respect to cause and effect, in the way that we went far [in speaking] of the sefirot. And it is fitting to go further and further in the matter of the pillars, because they are parts and aspects of one sefirah; and further, because they are in this sefirah, which is subtle and spiritual, the first emanated, unified with the Emanator, as is known.
And we have yet another explanation of this wording, and it will be explained in the coming chapter, with the help of the Rock.

"And they are exalted in reading and combining and reckoning." This matter is, at first sight, very difficult; for these matters are five: arrangement and permutation and reading, combining and letter-reckoning. And so their explanation came in Sefer Ma'ayan ha-Chokhmah, and these are its words: "This is arrangement and permutation and reading, combining and reckoning—that is, of the explicit name, which is unified in the branches of the root of the movement that prevails in thirteen kinds of substitution. How is the arrangement? To bring out a teaching from a reading and a reading from a teaching; and an arrangement from a permutation and a permutation from an arrangement; and combining by reckoning and reckoning by combining; until all things are set in the wellspring of the flame, and the flame in the wellspring, beyond searching out and beyond number, to the light that is concealed, with the increase of the darkness that is hidden; and to bring everything into the completed work, in thirteen kinds of substitution." Thus far its words.

And behold, at first sight it implies that Rabbi Nechunya wrote only three, which are reading and combining and reckoning; and we need to know what this is and why this is. First it is fitting that we enter into the explanation of these five matters, [and] what their description is. And in Sefer ha-Kanah he explained them briefly, and these are its words: "The arrangement is that you know the name from its beginning to its end, as it is written. And permutation is as you permute it by the twenty-two alphabets that are in the Sefer Yetzirah of Abraham our father; and you shall know how to make a reading from each and every permutation; and afterward to combine everything together, which is the combining; and afterward to know by reckoning, so that you not err in the permutation of the letters, nor in their vowels." Thus far its words.
And his words are in the explanation of the forty-two-letter name that comes out of Bereshit, as we shall explain in the Gate of Particulars of Names.

And behold, he explained that the arrangement is that a person know the name with respect to the order of its writing and its arrangement. And this is also explained in a certain baraita that is attributed to Shimon ha-Tzaddik, peace be upon him, and these are its words: "Shimon ha-Tzaddik said to his disciples: Know that the explicit name is divided into five parts, and these are they: arrangement and permutation and reading and combining and reckoning. The arrangement is that a person begin its ordering from beginning to end, as with the three verses that are called the name of seventy-two, which are ויסע (vayissa), ויבא (vayavo), ויט (vayet) (Exodus 14:19–21): the first from its head to its end, and the middle from its end to its beginning, and the last from beginning to end; and this is the order of their reading: והו ילי סיט (Vehu, Yeli, Sit)," etc. Thus far its words, for our matter.

And behold, his words agree with the words of the Kanah, who said that the arrangement is for a person to know first the arrangement of the name with which he is occupied, and afterward from there he is drawn on to other matters. And it is possible that this matter is called "arrangement" because it is the arranging of the name and its order, without confusion or corruption; and this is arrangement. But the words of Sefer Ma'ayan ha-Chokhmah do not indicate so, for it said: "How is the arrangement? To bring out a teaching from a reading and a reading from a teaching," etc.; and these words do not, at first sight, correspond with what we explained in the matter of the arrangement. Therefore we shall need to explain the words of Sefer Ma'ayan ha-Chokhmah.

And behold, the permutation—the example of it is this: if we have before us the four-letter name, which we wish to permute, the permutation of its letters will come to twelve words, as they are permuted in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapter 9, in the twelve-letter name.

And behold, after the twelve are complete and we come to the thirteenth, the permutation returns to the arrangement, which is its source. And this is "the arrangement that comes to the permutation, and the permutation that returns to the arrangement"; for when the permutation is finished, the thing returns to its source, namely the arrangement, which is the name as it is written. And this certainly indicates the hold of the branches—which are the permutations that are permuted out of the name, which is the root—and they hold fast to their root, and go forth and spread out, and return and enter into their source. And such is the way with the permutation and the substitutions of the name by the twenty-two alphabets that we wrote of in the Gate of Permutation, by means of which it is permuted twenty-two times; and when we come to permute it the twenty-third [time], the permutation returns to its source, namely the arrangement. And all this indicates the branches that are unified in the root: the permutation returns to the arrangement, and the arrangement to the permutation. Therefore one who contemplates the wisdom of permutation must, before he comes to the permutation, know whether the name that is before him is a root or a branch, so that he may know the place where the branches suck from the root, so as to be able to unify the branches in their root. As if to say: if he had before him מצפץ (M Tz P Tz), which is יהוה (YHVH) by at-bash, he needs to know whether this name,  M Tz P Tz, is a source or a root, and afterward cycle it into permutation. For the example of this: if he cycles  M Tz P Tz, when he reaches the twenty-third, which is the completion of all the alphabets and their beginning, the name will of necessity return to  M Tz P Tz, which was their source. So the poor man turns out, in his folly, to have reversed the order: he thought that  M Tz P Tz  is the root, and that twenty-two branches spread out in it, and that the four-letter name, which comes out of it by way of the substitutions of at-bash, is a branch. Certainly he "walked in darkness and had no light" (Isaiah 50:10); for what he thought a branch is the root, and what he thought the root is a branch. And this is why the arrangement is needed: "to bring out a permutation from the arrangement and an arrangement from the permutation," which is said in Sefer Ma'ayan ha-Chokhmah. And so is the matter with reading and combining. For it belongs to the secret of permutation that one know how to make a reading from it. The example of this: after he has cycled, in permutation, one permutation among the permutations, he makes from it a reading in which there is some sense. As in this example: when a person permutes the word שלמה (Shlomo), he makes from it a reading from which some derivation is understood, such as של מה (shel mah), which are two readings; and their derivation: mah amounts in gematria to the four-letter name spelled out in full, namely Chokhmah; and shel means that he is "of" Chokhmah, which is called mah, as we have explained. Or it means that Tiferet, which is called Shlomo, is shal—as in "and the iron slips off [ve-nashal]" (Deuteronomy 19:5), namely removal: he was removed and emanated from Chokhmah, which is mah. And afterward we permute it into שלם ה (shalem heh), meaning that by their effluence Malkhut, which is the Heh, is made whole [shelemah]. And this is reading. And what he said, "to bring out a reading from a teaching and a teaching from a reading," means that after he makes a reading from the permutation, he makes a teaching from the reading, and a reading from the teaching. The example of this: the arrangement שלמה (Shlomo), which is the source—we permuted it into של מה (shel mah); this is permutation. Afterward he makes from this permutation a reading, namely ש מלה (shin millah). Afterward he makes from it a teaching, that is, an interpretation. And its interpretation: Tiferet, which is called shin millah [the printed text has ש למה]. It means: Shin is Binah, which is called Shin, the root of the tree, as explained in the Tikkunim, and we copied it in the Gate "From Below to Above"; and millah, "word," means voice, which is Tiferet, coming forth from Binah. Further, from the permutation שמלה he makes a reading, which is שם לה (shem lah, "a name to Heh"). Afterward he makes a teaching from this reading, and it is the interpretation of the reading: "name" means the four-letter name, which is unified with Malkhut; that is, "a name to Heh," meaning to the final Heh, which is Malkhut. And after he makes the teaching, the matter returns to the reading. And afterward he makes a combining from the reading; and the matter of combining is to combine word with word, if need be. The example of this: שלמה אלקים (Shlomo Elohim): he joins the two words together and combines them to make a reading, and says שלם האל מיה (shalem ha-El mi-Yah, "the wholeness of El is from Yah"); the one who permutes has the power to do this and to combine the two of them together. And he makes a teaching from them, meaning: the root of the wholeness of El, which is Chesed, is from Yah, which is Chokhmah; and all by means of Shlomo Elohim, Tiferet and Malkhut, for by means of them is the pouring-forth of the effluence out of the union. And likewise he combines them into השל מהאל מי (ha-shal me-ha-El Mi); and this is combining and reading. And he makes a teaching from them, which is the interpretation: Mi, which is Binah, brings down and pours forth the effluence from El. And since combining is a thing that confounds the intellect with much confusion, therefore one needs to know the count of the letters and their reckoning; and this is "and reckoning." And the matter also needs the count of the letters—that is, their reckoning and their number—so that if he needs to make two out of one letter, or one out of two, by way of the joining and separating that we explained in the Gate of Permutation, he will do it and not err; and this is "combining by reckoning and reckoning by combining." "Until all things are set in the wellspring of the flame," etc.: when the letter-reckoning returns to the combining, and the combining to the reading, and the reading to the permutation, and the permutation to the arrangement—this is the return of the flame to the wellspring; for the particulars return to the generalities, and the generalities to the source, which is the permutation, and the permutation to the arrangement; that is, even the flame itself into the wellspring. And in order to fix this matter in our intellect we shall speak of it at further length, although it is not among the things that belong to this Gate. And we say that the matter is this: every gathering of the letters of the names, and every gathering of the letters of the Torah, are powers unified together. For each and every letter has a spirituality and a soul of its own; and when so many letters are joined together, as [in] the word bereshit, it is one angel and power, beneath which are six powers, which are the six letters, and beneath them many kinds of powers and many kinds of spirituality. For whatever comes into the hand of the discerning one by permuting them, let him not think that he has brought into being what was not in the world; for he has brought out only some of the concealed powers that branch out. And all the permutations of the word are branches branching out from that power and spirituality; and the farther the permutation is from the word, the more it branches out into particularity. And from this a person can recognize the glory of his Maker and the greatness of His exaltedness.

And behold, in returning the things to the wellspring of the flame he will know and recognize, out of the force of the permutation, the height of its ranks. And should he wish to permute one word of the words of the Torah in all the permutations that are possible, his days and his nights would come to an end, and they would not come to an end, on account of the multitude of the matters apprehended by means of the twenty-two alphabets of Sefer Yetzirah, and by means of the numbers and the permutations, without end. And therefore one must "set the things in the wellspring of the flame, beyond searching out," etc., "to the light that is concealed, with the increase," etc. Meaning: he will know, out of the arrangement, the permutation, the reading, the combining and the letter-reckoning, that there is no searching out of the light that is concealed—which are the branches that are revealed out of the permutation, and return and are concealed in their source, which is the supernal Keter; for there is the concealment of all the branches, in the secret of the return of the things and the threads and the flames to their source. "With the increase of the darkness that is hidden": meaning, with the increase of the holiness of the Emanator, the Ein Sof, who is darkness relative to apprehension; and therefore He is called "hidden darkness," for according to the truth He is light to all the lights. For when the branches are concealed in the supernal Keter, and Keter in the Ein Sof, then certainly there the things are exalted, so that thought cannot picture the power of the exaltedness of the branches. And therefore one must "bring everything into the completed work"—meaning, it is the Malkhut that is in Keter, in which is the concealment of all things; and there is the station of apprehension, for from there and upward there is no intellection. And this is the reverse of what he said at the head of his words, "in the branches of the root of the movement that prevails in thirteen kinds of substitution"; for that indicates their root, which prevails over the thirteen attributes, for there is the root and source of all things, and from there is their going forth and their emanation; for it is the root, and the powers are branches branching out from it.
