And he objected: "And in the outer chambers there is not?" etc. Meaning: granted, according to me there is no difficulty, for I say the reverse—that in the outer chambers there is, and this is "And He called," etc., and in the inner chambers there is not, and this is "there is no sorrow"; and nothing was difficult for me except this, "But if you will not hear it," etc., as we objected at the outset. But according to you, who said the reverse—that in the inner chambers there is sorrow and agitation and judgment, and this is "in hidden places shall weep," etc., and in the outer chambers there is not, and this is "there is no sorrow"—it is difficult: for it is written, "And on that day YHVH Tzeva'ot called to weeping and to mourning"; and "calling" implies making heard outside.

And further, it is written, "And YHVH Tzeva'ot called," and this is a calling of pouring-forth. And he means that Tiferet, that is, YHVH, and Netzach and Hod, that is, Tzeva'ot—and likewise Yesod, which is "a sign in His host"—poured forth "on that day," which is Malkhut, as is explained in the Zohar (Shelach, fol. 171) on the verse "And it shall be on that day that living waters shall go out" (Zechariah 14:8), which we shall copy in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 3. And behold, it is proven that judgment was poured forth and increased in the outer chambers; and it is difficult for you. And he answered: the destruction of the Temple is different, for then it was increasing, for the reason that the attribute of compassion departed. And the matter is this: while the attribute of judgment pours forth and the attribute of compassion also pours forth, the more the judgment is poured forth by way of the grades, the more it decreases and is sweetened, by means of the blendings known in the arbiters. But when, God forbid, judgment comes to pass and compassion departs, then judgment increases—and all the more so when the attribute of compassion is turned into judgment, for then the judgment is added to and increases the more it is poured forth. And this is what he said: "The destruction of the Temple is different, for even the angels of peace wept": [not only] the aspect of compassion and the grades of Chesed—and all the more so the attribute of judgment, and needless to say this—but even the emissaries of the attribute of compassion, which spread outward, even in them judgment increased. And this is "even the angels of peace wept, as it is said," etc.

And behold, in this the explanation of this passage has been included, and it is settled in its proper measure, and the matter of judgment has been set right. And what appeared to be our enemy has become our ally, and the explanation is complete.
(See Zohar, Vayikra, fol. 15b, in what is written: "And then it is called 'and it was grieved' [va-yit'atzev]—'and it was grieved' in the outer chambers," etc.; and it requires consideration.)

After we went to great lengths to speak, according to our measure, of the matter of judgment in the first three, we wish in this chapter to speak of a matter that is explained concerning them in the prayer of Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah, peace be upon him; and we shall not copy his wording, so as not to lengthen, but [give] the matters in brief. He said that these first three are reckoned as one; and he said that they are the knowledge, Keter; and the knower, Chokhmah; and the known, Binah. And the explanation of this matter is that the knowledge of the Creator is not like the knowledge of the other existents. For with the knowledge of the other existents, they and their knowledge are not one; rather, they know things by a knowledge that is outside them. The example of this: a person who knows one of the forms, or some thing that is pictured in his mind—in any case there will be three things. The first is the mind, which was devoid of that form before his knowing it. And the second is the mind by which he recognizes and knows that form. And the third is the known form, pictured in his mind. And they are three: the knowledge, and the knower, and the known. And some have titled them with the terms intellect, intellecting and intellected [sekhel, maskil, muskal]. And the knowledge of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so; rather, He is the knowledge, and the knower, and the known. And the matter is that His knowledge of matters is not from the side of His providence over them after their separation from Him; rather, by the intellection and knowledge of His own Self He knows and watches over all the matters of the world. For the things that are in reality are existent and unified with Him in His Self; for He is the mold of all the existents, and they are in Him in the subtlest and choicest manifestation in the world, so that all the existents have no completeness except their completeness in that choice manifestation, which is unified in the One who brings them into being; and according to their descent from before Him, so they descend from their completeness and from their rank.

And behold, all the existents are pictured in the sefirot, and the sefirot in their Emanator. So all the existents and all the sefirot are found to be included in Keter, Chokhmah, Binah; for so they are included before their spreading forth. And these are the three that are stored away, which are "heads of heads," which Rav Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, explained, as we shall explain in the Gate of Tzachtzachot.

And behold, the first three are unified there with the utmost union, so that even after their emanation they went to great lengths regarding their union, saying that the first three are reckoned as one, as we shall explain. If so, the three of them are found to be the knowledge, and the knower, and the known. And the matter is that Keter, which is the first emanated, is concealed, and the existents are still concealed, so that a knower is not judged in them—that is, the manifestation of the exaltation of the existents—but knowledge, which is like a simple form without any revealed manifestation at all. And in Chokhmah is the knower already, because in it is the unformed matter [golem] from which all the existents are pictured. And all the existents as a whole are Binah, which includes the whole Structure; and this is the known. And the reason that the existents are called by the term of knowledge is that the manifestation of all the existents is the concealed Da'at [knowledge], which is the six extremities, called "the order of times." And let us return to the matter: for this reason the holy one said that the first three are the knowledge, the knower and the known, as many have explained, to indicate their union. And to this matter they said that these three sefirot are neshamah, ruach, nefesh—and the intent is not that they are the source of these three; for it is established for us that the neshamah has its source from Binah, and the ruach from Tiferet, and the nefesh from Malkhut, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul. Rather, the intent is that just as the neshamah and the ruach and the nefesh are three grades, one above another, and they are in one union, so these three sefirot are one union, although they are three grades, effects one of another. And now it is fitting that we examine what the intent is in our saying that the first three are reckoned as one; for it indicates that this oneness is in these three sefirot more than in the other sefirot; and this is a thing strange in the extreme. For it is known that our faith ought to be in the union of all the sefirot: although they are ten, they are a unified oneness. And this is one of the principles of this wisdom: that it not be in our mind that the Emanation is divided into parts, God forbid. And since this principle is a peg fixed in the heart of those faithful in the faith, how then can our words be true, that the first three are reckoned as one? For all ten are also reckoned as one. And this matter weighs on us all the more when we see the reverse of all this in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 1b), and these are his words: "'As a bird that wanders from its nest, so is a man who wanders from his place' (Proverbs 27:8). And 'bird' is none other than the Shekhinah, who is driven from her place. This is what is written: 'You shall surely send away [shale'ach teshalach] the mother,' etc. (Deuteronomy 22:7): et ['the'] to include the lower Shekhinah; 'the mother,' the upper Shekhinah. This is what is written: 'and for your transgressions was your mother sent away' (Isaiah 50:1); for the two of them are driven from their places. And therefore shale'ach teshalach—two sendings: one from the First Temple, and the second from the Second Temple." Thus far his words, for our matter. And although the wording needs a broad explanation, we shall not lengthen here, for it is already explained by us with a broad and long explanation. And nonetheless, from within it we learn that just as the lower Shekhinah is alone and desolate, driven from her place, and is not unified with her husband, so the upper Shekhinah, Binah, is in this matter also driven away. And how can a person restrain himself before this thing, which is the reverse of the principle that we said above, and the reverse of the words of the holy Rabbi Nechunya?

And further, another passage in the Tikkunim besides this, and these are its words (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 117): "'If you lie between the sheepfolds [shefatayim]' (Psalms 68:14): happy is he who lays the supernal Mother between his lips; and because of her it is said, 'If [im] you lie,' etc.—do not read im but em [mother]. And they are two: the upper mother, the lower mother; the upper Shekhinah, the lower Shekhinah, of which it is said shale'ach teshalach—two sendings corresponding to them. Of them it is said, 'and the two of them went' (Ruth 1:19). Happy is he who lays them in his lips, in prayer, in Torah," etc. Thus far its words.
And further, this matter is explained in the Tikkunim in places other than these; and we shall not copy them, so as not to overload the discussion.

And behold, the resolution and settling of these doubts requires that we state first that the union of the sefirot is in one of three ways. The first is in that they are unified from the side of the Holy One, blessed be He, having watched over them at the beginning of their emanation, and fixed for them His effluence, and shone His light in them; for in this nourishment and effluence they are unified with a true, strong and firm union—so that if, God forbid, it should enter the mind that that effluence be withheld, the world would come to an end and be lost, and the spirituality would return to its source, as before their emanation. And this is the intention of the reading of the Shema, according to the correct intention. For the intention in the union of the reading of the Shema is not to pour forth into the emanated more abundant effluence than their effluence by which the world follows its custom, and on which the sustaining of things and the bond of the elements depend. Rather, the intention is that we unify all the sefirot one to one, and all of them in the Emanator, and make Him King over all the existents, great and small, to show that He is the cause of their sustaining, and that this is our complete faith—not to add to and increase what is customary, but to show the union that is necessary to sustain it, to establish it and to set it up, so that the creatures may be complete in their power, in their creation, as before the sin of the first Adam, when the creation was strong in the power and strength of the effluence poured forth; except that the earth was impoverished, and the beauty of things diminished, by his sin, as is known. The second union is to pour forth abundant effluence by way of the channels, beyond the matter of the creation; and it is according to the need of the time. There is a time when the need of the time will be for pardon and forgiveness and atonement; and then we draw down the effluence from the supernal whiteness, Keter, which whitens the iniquities of Israel, by means of Binah—for it is the root of repentance, for the forgiveness—and by means of it, in union with the father, who is Chokhmah, that effluence is poured forth to Malkhut, and Binah and Malkhut are unified, by means of six intermediaries, that is, "one; one and one," etc. And then it is the Day of Atonement, "and it shall be forgiven all the congregation of the children of Israel" (Numbers 15:26); and this is the essence of the service of the Day of Atonement, as is proven from the words of Rashbi in the Zohar. And there is a time when they will need wisdom, in order to become wise in the Torah; and then the effluence of Chokhmah is poured forth by way of Chesed—and this is "one who wishes to become wise should turn south"—and from there to Tiferet, which is the Torah, and from there to Malkhut, that is, the lower Chokhmah. And there is a time when wealth will be needed; and then the effluence of Binah is poured forth to Gevurah—and this is "one who wishes to become wealthy should turn north"—and from there to Malkhut. And there is a time when they will need might and power to take vengeance on the enemies; and then Binah pours forth judgment to Gevurah, and from Gevurah to Hod, and from there to "the sword that avenges the vengeance of the covenant" (Leviticus 26:25), with the help of Netzach; and then they will prevail over the enemies and defeat them. And there are many matters like these, which the discerning one will consider when he occupies himself with the words of Rashbi; and we shall not lengthen on these matters, since they are not among the things that belong here.

And behold, this matter will be understood further when the inquirer occupies himself with the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And in truth all these matters and drawings-down are called effluence and abundant good, beyond the allotment that He allotted at the creation of the world for the standing of the creatures. And there is yet a third union, which is particular to four sefirot, which are Chokhmah and Binah, Tiferet and Malkhut; and it is the matter of coupling, which is found only in these sefirot. And this matter is like the coupling of a man and his wife—a thing that a person cannot grasp unless we compare the second union to the food that a man gives to his wife in abundance, although it may at times be by means of an agent; and the third union is like the matter of literal coupling, in which he couples with her "to bring forth a vessel for his work" (Isaiah 54:16) (see Asis Rimonim). And it is a matter so exalted that the mouth cannot [speak, but only] soothe the ear in matters such as these; and we shall broaden the explanation of this in this Gate, in a chapter of its own. And now, after we have stated first the matter of these three unions, we shall come to explain the matter of the resolution of the doubt that we raised. And we say that the first union is equal for all the sefirot, and faith does not judge among them division and separation, God forbid, with respect to that union; rather, the providence is always equal in them, from end to end, from the first to the last. But with respect to the second union, it will often be lacking in the seven sefirot of the Structure, and at times there will be found in this one what is not found in that one, because it is an addition of effluence, and all is according to the need. At times the world needs more judgment than compassion, as at a time of war; and at times the world needs the prevalence of Chesed more than another attribute, and the effluence is found to increase in it more than in the other sefirot; and so for all the sefirot, according to the need. And this separation will be only in the seven sefirot of the Structure; but the first three are always reckoned as one sefirah with respect to this. For if this effluence departs, it will never depart except from the Structure; but from Binah upward it will always stand in radiance and unified light. And therefore it is found that, for most of these supernal matters, there is no division among these three; rather, what is in this one is in that one, and what is in that one is in this one. And likewise Keter has in it the aspect of Chokhmah from the side of Chokhmah, and the aspect of Binah from the side of Binah; and Binah the aspect of Keter from the side of Keter, and the aspect of Chokhmah from the side of Chokhmah; and Chokhmah the aspect of Keter from the side of Keter, and the aspect of Binah from the side of Binah—as we shall explain in the Gate of Arbiters—which is not found so for all the other sefirot. And these are אשר (asher), ראש (rosh), שאר (she'er), which are titles for the first three, as we shall explain in the Gate of Titles (see Pelach ha-Rimmon, chapter 10). And the third union, which is the union of coupling—this union is lacking, through iniquities, also in Binah, because her union depends on the union of Tiferet and Malkhut; and as long as there is no union of son and daughter below, there is no union of father and mother above. And so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 103), and these are his words: "He said to him: And the letters of YHVH, which are 'an offering that rises and descends' [korban oleh ve-yored]—who rises first, or who descends? Vav descends first to Heh, and afterward Yod rises to the upper Heh; for so they have established: 'I will not enter into the Jerusalem above,' etc. Yod will not enter into the upper Heh, which is the Jerusalem above, until Vav enters into Heh, which is the Jerusalem below." Thus far his words.

And this thing R. Shimon asked of the Elder who was occupied before them with the verse "I sleep, but my heart wakes" (Song of Songs 5:2); and the Elder explained that matter there, in the letters of the Name, and these are his words: "At the time that the redemption [purkana de-fiku] comes, it rises and descends, like an offering that rises and descends: the upper Heh rises to the Yod, and the lower Heh descends to the Vav. What was  Y H H V  returns to be  Y H V H: father with mother, son with daughter." Thus far his words.

And he said that "an offering that rises and descends" is the ascent of Binah to Chokhmah and the descent of Malkhut to Tiferet, so as to unify them with a complete union. And this is "an offering to YHVH" (Leviticus 1:2), whose explanation is the union of the letters of the four-letter name and their drawing near [kiruv], as Rashbi explained (there, fol. 103b). And behold, since at times the daughter is with the father—as in the matter of "YHVH by wisdom founded the earth" (Proverbs 3:19)—and the son with the mother—as in the matter of "by understanding He established the heavens"—then, when this matter is so, the order of the letters of the Name is thus:  Y H H V. And the first Heh is Malkhut and the second Binah; for it is impossible to say that the first Heh is Binah and the second Malkhut, for then he would turn out to enter the upper Jerusalem before his entering the lower Jerusalem, and this is the reverse of what is fitting. Therefore the first Heh of the name  Y H H V  must be in Malkhut—and this is the daughter with the father—and the second Heh in Binah, the mother with the Vav, which is the son. And since this matter is so, when there is "an offering that rises and descends"—meaning the ascent of Binah to the father and the descent of Malkhut to the son—the Name is then found to be set in order as it is written, straightforwardly: the name  Y H V H. And on this he explained there what is said, "Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife" (Genesis 2:24): that is, Tiferet, which was separated from the first Heh and was unified with the last Heh; and they are father with mother, son with daughter. And since this matter is so, Rabbi Shimon asked that Elder and said: what was first—the ascent of Binah to be unified with Chokhmah, or the descent of Malkhut to Tiferet? And this is what he said: "Who rises first, or who descends?" And that Elder answered and said that necessarily [first comes] the descent of Tiferet, from the place of its distance, to Malkhut, who is exiled in exile; and afterward Yod, which is the father, rises to be unified with Binah. And they said, "Vav descends first"; and it would have been fitting that he say "Heh descends first," for this is  Y H H V, as we have explained, and likewise "the upper Heh rises to the Yod"; and he did not say so, but "Vav descends," etc., because it is the explanation of the name  Y H V H, which is son to mother and father to daughter. And it too rises and descends: for in order to unify them it is necessary that Vav descend to Heh, which is Tiferet to Malkhut, and that Yod rise to Heh, which is Chokhmah rising to Binah. And he said that first Vav, which is Tiferet, is unified with Malkhut, which is Heh, before Yod, which is the father, is unified with Heh, which is the mother. And he gave a reason for the thing: "and I will not enter into the city" (Hosea 11:9); and they expounded (Ta'anit, fol. 5a): "I will not enter into the Jerusalem above until I enter into the Jerusalem below." And the upper Jerusalem is Binah; and Chokhmah will not enter and be unified with her until Tiferet enters and is unified with Malkhut, which is the Jerusalem below.

And behold, he has revealed to us in this that Chokhmah and Binah are not unified in the secret of the coupling of male and female until Tiferet and Malkhut, bridegroom and his bride, are coupled; so that because of this they said that it is necessary that first Vav be unified with Heh, and afterward Yod with Heh. And behold, with respect to this aspect is the matter of the divorce: that the two mothers were driven away—and the verse shale'ach teshalach, and "the two of them went."

And further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, himself explained this matter in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 50, fol. 84), and these are his words: "And it is necessary to return Yod to Heh, which is the place above, and to return Vav to Heh, which is the place below; because the Holy One, blessed be He, swore that He would not return to the Heh above until He returns to the Heh below. And the secret of the matter: 'and I will not enter into the city,' etc.; and they have established it." Thus far his words. And for our intent it is clear.
And behold, this chapter is complete.

After we have set this matter upon two strong pillars, the words of the divine Rashbi, we have seen fit to set right a few passages that appear at first glance to oppose this matter. First, in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 4), and these are its words: "Rabbi Shimon said: It is all well [said]; but the secret of the matter is: 'Eat, friends,' above; 'drink and be drunk, lovers,' below (Song of Songs 5:1). Rabbi Elazar said to him: Who are those above, and who are those below? He said to him: Your question is fitting. This is the supernal place, those who are in joy, in oneness, who never separate; these are called 'friends.' This is what is written: 'And a river goes out from Eden' (Genesis 2:10). And Eden and that river never separate, and they are found forever in desire, in oneness, in joy. 'Drink and be drunk, lovers': these are the ones below, who are called 'lovers' at known times; and we have already established it. Come and see: of those upper ones, eating is written without drinking. What is the reason? One who has jugs of wine needs food; and because the guarded wine dwells there, eating is written of them. And of those lower ones, who need watering, drinking is written of them; for all the plantings need watering from the deep stream. And therefore, of these, eating, and of these, drinking; these are friends and these are lovers. Rabbi Elazar said to him: It appears that 'lovers' are [a term of] affection; what is the reason they are the lower ones? He said to him: Those who crave one another and are not found [together] constantly are called 'lovers'; and those who are found [together] constantly, and are not covered, and do not separate from one another, are called 'friends.' And therefore these are friends and these are lovers: these in desire, in oneness, in joy constantly, and these in craving at times. And this is the perfection of all, so that Knesset Yisrael is blessed; and then there is joy in all the worlds." Thus far his words.

And at first glance it appears that Chokhmah and Binah are the friends above, and they never separate; and the lovers below, who are Tiferet and Malkhut, have joining and union at intervals. And this thing opposes the matter of the third union, which we proved from the words of Rashbi in the previous chapter. And one cannot deflect this and say that the matter of the union mentioned in this passage is the second union, which concerns the effluence that increases and [in which] the first three are reckoned as one, as we explained in the previous chapter. For if so, why specifically "lovers," who are Tiferet and Malkhut, of whom he said that they crave one another and their union is at intervals? Let all seven sefirot of the Structure also be lovers; and why specifically the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah? Rather, this certainly appears to oppose the matter that we explained above. And before we enter into the explanation of this passage, we shall set forth one premise, and by it everything will be set right. For although in the previous chapter we said that the matter of coupling is in Chokhmah with Binah and in Tiferet with Malkhut, nevertheless the coupling of Chokhmah with Binah is not like the coupling of Tiferet with Malkhut, and there is a great difference between them. For the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut is at intervals, that is to say, at known hours, as in the matter of the hour of the Amidah, at "Sim Shalom" [Grant peace], as is explained in the words of Rashbi, and as will be explained in a book of its own, if God decrees life.

And behold, that coupling does not stand all day and all the time, but only a known hour, at a fixed time; and after that time each one returns to its place, and Malkhut comes to her place to lead the lower ones and to pasture the flocks of her sheep, for she is a shepherd. Although she will be in great peace and great effluence, that good effluence will not be the cause of the coupling; for "does the plowman plow all day to sow?" (Isaiah 28:24). Rather, he pours forth to her effluence and food for her and her maidens (Proverbs 31:15), and they take pleasure with great pleasure. But "the seed of man" (Jeremiah 31:27), which is the souls, will be only at alternating times, and known days, and appointed hours. This is the matter of the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut. But the coupling of Chokhmah and Binah stands forever; it will never change; they are joined and will not separate (Job 41:9). And what we say, that their coupling will never change and never separate, the intent is not that it will never separate at all. Rather, the intent is that their coupling is not like the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut, who even in a time of peace separate and unite from time to time, and after their uniting they separate until the time of their turn comes. And Chokhmah and Binah are not so; rather, they are always joined and do not separate, except in the time of the destruction, when there is no union there, because of the time in which He will not enter into the Jerusalem above, etc., as we have explained. And with this premise this passage will be understood. And now we enter into its explanation. "Rabbi Shimon said: It is all well [said]." The matter is that above this passage they expounded the verse "I have come into my garden," etc. (Song of Songs 5:1), and explained various explanations of it. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, answered on this that "it is all well [said], but the secret of the matter" — meaning that they did not explain the matter of lovers and friends, and he came to explain it; and he intended to hide the secret, and included much in few words. And they said, "Eat, friends, above; drink and be drunk, lovers, below." And the explanation of "above": the intent is the known friends, who are father and mother, Chokhmah and Binah; and the lovers are son and daughter, Tiferet and Malkhut. And Rabbi Elazar too was not ignorant of this premise, for "it is known in all the earth" (Isaiah 12:5) to all who enter the gate of this wisdom. But he was in doubt about two things. One, the matter of eating above and drinking below, which is the reverse of the matter, as we shall explain.

And further, "lovers" seems [to denote] coupling and love more than "friends"; for "friends," on the face of it, is mere friendship, while "lovers" is a word of love and affection. And on the contrary, it would be more correct that "friends," which is not so much coupling, be below, and "lovers," which is more so, be above; because above they do not separate, which is not so below, where they separate, as we have explained. And Rashbi answered both of them, and said, "Your question is fitting" (so is the principal reading; and there are books that read, "This question is fitting"). It is possible that he wondered at him, since he was a lion son of a lion and expert in the chambers of wisdom, that he should be in doubt even about these things; [this was] because of the great subtlety of their intellect and the depth of their dialectic. And he answered the first thing first: to what he said, that it would have been fitting to say "lovers above, friends below," as we have explained, he answered: "the supernal place, those who are in joy, in oneness, who do not separate," etc. He tripled the matter, to allude to the three unions. "In joy" is the second union, which is the pouring-forth, [in which] the three of them are reckoned as one, as we explained in the previous chapter; and the matter of their union is in an abundance of effluence and gladness that unites them, and this is "in joy." And for the first union, which is their union from the beginning of their emanation, he said "in oneness," namely, the union of the sefirot. And for the third union, which is the coupling, he said "who never separate," all the days that there is peace in the world, as we explained in the premise. "These are called friends": meaning, for this reason, because their union is the utmost union, so that they never crave one another, they are called "friends." For just as it is not applicable to say of friends that they crave one another, so these sefirot, being forever united and not craving one another, are called "friends"; and this is his saying, "these are called friends." "This is what is written: 'And a river goes out from Eden.'" It was difficult for him, for the verse said the reverse of this, in saying "and a river goes out from Eden," explained as: "and a river," Binah, "goes out from Eden," Chokhmah, as it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Mishpatim, and we shall copy its wording in the Gate of Names, chapter 11.

And behold, the verse said "and a river goes out from Eden," meaning Binah, who separates from Chokhmah after the coupling; and this opposes what he said, "who never separate." To this he answered and said: on the contrary, from the verse there is a proof; and this is what he intended in saying, "This is what is written: 'And a river goes out from Eden.'" "And Eden and that river never separate": meaning, be precise, for it said "goes out" and did not say "went out," in the past tense, which would imply that after they were united their union separated; for this reason it said "goes out," which is the present, which implies that they are forever united, for it forever goes out from it and stands in it. And this is what it says: "and Eden," namely Chokhmah, "and river," namely Binah — the verse intended to tell us that they never separate. "And they are found in desire, in oneness, in joy": he intended to triple the expression in order to point to the three unions. When he said "in desire," that is the third union, which is the coupling, which is the pleasing will, namely, desire [re'uta]. "And oneness" is the union that unites them from the beginning of the Emanation; it is the first union that we mentioned. "And joy" is the second union, the effluence "that gladdens God and men" (Judges 9:13). And in truth these three have no order, and we have not found a reason for this matter. "'Drink and be drunk, lovers': these are the ones below," etc. He intended to attribute the name "lovers" specifically to those below, because their union is at known times, as he explained at the end. And this is what he said, "who are called 'lovers' at times"; and therefore only the name "lovers" fits them. "And we have already established it": it is possible that they had engaged in this exposition on another occasion. Or he means, "and we have already established it" by what he opened with at the beginning of his words, "drink and be drunk, lovers, below"; and after he explained the matter of "friends," the reason for "lovers" is implied of itself, and therefore he said "and we have already established it." And after he resolved the matter of friends above and lovers below, he came to resolve the matter of eating and drinking, and said, "Come and see: of those upper ones, eating is written," etc. Meaning: the matter of eating is a title for the things that are revealed in the Emanation, in the likeness of eating, which applies only to thick and coarse things; but drinking is titled for things more subtle than eating. Therefore it was difficult for Rabbi Elazar, for it would have been fitting to say "drinking" of Chokhmah and Binah, who are the friends, since Chokhmah and Binah are subtle with the utmost subtlety; and therefore their matter and their action, and their effluence that is poured to them, ought to be titled with the expression "drinking," which is a title for subtlety, as befits them. But of Tiferet and Malkhut, who are more revealed, it would be fitting to say "eating," which is an allusion to thick and coarse effluence, which is not like the subtlety of the former, as befits their rank. And therefore Rashbi, peace be upon him, answered that, on the contrary, "one who has jugs of wine needs food," etc. For the sefirot that are above are in subtlety, and they are the grapes in which the wine is guarded. And therefore their union and their perfection is when the sefirot that spread out and are revealed below, which is the eating, rise to them, to the subtle manifestation. And so the sefirot in subtlety turn out to include also the sefirot after their revealing; and the roots turn out to be unified with the branches, by way of the ascent of the branches to the place of the roots. And from this great benefit is drawn to the supernal subtlety, for they receive abundant effluence and blessing by their means, as in the matter that they said, "the Shekhinah among the lower ones is a need on high," as will be explained in this Gate. "And of those lower ones, who need watering," etc.: meaning, and in those lower ones, which are the expansion, son and daughter, in whom all seven sefirot are included, their essence is eating, that is, revealing. And therefore they need to unite with the upper sources, the subtle ones concealed in Chokhmah and Binah, so that by their means they receive abundant effluence and good. And when they are united in their source, and their source in them, they receive effluence from above in subtlety, which is likened to drinking. Because the expression "eating" was also correct of them, being the effluence to their rank below — and therefore he could also have said "eat, friends and lovers" — therefore he answered and said, "for all the plantings," etc. Meaning: all the sefirot that spread out need to receive the effluence "from the deep stream," namely Binah, the source of all the sources, in the secret of planting and transplanting that we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 6. And therefore they always need the drinking, which is the principal thing, so that they suck from the deep stream; that is, so that the effluence that is poured below be like the subtlety that is above, and not become thick, though it is poured by way of the channels. And because of this great benefit, it is said "drinking" below and "eating" above. "And therefore, of these, eating," etc.: meaning, now, by what he said, the matter of eating above and drinking below is resolved, and likewise the matter of friends above and lovers below is resolved. "Rabbi Elazar said to him: It appears that," etc. Rabbi Elazar asked this matter because Rashbi was lengthy in attributing friends to above and brief in attributing lovers to below, for he said only "lovers: these are the ones below, who are called 'lovers' at known times"; and on the face of it this implies that they are lovers [only] at times. If so — "lovers" is a word of love and affection — then why should he not title the upper ones "lovers," since the expression "lovers" applies to them as well? And it is fitting for a master of language to say of the upper ones what would not be correct of the lower ones, and to say of the lower ones what would not be correct of the upper ones. And here, since the expression "lovers" is a word of affection, then at the least "lovers" should be equal to the word "friends"; if so, why are they the lower ones, so that the word "lovers" is not on a par with the word "friends"? "He said to him: Those who crave one another," etc. He came to explain that the word "lovers," although it is an expression of affection, is an affection that indicates distance; for only those who are distant from one another are called "lovers." And this is the expression "lovers," whose explanation is that each one of them is a lover [dod] to his fellow and craves him, and they are not found together except from time to time. But "friends" is explained by their being companions and united forever, never distanced so that they would crave one another; and these are Chokhmah and Binah, who never separate, etc. "And therefore these are friends and these are lovers": meaning, for this reason "lovers" is correct specifically of Tiferet and Malkhut and not of others, and "friends" of Chokhmah and Binah and not of others. "These in desire, in oneness, in joy constantly": and in saying these three words he alludes to the three unions, as we have explained. "And this is the perfection of all": because he explained, according to the give-and-take, that the lovers and friends are Tiferet and Malkhut and Chokhmah and Binah; but from the verse it is implied that the union in this verse is the union of the six extremities, as in the matter of "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey, I have drunk my wine," etc. (Song of Songs 5:1), which is the union of Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet with Netzach, Hod, Yesod and Malkhut, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Pinchas, fol. 244), and we copied its wording in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 3. If so, how does the verse deal with the lovers and friends alone? It ought to have dealt with all six extremities. And to this he answered, "And this is the perfection of all, so that [Knesset Yisrael] is blessed," etc. Meaning, in the blessing of the bride from the bridegroom, that is, the union of Tiferet and Malkhut; and their coupling is the union of all six extremities, and it is all one matter. And so they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 37), and these are its words: "And when they receive, all the sefirot receive from one another, and the angels below receive one from another; this is what is written, 'and they receive one from another.' And each and every one gives permission to enter into the domain of its fellow, as it is said, 'and they give permission to one another.'" Thus far its words.

And the intent is that when Tiferet and Malkhut unite — for it is about them that [the passage] stands there — he says that all the sefirot unite in their union. Or he means to say, "And this is the perfection of all," etc., meaning: it was difficult for him that at the beginning of the verse, "I have come into my garden," etc., which are the words of the bridegroom to his bride toward union — if so, how did he say "eat, friends," who are Chokhmah and Binah, who have no relation at all to this? To this he said, "And this is the perfection of all, so that Knesset Yisrael is blessed": meaning, for union is impossible for the upper ones, who are Chokhmah and Binah, except through the union of the lower ones, who are Tiferet and Malkhut. "And then there is joy in all the worlds": meaning, for even the angels that are below the Emanation have great benefit in this, for they unite and receive from one another; for there are male angels, who are angels of peace, from the side of the male, and angels of righteousness from the side of the female. And when righteousness and peace unite (see Psalms 85:11), which is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, these angels unite in the secret of males and females. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim in many places. Thus far the explanation of the passage. And so we learn that when iniquity does not cause [otherwise], and there is peace in the land, and the Temple is on its foundation, then Chokhmah and Binah are united and never separate from one another. And their union is forever "like a man joined with his companion" [ke-ma'ar ish ve-loyot] (1 Kings 7:36), since Malkhut takes pleasure in abundant peace, although she couples with her husband only at known times, as is explained above. But through iniquities, as in the time of the destruction, there is no union and coupling, neither in the Jerusalem above nor in the Jerusalem below. And indeed, the difference for Malkhut between this time and the time of peace is that now her sustenance is by means of an agent, and she is in a house by herself; she suffices for small matters and does not suffice for great ones. And after there is a time of peace, she will unite with her husband in a house set apart for the two of them, and effluence and food will be poured upon them without end. And she will be "married to a husband" [be'ulat ba'al]: "in the rising [be-aliyato] of the husband she rises with him, and does not descend" (Ketubbot 61a); and she will suffice with light and effluence for great and small. And this is not the matter of the coupling; for the coupling is the union "like a man joined with his companion," to beget, in likeness, new souls. And even afterward, when "the light of the moon will be as the light of the sun," etc. (Isaiah 30:26), nevertheless the coupling will be at intervals, as before her diminution, though also more praiseworthy. And therefore these are friends and these are lovers: this is a coupling that does not separate, and this is a coupling that separates until the time of its turn comes; and so they will couple each and every day. Thus far reaches what appears to us in resolving this matter. Further, there appears at first glance to be a contradicting passage, found in Parashat Lech Lecha (fol. 95), and these are its words: "We have learned: when Yod and Heh join [kad mitchabberan yod be-heh], then it is written, 'And a river goes out from Eden to water the garden' (Genesis 2:10). And do not say 'when they join'; rather, 'they join,' certainly." Thus far its words.

And at first glance it appears that it is not applicable to say of them "when they join," for it would seem that they join at intervals, and there are times when they are not joined and united. To this he said, "they join, certainly," namely, that above the two of them join and never separate from one another. Nevertheless, when it is examined with good insight, one will find that it is "our man of peace" (Psalms 41:10), especially by what we set forth in the previous passage. And before we enter into its explanation, we must be precise: why did he say "when they join," so that he needed to say "and do not say," etc.? Let him say from the outset, "Yod and Heh join and never separate, and then it is written, 'And a river goes out from Eden'"; and why did he twist his language? And the matter is that "the river" can be explained as Tiferet or as Binah, and "the garden" is Malkhut or the six extremities, according to the explanation. And the title "river" [nahar] is a title for a manifestation of great light, from the expression "and light [nehora] dwells with Him" (Daniel 2:22). And likewise it is an allusion to the running of the shining effluence, like the matter of a river, which never ceases. And now he said "when Yod," namely Chokhmah, "and Heh," namely Binah, "join"; and then, by means of their union, Tiferet is exalted, so that it is called "a river that goes out from Eden," Binah, etc.; for then its effluence shines and increases and is poured to Malkhut. Or then, by means of their union, Binah is exalted until she is called "a river that goes out" from Chokhmah, which is Eden, and waters the garden, that is, the seven days of the Structure. And he said "and do not say," etc., so that we not err and say that the union of Chokhmah and Binah is like the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, who separate after their union. Rather, "they join, certainly," for their union is forever and they never separate from one another, at a time that is a time of peace. And he said "when they join" because there is a time when they are not united, as in the matter of the exile, which is a time of emergency; for then He swore, "and I will not enter into the city" (Hosea 11:9), that He will not enter into the Jerusalem above, etc., as is explained above. Or it is possible to explain it in another way: "when they join" means "with respect to their joining and their union, it is written, 'And a river goes out,'" etc.; and "and a river goes out" is explained according to the explanation we explained above, in chapter 14. And this is to inform us of this choice quality: that the matter of "the river," and the matter of "goes out," which is the present, whose explanation is that it forever goes out and does not cease — this is with respect to her knowledge. And his saying "and do not say" means: so that we not err in his words and say that the matter of "when they join" means that there is a time when they do not join; rather, they join forever, certainly. And the word "when" [kad] is to indicate that this matter is only with respect to their joining.

And the matter of joining can be explained as we explained above, namely, in a time of peace. Or we may explain: "and a river" is Chokhmah, "and Eden" is Keter Elyon, "and garden" is Binah; for so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 55, fol. 85). And now, the matter of "when they join" is not intended for literal coupling, which is the third union that we explained in the previous chapter; for if so, he ought to have said "when they couple." Rather, the intent is the second union, which is the aspect [in which] the three are reckoned as one. And he said that this is the aspect of "And a river goes out from Eden to water the garden"; for it is with respect to the union and joining of Chokhmah with Binah that the verse said "and a river goes out from Eden." Meaning, the verse did not come to expound to us the union and oneness of Chokhmah in Keter — for "who does not know in all these?" (Job 12:9) — but rather it is the aspect of the union of Chokhmah and Binah that the verse intended to explain to us. And because from the word "when" one could come to error, thinking that at times they are united and at times they are not united, therefore he said, "and do not say 'when they join,'" which is an indication of time; for this is not so, but rather, certainly, "they join." Thus far reaches the explanation of this passage. And by one of these ways the inquirer will be able to set right "wherever any breach is found" (2 Kings 12:6), so that the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, do not contradict one another, God forbid.

After we have walked in the previous chapters as we have walked in the matter of the first three, we have seen fit in this chapter to speak of them, and of the lengths to which our sages, of blessed memory, went in saying that it is not fitting to speak at length about them. And it is found in the book of the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (fol. 93a; and similarly in Parashat Vayetze, fol. 158), and these are its words: "'You shall surely send away the mother, and the young you may take for yourself,' etc. (Deuteronomy 22:7). [The mother is] the secret of the supernal world, in which permission to gaze was not given; and one must send away questioning and gazing from it. 'And the young you may take for yourself': as it is written, 'For ask now of the first days,' etc., 'and from one end of heaven to the other end of heaven' (Deuteronomy 4:32). But above the end of heaven, 'you shall surely send away' asking from your thoughts. And of this it is written, 'that it may go well with you, and you may prolong your days,' etc. As it is written, 'you may take for yourself': it is in a person's domain." Thus far its words.

And among what is fitting to be precise about in this passage is his saying, "'You shall surely send away': the secret of the supernal world," etc., "and one must send away questioning" — that it is not fitting to ask about it at all, and this is "to send away questioning." And so it is proven from what he said: "'And the young you may take for yourself': as it is written, 'For ask now of the first days.'" Meaning: if you wish to speak and to ask, [do so] specifically about the days, which are the young; for of the mother, "you shall surely send away," etc. The sum of the matter appears to be that it is forbidden to ask from Binah upward, and even about Binah it is forbidden to ask. And it is difficult, for in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 126b), Rashbi explained that it is permitted to ask. And these are his words: "'Who' [Mi]: we have established it — the supernal grade above, the beginning that stands in question." Thus far his words.

This implies that it is called Mi, "Who," an expression of questioning, to indicate that here is the place of the question. And it is forced to say that the intent is to say that here there is a place of question, but not that it is permitted to ask; because elsewhere in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 193a) the reverse of this appears. And these are its words: "Rabbi Elazar opened and said: 'YHVH, You are my God; I will exalt You, I will praise Your name,' etc. (Isaiah 25:1). This verse is the secret of the faith. YHVH: the supernal secret, the beginning of the supernal point, enclosed, which is not known. My God [Elohai]: the secret of 'a still small voice' (1 Kings 19:12); and it is the beginning that stands for question, and it is enclosed and not known, and there is none who answers about it, because it is enclosed and concealed and stored away. You [Atah]: this is the right, the beginning that stands for question and for answering about it; and it is a priest forever, as it is said, 'You are a priest forever' (Psalms 110:4)." Thus far its words, as relevant to our matter. And its intent is clear: that YHVH is certainly Chokhmah; and Chokhmah is called "beginning" because it is the beginning of the revealing of the Emanation. "Enclosed, which is not known": the intent is that above Chokhmah is Keter, and it is in hiddenness and concealment, for Keter is not apprehended, not even its concealment, as we went at length on this in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter. "My God: the secret of 'a still small voice,' and it," etc.: meaning, for Binah too is called "beginning," and in that she is a beginning, [she is] the place of the question. And the intent is certainly that there questioning is permitted, although there is no apprehension of an answer; since he said, "You: this is the right, the beginning that stands for question and for answering about it," it implies that there is no difference between this one and that one, except that in Binah there is question and no answer, and in Chesed there is question and answer. And just as in Chesed it is certainly permitted to ask — as he said in the passage before us, "For ask now of the first days" — so it is certainly permitted to ask about Binah, although there is no answer. And from where do we [derive] to distinguish between this one and that one, since he did not vary his language, and of all of them he said alike "that stands for question," etc.? And besides all this, one must investigate the matter of sending away the mother, and that it is not fitting to speak of the first three: what are we dealing with? If it is to tell us that it is not fitting to expound them or their matter — that is impossible, for we have seen Rashbi, peace be upon him, engaging with them and with their matter: whether in Keter, in the matter of the 620 pillars of light, and many matters expounded about it in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and especially in the Tikkunim; and likewise in Chokhmah, in the matter of the thirty-two paths of wisdom, and several other expositions expounded without searching out and without end; and likewise in Binah and her fifty gates. And we will not believe that Rashbi, peace be upon him, was one who expounds well but does not practice well, God forbid. And if we wish to say that the matter of this warning is to the prophets who gaze through the mirrors [aspaklariot], that they should take care not to ask about the matter of these three attributes — this is difficult, for in prophecy they apprehended as far as Keter, and only Keter alone was hidden from them; as is alluded to in the visions of Ezekiel, when he reached Keter he said, "[and I saw,] and I fell upon my face" (Ezekiel 1:28), as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Introduction, fol. 6b). And although he apprehended them only in images, "like a seal of wax," as will be explained in the Gate of ABYA, even so he already apprehended as far as Keter. And according to the truth, a prophet never apprehended the sefirot themselves, God forbid, as will be explained in the Gate of the Palaces. And if so, when we investigate the matter of this warning about the first three, we do not find a place for it at all. And therefore we say that the matter of these attributes is that they are predicates of the Emanator, blessed be He: as in the matter of Chesed, that is to say, "kind" [chasid], for He performs kindness by means of this Chesed and is called by it "kind"; and likewise wise through Chokhmah, mighty through Gevurah, understanding through Binah. And now, when the inquirer wishes to contemplate His attributes that belong to Him, we shall say of some of them how: since the first is called Thought or Intellect, and it is Keter — behold, when a person comes to apprehend its essence, it is certainly forbidden, for he has imagined he could apprehend what is not within possibility. And is it possible for a person to apprehend the Thought of the Emanator, who emanated from the head of the Emanation through the whole order of the great and awesome grades, and brought forth all the existents from privation into being? Certainly such a man, as it were, touches the Keter [crown] of the King of the world. And likewise Chokhmah is the wisdom of the Emanator, and He and His wisdom are one. And is it possible for a person to apprehend the wisdom of the King of the world, God forbid? For Chokhmah is literally near to His intellect and His thought; yet Chokhmah is not literally the intellect, for the intellect is more unified with His Self, since the intellect is more subtle than wisdom. And from man we can know this matter: for the intellect is literally the person, while wisdom is a thing outside him. And in the Emanator it is not so; rather, He and His wisdom are one. But with all this, His wisdom is not unified like the union of His intellect and His thought, which is Keter; for this is the first emanated, and that is the second emanated. And likewise Binah is a person's power to apprehend something out of wisdom; and behold, it is not fitting for a person to imagine contemplating the understanding of the Emanator, since they are among the things that touch His Self, and they are literally His very Self. Although all the attributes are His Self, with all this these differ from all of them, since their service is in the place of holiness; and since they are in the Self, it is forbidden to gaze at their essence and Self. For one who wishes to apprehend the essence and Self of these three touches the Self and essence of the Emanator Himself, and "breaches a fence" (Ecclesiastes 10:8), whereby harm will reach him and not benefit — as it were, he rebels against the Kingdom. And to this end they said that the first three are reckoned as one, for they are the intellect, the wisdom and the understanding. And therefore He warned us in His Torah not to rebel against His crown, God forbid, and not to imagine we could apprehend the essence of the Self of His intellect and His wisdom and His understanding. But Chesed and Gevurah and Tiferet and Netzach and Hod and the Righteous One and Malkhut are attributes, as it were, other than Him; that is to say, they are united in Him with the utmost union, but they are for the governance of the world, and apprehension of them is possible. For from His kindness in the world we know the way of the governance of His Chesed in the world, and we can apprehend the way in which the Emanator conducts Himself with the attribute of Chesed. And likewise Gevurah; and likewise His being glorified in this world we can apprehend from His awesome deeds that He has done; and so His eternity and His victory, and likewise His majesty, and likewise His righteousness, and likewise His kingship. All these attributes we can discuss [lit. give and take in], since they are attributes in which we can apprehend some apprehension of the way of His governance by them, according to the actions born of them in this world. But in His intellect, which is His thought, and in His wisdom and His understanding — who can apprehend the matter of His thoughts, which are deep and lofty (see Psalms 92:6)? And who can apprehend the side by which He conducts Himself in His thought, and the way in which He grows wise in His wisdom, and likewise the way in which He conducts Himself to understand in His understanding? This is impossible, and it is among the things from which we are warned to keep apart, so that we not stumble, God forbid. And since these three grades are not equal, as we have explained — for each one is more distant from our apprehension than its fellow, by reason of its nearness to the Emanator — therefore they are concealed in the language of the Torah, as in the matter of "YHVH, You are my God," expounded in the Zohar, which we copied above.

And behold, in Chokhmah no pronoun suffix [kinnui] at all was required, as in the matter of Elohai, whose explanation is "my God"; rather, YHVH, without anything indicating revelation at all — to indicate that it is in concealed Chokhmah, and it is the beginning of revealing, as in the matter of the prophets, where the station of their apprehension is in the seeing of visions [ra'ayonim] in the apprehension of prophecy. And this is what is intended in the words of the passage in saying "the beginning of the point," etc. The intent is that he did not mention Keter, since it is more concealed than Chokhmah; but Chokhmah is "the beginning of the supernal point," etc., for in it there is the beginning of revealing to the prophets, as we have explained — not the apprehension of the Self and the essence, God forbid, but the apprehension of its effluence and its light, "running and returning" (Ezekiel 1:14). And of Binah, because she is more apprehended, he said "my God," for there is in it some indication of revealing, in saying Elohai, whose explanation is "my God." And this is what he said: "and it is the beginning that stands for question," etc.; and the matter of the question we shall explain. "You" [Atah] indicates what is apprehended, as one speaking to Him in the second person; and this is what he said: "this is the right, the beginning that stands for question and for answering." And the more one engages in them, the more praiseworthy he is, provided only that he take care against error, God forbid. And he said, "and it is a priest forever": meaning, this attribute is the beginning of engagement and speech toward all the worlds, for from there is the beginning of apprehension, and it is drawn from there to the end of the grades. And we shall say that there is a difference between Chokhmah and Binah. For Chokhmah is what already belongs to Him, and not an addition of anything; and therefore in the engagement of His wisdom it follows that no consequent action comes to be, since He revels in His wisdom, not that from that reveling a consequent coming-to-be would follow — as in the matter of a person who revels and takes pleasure in what he has become wise in, not that from that reveling any addition of wisdom is born at all; for if so, that would be Binah, which is the one who understands one thing out of another. And so is the matter with the Emanator, with the distinction that is between us and Him, which the mouth cannot speak or liken. But when He understands with His understanding, behold, [something] will be understood, and a new coming-to-be will come to be, which was not until now; and this is a coming-to-be drawn out to the lower ones from Binah, which is what is understood out of the action in Binah. And it is the manifestation of the roots concealed in Binah, which is the voice that goes out of the shofar while it is concealed within the inwardness; and this is the "still small voice" mentioned in the passage "YHVH, my God," which we explained. And there it "stands in question," but not so that it is apprehended, since it is concealed within the depths of Binah. And the apprehension of those attributes within Binah, in the manifestation of His governance by them, has question and no answer, according to their nearness to Binah, about whom questioning is still forbidden. And therefore the apprehension of His governance in Chesed and in Gevurah and in Tiferet and in Netzach and in Hod and the Righteous One [text: ve-ha-tzedakot] and Malkhut, which are concealed there, is permitted for questioning, but there is no answer; for there is no knowledge to apprehend, because of the concealment and hiddenness, by reason of the nearness to Binah, about whom questioning is forbidden, as we have explained. And now the words of the passage are correct, in saying "For ask now of the first days," which are these attributes. But as for the first three, apprehension of their Self and their essence is forbidden altogether. And with this the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, have been explained "in all their dwelling places," and the rest of the wording of the passages is clear. And from God we ask forgiveness and atonement for what has been expounded.

Since it has already risen in our agreement that speech about the apprehension of His governance in the six extremities of the Structure is permitted, if so, we shall not withhold our hands from discussing what the early ones wrote about them. The first is the attribute of Chesed. And its action is chesed [kindness], after its name, and its actions are drawn from Chokhmah. And the essence of its governance is to annul the power of the husks, to subdue them and to make them cease. And this is the reason for the Flood, which was by water: although those waters were from the Other Side, nevertheless it was already in water. Or it would be a husk from the side of Chesed; or the accuser receives from its side in order to purify the world of all the impurities of that evil generation. And because the action of this attribute is against the impurity and the husk, of it is said, "and a God who is indignant every day" (Psalms 7:12); and it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tzav, fol. 31) that He is indignant at the accusers, so that they not accuse. And this action was necessitated in this attribute because its attribute is to act in kindness, that is to say, not according to judgment, but to sustain and to do good to the wicked and to the good.

Behold, at the tranquility of the sinner the husk cries out "violence!", saying, "These are idol-worshippers," etc., as is its evil custom, to accuse and to expose the blemishes of human beings. And if it were not within its power to be indignant at them and to annul them, its action would be annulled and judgment would go on increasing. Therefore, in order to perform its action and "to stop the mouth of those who speak falsehood" (Psalms 63:12), it was necessary, according to the decree of His wisdom, may He be exalted, that the ability to make the husks cease be in its hand, so that they not accuse and confound its joy; for its joy is in its action, which is the action of kindness.

And behold, among the action of this attribute are all the things that are in the secret of whiteness; that is to say, all the things in which whiteness indicates the attribute of Chesed — such as the stones that are white in their color, which by their special property are for grace and for kindness, since their manifestation is poured forth from Chesed; and things besides these, which are explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles.

And further, among the actions of this attribute is love; for such is its action above, in the secret of coupling: to love and to bring near the bridegroom and his bride. And although this action is at times found [attributed] to Gevurah, as will be explained in the Glossary of Titles, the matter is that love is aroused from Gevurah and completed by means of this attribute. And "from our flesh we behold God" (see Job 19:26): for first a man is aroused to love of his female from the side of ardor and heat, and afterward that love is fixed in his heart from the side of the softness of his heart. And there are times when it will be the reverse; all according to the one who marries and the one who is married [ha-nose ve-ha-nasu]. And it is explained from the words of our sages, of blessed memory, and of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that wisdom is poured forth to a person from the side of this attribute, in partnership with Chokhmah, which is above it; and they gave a sign for the matter: "one who wishes to become wise should turn south" (Bava Batra 25b). And likewise they said that light, and what resembles it, is alluded to in it; and the secret is "the menorah in the south," and from there its light goes out to the world. And there are many matters of the actions that it is impossible to include here, but [only] in the explanation of the titles in the Glossary of Titles. And this attribute is not compassion and kindness like Chokhmah, since it was blended and unified with Gevurah in the secret of the Binding [of Isaac], as we shall explain; for it is of the perfection of this attribute that it be forever unified with Gevurah. And therefore, from the side of the Gevurah that is in it, some of the actions of judgment are attributed to it, in dryness, on the southern side; for so it is called Negev [the dry land]. And as the verse said, "Your right hand, YHVH, glorious in power" (Exodus 15:6), as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Beshalach, and many places besides. And this way [applies] also to Gevurah: that it is of its perfection, although it is the strength of judgment, that it be included in Chesed; and this is the secret of moisture in the north, although the north is an allusion to Gevurah. And this is the secret of the Binding of Isaac, in which fire was included in water and water in fire, as is explained in the Zohar, in the portion of the Binding. And it is known of this attribute that there are in it seventy-two bridges; and the allusion to them is the seventy-two names that are in Vayisa, Vayavo and Vayet (Exodus 14:19–21). And Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah, peace be upon him, explained this matter in his lovely prayer, and these are his words: "You are One, in the hiddenness of the radiance; it is divided into seventy-two bridges, which indicate the sweat of the Chayyot, and from them [come] the upper waters; and they are called the fourth sefirah, and it is Chesed. And each and every bridge has a name, and they are crowned, arrayed in prepared words, going out from potential into actuality; and they are  V H V,  L Y," etc. Thus far his words.

And according to what appears from the expression "bridges," it is that these seventy-two lights in Chesed are channels and sources for the effluence poured forth from the upper ones by way of Chesed, which is the beginning of the Structure; and they are bridges to the waters of Chesed. And we may think that the seventy-two bridges are an allusion to three times twenty-four, twenty-four for each of the upper sefirot: twenty-four for Keter, twenty-four for Chokhmah, twenty-four for Binah.

And behold, these twenty-four are the twenty-four permutations that are permuted from the four-letter name, as we shall expand the explanation in the Gate of Particulars of Names, at the name of seventy-two. And since each name of the three four-letter names is an attribute in itself and a matter in itself — for Keter is the root of compassion, and Chokhmah the root of Chesed, and Binah the root of Din — therefore they were divided into the three divisions, twenty-four for each part. And the reason is that each and every name has four letters, which indicate in particular four sefirot, which are Chokhmah and Binah and Tiferet and Malkhut. And they are four, corresponding to the arrays in which the six extremities are revealed, as is explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation; therefore four times six is twenty-four. And likewise their permutation: six times for Yod, six times for Heh, six times for Vav, six times for Heh.

And the matter of the division of the names and their permutation into sixes and into twenty-fours is well resolved, as we shall explain their relation, their division and their matter in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapter 9. This is what appears to us at first glance concerning these seventy-two, without our lengthening on it at all; for it is clear to us that the matter bears an expansion of explanation, as the inquirer roams with his intellect. And brevity is good, especially in a place where we have no tradition about them and no sufficient revelation. And because each attribute of the first three includes all three, as we shall explain in the Gate of Arbiters, therefore seventy-two was poured forth to each one of the three Patriarchs. For from the three in Chokhmah, seventy-two [are poured] to Chesed; and so Chokhmah [chokhmah] amounts to seventy-three: seventy-two bridges, and Chokhmah, the great Chesed, hovering over them. And from the three in Binah seventy-two are poured to Gevurah, and from the three in Keter seventy-two is poured to Tiferet. And the principal seventy-two came in Chesed, and they are [said] in a borrowed sense of Tiferet and of Gevurah. Because in Keter and Binah the three points, which are the first three, are not in order: for in Keter they are the aspect of Keter, the aspect of itself, and the aspect of Chokhmah and Binah because of its pouring forth into them; and they are not in order. And in Binah they are likewise, because she receives from both of them, from Keter on one side and from Chokhmah on another side. And so for Keter, Chokhmah and Binah are in one equality; and likewise for Binah, Keter and Chokhmah are in one equality. But for Chokhmah, the aspects are in order: for it has the aspect of Keter, preceding all, from the side of its receiving from it; and its aspect from the side of itself, in the middle; and the aspect of Binah, from the side of its pouring forth into her. And behold, in it are the two aspects, each one according to its value; and therefore the principal seventy-two bridges are in Chesed.
And the matter of the seventy-two in Gevurah and the seventy-two in Tiferet will be explained in the Gate of the Palaces, in chapter 4.

And the second sefirah of the six days of the Structure is Gevurah. And it performs might [gevurah] and judgment, after its name, and all matters of judgments and mighty acts are poured forth from it. And it is a strap to chastise people with its discipline, to strengthen them and to arouse them in the service of the Creator. And likewise, by means of it, it gives power and might in a person to make the good inclination prevail over the evil inclination, as we explained in chapter 3. And likewise all the might by which Israel prevailed over their enemies was by its means, as it is written, "Through God we shall do valiantly" (Psalms 60:14). And every mighty man principally sucks from Gevurah (see the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 10: "and there, mighty men," etc.). And from the side of this attribute all the outer ones and the masters of judgment are poured forth; but there is a great difference between them. For the pure masters of judgment are poured forth from it from the pure side, in the secret of "pure gold"; and the lower ones, the masters of the husks, are poured forth from it from the side of the dross of the gold. And it needs those powers to judge this world in the damages of horn and ox and pit and donkey and the like. And they are impure straps "to chastise with scorpions" (1 Kings 12:11) the transgressors and the wanton. And among the actions of this attribute are all the things that are in the secret of redness; and from this attribute [come] the things in which redness indicates Gevurah, such as the stones that are red, whose special property is to cast fear upon creatures, because they suck from this attribute. And whatever else is found like these things is explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And from the side of this attribute also is the arousal of love, in the secret of the ardor of the inclination, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained: "the affection of intercourse." And from this attribute is the arousal in the secret of "and he loved her" (Genesis 24:67) (see Zohar, Chayei Sarah, fol. 133). And although love is also in Chesed, nevertheless the beginning of the arousal is from Gevurah, as will be explained in the Glossary of Titles, under the entry "love." And it is explained from the words of our sages, of blessed memory, and of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that wealth is poured forth to a person from this attribute; and they gave a sign for the matter: "one who wishes to become rich should turn north" (Bava Batra 25b). And likewise they said that fire and its like, and flame and its like, are in this attribute.

And further, they said that the principal sustenance is poured forth from this attribute; and the witness to this is "the table in the north," and from there sustenance comes to the world. And likewise the rains are poured forth from it, and therefore our sages, of blessed memory, titled them "the might of rains" (Mishnah Ta'anit 1:1), and explained: because they come down with might. And the hearing of every matter of outcry and prayer is in this place; and so it is explained from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. True, it is with the assistance of Binah; and therefore hearing is found for judgment and for compassion with the name Elohim — such as "And Elohim hearkened to her" (Genesis 30:22), and "And Elohim heard the voice of the lad" (Genesis 21:17); for judgment: "And Elohim heard, and His anger was kindled" (Numbers 11:1) (in our texts: "YHVH," and not Elohim). And seeing is in Chesed, and likewise "And YHVH saw"; and it is found for judgment and for compassion, and nevertheless all is in Chesed. And he gave a sign: re'iyah [seeing] is aryeh [lion], and the lion is in Chesed, as is known; and the letters of aryeh are yir'ah [fear], and that is judgment. And in this attribute there are "sixty mighty men" (Song of Songs 3:7), and their allusion is in the six gevurot of the six extremities that are in it. And likewise the matter of the seventy-two of the Sanhedrin, as we explained their matter above. And there is more among the actions of this attribute, and it will be explained from the Gate of the Glossary of Titles.

The third attribute of the six days of Creation is the one called Tiferet. And its name testifies of it, for all splendor [pe'er] and glory is poured forth from this attribute. And so it is, for glory and beauty are the composition of red and white, as is well known; and therefore it is said, "My lover is white and ruddy" (Song of Songs 5:10). And all matters of the composition of red and white are in this attribute — such as the precious stones that in their color are green like the yolk of an egg, whose special property is for peace, just as this attribute mediates peace between the extremities. And all the matters in which the element of air prevails are poured forth from this attribute. And likewise the Torah and engaging in it depend on this attribute; and the witness is the Ark, in which are the Tablets of the Covenant, which is placed between the north and the south — and specifically the Written Torah, as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And children depend on this attribute. That is to say, when a person prays, he should intend that his prayer rise to the upper mazal, which is the first three in general, where the children are; as our sages, of blessed memory, explained: "Children, life and sustenance," etc., "[do not depend on merit,] but the thing depends on mazal" (Mo'ed Katan 28a). And they did not say "the thing is [havya] in mazal," which would imply that they are there, in the mazal, but "depends" [talya], that is, their dependence; but their place is Tiferet, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 14), and these are his words: "Turn to the east, and the central pillar takes it, and 'my children' is sealed in it." Thus far his words.

And the resolution of the matter is that he must raise the purity of his prayer above, to the mazal [the upper one, which is Keter], and then they will give him from the storehouse of children, which is in Tiferet. And it is possible that the reason children depend on this attribute is that it is the master of the souls, and they are the fruit of its grapes, as is explained in the Zohar in many places, and as will be explained in the Gate of the Soul. And therefore it is not fitting to give children except with the permission of the master of the fruit, which is the children. For the pouring forth of children is from the brain, which is in the matter of the first three; and likewise the place of the souls is in Binah. Therefore Tiferet must be raised to the mazal, as we explained. And the manna came down to Israel from this attribute, as the verse taught: "Behold, I will rain down for you bread from heaven" (Exodus 16:4) — which is Tiferet. And among the actions of this attribute is the effluence of the souls, by means of the union of Tiferet and Malkhut. And it is a matter found in these two attributes that is not found in others, except in Chokhmah and Binah. And the matter is as we explained above in chapter 13: that this union is not like the matter of the union and bond of the other sefirot; rather, it is a praiseworthy matter, like the union in which a man unites with his wife at the time of coupling, which is an effluence that he pours into her, and from that effluence offspring of something come to be.
