And this matter is literally in Chokhmah and Binah, who are titled by Rashbi many times Abba Ila'ah and Imma Ila'ah [the supernal Father and the supernal Mother]. And the matter is that when Chokhmah couples with Binah, spiritual beings come to be from there. And so it was in the matter of the sefirot at the time they were emanated from Binah: Chokhmah united with her in a complete, particular union, like the coupling of a man and his wife; and from the brains of Abba [mochin de-Abba] were drawn the six sefirot of the Structure, all of it included in son and daughter, who are called double-faced [du-partzufin]. And this is what Rashbi explained concerning Tiferet: the son who is drawn from the father's brain. And he drew the sefirot forth in great subtlety and poured them into Binah, who is the mother; and the mother became pregnant with them, like a pregnant woman. And just as "the bones in the womb of her who is with child" (Ecclesiastes 11:5) come to be from the subtle matter, and grow, and come to be there into the manifestation of the form of the fetus, so the sefirot. And therefore Rashbi explained that the Emanation tarried in Binah twelve months — the great pregnancy that there is in a human being, which is twelve months, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Tractate Niddah, fol. 27). And we wrote the passage in the Gate of Self and Vessels (chapter 7), and there we explained that the words are not according to their plain sense. And therefore Chokhmah and Binah are father and mother to all the Emanation, and the whole Emanation is children to them; and Binah is called "the mother of the children, joyful" (Psalms 113:9). And it asks in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 219a): "The mother is known; the children, who are they?" Because these children have two aspects, or their aspect with respect to birth. And the matter is that just as a woman, when she conceives twins, all of them are placed in one womb — for a woman does not have two wombs, but one; but there are chambers in it, so that it can receive up to seven — so too in Binah all are included as one at the time of their gestation there; but the truth is that they are many chambers, as we explained the matter of "and by knowledge [da'at] are the chambers filled" (Proverbs 24:4) in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter. And we return to the matter: for while they are there, all of them are included in the double-faced; and after they go out, at the time of the Emanation, they are particularized into seven. And therefore he said, "the children, who are they?" — whether the inner aspect, in which they are included in the double-faced, or the outer aspect, which is after the birth, in which they are particularized into seven. And he answered there, as relevant to our matter; see there.

And behold, Leah was in the place of Binah, as is explained in the words of Rashbi. And now one must ask: how did she conceive from Jacob, who is Tiferet, and he is the son? And although there is no forbidden relation above, nevertheless it is not possible that it be. For although the union of the son and the mother is permitted, how is it possible that the mother should conceive from the son, when he is the son himself? And the matter is that the union of Chokhmah and Binah is by means of the concealed Da'at, which is the manifestation of Tiferet before its emanation; that manifestation is called Da'at, and Da'at unites them, just as Yesod unites Tiferet and Malkhut, as is explained in the aforementioned Gate. And although that manifestation is not the chariot of Jacob, who is [a chariot] only for Tiferet specifically, and outside, as was explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 2, nevertheless it availed him to rise up at the known time, so that by this Leah would conceive. And further, Da'at is clothed in Tiferet and is a soul to it, as we shall explain in Sefer Or Yakar.

And behold, the matter of the union and coupling of Chokhmah and Binah at the time of the Emanation has been explained. But one must ask: granted at the time of the Emanation, when this coupling was needed in order to emanate the children; but now, after the Emanation, what do their marital relations accomplish? That is to say, for the matter of the effluence it is impossible, for that is not coupling — as we proved above in chapters 13 and 14, that the matter of the effluence is not marital relations but sustenance, like the man who sustains his wife and gives "food to all her household and a portion to her maidens" (see Proverbs 31:15).

And the matter of marital relations is that there come to be a new coming-to-be; if so, what is the coming-to-be that is renewed from their marital relations? And to resolve this matter we shall ask another question. For granted, in the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, which is at times, and they return and unite again — fine, they bring souls into being, as we shall explain, for in each and every union he makes souls. But in the union of Chokhmah and Binah, who never separate — if so, what is the matter of their bringing-into-being? Or how and when is the one completed and the other comes to be, since they never separate, as all these particulars were explained above in chapters 13 and 14? To this we say: it is known that were it not for the manifestation of the emanation of Chokhmah and Binah, it would not be possible for the Emanation to exist at all, as we explained some of this matter in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapters 4 and 5. And the reason is that there is no creature without male and female; that is, that things are in subtlety, and are revealed and become thick. And "a refining pot and a furnace" (Proverbs 17:3) for the six days of Creation, so that they come to be and be revealed from Keter, were Chokhmah and Binah, in the secret of their union, in the secret of father and mother. And were it not for Chokhmah and Binah, the six days would have no power to come to be. And Rashbi explained this matter in Parashat Ha'azinu (fol. 290a), at the time of his passing, and these are his words: "Come and see: at the hour when Atika Kadisha, the Enclosure of all enclosures, wished to be arranged, He arranged all like male and female. After male and female were included, they did not endure except in another endurance of male and female. And this Chokhmah, the totality of all, when it went out and shone from Atika Kadisha, it shone only in male and female; for this Chokhmah spread out and brought forth Binah from itself, and it was found to be male and female. Chokhmah father, Binah mother; Chokhmah and Binah were weighed in one balance, male and female. And for their sake all endures in male and female, for were it not for this they would not endure. This beginning is father to all, father of all the fathers; they joined one with another and shone one in another. Chokhmah father, Binah mother, as it is written, 'for you shall call understanding [Binah] mother [em]' (Proverbs 2:3)." Thus far his words. And although from the plain sense of the words we have proof for what we seek, nevertheless we shall not withhold our hands from explaining his words — and further, in order to resolve a mighty question that falls in this matter. For one must ask: Chokhmah and Binah themselves, how were they emanated without male and female, since the whole Emanation requires male and female? And this is the main intent of Rashbi in the explanation of this passage. And he said, "Come and see: at the hour when Atika Kadisha," etc. — this is Keter. And he called it "the Enclosure of all enclosures" because it is before the expansion, and then Keter is enclosed and concealed even from all the enclosed ones, which are the concealed emanated ones; and even they do not apprehend Keter, because of the greatness of its concealment. "Wished to arrange": that is, when He wished to emanate the rest of the Emanation. And there are two versions in this: either be'a le-atkana ["wished to arrange"] or be'a le-ittakkana ["wished to be arranged"], and all is one matter. For in arranging the Emanation He arranges Himself, for His tikkun is His revealing, and His revealing is the tikkun of His Emanation; if so, "to arrange" or "to be arranged" — all is one. "He arranged all like male and female": meaning, He emanated the whole Emanation in the likeness of male and female — as Chokhmah and Binah, male and female; Tiferet and Malkhut, male and female. "After male and female were included": meaning, he intended to resolve the question that we asked, how Chokhmah and Binah were emanated without male and female. And he answered that in Keter itself male and female were included, for part of it is the aspect of male and part of it the aspect of female, as we shall explain in the Gate "From Below to Above."

And the matter of male and female in Keter: they are the aspect of Chokhmah in it, male, and the aspect of Binah in it, female. And both of them are included in it in the secret of primordial light, clear light, refined light that is in Keter, as we shall explain in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. And although male and female were included in Keter, nevertheless the manifestation of male and female in Keter did not suffice to emanate the Emanation by its means. And this is what he says: "after male and female were included," namely in Keter, nevertheless "they did not endure" — meaning, the Emanation had no endurance to be emanated — "except in another endurance of male and female," namely Chokhmah and Binah. Or he means, "after male and female were included": meaning, although the Emanation was included in male and female, which are Chokhmah and Binah, nevertheless the Emanation did not endure except in another male and female, which are Tiferet and Malkhut. And the first reading is the principal one. "And this Chokhmah," etc., is to resolve our questions: that even Chokhmah was emanated only by means of male and female, which are in Keter, as we explained. And this is what it says: "And this Chokhmah," etc., "when it went out" — meaning, when it was emanated from Keter; for it was emanated including nine sefirot, for eight sefirot were concealed in it, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. "When it went out and shone from Atika Kadisha": meaning, when it was emanated from Keter, it was emanated only by means of male and female, which are the aspects of male and female in Keter.

And the matter of our saying that in Keter there are literal aspects of male and female is necessary, and is explained in the Tikkunim in many places, and we shall explain them in the Gate "From Below to Above" (chapter 5; see there). "For this Chokhmah spread out," etc.: it was difficult for him — granted that Chokhmah was emanated by means of the male and female in Keter; but Binah, how was she emanated without male and female, for Chokhmah emanated Binah? And he answered that the emanation of Binah was only a mere expansion; for Chokhmah and Binah were emanated at once by means of Keter, and when Chokhmah emanated Binah it was only a mere expansion. And this is what it says: "for this Chokhmah spread out," etc. And there male and female are found, which are Chokhmah and Binah; and this is what it says: "they were weighed in one balance, male and female" — meaning, they were emanated in one point and weighed in one weight, as we explained. "And for their sake," etc.: meaning, by their cause all endures, for they are male and female; "for were it not for this they would not endure," because every creature must be created by means of male and female. "This beginning is father to all": meaning, Chokhmah is father to the whole Emanation, for the whole Emanation is children to Chokhmah. And so that we not err and say that it was also father to Binah — and if so, the difficulty returns to its place, that Binah was emanated without a mother — to this he said, "father of all the fathers," meaning that it is father to Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. "They joined one with another," etc.: that is, in order to emanate the whole Emanation, as he goes on to explain. Thus far. And behold, from it it has been explained that the principal endurance of the Emanation is by means of the father and the mother.

And behold, just as in the matter of the union of a man and his wife there are two aspects — the one is to beget anew, and the second is to make the plantings grow, that is, so that the child come forth vigorous, as we explained in the previous Gate, chapter 3 — so too Binah and Chokhmah: their union is not to make a new coming-to-be, but to establish the beings in their vigor, so that they stand in their full form. And the matter is that, in order for Tiferet and Malkhut to be crowned so that they unite, it is impossible for them to be crowned with those praiseworthy diadems that invigorate and arm the sefirot except through the union of Chokhmah and Binah. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 61b), and these are his words: "Come and see: it is written, 'And a river goes out from Eden to water the garden' (Genesis 2:10). This river spreads out to its sides at the hour when this Eden couples with it in a complete coupling, in that path that is not known above or below, as it is written, 'a path that no bird of prey knows' (Job 28:7); and they are found in desire, never separating one from the other. Then springs and streams go out and crown the holy son with all those crowns; and then it is written, 'with the diadem [atarah] with which his mother crowned [ittrah] him' (Song of Songs 3:11). And at that hour that son inherits the inheritance of his father and his mother, and then he revels in that pleasure and those delicacies. And we have learned: at the hour when the supernal King sits in His diadems, in royal delicacies, then 'while the king was at his table, my nard gave forth its fragrance' (Song of Songs 1:12) — this is Yesod, which brings forth blessings for the holy King to couple with the Lady at this grade; and then blessings are given in all the worlds, and upper and lower ones go out and are blessed by its means." Thus far his words.

Behold, from this passage it is explained explicitly that there is no diadem for the union of son and daughter — namely the diadem of all the crowns, as explained in chapter 10 — except at the time of the union of Chokhmah and Binah; and since their union is constant, the diadem will be [there] for the children at the time of need.

And behold, Rabbi Yose went to great lengths in recounting the tikkunim of this diadem. And these are his words in the Zohar, Parashat Balak (fol. 209a): "'And the angel of YHVH stood,' etc. (Numbers 22:24). We have learned: from the side of Imma, when she is crowned, one thousand five hundred engraved sides go out in her diadem, in her ornaments. And when she wishes to couple with the King, she is crowned [mit'atra] with one diadem [itra] of four colors. Those colors blaze to the four sides of the world; each and every color blazes three times on that side, so that they are twelve engraved borders, and they enter and are included in twelve others. At the head of the diadem there are four walls to the four sides, and they are towers, as it is written, 'towers of perfumes' (Song of Songs 5:13). What is 'perfumes'? As it is written, 'of all the powders of the merchant' (Song of Songs 3:6). And on each and every tower, three gates set with precious stones, on each and every side. This diadem shines with the sparklings of Ophir, for the sake of the honor of the King, as it is written, 'I will make man more precious than fine gold, a human than the gold of Ophir' (Isaiah 13:12). Beneath the diadem hang bells of gold all around it: a bell of gold on this side and a bell of gold on that side, and one pomegranate. Within that pomegranate there are a thousand bells, and each bell of them blazes in red [and] in white. That pomegranate is split into four splits and stands open to show its bells: three hundred and twenty-five bells on this side, and so on each and every side, until the four sides of the world blaze from the appearance of each and every segment; and they are 'a slice of pomegranate,' as it is written, 'your temple is like a slice of pomegranate' (Song of Songs 4:3). Four wheels in the segment, four corners; they carry that diadem in rolling, and when they carry it they lift it upward, until they reach the rolling of the supernal sphere that roars day and night. All those segments join and carry the diadem and lift it. And the sound of those wheels is heard in all the firmaments; at the sound of the melody all the hosts of heaven tremble, and all of them ask one another, until all of them say, 'Blessed be the glory of YHVH from His place' (Ezekiel 3:12). When the King couples with the Lady, this diadem rises and settles on the head of the Lady. Then one supernal diadem descends, set with every precious stone, with lilies and roses all around it; with six wheels it comes to the six sides of the world; six wings of an eagle carry it. On its segments are fifty grapes all around it, which the supernal Imma engraved in it, set with precious stone, white and red and green and black, blue and purple. Six hundred and thirteen corners to each and every side; one thousand six hundred towers to each and every side. And on each and every tower, rows [of stones] set, flowers above, drawn up from the table of the supernal Imma in her anointing oil. Then Imma, in a whisper, draws down supernal gifts, and sends and sets them in that diadem. Afterward she draws down streams of the holy anointing oil upon the head of the King; and from His head that good supernal oil descends upon His precious beard, and from there it flows upon those garments of honor of the King. This is what is written: 'like the good oil upon the head, running down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron,' etc. (Psalms 133:2). Afterward the diadem returns, and the supernal Imma crowns Him with that diadem, and spreads over Him and over the Lady garments of honor, with that diadem. Then a voice is heard in all the worlds: 'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Zion, upon King Solomon,' etc. (Song of Songs 3:11). Then there is joy among all those sons of the King. And who are they? All those who come from the side of Israel," etc. Thus far its words, as relevant to our matter. And let the inquirer not think that the matters of this diadem are things according to their plain sense, God forbid; rather, it is all a parable for many wondrous matters in the Emanation, to know whose matter the wise would weary days and nights, and come away with toil and labor. For there is none who has descended into the depth of these things except Rashbi and his companions, "whose dwelling is not with flesh" (Daniel 2:11); and nevertheless I explained it in Sefer Or Yakar, in the explanation of the portion. And indeed, for our purpose, what emerges for us from all this is that the matter of this diadem, and the garments of honor mentioned in this passage, is from the side of Imma; and that is specifically by reason of the union of the father with her, for from there is the principal "good oil" mentioned in the passage. And since this matter is so, we have learned a great principle concerning the union of Abba and Imma: that it is needed for the union of Tiferet and Malkhut. And since we went at length in the previous chapters in the negations of speech about the first three, the remark expounded about their union up to now suffices for us; and we shall speak of the union of the son and the daughter.

Just as this matter of union is found in Chokhmah and Binah together, so too it is found in Tiferet and Malkhut. And therefore both of them are titled with the expressions "bridegroom and bride," "a man and his wife," and the like, in these matters. And there is a difference between the union of Chokhmah and Binah and the union of Tiferet and Malkhut. For the union of Chokhmah and Binah — they never separate from one another, as explained above in chapters 13 and 14; but the union of Tiferet and Malkhut is at times and at moments, as at the time when Israel reach "Sim Shalom" in prayer. And this coupling needs the arousal from below; and if a lower arousal, which is from this world, does not come first, they will not unite as is fitting. And this matter is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 35a), and these are its words: "Come and see: Adam and Eve were created side by side. What is the reason they were not created face to face? Because it is written, 'for YHVH Elohim had not caused it to rain upon the earth' (Genesis 2:5), and coupling was not found in its tikkun as is fitting. And when this was set right below, and they turned face to face, then it was found above. From where do we know? From the Tabernacle, as it is written, 'the Tabernacle was set up' (Exodus 40:17): because another Tabernacle was set up with it; and until it was set up below, it was not set up above. So too, when it was set right below, it was set right above. And because until now it had not been set right above, they were not created face to face. And the verse proves it, for it is written, 'for YHVH Elohim had not caused it to rain upon the earth'; and therefore 'and there was no man to till the ground' (Genesis 2:5), for he was not in his tikkun. And when Eve was completed, Adam was completed, and before that he was not completed. And the secret of this is that until here there is no letter Samekh in the portion. And although the Companions said [so], but Samekh — this is 'help' [ezer]. And this is the help above, which turned above face to face; male and female were supported one opposite the other. Certainly: 'They are upheld [semukhim] for ever and ever, made in truth and uprightness' (Psalms 111:8). 'Upheld': this is male and female, who are upheld together. This world that we mentioned depends on the world below; and when the world below was not set right, that world that we mentioned was not set right. 'For YHVH Elohim had not caused it to rain upon the earth': for one is supported by the other. This lower world, when it was set right, and they turned face to face and were set right, support was found above. For before this the work was not in its tikkun, because 'YHVH Elohim had not caused it to rain upon the earth,' and one depends on the other. What is written after it? 'But a mist went up from the earth' (Genesis 2:6) — this is the tikkun below; afterward, 'and watered the whole face of the ground.' 'But a mist went up from the earth': this is the craving of the female toward the male. Another explanation: what is the reason He had not caused it to rain? Because the tikkun of 'went up from the earth' was not found; and therefore from the lower earth the work above is aroused. Come and see: smoke rises from the earth first, and the cloud is aroused, and all joins afterward, one with another. In this manner, the smoke of the offering arouses from below and makes perfection above, and all joins one with another and is completed. In this manner above: the arousal begins from below, and afterward all is completed. And were it not that Knesset Yisrael begins with arousal first, that which is above would not be aroused toward her; and by the craving below it is completed above." Thus far his words.

And because we have seen that this passage skips in its words from matter to matter, and within the same matter, we have seen fit to explain it. Meaning, "were created side by side," as is alluded to in the Tractate (Berakhot, fol. 61a): "they were double-faced." "What is the reason they were not created face to face?": meaning, for they were back and front, and they were back to back; and therefore he asks, what is the reason this creation was in vain, since this creation of theirs is of no benefit at all — and the proof is that afterward it was necessary to set them right. And he answered, "because it is written, 'for YHVH Elohim had not caused it to rain'": meaning, that there was no union above for Tiferet with Malkhut. And because it was difficult for him that it is impossible to say that coupling was not found in the Emanation — for he explained explicitly that there was coupling in the matter of the emanation of the soul of the first Adam, as we shall explain his words — therefore he said, "and coupling was not found in its tikkun": meaning, there was coupling, but not a complete coupling in its tikkun, namely face to face. "And when it was set right," etc.: for the tikkun of the upper depends on the tikkun of the lower ones, as he concludes, that the upper ones depend on the arousal of the lower ones; and therefore, since there was no arousal below, there was no complete union above. And because this matter appears at first glance difficult — that we should say that the cause depends on the effect, and the cause needs the effect that comes from it — he proved the matter from the Tabernacle, from what is expounded in the expression "was set up" [hukam], whose explanation is: "the Tabernacle was set up" — another Tabernacle above, namely the Shekhinah. And because it was difficult for him [that] we might say: it is true that another Tabernacle was set up above, for we do not deny that the doing of the commandments certainly makes an impression above; but nevertheless there is no proof from here at all. For we might say that the matter of "the Tabernacle was set up" is that a new matter was renewed above because of the setting up of the Tabernacle — but not that we should say that there would be no manifestation for the upper ones except by means of the lower ones, as we need to say concerning union. Therefore he said, "and until it was set up," etc.: for in the explanation of "was set up," the intent is that what had had no standing at all before was now set up. And he did not need to prove this explanation, for it is proven of itself; because one cannot say that the intent of the verse is to say that the making of the Tabernacle made an impression above like the rest of the doing of the commandments — for that is obvious. And is the making of the Tabernacle, though it alludes to the creation of the upper, middle and lower world, less than the rest of the doing of the commandments? And what need was there to inform us that it made an impression and a matter of holiness above? Rather, certainly this is only so that the intent is to inform us that before the setting up of the lower Tabernacle, it was not possible for there to be a setting up of the upper Tabernacle; and this is what it says, "and until it was set up," etc. "So too here," etc.: in the matter of the creation of man, while there was no setting up for the lower ones, namely the coupling, the upper ones did not have completeness of coupling. "And because until now," etc.: the intent is to indicate that the lower ones too depend on the doing of the upper ones; for Adam and Eve were not created face to face because the cherubim above were not face to face. "And the verse proves it, for it is written," etc.: meaning, from the verse there is a proof that the union above was not in its tikkun at the time of the creation of the world; and this is what it says, "for YHVH had not caused it to rain," namely, "for he was not in his tikkun," etc. Meaning, the intent in the expression "and there was no man" is not that there was no manifestation of the creation of man at all; for if so, it would appear that with the creation of man everything was set right, and it would not follow that with an arousal below there was an arousal above. Rather, the intent is: "and there was no man" complete in his tikkun; and man is not complete except with the tikkun of the female, his mate. And when the female was completed — after the Holy One, blessed be He, sawed her off and braided her, as is explained in the Gemara there on "and He brought her to the man" (Genesis 2:22) — then the man was completed. And the reason is that he is called by the name "man" [adam] only when they are together, complete, male and female; as we say (in Yevamot, fol. 63) on "male and female He created them ... and He called their name Adam" (Genesis 5:2). And therefore "and there was no man" means a man complete in male and female, as is fitting. And this is what it says: "and there was no man to till," etc., "for he was not in his tikkun; and when Eve was completed, Adam was completed, and before that he was not completed." If so, it is correct throughout to say "and there was no man" until Eve was completed and coupled face to face. "And the secret of this is that until here there is no letter Samekh in the portion": the intent is, the secret of the matter indicates that in the whole creation of man, in that whole portion, the letter Samekh is not mentioned. "And although the Companions," etc.: meaning, although the Companions explained (in Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 17) that while Eve had not been created Samekh was not mentioned in the portion, and wished to explain this whole matter in the plain sense, concerning Adam and Eve his wife — nevertheless, "but Samekh — this is help," etc.: meaning, the intent is to explain the matter concerning the upper help. And the intent is that while the lower Eve had not been sawed off, the Shekhinah was not face to face; and therefore the lower ones were created back and front. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, sawed off Eve, the Shekhinah became a support [samekh] above. And the explanation of "Samekh — this is help": granted, according to what the Companions explain, that is the matter of "support," for Eve is a support for Adam; but above, concerning the Holy One, blessed be He, it is not applicable to say that the Shekhinah is a support for Him — on the contrary, He is a support for her. Therefore he said "Samekh — this is help": he took it out of the expression samekh, whose explanation is leaning, that the male leans upon the female, and explained it with the expression "help," that is, some assistance to the governance by reason of the union face to face. And this is what it says: "Samekh — this is help; and this is the help above," that is, the Shekhinah, who turned face to face; "male and female were supported one opposite the other."

Behold, regarding literal support, he said that there was support for both of them: for just as the Shekhinah is a support for Tiferet, all the more so Tiferet is a support for the Shekhinah. And therefore he brought proof that this one is a support for that one from what the verse said, "They are upheld [semukhim] for ever and ever," in the plural — as it appears that it is also correct that the Shekhinah is a prop and support for Tiferet. "Upheld: this is male and female," who are Tiferet and Malkhut; "and they are upheld together," equally — for just as Tiferet supports Malkhut, so Malkhut supports Tiferet. "This world that we mentioned depends on the world below": meaning, Tiferet, the upper world, depends on Malkhut, the lower world; and the intent is to prove that Tiferet needs the support of Malkhut. And this is what it says: "and when the world below," which is Malkhut, "was not set right," Tiferet was not set right. "For [YHVH] had not caused it to rain," etc., "for one is supported by the other": meaning, Tiferet is supported by Malkhut, and Malkhut by Tiferet. "And this world": meaning Tiferet. "Lower, when it was set right": that is, Malkhut, as he concludes. "This is the craving of the female": that is, the souls of the righteous, as we shall explain in the next chapter — that Malkhut casts up female waters to receive male waters, as we shall explain. "What is the reason He had not caused it to rain? Because," etc.: all this circling that he has circled until now is to explain how the matter of the union of Tiferet with Malkhut depends on the lower man. And it is clear: for since the completeness of Tiferet is when Malkhut is with him face to face, and she does not unite with him face to face except by means of the arousal of craving, that is, the deeds of human beings below, as we shall explain — and man below was not in completeness — therefore "He had not caused it to rain." And this is the sum of his words, and this is the cause of his circlings. "And come and see," etc., is a proof for this matter, as he goes on to conclude. Thus far.

And behold, from this passage we have learned that in the matter of union the upper ones depend on the arousal of the lower ones, as we explained. And now it is fitting that we investigate the whole matter of this arousal, as to its essence and its matter; and for this we shall devote to it a chapter of its own, and there we shall explain the root and principle of this arousal.

Since it has risen in our agreement in the previous chapter that the matter of the union between Tiferet and Malkhut needs the arousal of this world, it is fitting that we investigate to know what the matter of this arousal is. And this Rashbi explained to us in Parashat Noach (fol. 60a), and these are his words: "Rabbi Shimon said: At the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned [mit'atter] with His diadems [itrohi], He is crowned from above and from below. He is crowned from above, from the place that is deepest of all; He is crowned from below — with what? With the souls of the righteous. Then life is added from above and from below, and the place of the Sanctuary is included from all sides, and the well is filled, and the sea is completed, and then it gives to all. It is written, 'Drink waters out of your own cistern, and flowing streams out of the midst of your own well' (Proverbs 5:15). Why here 'your cistern' first and afterward 'your well'? For only an empty one that does not flow is called a cistern; a well [is] waters that flow. Rather, it is all one place: [rather, the place] that the poor hold on to is called a cistern, for it has nothing of its own but what is put into it; and who is it? Dalet. Afterward it is made a well, which is full from all sides; and who is it? Heh. It is filled from above and flows from below: it is filled from above, as we have said, and it flows from below, from the souls of the righteous. Another explanation: 'Drink waters out of your own cistern' — this is King David, of whom it is written, 'Oh that one would give me water to drink from the cistern of Bethlehem' (2 Samuel 23:15). 'And flowing streams' — this is Abraham. 'Out of the midst' — this is Jacob, who is in the middle. 'Your well' — this is Isaac, who is called 'a well of living waters.' Behold, in this verse the supernal holy chariot is found, of the Patriarchs and King David, who is joined with them. And there is one who says: 'And flowing streams' — this is Isaac; 'out of the midst' — this is Moses, who is in the middle; 'your well' — this is Aaron, who is called 'a well of living waters'; and King David, who is joined with them. The craving of the female toward the male is only when the spirit enters into her and she casts forth waters to receive the upper male waters. So Knesset Yisrael: craving is not aroused toward the Holy One, blessed be He, except through the spirit of the righteous who enter into her; and then waters flow within her to receive the waters of the male. And all becomes one craving, and one bundle, and one knot; and this is the desire of all, and the stroll that the Holy One, blessed be He, takes with the souls of the righteous." Thus far his words, as relevant to our matter. And the intent of "at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned with His diadems" is the time of coupling, as explained above in chapter 17. "With His diadems," in the plural, because the diadem includes six extremities; for the diadem with which He is crowned is that the roots of the six concealed extremities are revealed upon the six lower sefirot, that is to say, the Emanation. And therefore he said "with His diadems," for they are many diadems. And this is what Rabbi Yose intended in the passage that we copied above in chapter 17, in saying, "and spreads over Him and over the Lady garments of honor" — that is, they are clothed in the concealed roots, and then is their union and their coupling. And likewise the diadem was explained in the passage that we explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 2, where the Tannaim disagree: there is one who says that the diadem is from six, as we say, and there is one who says from those three, namely Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, which are three colors. And it is possible to say that with respect to coupling they do not disagree, that they are six. But one holds that the three, which are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, are of Tiferet — and in this they disagree there — and the remaining three are a diadem for Malkhut, namely Netzach, Hod, Yesod, which are the manifestation of the Heh in her, with which she adorns herself at the time of coupling, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2. But with respect to the manifestation of coupling, all agree that they are six, for so it is proven in the Zohar in several places. And this is what is explained in the Zohar concerning the seven years that Jacob served for Rachel: so that he would be crowned from the six extremities, which he needs in order to unite; and this is "His diadems" mentioned in the passage. Or it is possible that "His diadems" are the two diadems that He inherits, one from Abba and one from Imma, and they are the Chesed in Chokhmah and the Gevurah in Binah; and so Rashbi explained at the time of his passing, in Parashat Ha'azinu. And I explained in Sefer Or Yakar that Tiferet inherits these two diadems from Chokhmah and Binah. "He is crowned from above and He is crowned from below," as he concludes: "from above," that is, by means of Chokhmah and Binah, which are called "the deepest of all"; and this is what Rabbi Yose explained in the passage that we copied in chapter 17, concerning the matter of the good oil — and oil is from the side of Chokhmah, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. "He is crowned from below — with what? With the souls of the righteous": meaning, the souls of the righteous who are in their lifetime. For among the dead they are "free from the commandments" (Shabbat 30a), and their Torah and their good do not pour forth and do not avail for this; for this matter was given only to the lower ones, who are possessors of free choice.

And the matter of his saying "with their souls" is that the souls have their manifestation above, and they are a thread that chains down from on high, from Tiferet, to this lower world; for they chain down manifestation from manifestation, and manifestation from manifestation, until they reach this manifestation. And at the time that their good deeds rise, they rise by way of this channel and chain until they reach there, and from there they draw the effluence below. And this is what he said: "He is crowned — with what? With the souls of the righteous," which are the upper manifestations of the souls, which raise the fragrance of their deeds before Him, and He is crowned with them, as this matter will be explained at length in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 7. "Then life is added from above and from below": meaning, from the side that they pour forth the vitality and the effluence from above, and likewise from below, in the secret of the reversing light, the returning light, which indicates the strength of the light that comes, so that there is power in it to magnify that which turns over.

And this matter will be explained in the Gate "From Below to Above." "And the place of the Sanctuary is included": meaning, the last aspect in Malkhut, her lowest aspect, is what is called "the place of the Sanctuary," meaning the place of the indwelling of the Sanctuary, in which the Sanctuary dwells. And this last aspect in Malkhut is included from all sides; for because she is last, she is included in all by means of the effluence of the blessings. And his saying "from all sides": it is possible to say, from three sides, which are the line of the right, the line of the left and the middle line; or it is possible to say "from all sides," from two aspects — the aspect of the light from above to below and the aspect of the light from below to above. "And the well is filled," etc.: that is, the middle aspect of Malkhut, in which there are many waters, and she is full. But her upper aspect is what is called "sea," which is completed with every kind of completeness. And although she is called by the title "sea" in the secret of her lower aspect, where are "the depths of the sea," as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, nevertheless it is possible to explain it above, in a borrowed sense, because of the abundance of the waters, more than the well; and this explanation is necessary. "It is written, 'Drink waters out of your own cistern,'" etc., "for only [an empty one] is called a cistern," etc. And if so, what is a cistern is not a well, and a well is not a cistern; and if so, how does he title Malkhut with two titles, when both are impossible? For if the title "well" is correct, the title "cistern" will not be correct; and if the title "cistern" is correct, the title "well" will not be correct of her. And to say that they are two sefirot is impossible, for we have not found a sefirah that is called "well" and "cistern" except this one. To this he said, "Rather, it is all one place": meaning, it is always one sefirah that is called thus and is called thus. And the matter is that she has two aspects, as he concludes. "The place [that] the poor [hold on to]": that is, her aspect in which she is poor and has no vitality in abundance; and therefore the poverty of the poor is drawn to them from there, because they were born in the deficiency of the moon. And this is "the place that the poor hold on to is called a cistern," for the effluence does not increase in her, for the reason that she does not then have the deeds of the righteous, to request the effluence by their means. "And who is it? Dalet," etc.: meaning, behold, the manifestation of Heh is the manifestation of three Vavs, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, as explained above in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And if so, the manifestation of Dalet is two Vavs, which are Netzach and Hod; and this is not by means of her husband, which is the coupling, but by means of her receiving from both of them. And she has no union with her husband, which is by means of Yesod, because she has no deeds so as to be flowing from within; and therefore she is poor, in poverty. "But afterward": meaning, after she has received from Netzach and Hod, which is the secret of the right and the left for the coupling, as we shall explain — that is, the secret of the embrace — then she is made a well, which is the manifestation of Heh, within which is a small Vav, which is the manifestation of Yesod, which empties out the blessings into her by the power of the deeds of the righteous, which are female waters that arouse the craving. And this is what he says: "Afterward it is made a well, which is full from all sides," that is, from all three lines, right and left and middle; and then it is a well that flows from within itself, as he concludes, "and it flows from below, from the souls of the righteous," namely the female waters mentioned, as he concludes. "Another explanation," concerning cistern and well: that in Malkhut it is a cistern alone, and "well" is in another sefirah. "'Out of your own cistern' — this is King David": meaning, in this aspect David was a chariot for Malkhut, with respect to her aspect called "cistern"; and the proof is that he craved its waters and called it "cistern." If so, the aspect of David is what is called "cistern." And so it is proven there (in the Zohar, fol. 63), on the verse "Hearken, O Laishah," etc. (Isaiah 10:30). "'And flowing streams' — this is Abraham" needed no proof at all, for it is implied of itself that flowing and poured-forth waters are from the side of Chesed, the attribute of Abraham. "'Out of the midst' — this is Jacob": for he is the middle one and the mediator between the Patriarchs; and this is what it says, "who is in the middle." "'Your well' — this is Isaac, who is called 'a well of living waters'": meaning, from the side of the spring of life, which is Binah, which is above it; and with the word "living" he proved the matter. "Behold, in this verse is found," etc.: since he was forced in the matter of relating the titles to the attributes, in what can be explained in other ways, therefore he said: although it is possible to explain it in the way that was explained above, or as some explain it, nevertheless in this way we have gained that "in this verse the supernal holy chariot is found," which are the four legs of the chariot, Chesed and Gevurah, Tiferet and Malkhut. And it is a fine matter for these four to be mentioned together in the verse, for they are attributes related to one another, as is known — which is not so according to the previous explanation, in which all is in Malkhut and he was not precise in the other words. "The supernal holy chariot, of the Patriarchs and King David, who is joined with them": meaning, for although according to these explanations that the [other] explainers explained, as we need to say, also according to that way there are four attributes in the verse, nevertheless they are not literally the three Patriarchs, but Isaac and Moses and Aaron and David. And according to the truth, David in essence has no relation with these three, but with the Patriarchs, as is known in the matter of his kingship in Hebron, in order to be unified with the Patriarchs, as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Va'era (fol. 31a; and in Parashat Vayechi, fol. 246b). And if so, it turns out that this explanation, in these aspects, is more praiseworthy than the two other explanations. "And there is one who says," etc.: these explainers left the first explanation because of the difficulty of "well" in Gevurah — for a well is more than flowing streams — and this is forced. And the first explanation was not forced in this, because of the order of the Patriarchs; and although their order is Abraham, Jacob, Isaac, nevertheless he already gave a reason for the matter and said, "who is in the middle," and therefore he is in their midst. And to the precedence of David too he gave intent, in saying "of the Patriarchs and King David," etc.; for the explanation of the verse is David, who is related to the three Patriarchs, and therefore David came before the three of them; and this is what he intended in saying "who is joined" already. And the [other] explainers, since they saw that the order of the Patriarchs was in any case not as it should be, therefore wished, within the confusion, that the titles at least be somewhat related; and for this they said, "'And flowing streams' — this is Isaac," for he already has some waters in him, as in the matter of "the might of rains." "'Out of the midst' — this is Moses": we have already explained the difference between Jacob and Moses in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 2 — that Jacob is outside, Moses inside, etc.; let it be examined there. And because he explained that "flowing streams" is Isaac, and the manifestation of "flowing" indicates compassion, he said that the intent here is only to their concealed manifestation: Isaac like Moses. And this is what he said, "'Out of the midst' — this is Moses, who is in the middle," in the ways that we explained above.

And further, he wished to explain "'out of the midst' — this is Moses," to be precise well about the expression "out of the midst" [mi-tokh]: he did not say "midst" [tokh] but "out of the midst," which is to say the innermost of the midst, namely Moses, "who is in the middle" and within, as explained in the aforementioned Gate. "'Your well' — this is Aaron," over against Moses; and it is certainly "a well of living waters," for there is the abundance of the waters of Chesed, and especially in the grades of Aaron, who is over against the grade of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him; and therefore in it there is an abundance of waters — which is not so with Abraham, whose attribute is "southward" [negbah], an expression of dryness [nagov], as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, under the entry negbah. "And King David, who is joined with them": he was precise in "with them," and did not say "with the Patriarchs," as we explained above. And he said "and King David," etc., to set right the difficulty mentioned above in the first explanation. "The craving," etc., returns to explain the first matter. "The craving of the female," etc., "is only when the spirit enters into her": meaning, it is a parable: when Yesod enters into her, that is, the extension of Tiferet, the extension of the Vav; and then she casts forth waters, that is, the deeds of the righteous, which are the female waters. And she casts forth these waters to receive male waters; for by their merit she receives from the male, and she demands by their merit. And this is "casts forth," for she shows her action from below to above, in the secret of returning light. And this is what it says, "So Knesset Yisrael," etc.; for "from my flesh I behold God" (Job 19:26). And therefore the female waters are the deeds of the righteous, which rise by means of their souls, in the way we explained above. "And all becomes one craving," etc.: that is to say, Tiferet and Malkhut make one craving, which is their arousal; "and one bundle," that is, the manifestation of the embrace, which is "his left hand under my head" (Song of Songs 2:6), which we shall explain; "and one knot," that is, the manifestation of the union. These are three aspects in the union: the first is this one, with which we have engaged in chapters 18, 19 and 20; the second is the one with which we shall engage in chapter 21; the third is the one with which we shall engage in chapter 22. "And this is the desire of all": meaning, this matter and this arousal is pleasing and lovely to all — to Tiferet and to Malkhut and to the righteous. "And this is the desire of all, and the stroll that the Holy One, blessed be He, takes," etc.: from the wording it is implied that the arousal is by means of the souls that are in the Garden of Eden, since he said, "And this is," etc., "and the stroll that [He] takes," etc.; and the matter is with the souls of the righteous that are in the Garden of Eden. And this is difficult with the passage that we wrote above in chapter 18, that an arousal from below is required, that is, from this world. And so it is implied in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 74), and these are its words: "Rabbi Yehudah said: At the hour when the righteous are many in the world, Knesset Yisrael raises good fragrances and is blessed from the holy King, and her face shines. And at the time when the wicked are many in the world, as it were, Knesset Yisrael does not raise fragrance, and she tastes bitterness from the Other Side; then it is written, 'He cast down from heaven to earth,' etc. (Lamentations 2:1), and her face is darkened. Rabbi Yose said: At the hour when the righteous are many in the world, it is written, 'His left hand under my head, and his right hand embraces me' (Song of Songs 2:6); and at the time when the wicked are many in the world, it is written, 'He has drawn back His right hand' (Lamentations 2:3). Rabbi Chizkiyah said: From here: 'and a whisperer separates the chief friend' (Proverbs 16:28) — that is to say, he separates the King from the Lady," etc. Thus far its words.

Behold, from the words of these Tannaim it is implied that the matter of the union is by means of the deeds of the lower human beings, as he said: "at the hour when the righteous are many in the world, Knesset Yisrael raises good fragrances," that is, the fragrance of the doing of the commandments. And concerning this matter Isaac said of Jacob, "See, the fragrance of my son is as the fragrance of a field," etc. (Genesis 27:27); for he smelled in him the fragrance of the Shekhinah when she receives from Tiferet. And this is what it says, asher, whose explanation is "when": "the fragrance of a field when YHVH has blessed it" — which is Tiferet. "And at the time when [the wicked] are many," etc., and there is nothing by which to unite, "she does not raise fragrance," because there are no good deeds.

And the matter of "and she tastes bitterness" was explained in the Gate of Channels, chapter 4. "Rabbi Yose said: At the hour when the righteous are many," etc.: it is possible to say that Rabbi Yehudah spoke only of the general effluence alone; and this is what it says, "and is blessed from the holy King," that is, His effluence — and not "is united" or "is coupled." But Rabbi Yose explained concerning the literal union; and this is what it says, "his left hand under my head," that is, the embrace of which we shall speak.

And further, besides this, in Parashat Vayakhel (fol. 200b), Rabbi Chiyya, in the name of Rashbi, was telling Rabbi Abba the tikkunim of prayer; and in the tikkun of the falling on the face he said there: "And then one must fall on his face and give over his soul, at the hour when she takes vital souls and spirits; then it is the hour to give over his soul within those vital souls that she takes, for then the bundle of life is as is fitting. This word I heard among the secrets of the Holy Lamp, and permission was not given to me to reveal it, except to you, supernal pious ones. For if, at that hour when she takes vital souls and spirits in the desire of a single cleaving, he sets his heart and his desire on this, and gives his soul in cleaving, in that desire, to include it in that cleaving — if it is accepted at that hour, in that desire of those vital souls and spirits and souls that she takes, this is a person who is bound in the bundle of life in this world and in the World to Come. And further, for she needs to be included from all sides — the King and the Lady — from above and from below, and to be crowned with their souls on all sides: she is crowned with the souls above, and she is crowned with the souls below. And if a person directs his heart and his desire to all this, and gives over his soul from below in cleaving, in desire, as has been said," etc. Thus far its words, as relevant to our matter.

And behold, it appears explicitly that what the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah are included from below is through this man who gives over his soul in the falling on the face after his prayer; so that she be included from above, in the secret of the souls poured forth from above, which are renewed — that is, the effluence of the male and the male waters — and from below, that is, the female waters, which is in the secret of this man and the like. And as they expounded in the Zohar (Vayetze, fol. 153b) concerning Joseph and Benjamin, that this one is a righteous one below and that one a righteous one above; and so the Shekhinah turns out to be a female between two males, that is, Benjamin below, in the secret of female waters. And so it is explained in Parashat Terumah (fol. 128b), and these are its words: "Once they reach 'Sim Shalom,' then that river that goes out from Eden performs marital relations in this chamber; and then all must go out from before the King, and no person and no other needs to be found there, nor to ask requests; rather, one must fall on his face. What is the reason? Because that hour is the hour of marital relations, and every person must be ashamed before his Master and cover his face in great shame, and include his soul in that marital relation of vital souls; for that chamber is included from above and from below with vital souls and spirits." Thus far its words, as relevant to our matter. And from it it is explained that the arousal from below is the souls of the living, who stand in life in this world. And the matter is proven of itself; for it is not fitting that we say that this matter would be by means of the righteous who are in the Garden of Eden, for they are free from the commandments, and their deeds neither raise up nor bring down.

And further: for if so, that the coupling is by means of those souls, then it ought never to be lacking, but on the contrary, to increase; and this is difficult for Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Chizkiyah, who explained that it depends on this world, whether the righteous are many or whether the wicked are many. And in order to resolve this matter we shall ask a further question, according to what is implied, that the matter of "casts forth," etc., is the matter of the stroll and the reveling of the Holy One, blessed be He, with the righteous. Behold, we know from the previous passages that the matter of union and coupling is at the time of "Sim Shalom"; and the reveling is at midnight, as is implied in several places in the Zohar. And these are its words in Parashat Lech Lecha (fol. 92b): "'At midnight I rise to give thanks to You for Your righteous judgments,' etc. (Psalms 119:62). What did David see, that he said 'midnight' and did not say 'at midnight'? Rather, 'Midnight' certainly — and he said this to the Holy One, blessed be He. And is the Holy One, blessed be He, called thus? Yes; for at literal midnight the Holy One, blessed be He, is present, with His company, and then is the hour when He enters the Garden of Eden to revel with the righteous," etc. Thus far its words. And he lengthens there much further on this matter. Behold, it is implied explicitly that the reveling of the Holy One, blessed be He, with the righteous in the Garden of Eden is at midnight.

And further, in Parashat Noach (fol. 72), and these are its words: "Every person who rises to engage in Torah from midnight, when the north wind is aroused — the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to revel with the righteous in the Garden of Eden; and He and all the righteous in the Garden, all of them listen to him and hearken to those words that come out of his mouth," etc. Thus far its words, as relevant to our matter. And from it it is explained that the reveling of the Holy One, blessed be He, with the righteous in the Garden of Eden is at midnight. And in order to resolve this matter we say that the reveling of the Holy One, blessed be He, with the righteous in the Garden of Eden — this is the matter of the Shekhinah, Malkhut, with Tiferet, who revels with them in the secret of Beriah and Yetzirah and Asiyah: that is, the upper Garden of Eden, beneath the Throne of Glory; and the lower Garden of Eden, Yetzirah; and the dwelling of the vital souls, Asiyah — as we shall explain below in the Gate of the Soul. And so it is proven from the wording of the Zohar that this reveling is not a union in which Tiferet is united with the Shekhinah in the secret of the Emanation, high above, but a receiving of effluence that she receives from the supernal river, and likewise the righteous receive. And Tiferet with Malkhut is revealed among them, and in the secret of their manifestation they unite, and the light of the righteous increases; and this is the reveling. And these are its words in the book of the Zohar, Parashat Lech Lecha (fol. 92a): "At midnight, when the birds awaken, the side of the north is aroused with a wind. The scepter that is on the side of the south rises in its standing and strikes that wind, and it subsides and is sweetened. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, is aroused in His custom to revel with the righteous who are in the Garden of Eden. At that hour, happy is the portion of the person who rises to revel in the Torah; for the Holy One, blessed be He, and all the righteous, all of them listen to his voice. This is what is written: 'You who dwell in the gardens, the companions hearken to your voice; let me hear it' (Song of Songs 8:13). And not only this, but the Holy One, blessed be He, draws over him a thread of lovingkindness, so that he be guarded in the world; for the upper and the lower ones guard him. This is what is written: 'By day YHVH will command His lovingkindness, and in the night His song is with me' (Psalms 42:9). Rabbi Chizkiyah said: Whoever engages in Torah at this hour certainly has a portion constantly in the World to Come. Rabbi Yose said: What is the reason for 'constantly'? He said to him: Thus have I learned: that every midnight, when the Holy One, blessed be He, is in the Garden of Eden, all those plantings of the Garden are watered more from that stream that is called 'the ancient stream' (Judges 5:21), 'the stream of delights' (Psalms 36:9), whose waters never cease. As it were, the one who rises and engages in Torah — it is as if that river were poured upon his head and watered him among those plantings that are in the Garden of Eden. Rabbi Yose said: And not only this, but since all the righteous who are within the Garden listen to him, they set a portion for him in that watering of the stream. It turns out that he has a portion constantly in the World to Come." Thus far its words.

And from it it is explained explicitly that the intent of the matter of this reveling is not the upper coupling between Tiferet and Malkhut in the Emanation, but the effluence that the Holy One, blessed be He, pours upon them. And in truth, "the Holy One, blessed be He," mentioned in all these places — the intent is not to Tiferet specifically but to Malkhut, which is also called "the Holy One, blessed be He," in most places. And I went at length in explaining the secret of this matter in the Zohar, Parashat Balak, section 5 of Gate 8; see there. However, the stroll mentioned in the passage before us is their union in the Emanation. And his saying "with the souls of the righteous" does not mean the souls that have already departed from this world, but those souls that are still in their lifetime, by means of their pure and clean deeds, in the way that we explained. For it is not in the hand of the righteous who are in the Garden of Eden either to unite or to cut off; and the principal thing is the righteous in the world of action. And although we said that the reveling is by means of the living, we do not deny that at the time when a righteous person departs from the world, Knesset Yisrael is united with Tiferet by means of his soul that withdraws from the world; for so it is proven from some precision in the wording of the Zohar. But nevertheless the female waters mentioned in this passage are only by means of the literally living. And therefore (in the passage of the Zohar from Parashat Noach, fol. 60, mentioned above) he did not mention "with the righteous in the Garden of Eden," but only "and this is the desire of all, and the stroll that the Holy One, blessed be He, takes with the souls of the righteous," and he did not say "in the Garden." And in any case it is possible to say that it is at the time of their withdrawal from the world. From the whole of the previous chapters we have learned concerning the union of Tiferet with Malkhut that it is impossible except by means of a lower arousal; and this arousal is the fragrance of the commandments of the righteous.

Since we have already explained above the manifestation of arousal and its essence, we wished to explain the matter of the arousal from its beginning, and its reason. And the matter is that blessing does not dwell in the upper ones unless it dwells in the lower ones. And this is what is expounded in the book of the Zohar many times: "the Shekhinah among the lower ones is a need on high." And the matter is that the manifestation of the whole Emanation was emanated only for the need of the lower ones, as we went at length in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation. And since it is so, that its principal [purpose] is for the lower ones, if so, when the lower ones are fit for the blessing to dwell upon them, then the blessing and the effluence dwell in the upper ones; and when blessing does not dwell in the lower ones, because of the badness of their preparation, the blessing does not dwell in the upper ones. And therefore "the Shekhinah among the lower ones" — meaning, that the dwelling of the Shekhinah be among the lower ones, that is, in the lowly world — "is a need on high," meaning, a need for the upper Emanation that is above it. And the parable for this is the nursing mother: for when her child is alive and has the preparation to nurse, the milk increases in her breasts; and when she has no child to nurse and to pour forth upon, then the milk lessens in her breasts. And the intent is that the matter of arousal that we speak of is the preparation and the throne for the effluence and for the blessing. And therefore arousal is needed from the lower righteous one, who is in this world, toward the Shekhinah, so that the righteous one be a throne and a dwelling for the effluence that is poured forth to this world from the Shekhinah, and by his merit it will be poured forth to the lower ones; and then the Shekhinah is a throne and a dwelling for Tiferet, and the effluence is poured forth. However, when no effluence is poured forth from the Shekhinah to the lower ones, because she has no throne and dwelling in this world, then the effluence withdraws from her and she has no union and coupling with Tiferet. And the divine Tanna Rabbi Yehudah revealed this matter in the book of the Zohar, and these are his words, in Parashat Lech Lecha (fol. 88a): "Rabbi Yehudah opened: 'I am my lover's, and his yearning is toward me' (Song of Songs 7:11). We have established that by an arousal below an arousal above is found; for there is no arousal above until there is arousal below. And the blessings above are found only in what has substance in it and is not empty. From where do we know? From the wife of Obadiah, to whom Elisha said, 'Tell me, what do you have in the house?' (2 Kings 4:2). For the blessings above do not dwell on an empty table, nor in an empty place. What is written? 'And she said, Your maidservant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.' She said to him: the measure of this oil is only enough for anointing the little finger. He said to her: You have comforted me; for I did not know how the blessings above would dwell in an empty place; but now that you have oil, this is a place in which blessings are found. From where do we know? For it is written, 'Like the good oil upon the head,' etc. (Psalms 133:2), and what is written at its end? 'For there YHVH commanded the blessing, life forevermore' (Psalms 133:3). And in this place blessings dwell. And if you say, 'like the dew of Hermon that descends upon the mountains of Zion' (Psalms 133:3) — and it is not written 'oil' but 'dew'? Rather, it is oil and it is dew: that dew is what the Holy One, blessed be He, casts down from the supernal anointing oil; for that oil goes out to the right side. Two they are, wine and oil, and they go to two sides: wine to the left side and oil to the right side; and from the right side blessings go out to the world, and from there the holy kingship is anointed. And because oil was set in order below first, oil is ready above — the emptying of blessings. Come and see: from the arousal of this oil, the one above stands ready to pour upon David and Solomon, so that his children are blessed. From where do we know? For it is written, 'And the oil stood' (2 Kings 4:6); it is written here 'stood,' and it is written there, 'the root of Jesse, which stands for a banner of the peoples' (Isaiah 11:10). Come and see: the table of the showbread, from which blessings go out, and sustenance to the world, must not be found empty even for one moment, so that the blessings not withdraw from there. So too, one does not bless over an empty table, for the blessings above do not dwell on an empty table. Come and see what is written: 'I am my lover's, and his yearning is toward me.' 'I am my lover's' first, and afterward 'his yearning is toward me.' 'I am my lover's' — to prepare a place for him first; and afterward, 'his yearning is toward me.'" Thus far its words, as relevant to our matter.

And behold, he explained explicitly that the reason for the matter of arousal is so that there be a dwelling and an abode and a throne for the Emanation; and this is the principal arousal, which indicates that there is an abode and a preparation for the effluence, as we explained. And this matter is because the light of the Emanation is not revealed without its having a sheath in which to be stored away.

And behold, when there is no sheath and abode in this world in which to be stored away, it is compelled to rise, and the effluence does not descend except enough for the sustenance of the lower ones; and therefore the light is not revealed in Malkhut except enough for her sustenance. However, when there is in this world a sheath and an abode in which the descending light and the effluence may be concealed, then the light is revealed and seen, and the effluence descends to Malkhut in plenty, so that the lower ones are sustained and "take pleasure in the abundance of peace" (Psalms 37:11). And this matter has a revelation in the Zohar, but we do not wish to lengthen. And now one must ask whether arousal is also needed for Binah, just as arousal from the lower ones is needed for Malkhut, so that the bridegroom and his bride couple. And we say that it is also needed; and this is the reason that there is no coupling above, in Binah with Chokhmah, when there is no coupling for Malkhut with Tiferet, as we proved in chapters 13 and 14. And so Elijah, of blessed memory, taught in the explanation of the Zohar Chadash on the Song of Songs (fol. 74a), and these are his words: "Just as an arousal of joy needs to be aroused from this world above, so it is necessary to arouse joy and gladness from the world of the moon toward the supernal world. And therefore the worlds stand in one pattern, and arousal rises only from below to above." Thus far his words.

Behold, arousal from Malkhut is needed for the upper union, that is, for Binah. And by this it will be understood what is the reason they said that the Shekhinah sings constantly: because the union of Binah with Chokhmah is [such] that they never separate, therefore arousal is needed constantly. But the union of Malkhut with Tiferet is at the time of morning; therefore the principal song is in the morning, at the time of our prayer, in order to unite her with her husband. And the principal [explanation] of this passage we explained above, in chapter 6. And the matter is that the worlds chain down one from another and are a throne one for another; and this world — that is to say, the man in it — is an abode and a throne for the Shekhinah; and therefore our sages, of blessed memory, expounded, "the principal [dwelling of the] Shekhinah was among the lower ones." And the Shekhinah is a throne and an abode and a palace for Tiferet, and Tiferet for Binah, and Binah for Chokhmah. And the matter is clear. And one must ask: since it is so, that there is no union and coupling except by means of arousal, if so, how was the soul of the first Adam emanated? And to say that it was by means of arousal is impossible, for still "there was no man" (Genesis 2:5). And to say that it was a coupling from the back, God forbid — this is certainly forced, for there is no coupling except face to face. If so, how was it emanated? And for this it occurred to us to resolve it in the way that they resolved this matter in the book of the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 167), concerning that child who was the son of Rav Safra, when he engaged with the five times "light," and five times "water," and five times "firmament," which are in the likeness of the seed of man: which is first, that is, in the brain, light; and afterward water; and afterward firmament, that is, the extension of the body of man. And so it was in the matter of the Emanation: light from the side of Chesed, water Gevurah, firmament Tiferet. And he asked further about this and said to them: "This that I said, that here was clarified the secret of man in the light of that seed, and afterward it was made water, and from within those waters a firmament spread out, the likeness of man, as we have aroused — granted, when this is done within the womb of a woman; for the seed is formed only within the womb of the female, for the likeness of man to spread out in it. But here, if these five grades are the likeness of man, in what place was this likeness formed and spread out within those waters? If you say within a female — this would be the World to Come — it is not so; for the form and the likeness were not formed until the letters went outside, and afterward took shape. And further, the World to Come was the craftsman, as it is written, 'And Elohim said, Let there be light, and there was light; and Elohim said, Let there be a firmament' — behold, it was the craftsman. And if you say, in the lower female — it is not so; for until then she did not exist, and when this likeness of man went out, his female went out with him. Behold, the likeness of man was not formed in her. If so, in what place was this seed formed and engraved, to be the engraving of the likeness of man? Rather, this is a supernal secret: the first Adam was formed and engraved without a female; the second Adam, from the power and the seed of this one, was engraved and formed within a female. The first Adam — the engraving of the form and the likeness of the body was not in a female, and it was without any form at all; and it was formed and engraved below from the World to Come, without male and without female. Those letters took shape within a measure, and in them the secret of man was formed and engraved. And the letters, in a straight way, in their order, from the secret of the primordial light, began to be engraved and to be formed; and this light was sown within it, within the measure. When it reached within the measure, it turned into water; within the water a firmament spread out, the form of man, the likeness, as is fitting. After the female was adorned for him and they turned face to face, this likeness of man entered in craving toward the female, and there [the next] was engraved and formed in his pattern; and of him it is written, 'and he begot in his likeness, after his image' (Genesis 5:3). This one was formed within a female, which that first one was not; for that first one was formed within itself, in measure, within the measure, as has been said. In this manner below. Below, what is written? 'And the man knew Eve his wife,' etc. (Genesis 4:1)." Thus far its words, as relevant to our matter. And from it the matter of the upper Adam has been explained, who was made of himself, without a female, as he goes on to explain. We too shall say concerning the first Adam that he was made without a female; rather, [just as] the very light, water and firmament took shape of themselves, from the side of the expansion, so is the matter with the soul of the first Adam, which took shape. And there is some proof for this from what is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 107) concerning "what is his name, and what is his son's name" (Proverbs 30:4): that the first Adam is "what [mah] is his name," and Moses is "what is his son's name." And in Adam there is mah, and in Moses there is mah. And in Moses, mah is the four-letter name in its filling, which is in Tiferet, which is called "son" to Chokhmah — which is also the four-letter name in its filling, amounting to mah [45], thus: Yod, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Alef. And since the soul of Adam was emanated from a high place, it did not need coupling. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim that Adam is Chokhmah and Eve is Binah (for the filling of the name of 45 is in numerical value Chavah [Eve]); and therefore of her it is said, "for she was the mother of all living" (Genesis 3:20). And therefore their emanation did not need a lower coupling. But in the Zohar (Bereshit, fol. 34b) it appears explicitly that Tiferet and Malkhut coupled to bring forth the soul of the first Adam. And it would already be possible to say that what is expounded in the Zohar, that they coupled to bring forth, means to reveal his soul, which was concealed in Binah. And so it is implied from its wording there, for it said, "and the east cleaved to the west and brought him forth"; and it did not say "and he was made from it," but "and brought forth," meaning that they brought him out of the concealed place where he had been. But the expression "Let us make man" (Genesis 1:26) is somewhat difficult. And it is already possible to resolve it: "let us make" means, let us bring him out from the grade of Emanation to an outer grade, which is the grade of Asiyah [Making]. But nevertheless we do not get out of the difficulty; for in that passage it says explicitly that they coupled in the secret of "his left hand under my head, and his right hand embraces me" (Song of Songs 2:6). And what is it to us whether the coupling was to bring him forth or to bring him into being? In the end, they coupled. If so, since "there was no man," and there was no arousal, how was he emanated, or brought forth? And according to all the explanations it is difficult. And therefore we say that the coupling was from the back.

And the matter of "from the back" is this: when there is arousal from below, by the power of that arousal there is power in Malkhut to shine her face toward Tiferet; and after she shines her face toward him, he shines his face toward her, in the secret of the channels that we explained in the Gate of Channels, chapter 1. However, when Malkhut has no deeds, she has no power to shine her face toward Tiferet in the secret of returning light, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, under the entry "water." And since they do not shine face to face as is fitting, behold, it is a coupling from the back. And this matter — to say that their coupling was from the back — is necessary, because from the side of the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut a soul of male and female was emanated, as we shall explain.

And behold, when they are face to face, the souls are emanated face to face, as in the matter of the souls that were emanated after the world was created. And Adam and his wife were emanated face to back; and the witness to this is the matter of his body, which was so, for the body is a garment for the soul — until afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, sawed her off. And after He sawed her off, when there was arousal from below, the souls emanated above were face to face; and the witness is Seth and his mate, who needed no sawing at all. And this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, intended in his wording, in the passage that we wrote in chapter 18: "Come and see: Adam and Eve were created side by side. What is the reason they were not created face to face? Because it is written, 'for YHVH Elohim had not caused it to rain upon the earth,' and coupling was not found in its tikkun as is fitting."

Behold, he did not say that there was no coupling at all, but that it was not as is fitting, for it was from the back, as we explained; and the matter is as we explained. And it remains for us further to explain a matter found in the Zohar, Parashat Tazria (fol. 45), and these are its words: "Come and see: at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, is with Knesset Yisrael, at those times when He is with her, and she arouses desire toward Him first and draws Him to her in great affection and craving, then she is filled from the right side, and many hosts are found from the right side in all the worlds.
