And when the Holy One, blessed be He, arouses affection and desire first, and she is aroused afterward, and not at the time that He is aroused, then all is found on the side of the female, and the left is aroused, and many hosts stand and are aroused on the left side in all the worlds. In this manner it is written, 'If a woman conceives and bears a male,' etc. (Leviticus 12:2). What is the reason? We have learned: the lower world is found like the upper world, and this one is in the pattern of that one. And therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed male or female, so that desire be found in the world." Thus far its words.

And behold, he taught that sometimes Malkhut is aroused only last, and then many masters of judgment are aroused, etc. And it would have been fitting to ask: since she has the power to be aroused, as he said, "and she is aroused afterward," if so, why is she not aroused first, so that there would be no matter of judgment? And the matter is this: when Malkhut has no manifestation and power to be aroused at all, God forbid, then she becomes a menstruant [poreset niddah], in that she sucks bitterness, as we explained in the previous chapter and in the Gate of Channels, chapter 4. And when she has deeds, but they are few, because of the iniquity of the generation, or [when] Israel are half meritorious and half guilty, then she is not aroused at all; but Tiferet, in the abundance of His compassion for Israel, is aroused over the mother, and then He arouses her, and the compassion is aroused, and the mother is aroused last, with the few deeds that there are in the generation. And then many masters of judgment are aroused, because they demand judgment and say, "These are idol-worshippers and those are idol-worshippers; these uncover nakedness," etc.; and therefore the power of judgment is aroused. And concerning a matter like this is our prayer that we say: "When You behold the poverty of our deeds, bring near righteousness of Your own accord." Meaning: when You see that the deeds of the people of the world are poor — but there are already deeds, only they are few and poor — then bring near Tzedek, Malkhut, which is called Tzedek [righteousness], of Your own accord; and do not, because of this, annul, God forbid, Your union with her, but bring her near of Yourself, by Your being aroused first. And it turns out, according to this, that in the aspect of arousal there are three aspects. The first aspect, and it is the chosen one: "when the righteous are many in the world"; for then the world is judged according to its majority, and she is aroused first; and then "and bears a male" — meaning, "whoever is stronger prevails": the power of compassion prevails over the power of judgment, and therefore all is compassion and the world is at ease. The second aspect is when the world is guilty but there are some meritorious ones in it; for then she bears last, for she has no power to be aroused first because of the fewness of the deeds, and she is aroused last, as we explained; and then it is a time of coupling, but there are accusers in the coupling, as we explained. The third aspect is when the majority of the world is guilty, or all of it; and this is what he said, "when the wicked are many in the world"; for then "she tastes bitterness," for she sucks from the outer side, meaning from the excess, as we explained in the Gate of Channels, chapter 4. And what remains of the explanation of this passage will be explained in the coming chapters. And this remark is enough for us on this, concerning the matter of arousal. And we come to explain the matter of the second aspect of coupling, and it is the aspect of the embrace and the kiss.

What is intended in this chapter is to explain the matter of the parable, in the upper coupling, of the embrace and the kiss. And these are its words in the book of the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 34b): "Rabbi Shimon rose and said: I was contemplating: when the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to create man, all the upper and lower ones trembled. And the sixth day was rising in its grades, until the supernal desire rose and illumined the beginning of all lights. And it opened the gate of the east, for from there light goes out. And the south showed the strength of the light that it inherited from the head, and was strengthened in the east. The east strengthened the north; and the north was aroused and spread out and called with great might to the west, to draw near and to be partner with it. Then the west rose in the north and was bound to it. Afterward the south came and took hold of the west, and south and north surrounded it, for these are the fences of the Garden. Then the east drew near to the west, and the west dwelt in joy and asked of all of them, and said, 'Let us make man in our image, after our likeness' (Genesis 1:26) — that he be in this manner, in four sides and above and below. And the east cleaved to the west and brought him forth. And therefore we have learned: man went out from the place of the Temple." Thus far its words.

"I was contemplating": meaning, I was examining the matter of the creation of man. "Trembled," etc.: because the creation of man was not right in the eyes of the upper ones, because by means of man the principal [dwelling of the] Shekhinah is among the lower ones; and therefore they said, "What is man, that You are mindful of him?" (Psalms 8:5), as our sages, of blessed memory, explained. And so it is explained in the Zohar concerning Uza and Aza'el. And therefore the upper and lower ones trembled, because all of them were given into his hand and he rules over all of them, as it is written, "and have dominion over the fish of the sea" (Genesis 1:28). "And the sixth day" is Yesod, the sixth day.

And the matter of "was rising in its grades" means: it was rising with Tiferet and Malkhut, for it is what unites them. And the matter is that it was aroused toward the coupling that is done by its means; and it rises to Tiferet and descends to Malkhut. "Until the [supernal] desire rose," etc.: meaning, until the will rose before Him; and the meaning is, until effluence was poured to Keter from above, and it poured forth to Chokhmah, which is what is called "the beginning of all lights," as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapters 3 and 7. "And it opened the gate of the east": he did not say "the east," which is Tiferet, but "the gate of the east," which is Chokhmah; for from there the east shines, at the time of its emanation and even after its emanation; and from there, by way of this gate, its light goes out to the whole Emanation. "And the south showed its strength," etc.: meaning, Chesed, which is what is called "light"; and the principal sucking of Chesed is from Chokhmah, and therefore Chesed shone its light, which it receives from its head, which is Chokhmah. "And was strengthened in the east": meaning, Chesed took hold of and was united with Tiferet, from the side of their relation together; for Chokhmah is the gate of the east, and the south receives from there, and therefore Chesed is united with the east. And by this will be resolved what is found in some places, the title "east" for Chokhmah, for the reason that we said.

And behold, Chesed is united with Tiferet from the side that it inclines toward Chesed. "And the east strengthened the north": meaning, Tiferet, after it has already been united with the south and received from it, goes to unite with the north, to do its work: to tip Gevurah toward Chesed. "And the north was aroused and spread out and called with great might": meaning, it arouses the power of judgment, so that judgment not be annulled; and therefore it pours judgment into Malkhut, who is called the lower Gevurah. And this is "to draw near and to be partner with it," in the way of those who wage war, who do not scatter, so that all of them be one band. "Then the west rose" — and it is Malkhut — and is united with Gevurah, for the secret of her inclination is toward judgment. "Afterward the south came and took hold of the west": meaning, Chesed, when it saw that judgment was prevailing by means of Malkhut, and that she was united with Gevurah, prevails and takes hold of Malkhut, who is called "west" [ma'arav] because there is the mixing [eruv] of the powers, for she receives from all. "And south and north surrounded it," etc.: meaning, the aspect of Malkhut is an aspect by itself, which is the manifestation of Yod; and [it is] by means of the north and the south, which adorn her and make fences for her around her — that is, the manifestation of Heh — as we explained above in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2, and shall explain in the Gate of Manifestations. "Then the east drew near to the west": meaning, by means of Chesed and Gevurah there is a manifestation of union for Tiferet with Malkhut; but before this matter they have no drawing-near.

And the matter of his saying "the east drew near to the west": the intent is not to the manifestation of literal coupling, but it is the matter of embrace; for this union is called embrace, which is by means of the two arms: "his left hand under my head, and his right hand embraces me" (Song of Songs 2:6). And the intent is that Malkhut puts the left before the right; that is, "his left hand," which is Gevurah, which comes to her first, as I explained; and afterward "his right hand," which is Chesed, which is the south that takes hold of the west, which is Malkhut; and of it is said, "and his right hand embraces me." And this is what is called embrace, toward the upper union. And this is "the east drew near to the west," which he says, that it is in the secret of the embrace. "And the west dwelt in joy": this is the secret of her gladness, lying in the bosom of the King between His two arms. And it is possible that it alludes to the kiss, which we shall explain afterward. "In this manner, in four sides and above and below": meaning, the four sides are east, west, north and south mentioned in the passage, which are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Malkhut; and above and below are Netzach and Hod, which are the two testicles of the male, although they were not mentioned; and they are called above and below, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter. And likewise man includes all of them, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul. "And the east cleaved to the west": that is, the union and coupling itself; for so he said "cleaved," and did not say "drew near" as he said above. "And brought him forth": meaning, emanated his soul, as we explained in the previous chapter. "And therefore we have learned: man [went out] from the place of the Temple": that is, Malkhut, which is called "the Temple" [beit ha-mikdash, the house of the Sanctuary]. And it is possible that Malkhut is called "house" and "palace" for the upper Holy that hovers over the house and sanctifies it — which is Tiferet, which is called "holy" from the side of Chokhmah, which is called "holiness" [kodesh]; and it is sanctified from there and sanctifies its house and its palace; and this is their union, and from there was the emanation of the soul of the first Adam. Thus far. And from it we have learned the matter of the embrace for the upper coupling: that it is by Chesed's uniting with Tiferet, and Tiferet's uniting with the north, which is Gevurah; and Gevurah takes hold of Malkhut, and Chesed takes hold of Malkhut; and then Malkhut and Tiferet are embraced and bound together in longing, in the secret of "his left hand under my head, and his right hand embraces me" (Song of Songs 2:6), as we explained. And the reason that they have no embrace and drawing-near except by means of Chesed and Gevurah is that Malkhut is the element of earth, and its nature is cold and dry; and Tiferet is the element of air, and it is hot and moist. And behold, they are opposites in their nature, one from the other, for this one is hot and moist and that one is cold and dry. And it is impossible for them to be equalized and completed except by means of water and fire, which are intermediate between them: for water, cold and moist, is equal to air in its moisture and to earth in its coldness; and fire, hot and dry, is equal to earth in its dryness and to air in its heat. And behold, they are united, although they are opposites, by means of fire and water, which are Gevurah and Chesed, as we explained above. And this union is explained in the Zohar in several places. And what one must be precise about is that we have found that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this matter contrary to this intent, in the Zohar, Parashat Bamidbar (fol. 120a), and these are its words: "Rabbi Elazar asked Rabbi Shimon his father: From where is the sign for the coupling of union? He said to him: My son, although we have established words on every side, and they are scattered, a word here and a word there, take this sign in your hand, and so it is: like the circuit of the altar. For we have learned, 'And he came to the south-eastern corner, the east-northern, the north-western, the west-southern' (Mishnah Zevachim 5:3). He said to him: But it is not possible until a person first receives upon himself the yoke of the holy Kingdom and places this yoke upon himself; and you said that he comes to the south first! He said to him: All this I have told you; for I said 'and he came to the corner' first, and you know the secret of 'corner,' and this is the yoke of the holy Kingdom. Afterward, 'south-eastern,' for there is the Tree of Life; and this is to couple it with the east, which is Abba Ila'ah, for the son comes from the side of Abba. And therefore from south to east, for the strength of the south is in the east, and the south must be bound together with the east. And the east, which is bound to the north, as it is said, 'and whose belly You fill with Your treasure [tzefunekha]' (Psalms 17:14), because this one completes and fills streams and springs; and therefore 'east-northern': these are Abba and Imma, who never separate, as we have established. And what is said, 'northern,' for it is the supernal concealed one, and from its side the north goes out, and judgments are aroused from its side, although it is compassion and joy, as we have established. And when it goes out, the north goes out with it, which is included and bound in the south. Afterward, 'north-western,' for from the side of Abba the son goes out, and from the side of Imma the daughter goes out. And therefore 'north-western'; and this is the first corner, for now it is bound to the north plainly. Afterward one must bind it to the south, for there is the bond of all, and the body is found in it; and therefore 'west-southern.' It turns out that this corner is three times: one, for a person to receive it first; and afterward two, to bind her with two arms, to be joined with the body and for all to be one. And this is the order of the complete union; and each and every side in that bond that is fitting for it, and let him not exchange a side for another side that is not fitting for it, so that he not be punished. And whoever performs this union as is fitting, as we have said, happy is his portion," etc. Thus far its words, as relevant to our matter.

And behold, from it it is explained that, besides the change of the directions — for he explained south as Tiferet, east as Chokhmah and north as Binah — he further changed this matter of the embrace; for he wished to explain that the principal union is to unite Tiferet and Malkhut between Chokhmah and Binah. And to explain the matter so in the previous passage is impossible, according to the nature of the wording of the passage. And therefore it seems [right] to be precise in the wording of the passage at its end, where he said: "It turns out that this corner is three times: one, for a person to receive it first; and afterward two, to bind her with two arms." And the intent is that Malkhut is mentioned three times in the first mishnah: in what he said, "and he came to the corner," that is, the entrance, which is to receive the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven first, as Rabbi Elazar explained; and two are "north-western," that is, west, which is Malkhut, and "west-southern," which is Malkhut also. And he said that they are to unite her with two arms, which are Chesed and Gevurah, that is, "southern" and "northern," for each one of them is mentioned with the west. And this is difficult, for this is not his previous way; for above he said that south is Tiferet and north is Binah. Therefore we say that when we are precise in his wording, Rabbi Shimon never changed. For the south is Chesed, and likewise the east, which is Chokhmah, is in the way that we explained above. And so he was precise in saying, "Afterward, 'southern,' for there is the Tree of Life"; and he did not say "'southern,' which is the Tree of Life," but "for there"; for the intent is that Tiferet's inclination is toward the right, which is Chesed. And this is what he says, "for there is the Tree of Life," meaning in the south, which is Chesed. And afterward he said, "And what is said, 'northern,' for it is the supernal concealed one, and from its side the north goes out," etc. Behold, he said that the reason Binah is called "north" [tzafon] — the intent is that she is concealed [tzafun], that is, the expression tzafon; and further, that from there the north is drawn.

And behold, it turns out according to this that the principal north is in Gevurah. And the reason that this union needed Binah over Gevurah and Chokhmah over Chesed is that he came to resolve the matter that is difficult in this matter of the embrace. For Tiferet always sucks from Chesed and from Gevurah, and likewise Malkhut sucks from Chesed and from Gevurah; if so, what is different in this matter of union, that they need to receive from Chesed and from Gevurah? Behold, they always receive from there! Rather, the difference is that Tiferet receives from Chesed in the aspect of Chesed alone, and from Gevurah in the aspect of Gevurah alone; but for the union they need to receive from Chesed in the aspect of Chokhmah, which is above it, and from Gevurah in the aspect of Binah, which is above it. And one cannot say that the union of Tiferet with the north is not [found] in this passage; for he was precise and said, "and the south must be bound together with the east, the east that is bound to the north," as we say, etc. The intent is that one must unite the south, where Tiferet is, in the way that we explained, with Chokhmah; and Chokhmah is already united with Binah. It turns out that Tiferet, by means of Chokhmah, is united with Binah. This is what emerges for us from these passages: that Tiferet must receive from Chesed with Chokhmah — the intent is the effluence of Chokhmah upon Chesed — and from Gevurah by means of the effluence of Binah; and afterward Gevurah pours into Malkhut the effluence that it receives from Binah; and afterward Malkhut further receives from the effluence of Chokhmah that is in Chesed. And the intent is that all of them are united for this embrace.

And further, [it comes] to indicate, also in the matter of the embrace, the bond and union of Chokhmah with Binah; for certainly Yod must also be united with Heh, and by its means Vav will be united with Heh. Or it is possible to say that these two passages never agree together, and nevertheless they do not disagree. In the first passage, which is in Bereshit, we are dealing with the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut for the matter of the souls; and therefore he said that Tiferet must be united with Chesed and Gevurah, with the effluence that comes to them from the upper ones, for so it is necessary, as we explained. And so it appears from the words of the passage, which said, "and the south showed its strength, which it inherited from the head" — that is what Chesed receives from Chokhmah; and likewise Malkhut receives from Gevurah and from Chesed, and by its means they are united. And in this passage we are dealing with union, meaning in the intention of the Reading of the Shema. And he said that one must enter at the corner, which is Malkhut, that is, "Hear"; and afterward the south, that is, Tiferet, which is "Israel"; and afterward its union with Chesed; and from there unite Tiferet with Chokhmah, which is the east, that is, YHVH. And afterward he should intend that Chokhmah is united with Binah, that is, "our God," which is the north; and in the name "our God" he should intend Binah, and Gevurah, which is the north, and Malkhut, for the three of them are called Elohim. And afterward he should unite Malkhut in YHVH, which is Tiferet, which is the south. And afterward, with the word "One," he alludes that all of them are united in a complete union. And one should not wonder that there are several ways in the matter of union; for so Rashbi explained explicitly in answer to the question of Rabbi Elazar, who said, "the sign for the coupling of union" — as it appears, he did not ask about the manifestation of the known coupling, but about the union, which is the explanation of the Reading of the Shema. This is another way to set this matter right; and nevertheless, with us the first is the principal one. And since we have been aroused concerning the matter of the embrace, we come to the explanation of the matter of the kiss. And first it is fitting that we say: the kiss is with the mouth, for so it is written, "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" (Song of Songs 1:2). And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 70), and these are its words: "'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth': this is the supernal craving; for desire goes out from the mouth to kiss, and does not go out from the nose, when fire goes out. For when the mouth is joined to kiss, fire goes out with desire, with the shining of the face, with the joy of all, with the cleaving of rest. And therefore, 'for your love is better than wine,' etc." And from it it is explained that this kiss is not by means of Gevurah, from which is the pouring forth of the intoxicating wine and the burning fire, as is known and will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. Rather, the kiss is with the mouth, which is more compassion and more praiseworthy. For from the nose judgment sometimes goes out, but the mouth is compassion; and by means of the kiss the power of Gevurah is aroused in the secret of the effluence of Binah, the guarded wine, the wine that gladdens; and this is "fire with desire, with the shining of the face," which he said.

And they added further in the explanation of this kiss, in Parashat Mishpatim (fol. 124b), and these are its words: "'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.' What is the reason for 'let him kiss me'? It ought to have said 'let him love me'; why 'let him kiss me'? Rather, thus have we learned: what are kisses? The cleaving of spirit with spirit. For therefore the kiss is with the mouth, for the mouth is the outlet and the source of the spirit; and therefore they kiss with the mouth in affection, and spirit cleaves with spirit, so that they do not separate from one another. And therefore one whose soul goes out in a kiss cleaves to another spirit, to a spirit from which it does not separate; and this is called a kiss. And therefore Knesset Yisrael said, 'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth,' to cause spirit to cleave with spirit, so that they not separate from one another." Thus far its words.

And behold, from it it appears that the kiss is a thing more concealed and lovelier than love; for love is the matter of the embrace of which we spoke before, and the matter of the kiss is after love; and he said that by its means is the cleaving of spirit with spirit. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Midrash (in the Zohar Chadash, Song of Songs): "'The Song of Songs' — the cleaving of body with body; 'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth' — the cleaving of spirit with spirit," etc. Thus far his words.

And behold, he taught that the matter of "the Song of Songs," which he explained there of the sefirot, is the cleaving of body, that is, the sefirot in their outer aspects; but the kiss is the cleaving of spirit with spirit, in the secret of inwardness and soul for the sefirot: that the two inner spirits cleave together, like a man who kisses his beloved with his mouth. For by means of the mouth he unites mouth with mouth, breath with breath [neshimah] — and this is soul with soul [neshamah], spirit with spirit. And the principle that emerges for us concerning the mouth and the kiss, from some places of the Zohar, is that the mouth is the matter of Malkhut in her aspect concealed in Tiferet; and through it is the outlet of the inner spirit concealed in Tiferet, and likewise of the inner spirit concealed in Malkhut; and by their means is the kiss. And the matter of the kisses is aroused from the inwardness of the sefirot, which shines from the Ein Sof.

And this matter is that just as they are united from the side of the outer aspects of the sefirot, so they are united from the side of the inner aspects of the sefirot. And the secret of "spirit with spirit" will be explained in Sefer Or Yakar, in the first part; and in these matters I went at length there, on the Zohar, in the account of the Old Man and in Parashat Vayetze; see there. And it remains for us to explain a matter explained in the book of the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 100b), and these are its words: "Rabbi Abba sent to Rabbi Shimon, saying to him: When is the coupling of Knesset Yisrael with the holy King? He sent to him: 'And moreover she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife' (Genesis 20:12). Rabbi Abba was agitated; he raised his voice and wept, and said: Rabbi, Rabbi, Holy Lamp, woe, woe! Woe to the world when you depart from it; woe to the generation that will be in the world when you withdraw from them and they remain orphans of you. Rabbi Chiyya said to Rabbi Abba: This that he sent you, what does it say? He said: Certainly the coupling of the King with the Lady is only at the time when she is illumined from Abba Ila'ah; and when she is illumined from it, we call her 'holy' [kodesh], for from the house of Abba she takes this; and then they couple together. For the King is called 'holy,' as it is written, 'Israel is holy to YHVH, the first fruits of His harvest' (Jeremiah 2:3), for it takes from the place that is called 'holy.' Then: 'my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother' — for from the house of Abba is this name, and not from the house of Imma. And therefore 'and she became my wife': to couple together at this time and not at another time — at the time that she takes from the house of Abba, and not at the time that she takes from the house of Imma. And the Day of Atonement proves it, for marital relations are forbidden, because coupling is not found, for she takes from the house of Imma and not from the house of Abba. Rabbi Chiyya said: Certainly happy is the generation in whose midst Rabbi Shimon dwells; happy are those who stand before him every day." Thus far its words.

And behold, he explained explicitly that there is no union of Tiferet with Malkhut except when Malkhut receives from Chokhmah, and then they are united; but when she receives from Binah alone, they are not united. And the Day of Atonement, which is Binah pouring forth into Malkhut, proves it: for it is forbidden in marital relations, which indicates that there is no union above. And this is the choicest explanation of this wording. And there is no wonder from the matter of the embrace, in which we unite her in the north, which is Gevurah, from the effluence of Binah, as we explained above; because he already returns and says "west-southern," which is to unite her on the right, in Chesed, where Abba is.

And further, for Chokhmah is united with Binah, as we said, "the east that is bound to the north," that is, Chokhmah is united with Binah. And there is no doubt that all her receiving from Chokhmah is by means of Binah. And what he said, "but not the daughter of my mother," means: but not when she receives from the aspect of Binah, in the aspect of her own self alone; but when she is "the daughter of my father," that is to say, that she receives her aspect with Chokhmah, that is, literal Chokhmah. And this matter is necessary from several places.

The intent in this chapter is to explain, concerning the union proper itself, what its matter is and its pleasure, and what is drawn from it. And this matter has already been explained somewhat from the wording of the passage of the Zohar that we wrote in chapter 20. And these are its words elsewhere, in Parashat Vayikra (fol. 7a): "'And a priest's daughter' (Leviticus 22:12): this is the holy soul, which is called the King's daughter; for they have established that the holy soul goes out from the coupling of the King and the Lady. And therefore, just as the body below is from male and female, so is the soul above." Thus far its words.

Behold, he taught that the coupling is to receive the souls. And so it is explained in Parashat Lech Lecha (fol. 85b), and these are its words: "'And his fruit is sweet to my palate' (Song of Songs 2:3): these are the souls of the righteous, who are all the fruit of the works of the Holy One, blessed be He, and they stand with Him above. Come and see: all the souls of the world, which are the fruit of the works of the Holy One, blessed be He, are all one, in one secret. And when they descend to the world, all of them separate into forms, male and female; and those male and female are joined together. And come and see: the craving of the female toward the male makes a vital soul, etc. And the desire of the craving of the male toward the female, and his cleaving to her, brings forth a vital soul, and includes the craving of the female and takes it; and the lower craving is included in the upper craving, and they become one desire without separation. And then the female takes all and conceives from the male, and the cravings of both of them cleave together. And therefore all is included, one in the other. And when the souls go out, male and female go out together; and afterward, once they descend, they separate, this one to its side and that one to its side. And the Holy One, blessed be He, couples them afterward; and the coupling is not given to another, but to the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, for He knows their coupling, to join them as is fitting. Happy is the person who is meritorious in his deeds and walks in the way of truth, so that vital soul is joined with vital soul as they were at the outset. For if he is meritorious in his deeds, this is a person complete as is fitting. And therefore it is written, 'and his fruit is sweet to my palate,' for he is in [his] tikkun, blessed, so that worlds are blessed from him; because all depends on the deeds of a person, whether he is meritorious or not meritorious. Rabbi Chizkiyah said: Thus have I heard, for it is written, 'From Me is your fruit found' (Hosea 14:9): for the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Knesset Yisrael, 'From Me, certainly, is your fruit found.' It is not written 'My fruit is found,' but 'your fruit': that craving of the female that makes a vital soul and is included in the strength of the male; and vital soul is included in vital soul, and they become one, included one in the other, as we have said. Afterward both of them are found in the world; and [so], by the power of the male, the fruit of the female is found. Another explanation: by the craving of the female the fruit of the male is found; for were it not for the craving of the female toward the male, fruits would never be made. This is what is written: 'From Me is your fruit found.'" Thus far its words.

And from the whole of the passage it is explained that the souls are from the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut. And when we come into the depth of understanding it, it appears from it that the soul of the male and the soul of the female are united, and are twins in one gestation; and it is impossible to picture the soul of the female without a male, or the soul of the male without a female. And the reason is that they are two powers from two sefirot that are united: from the power of the female a female is drawn, and from the power of the male a male is drawn. And we have found that the souls, whether male or female, come to be from the union of Tiferet and Malkhut. And there is a difficulty with this: for we hold that the souls are from Binah, as will be explained in the Gate of the Soul; and since they are from the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, how is it possible that they are from Binah? And one cannot say that this matter expounded here concerns the spirits, which are from Tiferet, or the vital souls, which are from Malkhut — and so he said "vital soul with vital soul" — for at the beginning of his words he said "souls" [nishmatin], as he said, "'and his fruit is sweet to my palate': these are the souls," etc. And further, "its fellow tells of it" (Job 36:33): the previous passage, in Parashat Vayikra, which also said "soul" [nishmata].

And further there is a difficulty: for in the Zohar it appears explicitly that from the union of Tiferet and Malkhut there comes to be only either a male or a female; and so it is proven from the wording in Parashat Tazria that we wrote in chapter 20. And in Parashat Pekudei (fol. 245b), concerning the palaces, in the first palace, it is found, and these are its words: "In this palace there is a spirit called Satutriyah, and this is a fair appearance (another version: sapphire) that sparkles to every side; and this is what stands to two sides, and from these sparks separate, like the sparkling of a lamp, as we have established in several respects. And many colors blaze from this on the right side. When that upper firmament, the river that flows and goes out from Eden, brings forth souls to bring them into the seventh palace above, that seventh palace takes them. And when those holy souls go out from within that seventh palace, they descend until they reach, etc.; and that holy spirit, Satutriyah, which is on the right, takes them. And all those male souls that are destined to fly into righteous males on the right — it takes all of them, and they tarry there until they are included in the souls of the female. For from this spirit another spirit goes out to the left, which is seen and stored away and included in this first spirit, and they are one, included one in the other; and this spirit is called Adiriyah Sangiyah; this is the spirit on the left. And this stands so that when [there is] the craving of the seventh palace to cleave to that river that flows and goes out, that desire that rises from below to above makes souls by its desire, and they are females. And when the desire of that river descends and cleaves from above to below, they make male souls. The desire from above makes males; the desire from below makes females. And when these female souls go out from within that seventh palace, they descend until they reach this spirit on the left, which is called Adiriyah, and is called 'the sapphire pavement' (Exodus 24:10), as we have established in other respects. Once those female souls reach this spirit, this spirit takes them, and they stand in it. And afterward this spirit of the left is included in this spirit of the right; and then those souls become included, male and female together; they couple and fly from this palace and separate into human beings as is fitting." Thus far its words.

And behold, from this passage there follows a demolition of the two fences that we fenced above concerning the soul. First: for he said that they come to be male and female by themselves, these to the right and these to the left — true, they are united by means of those two powers, set out with known names, as is explained from the plain sense of the passage. Second: he said above that they are from the union of Tiferet and Malkhut; and behold, he said here explicitly that they are only from the union of the seventh palace with the river that flows and goes out, which is in Binah, and not from the union of the bridegroom and the bride. Further, there follows from this passage a demolition of the passage from Parashat Tazria that we wrote in chapter 20. For there he said that desire from below to above is compassion and is male; and this is "If a woman conceives and bears a male" (Leviticus 12:2), and our sages, of blessed memory, explained, "if the woman emits seed first, she bears a male" (Niddah 31a). And here he says, "that desire that rises from below to above takes souls by its desire, and they are females." Behold, he said explicitly that when the desire is from below to above, then they are females; and afterward he said, "and when the desire of that river descends and cleaves from above to below, they make male souls" — the reverse of what he said in Parashat Tazria, that when the arousal is from above to below, then it is female and judgment. And it seems [right] to resolve that this third is not a question, because the matter mentioned here is another matter, and what is mentioned in Parashat Tazria is a matter by itself. And to the first two, it seems [right] to say that what is mentioned in this passage is a matter by itself, and what is mentioned in the other passages, from the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, is a matter by itself. And to explain this matter we shall put forth a premise: for it is known that the palaces are vessels revealing the actions of the sefirot, and the sefirot pour forth into the palaces, as we shall expand the explanation in the Gate of the Palaces.

And behold, this first palace is over against the ninth sefirah; and it was the tenth before the diminution, and therefore its palace is this first one, [counting] from below to above; and it is called "the sapphire pavement." And it is known that Yesod includes the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, as we shall explain further on; it is alluded to in the name יאהדונה"י; and therefore in the palace of Yesod is the revealing of the coming-to-be of the souls. And the two spirits that are in this palace — those of which he said, one to the right and one to the left — are a dwelling and a throne for Tiferet and for Malkhut; for the male's inclination is always to the right, in the secret of compassion, and the female's inclination is always to the left, in the secret of judgment. And it is known that the principal [source of the] souls is in Binah, which is called in this passage "the river that flows," and her dwelling among the palaces is the seventh palace. And behold, it is known that the manifestation of the drawing of the soul from Binah to Tiferet and Malkhut is in concealment and in subtlety, in the way of the seed poured from the brain of the male to the male, and from the brain of the female to the female.

And behold, it is known that the secret of the male is in direct light, from above to below, by way of the drawing of the sefirot; and the secret of the female is in returning light, from below to above. And therefore, when the effluence of the soul is poured to Tiferet, it is poured upon him in the secret of his direct light, which is from above to below; and when the effluence of the soul is poured to Malkhut, it is poured upon her in the secret of her light, which is from below to above. And therefore he said concerning the male, "when the desire of that river descends from above to below, they make male souls": meaning, when this effluence is in the secret of direct light, and it is the light that descends from above to below, then the souls are males. Meaning, it is the effluence fit for the male, to bring into being from it the soul of a male; and then the right light, which is the dwelling and seat of Tiferet, who is the male, receives it. However, when the effluence is in the secret of returning light, which is the light that rises from below to above, then the souls are females; meaning, effluence fit to bring into being from it the soul of the female; and then the left light, which is the dwelling and throne for Malkhut, who is the female, receives it.

And the matter of the descent of this effluence from the river has no form at all, but is a power poured forth from the brain by way of the spinal cord. However, the manifestation of the soul in its coming-to-be in the form of a soul is in the two powers, which are the right and the left light, which are the dwelling of Tiferet and Malkhut; and by their means the male and the female are united, as he explained in the passage. And by this it turns out that this passage does not disagree with any one of the passages mentioned. And from it there emerges for us, for the matter of coupling, that the beginning of the effluence fit for the soul is poured from Binah to Tiferet — fit for the male — and to Malkhut — fit for the female; and this is the matter of the souls being from Binah. Afterward Tiferet and Malkhut are united, and by means of their union the souls are united as twins, male and female, until they come to human beings, and from there each and every one is separated by itself. And what he wrote in Parashat Tazria, concerning the matter of "the woman emits seed first," is not for the matter of the souls, but for the arousal that precedes the coupling, as I explained in chapter 20. And what one must now investigate in this matter is this: from all these passages in general it appears that souls come to be from the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, as is proven above; and this is a thing not possible, for Rashbi, peace be upon him, said explicitly that all the souls were created [already] from the creation of the world, at the least. And these are his words in the Zohar, Parashat Lech Lecha (fol. 90b): "Come and see, for Rabbi Shimon said: It is written, 'This is the book of the generations of Adam' (Genesis 5:1). And did he have a book? Rather, they have established that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed the first Adam each generation and its expounders, etc. How did He show him? If you say that he saw with the holy spirit that they were destined to come into the world, like one who sees with wisdom what will come into the world — it is not so; rather, he saw all of them with the eye; and that likeness in which they are destined to stand in this world — he saw all of them with the eye. What is the reason? Because from the day the world was created, all the vital souls that are destined to stand in human beings, all of them stand before the Holy One, blessed be He, in that very likeness in which they are destined to stand in the world. In this manner, all those righteous ones, after they go out from this world, all of them go out and rise, and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares for them another likeness to be clothed in, like what they were in this world. Therefore all of them stand before Him, and the first Adam saw them with the eye. And if you say that after he saw them they did not stand in their existence — come and see: all the words of the Holy One, blessed be He, are in existence, and they stand before Him until they descend to the world. In this manner it is written, 'with him who is here [standing with us this day],' etc. (Deuteronomy 29:14); they have established that all human beings who are destined to be in the world were all found there. Here there is something to look into, for it is written, 'and with him who is not here,' etc., and it implies all those who will come out from those who stood there; for it is written, 'with us this day,' and it is not written, 'standing with us this day.' Rather, certainly here all of them stood there and were not visible to the eye; therefore it is written 'with us this day,' although they are not visible. And if you say, what is the reason they were not visible here, as they were visible to the first Adam, who saw them eye to eye — and here it should have been more visible? Rather, here, when the Torah was given to Israel, they were seeing another vision and supernal grades, and gazing eye to eye, and they craved to gaze and to see the glory of their Master; and therefore they saw the supernal glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, and not another. And therefore all human beings who are destined to stand in the world, etc. This is what is written: 'Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and in Your book they are all written' (Psalms 139:16). 'Your eyes saw my unformed substance' — what is the reason? Because another, supernal likeness was like this one. And therefore it is written, 'And who is a rock [tzur] except our God?' (Psalms 18:32): who is a good fashioner [tzayyar], who includes all, one in the other, like the Holy One, blessed be He." Thus far its words.

And behold, from it it is explained explicitly that the souls were emanated, pictured with a revealed picture; so much so that Rashbi, peace be upon him, took care that we not say that the souls that the first Adam saw were those still destined to be emanated, and that he saw by the power of prophetic vision; but rather that he saw them emanated, pictured with a revealed picture, for he saw them with his eyes, as is proven from his wording. And likewise, in the matter of "him who is not here with us this day," it was difficult for him why it did not say "standing," and why they did not see them; and he needed to resolve that they did not set their heart to the matter, because they were seeing more supernal matters, which are the thrones of the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. And since it is so, it is fitting to know what is the matter of the soul that is emanated at the time of coupling.

And further, it is impossible to say that there was coupling before the first Adam, from what has been explained in the previous chapters, that there was no complete coupling until after the first Adam was created. And we do not find that Seth and his mate came out back to back, nor Abel and his mate, nor Cain and his mate. And if it is true that they were emanated in a coupling that was before the first Adam, then all of them ought to have been back to back. But indeed this matter is found only in Adam and his mate, whether in his body or in his soul. And one cannot say that so were the souls at the time of their emanation, before the sawing of the first Adam; for if so, a Tanna would not have omitted to explain this in one place. Therefore it seemed [right] to explain that at the time of the emanation of the soul of the first Adam all the souls in the world were emanated — that is to say, all the generations that stand until the resurrection — and those souls that come to be from the coupling are kept for the future to come; for then the Holy One, blessed be He, will renew His world with new souls. And this is forced.

And further, it would be possible to say that from this passage there is no necessity that [the souls] were emanated, but only the sheaths of the souls and their likeness, in which they are clothed after their emanation. And so is it precise in his saying, "and that likeness in which they are destined to stand," etc., which implies that it is not literally the soul, but a likeness in which the soul is clothed.

And further, so is it precise in his saying, "and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares for them another likeness to be clothed in," that is, sheaths and garments for all the souls. And so is the wording of the verse precise, "Your eyes saw my unformed substance [galmi]," that is, the unformed substance of the garment in which the soul descends after its emanation. And this too is somewhat forced in our view: for if there are not yet souls, why garments? And did not the creation of the likeness suffice at the time of the emanation of their soul?

And it further appears [possible] to resolve, and we say: at the time that the Holy One, blessed be He, emanated the emanated soul of His handiwork, it included sixty myriads of souls; for there is no generation of fewer than sixty myriads, and so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim.

And behold, since his soul included those sixty myriads, as long as the people went on multiplying his soul was spreading out in them, and his soul never lacked anything; and this is the reason for the penalty of death for all who came after him, for all of them sinned in that deed. And he goes on joining with all the souls. And we have some glimmerings of proof: for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is Seth, as is expounded in the Tikkunim — and of him it is said, "and he begot in his likeness, after his image" (Genesis 5:3) — included sixty myriads, like his father; for he is the son drawn [from the brain of] the father; and therefore he brought out sixty myriads from Egypt. And of him it is said, "one woman bore sixty myriads in one womb." And to this they alluded, that Moses is equal to all Israel. And of this he said, "six hundred thousand on foot are the people in whose midst I am" (Numbers 11:21); for his people literally came out of him and were included in him, and therefore all of them sucked Torah from him. And to this he alluded, "Did I conceive all this people? Did I beget them?" (Numbers 11:12): for although they are included in him, nevertheless I am not the one pregnant with them — which alludes to the Shekhinah, who becomes pregnant with them; and also I am not the one who begets them — over against Tiferet, who is the father who begets. And of this he said, "But YHVH was angry [va-yit'abber] with me for your sakes" (Deuteronomy 3:26), for the Shekhinah became pregnant [me'ubberet] through me; meaning, all her fetuses were in me, and I was your afterbirth — certainly "for your sakes." And therefore it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 108 and fol. 110) that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, spreads out in each and every generation in sixty myriads, that is, the cycle of the transmigration of sixty myriads, of which it is said, "One generation goes and another generation comes" (Ecclesiastes 1:4) — and the explanation is: the generation that goes is the generation that comes. And therefore in each and every generation he spreads out in sixty myriads, and his Torah shines in them, and all of them suck from him, as this matter is explained in the Tikkunim on the verse "And she again bore," etc. (Genesis 4:2). And by this will be understood what is expounded in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Parashat Ki Tetze, fol. 280), that Moses our teacher is in this world in a despised body among Israel, as is explained there. And God forbid that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, the choicest of all creatures, should be transmigrated at all, all the more so in disgrace. Rather, the intent is the manifestation of the light of his Torah, which shines in the masters of Torah, and the sixty myriads who suck from him; and they are despised among the ignorant [amei ha-aretz]; and this is true, with no doubt about it, for that matter. And we return to our matter: that the soul of the first Adam included sixty myriads, which is the measure of one generation. And this is explained in the Midrash Rabbah (Ki Tissa, chapter 40), and these are its words: "While the first Adam was lying an unformed mass [golem], the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him each and every righteous person who was destined to arise from him. There is one who hangs from the head of the first Adam, and there is one who hangs from his hair, and there is one who hangs from his forehead, and some from his eyes, and some from his nose, and some from his mouth, and some from his ear, and some from his earlobes (and this is the place of the ring). And know, that at the hour when Job sought to dispute with the Holy One, blessed be He, he said, 'Oh that I knew where I might find Him,' etc., 'I would set my cause in order before Him' (Job 23:3–4). The Holy One, blessed be He, answers him: You seek to dispute with Me? 'Where [eifoh] were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?' (Job 38:4). What is eifoh? Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Job, tell Me, your ephah [measure] — in which place was it hanging? On his head, or on his forehead, or on which limb of his? If you know in which place your ephah was, you may dispute with Me. Thus: 'Where [eifoh] were you?'" Thus far its words.

And from it our intent is explained explicitly, without doubt. And he said, "while the first Adam was lying an unformed mass," because after the Holy One, blessed be He, set him up and established him in his full form and in his standing, the plantings included in him spread out in the Garden of Eden, until bodies would arise for them to be clothed in; but they were included in him before the completion of his creation, when he was an unformed mass, that is, a rolled-up lump of dough. And since we have mentioned this matter, we say that the wording of the passage was precise, that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed the first Adam "each generation and its expounders": behold, He showed him only according to the number of this generation, which is sixty myriads; but those added beyond sixty myriads were not yet created, for they are emanated by means of the coupling; and they are the new souls, from which too the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to renew His world, as we explained above. And by this will be understood what our sages, of blessed memory, expounded: that Adam saw David, who had no life, and gave him seventy years of his own life — although this matter is expounded in the Zohar in another way. This is what appears to us in setting this matter right, and the chapter is concluded. And we shall now explain a fine matter concerning union that is found in the book of the Zohar.

In the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and these are his words: "The foundation [yesoda] of the world is the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah." And many like these. This indicates that the union of Tiferet and Malkhut is by means of Yesod; and Yesod is the groomsman who binds and unites the bridegroom and the bride — and not only a groomsman, but literally it is the member [ammah] that unites the male with the female; and likewise all the titles of this attribute indicate it. And as the saying of our sages, of blessed memory, "body and covenant we count as one": meaning that Tiferet is over against the body of a person and Yesod over against the member. And there is no doubt that in Malkhut, for the matter of union, there are three aspects: the first, an aspect toward Yesod; the second, an aspect toward Tiferet; and the third, her aspect toward Gedulah and Gevurah and Netzach and Hod. And the reason is that just as in the union of a man and his wife there is an aspect in the female toward the member, and an aspect toward the spine, which is the whole of the body, and an aspect toward the arms and toward the thighs, so is the upper union, in which they are united six over against six. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim, and these are its words, in Tikkun 51 (fol. 86b): "'In the beginning Elohim created et [the heavens],' etc. (Genesis 1:1). What is et? Rather, the early ones have established that every et is for inclusion. And this is et [Alef-Tav]: the Torah, included from Alef to Tav, by which heaven and earth were created.

"And further, et ha-shamayim: shamayim [heaven] — this is the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, 'then hear in heaven' (1 Kings 8:32); et — His mate with Him. Ve-et — this is the Righteous One and his mate. Ha-aretz [the earth] — the vessel of all of them, to bring forth seeds and fruits." Thus far its words.

And behold, one must certainly ask: what is the mate of the Righteous One, and what is the mate of the Holy One, blessed be He, and what is the vessel of all of them? For all is one. Rather, certainly it is as we have explained: the Shekhinah is called et, and the verse comes to inform us of the matter of the union in all its aspects. And the first, he said, et ha-shamayim, that is, the aspect of the union of Tiferet with Malkhut, which is body with body. Second, he said ve-et, for the Vav is Yesod, which is called the small Vav; and this is "the Righteous One and his mate," which is the middle point, the manifestation of the essential union. "Ha-aretz, the vessel of all of them": that is, her aspect toward the arms, which are Gedulah and Gevurah, and toward the thighs, which are Netzach and Hod. And just as union is found for Tiferet and Malkhut, so union is found for all their aspects and the upper spiritual limbs; so that union and coupling is found even in the angels of the Shekhinah, who are united with the angels of the Holy One, blessed be He. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 113b), and these are its words: "And when she rises upon them, immediately the Holy One, blessed be He, descends to receive her with many hosts and camps. Camps rise with the Shekhinah, and the camps of the King descend upon them; and they are a lower chariot from upper ones, and these receive from those in joy, with a kiss. And the secret of the matter: 'and behold, the angels of Elohim ascending and descending on it' (Genesis 28:12) — behold, the angels of the Shekhinah, who is Elohim, ascend, and angels descend on it toward her." Thus far its words.

And the intent is clear: that when the Shekhinah rises, with all her camps, to unite with her husband, her husband goes out toward her; and as he comes to unite with her, so his angels descend to unite with the angels of the Shekhinah, since these are males and those are females. And it is possible that these angels are emanated spirits, these from the male and those from the female, like the 248 limbs in a man. And it is possible that these are the 248 powers to which Rashbi alluded in the Commandments, in the commandment of the Reading of the Shema (in Parashat Va'etchanan, fol. 263a), where he said that for the union 248 upper limbs are united, as is expounded there. And these two aspects expounded in this chapter are explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 37), and these are its words: "And when [they receive, all the sefirot] receive from one another, and the angels below receive one from another, as it is said, 'and they receive one from another'; and each one gives permission to enter into the domain of its fellow, as it is said, 'and they give permission to one another.'" Thus far its words.

And the intent is that when Tiferet and Malkhut are united — for it is about this that [the passage] stands there, but we have abbreviated his words — he said that then the sefirot receive from one another, and likewise the angels. He indicated the two aspects expounded in this chapter in the matter of union, which are the union of male sefirot with female, and the union of male angels with female. Further, it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 33) that Chokhmah and Binah have three unions — that is to say, union in three places — and likewise Tiferet and Malkhut; and they are these. First, they are Chokhmah and Binah: YHVH in Chokhmah, Ehyeh in Binah; and Ehyeh is a palace for the four-letter name, "the sheath of the sword," as is explained in the Tikkunim — that is, the four-letter name that is in Chokhmah; and Ehyeh is in Binah: this one to the right and that one to the left, in the way of the male and the female. For the male's inclination is always to the right, and the female's inclination always to the left, in the secret that every female inclines to judgment; and therefore this one is on the right and that one on the left, each one as is fitting for it. And the two of them are united in the secret of their union in Keter; and their union is alluded to in this name, יאההויה"ה; for it is a name composed of two names, indicating that Ehyeh is a palace and an abode for the name YHVH, and also indicating that YHVH is in His palace. And therefore, to indicate their union in the sefirah of Keter, both are united there in the aforementioned name. And likewise they separate to the right and to the left in Gedulah and Gevurah, thus: YHVH in Chesed, Ehyeh in Gevurah; and they are united in the middle, which is Tiferet, thus: יאההויה"ה. And likewise they separate to the right and to the left in Netzach and Hod, thus: YHVH in Netzach, Ehyeh in Hod; and they are united in the middle, which is Yesod, thus: יאה"הויה"ה. And both of them are in Malkhut, which is called Kiryat Arba [the City of Four], because in it four names are included: the name YHVH, Ehyeh, YHVH, Adonai. For these four names are the four letters in the four-letter name: the first name is over against the Yod, which is in Chokhmah; the name Ehyeh over against the Heh, which is in Binah; the second four-letter name is Tiferet, which is over against the Vav; and the name Adonai is over against the last Heh, which is in Malkhut. And the initials of these four names are  Y A Y A  [יאיא], etc., a holy name; and it is the initials of "YHVH Eloheinu YHVH Echad" (Deuteronomy 6:4), which are the four letters in the name, as we explained.

And behold, the union of YHVH in Chokhmah and Ehyeh in Binah is in the secret of [going] from above to below, because both of them pour forth, and the secret of the one who pours forth is in the secret of direct light, from above to below. And YHVH [and] Adonai, in the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, are poured into, and their union is from below to above. And therefore in Netzach and Hod they separate, YHVH [and] Adonai, this one to the right and that one to the left, in the way of male and female, for the male is always to the right and the female always to the left; and both of them are united in Yesod, and both of them are יאהדונה"י, a name indicating that the name Adonai is made a throne and an abode and a dwelling for the name YHVH, and the name YHVH dwells in the palace, which is Adonai; as it is written, "But YHVH is in His holy palace; let all the earth be silent [has] before Him" (Habakkuk 2:20) — has [הס] is the number of Adonai and the number of heikhal [palace]. And likewise both of them separate to the right and to the left in Gedulah and Gevurah: YHVH in Gedulah, Adonai in Gevurah, this one to the left and that one to the right — the female to the left, in the secret of her inclination toward judgment, and the male to the right, in the secret of his inclination toward compassion — and both of them are united in Tiferet, which is the middle, thus: יאהדונה"י. And likewise the branches separate in Chokhmah and Binah and are united in Keter. This is a transcription of the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, from the Tikkunim, with a few additions, small and not great, in explaining some of his words. And what has been expounded up to here suffices us in explaining the matter of union. And what remains concerning their union on weekdays by means of Metatron, and on the Sabbath by means of Yesod, we shall not speak of here, since we shall explain it in the Gate of ABYA, for there it belongs. And we return to explain the matter of the essence of the attributes, in judgment and in compassion, and in their action.

Since we have explained in the previous chapters the matter of Gedulah and Gevurah and Tiferet, we shall now explain the matter of Netzach and Hod and Yesod. And with these attributes there is no need to lengthen on their matter, whether judgment or compassion, for they are branches that branch out from Chesed and Gevurah and Tiferet; and as are the actions of those, so are the actions of these, except that their judgment is not so strong, nor the Chesed so strong, because they suck from Tiferet. And the matter is that Netzach is the branch of Chesed, and therefore its action is kindness, and likewise in the matter of water, as is explained concerning Chesed; but because it sucks from the side of Tiferet, in which is the power of Gevurah — as is known, for it is "the man in between" — therefore its actions do not prevail on the side of Chesed like Chesed itself. And besides this, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 14) that in Netzach the power of life is sealed, from the side of Chokhmah; and these are his words: "He looked above, toward Chokhmah, and was bound to the right thigh, and sealed life in it." Thus far his words.

He taught that although life is in Chokhmah, as in the matter of "wisdom gives life to those who have it" (Ecclesiastes 7:12), nevertheless the storehouse in which life is placed, to give life to the people of the world, is Netzach — although its opening depends on the first three, as they said, "Children, life and sustenance [do not depend on merit], but the thing depends on mazal"; and we explained it in chapter 17. And like Netzach, so is Hod, whose actions are like Gevurah, for it is a branch drawn from it; and therefore its actions are in judgment and fire, as is explained concerning Gevurah. But because it sucks from Tiferet, in which is the power of Chesed — as is known, for it is "the man in between" — therefore its actions do not prevail on the side of judgment like Gevurah itself. And besides this, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that sustenance depends on it; and these are his words there: "He looked above, toward Imma Ila'ah, and was bound to the left thigh, and sealed sustenance in it." Thus far his words.

And the matter of sustenance in Hod is in the way of life in Netzach, as is explained above. And what one must be precise about in the matter of these two attributes is that we have found them different in their matter more than the other sefirot. For the other sefirot each have a name by itself, as we shall explain in the Gate of Names; but these two sefirot have one name only, which is Tzeva'ot, as will be explained there. And likewise in most of their titles they are always joined. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained: "Netzach and Hod are two halves of the body" — which indicates that the two of them are one matter, something not found even for Tiferet and Malkhut, although they are double-faced and the two of them are one. And so he explained concerning heaven and earth, in the action of the attributes, regarding "King Solomon made himself a palanquin" (Song of Songs 3:9), in Parashat Terumah, and we copied it in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation, chapter 4; and he said that the fourth day, which is Netzach, did not bring forth its actions in completeness until Hod came, because the two of them are one matter; let it be examined there. And now one must be precise about this matter in every way possible. And indeed, as to what we asked — why a name by itself was not set apart for each one of them, but one name for the two of them, which is Tzeva'ot — we have found that Rashbi, at the time of his passing, in Parashat Ha'azinu (fol. 296a), explained this matter, and these are his words: "Further, the body spreads out into two legs, and between them are held two kidneys and two testicles of the male; for all the oil and the fatness and the strength of the male, of the whole body, are gathered in them; for all the hosts that go out, go out from them; and all rest at the mouth of the member. And therefore they are called Tzeva'ot [Hosts], and they are Netzach and Hod. Tiferet is YHVH; Netzach and Hod are Tzeva'ot; and therefore, YHVH Tzeva'ot. The member of the male is the end of the whole body, and it is called Yesod," etc. Thus far his words, as relevant to our matter. And he is speaking of the matter of the expansion of the Emanation as far as Netzach and Hod; and he said that they have three aspects, like the form of the body, and they are the legs and kidneys and testicles of the male, because they are limbs needed for the manifestation of coupling. And the reason is that the anatomists have said that the passage of the seed is by way of two channels, one to the right and one to the left; and their descent is by way of the thighs, and from there they descend to the kidneys and pass through there, and from there they are drawn to the testicles, and from there to the mouth of the member. And therefore he said, "for all the oil and the fatness and the strength of the male," etc., that is, the seed of the male; and therefore he said, "for all the hosts that go out," etc., "and all rest at the mouth of the member": that is, the seed drawn from the thighs and from the kidneys and from the testicles to Yesod, to the aspect that is united in it, which is what is called the mouth of the member.

And behold, it turns out that the thighs, which are Netzach and Hod, have three aspects. The first is called "thighs"; and that is their aspect that draws near to their aspect called "loins," which is their aspect toward Tiferet and toward the arms, which are Gedulah and Gevurah; and this aspect is called "thighs."
And a further aspect, nearer to Yesod, and it is called "kidneys."

And a further aspect, nearer still, and it is called "testicles." And all of them are needed for the union of a man and his wife, as is explained above. And therefore, for the upper union, these three aspects flow into Yesod, in its aspect that is united in Malkhut and concealed within her, which is what is called "the head of the Righteous One" (Proverbs 10:6), that is, from the diadem upward, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And he said, "and therefore they are called Tzeva'ot," to allude to two things: one, on account of the hosts that go out from there, as we explained above. And this is a reason for the name Tzeva'ot, an expression of hosts: because their drawing and their pouring forth is to Yesod, and this is the principal host that is titled in them; therefore they are called Tzeva'ot, by one name equal for the two of them, which indicates multitude — which is not so in the other holy names. And to indicate their union with the body, which is Tiferet, he said, "Tiferet is YHVH; Netzach and Hod are Tzeva'ot" — contrary to the view of those who say that Netzach is called YHVH Tzeva'ot and Hod Elohim Tzeva'ot. And only Netzach and Hod together are included in the name Tzeva'ot, as we shall expand the explanation in the Gate of Names.

And behold, from this passage the reason has been explained why the two of them have one name, as we explained. And for the rest we say: since we know the explanation of this name for the union, and its relation, and the matter of the aspect of these attributes toward the coupling, if so, it is fitting that both of them be called by equal names, since it has already preceded for us that sowing is only by means of these two limbs. And although there is a difference between the anatomists and the sages of Israel in Tractate Yevamot, in the chapter Ha-Arel (Yevamot, fol. 75; see there in the Tosafot), for [the sages] hold that it is already possible to beget with one testicle, nevertheless the anatomists have already conceded that with one he will beget only males or only females, according to [which] limb is lacking. And since it has already preceded for us in the previous chapters that male and female are drawn from the upper coupling, if so, the manifestation of coupling is impossible except by means of both of them together; and therefore they are certainly "two halves of the body." Besides that, it is impossible for the body to stand in its standing except by means of the two thighs that hold it up — which is not so with the other pairs among all the limbs of a person. And this explanation of this matter suffices us.

And as to the matter of Yesod: it is known that its attribute and its actions are like the action of Tiferet; and our sages, of blessed memory, gave a sign for this in saying, "all that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph"; and it is a branch of Tiferet, drawn from it. And therefore its actions are in compassion, in the secret of air, as we explained concerning Tiferet. But because Yesod sucks from Netzach and Hod, and the power of Gevurah from Hod prevails over it, therefore its inclination is more toward the side of judgment, as we explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 2. And although we say that its actions are like Tiferet, it further has actions equal to all the sefirot, because in it all the powers and the effluence of the sefirot are mixed, as is known. And besides these there are many actions of these attributes that it is impossible to explain except in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, by means of the explanation of the titles.

And among the attributes of Malkhut are all the matters related to the female in the matters of the world, and likewise the things related to the element of earth, as we explained above. And it is explained in the words of Rashbi that her inclination is toward judgment, and she is the attribute of judgment — but not hard like Gevurah, but soft; and her attribute is to reward and to punish, by the power of the upper attributes that are above her. And in her all the powers are held, whether good or evil, like the matter of the king, who needs the evil and the good to complete what he delights in. And with this the matter of the seven attributes and their essence in judgment and compassion is concluded.

The intent in this chapter is to explain two aspects in which the Emanation is regarded. The first aspect is divided into three aspects: the first they called the intelligible world, and they are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah; the second is called the perceptible world, and they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; the third they called the natural world [olam mutba, "the imprinted world"], and they are Netzach, Hod, Yesod. And in each one of these three aspects there are three sefirot, besides Malkhut, who receives from all, as we explained. And the second is also divided into three other aspects. And they are: the first aspect, the aspect of the right, and it is the aspect of Chesed, and in it three sefirot are included, and they are Chokhmah, Chesed, Netzach; and the second, the aspect of the left, and it is the aspect of Din, and in it three sefirot are included, and they are Binah, Gevurah, Hod; and the third, the aspect of the middle, and it is the aspect of Rachamim, and in it three sefirot are included, and they are Da'at, Tiferet, Yesod. And Malkhut receives from all of them, and Keter includes all of them, as he explained.

And this matter is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 216b), for Rabbi Elazar said: "The Shekhinah does not dwell amid sadness, as it is written, 'But now bring me a musician [menagen]; and it came to pass, as the musician played [ke-nagen ha-menagen]' (2 Kings 3:15). Menagen, menagen — three times. Why? In order to arouse the spirit from the perfection of all, which is the complete spirit. Rabbi Abba said: Two. We have learned: from four sides all is found. Rabbi Abba said: And all the roots of the upper and the lower ones are all held in them. And it has been taught: this one enters and this one goes out; this one is enclosed and this one is spread out; they are joined, one with its fellow, and they are the fathers of all. Rabbi Shimon said: 'Only in your fathers did YHVH set His longing' (Deuteronomy 10:15) — it is written 'your fathers,' literally three; and it is implied, for it is written 'only' — literally 'only.' And from these all the other others separate and are joined, and the name rises to be crowned." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: in the matter of Elisha mentioned in the verse there are three [mentions of] playing. And Rabbi Elazar explained that they allude to Tiferet, as it includes the three Patriarchs; and this is his saying, "to arouse the spirit from the perfection of all." And he intended what Elisha needed: the spirit of prophecy, which he did not have; he needed an arousal from Tiferet, which is called "spirit"; and as it is complete with Gedulah and Gevurah, it is a complete spirit, including all the aspects, which are Chesed, Din and Rachamim; so that the spirit of prophecy would come upon Elisha from the right and from the left and from the middle, in the secret of the drawing of the effluence to Netzach and Hod, which are the place of prophecy, and to Yesod, which unites them. And this is the matter of the three playings, which are over against the three Patriarchs, included in Tiferet, which is called "spirit," and poured to Malkhut, which is called "prophecy." And this is the secret of "the spirit of prophecy": Tiferet and Malkhut united by means of Netzach and Hod — Tiferet to the right and Malkhut to the left — and both of them united by means of Yesod, in the secret of יאהדונה"י, as we shall explain in the Gate of Names, chapter 2, and as we explained above in chapter 23. And Rabbi Abba disagreed with Rabbi Elazar, because he holds that in the verse there are only two playings; for "But now bring me a musician" is not of the count, for it is a mere narration of things, and the principal is "and it came to pass, as the musician played," which are two playings. And this is what Rabbi Abba said, "two": meaning, two playings only. And he also disagreed with him in that the totality of the Emanation is not in three but in four, and they are included in two; and they are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet and Malkhut; for Tiferet is united with Malkhut, and Chesed with Gevurah.

And behold, when they are included in two, which are the two playings, then prophecy would dwell upon Elisha. And this is his saying, "we have learned: from four sides all is found": meaning, that all the existents are composed of these four spiritual elements. And he further added the saying of Rabbi Abba after it, to indicate that Rabbi Abba's view is that in these four the whole Emanation is included; and this is what it says, "and all the roots of the upper and the lower ones are all held in them," meaning, in these four all is included. "And it has been taught," etc.: he added, to explain how they are four and are included in two. For "this one enters and this one goes out": meaning, Chesed's work is to bring in and to draw near, and the left's to scatter and to distance, as they said, "the left pushes away and the right draws near"; and therefore one must unite them and blend them toward the mean. "This one is enclosed and this one is spread out": meaning, Tiferet is concealed and Malkhut is revealed; and therefore one must unite them, so as to reveal the concealed through the revealed; and this is "they are joined, one with its fellow" — meaning, so that, being four, they are included in two powers, toward the mean. "And they are the fathers of all": meaning, these four are the fathers and the root of the Emanation; the intent is that in these four aspects all is included. And Rabbi Shimon disagreed with Rabbi Abba and said that all is included in Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, which are Chesed, Din and Rachamim; for Malkhut receives from them and is of their totality — not that she is a fourth aspect by herself. And this is what it says, "your fathers, literally": three fathers, which are Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, that is, Gedulah and Gevurah and Tiferet, which are Chesed and Din and Rachamim — three specifically, and not four, as Rabbi Abba explained. "And it is implied, for it is written 'only'": meaning, the verse intended to negate the view of Rabbi Abba in saying "only" — that is to say, these, and no others with them, for in these three alone all is included.
