After we refuted in the previous chapter that it is fitting to say that Binah tips the balance between Keter and Chokhmah, we say that it might already occur to the mind that the arbiter between Chokhmah and Binah is Keter, which is in truth intermediate between the two of them. And one may find support for this opinion in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the book of the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 119), and these are his words: "All the names among the havayot that begin with Yod — their root is Chokhmah; and all the names that begin with Alef — their root is the supernal Imma. And just as the central pillar is included of right and left, so the supernal Keter includes these two names of Abba and Imma, and it is a crown upon their heads." Thus far his words.

He said explicitly that just as Tiferet is included of the two extremes, so as to tip the balance between them, so is Keter. And we say that it is impossible for Keter to tip the balance between Chokhmah and Binah, because the way of those in dispute is that they hold the extremes, and the arbiter is a thing intermediate between the two of them. And such is the way of Chesed and Pachad: for this one is Din, fire, and that one is Chesed, water — two opposites — and the air, Tiferet, is intermediate between the two of them. But Keter between Chokhmah and Binah is not so; for Keter is simple compassion, more than Chokhmah and Binah, and how will the holder of the one extreme be the intermediate arbiter between the intermediate one and the holder of the second extreme? And according to this, it would seem more correct to the mind that Chokhmah tips the balance between Keter and Binah, being intermediate between the two of them: for Keter is complete compassion, and Binah has some judgment in her, and Chokhmah is intermediate between the two of them — not complete compassion like Keter, and not inclining to judgment like Binah. And one can find support for this view in the words of Rashbi in the Ra'aya Mehemna (in Parashat Tetze, fol. 281b), and these are his words, in brief: "And he is  K B  of  K V K B  [kokhav, star];  K V  [26]: 'For YHVH Elohim is a sun and a shield' (Psalms 84:12), YHVH Tzeva'ot; the Shekhinah, the holy Kingdom:  B K  [bekha], 'by you shall Israel bless' (Genesis 48:20); the twenty-two [K B] letters of the Torah.  K B  is included of three grades: Kaf, Keter; Bet, Binah; YHVH, which includes both of them, Chokhmah. And all is included in kokhav, the grade of the central pillar. And the Shekhinah is the moon," etc. Thus far his words.

Behold, he taught explicitly that Chokhmah is included of Keter and Binah and tips the balance between them, as we explained. And to this we say that it is impossible for Chokhmah to tip the balance between Keter and Binah, for the reason that it is the way of the arbiter to be intermediate between the right and the left; not so Chokhmah, which according to the truth is on the right, as we proved in the Gate of Their Standing; and according to the view of some it is on the left; and in either case it is not in the middle. And a Tanna would not have omitted to tell us, in a single mishnah, that it is in the middle.

And further, and stronger than all of these: for Chokhmah is the root of Chesed, and Binah the root of Din, and Keter the root of Rachamim, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 25 and 26. And if so, how is it possible to say that Chokhmah, the root of Chesed, tips the balance, when it itself is the pan of merit? And how is it possible to say that Binah, the root of Din, tips the balance, when it itself is the pan of liability? And the principal arbiter is the tongue that tips the balance between the pan of merit and the pan of liability, and merit and guilt need the arbiter. And from the matter of the previous passages there is no proof at all; and they are explained by what we set forth in the previous Gates concerning the matter of three aspects in each and every sefirah. And nevertheless we shall not withhold our hands from explaining them; and they are these: first, with respect to what it receives; second, with respect to what it pours forth; third, with respect to the aspect of itself. And the intent is that these three aspects necessarily exist in each and every attribute. The example of this: Gedulah includes three aspects. The one aspect is from the aspect of Chokhmah, which is a subtle aspect, in which Chesed is somewhat equal to Chokhmah, so that because of this it receives from Chokhmah; and if it were not subtle, near to the subtlety of Chokhmah, it would not be possible for it to receive from it. And afterward the effluence becomes thick and is revealed into the manifestation of Chesed, the aspect of itself. And when it pours forth to Netzach, it must be revealed further, so as to be equal to Netzach, so that Netzach can receive from it — until Netzach rises to the first aspect to receive from it. And in the way of the three aspects mentioned are the aspects of Keter, Chokhmah, Binah in each one of them. How so? Keter includes Chokhmah and Binah: from the side that it pours forth into both of them, it includes Chokhmah from the side of Chokhmah and Binah from the side of Binah. And likewise Chokhmah includes Keter and Binah: it includes Keter because it receives from it, and includes Binah because it pours forth into her. And likewise Binah includes Keter and Chokhmah, because she receives from both of them: from Chokhmah from the side of Chokhmah, and from Keter from the side of Keter. And these three aspects are alluded to in three words, and they are  A Sh R,  R A Sh,  Sh A R  [asher, rosh, she'ar]. And there is no doubt that the three letters in these three words mean: Alef, Keter; Resh, Chokhmah, which is reshit [beginning]; Shin, Binah, the root [shoresh] of the tree — as we shall expand the explanation of this matter in the Gate of Permutation, chapter 3. And with this no doubt remains in the previous passages, or their like if they are found; for the intent is the aspects in each one of these attributes, as we explained. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, was precise in saying, "and just as the central pillar is included of right and left," etc.: he indicated judgment and compassion, right and left. But of Keter he said "includes two names," for the intent is not arbitration, judgment and compassion, right and left, but that it includes the aspect of Chokhmah and the aspect of Binah, as Tiferet includes the aspect of the extremes. And since we have already removed all the views it is possible to entertain concerning the arbitrations, we say that it is already possible that there is no arbitration between them at all. For of the whole matter of arbitration and its reason, in the previous chapters and especially in the first chapter, he said that it is because the reward is intermediate and the punishment intermediate, etc., as we explained there. And if so, since Keter and Chokhmah and Binah are compassion, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, our saying that there is an arbiter between them would not be correct at all, for they do not need arbitration, for they are "men of peace." And it is already possible to say that this is what those intended who say that the first three are reckoned as one: for just as an arbiter does not apply in one sefirah, from part of it to part of it, so it does not apply in the first three. But this opinion is not correct, as will be explained from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And the matter is this: since Chokhmah is the root of Chesed, as is known, and Binah the root of Din — although it is not literal judgment, nevertheless "from her judgments are aroused."
And behold, for that arousal arbitration is needed to subdue it, since it is the source; for if they do not extinguish the fire in its source, its extinguishing outside its source will not avail.

And it turns out according to this that judgment needs three arbitrations. First, in its source, which is the place of the upper roots, that is, the first three. Second, it needs arbitration in the place of Din and Chesed themselves, which is in Gedulah and Gevurah themselves. Third, it needs arbitration in the place of the branches, which are the messengers that perform the actions, which are Netzach and Hod, as we went at length in explaining this matter in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 24 and 25. And the reason is that in these three grades are the sources and the actions. And in the sources is the principal thing, for all depends on it; and therefore this arbitration must come first, in the sources, which are the upper roots, so that judgment not prevail from the source and the arbiter tip toward the pan of judgment, God forbid. Further, it is needed in the place of judgment and justice, that is, in Gedulah and Gevurah, where the action of Din and Chesed is; and afterward in the agents of Din and Chesed, which are Netzach and Hod, so that judgment not be roused again there. And since this is so, we say that the arbiter, whether above or below or in the middle, is always the line of Rachamim, which is the arbiter between the pan of merit, which is the line of Chesed, and the pan of liability, which is the line of Din. And there is no escaping its being the arbiter, for it is intermediate between the two lines, as is known and explained above.

And behold, the head of the line of Rachamim is Da'at; meaning, it is the manifestation of the subtlety of Tiferet, which mediates between Chokhmah and Binah, and by its means is their union, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 8, and likewise in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 25. And besides them, Rashbi explains the matter of this arbitration, besides what he explained concerning their union by its means, as we explained in the Gate mentioned, in the chapter mentioned. And these are his words in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 3), much abbreviated: "And by its name the central pillar is called Israel: shir El [the song of El]. Shir — of the Levites, from the left; El — from the right, of the priests. The central pillar, Israel, includes both of them. Chokhmah descends with the blessing of the priest, on the right, and by it 'one who wishes to become wise should turn south'; Imma descends with the holiness of the Levites, from the left, and by it 'one who wishes to become rich should turn north.' The central pillar is the bond of the two of them, the union of the two of them." Thus far his words.

And behold, he intended to say that Tiferet's being called Israel is with respect to its being in the secret of Da'at, which is called "Israel rose in thought," that is, Chokhmah. And he says that what is intended by the name Israel is shir El; and shir is from the side of Binah, for such is the service of the Levite toward Binah. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Vayetze, fol. 154), and proved the matter from the verse "and the Levite, he [hu] shall serve" (Numbers 18:23); for Binah is called Hu [He], and the service of the Levite, which is song, was toward this attribute. "El from the right, of the priests": as is known, the name El is in Chesed. "Israel includes both of them," etc.: meaning, the word Israel includes shir El, which are Binah and Chokhmah, as he concludes. And this is what he said, "Chokhmah descends with the blessing," etc.; for there is no manifestation of judgment and compassion in Chokhmah and Binah with respect to their own aspect, but only with respect to their being the roots of Chesed and Gevurah. And this is what he said, "Chokhmah descends with the blessing," etc., and likewise "Binah descends with the holiness," etc. And therefore the central pillar, which is the middle line, the line of Rachamim, is the union of the two extremes, as we explained — that is, the roots with respect to their aspect below. And such is the view of Rabbi Moshe de León in this matter; and these are his words in Sefer ha-Shem, in the sefirah of Tiferet, under the word Da'at: "Da'at: on account of the effluence that comes to it from the enclosed brain and descends by way of the spinal cord to the covenant of the member, as far as the house of Malkhut, to appoint her for itself. And on account of [its being] the third view, and it tips the balance; for the middle line is between every two views. The beginning of its arbitration is Gedulah and Gevurah. When it rises, at the time of favor, as far as Keter, to receive simple compassion, it tips the balance between Chokhmah and Binah, and rises above the rank of its fathers, as it is said, 'The blessings of your father prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors,' etc. (Genesis 49:26). And when it descends and knows the Diadem, it tips the balance between Netzach and Hod. And therefore you will find it, in the diagram that the masters of the Kabbalah draw in order to understand a likeness in the Emanation, sometimes above Gedulah and Gevurah, and sometimes intermediate between the two of them, and sometimes beneath them. And understand and know that 'if there is no understanding [binah], there is no knowledge [da'at].'" Thus far his words.

And most of his words agree with our intent in the inquiry, apart from other points, which relate to matters other than the inquiry: some of them explained in another matter above, and some to be explained with the help of Heaven. And he taught that Tiferet, in its aspect that is called Da'at, tips the balance between Chokhmah and Binah. And the matter of the arbiters has been given a complete explanation, and this Gate is concluded, with the help of Heaven.
The Tenth Gate: The Gate of Colors.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain the matter of the colors mentioned by the commentators, and in the Zohar in the words of Rashbi. And likewise we shall explain the color of each and every sefirah, and the reason for it; and this in great brevity.
Chapter One:

Many times the inquirer will find in the books of the kabbalists and in the Zohar known colors attributed to each and every sefirah. The inquirer must take care, and let it not rise in his heart and his thought that the things are according to their plain sense, God forbid. For color is a corporeal thing, one of the attributes and accidents of body; and what is not body is not fit to be described by the accidents of body, God forbid. And one who thinks that those colors are in the sefirot according to the plain sense of the passages destroys the world and the boundary that the early ones set, and is found to be a corporealist, God forbid. Therefore the inquirer must take care in this matter. And what is intended by the colors is a parable for the actions drawn from the upper roots. The example of this: Gevurah, which conquers in war, is fit to have red attributed to it, since its way is to spill red blood; and also red indicates cruelty, fury and overflowing anger; and this matter is clear. Therefore to the place of strong judgment they attributed redness.

And further, there is no doubt that the red things are drawn from the power of that root, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And likewise white indicates compassion and peace; and it is the way of the white-haired to be compassionate, like the old and the grey-haired, whose way is not to wage war; and therefore, when we wish to attribute peace and Chesed and compassion, we attribute it with whiteness. And there is no doubt that the white things are drawn from the power of that root, as we explained in the Gate mentioned. And this is what is intended by colors for the sefirot: a parable for the actions drawn according to their nature and their matter. And we have no place and definition by which to liken and define the matter of their division except by the parable and definition of colors, which are divided and rise and multiply according to the prevailing of one color over another. Therefore we liken the matter of the upper actions to the parable of colors — and all to put it gently to the bodily ear, in what it can hear. And there is no doubt that colors have an entry into the actions of the sefirot and the drawing of their effluence. And for this reason, when the one who draws down needs to draw down an effluence of compassion from Chesed, he pictures before him the name of the sefirah in the color of the matter he needs, according to the color of the attribute: if complete Chesed, complete whiteness; and if not so much, he pictures a whiteness like the plaster of the Sanctuary, and the like, as we shall explain in the Gate of Intention. And likewise, when he wishes to perform an action and needs the drawing down of judgment, then that person clothes himself in red garments and pictures the form of the name YHVH in redness; and so for all the actions and drawings down; and when he needs Chesed and compassion he wraps himself in white. And we have clear proofs of this from the priests, whose drawing down is from the side of Chesed, and their garments are white garments, to indicate peace. And this is the matter of the High Priest on the Day of Atonement, who would remove the golden [garments] and put on white, because the service of the day was in white garments; and they gave a reason for the matter, "an accuser does not become a defender" — they taught explicitly what is expounded here. And in this way, certainly, regarding amulets: when a person makes an amulet for Chesed, he pictures that name in a shining whiteness, for then the action of that name grows. And likewise for judgment, to picture the name of judgment in redness — and all the more so if he pictures it in the blood of a goat, for then the color and its cause all indicate judgment. And these things are known and explained among the writers of amulets, and we have no part in their toil. And we have already seen one who pictured names in amulets — those indicating judgment in red, those indicating Chesed in white, and those indicating compassion in green — all according to true maggidim who instructed him in the making of the amulet: all to show that the matter of colors has an entry into the actions drawn from above. (And close to this matter did the worshippers of the stars and constellations do: for their worship was with an incense known to them, to draw down to them power from that constellation, and they would clothe themselves in garments related to their action, according to their folly.) And the faithful witness to this is the stones of the breastplate: twelve stones related according to the drawing down of the twelve tribes of Israel from a high place. And this matter should not be thought far-fetched. For the naturalists have said that if a person looks with his eyes at the running of many waters, the white [humor] is aroused in him; so that for the sick, who have no rest and whose sleep is not sweet to them, they make streams of water run before them, so that the white humor be aroused and increase the moisture, and he sleep. And so is the matter here: when the inquirer roams with his intellect he will find ten handles to this matter. For from the colors seen by the eyes, or pictured in the intellect in a bodily way, the spiritual is affected; and the vital soul arouses the spirit, and the spirit the soul, and the soul [rises] from manifestation to manifestation, until it rises to the place of its sucking and is aroused according to the manifestation of its picture — because they are "as water, face answers to face" (Proverbs 27:19). For by its means the source sees the face in redness, and redness is poured forth to it; and likewise if whiteness, whiteness — as is explained in the Gate of Channels, chapter 1 — for the arousal and the lower face are by means of human beings, and as is explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 18.

And behold, according to the arousal and its measure will be the pouring forth. And when the inquirer sees this he will rejoice and exult, after passing over in his mind all the expositions mentioned; for the hand of the tongue is too short to go on at length. And this is the reason for the whitening of the strip of crimson on the Day of Atonement: for when judgment is annulled in the upper root, the lower branches are annulled; and just as the source, on which redness principally depends, would change from judgment to compassion, so the lower branch would change from redness to whiteness. And this is the reason that the early pious ones, in days of drought, would pour out water before them at the time of their prayer: so that their heart would be directed to that matter and their soul be affected and draw down according to its arousal, as we explained. And there is no doubt that this is the reason for the wrapping in black of the mourners of Zion: so that they be affected by the absence of light and the prevailing blackness, as in "I clothe the heavens with blackness" (Isaiah 50:3), "Do not look upon me, that I am swarthy" (Song of Songs 1:6). And likewise the matter of wrapping, as in "for why should I be as one who is veiled" (Song of Songs 1:7). And there are many, many matters that indicate this and testify to the matter and its truth; and brevity is good, for many reasons. And since we have already explained the matter of the colors, their essence, and what is intended by them in the sefirot, it is fitting to explain the color of each sefirah according to what the kabbalists, and Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the book of the Zohar, agreed.

On the colors of the sefirot, each one by itself. First, Keter. There are those who explained that there is no color in Keter at all, because no action is grasped in it, because of the greatness of its concealment; and they called it in general "concealed light," to indicate the concealment of its action. And there are those who explained that the color white applies to it: white light, the utmost whiteness. And the commentators have a proof from the verse that said, "and the Ancient of Days sat; His garment was white as snow," etc. (Daniel 7:9). Behold, the Ancient of Days is in Keter, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in places beyond number; and nevertheless the verse titled it with whiteness, it being the utmost whiteness, according to the measure of its compassion. And it would already be possible to deflect this proof and say: "His garment," it says, and not literally Him; "His hair," it says, and not Him. But according to the truth, whiteness is attributed to it. And these two views do not disagree at all, and all is one matter. For in Keter, while the effluence is above, in the root, no color is judged in it, but it is concealment; and the effluence is fit for whiteness, so as to be revealed and become white.

And this matter is likened, in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Idra, to dew, which is drops in which no color is judged, as is known; but after its descent it becomes thick by means of the cold, and its color is revealed — the color of "the terrible ice" (Ezekiel 1:22), in the strength of whiteness. And so is the matter in the actions of Keter: according to the truth, not even the action of compassion is judged in it, because of the greatness of its concealment; but from the side of the aspect of its revealing and its spreading in the sefirot its color is revealed: whiteness at the utmost of whiteness, the intent being the utmost of Chesed and compassion. And "His garment" and "His hair," said in the verse, are all a parable for concealed worlds, as is proven in the Idra. And therefore it is called "the laying bare of the white" (Genesis 30:37), whose explanation is the revealing of the white: for after its revealing it is whiteness; and this is from the side of its aspect toward the sefirot and its spreading, as we explained. And there are those who explained in Keter the color black, to indicate the light that is concealed in the utmost hidden darkness. And this view does not disagree with the two previous views. For Keter is called darkness from the side of the aspect of its concealment, high above, until it is darkened for it, and even the sefirot do not apprehend it; and this is the aspect of its union with its Emanator. And this is not apprehended by any other, since it is an aspect in which the Emanator is equal to the emanated — although there are very many advantages and excellences to the Emanator over the emanated, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 1. The principle that emerges is that in Keter there are three aspects. The first aspect is its aspect with the Emanator; and this is called darkness, for the reason that we said. The second aspect is the aspect of itself, revealed and not revealed; the name "dew" applies to it, which is a revealed manifestation but has no color at all. The third aspect is the aspect of whiteness at its utmost, which is the dew that becomes thick like the terrible ice and like the appearance of crystal; and it is its aspect toward the sefirot. And besides this, there are in Keter three kinds of darkness, all of which they attributed to it in the Tikkunim, in various places, and in the Zohar. The first darkness is literally to attribute absence of light. And the intent is that over against the upper light, which is the first existent that brings all the existents into being, it is darkness. And this is what Rashbi said in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 130): "The supernal Keter, although it is clear light, etc., is black before the Cause of Causes." Thus far his words; and we explained it in Gate 3, chapter 2.

Behold, he titled it with an expression of blackness, so as to attribute whiteness and light to the One who gives light to every luminary. Second: the upper aspect in it, mentioned above, is called darkness; and it is called darkness and blackness for the opposite reason to the one mentioned: to show the greatness of its concealment and its subtle light, which the upper ones do not apprehend. Third: the last aspect in it is called darkness and blackness, the aspect of the females in it, which is "the black female to its white"; and as for this blackness, it is impossible to understand its matter except in the Gate "From Below to Above," chapter 5. And with this what is found concerning the colors of this attribute in the words of the kabbalists is concluded.

Second, Chokhmah. There are those who explained that its color is red; and the reason is that it rose in their mind that Chokhmah was judgment. And we have already refuted the words of the holders of this view in Gate 8, chapter 5. And other commentators attributed to it a sapphire color, which is the color that receives all colors; and there are those who added that it is the color blue [tekhelet], which is the utmost [takhlit] of all colors. And according to the truth, as to the blue that they attributed, it is possible to say that blue is the first opening of blackness toward color; and perhaps for this reason they attributed to it the color blue, since Chokhmah is the opening of Keter and its sparkling. But what they said, that it receives every color and that it is the utmost of all colors, applies only to the Righteous One or to Malkhut, as we shall explain, for so Rashbi explained. But the color attributed to it is a color from which all colors are poured forth, so that that color is their source; for so it appears from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And perhaps this was the intent of the commentators in the color blue and sapphire: that it is the opening of all colors, from no color to color, and from it they are divided into colors according to its revealing and its brightness and its composition; and likewise Chokhmah is the source of all the actions, by means of its pouring forth into Binah. And nevertheless there is another blue, which is a title for judgment, as we shall explain; and this is not of its kind, God forbid. And what he said, that it is the utmost of all colors: the intent is that from it all of them are drawn and to it they return, like a wheel, whose place of beginning is its end. And there is one who explained that there are seven colors in Chokhmah; and these are his words: "The attribute of Chokhmah is called yesh [there is]; and therefore they said, 'Is [ha-yesh] YHVH among us?' (Exodus 17:7); and this is what he said, 'there is [yesh] a reward for your work' (Jeremiah 31:16). And, as it were, this attribute is called 'nut,' and it is called ayin [eye], for in it there are seven colors, corresponding to the colors of the eye. And these are the colors that are in the attribute of Chokhmah. The first, which surrounds the eye, which goes around the attribute of Chokhmah, is the color red; and therefore in a person, in the eye, there is a red color that surrounds the eye; and from here goes out a spring, of which the verse said, 'My lover is white and ruddy' (Song of Songs 5:10), and it is written, 'Who is this that comes from Edom, with crimsoned garments,' etc. (Isaiah 63:1). And the second color is white; and the proof that white is adjacent to red, for it is written, 'though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be white as snow' (Isaiah 1:18) — they are compared to one another; and therefore in the eye of a person there is white. And the third color is like green, seen and not seen; and from here is the drawing of the intermediate, and from here the middle line is drawn. And the fourth color is like leek [karti]; and over against it, among human beings, are those who transgress [sins of] karet [cutting off]. And the fifth color is like the blue of the tzitzit; and it is what gives light to the four colors that I mentioned, and it is literally the pupil of a person's eye. And the sixth color is like water, between green and leek, and stands between these attributes; and from here is the drawing of the son who is a Torah scholar to the masters of commandments. And the seventh color is the Holy of Holies, which gives light to all of them; and it is the color drawn from Keter Elyon; and therefore our sages, of blessed memory, said, 'all the sevenths are holy.' And from here is the sucking of all the wisdoms. And Keter Elyon is what goes around this attribute, and its color is white; and over against it the High Priest would wear white garments on the Day of Atonement." Thus far his words.

And although his words are words of tradition and holy of holies, in the matter of the eye, in his attributing it to Chokhmah, they are not correct, for several reasons. For there is no eye in Chokhmah; but either the open eye, which is above, in Keter — and there it is the white eye, without color — or the eyes with these colors, which are in Gevurah, as is proven from the Idra. Unless we say that the matter of these colors is by means of the thirty-two paths that are drawn below, so that their action changes to judgment and to compassion; [then] perhaps it would be correct.

The third, Binah. There are those who explained that she is redness inclining to whiteness; and this view we have already refuted above, in the previous Gates. But all of them agreed that she is the color of green light, and they said that she is "the green line that surrounds the world." And such is the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him, as we shall explain in chapter 5. And this green is green like leek and like grasses. And the commentators explained the reason for this color: just as green precedes all the fruits in the world, for their beginning is green, as is known, so this attribute precedes all the work of Creation, as in "And God said" (Genesis 1:3), whose allusion is in Binah. And this does not suffice, for it is not fitting that the corporeal be a reason and proof for the spiritual. And it is possible to say in this that when green like the yolk of an egg or like saffron is mixed into blue, green like grass comes to be from it. And therefore, since Binah is judgment and not literally judgment, she is not red, for she is not literally judgment in essence; but she would be green like saffron, which is red and white mixed. And therefore, when it is mixed with the blue, which is the light of Chokhmah, there comes to be from it the color green, literally like grasses, as the matter of this composition is known to the dyer. Further, it is possible, close to this: that from Binah are drawn the white, which is Chesed, and the red, which is Gevurah, and that composed of both of them, which is the green like saffron, which is the central pillar; and the manifestation of Binah is the gathering of these three that go out from her. And if so, when these colors are gathered in her, green like the yolk comes to be from them; and when the blue, which is the effluence of Chokhmah and its light, is mixed with this green, her color will be green like leek. Therefore the color green like grasses is attributed to Binah, because it is the gathering of Chokhmah and Gedulah and Gevurah and Tiferet, as is known.

After we occupied ourselves in the previous chapter with the colors of the first three, and wrote about them as far as was possible for us, we come in this chapter to explain the colors of six sefirot — apart from Malkhut, for which a chapter of its own will be set apart, to speak of her.

The fourth, Gedulah. There are those who explained it as simply white. And others said that it is blue made white. And the reason is that Chokhmah is blue, and Chesed is blue made white, that is, the revealing of Chesed, which is concealed in Chokhmah. And they explained thus, and not literally white, to distinguish between the whiteness in it and the whiteness of Keter Elyon; for the whiteness of Keter Elyon is the utmost whiteness, as we explained, but as to Chesed it is not so, but whiteness inclining to blue; and this is their saying "blue made white." And when we look closely at this color we find that it is literally the color of silver, which is attributed to this attribute according to the words of Rashbi. For silver is not literally white unless the craftsmen whiten it, but by its nature it inclines somewhat to blue; and this is "blue made white." And sometimes literal whiteness is attributed to it, in the color of milk and the like; and perhaps the reason is the prevailing over it of the upper Chesed, which is Keter Elyon.

The fifth, Gevurah. All of them agreed with one mouth that its color is red light, in redness, to indicate the strength of judgment; and so Rashbi explained in the Zohar in many places. And in some places he titles this attribute black, and in some the color blue; and so our sages, of blessed memory, said, "whoever sees blue in a dream," etc. — meaning tekhelet, which consumes [mekhaleh]. And the intent in attributing these three colors to this attribute is that there are three aspects in it. The first aspect is the judgment that draws near to Tiferet, which receives the power of arbitration; and it is near to whiteness and compassion. And this is the aspect of the red that is golden and gladdening, which is the good judgment that arouses love and joy. The second aspect is the aspect of the strong judgment that saddens and kills; and it is black, which blackens the faces of creatures, the fire of Gehinnom. And therefore they said, "black is red, only it was stricken" — that is, the fire of Gehinnom, which held on in the secret of holiness, in the secret of redness, and did not want arbitration; therefore it was stricken, and separation was said of it, and it descended to the fire of Gehinnom, that is, the husk. And likewise it was said of Korach's congregation, "Separate yourselves," etc. (Numbers 16:21), as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 1. And therefore separation is said on the second day, between the light and the darkness, which is the side of the left that holds on to Gevurah. The third aspect is the aspect of the judgment that acts; and it is poured forth by way of holiness, and it is just judgment, and it is titled with blue; and it is poured forth to Malkhut, for there is the principal blue, as we shall explain; and it is the attribute of soft judgment. And in it is "a cloth all of blue" (Numbers 4:6), to consume the effluence and to bring sin to an end. A fourth color further is the color of gold, which they titled to Gevurah because it is red, and so in some passages of the Zohar; and there are those who titled it to Binah, and so in some passages of the Zohar. And the compromise in this matter is that gold is the arousal of Binah with Gevurah and the union of both of them, in the secret of the judgment that gladdens. And so they explained in the Zohar, close to this matter, in Parashat Terumah (fol. 148), and these are its words: "Gold: it has been said that there are seven kinds of gold. And if you say that gold is judgment and silver is compassion, and gold has risen above it — not so; for certainly gold has a rising above all. But gold is in an enclosed way; and this is the supernal gold, which is the seventh of all those kinds of gold; and this is the gold that shines and sparkles to the eyes; and this is the one that, when it goes out to the world, whoever reaches it conceals it within himself; and from there all the kinds of gold go out and are drawn. When is it called gold — what is called gold? When it is in light and has risen in the glory of awe, and it is in supernal joy, to gladden the lower ones. And when it is in judgment — when it changes from that color to the color blue, black and red — then it is in strong judgment. But gold is in joy, and it stands in the rising of the awe of joy, and in the arousal of joy. And silver is below, the secret of the right arm; for the upper head is gold, as it is written, 'its head of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver' (Daniel 2:32), below. And when silver is completed, then it is included in gold," etc. Thus far its words.

And he said that gold is above silver, which is in Binah, and that the completion of silver is only in its union with gold, which is concealed. And although he said that it is above the aspect of red [sumak], and red is judgment and does not gladden — he was not precise about the color red, but it is a habitual turn of phrase; for so Rashbi himself explained, that red and gold are all one matter, the intent being that red is an aspect near to the aspect of gold. And these are his words (there, fol. 149b): "Red and black. And blue: red is its own, from the second day itself, like the color of fire; and this is Elohim, and it inherits the color of gold, for all is one color. Blue goes out from within that red color; and when it descends below, the red color is distanced, and it enters within that place that is the sea, and is dyed the color blue. That red enters within the sea, and its color is weakened, and it turns blue. And this is Elohim, but it is not strong like the first. Black: this color goes out from the dross of the red, when it is melted and weakened below, in the dross of filth," etc. Thus far its words.

And behold, from it is explained the matter of red and gold, that they are near to one another, though one rises somewhat above its fellow; for gold is the aspect of Gevurah with Binah, in the secret of the wine that gladdens. And therefore gold is more precious than silver, for silver is below, in Chesed alone.

And the matter of black and blue and red we explained above. And concerning the seven kinds of gold, I have seen one who spoke of them at great length; and these are his words: "Seven kinds of gold there are: three kinds of gold above, in the secret of the awesome faces, and four below, in the secret of 'the holy stones lifted up' (Zechariah 9:16). The three are as we said, and these are they. Closed gold (1 Kings 6:20) is the gold hidden and closed on all its sides, which 'no eye has seen, O God, besides You' (Isaiah 64:3). Beaten gold [shachut] (1 Kings 10:16) is in the secret of the north, at the time when an evil wind comes from the north; for the cause changes and the point changes. When it is in judgment upon the world, the gold is called beaten gold; and when it is sweetened in the points of the right, it is called gold of Tarshish — this is what comes from trei shesh [two sixes]: two points, each one of which includes six extremities. But when it is in judgment it is called beaten gold, as we said. Greenish gold (Psalms 68:14) is Malkhut, in the secret of the attribute of judgment below: 'Esther was greenish.' And the Messiah sucks from these two causes, from beaten gold and from greenish gold; and therefore he slaughters [shochet] and turns every face to pallor, according to the causes from which he sucks. And four are below. Gold of Ophir: it is a place of judgment that comes after judgment, and it sucks from the secret of the gold of Sheba; it is a place of judgment, hidden in the secret of the female, and the secret is 'and Sheba fell upon them and took them' (Job 1:15), according to the secret that Rav Yosef translated in this verse. Pure gold: all of it good, because of the secret that we said; and it is above, in the secret of 'beaten silver brought from Tarshish' (Jeremiah 10:9), and in its secret is gold of Tarshish; and it is a building from the sides of the good, and the choice part is below, as in the mixture of the good. And therefore King David, peace be upon him — all these seven kinds of colors of gold were seen in him, in his hair, in seven places: in the hair of the head, in the hair above his eyes, in his eyebrows, and in the beard, and in the throat, and in the chest, and under his arms; and we have already alluded to this in the commentary on Ecclesiastes. But they said that the hair in the throat, under the beard, is what is called gold of Sheba, according to the secret that we said, that the secret of the gold of Sheba is the secret of judgment hidden in the female, as in their saying, 'and Sheba fell and took them,' which Rav Yosef translated, 'and Lilith the guilty went out.' But the secret of her matter is hidden: for she is the croup, which was created on the fourth day in the work of Creation; and not for infants only, but she rouses many of the people of the world. And of this secret it is said of King Messiah, 'and he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba' (Psalms 72:15): He will place life in him first, before he enters into her, because she is the croup; and the Holy One, blessed be He, will give of that judgment that is found in her, that her works be in the great city of Rome, and by it its inhabitants will fall. And this is the secret of 'there Lilith shall repose, and find for herself a place of rest' (Isaiah 34:14), for from root to branch she will destroy. And therefore in King David, in the place of the throat, there the gold of Sheba is stored away, to show that in the place of the croup there is life." Thus far his words. And his words are certainly words of tradition, sweeter than honey; and therefore we went at length in them.

The sixth, Tiferet. There are those who explained in it a sapphire color, and it does not settle. But most of the commentators explained in it the color red and white. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, agreed that it is included of white and red; and the reason is that it is included of the right and of the left, white and red. And it is already possible to say that this inclusion is from the side of the arbitration, in which it includes both of them; and the sapphire color is from the side of its subtle, inner aspect, which is called "firmament," as we explained in Gate 1, chapter 2. And Rashbi in some places explained in it the color green. And the truth is that this green is the green like saffron and like the yolk of an egg, which is literally the inclusion of red and white; and so Rashbi explained, "green, included of white and red," and it is clear. And in many places Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that in Tiferet its color is argaman [purple],  A R G M N, whose explanation is: Uriel, Raphael, Gabriel, Michael, Nuriel. And these are four colors in the four letters of the name: Yod in Chesed, the line of Chesed, Michael, white; Heh in Gevurah, the line of Din, Gabriel, red; Vav in Tiferet, green — that is, Uriel from the side of Chesed, Nuriel from the side of Gevurah, and this is "included of white and red"; Raphael from the side of Malkhut, Heh, the mixture of all, as we shall explain. And the four colors, which are the totality of the six extremities, are called argaman; and the reason is that Tiferet is included of all the colors, and therefore it is called the beauty [tiferet] of all the colors.

The seventh, Netzach. They explained in it red inclining to white; meaning, that it inclines more to whiteness, which is compassion, than to redness, which is judgment. And the reason is that it sucks compassion from Chesed, and judgment and compassion blended from Tiferet; and because of the prevailing over it of Chesed, which is its root, its inclination must be more toward compassion.

The eighth, Hod: white light inclining to red; meaning, that it inclines more to redness, which is judgment, than to compassion, which is whiteness. And the reason is that it sucks judgment from Gevurah, and judgment and compassion blended from Tiferet; and because of the prevailing over it of the judgment of Gevurah, which is its root, its inclination must be more toward judgment.

The ninth, Yesod. There are those who explained in it a sapphire color; and it is possible to settle it in the way that we explained concerning Tiferet. And there are those who explained in it a light included of white and red — of the white that inclines to red and of the red that inclines to white — whose matter is its sitting between the two attributes Netzach and Hod; and its greenness must be redder than the green of Tiferet, since it inclines to judgment and Tiferet to compassion, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 4. And there are those who explained in it a color included of every color; and this settles, since it receives from all. And such is the explanation of Rashbi, peace be upon him; and the sign is "And Joseph was of beautiful form and beautiful appearance" (Genesis 39:6); and it is "a tree pleasant to the sight" (Genesis 2:9), for all beautiful colors are seen in it. And nevertheless the principal mixture of the colors is in Malkhut, as we shall explain.

The tenth is Malkhut. And they explained of her that she is included of every color; and it is correct, for she is the one who performs the actions by means of all of them. And in the Zohar, in some places, it attributes blackness to this attribute, for the absence of her light; and this will be in the days of her deficiency, when it is said, "Do not look upon me, that I am swarthy" (Song of Songs 1:6). And sometimes she is clothed in the color blue, to indicate the strength of judgment. And although there is already a revelation of this matter in what we wrote in the previous chapter on Gevurah and its aspects, nevertheless we have seen fit to copy here the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, from which benefit will be drawn for this inquiry. And these are his words in Parashat Terumah (fol. 139a): "'And blue' (Exodus 25:4): this is the blue of the tzitzit. This blue is the throne, the secret of the tefillin of the hand. This blue is the throne on which capital cases are judged; for there is a throne on which monetary cases are judged, and there is a throne on which capital cases are judged. And therefore all colors are good for a dream except the color blue, so that he know that his soul rises in judgment; and when his soul rises in judgment, the body is judged to be destroyed, and that dream needs much compassion. This blue is the throne of which it is written, 'as the appearance of sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne' (Ezekiel 1:26); and it is written, 'and a fire flashing, and a brightness round about it' (Ezekiel 1:4), because with it they make the windings of the tzitzit. And when 'a brightness to it' [comes], it turns to the color green, like the color of leek; from that hour on the time for the Reading of the Shema is permitted, for the color blue has changed from what it was. And therefore it is forbidden to judge capital cases at night, because that color blue rules at that time, and permission is given to snatch a soul without justice, for justice does not rule at that time. When morning comes and the right above is aroused, that light from above goes out and reaches as far as this blue, and it changes from what it was; and then another, holy throne rules over it and cleaves to it. From that hour on is the time for the Reading of the Shema." Thus far its words.

And the matter of this color, the color blue in Malkhut, is in her lower aspect, which draws near to the side of the outer ones. And so they explained in the Zohar (Shelach, fol. 163b), and these are its words: "For the holy moon is beautiful in whiteness, and all colors sparkle in her and are embroidered; and she is like that beauty and whiteness of the sun, literally. And in that sea of hers, within seventy years, one fish goes out, and the color blue is brought out from it; and she takes this color and arranges it, and is covered outside with this color. Not that this color is her garment, for 'fine linen and purple are her clothing' (Proverbs 31:22); but this color is the outer covering. In this manner was the Tabernacle: all of it embroidered in beauty within, and afterward 'they shall spread over it a cloth all of blue' (Numbers 4:6). What is the reason? Because beneath this sea there are 'the depths of the sea' (Micah 7:19), including male and female, and they have an evil eye to gaze; and when they gaze, the color blue meets their eye, and their eye cannot rule. And she is arranged within in all colors, embroidered, as is fitting." Thus far its words.

And when this passage is looked at well, it emerges for us that there are three aspects in Malkhut. The first aspect is the color proper to her in herself, which is a shining white color, that is, "like the beauty of the sun," which is her husband, from whom she was taken. And she has a second aspect, which is her garment, that is, "fine linen [shesh] and purple are her clothing." And he was precise in the word shesh [six]: that she is included of six colors, which she receives from the upper sefirot, which are the six extremities. And argaman too is when she receives four colors together, which are four sefirot: Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet and the manifestation of Malkhut. And therefore  A R G M N  is the initials of Uriel, Tiferet; Raphael, Malkhut; Gabriel, Gevurah; Michael, Chesed; Nuriel, also Tiferet — but all according to its aspect, sometimes receiving from the right, sometimes from the left, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Palaces, chapter 5. And her receiving from above, and her being clothed in all the colors together, is called "fine linen and purple are her clothing"; and then she is clothed in compassion. And she has a third aspect, and it is the lower garment, the aspect that draws near to the husks, which are called "the depths of the sea." And this color is blue, as the Zohar mentioned above explained. And this is what he said, "and blue — this is the blue of the tzitzit," which indicates the strength of judgment, as Rashbi explained in the Commandments, the commandment of tzitzit (in Parashat Shelach, fol. 175); see there. And he needed to say so because there is another kind of blue, which is the color of sapphire, whose color inclines to blue; and that blue is compassion, which alludes to Chokhmah, as we explained above. And the intent in it is not the expression of destruction [kilayon], God forbid, but the expression of utmost [takhlit], because Chokhmah is the utmost of all the work of Creation, being the end of being from below to above, and from it is the coming-to-be of being. Which is not so with the blue in Malkhut: for the blue in Malkhut is an expression of "destruction decreed" (Isaiah 10:22). And this is what he said, "this blue is the throne": meaning, it is the lower aspect of Malkhut, which is called "throne," in the secret of the tefillin of the hand, which is the gathering of all the camps, as is explained. And this blue means the end and destruction of a person, God forbid, in the strength of judgment. And this is what he said, "this blue is the throne on which they judge," etc. And the reason is that this throne is not like the other thrones: for on the other thrones they judge the matters of a person in his particulars, that is, monetary cases; but on this throne, which is the color blue, they judge capital cases, etc. "And when a brightness to it, it turns to the color green," etc.: the intent is that blue is the color anil in the vernacular, and its name is azul; and green is green like grasses; and this green is composed of the green like saffron or like the yolk, with the blue. And when the two of them are mixed together, the color blue is turned to the color green. And therefore, when the morning becomes light and the sun rises, the light of the sun — which is Tiferet, whose color is green like the yolk, as we explained above — is mixed with the color blue, which is Malkhut in the aspect of "the depths of the sea," as we explained above. And this color blue rules at night, in the secret of the husks that rule at night from her side; and at the beginning of the light of the sun to rise, then the blue turns to green like leek. And this is the matter of "from when one can distinguish between blue and leek-green": that is, when the day becomes light and the light of the sun prevails in Malkhut, until the color blue is somewhat sweetened and turns to green; and then it is the time for the Reading of the Shema, which is Abraham, Chesed. And with this the intent of the passage has been explained, from its beginning to its end; and the colors of Malkhut have been explained: the fine linen and the purple, and the blue, and the green, and the white, as is explained.

After we have included in the previous chapters all the colors of the sefirot and their matter, according to what is "inscribed in the writing of truth" (Daniel 10:21), our wish is to point out concerning this matter that the matter of the colors is a fitting parable for the actions and the matters drawn from the sefirot, as we explained in chapter 1. If so, it turns out that just as the actions of the sefirot are not revealed except by means of Malkhut, and no action is judged in any one of the sefirot except by her means, so the matters of the colors are all in Malkhut; for in the sefirot the colors are not judged. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 9), and these are his words: "B R A Sh Y T:  B T  R A Sh Y  [daughter of my heads]: 'These are the heads of their fathers' houses' (Exodus 6:14). Bat [daughter]: of her the masters of the Mishnah established, 'a daughter first is a good sign for sons.' And she is the Yod of  A D N Y, a precious pearl included of every color. For the letter Yod of YHVH does not hold any color at all; this is what is written, 'I YHVH have not changed' (Malachi 3:6): it does not change in any color at all, but shines from within the colors. For the name YHVH is like the soul in a person's body, or like a lamp in a palace. And the letter Yod of  A D N Y  is sapphire: it takes the color blue and black from the side of judgment, and white light shines in it from the side of compassion; and it is the letter Yod of  A D N Y. Ruby from the side of Gevurah, topaz from the side of the right, emerald from the side of the central pillar. She is Alef, Dalet, Nun, Yod, included of twelve colors. And all of them are tripled in the Patriarchs, tripled in priests, Levites and Israelites: 'they triple holiness to You.' Every stone whose color is white takes from Chesed, and its special property is for love; and the secret of the matter is, 'I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with kindness' (Jeremiah 31:3). A red stone takes from Pachad, and its special property is that its dread be cast upon the creatures of the world. A stone included of two colors, white and red, is the central pillar. Green, from the side of the supernal Imma, who is repentance: 'the green line that surrounds the whole world.'" Thus far his words.

Bat rashi: meaning, "daughter" is Malkhut, and specifically in her manifestation that is called the pupil [bat ayin, "daughter of the eye"]. And it is her manifestation alluded to in Yod, which is the manifestation that she has from Chokhmah, as we shall explain in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 3. And "my heads" are the Patriarchs, the three colors that surround the pupil. And they are also the three colors of the rainbow, which surround her and build a building for her around her; and they are the colors of Chesed and Rachamim and Din, as we shall explain. And these three colors are alluded to in the Heh in her, as we shall explain in the Gate mentioned. And he proved that the Patriarchs are called "my heads" from the verse, "These are the heads of their fathers' houses," etc., which are the three letters Heh-Vav-Heh and the three letters Alef-Dalet-Nun, as we shall explain. "Bat: of her the masters of the Mishnah established, 'a daughter first'": the intent is first among the letters, when she is above, in the name  Y H V H, which is Yod over Heh-Vav-Heh: it is "a daughter first, a good sign for sons," who are compassion, and the havayah is male. But when the daughter is last, which is Yod below Heh-Vav-Heh, thus:  H V H Y, then it is judgment, and the havayah is female, and it is judgment. And these things will be well explained in the Gate "From Below to Above," chapters 1–2, for there is the principal place of this exposition and its reason. "And she is the Yod of  A D N Y," etc.: the intent is that the three letters, which are Heh-Vav-Heh, are the three Patriarchs, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. For in Abraham is the Heh, in the secret of Avram-Avraham; and the second Heh is in Isaac, as is known, which is the inclination of judgment to the left, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 2 and 3; and the Vav is in Tiferet, the middle line. And so Rashbi explained in the Ra'aya Mehemna (in Parashat Tetze, fol. 279), and these are his words: "What was the King's daughter? Yod over Heh-Vav-Heh, which are included in the Patriarchs: the first Heh in Abraham, the second Heh in Isaac, Vav in Jacob." Thus far his words.

And he was precise in saying "Heh in Abraham," as we said; for since there is a Heh in him, therefore his name is called by it. It turns out that Heh-Vav-Heh are the three Patriarchs, in whom the colors are included, as he says, "and all of them are tripled in the Patriarchs," as he concludes. And likewise Alef-Dalet-Nun are three letters in Malkhut, corresponding to the three colors of the Patriarchs, in which are the colors, as he concludes. And now he will say that the colors are all included in the Yod of  A D N Y, which is the last aspect, which shows the actions below; and so all the colors are seen in her; and this is "a daughter last," which is the lower pupil. But the upper pupil, which is the Yod of Chokhmah, has no color, but it is the light by means of which the colors are revealed. And it is like a lantern made of many colors: while the light does not shine in it, the colors are concealed and not seen; but when the light shines in it, then the colors are seen.

And behold, the source of the light that shines in the colors is the Yod of Chokhmah. And the intent is that the sefirot have no action except by means of the effluence poured forth from the upper source, which is the Yod of Chokhmah. And when that effluence and vitality is poured forth within the sefirot, then all the sefirot perform their action; and Heh-Vav-Heh shine in Alef-Dalet-Nun, and make the colors shine in the Yod of  A D N Y; for the Yod of  A D N Y, in receiving the colors, is over against the Yod of YHVH in making them shine, as we explained. And with this most of the essence of the passage is explained. "And the letter Yod of  A D N Y," etc., "takes the color blue and black," etc.: we already explained above that blue is a title for the judgment poured forth to her from Gevurah. But "black" — the intent is not the blackness that is poured forth to her from Gevurah, for the blackness from Gevurah is in the outer one, as is explained above in chapter 3; rather, the intent in saying "black" is the absence of light. And of blue and black he said natil, an expression of taking; and of white light he said nahir, shining: to explain that her principal sucking is from the left; and therefore he said natil, that she receives it by her nature; but in the secret of Chesed he said nahir, for Chesed shines in her not by her nature. "And its special property," etc.: he proved the colors by the power of the special properties. "Green, from the side," etc.: meaning, green like grasses; and he proved that Binah is the color green, being called "the green line that surrounds the whole world"; and he proved it from her being called teshuvah [return], in the secret of the return of the colors to her, in the secret of the Jubilee; and then she surrounds all.
And behold, the explanation of the remaining details of the passage will be expanded in Sefer Or Yakar, part two.

And behold, in a general way it is explained that the principal colors are in Malkhut, in the secret of her receiving the actions from the upper attributes, for the principal governance is by her means, as we explained. And with this the matter of the colors in the sefirot has been explained. But as for the colors of the channels, some of the commentators explained that the color of each and every channel is according to the measure of the color of the attribute from which the channel is drawn: for example, the channels drawn from Keter are like Keter, and from Chokhmah like Chokhmah, and so for all the other sefirot. And according to our way, which we took concerning the channels in the Gate of Channels — where we said that the channel is mixed from the two attributes, like the channel that goes out from the eye, as is explained there at length — it follows that the colors of the channels are of a color composed of two colors, from the receiver and the giver. And likewise, according to the aspects of the union by which the two sefirot are united, so will be the matter of the channel. For example, if the union of Tiferet and Malkhut is by means of the aspect of Chesed, the color in the channel will be white — and not white like the whiteness in Chesed literally, because there is some admixture of redness in it; but it will be a white color mostly inclining to whiteness, or all of it nearly so. For Tiferet pours forth white near to the whiteness of Chesed, and Malkhut near to the redness of Gevurah, because her principal sucking is from Gevurah. And by this we may reason for the other sefirot in the matter of the channel, each one according to its matter. And with this this chapter is concluded, and this Gate is completed, with the help of God.
The Eleventh Gate: The Gate of Tzachtzachot.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain the matter of the Tzachtzachot, which are the sefirot concealed in the Root of all roots, according to what is received from the mouth of all the Kabbalists and of Rashbi, peace be upon him.
Chapter One:

The first among the commentators to reveal the matter of this inquiry is our teacher Hai Gaon, in a responsum. And although his wording is long, goes beyond our subject, and needs a broad explanation, nevertheless we shall not withhold our hands from copying it, since it is of great benefit.

And these are the words of the Geonim: A question was asked of the great luminary, the master of wisdom, our teacher Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, by Rav Paltoi and his companions: "Let our master teach us. For we find that our Sages, of blessed memory, [speak of] thirteen attributes that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, received; and for Abraham our father, in a book that our Sages, of blessed memory, attributed to his name, which is Sefer Yetzirah, [the author] counts ten sefirot. And we need to learn from his holy mouth: if the ten sefirot are ten attributes, then we find thirteen attributes, [but] thirteen sefirot we do not find. Or are there thirteen attributes alone, or ten sefirot alone? We are in need of your teaching, and we await your answer." The answer to this question needs [going] within, and within the within. And many times before us and before you this question has been asked, in the days of the first generations and in the days of our ancient elders; and the explanation is long, not for one day nor for two days, until one is held in the cords of the concealed wisdom, stored away in the chambers of the prophecies and in the tradition of the sages, the masters of inscriptions [ba'alei reshumot]. Nevertheless, in view of your wisdom and your standing, we do not see that your question should be left wholly empty; and the paths of this answer are deep, if it reaches your hands in brief. The thirteen attributes spoken of in the Torah are derivative branches issuing from ten degrees called sefirot, these corresponding to those, together with the three that are stored away, heads of heads. And if these are not available to you, they are traditions of the ancients, each from the mouth of the other, up to the mouth of the prophets, of blessed memory. And the derivatives are the very actions, called attributes; and the roots, which are the fathers, are called sefirot, not because they have a number, or are themselves reckoning and count, but by way of the secret of ten worlds that were made new from them, which have no reckoning and no way to apprehend them except for the One who created them alone; and He is Lord over all, who is not apprehended in any way or by any knowledge at all, blessed be He in His concealment. And Solomon alluded [to this] in the Song of Songs, saying (Song 6:8): "and maidens [ve-alamot] without number." And out of honor for your Torah, we have seen fit to hand over to you the names of the sefirot as we received them from our elders, of blessed memory; and we have no permission to reveal more, out of [regard for] the concealed glory, as is written in the book of Proverbs (Prov. 25:2): "It is the glory of God to hide a thing." The ten sefirot were divided in their formation. The first three: the first is wondrous light [or mufla], a light that is not apprehended; rather it is unified, and compared to pure thought. And compared to it are the luminaries of knowledge [mada'] and intellect [sekhel], for thought judges between the two of them. And the last seven are seven luminaries; and three of them are the scale-pan of merit and the scale-pan of liability, and the tongue of forgiveness tips the balance between them. And the fourth luminary is the one that renews the world of souls; they called it "the foundation of the world" [yesod olam], [and] the masters of inscriptions and the sages of the Talmud called it "the Righteous One of the world."

And there is further an outer light, called "consuming fire," and its arms are north and right; and it is the end of all the luminaries and the beginning of all the deeds. And now I shall allude for you to the three supernal luminaries above the ten sefirot. They have no beginning, for they are Name, Self, and Root [ש"ם ועצ"ם ושר"ש] of all roots; and thought cannot apprehend them, for the apprehension and knowledge of every created entity falls short of apprehending [them]. In the name of our holy elders we have received their names: inner primordial light, which spreads forth in the concealed root and sparkles from the power of its spreading, in the likeness of two great lights, refined light and clear light; all of it one light and one root, concealed without end [le-ein sof]. And the sages of the Talmud warned against expounding the wisdom and the thought concerning what is not apprehended by any created entity, and said: "What is too wondrous for you [ba-mufla mimkha], do not investigate"; "you have no business with hidden things." And as for what the masters of inscriptions said, that the sefirot are like luminaries: [this is] not in the likeness of the luminary of the sun, the moon, and the stars, but [they are] spiritual luminaries, subtle and pure, inward, a radiance that makes the souls radiant. And we searched on every side of investigation, among our teachers the Kabbalists, [who received] from the mouth of the ancient elders, to know whether the three supernal ones have names distinct in themselves, as do those below them. And we found them all agreeing in one agreed view: that they have no known name, because of the greatness of their concealment, other than the names attributed to them under the name "luminaries"; and likewise the root, which has no beginning, has no known name. And the four-letter name, and all the more so all the other titles, are all particular to a created glory. And indeed, the name Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh, which is the foundation of the degrees: the form of the first letter, in the likeness of a very fine point, was formed in its writing, a writing known to the masters of inscriptions, to indicate a wondrous secret: that there took shape and were formed a spiritual matter [golem] and form from the power of the three degrees, which are Name, Self, and Root. And from the concealed root there rose and spread an exalted and simple light of thought, and they spread in the very root and within it (another version: "and from the spreading in the very root they came, not," etc.), not outside it; and from them there took shape and were formed the power of knowledge and the power of intellect, and they are the beginning of a concealed spiritual formation. And this point received a strong and wondrous power of form, so that ten degrees were formed in it, subtle to the utmost subtlety; therefore their number rose to the number ten. And from the power of this point ten degrees took shape in the form of the letter Heh that is founded after it, and in the point of its writing, in the order that we have received from our teachers and our ancient elders; and all the powers were stored away within it, in the likeness of a spiritual treasury. And from the power of this second form there took shape and were formed the six extremities of the world of shaping [ha-gelimah]: a spiritual matter and form, simple and revealed, [issuing] from the first, which were stored away in the second letter; and they are the beginning of the revealing of the concealed worlds. And therefore the sages of the sefirot called this sefirah "the mirror of the hidden world." And the final Heh is the tikkun of the agents, and it brings all the stored-away powers out into complete action, and it is the completion of all the powers. Thus far the orders of the degrees; but it is not in our hands to write and explain this honored and awesome secret with an explanation broad and long beyond measure. And may the Lord, Former of all, give us and you a heart to know, etc. Thus far the words of the responsum of Rav Hai Gaon, of blessed memory. And because of the great concealment of his words, on which most of the bodies of the wisdom depend, we have seen fit to explain it here in a chapter of its own, for the scroll is too short for some of his pleasant words.

We have already explained in Gate One, chapter 7, that the Gaon's intent in this responsum is not to say that they are thirteen sefirot, God forbid, as appears from the plain sense of his words; and we proved this there conclusively.

And the matter of the three concealed ones will be explained. And so he was precise in his wording, saying: "The thirteen attributes spoken of in the Torah are derivative branches issuing from ten degrees called sefirot, these corresponding to those, together with the three that are stored away, heads of heads," etc.

See: he did not want to bring "thirteen sefirot" into his mouth, God forbid; rather he said "from ten degrees called sefirot": that the ten are sefirot, and above the ten there is no sefirah at all; and with regard to the attributes, they rose to thirteen with the three mentioned, which are the concealed ones, as their matter will be explained. He further said: "And the derivatives are the very actions, called attributes; and the roots, which are the fathers, are called sefirot." He means to explain the matter of Self and vessels. For the attributes [middot] are the vessels that measure out [moddedot] to a man according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds, whether little or much, whether good or bad, for they are subject to change. And not so the Self, which is what he titles with the language of "roots" and "fathers," because they are roots spreading forth from the light of the simple Self; and they are His Self, and they have no actions of change intrinsically, as we explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels. And he called them "fathers" since they are fathers and causes to derivatives, which are the attributes, the vessels that measure out, as we explained. And the Self is called "sefirot" from the word sapphire [sappir], for it is a sapphire light; language wearies of telling its subtlety except by the parable of sapphire. "Not because they have a number, or are themselves reckoning and count, but by way of the secret of ten worlds that were made new from them." The meaning: as for the definition of the number ten meant in our language, the intent is not that the roots are divided into ten literally, God forbid, for the simple One is not divided into parts. Rather, number [applies] to them because the root spreads forth into ten worlds that were made new from the supernal roots, which are the Self, as we explained. And number can properly be said of them from the side of the aspect of ten worlds, just as judgment and compassion are said of them from the side of the aspect of the vessels, as we explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter 4. "Which have no reckoning and no way to apprehend them except for the One who created them alone": explanation: even the vessels, although they are what necessitate reckoning in the roots, we do not on that account necessitate that they are a number, God forbid, and that they are revealed worlds; rather they are concealed, and they have no reckoning, God forbid. For their reckoning is from the side of their being divided by way of cause and effect, as we explained in the preceding gates. "And He is Lord over all," etc.: explanation: He is Lord over the roots and the attributes, all of them together. "And Solomon alluded in the Song of Songs: and maidens [ve-alamot] without number": the meaning is the ten worlds [olamot] made new from the ten concealed roots, which necessitate the number ten in the roots; nevertheless they have no number, [for] the number ten in the sense of limit cannot properly be said of them, since they have no number and division, and their number is by way of cause and effect, as we explained. "And we have no permission," etc.: to excuse himself for the reason that he did not reveal the matter of Self and vessels except by hint and extreme brevity. "And the ten sefirot were divided in their formation": explanation: in their emanation. For "formation" [yetzirah] with regard to the sefirot is emanation, just as we have seen "In the beginning He created [bara]," and the meaning is "He emanated," and many like them. And the meaning: when we say that they are divided into ten, the meaning is not that they are divided from the side of the Emanator; for in their aspect relative to the Emanator they are equal, unified with the utmost union. And their division, and their descent one from another from cause to effect, is from their own side, from the side of their emanation: for the cause is above the effect, and the effect below the cause.

And behold, he intended to divide the sefirot, the first three by themselves and the last seven by themselves, because of the superiority of the three over the seven, as explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And he said that this division is from the side of their emanation: these are near to the Emanator, and these descend further from before Him. "The first is wondrous light, a light that is not apprehended; rather it is attributed and compared to pure thought." Explanation: the Supernal Keter is called "light," for we have nothing in the corporeal world as subtle as the subtlety of light, by which to represent spiritual things. And because of the subtlety and concealment of Keter beyond the other sefirot, they called it "wondrous" [mufla]; explanation: concealed, from the language "seeing it is wondrous [peli]" (Judg. 13:18). And this is what he further explained, saying "a light that is not apprehended." For although we say that it is wondrous light, our intent is not to say that we apprehend its wondrousness, so that we might say of it that it is wondrous light; rather, that it is a light not apprehended by any apprehension in the world at all. So that when we come to relate the sefirot to the limbs of the body, we relate it and compare it to thought, subtle to the utmost subtlety, which is not a limb among the limbs of the body nor a substance among its substances, but is an action that prevails over the body; and it is the subtlest and most spiritual action among all the actions of the body. And he called it "pure thought": that is to say, not when that thought is in a man about corporeal things, for that is certainly a coarse thought; rather the meaning is pure thought, that is, when he thinks about pure, subtle, and spiritual things, for then that thought is without doubt exalted above intellect and knowledge, for it is thought about things subtler than the human intellect. "And compared to it are the luminaries of knowledge and intellect": these are two spiritual powers in the body of man, and Chokhmah and Binah are likened to them. And thought is subtler and more spiritual than knowledge and intellect. For knowledge and intellect are two powers in the body that are more revealed; but thought is more spiritual, superior, without being discernible. For such is the law of Keter, which is subtler than Chokhmah and Binah. And he used the expression "and compared to it," etc., to hint that the three of them are reckoned as one: and just as knowledge and intellect are one with thought, which rides upon them, so it is with the sefirot, and Chokhmah and Binah are attached to Keter and included in it. And he says "luminaries," that is to say, the spirituality that spreads from Keter into Chokhmah and Binah. And they said that thought judges between the two of them: that is, insofar as the arbitration between Chokhmah and Binah is drawn from Keter, in the secret of Da'at, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 6. "Three of them are the pan of merit," etc.: that is, Gedulah is the pan of merit, Gevurah the pan of liability. "And the tongue," etc.: this is Tiferet, called "the tongue of forgiveness," because it is called "tongue" in its aspect with Binah, as we explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 2; and therefore it is then the tongue of forgiveness, for Binah is the Day of Atonement, as is known, and it is the tongue of forgiveness from her side. "And the fourth luminary is the one that renews," etc.: this is Yesod; and he put it before Netzach and Hod for the reason we gave in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 4.
