And Malkhut is called "the world of souls," for through her Yesod begets the souls, as is known. "And the sages of the Talmud," etc.: like what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Chagigah 12b): "On what does the world stand? On one pillar, and Righteous is its name, as it is said (Prov. 10:25): and the righteous is the foundation of the world." And by this they taught that the standing and subsistence of Malkhut is through Yesod and through its renewal; and this is what was expounded above.

"And there is further an outer light," etc. And he related [text: ve-yichad, read ve-yichas] Malkhut to Yesod, so that it would be in the order Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut. And nevertheless he explained "an outer light," etc., that is, the revealed one among them all. And the witness to this is (Exod. 24:17): "And the appearance of the glory of the Lord was like consuming fire on the top of the mountain, in the eyes of the children of Israel"; and therefore he titles her with the name "consuming fire." And the reason she is called so is to indicate judgment. "And its arms are north and right": explanation: the arms of Malkhut are Netzach and Hod. "And it is the end of the luminaries and the beginning of all the deeds": explanation: Malkhut is the end of the luminaries, which are the sefirot, and she is the beginning of all the deeds, as in the matter of (Ps. 104:24) "In wisdom You have made them all," for she is the architect through whom all the work of creation was made. [This is] to indicate that she is the end of all the Emanation. And he dwelt at length on this to indicate that although he put Malkhut before Netzach and Hod, it is not on that account necessitated that she be eighth in the Emanation; rather she is always tenth, and the reason for putting her first is as we explained. "And now I shall allude," etc., "they have no beginning." Explanation: the apprehension and knowledge of the sefirot is [given] to the prophets from effect to cause. The illustration of this: when the prophet apprehends the effect, he rises up to the cause; and from this cause he rises from there to its cause. The illustration of this: when he apprehends Malkhut, which is the effect of Yesod, he rises in his understanding and his apprehension and apprehends that the end of Malkhut, from below upward, is the beginning of her cause, which is Yesod. And likewise from Yesod he understands and knows that its end is the beginning of its cause, which is Hod. And in this way he rises in the seeing of his prophecy up to Keter. But in Keter itself, and from Keter upward, there is no apprehension for any prophet or seer. And this matter is likewise explained in Ezekiel: he said the word "appearance" up to ten [times], and at the tenth he said (Ezek. 1:28) "and I saw, and I fell on my face," for he no longer retained the strength to apprehend, for it is impossible. And so Rashbi explained in the Book of the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 6, and these are its words): "And when he reached the likeness of Keter, which is the tenth grade, see what is written of it: 'and I saw, and I fell on my face,' for he could not bear it." Thus far its words.

And to this the Gaon intended in saying "they have no beginning": for even in Keter "you shall see the utmost part of it, but you shall not see all of it" (Num. 23:13); so how should one apprehend even the beginning of what is above Keter? "For they are Name, Self, and Root," etc. It was difficult for him: if so, if there are already three worlds above Keter, so that they are concealed for a known cause, in the end they are thirteen sefirot. If so, there is a difficulty with what the author of Sefer Yetzirah said, that they are "ten and not nine, [ten] and not eleven," and "a single Lord," etc.; for are they not thirteen according to his way? To this he said that they are not in the count of the sefirot, God forbid; rather they are Name, Self [ש"ם ועצמו"ת ושר"ש], and Root of all roots. And he said "Name, Self, and Root," which are three things and all one, and all is Ein Sof. For the Name is the Self, and the Self is the Root, and He and His Name are one, unified. And therefore He has no name at all. For just as the manifestation of His Self is not bounded, so His Name is not bounded, and He has no name at all; rather, He is necessarily existent, and the Name is known to His Self and not to another. And since the three concealed ones are in Him, therefore they are not sefirot, but the very Self of the Ein Sof. "And thought cannot apprehend," etc.: as we explained, that no thought grasps the Ein Sof, for the reason mentioned. "Primordial light, refined light, clear light": these three names, in the name of light, primordiality, and clearness, all indicate concealment: just as the clear and bright light, which the eye cannot master, so the three concealed ones admit no apprehension by the sight of the intellect, of the prophet, or of others. And the first is called "primordial" to indicate its primordiality over all in the Root. And as for the matter of clear [and] refined, we shall explain further on, with God's help, which of them comes first. And the Gaon explained that these three names are found for these luminaries; and the reason for their division into these three is because of their spreading within their Self, not because of their being revealed outward to another; rather their spreading and their revealing is within their Self. And this is what he said: "and it spreads forth in the concealed root," etc. And to indicate that although with our mouths we call them and title them in the likeness of three lights, in their Self they are one, he said "all of it one light, and one Self, and one root." And because thought and investigation concerning them are a cause of danger, he said "and the sages of the Talmud," etc. And he said that they have no known name, just as the Ein Sof has no known name, because of the greatness of its concealment, as we explained.
And the matter of the names and the titles, and even the four-letter name: all of it is a hint to the sefirot, as he goes on to explain.

And the matter of the four arrays mentioned in his wording, in the letters of the Name, will be clear to the inquirer when he remembers what we wrote in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 5; and this matter will be explained further in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, chapter 4.

We have seen fit in this chapter to explain the matter of these three concealed ones in a fine light, so that it may settle in the intellect of the one who understands. And the matter is that "His thoughts are not our thoughts, nor His ways our ways" (cf. Isa. 55:8). For when a man imagines in his intellect bringing some manifestation into being, whatever it may be, his thought does not act. And even if he imagines and depicts in his intellect the form of the manifestation that he wills to bring into being, nevertheless it is as though it had not been, until he acts and it goes out into actuality. And so actuality turns out to be more complete than potentiality: for potentiality lacks manifestation and has no manifestation or completeness at all, and actuality is the principal thing and the manifestation, and apart from it there is nothing. And not so are the actions and the beings of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. For when it arose in His will to bring into being and to emanate the pure and holy Emanation, then it was emanated and formed wholly in His Self, without change in Him, God forbid; rather [it was] a manifestation unified with Him, so that there is no difference at all between the Emanator and that manifestation; rather He and they are all one, one Self and one root. And even if we relate that Emanation to the three aspects, as we shall explain, which are primordial, clear, and refined light, the aspect of their division is not relative to their Self, but relative to the aspect of their branches, which spread forth and are emanated. And the matter in this: we have already explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation that the Emanation is included in Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah, because they are the root of Chesed, the root of Din, and the root of Rachamim. And likewise in the order of their emanation, Netzach was in Chesed and Chesed in Chokhmah, included in one another, and all is one; and likewise Hod in Gevurah and Gevurah in Binah, included in one another; and likewise Malkhut in Yesod and Yesod in Tiferet; and all in Keter. And therefore, when the will arose to emanate the Emanation, there were formed in the very root three points, which are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, and in them all the Emanation is included. And as for the reason for their being divided into three although they are unified with the utmost union: the manifestation of this division is impossible except in a borrowed sense. For just as the very root is one, so the three points are one, and likewise the point and the root are all one thing; but we relate them to three because they are root and source to three branches, which are Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah. And [these are] not Keter, Chokhmah, Binah literally, but Keter, Chokhmah, Binah as formed in Keter, from the side of the manifestation of the beginning of their spreading from the very root into Keter.

And so it turns out that Keter, Chokhmah, Binah draw effluence from their sources, unified in the Keter, Chokhmah, Binah that are in Keter; and the Keter, Chokhmah, Binah that are in Keter draw from the concealed source in the very root, which is primordial, clear, and refined light, unified with the utmost union. And when it comes to our mind how mighty is the union of Keter, Chokhmah, Binah as revealed in the sefirot (that is to say, the sefirot themselves, as we were compelled [to hold] concerning their union in particular: a union exalted above the union of the other sefirot, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance), and we exalt above their union an exaltation and intensification of union, all the more so [must we exalt] the union of the Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah that are in Keter, until we say that in Keter there is only one source, one Self, and one root. And if we relate it to three, it is because of the nourishment of the three sefirot from there, which are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. And when afterwards we go further still and exalt, above the union of the three roots that are in Keter, the union of the three concealed [points], then their union, with great intensification, will not be far from us; and they are related to three lights only insofar as three roots, which are one, draw from them; and they are related to three because they pour out effluence and blessing to the three sefirot, unified with the utmost union. And from here the inquirer may go further in the union of the sefirot in the very root, that they are all unified with a mighty union: Netzach within Chesed and Chesed within Chokhmah, thus:

in the way we explained in the Gate of Their Standing, with God's help.
And likewise Hod within Gevurah and Gevurah within Binah, thus:

And likewise Malkhut within the Righteous One, and the Righteous One within Tiferet, and Tiferet within Keter, thus:

And all this while they are within Keter. And how much more are they unified while they are within the unified root, which is not divided into parts at all! And if we relate the number three to it, it is because they are sources to the three sources of three branches, as we explained. But relative to themselves, in their spreading, they are unified with the utmost union.

And behold, this manifestation, union, and source was revealed in its simple manifestation from the side of the aspect of His will toward the Emanation. And when we said "was revealed," the meaning is the manifestation of the being [havayah], which was not pouring forth [text: mashpa'at; read mushpa'at, "receiving effluence"] because of the concealment of the Emanation within His Self; and now, from the side of its spreading into the Emanation, it pours forth effluence into those sources. And this is [what we mean by] revealing: not that they are revealed to the emanated ones, all the more so not to the created ones, all the more so not to the formed ones, all the more so not to the made ones. For their manifestation is not revealed to any other than Him, as we explained. Rather, relative to the drawing forth of His providence into the Emanation, this matter is attributed to Him as spreading and revealing, not that it is revealed to any other than His Self, as we shall explain in the coming chapters. And the divine Rav Chamai Gaon revealed this matter further, and we shall copy it in a chapter of its own, as we found it copied by Rabbi David in the book Magen David (although he did not intend this inquiry at all), with the explanation of Rabbi Aharon upon his words; for he is a true teacher in this delightful inquiry, with the help of Heaven.

Rav Chamai Gaon wrote in the Book of Union [Sefer ha-Yichud] [concerning] the three first beings, which he placed above Keter, as we explained in the first chapter, in the responsum of our teacher Hai: "For these three names are all one matter and one Self, cleaving with a mighty cleaving, without separation and without joining, in the Root of all roots; like a corporeal parable: the heart, the lungs, and the spleen, one root for all of them and for the other limbs in the whole cavity. And from primordial light pure thought was drawn, like the drawing forth of the thoughts of the heart; and from the refined and the clear light, as from two springs, knowledge and intellect were drawn. And by means of intellect and knowledge all the spiritual flames took substance, this in this and this with this, like the matter of the flames that hold fast to the strength of the coals; and what would be (another version: "what was") gathered and hidden, this within this and this within this, until the time of the will of the Primordial Agent arrived, and the spiritual things went out from potentiality into action, and the Emanation of the upper world was emanated, down to the foundation of the tenth stone, called in the language of the sages of the secrets "thick light" [או"ר ע"ב]. And because of the great density they also called it "mixed darkness," for all the powers of the flames are mixed in it and change within it; and it is the foundation of all the worlds, spiritual and corporeal. And how many kinds of colors take substance in them and are formed in its power, some of them spiritual forms and some of them corporeal forms; for it is the last seal of all the seals." Thus far the words of the master, our teacher Chamai Gaon, in the Book of Union. And this is the explanation of our teacher Aharon, peace be upon him:

"Behold, the master's intent is to explain that these three names are one matter and one Self, cleaving with a mighty cleaving, without separation. And I think he said this not to distinguish them from the angels and the composite things, but to distinguish them somewhat from the ten sefirot, which are one. That is to say: the ten sefirot, although joining and separation are not to be pictured in them, [are so] with regard to the drawing forth of the effluence; but these three are all one Self and one matter in the Root of all roots, and they are His very Self; and understand. For he did not say 'from the Root of all roots' but 'in the Root of all roots,' to indicate the greatness of the union: that they are in His Self, blessed be He, and His Self is in them. And because the thing is hard to picture, that there should be three and all one matter, he brought a corporeal parable, and said that this is 'like a corporeal parable.' He said: the heart, the lungs, and the spleen are one root for all of them. And we see that they are separate limbs; and we are compelled to say that before they were formed in actuality in these forms, they were stored away and mixed in that unformed mass [golem] from which they would come to be at the beginning of their coming-to-be from the seminal drop, while the action of coming-to-be had not yet spread forth to distinguish each and every thing by itself. Rather, those powers of the limbs were stored away and mixed in that mass, not separate from one another, so that you would decree of the three of them, and of the other powers of the limbs stored away there, that they were then one matter and one Self, although we say that there were stored away there the power of the heart, the power of the lungs, and the power of the spleen. And so one may illustrate with some resemblance, although it is not a true parable. And we say: we know from tradition that the most spiritual, subtlest, and most concealed spreading of all the Emanation was the three upper, spiritual sefirot, which are Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah. And if so, it is necessary that these three sefirot, although they are unified in a wondrous oneness and a concealed subtlety, were far more wondrous and concealed when they were already formed in the Root of roots, which is the Ein Sof, in a oneness, subtlety, and concealment more wondrous than they are after their spreading. For whatever comes nearer to the root is more unified, like the branches of a tree; for if it were not so, the matter would go on to infinity. And we do not say that the parable resembles the thing illustrated on all its sides. And this is it: the limbs, after they went out into actuality, nothing remained of them of that manifestation which they had before their going out; but not so here: for because the Ein Sof does not receive change, [Keter, Chokhmah, Binah] remained stored away there after Keter, Chokhmah, Binah were emanated, just as they were before the spreading of their emanation. For the Emanation is only like one who kindles a lamp from a lamp, with regard to the absence of change in the Emanator. And because the stored-away ones are more concealed, they are distinguished. And so we can say of all the other sefirot: that Binah is the six extremities, and likewise the six extremities are Binah itself, since the six extremities remained there concealed, and there is no difference between them except from the side of concealment and revealing. And this is what he said, that there is no separation at all between the sefirot, so as to say that they are substances separate in themselves; rather they are all one, for each one is included of them all. And he said: 'from primordial light pure thought was drawn,' that is, Keter, drawn from it like the drawing forth of the thought of the heart; 'and from the refined and the clear light,' which are like two springs, 'knowledge was drawn,' which is Chokhmah, 'and intellect,' which is Binah. 'And by means of intellect and knowledge all the spiritual flames took substance, this in this and this with this': so that you do not find the one without the other, nor the other without it; so that if you picture yourself pointing with your finger to one of them, you are pointing to all of them, for they are all in it.

"And the matter of the spreading from intellect and knowledge is like the matters of the flames that hold fast to the strength of the coals. And what was stored away and hidden, this within this and this within this, was forever in that mode of being stored away, until the time of the will of the Primordial Agent arrived, and the spiritual things went out from potentiality into action, and the Emanation of the upper world was emanated, down to the foundation of the tenth stone, which is Malkhut, which is called in the language of the sages 'thick light.' And because of her great density in comparison to what is above her, they also called her 'mixed darkness,' for all the flames are mixed in her; and she is the foundation of all the spiritual worlds, which are all the sefirot, for through her they act, and without her they would not act. And she is the foundation of the corporeal worlds, for she pours forth to them their manifestation. And how many kinds of colors take substance in her and are formed within her, according to the power of each one of the sefirot that pour effluence into her, some of them spiritual forms and some of them corporeal forms, according to what is needed to act; for she is the last seal of all the forms." Thus far his words.

Behold, in the explanation of a holy mouth, filled with the praise of the Lord, blessed be He, he speaks of the matter of the three concealed ones: how they are a manifestation of the first three that remained there in the very root, a manifestation subtle and concealed, fairer and more complete by far than their revealed manifestation; and they are unified with the utmost union, and the count of three is not to be pictured in them except relative to their manifestation revealed after the spreading.

And behold, through the Gaon Rav Chamai and the explanation of Rabbi Aharon upon him, we lack nothing at all of all that we sought; and they serve us as support for all that was expounded on this matter in the preceding chapter, without our remarking on their words and their explanation at all, for love of brevity.

And behold, now it is not difficult for us that they are thirteen attributes, since they are a manifestation of the first three, concealed in their source; just as we have no difficulty from the manifestation of the six extremities concealed in Binah, as the master explained. And they are the very ten Tzachtzachot, because each one of the first three includes, in its middle and in its manifestation, unified in its self, all the lines: the line of Chesed in Chokhmah, the line of Din in Binah, the line of Rachamim in Keter, as we dwelt on at length above. And by this is explained what the master, our teacher Hai Gaon, explained in his responsum, when he said that the first array, which is in the form of the Yod, which has three points, a tip above, a tip below, and a point in the middle, indicates Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah, which spread from Name, Self, and Root [מש"ם ועצ"ם ושר"ש], that is, the three concealed ones. And they said "took shape and were formed": the meaning is the matter [golem], which is the vessels, and the form, which is the Self, that is, the form and soul of the Emanation, as explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter 4. And he said that they are "from the power of the three concealed ones," for through them they were emanated. And the meaning: at the time when the will arose before Him to emanate the Yod, which [sefirot] are included in three points, that is, three Yods, the three points that are in the Yod, as we explained above, then the three acquired manifestation in the very root, as we explained in the preceding chapter. And from the power of that manifestation, which spread in the root itself, the first three were emanated, with the three included in three. For in Chokhmah two are included and concealed, not seen, which are Chesed [and] Netzach; and in Binah two are concealed, which are Gevurah [and] Hod; and in Keter three are concealed, which are Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut, as we explained. And the rest of the responsum is clear.
Behold, the matter of the Tzachtzachot concealed in the Ein Sof has been explained from the words of the Geonim.

And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (folio 239a), and these are his words: "Ein Sof does not stand to be made known, nor to make an end, nor to make a matter [davar], as the First Nothing brought forth beginning and end. Who is the beginning? This is the supernal point, which is the enclosed head of all, which stands within thought; and it makes an end, which is called 'the end of the matter' [sof davar]. But there, Ein Sof: not for desires [re'utin], nor for lights; not lamps in that Ein Sof. All these lights and lamps depend [on it] to subsist by them, and they do not stand to cleave. The one who knows and does not know is none other than the supernal desire, the Enclosure of all enclosures, Nothing. And when the supernal point and the World to Come ascend (another version: 'ascended'), they know only the scent, like one who smells scents and is settled." Thus far its words.

And the explanation of his words: the Root of roots, called Ein Sof, does not stand to be revealed, because of the greatness of its concealment, for there is no knowledge of it at all. And this is what he said: "does not stand to be made known." And he said that besides its being impossible to know it and to apprehend it relative to its aspect, according to the manifestation of its concealment, it also does not stand to be revealed and to spread forth so that one might recognize it and apprehend it. For its Self is not apprehended in any way, except for the apprehension of its actions, that is, its sefirot. And it is known that revealing and spreading forth come through a thing's coming to be with a beginning and an end, for this is the definition of coming-to-be, that it has a beginning and an end. To this he said that the Ein Sof does not stand to make beginning and end, which is "end" and "matter." And the meaning: "end" is its one extreme, and "matter" is its second extreme; and this is "end" [סו"ף] and "matter" [דב"ר], for from above downward the beginning of a matter is [its] end. And he said that the Ein Sof does not stand to reveal its manifestation in "end" and "matter" so as to be apprehended, like Keter, which is called Nothing [Ayin]. And he said "the First Nothing," to indicate that even in its concealed aspect, called "First," that is, its aspect relative to the Emanator, it does not resemble Ein Sof at all, because of the greatness of its concealment. [This is] because "the First Nothing brought forth beginning and end": explanation: Keter is revealed, and its revealing is through the beginning and the end, that is, Chokhmah and Malkhut, as he goes on to explain. And through it is the revealing of Keter, because in Keter is the aspect of Chokhmah, which is the beginning, and the aspect of Binah, which is the aspect of the end; and its revealing is through Chokhmah and Malkhut, which are the beginning and the end, with the middle certainly included. "Who is the beginning? This is the point," etc.: explanation: the intent is Chokhmah, for it is the beginning and first of the Emanation, in the way we explained in Gate Three, chapters 3 and 7. And he said that although it is the beginning of revealing, it is not that it is revealed with an intrinsic revealing; rather [it is] the beginning of a slight revealing. And therefore he went further and said "enclosed, which stands," etc., and it is apprehended only in thought alone. And insofar as the beginning of thought is there, therefore it is the first of the revealing of Keter. "And it makes an end," etc.: explanation: for the beginning of thought is the end of action; for there is Chokhmah at the beginning and Chokhmah at the end, and this is Yod at the beginning and Yod at the end. And the emanation of Malkhut is from there, as in the matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, folio 103): "I am asleep [yeshenah]: I am second [sheniyah] to Chokhmah," and as we shall explain in the Gate of Manifestations. And therefore Chokhmah "makes an end," which is Malkhut, the end of the Emanation. "But there," etc.: explanation: the whole matter of the beginning and the end is in the Emanation and in the sefirot; "but there," in the Ein Sof mentioned, [it is not so]. "Ein Sof: not for desires," etc.: the meaning is that will in the Creator, that is to say, in the Ein Sof, is impossible; because if we said that He wills, He would turn out to change from will to will, and this is impossible in the law of the Ein Sof, necessarily existent, who is not subject to changes. Rather, the matter of will is the first emanation, which descends from Him in a chain, and through that will He performs His will, in the likeness of the Self and the vessels: for the vessels are subject to change, and the Self performs the change through them. And therefore the beginning of the spreading of the Emanation is the will to emanate. But this will is concealed, for it is not literally a revealed emanation; rather it is a will through which He is willing to emanate.

And behold, this will is not the One who wills; rather the Self of the Ein Sof is the One who wills, and He is called "willing" through the will, in the way we explained concerning the matter of judgment and limit in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter 4. And in this way it turns out that the will is so near to the Emanator that it is not emanation; rather it is Self, and not literally Self. Rather it is the manifestation of the arising of His will to emanate the emanated ones; and therefore the will is the emanated ones themselves, which came to be and were found in the manifestation of His Self from the side of the arising of His will to emanate the emanated ones, as we explained in chapter 3.

And behold, according to this there will already be a will to bring a will into existence; for a will arises to bring a will into existence, until there is a point level with the Emanator. And these wills, in the secret of their intrinsic union in the very Emanator, are called "desires" [re'utin]. And because of the concealment of the Ein Sof, in which the desires are, he said "Ein Sof: not for desires nor for lights," for they are likewise titled with the name "lights," as in the matter of primordial light, clear light, refined light. But the will through which He works change in this world is Keter, which is what is called "will"; and through it the Ein Sof wills, just as through Chokhmah He is called wise. "Not lamps in that Ein Sof": explanation: even when the sefirot shine and are titled with the name "luminaries," they do not resemble the Ein Sof. And not only the Ein Sof, but even the concealed luminaries unified in His Self, as we explained. "All these lights," etc.: explanation: all the sefirot depend on those concealed roots, because they are sources to the sefirot; for through the concealed luminaries the sefirot draw effluence from the Ein Sof, like the tree, which draws moisture from its roots, and the main watering is to the roots. So the sefirot turn out to depend on the roots and to subsist through them. "And they do not stand to cleave": explanation: although the concealed sources and roots, which are the Tzachtzachot unified in the very root, are the life and subsistence of the sefirot, nevertheless the roots are not revealed to the sefirot, and the sefirot do not apprehend them, because of the greatness of their concealment. And this is what he said, "and they do not stand to cleave": explanation: they do not stand in a state to be apprehended at all. "The one who knows and does not know," etc.: explanation: those of whom it can properly be said that they know and that they do not know are only Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah. For the other sefirot never know, and never did know, and the roots were never revealed to them, such that we might say that there is a time when they do not know. But the matter of "knows and does not know" can properly be said of Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, as he concludes. And nevertheless these three are not equal in their apprehension. For Keter, in its concealed aspect, which is called "the supernal desire" [re'u ila'ah], which is a title in the language of will, like "desires" [re'utin] mentioned with the Ein Sof; and it is "the Enclosure of all enclosures," called Nothing, for "Something" does not apply to it at all: this aspect is always unified in the concealed roots, which are its cause, and the cause of the roots concealed in it, as we explained above. But Chokhmah and Binah: their apprehension is at times, that is, only at the time of their ascent to the concealed aspect in Keter, which is the source, in which there are likewise three roots, as we explained in chapter 3. And this is what he said: "And when the supernal point," which is Chokhmah, "and the World to Come," which is Binah, "ascends," that is, at the time of the union of the two of them with the utmost union, so that "ascended," in the plural, cannot properly be said of them, but "ascends," in the singular. And then, at the time of their ascent in union in the supernal root, Keter, nevertheless they do not apprehend the roots, except like the scent of one who smells a good scent without touching the spice; rather he smells it, and through it he is settled and sweetened. So these sefirot, after their ascent, [apprehend] the roots and draw sustenance from them through their root that is exalted in Keter; not that they themselves draw sustenance and draw and apprehend the very concealed root. And therefore their nourishment is called [nourishment] from Ein Sof, and likewise their ascent [is called ascent] to Ein Sof.

Behold, from this passage, as explained, it appears that with regard to the apprehension of the roots the whole Emanation is divided into three divisions. The first is the seven days of the Structure, which do not apprehend the concealed ones at all; rather their ascent is up to Binah, in the secret of the Jubilee, and from there upward they do not apprehend, but from there they draw sustenance from Keter and from Chokhmah; except for Tiferet and Malkhut, for in the secret of their union they ascend up to Keter, where their source, the Self, is, as the matter and its reason were explained in Gate Five, chapter 6. And the second is Chokhmah and Binah, which apprehend the concealed roots only at intervals, at the time of their ascent; and that apprehension is not in the very Emanator, but "like one who smells," etc., as we explained above. And there is no doubt that even so the apprehension of Chokhmah will not be equal to the apprehension of Binah, but certainly with the exaltation of one over the other, although they ascend together, because they are male and female, and the one does not suffice without the other. The third is Keter, whose apprehension, in its concealed aspect, is always equal; it is never separated from its root, and it and the root are all one thing, unified in its upper aspect, as we explained.
And Rashbi further dwelt at length on the explanation of these Tzachtzachot and the roots that are in the Ein Sof:

In the book of the Zohar, Parashat Noach (folio 65a), in some versions in the books, and these are its words: "Rabbi Shimon said: I raised my hand in prayers above. When the supernal desire, above and above, stands upon that desire which is not known and not grasped at all, forever, [it is] the head that is enclosed more, above. And that head brought forth what it brought forth, which is not known, and illumined what it illumined, all in an enclosure. The desire of supernal thought is to pursue after it and to be illumined from it. One hanging is spread, and from within that hanging, in the pursuit of that supernal thought, it reaches and does not reach, etc. Then this light of thought that is not known strikes the light of the hanging that stands, which shines from what is not known, etc. And then this light of thought that is not known strikes the light of the hanging, and they shine as one, and nine palaces are made, palaces for palaces, which are not lights and are not spirits and are not souls, and there is none who stands in them. The desire of all nine lights that all stand in thought, which is one of them in the count, all of them [is] to pursue after them at the time that they stand in thought; and they do not cleave and are not known. And these stand neither in desire nor in supernal thought; they grasp them and do not grasp. In these stand all the secrets of faith; and all those lights from the secret of supernal thought that are below are all called Ein Sof. Up to here the lights reach and do not reach, and are not known. Here there is no desire and no thought. When thought shines and does not know from what it shines, then it is clothed and enclosed within Binah, and it shines what it shines, and it enters this into this until they are all included as one. And in the secret of the sacrifice, when it ascends, all is bound this with this and shines this in this. Then they all stand in ascent, and thought is wrapped in Ein Sof. That light which shines from it, [from which] supernal thought [shines], which does not know it at all, is called Ein Sof; for from it it is found and stands and shines to whom it shines. And on this all stands. Happy is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come." Thus far its words.

And its way is concealed and lofty; and nevertheless we shall not withhold our hands from discussing it in every way possible, because the commentators copied it into their books, in particular Rabbi Yehudah Chayat, and did not explain it at all. Therefore we shall explain it with a strong hand. "Rabbi Shimon said: I raised my hand," etc.: the reason for the raising of the hands in prayer is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (folio 67a), and its place is not here. And because Rashbi's intent in this passage is to reveal hidden matters in the Ein Sof, therefore he sanctified himself, "and his hands were steadfast" (Exod. 17:12) until he finished speaking. And thus he said: "When the supernal desire, above and above." Explanation: Chokhmah is called "desire" [re'uta], as explained in many places; and the reason is that it is the subtlest of the subtle, and therefore the language of will is attributed to it, as we explained, for will indicates subtlety and primordiality. And likewise the Supernal Keter is called "desire," for it is the true will among the sefirot. And the will that is supernal over them all is the Ein Sof, in the way we explained in the preceding chapter.

And behold, he said "the supernal desire," and not [the will] of Chokhmah, but "above," which is above the will of Chokhmah; and not Keter, which is the will that is above Chokhmah, but "and above," which is the will that is above the will, which is the Ein Sof, which is above Keter, which is the will that stands over Chokhmah, which is called "will," as we explained above. And he did not suffice with saying "the supernal desire," because Chokhmah too is called "the supernal desire," as is evident in the Zohar many times. "Stands": explanation: rests and abides "upon that desire," explanation: upon Keter. "Which is not known": explanation: relative to its concealed aspect, which is not apprehended. "And not grasped at all, forever": explanation: not only its concealed aspect, which is concealed except at rare times, as at the time when Chokhmah and Binah ascend to it, as we explained in chapter 5; but that concealed aspect, at the utmost of concealment, which was never revealed and never apprehended by any other than it among the emanated ones, and will not be apprehended. And in that aspect it is a throne for the Emanator, an aspect that draws near to Him. "The head that is enclosed more, above": explanation: the Ein Sof, which is the head that stands, is joined, and rests upon this aspect, and is more concealed than this aspect, although that is concealed at the utmost of concealment, as explained. "And that head": explanation: the concealed aspect of Keter, which is head to the other aspects of Keter, and all the more so to the rest of the Emanation. "Brought forth what it brought forth": explanation: emanated what it emanated; and this is the concealed sefirot, which are vessels to the concealed Self. And although they are like a garment to the Self, nevertheless it is not known; and this is what he said: "which is not known." "And illumined what it illumined": this is the Self that spreads within the garment; and therefore it is titled with the language of light, which is the light of the lantern. And because the concealment of the Self is exceedingly greater than the concealment of the garment, he said "all in an enclosure," which goes further in concealment than his saying "which is not known." For "not known" indicates that it is revealed but not known; but "all in an enclosure" indicates its being enclosed of itself in every respect. And with this it will be understood why it was necessary to emanate through "head" and "head," which are the Ein Sof and the first emanated one: because through the Ein Sof the Self that spreads was emanated, and through Keter, which bears the Self and is filled from it, the vessels were emanated, and all by the will of the Emanator. And would that the inquirer would go deep into this, for it is not our way to exaggerate the secrets. And the matter: since the roots that are unified in the very root are, according to the truth, roots of the vessels and not the root of the Self (for the Self is all one, and needs neither root nor source), then just as in the vessels, the outer sefirot, that is to say, the sefirot of the Emanation, the Self spreads in them, so in their root the Self spreads in them; although it is revealed in them more and more, until they are literally His Self and they are the very root. And this matter is among the matters in which contemplation beyond measure is forbidden, and it is in "running and returning." "The desire of supernal thought": explanation: Chokhmah. And he called it "supernal" in its upper aspect, the most concealed, which is unified with Keter. And although its subtlety and its concealment are so great, nevertheless its longing and its craving is to cleave to these concealed roots and to be illumined from them; and therefore it pursues after them. And this is what he said: "to pursue after it and to be illumined from it": explanation: to be receiving and shining from this unified concealed root, emanated from the two heads mentioned above; and it has no apprehension at all, nor even reception from them. "One hanging is spread": this is Keter itself, emanated and revealed, which is a screen between the emanated ones and the sources that are unified in the very root. "And from within that hanging, in the pursuit of that supernal thought": explanation: from within Keter, which is called "hanging," as we explained concerning the reason for the darkness; and the arousal, that is, the pursuit mentioned, by which Chokhmah, called supernal thought in its upper aspect, as we explained, arouses.

And the matter of the pursuit and the arousal is the revealing of her face and her light toward the light of the screen that separates between her and the root and the Self. "It reaches and does not reach" up to that hanging: explanation: the concealed roots mentioned above reach and do not reach Keter, which is the hanging.

And the matter of "reaches and does not reach": explanation: revealing and not revealing relative to Chokhmah, and all the more so to the other emanated ones; but it "reaches" relative to the hanging.

And the matter of "reaches and does not reach" is an action related to the garment, which is what was titled above with the language "brought forth." And afterwards he said "illumined what it illumined," which is a title for the Self unified in the root, which is what was titled above with the language of light, as we explained. And he said "illumined what it illumined" to indicate the concealment, and that it is not properly apprehended, [as befits] the concealed root. "And then it is supernal thought": explanation: then, when the concealed light shone to the hanging, which is Keter, thought, which is Chokhmah, is illumined from it. So it turns out that the light descends in a chain of three aspects: the aspect of the Ein Sof, that is, in the concealed root; and the aspect of its shining in the hanging, which is Keter; and the aspect of the shining of what is in the hanging into thought, which is Chokhmah. And nevertheless the light and the root revealed in Chokhmah is concealed and not revealed at all, although it has already been revealed to a third grade, as we explained. And the matter is that this thought is not literally the very self of the revealed Chokhmah; rather it is the aspect of Keter toward Chokhmah, that is, Chokhmah in its aspect in Keter. Therefore all is concealed, for all is in the wondrous and covered Amon, which is Keter, as we explained. And this is what he said: "And then it is supernal thought, shining with an enclosed light that is not known, and that thought is not known. Then it strikes," etc., "from what is not known, and was not made known, and was not revealed." Explanation: for even now, after the light has been revealed in its chain-descent to thought, which is the aspect of Chokhmah, nevertheless that thought did not on that account apprehend at all, by means of the concealed shining light, what was concealed at first; rather, as its concealment was then, so is its concealment now. And it added no apprehension in the concealed, except the light that shines in it and is apprehended by it, which is the third aspect of the light alone. And he said "which is not known, and was not made known, and was not revealed," for these are three aspects, that is to say, three matters. The first matter is "not known," that is, that it is not known to Chokhmah in the aspect of thought mentioned above. The second matter: not only to thought is it not known, but even above it, that is, the hanging, "was not made known"; explanation: it did not add to its apprehension at all because of this revealing; and this is a solitary verb [po'al boded] in the light. And "was not made known": explanation: to any other than it, neither to Chokhmah nor to other than Chokhmah. The third matter, "and was not revealed": that not only was it not known, but the light itself was not on that account revealed and spread forth from itself to itself more than it was, because of this revealing. And he went so far in this in order to remove change from the very Emanator; rather [it is] like one who kindles a lamp from a lamp, and the Emanator is not diminished, nor known, nor changed, God forbid, as Rabbi Aharon explained, as we wrote in chapter 4. "And then this light of thought that is not known," etc.: explanation: the revealing of the light that shone in thought by means of the light that shone in the hanging, which is a concealed light "that is not known." And therefore it has power to strike the light of the hanging, which is the second light, shining in Keter from the power of the first light, which is unified in the very root. "And they shine as one": explanation: when the light of thought strikes the light of the hanging, then the two lights shine together. "And nine palaces are made, palaces for palaces": explanation: from their shining together there are made nine palaces, nine concealed sefirot; and they are palaces, vessels, and garments for those concealed palaces, which are the supernal lights emanated from the Ein Sof in the first aspect, as explained above. "Which are not lights and are not spirits and are not souls": explanation: they are palaces for those palaces that are neither in the grade of luminaries, nor in the grade of spirits, nor in the grade of souls.

And behold, he mentioned in this three things: lights, spirits, souls. And there is no doubt that "lights" is like "vital souls" [nafshin], and the witness to this is "spirits" and "souls." And the meaning: Rabbi Shimon explained elsewhere that Keter, which is the secret of the cantillation marks, is the soul [neshamah]; and Chokhmah, which is the secret of the vowel-points, is the spirit [rucha]; and Binah, which is the secret of the letters, is the vital soul [nefesh]. And he said that these luminaries are neither Binah nor Chokhmah nor Keter, even in the secret of their upper roots that are in Keter; rather they are a Self with which the root is unified, and He and they are all one thing. Or he means "which are not lights": that they are not the sources of the sefirot, but on the contrary they are clothed in the sources of the sefirot, which are the lights in truth; "and are not spirits": that they are not the sefirot themselves, which are like the spirit to the soul, which is the Self that spreads. And he said that they are also not the Self that spreads within the sefirot, which are the souls of the sefirot; rather they are luminaries and roots unified in the very root, and He and they are all one thing. "And there is none who stands in them": explanation: even now, when they are clothed in the lights emanated from the light of the hanging and the light of thought, nevertheless they are not apprehended, "and there is none who stands in them," because of the greatness of their concealment and the greatness of their attachment to their cause, which is the very root, as we explained. "The desire of all nine lights that all stand in thought, which is one of them in the count, all of them [is] to pursue after them at the time that they stand in thought; and they do not cleave and are not known": explanation: the longing of the concealed sefirot in the manifestation of Chokhmah itself is only to apprehend and to know these concealed lights and sources. "Which is one of them": explanation: in saying "lights that all stand in thought," the intent is not the lights that come to be from within the light of the hanging. For of those luminaries we have already said that they are unified in the light of Keter, which is the hanging, and become palaces for the concealed luminaries; and behold, they are palaces to them, so how could they not know them? Rather these are certainly other luminaries, which are of the self of thought, which are the sefirot emanated from the aspect of Chokhmah in the aspect of Keter, downward to ten. And of those he said that although these luminaries were clothed and revealed, nevertheless the longing of the other luminaries, which are of the self of thought, is to apprehend them and to know them after their spreading in thought; and nevertheless they apprehend nothing of Keter. And this is what he said [: "which is one of them"]; for Chokhmah itself, in the secret of its aspect with Keter, is the Keter among them, and it is one of them, of those nine sefirot in the count; which is not so for the supernal luminaries, of which thought is not [one]: rather [they come from] the light that shines in thought from the body of the hanging, which is a concealed and praised light, and from within it and from within the light of the hanging those lights come to be. Rather certainly these are by themselves and those are by themselves. "All of them to pursue after them": after those supernal luminaries that are clothed, and after those that come to be, added to thought, even at the time of their shining in thought and their being clothed in that light; and this is what he said, "at the time that they stand in thought." And nevertheless "they do not cleave": explanation: they do not apprehend them with any apprehension at all. And needless to say they do not cleave, which is an apprehension that apprehends them; but they do not have even a manifestation of knowledge at all. And this is what he said, "and are not known": explanation: the luminaries of thought itself have no knowledge of them at all, as we explained. "And these stand neither in desire nor in thought": explanation: the reason these lights are not apprehended at all, even by the luminaries of thought, is because their standing is neither in Keter itself, which is "desire," nor in the manifestation of thought, which is Chokhmah itself; rather their standing is that they are clothed and spread in the light that shines from them in Keter and in Chokhmah, that is to say, the two aspects, as we explained above. So it turns out that Keter and Chokhmah are a polished substance which the light strikes, and from them come to be sparks of light that are not literally Chokhmah and Keter but subtler than Keter and than Chokhmah; and in them the concealed luminaries are clothed, and therefore it is impossible to apprehend them. "The supernal ones grasp them and do not grasp": explanation: even those supernal lights in which they are clothed, which are those that come to be from the light of Supernal Keter and Chokhmah, apprehend them and do not apprehend; although they are palaces to them, as explained above, nevertheless their apprehension is slight, because of the greatness of their concealment and subtlety, for they are unified in the very root. "In these stand all the secrets of faith": explanation: on these concealed, subtle lights depend all the sefirot and the whole Emanation, in general and in particular, for the reason that they are the concealed Tzachtzachot, which cleave to their cause, high above, and they and the root are all one thing and one Self, as we went so far concerning their union above and in the preceding chapters. "And all those lights from the secret of supernal thought and below are all called Ein Sof": so is the reading in some books; and there are those who read "that are below." And according to the books that read "and below," he means that the supernal roots mentioned above are all manifestations of the sefirot that were formed in the very root, from the side of the arising of the will to emanate the Emanation, as we explained above and in chapter 3. And therefore it turns out that all those luminaries that are the secret and the concealment of [what is] from thought downward, that is, the ten sefirot of the Emanation (for thought is Chokhmah in the aspect of Keter, so that from it downward are the ten sefirot): he said that all these luminaries that are above are called Ein Sof. And the meaning: although he said that they are ten clothed in ten, etc., as explained above, this number does not necessitate limit and reckoning for them, nor does it indicate any apprehension; rather, nevertheless they are called Ein Sof. And indeed, the reason for the number ten and three is because they spread and are emanated outward, and after their emanation they are counted in the number ten, as we explained in the preceding gates. And according to the books that read "that are below," he means that even those luminaries that shine from the power of thought (as we explained, that thought shines from the power of the hanging), he said that even those luminaries that shine from the power of supernal thought [are called Ein Sof]. And he said "that are below" because thought is below those luminaries that shine from it; and therefore it is grasped in thought, and the luminaries are not known, as we explained above. And this is because the luminaries shine from it upward, like a mirror sunk in the ground which, from the power of the sun, shines sparks upward. And he said that all those luminaries are called Ein Sof because of the greatness of their concealment, although they are emanated from the power of thought; since the matter is that the light of the hanging, which is from the light of the concealed luminaries, strikes the light of thought, and it shines upward; and therefore they are titled with [the name] Ein Sof, since they and the root are all one thing. "Up to here the lights reach and do not reach, and are not known": explanation: up to here are the concealed luminaries that are not known and not apprehended, as we explained. And he said "reach and do not reach," as if to say: up to here the luminaries reached; and not literally that they reached, for they have neither limit nor place, for He is found in every place, above the sefirot, and between the sefirot, and below the sefirot, as befits the holiness of the Ein Sof. "Here there is no desire and no thought": explanation: the luminaries he has mentioned until now are neither the sefirah of Keter, called will, nor the sefirah of Chokhmah, called thought; rather they are luminaries unified in the very root, necessarily existent, and He and they are all one thing. And although he said that they are from the light of the hanging and from the light of thought, that is only from its light that spreads upward. And as for the reason for the matter of these two kinds of luminaries in the Ein Sof, which are the concealed lights,

and further, palaces to them from the power of the light that shines from the hanging and thought, which are Keter and Chokhmah, as explained above: the matter is that the Being that precedes all beings, the King of kings of kings, knows all beings, and not from the side of the knowledge of the beings, for this is impossible in the law of His completeness. For just as His divinity is not divided into parts, so His knowledge is not divided into parts, because He and His knowledge are one, unified. Rather, He knows the matters and understands them from the side of His understanding of Himself; for in apprehending His Self He apprehends every being other than Him, and He and they are all one, unified thing. And therefore it is necessary that the manifestation of the sefirot be concealed in His Self, because the sefirot are a mold and cause to all of manifestation. And through the roots concealed in His Self He understands and knows all that descends from them in a chain, whether much or little, whether small or great; not one of them is missing. And the depiction of forms in the knowledge of the one who depicts is of two kinds: the one, when a man depicts the form before it comes to be, and then it is the subtlest of the subtle, for it has not yet come to be in revealed manifestation; the second, when a man depicts the form after it has come to be, for then it is subtle in his intellect, but not like the first, because it has already come to be and gone out into the manifestation of body. And complete knowledge is when the knowledge is of matters before they are in manifestation, in the privation that precedes coming-to-be, and likewise in knowing them after their coming-to-be; and if one of them is lacking, the knowledge is not complete. If so, it is necessary that there be in the manifestation of the concealed Being two kinds of knowledge: the first in the privation that precedes coming-to-be, which is the manifestation of the concealed roots, the first, preceding luminaries, as we explained above; and the second after their coming-to-be, and this is the manifestation of the light that returns upward from Chokhmah and Keter, as explained, for this is the return of things to the root after their revealing. And therefore they are not in the subtlety of the first ones, but on the contrary they are a garment to the preceding ones, like coming-to-be that clothes privation, in the way they said (in Sefer ha-Bahir): "What is bohu [void]? A thing that clothes the tohu [formlessness]." And therefore [he called] them "palaces for palaces," as explained above. And would that the inquirer would contemplate this, and put his hand to his mouth, and let his contemplation in this inquiry be in "running and returning"; and from God we ask pardon. "When thought shines and does not know from what it shines": after the inquiry concerning the Necessarily Existent and the roots unified in Him was completed and concluded, he began to engage in the matters of the emanated ones. And even if [this] was not mentioned in the very Keter, it was already hinted at above. And he said that when thought shines, in which Keter is included in its aspect toward Keter, that is, Keter toward revealing, which is one of the three brains (for the three aspects of Chokhmah are the first three in their order, Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, as we explained in Gate Three, chapter 7), "and does not know from what it shines," as we explained above, that it has no apprehension of the concealed sources. "Then it is clothed within Binah": it has already been explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance that the relation of Binah to Chokhmah is like the relation of Malkhut to Tiferet. And just as Malkhut is a palace to Tiferet, as in the matter that is said (Hab. 2:20), "But the Lord is in His holy palace; hush [הס] before Him," etc., [has] being the number of Adonai and the number of heikhal [palace], so Binah is a palace and a storing-place for Chokhmah. And therefore when it shines, then it is stored away in Binah; and likewise in the secret of their union as male and female; and therefore blessing is added to them, as he says, "and it shines what it shines," that is, an increase of light to the union. "It enters this into this, until they are all included as one": explanation: the whole Emanation, that is to say, the sefirot, are included together. "And in the secret of the sacrifice," etc.: explanation: and this is the secret of the sacrifice [korban], as is written (Lev. 1:2), "a sacrifice to the Lord"; and it is explained in the Zohar (Vayikra, folio 5) that he did not say "drawing near" [keruv] or "nearness" [kerivut], which would seem to mean one thing that is brought near to the Lord, but said korban, which is a solitary verb, a verbal noun standing as a name in itself. And this is that the four-letter name itself draws near, self to self, and joins and draws near: Yod with Heh, Vav with Heh. And this is what he said: "when it ascends, all": explanation: the whole Emanation; "and is bound this with this": explanation: Heh is unified with Vav, Heh with Yod, from below upward; "and shines this in this": in the secret of the returning light. "Then they all stand in ascent": for after they are unified and bound together, then thought, which is head to them all, is wrapped in its cause above. And this is what he said: "and thought is wrapped": explanation: is included within the Ein Sof, in the way of one who wraps himself in a tallit, who is stored away and included within it. "That light which shines," etc.: explanation: and not in the Ein Sof literally, but only in that light from which it shines, which flows upon it. And incidentally we have learned that the matter of this wrapping is that it shines from its power. "For from it it is found and stands and shines to whom it shines": he intended three things. First, "is found": the manifestation of emanation. Second, "and stands": that is, the effluence of its subsistence, which is its nourishment. Third, the effluence that it pours forth to others; and this is "and shines to whom it shines." And since these three aspects are from that light alone, which is not apprehended, not from the concealed Self, then even when they are unified, it ascends only up to that light alone, and not to apprehend, but to draw sustenance from it; and this is its wrapping in it. Thus far the explanation of this passage. And from within it many awesome matters concerning the Tzachtzachot have been explained to us; and likewise it is necessitated that the principal roots, which are the Tzachtzachot, are concealed in the Ein Sof.

After the matter of the Tzachtzachot in the Ein Sof has been explained in the preceding chapters according to the words of Rashbi and the Geonim, there is a point to examine: for the opposite of this is found in Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 135b), for there he explained that these three concealed ones are in Keter. And these are his words: "The Supernal Keter, although it is primordial light, and clear light, and refined light, is black before the Cause of causes." It appears clearly that the three concealed ones are in Keter.

And we further examine his wording, that he did not state them in the Gaon's way; for the Gaon ordered them primordial light, and afterwards refined light, and afterwards clear light. And reason inclines, at first glance, to this matter: for "refined" [metzuchtzach] indicates clearness and great whiteness, so that its letters were doubled to indicate the strength of the action; and therefore it is fitting that it be exalted in its clearness above "clear" [tzach], which is only a single clearness. And it is possible to say that the matter is as we already set out in the preceding chapters: just as the manifestation of the first three, in the totality of the ten, remained concealed in the Ein Sof, so at the time of their emanation they were formed in Keter, and their manifestation remained there; except that they are not in the order in which they are in the Ein Sof. For in the Ein Sof they are primordial light, and afterwards refined light, and afterwards clear, and their mnemonic is קמ"ץ [Kamatz]; but in Keter clear precedes refined. And the reason is like the likeness of the seal that is reversed; not literally like a seal, but because the emanation of Chokhmah preceded the emanation of Binah, therefore its revealing came first, and [Binah] is last, near to the revealing and the emanation; and therefore they are primordial light, and afterwards clear light, and afterwards refined light. And by this the words of Rashbi are explained in all their modes. However, we found in the book Ma'ayan ha-Chokhmah, attributed to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, the master of the prophets, a matter concerning these Tzachtzachot that disagrees with the view of the Geonim and the words of Rashbi. And these are its words: "And these were springing forth from the darkness; and they are: light from light, and radiance from radiance, splendor from splendor, and radiance from light, light from radiance, splendor from light, and light from splendor, and splendor from radiance, and radiance from splendor, and burning from burning. Behold, ten. The first is wondrous light, and this is light from light; and the second is hidden light, and this is radiance from radiance; the third is sparkling light, and this is splendor from splendor; the fourth is clear light, and this is radiance from light; the fifth is refined light, and this is light from radiance; the sixth is resplendent light, and this is splendor from light; the seventh is purified light, and this is light from splendor; the eighth is clear and refined light, and this is splendor from radiance; the ninth is bright light, and this is radiance from splendor; the tenth is glowing light [or nogah], and this is burning from burning." Thus far its words.

And although the words are obscure and concealed, not making known from within whether they treat the Tzachtzachot or the sefirot, nevertheless there is a difficulty for every interpretation. If the sefirot, behold, he attributed the name of the concealed ones to the sefirot. And if the concealed ones, there is likewise a difficulty: first, that he counted ten and the Geonim three. And although this is not a difficulty, for he already said above that ten and three are all one matter to them, as we explained in the preceding chapters, yet it is difficult that he related clear light to Chesed and refined light to Gevurah. And this is difficult, for both according to Rashbi, peace be upon him, and according to the Geonim, all agreed that they are Chokhmah and Binah. And this we can resolve with strain, and say that since Chokhmah is the line of Chesed and Binah the line of Din, and the lines were included in clear and refined, then clear may already be related to Chesed and refined to Gevurah, after their roots. But it is very difficult: for the Geonim said that refined light is superior to clear, and here it implies that clear is superior, as he said that the fourth, which is Chesed, is clear, and the fifth, which is Gevurah, is refined. And so too the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim imply, although we settled it with strain above. Therefore it seems right to say that the correct order is thus: primordial light, clear light, refined light. And the matter is: the first is called "primordial," which indicates its primordiality, its wondrousness, and its concealment; even after its emanation it is related by this name, for Keter is called "primordial air," and likewise it is called "wondrous Amon," and all is one matter. And therefore the book Ma'ayan ha-Chokhmah related the first by the name "wondrous light." The second is clear. And it is called "clear" to show the whiteness and the clearness, as befits Chesed, and also Chokhmah, which is the line of Chesed, of whiteness and clearness. The third is refined; and therefore the book Ma'ayan ha-Chokhmah related this name to Gevurah, because Gevurah is the line of Din in actuality. And the explanation of "refined" [metzuchtzach]: he means a light made spot upon spot [baheret baheret], like stains, from the language "drops of milk" [tzichtzuchei chalav] which comes in the language of our Sages, of blessed memory (in tractate Avodah Zarah, folio 35), and the meaning is points like stains. And because the light of Gevurah has in it the power of judgment, therefore it is called refined light, for they are the stains of darkness and judgment that mix with the light. Or we may mean that Chokhmah is concealed and is revealed only in Binah, which is its palace, as explained in the preceding chapter; and therefore in Chokhmah there is "clear," one alone, but in Binah there are two clearnesses, which is metzuchtzach: the clearness of Binah itself, and the clearness of Chokhmah, which appears in Binah. And close to this matter Rashbi explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (folio 224), on the verse (Isa. 58:11) "and He will satisfy your soul in dry places [be-tzachtzachot]," with the doubling of tzachtzachot with respect to the soul, as explained there. And in this way we shall say that it is the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim, that clear precedes refined; and the Geonim were not precise about their order.

And behold, concerning the manifestation of these Tzachtzachot that are in Keter, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim the name יו"ד ה"י וא"ו ה"י [Yod, Heh-Yod, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Yod]; and they are three Yods, a segolta, three points: these are the concealed ones in Keter. And not that this name is in Keter in its own aspect literally, for no name grasps it, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, chapter 2; rather the intent is Primeval Chokhmah, the name of the Supernal Keter, as explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 117a), and as explained in the book Or Yakar. And the secret of the middle Alef in וא"ו is "the skull that covers over the brain"; that is, [the text seems defective here] and the whole amounts to the number of א"ל [El, 31]. But it is sometimes filled with four Yods, thus: יו"ד ה"י וי"ו ה"י. And this means: the three [last] Yods hint at the three concealed points that are in Keter, and the first Yod hints at the three heads of heads that are in the very root. And this is the first Yod, which is likewise three Yods, thus: a tip above, a tip below, and a body in the middle, to indicate the superiority of the three concealed ones in the Ein Sof over the three in Keter: for these are depicted in three letters, and those three in the form of one Yod alone, to indicate one Self and one manifestation. And all these names are only in Chokhmah; and the number testifies to this, for this name amounts to 72 [ע"ב], and with the name [itself] it is 73 [ע"ג], and Chokhmah is 73, to indicate their union. And likewise the name of 63 [ס"ג] with its ten letters is 73; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. And concerning the Tzachtzachot concealed in Keter, the commentators attributed names to them, and these are their words: יהוה יהוה יהוה יהוה יהוה יהוה יהוה יהוה יהוה יהוה יהוה [the vowel-points that distinguish these names are not in our text]. Concerning these names they wrote, and these are their words: "Ten Tzachtzachot are above the Supernal Keter, and they are the ten supernal sefirot, and they are called branches to the Supernal Keter; and this is what it says in Shi'ur Komah, and it is called the whiteness of the head. And the Tzachtzachot are branches above the Supernal Keter, and they are the [text: ha-meyuchas] that stand by the Cause of causes." Thus far their words, letter for letter. And although the Gaon, our teacher Hai Gaon, wrote that they have no name among the holy names, nevertheless it is already possible to say that these, which are in Keter, should have names. Or it is possible that we say that while they are above they have no names at all, but after their spreading these holy names are attributed to them, divided according to their vowel-points in the division of the names of the sefirot, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. And just as they attributed ten Tzachtzachot to Keter, so they attributed them to Tiferet. And these are their words in the Commentary on the sefirot, on the sefirah of Tiferet: "The sixth sefirah is Tiferet. It is a sefirah that gives power and beauty [pe'er] to all the sefirot, and all of them glory [mitpa'arim] in it; and it is an ornament to them all, and all of them are made equal in it, and it is the equalizing of all. And in it is the completion of ten utterances. The first is called clear light, because it gives clearness to make all the sefirot clear in power. The second is called refined light, because it gives clearness to itself, and from itself to the ten others. The third is called clear and refined light, because it gives an effluence of clearness, an effluence in the inwardness of the sefirot, from within and from without. The fourth is called bright light, because this light stands in one place and has no movement at all, as it is said (Job 37:21): 'And now they do not see the bright light; it is in the skies.'

"And further, because it is like a white spot engraved in its whiteness in the place of the supernal holiness. The fifth is called resplendent light; the correct reason for it is because the radiance rolls within it and becomes one matter, cleaving, standing in its place, and it does not split to any side at all; and its radiance is revealed and increases by means of a complete middle; through this it is called resplendent light. The sixth is called the light of burning, because it attains for them, from the burning of the power, a side that increases and is exalted on all its sides. The seventh is called sparkling light, because many powers and many matters sparkle from it, and all of them bound to one another, like the branches of the tree that are rooted in the trunk of the tree and increase and are exalted from it, and from the branches branches, without end. The eighth is called strengthening light, because it strengthens from increase to increase, and from increase to exaltation, and from the completion of the subsistence of the power to its end. The ninth is called intelligible light [or muskal], because from it intellect is emanated in the upper ones and in the lower ones without end; and this power has no motion at all except from its own side. The tenth is called the light of the work [or mif'al], because it is the primordial work, and no man can know the root of this work at all; and this work is from the Supernal Keter, which are called by this attribute." Thus far its words.

And behold, he changed these names a great deal; for we said that clear and refined are among the first ones; and there are further changes, and we have not the strength to reconcile them. And nevertheless from it we have learned that there are ten Tzachtzachot in Tiferet as well. And perhaps the reason for this is that its head reaches the supernal whiteness, in the secret of the concealed Da'at, as explained in the preceding gates. Or otherwise, perhaps it is because Tiferet includes the first three, as explained in Gate 23, in the entry Ish. And since this is so, it is fitting that every relation of the first three be attributed to it.
And behold, this Gate is concluded, with the help of Heaven.
The Twelfth Gate: The Gate of Paths.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain the matter of the thirty-two paths, as the sages of the Kabbalah, early and late, agreed. And in this Gate their matter, their source, and their action are explained one by one, as far as it is found by us. And before we enter into their explanation, we let the inquirer know beforehand that he should not be astonished at what he finds explained of them in Sefer ha-Kanah, for it is copied from the long book of Rabbi Yosef, the author of the commentary on Sefer Yetzirah, as we shall write some of his words.
Chapter One:

All the Kabbalists, early and late, agreed on the thirty-two paths that are in Chokhmah. And the first to reveal this inquiry is Sefer Yetzirah. And these are its words, in the first mishnah of chapter 1: "With thirty-two wondrous paths of wisdom, Yah, the Lord of hosts, engraved His world, with three books [sefarim]: with sefer, sefar, and sippur." Thus far its words.

And there are those who read: "Yah, YHVH of hosts, the God of Israel, living Elohim, El Shaddai, high and exalted, dwelling forever, and holy is His name, engraved His world," etc. Thus far its words.

And they are ten, between the titles and the names; and they explained that this is a hint to the ten sefirot. And this is not sufficient, for these names have no relation and order with the count of the sefirot, as is well known to everyone who understands. And likewise there are those who read "with three things [devarim]" in place of "with three books." And the more correct is "books," for "things" are literally books; and "books" relates to sefer and sippur, which is a play on words, as we shall explain. And in the name "Yah, YHVH of hosts" the ten sefirot are likewise included, as we shall explain. Therefore the reading most correct and settled with us in this mishnah is as we copied above. And now we come to its explanation. "With thirty-two paths," etc.: the matter of these paths is in Chokhmah. And indeed, the manifestation of their division is certainly by way of cause and effect: as if we said, the first path is cause to the second, and the second to the third, and the third to the fourth. And this is their count and their division, in the way we explained in Gate Eight, chapter 3, concerning the 620 pillars of light that are in Keter. And there is no doubt that these paths are ways and channels for the effluence, and they are sources coming from Chokhmah to Binah; for there is "the cascade of the paths" [eshed ha-netivot], as explained in the Tikkunim in many places. And therefore she is called kavod [glory], which amounts to the number of the paths that flow [32], and likewise she is called lev [heart, 32] after them. And by way of these paths all the work of creation was performed, as is evident from the count of [the mentions of] Elohim, which are thirty-two, as we shall explain. And the matter is that the mold of all the created entities is in Chokhmah, as is written (Ps. 104:24): "In wisdom You have made them all"; and from there they are drawn in subtlety down to Malkhut, from thirty-two to thirty-two, down to Malkhut, which is the lower Chokhmah, and they are the lower thirty-two. And through her the deeds go out into creation; and she is the architect mentioned in the work of creation, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (in Bereshit Rabbah, section 27). And therefore it was necessary that the mold of all the created entities be in the thirty-two paths; and the thirty-two paths are "the clay ground in which the King cast them" (1 Kings 7:46). And therefore some call Chokhmah golem, because it is the matter that bears all the forms in the world. And likewise חכמ"ה [chokhmah] amounts to 73, [as does] גל"ם [gelem]; explanation: hyle, which bears all the forms in the world. And this is the intent of the mishnah in saying "with thirty-two paths of wisdom He engraved," etc., "His world."

Behold, the engraving of the world was in the thirty-two; and so the thirty-two paths are to the world as parchment to writing. Or he means that the thirty-two paths literally acted [to make] the world, and they were what imprinted the world.
