And all comes to one place, for the one does not suffice without the other: for if their form had not preceded them from above, from the depths of Chokhmah, they would not act at all. If so, first the world was formed in them, and afterwards they formed the world. "Paths": paths without qualification are certainly concealed, and are not like ways, which are revealed, as it says (Jer. 6:16): "Stand by the ways and see, and ask for the paths of old." Behold, of the ways he said "see," but of the paths he said "and ask." And nevertheless the tracks [shevilim] are more concealed from understanding than the paths. And so it is explained in the book Ma'ayan Chokhmah of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him; and these are its words: "The tracks are narrow and short, and the paths are more ample, and the ways are wide. And the tracks are like children, and the paths like mothers." Thus far its words.

And it is possible that the tracks are the paths included in each and every path. For it is certain that the paths are included each one of its fellow, and each and every path is included of thirty-two short and narrow paths, which are what are called tracks. And therefore the paths are mothers to the tracks. And the ways are a further revealing of the paths, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, under the entry derakhim. And because the paths are concealed, therefore he said "wondrous" [peli'ot], which is explained from the language (Deut. 17:8) "if a matter is too wondrous [ki yippale]," which Targum Onkelos renders "if it is covered"; and likewise from the language of "wonder." And they said "His world": that is, Binah, which is called "world." And he said "with sefer, sefar, and sippur": on these three words the explanations among the commentators are many. "And I know neither chilak nor bilak; I know [only] the Mishnah." And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (folio 137b), on the verse (Ps. 19:2) "The heavens tell [mesapperim] the glory of God [El]": "The heavens take from the source of life first, and they illumine and set right the supernal Glory, from the secret of the supernal sefer, Abba of all, and from the secret of sefar, the supernal Imma; and it is from the secret of sippur. And therefore mesapperim, as we said, in the secret of these three names that rule on the Sabbath day over all the other days." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: from what the verse said, "the heavens," this is Tiferet, which is called heavens; and these heavens pour forth effluence and give light to Malkhut, which is called "the glory of God." And he wished to be precise about the word mesapperim, which is derived from the word sefarim, which are the books mentioned in this mishnah, which are sefer, sefar, sippur. And because the books have been explained as three letters, which are Yod-Heh-Vav, which are Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at, by which the world was created, if so, how is it possible to say that "the heavens tell [mesapperim]" is the language of sefarim, which are sefer, sefar, and sippur, which are Yod-Heh-Vav, that is, Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at? For behold, they are not the heavens. To this he said: "The heavens take from the source of life first": explanation: the heavens, which are Tiferet, receive the light and the sparkling from the place of life, which is Chokhmah and Binah. For life is in Chokhmah, as is written (Eccl. 7:12): "wisdom gives life to those who have it"; and the source of life is Binah, for through her life flows. And Tiferet receives the life and the effluence from Chokhmah and Binah before all the Emanation, and afterwards they pour forth effluence to the supernal Glory, which is Malkhut. So according to this it turns out that "all the words of his mouth are in righteousness" (Prov. 8:8) in saying "the heavens," which is Tiferet: for although the sparkling is from a high place, since it flows through it, therefore it is attributed to it. And he called Malkhut "supernal Glory" to be precise about the language of the verse, which said "the glory of El"; and the explanation is like (Ps. 36:7) "the mountains of El," and it is derived from (Ezek. 17:13) "and he took the mighty [elei] of the land." And this is not forced; for is not El in "the glory of El" holy? For the whole essence of this name has this explanation, as we explained in the Gate of Names. And he called Malkhut "the glory of El" for the reason that all the other days of the Structure, from Tiferet downward, are attached to her, as is evident there at the beginning of his words. "From the secret of the supernal sefer, Abba of all": explanation: there is sefer and there is sefar, and so Rashbi explained, and we shall explain it in its entry. And therefore he said that the sefer meant here is the supernal sefer, which is Chokhmah. And he said "Abba of all" because Chokhmah is called sefer for the reason that in it all the subtle sources for the particulars of things, emanated, created, formed, and made, are all included in subtlety in Chokhmah, in the secret of the thirty-two paths, by which all things, great and small, that are from it downward were created and engraved. And therefore it is called sefer [book], for there all things are written and ordered as in a book. And to indicate this reason he said "the supernal sefer, Abba of all": explanation: that it is called sefer because it is father to all that is from it downward, in the secret of the thirty-two paths, as we explained and as will be explained at length. "And from the secret of sefar, the supernal Imma": explanation: sefar from the language of counting things, and its fellow (2 Chron. 2:16) "after the census [sefar] with which David had counted them." And so through Binah the things standing in the sefer are particularized. For all the things that are in Chokhmah in subtlety go out into revealed actuality through Binah. For Chokhmah is to Binah as the male to the female, in the likeness of the relation of Malkhut to Tiferet. And just as the female brings into actuality what is in the potentiality of the male, so Binah brings into actuality, and into particulars, what is within Chokhmah. For number indicates that the things are particularized in particulars, one by one. And therefore he called her "the supernal Imma," for she is the mother of all the things that go out from Chokhmah, which is the father, as we explained. "And it is from the secret of sippur": explanation: Tiferet, which is the heavens mentioned above, is in the secret of sippur [telling]. For it is the very self of the things counted, for through it the six extremities went out from Binah, and it is what includes them. And they are the six days of creation, and they are the sum of the things counted from the sefer and the sefar. And therefore it is called sippur, for it is the telling itself, that is, the thing acted upon through the sefer and the sefar. And they are called sefer, sefar, sippur also from the language of sefirot. And since the effluence comes from Tiferet to Malkhut from the totality of the three books, therefore he said mesapperim, the language of sippur. And this is what he meant: "And therefore mesapperim," etc.: explanation: he used the word mesapperim so that it would be derived from the word sefer, the word sefar, and the word sippur, in the secret of three names, which are Chokhmah, Binah, and Tiferet, which are Yod-Heh-Vav. And this is the explanation of sefer, sefar, sippur expounded in our mishnah. And the sense of the language of the mishnah is that the ten sefirot, which are the seal of all beings, were included in the sefer, the sefar, and the sippur. And the reason that four books were not mentioned, which are the four (letters) of YHVH, but three, which are Yod-Heh-Vav, is because the rib had not yet been taken from the man, and the whole Emanation was included in Chokhmah, Tevunah, and Da'at; and the rib, which is the [final] Heh, had not yet been emanated.

And behold, the will incised all beings in the golem of the thirty-two before their going out into the manifestation of intrinsic Something, and emanated them from the supernal Nothing to the subtle Something that is in Chokhmah, in the matter of the thirty-two, and from there to the sefirotic manifestation, the manifestation of revealed Something, the revealing of the six extremities; and this is the thirty-two [mentions of] Elohim mentioned in the work of creation, as we shall explain, with the help of the Rock and His salvation.

The general rule that emerges from the preceding chapter is that the thirty-two paths are the sum of all beings, above and below; and for this reason the name Elohim is mentioned thirty-two times in the creation of the world, to indicate that each one of the thirty-two paths was revealing what had been formed in it of the matter of creation. And [the name] came thirty-two times as Elohim, and not thirty-two times as Yah, as would befit Chokhmah, because the revealing of the beings from Chokhmah is through Binah, where "the cascade of the paths" is, as we explained; and therefore they came in the name Elohim, whose hint is to Binah. And as for the reason it is written as the name Elohim in its own letters, and not as the four-letter name with the vowels of Elohim, which is the name hinted in Binah (although the name Elohim also hints at her, as we shall explain in the Gate of Names, chapters 4, 7, 8, and 9, and as we also explained in Gate Eight, chapters 7 and 8): it is written as the name Elohim in the letters of Elohim to hint at the strength of the judgment of Gevurah, for it is the world of nature. And likewise the name Elohim amounts to the number of ha-teva [nature, 86], which is in it. And the reason is that the shemitah was in Gevurah, as is agreed among most of the commentators; and the shemitah impressed upon its world according to its imprint [teva] and its will, for nature is a divine will. And therefore the creation of the world was in complete judgment, until He saw that it could not stand, and joined the attribute of compassion with it, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained.

And because this shemitah is the attribute of Gevurah, the beginning and the end of the Torah are Lamed-Bet [32]: the Bet of Bereshit, the Lamed of Yisrael. And at its beginning comes the name of forty-two that issues from Bereshit, and likewise at its end, "and in all the mighty hand," etc., as we shall explain in the Gate of Particulars of Names. And all this is to indicate that the thirty-two, in which the letters of the Torah are, are sealed with the name of Gevurah and judgment, which is the name of forty-two. And likewise the name of forty-two is thirty-two paths and ten utterances, and by it was the creation of the world, as the verse of Bereshit proves. And after we have set out this matter, we come to explain the thirty-two paths by their names and their action, as the ancients explained. And before all else we copy here the thirty-two [mentions of] Elohim in the work of creation, by whose explanation light will be seen:
1. In the beginning God created the.
2. And the spirit of God hovered.
3. And God said, Let there be light.
4. And God saw the light.
5. And God divided between the light.
6. And God called the light Day.
7. And God said, Let there be a firmament.
8. And God made the firmament.
9. And God called the firmament Heaven.
10. And God said, Let the waters be gathered.
11. And God called the dry land Earth.
12. And God saw that it was good.
13. And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass.
14. And God saw that it was good.
15. And God said, Let there be luminaries.
16. And God made the two luminaries. 17. And God set them in the firmament of the heaven.
18. And God saw that it was good.
19. And God said, Let the waters swarm.
20. And God created the great sea-creatures.
21. And God saw that it was good.
22. And God blessed them.
23. And God said, Let the earth bring forth.
24. And God made the beast of the earth.
25. And God saw that it was good.
26. And God said, Let us make man.
27. And God created man.
28. In the image of God He created him.
29. And God blessed them.
30. And God said to them, Be fruitful and multiply.
31. And God said, Behold, I have given.
32. And God saw all that He had made.

Behold, these are the thirty-two paths in Parashat Bereshit; and so Rashbi counted them in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 130a). Then the Geonim gave them names according to what they had received of their action. And Rabbi Yosef copied them in the long book of the commentary on Sefer Yetzirah that he composed. And likewise the author of Sefer ha-Kanah copied them, although he was clever enough to write them in the name of maggidim; and they are clearly found [to belong] to the Geonim. And these are their names, "each by his own standard, with the signs" (Num. 2:2):
Path 1 is called the wondrous intellect [sekhel mufla]. And it is the primordial intelligible light, and it is the first glory, whose manifestation no creature can attain.

Path 2 is called the resplendent intellect [sekhel mazhir]. And it is the crown of creation and the radiance of the equal unity, exalted as head over all; and it is called in the mouths of the masters of the Kabbalah the second glory.

Path 3 is called the sanctified intellect [sekhel mekuddash]. And it is the foundation of primeval wisdom, which is called emunah omen [faith, fosterer], and its roots are amen; and it is the father of faith, from whose power faith is emanated.

Path 4 is called the fixed intellect [sekhel kavu'a]. And it is called so because from it all the spiritual powers are emanated in the subtlety of the emanation, which are emanated, these and these, by the power of the Primordial Emanator.

Path 5 is called the rooted intellect [sekhel nishrash]. And it is called so because it is the substance of the equal unity, and it is unified in the substance of Binah, from the bounds of holy Chokhmah.

Path 6 is called the separate intellect [sekhel nivdal]. And it is called so because in it the effluence of the emanation increases, and it pours that effluence upon all the pools [berekhot; text: beri'ot, "creations"] that are unified in its substance.

Path 7 is called the hidden intellect [sekhel nistar]. And it is called so because it is a resplendent radiance to all the intellective powers that are seen by the eye of the intellect and in the contemplation of faith.

Path 8 is called the complete intellect [sekhel shalem]. And it is called so because it is the disposition of primordiality, which has no root in which to settle except in the chambers of Gedulah, which are emanated from the substance of its subsistence.

Path 9 is called the pure intellect [sekhel tahor]. And it is called so because it purifies the sefirot, and tests and makes shine the decree of their design and the measure of their unity, for they are unified without cutting and separation.

Path 10 is called the sparkling intellect [sekhel mitnotzetz]. And it is called so because it is exalted and sits upon the throne of Binah, and shines with the radiance of all the luminaries, and pours forth the effluence of increase to the Prince of the Countenance.

Path 11 is called the refined intellect [sekhel metzuchtzach]. And it is called so because it is the substance of the heavenly curtain [pargod] that is arranged in the order of the array, and it is a relation of the paths [text: ha-netinat; corrected ha-netivot] to stand before the Cause of causes.

Path 12 is called the bright intellect [sekhel bahir]. And it is called so because it is the substance of the great wheel [ofan], called Chazchazit; explanation: the place from which the vision of those who see in the appearance issues.

Path 13 is called the intellect that guides the unity [sekhel manhig ha-achdut]. And it is called so because it is the substance of the Throne of Glory, and it is the completion of the truth of the unified spiritual ones.

Path 14 is called the illuminating intellect [sekhel me'ir]. And it is called so because it is the substance of the Chashmal, and the teacher of the mysteries of the holy secrets and their disposition.

Path 15 is called the establishing intellect [sekhel ma'amid]. And it is called so because it establishes the substance of creation in clouds of purity. And the masters of contemplation said that it is the thick cloud [arafel], and this is (Job 38:9) "and thick cloud its swaddling band."

Path 16 is called the eternal intellect [sekhel nitzchi]. And it is called so because it is the bliss [idun] of the glory, for there is no glory below it as it is; and it is called the Garden of Eden prepared for the righteous and the upright.

Path 17 is called the intellect of sensation [sekhel ha-hergesh]. And it is prepared for the pious of faith, to clothe themselves in it with the holy spirit; and it is called the foundation of Tiferet in the station of the upper ones.

Path 18 is called the intellect of the house of effluence [sekhel beit ha-shefa]. And from within its investigation they draw a secret and a riddle, those who dwell in its shadow and cleave to the investigation of its self [text: mamashuto, "its substantiality"; corrected atzmuto], from the Cause of causes.

Path 19 is called the intellect of the secret of all the spiritual actions [sekhel sod ha-pe'ulot ha-ruchaniyot]. And it is called so because of the effluence that spreads in it from the place of the upper pool and the exalted glory.

Path 20 is called the intellect of the will [sekhel ha-ratzon]. And it is called so because in it is the disposition of all the formed beings, and by this intellect the whole manifestation of primeval wisdom is known.

Path 21 is called the intellect of the sought delight [sekhel ha-chefetz ha-mevukash]. And it is called so because it receives the effluence of divinity so as to pour forth from its blessing to all beings.
Path 22 is called the faithful intellect [sekhel ne'eman]. And it is called so because in it spiritual powers increase, so that they may be near to all who dwell in their shadow.

Path 23 is called the enduring intellect [sekhel kayyam]. And it is called so because it is the power of subsistence of all the sefirot. (Another version: "subsistence for all who hold fast to it, to clothe them with His holy spirit.")
Path 24 is called the imaginative intellect [sekhel dimyoni]. And it is called so because it gives likeness to all the likenesses that were created in their likeness, fitting to their aspect.
Path 25 is called the intellect of trial [sekhel nisyoni]. And it is called so because it is the primordial trial with which God tries all the pious.

Path 26 is called the renewed intellect [sekhel ha-mechudash]. And it is called so because in it the Holy One, blessed be He, renews all the new things [text: ha-chasidim, "the pious"; corrected ha-chadashim] that are renewed from the creation of the world.
Path 27 is called the perceptible intellect [sekhel murgash]. And it is called so because from it was created the intellect of every created entity beneath the upper sphere, and their perceptions.
Path 28 is called the natural intellect [sekhel mutba]. And it is called so because in it the nature of every being beneath the sphere of the sun is completed, in the completeness of the spheres.

Path 29 is called the corporeal intellect [sekhel mugsham]. And it is called so because it depicts every body that becomes corporeal beneath the disposition of the spheres, in their growth [text: bi-gevulam, "in their bounds"; corrected be-gidulam].

Path 30 is called the general intellect [sekhel kelali]. And it is called so because in it are included the astrologers, in the judgments of the stars and the constellations, their contemplation and the completion of their knowledge in the modes of their revolution.
Path 31 is called the perpetual intellect [sekhel temidi]. And it is called so because in it the course of the sun and the moon continues according to their disposition, each one as befits it.
Path 32 is called the served intellect [sekhel ne'evad], because it is arranged for all who make use of the worship of the seven planets in their bounds.

Up to here reaches what is found in the explanation of the paths in the words of the Geonim; and their words are concealed and hidden and need explanation, and we shall explain [them] in the coming chapters. And we have seen fit to divide them into four parts, eight in each chapter, in order to give space between section and section.

All these paths are called intellective. And the intent is that intellection [haskalah] is in Chokhmah. And this is what we say in the prayer, "knowledge, understanding, and intellection" [de'ah, binah, ve-haskel], which are Da'at, Tevunah, and Chokhmah, from below upward. And because these paths are drawn from Chokhmah, therefore they are called "intellective" after their source, for all intellection is in Chokhmah, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, under the entry maskil.

Path 1 is called the wondrous intellect. Rabbi Yosef explained it from the language (Deut. 17:8 [text: 16:8]) "if [a matter] is too wondrous [ki yippale]," as its Targum [renders it], "if it is covered"; and he explained: a concealed and hidden intellect, not apprehended by any other than it, like the Cause of causes. And he said that all the paths are included in it in a general way; and this is the reason of פל"א / אל"ף [pele, "wonder" / Alef]: just as the form of the Alef includes all the letters, so this path includes all the paths. And it is called primordial, for it precedes all beings. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30, folio 73b), and these are his words: "The first path: of it is said (Job 28:7), 'a path that no bird of prey knows, nor has the eye of the falcon [ayyah] seen it.' What is 'the eye of ayyah'? It is from those angels of whom we say, 'Where [ayyeh] is the place of His glory, to adore Him?' When she is in this path, they have no knowledge of her, for she is enclosed away from the living creatures of the Chariot." Thus far its words.

And the intent: when the Head Stone ascends to her father's house, in the secret of Chokhmah, to this path, then there is the withdrawal of their effluence and the concealment of the Shekhinah from them completely, until they ask, "Where is the place of His glory, to adore Him?" For she is the Shekhinah, called כבו"ד [kavod, glory] after the thirty-two. And for this reason this path is called wondrous, because of its great concealment, as expounded. It is further called "wondrous": explanation: crowned with the Keter, which is called "wondrous and covered." And in this concealed path is the aspect of the union of Chokhmah in Keter, and therefore it is called wondrous. And there is no doubt that this path is the very self of Chokhmah itself, that is to say, the self of Chokhmah; which is not so with the other paths, which are branches spreading from Chokhmah. And therefore this path includes all the paths, and it is a point from which all of them draw, because it is cause to all the paths; and therefore it is the cause of their subsistence. And through this path is the union of Chokhmah with Binah; and not [only] union, but literal coupling. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (folio 61b), and these are its words: "Come and see: it is written (Gen. 2:10), 'And a river goes out from Eden to water the garden.' This river spreads to its sides at the time that this Eden couples with it in complete coupling, in that path which is not known above and below, as it is written, 'a path that no bird of prey knows,'" etc. Thus far its words.

And we copied it at length in Gate Eight, chapter 17. And for our matter it is explained from within it that the union of Eden, which is Chokhmah, with the river, which is Binah, is through the concealed path. And there is no difficulty from what was explained in the gate mentioned, that the union of Chokhmah and Binah is through Da'at; because Da'at and this path are all one matter. For the principal drawing-forth of Da'at is from the aspect of Chokhmah with Keter, which is the path mentioned, as we explained in Gate Three, chapter 8, where he spoke of the matter of the third brain, drawn from above to the head of Zeir Anpin; see there. And likewise it is possible to say that when Da'at ascends to this aspect, which is this path, it unites them. And through this path was the emanation of the whole Emanation, which is included in the four-letter name YHVH, which are Chokhmah, Binah, Tiferet, Malkhut. And so it is hinted in the verse: "In the beginning" [bereshit], whose hint is Chokhmah, from Keter, in Keter; "Elohim created": this is Binah; "the heavens": this is Tiferet; "and the earth": this is Malkhut. He further said: "And it is the primordial intelligible light": explanation: a light composed of two aspects of two sefirot, which are Keter and Chokhmah; and therefore it is called "intelligible" from the side of Chokhmah, as we explained above, and "primordial" from the side of Keter, which is what is called primordial. "And it is the first glory": explanation: everything called kavod is so from the side of the totality of the thirty-two, as we explained; therefore this path, because it includes all the paths, is called kavod. But it is the first, and the cause of all that comes under the name kavod, for from it is the source of the thirty-two, as we explained. And there is a distinction between kavod and lev, as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, under the entries kavod and lev.

Path 2: Rashbi explained this path (in the Zohar) [in the Tikkunim mentioned], and these are his words: "The second path: 'And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters.' What is 'and the spirit'? At the time that the Shekhinah is in exile, this spirit blows upon those who engage in the Torah, because of the Shekhinah that is found among them. And this spirit becomes a voice," etc. Thus far its words.

His intent is to say that this spirit is what pours effluence upon the Shekhinah, and illumines her, and moistens her from the waters of Chesed; and through this the masters of Torah, among whom the Shekhinah dwells, receive effluence. And therefore they called this path "the resplendent intellect," whose explanation is: it makes the Shekhinah resplendent with the radiance of Chokhmah. And Rabbi Yosef said that because the first path is called Nothing, and coming-to-be and creation have no revealing in it, but [only] from the second path, which is Something, therefore this path is called "the crown of creation." And it seems that it is called so for the reason that in the first path is the matter of the Emanation, as we explained above, and this path is to illumine Malkhut, as we explained and as will be explained; therefore it is called "the crown of creation," for Malkhut is a crown to creation, and she is head to all the created entities. For the whole substance of creation was created only from her, as will be explained in the Gate of ABYA. "And the radiance of the equal unity": as we explained, it is radiance to Malkhut, which is called "the equal unity," because she makes the attributes equal, unifies them, and binds them. And some say "the equal unity" is the Supernal Keter, for it is one, equal on all its sides, and it is the One above which there is not even the count of one, as we explained in the preceding gates. And this second path is the radiance drawn from it, "exalted as head over all." If in Keter, its explanation is that Keter is the true, equal light, and this radiance is drawn from it, and it is head over all, as explained. If in Malkhut, it will likewise be explained, for of her it is said (1 Chron. 29:11): "Yours, O Lord, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all." And the explanation: through this path she is exalted as head over all, because this path is Something from Nothing. And through this path is the abolishing of the husks and their subjugation, and the removal of idols from the earth. And the verse explained this in saying (Gen. 1:2), "And the earth was formlessness and void, and darkness": these are three hard husks, which correspond to the three colors of the rainbow, as we shall explain in the Gate of Substitutes, chapter 6. And he said that the earth, which is Malkhut, was clothed in these husks; but the second path, which is the spirit of God, hovers over the face of the waters, the waters of Chesed, so that a thread of Chesed is drawn over Esther, to remove the greenness of judgment from her face; and through her the husks are burned away. These are a summary of the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim mentioned. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, called this path the holy spirit, because Malkhut, from the side of Chokhmah, is called the holy spirit, as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles; and this is through this path, which is drawn from Chokhmah upon her. And likewise he said there that this path is the spirit of the Lord that is drawn upon the Messiah: "the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord" (Isa. 11:2).

Path 3 is called the sanctified intellect. We have already explained concerning the two preceding paths that one of them, the wondrous intellect, resembles the Emanator, and the second, the resplendent intellect, resembles Keter, as explained in the two preceding paths. And this third resembles Chokhmah; and therefore it is called the sanctified intellect, for all holiness is in Chokhmah. For the order of the paths is: the first ten correspond to the ten sefirot, and twenty-two correspond to the twenty-two letters, as we shall explain. And because each one of the sefirot that is below is a mirror to what is above it, therefore the first path makes known the greatness of the Emanator, and therefore the matter of the Emanation is in it, as explained; and the second path makes known the power of Keter; and the third makes known the power of Chokhmah; and so in this order until their completion. He further said, "And it is the foundation of primeval wisdom," to indicate what was expounded. For the first path is the aspect [of Chokhmah] that is unified with Keter, which is in Keter; and the second path, the aspect of its self, makes known and shows the greatness of Keter; and the third, its aspect that pours forth effluence toward Binah, makes known the self, the inwardness, and the foundation of Chokhmah. He further said: "which is called emunah omen": explanation: Binah is called emunah, for she is fostered [emunah] and raised by Chokhmah; and Chokhmah is omen, her fosterer and the one who raises her. Or it is possible that emunah is related to Malkhut, for she too is fostered and raised by Chokhmah, as we shall explain in the Gate of Manifestations. And in the words of Rashbi (there): "'And God said, Let there be light [or]': let there be air [avir]: light [or] [with] Yod. And when this point is wrapped in this light and becomes air, from here all the beings are drawn." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: the creation of the world was through Chokhmah, and it is an explicit verse (Ps. 104:24): "In wisdom You have made them all." But all was through Binah, as explained in the preceding chapter. And the matter is that Chokhmah was clothed in Binah, and through Binah the beings were drawn. And they are the five [mentions of] "light" in this passage, the hint to Binah, which is the first Heh of the Name; and so Rashbi explained in this inquiry there. And the clothing and wrapping of Chokhmah in Binah is hinted by avir, which is Yod, that is, Chokhmah, wrapped in or, which is Binah. And because Keter is unified with them and shines in them at the time of their union, and it includes the two of them together, therefore avir hints at it. And it is likewise called "the tower that flies in the air," for it flies and swims over the two of them; although this name is also related to Binah, because Tiferet too is called avir, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And the intent is that through this path the beings are drawn at the time of the union of Binah and Chokhmah.

Path 4 is called the fixed intellect, etc. And Rabbi Yosef, of blessed memory, explained: all the powers in it were emanated from it in the subtlety of the emanation. Just as the form of the building, in the subtlety of its depiction, is in the thought of the builder, and that subtle form is the cause of the building, so it is with this path: the subtlety of the emanation that is in it is the cause of the drawing forth of the revealed Emanation, "by the power of the Primordial Emanator": explanation: for this path is by the power of the first path, which is called primordial. And it has already been explained that this path reveals what is within Binah. And behold, in Binah are the sefirot in subtlety, that is to say, the six extremities. And in the verse: "And God saw the light."

Behold, this light is Tiferet; for the two preceding luminaries are Gedulah and Gevurah. And he said that this path showed and set right the reason of this light, which is what includes the six extremities, as is known. And by this path the light was stored away for the righteous in the time to come; and it is known that the light of the righteous one is Tiferet, and it was stored away for the time to come, which is Binah. All this is a complete indication of our intent.

Path 5 is called the rooted intellect. The intent is that the roots of Malkhut are fixed in this path, because the principal of Malkhut is from Chokhmah, for there is her house, and there her roots, and from there her manifestation, hinted in the Yod, as will be explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And therefore the beginning of her being taken from the man, in the manifestation of the rib, is from this path.

And behold, according to the way of the paths, this path reveals what is in Chesed. And it is known that the matter of the taking of the rib was through Chesed, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and we shall explain it in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon, chapter 4. And it is called "rooted" because the roots of Malkhut, [that is,] her taking, were from it, as explained. And Malkhut is called "the equal unity," as we explained above in path 2. And it is called nishrash, in the passive form, because it is acted upon by the roots of Malkhut; "and it is unified in the substance of Binah." And it has already been explained that the preceding path reveals the power of Binah, and this path reveals the power of Chesed.

So it turns out [to be] "unified in the substance of Binah" in the union of Chesed with Binah. And besides this, this path hints at Malkhut, and the preceding path hints at Tiferet; if so, the two of them turn out to be unified in the union of Tiferet and Malkhut. And in the verse: "And God divided between the light and between the darkness": for the light is Tiferet and the darkness is Malkhut, and through it was their division, as we explained. And Rashbi has another way in it: this path divides between the light, [which is] Chesed, and the darkness that is in Gevurah. For from the side of the darkness [that is in Gevurah] there is no arbitration at all; rather it is divided from holiness, as we explained in the Gate of Colors, chapter 3. And it is what divides between impurity and purity everywhere; and it is an explicit verse, "And God divided between," etc.: between the light of the right and the darkness of the wicked. And there is no doubt that this matter is by the power of Tiferet and Malkhut; for Rashbi explicitly explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 116b) that just as the central pillar unites in the extremities of holiness, so it divides between the outer ones. And behold, the union in the right and in holiness is through Tiferet and Malkhut, as we explained in Gate Nine, chapter 3; if so, the two of them turn out to divide between the light, that is, holiness, and the outer left. And by this our words are true together with the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him; and there are seventy faces to the Torah.

Path 6: the separate intellect. And there are those who read "separate effluence" [shefa nivdal]; and the explanation is that it pours forth to all the grades the increase of this effluence that increases in it. And in the verse: "And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night," etc. And this darkness is not like the darkness mentioned above; for there is impure darkness and pure darkness, and this matter is explained in the Gate of Colors. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30), and these are his words: "And there is darkness from the side of purity, etc.; this is what is written (Ps. 139:12): 'Even darkness is not dark for You,' etc. And darkness is the female, who receives from the light, which is male light, like the moon, which receives from the sun. And the two of them are the speculum that shines and the speculum that does not shine. And there is darkness of the Other Side, in which there is division and not joining." Thus far its words.

He taught explicitly that they are two kinds of darkness, one impure and one pure: the impure one is that of which division is said. And he doubled [his words] in saying "in which there is division and not joining," because there is already division in holiness itself, in the matter of the diminishment; but it is a division after which there is joining and union. But impurity and the husk have no joining ever. And the darkness of purity is called night, and it is Malkhut, which is called the attribute of night, and she receives from the day. And all the more so since she is called לילה [laylah], whose explanation is ליל ה' [the night of Heh], for she is adorned for the union, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2. And the sense of the verse: "And God called the light Day": this is Tiferet, which is light; and He called it and set it right as day, that is, its aspect to pour effluence into the night. "And the darkness He called Night": that is to say, Malkhut, who is darkened, He set right and adorned in her aspect called night, so that the attribute of day may be able to unite with the attribute of night, and the attribute of night with the attribute of day.

And behold, the day and the night are twenty-four hours, twelve and twelve: this [ז"ה, 12] receives from this [ז"ה], twelve from twelve. And that is, that at times the night grows longer and at times the day grows longer, for sometimes the male prevails and sometimes the female prevails. And this is (Isa. 6:3): "And this called to this," which the Targum renders "and they receive from one another." So it turns out that the tikkun of these attributes and their adornment is through this path. And therefore it is called "separate," since its effluence is to set right Tiferet and Malkhut, which are separate from one another. And it is known that in the union of Tiferet and Malkhut and their receiving, all the sefirot receive; and therefore this path "pours that effluence upon all the pools that are unified in its substance": explanation: that are unified through them, that is, the sefirot, which are unified through Tiferet and Malkhut.

Path 7 is called the hidden intellect. The name "hidden" [nistar] is attributed only to a thing that was revealed and afterwards hidden. That is to say: a thing that is sometimes revealed and sometimes hidden is called hidden; and a thing that is not revealed at all is not called hidden, but concealed [ne'lam] or wondrous [nifla] and the like; and this is clear. And this path is called hidden because at times it is revealed, to pour effluence to the intellective ones and the powers that are unified in their roots, which are in Malkhut; and she is what is called emunah, as explained above in path 3, and as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And in the verse: "And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between waters and waters."

And behold, this firmament is Metatron, who is the messenger of Tiferet, and through him is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut on the six weekdays, as will be explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapters 6, 7, and 8. And he divides between pure waters and strange waters, because "her feet [that is, Metatron's] go down to death" (Prov. 5:5), as is known, and as will be explained in the Gate of Substitutes, chapter 6. And therefore the division is through this path, for it fences him in before the violent beasts.

Path 8 is called the complete intellect. In order to understand the matter of this path, one must first set out that Tiferet and Yesod receive effluence from Binah, and the ascent of both of them is there. The illustration: like the organ of generation, which draws its power by way of the spinal cord, and by a concealed way its ascent is up to the brain. And all this is to indicate that it will be whole at its head, [joined] to the one ring, which is Binah. And the witness to this is the two bones of the arm, which are one above the other: when a man folds his arm he will find the two bones unified at the one ring, which is the upper joint, to indicate that the two Vavs have their head toward Binah. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained all this in the Tikkunim there. And likewise the Zohar explained (in Parashat Balak, folio 204; see there) that the emanation of Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut is from Binah. So according to this it turns out that a man cannot attain the substance of the emanation of Yesod except in Binah, which is "the chambers of Gedulah"; for there are no chambers except in Binah, and she is over Gedulah, and its chambers are there. And when he ascends to the chambers of Gedulah, there, in substance, they will understand the root of Yesod, and there he will see that this path pours effluence upon it and sustains it. And this is "And God made the firmament": which is the Righteous One, which is a firmament dividing between male waters and female waters, for these are above it and these below it. And this is the beginning of the diminishment, on the second day, on which the luminaries were created, although they were not hung until the fourth day. And by this matter that we have explained, the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and the words of the commentators are brought to a compromise together. And it is called "complete" [shalem] because it completes and prepares Yesod, called shalom [peace]; and Yesod is "the disposition of primordiality," which a man cannot attain in its manifestation except "in the chambers of Gedulah," which are in Binah; for those chambers "are emanated from the substance of the subsistence" of Yesod, [through] this path, which emanates it and sustains it. Up to here the explanation of eight paths in one chapter.
(In this chapter eight further paths are explained.)

Path 9 is called the pure intellect. Because through this path Tiferet has the power to give life to the six extremities, to include them in itself, and to unify them, as in the matter that is written (1 Chron. 29:11), "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness," etc.; and that name hints at Tiferet, to confirm the explanation. And there is no question how it can be counted twice, for it has two aspects: an aspect that includes all six extremities, and this is that it is called "heavens," which includes the whole Emanation [the extremities]; and the aspect of itself, and it is called "firmament." And this is "And God called the firmament Heaven," as we explained in Gate One, chapter 2, in the name of Rashbi; see there. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained all the matters of these firmaments explicitly in the Tikkunim. And it is called "purifying" because it purifies them from the rust of transgressions. And of this it is said, "and may Your compassion roll over Your attributes," for it is what receives the most compassion from the Supernal Keter.

Path 10 is called the refined intellect. Through this path all the effluence is gathered to Tiferet, and it rises (to receive it) up to Binah, and from there it is included with all the sefirot, and it does not pour effluence to Malkhut, as we explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, under the entry hoy. And so the verse is explained, in the way of Rashbi, peace be upon him: "And God said, Let the waters be gathered": that is to say, let the waters, which are the effluence, be gathered "from under the heavens": explanation: Malkhut, which is under Tiferet, called heavens. And the matter of "be gathered": explanation: let the effluence rise and be gathered from her "to one place" [מקו"ם, makom], which is Tiferet. And so the four-letter name amounts to makom. How? Yod times Yod is a hundred; Heh times Heh is twenty-five; Vav times Vav is thirty-six; Heh times Heh is twenty-five: all together it comes to 186, the number of makom. And it is called "one" [אחד] in the union of ten sefirot. How? Alef: Keter; Chet: eight sefirot; Dalet: Malkhut; and they are all included in it together. And the matter of the withdrawal of the effluence from Malkhut, in the strength of judgment, is this path, called refined, whose explanation is judgment, as we explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. Or he means that "refined" includes all the attributes and the Tzachtzachot with regard to withdrawal, as we explained there. And behold, this path becomes a heavenly curtain and a partition to hold back the effluence because of the strength of its judgment; and the effluence rises, and the dry land appears, and above there becomes a gathering of waters, so that the effluence does not descend, God forbid; and so the strength of judgment is found, and the world is lost, and the sword avenges the vengeance of the covenant of the Torah, God forbid, until the Lord looks down and sees from heaven (Lam. 3:50).

Path 11 is called the sparkling intellect. And it is the sparkling of Tiferet to Malkhut, through its drawing sustenance from the milk of the mother. And what was dry land, in the secret of the heat and dryness of fire and judgment, becomes אר"ץ [eretz, earth], from the language of ratzon [will]. And this is the explanation of the verse: "And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters He called Seas": explanation: Tiferet, which is the gathering of the waters, He called, unified, and made to pour effluence to the lower seas that are in Malkhut. And all this tikkun and appeasement is through repentance, that is, through path 12, as we shall explain. And the Prince of the Countenance is Malkhut, for she is the prince of the face of the sefirot, for they all shine in her; and all this goodness and compassion is through the effluence that this path pours from its holy dwelling. And it opens the channels and raises Tiferet to receive simple compassion, and it spreads in all the sefirot. And behold, these two paths we have reversed, the eleventh to the tenth and the tenth to the eleventh, in order to settle them with the order of the verses and the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, on the paths, as we explained.

Path 12 is called the bright intellect, etc. And it is called so because from its great brightness it pours brightness into Malkhut; and the prophets gaze into her to apprehend the upper grades that are seen in her. And from there they understand and discern "for what the land was lost" (Jer. 9:11), and they turn the people back from their evil way. And through this path they are received in repentance, as in the matter (Ezek. 1:8) "and the hands of a man under their wings"; and likewise His right hand is stretched out to receive those who return. And this is "And God saw that it was good": this "good" is to complete the lack of goodness that was on the second day because of the strength of its Gevurah, and to moisten the dryness of the earth. And close to this matter it is explained in the Tikkunim, Tikkun 43 (folio 82a), and these are its words: "'And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass,' etc. Rabbi Elazar said: Father, but behold, He called it dry land; whence 'let the earth bring forth'? He said to him: My son, here He teaches repentance to the children of the world. For if a person returns in repentance, the flow that had withdrawn comes down to it, and what was dry land He called earth; and the river that was waste and dry He called the gathering of the waters, and seas. This is what is written: 'And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters He called Seas.' At that time when it is called earth, what is written of it? 'And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass.'" Thus far its words, for our matter. Behold, from this passage there is a proof of the order of the paths, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth, and there is no doubt in them. And Malkhut is called Chazchazit, for there is "the valley of vision" (Isa. 22:1).

Path 13 is called the intellect that guides the unity, etc. After the compassion is poured forth through the path called the sparkling intellect, which is the eleventh, and the female conceives, there is still need of power from this path, called "the one that guides the unity," which is Malkhut, for she is what unifies all the sefirot, as we explained. And through this path she brings out into actuality the subtle and spiritual things and the souls that are in her. And by its power Malkhut completes all things, for it is what makes grass sprout from the earth. And this is what is written: "And God said, Let the earth," which is Malkhut, "bring forth grass," which is the beings of the powers that are in her; "herb," etc.: Tiferet is called so, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles; "fruit tree": Yesod. And through this path is "and the earth brought forth," etc.

Path 14 is called the illuminating intellect. And it is the path through which the Chashmal came to be, which is the matter that bears (the forms that are said) [the forms and the visions]. And in it all the forms were impressed, from the power of Malkhut, into a more revealed manifestation; and they are the living creatures of the Chariot. And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Chagigah 13b): "What is Chashmal? Living creatures of fire that speak"; and they are under the Throne, and in them the secrets are explained and the visions revealed. And this is "And God saw that it was good"; and the explanation is the teaching of things and their illumination, from the language (Exod. 30:7) "when he tends [be-heitivo] the lamps."

Path 15 is called the establishing intellect, etc. The intent is that the Shekhinah is called arafel [thick cloud] from the side of her drawing sustenance from the left, which is the strength of judgment; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And she is called "the substance of creation," for she is the cause of creation, and in her very self the created entities were created. And through this path she enters into her drawing of sustenance from judgment; and the created entities are gathered in by the strength of judgment. And for this reason it comes in the verse "And God said, Let there be luminaries [מארת]," defective, without Vav, to indicate the curse [me'erah], and the tumult, the rebuke, and the croup among the children, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said; and the division of the day and the night, for she lacks light. And she is bitter, like a poor woman separated from her husband. And this is the cause of the festivals: for at a time when joy is present, it will be through her; and when the light is lacking, there will be weekday, and night, and the lack of the moon, until the Lord has compassion and restores the diadem to its former state.

Path 16 is called the eternal intellect, etc. The matter is that just as the lack of the moon is on the fourth day, so its fullness and its tikkun are on that very day. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in [his commentary on] the Song of Songs (in Zohar Chadash, folio 82): that a virgin is married on the fourth day, to show that the rising of the Virgin of Israel is on the fourth day. And a heavenly voice proclaims in the household above (Mic. 7:8): "Rejoice not against me, O my enemy; though I have fallen, I have risen": rising on the day of falling. And likewise in this verse [text: "path"], "the two luminaries": it is falling, from the small luminary; it is rising, from the great luminary. And in the place where she fell, there she will rise, through the path itself. And this is what he said: "the bliss of the glory, for there is no glory below it": explanation: this path is the cause of the bliss, for the bliss depends on the filling of the moon, and the lack is the cause of Gehinnom. And "the bliss of the glory, for there is no," etc., is Malkhut, and her bliss will be because of the path itself. And it is called "eternal" [nitzchi] from the language of victory [netzichah], for the side of compassion will be victorious, so that she rises to her height, for there is her house, and she will not descend again. And it is what is called the Garden of Eden: explanation: for Malkhut is called the Garden of Eden for the pious, etc.; and the true Eden is only in the filling of the moon. Up to here the explanation of eight paths.
In this chapter too eight further paths are explained.

And there are those who wanted to say that sixteen paths are for the governance of the upper ones and the remaining sixteen are for the governance of the lower ones. And the matter does not settle at all, neither in the sefirot nor in the paths; for all of them are in the upper ones and all of them in the lower ones, as is evident in the work of creation, which is explained wholly in Atzilut, and likewise wholly in Yetzirah, and likewise wholly in Asiyah; and there is no room to divide.

Path 17 is called the intellect of sensation. And this is the matter: in the Garden of Eden the souls of the righteous are clothed in a garment like the likeness of the body that they had in this world. And there is [a soul] that is clothed at its ascent, and there is [one] that is delayed some time until it is clothed, all according to the merit of the soul and its deeds. And that garment comes to be from the light of the Garden, which is Malkhut. And so it is said (Esth. 8:15 [text: 5:1]), "And Mordecai went out from before the king in royal [malkhut] apparel"; and likewise (Esth. 5:1), "And Esther clothed herself in royalty [malkhut]." The intent is to hint that they merited to be clothed in the pure garment in which the righteous are clothed in the Garden of Eden, and they saw their world in their lifetime. And to this God, blessed be He, hinted to Moses (Exod. 3:5): "Remove your shoes," which is the stripping off of the body.

And behold, the air from which the righteous are clothed in the Garden of Eden is through this path. And it is called "sensation" because it is what clothes the righteous with something sensed, the likeness of the body. And it is called "the foundation of Tiferet": for the foundation of Tiferet is (Binah) [Yesod], and the Garden is Malkhut, and the World to Come is Binah. And the matter is that the scent of Binah flows to Malkhut, and from her the souls are clothed; and the principal flow is through Yesod, and there is the station of the souls. And this is what it says: "And God set them in the firmament of the heaven." And our Sages, of blessed memory, explained that this verse is said of the righteous; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that the righteous are in Yesod, which is the firmament of the heaven. "To give light upon the earth": the intent is to pour effluence to Malkhut. For the souls of the righteous are channels for the effluence, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 5. "And to rule over the day," etc.: the righteous rule over the sun, which is the day, and the moon, which is the night, like Joshua (Josh. 10:12): "Sun, stand still at Gibeon," etc. And so our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (in Bereshit Rabbah, section 6). And all is by the power of this path, which makes them rule over the created entities by its power.

Path 18 is called the intellect of the house of effluence. Explanation: when all the effects look to their cause, much effluence and blessing is drawn to them from this path. And if so, it must be that all who cleave to it and investigate its self receive much good. And this is what it says: "And God saw that it was good," like (Exod. 30:7) "when he tends [be-heitivo] the lamps"; for it is what does good to and illumines all who dwell in its shadow. And therefore it is called the house of effluence, for it is the principal effluence, as we explained.

Path 19 is called the intellect of the secret of the spiritual actions, etc. Explanation: through this path the effluence that flows from the path we mentioned above is transformed into the nature of the one that receives it. And the illustration of this: like the liver, which cooks all the food into the nature of the body, and from there, by way of the veins, that blood is transformed for each one according to its nature. So through the preceding path a general effluence flows to all that need it; but through this second path it is transformed into the nature of each recipient, each according to its power. And this is hinted in the verse: "And God said, Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures."

And behold, the waters made each and every one swarm after its kind, even the bird, which is from the marsh. So this path made each and every thing swarm according to its nature. And at times also the effluence of the souls: and through this path souls and kinds of emanated ones swarm in the upper sea, each one according to its nature and its root; as in the matter of the souls, according to their separation in the sefirot, each to its root: there is the wise in Chokhmah, and the understanding in Binah, and the pious in Chesed, and likewise for the other attributes. And likewise the angels, such as Chasdiel and Michael from Chesed, Gabriel and Daniel from Gevurah, Uriel and Rachmiel from Tiferet, and in this way for each and every sefirah. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 45, folio 82b) (and in the Introduction to the Zohar, folio 12) on this verse.

Path 20 is called the intellect of the will, etc. The matter is that when some being comes to be in this world, as we said of the upper souls, it is necessary that the source of its blessing be in the upper world, for from there "all flesh is fed."

And behold, as for the dependence of all things, that is to say, the beings and the souls that are emanated: the dependence of their concealment must be on this path. And in this path they are found as a likeness, subtle to the utmost subtlety, like the illustration of the builder that we explained at the fourth path. And there is a distinction between this path and the fourth path: for the fourth path is the root of the powers emanated at the beginning of the six days of creation, and this is the dependence of the effects on the will of their Emanator, from these waters mentioned above, which are things in themselves. And this is "And God created," etc.: the things that the waters made swarm.

Path 21 is called the intellect of the sought delight. Explanation: through it all the things created in the intellect of the will that we mentioned receive effluence; and through it [their growth] flows below, in their place, in the way of "there is not a single blade of grass below," etc., which our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded (in Bereshit Rabbah, section 20) on the verse (Job 38:33) "Can you establish its rule on the earth?"

And behold, this path receives from their source, which is in the Godhead, and pours forth to all those created entities that are below. And this is "And God saw that it was good," in the way we explained.

Path 22 is called the faithful intellect. Explanation: through this path the upper things increase, to keep their faith with the lower ones, for all that they beget after them; as it has been explained that the things of holiness increase from time to time, without measure or end. And this is what the verse says: "And God blessed them, and God said to them, Be fruitful and multiply."

Path 23 is called the enduring intellect, etc. Know that all the things created in the world are a mold and shadow of the upper world, even of the kind of the cattle and the beast and everything. And this is the reason for the forbidden and the permitted: for the image of the forbidden is on the side of impurity, and the image of the permitted is on the side of purity; and in this way also the fit and the unfit, the pure and the impure. And just as there are upper sefirot, so there are lower sefirot, in world, year, soul [עול"ם שנ"ה נפ"ש], and their mnemonic is עש"ן [ashan].

And behold, before the creation of the lower ones, the coming-to-be of the sustaining power was necessary. And their power is through this path, and it is "the power of subsistence" of the lower sefirot, as we shall explain their matter in the Gate of ABYA. And in the verse: "And God said, Let the earth bring forth": the earth is Malkhut, and the matter of the bringing forth is the bringing forth of the power of the things; for the things themselves are through the other path.

Path 24 is called the imaginative intellect, etc. Explanation: it makes the things according to what befits their power, which was emanated from the upper earth mentioned above in path 23. And this is because at this path it says "And God made," for making is the becoming-corporeal of the things; and their power is like a soul to the spirit that is made. Up to here the explanation of eight paths.
In this chapter eight further paths are explained.

Path 25 is called the intellect of trial, etc. The matter is that this path necessitates the trial of the righteous and the pious, like Abraham our father, peace be upon him. And all kinds of created entities, such as the angels and the seraphim, are at times punished, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Chagigah 15a) in the matter of Elisha Acher, that they struck Metatron sixty lashes of fire; and likewise concerning Rabbi Chiyya, that they struck Elijah (Bava Metzia 85b); and likewise it is found in the Baraita of Rabbi Ishmael, peace be upon him, that the angels were punished when they did not make their melody right in the Kedushah. And their trial flows from this path. And this is what it says: "And God saw that it was good": the intent is, He tried them and saw them good and strong, quick and good in their service, and standing in their trial.

Path 26 is called the perceptible intellect, etc. The matter is that the intellect of man was created from the source of Chokhmah. And so it is explained in Midrash Ruth (from Zohar Chadash, folio 92), and these are its words: "He opened and said (Ps. 104:24): 'How many are Your works, O Lord; in wisdom You have made them all,' etc. The whole world came only through wisdom, and the human being is filled with everything. The other creatures are in the form (another version: in the addition) of the wisdom that remained in the human being. And although all the creatures are so, there was no creature light enough to pursue after the deeds of human beings, like the bird," etc.; see there. Thus far its words.

Behold, explicitly: the intellect of man flows from Chokhmah, and from the surplus of man it flows to the other creatures. And this is intended in this verse: "And God said, Let us make man in our image," etc.: the intent is to knowledge [da'at]. And so it is said when he sinned (Gen. 3:22): "Behold, the man has become like one of us, to know [לדע"ת]." And the intent is that the image and likeness of man flows from Chokhmah, from this path, which is the intellect; and for this reason it is called "perceptible" [murgash]: explanation: it was perceived in this world.

Path 27 is called the corporeal intellect, etc. It is known that the body of man is in measure and weight, and all its limbs in a supernal disposition, so that it is a shadow of the upper ones, "each man at his service and at his burden" (Num. 4:19), to be a shadow over his head, the likeness of the upper world, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 8. And behold, its shape is outlined with a compass by the fingers of the hand of its Creator, through this path. And behold, through it the limbs keep their measure and their disposition, so that it does not lengthen or shorten from the proportion that the Maker outlined for them. And this is "And God created man in His image." And there is no doubt that through this path is the form of the embryo in its mother's womb.

Path 28 is called the natural intellect, etc. The completion of nature is through the female; for so our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yevamot 63a) on what the verse said (Gen. 5:2), "Male and female He created them, and He called their name Adam": both of them together are a complete Adam.

And behold, the woman is for the subsistence of nature in the human species, as is known. And likewise all the upper things are male and female, like the sun and the moon. And this is what the verse says: "In the image of God He created him; male and female He created them." And there is no doubt that through this path are the couplings of man, whether first or second.

Path 29 is called the general intellect, etc. The intent is that the Holy One, blessed be He, in His compassion, poured forth to man intellect in concealed knowledge concerning the motion of the heavens and the spheres and their powers that move them; and likewise the angels of the seasons, the months, the days, and the constellations, for each one of them has a power and an angel that moves it. And of this it is said (Deut. 4:6), "For this is your wisdom and your understanding," and our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat 75a): "these are the seasons," etc. And not concerning the false astronomy that Euclid invented in his foolishness, but the true astronomy, which was known to the Sages, of blessed memory, as in the matter that is expounded somewhat in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer and in Pirkei Ma'aseh Bereshit; for this was certainly "wisdom in the eyes of the nations." And through it man knows the governance of the world in the future. And this is "And God blessed them": explanation: He poured forth to them knowledge of the seasons, and other matters, and concealed knowledge.

Path 30 is called the perpetual intellect, etc. The intent is that the motion of the spheres and their course is through this path, for it is what gives power and strength to the one that moves them. And He stipulated with them that they be subject to those who fear the Lord and think of His name. And this is "And God said to them," etc., "and have dominion over the fish of the sea," etc.: the intent is that He gave him dominion even over the angels emanated from the upper earth, for they are what move the spheres.

Path 31 is called the served intellect, etc. The intent is that the knowledge of concealed things is through the things revealed in this world. And the illustration of this: when we wish to know the nature of the moon, we examine the lower actions that are drawn from it; and when we see that cold things grow by its power, we know that it is cold in its nature; and likewise the test for the sun, and likewise even for the emanated things. And this is what the verse meant in saying, "And God said, Behold, I have given you all," etc., "for food [לאכל"ה]": the intent in "eating" is the knowledge of the hidden things from the revealed ones. And all is through this path.

Path 32 is called the renewed intellect, etc. The intent is that through it the Holy One, blessed be He, sends effluence to all the emanated ones, so that they are renewed as at the beginning of their creation; as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot 59b) concerning the sun, that from twenty-eight years to twenty-eight years it returns in its cycle as at the beginning of the work of creation, and a blessing is said over it. And likewise the things among the emanated, created, formed, and made ones: all of them are renewed from time to time; and all is through this path. And this is what the verse says: "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good." And he said "very" to indicate the renewal by which they are renewed, which is the goodness beyond the goodness of creation. And in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (folio 68b), Rabbi Elazar explained on the verse "And God saw all that He had made": "that He looked," etc., "at all in one totality, above and below," etc. Thus far its words. This teaches all that we have explained.
Up to here reaches the explanation of all the paths. And with this this Gate is completed and concluded; and praise to the true God.
The Thirteenth Gate: The Gate Called Gates.
What is intended in this Gate is to explain the matter of the fifty gates attributed to Binah, as all the Kabbalists, early and late, explained them; and the reason for their number and their matter.
Chapter One:

Rashbi explained in many places that the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned fifty times in the Torah, corresponding to the fifty gates of Binah. And these are his words (in Tikkun 39, folio 77): "'I am the Lord your God,' etc. Rabbi Elazar said: Father, if someone is under the bondage of his master, and his master promised him to bring him out to freedom, and brought him out, is he to praise himself for having brought him out of bondage? And behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Abraham (Gen. 15:13), 'Know surely that your seed shall be a stranger,' etc.; and behold, He promised to bring his children out of exile, as it is written (Gen. 15:14), 'and afterwards they shall come out with great substance'; and He praises Himself many times, 'who brought you out of the land of Egypt.' He said to him: My son, you have spoken well; but this is not to praise Himself. Rather, each and every sefirah is called head to its fellow. And in order to make known to them from what place He brought them out of bondage, He opened with Anokhi ['I'] and mentioned in it 'who brought you out of the land of Egypt,' etc., fifty times, corresponding to the fifty gates of Binah." Thus far its words.

And behold, clearly the many mentions of the Exodus from Egypt in the Torah were a difficulty for Rabbi Elazar. And Rabbi Shimon his father answered him that the intent is not to praise Himself, God forbid, but the intent is to make known to them from what place their redemption was. And therefore the Exodus from Egypt was written fifty times in the Torah, corresponding to the fifty gates that are in Binah. And the intent is that each and every verse in the Torah teaches us one gate, what its fellow did not reveal; and therefore it had to be written in the Torah fifty times, in order to show us the power of the fifty gates of Binah and their spirituality. And there is room to object: since the intent of the fifty times was only to show us that He brought them out by the power of Binah, it would be fitting that He mention the matter in one of the words that hints at Binah, and so teach us that their going out was by the power of Binah. And one cannot say that in each and every verse in which it is mentioned He revealed to us one gate that its fellow did not reveal, and therefore it had to be mentioned fifty times; because this does not suffice for Rabbi Elazar's question: for in the end it would have been fitting that He indicate by one word or one title that the Exodus from Egypt was by the power of Binah, and reveal the gates in another way, and not in a manner that would make it difficult for us that He praises Himself. Rather, certainly the intent in Rabbi Shimon's answer is that it was necessary to pour effluence from all the gates in order to bring them out of Egypt; and if He had not poured effluence from all of them, it would not have been possible for them to go out in any way in the world. And therefore the Exodus from Egypt had to be mentioned fifty times, to show the effluence of the fifty gates of Binah to the redemption; and what one gate poured forth, its fellow did not pour forth. And so we can infer somewhat from within the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who said: "And in order to make known to them from what place He brought them out of bondage, He opened with Anokhi": explanation: to make known to them that their redemption was from Binah, He said Anokhi, whose hint is to Binah. "But He mentioned in it 'who brought you out of the land of Egypt' fifty times, corresponding," etc.: explanation: He further needed to mention it fifty times, corresponding to the fifty gates, to make known to them that their redemption was from all fifty gates (and so it is in the Zohar, Va-etchanan, folio 62a, in the passage beginning "The second house"). And the reason is that Israel, while they were in Egypt, entered within the husk and abandoned themselves, until the husk ruled over them from fifty gates of husks; and in order to break these husks, effluence had to flow from each and every gate, so as to break all the gates of impurity. For just as there are forty-nine faces pure, so there are forty-nine faces impure; and all of them were enslaving Israel; and therefore they all had to be abolished, one by one, by the power of the fifty gates of Binah. And this is what he said: "Rather, each and every sefirah is called head to its fellow," and rules over it; and what is in the power of this one is not in the power of that one. And therefore, since the gates of impurity are against the gates of purity, it was not in the power of the lower sefirah to nullify what is against the upper one; and therefore it had to be from Binah and from its fifty gates. And when we came to count the verses of the Torah concerning the Exodus from Egypt, we found them to be more than fifty, by eleven. And these are the fifty gates and the eleven extra ones:
1. "And you shall know that the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt": in Parashat Beshalach.
2. "That they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt": there.
3. "That the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt": in the passage "And Jethro heard."
4. "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt": there.
5. "The feast of unleavened bread you shall keep," etc., "for in it you came out of Egypt": Mishpatim.
6. "And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt," etc.: Tetzaveh.
7. "Go, get down, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves": Ki Tissa.
8. "Lord, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt," etc.: there.
9. "Depart, go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt": there.
10. "The feast of unleavened bread you shall keep," etc., "for in the month of Aviv you came out of Egypt": there.
11. "For I am the Lord who brings you up out of the land of Egypt": Shemini.
12. "Just balances," etc., "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt": Kedoshim.
13. "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God," etc.: Emor.
14. "That your generations may know," etc., "when I brought them out of the land of Egypt": there.
15. "You shall not give him your money," etc., "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt": Behar.
16. "For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold as bondmen are sold": there.
17. "For to Me the children of Israel are servants; they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt," etc.: there.
18. "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that you should not be their bondmen": Bechukotai.
19. "And you wept before Him, saying, Why did we come out of Egypt?": Beha'alotekha.
20. "And the Egyptians shall hear, for You brought up this people in Your might from among them": Shelach.
21. "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt," etc.: there.
22. "And He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt": Chukkat.
23. "And why have you brought us up out of Egypt?": there.
24. "God who brings them out of Egypt," etc.: Balak, [Num.] 23.
25. "God who brings him out of Egypt," etc.: Balak, [Num.] 24.
26. "These are the journeys of the children of Israel, who went out of the land of Egypt": there.
28. "But the Lord has taken you, and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt": Va-etchanan.
29. "And He brought you out with His presence, with His great power, out of Egypt": there.
30. "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt": there.
31. "Beware lest you forget the Lord, who brought you out of the land of Egypt," etc.: there.
32. "Then you shall say to your son: We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of Egypt," etc.: there.
33. "And the Lord gave signs and wonders," etc., "and He brought us out from there": there.
34. "But because the Lord loved [you]," etc., "the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you from the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt": there.
35. "You shall surely remember," etc., "the great trials," etc., "by which the Lord your God brought you out": Ekev.
36. "Then your heart be lifted up, and you forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt," etc.: there.
37. "And the Lord said to me: Arise, get down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of Egypt have corrupted themselves": there.
38. "Do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance, whom You redeemed through Your greatness, whom You brought out of Egypt," etc.: there.
39. "Lest the land from which You brought us out say: Because the Lord was not able," etc.: there.
41. "And that prophet," etc., "who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you," etc.: Re'eh.
42. "And you shall stone him with stones, that he die," etc., "who brought you out of the land of Egypt," etc.: there.
43. "And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you," etc.: there.
44. "For in the month of Aviv the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt by night": there.
45. "You shall eat no leavened bread with it," etc., "for in haste you came out of the land of Egypt": there.
46. "That you may remember the day when you came out of the land of Egypt": there.
47. "At the going down of the sun, at the season that you came out of Egypt": there.
48. "And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt": there.
49. "And the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand": Ki Tavo.
50. "But I will remember for them the covenant of the ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt": in Parashat Bechukotai.

These are the fifty gates of Binah hinted in the Torah in the fifty times [it mentions] the Exodus from Egypt (editor's note: the twenty-seventh and the fortieth gates are missing). But we found more than fifty, and they are these that we shall now mention; and they are the eleven extra ones:
1. "In the third month after the children of Israel went out of the land of Egypt": Yitro.
2. "In the second year after they went out of the land of Egypt": Bamidbar.
3. "In the wilderness of Sinai, in the second year after they went out of the land of Egypt," etc.: Beha'alotekha.
