4. "Behold, a people has come out of Egypt; behold, it covers the face of the earth": Balak.
5. "Behold, the people that came out of Egypt": there.
6. "And Aaron the priest went up," etc., "in the fortieth year after the children of Israel went out," etc.: Masei.
7. "These are the testimonies," etc., "which Moses spoke to the children of Israel when they went out of Egypt": Va-etchanan.
8. "Beyond the Jordan," etc., "and the children of Israel, when they went out of Egypt": there.
9. "From the day that you went out of the land of Egypt until you came to this place": Ekev.
10. "Remember what Amalek did to you on the way, when you went out of Egypt": Ki Tetze.
11. "And they shall say: Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of the land of Egypt": Nitzavim.

And we saw a commentator who copied these verses and divided them as we have copied them above, and resolved [the difficulty of] the eleven extra ones; and these are his words: "It seems that the fifty times are the principal, for the foundation established to remember the Exodus from Egypt because of the great miracle. But in the remaining ones the principal intent is not that, but to remember the event that happened at that time, on such-and-such a day of the Exodus from Egypt, or in such-and-such a year from the going out of Egypt, or to remember the people that went out of Egypt; for the intent in them is not to remember the miracle. But in the fifty, the intent in them and their principal is to remember the miracle; and this is 'and you shall know,' etc., 'that your generations may know,' etc., 'you shall surely remember,' and so all of them."

Although in the commentator's division that we wrote in the preceding chapter there is room to reject some of the fifty mentioned and to put others in their place, nevertheless the sage agreed well in his resolution. And we found support for this resolution in the book of the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (folio 83b), and these are its words: "Rabbi Yehudah said: From the day that Israel went out of the land of Egypt until the day that the Torah was given were fifty days. What is the reason? Rabbi Yehudah said: Because of those years of the Jubilee, as it is written (Lev. 25:10), 'And you shall hallow the fiftieth year.' We have learned: Rabbi Shimon said: That Jubilee brought Israel out of Egypt. And if you say: the Jubilee itself? Rather, from the side of the Jubilee. And from the side of the Jubilee judgment was aroused against the Egyptians. And therefore these fifty days were of the Jubilee. We have learned: corresponding to this, the customs of Egypt are said and mentioned fifty times in the Torah, and all of them praises: 'who brought you out of the land of Egypt,' 'and the Lord your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand,' 'for with a mighty hand He brought you out.' And all of them are fifty times, and no more; because all is crowned in the Jubilee, and from the side of the Jubilee all came. And therefore the Torah, which comes from Gevurah, was crowned in the right, as it is written (Deut. 33:2), 'from His right hand a fiery law for them.' And it is taught: there were five voices, and all were seen in them, and included in them, and crowned in this." Thus far its words.

And there is room for doubt in this passage. First: they said that the fifty days between the Exodus from Egypt and the receiving of the Torah correspond to the years of the Jubilee; if so, it would be fitting that there be days in the Jubilee, or years between the giving of the Torah and the Exodus from Egypt. And since the matter is not so, let us say that they do not correspond to the years of the Jubilee, and seek another, more fitting reason for them. Second: that he brought a proof from the verse "And you shall hallow the fiftieth year"; for the fiftieth year is one year alone, the Jubilee, since the last year, which completes the count of fifty, is the Jubilee. If so, what proof does he bring that they are the years of the Jubilee? Third: there is a refutation of the very basis of the matter. Even if we say that the years of the Jubilee are fifty, which are Binah, what is the matter of forty-nine days to the receiving of the Torah, that they did not receive it immediately when they went out? And all the more according to the words of Rabbi Shimon, that all fifty had already been aroused over them, as he goes on to explain; if so, what need was there for this delay? And still the difficulty stands in its place. Fourth: "We have learned: Rabbi Shimon said": what is it doing here? For if it is because he engages with the Jubilee, then let him bring all the words of Rabbi Shimon who engages in it, and they are many. Fifth: they said "that Jubilee": what is "that"? Let him say "the Jubilee brought out," etc., for this is the usual way. Sixth: they said "that Jubilee": he should only have said "the side of the Jubilee brought out," for this is what he concludes, that it is not the Jubilee but the side of the Jubilee; and why say "Jubilee," so that he then needs "and if you say"? Seventh: they said "and from the side of the Jubilee was aroused," etc.: what is it doing here? Eighth: they said "was aroused," which shows that it was aroused, but not that it was literally [the Jubilee], only the arousal. And if it was aroused from the side of the Jubilee, in what was it? Ninth: they said "and therefore fifty days," etc.: what is "and therefore"? Granted, if it were literally the Jubilee, that is "and therefore," for the Jubilee is fifty years; but since it is the side of the Jubilee, why fifty? And if we say that it refers back to the beginning, where he said "Jubilee," then he should have put "and therefore" before "and if you say"; and moreover it is forced. Tenth: they said "these fifty days were of the Jubilee"; but in the Jubilee they are years, not days. Granted, according to Rabbi Yehudah, who said "corresponding" and not literally, it is not very difficult; but according to Rabbi Shimon, who said "these fifty days were of the Jubilee," which implies that they literally were, it is difficult. Eleventh: they said "and all of them praises": what does he mean? Twelfth: they said "and all of them are fifty times, and no more": what is "and no more," which seems superfluous wording? Thirteenth: they said "and no more," yet there are eleven extra, as above in chapter 1. And if you say that they are not extra, as that young scholar resolved above, he should have explained and resolved it as we resolved above, for it is no small thing. Fourteenth: they said "because all is crowned in the Jubilee": what is it doing here? For it is a clear thing, the very thing he is dealing with; what need is there to say it? Fifteenth: they said "crowned," and above he said "aroused": what is the difference between them? Sixteenth: they said "all is crowned in the Jubilee": who is the "all" that is crowned in the Jubilee? Who are they, and in what are they? Seventeenth: they said "and from the side of the Jubilee," etc.; for he contradicts himself: above he said that the Jubilee [and the side of the Jubilee] are not one thing, and now he makes them equal, saying "all is crowned in the Jubilee, and from the side of the Jubilee came," etc. Eighteenth: "And therefore," etc.: what has this to do with that, that he says "and therefore the Torah, which comes from Gevurah, was crowned in the right"? For at first glance they have no relation at all. Nineteenth: they said "and it is taught," etc., which seems to come as a proof, and at first glance there is no proof from there at all. Twentieth: they said "and all were seen, and were included, and were crowned": it seems a needless doubling. Twenty-first: they said "and were crowned in this": in what? If you say in the voices, he should have said "in them," for so he says, "were seen in them and included in them." Thus far what we saw fit to remark on this passage. And before we enter into its explanation, we need to set out some preliminaries, and we shall devote a chapter of its own to them.

In order to understand this passage in its proper form, we need to set out five preliminaries, and these are they. First: the distinction between days and years. And the matter is that "year" without qualification is in Binah, and "days" without qualification is in Malkhut; as is known that Malkhut is "commandment," which is one day. And the matter is clear: for in the year there are 365 days, and they are called the 365 days of the sun. And it is known that the courses of the sun and its matters are by the power of Binah, and of it is said (Eccl. 1:5), "And the sun rises." And they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (folio 146), that its rising is from Be'er Sheva, which is Binah, and from there it draws its power and its effluence; so that the title "sun" is related to Binah in most places in the Zohar. And the reason that the days of Binah are 365 is because she is female and her inclination is to the left, and in her are the 365 negative commandments; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, folio 248). And even if "year" is sometimes found in Tiferet, all is through Binah, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, with the help of Heaven. And in her the twelve months are hinted, as we explained in Gate Four, chapter 7. And the matter is that there is the manifestation of the six concealed extremities, because through her the whole Emanation was emanated, as explained there.

And behold, the six extremities sometimes incline to judgment, sometimes to compassion; therefore they are twelve, and in her is the beginning of the twelve boundaries, as we shall explain in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapter 6. And therefore "year" is always in Binah. And therefore the days in the count of the year are from Yom Kippur to Rosh Hashanah; and Yom Kippur is the gathering of all the days, and it is the day marked out in the year, which corresponds to the whole year; [and on it] all the days of the year rest: just as after six days, the Sabbath; after thirty days, the New Moon; after a year, one day, which is Yom Kippur, the Sabbath of the World to Come. And every year has in it 365 days; and the ten that are extra over the year are the ten days of repentance, which are the seal of the year, the seal of the resting; for they are days of teshuvah, literally teshuvah [return], which is Binah, to which all the days return. And therefore they are the days in which a man can set right the days in which he made [things] crooked, before he comes to see the face of the Master, the Lord; and therefore they are days of repentance, as we explained. And although one may find a year that has in it only 353 days, and likewise 354, and likewise 355, according to the years of the cycle, this is nothing; for this is that the year borrows from its fellow and repays, and the days of the sun are always 365, and their hint is to Binah, as we explained. And after [it has been explained] that the days and the years are, these in Binah and these in Malkhut, which is one day, we come to explain the second preliminary, which is the preliminary of the division of the times in their hinting:

The second is the division of the times in their hinting. And we say that time is divided into seven parts, and they are: first, Jubilees; second, shemitot [sabbatical cycles]; third, years; fourth, months; fifth, sabbaths [weeks]; sixth, days; seventh, hours. And we shall explain their matter. The Jubilee is the gathering of seven shemitot; a shemitah is the gathering of seven years; the year is the gathering of twelve months; the month is the gathering of four sabbaths; the sabbath is the gathering of seven days; the day the gathering of twenty-four hours. And the matter is that "hour" without qualification is in Malkhut, and she performs the action and change of time by the power of the order of time that flows upon her. And the order of time is the seven sefirot from Chesed downward; and the order of time acts by the power of Binah, which flows upon them as a mother upon the children. So the principal of the tree turns out to be Binah, and she is the root of the tree, whose roots spread without end. And so they titled her in the Tikkunim with the language "root of the tree," as we shall explain his wording in Gate 15, chapter 2. And she is the Jubilee, and she has seven branches; and her seven branches are seven shemitot, which are seven sefirot. And of these seven branches, each one has seven branches, and they are seven years. And we do not deny that, although the name shemitah is attributed to all the sefirot, and even to Malkhut, nevertheless they do not rise to the matter of shemitot except by the power of Binah, which flows upon them. And so they explained explicitly in the Tikkunim: for from the side of Chokhmah the sefirot are included of ten, and from the side of Binah included of seven.

And behold, it turns out that they do not have the totality of seven, so as to be shemitot, except by the power of Binah, which shines into the concealed roots, from which the whole tree draws sustenance. And to each and every branch of the seven branches there are a further twelve branches, and they are the twelve months in each and every year; and they are the twelve havayot, which are the twelve boundaries, which are the twelve leaves of the rose, six red and six white, because their inclination is at times to judgment and at times to compassion. And concerning the matter of the months and the havayot there are many, many matters; if we were to enter into their explanation we would go out from what is intended, and we have only to be brief and to go up.

And behold, the twelve havayot are permutations that are permuted from the four-letter name, thus: יהו"ה יהה"ו יוה"ה, behold three with Yod. And likewise three others with the letter Heh: ההי"ו ההו"י היו"ה, behold three with Heh. And likewise three others with the letter Vav: והי"ה והה"י ויה"ה, behold three with Vav. And likewise three others with the letter Heh: הוי"ה היה"ו הוה"י, behold three with Heh. And their initial letters are the four-letter name. And likewise in each and every month there are thirty days; and when we divide them, three come to each and every week, and they amount to twenty-four days. For the Sabbath day has none at all, for it is the gathering of the havayot; that is to say, all the havayot are on the Sabbath day, which are three havayot. And so they said that from there all the days of the week are fed; therefore all three havayot of the week rest on the Sabbath day. Afterwards two letters are divided for each day: one in the day and one in the night, this male and this female. For in the havayah there are two letters, Yod [and] Vav, males, [and] Heh [and] Heh, females; and at times both are male and both female, and sometimes the night is male and the day female, all in the secret of the reversing light. And likewise there are days that have more judgment in them than their fellows, as we explained this matter in the book Or Yakar, on the portion "This month shall be for you," which we began to compose (see in Asis Rimmonim). And however it may be, the days turn out to be branches to the sabbath [week], and the sabbath a branch to the month.

And behold, in the week there are seven days, corresponding to the seven sefirot; further, in each day twenty-four hours: twelve of day, male, compassion, and twelve of night, female, judgment; all according to the division of the havayot, as we shall dwell at length in explaining this matter in the book mentioned, and likewise further on in this book. And now it is not difficult for us whether the constellation of the day is determinative or the constellation of the hour is determinative, which is mentioned in Shabbat (folio 156a); or whether the constellation of the year, or the constellation of the month, or of the shemitah, or of the Jubilee. And open your eyes. And now it will not be withheld from us that the hours are channels of light flowing from the days, and the days are channels of light flowing from the weeks, and the weeks channels of light flowing from the months, and the months channels of light flowing from the years, and the years channels of light flowing from the shemitot, and the shemitot channels of light flowing from the Jubilees.

And behold, there is no doubt according to this that the branches always return to their source. For the hours return to the days; and therefore they said in the book of the Zohar that a man should confess his iniquities before he lies down, to set right what they made crooked; and likewise the soul ascends and confesses its iniquities. And likewise the days return to their source, which is the week; and therefore there are those who wrote that the Sabbath atones; and it is correct, for it is the rest of the days. And let the soul of the inquirer not be astonished and hasten to reply: do not the coming days feed from the Sabbath? And this is no difficulty at all; for the priests in their watches will prove it, for on the Sabbath day they served in two watches, the outgoing and the incoming; and this certainly indicates the bond and the union. And likewise the weeks return to the month, and atonement is said of it, as we pray: "New Moons You gave to Your people, a time of atonement for all," etc. And likewise the months to the year; and from there to teshuvah, which is Yom Kippur, on which they used to pray nine blessings: all to indicate the source. And now, with this preliminary, it is not forced that the day should at times reveal the power of the year, when the source wishes to strengthen the light and the effluence in it; and nevertheless it will not be literally equal to the year. And after this principle has been explained, the matter of time is known: that what is this day is not its morrow, and what is its morrow is not the day that has passed; and likewise in years, and likewise in shemitot, and likewise in Jubilees: what is this Jubilee is not that one; for the roots spread upward without end, in what is not fitting to contemplate. And after we have set out what suffices for the matter of the division of the times and their hinting, we come to explain the exile of Egypt in a preliminary, in brief:

The third is the matter of the exile of Egypt. For until the light of Abraham shone forth, the Holy One, blessed be He, was pouring the effluence of His souls into the choicest among men, for so it was fitting. For if Adam the first man had not sinned, he would have had garments of light [אור], with Alef, which hints at the oneness of the Name and its union. But when he sinned and mixed holy with profane and profane with holy, and the serpent came upon Eve and cast filth into her, the holy was mixed, and she bore Cain, a nest of impurity; and the world went on being spoiled, and the bread growing moldy. And therefore he was clothed in garments of skin [עור], which is seventy nations [as the number seventy, which is in עור]. And the Holy One, blessed be He, did not divide them, for the honor of Heaven, since the light of Abraham had not yet shone, until the generation of the Dispersion; and the Holy One, blessed be He, divided them, each one according to the place fitting for it. And He took Abraham, who is light, as His portion; and the garments of light with Alef were set right; and not a complete tikkun, for there was still dross mixed in the silver and silver in the dross: for among the nations there were holy souls, and among holiness there was still filth.

And behold, at first the Creator acted wisely to purify the holy ones; and from Abraham came out Ishmael, and from Isaac Esau; and Jacob, his bed was whole, pure, and clean. Afterwards He wished to purify and to gather the banished sparks, for His will is "that none who is banished be banished from Him" (2 Sam. 14:14). And He put the clean silver within the iron furnace, the servitude of Egypt, in the strength of the husk. And there all the sparks were gathered to the mass of clean silver; and therefore there all the generations transmigrated: the generation of the Flood, of whom it is said (Exod. 1:22), "Every son that is born you shall cast into the river"; and the generation of the Dispersion, of whom it is said (Gen. 11:3), "Let us make bricks," and likewise in Egypt it is said (Exod. 5:18), "yet you shall deliver the quota of bricks"; until the silver came out refined, clean, purged of all dross: six hundred thousand. And it would have been fitting not to accept converts any more. And of this it is said (Hab. 3:6), "He beheld and released the nations," and our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Bava Kamma 38a): "When Israel stood," etc., "He released to them the seven commandments," for there were no longer sparks; just as there will not be in the days of the Messiah, as in the matter our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yevamot 24b): "Converts are not accepted in the days of the Messiah"; and as it is said (Deut. 32:12), "The Lord alone shall lead him," etc. But we spoiled [it] with the Calf: [the release] became for them as a permission, and they had to transmigrate into what was permitted, and to serve it, and to come into the furnace of the other exiles. And let us return to the matter: that at the Exodus from Egypt Israel were clean, six hundred thousand; but in Egypt the husk and the dross prevailed over them. Although it was refined silver, "the tribes of Yah, a testimony to Israel" (Ps. 122:4), nevertheless they entered within the husk and went down wondrously, and the dross and the lead ruled over them, until they entered the gate of the forty-nine faces impure. And had the forty-nine faces pure, the fifty gates of Binah, not been aroused, "we and our children and our children's children would still be enslaved," etc. And therefore this trembling was necessary: to harden Pharaoh's heart [and to strike him with the plague of the firstborn], and "to break the jaws of the wicked, and pluck the prey from his teeth" (Job 29:17). "And Pharaoh rose up at night" and proclaimed, "You are free men," so as to uproot the husk and break it completely. And behold, when Israel went out of Egypt they were not yet completely clean, as we shall explain in the fourth preliminary:

The fourth is that it is not fitting to think that when Israel went out of Egypt all fifty gates of Binah had already been aroused over them and they had been purified from the husk completely; for this is an error, since if so they would have received the Torah immediately upon their going out. Rather they needed to count days of whitening: at their going out the impure blood ceased, and afterwards they counted seven weeks, as in the matter (Lev. 15:28) "and she shall count for herself seven days." And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (folio 97a), and these are its words: "Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Chiyya were going on the way. Rabbi Chiyya said: It is written (Lev. 23:15), 'And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Sabbath,' etc. What is it speaking of? He said to him: The Companions have established it. But come and see: Israel, when they were in Egypt, were in another domain, and were held in impurity, like this woman when she sits in the days of impurity. After they were circumcised they entered the holy portion, which is called covenant. Once they held fast to it, the impurity ceased from them, like this woman when the blood of impurity ceases from her. After it has ceased from her, what is written? 'And she shall count for herself seven days.' So too here: since they entered the holy portion, the impurity ceased from them, and the Holy One, blessed be He, said: From here on, a count for purity. 'And you shall count for yourselves': 'for yourselves' precisely, as it is said, 'and she shall count for herself seven days,' for herself, for her own self; so too here, 'for yourselves,' for your own selves. And why? In order to be purified in upper, holy waters, and afterwards to come to be joined with the King and to receive the Torah. There, 'and she shall count for herself seven days'; here, seven weeks. Why seven weeks? In order to merit to be purified in the waters of that river that flows and goes out and is called living waters; and from that river seven weeks go out. And therefore certainly seven weeks, in order to merit through it. Just as a woman's purification is at night, for marital relations with her husband, so it is written (Num. 11:9), 'And when the dew fell upon the camp at night.' 'Upon the camp' is written, and it is not written 'and when the dew fell at night.' And when did this dew descend? When Israel drew near to Mount Sinai; then that dew descended from that river upon those days, which were called a camp in completeness; and they were purified, and their filth ceased from them, and they were joined with the holy King and received the Torah; and the Assembly of Israel was joined with the holy King; and this they have established. And at that time certainly 'all the rivers go to the sea' (Eccl. 1:7), to be purified and to be washed, and all were bound and joined with the holy King. Come and see: any person who does not count this count of those seven complete weeks, so as to merit this purity, is not called pure, and is not in the category of the pure, and is not worthy to have a portion in the Torah. And whoever arrives pure at this day, and the count was not lost from him, when he reaches this night he needs," etc. Thus far its words.

And although our intent is clear from within it, nevertheless we shall explain it, since it is of our matter. And the explanation: the verse that said "And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Sabbath" was difficult for him: why did it make the counting depend on the morrow of the Sabbath? For it would have been fitting that it say "and you shall count for yourselves from the sixteenth day of the month"; why should it care about the morrow of the Sabbath? And to this he answered that while Israel were in Egypt "they were in another domain, and were held in impurity." And the intent is that they were within the husks, into which the Holy One, blessed be He, had put them, in the furnace, to refine them like silver, as we explained in the third preliminary. And had there been only this, it would not have been so [grave]. But "they were held in impurity": for they abandoned themselves to impurity and held the deeds of Egypt in their hands. And this is "and they were held," as it is written (Exod. 12:21), "Draw out and take for yourselves lambs," and our Sages, of blessed memory, explained: draw your hands away from idolatry. "Like this woman," etc.: they are likened to the woman who flows in the days of her issue. And the cessation of their issue was on the first day of Passover. For so our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in Midrash Rabbah (Bo, section 19), and these are its words: "And many of them would not accept upon themselves to be circumcised. The Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses to make the Passover offering. And when Moses made the Passover offering, the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed to the four winds of the world, and they blew in the Garden of Eden; and from the winds that are in the Garden of Eden they went and cleaved to that Passover offering, as it is said (Song 4:16), 'Awake, O north wind, and come, O south.' And its scent went a distance of forty days. All Israel gathered and said to him: Please, feed us from your Passover offering; for they were faint from the scent. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: If you are not circumcised, you do not eat, as it is said (Exod. 12:43), 'And the Lord said to Moses,' etc., 'This is the statute of the Passover,' etc. Immediately they gave themselves and were circumcised, and the blood of the Passover was mixed with the blood of circumcision." And although there is room to scrutinize this passage, nevertheless it emerges for us from the whole of it that their circumcision was at night, near the time of their eating, since they were asking Moses, "Feed us from your Passover offering." And therefore it is written "from the morrow of the Sabbath [ha-shabbat]": explanation: from the morrow of the day of ceasing [shevitah] and stopping of the impure blood. And this is what he intended in saying "once they held fast to it, the impurity ceased," etc., up to "so too here, 'for yourselves,' for your own selves."

And their filth, that is, their going out from under the servitude of the husks and the hand of Egypt, had not yet ceased until after midnight, when He said to them (Ps. 113:1), "Hallelujah, praise, O servants of the Lord"; and our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Megillah 14a): until now servants of Pharaoh, from here on servants of the Lord. And likewise the husks were not subdued and broken except at midnight, in the plague of the firstborn, as it is written (Exod. 12:29), "from the firstborn of Pharaoh," etc.; and they are the four husks. "And why? In order to be purified in upper, holy waters": it was difficult for him: since they had already entered the grades of holiness by circumcising themselves, what is the matter of the counting afterwards? They are already pure and holy, cleaving to holiness. And if it is true that they still need purification, then it would have been fitting that they count the days of the counting before the circumcision. And to resolve this, what we said, that it would be fitting that they count the counting before their entering holiness, before the circumcision, he said: "[And why?] In order to be purified in upper, holy waters." Explanation: know why the circumcision came first: because if they had not entered holiness at all, and had counted before their entering, they would turn out never to be purified. For the purification is in the waters of holiness, upper, inner waters, which are not in the first grade of holiness, but are "upper, holy." And if they had not entered somewhat into the grades of holiness by the commandment of circumcision, they could never have immersed in the upper waters, which are very inward, as explained, because they would still be outside. Therefore they needed to enter somewhat into holiness, so that after their counting they would merit the upper waters, to be purified. And with this the reason will be understood that the circumcision of the convert precedes the immersion, and if he immersed and afterwards was circumcised, his immersion does not count for him. And as to what we asked, that since they had already been purified, why do they need further counting and immersion, he answered: "to be joined with the King": explanation: to be unified with Tiferet, that is, the receiving of the Torah, as is known. And the matter is that by circumcision Israel rose out of the husk and merited that the Shekhinah be with them; but into the grades of the male, which are from Yesod upward, they did not enter until after the counting of the forty-nine days, the days of whitening; and then the male was unified with the female. And now it is well [explained] why Israel performed milah and not periah: that is, they cut off the husk, and did not uncover, which is the revealing of the Yod, which is Yesod; for the reason that it was forbidden for them to defile the sign of the covenant, God forbid, in the days of whitening, as we explained. "There, 'and she shall count for herself seven days'; here," etc., "why," etc.: it was difficult for him: just as the purification of the woman is in seven days, so too seven days should suffice for the purification of Israel; why were there seven weeks? And he answered: "in order to merit to be purified," etc. Explanation: so that they would be fit to receive the effluence of Binah, which is called "the river that flows," etc., and it is what is called living waters; and the immersion must be in living waters, not in drawn water. And therefore, even if they drew from them with a vessel, which is Malkhut, they were not purified until they merited to reveal fifty days, as we shall explain. "And from that river seven weeks go out": it was difficult for him: in the end they are the six days of creation, the days that are between Binah and Malkhut; and if so, the difficulty returns to its place: seven days should suffice, as for a woman with an issue. And he answered that at the time of the emanation of the upper days they are seven weeks, each one included of seven from the side of Binah, as we explained in the first preliminary; and therefore they had to count seven weeks, which are seven times seven. And this is what he said: "and therefore certainly seven weeks," etc. "Just as a woman," etc.: it was difficult for him: if so, what need is there of the fiftieth day? On the forty-ninth day they should have received the Torah. To this he said that just as the purification of a woman is on the night of the eighth of her counting, so Israel need the night of the fiftieth day for their purification. "'And when the dew fell upon the camp at night,' and it is not written 'and when the dew fell,'" etc.: explanation: if he had meant to say that it was the dew that descended with the manna, according to the plain sense of the words, it should have said "and when the dew fell at night"; why "upon the camp"? For it was descending around the camp. Rather, since it says "upon the camp," it implies literally upon the camp; and that is the dew that descends to purify Israel. "And when did this dew descend," etc.: explanation: according to this explanation we must say that the matter of the descent of the dew was only on the night of the fiftieth day, "when Israel drew near to Mount Sinai." And the matter is: ט"ל [tal, dew] amounts in number to Yod-Heh-Vav [spelled out, 39]; and the intent is that Chokhmah pours effluence to Binah, and Binah into Tiferet, and Tiferet descends and gives the mother's milk to the children to drink; and the husks are burned away from all the plantings that do not draw sustenance from holiness. "Then that dew descended," etc.: the matter is that the souls of Israel are channels pouring effluence from Binah to Malkhut, and likewise from there downward, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul and in the Gate of Intention.

And behold, when a man blemishes his soul, that blemish necessitates some blemish above, in the way that we shall explain there. And therefore, while Israel were not pure, the effluence was not descending upon the upper camp, which is the gathering of the sefirot; and when Israel were purified, then immediately "that dew descended from that river," which is Binah, "upon those days," which are the seven upper weeks, whose gathering is called a camp. And then, through the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, all the upper days receive effluence. And the rest of the words of the passage are clear.

And behold, we bless over the counting of the Omer [sefirat ha-omer]. The Shekhinah is called omer, and sefirah is from the language of sapphire. And the intent is that we adorn Malkhut in the days. And because there are gates in her as the number of the upper gates, it is necessary to illumine the lower ones, so that the upper ones pour effluence into them. And on each and every day we set right and adorn [and count] one gate; and therefore we must say "today is such-and-such a day," which is the gate that is revealed, and join it with the preceding days, so that their illumination may be all together; and count weeks, which are so many gates for each and every sefirah, so as to unite the branch in its root. And after we have explained all that is needed in this fourth preliminary, we come to explain the fifth preliminary:

The fifth is that there is a great distinction between "Jubilee" and "the side of the Jubilee." And this preliminary is useful for the words of the language of the Zohar; and so we received it from our teacher. For when he says "Jubilee," it is literally the Jubilee, explanation: the very self of Binah; but when he says "from the side," he means what is drawn from her, not she. And so it is explained in the Zohar explicitly, in Parashat Lekh (folio 90b), and these are its words: "'Thus' [koh]: that side which comes from the side of Gevurah; for from the side of Gevurah Isaac came. And that side of Gevurah is called koh, for from there come fruits and produce to the world." Thus far its words. He taught that Malkhut is called koh from the side of Gevurah, and the reason is that she is drawn from Gevurah. And this is [the difference] between "Jubilee" and "the side of the Jubilee"; and wherever it is mentioned in the Zohar, such is its rule. And after we have concluded these preliminaries, we come to the explanation of the passage of the Zohar from Parashat Yitro, in a chapter of its own, with the help of Heaven.

"Rabbi Yehudah said: From the day that they went out," etc. It was difficult for him why Israel delayed fifty days before receiving the Torah, and did not receive it immediately upon their going out of Egypt. And to this he answered: "because of those years of the Jubilee." He was precise not to say "corresponding to the years of the Jubilee," because they are fifty days; and since they are days, they are in Malkhut, as we explained in the first preliminary; and moreover they were days of whitening, and they are in Malkhut, as we explained in the fourth preliminary. Therefore he said "because of those years of the Jubilee": explanation: on account of the years of the Jubilee, which are fifty, the days had to be fifty, in order to count Malkhut and to illumine her from the Nun [fifty]. And in order to crown her and adorn her with them, it is necessary to illumine fifty faces in them, so that the light flows "as water, face to face" (Prov. 27:19), in the way we explained in the Gate of Channels, chapter 1. And because it was difficult for him that the years of the Jubilee are at first glance only one year, to this he proved that the Jubilee is literally all fifty years, as we explained in the preliminaries. For otherwise it should say "And you shall hallow the fiftieth year," which would imply the year that is after forty-nine years, whose number is fifty, and be silent. But since it says "the year of the fifty years," learn from it that it speaks of a year that is in itself fifty years, as we explained in the second preliminary. And difficulties 1, 2, and 3 are settled. And he brought a proof for his words from the words of Rashbi, who said "that Jubilee," etc. And the intent is not Binah, for if so let him say "Jubilee" without qualification; what is "that"? Rather, as if to say, "that Jubilee": explanation: the lower Jubilee, which is the Jubilee revealed in Malkhut, as we explained in the second preliminary, which is a Jubilee of days, not years. And it is called "that": explanation: the Jubilee in which they were standing, which is the one they entered when they were circumcised, and not the great Jubilee. And he objected, "And if you say," etc.: for who tells us that it was the lower Jubilee? Let us say it was the upper Jubilee. And moreover it is necessary that the freedom is from there. And moreover Israel were within forty-nine husks, and if these had not been subdued it would not have been possible for them to be redeemed. If so, let us say it was literally the Jubilee, which is the upper Jubilee, the Jubilee of years. To this he answered: "rather, from the side of the Jubilee." For "rather" always uproots the original supposition; and now he says that it was the lower Jubilee, as we explained. And what is difficult for you, concerning the matter of freedom and likewise the breaking of the husks, will be settled: for this lower Jubilee receives effluence from the upper Jubilee. And this is the lower days shining in the secret of the upper years, and the years clothed in the days, as we explained in the second preliminary; and therefore they had freedom. For one cannot say that it was in the upper Jubilee; for if so, it would have been a freedom after which there is no servitude, as we hope that our redemption will be with the great shofar, and no further distress will answer us. And since we see that they returned and were enslaved, it implies that it was not in the very Jubilee but from the side of the Jubilee, which is what is drawn and flows from it, as we explained in the fifth preliminary. And the intent is that from the fifty gates of Binah [something] was drawn and spread from it and clothed in Malkhut in her fifty days, as we explained. And he proved the matter: "And from the side of the Jubilee judgment was aroused," etc. Explanation: granted, if we say that it was from the side of the Jubilee, that is why judgment was aroused from there; for so we say, that from the side of the Jubilee judgments are aroused upon Gevurah, as we explained in Gate Eight, chapters 6 and 7. But if we say that it was literally from the Jubilee, from where were they aroused? For judgments are not in the Jubilee. And this is "and from the side of the Jubilee judgment was aroused against the Egyptians." "And therefore these fifty days," etc.: it was difficult for him: if so, since it is impossible to say that it was literally the Jubilee, because after their freedom there was servitude and after their exile exile, then let us say that it was neither the Jubilee nor from the side of the Jubilee, but Malkhut herself, and therefore there was no complete redemption at all. To this he said: "and therefore," etc. Explanation: this proves the matter from all its sides: since we see that they were days, it implies that it was not the upper Jubilee; and since we see that they were fifty, it implies that it was from the side of the Jubilee. And because his intent is only to prove that the Exodus from Egypt was only from the side of Binah, he brought proof only from the count of the days, which are fifty. And with this difficulties 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 are resolved. "We have learned: corresponding to (this," etc.): this is to prove that the Exodus from Egypt was by the power of the Jubilee, from the fact that the going out from Egypt is mentioned in the Torah fifty times. And because the mentions of the Exodus from Egypt are more than fifty, he intended to prove that not all of them are in the count of the Exodus, in saying "the customs of Egypt, and all of them praises," etc. Explanation: places where the Holy One, blessed be He, praises Himself, or where the Exodus from Egypt was mentioned as praise. For there are places in which the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned and they are not as praise, and it is not fitting that they be in the count, as that young scholar whom we wrote of in chapter 1 resolved. And to show the way he mentioned some of them; for those like them are the ones fitting to be counted; but those that come to indicate a date, like "in the second year after the children of Israel went out of the land of Egypt" and the like, it is not fitting to count them. "And all of them are fifty times, and no more": it was difficult for him: what proof is there in His having mentioned the Exodus from Egypt in the performance of the commandments? For let us say that the Holy One, blessed be He, says thus in each and every commandment: although I trouble you with the performance of the commandments, nevertheless you are obligated to fulfil them, because you are obligated to My honor, for I brought you out of the slavery of Egypt; and if so there is no proof from here. To this he said: "and all of them are fifty times, and no more." Explanation: if the intent were to show us the obligation in the performance of the commandments, it would have been fitting that the mentions be as the number of the commandments; but since we see that they are fifty and no more, it certainly implies that with deliberate intent they were as the number of the gates, to make known to us that through the effluence of all of them was our going out of Egypt. Or he means that what Rabbi Elazar asked Rabbi Shimon (in the Tikkunim), as we explained in the first chapter, was difficult for him; and he answered that they are fifty and no more, to show the strength and might of the redemption, that all fifty gates had to pour forth, as we explained there. And difficulties 11, 12, and 13 are resolved. "Because all is crowned in the Jubilee": explanation: it was difficult for him: since it is not literally the Jubilee but the side of the Jubilee, as he said above, why were there fifty, which indicates that it was literally in the Jubilee? To this he said that there were fifty because all of them were crowned in the secret of the great Jubilee, as we explained, that the years were clothed in the days and the days were crowned with them. "And from the side of the Jubilee all came": explanation: but as to acting, there was no action drawn literally from the years; rather [from the side of the Jubilee] all came. Explanation: from their side it flowed to the days, and the days acted according to their power. And he was precise: of judgment he said "was aroused" [it'ar], that is, judgment is aroused from there; but of the fifty gates he said "was crowned" [it'atar], for they are crowned in the upper ones, as we explained. And with this questions 14, 15, 16, and 17 are resolved. "And therefore the Torah," etc.: he proved that all the matters of the redemption were by the power of the Jubilee from what we see: that the giving of the Torah was when Gedulah was included in Gevurah and Gevurah in Gedulah; and this is impossible except by the power of Binah, which unifies them and couples them, for from her power the right and the left came out.

And further he brought proof from that baraita which says that at the giving of the Torah there were five voices, and each one of them was included of all ten; behold, there were fifty gates, as will be said further on in the reason for the fifty. And this is what it said: there were five voices at the giving of the Torah, as it is said (Exod. 19:16), "And there were voices and lightnings," etc. "And all were seen in them": explanation: all the sefirot were seen in each one of the five voices; and not that they were seen in them like a face seen in a mirror, for if so they would always be only five; rather they were literally all included in them. And therefore five times ten, which are fifty; and they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, and each one included of ten, behold fifty, as we shall explain. And this is what he said, "and all were seen in them," that is, that all ten were seen in each one of the five voices. And because the language "were seen" implies that they were seen in them but not that they were literally included of them, therefore he went back and said "and were included in them." And if he had said only "were included," it would imply inclusion there, but not as a visible inclusion, rather a concealed one, like the inclusion of the other attributes in general; therefore he said "were seen," that is, visible and literally included. "And were crowned in this": explanation: since it was not literally they that acted, but the lower ones were crowned with the upper ones. And they said "in this": explanation: in Malkhut, for she was the voice that includes all the voices. Thus far the explanation of the passage, and all the remaining difficulties are resolved. And from within it is explained the resolution as to the Exodus from Egypt being mentioned fifty times in the Torah, as we explained. And we dwelt at length on this matter because it relates to the matters of the gates, how the upper ones are revealed in the lower ones, as has been explained from within the preceding chapters. And now we come to the explanation of the gates, and the reason for their matter and their number:

After we engaged above, in the preceding chapters, with the manifestation of the gates and their dependence on Scripture, we come in this chapter to give a reason for their number. And in this there is one who explained that they correspond to seven sefirot, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut, and each one is included of the seven: they are seven times seven, they are forty-nine; and Binah itself is the fiftieth gate: behold fifty. And these are his words: "Binah is called the Great Sabbath. The reason is that the seventh includes all the days, and it is the Sabbath. And do not think that God created the first day, and afterwards the second day, and so on to the sixth, God forbid. Rather, God, blessed and blessed be He, is single in His world; and just as He is single, so He created a single action, and it is the Sabbath; for it is an honored work, and with it the six extremities come to be, which are six sefirot. And it is the inner middle point; and by the way of every point, it has six extremities, and the point is the subsistence of the extremities, and they are the hollow [chalal] of the point, and they are pairs; if so, the Sabbath has no pair; if so, it is single. Therefore whoever makes extremities of the point, which is hollow, destroys all the extremities. Therefore it says (Exod. 31:14), 'Those who profane it [mechalleleha] shall surely be put to death': for he makes of the point, which is single, and it is holy, and it is the subsistence of the extremities, which are called hollow; whoever makes it hollow like the rest of the hollow shall surely be put to death. Therefore the Sabbath, which is a point with the extremities (for it is impossible for a point to be without extremities), they are emanated from Binah; if so, the Sabbath stands in the power of Binah, for it was not manifest as long as it had not gone out into actuality. That is to say: the point with the extremities is called a complete Sabbath; but while it is in potentiality it is called the Great Sabbath; and all things were standing in potentiality in the midst of Binah, and they are called the fifty gates of Binah. And the reason is that this point that we mentioned, against the extremities, was against the Structure: the point cannot be without the extremities, nor the extremities without the point; if so, each one of the sefirot has the power of all of them; if so, it shines seven times seven, and they are forty-nine; and all of them are emanated from Binah, as we said; and with her, who is the great gate, there will be fifty gates. For the King is single, and it is not the way to relate [Him] with the things emanated from Him; just as the seventh is a place for the extremities, so Binah is a place for all of them. And just as it is not fitting to relate [Him] with the branches, so it is not the way to relate the point, which is the seventh, with the extremities. Therefore the countings of the Omer are forty-nine, and they are seven weeks, which correspond to the seven sefirot; and it would have been fitting that they be fifty days, but we count only forty-nine days, for the reason we said, that it is not fitting for us to relate Binah with the forty-nine gates, because she is concealed from them; and likewise one does not relate the seventh, which is concealed, with the extremities. And therefore it is a commandment to count days and a commandment to count weeks. If so, they are the fifty gates of Binah. Therefore it is said of Moses (Ps. 8:6), 'And You made him a little lower than Elohim': for Binah is called Elohim; one gate was lacking to him, which is Binah, and he attained only forty-nine, which is the Structure." Thus far his words. And behold, the intent is clear: that the fifty gates are seven included of seven, which are forty-nine.

And behold, the forty-nine are in the seven days of the Structure, and the fiftieth gate is Binah herself, from whom all seven were emanated and from whom they draw sustenance; and therefore they are gates showing her power and her actions, and her very self is concealed, even from Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. And likewise this is the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him, as we proved above concerning the matter of the forty-nine days between Passover and Shavuot. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 112) [there is something] close to this, and at first glance departing somewhat from this view; and these are its words: "And seven sabbaths, for each seven days: they amount to forty-nine. And this is (Lev. 25:8) 'And you shall count for yourself seven sabbaths of years': they are forty-nine years. And forty-nine days, seven sabbaths, correspond to these seven names, which are אבגית"ץ, etc. Those seven names, each one six letters, correspond to the six days of the week for each and every sabbath. And these are what is said (Isa. 6:2), 'Seraphim stood above Him; six wings, six wings to each one.' And all of them forty-nine [seven sabbaths and forty-two weekdays]. And the seven sabbaths are seven sefirot, and for each one six grades, and they amount to the forty-nine faces of purity of the Torah. The supernal Imma is the fifty days of the counting of the Omer, the upper Heh of מט"ה [forty-nine and Heh]." Thus far its words, for our matter. And at first glance it implies that his view in this passage is that seven sefirot are included of six extremities, which are forty-two; and the seven sabbaths themselves, which are the manifestation of the sefirot that includes the totality, are forty-nine; and Binah herself is the fiftieth gate. And when we wish to scrutinize his words with good contemplation, we find him agreeing with the commentators. And it is that in each and every sabbath there are six extremities, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod; and the point of the hollow is the Sabbath, which is Malkhut, who is "fourth to every three," as explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 3b), thus: Gedulah, Gevurah, and Tiferet above her, and she below the three of them, for so she is the fourth leg of the Chariot, and likewise her place beside her husband before the diminishment; and below her Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and she is fourth to the last three. Her place turns out to be the middle point of six extremities; and she is likewise the Sabbath of each and every week, which are six days, and the Sabbath the gathering of all the days, as we explained in chapter 3, in the second preliminary. And so according to this, the seven sabbaths in truth are seven manifestations of Malkhut: the first, her manifestation from Chesed; the second, her manifestation from Gevurah; the third, her manifestation from Tiferet; the fourth, her manifestation from Netzach; the fifth [text: "the eighth"], her manifestation from Hod; the sixth, her manifestation from Yesod; the seventh, her manifestation from herself, and she is the point surrounded by six extremities, and she is the Sabbath, the gathering of the six extremities, which are the days of the week. You turn out to say that he is always speaking of seven sefirot included of seven. And as for his speaking to them thus, it is to let us hear that they are forty-nine, in the sefirot and in the gates.

And the matter of the seraphim, which are in Binah and have only six wings: the reason is that the seraphim themselves are in the count. And likewise the sefirot are included of six extremities, and seven sabbaths are in the count; and the seven sabbaths are the very self of Malkhut, which includes the sefirot, as we explained, for she is the middle point between her boundaries, and she is a point in her hollow. And moreover she is not one of the extremities, for the extremities are only her ornaments; and she is not any one of the extremities, as we explained, but she is a middle point. And with this the words of Rashbi and the words of the commentators are brought to a compromise, besides what is explained on this in the book Or Yakar, with God's blessing.

Besides this view, we further found in Rashbi, in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 6b), [something] opposed to this; and these are its words: "'From the appearance of his loins upward, and from the appearance of his loins downward' (Ezek. 1:27): these are the two thighs, two prophets of truth; and they are fourth and fifth to Chesed, for from there is the building of the world; this is what is written (Ps. 89:3), 'The world is built by Chesed.' The upper Heh, Binah, spreads to Hod: fifty gates. And therefore it is hinted of her: 'I saw as it were the appearance of fire, a house for it round about' (Ezek. 1:27), and in it are six appearances." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained there all the appearances of Ezekiel, and they are ten appearances. And after he explained three appearances, he said that the fourth and the fifth, which are "from the appearance of his loins upward and from the appearance of his loins downward," are Netzach and Hod; and he called them thighs because, since they are thighs, the title "loins" is related to them. And afterwards he said "two prophets of truth," to hint that since the verse unified these two appearances as one, there is no place for them to be related except to Netzach and Hod, which are the two halves of the body, which are the two thighs that are always unified. And likewise they are two prophets of truth, who are always brothers and are not separated; for they are the place of the visions of the prophets, for the two of them together amount to ten sefirot. For Adonai is in Hod and YHVH in Netzach, and the two of them unified amount to יאהדונה"י, which is eight letters; and the substance of the two names is ten appearances, ten sefirot seen by the prophets. If so, the two of them turn out to be one manifestation and one substance, which is not so with the other sefirot; and therefore these two appearances are related only to Netzach and Hod. And likewise Rashbi explained this matter concerning them in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 2a), and these are its words: "'Seers, prophets': from the side of Netzach and Hod, in which two names are included, which are יאהדונה"י, in which are eight letters, corresponding to eight books of the Prophets; and 'prophets' (two: behold ten), corresponding to ten sefirot; corresponding to it Ezekiel saw ten appearances." Thus far its words.

And it is clear for our matter; and more will be explained in the book Or Yakar, part two. And likewise he called them "prophets of truth" [keshot], whose explanation is "truth" [emet], which is Tiferet; and from the side of Tiferet, which is the body, "loins" and "thighs" are related to them. And to prove that these appearances are in them, he said "and they are fourth and fifth to Chesed, for from there," etc. The intent is that the beginning of the appearances of Ezekiel was from Chesed, and likewise the beginning of the creation of the world was from Chesed, as he concludes; and these are fourth and fifth to Chesed; and if so, it is fitting that the fourth and fifth appearance be related to them and not to others. And all the proofs were needed because of the confusion of the sefirot in the appearances, as explained there. "The upper Heh, Binah," etc.: he wishes to explain that the third appearance, which is "as the appearance of fire, a house for it round about," is Binah. And because this is not the relation of the order (for what has Hod and Netzach to do with Binah?), he said first that she has a relation, and the relation is that "Binah spreads to Hod: fifty gates." And the matter is that Binah and her fifty gates are up to Hod. How? Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, which are five sefirot: ten times five, for each one is included of ten; and they are fifty. And therefore, since her gates spread up to Hod, it is fitting to count Binah next to Netzach and Hod. And this is what he said: "and therefore it is hinted," etc.: explanation: because of this this appearance hinted at her next to the appearance of Hod. And because of this he called Binah "the upper Heh," etc., for she is called Heh [five] to hint at these five sefirot that spread from her, as we explained.

Behold, he taught explicitly that the gates of Binah spread from her only up to Hod, which are five sefirot, each one included of ten. And so he explained explicitly further (there, folio 6b), in the explanation of the aggadah of Rabbah bar bar Chanah, who saw that bird of the sea [whose water] reached up to its ankles; and he explained there that the sea is Binah, and its ankles are Netzach and Hod: "For the supernal Imma is a sea that spreads to fifty gates, up to the ankles of that bird. Therefore Yod is ten, Heh is five; ten times five, behold they are fifty gates: ten in each sefirah of these five, from Chesed to Hod. Yesod takes them all and is called kol [all], included of these fifty." Thus far its words.

Behold, a proof that he explained explicitly that the fifty gates are from Chesed to Hod. And incidentally we have heard that Yesod is called כ"ל [kol], which amounts to fifty, because it receives fifty gates from Binah and pours them to Malkhut, who is called כלה [kallah, bride], explanation: כל ה' [kol-Heh], kol amounting to fifty. And likewise in the verse (1 Chron. 29:11), "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the might," etc.: ל"ך [lekha] amounts to fifty, and it is Binah, after the fifty gates that spread in Gedulah, in Gevurah, in Tiferet, in Netzach, and in Hod; and afterwards Yesod is called kol, for it receives the fifty; and it is like the likeness of the reversed seal: כ"ל, ל"ך. And now it is fitting to investigate "whether this shall prosper, or that, or whether both alike shall be good" (Eccl. 11:6). And since it is fitting to believe that the words of Rashbi do not contradict one another, God forbid, therefore we come to explain them in a chapter of its own, with the help of Heaven.

In order to enter into the compromise of the words of Rashbi, one must know the matter of these gates to Binah, what their matter is. And we say that the relation of Binah to the whole Emanation, that is to say, the last seven sefirot, is like the relation of the mother to the children. And likewise for the reason of this matter she is called "the mother of the children," and the lower sefirot are children to her, as this matter is explained in the Tikkunim and will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. But this relation is not only because she hovers over them as a mother; rather it also hints that, just as the mother conceives from that drop, and bears it, and makes it grow, and brings it into existence from the beginning of its being Something up to the natural limit, to go out into the air of the world, so Binah received the sefirot, and bore them, and made them grow, and brought them into revealed manifestation, to emanate them to their place. But the parable differs somewhat from the thing illustrated: for in the parable, the natural mother, after she has borne the being that came to be in her womb, remains empty of that manifestation; which is not so with the spiritual emanating mother, for after she has borne the children, their subtle manifestation remains there as before she bore. And this matter is necessary of itself, and it is a superiority in the divine Emanation, as will be explained in the next gate.

And behold, there emerges for us from this preliminary that the roots of the whole Emanation are in Binah in a subtle manifestation. It is further explained in the words of Rashbi that the manifestation of the Emanation concealed in her is not like its manifestation that is now revealed, but in another form. For the manifestation here reaches down to Malkhut, which is the seventh to the extremities; but in the mother's womb they are included in five alone, and they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod alone; for Yesod and Malkhut are unified with Tiferet in one sefirah. And so Rashbi explained in the Zohar in many places.

And behold, it turns out that above, in Binah, there are only five sefirot; and Malkhut and Yesod are the spreading of Tiferet, which spread after its emanation. And therefore the final letters, which are final Kaf, Mem, Nun, Peh, Tzadi, are concealed in Binah. And there is no doubt that they are a hint to the five sefirot concealed there; for they are outside the count of the twenty-two bent [letters], for the beginning of the letters is from Chesed, for so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (folio 159a). And these five letters are of the bent ones, except that they are straight, because they hint, in a high place, at the concealed manifestation. And the relation of this inquiry is not here.

And behold, it turns out that the gates of Binah, which are sources to the revealed sefirot, have two aspects. The first aspect is in the aspect of their being unified with a complete union, and then they are included in five; that is, Malkhut is unified with Tiferet through Yesod. And then certainly the sources are opened in complete compassion, and they pour forth their effluence in the secret of their receiving from all the first three, from within the depths of the Nothing. And when there is no union, but they are seven, then they pour forth, and not a concealed effluence, but from the power of the effluence that is in them. And for this the gates of Binah are found in two aspects. The first aspect is when the extremities are included, and then her gates are included, so that each one is included of ten; since the sefirot's being included of seven is from Binah alone, and their being included of ten is from the side of Chokhmah and upward. And when they are in the secret of union, Keter and Chokhmah are revealed over them to pour forth, and they are included of ten, and they are fifty, five times ten. Tiferet, Malkhut, and Yesod are a unified oneness, and they are all included in ten alone; and this is their superiority in their union into one substance. And when there is no union, then the roots do not pour forth their effluence except from their own side, that is, the effluence of Binah; if so, they are included only in seven, and they are seven times seven, they are forty-nine. And with this a great light comes out for us concerning what it is fitting to ask: why, when they are seven, are they forty-nine and the fiftieth gate concealed, and when they are five, they are a full fifty and the fiftieth gate is not concealed? And the matter is that Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim that the fiftieth gate is Binah, as we wrote in chapter 5, for the Heh of מט"ה is the upper Heh, the fiftieth gate. And elsewhere in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, folio 67) he explained that the Supernal Keter is the fiftieth gate; and these are its words: "The Supernal Keter: this is the completion of the fifty gates of Binah; and this is what was not given to Moses, of which it is said, 'a path that no bird of prey knows.'" Thus far its words. He taught explicitly that the fiftieth gate is Keter. And they do not disagree, for the first three are unified; and in particular since he said that it is "a path that no bird of prey knows," and it was explained in the Gate of Paths that this path is the place in which Chokhmah is unified with Keter, and in it is the union of Chokhmah with Binah, as we proved there in chapter 3, at path 1, from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And if so, it turns out that this indicates precisely their being unified. And when the sefirot below are unified, the source pours forth from the effluence of the depths of the Nothing; for when Yesod [text: "the union"] and Malkhut are in Tiferet, there is the union of Chokhmah and Binah, as explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. Therefore they pour forth from the secret of their union, and the concealed gate is revealed, and then there are a full fifty gates revealed in the sefirot. But when there is no union below, then there is no union above, and the fiftieth gate is not revealed, and they are included only in seven, from the side of Binah alone, because she is not unified above with Chokhmah and Keter. And with this the words of Rashbi are brought to a compromise, and they agree in one matter. And incidentally the matter of the fiftieth gate, and its concealment and its revealing, has been explained. And now we wish to reveal an astonishing matter found in the Tikkunim; these are its words: "Forty-nine letters of the union, which are the twenty-five letters of the six words, which are 'Hear, O Israel,' etc., which is the central pillar; and the twenty-four letters of the Righteous One, which is the small Vav, including the six words of 'Blessed be the name of the glory,' etc., in which are twenty-four letters," etc. Thus far its words.

And behold, it is very difficult: why should the Righteous One lack one letter, which is one gate? And one cannot say that the one gate that is lacking is the fiftieth gate, which is revealed only at times, as we explained; because the matter here is the verses of the union, and if so it would have been fitting that there be a full fifty gates, as we explained.

And moreover, since what is lacking is the fiftieth gate, it would have been fitting that it be lacking in Tiferet, which is above Yesod, for the fiftieth gate is superior to all the gates. Therefore we say that the matter is that the fifty gates are in five sefirot, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod; and the fiftieth gate is revealed because of the union, for we are dealing with the verses of the union. But Tiferet receives ten from Gedulah, and ten from Gevurah, and five from the Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah that are in Tiferet: behold twenty-five in Tiferet. And Tiferet receives them to pour them to Yesod, which is kol, so that it pours them to the bride, which is Malkhut, in the secret of the union. And Yesod receives ten from Netzach, and ten from Hod, and four from Tiferet. How? Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut [of Tiferet]; for the Tiferet that is in Tiferet receives the upper twenty-five, and it is not in the count of the upper ones, for it is what receives them; and it is not in the count of the lower ones, for Yesod receives it only in the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, to pour to the bride, as we explained. Therefore they are twenty-five in Tiferet and twenty-four in Yesod; and the fiftieth gate is always revealed, and nothing is lacking from the fifty, as we explained.
And behold, with this this chapter is completed, and this Gate is completed.

And the commentators further added an explanation of the fifty gates in the Response of Elijah [Ma'aneh Eliyahu]; and because it does not settle with us, we did not want to copy it; and this is enough for us, until a true teacher comes. Blessed be the Compassionate One who has helped us.
The Fourteenth Gate: The Gate of Manifestations.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain the matter of the manifestations of the sefirot: for although they are only ten, they have manifestations within manifestations. And further, to explain known manifestations of the sefirot, as explained in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim, with God's help.
Chapter One:

The matter of the manifestations in this wisdom is a key that is used in many of the gates of this wisdom. And the matter is that the things of holiness, of the Emanation, and of subtle spirituality are not like the matters of this low, corporeal world. For the matters of the body, being corporeal and of lesser worth: when a man wants to perform an action on some corporeal thing other than himself, it is impossible for him to perform the action he wants unless all the manifestations of body that preceded in those corporeal things are first nullified, so that they are turned into the thing he wants in it. The illustration of this: when a man wants to bring into existence for himself a garment to wear, behold, he shears the wool or the hair from that animal. And behold, in truth, the wool acquires a condition different from what it was, and the animal remains stripped, naked, and in want of all.

Behold, the first manifestation was nullified when it came to be acted upon into another manifestation. Afterwards that wool is further whitened; and after its whitening the first manifestation that it had while it was in the fleece does not remain, for the first body has passed and gone, and it has acquired a manifestation fairer and choicer than the first, which is the manifestation of pure, whitened wool. And when that wool is spun, its first manifestation does not remain in it, for it has already been turned into something more praiseworthy, which is the yarn. And when the garment is woven, the manifestation of the yarn does not remain, for through the work it has stripped off its first form and put on a more perfected form. And in this way, as the works multiply, the forms are stripped off, and nullified, and pass away, and are as though they had not been, and its first forms will not be remembered.

And behold, this matter is in the accidents of bodies. But the things of holiness, of spirituality, and of the Emanation are the opposite of this matter, for these do not have its accidents. And although the kinds of the emanated and spiritual things spread forth and put on a form more revealed than they were before their spreading, their first manifestations are not on that account nullified, God forbid; but on the contrary, the things multiply without end, rising without limit. And even if the subtle spiritual thing is changed into a more revealed manifestation, nevertheless its first manifestation does not move from its place, and its seat is not vacant. Spirituality further differs from the corporeal in this matter: for the corporeal and all its newly arising manifestations are superior to the preceding ones, in particular in the actions intended by human beings; for the more it is acted upon, the nearer it comes to what is wanted, and this is its praise. And not so the spiritual; but on the contrary, the more it is revealed, the preceding manifestation is the principal and the root of its manifestations that arise and are emanated. And the root draws from its root, and its root from its root, according to the multitude of manifestations, until this depends on this and this depends on this, up to what precedes them all. And the higher they rise, the more praiseworthy they are, near to the source and the true root, which is the Root of all roots and the Source of all manifestations, the King of kings of kings. And a proof for the matter of manifestation is from the vessels of the Sanctuary and the articles of holiness: for if they replace them with new ones, the first ones are stored away, for their holiness still stands in them; for there remains in them a subtle holiness and spirituality, and its manifestation stands in its place; and the holiness remaining in them is the subtlest of the subtle, so that the eye cannot judge them at all. And even if the proof does not resemble the thing illustrated in every respect, because there the preceding is principal to what is emanated, as we explained, and this is not so in the illustration (for certainly the articles of holiness that stand to serve are more praiseworthy than those that have already been set aside), nevertheless the law is a true law, even if they do not resemble in everything. And the reason is that the articles of holiness are corporeal, and for the spiritual we have no apprehension by which to illustrate it. And for this reason our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded (Megillah 28a) "and I will make your sanctuaries desolate" (Lev. 26:31): even when they are desolate, they stand in their holiness. Because the Shekhinah dwelt there, something of holiness remained in them, which the eye cannot apprehend except with the eye of the intellect, according to our holy Torah. And according to these words was the matter in the sefirot: for when the will arose before Him to emanate them, there were formed the manifestations of the subtle, concealed Tzachtzachot, as we explained at length in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. And from that subtle manifestation the grades descended in a chain down to the revealing in thought, and there too second manifestations were formed. And we said "second" because one is not to investigate what is between Ein Sof and Keter at all, except that they are in subtlety in the Ein Sof, and they are emanated in Keter, which is what we called the manifestation of the revealing in thought. And the subtlety that is in the Ein Sof draws effluence to the subtle roots that are in Keter. And so manifestations were emanated from grade to grade. And the nearer they come to the Emanator they are called "face," and the farther they go they are called "back." And therefore [there are] "how many faces within the awesome faces, and how many backs behind backs that are not seen"; for the sefirah is not one substance of which one judges only one matter. Rather, in each and every sefirah [there are] how many manifestations, how many worlds, how many matters, which the intellect cannot apprehend. Their matter is revealed in the Torah, and the intellect of man cannot encompass them; for how is it possible that an effect of an effect, the smallest of the small, could encompass the cause of its cause, and not the cause of its cause alone, but descending from cause to effect without end? Except that the Holy One, blessed be He, wanted to give merit to Israel, and accustomed them to His Torah, etc. And nevertheless there is none who goes down to the depth of one of its secrets, because of its great concealment, except [by] this little light that comes out between the chinks and cracks of the gate, as thick as a needle; and these are the words of the divine, holy Rashbi, peace be upon him. And he taught us this matter in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 119b), and these are its words: "And how many inner sefirot, and how many back sefirot, and they are one upon the other; this is what is written (Eccl. 5:7), 'For one higher than the high watches, and there are higher ones over them.' And concerning them it is said, 'How many faces within the awesome faces, and how many backs behind backs that are not seen.' And these inner ones are יו"ד ה"י וי"ו ה"י, יו"ד ה"י וא"ו ה"י, יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א. The back ones are י' י"ה יה"ו יהו"ה, א' א"ה אה"י אהי"ה," etc. Thus far its words.

Although this passage has been explained in its place at length in the book Or Yakar, part two, nevertheless from within it a great light comes out for us toward what is intended: that the sefirot have many aspects, matters, and manifestations, which knowledge cannot include, for the reason mentioned. And besides this, there are further aspects in the sefirot, according to the aspect by which we wish to consider them: [one] is called thus, and this aspect is called thus; and this is the manifestations of the names related to each and every sefirah, for they are many, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And Rashbi explained it in many places; and these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 56, folio 87): "Heh [and] Heh: they are woman and her daughter, bride and her mother-in-law; according to the branches [of the tree], so are they called." Thus far its words.

And the intent is that Binah, which is the first Heh of the Name, and Malkhut, which is the final Heh of the Name, are sometimes called woman and her daughter, and sometimes bride and her mother-in-law. And it was difficult for him why their names change, so that they are called sometimes thus and sometimes thus. And he answered that this is not forced, for according to their branches so their names change; and the intent is, according to the change of their aspect, as will be explained in the gate mentioned.
