And this is a great opening and entrance in this wisdom. And there are many other distinctions; they will be explained in chapters of their own.

Besides the manifestation and the aspects mentioned above, there are yet other aspects. And it is that when we wish to consider the Emanation in the secret of its composition of judgment and compassion, that will be one aspect. And when we wish to consider it from the side that all of it is compassion, it will be another aspect. And likewise when we consider it from the side of each sefirah, from the side of its action by itself, without its fellows joined to it, it will be another matter. And when we wish to join one of them, according to which one is joined, their action and their aspect will change, and the aspects will rise to ten. And likewise when we wish [to join] two, it will change according to the change of the two. The illustration: when we join Malkhut to Yesod and Hod, it is one aspect in Malkhut; and if she is joined to Yesod and Netzach, it is another aspect; and if she is joined to Hod and Netzach, it is another aspect. So the aspects rise without end and without number, in the way we explained in the Gate of Channels, chapter 5. And besides this, when we consider the whole Emanation, for example as seven sefirot alone, or as ten together, or as the first three alone, certainly they are aspects that are not equal, and all is not one matter. And by this a mishnah in Sefer Yetzirah will be understood, and these are its words: "Ten sefirot belimah, and twenty-two letters of foundation: three mothers, and seven doubles, and twelve simples." Thus far its words. And it is the second mishnah; and the one preceding it we explained in the Gate of Paths, and there, in that mishnah, he said that they are thirty-two paths. And now in this mishnah he comes to explain their division and their number: since the sefirot are only ten, how are the paths thirty-two? And he said that they are ten sefirot and twenty-two letters, etc. And the matter is that the relation of all of them together is not equal to [what it is] when they are seven alone, for the shining of these is not like the shining of those; and this is examined in several ways, whether by way of likeness or by way of reckoning. And the illustration of this: the sefirot are ten, and each one is included of ten, as is known; behold, they rise to a hundred. And their reckoning will rise without end in the reckoning of tens and hundreds, for each part is also included of ten, without end; for there is no part of which we say, this is Keter alone and this is Chokhmah alone, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 2. And this is not [so] when we consider them relative to the seven, for [then] we say seven times seven, or seven times ten; and their reckoning will rise in another way, which is by way of sevens, although it too rises without end.

And behold, the reckoning of ten will not resemble the reckoning of seven. Further, by way of likeness: when we wish to liken the ten colors that are in the sefirot, behold, they will combine, and the colors will rise in a manner fairer and more praiseworthy in the multitude of its colors than what would rise if they were only seven; for the combination of the colors would not yield as praiseworthy a color as when they are ten. Further, we can give this parable in a manner more fitting to the thing illustrated: if the great theriac is made, which has many kinds of drugs in it, its virtue will be greater than what there will be in the theriac of four kinds; for this one helps against the deadly, venomous poison, and the small one helps, but not so much; and this is clear. And in this way we compare it to the sefirot, after we know their division into judgment and compassion, as came before us in the Gate of Essence and Governance.

And behold, when the compassion of the first three is with the seven, the blending will incline more to compassion; and the reason is that the compassion is simple in the blending. And when the first three are alone, the compassion will spread more and more, and the whole blending will incline to compassion, which will not be so when they are joined to the last seven sefirot. And when the seven are alone, then the blending inclines more to judgment than [in] the two preceding arrays. And with this preliminary this mishnah will be understood. For there are four arrays in the thirty-two paths, and all in the very substance of the sefirot. The first array is the blending of all ten together, and that is the ten sefirot mentioned in our mishnah. Further, the second array, and they are the three mothers, which are Alef-Mem-Shin, which are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, which are mothers to Chesed, Din, and Rachamim, as explained in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 3. Further, the third array, and they are the blending of the seven sefirot alone, which are hinted at by the double letters, which are Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaf, Peh, Resh, Tav. And they are called doubles because they receive dagesh and rafeh and serve for two; and dagesh and rafeh are a hint to judgment and compassion, and a hint to the seven sefirot of the Structure, which sometimes act in judgment and sometimes in compassion. And the twelve simples are the fourth array, which are the twelve boundaries, which are the twelve havayot, and they are the six extremities acting judgment and compassion, as will be explained at length in the Gate of Particulars of Names, on the name of seventy-two, in chapters 7, 8, 9, and 10.

And behold, they are not the seven sefirot, but they are the six extremities, which in known places are particular branches, as will be explained in the gate mentioned. And again we found a passage in the Zohar close to this mishnah, in this preliminary; and it is in Parashat Pekudei (folio 227b), and these are its words, on the verse (Exod. 38:28) "And of the thousand and seven hundred and seventy-five he made hooks [vavim]," etc.: "All those Vavs Betzalel made, to give them to rest upon the female ones [nukvei, the sockets]. And they come out from the secret of the thousand, which is a complete reckoning; and seven hundred, which is a complete secret; and five likewise; and seventy, all one secret. And therefore from this secret and this reckoning he made hooks; and all was made in the secret of Vav and the image of Vav, and all in the supernal secret." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: he comes to explain the matter of the Vavs in their number: that it is not fitting to believe that their weight came so by way of accident and chance, but the matter was with deliberate intent. And this is what he meant in saying "all those Vavs that Betzalel made": explanation: since Betzalel made them. And our Sages, of blessed memory, have already expounded that Betzalel knew how to permute the letters by which heaven and earth were created; and likewise the verse testified of him (Exod. 31:3), "And I have filled him with the spirit of God," etc.; and they explained that just as the creation of heaven and earth was with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, so was the work of the Tabernacle. And the place of the dwelling of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge was upon Betzalel; and for this reason it was necessary that he knew how to permute the letters by which the world was created, since the spirituality of the letters, which are included in Chokhmah, Tevunah, and Da'at, was included in him. "To give them to rest upon the female ones," etc.: the intent is that those Vavs hinted at the male, which is Tiferet, called Vav. And although they were upon the pillars, and the pillars themselves are male, as is well known, nevertheless the principal was the Vavs, which were from the side of Tiferet, which is the principal of the Vav; and from them the effluence of the lower earth, hinted in Malkhut, was drawn; and the pillar was between them, to indicate the pillar that unites heaven and earth, as is known: "The Holy One, blessed be He, has one pillar, and Righteous is its name," etc. "And they come out from the secret of the thousand, which is a complete reckoning": explanation: it is known that all the sefirot are included of ten; and behold, according to this they are ten times ten, rising to a hundred; and each one of the hundred is included of ten: they will rise to a thousand. And because this number includes all ten sefirot with the inclusion of their inclusion, he called it "a complete reckoning," meaning a complete number; which is not so with other numbers, which do not include all the branches as the number thousand does. And one is not to explain that "complete number" means that the thousand is a complete number because it includes units, tens, hundreds, thousands; for the sages in the science of number have already written that the completeness of number is ten, for the reason that from ten upward is the doubling of the units and the tens, and by the joining of these parts the number rises and is multiplied without end; and if so, the complete number is ten, and this is a clear thing.

And further, we can explain it in this way: in the alphabet the number is found up to nine hundred, and from there it turns the thousands back to units. So according to this the thousand is the complete number, which embeds the end of the number in its beginning. And we shall depict here a fine figure by which our intent will be explained in brief, thus:

And behold, when the hundreds are completed, the number of the thousands is equal to the units; and the Alef is what embeds its end in its beginning; for אל"ף [Alef] is אלף [elef, thousand], is פלא [pele, wonder]; and it is the Supernal Keter, which embeds its end in its beginning and its beginning in its end, in the secret of אי"ן / אנ"י [ayin, Nothing / ani, I], which we explained in Gate Three, and likewise we shall explain it in the Gate "From Below to Above." And for this reason the Alef is called a complete number; and it is the drawing forth of Tiferet from Keter, for the inclusion of the sefirot of ten is through Chokhmah, and all the more in its ascent from ten to ten, as we explained. "And seven hundred, which is a complete secret": he was precise not to say "complete number," as he said above, because it is not complete for all of them; but he said "a complete secret," because the seven sefirot are full and complete in the whole inclusion of ten (a word is missing) of ten, in the way of the preceding ten; except that the foundation of the preceding ones is ten, and therefore they rose to a thousand, and the foundation of these is seven, and therefore they rose only to seven hundred. And therefore he did not say "complete number," because the number ten was not completed. And it is called complete for the reason of the completeness of each one of its sefirot in a hundred gates; and for this he said "a complete secret." "And five likewise": explanation: for five too are in the secret of the Vav, as the number of the sefirot, in the secret of the inclusion of the seven in five, as we explained in the gates. And likewise when we remove from the count of the seven the pillar and the socket, five remain. "And seventy, all one secret": explanation: for the seventy too is in the secret of seven hundred, except that these are included in a great inclusion, and those are included in one inclusion only, that is, each one of the seven is included of ten: the seven turn out to rise to seventy. "And therefore from this secret and this reckoning he made hooks": explanation: to hint at this great secret, that Tiferet be included of all these aspects. "And all in the secret of Vav," etc.: it was difficult for him: for the Alef is a hint in all ten, and the seven hundred and seventy are in the seven, and the five likewise; and if so, what relates this number to Tiferet? And to this he answered, "and all in the secret of Vav"; and a proof for this is their form, for they were made like a Vav; except that it is Tiferet when it is included of all these manifestations. And so these [hooks] turn out to be in the secret of the upper ones in their form, their hinting, their place, and their reckoning: in their form, that they were in the form of Vav; in their hinting, for so they were hinting at Tiferet; in their place, that they stood upon the pillars, in the secret of the Vav upon the continuation of the Vav, which is Tiferet upon the Righteous One; and in their reckoning, in the secret of the thousand, and the seven hundred, and the five, and the seventy. And now there is no escaping saying that the seven hundred are not part of the thousand; rather it is a manifestation by itself, for the manifestation of the thousand is choicer than the manifestation of the seven hundred; and likewise for the seventy, and likewise for the five: each one is a manifestation by itself. And it was necessary for the matter of the Tabernacle that the Vav be included of all the manifestations, for the reason that Malkhut too should be included of all the manifestation. And the illustration of this: when we take a stone from the stones, or a piece of wood from the woods, and divide it in two, behold, of necessity those parts will be found, from the side of their unity, equal in their fibers and their figure, and this figure will not differ from that figure, for both were one piece, and one manifestation is necessary for them. And so is the matter in the emanation of Tiferet and Malkhut, since they were double-faced, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon.

And behold, although the Holy One, blessed be He, sawed them apart, nevertheless they are equal, like the parable we gave. And therefore, when the male is unified with the female in all his limbs with a complete and whole union, it is necessary that they be equal with a complete equality, the female receiving to the male and the male to the female, for they are like receiver and giver. And all the more since we have seen the matter of the channels, which we explained in chapter 1 of the gate we devoted to them. And therefore in the Tabernacle, to hint at all the divisions of their division, so that the union be complete, it was necessary that they be according to that number, so that the Vav be included of all the parts and aspects by which it can be considered, so that the female too may be considered in all those aspects, to receive from him. And from this reason the necessity will be understood why all that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph (Bereshit Rabbah 84:6): because Yesod unites Tiferet and Malkhut in all the parts and aspects of the two of them; and if so, it is necessary according to this that there be in it an aspect equal to the aspect of Malkhut and Tiferet, so that "the loops may be opposite" (Exod. 26:5), "and together they shall be whole at its head" (Exod. 26:24).

Our intent in this chapter is to explain manifestations that are explained in some of the passages of the Zohar, which are very much needed for contemplation in this wisdom. And it is the manifestation of Binah, the manifestation of Tiferet, and the manifestation of Malkhut. As for the manifestation of Binah, there are two manifestations in her. The first, a manifestation that has no relation with the Emanation at all; and it is hinted in the manifestations of Yod, the subtle point that is in Binah. And the second, a manifestation that is related to the Emanation, from the side of the manifestation that she has. And one cannot say that the manifestation of the Yod is only in Chokhmah, and that the letter of Binah is Heh; for the letter of Binah is also Yod. And so it is explained in the words of Rashbi, that three Yods are the first three; and that is the aspect of Binah with the two upper ones, and she is hinted in Yod, like each one of the other upper ones. But when she emanates the Emanation in their place, then she has the aspect of the Heh.

And behold, the aspect of the Yod is called Mi [who], which is a question without an answer, because of her great concealment. And the aspect of Heh is hinted in Eleh [these], which are the three fathers, that is, the three Vavs that are in the form of the Heh, thus: ה; and the right Vav is Chesed, and its roof is Gevurah, and the hanging leg is Tiferet; and they are called Eleh. And to understand this matter well, one must contemplate what we shall write in the Gate of Names, chapters 8 and 9, and in the Gate "From Below to Above," chapter 5, on the name אלדי"ם [Elohim], which is the permutation of מ"י אל"ה [Mi Eleh]: Heh upon Yod, as explained in the Tikkunim many times. He means the Heh, which is a garment to the Yod, thus:

And therefore she is female, for the aspect of revealing caused her to be female. But before, she is Yod alone, in the secret of a point equal to the two points. But by reason of her emanation, to emanate the Emanation, the manifestation of three lines was formed in her. For when she oversees in Chesed, to pour them forth, it is necessary that there be in her the aspect of Chesed; and when she oversees in compassion, it is necessary that there be in her the aspect of compassion; and when she oversees in judgment, it is necessary that there be in her the aspect of judgment. And these three aspects that were formed in her are certainly the manifestation of the source of the three lines, which remained there in subtlety, which are root and source to the revealed ones. And there is no question to say that the fathers are not Vavs, but only Tiferet; for so they explained in the Tikkunim, apart from this inquiry, and said that the three verses וayyissa, וayyavo, וayyet (Exod. 14:19–21) are three Vavs in three fathers. And after we have explained these two manifestations in Binah, we say that both of them are also in Malkhut. And they are hinted in these two letters literally, in Heh and Yod: for her principal is Yod, and her manifestation that is emanated to her receives the three lines [which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod] and becomes Heh. And close to this matter it is explained in the Zohar (Shelach, folio 171a), and these are its words: "That child [yenuka] opened and said (Zech. 14:8): 'And it shall be on that day' [ba-yom ha-hu]: it is not known who it is. But everywhere 'on that day' is the last day. Why is it called 'that day'? But this is the secret: it is the day that holds the end to the beginning. The beginning is called hu ['he,' 'that'], as it is written (Num. 18:23), 'And the Levite, he [hu], shall do the service': the service of the Levite is to the grade called hu, concealed and stored away. And it is called hahu ['that'] to show the end of all the grades, which is the beginning, and all is one; and because it is the end, Heh was added to it. Jerusalem is destined to bring forth waters and to make springs flow. Here there is [room] to say: the end of all the grades is not Jerusalem. But certainly Jerusalem and that day are all one. What is [the difference] between this and that? But Jerusalem: all her holy grades, when they go around, are called Jerusalem, and so they are bounded. There are grades that go around and are called courts, these inner and these outer; and there are grades that, when they go around, are called chambers; and there are grades that, when they go around, are called Heikhal and Devir. Within all those grades there is one point: 'All glorious is the king's daughter within' (Ps. 45:14). This point is called 'that day'; and your sign: 'that too is reckoned a land of Rephaim' (Deut. 2:20). And when this day rises from within the (vaults) (lattices) of the court, the flow of waters will rise; and this flow [goes] to the former sea [ha-yam ha-kadmoni], to be like a mother whose son is between her arms, and the milk increases, and the suckling's mouth is filled, and it grows by it, and it pours the milk out into its mother's mouth. So 'half of them to the former sea'" (Zech. 14:8), etc. Thus far its words.

And behold, this passage is long in its place, and we have abridged it and copied from it what we need. And the matter in brief: this yenuka was a child who departed from the world for a reason known to Him, blessed be He; and when his soul ascended to the entrance of the gates of the Garden of Eden, the cherubim, the guardians of the Garden, held him, so as not to let him enter, for a reason stated there. And meanwhile the head of the academy of the righteous was expounding on this verse, "And it shall be on that day"; and the child, from outside, objected, and these are his words: "Waters that are below: how do they rise from it to a place higher than it by many grades? And what need have those [above] of those waters? And a place from which all the springs and streams go out, and there is no ceasing to its springs and streams, is watered from a dry place? Who has seen the digging of a well give water to the spring that flows? And does Jerusalem give water to the former sea, the place from which all the waters of the world go out?" Thus far its words.

And it is a strong difficulty: for Jerusalem is Malkhut, and the former sea is Binah, and therefore it is called "former"; and how is it possible that Binah should be watered from Malkhut? And to answer this difficulty, after they brought him into the academy, he opened and said: "And it shall be on that day: it is not known," etc. For the word hu indicates the hidden [third person], and it is a title for concealment, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles; and the Heh of knowledge [the definite article] indicates the revealed, as is well known. And behold, they are two opposites in one word. And this is what he intended in saying "hahu: it is not known who [hu] it is": explanation: hu indicates concealment, and hahu indicates revealing, and they are two opposites. And he answered: "But everywhere 'on that day'" is Malkhut, which is the last day. And although she is the attribute of night, she is also day, for there are seven days, and the name "day" is already related to her. And since she is Malkhut, it is fitting that it come with the Heh of knowledge, because she is revealed and known; but the word hu cannot properly be said, for it indicates concealment, as we explained. And he answered: "But this is the secret: it is the day," etc. Explanation: to indicate the manifestation of the Yod, which is a concealed manifestation that is in her. For Malkhut is beginning and ending, which is beginning and end, as we say, "the beginning of thought is the end of action": for she is above in Chokhmah, in the manifestation of Yod, and she is the end of action in Malkhut, in the manifestation of Heh. And he said that the concealed manifestation, which is the beginning, is called hu, which indicates beginning. And a proof is from what is written, "And the Levite, he [hu], shall do the service"; and the service of the Levite is to Binah, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 10.

And behold, hu indicates the beginning, which is first and earliest; for Binah is called "the beginning that stands to be asked about," as we explained there in chapter 15. And the aspect of the revealed manifestation, which is the end of all the grades, is called hahu, with the Heh of knowledge. So the word hahu turns out to indicate the two manifestations together. And behold, the yenuka explained her two manifestations, in the Heh that surrounds the Yod, in the matter of hahu.

And behold, the middle point is called "All glorious is the king's daughter within." And likewise it is called "the apple of the eye" [bat ayin], for it is like the pupil of the eye, a tiny, fine point, and around it three colors, which are the colors of the rainbow; they are the three fathers.

And behold, this point ascends to its place, its height, to her father's house, Chokhmah, by means of the effluence of Binah, which is the mother who nurses her with the milk; and through her she is exalted, until she ascends and pours effluence even into Binah herself, as he said, "like a mother whose son," etc. And likewise she pours effluence into her literal lower manifestation (which is the Heh, to feed the lower ones by it); and this is "and half of them to the latter sea." And the sum of the matters: Binah has Heh, and her manifestation is the three fathers; and Malkhut has Heh, and her manifestation is Netzach, Hod, and Yesod. And these two preliminaries are explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Terumah, folio 158), and these are its words: "The vessel of the Holy One, blessed be He, is the Shekhinah, which is a vessel to serve her husband. She is His candelabrum, of which it is said (Ps. 119:164), 'Seven times a day I praise You,' which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and Malkhut, seven included. Of these seven grades, three branches of the candelabrum from its one side: the body and the two arms of the King; she is a lamp of commandment to illumine by them. And three branches of the candelabrum from its second side: they are the two thighs and the covenant; and she is the western lamp to illumine by them. She is called the King's candelabrum, and she is a lamp to illumine by it, the lamp of commandment, of which it is said (Ps. 19:9), 'The commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.' And who is the head of the candelabrum? Binah, the upper Heh, which has three branches, in this image, ה: three Vavs, which are the three fathers. The second Heh: three second branches, in this image, ה: three Vavs, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod. Vav: the middle candelabrum, son [ben] of Yah; after his name Binah [bin-Yah] is called; he includes six branches below, in the reckoning of Vav, in his six branches. Yod: 'a woman of valor is the diadem of her husband' (Prov. 12:4), the crown of the Torah scroll, in the form of Zayin. From the side of the World to Come she is not a vessel for Him, and does not serve Him, but a diadem on His head. But in this world she is like this, הוה"י: she is a vessel beneath Him, His service," etc. Thus far its words. And in it, explicitly, that each of the two Hehs is three Vavs. And also the manifestation of Malkhut, that she is sometimes Yod, when she ascends above; and then she is called "a woman of valor, the diadem of her husband," for she is Yod, a diadem upon Vav, and becomes Zayin; and she is the diadem of Tiferet. And this is when she ascends to Binah to be unified with Chokhmah, from which is her manifestation, as we explained above. And now we come in a further chapter to explain further the matter of the manifestations of the Yod to Malkhut in the Heh, although it will be explained in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon.

Since above we said incidentally that the manifestation of Malkhut is from Chokhmah, we come in this chapter to decide concerning some passages of the Tikkunim, and these are their words (in Tikkun 69, folio 103): "And further, 'I am asleep [yeshenah]': second [sheniyah], certainly, to Chokhmah, which is Yod, when my beloved, who is Vav, is far from me. And the secret of the matter: Heh: 'The Lord founded the earth by wisdom; He established the heavens by understanding [tevunah]' (Prov. 3:19). Chokhmah, which is Abba, Yod, founded the daughter, who is earth, small Heh: 'the earth,' certainly. 'He established the heavens': this is Vav. 'By understanding': this is the supernal Imma. For she is called Binah above, when she is with her husband; she is called Tevunah below, when she is with Vav below; and it is ב"ן ו' [ben, Vav], and Tav, which is Tiferet; she remains Heh with him. And at that time, when the letter Vav is with Imma and he is far from her, it is said of her, 'I am asleep' in exile, and she is second to him." And the intent is that when Malkhut is above she is second to Chokhmah, and she is literally Yod, like it, as he explained in many places. And this is what he was precise about in saying "second, certainly, to Chokhmah, which is Yod": in the secret of the manifestation of the Yod, in which the two of them are equal: this is the Yod of the four-letter name, and this is the Yod of Adonai. (And in the Sifra di-Tzeni'uta, Parashat Terumah, folio 176) among the havayot he brings a havayah like this, יהו"י, and it indicates the secret of the matter mentioned; and these are its words: "יהו"י: the last Yod is the Shekhinah (below), just as the Heh is found [to be] the Shekhinah; and they are weighed on one scale." Thus far its words.

And they said "when my beloved is far from me," etc.: explanation: Malkhut says that she is second to Chokhmah at the time that she has been distanced from her husband. And the matter is that in the four-letter name, whose letters are ידו"ד in their order, they are sometimes permuted to ידד"ו; and he means that Malkhut has ascended to Chokhmah, to her father's house, and Tiferet is unified with Binah. And this is what he explained: "And the secret of the matter: Heh: 'The Lord founded the earth by wisdom,'" etc. Explanation: by Chokhmah, which is Yod, was the foundation of the earth; for the earth is Malkhut in the manifestation of Heh, and the foundation of the Heh is Yod, which is the manifestation of the rib that was taken from the man. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 12, folio 27a), and these are his words: "And it is said there concerning Adam (Gen. 2:22): 'And the Lord God built the rib that He had taken from the man': this is Chokhmah. 'And He brought her to the man': this is the central pillar," etc. He taught that the manifestation of the Yod is the manifestation of the rib, and she was taken from Chokhmah, which is the upper Adam, and was built in the building of the Heh, as we shall explain; and then He unified her with Tiferet.

And behold, the foundation of the building, which is Heh, is thus:

And this is what he said: "Chokhmah, which is Abba, Yod, founded the daughter, who is earth, small Heh: 'the earth,' certainly." Explanation: the manifestation called "earth," that is, her lower aspect, the matter of the earth, which is below all: the foundation of this earth was in Chokhmah, as we explained. "He established the heavens by understanding": and likewise the establishing and building of the heavens was by Tevunah. For their principal is from Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 2; for the manifestation of the firmament is from Chokhmah; but its establishment, that is, its building, and the aspect that surrounds and clothes the firmament, that is, the aspect called "heavens," was by Tevunah, which is Binah when she is unified with Tiferet, as he concludes. This matter is further explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 29, folio 73a), and these are its words: "And the lower Shekhinah, commandment, is included of four letters: she is called Yod from the side of Chokhmah, Heh from the side of the supernal Imma," etc. Thus far its words.

Behold, explicitly, that the manifestation of Yod is from the side of Chokhmah, and then she is called after Chokhmah; and so it is explained elsewhere (in the Introduction, folio 10): "When she is taken from Chokhmah, she is called Reshit [beginning] after it." Thus far. And likewise she is Heh from the side of Binah, that is, the building, as is written (Gen. 2:22), "And the Lord God built the rib"; and these two names indicate Binah. And so Rashbi explained in the commentary on the Song of Songs (in Zohar Chadash, folio 83), on the verse "like the curtains of Solomon" (Song 1:5); and there he explained that sometimes her building will be from Binah in the manifestation of Tet, which covers over the Yod. For Binah is Lamed; and when a building is built around the Yod of Malkhut, it is formed in the form of Tet, that is, a Lamed in a circle, thus:

And likewise the matter of this manifestation is explained in the episode of the yenuka; and for love of brevity we shall not dwell on bringing their wording here. And likewise they explained the matter in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, folio 246), and these are its words: "The holy Kingship does not receive complete kingship until it is joined with the fathers; and when it is joined with them it is built into a complete building from the upper world." Thus far its words. (And so it is in the Zohar, Va'era, folio 31.)

Behold, explicitly, that the principal of her building, that is, Heh, is through the three fathers, which are three Vavs, as explained in the preceding chapter. And likewise by their power she is built in three Vavs, that is, Heh; and the principal of the building is from the upper world, that is, the secret of Binah, as we explained. And likewise this inquiry is also explained in Sefer ha-Bahir; these are its words: "Rabbi Yannai said: The earth was created before the heavens, as it is said (Gen. 2:4), 'earth and heavens.' They said to him: But behold, it is written (Gen. 1:1), 'the heavens and the earth.' He said to them: A parable: to what is the matter like? To a king who acquired a fine object; it was not complete, and he did not call a name upon it, and said: I will complete it, and set right its base and its joining, and then I will call it a name. This is what is written (Ps. 102:26): 'Of old You founded the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.' And it says (Ps. 104:2–5): 'Who wraps Himself in light as a garment, who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters'; and it says, 'who makes His angels winds, His ministers a flaming fire'; and afterwards, 'He founded the earth upon its bases, that it should not be moved, forever and ever [olam va-ed].' When He set right a place for her, then she was strengthened in it, as it is said, 'that it should not be moved.' And what is her name? Va-ed. And her base is olam; and this is olam va-ed." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: "the earth was created": the intent is that Malkhut preceded Tiferet in the manifestation of the revealing of her emanation, as will be explained in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon, chapter 3. And he brought a proof for this from the verse (Gen. 2:4) "on the day that the Lord God made earth and heavens," which shows that the earth preceded the heavens. And they objected to him from the verse "the heavens and the earth," for the heavens were created first, as is evident from the plain sense of the verse. And he answered them by way of a fine parable: to a king who acquired a fine object, which is Malkhut; and the matter of this acquisition is the beginning of her emanation in Chokhmah, and it too is called king; and because it was not complete, for she was in the manifestation of a rib, lacking the building. And they said "and he did not call a name upon it": the intent is, he did not emanate it and did not reveal it so as to be bounded and titled with a name, but kept it standing until its preparation and until the preparation of its place, which is the Chariot upon which the glory of Malkhut stands: it is her base. And the completion is the building, the building of the rib, which is the manifestation of the Heh that is in her, as we explained. And he brought a proof for this from the verse "Of old You founded the earth": explanation: before the heavens, You founded the earth, which is Malkhut.

And the matter of "You founded" is the foundation founded in Chokhmah, as he said, "Abba founded the daughter," as we explained. And from this verse is a proof for the matter of the foundation of the earth, that it precedes the work of the heavens, that is, the establishing of the heavens; for its work is through Binah, as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And this is "and he said, I will complete it," which intended the building mentioned above. And for the matter of the base he proved from the verse "Who wraps Himself in light as a garment." And to understand the matter of this proof we must copy here what the Elder explained on it (in Parashat Mishpatim, folio 98), and these are its words: "'Who wraps Himself in light as a garment': this is the beginning of the first day. 'Who stretches out the heavens': here the left is included; and he did not say 'very'; the left is included in the right, to shine in the totality of heavens. 'Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters': here there goes out in joy that tree of life, the river that goes out of Eden; and in its waters were rooted those two willows of the brook, which grow in its waters; this is what is written, 'who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters.' What are 'His upper chambers'? These are the willows of the brook. And this is what is written (Jer. 17:8), 'and spreads out its roots by the stream.' And this is the secret of what is written (Ps. 46:5), 'There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God.' What are 'its streams'? They are these, its roots. And so they are called: its upper chambers, its roots, its streams; all of them were rooted in those waters of that river. 'Who makes the clouds His chariot' (Ps. 104:3): this is Michael and Gabriel; these are clouds. 'Who walks upon the wings of the wind': to give healing to the world, and this is Raphael. From here on, 'who makes His angels winds,'" etc. Thus far its words.

And although this passage needs explanation, nevertheless for our intent we learned that the order of the Emanation is mentioned in this verse: Gedulah, Gevurah included in Tiferet, and the two Netzachs, which are Netzach and Hod, and likewise the continuation of the river. But Malkhut was not yet mentioned. And therefore he mentioned the lower Chariot, which is Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael; and there is no doubt that Uriel is mentioned there, for this is the intent of "wings of the wind," in the plural; and likewise the other angels are mentioned. Behold, explicitly, that the chariots are mentioned, which are her base; and then he said "He founded the earth upon its bases." And this is what he meant in saying "When He set right a place for her, then she was strengthened in it": explanation: after He created the chariots, then she is strengthened and firm, and then "she shall not be moved." And he was precise in saying "And what is her name? Va-ed": explanation: the name of Malkhut, which is (her) foundation, the manifestation of the Yod, called va-ed. And perhaps the reason is that the Emanation reached up to her [adeha]; and we shall explain it in the Glossary of Titles (in the entry ad). "And her base is olam": for the base is from the side of Binah, for the building is built in Binah; and it is the manifestation of the Heh, which are from the side of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet; and from there are Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, or Uriel, as we shall explain in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 7. And for the reason that the principal of the base is after Binah, he said "and her base is olam," after Binah, which is called olam [world]. And this is "that it should not be moved, forever and ever [olam va-ed]." And the matter of "that it should not be moved": through her pouring effluence and receiving, she will endure, in the way of the Shekhinah in the lower ones, which we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance.

And behold, the explanation of the passage is completed; and from within it the principal of the preliminary that we are explaining has been explained. And with the matter of the preliminaries of the manifestations mentioned in this Gate, a very difficult matter will be explained, concerning the intention in the Shema, in the first paragraph of the Shema, at the word echad [one]: for we raise the sefirot to Binah and from there upward. For is this not the matter of the Jubilee, that the branches return to their root, and all returns to Binah, and the world is laid waste and lost? And if so, what is the tikkun that we bring about with this intention? And with this preliminary the matter will be understood: when we raise (when you raise) an attribute or attributes above, nevertheless their manifestation remains in its place. And this is not the matter of the Jubilee; for in the Jubilee the manifestations and the branches too return to their source. And so Rashbi explained concerning the commandment of the Kedushah (in the Zohar, Emor, folio 93), and these are his words: "And since Israel sanctify, the supernal Glory rises from below to above, until Vav, the secret of the upper heavens, ascends above. Since those heavens have ascended above, that holy [kodesh] shines in them, and then it is called above 'holy' [kadosh]. And afterwards that supernal light shines upon the Throne, which is heavens; and those heavens return to their place and are settled in that light, and then it is called 'holy.' Afterwards that light descends until the supernal Righteous One, the precious supernal grade, takes all as one, to sanctify all below. Since he takes all, then it is called 'holy,'" etc. Thus far its words.

And we shall explain it in brief. Above this, Rashbi explained that [there are] three "holy": one in Keter, one in Tiferet, one in Yesod; and all these three grades receive holiness from the supernal holy [kodesh], which is Keter. And it was difficult for Rashbi that in Keter there is no kadosh with Vav, but kodesh. And he answered this: that the heavens, which are Tiferet, called Vav, ascend above; and when the Vav ascends to Keter, called kodesh, what was kodesh becomes kadosh. And he went back and said, "afterwards that supernal light shines upon the Throne, which is heavens": explanation: the manifestation of Tiferet that remains in its place, which is a throne to the subtle manifestation, which is the secret of the firmament, as explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 2. And the revealed manifestation is called a throne to the manifestation that ascends; and as in this case of Tiferet, so from his words we learn concerning the manifestation of the other sefirot, that their manifestation remains in their place. And from there the second "holy" spreads, and the third, in Yesod, which is the continuation of the Vav. And incidentally we have learned the matter of the three Vavs: one in Keter, through the subtle Da'at that ascends there, as explained; and the second literally in Tiferet; and the third in Yesod. Thus far.
And behold, this chapter is completed, and this Gate is concluded.
The Fifteenth Gate: The Gate From Below to Above.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain the matter mentioned concerning the sefirot in the Tikkunim and in the Zohar, "from below to above" and "from above to below." For at first glance the matter is difficult: for what is from below to above is the same as what is from above to below, and he counts them twice, as will be explained.
Chapter One:

The matter is that the sefirot, just as they are from above to below in their order, Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and Malkhut, so they are from below to above, Keter, Chokhmah, etc. How? Keter in Malkhut, and Chokhmah in Yesod, and Binah in Hod, and Gedulah in Netzach, and Gevurah in Tiferet, and Tiferet in Gevurah, and Netzach in Gedulah, and Hod in Binah, and Yesod in Chokhmah, and Malkhut in Keter. And so that this matter may not be difficult in the eyes of the discerning, we shall give him a fine parable: it is like the ray of the sun that spreads from its source and strikes the polished mirror; then its light reverses and returns to its source; and this is what is called among the investigators "the reversing light." And likewise we, when we wished to hint at this secret in these our gates, called it by the name "the reversing light" or "the returning light," for all is one matter. And let us return to the intent: that literally like the light mentioned, so is the likeness of the Emanation. For the sefirot, which are the Emanation, spread from above to below in the direct order of the sefirot; this is what we have sometimes called in these gates "direct light," and it is that they spread in this order. And so the light does: its station is in Malkhut, and it returns to its source, up to Keter, and there is its station. And this is "their end is embedded in their beginning and their beginning in their end": for Keter abides in Malkhut and Malkhut in Keter. And not this alone, but even the Malkhut that is in Keter returns and descends below; and its conduct is in the way of the first light, until it becomes light for light and light for light without end; and all is embedded, end in head and head in end. And this is the secret of the havayah in directness and the secret of the havayah in reversal: this in the secret of the direct light, and this in the secret of the reversing light, thus:

The matter is hinted in the secret of Alef, which is Yod at the head and Yod at the end, thus:

And the secret is Yod at the head and Yod at the end, for the source of the light is always Yod. And from there the light flows: sometimes the Yod is above, and it is direct light, and source, and head; and sometimes the Yod is below, and it is reversing light, and the source of the returning light. And so their end turns out to be embedded in their beginning and their beginning in their end. And so Rashbi explained in the explanation of this mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, and these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, folio 60a): "And this stone is Yod at the head of Alef, and it is Yod at its end; of it is said (Isa. 46:10), 'declaring the end from the beginning'; and it is יו"ד ה"י וא"ו ה"י, including ten sefirot, for their end is embedded in their beginning and their beginning in their end." Thus far its words.

He intended in the name mentioned that the letters of the name are direct, יהו"ה, and the name reversed, הוה"י, and all is included in the ten letters that are in the filling of the name; and this is the matter of Alef, which is Yod at the head and Yod at the end. And it is "declaring from the beginning," which is Yod, in the secret of Chokhmah, and its tip, which is Keter; "the end," which is likewise Yod; and it is Chokhmah at the head and Chokhmah at the end. And after the matter has been explained in general and in brief, we come to decide the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim [in the Introduction, folio 6a]: "'There is none holy like the Lord' (1 Sam. 2:2): the Cause over all, concealed and stored away in Keter; and from it the light spreads upon יהו"ה, which is: Yod, Chokhmah; Heh, Binah; Vav, including six sefirot; Heh, Malkhut. And this is the spreading from above to below. And likewise its light spreads upon [the Yod of Adonai], from below to above, up to Ein Sof, which is hinted in אדנ"י: אי"ן, אנ"י. And therefore the two Yods of יאהדונה"י: ten, ten; the Kaf [of 'like the Lord']: this is the Kaf of Keter." Thus far its words. He taught explicitly our intent: that the direct light goes out and spreads from the source, which is Yod, to the end, which is Heh; and returns from the Yod of Adonai, which is Malkhut (for Adonai is a garment to YHVH, thus: יאהדונה"י, as we shall explain in the Gate of Names, chapter 13); and the name Adonai is the secret of the reversing light; for the name Adonai and the name הוה"י are all one matter and one hint. And this is the secret of אנ"י / אי"ן [ani, I / ayin, Nothing]: that is, ani is Adonai, in Malkhut, and ayin is in Keter; and all hints at "its end embedded in its beginning and its beginning in its end." And just as in the secret of Keter the Yod is over the Heh, so in ayin the Yod is over the Nun; for all is one hint and one matter. And just as in Malkhut the Yod is under the Heh, so in ani the Nun is over the Yod. And all is one: this in Chokhmah, which is Yod; Nun in Binah, which is Heh. And because two lights are unified in Keter, two measures in the sefirah, ten from above to below and ten from below to above, therefore it is called Kaf [twenty], Keter. And this is "There is none holy like [ka-] the Lord," whose explanation is: Kaf, Keter, which is the spreading of the light from above to below and from below to above, as we explained.

And behold, in this much is included in little: that the sefirot are ten from above to below, in the secret of the direct light, and likewise ten from below to above, in the secret of the reversing light, the returning light. And now we come in [the next] chapter to explain this matter even in some of the sefirot.

The intent in this chapter is to explain that the matter of this order is not only for all ten sefirot in their totality, but also for some of them. How? If we wish to say nine from Keter to Yesod and nine from Yesod to Keter; and likewise eight from Hod to Keter and eight from Keter to Hod; and likewise seven from Chesed to Malkhut and seven from Malkhut to Chesed. And not this alone, but even in one sefirah, as we shall explain. And all these aspects are explained in the Tikkunim, as we shall explain. And the reason for them is that just as there is the shining of the return of the light from Malkhut, so there is the return of the light from Yesod, and likewise from Hod, and likewise for all of them. And just as there is direct light from Keter, so from Chokhmah, so from Binah, so from Chesed; for each sefirah is a source for all that is beneath it, and each sefirah is a mirror in which the light of the upper one strikes and the light returns; until in this way the luminaries rise, direct and returning, without number, as the inquirer will understand with his intellect when he sets his heart to what is hinted. And now we come to explain this matter from within the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, folio 31b), and these are his words: "These go out, and Sagron closes the gate after them. Behold, the masters of the signs knock at the entrance and say (Ps. 51:17), 'Adonai, open my lips.' 'Open': this is Petachon. And these are the masters of the eighteen [chai] blessings of prayer, from the side of the Life [Chai] of the worlds, who unite the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah there; for the Righteous One is ninth from above to below and from below to above: nine vowel-points, nine cantillation marks. And of them is said, 'And God set them in the firmament of the heaven' (Gen. 1:17): and this is the Righteous One, in which are all the vowel-points; 'to give light upon the earth': this is the Shekhinah, which is included of all the letters." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: there are righteous ones who depend [above], each one according to his deeds, according to the emanation of his soul from the sefirot. How? Those whose Torah is their craft are called masters of Torah, and they are in Tiferet; and he who guards his covenant is called righteous; and those who stand in prayer in the Amidah are called masters of the legs. And they depend above, each one according to his place and the order of his service in this world, as he said above in the matter, that the righteous enter above in their prayer according to their deeds. And he said that at their going out the angel appointed over the closing and locking of the gates of the palace closes the doors, until the masters of the signs come to pray. This name is in the Righteous One, called "sign." And he called them masters of the signs because the Righteous One is called "sign," and now the intent is to explain the matter of Yesod; therefore he called them masters of the signs. And the angel appointed over the opening, called Petachon, opens the palace of the King for them. And he said that they are the masters of the eighteen blessings, which are in the Righteous One, called "the Life of the worlds," after the eighteen [lives] that depend on it. And he said that in the Amidah they unite the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah through the Righteous One, which unites them and binds them, as is known. "For the Righteous One is ninth": explanation: how are there eighteen in the Righteous One? And he says that they are nine from below to above and nine from above to below. And one cannot say that the matter is that when we reckon and count the sefirah from above to below it will be nine, and when we count from below to above it will be nine; for if so they would never amount to more than nine; and how does he count eighteen? Rather, certainly Yesod is in the secret of the direct light and the returning light. And like the matter of Malkhut for the count of ten, so Yesod for the count of nine, and likewise Hod for the count of eight. And these do not resemble those; for each and every number is a secret by itself and an aspect by itself, just as the direct light and the returning light are not one matter. And the reason is that the direct light is the secret of the principal light, a foundation established in the Emanation; but the secret of the reversing light does not shine in the secret of the direct light. Like the ray of the sun: what returns from its power does not resemble its own self; for the returning one is one of its offshoots, by reason of one of the receivers, and the direct ray is the very self of the ray itself; and in this way we compare it in the Emanation. And just as the light in its return from within lanterns and the mirror that does not shine does not resemble its return from within a bright mirror, "whose form is sapphire" (Lam. 4:7), so is the matter in the secret of the return of the light from Malkhut or from Yesod and the like. And likewise the change of the light according to the change of the colors in the mirror that receives the ray and returns its light to its original source. And these are distinctions in the aspects of the lights, besides another distinction that there is between the direct and the returning, as we shall explain.

And a further proof for the matter in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, folio 34), and these are its words: "And six constellations are from above to below, from Chesed to Yesod, and six from below to above, from Yesod to Chesed. From the side of Malkhut they are called the seven planets," etc. Thus far its words.

And behold, in this passage Rashbi counted six from Chesed to Yesod and six from Yesod to Chesed. And if it is not as we said, how are they twelve? They are only six. Rather, certainly as we explained; and that is in the secret of the direct light and the returning light, whose matter is not one, as we explained. And in this way also he further counted seven from Chesed to Malkhut; and if not in the way we explained, that "from the side of Malkhut" is the light returning from Malkhut up to Chesed, then the seven planets would turn out to be the six constellations, and all one. Rather, certainly as we explained. And because the light returning from Malkhut is not of the rank of the light returning from Yesod, therefore they are seven planets, which receive from the twelve constellations, as is known; and likewise Yesod pours effluence into Malkhut, and Malkhut receives from it. And with this preliminary what is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, folio 33) concerning the union will be understood, and these are its words: "Come and see: יהו"ה אדנ"י: they are the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, in the two thighs: YHVH to the right, Adonai to the left; and they are the speculum that shines and the speculum that does not shine. In the Righteous One the two of them are one, יאהדונה"י. [And so in the two arms: YHVH to the right, Adonai to the left; in the central pillar יאהדונה"י.] The two of them in one union, in the secret of אמ"ן [Amen]; and therefore greater is the one who answers Amen than the one who blesses. Behold, this is from below to above. From above to below: יהו"ה אהי"ה, the two of them as one in the Supernal Keter, in this way: יאההויה"ה; in Chokhmah and Binah, YHVH, Ehyeh; in the two arms, YHVH, Ehyeh; in the central pillar the two of them as one; in Netzach and Hod, YHVH, Ehyeh, this to the right and this to the left; in the Righteous One the two of them in union as one; and likewise in Malkhut," etc. Thus far its words. And he dwelt at length there on things like this a great deal. And the intent is as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 23: that the matter of coupling, as it is in Tiferet and Malkhut, so it is in Chokhmah and Binah, as explained there. And from the side of the coupling of Chokhmah and Binah the effluence flows to Tiferet and Malkhut, and the ray rises up above. And therefore, from above to below, to the right is the four-letter name, which is Chokhmah, and the name Ehyeh, which is Binah, to the left; and by way of the middle line they are unified; for Binah pours effluence by way of the left and Chokhmah by way of the right, and the middle is what makes the two extremes equal, as explained. But in the ascent, by way of the returning line, a ray rises from Tiferet and Malkhut by way of the grades: Tiferet to the right and Malkhut to the left, for this is the way of their ascent; and in the middle they are all unified in union. And we have already dwelt there on the explanation of this passage, in brief. And with the preliminary of the returning light that we have explained, further words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim will be understood, which at first glance contradict one another. In one place (in Tikkun 49, folio 83) he said that Shin is in Binah, the root of the tree; and elsewhere (in Tikkun 69, folio 107) he said that Shin below is the root of the tree in Malkhut, and likewise the lower Heh. And now it is difficult: if Shin, the root of the tree, is above in Binah, it is not below in Malkhut; and if it is below in Malkhut, it is not above in Binah. Rather, certainly, although the whole Emanation is one, unified, nevertheless in the aspect of the two lights mentioned they are two. There is a tree whose roots are above, in the upper source, and that is direct light, whose six branches spread out below; and there is a tree whose root is below, in the secret of the reversing, returning light, and whose six branches spread out above.

And the matter of his saying "Shin, the root of the tree": for Shin has in it three branches, in the secret of three lines, the line of Din, the line of Rachamim, the line of Chesed; and this is literally Heh, which is three Vavs, as we explained in the preceding gate. And after we have included much in little in this chapter, we come to explain the matter of the returning light itself and the need for it:

Now this is our intent: to explain the secret of the returning light from the side of its essence and its cause. And the matter is that the male, upper, always pours forth compassion, and the female, lower, receives judgment. And these four things are held to one another, that is to say: first, male or female; second, judgment or compassion; third, upper or lower; fourth, giving effluence or receiving effluence. And this thing will be understood in the secret that we explained in the Gate of Channels, chapter 1: that the light that rises, etc., is like the light that goes out from the eye, as explained there at length. And therefore, when Malkhut receives from the ten, behold, her face is turned to receive from all of them in the secret of their direct light; and she turns her face upward, and the name becomes ההו"י. And the upper male pours forth in order and in directness: it is the name יהו"ה. And this is the reason that the name in directness is compassion: because it is male, giving effluence in the order of the grades as they should be, this giving effluence to this. And Malkhut is the name in reversal of letters, thus: הוה"י, female, receiving. And therefore Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (in the Introduction, folio 3a): "Every havayah in which Heh rules over Vav, Heh over Yod, is female and is judgment": because the males are below the females; for the two Hehs are females, Vav and Yod are males.

And behold, when the female turns her face to receive, she certainly does not pour forth; and when the male pours forth, he does not receive. And so they said in the book of the Zohar and in Sefer ha-Bahir that a man is forbidden to remain with his hands raised in prayer more than three hours. And the reason is that the raising of the hands indicates pouring forth, as in the matter (Lev. 9:22) "And Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them," as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (folio 67). And because Malkhut is called "hour," and she receives from three lines [in three hours], behold, her pouring forth is three hours only; and if a man raises his hands longer, he is endangered. Because while the ten sefirot pour forth they do not receive; and if so, one must wait until they receive, so that they may pour forth. And this is the reason for (Exod. 17:11) "and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed."

Behold, a clear proof that while the sefirot pour forth they do not receive, and while the sefirot receive they do not pour forth. And even if somewhat to the contrary of this is found in the Zohar, in its saying "the Shekhinah in the lower ones," and all the details of this inquiry found in the Zohar, it is possible to say that this is specifically near its pouring forth, not while it is pouring forth. However it may be: because the secret of the havayah in reversal is the secret of the turning of the face from below to above, to receive, and it does not pour forth, this is the reason that it is judgment and it is female; and likewise the male who pours forth is compassion. And indeed, concerning the four-letter name in reversal, something close to this is found in one of the writers of secrets, of blessed memory: "Know that just as there are ten inner sefirot, from which the good comes to Israel, so there are ten outer sefirot that stand against them; and when Israel commit transgressions, they act according to the evil that Israel do, God forbid. And you, son of man, see also with the eye of your intellect: you already know that the Unique Name stands in four sefirot: for the Yod stands in the sefirah of Chokhmah, and Heh in Binah, Vav in Tiferet, Heh in Malkhut. And when Israel do the will of the Omnipresent and His commandments, then the attribute of compassion is clothed over the attribute of judgment: for the Yod that is in Chokhmah indicates compassion, and it is clothed over the Heh that is in Binah, which indicates the attribute of judgment; and likewise the Vav that is in Tiferet, indicating the attribute of compassion, is clothed over the Heh that is in Malkhut; and then the whole world is in peace, and He has compassion on His children as a father has compassion on his children. And if, God forbid, Israel do the opposite, then the attribute of compassion turns into the attribute of judgment: for the Heh that is in Malkhut is clothed over the Vav of Tiferet, and likewise the Heh that is in Binah is clothed over the Yod that is in Chokhmah, which indicates the attribute of judgment. And know that when the Yod begins the name, and afterwards Heh, Heh, then it indicates the attribute of compassion; and likewise the Vav, when it begins and afterwards Heh, Heh, it indicates compassion; and when one of the two Hehs begins, then they indicate judgment." Thus far his words.

And there is no doubt that in what he said at the beginning of his words, "just as there are inner sefirot," etc., "so there are outer sefirot," his intent is not the husks, since he concludes with the name in reversal of letters. Rather, certainly, the intent is the returning light, which raises the compassion in the secret of receiving; and this is the secret of the reversal in the letters. And needless to say [it holds] in the letters of the whole name, that this matter is so, as explained above; but even in two letters, such as Yod-Heh or Heh-Yod, and likewise Vav-Heh or Heh-Vav, as that young scholar explained. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim, as we shall explain in chapter 5. And likewise this principle is explained in Sefer Yetzirah, the last mishnah of chapter 3, and these are its words: "He made Alef king over air [ruach], and bound a crown to it, and combined them one with another, and formed with them the air [avir] in the world, moisture in the year, and the body in the soul: male in Alef-Mem-Shin and female in Alef-Shin-Mem. He made Mem king over water, and bound a crown to it, and combined them one with another, and formed with them earth in the world, cold in the year, and the belly in the soul, male and female: male in Mem-Alef-Shin, female in Mem-Shin-Alef. He made Shin king over fire, and bound a crown to it, and combined them one with another, and formed and sealed with them heaven in the world, heat in the year, and the head in the soul, male and female: male in Shin-Mem-Alef and female in Shin-Alef-Mem." Thus far its words.

And behold, in this mishnah all our intent is explained, and this is its explanation. And before all else it is fitting for the inquirer to understand what we shall write in the Gate of Particulars of Names concerning the matter of the formation of man by means of the rolling of the letters and their permutation; and there we shall explain at length the matter of "He made such-and-such a letter king and bound a crown to it." And nevertheless we shall not withhold our hands from explaining here what suffices for the understanding of the mishnah. And the matter is that the letters are branches branching out from the names, that is to say, powers emanated from the very self of the sefirot, like those who dwell "in the clefts of the rock, the height of their dwelling" (Obad. 1:3), as we shall dwell at length in the Gate of Letters. And because the powers do not perform their action except through their combination with their sources, and in their return and binding to their source much effluence flows upon them to perform their action with strength, as we shall dwell at length in explaining them in the Gate of Particulars of Names, therefore it was necessary for the formation that it be through the branches unified with their sources, that is, the sefirot. And the letters, which are branches branching out from them: when they are unified with the root and the powers return to their source, then their action is complete and good. And because the sources of the letters include ten sefirot, as we shall dwell at length in the Gate of Letters, therefore, to strengthen their power for creation, each and every branch was unified with its source. And this is what he meant in saying "He made the letter Alef king," or Mem, or Shin; and likewise for the seven doubles, Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaf, Peh, Resh, Tav; and likewise for the twelve simples, Heh, Vav, Zayin, Chet, Tet, Yod, Lamed, Nun, Samekh, Ayin, Tzadi, Kof. And the explanation of "He made king": He unified that letter and that spiritual branch with Malkhut; and afterwards "He bound a crown to it." And "bound" [קש"ר]: explanation: teki'ah, shevarim, teru'ah, which are the three fathers, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, with their branches, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and with their fathers, which are Chokhmah, Binah, Keter. And this is the "crown" explicitly mentioned in the mishnah; for the first three are included in the name Keter, as they are included in the name Nothing; and likewise the three of them are a crown to the three lines, Chesed, Din, and Rachamim. And according to all the explanations, the intent is to unify the letter in its root, which is the sefirot. And he said Alef with air, and Shin with fire, and Mem with water: the intent is that Alef-Mem-Shin hints at Yod-Heh-Vav. For the Yod is Chokhmah, for Chokhmah is the root of the waters of Chesed; and likewise Heh is in Binah, and likewise Shin is in Binah, the root of fire, which is the root of judgment, in the way we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 25; and the Vav is in Keter, in the secret of Da'at, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 6; and likewise the Alef, for Keter is the root of the air that arbitrates between the extremes, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters. And therefore, when we wish to unify the branch, we unify it in its root, unified in its ten sefirot. And this is what he meant in saying "He made Alef king over air, Mem over water, and Shin over fire": for the union and the binding is to unify the branch in the root particular to it, whether Chesed, whether Din, whether Rachamim, and in its ten sefirot that are found for it according to its nature. And after the union in the branches, it needs further to receive from the other sources themselves, so as to be included of Chesed, Din, and Rachamim; and for this he said "and combined them one with another," which refers back to the letters Alef-Mem-Shin mentioned from the beginning of the chapter until here. And through the combination the powers are unified with a true and complete union, and the lower rolls and rises, and the upper descends, until the thing becomes an inclusive havayah. And for this, after the union of the branch in its root with its ten sefirot, it had to be unified in three powers, which are Alef-Mem-Shin, which include the whole Emanation; and this is "and combined them one with another"; and then that manifestation was formed and emanated and brought into being in three places, which are world, year, soul [עש"ן], as we shall explain them at length in the Gate of Particulars of Names, on the name of seventy-two. And through their spiritual formation they were formed in the corporeality of these worlds. And because the Alef is head to the havayah and the principal of the form that is formed (for the principal of the manifestation is from the air, and the fire and the water are mere assistance, like the likeness of a composition, but the prevailing is from the air), therefore, both in the male and in the female, the Alef comes at the head of the combination, and the water and the fire are lower. And for the reason that the male is from above to below, the Mem, which is the water, comes over the Shin, which is the fire, as is their way, for the right is always over the left; and this is אמ"ש, which is וי"ה: Vav [and] Yod over Heh. And when the female comes, she comes from below to above, which is אש"ם: the Shin, which is the fire, over the Mem, which is the water; and this is אש"ם, fire over water, the left over the right, as is the way of the female, which is וה"י, which is Heh above Yod. The female is always the opposite of the male, for the male pours forth and the female receives; and therefore the female is judgment. And when He made the letter Mem king, which is the principal of the water, therefore both in the male and in the female the Mem comes first, and it is what prevails in the composition; for the attribute of (the day) [the water] is always determinative, and therefore the principal of the attribute prevails; and of the two attributes, which are the air and the fire, either this prevails or that. The male in מא"ש: the Alef, which is the air, over the Shin, which is the fire; and he made compassion prevail over judgment, as is the way of the male, to incline it to the right in compassion: Alef over Shin, which is Vav over Heh, male over female. And the female comes from below to above: the female in מש"א made the fire prevail over the air, the judgment over the compassion, Heh over Vav, making judgment prevail over compassion and turning upward; for the male pours forth and the female receives. And when He made the letter Shin king, which is the fire in the strength of judgment, the male came in שמ"א; for the principal always prevails, according to what is the principal element, both in the male and in the female. And therefore the Shin prevails both in the male and in the female; but the other letters of the composition were divided in disagreement: for the male made the element of water, which is the Mem, prevail over the element of air, which is the Alef, that is, הי"ו; for the Heh prevails, because it is the element of fire, as explained; but it is Yod over Vav. And the reason is that although the Vav, which is the air, which is the Alef, is compassion, nevertheless it is mediated compassion, and the compassion of Chesed is complete compassion; and therefore he chose the right for himself and made it prevail over the mediation, as is the way of the Yod, which is always over Vav. But the female comes in שא"ם: she made the element of air prevail over the water, and inclined it toward the fire; and so the letters are found in her from below to above, as is her way, the opposite of the male; for the female makes the air prevail over the water and turns upward, and the male pours forth and turns downward; and therefore the female comes in שא"ם, which is הו"י: the letters reversed, turning upward to receive. Thus far reaches the explanation of the mishnah; and from within it is explained the matter of the reversal even in two letters, as explained above.

This inquiry is further explained in a fine light in Sefer ha-Bahir; these are its words: "His disciples said to him: Our master, from above to below we know; from below to above we do not know. And he answered: But are not from below to above and from above to below one? [They said:] Our master, the one who ascends is not like the one who descends; for the one who descends descends at a run, and the one who ascends is not so. And not only that, but the one who ascends can ascend by another way, by which he did not descend. He said to them: Go out and see. He sat and expounded to them: The Shekhinah is below just as the Shekhinah is above. And what is Shekhinah? This is the light emanated from the first light, which is Chokhmah; it too surrounds all, as it is said (Isa. 6:3), 'The whole earth is full of His glory.' What is its work here? A parable: to what is the matter like? To a king who had seven sons, and he set each one in his place, and said to them: Sit one upon another. And the lowest said: I am below; I will not be far from you. He said to them: Behold, I surround and see you. That is, 'The whole earth is full of His glory.' And why is He among them? In order to establish them and sustain them. And what are the sons? I have already told you: the Holy One, blessed be He, has seven holy forms," etc. Thus far its words.

And the explanation: above in the matter, the master explained to his disciples the ten utterances one by one, to find a reckoning from above to below. And when he completed explaining them, his pleasant disciples asked: "Our master, from above to below we know," as you have explained to us; "from below to above we do not know." And the reason is that the disciples had already heard "from below to above" from the mouth of the master many times; and because of their great humility they did not see fit to press the hour, and did not ask their master, until they saw that the time was a time of favor, for the master had explained to them "from above to below" with a broad explanation; and for this they asked that he likewise explain to them "from below to above." And the master, in order to sharpen them and to see whether they had stood in the counsel of the Lord and gone down to the end of his knowledge, asked them: "But are not from above to below and from below to above one?" For all is one, and there is no distinction between them; and since he had explained to them "from above to below," they already know "from below to above," for all is one. And they, being "taught of the Lord" (Isa. 54:13), answered: "Our master, the one who ascends is not like the one who descends; for the one who descends descends at a run, and the one who ascends is not so." Explanation: from above to below, which is the giver of effluence, pours forth in the strength of compassion, and the effluence is not delayed but comes at a run. But the one who ascends is not so, for it is judgment, which is the side of the female, and it is not compassion, in the way of the male, as we explained. And they further stated another distinction: that the one who ascends can ascend by a way by which he did not descend. For the descent is by way of the right, for the right prevails over the left, because the right comes first, and afterwards it comes to the left; for first the effluence descends to Chesed and afterwards comes to Gevurah, and so in this way. But the one who ascends ascends from the left to the right, for the left comes first, and from the left he ascends to the right.

And behold, the ascent is by another way, which is not so with the descent. And they said "can," for it is already possible that the ascent be wholly by way of the right; for it is possible that it ascend by way of Yesod to Netzach, to Chesed, to Chokhmah; and behold, in this way the whole ascent will be wholly by way of the right. But [it is possible] that the ascent be by way of the grades: from Yesod to Hod, and from Hod to Netzach, and from Netzach to Tiferet, and from Tiferet to Gevurah, and from Gevurah to Chesed, and from Chesed to Binah, and from Binah to Chokhmah; and behold, the left always comes before the right, for it makes judgment prevail over compassion. And when the great master saw the answer of his disciples by a short way, and that they had gone down to the depth of the thought and knew the distinction between "from below to above" and "from above to below," and they had no doubt except about the way of the powers and the manner of the secret, he answered them with a good answer: "Go out and see. He sat and expounded: The Shekhinah is below just as the Shekhinah is above. And what is Shekhinah? This is the light emanated": from the direct light and the returning light; and the two lights are the two Yods, as explained above. And this is "the light emanated from the first light, which is Chokhmah," emanated from Keter, from which its light spreads from above to below, in the secret that it is the Yod of the Name. And there is no wonder at the expression "Shekhinah," for it is a borrowed expression, for the concealment of the figure of speech. And moreover, the whole Emanation and every revealing of the King of the world is called Shekhinah.

And moreover, the principal revealing and spreading of Chokhmah is through Binah, who is called Shekhinah; and likewise the name יאהדונה"י has in it eight letters, which is from Binah downward. And there is support for this in the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim on the verse "You shall surely send away" (Deut. 22:7), and there it is said that this name is eight sefirot, that is, from Binah downward. And the matter is that the Yod is a point in her palaces. "It too surrounds all, as it is said, 'The whole earth is full of His glory.'" Explanation: for the principal "from below to above" and "from above to below" is from the head of the Emanation, the Supernal Keter, downward, until it rises to the number ten, and ten from below to above, which are twenty, which are "ten, ten," the Kaf of Keter, as explained in the first chapter. And nevertheless, in the way that it is in Keter, it is in all the sefirot, for in each and every sefirah there is direct and returning light, as we explained in chapter 3. And therefore here, so as not to ascend into Keter and touch speech upon it, he said "the light emanated from the first light": Keter is by way of the cause; and he said of Chokhmah, "it too surrounds all." That is to say: as is the way of Keter, whose light spreads and returns to it above, its face toward its source, so is the way of Chokhmah. So according to his words the matter of Keter is explained in a concealed way, and Chokhmah in revealing. And they said "surrounds all": this is the light that descends below by way of the grades, and returns and ascends.
