And so according to this, "the whole earth is full of His glory," the whole Emanation equally; for Keter is in Malkhut and Malkhut in Keter, אי"ן / אנ"י; and Chokhmah is below in Yesod and Yesod in Chokhmah; and all the grades are held to one another. And this is what he meant in saying "the whole earth is full of His glory": for according to this, some revealing that is revealed below is equal to the way of what is revealed above. And to explain the matter well he said, "a parable: to a king who had seven sons," etc.; and he was precise that the lower ones who were below complained, until because of this he had to make them equal, in the secret of the returning light, by way of the grades from below to above and from above to below; and so their end is embedded in their beginning and their beginning in their end, and their middle embedded in each of the two extremes; and the whole matter is clear. Thus far reaches our intent in the explanation of the passage. And not this matter alone, but even in one sefirah it will be found that its light is from below to above and from above to below. The illustration of this: Yesod, which is between Tiferet and Malkhut, so that there are two: one Yesod that goes out from Tiferet to Malkhut, and one Yesod that goes out from Malkhut to Tiferet. And they explained this matter in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (folio 155a), and these are its words: "Rabbi Chizkiyah said: If so, behold, it has been said that all that the lower world begets is in separation, for it is written (Gen. 2:10), 'and from there it was parted.' What will you say of Joseph and Benjamin? If you say that the world is one in these, it is not so, for they did not come out from the upper world; and the lower world, what it begot it begot below and not above; and if so, it is separation. Rabbi Abba came and kissed him. He said to him: This matter is obscure; for the upper world was set right in twelve, which are its own. But come and see the secret of the matter: we see that at all times the Righteous One goes out from the lower world and enters it; enters it and goes out from it. And therefore he was built in this place; and his root is above and his root is below; and in the lower world he is always, forever. It is written (Gen. 35:18), 'And it came to pass, as her soul was departing, for she died' (another version: Come and see: in this lower world the Righteous One enters it and goes out from it. When he enters, he is in the secret of Joseph the righteous; when he goes out, in the secret of Benjamin; this is what is written, 'And it came to pass, as her soul was departing, for she died'). Who is 'her soul'? This is the Righteous One who goes out from her, and this is Benjamin. 'And she called his name Ben-Oni,' for she thought that she had begotten below, in the world of separation, and remained twelve (another version: eleven) in those above. What is written? 'But his father called him Benjamin': Ben-Yamin [son of the right], for he ascended above, into the upper world. For when Joseph was lost, Benjamin completed his place. And therefore the Righteous One enters and goes out in the lower world. And therefore Joseph and Benjamin, and all twelve, are like those above, in one union." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: above this passage, Rabbi Abba explained the matter of the sons of Leah, as is well known that Leah is a hint to Binah and Rachel to Malkhut. And the sum of his words: he said concerning the matter "and she ceased bearing" (Gen. 29:35), "because here the four supports were included." The intent is that until now there were four sons, a hint to the four legs of the Chariot: they are Reuben, Chesed; Simeon, Din; Levi, Tiferet; Judah, Malkhut. He further said afterwards, "and she ceased, for until here [they were] in one union; from here downward it is the world of separation." He taught that all that is from Malkhut, that is, Judah, downward is the world of separation, for "from there it was parted." And it was difficult for him in this: for if so, those born after Judah turn out to be from the world of separation, God forbid. And he answered: No, "for these two sons whom she bore afterwards were joined with these": explanation: they were unified with the four, in the secret of the two thighs unified with the four legs of the Chariot. And afterwards it was difficult for him concerning the sons of the handmaids; and he answered that they are four bonds, etc., as explained there. And now, in the passage before us, Rabbi Chizkiyah objected to him: "If so, behold, it has been said," etc. Explanation: since you have set right all the tribes, and about Joseph and Benjamin you did not speak, it appears that nothing is difficult for you about them; and it is very difficult. In particular in what you explained, that from Malkhut downward is the world of separation: if so, since Joseph and Benjamin are the sons of Rachel, who is Malkhut, her sons turn out to be below her, in the world of separation; and according to this it is difficult that Joseph and Benjamin should be from the world of separation, below the sons of the handmaids. For to say that they are in the upper world is impossible, since their mother is below, in the secret of Malkhut, and their birth is in the world of separation, as we explained. And he answered him: "This matter is obscure, for the upper world," etc. Explanation: one cannot say that they are all tikkunim of Binah, who is Leah, and she needs twelve sons, each one included in his fellow, etc., as is well known; because if so it would have been fitting that they all go out from Binah; and this is what he said, "in twelve, which are its own"; if so, this is no answer. But the principal answer is: "at all times the Righteous One goes out from the lower world and enters; enters it," etc. Explanation: Yesod has two aspects. The first aspect, and it is what precedes the union, is that Malkhut pours forth lower waters by way of it, in the secret of returning light, by way of arousal, as explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 17, 18, and 19.

And behold, according to this, "from her goes out": from within Malkhut this light goes out. "And enters": explanation: and afterwards enters it, in the secret of the direct light, for by way of it the effluence of the coupling flows to Malkhut. And this is why he put "goes out" before "enters": because such is the way of the aspects for the coupling, as we explained. And because such is not the order of the way of the aspects for the Emanation (for first is the aspect of the direct light, and by its power the returning light is emanated), he went back and said "enters it," that is, direct light, "and goes out from it," that is, the reversing light. And so in truth these two aspects turn out to be from the side of Malkhut: the one from the side of the arousal; and by the power of the arousal is the power of the effluence, and if there is no arousal there is no effluence. So Malkhut turns out to be the cause of both aspects; if so, it is fitting that Yesod be related to Malkhut alone, not to any other. And this is what he said: "And therefore he was built in this place": explanation: because of these two aspects mentioned, he was built in Malkhut, that is, Joseph and Benjamin, who were born from Rachel and not from Leah, because it befits her for the reasons mentioned. And he said "and his root is above, and his root is below": explanation: Yesod has a root above, that is, its aspect in the secret of the direct light; and it has a root below, that is, its aspect in the secret of the returning light. And Joseph was the secret of direct light, and Benjamin the secret of returning light, and both of them are in Yesod. And this is what he said: "and in the lower world he is [always, forever]": for Yesod is always related to Malkhut, for it is always unified with her. "It is written, 'And it came to pass, as her soul was departing'": in the way of (Ps. 25:1) "To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul." "'And she called his name Ben-Oni,' for she thought," etc.: explanation: because he was in the secret of the light that is renewed and emanated from her, she thought him to be in the world of separation; which she did not think concerning Joseph, but on the contrary she hoped for another son. And the reason is that it was "as her soul was departing," and he was from her power (therefore she thought as mentioned above); which was not so with Joseph, but he came from the power of Jacob, as is written (Gen. 37:2), "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph." "'But his father called him Benjamin,' Ben-Yamin, for he ascended," etc.: it was difficult for him why Jacob called him "son of the right," for he is not so, but son of the left, for the secret of the returning light is in the secret of the left; and if so, why Benjamin? And he answered, "for he ascended": explanation: for Benjamin too served in the secret of direct light, that is, his ascending to the upper root, and returning and spreading from there downward. And this was "when Joseph was lost": it was necessary that he be in the secret of Yesod in the direct light, serving in the place of Joseph in the secret of Yesod. "And therefore the Righteous One enters and goes out in the lower world," in the secret of direct light and reversing light. "And all twelve," etc.: that all of them are above, as we explained.

And behold, it has been explained that the matter of the reversing light is even in one attribute, like this that is mentioned; and the explanation of the passage will be broadened in the book Or Yakar on this portion.

After we have explained in the preceding chapters the matter of "from below to above" at length, as Heaven taught us, until we came to say that even in one of the attributes it can properly be said that there is in it the aspect of "from below to above" and "from above to below," we come in this chapter to explain still more than this: that even in one attribute in itself it can properly be said that part of it is from above to below and part of it from below to above, from it and in it, without its being considered relative to another. And the matter is that there is room to object to the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim, for his own words contradict one another: in one place he said that the four-letter name in the filling of Yods, thus, יו"ד ה"י וא"ו ה"י, is female, judgment; and these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 56, folio 89b): "'In the beginning Elohim created': Elohim: they have established that there is fear there, from the side of the letter Heh-Yod, which is to the left; for although the letter Yod is compassion, in a place where Heh rules over it, it is called female, like this: Heh-Yod. And this secret is revealed in יו"ד ה"י וא"ו ה"י: for there is no creature without male and female; for they are two partners, son and daughter, father and mother: one gives the male drop and one gives the female; and when the male rules over the female, it is male, and when the female rules over the male, it is female; and they have established it in the secret of (Lev. 12:2) 'If a woman conceives and bears a male.'" Thus far its words.

And how shall we keep silent and restrain ourselves, seeing that he said that the name in the filling of Yods is female and judgment, and not cry out "violence"? Alas, for there is no escape: for Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the opposite in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, folio 246), when he was praising Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. He said to him: "[Just as Lamed is exalted over all the letters,] so you are destined to be exalted over all creatures, because you have ascended to the name יו"ד ה"י וא"ו ה"י, in which are three Yods, whose reckoning is thirty. For at first you were in the name יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א, which is יאא"א, thirteen attributes of compassion, which are אח"ד [echad, one]; now you shall ascend in the name א"ל [El], which is ייא"י; for two names testify," etc.: "Have we not all one [echad] father? Has not one God [El] created us?" (Mal. 2:10).
And behold, the intent of the passage is clear: that the filling of Yods is above the filling of Alefs.

And behold, the filling of Alefs is known and famous in the words of Rashbi in countless places: that the filling of Alefs is in Chokhmah, and it is כ"ח מ"ה [ko'ach mah, 45], which is the reckoning of the filling of Alefs. And behold, in this way the filling of Yods will be found to be at least in the Supernal Keter; and how shall we restrain ourselves from saying that it is female? And moreover, the name in the filling of Yods is the brain, and in the filling of Alefs it is the air, and the Yods are clothed and concealed within the airs: all this Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 118). And it is difficult: for since the name in the filling of Alefs is in Chokhmah, which is Abba, male, certainly compassion, how shall we say that the name in the filling of Yods, which is above, is female? This is certainly difficult. And the matter is that, since we have said that the matter of the aspects in the secret of direct light and reversing light is the secret of giver and receiver of effluence, if so it is necessary that each sefirah pour forth by itself, from the Keter that is in it to the Malkhut that is in it, and the light returns in its own self and reverses from the Malkhut that is in it to the Keter that is in it.

And behold, in this way there will be in the Supernal Keter one aspect, which is that aspect that draws near to the upper root, and it pours forth and does not receive effluence; that is to say, the effluence is never lacking in it, but it is always flowing and coming. And this aspect does not rise in a name at all, because of its nearness to its source; just as in its source neither name nor point is attributed, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, so in it no name is attributed, because of the concealment of its cause in it, as he, peace be upon him, said (in the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, folio 6a): "The Cause of causes, concealed and stored away in Keter," etc. And therefore neither name nor point is attributed to it. But there is in it another aspect, which receives from this aspect, which is receiving, and it is the recipient of effluence, the female aspect. And so Rashbi explained explicitly (in Tikkun 56, folio 90b), and these are his words: "The black color of the eye, and its black hairs, and all the beautiful black colors were given to it from the side of Imma. The white of the eye and the whiteness of the face," etc., "were given to it from the side of Abba," etc. "And whiteness and blackness are both found from the Supernal Keter: blackness outside and whiteness inside. And of it is said (Job 37:21), 'And now they do not see the bright light; it is in the skies,' etc.; (Ps. 18:12) 'He made darkness His hiding place.' And the Companions have established: blackness is female to whiteness." Behold, Rashbi explicitly intended that in the Supernal Keter itself there is giver and receiver of effluence, as we have said.

And behold, since the aspect that receives effluence is female, it was necessary that she turn her face to receive from the giver; and therefore it is Heh over Yod, to indicate the secret of the returning light, whose root is below and whose branches spread out upward, which is Heh, as we explained. And now with this the language of Rashbi that we set out above will be explained with a fine explanation. And this is its explanation: "for there is fear there, from the side," etc. Explanation: in the name אלהים, which is Heh over Yod; for it was not written אליה"ם, which indicates male, compassion, and love, but אלהים, which is Heh over Yod, which indicates female, judgment, and fear. "For although the letter Yod," etc.: explanation: it was difficult for him: on the contrary, because there is Yod in the name Elohim, it should indicate that there is some compassion in it, for the Yod is a letter of compassion. To this he answered that although there is Yod in it, since the Heh rules over the Yod, it must be judgment; and he said that this secret is revealed in the name in the filling of Yods, in which the Hehs rule over the Yods. "For there is no creature," etc.: it was difficult for him: since the name in the filling of Yods is in Keter, how then can it properly be said that it is female and receiving? To this he answered: "for there is no creature without male," etc. Explanation: since the beginning of the Emanation is Keter, and Chokhmah and Binah are emanated from it, and they are father and mother to all that is beneath them: granted for them, for since they are male and female they can emanate all that is beneath them; but Keter, which is one alone, how is it possible for it to emanate Chokhmah and Binah? Is it not that "there is no creature without male and female"? And the reason for this we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 17, with a long explanation and a fine reason. Rather, certainly it must be that in Keter itself there are the power of male and the power of female, explanation: giver and receiver of effluence, as we explained. And the matter of the passage has been explained, and the Gate is concluded, with the help of Heaven. Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.
The Sixteenth Gate: The Gate of ABYA.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain a delightful inquiry found many times in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who said: ten sefirot of Atzilut, and ten sefirot of Beriah, and ten sefirot of Yetzirah, and ten sefirot of Asiyah, and their mnemonic is ABYA. And at first glance the matter astonishes the hearts, since it has come before us "ten and not nine, ten and not eleven"; all the more so [is it astonishing] that we should say that they are forty. And this matter will be explained in these chapters, with God's help.
Chapter One:
What is intended in this chapter is to explain the meaning of the words Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah.

Atzilut is derived from the language (Num. 11:17) "and I will draw [ve-atzalti] from the spirit," etc. And the explanation of the matter is that the power of the Emanator is in the emanated, and the Emanator lacks nothing; rather, like one who kindles a lamp from a lamp, and the first lacks nothing in the kindling of its fellow, so in the Ein Sof there is no lack after the Emanation, and there is no surplus in it before the Emanation or after the Emanation; but its power spreads within it, as explained in the preceding gates. And the word atzilut is derived from the language "beside [etzel] the altar," whose explanation is the matter of nearness. And the intent is to indicate the great attachment of the roots to their cause.

And behold, the sefirot, because of their great attachment to their source and their cause, are called the ten sefirot of Atzilut. And therefore all the very subtle things that multiply from the subtlety of their cause, in their nearness to their cause, are called by the name atzilut. And therefore the prophecy of the seventy elders is expressed in the language of atzilut, since all of them were drawing the holy spirit from Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and were attached to him like the attachment of the light of the moon to the ray of the sun, so that all is one, as is known. And therefore it is written, "and I will draw from the spirit."

Beriah: behold, beriah is derived from the language (Num. 16:30) "But if the Lord creates a creation [beri'ah yivra]," etc., whose intent is the coming-to-be of the thing in a coming-to-be more revealed than the Emanation. And because the density of things is impossible except through their distancing and separation from subtlety and spirituality, therefore, when the matter of coming-to-be spreads, to be created, it is necessary that the beings be separated and distanced from the Cause of causes, concealed at the utmost of concealment and far from density. And although those beings will not be dense with a corporeal density, God forbid, nevertheless they are far from the bounds of divinity, for they are subject to separation, and joining, and change, and limit. Therefore their distancing and separation from the root is necessary. And they are called by the name beriah from the word bar, with the vowel patach, whose meaning is "outside"; or from the language of cutting [as in (Josh. 17:18) "for it is a forest, and you shall cut it down" (u-veretato)]; and the intent is to indicate the separation of the thing from the source, although there is no separation, God forbid.

Yetzirah is from the language (Isa. 26:3) "the steadfast mind [yetzer samukh] You keep," which is denser and more revealed than Beriah. And like (Gen. 2:7) "And the Lord God formed [va-yitzer] man of dust from the ground": behold, with dust he used the language of yetzirah. And likewise (Isa. 43:21), "This people I formed [yatzarti] for Myself"; for the intent is the greater density of things.

Asiyah is a thing more revealed than the three preceding. And the name testifies to it, for the language of asiyah is the greatest density of things. And a proof for the order of the three of them is in one verse (Isa. 43:7): "Everyone that is called by My name, and for My glory I created him, I formed him, yea, I made him."

And after we have explained the meaning of the words in this preliminary, we come further to the explanation of the matter in its upper manifestation. And the matter is that the sefirot in their own self are the first ones, which draw near to the Cause of all causes, with which we have engaged from the beginning of the book until here. And it is the subtle Emanation that was concealed in its source, and after the will arose before Him it was revealed. And they are unified in their root with the utmost union, and they are related by the name Atzilut. And after the pure and holy Emanation, He, blessed be He, wished to create a being second to the Emanation, and it is Beriah; and it is called the Throne of Glory, titled among the sages of the Zohar kursaya; and it has ten sefirot. And the reason is that all the matters that are beneath the sefirot, their grades are ten, ten, like the sefirot themselves. For the ten that are in Beriah are a throne and a garment to the ten of Atzilut that are clothed in Beriah; and those branches that are emanated from the ten sefirot and shine in this Throne are called the ten sefirot of Beriah. And let no hearer suspect us that our intent is to say that Beriah, that is, the Throne, is the ten sefirot of Beriah. For this is not our intent; rather, the ten branches of the sefirot that spread in it shine in it, and they are the ten sefirot of Beriah. And according to the truth they are the very ten of Atzilut; but their spreading as far as Beriah, which is the Throne, caused them to be the ten of Beriah. And after this Throne He formed ten classes of angels; and they are related by the name Metatron, since Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Countenance, is appointed over them, to give each one his allotted bread, his effluence, and his life; and all of them draw from him. And he is over the angels like the likeness of the heart in the body, which is the dwelling of life, and from there all the limbs draw life; therefore we relate all the angels by the name Metatron. And it is what is called the world of Yetzirah; and the branches that spread from the ten grades of Beriah mentioned above shine in it and are clothed in it, and the ten grades that are in it are a garment to them; and they are what are called the ten sefirot of Yetzirah. And after this Yetzirah He further made Asiyah; and they are all the things made from the beginning of the point of Asiyah, that is, all that is mentioned in the particulars of the work of creation, down to the point of the abyss. And the husks are included in it, and all is called by the name Asiyah. When the concealed light that spreads from the world of Yetzirah, the world of the angels, spreads to the world of Asiyah, they are those related to the ten husks, and not in them literally, but through holy powers, as we shall explain. And the reason for the spreading of holiness in them is to subdue them and to humble them, as we shall explain; and this is called the ten sefirot of Asiyah. And our intent is not to say that Asiyah is the ten sefirot of Asiyah, nor Yetzirah the ten sefirot of Yetzirah, nor Beriah the ten sefirot of Beriah, nor [Atzilut] of Atzilut; for if so, forty sefirot would be a difficulty for us, and explicitly it is said in Sefer Yetzirah, "ten and not nine, ten and not eleven," as we explained in the first Gate. Rather, the intent is that the manifestation of Beriah is the Throne, and Yetzirah is the angels, and Asiyah is all that is beneath it, the firmaments, and the constellations, and the husks. And the light that spreads from the very self of the sefirot to oversee the upper ones and the lower ones spreads from the height of the worlds to the last point; and behold, the spark of their light that spreads in Beriah is called the ten sefirot of Beriah, and the spark of their light that spreads in Yetzirah is called the ten sefirot of Yetzirah, and the spark of their light that spreads in Asiyah is called the ten sefirot of Asiyah. And always the branches are from the upper light that spreads, and they are the sefirot themselves. And there is no doubt that in Beriah is the power of the ten, and in Yetzirah the power of the ten, and in Asiyah the power of the ten. And there is no doubt that the ten sefirot of Atzilut are not clothed in the ten of Yetzirah except through the intermediate ten of Beriah; and likewise the ten of Beriah are not clothed in the ten of Asiyah except through the ten of Yetzirah. Behold, we have learned that there is no ten of Asiyah except through the three upper grades, Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah; and there is no ten of Yetzirah except through the two upper grades, which are Atzilut and Beriah; and there is no ten of Beriah except through the grade of Atzilut. And now we say that what is in Beriah is not so in Atzilut, and what is in Yetzirah is not in Beriah, and what is in Asiyah is not in Yetzirah. For it is already possible for the world to be revealed and conducted in Yetzirah without Asiyah; so that concerning Asiyah Rashbi explained the reason: "to subdue those husks," to fulfil what is said (Ps. 103:19), "and His kingship rules over all." He taught that there is no delight in it for the governance of this world, except "to subdue," etc., as will be explained. And the ten of Yetzirah is the governance of the world through the Prince of the World, who is called the Prince Metatron.

And behold, the governance of the world through him was not necessitated except on weekdays or in the days of exile, as will be explained. But in Beriah it was necessary, so that Rashbi, peace be upon him, said of it: "garments of Sabbaths and festivals." And the matter is that on Sabbaths or festivals the upper light is revealed without a garment, without an intermediary, but itself, by itself, through Beriah; and then it is said of this matter that the Holy One, blessed be He, wears royal garments, garments of Sabbaths and festivals. But when the light of Beriah further needs to be clothed in the light of Yetzirah, then it is said that the King wears weekday garments. And [this is] not to deny that He wears Sabbath garments inside; but as long as the illumination is not through the inner garments but through the outer garments, it is said that He wears weekday garments. The illustration of this: a king who wears garments of freedom and embroidery, and over his robes has put on his linen robe: behold, then it will be said of the king that he wears weekday garments, for his appearance before his servants is in a linen garment, like one of the exiles. But when the light of Atzilut is pure, without the mediation of Yetzirah, but [only] through Beriah, which is necessary for the very self of the light and the weakness of the souls in the lower world, then it is said that the King wears garments of Sabbath and festival, garments of freedom and liberty. And when Beriah is clothed in Yetzirah, which is Metatron and the ten classes of angels, then it is said that He has put on garments of exile and servitude, since the light drawn to us is through the exile and the servant. And this is the summary of the passages that we shall explain further. And now we say that the relation of Beriah to Atzilut is like the relation of Atzilut to the Self that spreads, which we engaged in explaining in the Gate of Self and Vessels; and the relation of Yetzirah to Beriah is like the relation of Beriah to Atzilut; and the relation of Asiyah to Yetzirah is like the relation of Yetzirah to Beriah. And the matter is that changes, punishments, and corporeality are far from the Self, as explained there. But changes are effected through the vessels, which are the sefirot of Atzilut; and nevertheless, because of their nearness to their source, they are far from changes, so that they needed vessels to be clothed in, and they are Beriah. And Beriah is still far from corporeality and changes, so that they needed vessels to be clothed in, and they are Yetzirah. And Yetzirah is still far from changes, so that they needed Asiyah, which are the harmful spirits, who actually do evil. And for the lowly of soul (see Asis Rimmonim, chapter 7, and Pelach ha-Rimmon, chapter 3) they are sometimes their angels for good. And this is outside the Land; for in the Land of Israel Asiyah does not rule at all, for there are no husks, and even the angel of death is not there; and all the changes are effected through the ten of Yetzirah: for example, death is through an angel [of the branches of Yetzirah] clothed in judgment and in the cruelty of fury, not through the impure angel of death, God forbid. And when Israel are in exile, or on the weekdays, then, for our iniquities, they are smitten because of the judgment stretched out, and the world is conducted in Yetzirah, which is more subject to changes. And on the days of Sabbath and festival, when there is no judgment, but the righteous sit with their diadems on their heads, in the addition of their soul, then the world is conducted in Beriah, which is called the Throne. And less than this is impossible, because they would not be reckoned so much; for they have no capacity in this world to enjoy anything but the light of Beriah, which is the Throne, until the soul is stripped from the body; for then it will enjoy Atzilut, which is the sefirot. And after we have explained this matter in the generality of ABYA, we come now in the coming chapters to explain each and every part of these, each one by itself:
On the portion of Atzilut:

Behold, Atzilut is the very substance of the sefirot, emanated from the Ein Sof. And their union with the Ein Sof is through the Self that spreads in them; and their union with the Self is explained in Gate Four, chapter 15.

Behold, there are found in the very substance of Atzilut three aspects: first, the aspect of the Ein Sof; second, the aspect of the Self; third, the aspect of the sefirot themselves. And this is unified with this, and this with this, as we explained in the gate mentioned. And behold, Rashbi intended a hint to these three aspects in the Tikkunim [in the Introduction, folio 3b], and these are his words: "For in the ten sefirot of Atzilut, the King: He and His Self are one in them; He and His life are one in them; which is not so in the ten sefirot of Beriah, for they and their life are not one, they and their self are not one." Thus far its words. Behold, he was explicitly precise in his wording in saying of Atzilut "He and His Self are one in them," to indicate the three aspects mentioned. "The King, He": that is, the Ein Sof in its primordial aspect. "And His Self" [garmeh]: that is, in the aspect of the spreading of the Self in the sefirot; and he called it garmeh, as if to say "His Self." "One in them": explanation: in the sefirot, which are the third aspect. And because the union of the Ein Sof in the sefirot is through the Self that spreads, he said "He and His Self are one in them." And the word of oneness [stands] between "His Self" and "in them," to indicate that the union of the Ein Sof in the sefirot, although they are not His Self, is through the Self that spreads, and the Self that spreads is unified with the sefirot, as we explained in the gate mentioned. And there is no wonder that he called the Ein Sof "King," for He is the true King, the King of kings of kings. "He and His life are one in them": explanation: "He," who is the Ein Sof; "and His life," that is, the Self, which is His life-force that He sends to the sefirot. And the word "and His life": explanation: life that spreads from Him, and they are the life of the sefirot. And this is necessary because He is not a living being, such that we would say "His life," a life by which He lives in them, God forbid; rather, He is His life and He is His Self. "Which is not so": explanation: in Beriah, and all the more in Yetzirah, it is not so; because the light that spreads and Beriah are not one: for their life, which is the light that spreads, and Beriah itself are not one; for their true union is only above, in the sefirot of Atzilut. And this is the power of the Emanator in the emanated, which is the substance that spreads to the vessels, never separated, even for one moment; but in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah their union is at intervals, as explained in the preceding chapter. And indeed, to the King who is unified in His emanated ones are our worship, our prayer, our blessing, our praise, the fulfilment of our commandments, our engagement in Torah, our unifications, and our songs: to Him certainly, and not to His attributes, except in conjunction with His Self. And this is so that our prayers may be accepted, and so that we can bound Him in names, words, and things. For the Ein Sof in its own aspect is not bounded by a name, and is not titled either by a title or by a name; and through His emanated attributes we can title Him with names, according to the relation of each and every name to each and every sefirah. And all the holy names and all their titles, and the four-letter name and its fillings, all of them are titles for His Self through His emanated sefirot. But in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah there is no name among the names of the four-letter name and its fillings, nor a name among the names that are not erased, nor a title among His titles, blessed be He; and they are not related to them, for in these there is neither ability nor might. But when the light spreads within Beriah, then they are titled with the names that are not erased: with the name Adonai, and with the name explained in tractate Berakhot (folio 7a): "Rabbi Ishmael said: Once I entered the Holy of Holies, and I saw Akatriel Yah, YHVH of hosts," etc. And there is no doubt that Akatriel is the name of the prince of Beriah; and nevertheless three names are related to him, Yah, YHVH, of hosts, because of the power of the light of the sefirot that spreads within them. And therefore he said to him, "Ishmael my son, bless me," because it was a time of favor; and therefore he said, "May it be the will," etc., "and may Your compassion roll over Your attributes," that is, the spreading of compassion over the attributes while it is within Beriah, which is Akatriel.

And behold, he called him "Yah, YHVH of hosts": for in Yah the first three are included, and in YHVH the three fathers are included, as we explained in the name of Rashbi in the Gate of Names, chapter 1: for Yod-Heh is in Chesed, Vav-Heh in Gevurah, and in the middle Tiferet, YHVH, uniting the right and the left. And in "of hosts" [Tzeva'ot] Netzach and Hod are included, which are called Tzeva'ot, and likewise Yesod, which is a sign [ot] in its host [tzava]; and it itself is included in Malkhut, which is the name Adonai, at times, as will be explained. And for this reason at times a name among the holy names is related to Beriah. And this is the reason that a hint is found in the words of Rashbi that some of the matters of the sefirot are related to Beriah. And after we have spoken sufficiently on the matter of Atzilut, we come in [the next] chapter to explain the matter of Beriah:
On the portion of Beriah:

Beriah is the Throne, and it is called in the language of the Zohar kursaya. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him [in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Bo, folio 43a]: "And there is no other god over it who adds to it or takes away from it. Afterwards He made servants for these vessels: a Throne with four supports and six steps for the Throne: behold ten; and all of it is a Throne," etc. And what he said, "And there is no other god over it," etc., is explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter 8. And our intent in copying it here was to indicate the connection of the passage with the passage that we copied there, where we engaged in explaining the ten emanated sefirot. And he said "afterwards He made": explanation: after He completed the emanation of the ten sefirot, He further wished to create a Throne, which serves with its ten grades the ten sefirot of Atzilut, which are the vessels, as we explained there. And he explained that the servants are the Throne, which has four supports and six steps, which are ten. And because it was difficult for him that if so they would be eleven (the ten, and the Throne that rests on the pillars and the steps, would turn out to be eleven), therefore he said "and all of it is a Throne": explanation: the gathering of all is the Throne. For the Throne is not apart from the matter of the steps and the pillars, but the gathering of the steps and the pillars is the Throne.

And the matter of four supports and six steps is because so the sefirot are divided, as it is said in Sefer Yetzirah: one, two, three, four, and afterwards six extremities, as we explained in Gate Three, chapter 4. And they are called servants to the ten sefirot for the reason we explained in the first chapter: for it effects the changes when the light of the ten sefirot is clothed in the ten servants. Further in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 4), concerning the matter of the Throne, these are its words: "'As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire' (Ezek. 1:13): these are the vowel-points of the Torah, which are nine, by which the nine spheres of the Throne were created. The Throne is tenth to the nine spheres, and the ten letters of יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א shine in them, and by them they were created." Thus far its words, for our matter.

And behold, he explained that the nine vowel-points are nine sefirot, as is known, and as we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, chapter 4. And he said that through them were created the nine spheres of the Throne, which are themselves the very substance of the Throne, as we explained above concerning the pillars. And he said "the Throne is tenth": he intended to resolve why there are nine spheres and not ten, as is their rule; and he said that the reason is that the Throne itself completes the count, for the Throne is upon the spheres. "And ten letters shine in them": he intended the sparks of the sefirot that spread and shine their light in the Throne; and the ten letters are the ten sefirot themselves, as we shall explain in the gate mentioned. And he was further precise in saying "and by them they were created": explanation: by the power of the ten letters that are clothed in them it was created, "like the grasshopper whose garment is of itself"; for the Throne and its spheres are a garment to the letters, which are the sefirot, and the letters are the cause of the garments; so all turns out to be one. And so it is always fitting not to separate Beriah from Atzilut, for they are the garments of the festival. And Rashbi said in the Tikkunim (there, folio 3): "And happy is he who clothes the King and the Lady in the ten sefirot of Beriah," etc.; and the intent is the light that spreads in them, for the sefirot are the letters. And at the end of this passage Rashbi further explained (there, folio 4) that "In the beginning [bereshit] Elohim created" is explained as "with the Shekhinah," who is the Torah of truth, the Torah of Truth, that is, the Shekhinah, who is likewise called "beginning" [reshit]; and she is the one who teaches what is concealed in Tiferet, and therefore she is called the Torah of truth, for the word torah is the language of teaching. And he said that in Malkhut, which is called reshit, "He created" [bara], that is, Beriah: אלדי"ם [Elohim], which amounts in reckoning to הכסא [ha-kisse, the Throne], which amounts to the number 86. And he dwelt at length there on the matter; and the sum is that the Throne was created from the power of Malkhut, and it is the world of Beriah, a garment to Atzilut. Further in the Tikkunim (there, folio 6), these are its words: "Here the name YHVH: He and His title are one, because from Him His title is found. But from the side of the ten sefirot of Beriah, the name YHVH and His title are not one; this is what is written (Isa. 43:7), 'Everyone that is called by My name, and for My glory I created him,' etc. Behold, sefirot are called by the name YHVH and by the name Adonai; and those of Adonai were created," etc. Thus far its words.

And the explanation: above in the matter he explained the four-letter name with its fillings, "each by his own standard," in its letters; and afterwards he said, "Here the name YHVH, He," etc. The intent is the names mentioned, which are in Atzilut: the name YHVH, which is hinted in the whole Emanation in general, as we explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels, and as we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name.

Behold, in Atzilut "He and His title are one," as we explained in chapter 2, that in Atzilut there is complete union, the true union; but in Beriah the Self and the sefirot are not unified with a complete and true union, as we explained above. "Everyone that is called by My name," etc.: explanation: called by My name, but it is not literally My name; and this is "I created him": explanation: beriah from the language of separation, as we explained.

Behold, there is not complete union; but on the contrary, [it is] separate from the root. "Behold, sefirot are called by the name YHVH": explanation: Atzilut is called by the four-letter name; but Beriah is called by the name Adonai. And just as the name YHVH includes all ten, so the name Adonai includes all ten; for they are four letters corresponding to four, as we shall explain in the Gate of Names, that these four are a palace to those four; and likewise Beriah is a palace to Atzilut.
And behold, the matter of Beriah and the matter of the Throne is that when the Shekhinah of His might was driven away and the moon was diminished, He multiplied her hosts, to appease her mind.

And the matter of the multiplying of her hosts is that each and every sefirah gave and created from its power one branch; and ten branches were unified below Malkhut and became a Throne for her, and it is the Throne that we mentioned above. And these ten branches are a palace to the ten upper ones, and they pour effluence, each one according to his service, to its lower branch; and because they are below Malkhut, they are called after her name, Adonai. And this is what he said: "and those of Adonai were created." And by this matter it will be understood that in one place Rashbi, peace be upon him, divided ten branches into four supports and six steps, and elsewhere (mentioned above) into nine spheres and a Throne. And the reason is that, since they are branches created from the ten sefirot, therefore they are divided in the divisions of the sefirot, and the two divisions mentioned are divisions customary in the sefirot. And close to this matter we found further in the book of the Zohar, Parashat Mishpatim (folio 126a), and these are its words: "'This is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel' (Ezek. 10:20), etc. Who is this living creature? Rabbi Yose said, Rabbi Chiyya said: the small living creature. And is there a small living creature? Yes: the small living creature, and the upper living creature, and the smallest small living creature. 'And they saw the God of Israel' (Exod. 24:10), precisely, as I have said." Thus far its words. And his intent is that the living creature that is under the God of Israel is Beriah, and he called it "small" because of the upper living creature, which is Malkhut.

And behold, Malkhut is called "the God of Israel," explanation: the Shekhinah of Tiferet. And he objected, "And is there a small living creature?" For until now we have heard only of Malkhut being called "living creature." And he answered: "Yes: the small living creature," which is Beriah; "and the upper living creature," which is Malkhut; "and the smallest small living creature," which is Yetzirah. Or he means that he called Malkhut "the small living creature." And as to his asking "And is there," it is because it never seemed to us that there is a living creature above Malkhut, such that Malkhut would be called, relative to it, "the small living creature." And he answered: "Yes: the small living creature," which is Malkhut; "and the upper living creature," which is Tiferet, so that relative to it Malkhut is called small; "and the smallest small living creature," that is, Beriah, which is below Malkhut. And with us the first is the principal, and it is necessitated from within the passage in its place. And likewise further, close to our intent, we found in Rabbi Yitzchak ha-Kohen bar Ya'akov, of blessed memory, and these are his words: "You have already understood the roots of the emanation of the degrees, from the head of the Supernal Keter down to 'the blessing, life forever.' Now one must arouse the secret of the emanation emanated from them: an emanation of degrees like bodies for souls, designated by names, as we received them from the ancient sages and from the books of Rav Chamai. I have not seen them in all of Provence except with three pious men. The first was in Narbonne, an outstanding sage, a Kabbalist, from the mouth of an elder and master; and of his master too, that holy elder, they used to testify that Elijah was revealed to him from Yom Kippur to Yom Kippur; and the two [others] in Arles, which is the great city. The first emanation, which is like a spiritual body to the primordial emanation: his name is Sabi'el, and they call him the prince of the height of the degrees. The second to him is the emanation of Chokhmah, whose name is Peli'el; he is the prince of the wonders of Chokhmah; and we have received that his name in which his emanation was revealed is Zekuni'el, and his name is Sagsaga'el, in reckoning [as] 'and honor the face of the elder' (Lev. 19:32); and he is the planting of Chokhmah, 'the planting of the Lord, that He might be glorified' (Isa. 61:3); and the sign is 'on the day of your planting you make it grow' [tesagsegi] (Isa. 17:11), for Samekh and Shin interchange with one another and have one place of articulation. The third prince is the prince emanated from the emanation of Teshuvah, which is a treasury for all who know understanding and those of great fear; and his name is Yero'i'el. And the verse in the Torah hints at the three of them in one verse: 'Before the hoary head [seivah] you shall rise up, and honor the face of the elder [zaken], and fear [ve-yareta] your God' (Lev. 19:32). These three are called bodies for souls, bound to one another, like the flame bound to the coal, inwardness to inwardness. My help is from the Lord," etc. "The seven degrees: further, from them likewise seven degrees are emanated, in the likeness of bodies for souls, though they are spiritual. The name of the first degree is Miharon, the prince of Chesed, particular to water; the second to him is Gevirurun, he is the prince of the strong and awesome Gevurah; the third, his name is Yedidirirun, he is the prince of compassion, who is the beloved of the Lord; the fourth, his name is Setirirun, he is the prince of the foundation of the world, stored away and hidden in the middle line, called the supernal hiding place; and this is 'He who dwells in the hiding place of the Most High shall abide in the shadow of Shaddai' (Ps. 91:1); and enough for the discerning. The fifth, his name is Nitzchirirun, he is the prince of victory, he is the Eternal [Netzach] of Israel; the sixth, Hodirirun, he is a prince emanated from the emanation of Hod; the seventh, his name is Sefirirun, he is a prince emanated from the emanation of the end of all the degrees. 'These are the mighty men that were of old' (Gen. 6:4). And we have received in this that the first three are sealed at the end with the name El, and the seven with -run at their end. For the three are powers from the powers emanated by the power of the great, mighty, supernal Delight, over them all, Cause over all causes and Cause of all causes; and the seven are like burning candles, each one shining his lamp from the seven inner ones, which are like inner souls, and they are like spiritual bodies." Thus far the words of the sage, may his rest be glorious. And he said that these ten crowns are a garment to the ten crowns of the sefirot, and that they are a garment to the spirituality, like bodies for souls; and there is no doubt that this matter is the Throne mentioned above, which is Beriah. And afterwards the master added an explanation of three pillars emanated from the attribute of Malkhut. And their names: Malkhi'el, after the attribute of Malkhut; and the second Aturi'el, after the golden diadem, Binah; and the third Nashri'el, after Tiferet. And he said that all of them are emanated from Malkhut, and they carry her and do her service, and raise the Throne from emanation to emanation, up to the beloved of the Lord, who embraces her and kisses her by means of the foundation of the world. And he said that these thirteen branches are the thirteen attributes. And he gave a sign for these three pillars: נע"מ חרו"ן; and he explained regarding this name, which includes the three of them, that run hints at Tiferet, as it is written (Jer. 31:7), "Sing [ronnu] with gladness for Jacob," and Ayin-Mem, "the diadem [ateret] of their king [malkam]" (2 Sam. 12:30), which are their three sources, all of which are in Malkhut; and these are the last three attributes. And as an acronym, נע"מ חרו"ן: nose avon, mored, chet [bearing iniquity, rebellion, sin], so that He may turn from the fierceness [charon] of His anger and spare and have compassion. Thus far the sum of his words, in extreme brevity. And because it does not relate to our matter, we have abbreviated it as much as possible. And after the matter of Beriah has been explained in this chapter, we come to explain the matter of Yetzirah in other chapters:
On the portion of Yetzirah:

We have already explained that Yetzirah is Metatron; and not literally Metatron, but in the way we shall explain. And the matter is that this angel is called by two names: sometimes he is called Metatron, and sometimes he is called Mitatron, with Yod. And the intent is: when this angel is a garment to the Shekhinah, and the Shekhinah is concealed within him and shows her actions through him, then he is called Mitatron with Yod, a hint to the Shekhinah, included of ten, who descends and is concealed and hidden within him; and not the Shekhinah literally, but a spark and the light emanated from the Shekhinah, and it is a spark and light included of ten sparks. And, as it were, this thing is called the exile of the Shekhinah. And this is explained in the Tikkunim [Tikkun 21, folio 61a], and these are its words: "'And further, a man drew off his shoe' (Ruth 4:7): this is the body, which is a woman, his vessel; and this is Metatron. 'And gave it to his fellow': for sometimes the central pillar is found in him, and sometimes the Righteous One. And sometimes the upper Shekhinah is 'attestation' [te'udah] in him, and sometimes the lower Shekhinah is 'exchange' [temurah] in him. And this is 'a garden locked' [text: gal, 'a spring locked'] (Song 4:12), and in him 'a spring sealed,' which is the Shekhinah, Yod, included of ten sefirot: the Yod of Mitatron. All the sefirot act through him in this low world; and through him are levirate marriage, and chalitzah, and the bill of divorce. And all the letters in him are substitutions, such as מצפ"ץ; and he is the locking of festivals, and times, and holy days, the locking of the door before the borrowers. On Yom Kippur, which is the World to Come, YHVH is not called with Adonai, which is judgment [and is a shoe, the locking of the door]; and the door is not locked, but it is open to receive those who return. And therefore on Yom Kippur the wearing of the shoe is forbidden, for there is no union in it for the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Shekhinah: for sometimes it is the Shekhinah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, withdraws, and sometimes the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Shekhinah withdraws. And therefore the time of Torah scholars is on the Sabbath: for on the weekdays, when Metatron rules, it is said of him (Ezek. 46:1), 'it shall be shut the six working days': through him the gate is shut. 'And on the Sabbath day it shall be opened': the gate shall be opened, and the Shekhinah will go out from him, to be unified with her husband." Thus far its words. And this is its explanation: "a man drew off his shoe: this is the body": explanation: Tiferet, which is called body, and is called man, as is known.

And behold, Tiferet draws off the shoe, which is Malkhut, when she is in Metatron, who is likewise called "shoe," as we explained above. And it is already known that a shoe is a vessel; for so they decided in tractate [Bava] Metzia (folio 47a) concerning acquisition, which requires a vessel; and therefore Malkhut, which is called "vessel," is hinted in the word "his shoe." And this is why he doubled "a woman, his vessel": explanation: she is his wife, and therefore she is called "vessel"; and this is her relation in the word "shoe." "And gave it to his fellow": it has already been explained in the preceding gates that Tiferet and Yesod are two fellows with regard to Malkhut, for both serve with her: for sometimes Malkhut is unified with Tiferet itself through the Righteous One, and sometimes with the Righteous One alone. And as for his now calling Tiferet "body," it is for the reason that he calls Malkhut "woman, vessel," etc.

And the matter of drawing off is only of the foot; therefore he calls Tiferet "body," so that the expression "drawing off" may be related to it. "And sometimes the upper Shekhinah," etc.: the intent is to explain the language of the verse (Ruth 4:7), "Now this was formerly in Israel, concerning [redeeming and concerning exchanging (temurah) … and this was the attestation (te'udah) in Israel]"; and he dwelt on this at length to prove that Malkhut is within Metatron, as he goes on to explain. And Binah is called "attestation," and Malkhut "exchange." And he said "and sometimes the lower Shekhinah is exchange": explanation: she is called "exchange" in him, explanation: in Metatron; and this will be according as the governance of the world is through her, sometimes through Binah, sometimes through Malkhut, as we shall explain. And all this will be in the union of Tiferet and Yesod with both of them, as we explained. And the reason that Binah is called te'udah is that in her all the attributes assemble [mitva'adim], that is to say, the six extremities; or in the secret of the Jubilee. And Malkhut is called temurah because in her are the counterparts of all that is in the upper ones: its likeness and its counterpart is in her, like the sea, in which there is all that there is on dry land (see Zohar, Beshalach, 48b). "And this is a garden locked": according to what appears at first glance, the garden is Binah, which is locked in him, and the spring is Malkhut, which is sealed in him. But it is forced to explain so; rather, both refer to Malkhut, who is garden and spring, and there are two aspects in her: garden, relative to her aspect called the lower Shekhinah, that is, the manifestation of Heh; and relative to [the aspect] called Yod, that is, spring: explanation: the point of the spring and the source, that is, [the Yod]. And this is what he said: "which is the Shekhinah, Yod, included of ten sefirot"; and she is sealed within Metatron. And to this he hinted in saying "the Yod of Mitatron," which is the Shekhinah stored away within him; and the Shekhinah is called Yod to hint that she is included of ten when she is stored away within Metatron. And for this he said of necessity: "all the sefirot act through him in this low world": explanation: all the sefirot are clothed in Metatron to act through Metatron in this world; and for this it was necessary that the Shekhinah be included within him, as we shall explain further. "And through him are levirate marriage and chalitzah": explanation: in him is the matter of the drawing off of the sandal, which hints there at the stripping off of the shoe, as we explained; or levirate marriage, which is "and gave it to his fellow," that is, the Righteous One, who is a fellow to Tiferet and marries his wife in levirate marriage; and all through Metatron, as he said above, "and sometimes the Righteous One," etc. And likewise "the bill of divorce," which is the matter of divorce; and the divorce of the Shekhinah from her husband is when she is in exile in Metatron, as we shall explain. "And all the letters in him are substitutions": explanation: every change of names in the 231 gates is through Metatron, as will be explained there; and the substitution of YHVH by Adonai is in Malkhut. And [if] every substitution is in Metatron, how is this? Rather, it is that Malkhut is within Metatron.
And the matter of substitution will be explained in the Gate of Permutation.

And the matter of "the locking of festivals," etc.: it is known that festival and holy day without qualification are in Malkhut, and she does not receive while she is locked within Metatron; so Metatron turns out to be "the locking of festivals," etc. "The locking of the door before the borrowers": for he locks the door of the effluence before Malkhut, so that she does not receive from her husband; for on the weekdays they are not unified except through him.

And the matter of "borrowers": explanation: for the moon borrows from the sun, as in the matter that is said (Prov. 19:17), "He who is gracious to the poor lends to the Lord." Explanation: for Tiferet lends and pours forth its light and its effluence to Malkhut and her hosts, like the sun with the moon and the other stars. And Metatron locks the door: for when it is the weekdays, then she is locked and does not receive except through him. And not literally through him, but as we explained, that "the Shekhinah in the lower ones is a need on high": for when the mother nurses her children with milk, the milk increases in her breasts; and likewise, when Malkhut conducts the world, she herself distributes food abundantly to all her hosts and to the lower ones, and then the effluence and the good increase in her. And when it is the weekdays and the exile, then she pours forth only with contraction, and then she does not receive effluence abundantly. And this is what is sometimes found in the words of Rashbi, in the Tikkunim and in his other books, that Malkhut receives food through the messenger Metatron; and these words are impossible according to their plain sense, for who would put a formed angel within the Emanation? But [it is] as we explained; and we shall add further teaching on the matter in the next chapter. And on the weekdays and in the exile the door is shut and locked, conducted through this prince. And on the days of Sabbaths and festivals, then it is freedom and Jubilee. And with this matter the rest of the passage is explained. But to hint that the exile is the concealment of the Shekhinah within Metatron, it is further hinted in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 56, folio 90a), and these are its words: "When the Shekhinah was exiled, all the sefirot descended with her, and there is no separation between her and the ten sefirot; and when they descended, they were clothed in the six weekdays, six branches: Chesed on the first day, Gevurah on the second day, the central pillar on the third day, the three second sefirot on the three other days, which are the fourth, fifth, and sixth day," etc. Thus far its words.

Behold, explicitly, that the Shekhinah went into exile in the weekdays, which is Metatron. And as Rashbi explained elsewhere (in the Introduction, folio 2b), and these are his words: "And so מלאך [malakh, angel] amounts to the reckoning of the two names together; and therefore he is called the angel, the Prince of the Countenance, for through this messenger they are unified on the six weekdays." Thus far its words. And this is the matter of the coupling on the weekdays, which is through Metatron, as is found in the words of Rashbi. And further, like this matter, Rashbi explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (in Parashat Tetze, folio 281a), and these are his words: "'And concerning exchange': the lower Shekhinah, in what place is she concealed? In her youth, Metatron." Thus far its words.

And further in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 119a): "And the holy dove, all the six weekdays, goes wandering from place to place. And if she finds a righteous one in the world, she cleaves to him; and if not, she returns to her nest, in that place that is called 'the bird's nest.' And what is her nest? Metatron, whose name is [like] Shaddai, who guards the gate, of which it is said (Ps. 118:20), 'This is the gate of the Lord,'" etc. Thus far its words, for our matter. And above this passage he told of the praises of Malkhut on the Sabbath day and festivals, in her union with her husband above; and now he comes to explain that on the weekdays the matter is not so.

And the matter of these weekdays is in truth hard to grasp; for at first glance the discerning will be astonished. For, God forbid, it appears [to be] some withdrawal of providence, for He has handed over His providence to the lower ones. And it is likewise difficult that we should say that even when Israel are in their dominion, on the weekdays they are conducted according to this angel whom we mentioned; and behold, we were warned concerning him (Exod. 23:21), "do not rebel against him," and our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded: "do not exchange Me for him." And the resolution of these doubts will be explained in [the next] chapter:

The resolution of the doubts that we raised in the preceding chapter is explained in a passage of the Zohar, Parashat Noach (folio 75), and these are its words: "Rabbi Shimon opened: 'Thus says the Lord God: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall be shut the six working days; and on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened' (Ezek. 46:1). This verse is to be looked into, for it is a secret, as it is said: 'it shall be shut the six working days, and on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened,' etc. Why shall it be shut all those days of the six working days? But these are profane days, for this gate shall be shut so that the profane may not make use of the holy. 'And on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened': for then is the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, and then the moon is illumined to be joined with the sun. Come and see: this gate is not opened in those six weekdays, because in those weekdays the lower world is fed, and all those six weekdays rule over the world, except in the Land of Israel. And those that rule [do not rule in the Holy Land], because this gate shall be shut. But on the Sabbath day and on the day of the new moon they all pass away and do not rule, because this gate is open, and the world is in joy and is fed from there, and the world is not given to another authority. And if you say that all those six days they rule by themselves, come and see: 'that faces east': before they rise to rule, it looks constantly at the world; but it is not opened to feed the world from holiness except on the Sabbath day and on the day of the new moon. And all the days, all of them cleave to the Sabbath day and are fed from there; for then, on the Sabbath day, all the gates are open, and rest is found for all, for the upper ones and the lower ones. Come and see: 'And the Lord came down to see' (Gen. 11:5): He came down from the holy to the profane, and spread out a covering, to oversee what they built and established as an establishment, to arouse over the world, to make them fear." Thus far its words. And behold, Rashbi explained explicitly in this passage that the governance is not through this angel in the Land of Israel, in saying "and all those six weekdays rule over the world, except in the Land of Israel."

Behold, explicitly, that they do not rule in the Land of Israel, because "the Lord's portion is His people" (Deut. 32:9); and it is testified in the Torah (Deut. 11:12), "the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year." And this matter will be when Israel are in their dominion. And now with this matter a doubt will be explained, with which every inquirer will have difficulty in reading this passage: for in the Land of Israel the weekdays have no dominion, and in the other places, where they rule, it appears explicitly from within it that there is no union and opening of the gate except on the Sabbath and the New Moon. And it is difficult, for we hold that through the messenger they are unified on the weekdays, as explained in the preceding chapter; and it appears clearly from there that on the weekdays this entrance is open to the weekdays, for behold, through him they are unified, as explained there explicitly. Rather, certainly, that is in the weekdays of the Land of Israel, for then certainly in the Land of Israel they are unified. And it is impossible that in the Land of Israel too there should be no union except through the Righteous One; for if so, all the weekdays should be holy in the Land of Israel, and the matter is not so. Rather, certainly the matter is intermediate: that is, that they are unified, and the union is through this angel, and he does not have dominion to feed the Land of Israel, but the feeding is through the Shekhinah; but outside the Land their feeding will be through him. We can further say, to resolve this doubt, that what is expounded in the Tikkunim, that the union is through Metatron, is after the exile, for the Shekhinah went into exile through him, as we explained in the preceding chapter; but at the time of the Temple the union is not through him at all. And this in our eyes is forced. And after the Holy One, blessed be He, has brought us to this inquiry, it is fitting that we explain the matter of this union that is through this angel, what its nature is. For one cannot say that this angel enters within the Emanation to unify the sefirot. For although before he departed from the world he was flesh and blood, and from this side it was necessary that he have a soul emanated from above, like us, nevertheless, in the end, why should this soul be different from the other souls of the righteous and of the good and pleasant prophets, so that the sefirot are unified through it, while they do not rise to this grade in their souls? Since this union is through a soul (so that according to the truth she is unified with her husband through the souls of the righteous, as we shall explain), we do not on that account say that they are the ones who unify. And likewise, this soul, although it merited to unify these two sefirot, why should its rank be nullified on the Sabbath day? For on the contrary, it would be fitting that its power grow on the Sabbath to unify them. And nevertheless we do not on that account say that the union is to be attributed to it, as we explained.

And moreover, not because the soul is emanated would this angel merit to enter into Atzilut; for in the end the manifestation of this angel is literally the body of Enoch, as they expounded in the Pirkei Merkavah: "his body was turned into torches of fire," etc. And since this is so, it is not fitting that his body, however purified it may be, should enter the holy within, to unify the two sefirot. And if we say that the union is through the soul that he had, behold, according to this his soul is not literally the angel, for the angel is the body, as we explained; and if so, how did Rashbi say that they are unified through the messenger?

And further, in addition to all this: how is it possible that husband and wife be unified not through the organ of the holy covenant? And behold, Yesod is the holy covenant for the upper union; and if they are not unified through it, how is it possible that they be unified?

And further: while they are unified through the angel, where has Yesod, which is between them, gone, and what is its matter then? Therefore it is fitting to investigate first the matter of the union of Yesod, and from it we shall come to the union of the angel. And we say that besides Yesod's being a passage for the effluence, as the organ is a passage for the seed, it further has an action in the union, and it is the aspects of its light from below to above, as we explained in the Gate From Below to Above. And in that aspect Yesod receives the prayers of Israel and raises them above, and likewise the performance of their commandments. And they are the very female waters that the female casts forth to receive the upper waters, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 19. And they are the spirituality of the prayers, whose letters are purified and whose light shines; and likewise the light of the commandment, and its spirituality, and their life is the manifestation of the fair and pleasant light that rises up to Yesod. And this is what is expounded in the Tikkunim concerning the union mentioned, where he said there that the receiving of the prayers on the Sabbath is through Yesod. And the reason is that since the breath of a man's mouth is a power emanated from his soul, the measure of his prayer will be according to the measure of his soul.

And behold, on the Sabbath day, when there is in a man an additional soul from a high place, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul, it is necessary that the spirituality of the holy letters rise up to Yesod. And because of this the receiving of the prayer on the Sabbath is through Yesod; for there is power in the spirituality of the letters, in their manifestation one upon one, to rise by way of the ascent of the soul up to the Righteous One, where the soul shines, as explained in the Tikkunim on the verse (Dan. 12:3) "And the wise shall shine like the radiance of the firmament": "that they shine in the firmament," etc.; see there. And although the prayers that a man prayed on the weekdays do not have that power in them, nevertheless they are held back until the Sabbath day, so that by way of the ascent of the Sabbath prayers the other prayers rise with them. And there is support for this in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, in the Palaces, in the first palace; see there. And when the spirituality of the commandments and the spirituality of the prayer rise up above, in the secret of the spirituality of Yesod, the effluence that flows because of it is according to the measure of the subtlety of the commandments and the prayer. And therefore the union is in Yesod: explanation: according to the subtlety of Yesod, for so it is the mirror and that which pours forth the arousal. And this is on the Sabbath day. But on the weekdays the receiving of the prayers of Israel is not through Yesod but through an angel, because there is no power in the soul to raise the spirituality of the letters up above; for the prayer does not rise in spirituality except according to the measure of the soul and its power, as we explained. And when the prayer rises only up to this angel, behold, the arousal will be according to the measure of the subtlety of this angel. For when Malkhut gathers the deeds according to the subtlety of the measure of the angel, her husband pours effluence to her only according to the subtlety and spirituality of this angel: an effluence that is not complete and not so spiritual, but an effluence that is not completed, [being] only like the density of the angel. And this is the matter of the union on the weekdays; and not that this angel enters into Atzilut. And we have proofs for all the matters and preliminaries needed for this inquiry, but for love of brevity we did not want to dwell on them. And nevertheless, when the inquirer contemplates in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 19 and 20, and likewise in the Gate of the Soul, our words will be settled more and more, all the more so. And let us return to this passage that we are explaining. For because it appears at first glance that the matter of the weekdays and the shut gate is the withdrawal of providence, Rashbi escaped from it in saying: "And if you say that all those six days they rule by themselves, come and see: 'that faces east': before they rise to rule, it looks constantly at the world; but it is not," etc. Explanation: the intent in our saying "and all rule," etc., is not that the governance is through them, God forbid. For although he said that the gate of the court is shut, the intent is not providence, for in providence He always oversees His world; rather, the intent is the food, which flows only from below, by the upper word. And he said, "Come and see: 'that faces east,'" etc.: explanation: from this the prophet wished to escape, in saying "that faces east" [kadim]: explanation: that oversees the weekdays as before [ke-mi-kodem]; for that providence which was before is the very self of the providence that oversees now, and there is no dividing in the matter of providence. And the illustration is to the king who stands to judge the land, and inside, in his house, he has storehouses full of silver and gold; and on known days he feeds the members of his household with the inner silver and gold, and on other days he feeds them with the little silver and gold that is before him; and he is always the judge, he is the overseer and the feeder; but the payment and the expenditure have a distinction between the days. And so the matter is literally above. And what he said above, "and then the moon is illumined to be joined with the sun": he was precise in what he said concerning the matter of the union, for the matter of the distinction between profane and holy is the arousal and the illumination from below. And this is what he said: "and then": explanation: at the time of the Sabbath day, "the moon is illumined to be joined"; and he did not say "and then it is joined," etc., but "is illumined to be joined," that is, the upper arousal, in the secret of the subtlety of Yesod, as we explained. And what he said, "Come and see: 'And the Lord came down': He came down," etc., is to explain the matter of "And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower," etc. And he said that this descent was that the Shekhinah descended and was revealed in the profane, that is, Metatron. "And spread out a covering": explanation: for there was a veil between Him and the city and the tower that they built, which is the husk that they held fast to and established for themselves as a god. And let us return now in [the next] chapter to explain the passage of the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash) that we were dealing with, which says there:

"And the holy dove, all those six days, goes wandering from place to place," etc. Explanation: the Shekhinah wanders from place to place to oversee the masters of service and the men of deeds, to make her Shekhinah dwell in them; because through them her husband is unified with her: for they engage in Torah, which is Tiferet, and when she rests upon them she is found unified with her husband; and therefore she cleaves to the righteous one. And like this matter it is expounded in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (folio 66), on "And I will establish My covenant" (Gen. 6:18): "Rabbi Shimon said: This matter is obscure, in the arousal of the male toward his female when he is jealous for her. Come and see the secret of the matter: when a righteous one is in the world, immediately the Shekhinah does not move from him, and her craving is for him. Then the craving above toward her is in love, like the craving of the male toward his female when he is jealous for her. And therefore, 'And I will establish My covenant with you': craving is aroused on your account. Like this: 'But My covenant I will establish with Isaac' (Gen. 17:21). 'And I will establish My covenant with you': that My covenant may be in the world." Thus far its words.

And the matter is that the Shekhinah pursues the performance of the commandments, so that through them she may have union with her husband; and when a man is righteous in the world, she pursues him and is unified with him, so that through his good deeds she may arouse the union with her husband; and therefore she comes first. And since the matter is so, the righteous one comes first and is unified with her through those deeds; so the arousal of that righteous one turns out to cause the upper Righteous One to be unified with the Shekhinah. And the illustration of this: a woman who pursues a strange man; and from the greatness of her husband's love for her he is aroused, and is jealous for her, and is unified with her, so as not to remove his hand from her hand for a moment. So the upper Righteous One: since by the merit of the lower righteous one the Shekhinah rests upon him because of his deeds, the upper Righteous One hastens to be unified with her. And this is the matter of "the female between two righteous ones," mentioned in the Zohar in many places. And this is what he said: "And therefore, 'And I will establish,'" etc. And it is already known in this wisdom that "from my flesh I shall see God" (Job 19:26), and there is no union without erection; and this is והקימותי [ve-hakimoti, "and I will establish"], a literal raising, indicating the arousal of the Righteous One toward the Shekhinah; and this is the matter of his proof from the verse "But My covenant I will establish with Isaac." And this is "craving is aroused": literal craving, as we explained. And the matter is that through the deeds of the righteous one are the female waters, which she needs for the coupling, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 19. And after there are female waters, it is necessary that there be male waters; for He will not restrain [His] power, since there is merit, and He must remember the eternal covenant, as expounded in many places in the Zohar. And because this matter is on the six weekdays, when she has no coupling, she pursues and seeks rest for herself with the righteous one. And, God forbid, when she found no rest for the sole of her foot, he said, "she returns to her nest and is concealed there": explanation: she is concealed and hidden in that hiding place.
