And the matter is that when the righteous one is in the world, he will be a base and a foundation for the Shekhinah, and the Shekhinah dwells in the lower ones for the reasons we said; and the light of the Shekhinah will be revealed through the righteous one, the light of the Shekhinah literally, without intermediary. And since there is no righteous one in the land who would be fit for this matter, behold, that light is concealed and comes by way of the angel, which is the weekdays; and if she is unified, she is unified through him, in the way we explained in the preceding chapter. And let the inquirer not hasten to reply: since there are no deeds of the righteous, by what is she unified? For our intent is not to say that there are no good deeds at all, God forbid, for it is impossible to say [that the world is] without righteous ones; rather our intent is that there is no righteous one who so purifies himself that he would be a base and a watchtower for the light of the Shekhinah, as expounded above. And then she returns and is concealed in her nest. And he said that at that time this angel is called "the bird's nest," because he is a nest for the bird that wanders from her nest, which is the Shekhinah, as is known. "Metatron, whose name is [like] Shaddai," etc.: it is known that this name is related to the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, whether in Yesod or in the angel; and then his name is called Shaddai, like the name of his master; and likewise מטטרו"ן [Metatron] amounts to שד"י [Shaddai, 314]. And he brought a further proof: "for he guards the gate": explanation: the guardian of the upper entrance, and it is the veil of the screen before the Shekhinah, which is called "the gate of the Lord."

Behold, all that we have gone around in all this is to indicate the matter of the concealment of the Shekhinah in Metatron in the exile and on weekdays. And there are many more proofs in the words of Rashbi; and because the preceding ones suffice us, and for love of brevity, we shall not dwell further on this. And we say that this matter is called Yetzirah. And a proof is from the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 3), and these are its words: "And if you say that Ezekiel saw this secret: he saw only the likeness of these living creatures, and not that he saw the living creatures; but like a king who sent a document with his seal, and the image of the king is impressed on wax from his seal. For in the sefirot [of Atzilut] is the literal image of the King; and in the sefirot of Beriah, the seal of the King; and in the sefirot of Yetzirah, and in the angels, which are living creatures, the form of the seal in wax," etc.

And behold, he revealed to us explicitly that Yetzirah is the seal of wax, and they are those that Ezekiel saw. And he said "and in the sefirot of Yetzirah, and in the angels": he taught that Yetzirah is the angels, which are all included in Metatron. And besides this, further on in the matter he said (there, folio 6a): "And from the side of the forms of wax Ezekiel saw [those appearances that he saw]."

Behold, explicitly, that the appearances were in Yetzirah, and not in Beriah, and not in Atzilut. And further on in the matter he said (there, folio 6b): "'The seventh: as the appearance of the bow' (Ezek. 1:28). The bow: this is the Righteous One, the foundation of the world; 'as the appearance' of it below: Metatron; this Ezekiel saw, for he includes all the appearances." Thus far its words. Do you not see that all the appearances that Ezekiel saw, which we said were in Yetzirah, are Metatron? Further in the Tikkunim elsewhere (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 112), when he was engaged with the appearances of Ezekiel, these are his words: "The second vision: 'And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man upon it above' (Ezek. 1:26): here he saw the central pillar resting on the Shekhinah, and he saw it from within Metatron, who is Shaddai." Thus far its words.

And he was precise in the extra wording of saying "who is Shaddai": the intent is that this angel is what unifies these sefirot, which are Tiferet and Malkhut; and from the side of this aspect the name Shaddai is related to him, as we explained above; and therefore it is fitting to relate to him that in him Ezekiel saw the two attributes together, as we explained at the beginning of his words. And this is what the verse says: "And upon the likeness of the throne," that is, Malkhut; "a likeness as the appearance of a man," etc., that is, Tiferet; unified together, without our arranging that this is fifth and this last; rather, he saw them unified, this last and this second to her, because it is the way of the angel in whom the appearances were seen to unify these two attributes. Behold, explicitly from within this passage, that the appearances that Ezekiel saw, which he said elsewhere were in Yetzirah, were in Metatron, which are forms of wax, as we explained.

And further there (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash), these are its words: "And the Righteous One is Chashmal, the sum of these two names, which are יאהדונה"י; and he saw it from within the Prince of the Countenance." Thus far its words. And we shall not trouble ourselves to explain it here, because we shall explain it in the Glossary of Titles; and in any case we learned from within it that Ezekiel saw the Righteous One, the foundation of the world, from within the Prince of the Countenance, that is, Metatron, as is well known: his name is Metatron, the Prince of the Countenance. And he called him here "the Prince of the Countenance" [sar ha-panim] to show that just as the Righteous One is the prince of two faces, which are YHVH [and] Adonai, that is, Chashmal, so this angel is the prince of these faces; and therefore he saw the Prince of the Countenance from within the Prince of the Countenance.

And further in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Bo, folio 43), these are its words: "And He arranged for the Throne classes to serve it, which are: Mal'akhim, Erelim, Seraphim, Chayyot, Ofannim, Chashmalim, Elim, Elohim, Benei Elohim, Ishim." Thus far its words. And behold, he taught explicitly that the ten powers of the angels are the servants of the ten of Beriah, that is, the Throne, as we explained in chapter 3. And there is no doubt that they are Yetzirah, for Yetzirah is a garment to Beriah, as we explained in chapter 1. And after we have proved this part, we come in [the next] chapter to explain the part of Asiyah:

What it is fitting to know is that the breaking of the husks and their abolishing is in their entering within holiness, that is to say, in their drawing near to holiness. And this is our prayer that we say: "Let all who come into the world recognize and know that You are God alone." For in their drawing near to the service of God, this is their subjugation. And this too is "And let all that has breath in its nostrils say: the Lord, God of Israel, is King." For those that have breath in their nostrils are from the side of the husk, as explained in the Zohar (Tetzaveh, folio 182) on "Cease from man, who has breath in his nostrils" (Isa. 2:22). And this is the matter of "and all the works shall fear You, and all the creatures shall bow before You," etc. And likewise this is the cause of their subjugation and their abolishing: for they draw sustenance from the side of holiness, and are purified, and all their side of impurity is nullified; and when the dross is refined, it is burned in the fire. And this was the reason for the bulls of the Festival, which were seventy, as the number of the princes who pour forth outward; and concerning them it is expounded in the book of the Zohar (in Parashat Pinchas, folio 259) on "And the waters decreased continually" (Gen. 8:5): for they diminish because of their nearness to holiness. And there is a revealing of this matter there, and we shall not dwell on copying it here. And for this reason, when it is the will of holiness to subdue the husks, it is clothed in them in order to subdue them. And the matter is that of such it is said (Eccl. 8:9), "a time when man ruled over man to his hurt." And they expounded in the Zohar (Mishpatim, folio 95b): "'a time when man ruled': this is the man of Belial, the man of iniquity; 'over man': this is the man of holiness; 'to his hurt': of the man of Belial." For although he rules over holiness, that is, the effluence flows into him, and some profit would appear to him from this, it is to his hurt, for he will be nullified and subdued. And a proof is from the converts, who are souls snatched to them from the side of holiness; and through them the Holy One, blessed be He, is sanctified, as in the matter of Jethro, who was the priest of On, and the Holy One, blessed be He, was sanctified through him, in his saying, "Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods" (Exod. 18:11), as expounded there in the Zohar (Yitro, folio 67). And likewise the Shekhinah, in ten sparks of the ten sefirot, spreads to be clothed in ten husks, to subdue them and humble them, to fulfil what is said (Ps. 103:19), "and His kingship rules over all." And the matter is that if the husks were found without holiness within them, then it would be necessary that there already be a place of which we would say: this is not in the manifestation of divinity, God forbid. And this is impossible, because He gives life to all of them, and all the manifestation in the world has no manifestation and subsistence apart from Him, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, chapter 8. And therefore the clothing of holiness in the husks is necessary; and not that benefit should be drawn from this to the husk, but on the contrary, "to its hurt," as we explained. And Rashbi revealed this inquiry to us in the Tikkunim [Tikkun 69, folio 105a]: after he explained the ten husks by their names, he said: "And these lower crowns are husks to the ten sefirot, and the ten sefirot are kernel within them. And these husks are a partition between Israel and their Father in heaven. In these husks the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah are clothed, to fulfil in the Shekhinah 'and His kingship rules over all,' and to fulfil in Him 'for God is King of all the earth' (Ps. 47:8). But above, in His place, it is said, 'evil shall not sojourn with You' (Ps. 5:5)," etc. Thus far its words. Behold, explicitly, that the ten sefirot are clothed in ten husks. And he explained that the clothing in them is in two ways. The first, in the way of (Lam. 3:44) "You have covered Yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through," and to effect judgment through it in a time of emergency. And the second, to subdue them. And this is why he went back and said, "In these husks the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah are clothed," etc.

And further in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 10, folio 24), these are its words: "For this corresponding to that the Holy One, blessed be He, created. But the lower crowns are husks relative to the upper crowns, in which ten letters are clothed in exile, that they may be subdued beneath Him," etc. Thus far its words. And behold, he explained that because Israel are in exile, and the husks rule over Israel, and it is possible that they might perish in their exile, God forbid, therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, is clothed in ten sparks, and is clothed in them in order to subdue them. And one is not to believe that holiness is literally clothed in the husk, God forbid, for "evil shall not sojourn with You" is said; rather, the intent is through intermediate powers between it and holiness, as we shall explain in the Gate of Substitutes, chapters 6 and 7.

And the matter of the clothing of the Shekhinah is through known powers, which are called Ofannim, as has been explained. However it may be, we have learned that the sparks of holiness are clothed in ten husks. And this matter is called the ten sefirot of Asiyah; and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, folio 112b): "And what is said, that Adam the first man drew his foreskin: this is the Adam of Asiyah. And what is it? This is the husk in which he is clothed, to rule over all; this is what is written, 'and His kingship rules over all.'" Thus far its words. He taught explicitly that the matter of Asiyah is ten sparks clothed in ten husks, of which it is said "and His kingship rules over all," as above.

And this matter is further explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Bo), and these are its words: "And He arranged for the Throne classes," etc.: "Mal'akhim, Erelim, Seraphim, Chayyot, Ofannim, Chashmalim, Elim, Elohim, Benei Elohim, Ishim. And for these He made servants: Samael and all his classes, which are like clouds to ride upon them to descend to the earth, and they are like horses for them," etc. Thus far its words. He taught that the ten husks are servants and garments to the ten classes of the angels, which are servants and garments to the ten grades of the Throne, which are servants and garments to the literal ten sefirot, as explained in the preceding chapters. And after we have proved these four parts, each one by itself, we come in [the next] chapter to prove them together, according to what is found in the words of Rashbi, with the help of Heaven.

The intent in this chapter is to bring proofs that were not written in the preceding chapters, because they deal with the four divisions together, or with three of them, while our engagement was with each one alone. And therefore we bring them here, to decide the four aspects that we mentioned, which are the aspect of Atzilut, the aspect of Beriah, the aspect of Yetzirah, the aspect of Asiyah. And these are the words in the Tikkunim [Tikkun 6, folio 21]: "'You shall not take the mother with the young' (Deut. 22:6). The eggs are from the side of the Ofannim; the fledglings from the side of the youth, Metatron; the young from the side of the Throne. And she is the tabernacle of peace, which is the nest of the Shekhinah. For the supernal Imma nests in the Throne, in three upper sefirot; the central pillar, including six sefirot, nests in Metatron; the lower Imma nests in the Ofan, of which it is said (Ezek. 1:15), 'and behold, one wheel [ofan] upon the earth.'"

"And further, the Shekhinah from the side of the Throne is called eagle, and from the side of the youth dove, and from the side of the Ofan bird; and the Shekhinah [is] the likeness of a man to them."

"And further, 'You shall surely send away.' Come and see: there is an angel appointed over birds, from those souls that are called birds, and Sandalfon is his name. And at the time that Israel fulfil this commandment, and the mother goes driven away and the young cry out, he pleads merit for his birds and says to the Holy One, blessed be He: But behold, it is written of You, 'and His compassion is over all His works' (Ps. 145:9); why have You decreed against this bird, that she is driven from her nest? And likewise Metatron pleads merit for his birds, which are the spirits [that fly in human beings]. From the Throne they are souls, and from this living creature they are spirits, and from the Ofan vital souls; and they are in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. On Sabbaths and festivals souls, spirits, and vital souls descend upon them by way of Atzilut, which are the holy spirit from the ten sefirot; and every appointed one pleads merit for his birds," etc. Thus far its words.

And although it is true that this passage needs a broad explanation, nevertheless for our matter we have learned clearly what was sought. For it is known that soul, spirit, and vital soul are from Binah, Tiferet, and Malkhut; and we shall broaden the explanation in the Gate of the Soul. And he said that Binah nests in the kursaya, which is the Throne that we explained in chapter 3; and Tiferet nests in Metatron; and Malkhut nests in the Ofan: this is the matter we explained in the preceding chapter, that the Holy One, blessed be He, rules over the husks through the angels called Ofannim, which are what pour effluence into the spheres. So that there is one who said, according to a maggid, that if a man mentions the name Ofannim over some matter, that thing will rise between heaven and earth into the air of the world and revolve for so-and-so many hours.

Behold, it appears that the Ofannim are what pour effluence into the spheres and give them the power of their revolution. So that now what Joshua said (Josh. 10:12), "Sun, stand still at Gibeon," and the spheres stood still from their revolution, will not seem far-fetched; because he commanded the powers that pour effluence upon them not to act in the spheres. And the reason is that the Ofannim have two actions. The first, that they turn and revolve the spheres, as explained above. Second, that they subdue the husks through the Shekhinah that rests upon them, as we explained. And because there was then need for the subjugation of the husks with strength and speed, he commanded that they not perform their other action, which is the turning of the spheres, but that their action be in the subjugation of the husks. And this is what it says: "Sun, stand still at Gibeon, and moon, in the valley of Ayalon, until the nation avenged itself on its enemies" (Josh. 10:12–13). And let us return to our matter: for the spheres and the Ofannim are all one matter, except that this gives effluence and this receives effluence.

And the matter of the Shekhinah in them is to subdue the husks; for these heavens and spheres are related to them, as is evident in the words of Rashbi (in Tikkun 8) concerning the matter of "for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment" (Isa. 51:6); and likewise in a passage that we shall copy in the Gate of Substitutes, chapter 2, where he said that the Land of Israel is not conducted through the princes but through the Holy One, blessed be He, he said: "And if you say, how does the firmament rest for nothing over the Land of Israel," etc.; see there. And likewise in the book Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, folio 251), and these are its words: "The Faithful Shepherd said: Why did He command not to eat leaven seven days, and to eat matzah in them? And why 'it shall not be eaten,' and why 'you shall not eat'? But the seven planets are שצ"ם חנכ"ל [Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon], and they are from the side of good and evil: the light that is inside, matzah; the husk that is outside, leaven," etc. Thus far its words, for our matter. And from within it is explained that שצ"ם חנכ"ל are the powers of the leaven and the husk, and within them is clothed the light, which is matzah. And this is what is written (Jer. 10:2): "and be not dismayed at the signs of the heavens, for the nations are dismayed at them." However it may be, you turn out to say that the kursaya is a nest for Binah. And he said that from there it is Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah; but on the Sabbath the soul, the spirit, and the vital soul come from Atzilut, the very substance of the sefirot.

And behold, this is a complete proof for our intent in this inquiry, as expounded in the preceding chapters. Further, Rashbi explained them in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 3), and these are his words: "And happy is he who clothes the King and the Lady in the ten sefirot of Beriah, which are included in the name יאהדונה"י: as His name, so His garments; and he who prepares for Him the horse, of which it is said (Song 1:9), 'to my mare among Pharaoh's chariots,' etc., which is His chariot. For on the days of Sabbaths and festivals He wears the garments of royalty, which are the ten sefirot of Beriah; and on weekdays He wears ten classes of angels, which serve the ten sefirot of Beriah. For in the ten sefirot of Atzilut, the King: He and His Self are one in them, He and His life are one in them; which is not so in the ten sefirot of Beriah, for they and their life are not one, they and their self are not one. And the Cause over all shines in the ten sefirot of Atzilut and in the ten sefirot of Beriah, and shines in the ten classes of angels and in the ten spheres of the firmament; and He does not change in any place." Thus far its words.

And this is the explanation of the passage in brief, although our intent is clear. He said that the ten sefirot of Beriah are included in the name יאהדונה"י, which is eight letters, and two names: they are ten. And because it was difficult for him that this name is literally in Atzilut, and now he relates it to Beriah, which is the Throne mentioned, to this he said "as His name, so His garments": explanation: as the name that is clothed in them, so is the name of the garments; for the name of Atzilut is related to the garments when Atzilut is clothed in them. And therefore, since the sparks that are clothed are sparks of the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, which are Tiferet and Malkhut, the name of the union too is related to them. And because Beriah has two aspects relative to Atzilut (first, its being a chariot to it, and Atzilut dwelling upon it; and second, its spreading within it like a garment), therefore he compared them to two things: the first, in the parable of the garments; and the second, in the parable of the horse, which is its being only a chariot to Atzilut. And because it was difficult for him what superiority there is in this (for since Beriah is not of the very substance of Atzilut, what is it to us whether He is clothed in it or in another, for we are obligated in the matter of the union only in Atzilut), he answered that they are garments to Atzilut on the days of Sabbaths and festivals. The intent is that on holy days such as these the Holy One, blessed be He, reveals His light in the world through them, as we explained. And they are called garments of royalty, because they are not literally Malkhut, but they are garments of Malkhut, garments in which Malkhut is clothed. And what is renewed on the Sabbath day is that the light is (of male and female) (perhaps it should read: the aspect of the union of male and female through her), which is not so on the other days, when the light of the union is revealed only through Metatron, which are the weekdays. And this is what he said: "and on weekdays He wears ten classes of angels," who are all included in Metatron, as we explained above in chapters 4, 5, and 6. And he said "which serve the ten sefirot of Beriah," so that we should not believe that the light of Atzilut is literally clothed in Yetzirah, which is Metatron, the ten classes of angels; rather, it is clothed in them through the ten of Beriah, and the ten of Beriah are clothed in the ten classes of angels. And it is said of them that they are weekday garments because of the revealing of the light to the low world through him. And it was difficult for him: if so, it turns out that the lower ones never draw from the light of the very substance of Atzilut. To this he said that so it is: for it is impossible for the world that its governance be through it, just as it is impossible that its governance be through the Emanator, except after the light of the Emanator is clothed in the emanated ones and the emanated ones in the created entities, because of the need for changes, judgment, and compassion. And this is what he said: "for in the ten sefirot of Atzilut, the King," etc., as explained above in chapter 2. And since the ten sefirot of Beriah are not one with their life, it turns out that it is already possible for changes to be effected through them. "And the Cause over all shines in the ten of Atzilut, and in the ten of Beriah," which is the Throne, "and in the ten classes of angels," which is Yetzirah, "and in the ten spheres," that is, Asiyah, as explained above. And the end of this passage is explained at length in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, chapter 8. "And He does not change in any place": for the change is in the vessels and not in their soul, as we dwelt at length in the Gate of Self and Vessels. Thus far the explanation of the passage. And from within it is a proof of the four aspects mentioned, ABYA. And likewise all four of them are found (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Bo, folio 43), and these are its words: "Afterwards He made servants for these vessels: a Throne with four supports, and six steps for the Throne: behold ten; and all of it is a Throne. Like the cup of blessing, for which they ordained ten things; like the Torah, which was given in ten words; like the world, which is the work of creation, which was created with ten utterances. And He arranged for the Throne classes to serve it, which are: Mal'akhim, Erelim, Seraphim, Chayyot, Ofannim, Chashmalim, Elim, Elohim, Benei Elohim, Ishim. And for these He made servants: Samael and all his classes, which are like clouds to ride upon them, to descend to the earth, and they are like horses for them. And whence do we know that clouds are called a chariot? This is what is written (Isa. 19:1), 'Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt'; and this is the appointed one of Egypt. And immediately, when they saw that their appointed one, who is their god, they saw him like a horse beneath the chariot of the Holy One, blessed be He, immediately 'the idols of Egypt trembled before Him,'" etc. Thus far its words.

And although we have already copied it in the preceding chapters, we have brought it again here, to show a complete proof that this is beneath this, and this a garment to this, and that the husk is a chariot for spirituality to descend to this corporeal world; and that is outside the Land, as in the matter of Egypt; and that this is a subjugation for them, as it is written, "and the idols of Egypt trembled." And after we have explained the inquiry in the preceding chapters in these aspects, and have confirmed and established it as is fitting, it is fitting now to explain in a chapter of its own what is found at first glance to be opposed to this in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him:

Besides these passages, further passages are found that disagree with one another. In one place they said that Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet are Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, and in another place he said that they are Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah; and according to this there is found no Atzilut in all the sefirot, since Keter too is Beriah. And elsewhere he said that Netzach, Hod, Yesod are Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah; and elsewhere he said that Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut are Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. And we are obligated to reconcile them and explain them properly. And therefore we set out first and say that the whole matter of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah is like the sense of the four things called inscription, engraving, hewing, making. And when we go down to the depth of these four, we shall know those. And the matter is that inscription is like a thing inscribed, in which there is no grasp of anything except that it is a mere inscription, in which there is only the difference between "it is not" and "it is." That is to say: like the difference between the complete Nothing and the subtle Something, the beginning of being Something; for then the being Something is at the utmost of subtlety and nearness to the Nothing, so that there is no difference at all between the Something and the Nothing. And this subtlety is called a mere inscription. But this aspect is the aspect of Atzilut, the very self of the sefirot in their place; for they are not of limit, nor an intrinsic inscription; but they are between the Something and the Nothing, between limit and without limit, as their matter is explained in the preceding gates. And engraving is a thing that is grasped somewhat more than the inscribing; for the inscription is not sensed, and the engraving is sensed, like the scratch of a fingernail. And likewise Beriah is a being more revealed than the beings of Atzilut; and because it is still the subtlest of the subtle, it is titled with the name engraving only. And hewing is a revealing of the thing more than engraving, so that it is called by the language of hewing, which is a parable for one who hews a thing from its source, which is a thing sensed more than mere engraving. And it is a likeness to Yetzirah, which is a being more and more revealed than Beriah. And making is the revealing of things in substance, until they reach the grade of corporeality. And its name, asiyah, testifies to it; for this name is related only to the accidents of the body and corporeality.

And behold, Sefer Yetzirah used these four definitions for the matter of ABYA, and all is one matter, as we explained. And it is known that the world, from its first point to the point of the abyss, the Holy One, blessed be He, created grade after grade; and the beginning of the manifestation is from His Self, the King of kings of kings, and the manifestation descends wondrously, from cause to effect and from cause to effected. And the whole world, from its beginning to its end, is included in these four parts. And the first part is the part of the sefirot and the necessary Self, as explained in the preceding gates, and it is what is called inscription and Atzilut. And after this part, a second part, and they are the chariots and the thrones, which are subtler, more concealed, and more spiritual than the angels; and they are called by the name Throne. And it is known that there is a throne for a throne; for "how many faces within the faces that are seen, and how many backs behind backs that are not seen"; and so Rashbi explained, "thrones, seven within seven," as we shall copy in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 9. And like the matter of the sefirot, so is the matter of the thrones. And this Throne is called by the name engraving and by the name Beriah. And after this part proceeds the world of Metatron, which is the world of the angels, which are ten classes, and their hosts without end; and they are denser and more revealed than the Throne. And therefore the angels are the bearers of the Throne; and the Throne bears its bearers, for it is what pours effluence to all the angels; and it is what first draws the effluence from Atzilut and pours it to the angels beneath it, which are Metatron and the ten classes of the angels and their hosts; and they are called hewing and Yetzirah. And after this part proceeds the world of the spheres, and the many matters included in them, which is called the work of creation; for although the spheres are included in ten, their particulars are many, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the chapter of the work of creation; and they are called Asiyah. And each and every grade, each and every part of these four parts, is divided into ten parts, this above this: like the part of Atzilut, which are ten; and likewise Beriah, and likewise Yetzirah, and likewise Asiyah. But the tenth that is in Atzilut is near to the first that is in Beriah; and the tenth that is in Beriah is near to the first that is in Yetzirah; and the tenth in Yetzirah is near to the first that is in Asiyah. But there is a great distinction between them: as there is between the sphere of the moon and the point of the earth, so there is a distinction between grade and grade among the ten grades of Asiyah, and from Asiyah to Yetzirah, and between grade and grade in Yetzirah, and likewise between Yetzirah and Beriah, and between grade and grade among the ten grades of Beriah, and Atzilut, etc. For to each and every one, what is below it is reckoned before it like a mustard seed within the great sea; as the astronomers distinguished between the nine spheres and the tenth sphere, for the nine spheres are reckoned within it like a mustard seed; and in this proportion we reckon from it upward and from it downward. And our intent in saying "from it upward" is not superiority of place, God forbid, but superiority of rank and priority of cause, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing. And after this preliminary has been engraved in the knowledge of the inquirer, it will not be far from him that there may already be found in Atzilut: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. For since the explanation of ABYA intends the order of the grades of revealing, then the Supernal Keter is called Beriah relative to the subtlety of the Emanator, and Chokhmah Yetzirah relative to the Supernal Keter, and Binah Asiyah relative to Chokhmah. And not that it is literally Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, but Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah of Atzilut, that is to say, and all in Atzilut. And likewise Tiferet is called Beriah, and Yesod Yetzirah, and Malkhut Asiyah: not that they are literally Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, but to indicate the revealing of things grade after grade. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 116a): "For just as there is the Adam of Beriah, the Adam of Yetzirah, the Adam of Asiyah, in the image of the Supernal Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah, so it is in the image of the central pillar, and the Righteous One, and the lower Shekhinah; for in the sefirot all is Atzilut." Thus far its words.

Behold, he taught explicitly as we explained; and therefore he was precise in his wording, "in the image," etc.: and not Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah literally, but Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah in the image of Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. And the explanation: just as Keter, Chokhmah, Binah are one above the other, so in their likeness below are Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, three grades; and likewise they are in the likeness of Tiferet, the Righteous One, Malkhut, three grades one above the other, according to Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. And this is what he said: "for in the sefirot all is Atzilut"; for the intent is not Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah literally, but all is Atzilut, except that it is divided into these four parts, as we explained. And in this way too we will have no doubt when we see that Rashbi, peace be upon him, said that Keter, Chokhmah, Binah are Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, and likewise Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, and likewise Netzach, Hod, Yesod; for they are three corresponding to three, and in each three there is Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, in the way we explained. And these are the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 128): "And my son, I found in a mishnah, in the secret of tracings and forms and colors, in the hiding place of the secrets, the Concealed of the Concealed: that the Adam of Beriah, who is primordial to all the primordial, rides on the lion, turns to the right, and makes tracings, which are ways and tracks of the sea of the Torah; and of them it is said (Isa. 43:16), 'who makes a way in the sea.' The Adam of Yetzirah rides on the ox, and turns to the left, and takes fire in his mouth, and forms forms. The Adam of Asiyah rides on the eagle [and takes wind in his mouth], and turns to the east, and makes colors in the eyes, in the faces. He said to him: Who is the Adam of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah here? He said to him: My son, this is the one of whom it is said, 'and man is Nothing,' and 'the superiority of man over the beast is Nothing' (Eccl. 3:19). And it is the Adam of Beriah, for by this the Cause of causes created all creatures. The Adam of Yetzirah: Chokhmah; of it is said (Job 28:12), 'And wisdom from Nothing shall be found,' for it is the Yod of Ayin, etc. The Adam of Asiyah: this is the Nun of Ayin, Binah; she is the mother of all living, the work of creation, etc. The lion, by which he makes tracings: this is Chesed, the right. And the ox, by which he forms forms: this is Gevurah. The eagle in the middle, by which all the colors are recognized: and this is Tiferet, the beauty of all, in which all the colors shine. And Netzach, Hod, and Yesod correspond to the three fathers," etc. Thus far its words.

Behold, explicitly, that Rabbi Elazar asked, "Who is the Adam of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah here?": to hint that here was his question, for the matter of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah in Atzilut is all according to the place. And he answered him that Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah; and Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; and Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, Netzach, Hod, and Yesod. And elsewhere (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 134) he said: "And further, bereshit: bara shit [He created six]; and they are the upper Adam of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah and the lower Adam of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah." Thus far. To hint at Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, upper, and Netzach, Hod, Yesod, lower; and all in the way we explained. And there is another way, and it is that when the sefirah enters into Asiyah it is called Asiyah, and likewise Yetzirah, and likewise Beriah; in the way that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained: Binah, soul; Tiferet, spirit; Malkhut, vital soul; Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah; and we copied it above, in the preceding chapter. And up to here our poor and weak intellect has reached in the explanation of the inquiry, with the help of Heaven.
The Seventeenth Gate: The Gate of the Thigh of Jacob.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain a strange matter found in the Zohar concerning Netzach: that it was on the left, and when he touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh Netzach was blemished, and afterwards it was turned to the right. And the words are strange to the utmost strangeness and need a fine explanation; and this will be the business of this Gate.
Chapter One:

In this chapter we shall set out the words of Rashbi on this inquiry, and remark on what is fitting for the understanding of his words. And these are his words (in Parashat Bereshit, folio 21b): "'And he limped upon his thigh' (Gen. 32:32): this is the Eternal [Netzach] of Israel. 'Upon his thigh' is written, and not 'his thighs': this is the fourth grade, from which no person prophesied until Samuel came; and of it is written (1 Sam. 15:29), 'And also the Eternal of Israel will not lie.' Then this grade was set right, which had been weak since Jacob was endangered by the appointed one of Esau, and he touched the hollow of his thigh. When he came to Jacob, he took strength from that 'turning of evening' in harsh judgment; and Jacob was included in it, and he could not prevail against him. 'And when he saw that he could not prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh' (Gen. 32:26), and took the strength of judgment from there, because the thigh is outside the body. For Jacob was the body, and his body was included in the secret of two grades, in the secret that is called Adam. For since he took strength outside the body, immediately 'the hollow of Jacob's thigh was strained.' And no person prophesied from there until Samuel came; and therefore 'the Eternal of Israel' is written of it, 'for He is not a man [adam]' (1 Sam. 15:29). Joshua prophesied from the splendor [hod] of Moses, as it is said (Num. 27:20), 'And you shall put of your splendor upon him': Hod, this is the fifth grade; Netzach, the left thigh of Jacob. And therefore David came and included it in the right, as it is written (Ps. 16:11), 'pleasures in Your right hand forever [netzach]': 'Your right hand is netzach' is not written, but 'in Your right hand.' What is the reason the thigh of Jacob was weakened? Because the side of impurity drew near to it and took strength from it; and it was delayed until Samuel. And therefore he came [to recall that this is the thigh of Israel, as it is written, 'And also the Eternal of Israel']. And therefore all his words were in judgment, at the beginning and at the end. And moreover, the Holy One, blessed be He, afterwards included it in Hod. When? After he anointed kings. And therefore Samuel was weighed as Moses and Aaron: just as Moses and Aaron were in the two sides above, so he below, like those two sides. And who are they? Netzach and Hod, like Moses and Aaron above. And all the grades are held to one another, as it is written (Ps. 99:6), 'Moses and Aaron among His priests,' etc.; for the six sides were included and shine one in another." Thus far its words.

And there is room to scrutinize this passage. First: he proved that this thigh is Netzach because it is written "his thigh" and not "his thighs"; and this is no proof, except that we cannot say that both of them, Netzach and Hod, [are meant]; but to prove that it is Netzach and not Hod there is no proof here; on the contrary, it may be said of it that it is Hod, for of it too "his thigh" can properly be said.

Second: they said "the fourth grade" needlessly; for since he said that the thigh is Netzach, what need is there to make known to us that it is fourth to Chesed? And who does not know all these things?
Third: there is a refutation of the very basis: for it is only fifth, since it is the left thigh, as he concludes; if so, it is fifth and not fourth.

Fourth: the length of his wording, "no person prophesied from there," etc., "and therefore it is written, 'And also the Eternal of Israel.'" What proof is this? On the contrary, the opposite is implied.

Fifth: what he said, "Joshua prophesied from the splendor of Moses," etc. And what proof is there from Joshua? Perhaps, although Joshua did not prophesy from there, others prophesied. And moreover, the superfluity of his wording in saying "from the splendor of Moses": let him say "from Hod" without qualification.
Sixth: they said "and this is the fifth grade," etc. Did we not know until now that Hod is fifth? And all the more, since he already said above that Netzach is fourth, certainly Hod is fifth.

Seventh: his saying "What is the reason it was weakened?" He already explained above, in what he said, "and took the strength of judgment from there," etc.; and so according to this there is room neither for the question nor for the answer.

Eighth: they said "And moreover, the Holy One, blessed be He, afterwards included it in Hod." To what does it refer? If to what he said, "and therefore all his words were in judgment," etc., it is difficult, for the word "moreover" is to add; what is "moreover"? This is that.

Ninth: his saying "Moses and Aaron above, Samuel below." What is "above" and what is "below"? For the prophecy of Samuel is from Netzach and Hod, and that is the grade of Moses and Aaron, as is implied at a quick reading of the passage. This is what we saw fit to remark on the wording of the passage. Besides that this matter itself is difficult for two reasons. The first: who put Samael above in holiness, so that he blemished a sefirah? And is not Samael the prince of Esau, and the princes are below Metatron, for the prince of all the hosts above is Metatron? And moreover, he has no connection with the sefirot; for the sefirot are not apprehended even by the holy angels, all the more so by the unholy ones, that we should be able to say that Samael blemished a sefirah; and this thing is certainly unacceptable. And above all: since these sefirot were emanated in the order we wrote above, and it is known that their order is that Chesed is a branch of Chokhmah and Netzach a branch of Chesed, if so, what would make us think of saying that Netzach was on the left? And is it possible to say so? This is certainly a wonder.

And further, Rashbi explained the opposite in the book Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, folio 243a), and these are his words: "'And Abraham rose early in the morning' (Gen. 22:3): at the beginning of the first hour, at the end of the dawn, the Netzach of Jacob; for there is 'for the leader [la-menatze'ach], upon the hind of the dawn' (Ps. 22:1), to take vengeance on Samael, who touched the left thigh of Jacob, which is Hod; for of it is said (Lam. 1:13), 'He has made me desolate and faint all the day': דו"ה [davah, faint], הו"ד [Hod]," etc. Thus far its words.

And further in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 115), these are its words: "חק"ב טנ"ע: this is Hod; in it 'there He made for them a statute and an ordinance' (Exod. 15:25); for Hod was bound to Gevurah, and Netzach to Chesed. And it is said of Hod, 'He has made me desolate and faint all the day': in it he looked upon the destruction of the Temple and the many slain who were slain, to take vengeance on the nations of the world; and of it is said, 'and he limped upon his thigh.'" Thus far its words.

And behold, from all these passages it appears explicitly that the principal blemish was in Hod, which became davah; and of it it is said "and he limped upon his thigh," and not of Netzach. And in order to explain this inquiry well, we shall devote a chapter of its own to it:
To explain the passage well, we must set out two preliminaries.

The first: that the inquirer should not think that the husks enter within Atzilut, as many of the Kabbalists of our generation have thought. And although the plain sense of the words would necessitate the matter, one must understand them and direct them. And the matter is that when the cry of the adversaries enters (those called "others," who are outside (the academy) [Yetzirah], and do not enter to behold the pleasantness of the Lord), and they cry out outside concerning the debts and iniquities of Israel, and say: these are idolaters, and these, etc., these uncover nakedness, etc.: behold, then the anger of the Lord and His jealousy smoke, and in the place where it would be said "you are My people," it is said to them "not My people," God forbid, and the anger of the Lord is kindled. And in the place where it would have been fitting that much effluence and compassion flow in the attributes, God forbid, the power of judgment is aroused, and the dross of the gold flows to the outer ones, and the judgment is completed. And this is their entering into holiness: and not that they literally enter, but their demanding and their teaching of debts against "the enemies of Israel," and the entering of their cry there to raise fury and to arouse judgment to take vengeance: this matter is called their entering into holiness. And not only the flowing of judgment; but then, in the place where judgment is aroused, the face of compassion withdraws, and darkness and judgment prevail, and that attribute [on which the iniquities of the lower ones depend; from Asis Rimmonim] is blemished, until vengeance is taken for that matter. And then compassion is revealed and illumines the place of darkness, and with the multitude of waters the fire is extinguished, and the world is not given over to judgment. And besides this, that place is blemished, and it is dark in the hiding of the face of compassion from it, and it effects judgment. And behold, in the action of judgment there is no doubt that that attribute will be "a head to foxes"; for it is compelled to pour judgment to them, to spoil the vineyard of the Lord of hosts, the house of Israel, God forbid; and the judgment that flows to them is their food, which is the dross of gold. And it is the secret of the blood of menstruation [and the filth that the serpent cast into Eve]. And this is the blemish with which the attribute is blemished through the iniquities; and this is the power of the husk to blemish the upper roots, and not that they have entry there; and as we shall dwell further in explaining this matter in the Gate of Substitutes.

Second preliminary: we have already explained in the Gate of Arbiters the greatness of the completeness of arbitration and its superiority. And behold, for this reason, when His wisdom decreed that Tiferet should be the arbiter between Chesed and Gevurah, He further added to increase peace: that Netzach, although it is the branch of Chesed, should draw sustenance from the side of Gevurah, and Hod, although it is the branch of Gevurah, should draw sustenance from the side of Chesed. And by this judgment and Chesed were blended with a strong blending, until judgment and Chesed were one matter for them. How? Gevurah comes to pour forth judgment: it pours into Netzach, and Netzach is the branch of Chesed, and by its nature Chesed blends that judgment with a fine blending, until the judgment is sweetened. Hod comes to effect judgment: Chesed pours its effluence upon it, until its judgment is sweetened and moved to the side of Chesed. And when we wish to estimate the greatness of this blending, we know it from the words of David, peace be upon him, in saying (Ps. 132:9), "Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones sing for joy," as explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 3.

And behold, it is known that the matter of inclining to the right or to the left is through the effluence that flows in the attributes. The illustration of this: when the effluence of judgment prevails in Yesod, it will certainly be called left; and when the effluence of compassion prevails over it, it is called right. For the principal of right and left is the action, for there is no literal right and left in the upper ones, as explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And therefore, when Netzach was drawing sustenance from Gevurah, in the secret of the blending mentioned above, it was certainly left; because, although it is the branch of Chesed, the effluence that flowed into it was judgment, and it was sweetening the judgment and weakening it so that it would not act with strength. And likewise, when Hod was drawing sustenance from the right, it was right, since its action was in the secret of Chesed; and although it is the branch of Gevurah, nevertheless it had it in its hand to effect that Chesed in a fine, intermediate blending. And when the effluence prevailed in Hod with the power of judgment, it returned to its element, to be judgment. And therefore before, it was called הו"ד [Hod], whose meaning is Heh, Binah; Vav, Tiferet; Dalet, Malkhut: behold, it indicated the order of the grades, the union in the secret of the havayah in directness, the secret of the male and of compassion, because its inclination was to Chesed. But when the Heh came like the likeness of Dalet, [it was] to indicate its manifestation from the side of judgment, for it is the branch of Gevurah, as we explained. And when it inclined to the side of Gevurah completely, it became דו"ה [davah], which is the secret of the returning light, the reversing light, which is judgment: Dalet over Vav and both of them over Heh, reversed, to indicate the strength of judgment, and all the more when it is Dalet, poor [dalah] and afflicted. And with these two preliminaries there is no doubt that the doubts that we raised at the end of chapter 1 are resolved. For the matter of his saying "Netzach left and Hod right" is in the secret of the blending, as we explained. And what is said, "and he limped upon his thigh," of Hod, is because afterwards the judgment flowed to it according to its way. So according to the truth the limping is found to be in Hod: for Netzach was set right, in that it returned to draw sustenance from the right; but Hod was turned to destruction, since it now receives effluence from judgment after the limping. And after we have explained these preliminaries in this chapter, we come to explain the wording of the passage mentioned:

"And he limped upon his thigh: this is the Eternal of Israel." Explanation: Jacob is the aspect of Tiferet, and he is likened to the body; and just as the body has supports, and they are the thighs, so the upper thighs are called the supports of the upper body, as explained in most of the words of Rashbi.

And behold, from the side of the blemish that we shall explain, as it were, Tiferet limps upon its thigh: just as when the thigh is blemished in the lower human body the accident of limping happens to it, so, as it were, limping is related to the upper blemish. And although Netzach and Hod mentioned are "two halves of the body," explanation: equal at first glance, nevertheless Netzach is always above Hod. And although this matter does not settle in the thighs literally, so it is said, "from the appearance of his loins upward" (Ezek. 1:27), and Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 6) that it is Netzach, "and from the appearance of his loins downward" is Hod. And we always relate Netzach as over Hod. And therefore, since the verse said "and he limped upon his thigh," it implies literally upon his thigh; and which is the thigh upon which Tiferet literally is? You must say, this is Netzach. For one cannot say that it is Hod, since he said "upon his thigh," literally upon, as we explained. And because it would have been possible to say that it was both ("his thigh," Hod; "upon his thigh," Netzach), for this he said "his thigh" and not "his thighs": as if to say that if it were so, it would have been fitting that it say "his thighs," which is clear and has no length; and since it did not say so, it implies that it was one thigh. And to be precise about the matter of saying "upon," he said "this is the fourth grade." Or it is possible that we are precise thus from his saying "his thigh," with the pronoun suffix referring to him: and which is more related to him? You must say, this is Netzach, because it is the fourth grade, emanated from the third, which is Tiferet; and therefore this is related to it and not Hod. It is further possible that he intended in saying "the fourth grade" that we should not think, although it is said that it was on the left, that perhaps it was then fifth and Hod above it in the fourth grade; to this he said "this is the fourth grade": for although it was on the left, it never ceased being fourth, as we explained. And to prove the manifestation of the blemish in the honored roots, he said "from which no person prophesied until Samuel came." And what reveals this matter is that this is not mentioned in all the books of the Prophets until then. "And of it is written, 'And also the Eternal of Israel,'" etc.: and this is a proof that Netzach was blemished, as we shall explain. "Then it was set right": explanation: when Samuel came, then Netzach was set right, which had been weak through the blemish; and the matter of the blemish will be explained. "When he came to Jacob, he took strength," etc.

Behold, the prince of Esau wished to provoke Jacob and to pour judgment from Gevurah, to arouse the powers of judgment, for several reasons, whether the neglect of Torah or the marriage of two sisters; and he wished to pour judgment from "the turning of evening," which are the judgment and the darkness that are in Isaac, which is Gevurah, where his holding is; for from there is the nourishment of the fire of Gehinnom, as we explained in the Gate of Colors; and those powers that are in Gevurah are called "the turning of evening," in the secret of the color of darkness. "And Jacob was included in it," etc.: explanation: for Tiferet is the arbiter that tips Gevurah toward the side of Chesed; and therefore he did not succeed in pouring judgment from Gevurah to Tiferet. And therefore "he could not prevail against him [לו]": against Tiferet, against the Vav that is in Jacob. And this is "and Jacob was included," in the secret that it is called שמים [shamayim, heavens], fire [esh] and water [mayim], and it inclines the fire to the side of the water, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters. "And he touched the hollow of his thigh, and took the strength of judgment from there": explanation: from the side of Netzach he poured the strong power of judgment. And the reason he succeeded is that, although they too are supports of the body, nevertheless he touched them in the aspect in which they are not included in the body; and this is what he said: "for the thigh is outside the body."

And further, in the aspect of the thighs there is nourishment for the outer ones from there; and this is the hint of the knot that goes outward. And although it is said of something like this in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (folio 154a), "and all their hinder parts were inward" (1 Kings 7:25), in the end it is the back, and he has some portion in it, and all the more when the iniquity causes it; and therefore he took from it and from there it flowed. And because it is difficult (for in the end Tiferet is included in the six extremities; and if so, just as he could not prevail against him on the side of the arm, it would have been fitting that he could not prevail on the side of the thigh), to this he said that Jacob is not a chariot in the secret of the inclusion of the six extremities: for this is the secret of the chariot in the secret of Da'at, which is Vav including six extremities, and for this matter Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is the chariot, as explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine"; but Jacob is a chariot only in the aspect of Tiferet that is called Adam, which is right and left included in the middle line. And this is Adam, as it says (Ezek. 1:10): "And the likeness of their faces: the face of a man [adam], and the face of a lion on the right, and the face of an ox on the left," etc., "and the face of an eagle," etc. So the face of man turns out to include only right and left. And the sense of the wording: "for Jacob was the body": explanation: that he was a chariot to Tiferet in the aspect of the body, and it is the first, outer aspect; for "Moses inside, Jacob outside; this from the body and this from the soul," as explained in the gate mentioned. And the body includes only "two grades, in the secret that is called Adam," as we explained, which is the inclusion of right and left. "Since he took strength," etc., "immediately it was strained," etc.: explanation: he poured judgment, and that place was blemished, as we explained. "And no person prophesied": explanation: because of the blemish it was not set right to show its appearances to the prophets until Samuel came. And not that Samuel set right the whole matter, for the blemish was still standing in its place, for it was not fully set right, as we shall explain; but it was set right somewhat for prophecy. And nevertheless he said, "And also the Eternal of Israel will not lie nor repent" (1 Sam. 15:29): explanation: it does not retract its judgment because of the blemish mentioned; but since it judged Saul, to remove him from being king, with the strength of judgment, it does not again repent, that is, that compassion should flow upon him so as to set right the judgment. And the reason: "for He is not a man": explanation: for it is not a revealed branch of Tiferet, which is called Adam, that it should repent and that compassion should roll over judgment. "Joshua prophesied from the splendor of Moses": he wished to prove from here that it was Netzach that was blemished; and he said: Do you not see that Joshua was beneath Moses in grade? And if so, since Moses was in Tiferet, Joshua, who was below him, [ought to have had] his prophecy from Netzach, the fourth grade, since the grade of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was in Tiferet, the third grade; except that it was blemished, as we explained. "Netzach, the left thigh," etc.: it was difficult for him from the verse that said "pleasures in Your right hand forever," which appears [to say] that Netzach is to the right, the opposite of his view. To this he said that on the contrary, from there is a proof that it was to the left, except that David set it right and turned it to the right. And he proved this from what the verse said, "pleasures in Your right hand," and it did not say "Your right hand": it appears that it is a prayer that Netzach be to the right. "What is the reason it was weakened," etc.: it is not a question, for he already explained above; but a repetition of language. "What is the reason it was weakened? Because [the side of impurity] drew near to it," etc., as we explained in the first preliminary; and this is the reason that it was blemished. If so, it came to set itself right and to purify its judgment; and therefore it is impossible for it to repent. "And therefore all his words were in judgment," etc.: explanation: at the beginning, in the episode of Eli and his sons; and at the end, in the matter of Saul. "And moreover, the Holy One, blessed be He," etc.: explanation: besides its being purified through the judgment that it poured upon these righteous ones (that is, the sons of Eli, and Saul and his house) in place of Jacob, also the Holy One, blessed be He, who is Binah, included it in Hod, so that that judgment would be purified and nullified. "And therefore Samuel was weighed," etc.: explanation: since He included Netzach in Hod, Samuel turns out to hold right and left, that is, the two aspects Netzach and Hod; and he is weighed as Moses, who was a Levite, in Gevurah, and Aaron, the priest, the man of Chesed; and that is "above": explanation: above Netzach and Hod; and Samuel "below," in Netzach and Hod themselves. "For the six sides," etc., "shine one in another," etc.: it was difficult for him that this is not equal, but on the contrary beneath them, receiving from both of them; for he is in Hod included in Netzach, and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and Aaron in Chesed and Gevurah. To this he said, "for the six sides," etc.; and since these shine in those, if so, what is Netzach to me, and what is Chesed to me, and what is Gevurah to me, and what is Hod to me? All is one, unified. And Samuel, who held Netzach and Hod, turns out to be weighed as Moses and Aaron. Thus far the explanation of the passage, and this matter is resolved in its proper form. And after we have explained this passage, we come now to explain a passage that at first glance is opposed to this:

What is seen fit in this chapter is to explain a passage found in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (folio 168b), which at first glance is opposed to this. And these are its words: "The spreading of the good is thanksgiving [hoda'ah], which is called Chesed. And therefore one says, 'We give thanks to You' for such-and-such miracles and signs that were done from the side of the good. And if you say: but behold, it is written, 'pleasures in Your right hand forever [netzach]'; behold, it is from the side of the right. Not so; but each and every one shows that place from which it goes out. And if you say Netzach is in the right: behold, it is written 'pleasures,' and it is written (2 Sam. 23:1) 'the sweet singer of Israel'; and this is the left; and every left is included in the right; and thanksgiving gives thanks to the right, to show that from it it goes out. And this is the spreading of the good, which spreads in the land of the living. What is the reason there is no left here? Because the Other Side has no portion in the food of Israel. And if the left is aroused, the Other Side is aroused with it; and behold, he sold his birthright and his portion to Jacob our father. And we give a portion to that accuser in the filth of the last waters," etc. Thus far its words, for our matter. And the passage is long in its place. And at first glance it appears to disagree with what came before us in the preceding chapters, in that he objected, "And if you say: but behold, it is written, 'pleasures in Your right hand forever,'" and answered "Not so," etc.; and at a quick reading it implies that Netzach is not to the right. And before we enter into its explanation we shall remark on it somewhat. First: the doubling of his question: "And if you say: but behold, it is written," etc., and he answered "Not so"; and again he went back and said "And if you say Netzach is in the right." What does he say at first, and what does he say at the end? Second: there is a contradiction between his own words: at the beginning of his words it appears that he holds that Netzach is to the left, as we inferred; and at the end of his words he said, "and this is the left, and every left is included in the right, and thanksgiving gives thanks," as it appears that Hod, which is thanksgiving, is to the left, and not Netzach. Third: that he asked, "What is the reason there is no left here?", as it appears that the left is not mentioned in the Grace after Meals; and he explained above that thanksgiving is to the left; and behold, there is left. And now we come to explain the passage. Above in the matter he said that "and in His goodness we live," and likewise in the blessing "who feeds the whole world in His goodness," is in the attribute of Chesed, which is the attribute of good; and it is called "good" when all is included within it, as we copied the beginning of the passage in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 1. And now he explained that the blessing "We give thanks" is the spreading of Chesed, and that is Hod. "Thanksgiving, which is called Chesed": explanation: for Hod is called Chesed. And although intrinsically it is not Chesed, yet it is called so in a borrowed sense. And because it is strange to the utmost strangeness, for this he went back to prove the matter from the wording of the blessing itself, which says "We give thanks to You for such-and-such," etc.: explanation: for the good things that flow from Him in the inheritance of the land for Israel, and the giving of the Torah and the commandments, and life and food, as mentioned in the blessing itself. "And these are miracles and signs that were done from the side of the good." And it is known that the principal of the miracles is from the side of Chesed; for from the side of judgment and Gevurah all is by way of nature; and likewise the name Elohim amounts in reckoning to הטבע [ha-teva, nature], which is 86. And the reason is that the creation of heaven and earth was in the attribute of judgment, and likewise the whole work of creation. And the witness to this is that the thirty-two paths by which the whole creation was created came in the name Elohim, and this is the matter of nature. But afterwards, for the subsistence of the creation, He joined compassion with it, as our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded. And therefore the change of the orders of creation, which is the matter of a miracle, is the opposite of nature and against the attribute of judgment; therefore the miracle is in Chesed, which is good. And this is his saying "miracles and signs that were done from the side of the good"; and not "good" literally, because it is known that the miracles are through Yesod, which is called nes [banner, miracle]; and so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 111a). And although Yesod too is called good, now we are dealing with Chesed, which is called good; and therefore "from the side of the good," and not "good" literally, whose explanation is: from the side of the Chesed that flows to Yesod for the action of miracles. Or he means, for the reason that he explained above in the matter, that "good" is Chesed when all is included within it and it does not spread, and then it is called "good," as we explained at length in the Gate of Arbiters; and therefore he said "from the side of the good," and not "the good"; for "the good" pours forth neither miracles nor the change of miracles; but it is from the side of the good, which is the good that flows, that is, complete Chesed; and therefore "from the side of the good," and not the good itself. "And if you say: but behold, it is written," etc.: explanation: for he said that thanksgiving, which is Hod, is the spreading of Chesed; and it would appear that his view is that Hod is to the right, a branch of Chesed; and it would follow from this that Netzach is a branch of the left. To this he said, "And if you say: but behold, it is written": explanation: if it comes up in your mind that our intent is to say that Hod is to the right, and the verse "pleasures in Your right hand forever" is difficult for you, which implies that Netzach is to the right and Hod to the left: "Not so": explanation: let it not come up in your mind that our intent is that Hod is to the right, God forbid, for certainly Netzach is to the right. "But each and every one shows," etc.: explanation: and if so, that it is not drawn from the right and is [not] in the right, as you supposed, then why did you say that it is drawn from Chesed? To this he said, "but each one shows": explanation: it is true that Hod is to the left, drawn from Gevurah, as is well known; but it is known that "the waters conceived and bore darkness," and so Abraham begot Isaac; if so, Hod, which is the branch of Gevurah, turns out to be drawn from Chesed; and therefore the thanksgiving is in Hod, to tell that its emanation is from the right and it is drawn from it, as we explained. "And if you say Netzach is in the right": explanation: and it is impossible that we believe that Netzach and Hod are drawn from the right, as you said; for behold, the verse says "pleasures in Your right hand forever," which implies that Netzach is to the right and not Hod; so it turns out that Hod never has a hold in Chesed. To this he answered, "behold, it is written 'pleasures,'" etc.: explanation: on the contrary, from the very place you came from: for it says "pleasures," two; and Hod is called "pleasant." And a proof for the matter: David is called "the sweet singer"; and it is known that דוד [David] with the word [itself] amounts to הוד [Hod]; and likewise his chariot is in Hod, for so it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Vayikra, folio 4a). And the matter is that when the Emanation is the seven included in five, as we explained in the Gate of Gates, Malkhut is found in Hod; and likewise, in her ascent to be unified, she is in Hod and Tiferet in Netzach; and this matter is explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 23.

And further, the lyre on which David used to play, which played by itself, was by the north wind, which is in Hod. And likewise the wars of David were from the side of Hod. And this is what he said: "and it is written, 'the sweet singer of Israel'; and this is the left," as we explained, that it is to the left. "And every left is included," etc.: it was difficult for him: for above in the matter he said that in the matter of the Grace after Meals the left is not mentioned at all; and he said that even in the taking of the cup, which is to be settled in the right, the left should not assist there, because it is not fitting to include the left in this matter. And it is difficult, for now he explained that the blessing "We give thanks" is the left, and it is Hod; if so, the left is already found mentioned in the Grace after Meals. And to this he answered that the left is included in the secret of the right: for if Hod, which is left, is mentioned, it is mentioned only in the secret of its inclusion in the right. And he brought proof for this: "and thanksgiving gives thanks to the right, to show that from it it goes out." The intent is that the principal of Hod in this is in its being included in the right and drawn from it, to draw to Malkhut; and this is like the right literally; and the thanksgiving over this is the manifestation of the blessing, as we explained above. "And this is the spreading of the good, which spreads": explanation: the drawing forth that spreads from the aspect of Chesed, which is concealed and spreads, which is called "good," as we explained above; and it is to pour forth to Malkhut, which is called "the land of the living." And she is called "the land of the living" in the secret of her receiving from the upper life through the right, as in the matter of the cup of the Grace after Meals, one of whose ten conditions is "living"; and therefore she is called "the land of the living," for she has already received life. "What is the reason there is no left here?" He intended to resolve the matter of the left and Hod mentioned; and he said "what is the reason," etc. And the matter is that in the left there are three aspects. One aspect, the nourishment of the fire of Gehinnom, and it is the black color. Second, the aspect of judgment, the blue [tekhelet] color. Third, the red color, and it is the judgment tipped to the pan of Chesed. And he said: if the reason that the left is not mentioned in the Grace after Meals were because of fear of judgment, it would be fitting not to mention it at all, neither included in the right nor otherwise. But the reason is only because of fear of the husks, as he goes on to explain; and if so, even if the aspect of judgment that is unified with Chesed is mentioned, it does not matter to us, for they have no hold in it at all, and there is no fear in it.

And further he intended, in saying "for the Other Side has no portion in the food of Israel," to indicate that the whole principal of food is from the side of Gevurah, as in the matter our Sages, of blessed memory, said, "A man's food is hard," hinting at judgment, and that from it it flows; and therefore it is fitting to mention it. But so that we do not come to harm, how do we mention it? When it is included in the right, as we explained.

And behold, the passage has been explained with a fine explanation, and there is no demolition from within it of what is expounded in this Gate at all. For Netzach, after David came, was always included in the right. And so it is evident from the wording of the Tikkunim that we copied in chapter 1, which said "Hod was bound to Gevurah and Netzach to Chesed"; and the word "was bound" indicates that it was bound afterwards because of a deed that was done, which was not so beforehand. And so he was further precise in the Tikkunim elsewhere (Tikkun 30, folio 72a), and these are its words: "He is the right thigh, the priest, of whom it is said, 'pleasures in Your right hand forever'; and just as Netzach was bound to the right, so Hod was bound to the left." Thus far its words.

And behold, this points with a finger to the matter. And he said that we should not err in saying that Netzach was in the right and Hod stood in its place; but just as this was bound to the right, this was bound to the left; and by this the touching and the blemish are found. And the judgment flows to Hod; and this is what is intended in some places, that "and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was strained" is Hod. And a proof for this is from the verse (Dan. 10:8), "and my splendor [hodi] was turned" [into corruption], etc., that is, literally turned: for it was to the right and was turned to the left.
The Eighteenth Gate: The Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon.

What is intended in this Gate is the explanation of the matter of Tiferet and Malkhut, which are hinted at in the sun and the moon, and the matter of the moon and its diminishment, according to what is found in the words of Rashbi and the other commentators.
Chapter One:

Since we have seen that this passage is the central point of the inquiry according to the view of Rashbi and the other commentators, we have seen fit to copy it here, for it is the established foundation of this Gate in the business of its explanation. And these are its words, in tractate Chullin (folio 60b): "Rabbi Shimon ben Pazzi pointed out a contradiction: It is written (Gen. 1:16), 'And God made the two great luminaries,' and it is written, 'the great luminary and the small luminary.' The moon said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, is it possible for two kings to use one crown? He said to her: Go and diminish yourself. She said before Him: Master of the world, because I said a proper thing before You, shall I diminish myself? He said to her: Go and rule by day and by night. She said to Him: What is the greatness? A lamp at noon, what use is it? He said to her: Go, let Israel count days and years by you. She said to Him: The day too: it is impossible that they not count the seasons by it, as it is written (Gen. 1:14), 'and let them be for signs and for seasons, and for days and years.' He said to her: Go, let the righteous be called by your name: Jacob the small, Samuel the small, David the small. He saw that her mind was not settled. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Bring an atonement for Me for My having diminished the moon. And this is what Resh Lakish said: Why is the goat of the New Moon different, that 'to the Lord' is said of it (Num. 28:15)? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let this goat be an atonement for My having diminished the moon." Thus far its words.

And in the explanation of this passage we found the author of the book Me'irat Einayim, in his introduction; and these are his words: "Know that Teshuvah [which is Binah] is the King of kings of kings. 'The kings of the everlasting arms' are the double-faced kings, who are the two kings who serve and use one crown; for you already know that the double-faced were equal, this light like that light. And when she accused, that two kings should not use one crown, she was seeking for herself, and her light was diminished, so that she became the speculum that does not shine. For Teshuvah, which is the Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: 'Go and diminish yourself.' And the Holy One, blessed be He, said (which is Tiferet, for it too is called the Holy One, blessed be He): 'Bring an atonement for Me [alai],' to Teshuvah, which is over me [alai]: 'for My having diminished the moon,' that is to say, because of me she was diminished, for through me Teshuvah said to the Diadem, 'Go and diminish yourself.' And perhaps the intent of this offering, like the other offerings, is to bring her near to Tiferet, so that she may be blessed for us. And the reason for a goat, which is the left side, and not a lamb, which is from the side of compassion, is perhaps because her principal receiving is from there, and the matter was by way of accusation, and from there it comes. And the word alai our teacher Mordechai Ashkenazi explained in this way: 'Bring an atonement for Me' is like 'before Me': that the Holy One, blessed be He, says to Israel: It is upon you to bring an atonement for your souls before Me, for My having diminished the moon (a figure for the withdrawal of the light of the Diadem). And because of this the accuser, who is the evil inclination, the darkness in you, was strengthened, and you did not merit that first light, pure and bright; for had you merited it, you would be like gods, children of the Most High. And I found written in the words of the Kabbalists that Teshuvah said 'Bring an atonement' to the one who is over me. But its explanation is the language of the first debt and loan; and if so, his saying 'for My having diminished' is not difficult, for he is the one who says 'Go and diminish yourself.' And in the Kabbalah of Sforta: Know that they were double-faced, and since they acted equally, He feared, since her dominion was equal, lest the world err and say that there are two authorities, God forbid. Thus far. But according to the view of the sage, it is possible to say double-faced from the side that the power of the moon was included in the sun; and also that that power of the moon, twinned at that time in the sun, was not mixed in the power of the sun but was recognizable; as if you were to say, by way of illustration, that milk and wine were in one vessel, and the wine is recognizable by itself, except that they touch one another. And in any case it is possible to say that the power of the moon twinned in the sun at that time was also performing the action of compassion, as appears from the words of Sforta. For how is it possible to say that one attribute performs compassion and judgment as one? Rather, certainly the sun was acting in compassion, and the moon was assisting it in the action of compassion; and therefore the moon said: Is it possible for two kings to use one crown, and to receive equally from one place, and that both of them perform only one action? For what need is there for the moon, since the sun, which is one king, suffices for this action, since the whole action is of one kind; it will not change because it is twinned with the moon.
