And He said to her, 'Go and diminish yourself': this is the diminishment; for at first she was acting and assisting the attribute of compassion, and now she was diminished from the attribute of compassion and became judgment. And this is what he said: 'Bring an atonement for Me for My having diminished the moon': know that you need to bring an atonement to the one who is over me, for the diminishment of the moon, which was diminished from compassion to judgment; and because of that diminishment, by which she returned to judgment, you need atonement, so that she may always be included, the effluence of compassion flowing upon her." Thus far its words.

And behold, from within his words he appears to waver between the two opinions: whether we say that the moon was literally included in the sun and both of them were one power (and we found that Rabbi Bachya, on Gen. 38:30, inclines somewhat to this, according to what he explained concerning the matter of Perez and Zerah); or whether we say that there were two twinned powers, but each one by itself, like the wine and the milk in one vessel, as he goes on to explain.

And behold, these two opinions give us no satisfaction. First, if we say that she was literally included, we would ask: in what were the ten sefirot divided? Behold, they were nine, for Tiferet and Malkhut are as one, unified, whether in their power or in their action. And if we answer that it was because it was included of the power of maleness and the power of femaleness, as our teacher Bachya explained, this does not suffice, for in the end it was one power and one action. And even if it is included of two powers, so too all the sefirot are included of many kinds of powers, according to their aspects and their manifestation, as explained in the preceding gates; and nevertheless we relate to one sefirah each and every power included in all its generalities and particulars. And likewise these: although this power includes male and female, in the end they were one light and one power, and so the sefirot would be nine and not ten, contrary to the tradition. And further, since their matter was a power of equal, unitary light, how then did the verse say "the two great luminaries," which shows that they were two luminaries, except that they were great, that is, equal? And in our opinion this is not difficult for our teacher Bachya, if we say that his intent was not that they were one power except when they were above, concealed, before their emanation to the place fitting for them, that is, on the fourth day, where the place of the moon and the sun is; but when they were emanated to their place they were two. And it is already possible to infer so from within his wording in Parashat Vayeshev, and these are his words: "It is known that the name Elohim mentioned in Bereshit is the King of the world, and it is Teshuvah," etc. "And the verse said, 'And God said, Let there be light, and there was light,' to explain that from the power of the Kingship of Heaven, which is called Elohim, these two lights were emanated; and therefore it said 'and there was light' and did not say 'and it was so,' as in the rest of the work of creation. And you should understand that the intent is not that they were literally two lights; only there were two powers in it, the one a power of maleness and the second a power of femaleness; but the first light was only one. And it is one, including the power of maleness and the power of femaleness; and from this light the sun and the moon were emanated on the fourth day, as I explained there in the order of Bereshit; and the power of maleness was emanated upon the sun and the power of femaleness upon the moon." Thus far its words.

And according to the truth there is no room to object to our teacher Bachya; for it is possible that his intent is that when they were above, in Binah, they were one light and one power, as it is written, "Let there be light, and there was light," which taught that they are one light; but when they were emanated to their place they were two, each one by itself, the moon by itself and the sun by itself, as he said, "and from this light the sun and the moon were emanated on the fourth day, and the power was emanated," etc. But according to the view of the author of the book Me'irat Einayim, who holds that it is possible for there to be one power and action, it is difficult for us: in what were they distinguished so as to be two sefirot? For by way of cause and effect it is impossible: for this is the distinction of the other sefirot, and these two were unified in one light and one power. And since they have no distinction in cause and effect, in what are they distinguished, so as to be reckoned and rise to the count of two sefirot? For in its including two powers there is no proof, for the whole substance of the inclusion is certainly by way of cause and effect; and moreover, this is no distinction according to his explanation, as we explained above. And also to say that both of them were recognizable, each one by itself: the matter of their action is difficult, in her saying "it is impossible for two kings to use one crown": what does she say? For there were two crowns, each one by itself. And this was already difficult for the author of the book Me'irat Einayim according to the view of Sforta, and he intended to strain and settle the matter, and he did not succeed.

And further we saw that the company of the sages that the author of the book Me'irat Einayim brought all said that the matter of the double-faced and the two great luminaries is all one matter; and that the Holy One, blessed be He, sawed her apart, and likewise the diminishment of the moon, is all one matter. And this is the opposite of reason; for the matter of the double-faced, like Adam and Eve, was a lowering and a lack, and the union was not as is fitting; so that Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar (perhaps he means Bereshit, folio 35a; and see Zohar Pekudei 258b) had to give a reason for the thing: because the upper one was coupled from behind, and was not set right face to face until it was set right in the lower coupling, when the Holy One, blessed be He, sawed Eve apart. And behold, in the lower coupling it was for good, and in the upper coupling for bad, God forbid; this is certainly a difficulty. And besides this, it is difficult for me concerning them: for the double-faced expounded in the Gemara (Berakhot 61a) is that they were literally two bodies, except that they were joined at their backs until the Holy One, blessed be He, sawed them apart; and if so, how would it come up in their minds to say that they were one light? For behold, the language "double-faced" is the opposite, as we explained. And they wished to say that they were one light, so that duality would not be judged in it; and such is not the matter of the double-faced. And a difficulty already follows from this for the view of our teacher Bachya. This is what is difficult for us in the view of the rabbis, besides what is difficult for us in the matter of the inquiry itself, as we shall explain in explaining it. And apart from all this, several passages opposed to this passage at the beginning of our chapter are difficult for us, as we shall explain:

We have seen fit in this chapter to bring two passages from the Zohar that disagree with one another in the inquiry, and further disagree with the passage of the Gemara mentioned. The first passage is on the Song of Songs, from the Zohar (Zohar Chadash, folio 84b), and these are its words: "'And God created the two great luminaries,' etc. At first there were two lights [equal, this opposite this, as the Companions have established; and we have established that they were two lights in one secret], joined as one, and they were in one weighing, so that both of them were called 'great,' as we have established. Not that the moon was at first great and supernal; but at every time that the moon stands with the sun in one secret, because of him she is called with him 'great': the tail of a lion is a lion and is called lion. The moon said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Is it possible for one king to use two crowns together? Rather, this by itself and that by itself. He said to her: I see in you that your desire is to be a head to foxes; go and diminish yourself; for although you will be a head to them, you have diminution from what you were. And this is what the moon said (Song 1:7): 'Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you pasture': how is it possible for You to conduct the world with two crowns together? 'Where do you make [your flock] lie down at noon': for the moon is not worthy to give light, and it is impossible for You to conduct with two crowns together, with the sun and with the moon; for what light does the moon have at noon? Therefore it is impossible for You to use two crowns together. 'For why should I be as one who veils herself': how shall I be wrapped at noon, when the light and the strength of the sun go on growing strong? Behold, I am wrapped in shame before Him, and I cannot serve before You; and You, how can You conduct and use two crowns together? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: Behold, I know you: go and diminish yourself. 'If you do not know, O fairest among women' (Song 1:8): for you said before Me that it is impossible for Me to conduct the world with two crowns together: go and diminish yourself, and be a head to foxes. 'Go forth in the footsteps of the flock': go out and be head to all those multitudes and small hosts below, and pasture them, and conduct them, and be king of all the lower ones, and conduct each one as is fitting for him, and be ruler in the night. Certainly, go out and diminish yourself; and so it is fitting for you." Thus far its words.

And there is room to scrutinize this passage. First: they said "equal," etc., "so that both of them were called great." For what is the equality in the matter of the name alone? And behold, this greatness and honor is not so much that because of this alone it would be said "Go and diminish yourself"; and what is the diminishment in the absence of the name? Second: granted, if we say that they were literally equal, we can say that the moon's intent was that the sun should descend from its place and she remain in her place, as explained on the verse (Judg. 5:31), "But let those who love Him be as the sun when it goes forth in its might"; except that the judgment turned and she descended from her place of rank; and at this she complained, and was not appeased until He said "Bring an atonement for Me," etc. But according to what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in this passage, that the sun was always greater and greater, if so, certainly the moon's intent was not that the sun, which was greater, should descend and she remain great; but certainly her intent was that she descend [to be a head to foxes]. And if so, how did she say "because I said before You," etc.? And likewise "Bring an atonement for Me," etc.: why was she complaining, for this was her intent from before? Third: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained "it is impossible for one king to use two crowns," as it appears that she was stammering about "is the hand of the Lord too short to save?" (Isa. 59:1); and in the passage of the Gemara mentioned, "is it possible for two kings," etc., implies that she was stammering about the shortness of ability of the two kings, who are the sun and the moon, that they would not have the power to use one crown, which is the power above them. And although all rises to one place, nevertheless the matter is not one. And one cannot say that Rashbi disagrees with the Gemara, for this is forced, since this passage is written in the Gemara anonymously.

And further, Rashbi explains in many places the matter of "Bring an atonement for Me," as we shall explain. Fourth: from within these two passages it appears that the sun and the moon are two kings, or two crowns; and the one king, or the one crown, is the upper power, which it is impossible to use through them, or [for them] to be used through it; and the one who complained was the moon, who is one of the two crowns or of the two kings, according to the division of the explanations. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, folio 247b) Rashbi explained a third explanation that disagrees with both of them; and these are his words: "'And on your new moons [rashei chodsheikhem, the heads of your months]' (Num. 28:11). And how many heads does the moon have? But these are two points, like this: [ ]; the lower point is the moon. Her two heads are two points, which are a segol over her. At first she is a crown over two kings, like this:

and it was a segolta. And after she said 'it is impossible for two kings to use one crown,' the Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: Go and diminish yourself; and she descended to the feet of the two kings, like this:

and this is segol: what was segolta turned into segol. And the secret of the matter: corresponding to the two points, which are two kings, it hints 'two young bulls'; and corresponding to the point, a diadem over their heads, he said 'and one ram,' like one crown. After she said 'it is impossible for two kings to use one crown,' she diminished herself; so too 'and one goat of the goats for a sin offering' (Num. 28:15): the ram of Isaac turned into a goat; it was turned from compassion to judgment and was diminished. And therefore 'one goat of the goats for a sin offering,' and he did not say 'for a burnt offering,' to be a crown. And whence do we know that there is descent in the sin offering? This is what is written (Lev. 9:22), 'and he came down from offering the sin offering.' And why did he join the burnt offering with the sin offering in the descent? But to teach that the burnt offering was at first the attribute of compassion, and afterwards it turned to judgment in descent and was called sin offering; and all is one. And therefore 'Bring an atonement for Me [alai]': over me [alai] the moon was a crown, certainly, like this: וֹ; and afterwards she was diminished and descended to his feet, like this: וּ (in our version it is 'like this:

' etc., 'like this:

'). And at that time, 'Bring an atonement for Me,' it is said of her, 'she is the burnt offering [ha-olah]' (Lev. 6:2): she rose from his feet, of which it is said (Isa. 66:1), 'and the earth is My footstool,' to say of her, 'the heavens are My throne.' And this is the secret of 'a righteous one rules, the fear of God' (2 Sam. 23:3), who turns judgment to compassion. And the secret of the matter: 'the stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner' (Ps. 118:22), like this: הו"הי יהו"ה." Thus far its words.

And behold, from within it it is explicitly explained that Rashbi's intent in the matter of "it is impossible for two kings" is: it is impossible for Netzach and Hod, which are the heads of the moon, as we have said, to use Malkhut, which is a crown over them. And this explanation certainly disagrees [for according to his explanation] she has no accusation against the sun; and this is forced. And our Sages, of blessed memory [in Chullin and in Zohar Chadash], explained that the moon made her accusation against the sun. And before we explain the settling of these three passages, we must explain the emanation of these two attributes from their beginning, whose matter was not explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, because we designated it for this gate:

What is intended in this chapter is to explain the matter of the emanation of Tiferet and Malkhut from beginning to end. And the matter is that when it arose in His primordial will, may He be exalted, to emanate His pure and holy Emanation, there was a cause from Him to bring the things into being in an order in which they are not now in their manifestation. For the intent of the Emanation was that through it His greatness would be revealed, and the children of the world, which perishes, comes to be, and passes away, could be conducted through it; and further, for another reason. And this [without it] is impossible, for several reasons: whether because of the great concealment of His holiness, or because of the shortness of the apprehension of the created entities and their being finite, as explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation. And according to this, it turns out that the principal of the arising of the will was Malkhut, which conducts the world.

And behold, the greatness of our Former is the opposite of the thought of human beings, who are vanity and whose thoughts are breath. For it is not as when a man thinks of some thing, and the thing does not come to be until he toils over its existence in deed, and then it becomes a revealed being, as explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot, chapter 3. Not so our Creator, blessed be He: His thoughts are very, very deep and mighty; and when He thought of the beings, behold, the beings, before they came into being, acquired a manifestation choicer and superior to the manifestation of the deed. And it has already been explained that Tiferet and Malkhut are the principal of the Emanation, and all is included in them; as is known that the letters Vav-Heh are the totality of the Emanation from Binah downward, and they are the principal of the governance, and they are the order of time: for time comes to be through the circuit, which is Vav, six extremities, and Malkhut is Heh; the two of them are the attribute of day and the attribute of night. And therefore in the Thought (that is, Chokhmah) that preceded the Emanation were Tiferet and Malkhut. And because Malkhut is a more revealed being, her revealing came to be before Tiferet, and Tiferet was concealed; because Malkhut is a palace to it, and she reveals the glory of the King, and she is the revealed mirror in which Tiferet is revealed. And therefore the being first revealed in the Thought, which is Chokhmah, was Tiferet and Malkhut; and this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (in Bereshit Rabbah, section 3, on "And there was evening and there was morning"): "This teaches that there was an order of times before this." And the order of times is Tiferet and Malkhut; and they were before Him in the secret of the incising, when He was incising the world. And because no being is grasped in Chokhmah, because it is the beginning of being Something, as we explained in the gate mentioned, therefore it was necessary to emanate Binah, and from her the beings, which are Tiferet and Malkhut, would be emanated. And with this thing we will understand the matter of "they were created double-faced": that is to say, in Chokhmah, which is Yod. And the Yod: its permutation is the Yod that is in Chokhmah, and its filling is Vav-Dalet; because the Vav, which is Tiferet, and the Dalet, which is Malkhut, were the filling of Chokhmah, and she was pregnant with them like a pregnant woman; and this is the manifestation of the Yod of Malkhut and the manifestation of the Da'at of Tiferet. And for the reason that Tiferet is over Malkhut, Malkhut was in the aspect of Chokhmah itself, and Da'at, which is Tiferet, in the aspect of the Supernal Keter; for it was in the aspect of Chokhmah near to its source, the aspect of Chokhmah that cleaves to Keter. And when the will arose to reveal more, and He saw that the beings are not revealed through Chokhmah, He emanated Binah and placed Da'at within her; and the emanation of Da'at preceded Malkhut, because the cause of the Emanation was the concealment: for because the beings were concealed, they were emanated. Therefore the concealed Tiferet came first, to be revealed in Binah; and therefore the creation of Adam came before, in the parable, that of Eve his wife; and then the double-faced were divided, and Tiferet went out alone. And there is no earlier and later in this matter, for all is in one instant; and all is a parable for priority of rank, and the concealment of the manifestation and their multiplicity, not priority of time, God forbid, for divinity is not under time; and all this is a parable to let the ear hear, as we explained in the preceding gates. And when Tiferet was emanated in Binah, the Holy One, blessed be He, emanated Malkhut from her place that is in Chokhmah, and took her from Adam, which is חכמ"ה [Chokhmah]: אד"ם [Adam] is מ"ה [Mah, 45], the four-letter name filled as יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א, which amounts to Mah. And then she was in the aspect of a rib, from the side of a simple Yod, and she was built through Binah. And this is (Gen. 2:22), "And the Lord God built the rib that He took," etc.; and this name hints at Binah, as is known. "And He brought her to the man": this is Tiferet, in its [particular and revealed] place. And there He unified them with the union of husband and wife, face to face, in a complete union, as we hope it will be speedily in our days, as it is written (Isa. 30:26), "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun." And there the male was above the female, and the female served beneath him, as we shall explain further. And from there she was driven away and descended to be His footstool, until His anger turns and He comforts us. And now, according to this, Malkhut turns out to precede Tiferet, and Tiferet to precede Malkhut. For in Chokhmah, in its first manifestation, Tiferet was very concealed, so that it was not recognizable at all; and the revealing of Malkhut preceded it, because she is the principal of the governance of the world, and therefore her revealing came first. And Tiferet was concealed above, near to Keter, because of its being more concealed than Malkhut, as we explained; therefore its revealing was not made manifest until its revealed place. And in its revealed place the emanation of Tiferet came first, for it went out first, for it was the cause of the revealing, as we explained. And by this the words of the House of Hillel and the House of Shammai in Chagigah (folio 12a) are right: the House of Shammai say the heavens were created first, and the House of Hillel say the earth was created first, and the Sages say heaven and earth were created as one. For all is one, and the words of all of them are true, and they are the words of the living God. For in Chokhmah the revealing of Malkhut came first: behold, the earth was created first; and in their emanation [in Binah] Tiferet came first: behold, the heavens were created first; and in truth they were created as one [as the words of the Sages], except that this was revealed before that. And with this preliminary a passage in Sefer ha-Bahir will be explained, and these are its words: "Rabbi Rechumai said: The light preceded the world, which 'clouds and thick darkness are round about Him' (Ps. 97:2), as it is said, 'And God said, Let there be light, and there was light.' They said to him: Before the forming of your son, you make a diadem? He said to them: Yes. A parable: to what is the matter like? To a king who craved a son, and he found a fine diadem, and praised it and lauded it, and said: Keep this for my son, for his head, for it befits him. They said to him: Does he know that his son is fit for it? He said to them: Be silent; so it arose in thought, and it is known, as it is said, 'and devisers of devices.'" Thus far its words.

And although at first glance his words are hard to understand, with this our preliminary it will be easy and explained. And this is its explanation. Rabbi Rechumai says that "the light" [ha-orah], which is Malkhut, as explained in the Gate From Below to Above, chapter 4, in the explanation of a passage of Sefer ha-Bahir; see there. And he called her orah and not or, to hint at the light of Malkhut, which is called or-Heh [the light of Heh]. And he proved the matter from the verse "Let there be light," etc.: for the verse told us of the manifestation of the light before the manifestation of the firmament; for this light is in Malkhut, and the firmament in Tiferet, and the light precedes the firmament. And to this he intended in saying "the light," which is Malkhut, "preceded the world [olam]," which "clouds and thick darkness are round about Him," which is Tiferet. And the explanation: it is known that the whole circuit is called olam; and for this reason Binah is called olam, for in her is the inclusion of the circuit, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles; and the principal of the circuit is Tiferet, including six extremities, which are the days of the circuit. And for this he said that "the light preceded the world." And so that we should not err and say that the intent is that her emanation in Thought was before its emanation in the secret of Da'at (for this is not so, as we explained), for this he said "which clouds and thick darkness are round about Him": explanation: [this refers] to the revealed manifestation of Tiferet, which is between Chesed and Gevurah, which are cloud and thick darkness; and they are the aspects that Tiferet has with Chesed and Gevurah, and they are a garment in which Tiferet is clothed. And the disciples of Rabbi Rechumai, because a true tradition was fixed in their hearts that the emanation of Tiferet precedes Malkhut, objected with the force of figurative speech: how is it possible that Malkhut precede Tiferet? For Malkhut is a vessel to Tiferet, and Tiferet is master and ruler over her; and although she is sometimes exalted over it, at the least she will be a diadem on its head; and if so, in the end they asked him: Does a man make a diadem for his son before the forming of the son? And this is what they asked: "Before the forming of your son, you make a diadem for him?" And Rabbi Rechumai, because the tradition of the disciples is correct and true, that the emanation of Tiferet precedes the emanation of Malkhut, did not protest against them; but he answered them according to their way with a fitting and acceptable parable: "to a king who craved a son." And he was precise in using the language of "craved"; for craving is subtler than the thought of action; and likewise the manifestation of Tiferet is subtler and more concealed than the thought of action, and it is in the secret of Da'at, as we explained. "And he found a fine diadem": for the diadem is more revealed; and this is the reason for "and he found," for the language of finding can already properly be said of it somewhat. And he said "Keep this for my son": the intent is the language of "keeping," that it will still be concealed and kept in its concealed manifestation, which is called Yod, the diadem of Tiferet, "for his head, for it befits him"; which is not found in Tiferet, that its manifestation should be revealed below as much as Malkhut, for the reason of its still being concealed. And the modest disciples, because it was still difficult for them, for they had not received the concealed manifestation of Tiferet that is above the diadem, asked as those in doubt about the matter, so that he would explain much to them; and they said to him, "Does he know that his son is fit for it?" And they intended to ask as those in doubt about the tradition of the concealed Da'at. And the delightful master answered: "Be silent; so it arose in thought." And the intent is that it was already in thought, in the secret of Da'at; and this is "and it is known" [ve-noda], the language of da'at. And the intent is that the concealed manifestation of Tiferet arose in thought and was formed in the secret of Da'at; and this is ve-noda. "As it is said, 'and devisers of devices'": some read "and devising devices." And the intent, according to all the explanations, is to prove that Keter too is called thought, although at first glance we have thought only in Chokhmah. And he proved that there is thought in Keter from his saying "devices" [machashavot, thoughts], two: thought within thought. And therefore Tiferet was in the upper thought, as we explained above. And after we have explained in this chapter the matter of the emanation of Malkhut from the beginning of the Emanation to the end, we come to explain that the diminishment is not the matter of the sawing apart of Eve from Adam, as the commentators imagined:

In this chapter we will explain that the sawing apart of Eve from Adam is not the matter of the diminishment; for the sawing apart was for good, for the coupling and for begetting, which is not so of the diminishment. And there is no room to ask: since this is so, how was there begetting before the sawing apart, or why were they created thus, so that they would need the sawing apart? For this matter is explained in the Zohar, and we copied it in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 18. And perhaps the inquirer will imagine [a difficulty] against this from the words of Rashbi in parashat Acharei (77b), and these are its words: "We have learned: the upper Heh conceived in love, in affection, for the Yod never parts from her. She conceived and brought forth Vav; afterwards it stood before her and she nursed it. And this Vav, when it went forth, its mate went forth with it. Chesed came, roused beside it, and separated them; and trunks went forth from below to above, and branches spread out and multiplied, and the lower Heh was made. And she grew with her branches higher and higher, until she coupled with the upper tree, and Vav was joined with Heh. Who caused them? It is Chesed; it is certainly Chesed that joined them as one. Yod with the upper Heh: their joining does not depend on Chesed; rather their joining and their affection depend on mazal, that they never part. Yod is bound to Heh, Heh is bound to Vav, Vav is bound to Heh, and Heh is bound to all, and all is one bond and one thing. They never part from one another." Thus far its words.

At first glance it implies that Tiferet went out double-faced and was divided below in its place, and could not beget except through division, that is, the diminishment of the moon. And it turns out that this passage disputes all that has been explained, in several matters. First, it appears that after it went out, the division and the sawing of the rib came afterward, in saying "Vav, when it went forth," etc.; it appears that they were emanated and afterward sawn apart.

Further, we explained above that the division of Tiferet from Malkhut was through Binah, and here it appears that it was through Chesed. Further, it appears that this is the diminishment, in saying "and the lower Heh was made," which means the diminishment, that they lowered her; and so it is implied by the language of the passage. Therefore it seems right to me to explain this passage; and before we enter into its explanation, we will raise some remarks on it, in such a way that through them the intent of the passage will be understood. And what there is to remark: First, their saying "She conceived and brought forth Vav; afterwards it stood," etc.: what is "afterwards," and what is "brought forth," for all is one? "Brought forth" and "afterwards it stood": where did she bring it forth, that it was needed afterwards to stand it up? Second, their saying "Chesed came," etc., "and separated them": could it enter the mind that the diminishment was done by Chesed? But on the side of the diminishment croup takes hold of infants, as we say in the Zohar, parashat Terumah (folio 167), and these are its words: "Once the accuser went out, then it is written, 'Let there be lights' [me'orot], lacking Vav; and croup was drawn upon infants, and the light of the moon was lacking." Thus far its words.

Behold, it is explicitly implied that the moon was diminished on the side of the accuser. Further, who can say that the moon was diminished by Chesed? For it is understood from there that her diminishment was not done for her good, as she said, "Because I said before You a proper thing," and the matter of "Bring atonement for Me," and all that the Rabbis said there, as we explained in chapter 1.

Further, if so, that the union and coupling of the moon is found only through the diminishment of the moon, then in the future, when the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, how is it possible? For there will be no union and coupling. Third, what he said, "Yod with the upper Heh does not depend," etc.: what is it doing here, since we are not dealing with this?

Further, he said at the beginning of the teaching, "in love, in affection, that does not part," etc.; and why are both of them needed here? And now we will come to set right the passage from its root. We have already explained above that "the Lord God" is Binah, and the rib Malkhut, and the man Chokhmah. And so Rashbi explained (in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 12, folio 27a) on the verse "And the Lord God built the rib that He took from the man": "This is Chokhmah. 'And brought her to the man': this is the middle pillar, the grade of Moses. And this rib is certainly the bride of Moses." Thus far its words.

And it is known that "the Lord God" is Binah, as is known. And after this matter has been explained, it is fitting to know further that there is no building except through Chesed, as it is said (Ps. 89:3), "For I said, The world shall be built by Chesed"; and every building depends on it. And now it is necessitated that the building of the rib was through Chesed. Further, it is fitting to know that Binah, hinted at in the form of the first Heh in the Name, is not literally in the form of Heh; rather her principal form is Yod, as explained in the Gate of Manifestations; and the form of Heh that hints at her is a hint of the emanated ones that come from her. And the explanation of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is that the Vav within the Heh is the form of the emanated Tiferet. And now, according to this, it is difficult: just as the form of Vav, which is Tiferet, was formed within her, why was the form of Malkhut not formed within her, so that there would be within her Vav-Dalet, both of them: Dalet, that is, the form of Malkhut in the manifestation of the rib, and Vav, that is, Tiferet? Rather, what must you say? That the two of them were emanated at once. (And so it is proven there: Adam and Eve were double-faced after the creation. And if you say that they were double-faced in Chokhmah: there is no revealed being there, as Adam and Eve were when they were double-faced after their creation.) And Rashbi, peace be upon him, in our teaching explained this matter with a correct compromise, and it is this: that Chokhmah, at the time of the emanation of these, out of its union and its concealment within Binah, [Chokhmah and Binah] were united in love, in such a way that the two of them were one in a complete union. And this is what he said, "We have learned: she conceived," etc.: for they did not part, and their union was in the strength of love, such that there is no separation between them, God forbid.
And the matter of "that do not part" we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 14. And the reason that he called Binah here "the upper Heh" is that it hints at her pregnancy.

And the matter of "and brought forth Vav" is not literally the Vav of the Name; rather the intent is the Vav within the Heh itself, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the passage "Heh was Dalet, once she was joined," etc., which we copied in the Gate of Names, chapters 11 and 13; see there. And what he said, "and brought forth Vav," is the conceiving in the pregnancy, in which she brought out from Chokhmah and emanated within herself the Vav, that is, Tiferet and Malkhut together; but the female is not mentioned, because she was a rib. And what he said, "afterwards it stood," etc.: explanation: after she brought forth this son from within her, as we explained, and the rib was taken from it there, as we shall explain afterward. "It stood before her": explanation: she emanated it in the place particular to it, that is, its emanation below, in the Vav of the Name itself. And after he completed the emanation of Tiferet entirely, in all its manifestations, he returned to explain the difference between Tiferet and Malkhut in the emanation, and said, "when it went forth, its mate," etc., that is, the pregnancy and its conceiving, that is, "and brought forth Vav," which he said above, as we explained. And in that revealing within Binah, the two of them were included together in the secret of double-faced; and behold, in the Heh there is the form of ד"ו [Dalet-Vav] after its kind, except that they were still double-faced there. And this is one of the explanations of the Heh of Binah. "Chesed came," etc.: the matter is as we explained, that Binah and Chokhmah were united, and Chokhmah within Binah, and she is it, all is one. If so, it is already settled that they were still double-faced within Binah, and that the rib was taken from Adam, that is, Chokhmah. And with this the name Yah in Chokhmah will be understood: that Yod is Chokhmah in conjunction with Binah, which is Heh, and its form is ד"ו, that is, double-faced in Chokhmah and Binah. And with this it will now be settled that Binah took the rib, which is Malkhut alone, from Chokhmah, and took it also from Tiferet: for while the two of them were together within Binah, and Chokhmah still within her, the taking happened, in such a way that Tiferet alone was emanated below, and the rib remained in the aspect of Yod above, being progressively built. And because Chesed is the opening of Binah, and this separation and division was there, "for a door of hope" (Hos. 2:17), behold, they were divided through Chesed. And because all building is through Chesed, as we explained, behold, her building, that is, the form of He, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations, was through Chesed. And this is what Rashbi said in our teaching: "Chesed came," etc., "and separated them." And now all is resolved, and the language of the Tikkunim is set right, that the taking was from Chokhmah. And it is resolved that they were double-faced in their creation, that is, after the pregnancy. And it is resolved why the two of them did not remain in Binah as divided forms. And the matter of double-faced in Binah is resolved as well. And the matter of the building through Chesed is resolved. And above all, a great difficulty is resolved, which is difficult in what he said in the Tikkunim (that the man from whom she was taken is the very one to whom she was brought). And with this it is settled that Adam himself was there at the time of her taking within Binah: when Binah emanated Tiferet, then she took the rib from Chokhmah; it turns out that her taking from Chokhmah and her taking from Tiferet were at once. And let us return to the matter of the passage: "And trunks went forth from below to above": explanation: for before, they were ד"ו [double-faced, Dalet before Vav], that is, Malkhut above Tiferet; and therefore they did not beget. And the reason they were there thus has already been explained above: because Tiferet preceded Malkhut in emanation, and Malkhut remained above it. And this is also their form, as with a seal: for in Keter they were ו"ד [Vav-Dalet], Tiferet above, and this is in the aspect of Keter, and Malkhut in Chokhmah; and at the time of the revealing of Tiferet they became ד"ו [Dalet-Vav], like the reversed impression of a seal. And this is Vav-Dalet in Chokhmah, for Chokhmah is Yod and its filling is Vav-Dalet; and in Binah Dalet-Vav, that is, the Heh: Dalet before the Vav.

And behold, they were divided and separated through Binah; and in order to unite her with her husband, Malkhut was built in the form of Heh; for through this the union comes about, when she is adorned and spreads her branches and her adornments upward, so that He will remember the everlasting covenant and her husband will unite with her, which it was not possible for him to do until now. And the reason they were not divided until they went out below Binah is that the principal purpose of their union is to perform the action of bringing into being; for through the two of them the beings are revealed with an essential revealing. And because there is no essential being until below Binah, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, therefore they were in a state in which they had no union or coupling until they came to the place where the coupling is needed, through which the actions go forth into revealed beings, as we explained in the gate mentioned. And this is what he said in our teaching, "and the lower Heh was made": explanation: through Chesed they were separated and she was built [in the form of Heh], as he said, "and branches spread out," etc.; for through this the Heh was made below Tiferet, that is, the lower Heh. "And she grew," etc.: that is, the branches rising upward, which arouse the male with their beauty to unite. "And Vav was joined with Heh": explanation: in the union in which they united face to face they were united; that is, before the diminishment, for then she was in union with her husband always. "Who caused them," etc.: explanation: he wanted to prove that their separation from one another, and her building, were through Chesed, which is somewhat forced. For this he said: who caused them to unite? It is Chesed. Although the true unifier is only Yesod, nevertheless the principal cause was Chesed. And the proof of this is their saying, "Children, life and sustenance do not depend on merit but on mazal." And its explanation: although all the beings come through Tiferet and Malkhut, who unite through merit, that is, Chesed, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, nevertheless children, life and sustenance depend on mazal, which is Da'at rising into Keter, which unites Chokhmah and Binah: on it depend children, life and sustenance; for through the union and coupling of Chokhmah and Binah the three of them are bestowed. And this is what he said: Yod with the upper Heh: their joining does not depend on Chesed, as does the union of Tiferet and Malkhut; rather their union depends on Keter, and the matter is through Da'at, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter.

And behold, in a concealed way he explained the saying "children, life and sustenance," etc.; for it is the principal proof: for since we say "not on merit," that is, Chesed, it appears that the other things bestowed from the union of Tiferet and Malkhut come through Chesed. Behold a proof that the cause of their union was through Chesed, as we explained. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, brought all this around in order to settle the explanation of (Lev. 20:17), "And if a man shall take his sister," etc., "it is chesed": Chesed certainly; for the union of brother and sister is through Chesed. "Their joining," etc.: the intent is to explain that this is through Chesed, because the union below is at intervals; and it is at intervals for this reason: for when Chesed is present there is union, and when it withdraws there is no union. But the upper union is constant, through the mazal that flows [nozel] forever and does not cease; and their union is Yod in Heh, Chokhmah in Binah; and Binah, which is Heh, in Vav, which is Tiferet; and the Vav in the Heh, which is Malkhut; and Malkhut unites with all of them, for in her is the manifestation of Chokhmah in the rib, which is the Yod, and the manifestation of Binah in the Heh; and as for Tiferet, there is no need to explain. And this length was needed for the matter of the forbidden unions expounded there [text: מעל"ד, unclear], for whoever separates, his punishment is great; and we have not copied it because it is not relevant to our subject.

And behold, this passage has been finely explained. And from it we have learned the order of the emanation of Tiferet and Malkhut from the head of the grades to the end, and the matter of the sawing apart. And now that the matter has been explained sufficiently, as befits the intent of the inquiry, we will come to the explanation of the matter of the diminishment and to setting right the preceding passages:

The intent in this chapter is to turn our hand to the three passages mentioned above and to explain them with a strong hand. And first we will explain the passage of the Ra'aya Meheimna, because it is like one who stings with the sting of a scorpion.

First, he said that "the two heads of the moon" are Netzach and Hod, as he explained within his words; and they are two equal points, over which Malkhut was a point, so that it was a segolta; and she was above them and bestowed upon them. And when the moon accused, for the reason that we shall explain, she descended to beneath their feet. And her accusation was that she said: It is impossible for two kings, who are Netzach and Hod, to make use of her, who is one crown. And the matter is that Tiferet is male, and by its nature and essence inclines after compassion, to the right side; and Malkhut is female, and her nature and essence is to incline to the left side, to the side of judgment, as is explained in the Zohar, parashat Bo (folio 37), and these are its words: "'In the beginning God created [et the heavens ve-et the earth]': et: this is the right hand of the Holy One, blessed be He; ve-et: this is the left. We have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, extended His right and created the heavens, and extended His left and created the earth; this is what is written (Isa. 48:13), 'My hand also has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spread out the heavens.'" Thus far its words.

He taught explicitly that the emanation of the heavens and their essence is toward compassion, so that because of this it was necessary to include Chesed by the word et and Gevurah by the word ve-et, because the one is adjacent to "the heavens" and the other to "the earth." They explained this matter further in the Zohar, parashat Vayikra (folio 14a), and these are its words: "Rabbi Shimon said: We have learned, two crowns are joined as one, and they are the opening of all the other crowns. And we have learned: one is judgment and one is compassion, and they are sweetened one by the other, male and female. On the side of the male dwells Chesed; on the side of the female dwells judgment. [One white and one red, etc.] And therefore they are bound to one another. And this covenant holds onto them, day and night, in judgment and in Chesed: at first in judgment, and afterwards Chesed dwells in it, and it is sweetened by all. And this is the covenant that is called day and night, which holds onto both." Thus far its words.

And he said that they are the opening to all those crowns: explanation: through the apprehension of these two all is apprehended, for all of them are included in these. "One judgment and one compassion": as we explained, the male inclines to the side of compassion and Chesed, and Malkhut, judgment, inclines to the side of judgment and Gevurah; and in their color one is red and one white; and they are sweetened, red in white, judgment in compassion; for through the union of the male and the female judgment and compassion are united. And this is what he said, "And therefore they are bound," etc. But their binding and their union is through Yesod, the covenant that unites the attribute of day and the attribute of night; and on this the verse said (Jer. 33:25), "If not My covenant of day and night, the ordinances of heaven and earth," etc.: explanation: the covenant that unites day and night. And this is what he said, "And this covenant holds onto them, day and night, in judgment and in Chesed": explanation: the union of judgment and compassion is through the union of the attribute of day and the attribute of night. "At first in judgment": explanation: for Yesod is chai [18], and it inclines to the left side; and this is Yitzchak [208]: ketz [190] chai [18], as I explained in Gate 1, chapter 2. And therefore "at first in judgment": by its nature it inclines to the left, for its union with the female is constant; and afterwards it turns back and holds onto the male and inclines to Chesed, and through it judgment and compassion are united, "and it is sweetened by all." And therefore Yesod was required to include judgment and compassion. And this is why the covenant of Yesod is called "day and night": the attribute of day and the attribute of night are themselves included in it, so that through this it can unite the two attributes. And this is what he said, "which holds onto both": explanation: through this it holds onto two attributes, for it includes both of them, so that it can tip the balance, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters.
And behold, from the words of these passages it is explained that the principal of Tiferet is compassion and Chesed, and the principal of Malkhut is judgment and Gevurah.

And behold, before the accusation she was united with her husband in an essential union. Not that they were two powers included in one power; rather they were always two sefirot uniting in their action: for although the male inclines to compassion and the female inclines to judgment, the actions of judgment and of compassion were performed through them together. If judgment was bestowed, it was through Tiferet and Malkhut, but with the prevailing of Malkhut, whose action is the opposite of the action of the male; and if compassion was bestowed, it was through both of them, but with the prevailing of Tiferet, whose action is compassion. And we will give a fine physical parable for this matter, to let the ear hear: a parable of two halves of a sphere, like this:

which match each other, and through them pass two holes, one to the right and one to the left; and through them is the passage of the effluence, the right one for compassion and the left one for judgment. And there is no doubt that it is the nature of the upper one to prevail; and since Tiferet was above, it prevailed with its action, toward Chesed. Therefore her intent was that the two of them should each be in its place, each one performing its own action, like this:

Malkhut, which is the female and whose nature is judgment, would act and bestow the effluence of Gevurah and judgment; and Tiferet, which is male, compassion, would act and bestow Chesed, and so the action of compassion would be according to its nature. And although she was small then, and also now (for the right always prevails over the left), she did not intend by her request that Tiferet should descend, but that they should be equal: not performing one action, but each one performing its own action. And from this matter there appears to come benefit, or harm, to three aspects: in relation to what they receive, or in relation to themselves, or in relation to what they bestow. The first aspect, in relation to what they bestow, is that Netzach and Hod do not act properly; for the nature of Netzach is Chesed and the nature of Hod is judgment, and it is fitting for each of them to receive according to its action and nature. And this is what she said: It is impossible for two kings, who are Netzach and Hod, the one right and the other left, to make use of one crown, so that they receive from only one action, either judgment or compassion. But if Tiferet and Malkhut were equal, Malkhut would bestow upon Hod and Tiferet upon Netzach; and this is what befits them and what they can bear, for that uniform action is impossible. This is one aspect, and it is the one that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna that we are explaining. And the second aspect is in relation to themselves: for since Tiferet is compassion, the action of compassion befits it, and since Malkhut is judgment, the action of judgment befits her; and if their actions are exchanged upon them, their service will be heavy. And it is not the way of the world to change attributes thus; and therefore she said: It is impossible for two kings, who are Tiferet and Malkhut, sun compassion and moon judgment, to make use of one crown. And this Rabbi Shimon ben Pazzi revealed to us in tractate Chullin. And the third is in relation to the place from which they receive, which is Binah. And behold, the explanation is: it is impossible for one king, who is Binah, to make use of two crowns, for her service would be heavy, and it is almost impossible to bestow judgment to the place of compassion and compassion to the place of judgment. And behold, Binah was compelled, before the bestowal, to impress that imprint [teva] upon the effluence, so that the receiving attribute could bear it.

And behold, the two preceding claims the moon stated in the force of her rhetoric, saying: It is impossible for two kings to make use of one crown. But this third claim she did not want to explain so much, because of the honor of Binah, which hovers over them [therefore she said: Is it possible for one king to make use of two crowns, etc.]. And this third aspect Rashbi revealed to us in the Song of Songs passage mentioned above. And for this reason it was said to her from a high place, from the Glory hovering over them, which is Binah, called the Holy One, blessed be He: "Go and diminish yourself," etc. The intent is: since it is not her will thus, and she was hurling words upward, she shall descend below the two kings, who are Netzach and Hod; and not merely below them, but beneath their feet: that is, the kings are Netzach and Hod, and their feet are Yesod, and beneath their feet means below Yesod. And there she performs the action of judgment; for so she is called "a sword avenging the vengeance of the covenant" (Lev. 26:25), and other titles indicating judgment, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And this is her being turned from compassion to judgment: for in her place she sometimes performed the action of compassion, or mostly so, through the arbitration of Tiferet, and now she is mostly judgment. (He returns to explain the language of the Ra'aya Meheimna in chapter 2.) "The ram of Isaac turned into a goat," etc.: explanation: for above, her inclination was slightly to the left, although her principal action was compassion and Chesed, because of the compelling of Tiferet, which tips the balance to the right; and therefore above she was called "the ram of Isaac." But when she descended below, she drew sustenance from the force of the strength of judgment, and is called "goat," for this name is a hint of judgment. And this is the difference between the burnt offering and the sin offering: the burnt offering [olah] hints at her ascent [aliyah] to her place and to her husband, and then she is a ram of compassion, as we explained; and the goat for a sin offering hints at her descent to beneath the feet of the kings, performing judgment, head to the foxes that spoil the vineyards. "Goat" certainly, on account of her nourishing the goats [se'irim] with the strength of judgment. "And therefore they brought, Atonement for Me; for Me the moon was a crown," etc. Before we explain this language we must recall a small preliminary that we hinted at in the Gate of Manifestations, and it is this: that Malkhut, when she is a king's daughter married to her husband and united with him, most of the time is above him, and she is in the effluence of compassion, "a woman of valor, the diadem of her husband" (Prov. 12:4); and he did not cease to cherish her until he called her "my mother." And when, through our iniquities, she descended from her grade, she lost this honored grade along with the other things that were lost. And when we come and offer the goat for a sin offering, then we bring her distress to her husband's remembrance, and he will raise her to her first place, "for it was better for her then than now" (Hos. 2:9). And this is "Bring atonement for Me": explanation: the goat, which comes to atone for the strength of judgment: in its slaughter and its binding the judgment is bound and burned on the altar, for the destruction of the husk is in its drawing near to purity. And so that they do not defile, so that the wife will be purified for her husband, they offered the goat, like the offering of the seventy bullocks of the Festival, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 7. And this matter is explained at length in the Zohar (parashat Noach) (Pinchas 256; see there) and in other places in the Zohar. And this is "Bring atonement for Me": to atone for judgment and to purify it, and to raise her to her place, to be the diadem of her husband, in the effluence of compassion, receiving from the sun as before her descent. And what he said, "for My having diminished the moon": the intent is, on my account and by my cause, that is to say, by the cause of Tiferet, the moon was diminished; for it was the cause of her accusing and saying, "It is impossible for two kings," etc. And in the Zohar, parashat Acharei (folio 79b), Rashbi explained the matter of "for Me" [alai]: it hints that on the New Moon Binah is revealed in her effluence, like the effluence on the Sabbath; and therefore he said, "Bring for Me": explanation: bring atonement, so that judgment may be purified, because the light of Binah flows upon Me, and the Shekhinah too will receive light from her; and because Binah is revealed, it is a time of favor for her to be purified and to receive the effluence from her, and for them to unite. And "for My having diminished the moon" is explained there as we explained. "She ascends from His feet," etc.: explanation: she ascends from beneath Yesod, which is her ascent; of whom it is said, "and the earth" (which is Malkhut) "is the footstool" and seat for the feet of Tiferet, which is Yesod; "to say of her, 'The heavens are My throne'": explanation: she is My throne; that is to say, Malkhut, who is the throne, ascended to the heavens, which is Tiferet. Or it may mean: the heavens, which is Tiferet, is a throne for Malkhut, in the secret of "the diadem of her husband"; and the sense of the verse is: the heavens are My throne, although you see that the earth is My footstool. And according to the explanation that we gave above, that her ascent or her descent is through Yesod, this is what he said: "And this is the secret of 'a righteous one rules,'" etc. The righteous one, Yesod, rules over Malkhut from the side of judgment, called Elohim; and through her ascent above she is turned to compassion; and it is in his hand to stand her in her place, to turn judgment to compassion through the coupling. "And the secret of the thing: 'The stone that the builders rejected,'" etc.: in the aspect of her being the diadem of her husband she is Yod above, second to Chokhmah. And I have expounded this matter at length in the Gate of Manifestations, chapters 3 and 4.
And behold, the explanation of this passage is complete. And now we will come, in a chapter of its own, to the explanation of the two remaining passages:

Although the principal of these passages has already been explained through the preliminary of the preceding chapter, nevertheless we will not withdraw our hand from them, with the help of Heaven. The second passage, from the Zohar on the Song of Songs, which said "At first," etc., "cleaving as one," etc.: explanation: as we explained in the preceding chapter, the two of them together performed judgment and compassion together, and she was beneath him, subordinate to him, and was always half the body; except that she was not equal to him, for Tiferet is sixth in the Emanation and Malkhut seventh, caused by it, and it is her cause; and likewise Tiferet is compassion, right, and Malkhut judgment and Gevurah, left, and the right always conquers the left. And her degree was then certainly always more praiseworthy than now, many times over, for she was always in her fullness and her light shone, although she was not equal to him. "Is it possible for one king to make use," etc.: Rashbi revealed to us this reason, the more concealed one; and it relates to the verse "If you know not," etc. (Song 1:8). "I see in you that your desire is to be head to the foxes": it is known that foxes are a hint of angels of judgment and fury, as in the matter of (Song 2:15), "Catch us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards," which hints at the angels of ruin. And she asked this because in her place she inclines to the side of Gevurah, as we explained in the preceding chapter, and the intent was that the angels of judgment should be bestowed from her. Therefore it was said to her, "Go and diminish yourself": the intent is that she should descend from her degree and her place and be head to them, and there perform her action; and this is the diminishment, that she descended further from her degree and was diminished more than she had been. "For why should I be as one who is veiled" (Song 1:7); "how shall I be," etc.: the intent is that when Tiferet acts with the power of compassion and compels her to the side of compassion, then in any case her action is annulled, and she will not perform judgment and will not be able to serve, and she will be wrapped as to the power of judgment, when the power of compassion prevails. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, was precise in saying "and be ruler in the night," etc., for then judgment rules, and this is the dominion of the foxes hinted at above; and this is "and feed your kids" (Song 1:8), which are the goats, which are the strength of judgment, as is known. And now that we have explained the two preceding passages, we wish to explain the first passage, from the Gemara, on which the gate was founded. "The moon said," etc.: "Master of the world" is Binah, who is master and lord of the seven days of the circuit, which are called world; and she is the mother crouching over the children. "Is it possible for two kings," etc.: this was explained in the preceding chapter; and it is the middle aspect, in relation to themselves: that it was not possible for them to perform one action, but each would act according to its nature, Tiferet compassion and the Diadem judgment. "Because I said before You a proper thing": explanation: for such is the way of judgment, to seek after the strength of judgment and Gevurah. "He said to her: Go and rule by day and by night": explanation: that the effluence of compassion, which is day, and the effluence of judgment, which is night, should be bestowed to this world through her; and this is something of an elevation for her, that her degree below in the diminishment should be like her degree above, in the secret of her first place. And she answered, "What greatness is this," etc.: the intent is that this thing is of no benefit to her, for this was the cause for which she accused before, for this blending was not her will. And this is what she said, "A candle at noon, what use is it?" For when she is below, performing the compassion bestowed upon her from above, then too her action is annulled. And then He answered her, "Let Israel count by you," etc.: the intent is that Tiferet, which is Israel, will not be able to perform its actions below except through her; and accordingly all her lord's goodness is in her hand. And she answered this: "The day too, it is impossible," etc.: the intent is that there will be no tikkun for the loss that she lost. For granted, if the action were entirely through her, it would be well; but she too cannot act except through Tiferet, and this is no greatness, for Tiferet already prevailed over her in this, and she had this before too. And this is what she said, "It is impossible, for they do not count the seasons by it": explanation: the decree of things and the actions performed through the seasons and the revolution of the twelve boundaries, which are the twelve havayot in it, every three of which are one season, as will be explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names. And to this He answered her, "Let the righteous be called by your name," etc.: the intent is that through the cleaving of the righteous her husband will always unite with her. "And nevertheless her mind [da'atah] was not settled": explanation: her union, as in (Gen. 4:1), "And the man knew," etc.; for the intent is that with this she does not return in her very self to her first place where she was, at times rising over her husband to be for him a diadem of glory [ateret tiferet]. And to this He answered her, "Bring atonement for Me," etc., as explained in the preceding chapter.

And behold, these three passages have been fully explained. And what remains for us to explain is a mighty question that falls in this inquiry, so that the discerning one is almost astonished; and it is this: how is it possible that in the place of spirituality, the holiness of the pure and holy Emanation, the matter of accusation and provocation should occur? For this thing is among the disgraceful traits even in human beings; all the more so, by a fortiori of a fortiori, in the pure and holy Emanation; for who has put forth his hand to speak even a light word and been clean?

And further, second: since she said, "Because I said before You a proper thing," and He wished to appease her, it appears that her words were good and right. If so, how was she diminished for it, God forbid? It would have been fitting that she not be diminished.

And behold, these doubts are hard, and the discerning one is almost astonished in thinking of them. And we will answer that in the matter of judgment there are three aspects, and we explained them in the Gate of Colors, chapter 3. The first is the evil judgment, that is to say, the strength of the husk, which is judgment that does not accept arbitration, the fire of Gehinnom, of which separation is said (Gen. 1:4): "And God separated between the light and the darkness"; and the darkness is the fire of Gehinnom, which is separated from the light of holiness, for it does not accept the arbitration of compassion because of its hardness and its strength, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters. And there is a second aspect, and it is that which delights in arbitration, inclining toward Chesed. And there is a third judgment, and it is intermediate between the judgment arbitrated to the side of Chesed and the separated judgment.

And behold, Malkhut is bestowed and emanated from the side of the strong judgment, which is the blue [tekhelet] that consumes [mekhalah] all, as we explained in the Gate of Colors. Therefore, from the side of the strength of judgment, [she wanted] to perform the action of the strong judgment, and to incline to the side of her root, which is judgment, and not to perform compassion, as we explained in the preceding chapter. And for this she accused, and wished to go out from under the hand of Tiferet and to perform judgment by herself, because Tiferet annuls her action and tips her toward the side of compassion, as is its way with Gevurah. And because she did not want arbitration, and this resembles somewhat the matter of the fire of Gehinnom and the strength of the strong judgment, therefore she descended from her degree and was placed (in the green color, as explained in the Gate of Colors, chapter 4; and see the Gate of Paths, folio 67, at the end of the second path) in the greenness of holiness within the Emanation, to be head to the foxes who rule in the fire of Gehinnom, who are those that do not want arbitration. And because her demand was a proper thing from the side of her drawing sustenance from the strong judgment, nevertheless they acted for her from the side of compassion, so that "her feet go down to death" (Prov. 5:5), until the husk is annulled and "death is swallowed up forever" (Isa. 25:8): the husk will draw near to the kernel, and all the created entities will know that He alone is God. And the swine will turn out to be purified (that is, the husk of Esau, who is likened to "the boar from the forest" (Ps. 80:14)), and the fire of Gehinnom annulled. And Malkhut will return to her first strength, to the house of her husband as at first; and then will be fulfilled in her (Isa. 30:26), "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun," etc. And what is fitting to investigate is this: since before her diminishment her emanation was above, in the place of Tiferet, and the Righteous One was the last attribute, it is fitting to know how the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut took place, and through whom they coupled, and who was the intermediary groomsman. For if we say that they coupled without this intermediary, this is impossible: for it does not differ from the creation of man, and "from my flesh I shall see God" (Job 19:26); and in the creation of man, the union is through Yesod, the everlasting covenant. And further, several righteous ones served to unite and couple, such as Joseph the Righteous, and likewise Boaz and Palti son of Laish: their degree would then be annulled; and it is not fitting for us to say this.

And further, several things in the Torah and in the performance of the commandments indicate the union of Tiferet with Malkhut through Yesod; if so, shall we say, God forbid, that the fulfillment of that commandment or that verse is annulled? And to this we answer that the union never changed and will never change, forever and ever. For before the diminishment their union was through Yesod, and in the time of the diminishment too their union is thus, and so will their union be after she ascends to her exalted place with her husband as in days of old, her former state. And there is no wonder in Yesod's being the tenth grade; for we have already explained that at the time of the emanation of Tiferet, Yesod was emanated with it, for "body and covenant are reckoned as one." And it has two aspects, that is to say, two manifestations: a subtle and concealed manifestation, which is the extension of the Vav that precedes Netzach and Hod, and a revealed manifestation, which is after Netzach and Hod, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 8. And just as the union of Chokhmah and Binah is through Tiferet, in its concealed manifestation, that is, Da'at, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 17, and also in Gate 3, chapter 1, so too the union of Tiferet and Malkhut is through Yesod, in the subtle manifestation that it has, which is above, uniting with them. And this thing is necessitated by itself: for when Tiferet and Malkhut ascend higher and higher, united, Yesod too will ascend with them, and this certainly in the subtle manifestation that it has; and their union is always through Yesod. And the passage "The Sabbath said before the Holy One, blessed be He" we explained in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 4.
And behold, this chapter is complete, and this gate is concluded, with the help of the Rock, the true Helper:
The Nineteenth Gate: The Gate of the Four-Letter Name.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain something of the explanation of the four-letter name, so that its holiness, and its being distinct from the other holy names, may be explained, as we shall explain:
Chapter One:

After our Maker has helped us, and we have included in the preceding gates all that the inquirer needs in the matter of the inquiries concerning the manifestation of the Emanation, we now come in this gate to explain the name that relates to the totality of the entire Emanation, according to the explanation found in the words of Rashbi. And let the inquirer not expect of us that we include here, in this gate, all the explanations found concerning the Name in the words of Rashbi, for this is impossible; and further, the matter would weigh very heavily upon us, and the reading would not be easy for the inquirer. But we will write in it here as much as is needed to enter through it into the gates of the Zohar, so that study may be easy for the discerning; and behold, we enter into its explanation. All the expounders of inscriptions [dorshei reshumot] of our holy Torah, whether of the masters of the Kabbalah, or of the masters of the plain sense, or of the investigators of the roots of our Torah, all agreed with one mouth that this name is the proper name [shem ha-etzem] and no other. And they singled it out among the other holy names that may not be erased, to the point that they said that even the name Ehyeh, although it is a very awesome name, is not equal to this name. And concerning this name there are many reasons, and the most compelling of all of them is this: that from all the names that may not be erased some verb is derived, except the four-letter name, whose letters do not entail any verb at all by any reckoning. And this is because the names Elohim, Eloah, El are derived from the language of greatness, might and strength; as in (Ezek. 17:13) "and he took the mighty [eilei] of the land," and in (Ps. 36:7) "Your righteousness is like the mountains of God [El]," which are language of greatness and might. And the name Shaddai indicates that He overpowers [shoded] the arrays [of the heavens]. And the name Tzeva'ot indicates His being master of the hosts on high, and it is derived from the language of "the host [tzeva] of heaven." And the name Adonai indicates lordship, His being Lord of all the earth, and it is derived from the language of lordship. And Ehyeh indicates the matter of being, in the future tense, first person, in the simple conjugation; and so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded (Berakhot 9b): "I was with them in the exile of Egypt; I will be with them in other exiles," etc. But the four-letter name, very awesome: who can contain an explanation of it? For it has no explanation at all. The second reason: all these names we may use in profane speech if we wish, which is not so with the letters of the four-letter name. How so? El: Scripture uses it in profane speech, "another god [el]" (Ex. 34:14), and likewise "like the mountains of God," and many like it. And likewise Elohim, as "See, I have made you a god [elohim] to Pharaoh" (Ex. 7:1), and likewise "You shall not revile the judges [elohim]" (Ex. 22:27), and much like it. And Shaddai, as "and the creatures of the field [sadai] are with me" (Ps. 50:11), "he shall lodge between my breasts [shadai]" (Song 1:13): behold its letters, and they are only profane. And the name Tzeva'ot, as "all the hosts of the Lord went out" (Ex. 12:41), and the like. Adonai, as (Gen. 18:3) "And he said, My lords [adonai], if now I have found favor in your sight, do not pass away," etc.; and some of our Rabbis say that he said it to the greatest of them; and although there are those who disagree on this and say that it is holy, nevertheless the practical upshot according to all of them is that if one wishes to say to his master "Adoni," that is to say, "my lord," it is permitted to use it in profane speech. Ehyeh, as "for why should I be [ehyeh] as one who is veiled" (Song 1:7), "I will not be [ehyeh] a healer" (Isa. 3:7), and much like them. Which is not so with these four holy letters, YHVH: for although three of them are found, all four are not found in another, profane matter; as it is written (Eccl. 11:3), "In the place where the tree falls, there it shall be [yehu]"; but the four-letter name as a whole is not found. And this reason is somewhat close to the first reason. Further, the third reason: all the names are pronounced as they are written, except this holy name, for it was not pronounced by its letters except in the Temple, in the priestly blessing, and likewise by the high priest on the Day of Atonement. And the reason is that the other names are those that conduct the world, as is proven from their explanation; and the four-letter name has no explanation, and its action does not spread into this world except by being clothed in the other names, as we shall explain. And therefore it is permitted to mention the other names: for when the spirituality of those letters comes into being in the soul of the person [who mentions them, in the articulation of their letters], they are clothed in the air of this world to perform their action. But the four-letter name, because of its great holiness, is not clothed in the air of this world except in the Temple, in particular in the priestly blessing, as it is said (Ex. 20:21), "In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned I will come to you and bless you"; and the air is pure and clear, and it can be clothed, for it is clothed in the air of the Temple, that is, the Shekhinah, the name Adonai; and this is (Hab. 2:20), "But the Lord is in His holy palace." And let this preliminary not be light in the eyes of the inquirer, for it is of precious worth. And with it the reason will be explained why it is forbidden to speak words of Torah in a filthy place, in a bathhouse, and in a privy: for it is a place of the air of the husk and of filth; and words of Torah are the spirituality of holiness, and if one mentions them in a place of filthy air, it turns out that he combines pure with impure, and holiness is clothed in the air of the husk. And nevertheless, to keep someone away from a prohibition it is permitted; for then the words of Torah serve to tip the balance against the husk, to fulfill (Ps. 103:19), "and His kingship rules over all," as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 7.

And behold, they gave the four-letter name the title "the explicit name" [shem ha-meforash], and several explanations of this are possible: either from the language of explanation [perush], or from the language of setting apart and separation. From the language of explanation, it would mean that it was pronounced explicitly and uttered by its letters on the Day of Atonement, or in the priestly blessing in the Temple; or it would mean explicit, known. And from the language of setting apart, it would mean set apart from the thoughts of understanding, or set apart from mention and utterance. All this can properly be said of it. And let it not enter the mind of the inquirer to say that by our saying "the proper name" [shem ha-etzem, literally "the name of the self"] we mean the Self of the Emanator, the Ein Sof, God forbid; for this is an improper thing, as we explained at length in Gate 3, chapter 1. Rather the intent in our saying "the proper name" is that it is the self of the sefirot; explanation: the name that includes the whole self of the sefirot. And it is known that the matter of the Emanation as a whole is the name of the Ein Sof; explanation: it indicates His Self. The parable for this: as the name Isaac is a handle for that man, by which speech can take hold [of him]; and if we did not attach a name to him, we could not speak of him, for we would not know him. So the Ein Sof, through the Emanation, will have a handle and a name indicating His Self, so that we can speak of Him. And therefore the four-letter name is a name including all the Emanation, in general and in particular, etc.; and therefore we attribute it [the proper name] to Him, and His name, explanation: the Emanation. And the four-letter name, or the other names, are not to Him, may He be exalted, as proper names [shemot ha-etzem] are to people. For their names are conventional, and not such that the name indicates the character of the man at all, nor such that his name indicates his self. Not so His names, may He be blessed, for all of them indicate the character of the thing called by them. And therefore we said that the proper name does not indicate the Self of the Emanator, for there is nothing that can bound His Self and His unity and His manifestation, God forbid. And because this is true, the sages of Israel and their prophets agreed to title Him with names indicating the concealment of His holiness from the thoughts of the heart. And this is His name by which they call Him in the heights of heaven, all the hosts on high, array facing array: "Where [ayeh] is the place of His glory, to revere Him?"
