For they do not know a place for Him, nor understand an understanding of Him. But those that reveal to us His divinity and something of His exaltedness are His emanated ones. And according to the truth, it can accordingly properly be said that the Emanation is His name, which indicates something of His hiddenness and His concealment; and the proper name, which is the four-letter name, is what indicates the self of His emanated ones, in general and in particular, as was revealed, in the will of His compassion to grant us merit, [in His Torah given] to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. And as for the manifestation that includes all the emanated ones, the explanations of it are many, as we shall explain in a chapter of its own, with the help of Heaven:

Concerning the holiness of the four-letter name, its including the whole Emanation, the explanations are many. There are those who explained: "Yod is the image of the head of the Holy One, blessed be He. Heh is the right arm and the side of the body. Vav is the whole body, and thighs and legs and knees and the holy covenant. Heh is the left arm, and the Shekhinah of God. And this is its order: YHVH. And now it is to be explained, in each and every letter, how many sefirot go out from them in the vision of the eye; and this is their order, and all is one word:

And now we have to speak of where, from these images of these four holy letters, the tikkun of the body goes out," etc. Thus far its words, as relevant to our subject.

And behold, he has another way with the four-letter name: that Yod includes four sefirot, Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Chesed; Heh, Gevurah; Vav, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod; Heh, Malkhut. And he wished to explain that the Vav within the Heh is Metatron; and in our view it is not fitting to say this. And there are those who wish to say that in the Yod are two sefirot and the Ein Sof. This is the opinion of some commentators on the responsum of Rabbenu Hai Gaon that we wrote in the Gate of Tzachtzachot, chapters 1 and 2. And this is not the opinion of all the Kabbalists, for all of them agreed with one mouth that the four-letter name is in the sefirot, not above them, God forbid. And what most of them explained and agreed upon is that the Yod is in Chokhmah, and its upper thorn in Keter; the first Heh, Binah; Vav is the six extremities, as its name [six], which are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod; the last Heh, Malkhut. And close to this matter Rashbi explained in many places, and these are his words (in the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, folio 5): "YHVH is: Yod, Chokhmah; Heh, Binah; Vav includes six sides; Heh, Malkhut." Thus far his words.

And we have not found Rashbi saying that the thorn of the Yod hints at Keter; but elsewhere (Tikkun 5, folio 19b) there is some revealing, for he explained: "Yod: an upper thorn, a lower thorn, and its body in the middle; they are in the secret of letters, vowel points and cantillation marks." And the explanation: the letters are in Binah, and its lower thorn is in Binah; and the vowel points are in the middle body, in Chokhmah; and its upper thorn is in Keter, which are the cantillation marks. And likewise in parashat Acharei (folio 65b), and these are its words: "The upper thorn of the Yod hints at Nothing [Ayin]." Thus far its words. (And likewise in parashat Vayikra, folio 10b, that the upper thorn hints at the Supernal Keter; see there.) And Nothing is Keter, as is known. But we should be precise in his language, in saying "the upper thorn," etc.: explanation: the upper thorn is a hint of Keter in its lower aspect, which is the aspect that unites with Chokhmah and Binah; for this is the explanation of Ayin: Alef, Keter; Yod, Chokhmah; Nun, Binah, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles. And the reason is that in the aspect of itself above, in relation to its aspect that unites with its simple root, it has no name and no point, as we explained in the Gate From Below to Above, chapter 5; and the thorn of the Yod there is in its aspect that unites with Chokhmah and Binah, as we explained. And this is what is found in the Zohar in the explication of the Name, without specifying it (in its fillings) in all the sefirot. And for this reason they called it "the unique name," for it is the name in which all ten sefirot are united, unified as one. This is one way of the four-letter name in the sefirot. Further, Rashbi wrote in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 3a) another way in this: Yod, Keter; Yod-Heh, Chokhmah and Binah; Yod-Heh-Vav, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet; Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And these are his words: "'And I heard the sound of their wings' (Ezek. 1:24): with ten kinds of praises: with a simple song, which is Yod, Keter; a double song, which is Yod-Heh, Chokhmah and Binah; a triple, Yod-Heh-Vav, which is Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet; a quadruple, with YHVH, which is Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut." Thus far. And the relation of these letters to the sefirot is as we explained in Gate 8: that the sefirot are divided into these three lines: first, the line of Chesed; second, the line of judgment; third, the middle one, the line of Rachamim. And to these three lines belong three letters, which are Yod-Heh-Vav: Yod, the root of the line of Chesed; Vav, the root of the line of Rachamim; Heh, the root of the line of judgment.

And behold, Keter, although Vav can also properly be said of it, as explained at the end of the Gate of Manifestations, nevertheless the Vav is in a borrowed sense, because the root of compassion is from Da'at, as explained in Gate 8, chapter 25. And the Yod is hinted at in it because of its smallness and its subtlety and its concealment, to indicate the concealment of Keter and the little apprehension of it, just as the thorn of the Yod, that is, a small Yod, is related to it. Afterwards there is Yod in Chokhmah, which is the root of Chesed; Heh in Binah, which is the root of judgment. Afterwards there is Yod in Chesed, because it is a branch of Chokhmah; and further, because at times Chokhmah dwells upon it, as is known, in the secret of "whoever wishes to become wise should turn southward" (Bava Batra 25b). And Heh in Gevurah, for the same reason as the Yod in Chesed. And the Vav in Tiferet. Afterwards Yod in Netzach, for the reason that it is in Chesed; Heh in Hod, for the reason that it is in Gevurah; and Vav in Yesod, as is known, for it is the extension of the Vav, and likewise the small Vav, for the reason that it is in Tiferet; Heh in Malkhut, for there is its principal place, for it is the last Heh of the Name. And this is the relation of the ten letters, Yod, Yod-Heh, Yod-Heh-Vav, Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh, to the ten sefirot. Further, Rashbi explained that the four-letter name in its filling with Alefs is, in Chokhmah, ten sefirot, which are יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that it includes the Name in ten sefirot, a revealed inclusion; from this, that it is the totality of the existents, revealed in four arrays, as we shall explain in chapter 3. But from the side of Binah they are included only in the four letters YHVH alone. And the reason: when the light of Chokhmah prevails and shines in the sefirot, then כ"ח מ"ה [the power of Mah] shines, which amounts to Adam [45]; and this name, which amounts to Adam, indicates that the light is a bright and clear light, sparkling in ten sparks. But when the light is from Binah alone, the sefirot are revealed only in general, not in particular. How so? Yod-Heh in Binah (which is the totality of the first three); and so Tiferet is called "son of Yah" [ben Yah], that is, Binah, the letters of the one being the letters of the other; Vav includes six sefirot; Heh in Malkhut. It turns out that the sefirot are not revealed by themselves; rather the light of the sefirot is included within the totality of Binah, Tiferet and Malkhut; and this is YHVH in general. But יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א is from the side of the light of Chokhmah, and it reveals all ten sefirot together, without any generality; rather all of them are seen. And all this Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim; and so as not to lengthen by copying his language, which is scattered and dispersed, we will not lengthen. Further, Rashbi explained the four-letter name in the filling of Yods, יו"ד ה"י וא"ו ה"י, and it indicates more concealment than its filling with Alefs, as we shall explain in chapter 3. And the reason is that this is the light revealed from Keter, and it shows all the sefirot, but not with an essential revealing, as we shall explain. And although they are enclosed and concealed, they did not come included [in general letters], so as not to show poverty in the place of wealth. And this name is certainly in Keter, and not in the aspect of itself but in its aspect with Chokhmah and Binah; and therefore in this name there are three Yods, which are a segolta in Keter, the first three: that is, in the aspect of Chokhmah within it, the right Yod; and in the aspect of Binah within it, the left Yod; and the aspect above them, that is, the first Yod. And the Alef in the middle of וא"ו is the skull [karkafta] that covers the three brains, like this: י. And this is the secret of the name El, as they transcribe it thus; and Rashbi has already explained that it amounts to the number of El; for in Keter too there is the name El, which is supernal Chesed. Thus far reaches what we saw fit to say about the four-letter name including ten sefirot. But as for the four-letter name itself, in the explanation of its four letters, we shall explain in the Gate of Names:

Concerning the four-letter name in its filling, which we explained in the preceding chapter, Rashbi gave an explanation in parashat Emor (folio 92); and we will not copy his language, lest the labor weigh upon us, but we will write their essence, with additions, [in] a place that he left for us to distinguish ourselves in. And the matter is that, besides the four-letter name indicating the whole totality of the entire Emanation, as we explained, it further indicates [it] in four letters, each and every letter of them indicating the totality of the whole Name, that is to say, also including the whole Emanation. And this is that the Yod in its filling is יו"ד, Yod-Vav-Dalet: the Yod is in Chokhmah, and the Vav in Tiferet, and the Dalet in Malkhut; behold, the totality of the whole Emanation from beginning to end. For in the Yod the first three are included, as we explained in chapter 2, and the Vav in Tiferet includes six extremities, and the Dalet in Malkhut: these are ten sefirot included in the Yod in its filling. And to indicate the matter of the true union, the Yod in its filling is the form of Alef. How so? The Yod above the diagonal line, and the diagonal line is Vav, and the lower Yod in the form of Dalet: behold, Yod in its filling and Alef are all one. And now there is no wonder about the name Ehyeh, that its beginning is Alef while the head of the four-letter name is Yod; for Yod and Alef are all one, as we shall explain in the Gate of Names, on the name Ehyeh, with the help of Heaven. And the Hehs too are all one, and in them the Emanation is included, like the manifestation of the Yod itself. How so? The middle thorn between the two sides of the Dalet, that is, the thorn of the Dalet, is Yod (and so Rashbi explained in the Zohar, in a passage that we shall copy in the Gate of Names, chapter 11; see there); and the Dalet itself, behold Dalet; and the Vav within the Dalet: behold יו"ד. And in this way for the last Heh. And sometimes the particularity of the Heh is revealed essentially in its filling, which is the filling of Alef, like this: ה"א, indicating the revealing of the totality essentially. And the Vav too is filled with Alef: behold the totality of the Emanation. It turns out that the four letters reveal four arrays, four totalities, so that the part is in the whole and the whole in the part, for the multiplication of [the indication of] the unity. And the reason for these four totalities, which in their particulars are Yod Chokhmah, Heh Binah, Vav Tiferet, Heh Malkhut, is to hint at the four arrays in which we arrange the Emanation, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 5, with the help of Heaven. And there we explained that the Emanation is four arrays: the first array Chokhmah, the second array Binah, the third array Tiferet, the fourth array Malkhut. And therefore these four letters are inscribed and marked in these four arrays in particular, and their principal is in the whole Emanation; and their concealment, which is their filling, indicates the totality of the Emanation concealed within them. And what we should further know is that these letters are not equal in their arrays: for the Alef indicates the concealed Emanation with a more revealed revealing than the Yod; for the Yod indicates it in its filling, and this indicates it in its simple form, for the Yod in its filling is a simple Alef, as we explained. And because Chokhmah is more concealed than the other arrays, the revealing of the array that is in it came in great concealment, that is, the concealment of the filling of the Yod. But the Heh indicates the principal of the array itself, in the revealing of its very self, as we explained: for a simple Heh, without any filling, indicates the array within it; and when it is filled, the array is revealed more, to crown the delightful son, who is Vav.

Further, Heh and Vav are filled in two ways, either with Alef or with Yod. For when the array in Binah is revealed with an essential revealing, with Alef, then Tiferet, the delightful son, reveals the array in the manifestation of Alef, according to its drawing sustenance from its mother. But when the Heh is filled with Yod, like this, ה"י, then it indicates concealment, as we explained that Yod is more concealed than Alef; and then the Vav is filled with Yod, like this, וי"ו, indicating the concealment of the array, which was not revealed to it more than to the mother. And according to the filling of the Vav that is in Tiferet, so is the Heh that is in Malkhut filled, because she receives from it alone. And sometimes, although the filling of the Vav is with Alef, the filling of the Heh with Yod indicates that it was revealed and concealed; for such is the way of Malkhut, which is a veil, a screen, concealing and hiding the whole Emanation. And with this preliminary it will be understood that sometimes the Heh is filled with Heh, like this: ה"ה. And according to what we have explained, it turns out that the revealing of the arrays came in three kinds, either with Yod, or with Alef, or with Heh, and each one more concealed than its fellow. Yod is the most concealed of all, for the totality of the Emanation is not revealed in it except by way of filling. And when the Vav is filled with Yod, then the matter turns out to be concealed within concealed; for the simple Yod is concealed in וי"ו, and the Yod itself needs filling. And the reason is that the array revealed in the filling of the Yod is the array of the Emanation concealed in Chokhmah, and it is concealed with the utmost concealment. And when it is revealed in Binah, which is Heh, or in Tiferet, which is Vav, or in Malkhut, which is the last Heh, it is not revealed essentially except with great difficulty, according to the depth of the grades, by the power of the effluence of the light of Keter, as befits the subtlety that is in Chokhmah. And because Chokhmah is concealed, it is not fitting that the array be revealed except in the very concealment, that is to say, in the form of Yod, and not in the other letters. And therefore Yod has no filling but Yod, and is filled neither with Alef nor with Heh, unless it is a complete word, that is, Yah, where the Heh is a name and a palace to the Yod within it, and like a title to it and to the name within the sefirah, as will be explained in the next gate, with the help of Heaven. But the Heh is filled with Alef and with Yod, and in the opinion of some also with another Heh; and likewise the last Heh, and likewise the Vav. But the array is revealed in the very body of the Hehs without (revealing) [filling], as we explained. And they are excluded from the rule of the other letters: for Yod and Vav have in themselves no revealing of an array at all, except in their filling; which is not so with the Hehs, for the Hehs themselves are revealed in the form of the arrays, as we explained; for in the form of ה"א itself there is the form of יו"ד, that is, the form of Alef. And the reason is that Yod and Vav, which are Chokhmah and Tiferet, are males, for so they are called Father and Son; and Binah and Malkhut are females, for so they are called Mother and Daughter. And it is known that the generations and the beings are in the male in great concealment, for the children depend on the brain of the male; as is known from the parable of the seed, concealed in the male and revealed in the full womb through the union of the male and the female; and she reveals the actions essentially. And therefore in Chokhmah and Tiferet the beings, that is, the arrays that include the Emanation, are concealed, and they are not revealed in them except in great concealment, through the fillings; that is, after the actions go out from them, and they go out from them like the filling of a letter, which goes out from the letter and is outside the letter, as is known. But the females, which are the Hehs, show the actions in pregnancy within them, that is, the manifestation of the form of the Heh itself, and show more when they go out from before them, that is, the fillings. And one should not ask: but Binah is more concealed than Tiferet; if so, why did the revealing of the array come in Binah more than in Tiferet? This is no question: for Binah in relation to Chokhmah is female, and Tiferet in relation to Malkhut is male, and therefore each one is judged according to its relation. And now that the matter of the difference between Alef and Yod has been explained, that Alef reveals more than Yod, and Alef is female in relation to Yod, the reason for the four-letter name filled with Yods in Keter and filled with Alefs in Chokhmah will not be far from us: for this one reveals more than that. Thus far reaches the filling of the letters of the four-letter name, as far as is apprehended by us from the words of Rashbi in parashat Emor mentioned above:

Having explained in the preceding chapters the opinion of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that the four-letter name includes the whole Emanation, we will now explain another matter that he explained to us concerning this: that the four-letter name is in each and every sefirah. And these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 42, folio 82a): "There is no sefirah in which there is not YHVH, יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א."

And behold, he doubled the Name, in its simple form and in its filling, to reveal to us that just as the Name in its simple form relates to each and every sefirah, so the Name in its filling is in each and every sefirah, all according to the aspects that we explained in the preceding chapters. But it is fitting to investigate: if it is true that the four-letter name is in each and every sefirah, then in what are the sefirot distinguished in their names? And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this matter elsewhere in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 124), and these are his words: "Come and see: nine times He is YHVH, in each and every sefirah its own vowel point; and He is YHVH in Malkhut without a vowel point. And these are the vowel points that are obligatory for each and every sefirah. Nine vowel points they are: the first YHVH, the second YHVH, the third YHVH, the fourth YHVH, the fifth YHVH, the sixth YHVH, the seventh YHVH, the eighth YHVH, the ninth YHVH [with shuruk (which is melupim); Malkhut, YHVH, includes all of them] [the vowels written under each Name are not reproduced in this text]. It is called kamatz with this vowel point, YHVH, from the side of the Supernal Keter, which is closed like a clenched fist [kometz], which is enclosed in thought, so that a person does not know what is inside. And whoever is inside is enclosed in thought; we call him the Cause of Causes. And it is called patach with this vowel point, YHVH, from the side of Chokhmah, for in it the enclosed thought is opened [itpatchat] and revealed, in this manner: above, in this likeness, א; below, in this likeness, א. And these two vowel points are revealed in Imma [in the Supernal Keter they are enclosed], and they became tzeirei, YHVH; of them it is said, 'And the Lord God formed [va-yyitzer]' (Gen. 2:7), 'for in Yah the Lord is the Rock of worlds [tzur olamim]' (Isa. 26:4): He formed [tzayar] two worlds, this world and the world to come. Segol: this is Chesed, in which the Shekhinah is a segolta above and a segol below, YHVH; treasure [segulah] and love from the right side. Sheva, in this manner, YHVH, from the left side: 'For by fire [ba-esh] will the Lord judge' (Isa. 66:16); 'and Sheba [sheva] fell upon them and took them' (Job 1:15); 'It is better that I give her to you… abide [shevah] with me' (Gen. 29:19): for she is the Shekhinah, who is called sheva from the left side. And it is called cholam, in this manner, YHVH, from the side of the middle pillar: 'From there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel' (Gen. 49:24); 'the stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner' (Ps. 118:22). Every precious pearl is in cholam; this is what is written, 'a leshem, a shevo, and an achlamah' (Ex. 28:19); and by it, 'and we dreamed [va-nachalmah] a dream' (Gen. 41:11). It is called chirik from the side of the right thigh, in this manner, YHVH; in it is investigation [chakirah]: 'Can you find out God by searching [ha-chekker]?' (Job 11:7); and it is 'the terrible ice [kerach]' (Ezek. 1:22): ice from that terrible one, which is the middle pillar. Shurek is called Hod, in this manner, YHVH; from there the Shekhinah is called shurek, the knot [kesher] of the chariot; and it is the Hod of Moses, in which they were completed: 'And five bars for the boards of the second side [tzela] of the Tabernacle' (Ex. 26:27): as the number of its Heh [5]; there remains Vav-Dalet, double-faced; of it is said, 'Ten cubits the length of the board [keresh]' (Ex. 26:16): keresh, kesher. Shuruk, YHVH [written יההיווהו]: this is the Righteous One, who binds [kosher] the chariot, which is the Shekhinah, with the Holy One, blessed be He; this is what is written, 'for all that is in heaven and on earth' (1 Chr. 29:11), which we translate, 'who holds onto heaven and earth.' And of it is said, 'Yet I had planted you a noble vine [sorek], wholly a seed of truth' (Jer. 2:21): it is certainly a seed of truth, of which it is said, 'You will give truth to Jacob, Chesed to Abraham' (Mic. 7:20). He is seed, and the Shekhinah is help; this is what is written, 'I will make him a help meet for him' (Gen. 2:18). All these vowel points are obligatory in the holy Name from the side of nine sefirot; and Malkhut is the inclusion of all of them: 'the love of your espousals [kelulotayikh]' (Jer. 2:2)." Thus far its words.

And our intent in it is clear: that the sefirot are distinguished by their vowel points, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, set out. And nevertheless we will not withdraw our hands from explaining it somewhat. He said, "And He is YHVH in Malkhut without a vowel point": we have already explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance and in the Gate of Colors that all the sefirot bestow upon Malkhut, and through her they show their actions; and so is the matter with the vowel points: she receives all the vowel points from the sefirot to show their actions; and according to her receiving from above, so is her action, (to return) [for good] or for ill. "And these are the vowel points that are obligatory": the matter of the vowel points in the sefirot is not literal vowel points; rather the intent is that the spirituality of the sefirot is not bounded except by these vowel points; and this is what he said, "And these are the vowel points that are obligatory," etc. "From the side of the Supernal Keter": we have already explained this passage a little in Gate 8, chapter 2, with the help of Heaven; and nevertheless we will explain it here briefly. Kamatz is from the language of concealment, from the language of (Lev. 2:2) "And the priest shall take a fistful [ve-kamatz]"; and the intent is that just as with the fist that a person closes, no one knows what is inside it, so the Supernal Keter is clenched and closed, and there is none who apprehends what is inside it. "And whoever is inside": explanation: the parable is not like the thing it illustrates; for a clenched fist sometimes has nothing inside it, for the intellect cannot judge whether there is something in it or nothing at all. For this he said that it is not so in the thing illustrated, that is, Keter: for a person will not deny His manifestation, God forbid, because of the concealment of the Ein Sof within it. And this is what he said, "And whoever is inside is enclosed in thought": explanation: His manifestation is not denied at all; rather, the one who is within Keter is enclosed in Keter, which is called thought. "The Cause of Causes," etc.: explanation: that He is a cause for all the sefirot, which are causes for all that is caused by them; and the intent is the Emanator of the sefirot. And he said, "we call him": explanation: for this name does not indicate His Self, God forbid, for there is no name that bounds Him, as we explained; but it is a borrowed name, by which we title Him so, to distinguish when we speak of the cause or of the effects. "And it is called patach," etc.: the intent is that Chokhmah opens and reveals the fist. Not that [Keter] is revealed in Chokhmah, God forbid, for there too there is no apprehension; but the intent is that Chokhmah reveals Keter by having emanated Binah. And this he intended by the form of Alef: the upper thorn Keter, the middle line Chokhmah, and the lower thorn Binah; and in Binah they are revealed. "And these two vowel points," etc.: explanation: kamatz and patach became tzeirei in Binah; for she reveals all that is above, and therefore she is called Shekhinah, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And he proved from the verses that the tzeirei is by the power of Keter and Chokhmah, as we shall explain. For in the one verse he said "and He formed [va-yyitzer]," which is tzeirei: it would mean that in that tzeirei was the emanation of "the Lord God," which is Binah, called YHVH with the vowels of Elohim; and the two Yods in va-yyitzer also indicate the tzeirei. And because this verse is not a complete proof (for on the contrary, from there it appears that Binah formed, in its plain sense; and also we might explain tzeirei in Binah and say "and the Lord God formed," that the tzeirei that is in Binah formed; and there is no proof, for they have already explained it in the Idra in the secret of va-yyitzer, that is, He formed a form within a form, as is explained in the book Or Yakar, with the help of Heaven), therefore he proved the matter from the verse "for in Yah the Lord is the Rock of worlds." And the intent is that in Yah, which is Chokhmah, YHVH formed, which is necessarily Keter. And the explanation of "worlds" is to hint at this world, Malkhut, which receives the vowel points, as we explained, and the world to come, Binah, for she received the two upper vowel points and they became tzeirei. And from this it is proven that the intent of the verse "and He formed" is as we explained: that tzeirei is the two upper vowel points, Keter and Chokhmah. And from the matter of the Idra there is no difficulty at all; for the Yod of the four-letter name that is in Keter is one Yod, and the second Yod, of Ze'ir [Anpin], is the Yod of Chokhmah, that is, the head of Ze'ir; and see there. And in all these names the intent of Rashbi is also to prove that Malkhut too is called so, after that attribute; and this is what he said: this world, that is, Malkhut; and the world to come, that is, Binah.

Behold, it is proven from this that Malkhut, from the side of Binah, is called by the vowel point tzeirei. And tzeirei is kamatz and patach, and the two are proven from it, as is known; for she receives the first three through Binah, and therefore through the tzeirei she receives the kamatz and the patach. And this is his intent in all the vowel points, to explain Malkhut; as in his saying of segol, "a segolta above, a segol below," and likewise with sheva, and likewise with all of them, as we shall explain. "Segol: this is Chesed," etc.: segol is from the language of segulah, treasure, as it is written (Ex. 19:5), "and you shall be My treasure," etc. And treasure indicates love, as a person treasures the thing he longs for and conceals it, so that it will be his treasure; and love is in Chesed. "A segolta above," etc.: it is clear that Malkhut has a manifestation above, a crown over two heads, or below the two heads, which are Gedulah and Gevurah. "Sheva, in this manner," etc.: for ba-esh [by fire] has the letters of sheva, and fire indicates judgment; and likewise "and Sheba fell upon them and took them" indicates the strength of judgment. And the explanation of "It is better that I give her," etc.: and there it was said concerning Rachel, to hint that they too are in Malkhut. "Cholam, from the side of the middle pillar": it has already been explained that sometimes Malkhut is a diadem upon Tiferet, and then she is called "the diadem of Tiferet," and then she is a cholam over the Vav; and then it is said of her, "The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner." And when she is a diadem upon his head, "from there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel": explanation: the sustainer of fathers and sons (Targum Onkelos, Gen. 49:24); for even Jacob draws sustenance from her, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And then she is a precious pearl. And he brought a proof from the verse "a leshem, a shevo, and an achlamah": we have already explained in the Gate of Colors that all the stones are threefold in Malkhut, from the joining of the Patriarchs; and behold, according to this, leshem is from the side of Chesed, shevo from the side of Gevurah, and achlamah from the side of Tiferet.

And further he brought a proof from "and we dreamed," etc.; and the dream is from the side of Malkhut, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 5. "Chirik," etc., "in it is investigation," etc.: its explanation in Netzach we have not found, and it is strange to us; and there is no proof from this passage, for it is possible to say that the intent is Malkhut, and she is intrinsically investigation, for there all things are investigated; and likewise "the terrible ice," for she is ice from the terrible one, who is Tiferet. And if it is explained as Netzach, it will be for the reason that in it is counsel, and the way of counsel is to investigate things. "Shurek," etc.: five bars out of the ten bars, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod [and Yesod is included with Tiferet]; and they are divided, five for the right side and five for the left side. How so? Gevurah, and in it the power of Gedulah; Hod, and in it the power of Netzach included with it: behold four. And Tiferet sometimes inclines to judgment, or at least part of it, which is Yesod: behold five, for the second side of the Tabernacle.

And behold, they are completed through Hod, for it is the last of the five bars that are "for the boards," etc.; and likewise the Heh of Hod amounts to [five]; there remains of Hod ו"ד [Vav-Dalet], which are double-faced, and they are Tiferet and Malkhut. And Hod itself is in the Heh, which is the fifth of the bars; and this is three points, one upon another, bound together. Of it is said, "Ten cubits the length of the board," which is ד"ו, ten. Keresh, kesher: for Hod is the knot and the end of the bars, as we explained. And the Shekhinah is called "the knot of the chariot" because Malkhut binds the chariot and unites it. If so, it turns out in this that kesher, keresh, sharak are all one. Shuruk with Vav, and it is in the Righteous One: for the first, without Vav, comes to kesher, and this, with Vav, comes to kosher [binds]; and he is the one who binds Malkhut with Tiferet; and this is "who holds onto," etc. And likewise he is called seed, for he is the passage of the seed to the bride; and likewise the bride is called "a help meet for him." And all this is through the binder [kosher], which is the shuruk. "The love of your espousals [kelulotayikh]": explanation: the inclusion made in Malkhut by the sefirot, for she is included of all of them, as we explained. Thus far the explanation of this passage.

And behold, it has been explained from his words that the four-letter name is in each and every sefirah, and the names are distinguished according to their vowel points, as explained. And now let us settle this matter for the intellect, saying: all the sefirot are included in the four-letter name, and it is the proper name, as we explained. And because each sefirah includes ten, therefore in each and every sefirah there are ten sefirot. And the truth is that the ten sefirot in Keter are not equal to the ten in Chokhmah, and likewise for all the other sefirot; rather they vary according to the aspect of their action. And likewise Malkhut: just as her actions are hylic, according to her receiving, so her ten sefirot will have unmarked actions. And likewise each and every sefirah has a vowel point indicating the difference of its ten sefirot from those of its fellow, as is proven above. And let the inquirer not imagine that there are literal letters in the sefirot, God forbid; for one who thinks so corporealizes, God forbid and God forbid. But the intent is that there is no vessel that bounds the spirituality of the sefirot except this name. And not that the sefirot are bounded, God forbid, for they are not bounded things, as we expounded at length in the preceding gates; but the intent is that we have no place and no name to title them by, such that that name relates to their spirituality, except these names, one name including all of them. And the holy spirit revealed this name to us: that there is nothing that bounds that spirituality for us except the ten names of the four-letter name, divided according to their vowel points. And there is no doubt that these names are a palace and a vessel receiving and drawing the spirituality of the sefirot, as the Temple was a palace for the Shekhinah. And when we mention one of the titles related to the sefirot and intend the name of their vowel point, that is, the havayah mentioned, one arouses the upper power [text: כת, "class"], unless there is some preventing cause, as will be explained in the Gate of Intention, with the help of Heaven. And by this a person is saved from iniquity, and his heart is steadfast, trusting in the Lord.
And behold, the chapter is complete, and this gate is concluded, with the help of Heaven. Blessed be the Lord forever, amen and amen:
The Twentieth Gate: The Gate of Names.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain the ten names that may not be erased, which we attributed to the ten sefirot in Gate 1, chapter 10. And we have devoted a gate of its own to them because this inquiry does not relate to the preceding one; for in the preceding gate our concern was the proper name [shem ha-etzem], and now our concern will be the other names that may not be erased:
Chapter One:

The ten names particular to the ten sefirot are: Ehyeh for Keter; Yah for Chokhmah; the four-letter name with the vowels of Elohim, like this, יֱהֹוִה, for Binah; El for Chesed; Elohim for Gevurah; YHVH for Tiferet; and according to the opinion of the commentators, YHVH Tzeva'ot in Netzach and Elohim Tzeva'ot in Hod, but according to the opinion of Rashbi, peace be upon him, Tzeva'ot in Netzach and Hod, as we shall explain; El Chai in Yesod, according to the opinion of some, though what is agreed in the Zohar is that the name of Yesod is Shaddai, as we explained in Gate 1, chapter 6; Adonai in Malkhut.

And behold, these names are palaces to the four-letter names that are in each and every sefirah, as we explained in the preceding gate; as if we were to say that the spirituality bounded or inscribed in the name Ehyeh is a palace to the spirituality inscribed in the name YHVH with the vowel kamatz, and both are in Keter. And so with each and every name: they are like the body to the soul, in relation to the four-letter names that are in each and every sefirah. For these names that may not be erased are a garment to the four-letter names. And there is no wonder at this thing; for in the book Berit Menuchah he explained ten names of the four-letter name with known vowel points, and for each and every vowel point explained known lights, explained and specified, each one by a known name; and certainly all the words of that delightful book are words of the living God, said by the holy spirit or received from the mouths of great men.

And behold, those luminaries explained in each and every one of the names are a garment to that source. And likewise the matter is that the subtle self of the sefirah is a portion of the four-letter name that is unified in all ten sefirot.

Further, the ten sefirot branch out into a hundred branches, ten branches for each one of the sefirot; and those branches that branch out are a garment in which the principal sefirah, the spirituality, is clothed. And what branches out further from the ten branches is a garment to the self, the ten branches.

And behold, the ten branches are titled by the four-letter name with a known vowel point. And the branches that branch out further are a palace to their source, and they are titled by a name that may not be erased; and because of its distance from the source it is bounded by the derivation of an action, for whatever is nearer than its fellow is holier than it. And therefore the four-letter proper name has no vowel point at all, but is simple, having no derivation in it. And when it is filled, its vowel points will be like this: יוד הא ואו הא [the vowels are not reproduced in this text]; and they are nine vowel points, nine sefirot: four on the side of the Vav from here and four on the side of the Vav from there, which are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Chesed; Tiferet, the firmament, the Vav that separates between water and water, between judgment and compassion; and beneath it Gevurah, Netzach, Hod, Yesod. And the letters themselves [without the vowel points] are hinted at in Malkhut, which is the one that receives the vowel points, as we explained in the preceding gate. It turns out that the derivation of these vowel points is not a derivation; rather, on the contrary, it added concealment upon concealment, and indicated by its vowel points that they are more concealed than the letters; for the letters are judged by their form, which is not so with the vowel points, but they are concealed, and they are like the manifestation of Yods.

And behold, when we vowelled the proper name, it indicated more concealment; but we learned from this the vowelling of the proper name, like this: יהוה [the vowels are not reproduced in this text], to indicate a concealed secret, but one that spread out in measure; and from its spreading out it produced for itself a palace, by branching into its branches, and its branches were related to names indicating actions, which are the vowel points, as we explained. And nevertheless they are not composite vowel points that would indicate the pronunciation of the word, because of their great concealment still; rather they are names vowelled with equal vowel points (that is to say, the ten names of the preceding gate), to indicate a unity that is uniform and far from change, but not like the preceding source. And when it branches further into third branches and is clothed in them, like the snail whose garment is of itself, then it is pronounced in letters, which are Ehyeh, Yah, etc. But excluded from this rule is the name of Tiferet, which in all its garments is clothed in the four-letter name that hints at Tiferet among the names that we are explaining in this gate, the name mentioned in the passage of Rashbi from the Tikkunim in the preceding gate. For that name is a palace to the self of the Name, and it is a soul to this name that we shall explain. And therefore the four-letter name did not come in the Torah vowelled all with cholam, for this indicates subtlety and great concealment; but it came with the vowels of Tzeva'ot, like this: יהוה [the vowels are not reproduced in this text], for this name hints at Tiferet, which is a palace to the name vowelled all with cholam; and by its composition (that is to say, with vowel points that are not equal) it indicates that it branches out from its source. And although Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that this name is called chashak, cholam sheva kamatz, the hint is to Malkhut, which receives from the three Patriarchs; and these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, folio 41): "When she is vowelled from the side of kamatz, she takes from Chesed; and when vowelled from the side of sheva, she takes from Gevurah; and when vowelled with cholam, she is from the side of the middle pillar." Thus far its words.

This is no wonder; for we are compelled to say that he explained Tiferet in Malkhut. For this is his way throughout the Zohar: that the four-letter name written throughout the Torah hints at Tiferet; and he does not contradict himself. Rather, what must you say? That it is called [so] in Malkhut, in the union of Tiferet, "And the Lord is in His holy palace." And the hint of this is that Malkhut receives from her husband, whether from the side of Gedulah, or from the side of Gevurah, or from the side of himself. And the witness to this is that the name Adonai has exactly these vowels, and the four-letter name too is called by the name Adonai. And although in the name Adonai he added, for in place of the sheva there comes sheva-patach, on the contrary, from there is a proof: for in the addition of the patach, which is like a Vav, a Vav is hinted at in it, which is Tiferet, in place of the four-letter name itself; and this is true and correct, and there is no doubt in it. And the reason why the sheva precedes the kamatz in the vowelling of the Name, since the sheva is in Gevurah and the kamatz in Chesed, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained elsewhere in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 4), on the matter of "anyone whose fear of sin precedes his wisdom"; and these are his words: "And so too he put first the sheva, which is fear, in the name YHVH, before love, which is kamatz, compassion. Sheva is from the side of Gevurah: 'For by fire will the Lord judge.' Kamatz is from the right: 'and the priest shall take a fistful [ve-kamatz].' Because one ascends in holiness and does not descend; and because of this they put the 365 negative commandments, which are fear, before the 248 positive commandments, which are love. This is what is written, 'This is My name forever, and this is My remembrance' (Ex. 3:15): 'My name' [shemi, 350] with Yah [15] is 365; 'My remembrance' [zikhri, 237] with Vav-Heh [11] is 248." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: judgment everywhere is bestowed upon by, and receives from, compassion; for the female is judgment and the male compassion, as explained in the Gate From Below to Above. And because of this it is necessary to put fear, which is from the side of the female, judgment, before love, which is compassion. And likewise the Yod of Adonai comes before the Yod of YHVH: for the one is at the end of the word, below, at the beginning of the entry, and the other above, at the end of the ascent; and the reason is that one ascends in holiness and does not descend. And therefore one must put fear, which is the negative commandments, before the positive commandments, as it is said (Ps. 34:15), "Depart from evil and do good"; for the 365 negative commandments are from the side of the female, and the 248 positive commandments from the side of the male. And this is what the Torah said, "This is My name forever [written le-'alem, 'to conceal']," etc. And there it speaks of the unique name: "My name" with Yah, which are the letters of the male, amounts to 365.

And behold, "My name" is in Malkhut, and to mention the attribute of day at night it is necessary to mix Yah with her. And "My remembrance" [zikhri], which is the male [zakhar], with Vav-Heh, which are the letters of the female, amounts to 248; and we unite "My remembrance" with Vav-Heh to mention the attribute of night in the day. And the four-letter name is divided into two parts, Yah and Vav-Heh, the one male and the other female. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 51, folio 86b), and these are his words: "For all was created and set right by the name YHVH, which is et ha-shamayim, 'the heavens.' And the secret of the thing: Yah in the heavens; this is what is written, 'Yismechu Ha-shamayim, Let the heavens rejoice' (Ps. 96:11); Vav-Heh in the earth, 'Ve-tagel Ha-aretz, and let the earth be glad' [the initial letters spelling YHVH]." Thus far its words.

Explanation: et ha-shamayim are Tiferet, which is called heavens, and Malkhut, which is called et, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, with the help of Heaven. And there is no wonder at Vav-Heh being in the earth and Yah in the heavens; for the intent is that in the heavens is the effluence of Chokhmah and Binah, which are Yah, and it receives from them and bestows upon the earth its own effluence and the effluence of the receiver that is fitting for her, and these are Vav-Heh. And close to this matter is in the tradition of the Gaonim on the secret of the writing of the four-letter name and its engraving, and these are its words: "The instruction of the Gaon to his disciples: that the writing of each and every letter is in the form of three points; and he divides it into three heads, and divides each and every head into three points, until the whole number of the points amounts to twenty-four, in the number of twenty-four inner forms, to the number of the twenty-four books of prophecy: twelve bestowing and twelve bestowed upon, twelve giving and twelve receiving; and they are in the secret of 'the tribes of Yah, a testimony to Israel' (Ps. 122:4). And this is its drawing:

And each and every point has three heads. And the three holy letters with their crowns amount to the number of the hidden name, which is Mah [45]; and with the last letter, all of them amount to the number of the honored name designated seventy-two." Thus far its words.

Behold, from their words it is certainly implied that half of the Name receives effluence from its other half, in the manner of male and female. And the rest of their words will be explained from what we shall explain in the Gate of Particulars of Names, on the name of seventy-two, with the help of Heaven. And let us return to our subject: that the name written in the Torah is Tiferet, but not the self of the four-letter name mentioned in the preceding gate, chapter 4. For that name is vowelled with cholam, and the name of its garment is the four-letter name mentioned in the Torah, whose vowelling is chashak; and this name is a garment to it, just as the other names are garments to the four-letter name. And a proof of this is found in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 42, folio 79), and these are its words: "There is no sefirah in which there is not YHVH, יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א. And so all must be gathered into it in every place, for all the names are titles of it." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: there is no sefirah in which there is not the four-letter name, and also in its filling, to hint at the general and the particular, as we explained in the preceding gate, chapter 4. And therefore the one who directs his intention is obliged to bring his intention, in all the words of the prayer, to the four-letter name, as we shall explain in the Gate of Intention, with the help of Heaven. And this he meant in saying "And so all must be gathered," etc.; and he gave a reason for the thing: for even the other names are titles of the four-letter name. And likewise the four-letter name that is in Tiferet is clothed in the four-letter name with the vowels chashak, and that is a title to it. And there is no wonder how it is possible for a four-letter name to be a title to a four-letter name when their letters are equal. The parable: just as we do not wonder at two human beings, equal in beauty and in strength and in splendor and in glory, that the one's wisdom is greater than his fellow's, for all is according to the drawing down of spirituality that his father drew upon him at the time of the coupling, more than his fellow; so the letters: upon this one more spirituality was obliged than upon its fellow, from the Master of the will, may He be blessed. And just as intention is needed to draw down the soul for the newborn at the time of the coupling, so the writer needs intention in the writing of the letters. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in tractate Gittin (folio 54) that any Torah scroll in which the mentions [of the Name] are not written for their own sake is worth nothing. And likewise our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (in tractate Kallah, chapter 5): at the time that he writes the Name, even if the king greets him he should not answer him. And all this is so as not to cut the holy channels and the spirituality drawn by way of the writing of the letters; and all is according to the drawing down fitting for it. And all this will be explained in the Gate of Intention. And therefore it is already possible, and not far-fetched, that letters may be alike and equal, and these be holy and those not holy. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, have already said (ibid.) that if he needed to write the Name and intended and wrote Yehudah, and did not put the Dalet in it, he erases it; and even though it would be fit to write the Name there, since the intention was to write Yehudah, it was not sanctified. And all the more so may we say that there are letters whose holiness exceeds letters like them; and all the more so when they are distinguished by their vowel points, for the vowel points of the inner name are cholam, and of the name of the garment chashak. And the explanation is that it corresponds to the three Patriarchs, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, which is an aspect in Tiferet, which includes the three Patriarchs in itself. And likewise the hint in its vowel points is "was, is, and will be," and this is "[the Lord] reigns, [the Lord] reigned, [the Lord] will reign," which are the three Patriarchs, as explained in the Tikkunim many times. And all this is in the four-letter name that is a palace to the inner one, as we explained.

And behold, there are found in the sefirot, besides the proper name that we explained, three further divisions, and they are: havayot, names, titles. And the havayot are the ten havayot mentioned in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. And the first to reveal this is the author of Sefer ha-Orah, in his introduction, and these are his words: "Know that all His holy names mentioned in the Torah all depend on the four-letter name, which is YHVH, may He be blessed. And if you say: but is not the name Ehyeh the root and the source? Know that the four-letter name is like the trunk [nof] of the tree, and the name Ehyeh is the root of this tree, and from it roots take root and branches spread out to every side; and all the other holy names are like branches and twigs drawn from the trunk of the tree, and each one of the branches makes fruit after its kind." Thus far its words.

And the explanation of his words: all the names that may not be erased depend on the four-letter name, and from it they spread out, and from it they draw sustenance. And according to his words he raised a difficulty: why should they not depend on the name Ehyeh, which is in Keter, which is the root and the stock, as they depend on the four-letter name, which is not so [exalted], for it is in Tiferet? And on the basis of this question of his he gave a fine answer: that the name Ehyeh is the stock of the tree and its root, and the name YHVH is the trunk of the tree.

And behold, according to his words, the branches spread out from the trunk, not from the root, as is known: for Keter is the root, and because of its great concealment the branches do not spread out from it; and Tiferet is the trunk, from which the branches spread out; and likewise Tiferet is from the language of porot, branches; and likewise the six extremities branch out from it. And indeed his words are the words of the living God. But for us the difficulty still stands in its place, put in another way, and it is this: even according to his words, it does not prevent the name Ehyeh from being greater and more praised than the four-letter name, except that the branches do not branch out from it; and the four-letter name is in Tiferet, and although its praise is great, it is not like the name Ehyeh, which is the root of the tree. If so, why is the four-letter name, which is in Tiferet, not pronounced by its letters? (And may the Compassionate One save us from the opinion of those who say that Keter is a branch of Tiferet; for in our eyes this belongs only to those who lay hands on the very self of the Emanation, who overturn the bowl on its mouth and cut among the saplings, God forbid.) But when we recall what we set out in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, at the beginning of chapter 1, the matter will be well settled for us. For in Keter too the four-letter name is concealed with the utmost concealment. And these names, although their holiness is great and they may not be erased, are nevertheless palaces to the havayot, as we explained. And because of the concealment of Keter, no name at all is revealed in it that bounds and defines its spirituality by its pronunciation, as do the four-letter name and the other names. But the pronunciation of the name Ehyeh indicates concealment, for its explanation is "behold, I stand ready to be [and to be revealed]." And the intent is that although we say "the sefirah Keter," it is not because there is any apprehension in it at all, but because it is to be revealed below, in Chokhmah and Binah. And so the Gaonim explained that the meaning of Keter is the language of waiting, from the language of (Job 36:2) "Wait [katar] for me a little, and I will show you." And the intent is: do not delve into it, for there is no apprehension in it, and its apprehension is in the other sefirot. If so, it turns out that its pronunciation is the cause of its exaltedness and its concealment, as we explained. But if the four-letter name were pronounced by its letters, it would show that the Emanation is apprehended, and this is not fitting because of its great concealment. And therefore we pronounce it by its palace; for the apprehension of Tiferet is in Malkhut, as in the matter of (Hab. 2:20) "And the Lord is in His holy palace; hush [has]," the number of heikhal, the number of Adonai [65] (see in Asis Rimmonim and in Pelach [ha-Rimmon]).

And this preliminary will be further explained in chapter 2, with the help of the Rock. And now that we have set out this matter concerning the essence of the names, we come to the explanation of each and every name by itself, with the help of Heaven:

On the name Ehyeh. This name they related to the sefirah Keter. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained its meaning in Sefer ha-Shem, and these are his words: "The word Ehyeh indicates head and end. The Alef indicates His precedence, and there is no Alef without the concealed Heh; and Yod-Heh indicates the wisdom of Solomon. Further he said [that the principal of the Name] is Alef-Heh, and it is concealed; and therefore it is not mentioned in any blessing, for Moses did not reveal it to the elders." Thus far its words (see in Pelach [ha-Rimmon]).

And behold, his words are clear: that the name Ehyeh indicates "I am the first and I am the last" (Isa. 44:6); for the Alef, in the Supernal Keter, indicates His precedence and His being first to the Emanation. And the first Heh is concealed in the Alef, for there is no pronouncing of Alef without Heh. But Yod-Heh indicates Malkhut, for she is last of all the sefirot and she is the end of the Emanation.

And behold, the principal of the Name, which indicates Keter, is Alef-Heh, and it is concealed, etc. Further, the one who speaks by the mouth of a maggid wrote that its four letters correspond to the four letters of the four-letter name. For the Alef corresponds to Yod. How so? The thorn of the Yod of the Alef is in Keter, indicating its subtlety and its concealment; and the body of the Yod indicates its own self and the pure thought that spreads out; and the middle Vav of the Alef indicates the spreading of the channels from Chokhmah to Binah; and the lower Yod of the Alef is the manifestation of Binah cleaving to Chokhmah. And the Heh hints at Binah in her place, for it is open below, to bestow upon the rest of the Emanation beneath her, and it is open above with a subtle opening, to receive from Keter, and wide below, to bestow upon the whole spreading out. And the Yod in the middle corresponds to the Vav in the four-letter name; and behold, it is the beginning of the four-letter name that is in Tiferet, as is known. And the last Heh corresponds to Malkhut, for it is open below to bestow and open above to receive the upper subtlety, and wide below as well, to receive all the prayers and to raise them up by the subtle side, in subtlety. Thus far the words of the maggid, and we have abridged his language. And concerning this name we have found in the Zohar, parashat Acharei (folio 65a), and these are its words: "He said to him: If it pleases my Father, behold, I have heard concerning what is written, 'I will be that which I will be' (Ex. 3:14), and I have not grasped it. He said to him: Elazar my son, the companions have already established it; and now all is bound up in one word. And the secret of the thing is thus: Ehyeh: this is the inclusion of all. For when the tracks are enclosed and not separated, and are included in one place, then it is called Ehyeh, an inclusion, for all is enclosed within it and not revealed. After the beginning has gone out from it, and that river has become pregnant to draw all forth, then it is called asher ehyeh, that is to say, 'therefore I will be': Ehyeh is ready to draw forth and to beget all. Ehyeh, that is to say: now I am the inclusion of all, the inclusion of all the particulars. Asher ehyeh: that the Mother has conceived and is ready to bring forth all the particulars and to reveal the supernal Name. Afterwards Moses wished to know the particular of the matter, what it is, until he explicated and said Ehyeh: this is the particular, and here it is not written asher ehyeh. And we have found in the book of King Solomon: asher: in the binding of bliss, with the supernal palace, companionship is found; as it is said, 'Happy am I [be-oshri], for the daughters will call me happy [ishruni]' (Gen. 30:13). Ehyeh: that she is ready to beget. Come and see how it descends from grade to grade, etc., so that the Holy One, blessed be He, might show Moses the knot of faith. At first, Ehyeh, the inclusion of all, enclosed and not revealed at all, as I have said; and your sign is 'And I was [va-ehyeh] beside Him as a nursling [amon]' (Prov. 8:30), and it is written, 'Man does not know its value' (Job 28:13). Afterwards He brought forth, etc., and that river, which is the supernal Mother, conceived and is ready to beget. And He said asher ehyeh: ready to beget and to set all right. Afterwards it began to beget, and it is not written asher, but Ehyeh, that is to say: now all will go forth and be set right. After all went forth and each and every one was set right in its place, He left all and said YHVH: this is the particular, and this is the sustaining. And at that hour Moses knew the secret of the holy Name, enclosed and revealed, and cleaved to it as other human beings did not cleave. Happy is his portion. Rabbi Elazar came and kissed his hands." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: Rabbi Elazar heard the words of the delightful companions explaining the name Ehyeh asher ehyeh as being in Keter, Chokhmah, Binah: explanation: the first Ehyeh in Keter, asher in Chokhmah, Ehyeh in Binah. And it was not settled with him; for it is forced to say that the name Ehyeh should be equally for Binah and for Keter, and besides this, that the word asher should be in Chokhmah. And therefore he asked his father and said, "I have not grasped it": explanation: that it was not settled with him. And his father, Rashbi, peace be upon him, answered him, "all is bound up in one word." And the explanation: do not wonder that the name Ehyeh is related also to Binah, for all is one matter and one way, as will be explained. "Ehyeh: this is the inclusion of all": explanation: at the beginning of the Emanation, before the spreading out of the sefirot, the Emanation was included in Keter, and there, in the manifestation of Keter, Chokhmah and Binah were revealed, that is, "a point that includes three drops," as explained in the Zohar and as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And when we said that the first three were revealed, the intent is not an essential revealing; but the intent is some revealing, explanation: they came into being there in a concealed manifestation.

And behold, while Keter is included in this inclusion it is called the first Ehyeh in the verse. And this is what he said, "Ehyeh: this is the inclusion of all": explanation: the inclusion of the Emanation before the spreading out, in the concealment of the first three, somewhat revealed, in a complete union. And this is what he said, "for when the tracks are enclosed": for this is the concealment of Chokhmah in Keter, and there the paths [netivot] are concealed. And he called them tracks [shevilin] because tracks are narrower and subtler than paths; and while they are in Keter, not only were they not in the category of paths, but only of tracks, but even as tracks they were concealed and enclosed. "And not separated": it is known that the paths are called "wonders [pel'ot] of wisdom." And one of the explanations of the word pel'ot is from the language of (Deut. 17:8) "If a matter be too hard [yipale]," whose sense is distinction and separation; and the reason is that the paths are distinct, each one from its fellow, and are divided into thirty-two in Chokhmah. And therefore he said that because Chokhmah is concealed in Keter, the paths were not distinct from one another; and this is "and not separated." And it has already been explained that the revealing of the paths that are in Chokhmah is through Binah; and because of the concealment of Binah in Keter, since she had not yet been emanated, therefore they did not spread out into Binah, but were included in one place, that is, in the Chokhmah within Keter; and this is what he said, "and are included in one place." And it is possible to explain "and not separated" [itparshan] from the language of explanation [perush]: and the intent is that they were not explained, that is, by their spreading out into Binah; for Binah is the explanation and elucidation of Chokhmah, as is known. And all this inclusion, which is the inclusion of the entire Emanation while it is included in Keter, is called by the name Ehyeh. And the name Ehyeh, according to this, is in Keter, inasmuch as it hints at the whole Emanation included within it before its spreading out hither and thither; and this is what he said, "then it is called Ehyeh, an inclusion, for all is enclosed within it and not revealed." Explanation: "then it is called Ehyeh," that is to say, Keter, which is an inclusion, as we explained, for in it the whole Emanation is included; and this inclusion, "all is enclosed and not revealed": explanation: enclosed and concealed in relation to Keter, which is always enclosed, even after the Emanation; and in relation to the rest of the Emanation concealed in it they said "and not revealed," explanation: its manifestation was not revealed at all. "After the beginning has gone out from it": explanation: after the emanation of Chokhmah and its spreading out; and Chokhmah is called "beginning" [shiruta], as we explained in Gate 3, chapter 7, with the help of Heaven. "And that river became pregnant": explanation: Binah, which is called river. And behold, after the emanation of Chokhmah, Binah; and Binah is pregnant with all the sefirot of the circuit within her, for in her was the order of the Emanation: for Keter emanated Chokhmah, and within her all the eight remaining sefirot; and Chokhmah emanated Binah, and within her all the seven remaining sefirot, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And the seven sefirot within Binah are called her pregnancy; and now her emanation and her pregnancy are all one. And therefore he said, "And that river became pregnant to draw forth": explanation: she was filled with the sefirot, to emanate them and draw them to their place. And he called Binah "river" to indicate the will to draw forth, as we explained. "Then it is called asher ehyeh": it is known that the pregnancy of Binah and her filling are through Chokhmah; and Chokhmah and Binah are included in asher ehyeh, as he goes on to explain. "That is to say, therefore," etc.: it was difficult for him that, according to his words, the first Ehyeh indicates inclusion and concealment, as we explained, and the second Ehyeh indicates revealing and drawing forth; and how is it possible that equal words should indicate opposite matters? To this he came to settle each and every word according to its matter and its measure. And this is what he said, "that is to say, therefore, Ehyeh": explanation: the first Ehyeh, "therefore Ehyeh": explanation: "Ehyeh is ready to draw forth and to beget all." The intent is that the first Ehyeh is to be explained as the first person of the future: I will reveal and draw forth the matter in the Emanation, but I do not yet begin to be drawn forth. And although the word Ehyeh indicates future being, the intent is not that it is destined to be revealed; rather the intent of the word is to indicate to us that it is full of, and includes, the whole Emanation that is destined to be revealed. And this is why it is impossible to say this matter except by the word Ehyeh, which indicates: I am included with the whole Emanation that is destined to be revealed. And the intent is not that it is literally destined to be revealed; but the intent is: I am full of the whole Emanation that is destined [to be revealed]; and this is the word Ehyeh. And this is why he went on to say: "Ehyeh, that is to say: now I am the inclusion of all, the inclusion of all the particulars": explanation: the inclusion of the whole Emanation, which is the particulars of the sefirot.

And behold, he intended two things in his language by "that is to say." The one is the explanation of the word, whose intent is to say that it is destined to be revealed; and this is what he said, "Ehyeh is ready to draw forth and to beget all." And because the intent is not that it wishes to draw it forth, but the intent of this word is to tell us that in it is included the Emanation destined to be revealed, and there is no word that would include this except this word, this is what he said: "now I am the inclusion of all, the inclusion of all the particulars": explanation: the intent is only to make known that it is the inclusion of the Emanation that is destined to be revealed through Binah, not through it. But asher ehyeh is the spreading out of Chokhmah and Binah to emanate; and the explanation of "that the Mother has conceived and is ready to bring forth all the particulars and to reveal the supernal Name": explanation: asher is a language of preparing and readying, and so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained. And the intent is that the upper Ehyeh was readied and prepared to be revealed; and this is what he said, "and is ready to bring forth all the particulars," that is, the particularity of the sefirot, the world of the circuit, which are revealed through Binah, as is known; "and to reveal the supernal Name": explanation: the concealed Ehyeh. And this is asher ehyeh: explanation: the concealed Ehyeh, ready to be revealed.

And behold, asher ehyeh is Chokhmah and Binah, for both of them are included in the word asher, as we shall explain, with the help of the Name. "Afterwards Moses wished," etc.: explanation: he wished to know the Emanation itself, in its place below, in the place of its particularity; and Ehyeh was said to him a third time, indicating the Emanation in its place. And this is what he said, "the particular of the matter, what it is": explanation: the Emanation itself; and Ehyeh was said to him a third time; and this is "until he explicated and said Ehyeh." And because it was difficult for him that Ehyeh is not the particular but, on the contrary, is the inclusion of the Emanation, as we explained above, therefore he answered and said: since asher ehyeh is not said here (for it would have been fit to say "Ehyeh asher ehyeh has sent me," and he says only "Ehyeh"), learn from this that he said a new word; and this is the spreading out of the Emanation and its particularity. For if you do not say so, he should have said "Ehyeh asher ehyeh has sent me to you"; rather, learn from this, as we have said. "And we have found in the book of King Solomon," etc.: he brought a proof for the explanation of asher ehyeh, that is, Chokhmah and Binah, from Solomon, who explained the words in the Aramaic language. And kitura, explanation: knot and union; and kastira, explanation: palace; and so is its translation in the Jerusalem [Targum] (Gen. 25:16), "These are the sons of Ishmael… by their courts and by their encampments [u-ve-tirotam]": u-ve-kastrotehon. And now he came to explain the word asher, and said, "in the binding of bliss": explanation: in the union and binding of Eden, which is Chokhmah, with Binah, which is the supernal palace, that is, the supernal kastira; "companionship," explanation: complete union, "is found." It turns out that the word asher, and its matter, is that the aspect that Chokhmah has, to bestow upon Binah, is called asher; and Binah too is called asher in her first aspect, which cleaves to Chokhmah. And this is what Leah, who is Binah, said: "Happy am I [be-oshri], for the daughters will call me happy [ishruni]": explanation: the effluence bestowed upon her from Chokhmah, by which she is made happy among the daughters, that is to say, among the other sefirot. And Ehyeh is an aspect of Binah that is destined to be revealed and to beget the sefirot. "Come and see how it descends from grade to grade," etc.: he now comes to prove the matter of Ehyeh: that although they are three equal names, they indicate different matters. And he proved this from the verses: for the Name, may He be blessed, intended to make known to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, to understand and to contemplate the order of the Emanation, grade after grade; and therefore it is proven that the three Ehyehs are not equal, but each one is a grade below its fellow. "At first, Ehyeh," etc.: explanation: the first Ehyeh, its intent is Keter; and the reason is that it is the inclusion of all, as we explained above. "And your sign: 'And I was [va-ehyeh] beside Him as a nursling [amon]'": explanation: Ehyeh is beside Him, that is to say, beside Keter; there all is nursed, and grows, and is blessed, and is watered, and is raised up. "And likewise it is written, 'Man does not know its value'": explanation: there is none who knows the value of Chokhmah, and it is not apprehended even "in the land of the living" (Job 28:13), which is Binah; and the reason is that the emanation of Binah had not yet been, for all was included in the concealed Keter, as we explained above. "Afterwards He brought forth," etc.: explanation: after the emanation [of Chokhmah], Chokhmah emanated Binah; and this is the explanation of "afterwards." "He brought forth that river, which is the supernal Mother," etc.: he called her river and mother. He was compelled to say river to hint at the drawing that is drawn forth like a river; and he called her mother to hint that she is full and pregnant, like a mother who is pregnant and full of embryos. "And He said asher ehyeh: ready to beget," etc.: as we explained asher. The intent is that she is ready to beget the concealed Emanation, and this is Ehyeh. And we have already found that the prefixes Alef-Yod-Tav-Nun serve for the infinitive and the imperative; and likewise Ehyeh, although these prefixes are future, serves as an infinitive, which is the beginning of the beings, which are not yet completed. And this is "afterwards it began to beget": explanation: the beginning of the revealing, before the revealing is entire, is also called Ehyeh. And because this is very forced, for the principal explanation of Ehyeh is "ready to beget," as we explained above, for this he proved the matter from his saying Ehyeh, and not saying Ehyeh asher ehyeh. And what he said, "that is to say: now all will go forth," etc.: explanation: a partial revealing, as one who says of the part: now the matter will be completed entirely. And this is what he said, "and all will be set right": explanation: will be set right entirely; for it had already begun to go forth and was not yet completed, and therefore was not set right; and at its completion all will be set right, the inner as well. And the explanation of "will go forth": that is to say, something of the concealed will go forth. "After all went forth and each and every one was set right in its place": that is to say, while the Emanation and the order of the grades was not yet completed, it was included in the name Ehyeh; and after the tikkun of all the grades was completed, then it was included in the four-letter name. And this is what he said: "After all went forth and each and every one was set right in its place, He left all": explanation: He left the names Ehyeh and said YHVH. And therefore the name Ehyeh is no longer mentioned in the Torah, for it indicates a lack of completion and of tikkun and of the emanation of the grades; and therefore it is not fitting that the name Ehyeh be mentioned any more, but only the four-letter name; for the name Ehyeh was mentioned in the Torah only to teach the order of the grades and the order of their emanation. But afterward He said (Ex. 3:16), "Go and gather the elders of Israel and say to them: Thus says YHVH"; for it is not fitting that any but the four-letter name be mentioned, which indicates the bond of the worlds and their emanation from above to below, from beginning to end, as we explained in the preceding gate, in the explanation of the four-letter name, which includes all the grades in its four letters. And although the name Ehyeh indicates ten sefirot, as we explained above, nevertheless this is only while they are included above, before their emanation, as we explained; and the four-letter name indicates the spreading out of the branches and the twigs, as is proven. And therefore the name Ehyeh relates to Keter, not to show the revealing of something but to indicate the concealment; and the four-letter name does not relate to it, because it indicates the spreading out of the branches and the twigs. And therefore the four-letter name is not pronounced: because its pronunciation indicates revealing, and whoever does so outside the King's palace, "that soul shall utterly be cut off" (Num. 15:31). But the name Ehyeh, on the contrary, indicates concealment by its pronunciation. And we have already expounded this matter at length in the preceding chapter. And he said, "YHVH: this is the particular," etc., as we explained. "Moses knew the secret of the holy Name, enclosed and revealed": explanation: before the Emanation, when it was concealed, and also after the Emanation, after the revealing; and he apprehended the concealed and the revealed grades, which no one born of woman apprehended. Thus far the explanation of the passage. And from it the explanation of the name Ehyeh has been explained to us, each one according to its place and its matter. And although it emerges from this passage, and from the rest of the words of the commentators, that the name Ehyeh is in Keter, and so we explained above, in the preceding gate, that the four-letter name is concealed in it, this is according to the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Idra of Naso. But at the time of his passing he agreed that there is no name at all in Keter, and the four-letter name is from Chokhmah downward. And in the Tikkunim he explained the matter and said that no name can properly be said of Keter; but it is called by the four-letter name from the side of Chokhmah, and by the name Ehyeh from the side of Binah. And the thing itself is explained from his words: for Chokhmah has a manifestation above, in Keter, and likewise Binah; and this is the revealed part of Keter, not Keter itself; and therefore, if a name is titled to it, it is what is revealed of it. And the reason that Chokhmah is in the name YHVH, which is the particular, and Binah in the name Ehyeh, which is the inclusion, whereas it would have been fitting to be the reverse: that matter is explained by what he explained in the Idra, that Chokhmah is the brain and Binah the membrane that covers the brain. It turns out that Binah conceals and hides Chokhmah; and therefore Chokhmah is in revealing and Binah in concealment (that is to say, in the name Ehyeh, which conceals the light of Chokhmah; see Asis Rimmonim). And along the way we have gained that two names Ehyeh are in Binah, except that this one is her manifestation in Keter and that one is her manifestation in Binah itself; and the third name is her manifestation after the beginning of the Emanation. And we know that the inquirer will not be able to grasp our words in truth except from what we explained in the book Or Yakar, in Gate 5, on the Idra, in the matter of brain and membrane:

The name related to Chokhmah is the name Yah. The explanation of this name is a language of strength, as in (Song 8:6) "a flame of Yah [shalhevet-yah]," whose explanation is "strong." And the hint in this name is to Chokhmah, and it would mean the strength of the concealment of this attribute. And she is hinted at in the Yod of this name, and its Heh is a hint of Binah. And so it is explained in the Zohar (Vayikra, folio 11a), and these are its words: "The second, Yah: because Chokhmah brought forth Heh, and it is enclosed in it, and it never separates from it; and this has been established, as it is written, 'And a river goes forth from Eden,'" etc. And the explanation: for two reasons the Heh is related to the name of Chokhmah, although only the Yod hints at Chokhmah. The first, because the emanation of the Heh, which is Binah, is from Chokhmah.
