And because this would not suffice (for even while she was within Chokhmah she was not united with her in the letter Heh, because of her concealment, but in Yod; and according to this reason it would have been fitting for the name of Chokhmah to be two Yods, the one of Chokhmah and the second of Binah concealed in her), for this he said that even after her emanation she never separates from her, for Chokhmah and Binah are always united and do not separate. And the proof is from the verse "And a river goes forth from Eden"; and Eden is Chokhmah, and the river is Binah. And the verse said "goes forth" and not "went forth": the intent is that it is always going forth and is always with her. And so he also explained there (folio 10b), and these are its words: "The first, Yah: because Yod includes Heh, and Heh goes forth from Yod; because of this Chokhmah is called Yah." Thus far its words.

And it is clear. And just as Binah is included in Chokhmah for this reason, so Chokhmah is concealed in Binah; except that in Chokhmah it is Yah, that is, Yod over Heh (explanation: Yod, and within it Heh is included), but in Binah they are Heh-Yod, from below to above (explanation: Heh, which is Binah, is the principal, and within it Chokhmah, which is Yod, is included). And it is clear.

And behold, according to this, it will be found that when we unify Chokhmah in the name Yah, it indicates her being unified with Binah, as we explained, and Binah included with her. And there is no doubt that, since this name indicates the union, Keter too is included in it, that is, the true unifier, as we explained in the preceding gates; it turns out that this name includes the first three. And we wish to copy a question that the Rav asked in Sefer ha-Orah, Gate 9, concerning this name, and these are his words: "And now we need to make known to you why the first two letters of the Name are read by themselves, and the last two letters are not read by themselves. You already know what we explained concerning the secret of the union of the two Hehs of the Name: the first Heh, which is Binah, is united with the seven lower ones, and the last Heh, which is Malkhut, is united with the nine upper sefirot through Yesod. The upshot: the principal of all ten sefirot is the first three, from which all the seven lower ones are bestowed; and if, God forbid, the drawings of the three are cut off, then there is the destruction of the House and the burning of the Temple and the exile of the children among the nations. And therefore half the Name, which is Yah, can be read by itself; and half the Name, which is Vav-Heh, cannot be read by itself, for it is cutting among the saplings, etc. And when you read Yah, the last half of the Name is also included in it, and there is no cutting there. And likewise the secret of Yah, יו"ד ה"א, in its filling amounts to the whole [26], and its half is like its whole. And this is in the first half of the Name; but the last half of the Name, its standing and its sustenance is in the secret of Yah." Thus far its words.

And it is a correct reason, and his words are clear. And what he wrote, "And when you read Yah, the last half of the Name is included in it": explanation: for Heh is the likeness of ד"ו, and it is double-faced, which are Vav-Heh. And likewise they are included in יו"ד ה"א in their filling, which amount to 26; it turns out that all is included in the concealment of Yah. Thus far. And with this pleasant preliminary you will understand the matter of (what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, Shevuot folio 35) [Hebrew: "wrote"]: El of Elohim and Yah of YHVH are among the names that may not be erased, but Shin-Dalet of Shaddai and Tzadi-Bet of Tzeva'ot may be erased: for the reason that the letters hint at the joints of the chariot, as the four letters of the four-letter name hint at the known joints; and in this way all the names in their letters.

And behold, when he wrote Yah and El, there is nothing cut off there, and the spirituality can cause its Shekhinah to dwell, for it is a vessel receiving the spirituality without cutting; therefore it is sanctified and may not be erased. But one who wrote part of the other names, it is not sanctified, for it is not a complete vessel in which the spirituality may dwell, because of the cutting; since the vessel does not hold the whole, the spirituality does not dwell in it; and therefore they may be erased:

The third name, related to Binah, is YHVH with the vowels of Elohim. And there is one who explained the reason for this name and its vowels: because from Binah the double-faced ones, Tiferet and Malkhut, were emanated; and Tiferet is called YHVH and Malkhut is called Elohim; and to indicate the emanation of both of them it is written in this way and read in that way. But in the Zohar, in many places, another explanation of it is found, and these are its words (Vayikra, folio 10): "The second, YHVH that is called Elohim: because that river is compassion, and because judgments are aroused from it, the letters of compassion are written and the vowels are Elohim." And its explanation is clear: that her principal is compassion, but nevertheless from her the judgments of Gevurah are aroused, as explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 8 and 9, with the help of Heaven. And because of this YHVH is written, which is the name of compassion; and because through her bestowal judgments are aroused, it is read with the vowels of Elohim, in Gevurah. And for us these two explanations do not disagree, and all is one matter. For it is known that Malkhut is female, and her principal is judgment and her inclination is to judgment; and Tiferet is male, its principal compassion and its inclination to the side of compassion. And judgment and compassion are exactly male and female, and that is right and left. And when we come to be precise in the matter of the four-letter name, we find for it in the Torah two vowellings and two titles: the first, the vowels of Tzeva'ot, and its title Adonai [and so its vowels are like the vowels of Adonai] (and although in the name Adonai a patach is added with the sheva, we have already resolved this in chapter 1); and the second is the vowels of Elohim, and so is its title. And in the Tikkunim he said: a sword in its sheath. For YHVH is a sword, as he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, folio 43): "Yod is the head of the sword; Heh-Heh, the two edges of the sword; Vav, the body of the sword; Elohim, the sheath of the sword." And what is to be examined is that when its sheath is in Binah, which is Elohim, then it is judgment, and when its sheath is in Malkhut, then it is compassion, as he concludes there; and this is certainly a wonder, for the reverse would be reasonable. And likewise there is a further difficulty: for we have seen that Rashbi, peace be upon him, relates the name Ehyeh to this attribute in most places, and not the name YHVH with the vowels of Elohim, and elsewhere it appears the reverse. And it seems that this can be resolved, and the matter will be understood thus. When the name YHVH is unified with Malkhut, in the secret of (Hab. 2:20) "And the Lord is in His holy palace; hush," then it is certainly complete compassion, and its vowels and the vowels of its palace are all one matter. And it indicates its receiving from Gevurah and from Gedulah, in the secret of the embrace, which we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance (chapter 21), and afterwards it indicates its bestowal: and this is sheva from the side of Gevurah, and kamatz from the side of Chesed, and cholam, that is, its bestowal, the secret of the complete union. And because this union is through Netzach and Hod, for there is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, as explained in the gate mentioned, therefore its vowels are also in the secret of Tzeva'ot, to indicate one union and one bond; and then it is complete compassion. But when it withdraws to Binah, in the secret of "Woe!" [hoy], explained in the Glossary of Titles (see there), and then judgment is performed, and the world is destroyed and judgment comes to be, then its sheath is Malkhut, which is called Elohim, in the secret of the strong judgment bestowed upon her to take vengeance; and therefore it is not in the secret of union but in the secret of withdrawal. And because of its withdrawal to Binah in the secret of "Woe!", as we explained, the name Ehyeh relates to Binah, to indicate Tiferet withdrawing and being clothed in the secret of this palace and being inflamed in the secret of judgment. And concerning the vowels of the name YHVH, we have found that one of the pious ones who speak by the mouth of a maggid explained in the name that its vowels are sheva, segol, cholam, chirik. And the reason: the sheva, it is already known that it is the secret of judgment, as we shall explain in the Gate of Vowel Points; and the Yod is the secret of Keter and Chokhmah; and because through the compassion of both of them judgment is subdued, therefore the Yod is with sheva and segol, to hint at the first three in the secret of compassion. And the Heh, which is Binah, is with cholam, to hint at her drawing sustenance from the upper source, which is Keter. And the Vav is with chirik, although it is judgment, hinting at the bestowal of the effluence below according to judgment, in the secret of the Vav. Thus far his words, though not exactly his language, for the love of brevity. And what is found in the Zohar on something like this, that the reason the last Heh has no vowel point is that it has no known action, but according to her receiving so her action changes: this turns out to be a fine reason for most of the havayot, which have no vowel point at all on the last Heh. And concerning the matter of the reading being by the name Elohim and the writing by the four-letter name, and not the reverse: besides what is explained from his words, that it is a sword in a sheath, and we have never seen a sheath inside a sword, Rashbi, peace be upon him, nevertheless has a very honorable reason, explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 8 and 9; for there we expounded at length on the explanation of this name, with the help of Heaven, for there it fell to our lot:

The fourth name is related to Chesed, and it is El. And we wish to copy here the words of Sefer ha-Orah, Gate 7, on this name, to show that his words on this are certainly words of tradition. And these are his words: "For three hundred and ten camps of the attribute of judgment spread out in the world, all of them drawing sustenance from the side of the great judgment, full of wealth and possessions to pay out to all who are worthy, and full of good reward to pay the righteous; and of this it is said (Prov. 8:21), 'to cause those who love Me to inherit substance [yesh, 310],' which are three hundred and ten. And all these camps spread out in the world to complete judgment upon the sinners: some of them plunder, some of them despoil, some of them wound, some of them uproot, some of them afflict with plagues, and some of them make ill; and they are those who complete judgment upon each and every creature according to what was decreed in the court on high, not less and not more. And above these, from the attribute of judgment and Gevurah, there is the attribute of compassion and Chesed, El, and it is a tenth of the camps called yesh. And if there is a righteous one in the world who knows how to direct his intention to this attribute called El, then it goes out from its place, and all the 310 camps flee and are scattered, and the whole world is in compassion, and judgment has no power to act. And for this reason we say 'God, King, who sits,' etc., to quiet the power of judgment," etc. Thus far the abridgment of his words.

And behold, the reason is found why it is called El [31]: corresponding to thirty-one camps of compassion. And in the Zohar, parashat Terumah (folio 166), it is explained there that there are 310 kinds of lights, of which it is said, "to cause those who love Me to inherit yesh": two hundred and seven of them are in Chesed, and they are the number of or [light, 207], and one hundred and three are in Gevurah. And the language of the passage and its explanation we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, under the entry or. And it is possible that it disagrees with the words of Sefer ha-Orah; and it is possible that both this and that exist, for "there is no number to His troops" (Job 25:3). And as for what he explained, that Chesed is indignant at and rebukes the camps of Gevurah, so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, parashat Tzav (folio 31a), and these are his words: "El, everywhere, is the light of supernal Chokhmah, and it stands in its sustaining, etc. And were it not that this El is aroused in the world, the world could not stand one hour before the mighty judgments that are aroused in the world every day. This is what is written, 'These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created [be-hibar'am]' (Gen. 2:4): do not read be-hibar'am but be-Avraham; by the arousal of Abraham they stand. And when Abraham is aroused in the world, all those judgments that are found every single day, he thrusts them outside, and they do not stand before him. This is what is written, 'And God [El] is indignant every day' (Ps. 7:12): it is not written 'is met with indignation' or 'is the object of indignation' every day, but 'is indignant': every single day, when judgment is found, he thrusts them outside, and he stands and sweetens the world; this is what is written, 'By day the Lord commands His Chesed' (Ps. 42:9). And were it not for this, the world could not stand even one moment. And therefore all stand in the protection of Abraham," etc. Thus far its words.

And what he said, "El, everywhere, is the light of Chokhmah": explanation: even in the place where it is written (Isa. 9:5) "El gibbor," the explanation is not "God who is mighty"; for since El is Chesed, there is no might and indignation in Chesed, which is El. But the intent is El, which is Chesed, and likewise Gibbor, which is an attribute by itself. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained there explicitly, and we have abridged the passage so as not to lengthen. And in this way will be understood what we say in the standing prayer, "the great, the mighty God [ha-El ha-gadol ha-gibbor]": the intent is not God who is great and God who is mighty, but the intent is "the great God," and likewise "the mighty," and the word "mighty" returns to what he opened with, "our God and God of our fathers." And now the language will be understood that is found in the Zohar (there, folio 30b) and in many places in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, folios 65, 66): when he explains the name El as being in Chesed, he proves the matter from the saying "the great God" as a proof. And if the explanation of the matter were "the great God" and likewise "the mighty God," what does he prove from "the great God," which is Chesed? It is also in Gevurah, for it says "the mighty"! Rather it is certainly as we explained. And it turns out, according to this, that the words of Rabbi Moshe [de León] are rejected, who wrote that El gibbor is in Gevurah, as we shall write, with the help of Heaven. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, said explicitly there, concerning El gibbor, that they are two attributes, as we explained. But concerning the name El, it is fitting that we explain that Chesed is not called El except in the secret of the first aspect, which is illumined by and receives from Chokhmah. And this is what he said, "El is the light of Chokhmah": explanation: the first aspect, which shines from Chokhmah. And so he explained in parashat Acharei (folio 65b), and these are his words: "El: this is the light of supernal Chokhmah, and it is called Chesed." Thus far its words.

Further, in parashat Lekh (folio 94): "And what is Chesed? Chesed is El, which comes and goes forth from Chokhmah," etc.; "El is the light of Chokhmah," etc. And it is clear. And now it is implied of itself that it is impossible that Gevurah should be called El gibbor. Although in other places Chesed is called by the name of judgment and judgment by the name of compassion, judgment is not related at all to the name El; for Chesed is called El in the secret of the aspect that cleaves to Chokhmah, as we explained, and in this aspect only complete Chesed applies. And this is what he said in the passage mentioned above, "El is the light of supernal Chokhmah." And why did he call it "supernal"? Did we not know that it is the supernal Chokhmah? Rather, to hint that in the aspect that cleaves to Chokhmah judgment does not apply, because Chokhmah is supernal, and it is one of the three upper ones, where there is no judging of judgment at all, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 8, 9 and 16, with the help of Heaven. And concerning this name Rabbi Moshe [de León] wrote in Sefer ha-Shem, and these are his words: "This name is adjoined to many titles and many predicates; [I note this] because my intent in this book is to arouse our hearts. This name is called El Elyon [God Most High], and it is for Keter and also for Chokhmah and Binah, which are supernal. And it is called El melekh yoshev [God, King, who sits], and it hints at Binah, which is the king of the whole Structure. And therefore we say in our prayer, at the time of asking for forgiveness and compassion, 'God, King, who sits on the throne of compassion'; and the explanation is that He sits upon Tiferet, which is the attribute of compassion, and conducts Himself with piety, inclining toward Chesed, although we are not worthy of compassion. And when He acts with the attribute of Chesed He is called El gadol [the great God]; with the attribute of Gevurah He is called El gibbor [the mighty God]; and when He performs awesome deeds He is called El nora [the awesome God]; and He is called El olam [the everlasting God], for He is the master of the attributes that are called olam. And El hints at Yesod and at Malkhut, as will be explained. And when it says El without qualification, it hints at this attribute; explanation: strong, as (Ezek. 17:13) 'and he took the mighty [eilei] of the land'; and the verse said (Ps. 22:20), 'O my strength [eyaluti], hasten to my help.' And He is strong in His Chesed and makes His Chesed prevail over judgment and retribution; and He is strong and rules over the height of the attribute of judgment, and holds it back, and is long-suffering, and has compassion. And He is called El Elyon, for He is supreme over the whole Structure in His Chesed and His compassion; and Binah is called Elyon. And the verse said (Gen. 14:19), 'Blessed be Abram of God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth'; and the explanation: blessed be Abram, [who belongs] to Chesed, of God Most High, who bestows good and great kindnesses, and Maker of heaven and earth, Tiferet and Malkhut. El gadol, in pardon and forgiveness, from the side of the greatness of His Chesed." Thus far its words.

And behold, the sage, because he saw sometimes El gibbor and sometimes El olam, and likewise El melekh, etc., found it difficult that these titles should be in Chesed, and said that the word El, when it is in titles, hints many times at Binah. And his words are astonishing; and his difficulties are not so pressing at all that for their sake he should overturn the verses for us. Rather we say that Chesed is what is called El everywhere, whether alone or when it is joined to other titles; as in the matter of El gibbor, where the intent is not "God who is mighty," but the matter is as we explained above in the name of the Zohar. And know that El Shaddai (it is written in the Zohar, parashat Va'era) is in Malkhut; and it is called Shaddai, explanation: that it suffices [she-dai] for the world, enough for their sustenance. And all this is by the power of Chesed, which couples with Malkhut to bestow upon her. And when Chesed attends to Malkhut, the language "And God is indignant" fits in its plain sense, for such is its explanation without qualification. Further, it is possible to explain the verses and the titles in another way: that Chesed itself is called El gibbor when the power of Gevurah prevails over and subdues Chesed and tips the scale-pan of liability against the scale-pan of merit. Or sometimes there will be judgment, and that judgment the cause of compassion, like the plagues of Egypt, which were judgment for Egypt and compassion for Israel; and then El gibbor is called El from one side and Gibbor from the other side. And it is called El olam when it enters Binah; it would mean the El of the upper world. And El melekh yoshev: in the Zohar it explains that "El melekh yoshev," etc., intends Binah, which sits and dwells upon the throne of compassion; and from there is a proof that, because her action and her power are in compassion, the name of Chesed is related to her, because of the joining of Chesed. And the other aspects of the name El that accompany others of the titles and names will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, with the help of Heaven:

And concerning this name Rashbi explained in the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, folio 78), and these are his words: "The second chamber, El: this is the chamber and the hall of the right, in which there is a vision that is concealed and stored away; as soon as it goes out and shines for a moment, immediately it is stored away. El: why is it so called? Alef is the secret of the first light, which includes two lights; and therefore Alef is one. From there is the beginning, to shine and to spread lights to every side; and therefore it is first of all the letters, the beginning of all of them, the inclusion of three that are one. Three lights are included in the letter Alef: one arm on one side and one arm on the other side, Vav in the middle, which includes the two arms of the two sides; and the measure of the middle had to be [that of] the two arms of the two sides, because it takes them, and it alone is in both of them. Alef: fire from this side, water from that side, air [ruach] cuts through in the middle and takes from both sides; and all of them are one. And further: this Alef spreads out and is included in the inclusion of all of them. And since it is included in the completeness of the two sides, by the arousal from below its female is aroused toward it, and the Alef is turned over in another secret, and takes its female below it, and they are joined as one; and then the upper point rests upon it, to show that the upper light, the first point, in the secret of the supernal Shekhinah, rests only in the place where male and female are joined as one. Come and see: 'In the beginning God created et' [Bereshit bara Elohim et]: behold, here four Alefs are joined as one, male and female, in four words: in each and every word an Alef, which is male, and in each and every word one letter, which is female. And in the book of Rav Hamnuna Sava: Bereshit, Adam and his wife; bara, Abraham and his female; Elohim, Isaac and his female; et, Jacob and his female. And if you say, et is the female everywhere: come and see, Alef is male, Tav is female; both are included as one, and the female is seen in completeness, included in the secret of all the letters. And therefore et, although it is female, is in the secret of the inclusion of the male. And therefore there are four couplings here, and everywhere an Alef that is male, which is joined with the female in another letter. Kiryat Arba, because four great appointed ones of the world were buried [joined] there. Lamed: this is the tower that flies in the air, which is a great king; and therefore it is called El. The upper and the middle as one; the upper, and the head of providence, the head of all the letters, as one. El: Alef takes the support of that tower that flies in the air toward it, and with it rises in the Name. Thirty-two tracks there are that go forth from the Torah; they are the secret of ten utterances and twenty-two letters of the Torah; and all of them go forth from the secret of the upper point. The ten utterances are all included in the secrets of the Torah, which is the supernal King, the secret of the Written Torah, the world to come. And twenty-two letters spread out and begin to shine from the head of the first light, in the secret of the union, from which the letters are to be revealed; and from there the letters shine, and Alef rises, the secret of all the letters, in the secret of One." Thus far its words.

"El: this is the chamber and the hall of the right": explanation: that it corresponds to Chesed, which is toward the right, as is known. "In which there is a vision": explanation: because there is no comprehension and apprehension except from Chesed downward; and from Chesed upward, that is, in the first three, there is no apprehension at all, as it is written (Deut. 4:32), "For ask now of the first days," and it is written (Deut. 22:7), "You shall surely let the mother go," as explained in the Zohar (Yitro, folio 93) and as we explained in Gate 8, chapter 15, with the help of Heaven. And because above he spoke of a first hall, which corresponds to the first three, where there is no apprehension at all, he said now of this hall, which corresponds to Chesed, "in which there is a vision": explanation: there is in it comprehension and apprehension. "That is concealed," etc.: explanation: a comprehension that is stored away; for the apprehension of it does not stand, but is revealed and returns and is concealed; and this is what he said, "as soon as it goes out," etc.: explanation: the apprehension of it is like the lightning, shining for a moment and returning to be stored away, in "running and returning" (Ezek. 1:14), as we explained. "El: why is it so called?": the intent is to explain the relation of this name, in its letters, to Chesed. "Alef is the secret," etc.: explanation: the principal of the Alef is in Chesed, and it indicates its union with two sefirot and its inclusion of them, which are Gevurah and Tiferet. "And therefore Alef is one": it was difficult for him that we should say that Alef is the three Patriarchs, since such is its hint. For this he said that the principal of the Alef is in Chesed alone, except that Chesed includes the two, as we explained; and therefore the Alef is related to the matter of one, and this name cannot properly be said of the three. "From there is the beginning," etc.: it was difficult: since the Alef by its explanation entails that it be one and not three, it would have been fitting that we explain that the Alef is in Tiferet, for it itself includes the three Patriarchs, and this matter does not relate well to Chesed. And for this he proved and said, "from there is the beginning"; for Chesed is called reshit [beginning], as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And the reason is that from there is the beginning of the spreading out and the revealing: not of the Emanation, for the Emanation begins from Keter, but the beginning of the branching of the branches and of the spreading out of its boughs to every side; as is known, the first three do not spread out and are not revealed. And if we say that the Alef is in Tiferet, it turns out that the spreading out of the letters begins from Tiferet, not from Chesed, and this is not correct. Therefore the Alef must be in Chesed. And now it is correct: the head of the letters, which are the upper branches that spread out, and the head of the spreading out of the branches, are all one and unified. And this is what he said, "and therefore it is first," etc., "the inclusion of three," that is, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, "that are one": explanation: while they are one, that is, precisely before their spreading out, while they are included in the Alef. And the intent of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in this passage is that the twenty-two letters are all branches from seven sefirot; and when we come to divide them, we find three times seven, which are twenty-one, and one more. This indicates the union of three lines, which are Gedulah, the line of Chesed; Gevurah, the line of judgment; Tiferet, the line of Rachamim; and in each one of them seven branches, which are twenty-one letters; and the Alef, which is head to them, indicates their union in complete oneness in Chesed, which is the beginning of the spreading out.

And the matter of the letters and the branches we will explain at the end of the passage, with the help of the Name. "Three lights are," etc.: he returns to explain the manifestation of the three lines unified in the form of Alef: for the Yod on the right side is Chesed, and the Yod on the left side is Gevurah, and the diagonal line is Tiferet. "And the measure of the middle had to be," etc.: it was difficult for him: granted, according to what he explains further on, that the upper Yod is in Binah, the lower Yod in Malkhut, and the Vav literally in Tiferet, it is well that the two Yods should be related to two points, and Tiferet the Vav that unites them. But according to this explanation, that the one Yod is in Gedulah and the second in Gevurah, what relates to Tiferet in relation to them is only a third Yod; for such is their way: either all three are three Vavs or all three are three Yods. To this he answered that so it was needed: for Chesed is alone, and therefore its measure is a Yod; and Gevurah is alone, and therefore its measure is a Yod; but Tiferet, which unites them, is needed in both of them, and therefore it is hinted at in the diagonal line, in which is the measure of two Yods, to hint that it includes both of them, and in its manifestation is the manifestation of Chesed and the manifestation of Gevurah, so that it can make peace between them. And to prove this matter he explained their matter, that they are likened to fire, water, air. And the matter is that water is cold and moist, and fire hot and dry [and air is hot and moist, therefore it tips the balance], as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 3. And he said, "and all of them are one": explanation: in the form of Alef, to indicate its oneness, a unitary manifestation besides their arbitration. Or it would mean that the two manifestations that he has explained until now in the letter Alef are both one, although he explained them in different words, as we explained. "And further: this Alef spreads out," etc.: he has already explained above that the Alef includes all the letters and the branches; and therefore he returns to explain it in a way that it should include in it the whole Emanation, and further, that it should hint at the coupling, so that the matter of the Lamed in the name El may be explained. And this is "And further, this Alef spreads out and is included in the inclusion of all of them": for until now we said that the Alef includes the three of them in the secret of Chesed; afterwards it spreads out further and includes them in their very manifestation. "And since it is included in the completeness of the two sides": explanation: since the male, which is the body of the Alef, is included in completeness, essentially drawing sustenance from Chesed and afterwards from Gevurah; and therefore the beginning of its spreading out is from Chesed, and further it spreads out and is included also in Gevurah; for such is the way of the male, to begin from the right and finish on the left, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 21, with the help of Heaven. "Then by the arousal from below," etc.: that is, the arousal of Malkhut to the coupling and the union, as we explained there, in chapter 18, with the help of Heaven. "And the Alef is turned over in another secret," etc.: and this is the third manifestation of the Alef, that is, the middle Vav, Tiferet; the upper Yod, Binah; the lower Yod, Malkhut. "And takes its female below it": that is, Malkhut, "leaning upon her beloved" (Song 8:5). "And then the upper point rests": explanation: since it unites with Malkhut, then the upper point rests upon it; and the explanation of "upper point" is Binah; "to show that the upper light," etc., that is, Chokhmah; "the first point," in Keter. And the matter is that in the Yod the first three are included, for it has a thorn above, a thorn below, and its body in its middle, as we explained; and he said that the revealing of all the first three is through Binah, which is called Shekhinah because she causes all the manifestation of the first three to dwell [mashkenet] upon the Structure. And he said that she rests only if Tiferet and Malkhut are unified; and therefore the union must come first, and afterwards "the upper point rests." "Come and see: In the beginning He created," etc.: all this length is because his intent is to say that the Lamed of El is Binah; and against this there is a difficulty, for Binah is included in the upper Yod of the Alef; if so, what further need is there for the Lamed? To this he proved that the Alef, although the female, which is the lower point, is included with it, nevertheless needed another letter to hint at the female, as in the matter of et, etc., as we shall explain; if so, for the matter of Binah too another letter is needed to hint at her. And the matter is that the Alef, in its manifestation, shows all these unions in the secret of Chesed, and it is the secret of the male; afterwards the manifestation of the female needs to be unified, besides the union included in its branches. And close to this is the matter of et, which will be explained further on, with the help of the Name. And in this way it is also resolved concerning the Lamed, and it is clear. "Behold, here four Alefs," etc.: for in each one of the four words there is the letter Alef, which hints at the male, and one letter that is female. How so? Bereshit has in it Alef, male, and Tav, female. Bara has in it Alef, male, Bet, female. Elohim has in it Alef, male, Heh, female. Et: Alef male, Tav female. "And in the book of Rav Hamnuna Sava: Bereshit, Adam and his wife": Adam is Chokhmah, which unites with Malkhut in the secret of (Isa. 44:6) "I am the first and I am the last": Chokhmah at the head and Chokhmah at the end; the Yod of YHVH male, the Yod of Adonai female. And one cannot say that "his wife" is Binah, for then "Kiryat Arba," which will be explained further on as being in Malkhut, would not fit. Abraham and his female, in the secret of the Heh that was added to Sarah. And Isaac and his female, in the secret of (Gen. 24:67) "And Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother." Et: Jacob and Rachel, as is known. "And if you say, et is the female everywhere," etc.: explanation: for et is related to Malkhut everywhere, as is known and as will be explained in the Glossary of Titles; and if so, how do we relate it to the male and the female together? And to this he answered, "Come and see: Alef is male, Tav is female," etc.: explanation: I will always tell you that the Tav alone is the female in the word et, and the Alef is the male; and as for what you say from the word et, the intent is the female in her completeness, that is, in the secret of the male included with her, through whom she shows all the letters. And this is what he explains elsewhere: et is the Torah, included from Alef to Tav; explanation: Malkhut is included in all the letters of the Torah, that is, the powers of the male; for through the male she reveals all the letters. And always et hints: Alef male, Tav female. "And therefore there are four couplings here": explanation: therefore there are found four couples, for otherwise there would be only three; and in the book of Rav Hamnuna Sava he said that they are four.

And further, from the first three it is learned that the males are Alef; if so, how is the Alef of et less than the Alef of bereshit, and likewise that of bara? Rather, what must you say? As I have said, etc. And this is what he said, "and everywhere an Alef that is male," etc. "Kiryat Arba, because they were buried [joined]," etc.: explanation: Malkhut is called Kiryat Arba because she is united in these four places. And the intent is not that Malkhut couples with other than Tiferet; but all is according to the place in which she couples with her husband: sometimes she couples with him in the secret of the union of the coupling of Adam and his wife, which is his hint in the secret of Chokhmah, and sometimes on the side of Chesed, etc.; and it is clear. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim.

Behold, it turns out according to this that the manifestation of the Alef is in Chesed; and it has three manifestations. The first, the inclusion of the three Patriarchs in Chesed in complete union; afterwards a second manifestation, in the secret of its receiving from right and left; afterwards a third manifestation, that is, union with its female, which is Malkhut, the lower point, and Binah resting upon it, which is the upper Yod, in the secret of the first three, as we explained. And along the way we have learned that Abraham and his female are Alef and one female letter. Behold, Alef is related to Chesed, and this is the Alef of El. And now he returns to explain the Lamed of El; and this is what he said, "Lamed: this is the tower that flies in the air," that is, Binah, which flies and hovers over Tiferet, which is called air, as will be explained in the Glossary of Titles. And he called it "a great king": explanation: a king, which is Binah, and it hovers over Chesed, which is Gedulah [greatness], and because of it [Binah] is called "a great king." And that is the Lamed hovering over the Alef, which is in the air and in the manifestation of Chesed. And therefore this attribute is called El, to indicate this deep secret. "The upper and the middle as one": explanation: Binah, which is the upper, [as explained] above in the matter of Binah [dwelling] upon the union, and it is the Lamed, as we explained; and "the middle," that is, Tiferet, which is the middle of the Structure, as we explained. And one cannot explain "the upper" as the Alef and "the middle" as the Lamed, which is the middle of the letters; for according to this, what he says afterwards would not fit, "the upper, and the head of providence, the head of all the letters, as one"; for perforce the "upper" that he speaks of is Binah. Rather it is certainly as we explained. And the reason he said again "the upper, and the head of providence" is to indicate that although he said "the upper" is Binah and "the middle" is Tiferet, nevertheless we shall not deny that the matter of the Alef is precisely in Chesed, because it was the beginning of comprehension, the beginning of all the letters. "El: Alef takes the support," etc.: explanation: because the Alef, which is the union, as we explained, needs the help of Binah, which is the Lamed, therefore Chesed is called by the name El. "Thirty-two tracks there are that go forth," etc.: the intent is to explain two things: first, what he explained above, that the beginning of the revealing of the letters is from Chesed; second, what he said, that the Alef takes support from Binah, as we explained. For this he said: behold, the thirty-two paths are known to be in Chokhmah, and from her outward they spread out; and she is called Torah, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles.

And behold, it is known that these paths are thirty-two, and their details are ten sefirot and twenty-two letters, as explained in Sefer Yetzirah and as we explained in the Gate of Paths, chapter 1; and we copied the mishnah in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 2, with the help of Heaven. And this is what he said, "which are the secret of ten utterances," that is, the ten sefirot, "and twenty-two letters of the Torah." "And all of them go forth," etc.: explanation: their matter is not in Chokhmah, but they spread out from Chokhmah, which is the upper point; it turns out that their principal is from Chokhmah outward. If so, it turns out that when we come to divide them, behold, their beginning is in Binah, and there are ten paths there, for one may not add to her more than ten; and they are the ten utterances. And this is what he said, "in the secret of the Torah, which is the supernal King," that is, Binah; and she too is called Torah, as it is written (Prov. 1:8), "And forsake not the Torah of your mother," "if you call to understanding [la-binah]" (Prov. 2:3). And because it is forced to say that the ten utterances are in her who is called Torah (for, on the contrary, Chokhmah has in it ten utterances and is called Torah, as we explained above), therefore he said "the secret of the Written Torah": explanation: the Torah is not Tiferet but Binah, and she is concealed in the Written, which is Tiferet, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, chapter 22. And this is what he said, "the secret of the Written Torah"; and in this aspect she is called "the world to come," that is, she is bestowed and comes to Tiferet, that is, the Written. And now that we have proven that the ten utterances, which are the first ten paths, are in Binah, if so, the twenty-two letters begin their spreading out from Chesed, and that is the Alef in Chesed. And this is what he said, "and twenty-two letters spread out and begin to shine from the head of the first light," which is Chesed, the first day, "Let there be light," one, as is known. And now, since the head of the paths and their principal are in Binah, if so, the rest of the paths need to receive effluence from their cause; and this is "Alef takes support," etc., which he said above. "In the secret of the union, from which the letters are to be revealed": now he intended to explain the secret of the division of the twenty-two letters among the sefirot. For granted, the ten utterances are in Binah, and it is well, since she includes ten; but the twenty-two, how shall they be divided among seven sefirot, when they have no relation and connection [to them]? For this he said that the Alef is the secret of the union and head to the revealing, as explained above at the head of the passage; for it is not in the category of the letters, since it is the one that unites, and from it the letters shine. It turns out that the Alef is the secret of the oneness of all the letters; and this is what he said, "in the secret of the union, from which the letters are to be revealed": explanation: from the Alef downward is the beginning of the revealing of the letters. "And from there the letters shine": explanation: from it effluence and light flow to shine, because in the Alef the manifestation of all twenty-one letters is concealed, and the Alef is the source for the other letters, as in the matter of the sefirot, as explained in the preceding gates. "And Alef rises, the secret of all the letters," etc.: explanation: Alef rises as the secret of the union of all the letters; as if we were to say that the letters are only twenty-one, and their union and their upper manifestation is the Alef, that is, the gathering of their source; and this is what he said, "in the secret of One": explanation: the Alef testifies of itself that it is the one that unites all the letters; and this is the explanation of Alef, that is, One, unified. And this is what he said above, "and begin to shine from the head of the first light"; and "the head of the light" is the Alef, and from there they shine. And they are divided: seven letters for Chesed, and seven for Gevurah, and seven for Tiferet; and the Alef too is in Chesed, at the head of all of them, shining for all of them, the gathering of all the sources of the letters, as we explained. And there is no doubt that three are in Chesed and three in Netzach and one in Malkhut from the side of Chesed; and likewise three in Gevurah and three in Hod and one in Malkhut from the side of Gevurah; and likewise three in Tiferet and three in Yesod and one in Malkhut from the side of Tiferet. And the reason for three in each and every sefirah is that in it are three lines: the secret of its drawing sustenance from Chesed, and the secret of its drawing sustenance from judgment, and the secret of its drawing sustenance from compassion. And therefore they are also in Malkhut, in the secret of the three lines mentioned. And it turns out in this that they are seven in Chesed and seven in Gevurah and seven in Tiferet, and all is one matter. And the explanation of this passage is complete, and from within it the explanation of the name El is explained:

The fifth name is related to Gevurah: it is the name Elohim. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained concerning it in Sefer ha-Shem, and these are his words: "Elohim is after the name of judgment; for this name is applied to every judge and leader and magistrate; therefore God, may He be blessed, shares in it, and the angels, and the judges, and the leaders of the nations, and the messengers sent to complete the judgment for every judgment and for all that is created and done in judgment: to put to death and to give life, to impoverish and to enrich, to raise and to lower," etc. Thus far its words.

And the explanation: Elohim is a language of judges, as in (Ex. 22:27) "You shall not revile the judges [elohim]," and likewise (Ex. 22:8) "the cause of both parties shall come before the judges [ha-elohim]." And concerning this name Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Song of Songs, from the Zohar (Chadash, folio 78), and these are his words: "The third chamber, Elohim: this is a red radiance that sparkles like gold, a radiance that at times (craves) [shines] and is good, and at times is darkened in a darkness that has no sparkle like (that which was) [gold]. Elohim is the secret of arousal toward the female on that side. This name is in the secret of secrets, for those who know wisdom: for this name is male, and arousal toward the female. By this name all is aroused; and were it not for the arousal of this name, the Righteous One would not be aroused. And although all is judgment, and the Righteous One is from the side of the right, nevertheless his arousal is only from the side of the left. Adam left that side and was aroused by that dross of gold, which goes out from the filth of its smelting. Elohim: Alef is male; lehim is the arousal of the Righteous One, and it is milah [circumcision] with uncovering, without any side of foreskin at all. And this is when this name is mentioned for good, as in 'And God remembered His covenant' (Ex. 2:24), for the covenant is aroused in this secret, and 'God will surely visit you' (Gen. 50:24). On the Other Side, the Torah testified concerning its judgments, for from there the foreskin went forth. At times the female inherits this name, in order to judge the world by that name, the secret of the foreskin, when this Elohim is strengthened above, and that foreskin hardens, and uncovering is not found. And therefore it is for good in the uncovering of the foreskin, for the foreskin is uncovered and passes away, and the secret of the holy covenant is revealed. And all is in the secret of Elohim: for this color turns into several colors, at times thus and at times thus; and this is in the secret of Elohim. Elohim: there are three names. One, the living God, who is the everlasting King; the Elohim of the Fear of Isaac; the last Elohim, and from there they spread out. The Elohim of the Fear of Isaac: its providence is half toward the former sea and half toward the latter sea [Zech. 14:8; el ha-yam, 'toward the sea,' sounding as Elohim]. 'Toward the latter sea': precisely, to be called by this name. And therefore, what it takes from above, it has permission to include the right within it; and when the right is included within it, then it is in joy, and holds onto the lower sea, beneath the head, as it is written, 'His left hand is under my head' (Song 2:6); and then it is called Elohim, for it goes toward the latter sea [el ha-yam]. And this is the third chamber of that supernal King." Thus far its words.

And its explanation: we have already explained in the Gate of Colors, chapter 3, that in Gevurah there are three colors: the one red, or like gold, which is better than red, as explained there. And this judgment is beautiful, like the wine that gladdens and does not intoxicate. And there is wine that intoxicates, in the secret of the strong judgment, and in this there is blackness. And for this he said, "a red radiance that sparkles like gold": that is, the two colors of judgment, which is the beautiful one, which is tipped toward the scale of Chesed. "A radiance that at times shines," in the secret of Chesed and compassion, "and is good." "And at times is darkened": that is, the secret of the dark judgment, which has no beautiful sparkle but burns in the secret of judgment; and not literally black, God forbid, that is, the husk; but its light is not healthy "like gold," explanation: like gold, or like red; but it blackens somewhat, in the secret of the nearness of judgment to the husk. "Elohim is the secret of arousal toward," etc.: explanation: the name Elohim is in the secret of the gladdening wine, in the secret of the judgment that arouses the female to the coupling, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 21, with the help of Heaven.

And behold, the male too needs it, for the male too receives from the right and the left for the embrace and the craving; except that the male puts the right first, which is not so with the female, who puts first her receiving for the embrace from the side of the left; therefore her arousal from Gevurah, the name Elohim, is related to her. And for this he said, "the secret of arousal toward the female on that side," that is to say, on the side of the aspect of this name. "This name is in the secret of secrets, for those who know wisdom": explanation: although at first glance it seems that there is no matter of compassion in this name but judgment, nevertheless there are awesome secrets in it for those who know wisdom, as will be explained. "This name is male," as he concludes: Alef is certainly male; nevertheless it is arousal toward the female, as we explained, for by the power of this name is the arousal of the female. "By this name all is aroused": explanation: whether Tiferet, or Malkhut, as we explained, or Yesod, as he concludes. "And were it not for the arousal of this name, the Righteous One," etc.: explanation: the arousal of Tiferet, although it is in Gevurah, is nevertheless also in Chesed, which arouses it; and likewise Malkhut is aroused by the power of Chesed; but the Righteous One is not so: for were it not for this name it would not be aroused at all, for all its arousal is in this. And it turns out now that those aroused are three, Tiferet, Malkhut, Yesod, and they are in gradation: the first, Tiferet, but the principal of its arousal is from Chesed; and Malkhut, the principal of her arousal is from Gevurah, and nevertheless the arousal of Chesed is mixed with her; but Yesod, all its arousal is in Gevurah; and this is the order of their gradations. "And although all is judgment," etc.: explanation: he said that its arousal is in Gevurah and it has no arousal from Chesed; and against this there would be a difficulty, for on the contrary, its principal is toward the right more than Malkhut, and so it would be required that, just as the arousal of Malkhut is also from Chesed, so the arousal of Yesod should be with the help of Chesed; nevertheless, as to the matter of arousal, it has only the arousal of Gevurah alone; and there is a difference between the matter of its essence and its arousal. And there is no difficulty from here against what we explained in Gate 1, chapter 2, in the name of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that Yesod is toward the left; for Rashbi, peace be upon him, was precise there and said "the Righteous One takes to the left," and did not say "the Righteous One is left," but "takes," that is, its arousal. Further, it is possible to say that both this and that exist; and what he says here, that it is right, is in relation to Malkhut, as we have explained. And what he said, "nevertheless his arousal is not," etc.: he returns to explain the matter of the two colors mentioned above, and said that the first Adam, at the time that he came upon Eve, did not "know" with that knowing from the side of the beautiful color, the color of gold and of redness, but from the side of the blackening, that is, the dross of the gold, as he concludes. "Elohim: Alef is male": explanation: male from the side of Gevurah, as we explained in the preceding chapter, that Alef too is male from the side of Isaac and his female. "Lehim is the arousal of the Righteous One": the intent is that Alef is the secret of the male, that is, the manifestation of the body; and lehim means milah [both 85], that is, the covenant drawn from the body, that is, the arousal drawn from this name to the Righteous One. "And it is milah with uncovering, without any side of foreskin": for behold, the husks and the foreskins are three; and when one cuts the first, which is doubled into two, the third is folded inward; and it is the third husk of the nut, which is almost eaten; and this is called chazir [swine], because He is destined to restore it [le-hachaziro], as we shall explain in the Gate of Substitutes. And he said, "with uncovering, without any side of foreskin," that is to say, even this thin foreskin will not be mixed into the joy of this name; rather, on the contrary, it is diminished by its power. And he needed this length because he said lehim, which means milah, and that implies without uncovering; for this he said "with uncovering, without any side of foreskin," even the thin husk, as we explained. "And this is when," etc.: explanation: when there is the redness and the gladdening wine, then it is "And God remembered," etc., and likewise "God will surely visit," etc.; for all this indicates compassion. But when this name is in the secret of the blackening judgment, then the Torah testified explicitly concerning its judgment, as "and the anger of God was kindled against them," and the like. "For from there the foreskin went forth": explanation: from the side of this aspect is the source of the beings of the husks. "At times the female inherits this name": explanation: Malkhut is at times called Elohim; and he said that when Malkhut is called Elohim, then it indicates the strong judgment, to judge the world. For when this name is the male, it is compassion most of the time, but when it is female, then it is judgment. And it is not required that the name in the female always be judgment, but most of the time; for sometimes too, when it is in the female, it is compassion, as will be explained. "For this color turns into several colors": explanation: either Elohim meaning judges, that is, harsh judgment, or the explanation of Elohim as Alef-milah, which is arousal to compassion, as we explained. And all depends on the matter of the husk: if there is a husk, it is judgment and there is no milah, because the judgment is performed through the spoiling angels; and when there is no foreskin and husk, then Elohim, which is Alef-milah, is compassion. "There are three names": he wished to explain the secret of the matter of judgment and compassion briefly. And it is that the source is Binah, and she is "the living God" and "the everlasting King," in the secret that she hovers over and reigns over the world, which is the days of the circuit, etc. "The last Elohim": explanation: Malkhut. "And from there they spread out": explanation: from there is the spreading out of the judgments and of the powers that rule over judgment, good and evil. "And therefore, what it takes from above": explanation: when half of it is "toward the former sea," which is Binah, through her bestowal upon it it becomes Elohim, a complete name: for when Gevurah draws sustenance from Binah, Chesed, which is El, is included with it, and it bestows upon Malkhut, that is, ha-yam [the sea]; and through this Gevurah acquires the name Elohim: El from Chesed, and -him [the letters of ha-yam] from Malkhut. As it is written, "His left hand is under my head": that is, the arousal of Malkhut, as explained above. And we have expounded at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 21.
And behold, the explanation of the passage is complete, and from it the explanation of the name Elohim in Gevurah is explained:

Because we have seen that this name hints at Binah, as in the matter of the thirty-two [mentions of] Elohim in the Work of Creation, and further, as explained in the preceding chapter, we have seen fit to copy here a passage from the Zohar (in the Introduction, Bereshit, folio 2a), in which Elijah, of blessed memory, explained to Rashbi, peace be upon him, the matter of this name in Binah, and he explained it to the companions. And these are its words: "At the time that the Enclosure of all enclosures wished to be revealed, He made at the head one point, and this rose to be thought. He formed in it all forms, He engraved in it all engravings. And He engraved within the holy enclosed lamp the engraving of one enclosed form, holy of holies, a deep structure that goes forth from within thought, and it is called Mi [Who], the beginning of the structure. It stands and does not stand, deep and enclosed in the name; it is called only Mi. It wished to be revealed and to be called by a name, and it clothed itself in a precious garment that shines, and created eleh [these], and eleh rose in the name. These letters joined with those, and it was completed, and it rose in the name Elohim. And until it created eleh, it did not rise in the name Elohim. And those who sinned with the calf said, concerning this secret, 'These are your gods, O Israel' (Ex. 32:4) (etc.). And just as Mi is joined with eleh, so is the name, which is always joined; and by this secret the world is sustained." Thus far its words.

And the words of this passage are concealed, great in quality and small in quantity, according to the one who said them and according to the measure of the hearer. And this is its explanation. "At the time that the Enclosure of all enclosures": the Ein Sof is called "the Enclosure of all enclosures," and is concealed with the utmost concealment. For the sefirot are enclosed and concealed, but they are revealed, each one, to the attribute beneath it; as if we were to say that Chokhmah apprehends Keter, and all the more so Keter apprehends Chokhmah, although both of them are concealed with the utmost concealment; and likewise for the other sefirot. It turns out according to this that, although the sefirot are enclosed and concealed, they are apprehended by the concealed ones like them; which is not so with the Ein Sof, for it is concealed with the utmost concealment, until it is concealed even to the concealed ones; that is to say, even in relation to the subtle and concealed ones near to it, it is concealed. And this is the explanation of "the Enclosure of all enclosures": explanation: enclosed and concealed from apprehension even to the subtle ones that are enclosed and concealed. And let this rule be handed to the discerning also where "the Concealed of the Concealed" is found; for "the Enclosure of enclosures" and "the Concealed of the Concealed" are all one matter. And although in some places it is found that he gives these titles to Keter, this is no wonder, because at times the Ein Sof is concealed within it; it would mean that it is at times unified with its root, until it is fitting, because of its concealment, that these titles be related to it. And since it has come to our hands, we will explain it, with the help of Heaven. "Wished to be revealed": explanation: at the time that the will arose before Him to emanate His Emanation; for the Emanation is the revealing of the Emanator, as we explained in the preceding gates. "He made at the head one point": explanation: Yod. The head is Keter, for it is head to the whole Emanation, and within Keter was the matter of the emanation of Chokhmah. And this is "He made at the head," which is Keter, "one point," which is Chokhmah. And even if we explain the word "head" according to its plain sense, that is, "at first," we are compelled to this explanation; for always the beginning before the point is Keter, since above Keter "beginning" does not apply, for the reason that a beginning has an end. "And this rose to be thought": it has already been explained in the preceding gates that the nature of the word "thought" in divine things is the manifestation in which all the emanated ones are formed; that is to say, just as thought is that in which a person judges the matters and actions that he wishes to perform, so in divinity, the place in which the beings that went forth into actuality, as a revealed manifestation, were formed before their emanation is called thought.

And behold, this matter does not relate to the Supernal Keter, because of its great concealment; for no form of a being at all can properly be said of it, although they are included in it, but they are concealed with the utmost concealment, so that we cannot title that matter with the word "thought" at all. But of Chokhmah the word "thought" can properly be said in this way, for the reason that it is the first array of the four arrays that we arranged in the Order of the Emanation, chapter 5, with the help of Heaven. And this is his saying here in this passage, "and this rose to be thought": explanation: this and not Keter, for of Keter it cannot properly be said, for the reason we explained. And although it is found that Keter is sometimes called thought, this is for the reason that the thorn of the Yod can properly be said of it, which is a small Yod, to indicate the concealed subtlety, included in the name of an array that is subtler than the array of the Yod, which is in Chokhmah, as we explained the matter of the arrays in the letters of the Name in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name; or because of the manifestation of Chokhmah within it, for it is the inclusion of the Emanation in great subtlety; for of Keter itself it cannot properly be said, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Idra, and as we explained in the book Or Yakar, in Gate 5, with the help of Heaven. And above Keter it is called, remotely, "the Thought of all thoughts," because there the thoughts are [only] in relation to thought, as their concealment there is known, as we explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. And now the matter is correct for us, that Keter is the head, and Chokhmah the brain and the thought, for this reason: for in the brain the forms of thoughts are formed, but in the head nothing is formed within it; for there the Emanation is not revealed at all, even as a kind of thought; but Keter surrounds and includes Chokhmah, like the skull that surrounds and crowns the brain. And he said, "and this rose to be thought," whereas it would have been fitting to say "and this is thought": the reason is that first Chokhmah was emanated without the Emanation being revealed in it, and afterwards she needed to be raised up to receive power from the One who gives power to all, so that all the formed things and the Emanation might be revealed within her. And this is "and this rose": explanation: it was raised above, in the aspect of Keter itself, to its aspect that is unified with the Emanator, so that it would be related to thought, that is, the forming of the Emanation in its own self. "He formed in it all forms, He engraved in it all engravings": explanation: we have already expounded at length in the Gate of Self and Vessels on the matter of the sefirot and the self that spreads within them; for two things were emanated, the sefirah and the soul within the sefirah, as explained there. And therefore in relation to the soul he used the language of "forming," that is, the language of form, related to the soul of the sefirot and their light and their Self that spreads out; and the language of engraving, which is the densifying of things and their being more revealed, he used in relation to the vessels, which are like a body to the self of the sefirah. And this thing cannot be grasped except by much and subtle study in the gate mentioned. "And He engraved within the holy lamp," etc.: explanation: the language of carving and engraving refers to the vessels, and "form" to the form and the soul, as we explained. And the sense of the language is thus: and He engraved an engraving, which is a garment to the soul and the concealed form. And the matter is that the holy lamp is the Supernal Keter, and in it Binah is engraved; and she is called "holy of holies" for the reason that she is holy even in relation to the seven sefirot, which are holy ones; explanation: even to the holy ones she is holy by comparison, in the way that we explained "the Enclosure of enclosures." And the reason he called her here "holy of holies": the intent is that she is full of the lower holy ones; explanation: for she includes all the lower holy ones and sefirot, as is known; for in her the whole Emanation is included, for she is the second array of the Emanation, for she is exalted and concealed above all of them, and surrounds all of them, and is their cause. "A deep structure," etc.: explanation: although we said "And He engraved within the lamp," etc., the intent is not that she is literally in Keter, but the intent is within the thought that is in Keter. And so that we should not err and say that the form of Binah was within Chokhmah alone, for this he said "within the holy lamp": the intent is within Keter, explanation: within the thought that is in Keter. And so that we should not err that she is literally in Keter, he said "a structure that goes forth from within thought": how so? Within the Chokhmah that is within Keter. And he called her "a deep structure," etc., for the reason that Binah is the second array, which reveals the first array; for this he said "a deep structure," for in her the whole Structure is included, but nevertheless she is in depth and in concealment. "That goes forth from within thought": explanation: for the name Mi cannot properly be said of Binah while she is still concealed in Chokhmah; for Mi is the comprehension of something about which the question can fall, to say "Who is this?"; and this is the matter of Mi, even though there will be no answer to this question. And this is to say that the name Mi can properly be said only of Binah as she goes out from the inner aspect that is in thought. And this is the language of "that goes forth from within thought." And the explanation of "from within": the intent is that it goes out from the inner, essential aspect of thought to the outer aspect, at the junction of Chokhmah with Binah, and there it is called Mi; for when it is revealed essentially, to her own self, the name Mi cannot properly be said of her. And this is what he said, "the beginning of the structure; it stands and does not stand," etc. The intent: "it stands," for it is the beginning of the Structure, which is the circuit from Chesed downward; and not essentially, as when she is the beginning of the Structure, but while she is not yet revealed; and this is what he said, "and does not stand": explanation: revealed, and not essentially, as a matter that is already near to emanating the Structure but is concealed. And this is what he said, "deep and enclosed": for it has already come into being, but the being is deep, in the aspect of Chokhmah, which is called "depths"; for then she is enclosed, and it is not fitting that she be called by a name that entails any affirmation, bounding the thing within the definition of some matter; but rather Mi, whose explanation is: although it has already been emanated and has gone out from the depths of thought to a revealed aspect, the affirmation of a name still cannot properly be said of it, but only Mi, a question without an answer. "It wished to be revealed": explanation: it wished to be revealed through the emanation of the days of the circuit; for they are the revealing of Binah, as is known, for the seven days are those that reveal the things concealed in Binah. "And to be called by a name": explanation: for he already said that while she is concealed she has no name at all, and Mi is not a name but concealment; but when she is revealed, a name defining the thing with some definition can properly be said of her. "It clothed itself in a precious garment that shines": explanation: this is the manifestation of the upper Heh and its form, as we shall explain in this gate; and it is her garment in relation to Chesed and judgment and compassion; and she clothed herself in this garment to emanate Chesed and judgment and compassion, which are the totality of the whole circuit. And he said "that shines" because this is the revealed aspect that bestows upon the six extremities; and this is the language of "that shines": explanation: shining for the seven lamps that are beneath her. And this aspect is called Imma, explanation: mother of all the lower ones. Therefore now, when he comes to explain the matter of her aspect in relation to the Emanation, he said, "that shines, and created eleh": explanation: the circuit included in Chesed and judgment and compassion. And they are called eleh [these] because they are more revealed than her aspect called Mi, which is a question without an answer; but now, in eleh, they are an essential revealing, like a man who points with his finger and says "these." "And it rose in the name Elohim": explanation: for the aspect of Mi is not like the aspects of "head" and "point" mentioned above; for above, although it is revealed more, the concealed aspect is not revealed, but another manifestation, denser and more revealed than the preceding, becomes dense and is revealed. Which is not so in the aspect of Mi; for the aspect of Mi itself is revealed through eleh. And this is "and it was completed, and it rose in the name Elohim." And how is this name? For through the word Mi being unified with eleh, and with them, the name was completed and rose in the name Elohim. And this is "and it rose in the name Elohim." And he was precise in saying "and it rose in the name," explanation: it rose into a name; and he proved the matter, that until now there was no name. For the aspect of Mi itself rose in the name Elohim and is revealed; that is, the letters of Mi were joined with eleh in the name Elohim. For otherwise it would have been fitting that it be called eleh alone; but because the letters of Mi were joined with eleh in the name Elohim, Mi itself was revealed through eleh, and through this the name Elohim was completed, Mi in eleh. "And until it created eleh, it did not rise in the name": it was difficult for him: granted, if we say that the aspect of Mi was never revealed, in the manner of the other aspects that the Emanation has before its revealing, which are always concealed, it is well; for in relation to the concealed aspect we find Mi in Scripture throughout the Torah. But according to what he explained, that the aspect of Mi itself was revealed through eleh, it turns out that now, according to the truth, the aspect of Mi is before the Emanation and is not now, after the Emanation; and it is difficult, for we find it in the Torah. And it is forced to say that what was and is not now in manifestation, what was, was, like the name Ehyeh, which is mentioned only three times because what was, was, as we explained in chapter 2. And to this he answered, "And until it created eleh," etc.: explanation: for now too, at times, the aspect of Mi is examined in relation to what it was before eleh was in manifestation. And this was the iniquity of the makers of the calf: for they separated between Mi and eleh, and did not wish to join them and unite them and to reveal Mi upon eleh; if so, in this respect Mi is examined alone and eleh alone. And this is a criminal iniquity; for after they were unified they never separated, for the aspect of Mi is always unified and revealed through eleh, and there is never a time when they separate. "And just as Mi is joined with eleh," etc.: explanation: for it was difficult for him that the proof from the iniquity of the calf is no proof; for it is possible that Mi may be found without eleh (and then the language of the many verses in which we find Mi is well), and the iniquity of the makers of the calf was that they separated between eleh and Mi, for eleh without Mi is never found in any way, and this was their iniquity, that they separated eleh from Mi; but Mi without eleh may indeed be examined as found. For this he proved the reverse and said that just as eleh is impossible without Mi, so Mi is impossible without eleh. And this is "just as Mi is joined with eleh, so is the name," etc.: explanation: just as at the time of the arising of the will it was that Mi should be joined with eleh, so it is necessary that it be always. "And by this secret the world is sustained": he intended the sweetness of the honeycomb, pleasant words. For if eleh were required to be with Mi, and Mi not required to be with eleh, the world would turn out to be destroyed: for Mi would withdraw above, and at times eleh would be found without Mi, and the world destroyed; for eleh is not able to rise to Mi beyond its measure. Therefore the Emanator impressed [this], that Mi be joined to eleh in such a way that it will not be raised up [away from it], for [then] eleh would lose its degree; and therefore in the secret of Mi unified with eleh the world is sustained. And the reason of this matter is that "the Shekhinah among the lower ones is a need on high," as is explained in many places in the preceding gates. Thus far the explanation of the passage. And the upshot of the passage is that the name Elohim in Binah hints at two aspects, unified, revealed the one through the other. The first aspect is called Mi, and it is her aspect in relation to her standing in the last aspect that is in Chokhmah, at the time when His simple will arose to emanate her. And the second aspect is her aspect at the time when it arose before Him that Binah should emanate Chesed and judgment and compassion (see Asis Rimmonim); and this aspect is called eleh, as we explained.

And behold, when the Structure, which is the seven days of the circuit, is unified with Binah, that is, the union of the two aspects, Binah is called Elohim, whose explanation is Mi eleh in union. This is what we have drawn up concerning the explanation of the name Elohim in Binah from this delightful passage. But concerning the name Elohim in Malkhut, it is further hinted at there in the passage mentioned, and we will copy it here, with the help of the Name:

Further, on the name Elohim, there is a passage there (in the Introduction, folio 2a), and these are its words: "Rabbi Shimon said: Accordingly the heavens and their hosts were created by Mah [What], as it is written, 'When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers,' etc. (Ps. 8:4), and it is written, 'Mah [How] majestic is Your name in all the earth, who has set Your glory upon the heavens' (Ps. 8:2): 'upon the heavens': it is so as to rise in the name. For He created a light for His light, and this was clothed in that, and it rose in the holy name, the supernal Heh. And therefore 'In the beginning God created': this is the supernal Elohim. For Mah was not so, and was not built; but at the time that these letters eleh are drawn from above to below, and the Mother lends the Daughter her garments and adorns her with her adornments. And when does she adorn her with her adornments as is fitting? At the time that all the males appear before her, as it is written, 'before the face of the Lord [ha-adon] YHVH' (Ex. 23:17). And this is called Adon, as it is said, 'Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord [adon] of all the earth' (Josh. 3:11). Then the Heh goes out and the Yod enters, and she adorns herself in the garments of the male, facing every male in Israel. And the other letters Israel draws from above toward this place: 'These [eleh] I remember' (Ps. 42:5): I mention them with my mouth and pour out my tears in the desire of my soul, in order to draw these letters; and then 'I would lead them [eddadem]' from above 'to the house of God [Elohim],' to be Elohim like it. And with what? 'With the voice of joy and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping festival.'" Thus far its words.

And the explanation: "Accordingly the heavens," etc.: according to what had come to our mind in the Zohar in explaining the matter of Mi eleh, explained in the preceding chapter, it was difficult why the heavens and their hosts were created by Mah, as it is written, "When I behold," etc.; for what relation has the title Mah, Malkhut, to the matter of the creation of heaven and their hosts? But according to what Elijah explained to Rashbi, peace be upon him, on the name Elohim, whose explanation is Mi eleh, as we explained in the preceding chapter concerning the matter of Mi and eleh, the reason of Mah for the creation of the heavens and their hosts will be settled, as will be explained, with the help of Heaven. And this passage is the end of the preceding passage, in the preceding chapter. And before giving a reason for the word Mah for the creation, he proved the matter from the verse. For the verse said, "When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers," and this refers back to the name Mah mentioned; and it says that they are the work of Your fingers, Mah. And this is what it said before this, "Mah majestic is Your name": that is to say, Mah is Your majestic name, in Malkhut, which is called earth. And this he intended in saying, "as it is written, 'When I behold Your heavens,' etc., and it is written, 'Mah majestic,'" etc. And because the end of the verse, "who has set Your glory," seems difficult according to this explanation, and in truth it is a necessity for the matter, for this he finished the explanation of the verse and said, "'upon the heavens': it is so as to rise in the name": explanation: the glory of Your complete name is not in Malkhut, for Malkhut is Mah alone; but "Your glory" is "upon the heavens": its intent is Tiferet, which is called heavens; and [the glory] is Binah, which is upon the heavens, Tiferet. "For He created a light for His light": the intent is that He emanated eleh, in which Mi is clothed, as we explained in the preceding chapter; and they are luminaries in which the light of the concealed Binah, called Mi, is clothed. "And it rose in the holy name," etc.: explanation: then the name was completed, and the emanation of Binah was raised up in the name Elohim. "And therefore 'In the beginning,'" etc.: explanation: he proved the matter, as is agreed by the mouths of all, that this Elohim is Binah; for otherwise, who would tell us that it is in Binah? Let us say it is in Malkhut. Rather it is certainly for the reason we explained: that the name Elohim does not apply in Malkhut except through the ascent of the pilgrimage festivals, as he goes on to explain. And this is what he said, "for Mah is not so": for in the attribute of Malkhut Mi does not apply, but Mah. And since this is so, although she is unified with eleh, she will not rise in the full name Elohim, but only (as -hem, which are she, Mah) [as Eleh with Mah, for Malkhut is Mah], with Heh and not with Yod. And this is what he said, "for Mah is not so": explanation: it is not with Yod but with Heh.
