And further, "and was not built" so as to be called (by them, eleh) [by the name Elohim] except through the drawing down of the letters eleh; and this is impossible except through the power of human beings, as will be explained. And this is why he returned to explain the first point first. First, why she is called Mah: he said, "and the Mother lends to the Daughter," etc.: explanation: to understand this matter one needs what we explained in the Gate of Manifestations concerning the matter of Malkhut, that she has two manifestations. The first is the manifestation in which she is called Yod, and it is very subtle; and this is from the side of Chokhmah, the male; therefore then she is in the form of a male, and she is the sign of the covenant of circumcision, in the secret of the Yod within her. And from the side of Binah she has the manifestation of the Heh, which is the building with which she was built at her taking from Adam, as it is written (Gen. 2:22), "And the Lord God built the rib": Binah (Binah) [built] the rib, which is Malkhut in the secret of the Yod, and the Heh was built. And the reason that the Heh was built in her from the side of Binah is that Binah too has the form of Heh. And the Heh is three Vavs, in the secret of Chesed, judgment and compassion, as we explained in the gate mentioned.

And behold, Malkhut is not built from Binah with her delightful adornments, which are the manifestation of the Yod that is in Binah, hinted at in the Yod of Mi; but she lends to her from the building of the Heh, which is the aspect of Heh within her, for it is an aspect near to the word eleh mentioned. And behold, the Mem of Mi and the Mem of Mah are equal, for the reason that it hints at their inclusion from four sides, which are the four elements: Binah inasmuch as she bestows upon them, and Malkhut inasmuch as she receives from them; and in this, because it is a revealed aspect, they came out equal. But the adornments of Binah with which she adorns herself, which is the manifestation of the Yod, she does not have from the side of Binah at all times, but only when every male appears "before the face of the Lord YHVH," which is Malkhut in the aspect of the Yod, as he proved from the verse "the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth."

Behold, Malkhut is called Adon in the aspect of the Yod, and before her the males appear, as it is written, "before the face of the Lord." "Then the Heh goes out," etc.: explanation: because then the males appear before her; and not precisely the males, but the very maleness, the sign of the covenant, would appear for each one, if he had kept it in purity. And this is the language of zekhurekha [your males] (Deut. 16:16); and it is not written zakharekha, meaning that the male himself is seen, but zekhurekha, which is the holy organ, the sign of the covenant, Yod; and so he was precise in the Zohar elsewhere (Mishpatim, folio 124a, and parashat Shelach, folio 165b). And because the males would appear, therefore she would adorn herself with the adornments of Binah herself, which are from the side of Chokhmah, that is, Yod. And this is what he said, "and she adorns herself in the garments of the male," etc.: explanation: in the vessels of the male, that is, from the side of Chokhmah, and it is the sign of the covenant, as we explained.

And behold, then, through the males, there was the aspect of Mi. "And the other letters," etc.: explanation: the letters eleh, needed to complete the name Elohim, Israel would draw from above to below; the intent: they would unite Malkhut, called Mi, with the Patriarchs, which are Chesed and judgment and compassion, called eleh. And to indicate that the matter of this union and drawing down was a great toil and strain, he proved the matter from the verse "These I remember." And the explanation: the intent of "I remember" is not according to its plain sense, which is a remembering after the exile, but the very remembrance at the time of the pilgrimage festivals; for Israel would pray for their union in the letters eleh, with tears of the heart and with prayer and supplications; and this is that they would remember eleh in their prayer and would pour out tears, in order to draw down and unite the letters eleh to Mi. And this is eddadem [eddadem with the kolel is the number of Mi]: the intent: I would bring them down and move them and bestow them upon Malkhut, so that there would be the complete name Elohim. "And with what? With the voice of joy and thanksgiving," etc.: explanation: crying out. Or the explanation may be the song of the Levites, as it is written (Num. 18:23), "But the Levite shall do," etc.; and "the multitude keeping festival" are Israel, who go up for the pilgrimage festivals. And the explanation of this passage is complete; praise to God. And the upshot is that the Elohim that is in Malkhut intends Mi: explanation: the Mem of Mah, which is itself the Mem of Mi mentioned in Binah; and the Yod is the manifestation of her Yod, and it is bestowed from the side of Mi, which is the Yod of Binah from the side of Chokhmah, in the secret of the thorn of the first Heh, as we shall explain in chapter 11, with the help of Heaven; and eleh too is the eleh mentioned in Binah. The rule of this matter: (in Binah the Mem hints) in the secret that she bestows upon the four extremities, which are the four elements, and the Yod according to the secret hinted at; and in Malkhut the Mem is in the secret that she receives from the four elements, which are the four legs of the chariot. And there is no wonder that, since Malkhut is one of the four legs of the chariot, she receives only from three, for she herself is the fourth; for we have already explained in several places that the power of an aspect receives from itself and from the other sefirot above it. And eleh in Binah is in the secret that she bestows upon eleh, and in Malkhut in the secret that she receives from eleh. And now that we have been aroused to the explanation of this holy name in all its matters and its manifestations, we have found them to be three: the principal is in Gevurah, and that is its particular place; the second, Binah; the third, Malkhut. And it is fitting that we investigate how this name indicates judgment; for according to what we explained, on the contrary, its principal is compassion, and so is indicated by what we explained in each one of the three passages mentioned in chapters 7, 8 and 9. And to this we will answer by the preliminary that we explained in Gate 15, chapter 3: that everywhere that the grades are from below to above, it indicates judgment, and they are judgment; and therefore, because in this name the grades are from below to above, they are judgment. How so? For according to what we explained concerning Mi and eleh, it would have been fitting that the order of the name be Mi-eleh; for Mi is in the secret of the concealed, in the concealed aspect, as we explained, and eleh is in the revealed aspect. And therefore it came reversed, from below to above, in three ways. First, that eleh precedes Mi, as is plain.

And further, the Yod precedes the Mem: although in Mi the Mem precedes the Yod, the measure was reversed, and in the Name the Yod precedes the Mem. And although it is possible to reject this, for on the contrary, this is its principal order, that the Yod precede the Mem, this is no proof; for the principal in the Name is the meaning of Mi, which indicates the concealment of the thing; and if it were the word yam [sea], it would indicate revealing and a revealed aspect, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, chapter 4. And the reason: when the word is yam, it indicates revealing; for the Yod, which is concealed, spreads out to four sides, which is the Mem; and it turns out that the Yod, which is a point without breadth, widens into a Mem and spreads out to four extremities, like the sea, which keeps widening. But when the Mem precedes the Yod, it indicates, on the contrary, concealment; for the four sides, although they are wide and stretched out in the secret of Chokhmah, are nevertheless concealed and gathered in the secret of the Yod, for the Yod is a concealed point; and this is Mi, which indicates concealment. And therefore in Malkhut the Mem precedes the Heh, which indicates, on the contrary, more revealing; for the Mem is somewhat open but is not opened to all sides, and the Heh is a more revealed aspect. But as Mi it indicates that she is concealed, in the secret of the concealed aspects. And let us return to the matter: that Mi too came reversed, as yam. Further, it came reversed in a third way, and it is well known in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in many places in the Tikkunim: the Heh of the Name preceding the Yod and prevailing over it; and we explained it in the preceding gates. And behold, in these aspects, although the matter of the letters indicates compassion, judgment is judged in them because of these reversals. Thus far reaches what we saw fit to explain concerning this name:

The sixth name is YHVH, and it is attributed to Tiferet. And all agreed concerning it that it is complete compassion. But in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, folio 44b) the opposite of this is found, and these are its words: "For the head of the sword is Yod; the body of the sword, Vav; the two edges of the sword, the two Hehs; its sheath, Adonai [and the sword, YHVH]. And when it is YHVH outside its Shekhinah, it is judgment that cuts on every side; when it enters the sheath, it becomes compassion and does not cut judgments. And the secret of this, the sword in the sheath, is יאהדונה"י; so it certainly is. And at the time that YHVH is outside its Shekhinah, it is said of it, 'For the Lord your God is a consuming fire' (Deut. 4:24), for it takes from Gevurah to burn the world." Thus far its words.

Behold, it is explicit that the four-letter name is judgment, a consuming fire. And when we examine the language of this passage well, we find it at peace with us, and it does not disagree at all with the consensus of the commentators. And he was precise in saying that Yod is the head of the sword: because it is Chokhmah, at the head, and because it is compassion it has no part in the body of the judgment, except as with the back of the hand, in the hiding of the face; and it is the head of the sword. And the body of the sword is the Vav, Tiferet. But those that cut are its two edges: the one is Binah, which bestows judgment upon Gevurah, and from there Tiferet draws sustenance so as to be judgment, outside its nature and its attribute; and this is what he said, "for it takes from Gevurah," etc.; for without its drawing sustenance from there it is compassion on every side and in every aspect. And the other edge is Malkhut, which cuts and acts in judgment; but when it is in union with Malkhut, it is compassion. And the name that indicates the union is the eight-letter name, and it is a wondrous and holy name. And Rashbi also said explicitly that it is compassion, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 118), and these are his words: "And there is a limb in which YHVH is called compassion," etc. Rather, it is certainly as we explained, and it is correct and clear. And concerning the hint of this name, in the Zohar on the Song of Songs (Zohar Chadash, folio 79), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained: "The fourth chamber: the image of Jacob the elder, in the secret of Yod-Heh-Vav, who takes the inheritance of Father and Mother, and he grew up among them, and goes before them in the way of modesty. For the whole world, so it is seen, after the manner of the order of the letters of the Master of all, as they are ordered, YHVH: the ways of the male, to set his female always before him, to watch over her, and to remove from her suspicion and jealousy, and he does not set his eyes on another woman. Yod male, Heh female: Yod-Heh: behold, the female before the male, to look at her always. The son goes before his mother, to cover her from the eye, for the sake of her honor and the honor of his father, etc. [Jacob] takes (another version: guards) his female (and sets her before him), to watch over her always and not another; this is what is written, 'the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it' (Deut. 11:12), that she not depart from the eye one moment. And this is the order of the holy letters, that this order be above and below." Thus far its words.

And at first glance the manifestation of this passage as a whole is very far-fetched; for there is no jealousy and hatred above, nor setting of one's eyes on another woman. But [it is said] so as to give, by this means, a reason for the order of the letters of the holy Name.

Further, one must be precise in his words. In saying "in the secret of Yod-Heh-Vav, who takes the inheritance," etc., it appears from his words that the reason the letters Yod-Heh are in Tiferet is because it receives from them the inheritance of Father and Mother; and it is a correct reason. And afterwards, in the same breath, he said that the reason is "and he grew up among them," and this is a second reason. Afterwards, in the same breath, he said "and goes before them in the way of modesty." If so, it appears that Rashbi, peace be upon him, God forbid, is not settled in the matter as is fitting, for he turns from matter to matter. Further, one must be precise: what is "the inheritance of Father and Mother," and what is its matter, and likewise their saying "he grew up among them." (And the matter is) that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the fourth chamber and said that it is Tiferet, in the secret of Yod-Heh-Vav; that is to say, the principal letters of the Name in Tiferet are the letters Yod-Heh-Vav. And to this it was difficult for him: granted, if we say that the principal of the Name is all four letters, according to its plain sense, it is well, for he explains the reason: because it is the trunk of the tree, including all the branches, and from it they spread out; therefore a name including the whole Emanation, which is the four-letter name, is related to it. But according to what he explained now, that the principal of the Name in it is Yod-Heh-Vav, three letters alone, it is difficult: what reason is there for these letters? Either it should include all, or it should include only the Vav, which hints at it alone. To this he answered that the reason is "that it takes the inheritance of Father and Mother." And its explanation Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained at the time of his passing, as we explained in the book Or Yakar, with the help of Heaven. And this is the gist of his words: when Chesed was emanated from Chokhmah, the manifestation of Chesed remained there; and when Gevurah was emanated from Binah, the manifestation of Gevurah remained there. And when Tiferet rises in the secret of Da'at, just as the way of Tiferet is to arbitrate between Gedulah and Gevurah and include them in their place, as is known, so when it rises it inherits these two manifestations and includes them. And just as Tiferet prevails over Chesed and Gevurah emanated in their place, in the secret of its arbitration, so it arbitrates between those manifestations and prevails over them. And this is what he said, "that it takes the inheritance of Father and Mother," that is, the two concealed manifestations; and through this it is called by the name Yah. And because "he grew up among them," that is, a third manifestation, the arbiter, therefore Vav is formed in it. And this is the secret of Yod-Heh-Vav, which are the secret of three lines: the line of the right, Chesed; the line of the left, Gevurah; the middle line, Rachamim, Tiferet; and this is the secret of the Yod-Heh-Vav that is in it. And they are manifestations included in the very self of Tiferet, as we explained. "And goes before them," etc.: it was difficult for him that, according to these manifestations, it would have been fitting that the order of the Name be Yod-Vav-Heh, that is, the manifestation of the line of compassion between the right and the left, as we explained, and as he said, "and he grew up among them." And to this he answered that the reason for the order of the letters is that, since the letters of the four-letter name include the whole Emanation, and it is the concealed name that we explained in the preceding gate, their order is necessarily thus: YHVH; and also everywhere that these letters are found, it is fitting that they be only in this order. And this is what he said, "and goes before them": explanation: the reason the letter Vav is the outer one and not the middle one is "the way of modesty," as will be explained. "For the whole world, so it is seen, after the manner," etc.: explanation: everywhere that these letters are, it is fitting that they be ordered according to the order of the letters of the concealed Name that includes the whole Emanation. And therefore he said "of the Master of all," that is, the manifestation of the self of the Name, as we explained. And afterwards he gave a reason for the letters and their order, and said "the ways of the male," that is, Chokhmah, which is Yod, and it bestows upon Binah, and this is "his female before him." For from the side of the male, which is the side of compassion, compassion always prevails over judgment; and therefore from its side it is Yod over Heh, compassion over judgment; the right always prevails over the left. And this is what he said, "the ways of the male": explanation: this matter and this order of the letters is from the side of the male; for from the side of the female, Heh always prevails over Yod, judgment over compassion, as we explained in the Gate From Below to Above. And this is what he said, "to watch over her," as we explained: to bestow upon her, so that the light be direct, the male bestowing and the female receiving, and not the reverse, in the secret of the returning light, in which there is judgment and jealousy. And this is what he said, "and to remove from her suspicion," etc.: explanation: the husks. And although there are no husks above, behold, when the effluence withdraws in the secret of the returning light, husks certainly spread out below, because of the abundance of the judgment that is bestowed. And jealousy is a title for judgment, as we explained. And their saying "and he does not set his eyes," etc.: it is possible to say that when the effluence withdraws and it is returning light, the male turns out to withdraw his effluence and to bestow upward, to the place above him; and it turns out that "he sets his eyes on another woman." Or it is possible to explain: when the effluence withdraws to the outer ones; and even if this does not apply above, God forbid, nevertheless when its effluence withdraws this matter necessarily follows, as is known. And for the order of the letters, male over female, bestower over bestowed upon, compassion prevailing over judgment, he said, "Yod male, Heh female: Yod-Heh: behold," etc., as we explained. "The son goes before his mother": Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that the name Yod-Vav-Heh-Heh is Vav with Yod, two bestowers together, and the two Hehs are the secret of "and the two of them went" (Ruth 1:19), for the two of them go in exile, the supernal Mother and the lower Mother; and we explained the matter in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 13. And if so, it turns out that the son must be before the mother, "to cover her from the eye," so that the evil eye not rule over her; and the reason how this matter can properly be said of Binah has been explained in the gate mentioned. "For the sake of her honor and the honor of his father": for this thing touches principally on Binah, from whom the effluence withdraws, and therefore he put her first; "and the honor of his father," for above too there is a stirring of this: "the Shekhinah among the lower ones is a need on high." "Jacob takes his female": that is, Malkhut, which is the last Heh. And so that the light be direct, compassion, and the dregs of the husks not take hold of the wings of the Tabernacle, the Vav must be over the Heh, compassion prevailing over judgment. "That she not depart from the eye one moment": for Malkhut needs more guarding, because of her nearness to the husks. "That this order be above," etc.: explanation: everywhere that the letters of the Name are, even if they are not hinting in these places, nevertheless it is fitting that compassion always prevail over judgment, as we explained. Thus far the explanation of the passage.

And behold, it has been explained from it that the four-letter name that is in Tiferet does not hint at ten sefirot in these letters, as is its way in most places, because this name is not the proper name, as we explained in chapter 1. But he intended to explain the order of the letters in it, because it includes those diadems that are the secret of Father and Mother; and therefore three letters are included in it, in the secret of Yod-Heh-Vav, and the Heh is the Shekhinah that is united with it. And this name has many manifestations in the Tikkunim, such as: Yod, the head of the Leviathan; Heh-Heh, its fins; Vav, the body of the Leviathan. And likewise Yod, the head of the bird; Vav, the body of the bird; Heh-Heh, its wings (in Tikkun 45b). And likewise Vav, the stem of the rose; Heh-Heh, two fives: five leaves within, five leaves without; Yod, its bud (Tikkun 38b). And likewise Vav, the trunk of the tree; Heh, the branches of the tree; Heh, the root of the tree; Yod, the fruit of the tree. And there are many matters like these, the explanation of which would lengthen the matter for us without necessary need; therefore we will not lengthen. And whoever wishes [to know] their matter will find them scattered through the Tikkunim:

On the form of the letters of the Name and their relation to these attributes, besides what has been explained in these chapters, we have found in the Zohar, parashat Mishpatim (folio 123b), and these are its words: "Come and see: I saw him in my dream and asked before Rabbi Shimon: Yod, behold, I have learned before the master that it is Chokhmah, and so it certainly is. Heh: why is it Binah? He said to me: Come and see, behold, it is written, 'And a river goes forth from Eden to water the garden' (Gen. 2:10). Who is the river that goes forth from Eden? This is Binah. And therefore that river: Yod is enclosed within it, and Yod spreads this river out on all its sides, and it brought forth a son beneath it, which is Vav, in this manner: ה. Afterwards it gave birth and brought forth this son and set him before it. And therefore Yod-Heh-Vav: for the Vav sits before it, to nurse from it. And therefore we have learned in our mishnah: the Heh was a Dalet; once the male was joined with it, it conceived one son and was called Heh. Afterwards it gave birth and brought forth Vav, that son, and he stands before it. And of this it is written, 'And a river goes forth from Eden': from it it certainly goes forth; 'to water the garden': to nurse it." Thus far its words.

And these words are the words of Rabbi Abba to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon; and he was recounting to him this matter, that he saw Rashbi, peace be upon him, in a dream and asked him this question, and he answered him the words mentioned above. And it is fitting to be precise in the words of this passage: why was Rabbi Abba in doubt about the Heh, why it is Binah, and was not in doubt about the Yod, why it is Chokhmah, so that he said, "Yod, behold, I have learned," etc., "and so it certainly is," as it appears that there is no question there, and the principal question is about the Heh? And it is fitting to know this. Further, why did he not ask likewise about the Vav, why it is in Tiferet, and the last Heh, why it is in Malkhut? And we will say in explanation of this: the sefirot, being concealed, according to their nearness to their cause so is their concealment and their hiddenness. And for this reason they said that Keter, because of its great concealment, was revealed only in the thorn of the Yod, to hint at its subtlety and its concealment and its hiddenness, as this thorn is subtle and there is no judging of a letter and form in it at all; and some say that there is in it neither a letter nor a thorn at all, as we explained in the preceding gate. And Chokhmah, because it is the second effect, became distant by a second grade from its cause (not distant in place, God forbid, but that is to say, it is the second grade of the effects and the emanated ones); and therefore the hint to it is the Yod, since it is greater than the thorn hinted at in Keter. And because it is still concealed, this letter has no manifestation except in a black body, like matter [golem] without form; and it is also subtle, to indicate that because of its subtlety apprehension of it is withheld from us. And this is what Rabbi Abba said in his question to Rashbi, peace be upon him: "Yod, behold, I have learned before the master that it is Chokhmah, and so it certainly is": for so the form of the letter indicates in its manifestation, that it is certainly in Chokhmah, since its form is subtle and it has almost no form, but simple matter like a point that has no body, as we explained. "And if so, Heh: why is it Binah?" And he was precise: since in Chokhmah the form of a letter cannot properly be said at all, but a simple point, as we explained, if so Binah, which is its effect and is also concealed, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapters 6, 7 and 8, with the help of Heaven, it would be fitting that the letter hinting at her be an intermediate form between the Yod that is in Chokhmah and the Vav that is in Tiferet. For the Vav in Tiferet is settled, and likewise the Heh in Malkhut is related to the Vav in Tiferet, and for this reason he did not ask about it, since it is the lower grade; but the principal question is about the Heh in Binah, which does not relate to the Yod in Chokhmah nor to the measure of the Vav in Tiferet. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, shone upon him from his good effluence and answered him: "'And a river goes forth from Eden,' etc. Who is the river that goes forth from Eden? This is Binah." Explanation: on this verse the explanations in the Zohar are many, in many places; and among them it is explained that the river is Tiferet and Eden is Binah, and so we copied his language in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 5, with the help of Heaven. And if we explain this explanation in this verse, it turns out that there is no proof at all for Rashbi's explanation in this passage, because his principal intent depends on the explanation of the verse, as we shall explain. For this he said, "Who is the river that goes forth from Eden? This is Binah": explanation: the principal of Eden is in Keter; and even if it is found sometimes in Chokhmah and sometimes in Binah, it is in a borrowed sense. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 11b), and these are his words: "And Eden is only the Supernal Keter, which is wondrous and covered; and because of this it is said of Eden, 'No eye has seen, O God, besides You' (Isa. 64:3)." Thus far. Behold, the opinion of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is explicitly that Eden's principal is in Keter, and so he proved it from the verse. And if so, Eden can properly be said of Binah only remotely, and it can more properly be said of Chokhmah, because of its nearness to Keter. And if we explain that the river is Tiferet and goes forth from Keter, which is the true Eden, the word "goes forth" cannot properly be said of it literally from Keter; for it goes forth only from Binah, as is known and as is explained from the passage further on. And if we wish to explain the river as Chokhmah and Eden as Keter, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in other places, behold, "river" cannot properly be said of Chokhmah. For this he said, "Who is the river," so that the language of "goes forth" and the language of "Eden" may be precise? Only in Binah, as we proved above. And now "goes forth" is correct, for it literally goes forth from Chokhmah; and the language of "river" is correct, for she is called river; and the language of "Eden" is correct of Chokhmah, in a borrowed sense. "And therefore that river: Yod is enclosed within it": explanation: to hint at the place of its going forth and the place of its emanation, it was necessary that the manifestation of its source, which is Chokhmah, be formed in its own self; and therefore there is found in the form of the Heh, in its Dalet, in its middle thorn, a (cloud) [crownlet] in the form of a Yod, to hint at its source, which is Chokhmah, as we explained. "And Yod spreads this river out on all its sides": it is known that the emanation of Chesed, judgment and compassion is from Binah; and although Binah is not their principal, nevertheless they were emanated through her and by way of her, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 6, with the help of Heaven. If so, it turns out according to this that the sources of Chesed and judgment and compassion are necessarily concealed within her, and she is opened in the secret of these three lines. And this is what he said, "Yod spreads the river," etc.: that is, she spread out in a first manifestation to two directions, one to the right and one to the left, the one judgment and the other Chesed; and this spreading and its emanation is through Chokhmah, for Binah is emanated from Chokhmah. And this is "spreads this river out on all its sides," that is, the form of the Dalet within the Heh; "and it brought forth a son beneath it": it is the form of the Vav within the Dalet, through a second coupling and joining, as will be explained further on [in what he wrote], "the Heh was a Dalet." But it is fitting to know why the three spreadings, Chesed and judgment and compassion, were not emanated together, and why compassion was delayed until the second joining of Chokhmah in Binah, as will be explained. But the matter is that first there were the two extremes, which are judgment and Chesed, and afterwards they needed an arbiter between them; and it is fitting that the disputants come first and afterwards the arbiter. And our intent in saying "precedence" is not precedence of time, God forbid, but precedence of rank. And he said "a son beneath it, which is Vav," to indicate its concealed manifestation in the secret of Da'at, where its manifestation is a simple firmament in the form of Vav, as we explained in Gate 1, chapter 2. And he intended, in saying "beneath it," that it is only below her, and not yet between Gedulah and Gevurah; for it is in the secret of simple Da'at, without the aspect of judgment and Chesed, but below Binah, second to her. For when it is between Gedulah and Gevurah, it is below both of them, or between them at the least, and not directly beneath Binah, as now, in the first manifestation, when it is a firmament alone. "Afterwards it brought forth this son," etc.: explanation: this is the emanation by which she emanated it and brought it out between Chesed and Gevurah. And their saying "and set him before it": for all of them are before her, but not essentially beneath her. Or the intent may be the order of the standing of the letters: for when it is emanated from her outward and becomes Tiferet, in the secret of the boughs [porot] and the colors, which are Chesed and judgment and compassion, then it is before its mother, to cover her, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the passage in the preceding chapter. And this is "before it": explanation: in front of her, to conceal her from the eyes of the onlookers; for concealment is the cause of revealing, and revealing the cause of concealment; and it is clear that through the revealing of Tiferet Binah was concealed. "And therefore we have learned," etc., "the Heh was a Dalet," etc.: for it is known that the union of Yod in Heh is like the union of Vav in Heh, as we explained in Gate 8, chapter 13, with the help of Heaven. And because the manifestation of Tiferet is a firmament spreading out from the side of Chokhmah, in the secret of Da'at, as we explained in Gate 1 and in other gates, therefore Binah was a Dalet; for the emanation of the middle, intermediate line had not yet been, until Chokhmah emanated it in Binah, and from there it went forth to its place. And this is "was a Dalet": that is, the power of judgment and Chesed in Binah alone, until Tiferet went forth in the subtle manifestation that is within Chokhmah; and through it a Heh was made in Binah, and from there it was emanated below, to between the extremities, and became a garden [gan, 53], for it is the master of six plantings, as is known. "And of this it is written, 'And a river goes forth,'" etc.: it is clear, as we explained above. And this is his saying, "from it it certainly goes forth": the intent: it goes forth essentially from Eden; from it it goes forth immediately, as we explained above. It turns out that "river," "goes forth" and "Eden" are precise. But according to this, "to water the garden" is somewhat forced. For granted, according to the explanation Eden Keter, river Chokhmah, garden Binah, and likewise according to the explanation Eden Binah, river Tiferet, garden Malkhut, it is well; for the language "garden" is correct, since the principal plantings are in Binah or in Malkhut. But according to this explanation, that the garden is Tiferet, the language "garden" is not correct of it. For this he said, as one forced in this matter, "to nurse it": explanation: Tiferet; for the language "garden" can indeed properly be said of it, for it is the master of six plantings, etc. And because of this strain he said first, "from it it certainly goes forth"; for although the language "garden" is not correct, it is better that we be precise in the beginning of the verse, which is "And a river goes forth from Eden" (and further, these are three words), than that we be precise in one word. And for this he said, "from it it goes forth," that is, "And a river goes forth from Eden." And "to water the garden," "to nurse it," is also somewhat settled, for in it too there are plantings. Thus far what we saw fit to explain of this passage on the explanation of the four-letter name. And by what Rashbi explained in this passage concerning the matter of the Heh, that it is three lines (the right line drawn downward, with the roof drawn above, Chesed; the left line, Gevurah; and the middle Vav, Tiferet), what we explained in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 3, will be settled: that every Heh is three Vavs, which are the three Patriarchs; see in its place:
The seventh and eighth name: Tzeva'ot.

And behold, it is attributed to Netzach and Hod. But this name is found joined to the name YHVH and to the name Elohim, as in YHVH Tzeva'ot, Elohim Tzeva'ot. And they explained concerning it that Netzach is called YHVH Tzeva'ot, and the reason is that Netzach is a branch of compassion; and Hod is called Elohim Tzeva'ot, and the reason is that Hod is a branch of judgment. And they are called Tzeva'ot for the reason that upper and lower hosts [tzeva'ot] are drawn and bestowed from there. So all the commentators explained. And it is very difficult: for just as Hod, because it is a branch of Gevurah, is called Elohim Tzeva'ot after Gevurah, which is so called, it would have been fitting that Netzach, because it is a branch of Chesed, be called El Tzeva'ot. And one cannot say that because it is not complete compassion like Chesed it is not fitting to call it El, but it is called YHVH because it is intermediate, like the middle line. This is no answer; for Hod too is not complete judgment, and is called Elohim in a borrowed sense; so Netzach should have been called El in a borrowed sense. And one cannot escape by saying that El is always complete compassion, which is not so with the name Elohim (for sometimes Malkhut is called by the name Elohim, and likewise Binah is called by the name Elohim); for two reasons: first, that it has been said (Ps. 7:12), "And God [El] is indignant every day," and its plain sense is that He has some indignation; second, that the angel of Gevurah is Gabriel, and he is the prince of fire, as is known, and nevertheless the name El is fixed in his name. And if so, we return to our question: it would have been fitting that Netzach be called El Tzeva'ot. And one cannot answer that it is called YHVH Tzeva'ot because it is second to Tiferet (for the one is sixth to the Emanation and the other seventh, as is known), and for this reason it acquired the name of Tiferet. For behold, Tiferet and Netzach intervene between Hod and Gevurah, and nevertheless [Hod] is called by the name Elohim, by the name of Gevurah, and is not called by the name YHVH, which is Tiferet, which is nearer to it than Elohim, which is in Gevurah; for the one is second and the other third.

And further, although Netzach is second to Tiferet, its principal is Chesed, as we explained in the Order of the Emanation, chapter 6, with the help of Heaven. Therefore it seems right to answer that Netzach and Hod are two attributes united in all their actions, brothers, and they do not separate; and therefore most of their titles are theirs together, such as "channels of water," "troughs of water," and the like, as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles; and we explained the reason in Gate 8, chapter 24. And therefore the name including both of them together is the name Tzeva'ot. And besides this name, common to both of them, they have no other name among the names that may not be erased; and this name can properly be said only of both of them together, as the name "host" can properly be said only of a gathering of people. And likewise both of them together are called Tzeva'ot. And so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim: Netzach and Hod, Tzeva'ot. And likewise in the Zohar, parashat Vayikra (folio 11), and these are its words: "The seventh and the eighth are called Tzeva'ot"; and likewise in many places. But the names YHVH and Elohim are borrowed for them, for a reason that we shall explain. And the matter is that these two attributes, one right and one left, are both a dwelling and a seat for Tiferet and Malkhut, and there, through Yesod, they are united; for Netzach is a throne for Tiferet and Hod a throne for Malkhut. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, folio 33), and these are his words: "Come and see: YHVH, Adonai: they are the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, in the two thighs: YHVH on the right, Adonai on the left; and they are the shining mirror and the mirror that does not shine. In the Righteous One both of them are one: יאהדונה"י." Thus far its words.

And Rashbi, peace be upon him, proved the matter in his language, in what he lengthened and said, "and they are the mirror," etc. For it is already known that the shining mirror is Tiferet, and it is the grade of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him; and the other prophets are in Malkhut, which is like a mirror that does not shine. And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra 75): "The face of Moses was like the face of the sun, and the face of Joshua like the face of the moon." And the intent is that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, prophesied by the power of Tiferet, and it is the face of the sun; but Joshua, the face of the moon, which is Malkhut. And since this is so, how do they say elsewhere that prophecy is through Netzach and Hod, which are "two prophets of truth," as is frequent in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in numberless places? Rather, perforce, what must you say? That Tiferet is toward Netzach, for such is the way of Tiferet, toward the right, and this is the attribute of Moses; and Malkhut toward Hod, for such is her way, toward the left, as we explained in the preceding gates; and in Yesod they are united, as is known. And after this preliminary: it is already known that the name of Tiferet is YHVH and the name of Malkhut Elohim; and in most places where YHVH Elohim comes it is Tiferet and Malkhut, or, remotely, Chokhmah and Binah, which are called after Tiferet and Malkhut; and likewise Binah alone is called with the vowels of Elohim and written YHVH, to indicate them, as we explained in chapter 4, with the help of Heaven. If so, it is fitting that Netzach and Hod be called by their names, YHVH, Elohim. And there is no difficulty that according to this Hod should have been called by the name Adonai and not by the name Elohim, according to the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. This is no question: for Malkhut, when she inclines to the left, all the more so when she is in Hod, is called Elohim, as we explained above in chapters 7, 8 and 9. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, in this passage used Adonai to hint at the union by way of the rungs of the ladder, up to the highest rung, as he goes on to explain, "in Chesed and Gevurah," etc., "in the middle," etc., as we copied his language in Gate 15, chapter 2. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, parashat Vayikra (folio 11b), and these are his words: "The seventh and eighth: this is Tzeva'ot. And therefore YHVH is near in all, holding onto all sides: at times YHVH Elohim, for they are near, Tiferet to Gevurah; and at times YHVH Tzeva'ot, for they are near, Tiferet to Netzach and Hod, which are called Tzeva'ot. And it has been said that the words of the faithful prophets were recognized from their mouths, when they said 'Thus says YHVH Elohim' and when they said 'Thus says YHVH Tzeva'ot,' and they would know from what place the words came." Thus far its words.

And behold, he taught explicitly that, because Tiferet is near to Gevurah (which is fifth, and Tiferet sixth), and likewise it is near to Netzach and Hod, therefore it is fitting that the name YHVH be united either with the name Elohim, which is above it, or with Tzeva'ot, which is beneath it; and therefore YHVH Elohim is found, and YHVH Tzeva'ot. And from it it is explained explicitly that YHVH Tzeva'ot is Tiferet united with Netzach and Hod. And from this we may infer to Elohim Tzeva'ot, which is Malkhut: when she is above them, she is called Elohim Tzeva'ot. And likewise from it it is explained that Netzach and Hod are called only Tzeva'ot.

And further, there is a proof for this matter from the Zohar (Ha'azinu, folio 296), and we copied it in Gate 8, chapter 24. And one cannot tear down from this passage something of the building that we have built, and say that Elohim Tzeva'ot would be Gevurah over Netzach and Hod; for this has no reason, for one cannot say "for they are near," etc., and Malkhut is nearer, as we explained, with the help of Heaven. And this name is found sometimes in a borrowed sense for Tiferet; and he explained in the Zohar (there) the reason: that the souls and the bestowals go out from Tiferet to Netzach and Hod, which are called Tzeva'ot, their own name. And likewise Yesod is called Tzeva'ot in a borrowed sense, for the reason that the souls and the hosts bestowed from Netzach and Hod go out by way of Yesod. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar on the Song of Songs (at its beginning): "And because it brings forth sparkling radiances and makes fruit after its kind, this radiance is called Tzeva'ot." And there the concern is with the union; and he explained the reason: because it bestows souls of the righteous, that is, "fruit after its kind," it too is called Tzeva'ot. And he was precise in his language, and said "brings forth" and did not say "makes," as in the language of the verse, which says "making fruit after its kind" (Gen. 1:11); because the souls and the hosts are not in its hand, but they are bestowed from above it through it, and it is only the one that brings them out, like the organ of seed, in whose hand the seed is not, and which has no power to withhold it or to increase it, but is only a passage. Which is not so with Netzach and Hod, which are the testicles of the male, and they are those that ripen the seed bestowed upon them from Tiferet. And this is "the millstones [shechakim] that grind manna for the righteous"; and the manna is "from the heavens," as it is written (Ex. 16:4), "Behold, I will rain bread for you from the heavens"; and the manna is the effluence bestowed from the heavens, Tiferet; and Netzach and Hod are the millstones, the testicles that ripen the seed, which grind manna for the righteous, who are Tzaddik and Tzedek:

The ninth name: El Chai and Shaddai; for these names are attributed to Yesod. And the author of Sefer ha-Orah wrote the reason that Yesod is called El Chai: "because it is the end of the nine sefirot, which are called nine mirrors, and it is the one that draws from all the sefirot the attribute of Chesed and life to the attribute of Adonai, as I have made known to you. Because it draws the attribute of Chesed it is called El, and because it draws the attribute of life it is called Chai [living]; and when Chesed and life are joined together, it is called El Chai." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: the attribute of life is from Binah. And something close to this matter was explained in Gate 1, chapter 10; and there we expounded at length that the principal name of Yesod is Shaddai, from two passages of the Zohar. And likewise we have further found Rashbi, peace be upon him, in many places, [relating] the name Shaddai to Yesod. And these are his words in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Tetze, folio 283): "[But] from the side of the Tree of Life, Shaddai is Yesod." Thus far its words.

And he said "from the side" for the reason that there he explained that Shaddai is Metatron, and it serves below like Yesod, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 4; and now he said that above, from the side of the sefirot of the Tree of Life, this name is in Yesod. Further, this name is found in Malkhut, but from the side of the Righteous One. And these are his words (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, folio 257): "The Shekhinah is called mezuzah from the side of the middle pillar, of the letters of YHVH; and from the side of the Righteous One, the secret of the covenant, she is called Shaddai. Shaddai is the seal of the King, who is YHVH." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: from the side of the four-letter name she is called mezuzah, explanation: doorpost; for Malkhut is the doorpost and the gate by which to enter to the four-letter name. And from the side of the Righteous One, explanation: Yesod, the Righteous One, which is the covenant of circumcision, she is called Shaddai; explanation: the seal sealed from the Righteous One upon Malkhut, in the secret of the union, is Shaddai.

And behold, the Righteous One draws upon her the power of Tiferet, and it is called Shaddai, the seal of YHVH. Further, we have found in the Tikkunim (in the Zohar Chadash, folio 119) that Rashbi, peace be upon him, attributed this name also to Metatron: for since his craft is to unite on the weekdays, in the manner of Yesod on festivals, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapters 4 and 5, therefore this name is related to him, for it is related to the union, as explained above:

The tenth name: Adonai. This name is related to Malkhut, and she is called "the outer keys" in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, many times. And the reason is that this name is the entrance to the other sefirot. And concerning this name Sefer ha-Orah explained it from the language of the sockets [adnei] of the Tabernacle, a language of [a house of] receiving; for she is the treasury (and house) of receiving for the four-letter name and for all the sefirot, as is known. Further he wrote there, and these are his words: "The letters of the name Adonai indicate its dominion and its matter. How so? Its Alef is the secret of Ehyeh, which is above; its Yod is the secret of YHVH, which dwells in it; its Dalet-Nun is the secret of the fifty-four [Nun-Dalet] names of the havayah, which are the secret of all kinds of effluence and emanation and sustenance for all the created entities in the world. You learn, then, that all the dominion and the rule is in the hand of Adonai; and therefore it indicates the language of lordship, for this name is Lord of all the earth by the power of YHVH, which dwells in it." Thus far its words.

And the matter of the fifty-four havayot that he spoke of we shall explain in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapter 11, with the help of Heaven. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] in Sefer ha-Shem explained it in another way, and these are his words: "This name is the first, and the gatehouse to the union, to enter through it from below to above; and it is the end of the union from above to below. Therefore it is reckoned first and tenth; and therefore its beginning is Alef and its end Yod, and its end is wedged in its beginning, and it is first and it is last. And the letters of judgment [dan] are included in it, to say that all is in it; and therefore it is called Adonai." Thus far its words.

And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, folio 43) there is a fine matter on this name, and these are its words: "When she ascends, she ascends [by Imma, who is the Alef of Adonai, Ehyeh. And upon what does she ascend?] upon the middle pillar, which is Vav, wrapped about it like a ring on a finger; and she ascends by the Dalet of Adonai, which are two arms and two thighs, until she ascends to the letter Yod, which is Abba, Chokhmah, the upper Yod; for from there she was taken. This is what is written, 'The Lord by wisdom founded the earth' (Prov. 3:19)." Thus far its words.

And his intent is that the Yod at her end is related to this attribute, and it indicates her own self; but she ascends by way of the rungs, up to above, to receive effluence, and her degree there is supreme, without limit and end. And the way of her ascent is by way of the house of Imma; and because the general principle of her ascent is principally Binah, who is Imma, and by her power is the beginning of her arousal to ascend, therefore Alef comes first in her name, to indicate the Alef of Ehyeh that is in Binah; for so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar on the Song of Songs, and we copied it in chapter 2. "And upon what does she ascend?": explanation: the way of her ascent, by which way is it? By way of the middle. And this he meant in saying "upon the middle pillar, which is Vav." "Which is wrapped," etc.: for her ascent to her father's house is in the secret of (Prov. 12:4) "A woman of valor is the diadem of her husband"; and this is that she is like a ring at the tip of the finger, Yod over Vav; and likewise her hint upon it when she ascends, as explained in the Tikkunim there. "And she ascends by the Dalet": that is, she ascends over Netzach and Hod by way of her husband, and over Chesed and Gevurah by way of her husband, until her ascent to the Yod, which is Abba. This is the (division) [ascent] of the letters of the name Adonai. Further, we have found concerning this name and the four-letter name that the one is a palace to the other, after the likeness of Tiferet and Malkhut. For the names are the sefirot and the sefirot are the names, and there is no difference between them at all; and it is known that Malkhut is a palace and dwelling for Tiferet, in which it appears and shows its hosts, as is known. And the letters of the one are like the letters of the other, four corresponding to four, four faces and four wings. And this thing is explained in the Zohar, parashat Pekudei (folio 235b), and these are its words: "Adonai: this is the secret of the Tabernacle, after the manner of the supernal secret, the secret of the Ark, as it is written, 'Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth.' 'The Lord of all the earth': this is the holy secret of the name Alef-Dalet-Nun-Yod; and this is after the manner of the secret of the supernal holy name YHVH, and these letters are after the manner of those. Alef is the secret of Yod, in this manner: א; this has been established. Dalet is the secret [of Heh], and this is after the manner of that, and all is one secret and one manner. Nun is the secret of the letter Vav; and although this is male and that female, this is included in that, and this has been established. Nun-Vav is in the middle, because it is one inclusion. Heh is the secret of the letter Yod, because here this Yod is the secret of the small wisdom, which is called the wisdom of Solomon. And these letters are included in those, etc., and all is one, and all is one secret in the holy letters." Thus far its words.

And Rashbi, peace be upon him, intended in this to relate the four letters of the garment to the four letters that are clothed in them. How so? Alef is a garment to the Yod, for all is one matter; for the Alef (begins) [is related] in the Yod: that is, the upper thorn of the Yod is a Yod, and afterwards the body of the Yod widens, which is like the Vav in the middle of the Alef, and afterwards the lower thorn of the Yod, which is a Yod, like the lower Yod in the Alef. And just as these three matters in the Yod hint at the first three, as we explained in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, chapter 1, so the Alef hints at the first three, as we explained there in chapter 4, with the help of Heaven.

Behold, Yod is related to Alef. Further, Heh is clothed in Dalet. It is known that Dalet and Heh are all one, except that the one indicates the small Vav within it and the other indicates the self of Binah; as he said, "the Heh was a Dalet," as we explained in chapter 11. Further, Vav is clothed in Nun. And it was difficult for him, for Nun is in Malkhut and the Vav in Tiferet; and he answered that the Nun, that part of it which is straight, hints at the Vav. Further, Yod is clothed in Heh. And this is clear, for Heh and Yod in Malkhut are all one; and therefore he said "it is the small wisdom," etc., for Yod is clothed in Heh, and it is called the small wisdom. And although the way of Yod is to be clothed in Heh, and here Heh is clothed in Yod, there is nothing in this; for how many faces upon [awesome] faces, and how many backs upon backs, that are not seen! And therefore what is back for this matter is face for that, and what is garment for this is brain for that. Thus far reaches what was intended in this gate concerning the explanation of the names that may not be erased. But as for what is found, the joining of two or three names together, such as El Elohim YHVH, and such as Elohim El Chai, and likewise El Shaddai, and likewise Elohim Adonai, and the like, it is to indicate the joining of the attributes according to their action, and the coupling and the bestowals of the attributes upon the thing intended there; and some of them will be explained in the Glossary of Titles, with the help of the Name.
And behold, the chapter is complete, and this gate is concluded. Praise to God alone:
The Twenty-First Gate: The Gate of Particulars of Names.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain a great and wondrous matter found in most of the words of the commentators, and in particular in the prayer of Rabbi Nechunya ben ha-Kanah, which attributed particular and explicit names to the sefirot, such as the name of seventy-two and the name of forty-two and the name of twelve, and the like. And we wish to explain each one of them, its sources and its character, as far as our hand can reach to find anyone who speaks of them, whether much or little; for these things are handed down in tradition, and it is not permitted to add to them or to subtract:
Chapter One:

Before we enter into the explanation of the particulars of the names, we will set out in these chapters [matters] whose understanding is not apprehended. And when the discerning one sees this matter, let him consider it a preliminary of precious worth concerning these names in general. For when he considers in his mind that these names are remote from knowledge and understanding, and in them are found almost words that are not understood and not bounded in the utterance of the mouth, so that he might imagine them to be child's play or words of nonsense, God forbid, we were obliged to warn that he not be as one who thinks evil, and that he know in truth that, on the contrary, their degree is great and supreme, and all of them are engraved in the supreme place; and their source rises by way of the rungs of the ladder, higher and higher, until it reaches the source that indicates the sefirot themselves and their spirituality. And the soul of these letters is the sefirot themselves in their inwardness; and the names given to them, explained in the preceding gate, are a garment to them, as explained there in chapter 1; and therefore they are holy, not to be erased. But these names and the like are such as were revealed to the holy ones who served the Most High, and to the prophets who spoke by the holy spirit; and from them the Tannaim and the Amoraim received them, a tradition from mouth to mouth back to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, from Sinai, from the mouth of the Almighty. And the prophets, peace be upon them, by way of those letters, in great seclusion and by the merit of the pure soul, would apprehend that spirituality which is clothed in the letters, and the order of the union of the grades one with another, "the loops opposite one another" (Ex. 26:5), joined "each to its sister" (Ex. 26:3), "each one cleaving to his brother" (Job 41:9); and through them they recognized the bond of the worlds and added knowledge upon their knowledge, and they knew their power and their use: not to make use of them, God forbid, but to know the ability of their Maker. And because of the many troubles, the eyes of the sages were closed and the hearts diminished, and the strength of the expounders of the Torah was weakened from apprehending the plain sense of things, all the more so in the knowledge of speculative Kabbalah, the sefirot, all the more so practical Kabbalah; until there remained among them none with strength against the troubles except Rashbi, peace be upon him, and his companions, who stood and revealed the mysteries of the world. And even his words we do not apprehend, "from shortness of spirit and from hard labor" (Ex. 6:9); for we know clearly that our poor intellect does not reach even a little of the little of the depths of his passages in this wisdom, and all his words are concealed with the utmost separation and concealment. However, by striking with the hammer of the intellect upon the difficulties and the husks that are upon the teachings, light comes out to us from apertures as thin as the cracks of a needle. There was a further cause concerning practical Kabbalah, which was revealed in the days of Nachmanides, peace be upon him, and of Rabbi Elazar of Worms, his master, and Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla, and pillars of the world like them, and likewise in the days of the Gaonim, who made use of the Great Usage and the Small Usage [Shimmusha Rabba and Shimmusha Zuta]. And all this (they caused) [we lost] through our iniquities; for they themselves did not wish to reveal them, because they saw the men of piety being gathered in and the men of deeds diminished, and they feared lest a person who is not worthy make use of them, as we have seen in many of those who came after them, and near to us, such as Joseph della Reina and the like, who destroy the house of our God and multiply our breaches. And for this reason we will not inquire into the uses of the names, although they are found in the books of the ancients, beyond explaining them as far as will be useful to study. And what is fitting to know is that all the letters depend on the four-letter name, so that some of the letters almost acquire a manifestation like it: as the Alef, whose form is two Yods and a Vav, which amount to 26, the number of the Name; and likewise Lamed hints at 26, and likewise Tet, and likewise Kof. And to this matter the combining of the alphabets with the four-letter name hints, and the combining of the vowels: to return things to their source and to bestow upon them from the supreme source. And because the spiritual things and the flaming threads are divided according to their source, and this the vowelling indicates, as hinted above in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, chapter 4, therefore it is necessary that a letter of the Name be combined with a letter of the alphabet, and both of them with all the vowels that they can bear, so as to hint at all the sources, particular and general, so that they may be bestowed upon from the supreme source. And concerning the way of their combination the Kabbalists disagreed. Some of them did not wish to rotate its combination except through the five motions of utterance, which are [given by the mnemonic] notarikon; and if so, its combination comes, for each and every letter, to twenty-five words front and twenty-five words back. And the holder of this view is the author of Sefer ha-Nikkud, where he mentioned the order of the invocation of the four-letter name. And we have seen fit to copy his language here, even though it is long, because it is useful for the knowledge of its invocation, in the knowledge of the greatness of our Former. And these are his words: "It is known that the letters have no motion in themselves; and therefore the Name, may He be blessed, put into nature, according to the intellect, powers in the whole of the mouth to bring out the letters in utterance after the likeness of their existence that is found in the book. And vowel points were placed for the letters, indicating the motion of the utterance in their transfer from the book to the mouth. And if so, those that move essentially are the letters of the mouth, and accidentally the letters of the book. And there is joined to this a necessity from the place of the partial motions; for nothing that moves moves without place and without time; and the parts of place are the distances, and the parts of time are the revolutions reckoned in the counts of years and months and days and the like. And because of the distances a person needs to know how long to extend the utterance of each and every letter. And this is the secret of the invocation. At the time that you wish to mention this honored Name, adorn yourself and seclude yourself in a particular place, so that your voice not be heard by others; and purify your heart and your soul of all the thoughts of this world, and think that at that hour your soul will be separated from your body and you will depart from this world and live in the world to come, which is the source of the life that is found scattered in every living thing; and that is the intellect, which is the source of all wisdom and understanding and knowledge, from the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom all are in great fear; and it is the fear of the one who apprehends, and it is a double fear, the fear of love and the fear of exaltedness. And when your mind comes to cleave to His mind, which gives you mind, your mind must remove from upon it all foreign minds except His mind, which is shared between you and Him through His honored and awesome Name. And therefore you need to know the likeness of its utterance; and this is its drawing:

Behold twenty-five front.

"And further, twenty-five back, and they are these:

" And in this way with the Heh, and likewise with the Vav, and likewise with the last Heh. And we have abridged it, and further set it right according to its measure; for the author of Sefer ha-Nikkud jumbled them by way of a poem, to conceal, and revealed it at the end of his words; and we have arranged it as is fitting and proper. And let us return to his words: "This is its drawing. When you begin to mention the Alef, in whatever form you mention it, because it indicates the secret of the union, do not extend it except to the measure of one breath, and do not make any break at all in that breath until you complete its pronunciation. And extend that particular breath according to the measure of the strength of the length of your breath, as one, as much as you can extend it. And chant with the Alef, and with each and every letter that is in the likeness of the vowel, which is the cholam, upward. And when you begin to mention it, direct your face toward the face of the east, not upward and not downward; and you sit wrapped in white garments, washed and pure, over all your garments, or your tallit on your head, crowned with tefillin, facing the east, for from there the light goes forth to the world; and you have five extremities toward which to move your head. And with the cholam begin from the middle of the east, and purify your thought, and raise your head with the breath little by little until you complete it with your head above; and after you complete it, bow down to the ground once. And do not separate between the breath of the Alef and the breath of the letter joined to it, except by one breath, short or long. Between one letter of the Name and the next, in the straight or in the reversed, you may take two breaths without utterance, and not more; but fewer is within your discretion. And when you complete each and every row, you have permission to take five breaths alone and not more; but fewer is within your discretion. And if you changed or erred in a row of this order, return to the head of that row until you say it properly. And like the cholam, drawn upward, chant with the chirik, drawn downward, drawing the upper power to cleave to you. And with the shuruk do not raise your head up or down, but a middle drawing, facing the middle face. And with the tzeirei draw your head from left to right, and with the kamatz from right to left. And in all of them, after you complete, if you see a form before you, bow down immediately before it; and if you hear a voice, small or great, and wish to understand what it says, answer it immediately and say, 'Speak, my lord, for your servant hears'; and do not speak at all, but incline your ears to hear what it will say to you. And if you fear a great fear that you cannot bear, even in the middle of the invocation, bow down immediately. And if you neither see nor hear, leave the matter for that whole week. And it is good further to mention it once a week, in the likeness of 'running and returning,' for concerning this thing a covenant was made. And what more shall I add to make known to you? For it is already known that, if you are wise, from the hint you will understand the whole order. And if you feel that your intellect is weak in wisdom or in tradition, or your thought strong in the vanities of the time, do not mention the Name, lest you then add to sin. And know that between the page of Yod and the page of Heh you may take twenty-five breaths and not more, provided that you do not interrupt in between, neither in speech nor in thought; and likewise between Heh and Vav, and between Vav and Heh; only fewer than twenty-five you may breathe." Thus far the words of the Rav, the author of Sefer ha-Nikkud. And his words are words of tradition from mouth to mouth, or words of a maggid; and we have lengthened in them because they are of much benefit for the knowledge of the greatness of the glory of our Former, blessed be He. And in any case, a proof has come out to us for the rotation of the Name with the letters of the alphabet with five vowels alone, in the manner of combination in words and in vowels, as we shall lengthen and explain their matter further in the Gate of Permutation, with the help of God. But the other Kabbalists, seeing that the sheva is a motion by itself besides the five motions, for it is intermediate between the patach and the segol, as the grammarians explained (even if its motion is hidden from us), added its motion in the combination of the Name; and there turned out to be six motions, and they came to thirty-six, which are six times six, in the manner of combination, as is known. And from the motions and their reckoning came out delicacies and gematrias for wisdom. And because they lengthened in the matter much, we have seen fit to devote a chapter by itself to their words:

The author of the book Ma'arakhot Elohim Chayyim expounded the opinion mentioned at length, and these are his words: "And to cleave to Him with a wondrous cleaving, which is called oneness, it is fitting to bring Him to mind in each and every part of the hour, which is 1,080 parts; as the rotation of His Name, may He be blessed, with each and every letter, with the vowels whose sign is notarikon, and with the letter unvowelled, will be 144; and your sign: 'The eternal God [Elohei kedem, kedem = 144] is a dwelling place' (Deut. 33:27); you will see further on, with the help of the Name. And let us reckon to know this: that He is the God of old, Former and Creator and Maker and Emanator of all; and He is from the letters, for the word of the Lord goes out from its place, from which all speech goes out; and in the general category of speech is every name of every kind of the kinds of existents; and all the formed go out from one name, that is to say, the name YHVH, which is combined with each and every letter that is in the 231 gates, thirty-six times. And we have combined one letter, and so it will be with all the other twenty-two letters: this is the combination of Alef with Yod and with Heh and with Vav and with Heh; and understand this. And the reason for the going out of every thing and every language from the 231 gates in the rotation of the alphabet is that if you make, by way of example, twenty-two circles one within another, and in each one of them twenty-two letters, then you will see with your eyes how all the things and the languages are combined from their rotation in 231 gates; and it returns around, and the wheel returns front and back, 231 gates; that is to say, 231 gates of front and 231 gates of back. And behold, each and every letter of the 231 gates is combined with the four letters of the name YHVH 144 times. How so? The Alef is combined with the Yod and with the six vowels thirty-six times, and likewise with the Heh, with those same vowels, thirty-six times, and likewise with the Vav, with those same vowels, thirty-six times, and likewise with the last Heh, with those same vowels, thirty-six times: behold, 144 times with the Alef. And likewise with each and every one of the twenty-two letters; it turns out that 144 times 22 amounts to 3,168 words, in the twenty-two letters alone.

"And further, reckon 3,168 times 231 gates: their number amounts to 731,808. And all these are His names indeed, that is to say, the substance of the formation; for He clothed the formless thing with form, and made that which is not into that which is, and the emanation drawn from Nothing, which has no form or likeness or intellect, except that all the wisdom of the creatures is withheld from knowing them; and behold, through these havayot He brought out all the existents from nothing to something:

"Your eyes will look straight ahead [and see] how the rotation of the letters of the name YHVH with each and every letter, with the six known vowels, amounts to 1,080; therefore there are 1,080 parts to the hour. And likewise the rotation of the name YHVH with the Alef and the vowels is 1,080; and likewise with Bet, and likewise with Gimel, and likewise with all of them:

"See and understand the wonder of counsels: how in each and every part of the hour it is fitting for us to think of His awe. And this is 'Do not turn to the idols' (Lev. 19:4): 'do not turn to [what comes] from your own mind' (Shabbat 149a), for all the day you shall think of the love of Heaven. Therefore it is forbidden to speak idle words; for His Name, may He be blessed, is in the rotation of 1,080, and it is fitting to think of the glory of His Name 'when you sit, and when you walk, and when you lie down, and when you rise' (Deut. 6:7), in the four letters of the honored and awesome Name YHVH, which is with all; and therefore His Name is YHVH. And they are: the rotation of Yod with Alef, thirty-six words; and likewise the rotation of Alef with Heh, thirty-six words; and likewise the rotation of Vav with Alef, thirty-six words; and likewise the rotation of Alef with the second Heh: behold 144 [kedem] times with Alef, as we said above once; and they amount to 1,080 by gematria, for those who understand combination. Therefore there are 1,080 parts to each hour, for there are 1,080 parts for each and every letter in the rotation of YHVH: in the rotation of Alef-Yod, thirty-six words, amounting to 396; and the rotation of Alef-Heh, thirty-six words, amounting to 216; and the rotation of Alef-Vav, thirty-six words, amounting to 252; and the rotation of Alef-Heh, thirty-six words, amounting to 216. The sum total: 396, 216, 252, 216, which are 1,080 parts. And understand another secret, and it is this: if you combine and rotate all the twelve diagonal boundaries of the name YHVH, and Alef with all of them, they will be 1,080; therefore the day is twelve hours.

"And further, open the eyes of your intellect to see: if the name YHVH is at the head of the wheel and the Alef at the end (for the wheel turns front and back), it will also be 1,080; and behold two 1,080s, two hours for each constellation, that is to say, for each one of the twelve diagonal boundaries of the name YHVH, for which the divine constellations have the right [of the firstborn] over the constellations that are in the spheres, and 'at their command they encamp and at their command they journey' (Num. 9:20). And there turn out to be twenty-four hours and twenty-four 1,080s for the divine constellations mentioned, between the front and the back: twelve 1,080s for the back and twelve 1,080s for the front; and likewise twenty-four hours for one day, between the day and the night, twelve hours for the day and twelve hours for the night. Therefore in each part of the hour one should think of His awe and plant His love and His fear in our hearts, since He brought every thing into being, and within the heart the mouth of each and every man was emanated. And from Him are the twenty-eight times mentioned in the book of Ecclesiastes (chapter 3), fourteen of them one thing and fourteen others their substitutes, corresponding to the twenty-eight camps of the moon, which are twenty-eight camps of the Shekhinah. By the twelve divine constellations that we spoke of He changes the times, and 'to everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose' (Eccl. 3:1), from His ability and His being." Thus far its words.

And its fruits are sweeter than honey and the honeycomb. However, since it is clear and well known that the powers of the vowels are ten, even if their actions are five, then just as the sheva enters into the reckoning of the motions, so it is fitting that all the other motions enter; for in truth there is a great difference between the kings and the servants [the long and the short vowels], whether in their motion, that is to say, their sound, or in their action, that is to say, their power and their hint, as will be explained, with the help of the Name, in the Gate of Vowel Points. And if so, it is fitting that we combine the name YHVH with all the vowels, with the letters; and then the combination of all the powers with their source will necessarily follow, as we explained at the beginning of chapter 1. And behold, its combination will be in this way. When we search for the totality of the motions, they are found to be twelve, and they are: kamatz, patach, tzeirei, segol, shuruk, shurek, cholam, chirik, sheva, chataf kamatz, chataf patach, and chataf segol; and each one of them has a hint by itself; and although they were not counted in the vowels of the sefirot that we explained above, they will be explained in the Gate of Vowel Points, with the help of the Name. It turns out that the combination of the Name in the vowels with the letters is 144 [kedem] words; for they are twelve times twelve, which are 144, and they are "the eternal God [Elohei kedem] is a dwelling place," as explained above. And this is the order of their combination, with the help of Heaven:

And likewise for each and every letter of the four-letter name, front and back, and likewise for all the letters of the alphabet, until all of them are combined with their source and receive a great abundance of good effluence from the supreme source, as we shall lengthen on the matter of the letters in the Gate of Letters, with the help of Heaven. But we have seen some of the Kabbalists agreeing with the opinion of the author of Sefer ha-Nikkud; and so they wrote the name Koh [25], which goes out from the verse (Ex. 2:12) "And he turned this way and that way [koh va-khoh]"; and it is that they combine the word Koh twenty-five times front and twenty-five times back, such as Koh, Hokh, in the way that the author of Sefer ha-Nikkud wrote above. And likewise all who write the combination of the vowels wrote only the combination of five vowels alone. And likewise Rashbi, peace be upon him, concerning the vowels, gave the sign "engravings of a signet" [pittuchei chotam], and indicated that they are five emanated sefirot, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet (and in it are included Yesod and Malkhut, as we explained in the preceding gates), and Netzach and Hod. But in the commentary on Sefer Yetzirah, on the matter of the [creation of] man, they wrote like the words of the author of Ma'arakhot Elohim Chayyim, that they are six times six, which amount to thirty-six, and they wrote it in his language word for word; and it seems that the thing is necessary there, for there they spoke of the Work of Creation, in the mention of the alphabets, in the crowning of the letters in the creation of each and every limb. And likewise the author of the book Or Zarua wrote on the matter of the motions of the lulav that they are thirty-six; and he said: "Why thirty-six? To hint to you at the holy letters that are joined and combined in their motions and their rotations, thirty-six motions; and this is the order of their motions according to notarikon: Alef-Yod, etc.; and likewise Alef rotates with Heh, and likewise afterwards with Vav, and afterwards with Heh." Thus far its words.

And since this matter is a dispute of the great ones, and we have no revealing in it at all from Rashbi, peace be upon him, the thing remains pending until a teacher of righteousness comes. However it may be, from it it is explained what the matter of this need is, for the creation of man, of the combination of the alphabet, in crowning the letter by which the limb would be created, and its union with the four-letter name and its being combined with it. The reason is that, because the character of man (that is to say, his body and his veins and his sinews and the lines of his limbs and the measures of his limbs, all in measure and in weight) all hints at the upper limbs, his creation must necessarily include all the spiritual things, all of them; for so he is the mold of all the existents, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 8. And because the intellect and speech are a power given in him to hint at the Ein Sof, the Cause of Causes, who gives life to and conducts all things, corporeal and spiritual, and causes them to ascend until they reach His Self, so the intellect and speech conduct all the things that are included in the body, such as the powers of the soul and its matters. And a proof of this: did not [our Sages] of blessed memory say that the soul is found in the body of a person after his death, and prove it from the verse (Job 14:22), "and his soul mourns over him"?
