And nevertheless, although it is within the body, it does not perform its actions, because the effluence of the intellect is withheld from it, and because there is no word and language and letter and speech that includes it. Therefore those sages who engaged in the work of formation in the order of the alphabet, although they would create men, these did not speak, because of the absence of the power that resembles the Ein Sof, as we said, which was not bestowed upon him according to the order of the alphabets. And in this way will be understood what some write: the name of forty-two and the name of seventy-two and the other names, combined with their sources, like this: יאהבוג"ה, which is the name Abag combined with its source YHVH, and so the whole of it. And there are those who write it in another way, like this: אב"גיהוהית"ץ, and so the whole of it. And likewise there are those who write the name of seventy-two like this: יו"ה הוו"ה ייה"ל וי"ה, and so the whole of it: the name Vehu with its source YHVH, and the name Yeli with its source YHVH, to the end. And there are those who combine it with the name Ehyeh, for it too is its source, though not so supreme as the first, as we shall explain on the name of forty-two. And the reason for all this is that in the return of the thing to its source, or in its joining with it, it will bestow upon its particulars a great abundance of good effluence, like the combined name יאהדונה"י and the name יאההוי"הה, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 24. And with this the mishnayot of Sefer Yetzirah will be explained: "He crowned such-and-such a letter and bound a crown to it," etc. And the intent: "He crowned" [himlikh] hints at Malkhut; and "bound" [KeSheR] means teKi'ah, Shevarim, teRu'ah, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, as explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim and the Ra'aya Meheimna in numberless places; and in the three of them their branches are included, Netzach, Hod and Yesod, and likewise their heads, Keter, Chokhmah and Binah. "Crown" [keter] hints at the Supernal Keter; or it may hint at the first three, which are a crown to the Patriarchs. And then a great effluence was bestowed upon that letter, and it had in it power to create that limb and that constellation and that thing intended by it. And now that we have set out this matter in these chapters, we come to the explanation of the names one by one, with the help of the Living One:

Behold, in the prayer of Rabbi Nechunya ben ha-Kanah, peace be upon him, he attributed to Keter this name, which is Araritha [ארארית"א], and gave it a sign in the initials: "Echad Rosh Achduto Rosh Yichudo Temurato Echad" [One, head of His oneness, head of His union, His substitution One]. Thus far. And concerning this name Rav Hamai Gaon wrote in Sefer ha-Iyyun, and in his commentary he brought a baraita, and these are its words: "We have learned: Rabbi Yishmael said: That day I and Akiva ben Yosef were finishing [our studies] with Rabbi Nechunya ben ha-Kanah, and Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon was there. And I asked Rabbi Nechunya and said to him: Show me the glory of the King of the world, so that the knowledge of Him may be explained in my heart through His other works. He said to me: Son of the proud, come, let us engage with the great ring with which the heavens are sealed, whose name is Araritha, and with the ring of the earth, whose name is  A H V Y  [אהו"י], and I will show you all. I entered into the innermost part of the outer holy palace and brought out from there the book of Rabbi Nechunya ben ha-Kanah, which is called Sefer Heikhalot; and I found written at the beginning of the book thus: Mighty in the chambers of greatness, who sits on the wheels of His chariot, in the seals of Ehyeh asher Ehyeh, and in the great ring with which the heavens are sealed, whose name is Araritha; its sign: One, head of His oneness, head of His union, His substitution One; single and unified, One. And in the ring of the earth, whose name is  A H V Y; its sign: One, Was, and Will Be, Union; and the intermediate between the two of them is Is." Thus far the words of the baraita. And we wish to explain it according to the explanations that we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles.

And behold, Keter is mighty over them; for even in those chambers there is no complete and correct apprehension, for it is mighty and concealed from those chambers. But it sits on the wheels of the chariot, which are "the networks that are upon the capitals that are upon the heads of the pillars" (1 Kings 7:17), which are Chokhmah and Binah, which are over Gedulah and Gevurah, which are over the two pillars Netzach and Hod, Yachin and Boaz. And Chokhmah and Binah are a chariot to Keter, and to them it is more revealed, in that they are concealed in themselves, not on the side of Gedulah and Gevurah, which are drawn from Chokhmah and Binah. And it is further possible to explain: for in the Zohar Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that in Keter the manifestation of the Emanation is not revealed in its own self because of its great concealment, and all the manifestation of the branches that branch out from its own self are only Chokhmah and Binah, and they are those that spread out in the very Keter, to reveal and to emanate the Emanation in it itself; and nevertheless there is no emanation there except through the Chesed concealed there, and its branches spread out in the very Keter; and likewise Keter is called supernal Chesed. And this matter has been explained at length by us in the book Or Yakar, in the first part, in our commentary on the Idra, with the help of Heaven. However it may be, from there it is learned that the inner Chesed is Binah, and Keter branches out essentially from Chokhmah to Binah and not further. And it is possible that concerning this he said "mighty," and concealed; and the manifestation of its might is revealed "in the chambers of greatness" [gedulah], that is, Binah and Chokhmah concealed in it, and Gedulah branches out and builds between these two concealed chambers. And he said "who sits on the wheels of His chariot": it would mean that He sits upon Ze'ir Anpin, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, said in the Idra, that He sits upon "a throne of sparks of fire, to subdue them," and as we explained in the book mentioned, with the help of Heaven; and he used the language of the verse, "its wheels burning fire" (Dan. 7:9). And he said that the seal of Ehyeh asher Ehyeh is the first three, as we explained in the preceding gate; for these two names indicate the concealment of the Emanation in Keter and the paucity of apprehension of it, and likewise in Chokhmah and Binah; and this is the language "mighty," and likewise the language "in the seals," explanation: in concealment, for the seal is what conceals the thing sealed. "And in the great ring," etc.: concerning this name we have seen commentators who explained it from the language of ari [lion]; and the intent is the abundance of might and strength and majesty; and for this the mightiest in the world is called by the name lion, etc. And it is possible that because this name is the seal of the heavens, whose explanation is the sustaining of the world, made strong in His great compassion so as not to totter, it is called by the name of the lion, which indicates compassion, as it is written (Ezek. 1:10), "and the face of a lion on the right," etc. And it is known that above, in Keter, is the prevailing of simple compassion; and therefore the name was doubled, for the strength of the action. And it is possible that it is the language of arita de-dalayei mentioned in the Gemara (Chullin 107a), whose matter is the trough from which they water the plantings; and because Keter is the source to water all the upper plantings, therefore it is called by this name; and the letters Alef-Resh were doubled in it to indicate that it is the source of sources. Further, it is possible that its explanation is from the language of or [light], for it is light to all the lights. And nevertheless it is very difficult for us, for this name is a feminine form, and it is fitting to keep the matter of femininity far from Keter. But from this we can say that it is a title for the Binah that is in Keter, as we explained this matter at length in the Gate From Below to Above, chapter 5. And now with this his saying "and in the great ring" is correct; for he did not say rabba but rabbeta, a feminine form. And the explanation of his words: the ring is Binah, and in it Tiferet, which is called heavens, was sealed and found and emanated. Or it would mean "with which the heavens are sealed": explanation: the ring is Binah, in the secret of avir, or with Yod, "Let there be light," as we explained in the book Or Yakar, in Gate 3.
And behold, the heavens, which is Tiferet with the six extremities, are sealed in the very ring.

And behold, the ring is Binah, in the inclusion of Keter and Chokhmah; and the seal is Tiferet, which is the manifestation of the Da'at concealed in her. And it is possible in this way to explain that ar is ari, male, and arita female, to indicate the union of Chokhmah and Binah together within Keter. This is when we explain it as the language of lion, compassion, as we explained above. And likewise we can also explain it in the language of light: that they are two lights together, as we explained. "One, head," etc.: explanation: it is known that echad [one] is the manifestation of oneness itself, but the word meyuchad [unified] is the joining of a thing that has been joined, a unified union. And now it is known that the union of Chokhmah and Binah is in two ways. Either the manifestation of their union in the secret of avir, that is, Yod, Chokhmah, or, Binah, unified as avir; and this is their manifestation before their emanation, while they are in Keter itself, Chokhmah within Binah and both of them in Keter; and this union is called by the name oneness [achdut], for they are not separate ones that were unified, but they were always one from their beginning. But the second union that Chokhmah and Binah have is their union after their emanation, in their place, as Abba and Imma; this union is called by the name union [yichud], for after they were not unified, they were unified. It turns out according to this that Chokhmah and Binah with Keter have three aspects: either their union before their emanation, or the manifestation of their emanation without union, or their union after their emanation. And because there is never separation between them, for the first three are always reckoned as one, he said "One, head of His oneness": explanation: One is their true title at the beginning of their oneness together, that is, before their emanation. And likewise it is One also as "head of His union," that is, their union after their emanation. And also when this is changed, that is, when they are separate, God forbid, they are One; and this is what he said, "His substitution One": explanation: also when there are substitutions of the union, their true title is One; for it never changes, it does not lack and does not exceed. And after [he had spoken of] the union of the first three on all their sides, and also the union of the manifestation of Keter in the whole Emanation, he said "single and unified, One." And in Sefer ha-Bahir too something like this matter is found concerning Keter, and these are its words: "Alef: the Supernal Keter; blessed and blessed be His name and His people. And who are His people? Israel, as it is written, 'Know that the Lord, He is God; it is He who made us, and not we [ve-lo anachnu]' (Ps. 100:3): and to the Alef we are, to recognize and to know One, oneness, and unified, etc.; for He is one and unified in all His names." Thus far. "The Supernal Keter, blessed and blessed be His name": the intent is that the Supernal Keter is bestowed upon from the source of all the beings, and this is "blessed"; or it would mean the source of blessings, as we explained in Gate 23. And likewise "blessed be His name": explanation: the other sefirot, which are a garment to it, that is, the matter of "name," as we explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, under the entry shem. "And who are His people?": it was difficult for him that the matter of a people does not apply to Keter, that a people or the like should be related to it. And to this he answered: Israel; for the souls of Israel have their hold in Keter, for so Tiferet rises to it by way of the middle line. And for this he brought a proof from the verse: "and not we" is written with Alef and read with Vav ["and His we are"], and its explanation is "and to the Alef we are," that is, Keter; and so it is explained in the Zohar (Vayera, folio 120b). And now there is authority for the reading and there is authority for the written tradition: for because "His we are," "to the Alef we are."

And the matter of "One, oneness, and unified": explanation: One in relation to itself, for it has no second; and further, that it is the first that enters within the bounds of number, for before it there is no number, "and before one what do you count?" For "one" in itself does not apply to the necessarily existent, for the reason that the oneness of the one is apprehended, bounded on all its sides, and this is impossible in the Emanator, in whom there is no apprehension except that He is necessarily existent, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 1. For this he said that it is one and before it there is no number. "Oneness": explanation: unified in its branches and its aspects, so that there is no separation in it at all, but one that is unified in its own self. And the explanation of "and unified" would be: unified in the lower sefirot, and it unifies itself with them. And in this way we will explain "one, single, and unified": "one," as we explained; "single," explanation: unified in its branches; "and unified," explanation: unified in all the sefirot in complete union. And he said "single and unified, One," and did not arrange them in the order "one, single and unified": the intent is that also when Keter is single, that is, the manifestation of the union of its branches with its own self, as we explained, and likewise when it is unified, that is, its union in the emanated sefirot, it is always One; and it turns out that in all its aspects it is always One. And there are those who explained One, Single and Unified as Keter, Chokhmah and Binah: for Keter is called One, and Chokhmah Single, and Binah Unified; and they would be hard put to find a relation for them:

"And in the ring of the earth, whose name is  A H V Y": concerning this name some commentators said that this is the principal name of the Holy One, blessed be He, and it is  A H V Y; and the Holy One, blessed be He, hid His name for the discerning in the name Ehyeh and in the name YHVH, for from between the two of them the name  A H V Y  comes out, and it is the principal name, and these names, in which the letters are doubled, were given to the common people, etc.; and in this they lengthened with their mouths to deepen their traditions. And may the Compassionate One save us from this opinion; we will not consent to it nor listen to it; for the principal names are those that came in the mouth of the Torah. And although this name may be holy like the other names, the names that may not be erased are certainly holier than it, without doubt.

And further, from the words of Rabbi Nechunya we can object to them: for he said that the seal of the heavens is Araritha, and the name of the seal of the earth he said is  A H V Y; it turns out that the name Araritha is more concealed and exalted than the name  A H V Y, and there is no doubt about this. And we have lengthened in this to benefit the discerning, so that they not be enticed after that opinion. And Rabbi Nechunya was precise: for in the initials of Araritha, the seal of the heavens, he said "One, head of His oneness, head of His union, His substitution One"; because this name is in the Supernal Keter, the first effect, which draws near to its source, and whoever touches it is as one who touches the glory of the King of the world, he did not wish to derive any word from it at all, but language indicating oneness. And he said "His substitution One": the intent is that it is never exchanged as one for another, God forbid, whether before being and emanation or after being and emanation, as we explained. But in the name  A H V Y, which is below the sefirah Keter, which is the spreading out to Malkhut, he said Was, Is and Will Be, so that we may know that the language of being [havayah] is not derived from Keter upward at all, and not even in Keter, because every being has a beginning, before which it was not. And even if we say "Was, Is, and Will Be," explanation: "Was," that before that being it also was, nevertheless this is nothing; for whatever enters under being has an end and has a beginning; and the language "was, is, and will be" is derived only from Binah downward, and Binah is not included, because Chokhmah and Binah are the bound of being, that is, beginning and end, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation.

And behold, Rabbi Yishmael asked Rabbi Nechunya ben ha-Kanah, "Show me the glory of the King of the world," whose intent was that he should teach him the manifestation of the Emanation. And behold, by these two seals he taught him the manifestation of the Emanation before its emanation and its manifestation after its emanation: for in the name Araritha, which is the seal of the heavens, he taught him the manifestation of Keter, Arikh Anpin, revealed through Binah, as we expounded at length above; and the seal  A H V Y  indicates the spreading out.

And behold, this name differs from the name Ehyeh in two ways. For the name Ehyeh indicates concealment, as we explained above, and this indicates some revealing. And likewise the Yod in Ehyeh, Vav in  A H V Y, concerning the secret of the Vav, the six extremities that spread out; and because it is not a complete spreading out, the last Heh comes in the secret of Yod, to indicate the concealment; for Malkhut is not yet built in the secret of Heh, so as to be revealed below. And this is the secret of  A H V Y, whose explanation is "One, Was, and Will Be; and the intermediate between the two of them, Is." And these three are "[the Lord] reigns, [the Lord] reigned, [the Lord] will reign," for all is in Tiferet; and it is: "Was" in Gedulah, "Is" in Gevurah, "and Will Be" in Tiferet.

And this matter is bound up with the secret of the shemitot [cosmic cycles]: the preceding one Chesed, the future one Tiferet, and the present one Gevurah. And to the sefirah Chokhmah he further attributed a name like this: Ayah Beyah Geyah Deyah, etc., to the end of all the letters. And the reason is that the letters and the ten sefirot are thirty-two paths; the source is the name Yah, Chokhmah; and the twenty-two letters hint at twenty-two paths, and the source itself is the ten utterances; they are thirty-two paths, as explained in Sefer Yetzirah. And its vowelling is sheva and kamatz, to hint at (Lev. 5:12) "and the priest shall take a fistful [ve-kamatz]," in Chesed, and (Isa. 66:16) "by fire [ba-esh] will the Lord judge," (Job 1:15) "and Sheba [sheva] fell upon them and took them," in Gevurah; to hint at the spreading out of the paths in the secret of judgment and compassion in the sefirot below. And at its end there are further other havayot like these:

Further, Rabbi Nechunya ben ha-Kanah attributes to the first three these names: כוז"ו במוכס"ז כוז"ו [Kuzu Bemukhsaz Kuzu]. And these are his words in his prayer, after he mentioned three sefirot; at the end of the third sefirah he said: "And all became one head; and these are the names that make all of them equal: Kuzu Bemukhsaz Kuzu; and they are unified, YHVH our God YHVH is one." Thus far its words. (And in another book we have found other vowels for this name.)

And there is one who explained this name, and these are his words: "These three names, YHVH Eloheinu YHVH, are in the reckoning of the following letters; that is to say, you take the letters second to them in the alphabet: Yod-Kaf, Heh-Vav, Vav-Zayin, Heh-Vav; Alef-Bet, Lamed-Mem, Heh-Vav, Yod-Kaf, Nun-Samekh, Vav-Zayin; Yod-Kaf, Heh-Vav, Vav-Zayin, Heh-Vav. And its vowelling is like the vowelling of the written text. 'And they are unified,' etc.: explanation: although these names came in the reckoning of the following letters, and therefore would not indicate this oneness so much, for this he said: nevertheless they are unified, 'the Lord our God, the Lord is one.'" Thus far its words.

And we wish to explain what we have drawn up from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 55, folio 86), "a little here, a little there"; and we cannot copy his language because of its length. And the matter is that these two hands [yad, 14] are fourteen letters: a right hand, "the great hand," and they are YHVH Eloheinu YHVH, and they are right-sided; and further a left hand, "the strong hand," and they are Kuzu Bemukhsaz Kuzu, and they are left-sided, fourteen letters; and they are twenty-eight [koach, strength]. And corresponding to these hands there is further "a lifted hand," and it is YHVH, יוד ה"א וא"ו ה"א; and it is the lifted hand. And corresponding to it there is another hand, and it is Ehyeh, אל"ף ה"א יו"ד ה"א. And these two hands are twenty-eight, which are clothed in the twenty-eight letters of the Work of Creation. And of this it is said (Lam. 1:6), "and they went without strength [koach] before the pursuer," because that strength was withheld through iniquities. And of this Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Num. 14:17), "And now, let the strength [koach] of Adonai be great," which are the twenty-eight times of the moon, which are twenty-eight days, fourteen full and fourteen lacking, fourteen right and fourteen left; and therefore he said "let the strength of Adonai be great," which are twenty-eight. And the two hands, the great and the strong, are Chesed and Gevurah, and they are bestowed from Chokhmah and Binah. And it is known that one opens with merit first; therefore the great hand precedes the strong hand in its letters. And this strength is in Binah; and this is Chokhmah, koach mah: mah [45] is in Chokhmah, and so the four-letter name in its filling amounts; and koach [28] is in Binah. And of this it is said (Ps. 111:6), "The strength [koach] of His works He has declared to His people": the "work" is in Binah, and there is the koach; and "declared" means drew down. And it is known that the four-letter name is also twenty-eight in the filling of its filling. And this is Chokhmah, koach mah: for their totality is mah, which is in Chokhmah, and their particulars koach, which are in Binah. And these are: יו"ד ה"א is compassion, the world of the male; וא"ו ה"א is judgment, the world of the female, as we explained in the Gate of Names, chapter 1. And the female is always toward the left and the male toward the right; and although we said that Yah is compassion and Vav-Heh is judgment, nevertheless we shall not deny that the Yod is more compassion than the Heh, and the Vav more compassion than the second Heh.

And behold now, יו"ד ה"א are the five fingers of the right hand, and וא"ו ה"א the five fingers of the left hand. And it is known that in the fingers there are twenty-eight joints, fourteen for each hand. And likewise the five letters יו"ד ה"א have fourteen letters in the filling of their filling: יו"ד וא"ו דל"ת ה"א אל"ף: behold fourteen. In four letters, which are four fingers, there are three joints in each finger, three letters in each and every letter; and in the fifth letter, which is the thumb, there are two joints, two letters, as is known. And likewise in וא"ו ה"א, which are the five fingers of the left hand: in these five letters there are fourteen joints, like this: וא"ו אל"ף וא"ו ה"א אל"ף: behold fourteen. In four letters, which are four fingers, there are three joints in each finger, three letters in each and every letter; and in the fifth letter, which is the thumb, there are two letters, two joints, as is known. And we have already explained that the Heh always has judgment in it; therefore the masters of the lot, who cast lots with the fingers, say that one should not cast lots with the thumb, because the princes of judgment depend on it. Behold, these letters are hinted at in the lifted hand mentioned above, which is in Tiferet, as is known; and it includes two hands, as we explained above.

And behold, the hand bestowed in Tiferet is drawn from Keter, which is above it; and the root of all this is YHVH Eloheinu YHVH; and they are: YHVH in Keter, YHVH in Chokhmah, Eloheinu in Binah, and she is in the middle, just as judgment, which is Isaac, is between Abraham and Jacob, which are two teki'ot, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar. And although in chapter 2 we explained it in another way in the name of Rashbi, peace be upon him, nevertheless these and those are the words of the living God. And let us return to our subject: that Binah is between Keter and Chokhmah, so as to be sweetened into compassion, to bestow compassion upon Gevurah; and all the hands are unified in YHVH Eloheinu YHVH. And this is what Rabbi Nechunya explained in his prayer: "and they are unified in YHVH Eloheinu YHVH." Thus far. Further, we have found in the tradition of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, that from this name branches chain down, and they are in the number of its letters; and these are its words: "Keruvi'el the great, Vakhri'el the great, Za'ani'el the great (missing); Ba'arni'el the great, Mali'el the great, Va'ani'el the great, Kokhvi'el the great, Suri'el the great, Z"K the great; Kaspi'el the great, Velili'el the great, Zutri'el the great, and Mali'el the great." Thus far [the initials of the names spell Kuzu Bemukhsaz Kuzu]. And there is no doubt that these are sparks emanated from this name; certainly each and every letter emanates one power, as in the matter that happened with the name of forty-two, as we shall explain in chapter 12:
On the name of seventy-two. And it is related to Chesed, for so the holy Rabbi Nechunya explained, as we shall explain, with the help of the Name. And this is the whole of it:

והו ילי סיט עלם מהש ללה אכא כהת הזי אלד לאו ההע יזל מבה הרי הקם לאו כלי לוו פהל נלך ייי מלה חהו נתה האא ירת שאה ריי אום לכב ושר יחו להח כוק מנד אני חעם רהע ייז ההה מיב וול ילה סאל ערי עשל מיה והו דני החש עמם ננא נית מבה פוי נמם ייל הרח מצר ומב יהה ענו מחי דמב מנק איע חבו ראה יבם היי מום:

And it is called by the name seventy-two because there are seventy-two words in it. And there are those who call it Aryeh [lion], because its letters are in the number of aryeh, which amounts to 216. And Rabbi Nechunya related this name to Chesed and vowelled it as marked. But in the book of the one who speaks by the mouth of a maggid he said that its vowelling is with the name Ehyeh, in this way: segol, sheva, segol, and the last Heh has no vowel; "and with the vowels this great name acts with strength. And the secret of the segol is the secret of the whole spirituality, the secret of the white fire, and it is in three points to hint at this secret. And the secret of the sheva is the secret of the attribute of judgment; and in order to act with strength it was mixed with the segol, for it is wholly a piece of judgment, and the segol is complete compassion. And this is the secret of Ehyeh in its vowelling and in its combination and in its simple form." Thus far its words.

Further, Rabbi Nechunya wrote that it is a name for Chesed, which is divided into seventy-two bridges, and each and every bridge has one of these names. And he called them bridges as a parable for the crossing of the waters of Chesed. And this name goes out from the verses "Vayyisa," "Vayyavo," "Vayyet" (Ex. 14:19–21): two of the verses in their order, and the second from end to beginning. How so? "Vayyisa" is the secret of Chesed, in straight order; "Vayyavo" the reverse, in the secret of Gevurah; "Vayyet" in straight order, toward Tiferet. And so they explained the thing and its reason in the Zohar, and these are its words in parashat Beshalach (folio 51b): "The combination of these letters: the first letters are inscribed in their order, in a straight way, because all the first letters are found in Chesed, to go in a straight way, in an ordered arrangement. The second letters are inscribed in a rotation backwards, because all the second letters are found in Gevurah, to reveal judgments and weapons that come from the side of the left. The third letters are letters inscribed in their order, to show a hue, to be crowned in the holy King; and all is joined and bound in Him, and He is crowned with His diadems in a straight way, and inscribed on this side and on that side, as a king who is crowned with all. Here is inscribed the holy Name engraved in seventy-two words, which are crowned in the Patriarchs, the supernal holy chariot. And if you say: these third letters, why are they not written, some of them in a straight way in their order and some of them backwards, to make straight for this side and for that side? For we have learned, 'You have established equity [meisharim]' (Ps. 99:4): the Holy One, blessed be He, makes equity for two sides; and it is written, 'And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall pass through from end to end' (Ex. 26:28): this is the Holy One, blessed be He; Rabbi Yitzchak said: this is Jacob; and all is one. But [it is like] a king who is complete in all, whose mind is complete in all. What is the way of that king? His face shines like the sun always, because he is complete; and when he judges, he judges for good and judges for ill; and therefore one must be on guard before him. He who is a fool sees the king's face shining and smiling and is not on guard before him; and he who is wise sees the king's face shining and says: The king is certainly complete; he is complete in all; his mind is complete; I see that in that shining judgment sits and is covered, although it is not seen, for otherwise he would not be a complete king; and therefore one must be on guard. So the Holy One, blessed be He, is complete always, in this manner and in that manner; but He is seen only in the shining of the face; and therefore the wicked fools are not on guard before Him, and the righteous wise say: The King is complete; although His face appears shining, judgment is covered within it; therefore one must be on guard before Him. Rabbi Yehudah said: From here: 'I the Lord have not changed' (Mal. 3:6): I have not leapt to another place; in Me all is included; these two hues are included in Me; therefore all is seen in a straight way. And although the letters hold onto this side and that side, they are written in their order." Thus far its words.

And his words are sweeter than honey and the honeycomb, clear and refined. And from it it is explained that the verse Vayyet is in Tiferet, and so it is proven from within the passage there; and the combination of the Name from the verse Vayyavo is in Gevurah. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 112b) it is the reverse, and these are its words: "'And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea,' etc., 'and made the sea dry land [charavah]' (Ex. 14:21): by the strength of Gabriel, the messenger of Gevurah, who is appointed over the sword [charba]; and therefore it is said of it, 'and made the sea dry land.' From the side of Uriel, the messenger of the middle pillar, he separated between water and fire; this is what is written, 'And it came between the camp of Egypt,' which is a foreign fire, 'and the camp of Israel,'" etc. Thus far its words.

He taught explicitly that the verse Vayyet is in Gevurah and the verse Vayyavo in Tiferet, the reverse of the combination of the Name: for the verse Vayyavo is reversed, that is, the judgment of Gevurah, and the verse Vayyet straight, from the side of the compassion of Tiferet. And it is difficult. And it is possible to say that when we examine his language well, in that he said "from the side of Uriel," and likewise said "by the strength of Gabriel," it implies that "and made the sea dry land" was always in Tiferet and through Uriel its angel; but it was "by the strength of Gabriel" because the dry land (that is to say, the power to dry) is from the side of Gevurah; therefore it was done by the power of its angel, although it is an action done from the side of Tiferet. And likewise he said "from the side of Uriel he separated," etc.: that is, although that action was by the power of Gevurah; for the one who stands between the water and the fire is Tiferet; therefore it was necessarily in Gevurah from the side of its aspect with Tiferet; and this is what he said, "from the side of Uriel," etc. And likewise he was precise in saying "the middle pillar," for it is the man in between. This is what seems to resolve it at a time such as this; and in our commentary Or Yakar the matter will be lengthened, with the help of Heaven. And although these three verses hint at the three Patriarchs, nevertheless the totality of this name is in Chesed, as hinted in the prayer of Rabbi Nechunya; and likewise chesed amounts to seventy-two; and so are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in countless places. And there is no wonder in the thing; as is known, the essence of the particular is not like its whole, for each one is a manifestation by itself, as we expounded at length in the Gate of Manifestations.

And behold, its particulars are in the three Patriarchs, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, and the whole of it together is in Chesed. And according to the way of the combination of the Name marked above, Vayyavo, which is Gevurah, is found between Vayyisa and Vayyet, which are Gedulah and Tiferet, to hint at the arbitration of judgment toward compassion, in the secret of the teki'ot, as we hinted at the end of the preceding chapter. And for this reason its totality is Chesed; but its particulars are Gevurah, and so its letters amount to the number of gevurah, 216; and so it is well known in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in many places. And something like this is found in the Zohar (in the Introduction, folio 7b), on the matter of Habakkuk, the son of the Shunammite, whom Elisha revived. It is explained there that through the letters of the seventy-two names, which are 216, his body was sustained, and through this his name was called Habakkuk, which amounts to 216, the number of the letters in the name of seventy-two; and through the seventy-two words Elisha was clothed, to return his spirit to him. And from what he said, that the sustaining of the body was through the letters and the returning of the spirit was through the words, it appears explicitly from here that the seventy-two words are like a spirit and soul to the letters. And the matter is that the words are the gathering of the letters, like the great branches, which are the gathering of the nourishments of the small branches and the twigs and the leaves.

And behold, according to this, the Name as a whole, in its totality, which is the gathering of the verses, is like the whole tree; and the verse, which is the gathering of the words, is like the great branch that spreads out from the body of the tree; and from this great branch so-and-so many branches spread out, which are words; and from a word further thin branches and leaves spread out, which are so-and-so many letters. And it turns out according to this that the section, which is the gathering of the verses, is a soul to the branches, which are the verses; and the verses draw nourishment and effluence from their source, which is the section; and likewise the words draw from the verses, and the letters from the words; and this is a soul to that, and that a soul to this, and this a garment to that. And the matter is that the upper spirituality is in this way: for from the supreme source, necessarily existent, ten branches spread out, spiritual forms, drawing effluence from it; and it is root and stock to them, and on it all depends, like grapes in a cluster.

And behold, He performs through them the change, and the judgment and the compassion, as we explained. And for this the Emanation needed that many more branches branch out from them, through which they would perform the more particular changes; and likewise from the branches further small branches, until they multiply without number and without reckoning. And the reason for all this is that the nearer the thing is to the simple source, the more it must be devoid and abstracted from changes, for the simple does not change. Therefore it is clothed in the sparks that spread out from it, and performs change through them according to its will, as has been further explained in the preceding gates. And therefore it follows from this that the words are a soul and a source to the letters. And it turns out according to this that it is quite possible that the words indicate compassion and the letters judgment, because the spreading out of Chesed is a cause to Gevurah, and Gevurah is its effect; for Chesed is fourth in the Emanation and Gevurah fifth; and this is a husk to that, and that a kernel to this. Further, on the matter of this name, a certain author wrote concerning this sefirah, and these are his words: "Behold, I have taught you that in Chesed is the building of the world; and if so, you have to consider that it is its sustaining and it is what stands it up. And the world is divided into four parts, which are north and south and east and west, and they correspond to the four letters of the four-letter name, which is YHVH. And in each part you have to consider that there is in it height and depth and middle; if so, all the extremities will be twelve. And you need to consider that at each [extremity] there is one power holding it; and those powers are called the pillars of the world. And every pillar necessarily has six extremities, which are four sides, and above and below; and in all those extremities they have a power holding it. And when you reckon the extremities of the world, which are six times twelve, they will be seventy-two; and if so there will be seventy-two powers called names; and this is the name of seventy-two names that go out from the verses in the section Beshalach." Besides this he lengthened on the division of the names among the pillars, and there is no need to lengthen on it. But the root of this matter is in Sefer ha-Bahir:

In this chapter we wish to copy the words of Sefer ha-Bahir on this name and to explain it with a strong hand. For it is [written] there: "Rabbi Amorai sat and expounded: What is it that is written, 'The heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You' (1 Kings 8:27)? It teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, has seventy-two names, and all of them are fixed in the tribes, as it is written, 'six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the six that remain on the second stone' (Ex. 28:10); and it is written, 'and twelve stones he set up,' etc. (Josh. 4:20) (another version: 'And the stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel,' Ex. 28:21). He compared them: just as these are stones of remembrance, so those are stones of remembrance; twelve stones are seventy-two, corresponding to the seventy-two names of the Holy One, blessed be He. And why did he begin with twelve? To teach you that the Holy One, blessed be He, has twelve leaders, and in each and every one six powers; and what are they? Seventy-two names. The Holy One, blessed be He, has one tree, and in it twelve diagonal boundaries: the north-east boundary, the south-east boundary, the upper-east boundary, the lower-east boundary; the north-west boundary, the south-west boundary, the upper-west boundary, the lower-west boundary; the upper-north boundary, the lower-north boundary; the upper-south boundary, the lower-south boundary. And they keep widening forever and ever, and they are the arms of the world, and within them is the tree. And corresponding to all these diagonals there are officers, and they are twelve; and also within, in the sphere, twelve officers; and likewise in the heart, twelve officers. These are thirty-six officers with the diagonals; and each one has one power, as it is written, 'for one higher than the high watches' (Eccl. 5:7). It turns out that for the east direction there are nine, and for the west direction nine, and for the north direction nine, and for the south direction nine; and that is twelve and twelve and twelve, which are officers in the Teli and the sphere and the heart; and they are thirty-six; and their totality is thirty-six of thirty-six, for one power is included in its fellow. And although there are twelve in each one of the three, all of them cleave to one another; and all the thirty-six powers that are found in the first, which is the Teli, if you seek them in the sphere you will find them themselves, and likewise if you seek them in the heart you will find them themselves. Therefore each one has twelve; it turns out that for the three they are thirty-six; and they return around; it turns out that each power is in its fellow; therefore each one has thirty-six. And all of them are no more than thirty-six forms. And all of them are completed in the heart [lev], given over to thirty-two [Lamed-Bet], and there remained sixty-four; and they are sixty-four forms. And whence do we know that heart is given over to heart? As it is written, 'for one higher than the high watches.' And if so, these are sixty-four, lacking eight of the seventy-two names of the Holy One, blessed be He; and this is what is written, 'and there are higher ones over them' (Eccl. 5:7); and they are the (seven) days of the week; and one is lacking; and this is 'And the advantage of the land is in all' (Eccl. 5:8). And what is the advantage? The place from which the earth was hewn; and it is an advantage over what was. And what is it? An advantage of everything in the world: when the people of the world are worthy to take of its splendor, then it is an advantage. And what is the earth? (A stone) from which the heavens were hewn; and it is the throne of the Holy One, blessed be He; it is a precious stone; it is the sea of wisdom; and corresponding to it is the blue [tekhelet] of the tallit, in the tzitzit. For Rabbi Meir said: Why is blue different from all kinds of colors? Because blue resembles the sea, and the sea resembles the firmament, and the firmament resembles the throne of glory, as it is said, 'And they saw the God of Israel, and under His feet as it were a work of sapphire brick, and as it were the very heaven for clearness' (Ex. 24:10); and it says, 'as the appearance of a sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne' (Ezek. 1:26)." Thus far its words.

And behold, the words of this book are bright and dazzling, and from the abundance of their brightness and their dazzle they close the eyes of the inquirer; for their intent in all their matter is to reveal a finger's breadth and to cover two thousand cubits around. However, let what our hand can reach be revealed from it, and may God keep us from errors. He began with "the heavens and the heaven of heavens" for several reasons. Either because he wishes to expound something of the greatness of our Former, as he goes on to explain, and therefore he began with the praise and glory of "the heavens and the heaven of heavens," etc.; or perhaps the reason is that in this verse there are three grades of heavens: "the heavens," one; "and the heaven," two; "of heavens," three; and they correspond to three grades, which are the Teli, the sphere, the heart [teli, galgal, lev]; and their sign is "tagel [my soul shall rejoice]," etc. (Isa. 61:10), as we shall explain, with the help of the Name. And he said that the Holy One, blessed be He, has seventy-two names, as we explained above in the preceding chapter. "And all of them are fixed in the tribes": the intent is that the twelve tribes of Israel are a chariot to twelve supernal forms, which are in the sefirot themselves through the manifestations, as we shall explain. And those twelve supernal, concealed forms he called here tribes; and the language "tribes" [shevatim] is explained in Sefer ha-Bahir itself, as we shall explain. And corresponding to these supernal forms were the twelve oxen beneath the sea that Solomon made; and likewise Jacob took twelve stones under his head, and they became one, for they were unified in one union, since they hint at the place of the union; for although they are twelve, all is one. And corresponding to them are the twelve simple letters, and likewise the twelve constellations in the world, and likewise the twelve months in the year, and likewise the twelve powers in the soul; and they are world, year, soul; and your sign is ashan [smoke]: "and Mount Sinai was altogether on smoke" (Ex. 19:18); and they are explained in Sefer Yetzirah. And let us return to the explanation of the passage: that the seventy-two names are fixed in twelve forms, which are those called tribes; and he brought a proof for this from the verse that says, "six of their names on the one stone."
Behold a proof that six were on one stone. And concerning the breastplate the verse said, "And the stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel."

Behold twelve, which are twelve stones; and six names on each and every stone are six times twelve, which are seventy-two. And this proof is by way of analogy: for since the verse compared them, it appears that just as on these stones there are six names on each one, so on the twelve stones of the tribes there are six names on each one; for they are the seventy-two names of the Holy One, blessed be He. "And why did he begin with twelve?": it was difficult for him: if the intent is to tell us the secret of the seventy-two names that the Holy One, blessed be He, has, what is the point of saying that they are twelve stones, and these divisions? To this he answered that it is to teach us that there are six forms in each one of the twelve forms; for they are twelve heads, and under each one of them six others. And likewise there is a proof from the masters of practical Kabbalah, who divide this name into names of six and six, and for each six a separate action; and the seal of the six, at their head Agla [אגל"א], and likewise at their end. And I have found a support for them for the seal of this name: for the name Agla amounts to thirty-five, and with the word itself it amounts to thirty-six; and this is the thirty-six that he mentioned in the passage. And there are versions that add a Yod to this name, and it is Agila, and then it amounts to forty-five, the number of the four-letter name [in its filling]. And it is possible that this is another name; for the name Agla must necessarily lack the Yod, for it goes out from "Atah Gibbor Le-olam Adonai" [You are mighty forever, O Lord]; unless we say that this name is like the angel Metatron: just as sometimes he is called Mitatron and sometimes Metatron, so with the name Agla. And it is possible that the combination of this name is Aga'el, and it is the language of redemption, and it is in Chesed, as in the matter of (Ps. 60:7) "Save with Your right hand," etc., and likewise (Ps. 98:1) "His right hand has saved him." And according to this it will rise up to Binah, as the verse said (Ruth 4:4), "I [anokhi] will redeem [eg'al]," and it is Binah, which is called Anokhi. And now with this it is not far-fetched that it be the seal of the name of seventy-two. And because sometimes the right is in exile through iniquities, as it is written, "Save with Your right hand," therefore this name is combined with the language of exile [galut]: Agla. And nevertheless we hope for the mighty acts and the salvation of the Holy One, blessed be He; and therefore we say, through this name, "You are mighty forever, O Lord," etc., when He subdues His attributes against those who irritate Him. And likewise there is an important name, whose matter is in this name, and it is the name Aled [אל"ד], three letters. And it is possible that the El in the name Aled is the name El that is in Chesed, and all is one matter; and this name is the tenth in the name of seventy-two, and its actions are awesome. And now we enter into the explanation of this matter and of the boundaries, with a strong hand. And before anything: we have already explained in Gate 3, chapters 4 and 5, that the extremities are six, and they are those that the author of Sefer Yetzirah counted in that mishnah, "He turned upward," etc., as explained there; and they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod.
And behold, Tiferet always includes the six extremities, for it is the power of Binah and the seal; for it includes Yod-Heh-Vav, as is known; and this is not the place to lengthen on its matter.

Behold, it will be the tree between the six extremities. And likewise it is called Tiferet, the language of porot, whose explanation is branches; and the intent is that it holds and glories and branches out and intertwines in these sefirot. And therefore their manifestation is necessarily such that Tiferet is within them like a bridegroom within his canopy; and this is to settle the ear. And one should not ask: how is it possible to say that it is the tree within the extremities, when it itself is one of the extremities? For this is no question; for all is settled by way of the manifestations and the aspects, as we explained in many places in the preceding gates. And let us return to our subject: that the height of the canopy is Netzach, and the bottom of the canopy Hod, and the east of the canopy Tiferet, and the west of the canopy Yesod, and the south of the canopy Gedulah, and the north of the canopy Gevurah. And this order is necessary, and we explained it in Gate 3, with the help of Heaven. And the thing is near: for these six sefirot are three opposite three, in the manner of the extremities, which are three opposite three. How so? East opposite west: so Tiferet opposite Yesod. And Tiferet is called east [mizrach], for in it is the rising [zerichah] of the sun, and it shines light to all the extremities; and Yesod is west [ma'arav], for in it all the powers are mixed [yit'arvu]. And just as light goes out from the east and enters into the west, so effluence goes out from Tiferet and enters into Yesod. And just as north is opposite south, so Gevurah is opposite Chesed; and they have other relations, which we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 16, with the help of Heaven. And height and below are Netzach and Hod; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained: "from the appearance of his loins upward" (Ezek. 1:27), Netzach, "and from the appearance of his loins downward," Hod. And now that the matter of the spiritual extremities has been summed up, we will now explain the boundaries in the corporeal, and from there enter into the spiritual:

Every corporeal thing that has six extremities necessarily has twelve diagonal boundaries. How so? Let us picture in our mind a house with four walls and a floor and a ceiling, which are six extremities.

Behold, there must be twelve diagonal boundaries, which are twelve beings [havayot]. How so? The boundary in which the east wall joins the ceiling, which is the upper-east boundary; and likewise for the four walls: the upper-north boundary, the upper-west boundary, the upper-south boundary: these are four boundaries. And four other boundaries below: the lower-east boundary, the lower-north boundary, the lower-west boundary, the lower-south boundary: these are four other boundaries below; and they are eight. And four corners, the places where the walls join one another. How so? The east-north boundary, which is the north-east: behold one; and likewise the east-south boundary, which is the south-east: they are two; and likewise the west-south boundary, which is the south-west: they are three; and likewise the west-north boundary, which is the north-west: they are four. And they are called diagonal boundaries because they are on the diagonal, and they are not in the order of the six extremities, which are straight, east opposite west, north opposite south, above opposite below; but these are opposite one another diagonally: the upper-east boundary opposite the lower-west, and the upper-west boundary opposite the lower-east, and the upper-north boundary opposite the lower-south, and the upper-south boundary opposite the lower-north, and the east-north boundary opposite the west-south, and the east-south boundary opposite the west-north; and all of them are opposite one another diagonally. And when these things are settled, they are near to the intellect, in a very easy picture, as we explained. And like this matter is it with the sefirot (to distinguish with many distinctions, for all is by way of parable, to settle the ear). How so? Tiferet, which is the east, is unified with the north, which is Gevurah, and with the south, which is Chesed, and with Netzach, which is above, and with Hod, which is below. And just as the south is not equal to the north, that is, Chesed to Gevurah (for they are two sefirot, each of which has a separate action), so the union of Tiferet with Chesed is not equal to its union with Gevurah; and likewise the aspect of its union with Netzach is not equal to the aspect of its union with Hod. It turns out according to this that one aspect comes into being from the union of Tiferet with Chesed, and it is called the east-south boundary; and certainly from the union of these two attributes an aspect of compassion would come into being: behold one boundary. And opposite this boundary, which is east-south, is the west-north boundary, and that is the union of Yesod with Gevurah.

And behold, this union is judgment, for Yesod itself is judgment and Gevurah judgment, and from their union judgment comes into being; and this is the second boundary. Further, Tiferet is unified with Gevurah, and this will necessarily incline to judgment, for Gevurah is judgment; and this is called the east-north boundary: behold the third boundary. And opposite this boundary, which is east-north, is the west-south boundary, and that is the union of Yesod with Chesed; and this is certainly compassion, the reverse of the preceding boundary: behold the fourth boundary. And they are two opposite two, Tiferet opposite Yesod. Further, the south is unified with the height, and that is the union of Chesed with Netzach; and then it is certainly an aspect of compassion, for both of them are compassion; and that is the upper-south boundary: behold the fifth boundary. And opposite this boundary is the lower-north boundary, and that is the union of Gevurah with Hod; and this is certainly complete judgment, for both of them are judgment; and this is the union of the north with the below: behold the sixth boundary. Further, the south is unified with the below, and that is the union of Chesed with Hod, and it is an aspect of compassion; and that is the lower-south boundary: behold the seventh boundary. And opposite this boundary is the upper-north boundary, and that is the union of Netzach with Gevurah, and it is the reverse of the preceding boundary: behold the eighth boundary; they are two opposite two. Further, the height is unified with the east, and that is the union of Netzach with Tiferet, and it is an aspect of compassion; and that is the upper-east boundary: behold the ninth boundary. And opposite this boundary is the lower-west boundary, and that is the union of Hod with Yesod, and it is an aspect of judgment: behold the tenth boundary. Further, Netzach is unified with Yesod, and that is the upper-west boundary, and it is an aspect of compassion; and that is the eleventh boundary. And opposite this boundary is the lower-east boundary, and that is the union of Tiferet with Hod, and it is an aspect of judgment; and that is the twelfth boundary: behold two opposite two, Netzach opposite Hod. It turns out that the totality of these boundaries is six for judgment and six for compassion; and therefore their aspects are twelve, as we explained. And when we examine them in relation to the four extremities, which are east and west, north and south (which are the principal ones, and which rise also in the spiritual to the four legs of the chariot; and above and below are not reckoned by themselves but are subordinate to the four mentioned, as is known and well known in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, on the matter of the four legs of the chariot, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David; for Yesod and Malkhut are all one as regards the west, as is well known), they are twelve divided into four. How so? Three for each one of the four directions; and they are four times three, amounting to twelve.

Behold, the east-north boundary is drawn along the whole face of the east, and the upper-east boundary and the lower-east boundary: these are three boundaries for the east; and it stretches on until the south-east boundary, and from there is the beginning of the boundaries of the south. How so? The south-east boundary, and the upper-south boundary, and the lower-south boundary: behold three boundaries for the south; and it stretches on until the west-south boundary, and from there is the beginning of the boundaries of the west. How so? The west-south boundary, and the upper-west boundary, and the lower-west boundary: behold three boundaries for the west; and it stretches on until the west-north boundary, and from there is the beginning of the boundaries of the north. How so? The west-north boundary, and the upper-north boundary, and the lower-north boundary: behold three boundaries for the north; and it stretches on until the north-east boundary, which is among the boundaries of the east, as we explained. It turns out according to this: three boundaries for the east, three boundaries for the west, three boundaries for the south, three boundaries for the north; and all of them are boundaries to the middle tree, which is Tiferet, as we explained in the preceding chapter. And this is "The Holy One, blessed be He, has one tree, and in it twelve boundaries," and the tree is in the middle. And it is fitting now to devote a chapter by itself to the matter of the Teli, the sphere, and the heart, so as to put space between the joined things, to give room to the intellect to understand:

And behold, the author of Sefer Yetzirah summed up the matter of creation in world, year, soul [olam, shanah, nefesh]. And these are his words, in chapter 6: "The Teli in the world is like a king on his throne; the sphere in the year is like a king in a province; the heart in the soul is like a king in war." Thus far his words, as relevant to our subject. And according to the plain sense, his words "the Teli in the world is like a king on his throne" mean a king over the stars and the constellations; and the Teli is a body of fire and air and water, and is not seen by the eye; and according to the truth it is the straight line about which the spheres revolve, for that point never moves from its place, as if we said that it was a body of fire, air, etc. By way of parable: the line that passes from north to south between the fire that surrounds the world and the water and the air and the element of earth, upon which point is the revolution of all the spheres, and they do not miss by a hair, neither rising nor descending: this is called the Teli, and some of the astronomers call it the Dragon. And it is like a king on his throne, through the conducting of the spheres, as we explained. "The sphere in the year": explanation: the sphere of the sun, by which the matters of the year are ordered, in the seasons and in all the matters; and it is king in the matters of the year. "The heart in the soul": the intent is that in the cavity of the heart is the principal dwelling of the vital soul, and from there it spreads into the other limbs of the body; it turns out that the principal of the soul is in the heart, and it reigns over the other powers that spread from it, and it conducts the body and contends with the enemies of life, as is known to the masters of medicine; and this is "like a king in war." This is the way of its plain sense. And although the plain sense of the words is true, their hint is in the heights of the Exalted; for such is the way of the book: it speaks of this world, and its words stand in the height of the world. And the matter is that "world" means Binah, which is called world [olam] after the days of the circuit, which are the world in truth; and they are called olam because they are concealed [ne'lamim] in her, as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, with the help of the Name. And it is not needed now to lengthen on the proof that the six days of the circuit are within her, for it is known that she is the second array of the Emanation, as we explained in the preceding gates. And he said "the Teli in the world," from the language of (Song 5:11) "his locks are curled [taltalim]," that is, the manifestation of Tiferet stored away in Binah in the secret of Da'at; and this is the mound [tel] that gathers the six extremities concealed in Binah, as is known. "And it is like a king on his throne": for in the place of Binah it is called king, and its throne is its boughs, which are its six extremities, concealed; and because while they are there it lacks no effluence and blessing, therefore it is called "a king on his throne," in quiet and in security. And it is on its throne, united with Malkhut, a king, Tiferet, on the throne of Malkhut; for in her concealed manifestation there is no diminishment, as we explained in the Gate of the Diminishment, chapter 4. "The sphere in the year": "year" is the seasons of the six days in their place, in Tiferet; that is to say, the place of their emanation and their gathering and their manifestation there is called year, and Tiferet in its strength with them is called sphere. And because there is not there the quiet and the security from judgment, therefore he said "like a king in a province," a language of judgment; for there is certainly judgment, but he reigns over it; and this is that he is "a king in a province." And this is also its union with its mate, who is a city and a province; and she is so called when she is clothed in judgment because of her drawing sustenance from Gevurah, and the diminishment. "The heart in the soul": these two titles are in Malkhut. But "in the heart" would mean in the innermost of the manifestation of the self of the middle point; and "soul" is her own aspect in relation to the aspects of the six extremities that are in her; and she is a point in the middle, the manifestation of the point of Zion, opposite Tiferet. And now that the manifestation of six extremities in these three arrays has come before us, they are called world, year, soul; and the middle point, that is, the middle tree mentioned in the passage, is called Teli, sphere and heart; and the sign is ashan, tagel.

Behold, through it there will be the governance, in the rotation of the extremities in the arrays, which are array facing array, this drawing from that and that bestowing upon this; and by its power the corporeal world, year, soul were created, by way of the arrays, which are Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. And in all of them there is world, year, soul: as the order of Atzilut, so the order of Beriah, so the order of Yetzirah, so the order of Asiyah. And since it is known that twelve boundaries come by the power of six extremities, behold, there are found to be twelve boundaries in Binah, and twelve in Tiferet, and twelve in Malkhut. And we explained that they are divided into four, three boundaries for each direction, like this:
[The Hebrew text has no table here.]
Behold twelve for Binah and twelve for Tiferet.
Now we will write twenty-four combinations for Malkhut:
א דני אדיג אניד אנדי אינד אידג — south:
ד אני דאיג דינא דיאג דנאי דניא — north:
נ אדי נאיד ניאד נידא נדיא נדאי — east:
יאדג יאנד ינדא ינאד ידאג ידנא — west:

And behold, three times for the south, which is the Yod in Chokhmah, which is in Chesed, the south; and that is also the Alef of Ehyeh and the Alef of Adonai, for all is one, as explained in Rashbi, peace be upon him, where he speaks of the matter of the union of these three names, like this: יאהדונה"י יאההויה"ה. And they are three times for the north, which is the Heh, which is in Binah, which is in Gevurah, the north; and they are three times for the east, which is the Vav, which is in Tiferet (and they are three times for the west, etc., as is known). But as to relating the havayot, and likewise the names, to the boundaries, we have no power in this until a teacher of righteousness comes.

And behold, the Teli is the name Ehyeh, and the sphere is the name YHVH, and the heart is the name Adonai. And the four directions are the four letters of the Name, one letter for each direction; and the boundary is the combination of one name, as we have drawn.

And behold, each name of the twelve has six names of the seventy-two names; and this is what he said, "six of their names on the one stone." And the reason is that each boundary will include six extremities, for the power of all of them is in each one, in the way that we explained concerning the inclusion of the sefirot in the preceding gates. And each name is of three letters, which correspond to Chesed, judgment, compassion, in which the whole Emanation is included, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 25, with the help of Heaven; and likewise they are three letters, one letter from each verse, hinting at the three lines, as we explained above.

And behold, each one is included of its fellow, and all is to indicate the union and the governance. For just as the nature of the constellations varies, so is the thing with the havayot and the combinations, "each man to his service and to his burden" (Num. 4:19), "each man in his work that they do" (Ex. 36:4). And it has already been explained that these three attributes are the governance of the world, upper and lower, and they are included in the secret of YHVH, as is known; and from them all the havayot spread out in all the worlds, in world, year, soul (according to the plain sense), which are twelve [and] twelve, in the secret of the twelve boundaries, as explained in Sefer Yetzirah. And the upper forms spread out until they are twenty-four in Malkhut. For the reason that Malkhut is Yod and Tiferet Vav, and the measure of Vav is two Yods, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and we copied it above in the Gate of Names, chapter 6, with the help of the Name; and likewise the measure of Malkhut is a span, as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles, and the measure of Tiferet a cubit, as will be explained there, and the measure of the cubit is two spans, as is known; and likewise Tiferet, "the shekel is ten" (Num. 7:86), and Malkhut is five, half of the ten, as we explained in Gate 1, chapter 2, with the help of Heaven (so it should read, according to the Pelach); and likewise Malkhut is Heh, and that is, she is three Vavs, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations, and the measure of Tiferet is double, for it is six extremities: it is necessitated from all this that the measure of Tiferet is double the measure of Malkhut. If so, it is necessitated for this that, whereas six names of the seventy-two were included in the combination of the Alef of Ehyeh or the Yod of YHVH, two are needed in the name Adonai, because she includes of the extremities only three, as we explained; and therefore the combinations of Adonai came to twenty-four, which, three times twenty-four, are seventy-two. And so it is explained in Sefer ha-Bahir elsewhere.

And further he explained there that even in the four-letter name there are twenty-four forms, twenty-four combinations. And there is no wonder at this; for even if the havayot are equal in their letters, they are not equal in their hint. And the proof is from the letters Heh-Heh in the Name, which are equal in their form and different in their hint, as we explained in the Gate of Names, chapter 1, with the help of Heaven. And therefore we will reckon as if the second Heh's form were different from its fellow's, and twenty-four combinations, twenty-four forms, come out to us. And although the twelve resemble the twelve, they are like male and female, receiver and bestower; and likewise they are twelve hours in the day and twelve hours in the night: those of the night receive from the day, and those of the day bestow upon the night, in the secret of the attribute of day and the attribute of night.

And further it is fitting that we set out that Tiferet and Malkhut are united and cleave in all the sefirot and in all the upper limbs, sometimes in all of them together and sometimes in a particular place, as is explained from the secret of the prayers. For the morning prayer is attributed to Abraham, and there she leans upon her beloved through Chesed; and the afternoon prayer to Isaac, and there her union with him is through Gevurah; and the evening prayer to Jacob, etc. And as the order of the prayers, so the order of the festivals: for Passover is Chesed, and Shavuot Tiferet, and Rosh Hashanah Gevurah, and Sukkot Yesod, and Shemini Atzeret Malkhut, and Chanukah and Purim Netzach and Hod; for so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 111). And the intent is her union with her husband in these branches; and this is not the place for this inquiry, for we shall explain it in the book Or Yakar, with the help of Heaven. But the aspect changes according to the change of the place; and this thing will be revealed in the secret of the combination of the vowels, for the number rises without limit, as we shall explain in the Gate of Permutation, chapter 4, with the help of Heaven.

Behold, it is found now to be true that they are twenty-four forms, twenty-four combinations, and they are the very twelve forms, twelve combinations; for all is one, and all rises to one place. And with this the words of Sefer ha-Bahir in another place will be set right; for so he explained explicitly, as we shall explain, that twelve males and twelve females resemble one another, and they amount to twenty-four.

And behold, it is known that the male is the reverse of the female, as explained in Sefer Yetzirah: male with Alef-Mem-Shin, female with Alef-Shin-Mem. And we have two ways in this. Either we say that the arrangement of the males and the females is like Alef-Mem-Shin and Alef-Shin-Mem, and we always crown one letter at the head of the male and the female, that is, the letter of the direction in which the male is and in which the female is. For example, if we are in the east direction, which is the Yod of the name [text: Ehyeh], as explained above, behold, the male will be יאה"ה and its female יהה"א; and likewise if the male is יהא"ה, the female will be like it, יהא"ה, except that the male crowned the first Heh and the female reversed and crowned the second Heh. And likewise in Adonai: for example, the letter of the south direction is Alef, and the male will be אדנ"י and the female אינ"ד; and if the male is אדי"נ the female will be אני"ד; and if the male is אנד"י the female will be איד"נ. This is one way. Or we say twelve combinations, literally females, like the twelve males, and always the male and the female equal, like this: the male יהו"ה and the female יהו"ה, the male הוה"י and the female הוה"י, this one bestowing and that one receiving. And the two ways are equally weighted for us until a teacher of righteousness comes. And we have seen fit to divide this matter further into a chapter by itself, to put space between section and section:

And behold, with the matter of the twenty-four combinations, twelve and twelve, which we set out, what is written in Sefer ha-Bahir (section 46) will be explained; and these are its words: "The name that goes out from three verses, Vayyisa, Vayyavo, Vayyet: the letters of the first verse in order, etc. It turns out that in each and every name of the seventy-two names that go out from these three verses, etc.; and they are divided into three parts, twenty-four for each part; and over each part of the three parts there is a high prince over them; and each part has four directions to guard, east and west and north and south; and they are divided, six for each direction; it turns out that for the four directions there are twenty-four forms; and likewise for the second, and likewise for the third. And all of them are sealed with YHVH, God of Israel, the living God, Shaddai, high and exalted, who dwells eternally, and holy is His name, YHVH; blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever." Thus far its words.

And his intent is that the name of seventy-two is sealed with seventy-two names of the havayah. And he explained this there, above, and these are his words: "What is that which is written, 'The Lord bless you … the Lord make His face shine … the Lord lift up' (Num. 6:24–26)? This is the explicit name of the Holy One, blessed be He, and it is the name of twelve letters, as it is written, YHVH, YHVH, YHVH. It teaches that the names of the Holy One, blessed be He, are three hosts, and each name is of a host, and host resembles host, and its name is like its name; and all of them are sealed with יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א. And how? You combine YHVH twenty-four times: that is one host, 'The Lord bless you'; and likewise the second, and they are twenty-four names of the Holy One, blessed be He; and also the third, and they are twenty-four. It teaches that each host, their heads and their princes, are twenty-four. And now you combine twenty-four three times, and they will be the seventy-two names of the Holy One, blessed be He; and that is the seventy-two names that go out from Vayyisa, Vayyavo, Vayyet." Thus far its words.

And behold, it is necessitated from this passage that the four-letter name is combined in twenty-four combinations; and it will be explained in the way that we explained above. And thus is its explanation: although each and every host resembles its fellow, nevertheless it is a host by itself. And now we will enter into the explanation of all these passages properly, and from it the name of seventy-two will be explained according to its measure. It has already been explained in the preceding gates that the whole Emanation is included in Alef-Mem-Shin, which are air, water, fire, and that is Chesed, judgment, compassion; and their principal is in Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. And to these three the three names in the priestly blessing hint, which are also "[the Lord] reigns, reigned, will reign." And on the vowelling of these three names the explanations are many. There are those who wished to vowel them yif'al, yefu'al, yif'ol: that is, the first all patach; the second patach, cholam, tzeirei; and the third chirik, sheva, cholam. And there are those who wrote that its vowels are yif'al, yif'el, yif'ol: that is, the first all kamatz, the second all segol, and the third chirik, sheva, cholam. And in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 10a, and Tikkun 70, folio 134b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that its vowels are like the words that follow it, which are "reigns, reigned, will reign": that is, the first all segol, the second kamatz, patach, and the third chirik, sheva, cholam. And so he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, folio 217a), and these are his words: "Michael, lion: its four faces are YHVH; the four faces of the ox, and it is Gabriel, and they are YHVH; the four faces of the eagle, and it is Nuriel, and they are YHVH. And they are appointed under Chesed, Fear, Truth, the grades of the three Patriarchs; and the Rabbis established, the Patriarchs are the chariot; and the lights rise to the number of YaBaK [112]. And they are 'reigns, reigned, will reign.'" Behold, the three names are called the name of twelve; and of it they said, "whoever knows it and is careful with it," etc.; and it is good to direct one's intention to it at the seal of each and every blessing, in the secret of "was, is, and will be," that is, "reigns, reigned, will reign." And let us return to our subject: just as these three names are in the three Patriarchs, so the name of seventy-two from the three verses is in the three Patriarchs, as he explained in the Zohar (Beshalach, folio 51). It turns out that, after we combine the name of seventy-two and divide it into three parts, a part for each one of these three names mentioned, it amounts to twenty-four names for each name. Further, we will combine the four-letter name into twenty-four combinations; behold, there will be twenty-four names corresponding to the twenty-four that it has from the name of seventy-two; and there will be twenty-four havayot, sources for twenty-four names of the name of seventy-two. And these three havayot, from which the seventy-two combinations are combined: behold, each one of them will be prince over the twenty-four that are combined from it. And this is what he said above, "three hosts, and each name of a host," etc., and likewise in the preceding passage, "and over each part a high prince," etc. And when we divide twenty-four into four directions, which are four boundaries of the twelve mentioned above, behold, there will be six under one. For there will be four boundaries, and for each twenty-four names there will be six names of the name of seventy-two under six names of the four-letter name, these under one name of the twelve boundaries; and the twelve boundaries are combined from the four-letter name, as we explained. And we wish to draw a proper figure, by which all these things will be settled in the heart of the discerning; and the figure will be found on page 486 [of the printed edition; it is not in this text]:

Thus far reached the power of drawing in these matters. And like this figure for the name YHVH, so is the figure for the name Ehyeh, and likewise for the name Adonai. And the upshot is that the twelve boundaries are the combination of the four-letter name that is in Tiferet. And behold, Tiferet includes Chesed and Gevurah and compassion, for it is "a perfect man, dwelling in tents" (Gen. 25:27); and from this three names are entailed in the four-letter name, and one four-letter name includes the three of them; and the one is divided into twelve combinations, which are twelve boundaries, as we explained. And the twelve combinations are divided, each one into two, male and female: they are twenty-four. And the three, each one of them into twenty-four: they are seventy-two; they are six names of them for each one of the twelve, and for each one of [the three] twenty-four. This is their concealed source. But these seventy-two powers are clothed in the seventy-two names of Vayyisa, Vayyavo, Vayyet, each one of which is of three letters, hinting at Chesed and Gevurah and Tiferet, for so the verses hint. And the initial letters of the twelve combinations of the four-letter name that is in Tiferet are Yod-Yod-Yod, Heh-Heh-Heh, Vav-Vav-Vav, Heh-Heh-Heh, which are the three names mentioned; and all is from one place, and all returns to one source.
