And in this way we may infer to the name Ehyeh, for all is one, this like that; and to hint at the three (that are) [names] Ehyeh, which are Chesed, judgment and compassion, it is mentioned in the whole Torah only three times, that is, the first three. And Adonai too is in this way, for "the Lord is in His holy palace": there is no difference between this and that, except that we do not need to (double) the names. And according to our way we have learned that the source of the name of seventy-two is in the way that we said, and likewise Ehyeh, and likewise Adonai. But in Sefer ha-Orah he explained it in another way, and likewise in the Tikkunim; and we will explain it, with the help of the Name. Again, we have found the name of the twelve boundaries, besides the four-letter name and the name Ehyeh and the name Adonai, [as] one name. And these are its words in Sefer ha-Bahir: "And these are the explicit names, precious and glorious, the name of twelve for the twelve tribes of Israel:

אהציצהרון אכליתהרון טמקתון רמוהטרון וצפצפשיתרון יהורמרון ברחיה גאון עדשגדראון כסאות הוהויהה ויהאהאהיה והדמתתיהון, blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever. And all of them are included in the heart of the paths of the heavens, and they are divided into twenty-four names, and in them male and female are included; and its officers are in the Teli, the sphere and the heart; and they are the wellsprings of wisdom." Thus far its words.

And he was precise in his words, in that he said "male and female"; and they are a proof of what we wrote above concerning the twelve that are divided into twenty-four, male and female. And there is no doubt that these names are a garment to the twelve havayot, and to the twelve [forms of] Ehyeh, and to the twenty-four [of] Adonai, in the way that we explained above concerning the seventy-two themselves. And now that the matter of the twelve boundaries has been explained, according to the bestowal of the Name in His kindness upon us, we will devote this [next] chapter to the completion of the explanation of the passage:

He said that they are twelve officers in the Teli, the sphere and the heart, as explained above: that twelve boundaries are in the Teli, which is Binah, and twelve in the sphere, which is Tiferet, and twelve in the heart, which is Malkhut. "And they are thirty-six": three times twelve amounts to thirty-six. It would mean that each one of the Teli, sphere and heart raises the number of twelve that is in it to thirty-six; because Malkhut includes Binah and Tiferet, and Tiferet includes Binah and Malkhut, and Binah includes Tiferet and Malkhut; therefore it is necessary that each one of the twelve include the two others, which makes three, and three times twelve are thirty-six. "If you seek them in the sphere you will find them," etc. And what he said, "and their totality is thirty-six of thirty-six, for one power is included in its fellow": explanation: that each one of the thirty-six forms includes thirty-six forms. And the reason for this is that one power is included in its fellow: explanation: that all of them draw from one another and receive from one another; if so, it is necessary that in each one there be the aspect of all of them, so that they can receive from all of them. And he said further, "And all of them are no more than thirty-six forms": for although he said that they are three times thirty-six, and each one of the thirty-six includes thirty-six forms, nevertheless their true and principal root is only thirty-six, from the three arrays, which are three times twelve; and therefore only twelve [in each] enter into the reckoning, and the rest is the inclusion in which they were included, as we explained. "And all of them are completed in the heart [lev]": they are thirty-two. And perhaps the reason is that one must remove four from thirty-six, because the four letters are the foundation of the thirty-six; and therefore when we subtract four from thirty-six they will be completed and included in thirty-two. Afterwards he said, "given over to thirty-two, and thirty-two remain, sixty-four": explanation: when we give over and include the upper thirty-two in the lower thirty-two, they will be sixty-four. And he proved that thirty-two is given over to thirty-two because it is written, "for one higher [than the high watches]": behold, thirty-two are over thirty-two; and therefore they are included in sixty-four. Eight are lacking to complete seventy-two; and this is "and there are higher ones over them," which are the power of the seven sefirot above Malkhut, which is the heart, as explained above.

And behold, they are the seven days of creation, and Binah is the Sabbath day, one of the seven days of creation; and therefore he called them "the seven days of the week," for the week [shavua] is Binah. "And one is lacking": and Malkhut does not complete it, for she herself is the heart, as we explained. And he said that the number is completed in "the advantage of the land is in all." And he asked about its matter, and said, "the place from which the earth was hewn": explanation: the manifestation of Malkhut concealed in the secret of her source above, which is the manifestation of her advantage and her degree; and from there the light of the renewal of the moon is bestowed, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna, that from the middle point the moon shines; and that is like this: ( . And the middle point is the source of the light, and from there is her renewal; and that is the manifestation of the Yod that is in Malkhut, the middle point. And this is what he said, "And the advantage of the land": an advantage over what was in her, for she was lacking, and she is filled from within her, the pupil of the eye that illumines the whole eye; and from within this advantage she bestows life to the whole world. And this is "and the advantage of the land," which is the point, "is in all": explanation: upon all the children of the world she bestows her effluence. "When the people of the world are worthy to take of its splendor," etc.: explanation: when there is fitness of deeds in this world, then the moon is in her fullness and the light is bestowed. "And what is the earth from which the heavens were hewn?": he was precise in not saying "earth that was hewn from heaven," that is, the diminishment, but "earth from which the heavens were hewn," that is, the matter of the rib: that Tiferet, which is the heavens, was hewn from her, and she remained in Chokhmah, as explained in the Gate of the Diminishment, chapter 4, with the help of Heaven. "And it is His throne": explanation: afterwards she is a throne to Tiferet. "And she is a precious stone," which is "the treasure of kings" (Eccl. 2:8), in the secret of the upper Yod in Chokhmah; and in the secret of that manifestation she is the sea of wisdom; and corresponding to her is the blue, whose color is sapphire. And he brought a proof from the words of Rabbi Meir for the three manifestations that are in Malkhut: and they are her manifestation below, after the diminishment, and her manifestation with Tiferet before the diminishment, and her manifestation in Chokhmah. And this is what he said, "blue resembles the sea": that is, the manifestation of Malkhut in the secret of her lower aspect, and she is called sea, and beneath her is the depth of the sea, in the secret of (Prov. 5:5) "her feet go down to death." "And the sea resembles the firmament": that is, her manifestation with Tiferet, which is called firmament. "And the firmament the throne of glory": that is, Chokhmah, which is a throne to the glory that hovers over it, and it is (far) (Keter). And he proved these three manifestations from the verse "And they saw the God of Israel": "and under His feet" is Malkhut, which is under the feet of the God of Israel, for she is under Netzach and Hod, which are the feet of Tiferet. "As it were a work of sapphire brick": explanation: the matter of her manifestation in Chokhmah, for there is the sapphire. "And as it were the very heaven": that is, her manifestation in Tiferet. And likewise of her it is said "as the appearance of a sapphire stone"; that is, the Shekhinah is as the appearance of a sapphire stone, which is Chokhmah. "The likeness of a throne" [kisse]: explanation: that she is covered [mitkasseh] and concealed; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. And this remark at the end of this passage is enough, since it is not of our subject. And from it the matter of the twelve boundaries has been explained, and the seventy-two names for all of them together, as we explained at the end of the passage in this chapter; for they are six extremities, and their head and their end, as above. And enough for us of occupation with this passage and with this matter. And we come to explain in a chapter by itself the matter of the sources of this name, with the help of Heaven:

On the matter of the sources of this name, Sefer ha-Orah wrote, and these are its words: "You need to know that the Name, may He be blessed, has fifty-four four-letter names in the combination of YHVH, and they amount to the reckoning of 216 letters. And these fifty-four names are in the secret of the drawing of power into all the existents that are in the world, in the being of all that is; and they are like a soul to the 216 letters, which are Vayyisa, Vayyavo, Vayyet. And within these fifty-four all the things that are in the world are included; and these are what suffice the need of all the created entities through the Lordship [Adonai]." Thus far its words.

And as for what he said, that in the name of the havayah there are fifty-four names, we have received its combination like this: יהו"ה יוה"ה יהה"ו יוה"ו יהו"ו יוו"ה יוה"י יהו"י יוי"ה. והי"ה ויה"ה והה"י הוי"ו היו"ו הוו"י יוי"ה ויה"ו יהי"ו ההו"י ההי"ו היו"ה ווה"י ויה"ו ויו"ה ויי"ה והי"י ויה"י היו"ה היה"ו הוה"י היו"ו הוי"ו ווי"ה הוי"י היו"י היי"ו ויו"ו יוי"ו יוו"י ייה"ה יהי"ה יהה"י ווה"ה והו"ה והה"ו ווי"י ויי"ו ויו"י ההי"י היי"ה היה"י ההו"ו הוה"ו הוו"ה. These are the fifty-four combinations that are in the name of the havayah, as we have received them from men of heart. And in this way we will combine the name Ehyeh, for all is one matter, (to investigate) [as a source for] this name, as we explained:

אהי"ה איה"ה אהה"י אאי"ה אאה"י איא"ה ייא"ה ייה"א יאי"ה יאה"ה יהא"ה יהה"א איה"א אהי"א אהא"י יאה"י יהא"י יהי"א האי"ה האה"י ההי"א האא"י היא"א האי"א איי"ה איה"י אה"יי ההא"י היא"ה היה"א יאא"ה יאה"א יהא"א האי"י היי"א היא"י ההי"י היה"י היי"ה אאה"ה אהא"ה אהה"א ייא"א יאי"א יאא"י ייה"ה יהי"ה יהה"י ההא"א האה"א האא"ה אאי"י איא"י איי"א. Behold fifty-four combinations in the name Ehyeh, as we have received them; and they are a source for the name of seventy-two, according to the opinion of the Rav:

And there are those who divide the name of seventy-two into four letters for each and every name, and we have no concern with this matter at all. And there are some of the Kabbalists of practice who wrote that the source of this name is El, as for example Yeli'el, Sita'el, and so to its end; and it is correct, for so it is in Chesed, and the name El is in Chesed. And we could indeed say that the source El is included with it in another way, like this: יאלל"י, and likewise סאיל"ט; but we have seen El always at the end of the names of all the angels, and likewise in this name it is not changed. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, has another way concerning the source of this name; and these are his words in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 8a): "And the source of these havayot is in the reckoning of chesed, for with them one must build this building; they are from Chesed; for the source of the havayot is יו"ד ה"י וי"ו ה"י, which rise to seventy-two havayot, as the reckoning of chesed: all of them stone and beam, and the building that is built with both of them. And these are the seventy-two havayot that go out from יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א." Thus far its words.
And he wrote the havayot; and in all the books confusion and error fell into them; therefore it is most correct to combine them from within the name יו"ד ה"י וי"ו ה"י.

And behold, in this name, which is יו"ד ה"י וי"ו ה"י, there are four Yods and three Vavs and two Hehs. When we wish to combine these letters into words, there come out of them first יה"ו יה"ו וי"י: they are three havayot from the totality of the letters of the havayah that are in this name.

And behold, further we can combine the name יה"ו like this: יה"ו יו"ה הי"ו הו"י וי"ה וה"י: behold six havayot; and likewise from the second יה"ו: they are twelve. And the name וי"י bears three combinations, like this: וי"י יו"י וי"י. It turns out that the total of the combinations until now is fifteen. Further, we make [words] from the letters of the Name, which are four Yods, and combine each Yod of them with the two Hehs, and they will be יה"ה יהה"ה יה"ה; and their number will amount to twelve combinations, for we combine each havayah of these into three, like this: יה"ה הי"ה הה"י; and they are three times four, twelve; and with fifteen they are twenty-seven. Further, we combine three Vavs with the two Hehs, and it comes to וה"ה וה"ה וה"ה; and their number amounts to nine combinations, for we combine each havayah of these into three, like this: וה"ה הו"ה הה"ו; and they are three times three, nine; and with twenty-seven they are thirty-six. Further, we combine four Yods with two Vavs, and they will be יו"ו יו"ו יו"ו יו"ו; and their number amounts to twelve combinations, for we combine each havayah of these into three, like this: יו"ו וי"ו וו"י; and they are four times [three], twelve; and with thirty-six they are forty-eight. Further, we combine three Vavs with two Yods, and they will be וי"י וי"י וי"י; and their number amounts to nine combinations, for we combine each havayah of them into three, like this: וי"י יו"י וי"ו, which are three times three, nine; and with forty-eight they are fifty-seven. Further, we combine the two Hehs with two Yods, and they will be הי"י הי"י; and the number amounts to six combinations, for we combine each havayah of these into three, like this: הי"י יה"י יי"ה: they are six; and with fifty-seven they are sixty-three. Further, we combine two Hehs with two Vavs, and they will be הו"ו הו"ו; and their number amounts to six combinations, for we combine each havayah of these into three, like this: הו"ו וה"ו וו"ה: they are six; and with sixty-three they are sixty-nine. And the total of the letters that are the foundation of the combination in the Name are four Yods and three Vavs and two Hehs; we make of them three words, like this: וו"ו יי"י יה"ה: they are three; and with sixty-nine they are seventy-two. This is the way of the derivation of the seventy-two havayot that are in the name of seventy-two according to the opinion of Rashbi, peace be upon him; and their foundation is יו"ד ה"י וי"ו ה"י, which amounts to seventy-two. And now that we have summed up the order of its combination, we will draw now in this table the order of the havayot: יה"ו יו"ה הי"ו הו"י וי"ה וה"י יה"ו יו"ה הי"ו הו"י וי"ה וה"י יי"ו יו"י וי"י יה"ה הי"ה הה"י יה"ה הי"ה הה"י יה"ה הי"ה הה"י יה"ה הי"ה הה"י וה"ה הו"ה הה"ו וה"ה הו"ה הה"ו וה"ה הו"ה הה"ו. וי"י יו"י יי"ו וי"י יו"י יי"ו וי"י יו"י וי"י יו"ו וי"ו וו"י יו"ו וי"ו וו"י יו"ו וי"ו וו"י יו"ו וי"ו וו"י הי"י יה"י יי"ה הי"י יי"ה הו"ו וה"ו וו"ה הו"ו וה"ו וו"ה וו"ו יי"י יה"ה [the list as printed has seventy-one]: behold seventy-two. And each and every one of these havayot is of three letters, like the name of seventy-two, each one of which is of three letters. And there is no wonder at the doubling of the havayot, since the doubled letters are not equal, as we explained. And likewise there is no wonder at the havayah of three Yods or three Vavs, for the Yods are not equal in their spirituality, and likewise the Vavs.
And this matter, in the Hehs and in the Yods and in the Vavs that are in the Name: each and every one hints at a matter by itself, as explained in the preceding gates.

And behold, what is understood by us of the explanation of the name of seventy-two is complete and concluded for a time such as this, and there is no need to lengthen further. And we will journey on to the explanation of the holy name of forty-two, with the help of the Living One:
The intent now is to explain the name of forty-two; and it is so called because there are forty-two letters in it, as we shall explain; and this is the Name with its vowels:
אבגיתץ. קרע שטן. נגדיכש. בטרצתג. חקבטנע. יגלפזק. שקוצית [the vowels are not reproduced in this text]:

Thus far. As we have vowelled it, so we found it in the prayer of Rabbi Nechunya. And in the words of a Kabbalist [speaking] by the mouth of a maggid it is written, and these are his words: "Avgitatz: vowel it with patach and with sheva: the Alef and the Bet and the Gimel with patach, and the Yod with sheva, and the Tav with patach and with dagesh. Kera Satan: the Kof with sheva, and the Resh with patach, and the Shin with sheva, and the Tet with kamatz. Neged Yakhash in this way: the Nun with sheva, the Gimel with patach, and the Dalet with sheva, the Yod with patach, and the Kaf likewise. Batar Tzatag: the Bet with sheva, the Tet with patach, the Tzadi with sheva, the Tav with patach. Chakav Tana: the Chet with patach, the Kof with sheva, the Bet with patach and with dagesh, the Tet with sheva and with dagesh, the Nun with patach, and the Ayin without a vowel. Yagal Pazak: the Yod with sheva and with dagesh, the Gimel with patach without dagesh, the Peh with dagesh and with sheva, the Zayin with patach, the Kof without any vowel. Shakutzit: vowel it in this way: the Shin with kamatz, and the Kof with sheva, and the Vav with kamatz also, the Tzadi with chirik. This is the combination of its vowels. It is known that the secret of the patach is a great secret, to open from above upon the openings of complete compassion, since it is complete compassion. And the kamatz, its secret is (Ps. 77:10) 'Has He in anger shut up [kafatz] His compassion?'; that is to say, if you vowel it with kamatz, it shuts up in anger; and take heed that you do not vowel it with kamatz except to take vengeance. And in place of the sheva, chirik; and with it you will do and attain wonders of wonders. And with patach you will attain the actions of compassion, and it will open blessings without end; and this is what the verse says (Mal. 3:10), 'if I will not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out,' etc." Thus far its words, as relevant to our subject. And let us return to the matter of the explanation of the Name. It is hinted at in the sefirah Gevurah, and the place of its going out is from the verse "In the beginning" until the Bet of va-vohu. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim, in Tikkun 4, and these are his words: "Rabbi Shimon rose to his feet and said: Master of the worlds, 'open my eyes, that I may behold' (Ps. 119:18) them above; 'I will enter into them' [avo vam; bam = 42] (Ps. 118:19), into the forty-two letters of the explicit Name, to know each and every letter in its tikkun. And they are: 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth, and the earth was formless and void': בראשית ברא אלה ימאת הש מימואת הארצוה ארצהית התהווב; and they are אבגיתץ קרע שטן נגדיכש בטרצתג חקבטנע יגלפזק שקוצית. Each and every letter has an utterance and has a path: ten utterances are they, and thirty-two tracks; and all of them depend on Ayeh; and this is 'I will enter into them, I will thank Yah' (Ps. 118:19): Ayeh is in the reckoning of 'I will thank Yah' (Yah: Chokhmah and Binah; Alef: the Supernal Keter). And they are seven sefirot included in seven names, and Bat Sheva includes them all." Thus far its words.

And the sense of the verse is: "Open for me the gates of righteousness [tzedek]" (Ps. 118:19); and it is the Shekhinah, when she is called Bat Sheva [daughter of seven], because she includes these seven names, which are the seven sefirot; and then she is called Tzedek, the passage of the paths and the utterances. Afterwards, "I will enter into them [bam]," which are seven names, seven sefirot; and in them are included forty-two letters, which are ten utterances and thirty-two paths; and each and every letter has one power of the utterances or the paths. "I will thank Yah": they are the first three that remain.

Behold, it is explicit that the source of this name is from the verse "In the beginning" until the Bet of va-vohu; and there is some confusion in this, as we shall write. And there is one who divided these letters into three parts, which are three hands, the right hand, the lifted hand, and the strong hand; and this is its arrangement, with its vowels: בראשית ברא אלה ימ: thus far the great hand, the right. אתהש. מימואתהא. רצ: thus far the lifted hand, compassion. והארצה יתהתהו. וב: thus far the strong hand:

And he wrote further that these forty-two letters are at the end of the Torah, in the verse "and in all the strong hand and in all the great terror," etc. (Deut. 34:12); and there too are three hands, and they are these: ולכלהי דהחזקה ול: thus far the one hand. כל המוראה גדול אש: thus far the second hand. רעשה משה לעיני כל: thus far the third hand. So I found. And it is possible that these vowels are like the vowels of the letters in it, the vowelling of the letters from "In the beginning," as we hinted above. And we have heard it said that these words are the words of the pious sage Rabbi Shlomo Molkho, of blessed memory. And concerning this name we have found in Sefer ha-Kanah names whose initials are the name of forty-two; it appears from there that they are a garment to this name; and these are the names as he wrote them in his book:

אדירירוץ בהירירוץ גבירירון יגבהיה תלמיה צתניא קדמיה רגריה עריריה שנעיה טלטיה נהריה נשמריה געריה דהריה יעליה כסיה שניוניה בועליה טורריה רמיה צצציה תחבהיה גלגליה חנניה קתקיה בהבחביה טוהויה נתניה עממיה יהלשריה גורריה לממריה פקורקריה זהרזהר זהריה קמליה שתהודדיה קדושיה והאלאליה צעדיה יתהרריה תמתליה. Thus far:

And the intent is that the forty-two letters of the Name are forty-two luminaries, shining spiritual forms, and the name of each one is as mentioned above; and to hint at the letter of the Name, which is its source, the sign of the letter comes at the head of its name, to hint that the branch is wedged in the root and the root in the branch, and to indicate that it is an emanation emanated from that source. Further, I have found in the bag of the sages a second way: forty-two names whose initials are the holy Name, and these are they: Arpani'el, Bo'el, Gavri'el, Yofi'el, Tumi'el, Tzadki'el. The second name: Kavtzi'el, Ravchi'el, Azuzi'el, Shimshi'el, Tufi'el, Nagdi'el. The third name: Nachli'el, Gevuri'el, Dani'el, Yehudi'el, Kivshi'el, Shifri'el. The fourth name: Berakhi'el, Tifti'el, Rachmi'el, Tzefuni'el, Terumi'el, Gerud'el. The fifth name: Chaza'el, Kumi'el, Barki'el, Tahari'el, Nuri'el, Ami'el. The sixth name: Yisra'el, Gadi'el, Lahavi'el, Penu'el, Zekhari'el, Kedushi'el. The seventh name: Shalgi'el, Karvi'el, Vavi'el, Tzuri'el, Yalfi'el, Tavri'el. Thus far. And there is no doubt that the earlier names are concealed and exalted above these by a great deal. And there is a further, third way in this, according to what is found in the books of the ancients:
Now that we have written this name in the preceding chapter, we will now explain in this chapter, writing the manner of its derivation from the verses:

Bet: its substitute is Alef by Avgad: Alef. Resh: its substitute is Tet by Albam, and under Tet, Bet by Achas Beta: Bet. Alef: its substitute is Yod by Ayak, and under Yod, Gimel by Achas Beta: Gimel. Shin [text: Gimel]: its substitute is Yod by Albam: Yod. Yod: its substitute is Alef by Ayak, and under Alef, Tav by Atbash: Tav. Tav: its substitute is Kaf by Albam, and under Kaf, Tzadi by Achas Beta: Tzadi (this is the first name):

Bet: its substitute is Chet by Atbach, and under Chet, Kof by Albam: Kof. Resh: its substitute is Tet by Albam, and under Tet, Nun by Atbash, and under Nun, Resh by Albam: Resh. Alef: its substitute is Lamed by Albam, and under Lamed, Ayin by Atbach: Ayin. Alef: its substitute is Tav by Atbash, and under Tav, Shin by Avgad: Shin. Lamed: its substitute is Ayin by Atbach, and under Ayin, Tet by Achas Beta: Tet. Heh: its substitute is Nun by Atbach: Nun (this is the second name):

Yod: its substitute is Tet by Avgad, and under Tet, Nun by Atbash: Nun. Mem: its substitute is Bet by Albam, and under Bet, Gimel by Avgad: Gimel. Alef: its substitute is Tav by Atbash, and under Tav, Kof by Atbach, and under Kof, Dalet by Atbash: Dalet. Tav: its substitute is Alef by Atbash, and under Alef, Yod by Ayak: Yod. Heh: its substitute is Lamed by Achas Beta, and under Lamed, Kaf by Atbash: Kaf. Shin: its substitute is Resh by Atbach, and under Resh, Shin by Avgad: Shin (this is the third name):

Mem: its substitute is Bet by Albam: Bet. Yod: its substitute is Tet by Avgad: Tet. Mem: its substitute is Resh by Achas Beta: Resh. Vav: its substitute is Peh by Atbash, and under Peh, Tzadi by Avgad: Tzadi. Alef: its substitute is Tav by Atbash: Tav. Tav: its substitute is Kof by Atbach, and under Kof, Resh by Avgad, and under Resh, Gimel by Atbash: Gimel (this is the fourth name):
[Editor's note to the second name:] Perhaps something is missing, and it should read: "and under Nun, Tet by Atbash, and under Tet, Resh," etc.:

Heh: its substitute is Ayin by Albam, and under Ayin, Tet by Achas Beta, and under Tet, by Avgad [Chet; the letter is missing in the text]. Alef: its substitute is Tav by Atbash, and under Tav, Kof by Atbach. Resh: its substitute is Gimel by Atbash, and under Gimel, Bet by Avgad. Tzadi: its substitute is Yod by Atbach, and under Yod, Tet by Avgad. Vav: its substitute is Dalet by Atbach, and under Dalet, Nun by Avgad, and under Nun, Nun by Albam [this clause is garbled in the text]. Heh: its substitute is Ayin by Albam (this is the fifth name):

Alef: its substitute is Yod by Ayak. Resh: its substitute is Gimel by Atbash. Tzadi: its substitute is Kaf by Achas Beta, and under Kaf, Lamed by Atbash. Heh: its substitute is Tzadi by Atbash, and under Tzadi, Peh by Avgad. Yod: its substitute is Tzadi by Atbach, and under Tzadi, Zayin by Albam. Tav: its substitute is Kof by Atbach (this is the sixth name):

Heh: its substitute is Lamed by Achas Beta, and under Lamed, Alef by Albam, and under Alef, Tav by Atbash, and under Tav, Shin by Avgad: Shin. Tav: its substitute is Kof by Atbach: Kof. Heh: its substitute is Vav by Avgad: Vav. Vav: its substitute is Heh by Avgad, and under Heh, Tzadi by Atbash: Tzadi. Bet: its substitute is Kaf by Ayak Bakhar, and under Kaf, Yod by Avgad: Yod. Heh: its substitute is Lamed by Achas Beta, and under Lamed, Alef by Albam, and under Alef, Tav by Atbash: Tav (this is the seventh name):

This is the derivation of the name of forty-two according to recorded alphabets; for it was not permitted to produce it except through Atbash and Achas Beta and Albam and Avgad, Ayak and Atbach; for otherwise it would easily have been combined through the twenty-two alphabets. And as for what is found, that sometimes the letter of the Name is the letter of the verse, such as the Resh of bara, which is itself the Resh of Kera, and likewise the Shin of ha-shamayim, which is also the Shin of Yakhash, and nevertheless we derive it through the substitutions of the alphabets: it is not for nothing. For the Name had to be combined and to pass by way of the alphabets time after time; and if it descended and passed by way of the descending alphabets, it would return and ascend by way of the ascending alphabets; for all this is a hint at the ascent of the ascending grades, and of the combination in which the Name was combined and clothed until its coming into the verse "In the beginning." And all these things were received by the ancients, a true tradition in which there is no doubt. But as for their skipping the Vav of va-vohu and combining the Heh of va-vohu, it is against the opinion of Rashbi, peace be upon him, as explained above; and they themselves said that it is a doubt for them, and the tradition of the matter was forgotten; and all the copyists copied it with this combination. And concerning the source of this name: it has a source, and a source upon a source; and these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, folio 103b): "(And there is a name of forty-two written in the form of a wax seal.) And there is a name of forty-two in the drawing of the image of the King, engraved on the seal. And there is a name of forty-two that is the image (itself. The name of forty-two that is the image) is YHVH, יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א, יו"ד וא"ו דל"ת ה"א אל"ף וא"ו אלף וא"ו ה"א אלף. The name of forty-two that is the seal is Ehyeh asher Ehyeh. The drawing of forty-two in wax: this is אבגית"ץ." Thus far its words.

Behold the combination of the name of forty-two with the four-letter name, and it is the supreme source, and from it Ehyeh flows; and likewise twice Ehyeh amounts to forty-two; and likewise the name Ehyeh is combined like the name YHVH, except that one is lacking; and it is possible that the Name itself completes it, like this: אהי"ה אל"ף ה"א יו"ד ה"א. אל"ף למ"ד פ"ה ה"א אל"ף. יו"ד וא"ו דל"ת. ה"א אל"ף: behold forty-one, and the Name itself completes the number. And from it the name of forty-two that goes out from "In the beginning," with which we are occupied, flows and draws nourishment. Further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, has great and awesome matters concerning this name, and whoever wishes to understand their explanation should look in the Tikkunim, in its place. Further (in Tikkun 70, folio 135a), concerning this name: seven names vowelled like these names; and the seven days correspond to seven sefirot, and one name of these is on each day of the six days of creation. Avgitatz on the first day, and its name is YHVH, and its vowelling goes out from the verse "In the beginning God created et." The second name corresponds to the second day, and it is Kera Satan, and its name is YHVH, and its vowelling goes out from the verse "And God said, Let there be a firmament." The third name corresponds to the third day, and it is Neged Yakhash, and its name is YHVH, and its vowelling goes out from the verse "And God said, Let the waters be gathered." The fourth name corresponds to the fourth day, and it is Batar Tzatag, and its name is YHVH, and its vowelling goes out from the verse "And God said, Let there be luminaries." The fifth name corresponds to the fifth day, and it is Chakav Tana, and its name is YHVH, and its vowelling goes out from "And God said, Let the waters swarm." The sixth name corresponds to the sixth day, and it is Yagal Pazak, and its name is YHVH, and its vowelling goes out from the verse "And God said, Let the earth bring forth." The seventh name corresponds to the seventh day, and it is Shakutzit, and its name is YHVH, and its vowelling goes out from the verse "And God said, Behold, I have given." Thus far what we have seen fit to copy from the words of the divine Rashbi, peace be upon him. He explained some of them further, and because it is not found complete we have not seen fit to write it. And when we examine the vowels with which the holy one vowelled them, we find that the vowelling of the third, which corresponds to Tiferet, and the vowelling of the seventh, which corresponds to Malkhut, are equal, to hint that the sun shines in the moon. And there is no wonder that this name as a whole is in Gevurah and its particulars in the sefirot, for we have already given the answer to this in chapter 5. Further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote (Tikkun 69, folio 103b) that in each name there are six letters, corresponding to the six wings of the seraphim; and of this it is said (Isa. 6:2), "six wings, six wings to each one." And he said that it is good to mention this name before one's sleep, and likewise for a person near the time of his passing; for through these wings, "with two" (two letters of each name) the soul will cover its face, etc., "and with two" the soul will fly upward, and will merit to be saved from the angels of ruin and from all harmful spirits, and will merit the life of the world to come.
And behold, the explanation of the passage on the name of forty-two is complete:
On the name of twenty-two. And it is so called because there are twenty-two letters in it; and Rabbi Nechunya attributed it to Tiferet, and so the commentators agreed. And this is it:
אנקתם פסתם פספסים דיונסים [Anaktam Pastam Paspasim Dyonsim]; and it goes out from the priestly blessing, and this is its arrangement:

Yod: its substitute is Alef by Ayak: Alef. Bet: its substitute is Tet by Achas Beta, and under Tet, Nun by Atbash: Nun. Resh: its substitute is Kof by Avgad: Kof. Kaf: its substitute is Tav by Albam: Tav. Final Kaf: its substitute is Tav by Albam, and under Tav, Mem by Ayak. (The second name.) Yod: its substitute is Peh by Achas Beta. Heh: its substitute is Vav by Avgad, and under Vav, Samekh by Ayak. Vav: its substitute is Mem by Achas Beta, and under Mem, Tav by Ayak. Heh: its substitute is Vav by Avgad, and under Vav, Mem by Achas Beta. (The third name.) Vav: its substitute is Peh by Albam. Yod: its substitute is Mem by Atbash, and under Mem, Samekh by Ayak. Shin: its substitute is Yod by Albam, and under Yod, Peh by Achas Beta. Mem: its substitute is Samekh by Ayak. Resh: its substitute is Mem by Achas Beta, and under Mem, Yod by Atbash. Final Kaf: its substitute is Tav by Albam, and under Tav, Mem by Ayak. (The fourth name.) Yod: its substitute is Mem by Atbash, and under Mem, Dalet by Ayak. Alef: its substitute is Yod by Ayak. Resh: its substitute is Vav by Achas Beta:

Yod: its substitute is Tet by Avgad, and under Tet, Nun by Atbash. Heh: its substitute is Vav by Avgad, and under Vav, Samekh by Ayak. Vav: its substitute is Peh by Atbash, and under Peh, Yod by Achas Beta. Heh: its substitute is Vav by Avgad, and under Vav, Mem by Achas Beta. And the commentators explained concerning this name that each one of the four names mentioned has a special property by itself. The first, Anaktam, is good for having a prayer heard, and its explanation is "He hears the groan [enkat] of the perfect [tam]." The second, Pastam, gives "a handful [pisat] of grain" to those who need food. The third, Paspasim, from the language of (Gen. 37:3) "and he made him a coat of many colors [passim]," gives a garment to wear. The fourth, Dyonsim, works miracles [nissim] and wonders. And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, made use of them in saying (Gen. 28:20), "If God will be with me and will keep me," etc., "and will give me bread to eat and a garment to wear." This is the combination of the derivation of the Name from the priestly blessing, and we have not found anyone who speaks of this name further:

טוטרוסיא תרכוסיה וצליציה [Tutrusya Tarkusya Vetzlitzya]; and there are those who read (Vetzlitzya) in all of them, with the name Yah at the end. And so it seems: three names thus; and one does not read in the first name Tutru-, but without the second Vav, Tutr-, etc., so that the name be of twenty-two [letters]; for this name too is of twenty-two letters. And Rabbi Nechunya assigned it to the sefirah Netzach; and its derivation and its source are hidden from us until a teacher of righteousness comes:

אדע תבב לוש העת יבו כתם תוש יוב רתו אתק אדב יהוהא: this name Rabbi Nechunya attributed to the sefirah Hod. And its derivation is from the verse (Deut. 10:20), "You shall fear the Lord your God; Him shall you serve, and to Him shall you cleave, and by His name shall you swear." And now we will arrange its letters: the first letter from the first word, and the second, is et; and it skips the name YHVH, and the Alef of Elohekha, and it [YHVH-Alef] is the last name. And the first letters of the other words are להי"ך תיר"א, Alef [and afterwards in reverse, skipping a word and reading a word: that is to say, Tav from the tenth word, Vav from the eighth word: behold תו; Tav from the sixth word, Ayin from the fourth word, Bet from the second word, Dalet from the first word: behold תעבד]. And afterwards straight, skipping a word and reading a word, it is וב"ו ת"ד. And afterwards it is in reverse, at the ends of the words: ב"ק ובשמ"ו תשב"ע. And the reason for this matter is that this name hints at three branches, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, in the manner of the name of seventy-two. And the first is straight, and it is Netzach, compassion. And the middle, half of it straight and half of it reversed, is in Yesod, which draws sustenance from two sides, half judgment and half compassion. And the reason for skipping a word, etc., is to blend judgment with compassion, so that there be no separation within it between judgment and compassion; and the ends of the words are judgment, and therefore it is in reverse. And this is in the way that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained concerning the name of seventy-two, as we explained in chapter 5. And the name as a whole hints at Hod. And therefore Yesod comes half of it reversed, and not straight like Tiferet; because the name of seventy-two is in Chesed and compassion, and it inclines toward compassion, according to its name ("and abundant in Chesed": He inclines toward Chesed); and Hod is judgment, and therefore Yesod is intermediate:

This name Rabbi Nechunya attributed to the sefirah Yesod. And there are versions in which only nine havayot are written, and the three havayot at the head of the name are not written in them. And this does not seem to us to be the principal reading, because it is known that twelve havayot correspond to the twelve diagonal boundaries, and they are in Tiferet, and they are also in Yesod; for "all that befell Jacob befell Joseph," and Yesod is the mold of Tiferet. And it would have been possible to explain the reason: because the twelve boundaries are the thirteen tikkunim of the supernal beard, the beard of Arikh [Anpin], and the beard of Ze'ir [Anpin] is only nine; and therefore it is not fitting to relate to Yesod, which is the beard of Ze'ir, more than nine havayot. But against this the relation of the last three havayot is somewhat difficult, and in Yah (another version: in the name of the havayah). And to grasp the content of this matter one needs to study the book Or Yakar, which we composed. And concerning the vowelling of these havayot there are many differences; but Rashbi vowelled them in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 9b), and his words are always the principal for us; therefore we will write their vowelling according to them:

And these are his words: "ישמחו "השמים "ותגל "הארץ. "יתהלל "המתהלל "השכל "וידוע. "ידותיו "ולצלע "המשכן "השנית. וכל זה" איננו" שוה" לי". ולמפרשים ארצ"ה וישליכה"ו ארצ"ה ויה"י לנח"ש. לענין נקוד הכל אחד. "הסכת "ושמע "ישראל "היום. עיר"ה ולשרק"ה בנ"י אתונ"ו. וירא"ו אות"ה שר"י פרע"ה. "ודבש "היום "הזה "יהוה. "וירא "יושב "הארץ "הכנעני. ליהו"ה את"י ונרוממ"ה שמ"ו. "המר ימיר "והיה "הוא. וצדק"ה תהי"ה לנ"ו כ"י [verses whose initial or final letters spell the twelve permutations of the Name, and whose vowels give their vowelling]:

And further, the commentators wrote that יהו"ה הוה"י והי"ה היה"ו ההי"ו ההו"י, six, are hidden; יהו"ה הוי"ה היו"ה יוה"ה ויה"ה והה"י, six, are revealed. And we have not reached the depth of their opinion.

And further they said that there is no secret in these verses for these names, but that they set it as a mere sign. And in this too we are in doubt; for the verse is its secret, in the vowels of the havayot. But as to their vowelling, it is possible in two ways: a havayah from the initials of the words and its vowelling from the ends of the words, or a havayah from the ends of the words and its vowelling from the initials of the words; or a havayah and its vowelling [both] from the initials of the words, or from the ends of the words. And now we will devote a chapter by itself to the explanation of these havayot according to the secret, in the way that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained some of them:

On the explanation of the havayot and the division of their letters we have some revealing in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim, in scattered places; and we will not copy his language here, so as not to lengthen, and further because it is almost impossible, the matter being scattered, one here and one there. And nevertheless, as it has come to our hands, we will hint at it in brief language, as far as we can:

יהוה [text: יחוס] is the first havayah: the four-letter name in its proper order and form. And this name indicates the complete union and complete compassion; and this is the secret of "an offering [korban] to YHVH" (Lev. 1:2), and it did not say "to Elohim." And the explanation of korban is drawing near and union: that these four letters are unified, which are two males and two females, male and female, male and female; and that is Yod with Heh, Vav with Heh, as is explained in the Zohar, Vayikra (folio 5), and in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, folio 103b). And this is the perfection that is in this name, which indicates the order of the bestowal as is fitting and proper. And there are further many hints in it, which we hinted at in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name and likewise in the Gate of Names, and there is no need to lengthen:

יההו is the second havayah. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained it in the Tikkunim, and we copied his language in Gate 8, chapter 13. And the explanation: sometimes Malkhut rises and is unified with Chokhmah, and Binah descends and is unified with Tiferet; as in the matter of (Prov. 3:19) "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth": behold, Malkhut is in the secret of Chokhmah; and likewise "He established the heavens by understanding," for Tiferet is established through Binah. And this is the secret of יהה"ו: that the Heh unified with the Yod is Malkhut, and the Heh over the Vav is Binah. And this is necessitated for two reasons. The first: because it is impossible that the first Heh be Binah; for if so, Chokhmah and Binah would be found unified, and Tiferet and Malkhut would have no union, and this is impossible, as we explained in the gate mentioned; if so, it is necessary that the first Heh is the Daughter, Malkhut, who is toward Abba, and likewise the second Heh is Imma toward the Son. And the second reason: for from the side of the Son, which is Tiferet, Malkhut is always below it; and therefore the Heh that is above the Vav is Binah and not Malkhut. And we expounded at length in the gate mentioned; see there:

יוהה is the third havayah. And this too is explained in the Tikkunim: because the way of the male is to incline to the right, and the way of the female is to incline to the left, it is necessitated from this that Tiferet rose by way of Chesed up to Chokhmah, and Malkhut by way of Gevurah up to Binah; and it turns out that Tiferet, which is the Vav, is unified with the Yod, which is Chokhmah, and the last Heh, which is Malkhut, is unified with the first Heh, which is Binah; and this is יוה"ה. And he said that concerning the matter of Chokhmah and Tiferet it is said: the son who is drawn from the brain of the father. Further, another explanation: it indicates the matter that we explained in Gate 8, chapter 13, concerning the exile of the supernal Shekhinah and the lower Shekhinah, both of which were driven out of their places, and Chokhmah and Tiferet remained alone; and this is יוה"ה: the two Hehs are driven out, and Tiferet withdraws to Chokhmah, in the secret of (Ps. 10:1) "Why, O Lord, do You stand afar off?"; and in the secret of "Let our prayer come before You," Malkhut, which is before Tiferet, "and do not conceal Yourself [tit'alam] from our supplication," that is to say, Binah, that is, concealment in the concealed world:

היוה is the fourth havayah. It seems that it is Abba descending toward the Son: for when the havayah is יוה"ה, it indicates that the Son, Tiferet, withdrew toward Abba, Chokhmah; but when the havayah is היו"ה, it indicates the Father, who is Chokhmah, descending toward the Son. Further, another explanation: for Vav-Heh is on the right side, and this is the matter of the name Eloah, El, Vav-Heh; and on the left side, Elohim, where there is Heh-Yod, for the Heh, which is female, rules over the Yod, which is male, indicating judgment. And behold, when the left rules over the right, the havayah is found to be היו"ה: Heh-Yod, which is judgment, rules over Vav-Heh, which is from the side of the right.
And the matter of Heh-Yod on the left and Vav-Heh on the right we have expounded at length in the book Or Yakar, in the second part:

הויה is the fifth havayah. It indicates the Son rising toward Imma, Tiferet with Binah, which is Heh over Vav, indicating the mother who covers over the son; and Abba descending toward the Daughter, which is Yod over Heh. And behold, this havayah is the reverse of the second havayah that we explained: for there it is the Daughter toward Abba and Imma toward the Son, and in this havayah Abba toward the Daughter and the Son toward Imma, as we explained; and this is הוי"ה. Further, we can explain it in the secret of hoy [woe], which Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in parashat Acharei (folio 75), and we explained it in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles: that the Heh is Binah, the Vav indicates Tiferet, which withdrew to Binah, and with it withdrew the head of the Righteous One, which is the matter of the drawing of the blessings, and this is the Yod; and this is הוי"ה, and its explanation is hoy, which withdrew from the Heh. And for this reason, when He wished [to indicate] the strength of judgment, He said (Ex. 9:3), "Behold, the hand of the Lord is [hoyah]." And so Rashbi explained (in the Tikkunim, in the Introduction, folio 9a) on the matter of the secret of the tefillin, that this havayah indicates the strength of judgment. And the Yod, which is the head of the Righteous One, is the delightful manifestation that comes into being there; and it hints at the manifestation of the Yod of Yesod, which corresponds to the diadem, the head of the Righteous One, and it corresponds to Chokhmah. And we were compelled to turn the matter around so as not to depart from the custom that these four letters indicate four known sefirot, which are Yod Chokhmah, Heh Binah, Vav Tiferet, etc.:

היהו is the sixth havayah. And it indicates the Yod, Abba, descending toward the Heh, the Daughter, Malkhut, and the Daughter rising to her former place; and that is Heh-Yod Heh-Vav, for the middle Yod-Heh are Chokhmah and Malkhut, as we explained. And it also indicates judgment, and that there is no union. Or we can say that it indicates that the left rules over the right and tips toward the side of judgment. Explanation: for the Yod is toward the left and the Heh toward the right; and when the left rules over the right, Heh-Yod had to precede Vav-Heh; and because of the strength of its power, it turns Vav-Heh into Heh-Vav; and this is Heh-Yod Heh-Vav. And this havayah is near to הוה"י, which indicates complete judgment, as we shall explain. And nevertheless it is not literally like הוה"י; for הוה"י is reversed from its beginning to its end, and this is reversed partially, within itself: what was Yod-Heh became Heh-Yod, and what was Vav-Heh became Heh-Vav; and nevertheless Heh-Yod, which is upper, still rises above Heh-Vav, which is below it. Therefore it indicates judgment, and not judgment entirely, but indicates the returning light from Binah toward Chokhmah and the returning light from Malkhut to Tiferet. But הוה"י indicates the judgment returning from Malkhut up to the head of the grades, as we shall explain:

והיה is the seventh havayah; and this havayah is the reverse of the preceding one in all its particulars; and it indicates the right ruling over the left and turning the left to be compassion, in straight order. Explanation: in the right is Vav-Heh in its proper form; and behold, the Vav precedes, to indicate that the right is made to rule over the left and turns the left; for what was Heh-Vav became Vav-Heh. And according to the truth, right is found in left and left in right, for good; for Vav-Heh, its matter is receiving, and Yod-Heh, its matter is bestowing.

And behold, Yod-Heh are compassion and Vav-Heh are judgment, in the secret of bestower and bestowed upon. And behold now, because the right is blended with the left and the left with the right, it is hinted at in the secret of והי"ה. Further, we can explain it in another way: for in the right are Vav-Heh [in the left Heh-Yod], and in the middle is YHVH, for Tiferet is middle, including right and left; and their combination turns out to be והיהוהה"י. And when we combine the right of Tiferet with the right of Chesed, the secret of this havayah, והי"ה, comes out; and in the relation of the left of Tiferet to Gevurah, והה"י comes out, which is the ninth havayah; and we shall add further in its place, with the help of the Name:

ויהה is the eighth havayah. Concerning this havayah Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, folio 42a) that it indicates the exile of the supernal Shekhinah and the lower Shekhinah, both of which were driven out of their places, and Abba and the Son withdrew. And it was difficult for him that it should properly have been יוה"ה, Abba over the Son; and he resolved the matter there, and so as not to lengthen we will not copy it. Further, we can explain that both of them were driven out, and Abba descended toward them to guard them in exile. And close to this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Tetze, folio 278b), that Abba descends in the Righteous One to guard the Shekhinah in exile, etc. And if so, the Son is found over Abba; and this is ויה"ה:
והה"י: we have already explained it with the seventh havayah.

And further, we will explain it in another way: that it indicates the right ruling over the left, the Vav-Heh that is in the right ruling over the Heh-Yod that is in the left. And nevertheless it is not complete compassion like והי"ה; for there the right rules over the left and also turns it to compassion, but והה"י indicates the right ruling over the left while the left still conducts itself according to its custom, which is Heh over Yod, and there is some judgment in it:

ההוי is the tenth havayah. This indicates the exile of the supernal Shekhinah and the lower Shekhinah, and the Son who withdrew toward Abba; and that is Heh-Heh, (Ruth 1:19) "and the two of them went," and Vav-Yod remained, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained concerning the eighth havayah, ויה"ה. Except that the havayah ויה"ה indicates some bestowal and compassion in exile, that is, two males over two females, but there is no union, because the first Heh is still over the last Heh. Further, we can explain that Tiferet, which is the Vav, withdrew with the head of the Righteous One, which is the Yod, to Binah; that is, the explanation of hoy, as we explained above and as we shall explain in the Glossary of Titles; and the intent is that the Heh remained alone, and her husband withdrew above and became hoy; and that is Heh, hoy:

ההיו is the eleventh havayah. This too indicates the exile of the two sisters, in the secret of "and the two of them went," the daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law; and Abba and the Son withdrew. But not as Vav-Yod, as in the preceding havayot; rather they withdrew in the secret of some regard, and that is Yod-Vav in their order; and nevertheless the two Hehs are still above, to indicate the diminishment of the bestowal:

הוהי: this havayah indicates the strength of the strong judgment, the females ruling over the males in the secret of the returning light, as we explained in the Gate From Below to Above. And behold, through this havayah will be understood the matter of the verse (Amos 5:16), "and in all the streets they shall say, Alas, alas [ho, ho]," and the matter of the verse (Ezek. 2:10), "lamentations, and mourning, and woe [hi]," to indicate the strength of the judgment and the breaking that comes upon them from Heh-Vav and Heh-Yod, that is, this havayah, הוה"י. And when the wheel turns over in the secret of compassion, it is said (Ps. 118:22), "The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner," and what was הוה"י returns to be יהו"ה. And in the totality of these havayot there are found at the head of their combination, three havayot [to each letter], three Yods and three Hehs and three Vavs and three Hehs, like this: יי"י הה"ה וו"ו הה"ה. And it is explained in the Tikkun (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 120) that the three Yods are three right ones, in the secret of the line of Chesed, and they are Chokhmah, Chesed, Netzach; and the three Hehs are three left ones, in the secret of the line of judgment, and they are Binah, Gevurah, Hod; and the three Vavs are three middle ones, in the secret of the line of Rachamim, and they are Keter, Tiferet, Yesod; and the [last] three Hehs are the secret of the inclining of the last Heh, Malkhut, toward one of these three lines. And that matter will be sweet to the palate in the study of what we wrote close to this in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, chapter 4, with the help of Heaven. And this remark on the explanation of the havayot in their letters is enough for us:

It has already come before us in the preceding chapters that these twelve havayot are the twelve diagonal boundaries, and that they correspond to the twelve hours of the day and the twelve hours of the night, and to the twelve months, three months in each season [tekufah] of the four seasons, which are the four letters: Yod is the season of Nisan, Heh the season of Tammuz, Vav the season of Tishrei, Heh the season of Tevet, with three months in each season. That is to say: of these twelve permutations, the initials of the first three permutations are Yod, and they are the season of Nisan; the initials of the second three permutations are Heh, and they are the season of Tammuz; the initials of the third three permutations are Vav, and they are the season of Tishrei; and the initials of the fourth three permutations are Heh, and they are the season of Tevet. And likewise they correspond to the twelve constellations and to the twelve simples, which are ה"ו ז"ח ט"י ל"נ ס"ע צ"ק. And the meaning is that these twelve letters are called simples because they do not receive dagesh and rafeh like the seven doubles. And one cannot say that they are called simples because there is in them no composition of judgment and compassion, as the commentators explained (see the Gate of Letters, chapter 3). For it has already been explained that every havayah in which "Heh rules over Yod, Heh over Vav, is female and is judgment," as we explained in the preceding gates; and likewise all the havayot are composite of judgment and compassion, as we explained in the preceding chapter; and likewise the twelve boundaries are in Tiferet, in the composition of the six extremities, and there is no doubt that there is judgment and compassion in it. Rather, it is certainly as we explained. We could further say that they too receive a strong dagesh, as the grammarians explained. And they are called simples [peshutot] because they are branches spreading out [mitpashtot] from the sefirot, and are not the self of the sefirot as AMeSh are, and likewise BeGeD KeFeReT, which are ten, corresponding to the ten sefirot.

And behold, with the twelve letters were created the twelve months, the twelve constellations and the twelve organs. And these are the words of Sefer Yetzirah: "ה"ו ז"ח ט"י לנ"ס עצ"ק: He engraved them, combined them, weighed them, exchanged them, and formed with them the constellations in the world," etc.

Further there: "He made Heh king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Aries in the world, Nisan in the year, and the liver in the soul. He made Vav king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Taurus in the world, Iyyar in the year, and the gall in the soul. He made Zayin king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Gemini in the world, Sivan in the year, and the spleen in the soul. He made Chet king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Cancer in the world, Tammuz in the year, and the omasum in the soul. He made Tet king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Leo in the world, Av in the year, and the right kidney in the soul. He made Yod king, and bound a crown [text: קשר, a knot] to it, and formed with it Virgo in the world, Elul in the year, and the left kidney in the soul. He made Lamed king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Libra in the world, Tishrei in the year, and the gizzard in the soul. He made Nun king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Scorpio in the world, Marcheshvan in the year, and the stomach in the soul. He made Samekh king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Sagittarius in the world, Kislev in the year, and the right hand in the soul. He made Ayin king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Capricorn in the world, Tevet in the year, and the left hand in the soul. He made Tzadi king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Aquarius in the world, Shevat in the year, and the right foot in the soul. He made Kof king, and bound a crown to it, and formed with it Pisces in the world, Adar in the year, and the left foot in the soul." And we thought fit to draw them here in a fine figure, that it may be fixed in the mind of the inquirer; this is according to the version before us. However, the variant readings on this matter in this book are many. And however it may be, we have learned that the twelve simples are the twelve months and the twelve constellations, and they are the twelve organs; and all of it, in world, year and soul, is a hint at great matters, as we explained in the preceding gates. And now we shall know that from the actions the powers are known.

And behold, those expert in natural science said that the twelve constellations in their order, which are Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, are divided into divisions in their action, "each by his own standard, with the ensigns" (Num. 2:2) of his action. And this is their order: the standard of the camp of Aries is fire, and those encamped by it are Leo and Sagittarius. The standard of the camp of Taurus is earth, and those encamped by it are Virgo and Capricorn. The standard of the camp of Gemini is air, and those encamped by it are Libra and Aquarius. The standard of the camp of Cancer is water, and those encamped by it are Scorpio and Pisces. And their order follows their order in the firmament: the first fire, the second after it earth, the third after it air, and the fourth after it water. And the reason for this order is well grounded in what we explained, that the twelve constellations were created by means of the twelve boundaries, and they are the twelve simples. And it is known that the Emanation in the boundaries is divided into east, west, north and south, and these are four, corresponding to air, earth, fire and water, and they are the four letters of the Name, as we explained in the preceding chapters.
And behold, water and the south are the power of Chesed; fire and the north are the power of Gevurah; air and the east are the power of Tiferet; and earth and the west are the power of Malkhut.

And behold, from the binding and union of the constellations, the union and binding of the supernal boundaries may be examined. For fire is hot and dry, and the heat in it gives rise to the nature of dryness through the excess of its heat; and earth is dry and cold; and water is cold and moist; and air is hot and moist.

And behold, the extremes are bound and united by means of the intermediates. How so? Fire and water are opposites, contrary in two respects: water is cold and fire is hot, water is moist and fire is dry. They are bound on one side by means of air, and on the other side by means of earth. And likewise air and earth are opposites, contrary in two respects: air is hot and earth is cold, air is moist and earth is dry; and they are bound on one side by means of water, and on the other side by means of fire. How so? Air completes and binds the moist water and the hot fire, for it is hot and moist; so it is equal to fire on the side of its heat and to water on the side of its moisture. And earth completes and binds the cold water and the dry fire, for it is cold and dry; so it is equal to fire on the side of its dryness and to water on the side of its coldness. Thus fire and water are bound and united with a complete binding on all their sides, and there is no dispute between them. And likewise water and fire complete between air and earth. How so? Water is equal to air on the side of its moisture and to earth on the side of its coldness; thus the cold earth and the moist air are united by means of water. And likewise fire is equal to air on the side of its heat and to earth on the side of its dryness; thus the dry earth and air are united by means of fire. And this is the binding of the elements, and likewise the binding of the constellations, and likewise the binding of the boundaries. And likewise the binding of the supernal elements, which are the sefirot. How so? Chesed is the element of water and Gevurah the element of fire, and they are bound by means of Tiferet, the element of air, and by means of Malkhut, the element of earth: by means of Tiferet in one respect, and by means of Malkhut in the other respect. And let there be no wonder at our saying that Malkhut arbitrates between Gedulah and Gevurah; for at first, before the accusation, she served her husband and arbitrated between them. And now, being below, in truth the arbitration is not complete until the will goes up from Him, may He be blessed, and the wife is in her husband's bosom, speedily in our days.

And further, the union of Tiferet and Malkhut is effected through their receiving from the Patriarchs, as we explained in the secret of "he went up by the ramp," in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 21. And now we shall draw a correct figure for this matter here.

And behold, when we consider the matter of the seasons in the elements and the order of the months, we find them somewhat at odds in their matter. For the season of Nisan, which is the three months Nisan, Iyyar and Sivan, is the Yod of the Name, that is, Chesed, the element of water; and the season of Tammuz, Av and Elul, three months, is the Heh of the Name among the elements. Yet the season of Nisan, which is the element of water, is Yod, while the constellations and the months are: Nisan, Aries, fire; Iyyar, Taurus, earth; Sivan, Gemini, air. Thus far one season. And in the season of Tammuz, the element of air, it is Heh; the constellations and the months are: Tammuz, Cancer, water; Av, Leo, fire; Elul, Virgo, earth. Thus far one season. And in the season of Tishrei, the element of earth, it is Vav; the constellations and the months are: Tishrei, Libra, air; Marcheshvan, Scorpio, water; Kislev, Sagittarius, fire. Thus far one season. And in the season of Tevet, the element of fire, it is Heh; the constellations and the months are: Tevet, Capricorn, earth; Shevat, Aquarius, air; Adar, Pisces, water. Thus far one season. And the confusions came in this secret and in this matter to indicate the blending: that earth is included in water, fire and air, and likewise each one of them is included in the other three. And remarks such as these are enough on this.

Metatron. Rabbi Nechunya ascribed this name to Malkhut in his prayer; and the words are ancient, and they are explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapters 4, 5 and 6 [דה"ו], with the help of Heaven. And sometimes it is called Mitatron. And there we spoke at length. And this remark on these names is enough for us.
And behold, this chapter is completed, and this gate is concluded, with the help of Heaven.
The Twenty-Second Gate: The Gate of Titles.

What is intended in this Gate is to set out the matter of the titles: what they are about, and what they are. And in it will be explained the well-known matter that the human being is a chariot for the sefirot, with the help of Heaven:
Chapter One:

Among the astonishing things in the words of our Torah is what is written in the Torah: "and under His feet," etc. (Exod. 24:10); "written with the finger of God," etc. (Exod. 31:18); "the hand of YHVH," "the eyes of YHVH," "the ears of YHVH," and things like these, which are titles drawn from the body. And this cannot be attributed to Him, may He be blessed, for He is neither a body nor a power in a body. Therefore these matters cannot be attributed to His sefirot either, for they too are far from all the dimensions of body. For if not, since it is known that He is the soul of His sefirot and is the power in them, it would follow, God forbid, that He is a power in a body, far be it, far be it. Therefore it is fitting to remove the dimensions of body from the sefirot, and we are bound to this just as we are bound to remove them from the Self of the Ein Sof. If so, when [Scripture] speaks in dimensions drawn from the dimensions of body, such as "and YHVH saw," "and YHVH heard," "and YHVH said," "and YHVH spoke," which are dimensions that can be gauged only in corporeal organs, it is fitting that we believe that they describe a hidden matter, and not literal seeing, hearing or speech. And there is no doubt that in our holy tongue the eye is not called "eye," the ear "ear" and the mouth "mouth" by chance and happenstance, or by convention as in the other languages. And the proof of this is that this tongue of ours is called the holy tongue [leshon ha-kodesh], which certainly means that it is a divine invention, and not like the other languages. And there is no doubt that it is the tongue that the Holy One, blessed be He, invented when He brought His world into being; so the tongue certainly preceded the world. And the matter is this: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created Adam, the first man, He created him a holy body and a holy soul, beyond all measure, as his praises are recounted in the Book of the Tikkunim, so that his light shone in the body, and the glorious body dimmed the orb of the sun; so that he certainly did not enjoy an outer light, the light of the luminaries, sun and moon, but a fair and pure light, the light of the radiance of the Shekhinah in the Garden of Eden. And since Adam, the first man, was such a holy body, the Holy One, blessed be He, handed over to him the treasures of wisdom, and the keys of the Torah were given into his hand, and he occupied himself with it. Then He gave him the holy tongue, the glorious tongue, and holy letters were fixed in his mouth. And when he sinned, what had been "garments of light" [or] with an Alef, which is the holiness of the union of the world, became, when he abandoned himself to the husk, "[garments of] skin" [or] with an Ayin, which is the seventy [the numerical value of Ayin] branches that spread out from the inner to the outer. And there was not yet a portion particular to the Holy One, blessed be He, because the light of Abraham had not yet shone, until after the generation of the Dispersion, as we explained in the Gate of Gates, chapter 3. And when the light of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, shone, the Holy One, blessed be He, divided seventy nations among seventy princes, for seventy tongues; and He chose us and gave speech to us as our portion, which is our lot, a holy lot, and the holy tongue, a divine convention: that the ear should be called "ear" and the mouth "mouth," to indicate the powers that are a shadow over a man's head; and the organ was emanated from its supernal power, which emanates it and bestows upon it. And now, according to the truth, what is meant by "ear" is not the bodily ear but the action performed by means of the ear through the power that bestows upon it. And of this kind it is said (Ps. 94:9), "He that planted the ear, shall He not hear? He that formed the eye, shall He not see?" The explanation: since the creation of the organs of the human being is through the cycling of the holy alphabet, [letters] that draw effluence from the supernal powers, the roots, which are united in the Root of roots, there must necessarily be in that letter the power of the action through which the created organ acts; and likewise in the root that bestows upon the letter; and so from cause to effect down to the bottom. For from the actions the powers are known; and since their power is seeing and hearing, there must be in that root the power of hearing, and likewise of seeing; but not corporeal seeing and hearing, rather something spiritual. The parable: just as people, when they hear the sound of speech with their ears, weigh the matter that they hear, so the supernal power that receives that voice and weighs it, whether it is fit to receive it or not, is called "ear." And of this it is said (Job 34:3), "For the ear tries words." And likewise the matter with the angels, who have no bodily power such as our mouth, with which they would speak this speech of ours, which is bodily. Rather, when an angel looks at an angel they understand each other. For the effluence of the name YHVH [pours] into the selfhood and the spirituality of the letters that are wanted for the matter that he wants [to convey], and by this his fellow understands the thing that he wants; and that is their speech. And they have no eyes like the eyes of human beings, with which they see; but they have the spirituality of the action that brings about sight, and by it they comprehend and look far off. And it is more glorious than our seeing, as the seeing of the intellect is more glorious than the eye. For the eye sees only what is before it, and not all that is before it, but only a limited thing that the corporeal vessel of the eye can encompass. But the intellect sees even what is not before the eye: as a man now sees in his intellect many things that he saw many years ago, or even things that he has never seen, which he devises in his mind as though he were seeing such a matter; until the seeing of the intellect is so fine that it sees subtle matters that the eye cannot look upon. And greater than this is the seeing of the prophets: for the prophet apprehends spiritual things with his intellect, and as the breadth of the intellect, so the breadth of the apprehension. And so Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Prov. 27:19), "As in water face answers to face, so the heart of man to man": for the heart of man to man, they understand each other from self to self; and it is a bodily organ, and it has this power because of the influx of the soul, and likewise of the intellect that dwells upon it. And nevertheless, since it is a limited thing, its apprehension is limited; and according to the measure of the prophet, so is the level of his prophecy. And from this matter we ascend to the understanding of the angels one for another, and from there we attain many and many levels to know the existence of seeing and of the corporeal actions among the spiritual ones. And as the prophet said (Zech. 4:2), "I have seen, and behold, a lampstand all of gold"; and likewise (1 Sam. 9:9), "for he who is now called a prophet was formerly called a seer": the matter will not be a seeing with organs, nor will the word "seeing" be by way of parable; rather it is literally the seeing of apprehension. So it is above: seeing in the angels is that power of apprehension by which they apprehend matters. And this is the matter of Rabbi Eleazar son of Rabbi Shimon, who went to see Rabbi Yose ben Lakunya, his father-in-law (brought in the Addenda to the Zohar, part 3, fol. 304), and on their way they saw that matter of the serpent; Rabbi Eleazar spoke those words, and the companions were astonished, and he told them that he had not apprehended that matter through wisdom but through a seeing that he saw. Now can one say that Rabbi Eleazar saw those matters with eyes of flesh? Rather, this is certainly the seeing of seclusion [hitbodedut], by which a person apprehends matters that are to come and matters that have passed, and through the subtlety of the intellect hears the matters.

Behold, after this manner is the seeing among the upper ones, and among the upper ones above the upper ones, until "one higher than the high watches" (Eccl. 5:7). And this is no wonder, for even among the bodily vessels that are in us, the eye is not called "eye" because of the eye itself but because of the power of sight, which is truly called "eye"; and likewise the hand is not called "hand" because of the hand itself, but the action that issues from the hand is truly called "hand." And the proof of this is their saying, of blessed memory, in Gittin (85b): "Hands [yadayim] that are not evident: are they hands or are they not hands?" meaning the matter of taking hold; and so Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "yadayim: a handle and a grip on the matter, to hold on to it and to say that by it," etc. And likewise in the matter of betrothal and divorce: "a minor girl has no hand," or "has a hand"; and the intent is not that she has no hand because she is maimed, but the intent is the power of receiving, to receive betrothal or divorce. And likewise it is customary in the language of our Sages, of blessed memory: "the matter has legs," or "it has no legs"; and the intent is not that it has legs or has no legs, but it is a parable: just as the legs are a person's standing and support, so when a thing has a basis and an existence that settles in the intellect, it is said that the matter has legs; and when the thing does not settle, it is said that it has no legs. And likewise what is written in the Torah (Exod. 21:24), "eye for eye, hand for hand, foot for foot," where we learn "striking" from "striking" from "he who strikes the life of a beast shall make it good, life for life" (Lev. 24:18); and the tradition has come that the intent is not to say that if he cut off his hand they cut off his hand, and likewise the other organs, but the intent is that he pays him the whole value of the hand, and likewise the other organs; and that is what is called "eye," "hand" and "foot," since it is the worth of the power of the eye, the hand and the foot. And so are the matters among the spiritual ones: the power that spreads out from the sefirot to watch over the world, from the power of the Ein Sof, is called "eyes." And so (Zech. 4:10), "these seven are the eyes of YHVH, which range through the whole earth"; and the Kabbalists explained that they are seven powers, and they are called Orpaniel, Tagriel, Danel, Palmiel, Asimon, Safiel, Boel, and they are those that watch over the affairs of human beings. And since they have the power of providence they are called "eyes"; not that they are eyes, but that there is spiritual providence in them, as we explained above. And in them all deeds are inscribed, from good to bad; and through them the two luminaries testify concerning "the doings and the steps of a man," "the thoughts of a man and his schemes," and "the inclinations of a man's deeds" before the seventy judges, as is explained in the Gate of Palaces, in the Palace of Merit, chapter 4. And over these eyes there are yet other eyes, for "one higher than the high watches, and there are higher ones over them" (Eccl. 5:7). (And after this manner too in the verse (Micah 6:2), "Hear, O mountains, the controversy of YHVH": for just as the mountains hold up the world and keep it upright on the pan of a balance, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained, and they are high in the heights of the world, so the Patriarchs hold us up by their merit and keep the world standing in its place, and they stand in the heights of the world.) And likewise what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said to Jethro (Num. 10:31), "and you shall be to us as eyes"; and Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "every single thing that is concealed from our eyes, you shall enlighten our eyes." Thus far his words.

And since, just as the eyes show the body the right way in which it should walk, so the teacher of righteousness is called "eyes." And after this manner we may infer for all the other things that are said by way of title of the sefirot. For example, "father" and "mother": the intent is not, God forbid, that there are a father and a mother there, for that is heresy, God forbid. Rather the intent is that, just as the existence of begetting comes about through the joining of male and female, and through that joining that offspring comes into being, so it is with the sefirot: through the joining of Chokhmah and Binah, and the bestowal of Chokhmah into Binah, was the cause of the whole Emanation. For in Chokhmah the beings were subtle in the extreme, as the son is concealed in the brain of the father; and after they spread out into Binah they took on body and were given form, a more revealed form. And therefore Chokhmah is called "father": for just as the father's sons are in his self and in his brain, subtle in the extreme subtlety, as a drop, and by means of the joining of the male to the female that drop is aroused and comes to be a seminal drop, and he bestows it into the female, and through his effluence in her that offspring comes into being in her womb; so Chokhmah is the father, and Binah is the female, who receives all the forms that are bestowed from Chokhmah, and a more revealed form is formed in her, and she emanates that Emanation. And for this she is called "female" and "mother" of the Emanation, and the Emanation is called by the name "sons" to them, for the reason mentioned. And it is all a parable from the corporeal to the spiritual. And likewise when Tiferet and Malkhut are called "bridegroom" and "bride," and Binah "mother" or "mother-in-law," and Chokhmah "father" or "father-in-law."

And behold, sometimes the two of them are called bridegroom and bride, and Chokhmah and Binah father and mother; and sometimes son and daughter; and sometimes Malkhut is daughter to Chokhmah and daughter-in-law to Binah; and sometimes daughter-in-law to Chokhmah and daughter to Binah, and the like. And it is fitting to widen the explanation in these matters.

And behold, Tiferet and Malkhut are emanated from Chokhmah and Binah; and in the manifestation of their simple emanation they have no coupling together, as we explained above in the Gate of the Diminishment [of the Moon]. And they have union only after their tikkun, their arming and their adornment. Therefore, from that aspect Tiferet and Malkhut are called son and daughter, and Chokhmah and Binah father and mother. And Chokhmah is called father to Tiferet from the aspect of the concealed Da'at; and Binah is called mother to Tiferet from the side of the establishing by which she establishes him (from the language of "and by understanding [tevunah] it is established" [yitkonan] (Prov. 24:3)), which is a manifestation added to what is emanated from Chokhmah, as we explained above. For from Chokhmah they have a subtle manifestation, and from the side of Binah a more revealed manifestation. And from the side of the subtle manifestation that they have, which is the manifestation of a Yod for Malkhut and the manifestation of a firmament for Tiferet, as we explained in Gate 1, chapter 2, and in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 4, they are called sons of Chokhmah; and from the revealed manifestation that they have from Binah they are called her sons.
