And when they are afterward united in the secret of the diadems with which they are crowned, as it is written (Song 3:11), "Go forth, O daughters of Zion, and behold King Solomon," etc., they are called bridegroom and bride, man and his wife. And there is a difference between them: before their union, when they are prepared and ready for union, they are called bridegroom and bride, and they have adornments like the bridegroom and the bride; and after they are in union they are called man and his wife. And there are in the union many distinctions and aspects, which will be explained in many places in the book Or Yakar, with the help of the Name. And when the revealed manifestation is united with the revealed manifestation, or the hidden manifestation with the hidden manifestation, then they are simply children of Chokhmah and Binah, united together in a complete union; and they are son and daughter, brother and sister, permitted to one another. However, bridegroom and bride, [and] son and daughter, cannot be attributed to them together in relation to Chokhmah and Binah; for if he is son to Chokhmah he is son-in-law to Binah, and then Binah is called his mother-in-law, or Chokhmah his father-in-law if he is son to Binah. And similarly, if the revealed manifestation that is in Tiferet is united with the concealed manifestation that is in Malkhut, then the father of Malkhut is Chokhmah and the mother of Tiferet is Binah; and Malkhut is daughter-in-law to Binah, and Binah mother-in-law to Malkhut; and Tiferet is son-in-law to Chokhmah, and Chokhmah his father-in-law. And if the concealed manifestation that is in Tiferet is coupled with the revealed manifestation that is in Malkhut, then he is son to Chokhmah and she is daughter to Binah; and Malkhut is daughter-in-law to Chokhmah, and Chokhmah her father-in-law; and Tiferet is son-in-law to Binah, and Binah his mother-in-law. And after this manner the inquirer may infer for all the aspects. And after this manner all the other astonishing things in the books of the sages in this wisdom: for permission has been given to draw parables in them, as much as a person needs in order to understand, to comprehend and to reason about them; and of such it is said (Job 19:26), "and from my flesh I shall behold God." Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and ever.

The Rav, the author of Sefer ha-Orah (Gate 1, fol. 2), spoke at length on the titles and their matter, close to what we have dealt with; and therefore we shall copy his language here. And these are his words: "Know that the truth of the Self of the Creator, may He be blessed, is not apprehended by any other than Him; and none of all the multitudes on high know His place, how much less the Self of His truth. Do you not see what the angels on high say: 'Blessed be the glory of YHVH from His place' (Ezek. 3:12), wherever it may be? And if so among the upper ones, how much more so among the lower ones. And those matters that we read in the Torah, such as 'hand' or 'foot,' 'ear,' 'eye,' and all that is like them, what are they? Know and believe that all those matters, although they show and testify to His greatness and His truth, no creature can know and understand the essence of that thing that is called 'hand' or 'foot' or 'eye' or 'ear' and the like. And though we are made in the image and the likeness, let it not enter your mind that the eye is in the literal form of an eye, or the hand in the literal form of a hand, or the foot in the literal form of a foot; rather they are inner matters, and inner within inner, in the truth of the existence of the Name, from which the source and the effluence go out to all that exists (by the decree of the Name, may He be blessed). But the essence of the hand is not like the essence of a hand, nor is its shape like the shape of a hand, as Scripture says (Isa. 40:25), 'To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal?' And know and understand that there is no likeness between Him and us on the side of substance and shape; but the intent of the form of the organs that are in us is that they are made in the likeness of signs for inner, closed, supernal matters, which the mind cannot know except as a likeness of remembrance. As when one writes 'Reuben son of Jacob': for these letters and this form are not the self of Reuben son of Jacob, nor his form, his shape or his essence; but a remembrance that this 'Reuben son of Jacob' that is written is a sign corresponding to that known substance and shape that is called Reuben son of Jacob. And because the Name, may He be blessed, wished to give us merit, He created in the body of the human being many organs, hidden and revealed, in the likeness of a sign of the Work of the Chariot. And if a person merits to purify one of his organs, that organ will be like a throne for that supernal inner thing that is called by this name: if eye, eye; if hand, hand; if foot, foot; and so for the rest. How so? For example, if he guards and takes care with the sight of his eyes, that he does not look at forbidden unions or at any other shameful thing, but only at everything that is the holiness of the Name and His service, then that eye becomes as a throne for that thing that is called 'eye' above; and likewise the hand, and likewise the foot, and the other things.

"And further, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: 'The Patriarchs, they are the Chariot.' And they did not say 'each one of the Patriarchs is the Chariot,' but 'the Patriarchs, they are the Chariot.' How so? Abraham our father took the right side in purity and inherited the right [side] on high, which is the attribute of Chesed; and of this it is said (Gen. 12:9), 'And Abraham journeyed, going on still toward the south.' And Isaac took in purity the attribute of the left side, which is Fear [Pachad]; and of this it is said (Gen. 31:53), 'And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.' And Jacob took in purity the middle line; and of this it is said (Gen. 25:27), 'And Jacob was a whole man, dwelling in tents,' etc. Thus the three Patriarchs are found to be a throne for the Chariot." And "the words of a wise man's mouth are gracious" (Eccl. 10:12), even though there is some difference between his way and ours. And now we wish to set out one more premise concerning the titles:

And it is this: at first sight the thoughtful one will be astonished when he sees different titles for the ten sefirot, without number, whether in the Scriptures or in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory; so much so that on this account Rabbi Moshe de León wrote in the introduction to Sefer ha-Shem that the reason for the multitude of titles is that the sages intended to hide this wisdom, and each one devised hidden names for himself, to suppress the wisdom under his tongue. "Lo, these are but the edges of his ways" (Job 26:14); and we do not see it so, God forbid. But we will further ask: in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim, on the matter of the Tabernacle, the sefirot are hinted at many times. For the Tabernacle itself is the Shekhinah; the ten curtains are the ten sefirot; the curtains of the hangings, called in the language of the Torah "court," are the Shekhinah; the inner palace is the Shekhinah; one of the cherubim is the Shekhinah; one of the tablets is the Shekhinah; the ark is the Shekhinah, the table the Shekhinah, the lampstand the Shekhinah, the outer altar the Shekhinah, the frankincense the Shekhinah, the sockets the Shekhinah; and more like them, the bread on the table the Shekhinah, and the lamps on the lampstand the Shekhinah, and many matters besides these. Now what is this matter? Would one hint at the Shekhinah from among these things not be enough for us, without all these matters? Rather, the truth of the matter is certainly that the matter of the sefirot is not one substance that is not distinguished into different aspects, so that it would be called by one name alone. Rather, the sefirot are distinguished into many aspects, many matters and many manifestations; and for each and every aspect there is a name and a title; and what this title shows, that title does not show. And now, although this matter has already come before us in the preceding gates, such as the Gate of Channels and the Gate of Manifestations and others, nevertheless we shall not withhold our hands from dealing with it as much as is needed to understand this inquiry well. And we shall illustrate this matter with Malkhut, and from there infer to the other sefirot.

Behold, it was explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance that the sefirot are a power equal to each thing and to its opposite; and accordingly the attribute changes from aspect to aspect, according to the manifestation of its receiving from one of the upper sefirot, to act by the will of the Emanator. And now, when we consider that Malkhut receives from Yesod, there will be distinguished at least ten aspects in Malkhut that receives, and ten in Yesod that bestows. How so? Yesod may bestow on her what it receives from Tiferet and from its own self: that makes two; or it may bestow what it receives from Hod: that makes two. For Malkhut changes according to the effluence that is bestowed, and according to the bestower too. And likewise if it bestows on her from Netzach, and after this manner for the other sefirot. And although we say "changes," the intent is not, God forbid, a literal change; rather the aspect is in her, standing for ever, and the intent is that she shines in that aspect. And likewise she is distinguished into ten aspects with relation to each and every sefirah. And sometimes the aspect is in another manner: for she is distinguished in this aspect at a time when she receives from Tiferet when he is receiving from Gevurah and Tiferet bestows Chesed on her (in the secret of the blending); or she is distinguished in the aspect in which Tiferet receives from Chesed and bestows Chesed. For these aspects are not equal, and each one of them has a title of its own. And this is the reason that the sages of Israel agreed that we have no intention [kavvanah] at present: because the one who prays must be expert in the matter of the titles, to say: this aspect is equal to that aspect, and it is called by this name; and after this manner he will draw the effluence by way of the equal aspects, and the prayer will be received. And now that we have no knowledge of these matters, we say that we do not have intention. And this is the matter of the change of the aspects in each and every attribute. And for each and every title there is an aspect, so that this one shows what its fellow does not show, and a manifestation other than the manifestation of its fellow. And this premise is explained from many places in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 56, fol. 89b): "Heh, Heh: a woman and her daughter, a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law; according to the branches of the tree, so are they called." Thus far his words.

Behold, he explained that the two Hehs are a woman and her daughter, from the side of Malkhut's being daughter to Binah; and afterward he said that they are a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law, meaning that Malkhut is daughter-in-law to Binah; and these are almost opposite things. And he resolved it: this is no wonder, for "according to the branches of the tree, so are they called," meaning that according to her branches and her aspects she is called, with respect to this aspect and this branch, what she is called. Thus this title shows what its fellow does not show. And the matter of the titles is not by chance, as the commentators thought.

And the matter of the titles, in their matter, is the spreading out of the branches of the sefirot. It is as if we said that the four-letter name that is in each and every sefirah is the self of the sefirah; and each and every one of these ten names is clothed in the ten names that may not be erased. And we do not deny that the four-letter name includes the whole self of the sefirah and its root; and the holy name that may not be erased, which is one branch among the branches, does not include the whole self of the sefirah, as is proved from our explanation in the Gate of Names, chapter 1. And yet these branches have branches further, and they are the titles, which are more particular than the names: they are small branches that spread out from the large branches. Accordingly, the titles are a garment for the names that may not be erased, and the names that may not be erased are a garment for the havayot, and the havayot are a garment for the four-letter name in itself, which is explained in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name: like the branches of a tree, whose leaves cover its thin twigs, and its thin twigs cover its large branches, and the branches cover its main stem. And exactly so is the matter above. And this is why the Tikkunim many times mentions havayot, names and titles: the intent is these aspects. And now it is not far-fetched that one title should be more inward than its fellow, according to the difference of the aspects. And all the particulars of these matters will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, with the help of Heaven:

The intent in this chapter is to explain the matters of the human being as a chariot, since it is a matter that relates to this inquiry. And before anything we say that any person who is to be a chariot for any sefirah whatever needs two conditions. First, the purity of that organ more than all the rest of his body, until it is like white glass. And one must not think that the purity of that organ is enough even though he sins with the other organs, God forbid. Far be it to believe such a thing; for if he is blemished in any organ whatever, the Shekhinah does not rest upon him, for the Shekhinah does not rest on a blemished soul, God forbid. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 3b), and these are his words: "For He does not dwell in a blemished place; as it is written, 'whoever has a blemish shall not draw near' (Lev. 21:18). So too, He does not dwell in a blemished soul. Happy is he who perfects his soul, so that the name YHVH may dwell in it, and makes it a throne for Him." Thus far his words.

And so it is written, "evil shall not sojourn with You" (Ps. 5:5); and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded (Shabbat 149b): "the one who does evil shall not sojourn in Your dwelling," and that is the transgressor. Rather the matter is this: that he should purify his whole body from every blemish, and afterward be meticulous in some commandment and hold on to it most of all; like one whose Torah is his craft, who becomes a chariot for Tiferet. And so it is said of Jacob (Gen. 25:27), "a whole man, dwelling in tents": its plain sense is a complete man, who was not blemished in any of his organs, God forbid, but complete, without blemish; "dwelling in tents" means the tents of Torah, occupying himself with it. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Bereshit Rabbah on "and he lay down in that place" (Gen. 28:11): there he lay down, but for the fourteen years that he was in the house of study of Shem and Eber he did not lie down, for all his occupation was in the Torah. And therefore he became a chariot for Tiferet, in the secret of "dwelling in tents." However, Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was raised above him, because he occupied himself with the Torah more, and further taught it to sixty myriads; and although Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is also a chariot for Tiferet, he is more concealed, for he is in the secret of Da'at, as we explained in Gate 1, chapter 2, with the help of the Name. And likewise Abraham became a chariot for Chesed, because in this world he held on to the attribute of Chesed without end, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, spoke at length; and he bestowed kindnesses on souls and on bodies, as explained by our Rabbis, of blessed memory, on (Gen. 12:5) "and the souls that they had made in Haran": for he would feed them and give them drink and draw them near to the service of YHVH. And therefore he became a chariot for Chesed; and this is the attribute of Chesed of which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, "and the right hand draws near." And likewise Isaac became a chariot for Gevurah, because he held on to the attribute of judgment as his portion, and stretched out his neck on the altar, and made known to all who come into the world that the world has a Judge and a God, and there is judgment and there is a judge; and so they expounded in the Zohar. And likewise he would rescue the oppressed from the hand of his oppressor, restore the stolen thing from the hand of the robber, "and pluck the prey out of his teeth" (Job 29:17); and all matters like these are those that depend on the attribute of Gevurah. And this is the first condition. He further needs the second condition: that his soul be emanated from that attribute; for through this that attribute will bestow effluence upon him and do its action through him, until the soul becomes a source for the effluence that is bestowed from it. And therefore the soul of Abraham had to be from Chesed, and the soul of Isaac from Gevurah, and likewise after this manner for the other righteous ones. And behold, the soul of Joseph was from Yesod; and when he gained merit and perfected his soul through that great deed, that he did not defile the sign of the holy covenant and overcame his inclination, he became a chariot for the Righteous One; and from there he fed the world in the days of the famine, and likewise from there he sustained all his father's house all the days of his being. For it is the attribute that gives food for the sustenance of Israel. And likewise David, king, peace be upon him, merited kingship for himself and for his seed after him by the merit of his having set this attribute right and adorned it, in contending with her enemies round about. And this is why he would rise at midnight, and likewise never slept except as the sleep of a horse, and matters like these, of the adornments of the bride, as is known. And when we investigate the manifestations of the chariot, we find them to be three aspects. The first aspect is the aspect of David: that he adorned the bride in the aspect of Malkhut. The second aspect is the aspect of Joseph, that is, the aspect of Yesod, which is the passage of the effluence from all the sefirot to Malkhut. The third aspect is the aspect of the Patriarchs and of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, though one was raised above his fellows, as we shall explain with the help of Heaven.

And behold, we do not deny that the whole matter of the chariots is the tikkunim of the Shekhinah, that is, of Malkhut. And to this matter there are five aspects. The first is the aspect of Malkhut with respect to her adornments: that is, to bestow effluence from the upper attributes; and not the effluence of food, nor the effluence of the world's needs, but to set the bride right, so that she be adorned with her adornments, as explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance.
And behold, these adornments are tikkunim toward the coupling, not the coupling itself.

And behold, from this matter, and from the effluence that is bestowed for this tikkun, there is not yet so much benefit, until the coupling comes about; for then she receives the effluence to feed and sustain the upper ones and the lower ones. And this is the reason that David was in poverty, as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 63), on the verse "Hearken, O Laish" (Isa. 10:30): because all his matters were tikkunim, so that she would be adorned. And in the days of Solomon there was the coupling, and the moon was in her fullness; and so they explained in the Zohar on the Song of Songs and in other places. And this is the aspect of David. And this is the reason that "the builders," who are the Patriarchs, "rejected" [her] (Ps. 118:22) in this matter: because they saw that her complete coupling was far from being realized, until Israel should be on their land, quiet and at ease, and YHVH should give them rest round about, with the abolition of the husks and the enemies. And because of the remoteness of the matter they set right another aspect, as we shall explain. The second aspect is the aspect of Joseph, and it is the tikkun of Yesod; and it is certainly an honored level, raised above the preceding one, and it is through this matter. But this is not the coupling itself; rather it is a tikkun toward the coupling. For when the Righteous One is set right, he bestows effluence into Malkhut from his own aspect; and he is also prepared for more than the bestowal, for this is his tikkun toward the coupling, which is an aspect more choice than the bestowal of effluence. And in him both are found: effluence that he bestows, and further that he is set right for the coupling, for he is the holy organ, as is known. And just as the organ is needed for the union of a man and his wife, so Yesod is needed for the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, as explained in the preceding gates. The third aspect is the aspect of Abraham and Isaac, and it is an honored aspect (though it is not raised above the aspect of Joseph). And the reason is that it is an aspect toward the bestowal of effluence itself into Malkhut. For it is known that her nourishment is from the right and from the left: for it is the thread of Chesed that is drawn over her by day, and likewise from Gevurah much effluence and food is bestowed upon her. And there is a further need for them, for they are a preparation for the coupling, for the matter of the embrace, as explained in Gate 8, chapter 21, with the help of Heaven. And nevertheless they are not equal to the eminence of Yesod, because the eminence of Yesod is the more glorious, for it is the principal thing for the coupling, as we explained. The fourth aspect is the aspect of Jacob, who is the husband of the Lady [ba'alah de-Matronita]: that is, besides bestowing effluence into the Shekhinah, he further bestows into her the effluence of the coupling; that is, through him Tiferet is aroused to couple literally. And it is an aspect more glorious than the aspect of Yesod: for Yesod is the vessel for the coupling, as the organ is to the male; and there is no doubt that the principal thing is the body, which is Tiferet, which is the principal thing for the coupling, and Yesod is a passage and a channel for the matter that is bestowed. And this was the level of Jacob our father, that he was a chariot for Tiferet in these two ways: both in the bestowal of effluence, in the manner of the other attributes, and in the arousal of the coupling itself, which is an aspect all the more glorious, as is explained in the aforementioned gate, with the help of Heaven. The fifth aspect is the aspect of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him; and he is at the level of Jacob in effluence and in coupling, and beyond him, in that he is from the side of the concealed aspect that is in Tiferet, which is the secret of Da'at, and it is a subtle manifestation, as is explained in Gate 1, chapter 2, with the help of Heaven. And there we spoke at length of his eminence, so that the aspect of Malkhut, his mate, is only in the aspect of the rib, which is the Yod, as explained in the Gate of Manifestations; and she is the one who is called "the bride of Moses," certainly a king's daughter, as explained in the Tikkunim many times. Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, further added an eminence above all eminences: that through his aspect, the aspect of Da'at, there comes about the union of Chokhmah and Binah, as explained in the aforementioned gate. And through knowing these aspects many and many concealed sayings will be explained, over which the eyes of the inquirers in the Zohar have been closed. And now that we have explained the matter of these aspects, we shall further explain in what way this matter is in the upper sefirot, and what is meant by the matter of the chariot. And the matter is that it was already explained in Gate 8, chapter 19, that the matter of the arousal is through the deeds of the righteous. And the Shekhinah receives that spirituality and the matter that comes into being through the Torah or the commandment; and she receives it through a light bestowed from above according to the matter of the commandment: if the commandment is from Chesed, she receives from Chesed; and likewise from Gevurah; and likewise for the other levels. And likewise we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapters 3 and 4, that the Shekhinah pursues the righteous one, to be united with him, so that through him she may receive that power and that light.

And behold, since the matter is so, the soul of the righteous one, which performs the commandments, is found to become a chariot and a throne for the Shekhinah; and the Shekhinah is clothed and concealed within that soul. And it is a throne and a source for all the blessings, and from it the whole world is fed, and it is the source for them. And this is what was said to Abraham (Gen. 12:2), "and be a blessing" [berakhah], meaning: you shall be a pool [berekhah] for the effluence that is bestowed from above. And when the righteous one in this world occupies himself with matters of effluence from the side of Chesed, his level will be at the level of the chariot for Chesed, like Abraham our father, when the Shekhinah was without a palace and was clothed in the bird's nest, until he set right a palace for her in his holy soul. And Isaac set right a palace for her from the side of Gevurah through his deeds, to bestow on her from there; and not literal judgment, God forbid, for many kinds of effluence are bestowed from Gevurah for the benefit of the world, to feed it, etc., as was explained in Gate 8, chapter 16, and as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, with the help of the Name. And Jacob by his Torah merited to bestow into her, and further merited literally to couple with her; and he is called the husband of the Shekhinah in most of the words of Rashbi, of blessed memory. And this is the reason the mishnah said (Peah 1:1), "These are the things," etc., "and the study of Torah [talmud Torah, abbreviated ת"ת, as is Tiferet] is equal to them all": because it brings about the coupling and the union. And therefore one whose Torah is his craft is exempt from prayer. And Joseph the righteous merited that through his deeds his soul became a palace for her, so that through it Yesod might bestow into her the power to feed and sustain the whole world. And he added to this further that he assists the coupling, for Jacob needs him; and this is (Gen. 37:2), "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph," as explained in the Zohar; and likewise (Exod. 13:19), "And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him," as explained there. And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, merited that his soul became a palace for her, so that through him he might bestow abundant effluence into her, as in the matter of (Exod. 16:4) "Behold, I will rain [bread from heaven]," and the other matters of the miracles.

And further he added that he united her with the supernal Da'at, that is, in the secret of her concealed aspect. And David's soul became a palace for her, to adorn her and to set her right; and through praises and thanksgivings and his good deeds her adornments were bestowed from above (see Zohar Terumah, fol. 145). And behold, it is found that the light bestowed on the Shekhinah bestows on the righteous one; and that light, which shines in the Shekhinah from the power of that sefirah, is concealed in the soul of that righteous one, who is a palace for the Shekhinah; so it is found that he is a palace for the supernal light that is revealed in the Shekhinah. And this is their saying, of blessed memory, "Abraham is a chariot for Chesed," meaning for the light of Chesed that is revealed in the Shekhinah. For the righteous one is never a chariot except for the Shekhinah; and nevertheless it is attributed to him that he is a chariot for the upper attribute, for the reason that we said. And likewise Isaac was a chariot for the light of Gevurah that is revealed in Malkhut; and likewise Jacob for the light that is revealed from Tiferet to Malkhut; and likewise Joseph for the light of Yesod that is revealed in Malkhut; and likewise Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, for the light that is revealed from Da'at in Malkhut; and likewise David for the light of the adornments that is revealed in Malkhut. And by this will be understood many sayings of the Zohar that show that the righteous are never a chariot except for the Shekhinah, as (Gen. 17:22) "And God went up from Abraham": for there our Sages, of blessed memory, proved that the Shekhinah was revealed in him. And by the premise of this chapter, I know that many gates of light will open to the inquirer in the books of the Zohar on these matters; and they need to be fixed in the heart of the inquirers. And we have shortened them with the utmost brevity, so that the inquirer may take them in; "let the wise man hear and increase in learning" (Prov. 1:5):

What is intended in this chapter is to explain a wondrous matter found in Sefer ha-Bahir, where it says that Abraham did not wish to take as his portion anything but Chesed, and likewise Isaac Gevurah, and likewise Jacob Tiferet; and they rejected Malkhut, God forbid. And at first sight these appear to be astonishing words that need explanation. And these are its words: "For Rabbi Meir said: What is it that is written, 'And God said, Let there be light, and there was light' (Gen. 1:3), and it did not say 'and it was so'? This teaches that that light was very great, and no creature could gaze upon it. The Holy One, blessed be He, stored it away for the righteous in the time to come. And it is the measure of all merchandise [sechorah] in the world, and it is the power of a precious stone that is called socheret and dar (Esther 1:6). And on what account is it the measure of dar? Rather, this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, took from its radiance one out of two thousand, and built from it a precious stone, comely and adorned, and included in it all the commandments. Abraham came and asked for his power, that it be given to him; and they gave him this precious stone, and he did not want it. He gained merit and took his attribute, Chesed, as it is said (Micah 7:20), 'loving-kindness [chesed] to Abraham.' Isaac came and asked for his power, and they gave him this attribute, and he did not want it. He gained merit and took the attribute of Gevurah, that is, Fear [Pachad], as it is said (Gen. 31:53), 'And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.' Jacob came and wanted it, and they did not give it to him. They said to him: Since Abraham is above and Isaac below, you shall be in the middle and take (another version: include) all three. And what is 'the middle'? That is peace. But it is written (Micah 7:20), 'You will give truth to Jacob'! Truth and peace are one, as it is said (Esther 9:30), 'words of peace and truth,' [and] 'Is it not so, if peace and truth shall be in my days?' (2 Kings 20:19). And this is what is written (Isa. 58:14), 'and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father': that is, a complete heritage, which has Chesed and Fear and truth and peace. And therefore it said (Ps. 118:22), 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner': the stone that Abraham and Isaac, who built the world, rejected, has now become the head of the corner. And why did they reject it? Is it not said (Gen. 26:5), 'Because Abraham obeyed My voice and kept My charge, My commandments,' etc.? What is 'My charge'? Thus said the attribute of Chesed: All the days that Abraham was in the land, I did not need to do my work, for Abraham stood there in my place. 'And kept My charge': and this is my work, that I acquit the whole world, and even if they have incurred guilt I acquit them.

"And further, I bring them back and bring it into their hearts to do the will of their Father in heaven. All this Abraham did; and it is written (Gen. 21:33), 'And he planted a tamarisk in Beersheba, and called there on the name of YHVH, the everlasting God.' He set out his bread and his water for all who came into the world, and acquitted them, and spoke to their hearts: Whom are you serving? Serve YHVH, the God of heaven and earth. And he would expound to them until they repented. And from where do we know that he acquitted even the guilty? For it is said (Gen. 18:17–18), 'And YHVH said, Shall I keep covered from Abraham,' etc., 'seeing that Abraham shall surely become,' etc. Rather: I shall give him merit, for I know that he will ask for compassion for them, and he will gain merit. And can one say that the Holy One, blessed be He, did not know that (they could not be saved)? Rather, it is said to give him merit. From here they said: One who comes to purify himself is helped; one who comes to defile himself, it is opened for him. What is 'opened'? Those that are always open. 'My commandments, My statutes and My teachings': he said, Since I do not delight in it, I shall keep its commandments. And what is 'My teachings'? Rather, even the rulings and the dialectics that are taught above, he knew them, and argued them through, and fulfilled them. And what is (Gen. 49:24), 'from there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel'? From there the stone of Israel is fed. And what is 'from there'? You must say: that is the supernal Righteousness. And what is that? That is the great light that is treasured, and that is socheret. And the precious stone that He built (another version: that dwells [she-darah]) beneath it is called dar." Thus far its words.
And now we shall enter into the explanation of this saying from its beginning to its end; and along the way everything will be explained:

First, he found difficult the reason for the doubling of the verse, in saying "and there was light," and not saying "and it was so," as its way is in the other matters. And to this he answered that there were two beings [havayot]. First, the being of the great light, which the world is not worthy to use; and when He saw in His wisdom that the children of the world would have no benefit from it, as we shall explain, there was need of the second being, the second light. And this is "and there was light," whose explanation is the being of the second light. This is the sum of the verse as to the doubling. And now we shall return to explain his language in detail. These two lights: the first light is the first Chokhmah, and the second light is the last Chokhmah. And it is fitting to know: was His knowledge, may He be blessed, too short, God forbid, in the matter of the light, whether the world could gaze upon it or not, so that He needed to store away the one because of the other? A wonder! And let Him create the second and not the first! And this question was already resolved in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 4. And there we said that before all the beings, it arose in His primordial will that the beings should come about through Chokhmah; and because of the slightness of the something-ness in it, for it is very close to Nothing, so that "being" cannot properly be said of it at all, therefore there was need of the beings of the sefirot (the emanation of Binah), as we explained there. And there we explained that our saying "it arose in His will," etc., and likewise "He was incising," etc., is all a parable and a likeness of the decree of His wisdom in the matter of the order of the Emanation. And now our question, that there should be the second light and not the first, is not right. For the first light is the Chokhmah that is at the head, and the second light is the Chokhmah that is at the end. And if we ask: let Him emanate Malkhut and not Chokhmah, we answer that if Malkhut had been the second level, in the place of Chokhmah, then Malkhut would have been the level of Chokhmah, a second effect; and in the end the world could not bear it, and no creature could gaze upon it; that is, the created ones could not draw effluence from it because of its great subtlety and its nearness to its source. Therefore things had of necessity to be level after level: first Nothing [Ayin], and afterward Something [Yesh], and likewise from level to level, from inscription to engraving, and from engraving to hewing, and from hewing to making, as we spoke at length in the preceding gates. For while things are close to their source they are at the utmost subtlety; and as they go out from before Him, they come down wondrously by measured measures, from cause to effect, from point to point, from the upper point to the last point. And now we shall return to the language of the saying. He said: "This teaches that that light was very great." It is already known that Chokhmah is above Gedulah [Greatness], and it emanates Gedulah. Therefore he called it "great," in the secret of Gedulah; and he said "very," to show that it is above it, beyond what is beyond. "And no creature could," etc. It was already explained that the reason for the Emanation is to make known His eminence and His exaltedness to what is other than He; for before the Emanation the greatness of the necessarily existent One was not known to any other, since there was none besides Him. And the Emanation was so that creatures could know His power and His exaltedness, as we explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation; and so that existence would cascade down and go out from before Him and descend by way of the levels of the ladder whose head reaches to the God of gods and whose end is set on the earth. And this is what he meant in saying "no creature could gaze upon it": because of the great concealment of Chokhmah, the created ones have no apprehension of the Emanator through it. And for this he used the language of gazing, which shows much contemplation and great understanding. It is further possible to explain, as we explained above, that the created ones could not draw its effluence, because of its subtlety; and that is the gazing, which is the enjoyment of its radiance. "The Holy One, blessed be He, stored it away for the righteous in the time to come." It is already known that the world to come is Binah; and it is called "the world to come" because it is ever coming, for it is a river that never ceases. And "the world to come" and "the time to come" are all one, near enough, as is well known. And there is a difference between them, although both of them are in Binah: for Binah is called "the world to come" in her lower aspect, which bestows, as we explained, for it is "a river that flows and goes out and whose waters never cease for ever"; but "the time to come" is an upper aspect, which has not yet come but is yet to come, that is, the concealment of Binah, which is a palace in which Chokhmah is laid away and stored away. And it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (in the Tosefta, fol. 68b), and these are its words in brief: "That inscription [reshimu] needed to cover itself, and it made for itself a palace to be concealed in. That palace it brought forth from itself, and stretched it with a great and vast stretching to all sides. It set it up in garments of glory, opened for it fifty gates, within within. That inscription was concealed and stored away; once it was stored away in it and entered within it, it was filled with light." Thus far its words.

And behold, from this saying it appears explicitly that Chokhmah, which is the aforementioned inscription, called Something [Yesh], is stored away and laid away in Binah, which is the palace in which are the fifty gates, etc. And by this is explained what he said, "He stored it away for the righteous": that is, Tiferet and the Righteous One; for Tiferet too is called righteous, as it is said (Ps. 11:7), "For YHVH is righteous." For they draw light and effluence from Chokhmah by means of Binah, that is, "the time to come," as we explained. And he did not say "for the world to come," because Chokhmah is concealed in Binah only in her upper aspect, which has not yet been revealed. "And it is the measure of all merchandise [sechorah] in the world." The explanation: Chokhmah is the measure by which all the beings and all the encompassings come into being; that is, sechorah from the word sechor, the Targum of saviv [around]. And they said "in the world" because Binah is called "world," and the beings that are formed within Binah are by the power of Chokhmah, which limits them and gives them a measure without measure, as we explained. "And it is the power of a precious stone that is called socheret and dar": for Chokhmah [chokhmah] is ko'ach mah [the power of What], whose explanation is that the aspect of Chokhmah that is united with Binah is called ko'ach mah, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And it is also a precious stone, that is, the Yod, which is a point within the palace. "That is called socheret": the explanation is the language of going round and encompassing, for it encompasses all the sefirot and gives power and light in them. And it is possible that the explanation of "precious" [yekarah] is the language of shining, as in "and the moon walking in brightness" [yakar] (Job 31:26). "And on what account is it the measure of dar?" Because in the verse both are mentioned together, when it says (Esther 1:6) "and dar and socheret." And because from the explanation of dar the matter of "and there was light" will be explained, he therefore asked, "what is dar?" "Rather, this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, took from its radiance one out of two thousand." The explanation: dar is the manifestation of Malkhut that is taken from Chokhmah, which is the matter of the rib, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations, chapters 3 and 4, with the help of the Name. And this is what he said, that the Holy One, blessed be He, took "from its radiance," meaning from the radiance of the socheret, which is Chokhmah, that is, the first light. And the rib is "one out of two thousand" of its radiance: they are the two thousand years by which the Torah preceded the world, that is, the ten sefirot that are in Chokhmah and the ten that are in Binah; and each ten of them comes to a thousand, for they are ten times ten, which are a hundred, and ten times a hundred are a thousand; that is, ten included of ten, and ten of ten, and they are a thousand. And likewise the thousand that is in Binah: they are two thousand. And one out of these two thousand is Malkhut, which completes the two thousand. And they called them "two thousand" to show that her emanation, and the emanation of the other emanated ones, had not yet come about; for then Chokhmah and Binah are related to the name "two thousand," as they said, of blessed memory: "the Torah preceded the world by two thousand years." "And built from it a precious stone, comely and adorned." The matter of "and YHVH God built the rib" (Gen. 2:22) was already explained in the aforementioned gate, that is, the manifestation of the Yod that is in Malkhut. And he said that the rib is a precious stone, the manifestation of the Yod, a sapphire stone, as explained in the Tikkunim, second to Chokhmah. And it is comely and adorned in the secret of the manifestation of the building of her Heh; and that is "and there was light," which is the being of Malkhut from Chokhmah, which is the first light, as we explained. And it is called "precious" [yekarah] from the language of shining, as we explained above. And the explanation of "comely" [na'ah] is from the side of the effluence of Tiferet, who is her husband, who is Vav. And this is na'ah [נאה]: Nun is Malkhut; Heh-Alef comes to six, which is Tiferet; and since his effluence is bestowed into her to adorn her, he therefore is made [the number six] from Vav [and from] Heh-Alef. And the explanation of "adorned" is the adornments of the bride, which is the manifestation of Heh, which are her adornments, as in the matter of the three colors of the rainbow, which are a red line, a green line and a white line, which are Gedulah, Gevurah and Tiferet; and that is Heh, three Vavs, as explained in the Gate of Manifestations. "And included in it all the commandments": the explanation is that in Malkhut are included all the positive commandments and the negative commandments: the positive commandments from the right side, Chesed; the negative commandments from the left side, Gevurah; and she is included of right and left. And the reason that she is included of all the commandments is that the commandments depend on the ten sefirot, and she is included of ten sefirot; and therefore she is included of all the branches of the sefirot, which are the commandments.

And behold, the branches of the sefirot are two hundred and forty-eight from the side of Gedulah, and three hundred and sixty-five from the side of Gevurah; and so it is found that she is included in all the branches of the sefirot, from the right and from the left. And he needed to say this matter for the matter of the chariots, which we shall explain:

"Abraham came and asked," etc. The matter is this: although a person's soul may be emanated from one of the attributes, it is nevertheless possible that through his deeds he may be made a chariot for another attribute. For every soul is included of ten; and when a person exerts himself in Chesed he will be a chariot for the attribute of Chesed, even if his soul is emanated from another attribute, because he makes the side of Chesed prevail over his soul, until the principal shining of it is in Chesed. And likewise for the other sefirot; and we shall speak at length on this matter in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 1, with the help of the Name. And therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, wished that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, should be a chariot for the attribute of Malkhut, that he should make the portion of Malkhut prevail in himself; all the more so with Malkhut, which is included of all the sefirot, as we explained, and in particular from the side of Chesed, as we explained. And the reason that the Holy One, blessed be He, wanted the tikkun of this attribute more than all the other attributes is that it is the attribute that needs tikkun more than the other attributes, for the reason that it is the last attribute, and "her feet go down to death" (Prov. 5:5), and she needs tikkun, to set right her diminishment. And for this it was said to Abraham our father, peace be upon him (Gen. 12:1), "Go forth from your land and from your birthplace," etc.: the intent is that he should remove himself from the husks and from the arrays of the heavens, as they said, of blessed memory, "Go out from your astrology," etc. And this is "to the land that I will show you," that is, Malkhut; and the intent is that he should exert himself to set her right. And he took hold of Chesed as his attribute, in the deeds of piety, as [the saying] concludes. And this is "and he did not want it": the explanation, he did not want Malkhut, and he did fitting deeds to merit Chesed. And this is what he said, "he gained merit and took his attribute." And he said "his attribute" for the reason that the principal sparkling of his soul was from Chesed; and therefore he inclined to the principal [root] of his soul. And likewise when it was said to him, "to the land that I will show you," it is written (Gen. 12:9), "And Abraham journeyed, going on still toward the south": to the side of the south, to the side of the right, that is, Chesed. Behold, he pushed it away with both hands, and wished to cleave to his own attribute, which is Chesed:

"Isaac came," etc. All the matters of Isaac are from the side of Malkhut. And so it is said (Gen. 21:1), "And YHVH remembered [pakad] Sarah," and the language of remembering [pekidah] is from the side of Malkhut. And likewise it is said to him (Gen. 26:3), "Sojourn in this land"; and although it was said to him after the binding, nevertheless it is a proof that the Holy One, blessed be He, wished him to be a chariot for Malkhut. And he did not want it, but took the attribute of Fear. And he was precise in saying "and took the attribute of Gevurah," and did not say "his attribute," as he said of Abraham; because it was not truly his attribute, as with Abraham, who was by his nature a man of Chesed. But Isaac's attribute by nature was none other than Malkhut. For so they explained in the Zohar, that before the binding his attribute was Malkhut; and for this reason he made himself liable to death, for he was from the side of the Female, as is explained in the Zohar, for it is written (Gen. 18:14), "and Sarah shall have a son." And therefore he did not say of Isaac "and asked that it be given to him," as he said of Abraham, but "and asked for his power," that is, that he asked for another attribute besides this one, and pushed this one away. "And he gained merit and took the attribute of Gevurah," although it was not his attribute. And with this premise a second saying of Sefer ha-Bahir on this matter will be understood, and these are its words: "And by the merit of Abraham, who merited the attribute of Chesed, Isaac merited the attribute of Fear." And at first sight this is the reverse of the saying before us; for here he said that first they were giving him Malkhut, until he did not want it, etc. But it is as we explained: that he pushed away Malkhut, though it was his attribute, and he merited only Fear specifically and nothing else; but from the side of Abraham, who was in Chesed. And it is known that "the water conceived and bore darkness"; and therefore, since Isaac was the son of Abraham, Fear, the son of Chesed, was given to him. And he merited Fear through his binding, that he was bound on top of the altar. And the matter is that the altar is Malkhut, and the top of the altar is Yesod, and the wood that is on top of the altar is Tiferet, Netzach and Hod; and he was bound on top of the altar, "on top of the wood" (Gen. 22:9). Thus Isaac merited Fear through the binding. And we could further explain that the altar is Malkhut, and the top of the altar is Tiferet, and this top is "on top of the wood," for the wood is Netzach, Hod and Yesod, which are three Vavs, three pieces of wood (see Pelach ha-Rimmon):

"Jacob came." Behold, Jacob wished to cleave to Malkhut in all his matters. First, that "he went out from Beersheba" (Gen. 28:10), which is Binah, "and went toward Haran," which is Malkhut; and so it is explained in the Zohar. And further, that there "he lighted upon the place" (Gen. 28:11), which is the Shekhinah, and there he set up a pillar; and likewise he said (Gen. 28:22), "And this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be God's house." All his matter was in Malkhut, to cleave to her. And they did not give her to him, but [ruled] that he should be a chariot for Tiferet. And this was said to him in the matter of his marriage to Leah, who is Binah.

And behold, his intent was for Rachel, the mainstay of the house, and he deceived him with Leah; for it was from YHVH, since he is "the man in between," a male between two females. And likewise it is said to him (Gen. 32:29), "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel"; and Jacob is in Malkhut and Israel in Tiferet, as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. All this is to show him that he would be a chariot for Tiferet. And the reason is that Abraham and Isaac were two opposites, this one Chesed and that one judgment, this one water and that one fire; and peace between them was needed for the tikkun of the world. And this is what he said: "Since Abraham is above and Isaac below (etc.), you shall be in the middle" between them. And such is the way of Tiferet, which is in the middle between Chesed and Fear: this one above and that one below, and Tiferet in the middle. And this is the Vav in the middle of two Yods, like the shape of Alef, as explained in the Gate of Names, chapter 6. "And take all three": the explanation is that Tiferet, on the side of the arbitration, has the power of Gedulah from the side of the right, and Gevurah from the side of the left, and Tiferet in the middle includes all these aspects in the self of Tiferet, as explained in the preceding gates. "And what is 'the middle'? Peace," etc. It was difficult for him, for Tiferet is a middle aspect by itself, which is the line of compassion, and does not include all three. To this he said, "And what is 'the middle'? Peace," etc.: the explanation, the completing side, which unites the extremes, as explained in the Gate of Arbiters. "But it is written, 'You will give truth to Jacob'!" If so, it would follow that Jacob is not a chariot for Tiferet in the manifestation of peace, but in the manifestation of truth, which is an aspect by itself, a middle aspect alone. To this he answered: "Truth and peace are one": the explanation, the aspect that includes three aspects is the one called peace, and it is the one called truth. And he proved that the two titles are one by saying "words of peace and truth," and likewise "Is it not so, if peace and truth," etc. And nevertheless there is a difference between peace and truth: for truth [emet] is the Alef, in the secret of a Yod from here upward, Chesed, and a Yod from here downward, Gevurah, and a Vav in the middle, Tiferet, that is, the aspect of peace; and the Mem and Tav that remain are Malkhut, as will be explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, with the help of Heaven. And the root of the word emet is Tiferet; and therefore "truth and peace are one," for each one of them includes three aspects. "For it is written, 'and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father,' that is, a heritage," etc. We already explained in the Gate of Arbiters that only Tiferet is truly called peace, because it is the totality of all the extremes; and therefore it is called a complete heritage, which is not so with the two extremes. And this is what he said: "that is, Chesed and Fear and peace and truth," which are three aspects, which are Chesed, judgment and compassion, which is a complete, whole heritage; and "Jacob was a whole man" (Gen. 25:27), "a perfect man" (Targum Onkelos there), as is explained at length in the aforementioned gate. "And therefore it said, 'The stone that the builders rejected'": the explanation, David, whose attribute was Malkhut, said that the stone, which is Malkhut, "that the builders rejected," meaning all those who became a chariot for the Emanation and rejected her because she is last of the whole Emanation, she "has become the head of the corner"; for sometimes she is called "a woman of valor, the diadem of her husband" (Prov. 12:4), that is, that she rises above until she is a diadem over Tiferet; and then she is called "the crown of the Torah scroll," as explained in the preceding gates. "And why did they reject it?" The explanation: why do you say that they rejected it? It is not so, for the verse says, "and kept My charge," that is, Malkhut, who is called "keeping" [shimmur]; "My commandments," which are included in Malkhut, as he said above, "and included in it all the commandments." And accordingly it is found that he did not reject her; on the contrary, he perfected her and fulfilled her commandments and set her right. "What is 'My charge'?" The explanation: do not think that these words are the words of Malkhut, saying that Abraham kept the charge of Malkhut; they are only the words of Chesed, which is his attribute. And the intent of his saying "My charge" is Malkhut, who receives the light of Chesed by means of the soul of Abraham, as we explained in chapter 3. And the intent is that this verse showed that Abraham our father was a chariot for Chesed. "All the days that Abraham was in the land," etc. We have already explained in the preceding gates that the matter of the three aspects in which each and every sefirah is distinguished is this: the first aspect is what it receives from the attribute above it, and it is more glorious and subtler than the other aspects of the attribute, for the higher it rises, the subtler and more glorious it is. The second aspect is with respect to its own self, and it is intermediate between the first and the third. And the third is with respect to what it bestows below, and it is the most revealed of the two preceding ones. And likewise these three aspects are in Chesed: three different actions of compassion, with respect to the three aspects.

And behold, with respect to the first aspect, from below upward, he said, "and this is my work, that I acquit the world," and that is compassion. And afterward, corresponding to the second aspect, which is more compassion, he said, "and even if they have incurred guilt I acquit them": and the intent is that even though they are guilty and not fit for compassion, through the strength of the compassion that prevails in this aspect, I have compassion on them. And with respect to the third aspect, which is the one that draws near to Binah in its receiving from her, he said, "and further, I bring them back and bring it into their hearts," etc. And it is already known that repentance is always from the side of the aspect of Binah with Chesed; for Binah is called Repentance [Teshuvah], and it is written, "Your right hand is stretched out to receive those who return." "And bring them to do the will of their Owner": the explanation, Binah, who is the Owner [konah] of the souls and their source, for she emanates them, as is known. And to these three aspects exactly Abraham directed his deeds. And this is "he set out his bread and his water": behold, the first aspect, from below upward. "And he would expound to them until they repented": behold, the third aspect, which is repentance. "And from where do we know that he acquitted even the guilty?": this is with respect to the middle aspect; and he took it last, though it is the middle one, because for the deeds of human beings the hardest thing is to acquit one who has no merit, and this is almost not in a person's hand, so much so that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, did not succeed in saving the people of Sodom. And this is why the language of the saying was precise in saying "And can one say that He did not know," etc.: for it was already within His knowledge, may He be blessed, that a person has no ability to acquit one who has no merit. And "Shall I keep covered," etc., was said only because Abraham was exerting himself in the perfection of Chesed, and was fulfilling the two aspects in substance; [so] the Holy One, blessed be He, wished that he should exert himself in the third, so that his thought would be joined to deed, and he would be perfected in Chesed in substance. "One who comes to purify himself," etc., "one who comes to defile himself, it is opened for him. What is 'opened'?": the explanation, why did he not say "he is helped," as he said "one who comes to purify himself is helped"? Rather the reason is that when a person comes to purify himself, they open openings for him more than is due; as in the matter of (Gen. 25:21) "and YHVH let Himself be entreated [vaye'ater] by him": He dug [vayachtor] for him, for He opened an opening for him (see Zohar Toledot, fol. 137). And likewise with Manasseh, for whom the Holy One, blessed be He, dug an opening from beneath the Throne of Glory (in Sanhedrin, fol. 103). And this is "he is helped." But when he comes to defile himself, they do not open for him; rather the openings open by themselves, through which he may go out if he wishes. And this is "it is opened for him": that is, he has open openings through which he may go out. "My commandments, My statutes and My teachings": he comes also to resolve what was difficult for him at the outset, for the commandments are in Malkhut, so it appears that he perfected Malkhut. And now he resolved that the intent is not that he perfected her and cleaved to her, to be truly a chariot for her; rather the intent is that although he did not delight in her, he nevertheless kept her commandments, to bestow into her from his attribute; for this is what is meant by the matter of the chariot, as we explained in chapter 2. "What is 'My teachings'? Even the rulings and the dialectics," etc.: the explanation, even the eruv tavshilin. "And what is 'from there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel,'" etc.: it was difficult for him, for from there it appears that "from the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob" (Gen. 49:24) means Yesod, as is known, and "from there is the shepherd" is Malkhut, and "the stone of Israel" means [what is] fed from Yesod, as its Targum has it: "who feeds fathers and sons." And accordingly it would be found that Jacob is a chariot for Malkhut; and his words contradict each other, for he said that he is a chariot for Tiferet. To this he said that "from there" means the supernal Righteousness, that is, Binah, which is the palace in which the first light is stored away for the time to come, as we explained. "And that is socheret," etc.: the explanation, we have already explained that the first light is called socheret only when it is stored away in Binah, for then from it is "all merchandise in the world," as we explained. And this is what he meant in saying "and that is socheret." And the supernal Righteousness is only in Binah; for there is an upper Righteousness and a lower Righteousness: the upper in Binah and the lower in Malkhut. And now the explanation of "from there is the shepherd" will be: from the manifestation of Chokhmah that is concealed in Binah, from there Tiferet is fed, together with the twelve boundaries, for which Jacob and his twelve sons were a chariot. And now the words of the Targum, in explaining "fathers and sons," are right. "And the precious stone that He built beneath it is called dar": and he returned to the first matter, for his whole purpose came only to explain the word dar and the word socheret. Thus far our poor intellect has reached in the explanation of this saying, with the help of the One who graciously gives man knowledge. And the principle that emerges from the words of the saying is that through the deeds of human beings a person is made a chariot for one of the sefirot. And likewise of Enoch-Metatron they said that he merited that level for the reason that he was a stitcher of shoes, and with every single hole that he pierced with the awl he would bless for the need on High, etc.; for he would unite Malkhut, who is called "shoe," with Tiferet through all the channels that he has; and to this he hinted with the holes that he mentioned. And by this explanation it would have been fitting that he be a chariot for Malkhut. However, we have seen one who explained that Sandalfon is called "sandal" and Metatron "shoe," and he would join and bestow upon Metatron, and from there he was a cause that it be bestowed on the Shekhinah; and therefore he merited to be a chariot for Metatron, measure for measure. And this is what he said: he was a stitcher of shoes, and with every single hole he would bless, for he would unite Metatron with the attribute and afterward bestow on Malkhut.

And behold, this is a sixth aspect of the chariot, beside the five aspects mentioned above in chapter 3. And on the matter of Enoch and Metatron we shall lengthen the explanation in the Gate of Palaces, with the help of Heaven; and there the matter of Elijah will be explained, and likewise the matter of the angels, at long length, with the help of the Name, may He be blessed.
And behold, this chapter is completed, and this gate is concluded, with the help of Heaven. Thus far.
The Gate of the Glossary of Titles is the Twenty-Third Gate.

What is intended in this Gate is to explain all the titles whose explanation is found in the Zohar. And many commentators who preceded us in this work wrote the titles by way of the sefirot, setting down for each and every sefirah the titles that relate to it. But we, in our own way, [proceed otherwise]: because sometimes it happens that when the inquirer seeks one of the titles, his search is hard for him, because its place is hidden from him. Besides this, sometimes one title is related to several sefirot for known reasons; and sometimes its root is in one attribute, and it is related to another for a known reason, and the inquirer pays no attention to the matter, but only to the sefirah to which it is attributed. Therefore we thought fit to write the titles as entries in the order of the letters, and in each to explain the whole matter and the sefirah that is related to it; and by this the inquirer's search will be made easy for him:
Chapter One:

Father [אב, av]. Some explained it as Keter, for it is the father of compassion, and likewise from it Tiferet draws [sho'ev] compassion. And some explained it as Chokhmah, which is so called for the reason that it is the father and the source of all the beings, in the way that we explained in the preceding gate, in the first chapter; and this name shows that it bestows, like the father who gives to the sons. And it is near to say that it is in both of them together, and the letters show this, for they are Alef, Keter, and Bet, Chokhmah; and the reason is that the beings are bestowed from Chokhmah, from the source concealed in it, which is Keter, as is known:

Father of Faith [אב האמונה, av ha-emunah]. Some explained it as Keter, because it is father to Malkhut. And this is far-fetched: for as its relation is with Malkhut, so is its relation with the rest of the Emanation. And it is possible to say, with a strained reading, that sometimes Malkhut rises up to Keter, as is explained in the Gate of Manifestations, and then, when they rise there, she draws nourishment from Keter and bestows on everything; and it is possible that [then] Keter is called "Father of Faith," to hint at the Faith that is there. However, two explanations are attributed to "Faith": either Binah or Malkhut, as we shall explain further, with the help of the Name. And on both of them it would mean that Chokhmah is father to Malkhut, in the secret of "YHVH by wisdom [be-chokhmah] founded the earth" (Prov. 3:19), as we explained in the aforementioned gate; and likewise it is father to Binah, for she was emanated from it. And on all the explanations, Keter or Chokhmah is called "Father of Faith" only in the secret of the aspect of its bestowal on the Faiths:

The Compassionate Father [אב הרחמן, av ha-rachaman]: Tiferet is so called, for he is father to the souls; and he is called "Compassionate" by the power of (Keter) that bestows upon him in compassion, and in this aspect he is called "Compassionate." It follows accordingly that when he has compassion on the souls, in the secret of the compassion of Keter, he is called "the Compassionate Father." And this name has also been related to Keter, in the view of some of the commentators. And some explained it as Chokhmah; and the main thing is that it is called "Father," and it is "Compassionate" in the secret of the great compassion from Keter:

Av [אב, av], in the sense of a shoot, as in the matter of "while it is yet in its greenness [be-ibbo]," etc. (Job 8:12). Certainly it is the matter of the spreading out of the Emanation, and everything according to its context. The example of this is "the shoots [ibbei] of the stream" (Song 6:11): the stream is Tiferet, and "the shoots of the stream" are the branches that spread out from it. Or if we explain "stream" as Yesod, it would mean the branching out of Yesod. And likewise if we explain it elsewhere, everything according to its context. And "the month of Aviv" means the month that spreads out and branches out; for Nisan is the head of the months, which is the havayah in its order, YHVH, and from it the twelve havayot, the twelve months, branch out. And the matter of "fresh ears [aviv] parched with fire" (Lev. 2:14) is from this root. And from this the inquirer can judge whatever is like it:

Willing [אבה, avah] is from the language of will, and wherever it is found it means the rising of the will, that is, the bestowal of Keter, which is called Will; and from this one will judge according to its context:
Perished [אבד, avad], as in the matter of "the righteous one perishes" (Isa. 57:1): it means the withdrawal of his bestowal; and from this the inquirer may infer:

The point of the sword [אבחת חרב, ivchat cherev] (Ezek. 21:20) is the language of the flame of the sword, and it is the husk, as we explained in its place. And likewise some explained it as "the terror of the sword"; and it is all one matter:

The Mighty One [אביר, abir] is Tiferet; and likewise "the Mighty One of Jacob" and likewise "the Mighty One of Israel." And it is possible that he is so called in the secret of his might in tipping judgment toward compassion, as is known. And Yesod is sometimes so called, as is known, for it is the extension of the Vav:

Mourning [אבל, avel]: the language of mourning is a parable for the withdrawal of the effluence and the dominion of the outer ones to destroy, God forbid; and in this is the very secret of mourning, which is seven days of weeping. And it is possible that it is within holiness. Aval [Indeed] is from the side of the strength of judgment; and it is all one matter, for the effluence withdraws from the side of judgment. And every use of the word aval, as in the matter of "Indeed [aval], Sarah your wife" (Gen. 17:19), and likewise "We are indeed [aval] guilty" (Gen. 42:21), and the like, may be in Malkhut from the side of judgment; and there is evidence for this from the Scriptures:

Stone [אבן, even] is always in the secret of the Yod, and mostly in Malkhut, in the manifestation of the Yod that is in her. And likewise the Yod is a lump in the form of a stone. And likewise Malkhut is a foundation and a stone on which the whole upper building rests; and of her it is said (Zech. 3:9), "upon one stone are seven eyes":

And sometimes this title is accompanied [by another word], and she is called a tried stone [אבן בוחן, even bochan] (Isa. 28:16). And this is in the secret that she tries and tests the righteous, as in the matter of the ten trials with which Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was tried. And in this aspect there are two aspects: either the aspect of her drawing nourishment from judgment, and from there she tries the righteous; or from the side of her drawing nourishment from compassion, when she rises up to Keter; and she needs purification in order to rise, and then the judgment that is in her is bestowed to try the righteous, and she is purified and withdraws. And this is the secret of the sufferings of love, with which she chastens the righteous:
Further, she is called the head stone [אבן הראשה, even ha-roshah] (Zech. 4:7), in the aspect in which she is second to Chokhmah, as is explained in the aforementioned gate:

Further, she is called the stone that the builders rejected [אבן מאסו הבונים] (Ps. 118:22). And the explanation is that the fathers of the world, who built the Chariot, did not take her as their portion, and took as their portion Gedulah, Gevurah and Tiferet. And sometimes she is head of them all, when she rises up to the Ein Sof; and then she is called the crown of priesthood at the head of Chesed, the crown of Levitehood at the head of Gevurah, and the crown of Torah at the head of Tiferet. And this is "has become the head of the corner" [pinnah]. And the commentators explained that she "has become the head of the corner" because everything turns [ponim] to her: the upper ones to bestow into her, and the lower ones to draw from her:

Further, she is called the stone of Israel [אבן ישראל], and the reason is "from there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel" (Gen. 49:24): through her even Tiferet is sometimes bestowed upon, and in this aspect she is called "the diadem of Tiferet." And the commentators explained: the provider and shepherd of Israel below:

Further, she is called the Foundation Stone [אבן השתיה, even ha-shetiyah]. Some explained it from the language of giving drink [hashka'ah], for from there all the flocks are given drink; and this is strained. And its principal explanation is the language of foundation, for she is the foundation of all the upper ones, as is known:

Further, she is called the sapphire stone [אבן הספיר, even ha-sappir]. And all of them explained the reason: just as the sapphire receives all the colors, so this attribute receives the actions from above, whether for good or for ill. And in the Tikkunim (Introduction, fol. 6) he explained that she is so called when she is like Chokhmah, which is the one called sapphire, as we explained in the Gate of Colors, chapter 2; and then she is called "the sapphire stone." And when we look at the matter of the colors, [we see] that Chokhmah has no color and Malkhut has no color, as we explained there in chapter 5. It all comes to one place:

Further, she is called a whole stone [אבן שלימה, even shelemah], from the side of Binah. And the matter is that Chokhmah is a Yod and Malkhut is a Yod. And this is what Rabbi Akiva said to his disciples: "When you reach the stones of pure marble, do not say, 'Water, water'": that they are two kinds of water; for it is all one union, as it is said (Isa. 44:6), "I am the first and I am the last." As the verse says (Prov. 3:19), "YHVH by wisdom founded the earth": for the foundation of Malkhut, which is a Yod, is from the side of Chokhmah; and from there she is called simply "stone," the form of a Yod. However, from the side of Binah she is called "a whole stone," for then she is whole in her building; and of them it is said (Deut. 27:6), "You shall build the altar of YHVH your God of whole stones." And when she is whole in her building, then it is said of her (Dan. 2:34–35): "You saw, until a stone was cut out," etc., from Chokhmah; and she takes the power of judgment from the side of Binah; "and it struck the image," to remove the idols from the earth, "and the idols shall be utterly cut off"; and then "it became a great mountain," in her place, "and filled the whole earth," for she fills the whole earth in the secret of the manifestations. All this is learned from the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim, one here and one there:

And there is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense [אבן נגף וצור מכשול] (Isa. 8:14), and they are the husks. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (in the Sitrei Torah, fol. 151) and in Pekudei (fol. 249):

Further, there is a figured stone [אבן משכית, even maskit] (Lev. 26:1), and it is from the side of Beriah: the handmaid of holiness, from the side of Metatron. And it is explained in the Gate of ABYA:

Slimy stones [אבנים מפולמות, avanim mefulamot] are explained as Chesed. And they said that it is a parable for the source of the waters and their moisture. And in the Zohar is found: "slimy stones that are sunk in the deeps, and from them the waters go out." Further, it explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 227) that there are three husks:

The first is a green line, and that is formlessness [tohu]; and the second is slimy stones, and that is void [bohu], etc.; see there. And according to this they are in the husk. And it is possible to reconcile them: when Chesed is clothed within that husk, it is called "slimy stones"; for the three Patriarchs are clothed in three husks. And this will be explained at length in the Gate of Substitutes, chapter 7, with the help of the Name:

Stones of formlessness [אבני תהו, avnei tohu] (Isa. 34:11) are in Chesed, and they are like "slimy stones," on the two explanations that we explained of them above. And it is also possible that [they are] the husks, which are formlessness, void and darkness, as is known; and it is explained in the Gate of Substitutes, chapter 6:

Dust [אבק, avak]: the husk is so called. And the reason is that it is like the dust, which is the burnt earth under the furnace, which does not make fruit; so too the husk does not make fruit, for it is "burned with fire, cut down" (Ps. 80:17). So it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayishlach (fol. 170):

The powders of the merchant [אבקת רוכל, avkat rokhel] (Song 3:6). He explained in the Zohar (Mishpatim, fol. 117) that it is Binah; and it is possible that she is so called for the reason that in her all the forms are included, and in her they are formed, in the secret of "this day the world was conceived." And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 44) he explained it as Yesod; and it is possible that it is called rokhel because it is like the merchant [rokhel] who compounds spices. And so he explained (there, fol. 54): "He is the merchant, and she is his powder": the explanation, Yesod is the merchant, and Malkhut is his powder:

Pinion [אבר, ever]. Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (at the end of Tikkun 13, fol. 28), on the verse "He will cover you with His pinion [be-evrato]" (Ps. 91:4), that ever is the Righteous One; and it is called "a limb [ever] from the living," which is Yesod; and likewise the word ever hints at it, for it is the hidden use. And it is possible that the language of flying is also applied to it as a title, as in "Does the hawk soar [ya'avar]?" (Job 39:26); and it is "the bird of the heavens" and "the winged one" on the Sabbath day, as explained in the Tikkunim:

Abraham [אברהם, avraham]: its explanation is in Chesed; and for the reason that Abraham was made a chariot for Chesed, it is called by his name. And it is possible that it is called by the name Abraham only in the secret of the aspect for which Abraham is a chariot, which is the aspect called "southward" [negbah], as will be explained (in the entry "south" [negev]); and likewise in that aspect in which it bestows its kindness on human beings: in that aspect he was a chariot for it:

Bundle [אגודה, aguddah]: the explanation, the whole Emanation is so called when it is in Malkhut. And it is so called because in her all the sefirot are united and joined, and she binds them all together. And for this reason the lulav does not need a binding, because it is united with the etrog, and its binding is with it. And in the Zohar, Parashat Tzav (fol. 35), he explained on the verse "and has founded His bundle [aguddato] upon the earth" (Amos 9:6) that when the Emanation is united with her in union, she is called "bundle," as we explained:

Drops of dew [אגלי טל, eglei tal] (Job 38:28): its matter is the drops of the effluence and its revelations [gilluyav], which are bestowed from Tiferet, where the place of the dew is, in the secret of Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, which equals tal [39] in numerical value. And from this one will judge according to its place. And it is possible to explain it from the language of "a spring [gal] shut up" (Song 4:12), in Malkhut; see the entry gal:

Nut [אגוז, egoz]. Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24, fol. 67, and Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 136) that Malkhut is called "nut." And the reason is that she is clothed within the husks, as the kernel of the nut is clothed within its shells, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Substitute Palaces, chapter 7, with the help of the Name. And the kernel is divided into four parts, to show the four letters of the Name, which are the four legs of the Chariot, and all is unified. And this is close to the hand tefillin, whose four passages are the four letters; and they are four within and one without. And accordingly it is found that Malkhut is so called in the secret of her aspect that is clothed within all the husks.
