And elsewhere in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 26, fol. 69) he explained that Yesod is called "nut" and Malkhut "the garden of nuts." (And see the Zohar, Shemot, fol. 15):

Pool [אגם, agam]: the explanation, "a pool of water" (Ps. 107:35) and the like is Malkhut, when she receives the waters of Chesed, and the field becomes a pool of water. And the matter is evident of itself:

Basin [אגן, aggan]. He explained in the Zohar, Parashat Mishpatim (fol. 126), on the verse "and put it in basins" (Exod. 24:6), and these are his words: "Ba-aganot is written defectively, as it is written, 'Your navel is like a round basin, wherein no mingled wine is wanting' (Song 7:3)." Thus far his words.

And the intent is that "basin" is Malkhut when she is full and complete in all her circles; and this is the language of aggan and the language of circle [iggul]. And it shows the language of receiving, like this vessel that has a rim [ogen], which receives the thing that is put in it. And this is "wherein no mingled wine [mezeg] is wanting": the intent is that her fullness and her completeness, that is, her blending, should not be wanting:

Wing [אגף, agaf] is the matter of wings, as the Targum renders gappin; and it is a title for the gathering of the hosts that accompany the Shekhinah or Tiferet. For the language of wings [kenafayim] is also the matter of a company [kenufya] and a gathering. And it is a parable for the hosts that gather to the Shekhinah; that is to say, the spreading out of its aspect to take refuge under the wings of the Shekhinah, as in the matter of "under whose wings you have come to take refuge" (Ruth 2:12), which is expounded in the Zohar on the matter of the proselytes. We shall explain it in its entry:

Gathering [אגרת, agoret]: the language of gathering, as in "she gathers [agrah] in the harvest" (Prov. 6:8), etc. And it is a title for Malkhut, who gathers the effluence within her. And when the effluence is from the side of Chesed, she is called "a piece [agorat] of silver" (1 Sam. 2:36). And from this the inquirer may infer to everything found that is like it:

Mist [א"ד, ed]. He explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 52, fol. 84) that it is the last Heh, Malkhut, for ed [Alef-Dalet] comes to five, the number of Heh; and it is the Alef-Dalet of Adonai. And it is a hint at the arousal of Malkhut; and of this aspect it is said (Gen. 2:6), "and a mist went up from the earth." And it is an aspect in which she bestows the arousal upward:

Lord [אדון, adon] is Malkhut; and she is so called in her lower aspect, for she is like a lord sitting on the throne to govern the world, the upper ones and the lower ones. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 118) that Tiferet, when he is in Malkhut, is called "Lord," for he is the self of lordship, and by his name she is called Adonai. And the reason is that through his providence over the world he is called "Lord." If so, it is found that when he is in union with her below, in her place, she is called by his name. And so it is also explained in the Zohar, Bereshit (fol. 34). And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 242) he further explained "lord" as the Righteous One, on the verse "YHVH says to my lord" (Ps. 110:1), that it is in Yesod; and the reason is to bind it to the right, and this is "Sit at My right hand." And it is possible that it is so called for the reason that we explained for Tiferet:

Further, there is Lord of wonders [אדון הנפלאות, adon ha-nifla'ot]. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in Sefer ha-Shem that it is in Netzach; and it is so called because it comes from the power of the wonders of Chokhmah, the right; or because it works wonders for the lower powers, to overpower Hod, which is beneath it. And this is strained, for why should it be called "Lord"? Unless we explain it as Tiferet, and it is called "Lord of wonders" in the secret of its receiving from the supernal Wonder; and so he explained in the Tikkunim. And some explained it as Malkhut. And so there are found in the prayer of Yotzer, from "On high and Holy" to "Lord of wonders," ten levels corresponding to the ten sefirot: "On high" is Keter, "Holy" Chokhmah, etc., "Lord of wonders" Malkhut. And it is possible that it is called by the language of wonders because she receives the thirty-two wondrous paths of wisdom and reveals them among the lower ones:

Further, Malkhut is called Lord of lords [אדון האדונים], for she is head of all the princes on high. And it is possible that she is so called when she "gives food to her household and a portion to her maidens" (Prov. 31:15), "each to his work that they do": to Michael, Chesed, and to Raphael, healing; all to bestow upon and govern the lower ones. And therefore she is called "Lord," governing the governing lords that are beneath her, which receive from her:

Mighty [אדיר, adir]: some explained it as Binah. And to me it appears that it is a title for the power of Gevurah, from the side of judgment; and such is the sense of the word, for adir means strength. And it is possible that from the side of Gevurah Malkhut is called aderet [mantle]; all the more so when she is called "a mantle [aderet] of Shinar" (Josh. 7:21), for then it shows that she receives from Gevurah and bestows on the storm and tempest that are beneath her:

Man [אדם, adam]. "Man" without qualification is Chokhmah; and it is mah [45], the four-letter name in its filling Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Alef, which comes to mah [45], the number of adam; and it is Chokhmah [chokhmah], ko'ach mah [the power of What]; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. Further, Malkhut is called "man," and she is the lower Man. Further, the supernal Keter is called the Primordial Man [Adam Kadmon]; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 116): "There is no sefirah that is not called adam; but the first, supernal Man of them all is the supernal Keter," etc. And they called it there Adam Kadmon; and it is called kadmon [primordial] to show that it precedes the whole Emanation. And there is no doubt that it is so called only when it is in the utmost concealment, like the primordial light. Further, Tiferet is called "man" when he rises to Chokhmah; and these are the words of the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 255): "And in Chokhmah, which is the life of Tiferet, he rises to be called adam; as it is written, 'according to the beauty [tiferet] of a man' (Isa. 44:13)." Thus far his words.

And elsewhere he said that from the side of the upper Man and the lower Man, who are two Chokhmahs, he is called "man" when he unites the upper Man, Chokhmah, with the lower Man, Malkhut; and this is in the secret of the upper Yod and the lower Yod, with the Vav in the middle uniting them; and this is the secret of the Alef. And Tiferet is called "the stored-away man" because he is stored away and laid away in the secret of Da'at. And it is proved in the Zohar, in Parashat Tazria (fol. 48), that adam is more praiseworthy than ish [man]; and there he proved the matter at length, that the name adam is more praiseworthy than the name ish. And the reason is that in adam Malkhut is included with Tiferet: "male and female He created them, and called their name adam" (Gen. 5:2), the completeness of male and female; and ish is the male alone, as will be explained in its entry, with the help of the Name. And in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 34), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the Alef of adam hints at the supernal Keter in its upper, concealed aspect; and the closed Mem is in Binah, in the secret of the Mem of "for the increase [le-marbeh] of the dominion" (Isa. 9:6); and the Dalet is in Malkhut. Accordingly it is found that Tiferet includes these three attributes, and it is a more praiseworthy description than ish; for the word adam also shows the union of Malkhut, as we explained. And on the matter of the face of a man [penei adam]: many agreed that the face of a man is in Tiferet and the face of an eagle in Malkhut. And in the Tikkunim the reverse of this matter is found: for the principal face of a man is in Chokhmah, and it is the upper Man, and Malkhut is the face of the lower Man; and the face of a man is not in Tiferet at all, but the face of an eagle. And it is already possible that the face of a man should be in Tiferet in the way that we explained of adam, that it is by means of Chokhmah. And this matter will be explained more broadly in the book Or Yakar, with the help of Heaven:

Earth [אדמה, adamah] is in Malkhut; and she is called adamah to hint that she is beneath all the sefirot, like the earth, which is beneath all the children of the world. And she is called adamah when she draws nourishment from judgment and becomes red [adumah] with the redness of Gevurah. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 53, fol. 84) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verse "And YHVH God formed," etc., "from the earth" (Gen. 2:7), that it is Binah. And it is possible that she is so called in the way that we explained for Malkhut:

Ruddy [אדמוני, admoni] is Hod; and it is called "ruddy" and not "red" because there is some whiteness in it; for it draws nourishment from Tiferet too, and therefore there is some whiteness in it, some compassion:

Adonai [אדני, adonai] is Malkhut; (and she is called) so because she is a receptacle for the effluence that is bestowed on her. And the sockets [adnei] of the Tabernacle, which were a hundred sockets, hint at her: that she receives from ten, each one included of ten, and they are a hundred; and that is the hundred gates:

Master builder [אדריכל, adrikhal] is Malkhut. And the intent is: just as the master builder is the great craftsman who commands the craftsmen to make the building properly, by the mind of the owner of the work, so Malkhut is the one who commands in the building all the builders who are beneath her, to give form to the forms of the things that are in the world, by the power of Tiferet, who is above her. And she is so called when she forms what she is commanded by the upper ones:

Love [אהבה, ahavah] is in Chesed; and therefore Abraham is called "My lover" (Isa. 41:8), for he drew upon himself the power of love. And likewise the Shekhinah, when she draws nourishment from the side of Chesed, is called "love"; and so it is in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 29, fol. 71). And she is called "love" when she draws nourishment from the thread of Chesed, to couple with her husband. And this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, said in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36, fol. 76): "When she opens toward her husband she is called love." And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 196), that when she draws nourishment from the thread of Chesed she is called "love." And elsewhere (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 257) he explained that she is called "love" when she is included of all the Patriarchs. And we can say that she is called "love" from the side of Chesed; but first she draws nourishment from the north, for such is the order of her longing with her husband, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 21, with the help of Heaven; and afterward she receives from the south, and afterward she opens by means of the south and is called "love" from its side; and she is included of them all:

Further, she is called the love of YHVH [אהבת ה']. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 9), and these are his words: "And the love of YHVH is Malkhut, included of all the sefirot." And the reason is that through the joining she becomes included of ten sefirot; and when she is included by means of the bridegroom she is called "the love of YHVH." Further, there is great love [אהבה רבה], and it is Chesed; and Rashbi explained the reason in the Commandments (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Va'etchanan, fol. 263), and these are his words: "With the right of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is great love. Why is it so called? Because whoever stands in this love is bound to the upper world." Thus far his words.
Behold, it is explicit that when Chesed is joined with Binah it is called "great love," for it is very great:

Further, there is everlasting love [אהבת עולם, ahavat olam], and it is Malkhut. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the reason (there), and these are his words: "Everlasting love [ahavat olam]: this is the secret of the lower world without separation, to which his love is bound," etc.

Behold, it is explicit that she is so called in the secret of her union with Tiferet, who is also called "world" [olam], as will be explained in its entry. And in the Zohar, Parashat Chayyei (fol. 137), he explained that the arousal of love is from the side of the left; and therefore it is said of Isaac, "And Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother," etc., "and he loved her" (Gen. 24:67). "And as for what is said of Jacob, 'And Jacob loved Rachel' (Gen. 29:18): the side of Isaac that was in him did it to him." Thus far. It appears explicitly that love is from the side of Gevurah. And the resolution of this matter has been made clear to us from his words in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 245), on the verse "Many waters cannot quench love" (Song 8:7): that first it is from the side of Gevurah, in the secret of "His left hand is under my head" (Song 2:6), and that is the receiving of Malkhut from Gevurah, and through it the love and the embrace are crowned; and afterward Chesed bestows. And it is the way of Chesed to quiet the power of judgment; and therefore it would have been fitting that it quench the love aroused by the power of judgment, by means of the compassion of Chesed. And the verse explained to us the reverse of this, in saying "Many waters cannot," etc.: the explanation, the waters of Chesed that she received from it after she had received from the left; and this is "and his right hand embraces me," as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. This is the sum of the words of the Zohar in its place, and we did not think fit to copy it, for love of brevity; and whoever delights in it will find it there. However it may be, the sum of the words is: the beginning of love is through Fear, in the secret of "His left hand is under my head," and afterward through the right, through Chesed, that is, "and his right hand embraces me." And with this resolution the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, are right in all their aspects:

Ahah [אהה, ahah, Alas]. On the verse "Alas, O Lord God" (Jer. 1:6), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 74), that in ahah the Alef is in Keter, and the two Hehs are Binah and Malkhut. And the matter is that the Shekhinah, the last Heh, was cast down from heaven, and the blessings withdrew from Binah too, which is the upper Heh, and were held back in Keter, which is the letter Alef. And therefore one says ahah, to lament over these three levels, each one according to its matter; see there:

The Tent of Meeting [אוהל מועד, ohel mo'ed] is the Shekhinah, Malkhut. And she is so called because she is the house of meeting [va'ad] for Tiferet and his appointed place [mo'ed]. And likewise the Targum of "tent" is mashkan [dwelling], for she is the dwelling of YHVH. And likewise it is written (Exod. 25:22), "And there I will meet with you": Tiferet, who spoke with Moses inside the tent, face to face. And she is so called when she is adorned with her adornments to receive the face of the King, the bridegroom. And these are the words of the Zohar, Parashat Balak (fol. 200b), on the verse "And He called to Moses from the Tent of Meeting" (Lev. 1:1): "From the holy palace, from the palace that is set right, from the precious palace, toward which the upper ones and the lower ones yearn, and they cannot draw near to it." Thus far his words.

Its matter is when the bride is adorned to receive the face of her husband; and then she is included in herself, in the secret of "Do not look upon me, that I am swarthy" (Song 1:6), which is expounded on the Song of Songs in the Zohar; see there. And therefore she is called "the dwelling of time" [mashkan zimna], which means "at times," in which there is not a complete union. And the secret is "and Joshua son of Nun, a youth, did not depart from within" [the tent] (Exod. 33:11), etc.; and he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 143), that the Tabernacle was in the secret of the Youth. And then she is called "the dwelling of time," for times. But the principal dwelling is on the holy mountain, for there it is above, in the secret of "an established throne":

Or [או, o]: in our view this word hints at the Vav that is drawn from Keter, which is the Alef; and it is the middle line, which is between the right and the left. And therefore, to distinguish between one matter and another, one says this word:

Goose [אווז, avaz]. We found one of the commentators who explained that "goose" is in Chokhmah; and he found support for this in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Berakhot 57a): "One who sees a goose in a dream may hope for wisdom," etc. And we have no reason for this hint that would compel it, except that the goose is white and would hint at Chokhmah by its whiteness. And it seems to me that the intent of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, in the Gemara, "may hope for wisdom," is because the goose cries out with voices, in the manner of the sage when he occupies himself with the Torah. Therefore we say that it is in the lower Chokhmah, which is in voices; or in the upper Chokhmah, in the secret of "Wisdom cries aloud in the street" (Prov. 1:20), etc., which is after its revelation to Binah, and from Binah outward, in the secret of "she utters her voice in the squares," as explained in the Zohar (Toledot, fol. 141):

Woe [אוי, oy]. On the verse (Jer. 6:4), "Woe to us, for the day has turned away," Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Parashat Acharei, fol. 75) that when Tiferet has withdrawn to Keter, and the effluence is not even in Binah, and repentance does not avail to annul this decree, God forbid, then oy is said. And he explained that [the head of] Yesod [is a Yod], and it is the small Vav; and "the head of the righteous one" is the place of the dwelling of the blessings, as it is said (Prov. 10:6), "Blessings are upon the head of the righteous one": that is, the Vav, which is the extension of Tiferet upon Yesod. And when the effluence withdraws from Yesod to Tiferet, the head of the Vav withdraws upward to the Vav that is in Tiferet; and that is vay [Vav-Yod] (see below in the entry "letter"). And when Tiferet withdraws further to Keter, which is the Alef, so that it is not bestowed even in Binah (as it is known that the union of Chokhmah with Binah is through the Vav, in the secret of Da'at, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 8), then oy is said, showing the withdrawal of Yesod and Tiferet to Keter; and the channels are broken, and famine comes about, God forbid. All this is explained there at length; and it is a wondrous saying, explained by us in a fair light:

Ov [אוב, ov, a ghost]: in the matter of "a ghost [ov] or a familiar spirit [yidd'oni]" (Lev. 20:27), it is a title for the outer husk, and likewise yidd'oni; and they are two husks, and their matter is known. And we know that the inquirer will wonder at the matter of holy letters that show the outer ones, as in the matter of ox and ass and the like. And on the matter of ov I spoke at length in the book Or Yakar, with the help of Heaven:

A brand plucked from the fire [אוד מוצל מאש, ud mutzal me-esh] (Zech. 3:2) and the like is a title for what goes out from the power of judgment; and what is rescued from its fire and its judgment is called ud, as is known from its matter. And it is possible that it is a title for Malkhut, who is called ed [Alef-Dalet], as explained above; and when she is turned from judgment toward the side of Chesed by means of the Vav that is in her, ud, that is, ed with a Vav, she is called "a brand plucked":

Craved [אוה, ivvah]: [as in] "He has craved [ivvah] it for His dwelling" (Ps. 132:13). He explained in the Tikkunim (perhaps hinting at Tikkun 4, fol. 17) that it is the union of Alef, which is Keter, with Tiferet and Malkhut, which are called Vav-Heh. And the verse does not depart from our matter: for through the will and the effluence that is bestowed from Keter for the adornments of the bridegroom and the bride, they crave one another. And from this the inquirer can infer to the rest:

Ochim [אוחים, ochim, howling creatures]: the explanation of the verse "and their houses shall be full of howling creatures [ochim]" (Isa. 13:21). They are kinds of beasts, and it is a kind among the kinds of husks that dwell in a ruined place, like the matter of she'iyah [desolation], which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Bava Batra 21, and in the Zohar, Shelach, fol. 163), and the like. And it is possible that it is Lilith and Samael, who are brothers [achim] in brotherhood:

Enemy [אויב, oyev]: all its matter is from the side of judgment; and sometimes in the outer ones, who are true enemies. And according to the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Idra (the angels too are called enemies; and this is "a watcher [ir] and a holy one came down from heaven" (Dan. 4:10): the explanation, a holy enemy, from the language of "and it was Er"):
Fool [אויל, evil]: the language of folly and the like; and it is a parable for the husk; and likewise every term for madness and the like:

Air [אויר, avir]: the name "air" is attributed in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 255) to Tiferet, and these are its words: "Tiferet is air; and therefore they established that the release of vows flies in the air." And the explanation is that the vow is in Binah, and she flies over Tiferet, as is known. And elsewhere he said there, "Uriel, which is air"; and elsewhere (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Tzav, fol. 28), "And this is the central pillar, which is air."

Behold, from all these places it appears that air is in Tiferet. And on this matter, elsewhere (Pinchas, fol. 245), [he wrote], and these are his words: "For the letter Yod of YHVH wrapped itself in light [or] and became air [avir]; and that is: the air of the land of Israel makes wise, because the letter Yod, which is Chokhmah, is in the air. And this is the light in which He wrapped Himself when He created the world; as it is written, 'who wraps Himself in light as with a garment' (Ps. 104:2). And this is 'Let there be light' [or]: let there be air [avir]. And the masters of the secrets of the Torah established: before anything came into being, the beings came into being; and therefore 'Let there be light, and there was light,' which was there beforehand." Thus far his words.

And the explanation: the principal light is Binah, and in her are hinted the five lights mentioned in this passage, and they correspond to the upper Heh; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30, fol. 72, and Tikkun 47, fol. 82). And Chokhmah wraps itself in Binah, and this is "who wraps Himself in light." And this is the cause of the beings, which are drawn from there through the joining of the two of them; and this is "who stretches out the heavens," etc. However, it is impossible for Chokhmah and Binah to be joined except through Da'at, which unites them, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter and in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And since Da'at is the joining of the two of them, it is therefore called by their name, avir [Yod within or], as a likeness of their joining and their union. And only the subtle manifestation in the secret of Da'at is called "air." And with this the saying is explained:

Further, Keter too is called "air," and there are two aspects in it. The first aspect is called "air that is not grasped," and it is the one that cleaves to and is united with the Emanator. And the second aspect is called "air that is somewhat grasped." And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, on the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 87): "Since that striking settles in the brain, from within the pure air that is grasped; for there is a pure air that is not grasped at all. And this one that is grasped, when that supernal striking settles in that brain, then all the motions of the cantillation marks go out," etc. Thus far. And the cantillation marks are from Keter; and that is "the air that is grasped," its aspect that settles and rides upon Chokhmah, which is called "the brain," as will be explained with the help of the Name. And there is one aspect that is not grasped, and it is sometimes called "the primordial air," for "primordial" is particular to Keter, as we shall explain. And in saying "not grasped," our intent is not a literal grasping, for even Chokhmah is not grasped; but the explanation is that it is not grasped even by the sefirah Chokhmah, for it is subtle, united with the Ein Sof, as was explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. And Keter is called "air" when it rides upon Chokhmah and Binah when they are united in the secret of Da'at; for the secret of their union hints at avir, or with a Yod. And therefore Keter, which gives power to Da'at to unite them, is called "air"; and likewise it is sometimes called "a tower flying in the air," which are Chokhmah and Binah. And in the Tikkunim (22, fol. 62) he called Binah "pure air," and these are his words: "For she is the upper Heh, pure air, the air of the land of Israel, which makes wise from the side of Chokhmah, which is the Yod." Thus far his words. And the matter is not far-fetched, as we explained above:

Eater [אוכל, okhel]. On the verse "Out of the eater came forth food" (Judg. 14:14), he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 208), that the eater is the Righteous One, because he eats all the supernal effluence, to bestow it below on Malkhut, as it is written (Prov. 13:25), "The righteous one eats to the satisfying of his soul"; and the food that goes out from him is what is bestowed on the lower ones, which is the food of the Shekhinah:

Nurturer [אומן, omen]: the explanation, Yesod is called omen because he nurtured [omen] Hadassah (Esther 2:7), who is the Shekhinah, and bestows on her great good from the upper sefirot that are above him:

Aven [און, aven, iniquity]. In the Zohar, Parashat (Yitro, fol. 67), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that aven and oni are all a title for the side of the husk. And these are his words: "The priest of On [Aven] (Gen. 41:45): the Other Side, which is the side of the left. And this is the secret of what Rachel said when she saw that she was dying, as it is written, 'Ben-oni' (Gen. 35:18). And therefore Jacob hastened and said 'Benjamin' [Ben-yamin], and not Ben-oni: the side of the right [yamin], and not the side of the left." Thus far his words. And likewise every use of aven, as in "for iniquity [aven] does not come forth from the dust" (Job 5:6), and likewise every term for fraud [ona'ah] and the like. However, when they said "my might and the first of my strength [oni]" (Gen. 49:3), it means the language of power, and it is a holy power. And it is possible that it is the union of ani [I], which is Malkhut, with the Vav, which is Tiferet; and this oni is on the side of holiness:

Darkness [אופל, ofel] is Gevurah, and it is so called on account of judgment. And there is no doubt that it is called ofel in the third aspect of Gevurah, which is the aspect of darkness, as explained in the Gate of Colors:

Wheel [אופן, ofan]: Gedulah is so called because it is the great guide of the whole Chariot; so Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in Sefer ha-Shem. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 103) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the wheels of the Chariot are Netzach and Hod, and the Righteous One is "one wheel" (Ezek. 1:15). And so the Chariot is found to be four living creatures, which are Gedulah, the face of a lion; Gevurah, the face of an ox; Tiferet, the face of an eagle; Malkhut, the face of a man; and the two wheels of the Chariot, Netzach and Hod; and "one wheel upon the earth" is Yesod, which is upon the earth, which is Malkhut. And in the Zohar Chadash on the Song of Songs (fol. 75; see there) [he explained] that Malkhut has three faces looking toward the three Patriarchs, and they are called El, Elohim, YHVH; and below them is one face that receives from the three faces, and it is called "one wheel upon the earth" [ofan echad ba-aretz]: meaning that they ask about it, o pan, that is to say, "where [an] is the one face [pan]?" and they answer, "upon the earth":

Light [אור, or] is attributed to several places. First, in Tiferet, as it is written (Prov. 6:23), "and the Torah is light"; for he bestows light and shines in the pupil of the eye, which is Malkhut. Further, Binah is called "light," for she is the one who shines in five sefirot, which are Gedulah, Gevurah and Tiferet, the three colors of the eye, and the two cherubim of the eye, which are Netzach and Hod. And we have already explained that she is the one who shines in them, in the secret of the fifty gates of Binah. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 280; see there): "Yod is the pupil of the eye, 'for the commandment is a lamp, and the Torah is light' (Prov. 6:23): Vav, which shines in it. Heh: the three colors of the eye and the two wings of the eye. Light shines in them from within: the upper Heh, which is light," etc. Thus far. However, Tiferet is called "light" when he shines in Malkhut, and Binah is called "light" when she gives light to the five sefirot mentioned, with the light of the fifty gates of Binah. And it is fitting to know that the principal light, although it is in the two places mentioned, has its root in Chesed. And so it is found that on the first day five lights are mentioned, to hint at the five sefirot mentioned, which are five lights; and they are in her from the side of Binah, and they are called lights only from the side of Chesed. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fols. 166–167), in the story of Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Chiyya, who lodged at their inn, and these are his words: "And because these are five levels that were separated and drawn out from this first light, 'light' is written five times; and all of it was from the side of the right, and they were included in it." Thus far his words.

And through it they are called lights, for the principal light is in Chesed. And so it is explained there, above the matter, and these are its words: "'And the Torah is light': which shines for that lamp, and [the lamp] was kindled from it, from the side of the first light, which is the right; for the Torah was given from that side of the right, the first light, as it is written, 'from His right hand a fiery law for them' (Deut. 33:2): it was given from the side of the right. Although the left is included in it, for then it is the completeness of them all. This light is included in two hundred and seven worlds, which are stored away on the side of that light, and it spreads out in all of them. Beneath the supernal, concealed Throne these worlds dwell, from the side of that right; they are three hundred and ten. Two hundred and seven are on the side of the right, a hundred and three are on the side of the left, and they are three hundred and ten. And these are the ones that the Holy One, blessed be He, ever prepares for the righteous; and from these spread out many and many treasuries of delight, and all of them are stored away, for the righteous to take pleasure in them in the world to come. And of these it is written, 'to cause those who love me to inherit substance [yesh]' (Prov. 8:21), etc.; and of these it is written, 'no eye has seen, O God, besides You' (Isa. 64:3). Yesh [310]: these are the three hundred and ten worlds stored away beneath the world to come. And those two hundred and seven, which are from the side of the right, are called the first light; for even the light of the left is called light, but the first light is ready to make offspring for the world to come. And if you say, for the world to come and no more: rather, even on each and every day; for if not for this light the world could not stand, as it is written, 'I have said, The world is built by loving-kindness [chesed]' (Ps. 89:3)." Thus far his words.

And the explanation: before this he explained that "the lamp of the commandment" is Malkhut, and "the Torah is light" is Tiferet, who kindles and bestows to Malkhut; and he is the light that illumines and kindles her. And he said that that light is from the side of Chesed, for from there is the principal nourishment of Tiferet; and he brought a proof of this from the verse "from His right hand," etc. And this is what he said, "for the Torah," etc., "although the left is included," etc.; for it was difficult for him that from the verse it appears that the Torah was given from the right and from the left; and therefore it says, "from His right hand a fiery law [esh dat] for them." To this he said that the matter of "a fiery law" is the left that is included in the right; and the right is always the principal, and the inclusion of the left is also for the completeness of Chesed, for its completeness is when the left is included with it. "This light is included," etc.: he proved the matter of light in Chesed from the number of the worlds that are on the right, which is the number of or [207]; and from this it is proved that the left is included in the world on the right, and the right always prevails; for all the lights are included in yesh [310], as we explained: "they are three hundred and ten," etc., and of them two hundred and seven are on the right. And the reason is that these lights are included in three lines: the right line, Chesed, with a hundred and three in it; and likewise in the middle line, compassion, with a hundred and three in it; and because of its inclining toward Chesed, as is known, therefore, since "the law is from His right hand," there are two hundred and seven on the right, and on the left line there are a hundred and three.

And behold, the one left over is the manifestation of their union together. And therefore an Alef comes at the head of the word; and its sign: Alef, o [Alef-Vav], or [Alef-Vav-Resh]; and it is all one.

And behold, from the matter of these three hundred and ten worlds the name "light" is proved to be in Chesed: for the middle line inclines to the right, toward Chesed, and the number of the lights on the right is found to be the number of or, and on the left a hundred and three alone. And it is also proved that the matter of "a fiery law for them" is the inclusion that is included, as the lights are included, and they come to three hundred and ten lights. And the matter of the light is also proved to belong to Tiferet from the side of Chesed, for through it [the number] comes to or, in the secret of the right. And because the light is drawn from Binah, he therefore said, "And these are the ones that the Holy One, blessed be He": that is Binah. "Ever prepares," etc.: the explanation, she bestows into them and illumines them, and they are lights for the righteous in the world to come; and likewise of them it is said, "no eye has seen, O God, besides You," which is Binah. "And those two hundred and seven, which are from the side of the right," etc.: he comes to give the reason why Chesed is called "the first light." For "light" has already been explained; but "first" [why? To this he said]: the reason is that they act and bring beings into being in the secret of their receiving from Binah, because they are close to her, in the secret of Chesed, second to Binah; therefore it is called "first," in the secret of this priority. For the name "light" alone is also attributed, with a strained reading, to the hundred and three lights of the left. "And if you say, for the world to come," etc.: it was difficult for him: if so, their principal action is for the world to come, and no benefit is drawn from them in this world; if so, why is it said that the Torah was given from the side of the right, and that the matter of "the Torah is light" is from the side of the right, since those lights are only for the world to come? To this he said, "rather, even on each and every day," etc. And the principle that emerges is that the five lights are five sefirot, and they are called "light" from the side of Chesed, for it is the principal light. However, through the drawing out of Binah and Chesed it is called or, a hint at raz [207]; and Tiferet is called "light" when he is drawn from the right; and Malkhut is called orah, which means or Heh [the light of Heh], when she receives from Tiferet from the side of Chesed, as we explained:

Further, Tiferet is called the stored-away light [אור גנוז, or ganuz]. And he is so called when he is stored away and concealed and is revealed only to the Righteous One; and through him it is said, "the light stored away for the righteous"; and his storing away is for the world to come, which is Binah, as is known. And the five lights mentioned are included with him in the secret of the fifty gates that are in Binah, the world to come. And below them there is no light, but a firmament, which is Yesod; and it is the firmament [above] the heads of the living creatures that are in Malkhut. And of it it is said, "And God set them in the firmament of the heavens" (Gen. 1:17), for it is the firmament that stores away all that is above it. All this is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 38), and these are its words: "'The awesome' is the central pillar; and shurek is concealed and stored away from the side of the Righteous One, who is the covenant, the stored-away light, which is raz [207], the number of or; as the masters of the Mishnah established, 'Light is sown [zarua] for the righteous one' (Ps. 97:11); and this is the light stored away for the righteous. For the five [mentions of] light above it are all revealed":

Further, there is wondrous light [אור מופלא, or mufla], and it is the supernal Keter; and it is so called because it is wondrous and covered from every eye. And some explained that Chokhmah too is called "wondrous light," because it is wondrous and covered from the eye of all that is below it. And it seems to me that when the first three are united and concealed in the secret of Keter, which is called Pele [Wonder], then all of them are called "wondrous light," each and every one, for they are concealed and covered from the other sefirot. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in Sefer ha-Shem that Yesod too is called "wondrous light," for it is sometimes concealed from Malkhut. And likewise there are clear light [or tzach], sparkling light [or mitnotzetz] and refined light [or metzuchtzach]; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that they are in Binah; and the matter of these lights we explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. And some called Chesed white light, in the secret of the whiteness of compassion and Chesed; and Gevurah they called red light, in the secret of the redness of judgment; and Binah is called "sparkling light," and likewise Malkhut, because they turn over to judgment and to compassion. And some called Hod exalted light [or me'uleh], for it is exalted and glorified in its great splendor [hod], to do judgment and to fight battles; and they called Netzach burning light [or ha-yakod], for the reason that its sphere is Venus, which brings burning love into the heart of the one who longs. And likewise he said that Keter is called inner light and shining light: "inner" for the reason that it is inner and stored away from the light of the sefirot; and "shining" for the reason that it shines and gives light to all the sefirot; and concealed light, for the reason that it is concealed in the utmost concealment:

Treasury [אוצר, otzar]: with this word there is the treasury of life. And it is possible in many places, and all of them for one reason: either in Binah, and she is the treasury for the life of Chokhmah, as it is written (Eccl. 7:12), "wisdom gives life to those who have it"; and likewise it is possible in Tiferet, and likewise in Yesod, and likewise in Malkhut. And likewise the treasury of the souls applies to all of them, and likewise His good treasury (Deut. 28:12); and it would mean a treasury for the good, or a treasury that is called good. And the most fitting is in the two Hehs, which are palaces for the two males:

Way [אורח, orach]: it is the way that shines into many worlds concealed in Keter; and from it they are emanated into many ways and go out to Tiferet. So it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Naso, in the Idra. And there are strange ways on the side of the left, and they are called "crooked ways" (Judg. 5:6):

Sign [אות, ot]: everywhere, "sign," and likewise "it" [oto], is in Yesod, for it is the sign of the covenant. And so it is explained in many places in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 34). And in Parashat Vayera (fol. 112), these are his words: "[What is] 'and it' [ve-oto]? This is the holy sign [at] of the covenant, a sign for ever." The explanation of "a sign for ever": a sign from the side of the Vav. And likewise signs are Vavs. And likewise there is a sign for good and a sign for ill: for good from the side of Chesed and compassion, a sign for ill from the side of Gevurah; and from the side of Tiferet it is called "a long sign," for it is the intermediate, the long world. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 257): "The Shekhinah is called the sign of the covenant from the side of Yesod, the Righteous One of the world." And there he explained that the sign is a Yod over a Vav; and the Shekhinah is called ot hi [she is a sign], and Chokhmah is called ot hu [he is a sign], for both of them are called Yods, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations, chapters 3 and 4. And therefore he said that "sign" is Vav; and therefore the Shekhinah, from the side of the Righteous One, is called ot hi, for she is the Yod, a diadem on the head of the Righteous One, who is Vav:

(See the entry Ayin, fol. 72.) Then [אז, az]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is in Chokhmah; and he gave the reason that az in its number is eight, as it is one over seven, from Binah to Yesod. And it is a joining of the One up to the union, inclusive; and it is a hint at the Chet of echad in the reading of the Shema. And of it it is said (Job 28:27), "Then [az] He saw it and declared it," etc.; and that is the seeing of the heart. And it is "the King who alone was exalted from then [me-az]." And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fols. 32 and 33; see there) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that az hints at the joining of two names, which are YHVH Adonai, which are Tiferet and Malkhut, and the joined form  Y A H D V N H Y, which is eight letters. And to this "Then [az] you shall call, and YHVH will answer" (Isa. 58:9) hints. And the explanation of "Then you shall call": when you join the eight [az], at once "and YHVH will answer," He and His court. And they are: "He," Chokhmah, and "His court," Binah. And the two of them "will answer," for they do not cause their Shekhinah to dwell below except out of the union.
And further, there is another az, and it is two names, Ehyeh and YHVH, Binah and Chokhmah; and their union is  Y A H H V Y H H, and that is eight letters, the number of az:

Gone [אזל, azal]: the explanation, going; and it is because she goes sometimes upward and sometimes downward, and is not in a fixed place. And sometimes it is for ill, as in the matter of "the waters are gone [azelu] from the sea" (Job 14:11), which is a parable for the withdrawal of the effluence:

Ear [אזן, ozen]: the explanation, "ears" is a parable for the powers of Gevurah, and they are called "ears"; and in them is the receiving of prayer and of the outcry, as in the matter of "For the ear tries words" (Job 34:3).
And this matter will be explained at length in the book Or Yakar, with the help of Heaven:

Girdle [אזור, ezor] is a parable for Malkhut, who is united with Tiferet above Netzach and Hod: "As the girdle cleaves to the loins of a man," etc. (Jer. 13:11). The loins are Netzach and Hod, the man is Tiferet, the girdle is Malkhut:

Hyssop [אזוב, ezov]. Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Metzora (fol. 53), and these are his words: "Hyssop is the small Vav, which nourishes the Assembly of Israel." Thus far his words. And he spoke at length there in its explanation. And the intent is that the Righteous One, the foundation of the world, is called "hyssop" when he bestows to Malkhut and is united with her:

Brother [אח, ach] is Tiferet, for he is brother to Malkhut; and he is called "brother" from the side of Chesed. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 56, fol. 87), and these are his words: "There Vav is called brother."

And further, he is called ach when he is included of nine sefirot, down to Malkhut; and so he is ach: Alef, the supernal Keter; Chet [8], eight sefirot, from Chokhmah to Yesod. All this is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna and in the Tikkunim. Further, it explained there (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Mishpatim, fol. 115) that he is "a brother far off" (Prov. 27:10) when he withdraws to Binah, and he is far from Malkhut:

One [אחד, echad]: Tiferet and Malkhut are so called when they are together, included of the ten sefirot. For ach is nine, as we explained; and the Dalet is the Shekhinah; and the tip of the Dalet is Yesod, which unites them together. And this is "One": Tiferet and Malkhut together; and Tiferet without Malkhut is not called "One." And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 7), and these are its words: "We have learned: echad, what is echad? This is the Assembly of Israel, who holds [achidat] to the Holy One, blessed be He. For Rabbi Shimon said: the coupling of male and female is called One. In the place where the female dwells, it is called One. What is the reason? Because a male without a female is called half a body, and a half is not one; and when they are joined together, two halves become one body," etc.
And this matter will be explained by what we explained in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon, chapters 4 and 5:

Behind and back parts [אחור ואחוריים, achor ve-achorayim]: all of it is in Malkhut. Indeed, she is called "back parts" because she is the back of the Emanation; so Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained. However, he explained that only her last levels are called "back parts." And likewise he explained "the levels of the Shekhinah," and explained them as the levels that are below the Shekhinah, and they are her hosts. And likewise the word "behind me" [acharai], as in "And I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing," etc. (Ezek. 3:12):

Seize [אחז, achaz]: every term of seizing [achizah] is the cleaving of the branch that cleaves to what it branches from, as in the matter of "Seize [echezu] for us the foxes" (Song 2:15); and this is the cleaving of the left ones to the edges of the Tabernacle:

After these things [אחר הדברים, achar ha-devarim]: he explained in the Zohar, in the portion of the Binding (fol. 119), that it is a hint at the husk and the accuser. And he explained that "things" [devarim] is Malkhut, and what is after her is the husk and Samael. And so he explained in Parashat Vayeshev (fol. 189):

End [אחרית, acharit]: Binah is called so, for she is the end of all, in the secret of the Jubilee; and this is the "end" mentioned in Sefer Yetzirah. And there is another end, and it is "the end of days" [acharit ha-yamim], and it is Malkhut, when she is included with all her hosts, bad and good. And so he explained in the Tikkunim that she is the end for the supernal Chokhmah; and this is "declaring the end from the beginning" (Isa. 46:10), for Chokhmah is called "beginning." And likewise in the Zohar (Ki Tetze, fols. 189 and 130) Rabbi Chiyya, of blessed memory, explained: "'The end of days' is the whole tree, from its head to its end, which is the tree of good and evil," etc.; and there the intent is the Shekhinah, as is explained there. And in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei Mot (fol. 65), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the time of the rising of the dawn is called "the end of the sea" [acharit yam] (Ps. 139:9): the explanation, after the time of Malkhut, who is called "sea" [yam]. And the beginning of her time is from midnight onward, and her end is at the end of the night, as the dawn rises:

One [אחת, achat, feminine]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is in Binah; and she is called achat for the reason that she is one over the seven days of the Structure; and it is the secret of the number of the sprinklings of the Day of Atonement. Thus far his words.

And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Behar, fol. 108b) he explained that each and every one of the first three is called achat; and these are his words: "And Binah is one, and the lower Shekhinah seven, and above Binah one and one: behold, ten," etc. Thus far. And so it is proved in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 102). And the reason is that all three of them are seen in each one of them, in the matter of the aspects, as we explained in the preceding gates. And therefore we relate to each one of them the name achat: that is to say, all three that are seen in it are counted as one, and all are united:

Gently [אט, at], as in the matter of "and I gently [ve-at] fed him" (Hos. 11:4), and likewise "and I will lead on gently [le-itti]" (Gen. 33:14), and everything like it, is a title for Malkhut, who is one and receives from nine sefirot; and that is Alef-Tet [1 and 9]:

Bramble [אטד, atad]: it is understood from the words of the Zohar in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 249) that Malkhut, from the side of Gevurah and the harsh judgment, is called atad. And likewise atad in numerical value is fourteen, yad [hand]: that is, the left hand, Malkhut from the side of Gevurah: "Your hand [yadkhah]," a hand [yad] of koh [Heh]. And likewise dod comes to fourteen; and it is "a pricking brier" (Ezek. 28:24) for His enemies. And as in the matter (that he explained there): to tell you, what is this bramble? On every side of it there are many thorns and many briers; so the harsh judgment, on every side and quarter, has many harshnesses of judgment, many angels of judgment, and many who go to the left:

Where [אי, ei]. Rashbi explained (in Tikkun 19, fol. 40), on the verse "Where [ei] is Abel your brother?" (Gen. 4:9): "Come and see: these two letters withdrew from him, for by them he sinned; they caused him death: Alef, the wondrous and covered Amon; Yod, Thought." To hint that because of the iniquity these two withdrew from bestowing to Binah:

Terrible [איום, ayom], in the matter of "terrible and dreadful" (Hab. 1:7). The commentators explained ayom as Malkhut; but it is only in Tiferet, from the side of Gevurah. And Malkhut from the side of Gevurah is called ayummah ["terrible as an army with banners," Song 6:4]:

How [איך, eikh], and likewise eikhah, is a title for Malkhut when she draws nourishment from the side of judgment, where the desolation is; and its matter is "How [eikhah] has [the Lord] covered with a cloud" (Lam. 2:1). And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained it as ei koh [where is Koh?], as one lamenting over her:

Tree [אילן, ilan]. In the Tikkunim (Tikkun 49, fol. 83) he explained that Binah is called the root of the tree; and it is plain that she is the root of the direct light, while Malkhut is the root of the returning light. And this is your sign: ilan in numerical value is the name YHVH [and] Adonai [91]. Further, the name YHVH combined into the twelve havayot comes to a sum of 312; so ilan in its filling is twelve letters, Alef-Lamed-Peh, Yod-Vav-Dalet, Lamed-Mem-Dalet, Nun-Vav-Nun, and comes to 312. And "He is not a body, nor a power in a body" [eino guf ve-lo ko'ach be-guf] comes to 312, to hint at this true secret. Further, Rashbi explained in Parashat Pinchas: the upper tree is Binah, and the lower Malkhut:

A loving hind [אילת אהבים, ayelet ahavim] (Prov. 5:19) is Malkhut; and she is called "hind" in the secret of the renewal of the moon. And the horns are high, and they are the horns of splendor that she has from the side of the renewal, like this [figure not reproduced]; and sometimes one is higher than the other, like this [figure not reproduced]. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 248). And the explanation is according to her renewal: if she receives equally from the right as from the left, and her renewal is equal from the two places, then the horns are equally high. And if she receives more from the side of the right, and the right prevails over the left, then one horn is higher than the other; and then she is called "a loving hind," in the secret of the love of Chesed that prevails over her. And when the side of the left prevails more, then she is called "the hind of the dawn" [ayelet ha-shachar] (Ps. 22:1), on account of the blackness [shacharut] and the sorrow that she has in the exile. And there he further explained the reason she is called "hind": for the reason that the hind distributes food to all her companions; and so it is said, "and gives food to her household and a portion to her maidens" (Prov. 31:15). And likewise it is called ayyal [hart]; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 68), on the verse "As the hart pants after the water brooks" (Ps. 42:2). And in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 138), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and these are his words: "'My strength [eyaluti]' (Ps. 22:20): just as the hart and the gazelle, at the time that they go and go far off, at once return to that place that they left, so the Holy One, blessed be He, although He withdraws on high, on high, to the Ein Sof, at once returns to His place. What is the reason? Because Israel below hold on to Him and do not let Him be forgotten by them or go far from them." Thus far his words. According to the sense of his words, it appears that he said it of Tiferet. But the Tav of eyaluti is difficult for us, for it shows a title of the female; and it is possible that it means "his hind." And its explanation would be of Malkhut, as in the saying of the Ra'aya Meheimna and the saying of the Zohar (Parashat Acharei). And there is no wonder at the words "the Holy One, blessed be He," for this name too is related to Malkhut. Also in Parashat Acharei (there) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the word eyalot: "they are all those hinds that surround the precious, holy Throne; as it is written, 'sixty mighty men are round about it' (Song 3:7)." Thus far. Because of this we did not wish to explain the saying "My strength: just as the hart and the gazelle," etc., so that the intent would be Binah:

Terror [אימתה, eimatah], and likewise eimah: all of it is in Gevurah. And on the words "terror and dread" (Exod. 15:16) he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Beshalach (fol. 59), that eimatah is Tiferet; and the proof is the Tav, which is Tiferet. And it cannot be denied that this is Tiferet from the side of Gevurah:

Nothing [אין, Ayin]: all agreed that this title is in Keter. And it is so called for the reason that there is no apprehension there at all; and to one who asks about it, they will answer him: the apprehension of it is Nothing. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained a further reason: in a known language they call the beginning ayin, and so it is the beginning of every beginning. However, the author of Sefer ha-Orah explained, and these are his words: "Alef, the secret of the tip of the Yod, the world of compassion, Ehyeh. Yod, the secret of the world of Chokhmah, the spreading out of the Thought, the first letter of the Name. Final Nun, the secret of the drawing out of the effluence of blessing and compassion from sefirah to sefirah until they reach the sefirah of Malkhut." Thus far his words.

And behold, he intended to include all ten sefirot in Ayin. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 42, fol. 79), close to this matter, these are its words: "The wondrous and covered Amon, which is Ayin, includes three sefirot: Alef, Keter; Yod, Chokhmah; Nun, Binah." Thus far his words.

Behold, it is explicit that Ayin is not in Keter alone; rather [it is] as those who say that it is the first three, and those who say that it is in all ten. And there is one who explained that in Ayin the Alef is Ehyeh, the Yod YHVH, and the Nun is in Malkhut, which is Adonai:

Ein Sof [אין סוף, ein sof] is a hint at the Cause of causes; and the intent is that there is no limit and no end to His exaltedness, and there is nothing that includes Him. And this name is sometimes related to Keter (as is written in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 258); and the reason is that Keter is a throne for the Ein Sof, that is, the first, uppermost throne, above which there is no other throne. And because the Ein Sof rides upon it and is concealed within it, it is called Ein Sof; and it is so called only from the side of the upper aspect, which is united with and cleaves to the Ein Sof. And we have already explained what is sufficient on this name in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter:

Ephah [איפה, eifah]: the explanation, the language of a measure; that is, the ephah is the husk, as in the matter of "they were carrying the ephah" (Zech. 5:10), where it is a title for the husk. And likewise the word eifo, as in the matter of "Who then [eifo]?" (Gen. 27:33), where our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained that Gehinnom entered with him. And sometimes it is related to Malkhut, but from the side of anger and judgment. And every matter of eifah is derived from this, from the side of judgment and the strong fire [afiyah, baking]; and the chief of the bakers [sar ha-ofim] is like Samael, the chief of the accusers:

Alef-Yod-Kof [אי"ק, ik]. The commentators explained: if there is no Alef there is no Yod, and if there is no Yod there is no Kof; and this is in the secret of Kohen, Levi and Yisrael. Keter is the Kohen, Chokhmah the Levi, and Binah Yisrael. If so, Israel are obliged to complete a hundred blessings each day; and of the hundred they give ten to the Levite, which is the first tithe; and the Levite gives one to the Kohen, the tithe of the tithe. And if so, if they do not complete a hundred blessings each day, Keter, which is the Kohen, will not give effluence to the Levite, which is Chokhmah; and if there is no effluence for Chokhmah there is no effluence for Binah, from which Israel draws nourishment. And this is the secret of Alef-Yod-Kof: if there is no Kof there is no Yod, and if there is no Yod there is no Alef. Another explanation: if there is no Kof (the explanation, Kof in its filling [Kof-Vav-Peh] comes to 186, the number of makom), for she is called Makom [Place]; that is to say, if Israel do not keep the Oral Torah, which is a hint at Makom, effluence will not come from the supernal Chokhmah, which is called Yod, and it is the Written Torah; and if there is no Written Torah there is no Alef, which is the supernal Keter. And this is the secret of Alef-Yod-Kof: for the Alef hints at the self of the attribute in its root, in its oneness, which is one equal point in which there is no revealing. And from the self of its truth spread out ten points, for it is included of ten; and these ten points are a garment for the middle point, like this (the figure is missing). And further these ten points spread out, and each one is included of ten, and they are a hundred; and those hundred are a garment for the ten points, in the form drawn above. For the relation of the one to the ten is as the relation of the ten to the hundred; and just as the ten are branches covering the root, so the hundred are branches covering their root, for they are a garment for the root. And this is the secret of Kohen, Levi, Yisrael, in the secret of the camp of Israel being a garment for the camp of the Levites, and the camp of the Levites a garment for the camp of the priesthood, that is, the camp of the Shekhinah. And this is the secret of "the priests at their service, the Levites at their song and their music, and Israel at their station." And that is the secret of Keter, the middle point, revealed in Chokhmah, and Chokhmah revealed in Binah; so Binah is found to be a garment for Chokhmah, and Chokhmah a garment for Keter. And this relation [holds for] Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; and this relation for Netzach, Hod, Yesod; and this relation for Keter, Tiferet and Malkhut:

Man [איש, ish]: this name is in Tiferet, as is usual, as it is written, "YHVH is a man [ish] of war" (Exod. 15:3), etc., and YHVH is in Tiferet. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 49, fol. 85b), these are its words: "'By the greatness of might [onim]' (Isa. 40:26): this is the supernal Keter. 'And because He is strong [ammitz] in power [ko'ach]': this is Chokhmah. What is its power? The supernal Mother. 'Not one [ish] is missing': it is the totality of three sefirot. What is ish? 'YHVH is a man [ish] of war, YHVH is His name.' Ish: Alef, the supernal Keter; Yod, Chokhmah; Shin, the root of the tree, which is the supernal Mother, Repentance [Teshuvah] certainly." And at first sight it is understood that he disagrees with what was explained, that ish is in Tiferet, and his view is that it is in the first three. And one must be precise: he had already explained the first three in the earlier verse, so why should he expound them again in the name?

And further, in saying "What is ish? 'YHVH is a man of war,'" etc., it appears that his intent is to say that "YHVH is a man of war" is in its plain sense in Tiferet, as he explained in many places of the Zohar. Further, why did he double his language, saying "the root of the tree," and afterward "Mother," and afterward "Repentance"? And the matter is that first he expounded in the verse the first three in themselves, and said "'By the greatness of might': this is the supernal Keter"; for onim means powers, the language of strength, and it is the greatest of the powers of the emanated powers. "'And because He is strong in power': this is Chokhmah": the explanation, the one that strengthens and makes strong the power, which is Binah, as will be explained in its entry; and this is what he said, "What is its power?": the explanation, the power that receives from its strength. Or it may mean that Chokhmah is the strong hero, that is, strength in potential and not in act; and its power, which is the act that goes out from the strong one, is Binah; and this is what he said, "What is its power?" etc. "'Not one [ish] is missing': it is the totality," etc.: the explanation, for it is not literally the first three, which have already been expounded; but they are a manifestation included in the first three, and it is called ish, as we shall explain. "What is ish?" etc.: the intent is that since ish is not literally the first three, but a totality included of them, if so, what is ish? The explanation: where is it, in which of the attributes? And he explained it from the verse that said "YHVH is His name," that is, Tiferet, which is the four-letter name, as is well known. "Ish: Alef, the supernal Keter," etc.: he comes to explain how the first three are included in the word ish. "Shin, the root of the tree": it was difficult for him that Shin does not hint at Binah but at the three Patriarchs, that is, three Vavs. To this he says that Binah is the root of the tree: the explanation, the root and source of the three Patriarchs, which are the branches of the tree. And if so, it is possible that Shin hints at Binah, to show the place of the emanation of the extremities from within Binah, and their root, their manifestation and their subtle source concealed in her, as explained in the preceding gates. And because the root of the tree is also in Yesod or in Malkhut, as we explained in the Gate From Below to Above, he therefore said "the supernal Mother": for Binah is called Mother with respect to the fact that in her all the emanated ones from her downward came into being, and she is the mother and their true root. And because the word "Mother" does not prove this matter well, he said "Repentance," to show that she is the root of the branches, and there is the return [teshuvah] of things to their root, in the secret of the Jubilee; and likewise teshuvah shows that she returns [shavah] over the children to suckle them and bestow on them, as we shall explain in its entry:

The sum of the matter is that the hint is in Tiferet, when he includes the first three. And so this matter is explained in Sefer ha-Bahir, and these are its words: "Rabbi Amorai said: What is it that is written, 'YHVH is a man of war'? Rabbi Rechumai bar Bivi said to him: Do not ask about it; the matter is simple. Listen to me and I will counsel you. A parable: to what is the matter like? To a king who had fine dwellings, and he set a name for each one of them, etc., this one better than that one. He said: I will give to my son this dwelling, whose name is Alef; and also this one is good, whose name is Yod. What did he do? He gathered all three of them together, and made of them one name, and made of them one house. He said to him: How long will you close up your words? He said to him: My son, Alef is the head; Yod is second to it; Shin includes the whole world, because repentance [teshuvah] is written in it." Thus far its words.

And the explanation: for Rabbi Amorai the whole verse was difficult, in saying "YHVH is a man of war"; for YHVH is Tiferet, and it is a doubling; and further, the reason why Tiferet is called ish. And Rabbi Rechumai answered with a fine parable, of a king who had fine dwellings: the intent is the Emanation, which is a dwelling in which its Emanator dwells; and he called them "fine" to hint at the highest ones, which precede all that is emanated from Him, may He be blessed, and they are the ones that go out first from before Him. "And he set a name for each one of them": the explanation, "name" is a garment and a palace, as we shall explain in its entry; and the intent is that He made a palace for the spirituality of that attribute, as we explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels.

And behold, the self is called "dwelling," and the vessels are called "name," and throne, and garment for the aforementioned dwelling. "And all of them, this one better than that one": the explanation, although the three sefirot are concealed, nevertheless each one rises above its fellow; for the three of them are not equal, but rise in level each one above its fellow, from effect to cause, as is known. "He said: I will give to my son": the explanation, the son is Tiferet, called ben [son], meaning a branch; and "to my son" means the branches that branch out from the Ein Sof and are emanated from Him; for all ten names are emanated from Him, and the names and the sefirot are all one, as is explained. And the intent is that He emanated three manifestations from the three upper sefirot, Keter, Alef, Chokhmah, Yod, and Binah, Shin, and brought into being from them one name and one garment; for these three manifestations He included together and made a garment for Tiferet, and that is shem [name], as we explained; and that is the "one house" that he spoke of. And because of the force of the figure of this parable, he asked him to explain his words. And he explained that Alef is the head, which is Keter, which is the head of all heads; Yod is second to it, which is Chokhmah; and the Shin is Binah. And he said "includes the whole world," as it is known that Binah is the secret of everything concealed, for in her all the sefirot are included, the six extremities, in the secret of the whole circuit, which is what is called "world" [olam], as will be explained in its entry. And this is "and he shall serve him for ever [le-olam]" (Exod. 21:6): the olam of the Jubilee. And he asked: and why does Shin include the whole world, which means the whole circuit, more than the two preceding sefirot? And he answered, "because repentance [teshuvah] is written in it": it means, because there is the root of all six extremities, and there is the return, in the secret of the Jubilee, as we explained. And this is the reason for relating Shin to this attribute, as we explained above.

And behold, we have learned from this that Tiferet, when he includes the first three, is called ish; and so it is explained in the Tikkunim in many places. And so he explained in the book Me'irat Einayim, Parashat Miketz: "Ish is the hint of Keter, Chokhmah and Binah; and Tiferet is called ish by their name, for all his actions are by the power of the Thought." Thus far his words. And there is no doubt that he is called ish in the secret of his drawing nourishment from judgment, as it is written, "YHVH is a man of war," as we explained in the entry adam. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained "a man of war" as Gevurah. And it is possible that the intent is ish in Tiferet when he draws nourishment from Gevurah, and therefore he is called "a man of war," as we explained. And in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 59), he explained that Yesod is called "the man of the earth" (Gen. 9:20), which is Malkhut. And it is explained: all that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph:

Enduring [איתן, eitan] is a title for the strength of Gevurah, as in the matter of "an enduring stream" (Deut. 21:4). And according to what appears from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, eitan is a title for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, in his attribute, as in the matter of "And he looked on the Kenite and said, Enduring [eitan] is your dwelling place" (Num. 24:21) (as is written in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 238b):

Only [אך, akh] is explained as Malkhut. And it is right on a condition: that is, when her nourishment is either from the right alone or from the left alone, everything according to the context; for akh is half of the name of forty-two [Alef-Kaf = 21]. And therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Pesachim 5a): "akh divides." And it is possible that it is so from the side of Keter, for it comes to twenty-one, the name Ehyeh; and the name of the long final Kaf is from the side of Binah:

Akhtariel [אכתריאל, akhtari'el]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] gives this name as a title to Malkhut, and he said that this is the one (mentioned in Berakhot 7a) who said to Rabbi Ishmael, "Ishmael, my son, bless Me." And he meant: bless me from the source of the blessings; and therefore he said "from before You" and did not say "before You." And for us it is a hint at Beriah, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 2; and it is called Akhtariel, the language of keter [crown], because it binds crowns for its Master, in the way we explained there (see there); and further, it is a crown for all that are formed and made:

To [אל, el]: the explanation, the el that is not holy, as in "and he went for [el] his life" (1 Kings 19:3), and "and to [el] Moses He said" (Exod. 24:1), and many like it: all of them are in the world of the male. And this is the difference between el and et: that el is in the world of the male, and et is in the world of the female. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayigash (fol. 209), on the verse "and he went for his life"; see there:

God of thanksgivings [אל ההודאות, El ha-hoda'ot]: the commentators explained it as Hod; and every place where the language of thanksgiving [hoda'ah] is found, it is a hint at this attribute. And likewise God Most High [א"ל עליון, El Elyon]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Keter is called El Elyon because it is uppermost [elyon] over the whole Emanation; and certainly it is so called only when it acts in Chesed; and likewise it is called "supernal Chesed," as will be explained in its entry. And we have already explained in the Gate of Names, chapter 5, the name El Elyon and El Melekh; and there we explained that the name El is always in Chesed. And in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 87), on the verse "And Melchizedek king of Salem" (Gen. 14:18), he explained El Elyon as Binah. And it is possible that the word is well known: the one uppermost over El, and that is Binah, which is uppermost over Chesed, which is called El. Further, there is El Shaddai [א"ל שדי]: it is a hint at the joining of Yesod and Malkhut; and the matter of Shaddai in Malkhut has already been explained in the Gate of Names. And El is the language of strength; and the explanation: it bestows with the strength of its compassion, compassion on Malkhut, until their lips wear out from saying "Enough" [dai]; so the commentators explained. And it seems to me that El Shaddai is the union of Keter and Malkhut, for Keter is sometimes called El; and there is some support for this from the Zohar (Lekh, fol. 88), and these are its words: "Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see: before Abraham was circumcised, there was one level speaking with him; and which is it? This is the Vision [machazeh], as it is written, 'who sees the vision of Shaddai' (Num. 24:4). Once he was circumcised, all the levels rested upon this level, and then it spoke with him; as it is written, 'And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, as El Shaddai' (Exod. 6:3). And before he was circumcised, those levels did not rest upon it to speak." Thus far his words. And he spoke further at length there on the matter, and this will suffice for our purpose. And the intent is that while Abraham was not yet circumcised, the level of his prophecy was only from Malkhut alone, without the joining of another attribute; and this aspect is called machazeh; and this is what he said, "and which is it? This is the Vision." And he proved the matter from the verse "who sees the vision of Shaddai." And one must not say that Balaam attained in his prophecy the level of holiness, God forbid; and although he said "who sees the vision of Shaddai," the intent is the vision of [the side of] Shaddai, and not that the Vision of Shaddai appeared to him, God forbid. And likewise with respect to Abraham: the vision of the upper ones, and not the upper ones themselves. And there is a great difference between them, for they have no joining together, God forbid: for Abraham's prophecy was in Malkhut, which is the Vision of the upper sefirot; but in Balaam it is the vision of Shaddai, that is, the husks, which are beneath Malkhut, who is called Shaddai, for she overpowers [meshadded] them. And one must not object from the verse "the saying of him who hears the words of El" (Num. 24:4), for it is explained in the Zohar that this is another El. And we return to our matter: after he was circumcised, he attained to look in his prophecy from the side of Malkhut, in her aspect when all the attributes are seen in her; and then she is called El Shaddai: El in Keter, and Shaddai in Malkhut. And this is "I am the first and I am the last" (Isa. 44:6), from the head to the end. The principle is that Malkhut is called El Shaddai when she is included of all the upper attributes. And it is possible to explain that, since this binding and this inclusion are by means of Yesod, Malkhut is called Shaddai by the name of Yesod, which is the principal one in the name Shaddai, as explained in the Gate of Names, chapter 13. And there is support for this explanation from the Zohar there, in saying: "the covenant, the binding of all, is bound in it; and therefore," etc.; see there. And it is explained in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 247) that et Shaddai (Gen. 49:25) is more praise and compassion than saying El Shaddai. Because Malkhut is called et when she receives from Tiferet, who is called the Written Torah; and she is included from Alef to Tav. And Tiferet receives from Chokhmah; so Malkhut is found to receive the thirty-two paths from Chokhmah by means of Tiferet. And this is certainly more praise than saying "and El Shaddai," even though El is a holy name and et is a particle; and even though the name El Shaddai includes from beginning to end, as we explained. Nevertheless et Shaddai is more praiseworthy, because it is in itself the thirty-two paths that she receives from Tiferet by means of Chokhmah; and the Torah is included from Alef to Tav, and in it the ten sefirot are also included:

Further, a jealous God [אל קנא, El kanna]: and he explained that it is Hod; and all jealousy is from the side of the strength of the heart and its might, to be jealous over sins. And it is possible that it is so called when it is filled from Gevurah; and therefore it is possible to explain it in the ways that we explained for "the mighty God" [ha-El ha-gibbor] in the Gate of Names:

Curse [אלה, alah], as in the matter of "for because of the curse [alah] the land mourns" (Jer. 23:10), that is, the matter of the oath through the curse, as in the matter of "the curses of the covenant" (Deut. 29:20); and there is no doubt that it is in Malkhut from the side of judgment and Gevurah. And there is elah, the language of a tree [terebinth], and it too is in Malkhut. And it is possible that it is from the side of the strong judgment, and therefore the terebinth does not make fruit. And for this Jacob our father, peace be upon him, hid the foreign gods under the terebinth that was by Shechem (Gen. 35:4). And allon [oak] is the masculine of elah, as he said, "as a terebinth and as an oak" (Isa. 6:13). And it is possible to explain it in the matter of elleh [these], which are the three Patriarchs (see below in the entry elleh):

Idol [אליל, elil], as in the matter of "Do not turn to the idols [elilim]" (Lev. 19:4), and likewise "physicians of no value [elil]" (Job 13:4), and the like: all of it is a parable for the husks, which are "another god" [el acher], as is known. And likewise there is an el that is such, as "who hears the words of El" (Num. 24:4), that is, another el; and likewise "to El I have spoken." And likewise there is the name Eloah in this way, as he said, "to him who brings his god [eloah] in his hand" (Job 12:6); and so it is explained in the Zohar: that is, the spirit of impurity that rests on the hands:

These [אלה, elleh]. In the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 236), he explained on the verse "These [elleh] are your gods, O Israel" (Exod. 32:4), and these are his words: "And this impure spirit is the evil serpent; and there is one who rides upon it; and they are male and female, and they are called elleh, for they are ready in the world on all their sides." Thus far his words. He spoke further at length there on their blemish, and we have shortened it, for the little holds the much. And the explanation of his words is that for the reason that they make themselves ready of themselves to do evil, they are called elleh; for the word elleh shows that they are always ready, male and female, in their bands and evil companies, to do evil, may the Compassionate One save us. And just as there is elleh on the side of the husk, so there is elleh on the side of holiness; and they are the three Patriarchs: Chesed, Din, Rachamim, [that is,] Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. And of them it is said (Isa. 40:26), "Who created these [mi bara elleh]?", as explained in the Gate of Names.

And further, there is in holiness a second elleh, and they are Netzach, Hod, Yesod; and they are branches of the supernal Chesed, judgment and compassion, as explained in the preceding gates. And this is the secret: "These [elleh] are your gods, O Israel" is husk; "These [elleh] are the accounts of the Tabernacle" (Exod. 38:21) is holiness; though in Parashat Pekudei it is expounded the other way round.
