So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained elsewhere (perhaps hinting at what is written in Parashat Pekudei, fol. 221a); and there are seventy faces to the Torah:

Eloah [אלוה, eloah]: he explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Vayikra (fol. 23), and these are his words: "Eloah: El, this is Abraham, of whom it is written 'the great God [ha-El]'; Vav, this is the Holy One, blessed be He; Heh, this is the Assembly of Israel. And this is Eloah." Thus far his words.

And this is the intent: that in this name Gedulah, Tiferet and Malkhut are included; and accordingly this name is simple compassion. And likewise it is expounded in Parashat Lekh (fol. 94), and these are its words: "Eloah is thus: El is the light of Chokhmah; Vav, male; Heh, female. They are joined together and it is called Eloah." And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 120b) he wrote that the name Eloah is in Chesed, and proved the matter from the verse "Eloah comes from Teman" (Hab. 3:3). And the commentators said that it is in Tiferet. And who will speak after the lion?

Eli [אלי, eli, My God] is everywhere Binah, and likewise it comes to em [mother, 41]. And she is so called when she is included of the first three: Alef, Keter; Yod, Chokhmah; Lamed, Binah. And the reason for the Lamed in the middle is that the Alef corresponds to the aspect that she has from the side of Keter, and the Yod corresponds to the aspect that she has from the side of Chokhmah, and the Lamed is included in the middle, from the aspect of herself. And we have already spoken at length on this in the Gate of Arbiters. And the explanation of this word Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 55, fol. 86b). And there is no doubt that when there are two times "Eli, Eli" (Ps. 22:2), it hints at the two mothers, upper and lower, in the secret of Ayin [Nothing] and Ani [I]; so it seems to me:

Elisheva [אלישבע, elisheva]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemini (fol. 38), that Malkhut is called Elisheva because she draws nourishment from seven [sheva] upper attributes. And there is a great difference between Bat Sheva and Elisheva: for she is called Elisheva from the side of Chesed, and Bat Sheva from the side of Gevurah. And so they explained there; and likewise it is understood that Eli is from the side of Chesed, which is called El:

Chief [אלוף, alluf]: Tiferet is so called because he is the chief [alluf] and the husband of the youth of Malkhut (Jer. 3:4); and he is so called when he is in union with her, as it appears. And it is possible that he is so called because he bears the burden of the blessing, from the language of "our oxen [allufenu] are laden" (Ps. 144:14). And it is possible that he is so called when he draws nourishment from the side of Gevurah, which is called by the name "ox." Or it is possible that he is so called from the language of greatness and mastery; and he is so called when he draws nourishment from the side of Keter, which is Alef [alef]. And all these explanations settle well on him, and all of them when he is united with Malkhut; for then he draws nourishment from Gevurah and from Chesed, abundance of blessing, in the secret of "His left hand is under my head," etc., and from Keter, for from there is his principal drawing:

Our God who is in heaven [אלהינו שבשמים, eloheinu she-ba-shamayim] is Binah; and she is so called because her place is in the heavens [shamayim], which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, which are fire [esh] and water [mayim] and their composition together. And after this manner she is also called "our God who is in heaven." And she is called by this name when she bestows into them in particular.
And it is further possible that "heaven" is Tiferet; and it is all one:

The living God [אלהים חיים, Elohim chayyim] is sometimes related to Binah, for the reason that she bestows life on all the sefirot. And life too is from the power of judgment, as the men of the Great Assembly ordained in the blessing of Mighty Deeds, "who revives the dead," and further in the blessing "who formed you in judgment and will in the future revive you in judgment"; and for this reason the resurrection of the dead is with a quaking. And likewise Yesod is called by this name when it receives life from Binah. And when Malkhut receives life from Yesod, she too is called Elohim chayyim.

And further, because she gives life to all that is beneath her. And there is a great difference with Yesod, when it is called El Chai [the living God] or Elohim chayyim: for the one is the secret of life from the side of Chesed, which is called El, and the other from the side of Gevurah, which is called Elohim; though both of them are by means of Binah:

To you [אליך, elekha]: it seems to me that it is the first three: for Alef is Keter, as is known; Yod, Chokhmah; lekha [to you], Binah, as we explained in the entry [Eli] and in the entry li and in the entry lekha:

Your God [אלהיך, Elohekha]: all explain it as Malkhut. And it can already properly be said of Binah or of Gevurah, everything according to its place, for all three of them are called Elohim, certainly, as we explained in the Gate of Names. And some explained it as the whole Emanation; and it is not so:

God of gods [אלהי האלהים, Elohei ha-elohim]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is Tiferet; and it is so called because it is the prince of the seventy princes who surround His throne, and it governs them. And some explained that it includes the whole Emanation: how so? Elohei is Chokhmah and Binah; ha-elohim, the seven days of the Structure. And some explained it as the first three: Keter, Elohei; Chokhmah and Binah, ha-elohim. And above all, what seems to me is that Binah is called "God of gods"; for three Elohim are: the first in Binah, the second in Gevurah, and the third in Malkhut; and the last two depend on Binah, and therefore Binah is called "God of gods." And every name Elohei [God of] is to be explained according to its place: "the God of Abraham," Chesed; "the God of Isaac," Gevurah; "the God of Jacob," Tiferet. And it seems to me that Elohei is the aspect of Malkhut; and sometimes her aspect is from the side of Chesed, and she is called "the God of Abraham"; and so it is said (Gen. 17:22), "And God went up from Abraham." And likewise she was united with him in Gevurah from the side of Isaac, and this is "the God of Isaac"; and likewise everything similar. And some explained "the God of Abraham" as Chokhmah, "the God of Isaac" as Binah: that is, that they were Godhead and soul for Chesed and Gevurah, which are Abraham and Isaac; and likewise "the God of Jacob" Keter and Tiferet. And this suits the order of the blessing, although the title does not settle well:

God of hosts [אלהי הצבאות, Elohei ha-tzeva'ot] means Tiferet, who is over the hosts, which are Netzach and Hod. Or it is possible that it is Malkhut, who draws nourishment from the hosts, Netzach and Hod; and she is sometimes above, in her true place:

A thousand generations [אלף דור, elef dor] is Malkhut; and she is so called because she comes to a thousand, in the secret of the inclusion of the tens. How so? She is included of ten, and each one of the ten is included of ten: they are a hundred; and each one of those hundred is included of ten: they are a thousand. For she is for the generations of the cycle, as in the matter of "a generation goes and a generation comes, and the earth," etc. (Eccl. 1:4). And when she is called "generation" alone will be explained in its entry, with the help of the Name:

Widow [אלמנה, almanah] is Malkhut when Tiferet is not with her. And the intent is that her hundred gates are in darkness, in exile; and that is al maneh, meaning there are not a hundred [maneh] gates. And likewise when she is married her ketubbah is a maneh [a hundred]: that is, the return of the light to the hundred gates (see the entry Adonai above):

Mother [אם, em]: there are two mothers, the upper Mother and the lower Mother. The upper Mother is Binah, and she receives from the Father, who is Chokhmah, and bestows below; and from her all the lower sefirot are emanated, and in her they came into being, like the fetus that comes into being in its mother's womb, as we explained in the Gate of Titles, chapter 3. And when she is called "mother" it shows that she is female and is judgment; for the female without qualification receives, in the secret of the returning light. And sometimes it shows compassion, for she is like the mother who suckles her children with the milk of compassion:

And sometimes she is called the mother of the children [אם הבנים, em ha-banim] (Ps. 113:9); and two explanations are possible in it. The mother of all the children, as in the matter of Leah, who corresponds to Binah and bore six sons and one daughter; and that is the seven sefirot that go out from her and draw nourishment from her. Or possibly two children, son and daughter, Tiferet and Malkhut. And it is all one matter, for Tiferet includes the six extremities; and both these explanations are possible for "the mother of the children." And these are the words of the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 219): "It was taught: Rabbi Isaac said: It is written, 'the joyful mother of the children, Halleluyah' (Ps. 113:9). The Mother is known; the children, who are they? Rabbi Shimon said: We have learned, the Holy One, blessed be He, has two children, one male and one female," etc. And he proved there that it is fitting to explain as the principal [sense] that Tiferet and Malkhut are the children. And perhaps the reason is that when they are in Binah they are all included in the son, who is Tiferet, including the six extremities, and the daughter, who is Malkhut; and that is the Dalet and the Vav in the form of the Heh, Dalet-Vav. And Malkhut too is called "mother," because she is mother to all things that are beneath her, to the end of all the deep; for all of them were created through her, and she is mother to them all, and she brings them into being through Tiferet, who is her husband [ba'al], who is the father [av]. And she is also called "mother" from the side of the souls, for they are all emanated from her through the union, as explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Malkhut is called "mother" from the side of Binah, who is called Mother; and the reason is that through her is the building of the rib, as explained in the Gate of Manifestations. But Binah is called the mother of the souls for the reason that she is the source of the souls, as it is written (Job 32:8), "and the breath [nishmat] of Shaddai gives them understanding [tevinem]," as we explained in the Gate of the Soul. And each one of them is called "the mother of Solomon," as explained in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 248):

Cubit [אמה, ammah] is Tiferet; for every cubit is of six handbreadths, and likewise he is Vav, including the six extremities. And the half cubit is Malkhut, in the secret of the manifestation of the Heh, which is three Vavs, the three colors of the eye, three sefirot, three handbreadths, half a cubit. And she is also a Yod, and two Yods are the measure of a Vav. And by this two sayings of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim are reconciled; and these are his words (Tikkun 19, fol. 39b): "Everywhere, cubit is Vav; and therefore a cubit is of six handbreadths; and the half cubit is Yod. For two Yods are the measure of the cubit, and the letter Yod, its measure is three handbreadths."

Behold, it is explicit that the Heh is the half cubit. And elsewhere (in Tikkun 5, fol. 18) he said, and these are his words: "The cubit is the upper Heh, and the half cubit the lower Heh; 'the length of one curtain' (Exod. 26:2), this is Vav. And why is the lower Heh called the half cubit? Because it is called a broken matzah," etc. And by what we explained, that Yod and Heh are all one matter, it is reconciled: for in the Yod there are three Yods, which are three handbreadths, and likewise in the Heh three sefirot, which are three handbreadths. And therefore she is broken, for she lacks the mingled wine [mezeg], for she is not complete in all her circuit, like this [figure not reproduced], which is the secret of the upper Heh, which is six handbreadths, the six extremities, which are the six days surrounding the middle point, as explained in the preceding gates. However, she is a broken matzah, like this [figure not reproduced], that is, the secret of the half moon. And this will be understood by what we explained in the Gate of Manifestations:

Handmaid [אמה, amah]: "And if a man sells his daughter to be a handmaid" (Exod. 21:7). This matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 13): "The handmaid is the Throne of Beriah, which is a handmaid with respect to the Shekhinah, who is 'the king's daughter within' (Ps. 45:14)." And likewise he explained the matter of the verse "and she sent her handmaid" (Exod. 2:5), etc.:

Amen [אמן, amen]: explanations of it are many, and the principal is the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 35): that Amen is in Yesod, which binds and unites the bridegroom with the bride. And likewise the two names together, YHVH Adonai,  Y A H D V N H Y, come to [the number of] Amen [91]. And through Yesod they are united, as it is written (1 Chron. 29:11), "for all that is in heaven and on earth," and its Targum: "which holds on to heaven and to earth."
And behold, when it does this action it is called Amen, which is a hint at the three of them together: bridegroom and bride and groomsman:
Amon [אמון, amon]: in Bereshit Rabbah (section 1) four explanations of it are given, and these are its words:

"Amon, a tutor; amon, covered; amon, hidden away; amon, great." And they proved these four explanations there from the Scriptures. "Amon, a tutor": the explanation, from the language of omen [nurturer], and it is in Yesod, as we explained above in its entry. "Amon, covered" is in Keter; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in many places that the wondrous and covered Amon is in Keter, because it is concealed. "Amon, hidden away" is Tiferet, in the secret of what is called "the stored-away light," as we explained in its entry, for it is concealed in the supernal Keter. "Amon, great" is Binah. This is what seems to me in the explanation of this saying:

Faith [אמונה, emunah]: the explanation, this title is in two places, each one according to its matter. The first is in Binah, and it is from the matter of faith; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 5), on the verse "And He shall be the faithfulness [emunat] of your times" (Isa. 33:6), and these are his words: "Faith is the supernal Mother, from the side of Chesed, for in her is the reading of the Shema, which is faith." Thus far his words.

And the intent is that the reading of the Shema means the matter of the union of the sefirot, and it is from the side of Chesed; and that is faith, that we believe in His union; and this is in Binah. And there is Faith in Malkhut, and she is so called from the side of the Righteous One, when she is united with the bridegroom. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, there: "The lower Shekhinah is Faith from the side of the Righteous One, in whom two names are included, Amen, which are  Y A H D V N H Y." Thus far his words.

And they said "in whom are included" to hint that she receives the bridegroom upon her by means of Yesod. And these are the words of Rabbi Hezekiah in the Zohar, Parashat Balak (fol. 198b): "At the time that truth [emet] is joined with her for joy, and all the faces shine, then she is called Faith." Thus far his words.

And his words are clear and refined. And in Parashat Pekudei (fol. 223a) he said that the Shekhinah is called Faith for the reason that she receives upon her all the upper streams and brings them out by the number in which she took them in, in faithfulness; and therefore she is called Faith. And it is true that she is called Faith when she is included of them. And this does not disagree with what he explained in Parashat Balak; for through the union of Tiferet with her she receives the upper streams and is included of them, as is known. And in the Tikkunim he explained that from the side of the Cause above all the upper ones she is called the Faith of Israel. And he explained: from the side of her emanation, without the joining of her nourishment from the sefirot, but in the secret of the simplicity of her sefirah, emanated from the Emanator, blessed be He, she is called the Faith of Israel. And the reason appears to be that she is nurtured [amunah] and reared by Chokhmah, in the secret of the supernal Da'at, which is called Israel; and that is the one called Yod, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. Or it is possible to say that in this aspect of hers, which is her selfhood, the manifestation of the Yod, which shows the oneness of the sefirot in the secret of the Yod, a tip above and a tip below and a body in the middle, which shows "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God" (Isa. 44:6) in the middle. And this is the Faith of Israel: to believe in this union and this faith; and this is through the revealing of the Ein Sof in all His attributes through the union (and even on) [of Tiferet with] Malkhut; and through it He watches even over the point of the deep, as explained in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing. And behold, in the secret of this matter she is called the Faith of Israel. And so it is further explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 120b), these are its words: "And therefore he called her the great Faith of Israel; by her the upper ones and the lower ones are known, and the Cause above all the upper ones. And whoever unifies Him in her, it is as if he unifies Him and makes Him king over all the upper ones and the lower ones." Thus far his words.

Behold, it is explicit, as we explained, that on her depends the whole faith of Israel, because on her depends their whole faith, in her union with the Ein Sof; and this is impossible except through the union, for the Ein Sof is not revealed in the sefirot except in the secret of the strong union; and this is one of the special virtues of the union. And the matter is that the Emanation is not complete except in the secret of male and female; and then "male and female He created them, and called their name adam" (Gen. 5:2), complete. And the Ein Sof causes His Shekhinah to dwell only in a complete place, not in a blemished place, God forbid. And therefore the principal thing is through the union, as we explained:

Nurse [אומנת, omenet]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Malkhut is called "nurse" when the nurturer [omen] is within her, for then she nurses and rears everything. But it seems to me that "nurse" is Binah; for so it is said of Naomi (Ruth 4:16), "and she became his nurse." And it is well known that Naomi is in Binah and Ruth in Malkhut; and she is the nurse of the son, who is Vav, as is known:

Amora'im [אמוראים, amora'im]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 42) that the three Patriarchs, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, are called Amora'im, and Netzach, Hod, Yesod are called Tanna'im. And at first sight it would have been fitting to be the reverse, for the Tanna'im are greater than the Amora'im. But it is possible to say that it is in the manner of "understanding" [navon] and "wise" [chakham]: for the understanding one is greater than the wise, though understanding is in Binah and the wise is in Chokhmah. Rather, the reason is that the higher something rises, the less the knowledge of it. And likewise the matter: the Tanna'im are greater than the Amora'im, for they go down to the secret of the depth of the matter; and the Amora'im know the matter as by tradition, without so much revealing of the reason, like the actions of Chesed, Gevurah and Tiferet, the knowledge of whose action is concealed:

Word [אמרת, imrat] is Malkhut, as in "He has fulfilled [bitza] His word [imrato]" (Lam. 2:17); and he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 61): "He tore [bazza] His purple robe": the explanation, a garment. And likewise the Shekhinah is a garment and a palace for Tiferet, for the four-letter name may be mentioned only in its palace, that is, Adonai. And she is called by the language of imra when she is a diadem on the head of her husband, a hint at her being at the head, a top branch [amir], when she draws nourishment from the first three. And the language of imrato is the language of height and exaltation, from the root of "Say [imru] of the righteous that it shall be well" (Isa. 3:10):

Strong [אמיץ, ammitz], as in the matter of "Be strong, and let your heart take courage [ve-ya'ametz]" (Ps. 27:14), and the like: according to what appears from the matter of the verses, it is from the side of the strength of the strong Gevurah, but from the side of Binah, which bestows on it. And the proof is in saying "and strong in power" (Isa. 40:26; Job 9:4), which is the power of Binah (see above in the entry ish):

Saying [אמירה, amirah]: on this the commentators are many. One explained it as Malkhut, and proved it from the verse (Ps. 68:12), "Adonai gives the word [omer]"; and speech [dibbur] [he gave] to the attribute of Gevurah, and brought a proof of this from the verse (Exod. 6:2), "And Elohim spoke to Moses": he mentioned the language of speaking with the name Elohim, which is Gevurah; "and said to him, I am YHVH": he mentioned saying with the word ani [I]. And others explained the reverse: speech in Malkhut and saying in Tiferet. And in the Zohar, in Parashat Vayikra (fol. 17b), on the verse "and all this land that I have said [amarti]" (Exod. 32:13), he explained: "I have willed," that is, the language of will, which is her rising to the Forehead of Will; and he proved this from several verses. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 60), these are its words: "Lemor [saying]: this is the female." It appears explicitly that saying is in Malkhut; and likewise "Thus says YHVH," certainly. And in Parashat Yitro (fol. 83), on the word lemor, Rabbi Isaac explained: "Lemor: this is what is written, 'A woman of valor is the diadem of her husband' (Prov. 12:4); for it is written, 'Lemor: If a man send away [his wife],' etc. (Jer. 3:1)." And this needs explanation; and with precision in his language the explanation of what saying is will emerge for us. And one must be precise: why did he say, "this is what is written, 'A woman of valor,'" etc.? Are the titles of Malkhut too few? Second, what is the matter of his proof from the verse "Lemor: If a man send away," etc.? For in Parashat Noach he did not need a proof at all; and further, on the contrary, from there the reverse appears. And to this we say that the intent of Rabbi Isaac is not to prove to us that the word lemor is in Malkhut, for this is plain. Rather his intent was to say that she is so called when she rises to be a diadem; and therefore he said, "this is what is written, 'A woman of valor is the diadem of her husband'": the explanation, lemor is when she is a diadem on the head of the man. And this is the explanation of lemor: that it is from the language of "You have avouched [he'emarta] YHVH this day ... and YHVH has avouched you [he'emirkha] this day" (Deut. 26:17–18); "Say [imru] of the righteous that it shall be well" (Isa. 3:10); and many like it, which are from the language of exaltation. And the intent is that "these words," etc., were to raise Malkhut to be a diadem on the head of her husband. And he brought the verse that said "Lemor: If he send away," etc., because it was difficult for him, being contrary to his view, for lemor is said of her sending away. And to this he said: on the contrary, from there is a proof that lemor means that she is so called when she is the diadem of her husband, and she is sent away, God forbid; for when she is above, before she is sent away, she is called his wife. And this is what he intended in bringing the verse, as he said: when we look into this verse, on the contrary, we find that it proves our intent and is a proof for us. And now by this the words of the commentators are also right, in saying that saying is in Tiferet, since it is in Malkhut from the side of her being the diadem of her husband. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayera (fol. 102), these are its words: "In every place where it says 'and he said' without qualification, or 'and he called' without qualification, or 'said' without qualification, it is the angel of the covenant and no other. 'And he said,' as it is written, 'And he said, If you will diligently hearken' (Exod. 15:26), and it does not say who it is. 'And he called,' as it is written, 'And he called to Moses' (Lev. 1:1), and it does not say who it is," etc. "So too," etc., "it was the angel of the covenant," etc. Thus far his words.

And he also explained there that "And he said, I will surely return" (Gen. 18:10) is also the Shekhinah, who is called "the angel of the covenant." And it is understood from here that the language of saying is in Malkhut only when it is without qualification, and does not say who. And it is possible that when it says "And YHVH said," the saying is in Malkhut, and the intent is that Tiferet speaks by means of Malkhut; and when the saying is without qualification, it means by means of Malkhut alone. And so he was precise in his language in saying "it is the angel of the covenant and no other": for certainly if it is the angel of the covenant it is none other. Rather the intent is certainly that when it states saying or calling explicitly, the intent is by means of Malkhut. And on the matter of speech we shall speak at length in its entry, with the help of the Name:

AMeSh [אמש, emesh, yesterday]: the explanation, air [avir], water [mayim], fire [esh]. And it is explained as Chesed and judgment, with compassion arbitrating between them. And in Sefer Yetzirah: "Shin hisses, Mem is silent, Alef is breath, the law arbitrating between them." And the explanation is that the pronouncing of Shin is with a hiss, with the lowering of the letter downward, and it hints at the power of judgment; and the pronouncing of Mem is in the likeness of a [closed] Mem, hinting at the power of compassion; and the Alef is intermediate between them, hinting at the arbiter. And some read "Shin hisses, Mem is silent, the tongue," etc., and explained the reverse: for Shin is with a hiss, and as long as the breath is drawn out in it the hiss is drawn out; but Mem is silent, for it is not drawn out but falls silent. And the intent: Shin with a hiss, to hint at judgment, as in the matter of "they hiss and gnash the teeth [shen]" (Lam. 2:16); but Mem in the secret of Chesed, as in the matter of "a still small voice [demamah]" (1 Kings 19:12), from the side of the right and purity. And Alef is always intermediate, arbitrating. And these three letters are hinted at in Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, which are mothers to the whole Emanation; for they are three heads, Chesed, judgment and compassion, and from there three lines spread out, as we spoke at length on this, as much as needed, in the preceding gates. And indeed one says emesh of a day that has passed, which is concealed in these three, which were concealed: as if one said, "today" is Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, morning, evening and noon; and the day that has passed is in the three preceding ones, which are Keter, Chokhmah and Binah, the concealed ones:

Truth [אמת, emet]: all the commentators agreed that this word hints at Tiferet, and it is an explicit verse (Micah 7:20): "You will give truth to Jacob," and Jacob is a chariot for Tiferet. Except for Nachmanides, peace be upon him, from whose words it appears that Yesod is the attribute of Jacob, and it is the attribute of truth; and this is the reverse of the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in several places. And after we went over all the commentators, we found them saying of this word that it is included of beginning, end and middle [the first, last and middle letters of the alphabet], to show that this attribute is so included. Thus far. However, in the book of the Zohar (Parashat Shelach, fol. 163b) he explained that emet is a hint at Tiferet, as we explained in many places, and in particular in the Gate of Names, chapter 6, on the word tam: what remains of emet [Mem-Tav] is a hint at Yesod and Malkhut; for Yesod is called "a whole [tam] ox," and by its name Malkhut is called tam. But tam hints at their upper manifestation, as we shall explain in its entry, with the help of the Name.

And behold, when she is united with Tiferet above, then her manifestation is called [as belonging] to him, in the secret of "Set me as a seal [chotam]" (Song 8:6); and he is called by her name, emet. And because he is like the seal that is reversed, the manifestation that remains in him becomes [the letter Mem before Tav], the reverse of tam, in the secret of the combination and the sealing (see the Gate of Titles, at "Jacob came"):

Anna [אנא, anna, We beseech]: of this title the commentators explained that it is Binah, included in the first three. And they said that it also comes to [the] fifty gates of Binah [Nun], and two extra [Alefs] to hint at Keter and Chokhmah. And the root of the word is in Binah; and therefore an Alef on one side, which is Keter, and an Alef on the other side, which is Chokhmah, and the Nun in the middle, Binah, as we explained:

Sigh [אנחה, anachah]: we have some revealing from the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 19b), that the sigh is in Tiferet; and the verse "and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage" (Exod. 2:23) [means] not that they sighed; for it did not say va-yit'anchu but va-ye'anchu [and they were sighed over], as it were, above: that is to say, Tiferet sighs over them, for they had no strength to raise a sigh above. And there is no wonder at this matter, for greater than this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said on the verse "In all their affliction He was afflicted" (Isa. 63:9), [written] lo with an Alef and read with a Vav, in the Zohar at the end of Parashat Vayera, fol. 120:

I [אני, ani]: this word is shared by two attributes, Binah and Malkhut. And he explained in the Tikkunim that of both of them it is said (Deut. 32:39), "See now that I, I am He": one for Malkhut and one for Binah. And in Sefer ha-Orah he explained this word as Malkhut, and said that it shows judgment; and therefore it says, "then I too [af ani] will chastise you" (Lev. 26:28), and likewise "I kill and I make alive" (Deut. 32:39), and likewise "and you shall fear your God: I am YHVH" (Lev. 19:14). Thus far. And in Sefer ha-Shem Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that this attribute speaks to and chastises Israel lest they sin, and sometimes promises and comforts Israel; and the word ani is as one speaking face to face with his fellow, and it is a promise for good and also for ill. Thus far. And it is correct that Malkhut is called ani in the secret of the upper union, that is, that she receives from what is above. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 65), on the verse "And I [va-ani], behold, I am bringing" (Gen. 6:17). And what is sometimes found showing judgment, as he said, "then I too will chastise you," is in the way of "Cursed are the wicked, who turn the attribute of compassion into the attribute of judgment"; and this is what he said, af ani: the explanation, even in the attribute ani, which is not according to its nature. And this is the reason that sometimes it comes for judgment and sometimes it comes for compassion:

Ship [אניה, oniyyah]: the explanation, a vessel. And the matter is that the sea is in Malkhut, as will be explained in its entry, with the help of the Name; and the ships within it are her powers that are emanated from her. And so it is explained in the Zohar in many places.

And behold, when Malkhut receives judgment, then the sea grows more and more tempestuous, in the secret of the storm of judgment; and the ships have no quiet and rest, for they too draw nourishment from judgment:

Plumb line [אנך, anakh] is in Malkhut from the side of judgment; and the proof is from the verse "and behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumb line" (Amos 7:7). And it is possible to explain it somewhat of the outer ones:

Anokhi [אנכי, anokhi, I] is also a word shared by Malkhut and Binah; and it is "I, I am He who comforts you" (Isa. 51:12): one for Malkhut and one for Binah; so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30, fol. 72b). And in the Zohar he explained Anokhi: "Alef, male, Tiferet; Nun, female, this is certainly the lower Shekhinah." And the male receives from the upper male and female, which are Kaf-Nun: that is, Kaf, Keter, [and] Nun, Binah, female, as will be explained in its entry; Yod, male, Chokhmah. And they, male and female, receive from male and female. And the totality of the word is in the secret of Malkhut or Binah:
Be angry [אנף, anaf], as "lest He be angry" (Ps. 2:12), "Also with me YHVH was angry" (Deut. 1:37): it is from the side of the very strongest judgment:

Great faces, small faces [אנפי רברבי אנפי זוטרי, anpei ravrevei, anpei zutrei]: according to what appears from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in some places in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 70, fol. 125), the great faces are in the secret of the upper Vav, which has two faces in the secret of its filling, Vav-Alef-Vav: one Vav on the right, one face; the second Vav on the left, the second face. And they are in the secret of va-yissa, va-yavo [Exod. 14:19–20]: that is, Tiferet sometimes draws nourishment from the right and its inclining is there, and sometimes draws nourishment from the left and its inclining is there. And the two faces are united in the Vav, the long world, Tiferet, which unites them; and that is the Alef in the middle of two Vavs, and this is the secret of erekh appayim [long of faces]. And the small faces are in the Vav that is in Yesod, whose filling is also Vav-Alef-Vav; and they too are two faces, which are Netzach and Hod; and as is the way of Tiferet between Gedulah and Gevurah, so is the way of Yesod between Netzach and Hod. This is what appears in one place. And in another place it is understood that the cherubim, the great faces, are Netzach and Hod, in the way expounded above; and they are cherubim through whom the bridegroom and bride are united. And the small faces are Metatron and Sandalfon, who are lower cherubim, and through them too is the union. And the matter is still evenly balanced for us, and needs study:

Stomach [אסטומכא, istomkha]: Malkhut is called istomkha. For just as the stomach is what cooks the food and digests it, and separates the residue to cast it away, and sends the choice part to the place where it will be cooked and sent to the organs of the body; so Malkhut receives in her selfhood spiritual effluence from above, and sets that effluence right, and gives it body and form in coarseness, so that the chariots and her maidens can be sustained from it; for they are not in the subtlety of the Emanation, to receive the effluence according to the measure of its emanation. And the remainder she apportions to the side of the left; and this matter will be explained in the Gate of Substitutes, with the help of Heaven. And likewise the altar, which corresponds to her in this world, is the stomach, and digests the food by means of the lion crouching upon it; and the residue, which is the limbs and the fats, goes on being consumed all night; and to the side of the north, to the side of the husks, its smoke bends, as is explained in the Zohar (Terumah, fol. 130) and in the Gate of Substitutes (chapter 1). And for this reason the Torah said (Lev. 6:5), "and the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it, it shall not go out," so that it should not hold back the food:

Barns [אסם, asam], as in the matter of "YHVH will command the blessing upon you in your barns" (Deut. 28:8): certainly they are treasuries that are in Malkhut, in which she receives the effluence and lays it away:
Harm [אסן, ason], as in the matter of "and harm befall him" (Gen. 44:29): it is the hard husk, which accuses in the time of danger:

Mirror [אספקלריא, ispaklarya]: they are two, the one that shines and the one that does not shine. The one that shines is Tiferet, and the one that does not shine is Malkhut. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in Sefer ha-Shem that Tiferet is the shining and clear mirror; and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, prophesied and saw within it, and saw things clearly, without vision and riddle. But Malkhut is the mirror that does not shine; and one who prophesies by means of it prophesies by riddle and parable; and this is "I make Myself known to him in a vision" (Num. 12:6). Thus far his words.

And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 125b) it seems at first sight to oppose him, and these are its words: "Seven palaces: the palace of love; second, the palace of fear; third, the palace of compassion; fourth, the first palace, the palace of prophecy of the mirror that shines; fifth, the palace of prophecy of the mirror that does not shine," etc.

And behold, the palace of love is Chesed, the palace of fear is Gevurah, the palace of compassion is Tiferet, and "shines" and "does not shine" are Netzach and Hod; and this is the reverse of what he explained above. And reason supports it, for the principal [source] of the prophets is Netzach and Hod; and if so, how did he put the mirror that shines and does not shine in Tiferet and Malkhut? And this matter will be understood from a second saying in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 33), these are its words: "Come and see: YHVH and Adonai are the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah in the two thighs, YHVH on the right and Adonai on the left; and they are the mirror that shines and the mirror that does not shine." Thus far his words.

And behold, it is explained that Malkhut is the one that does not shine and Tiferet the one that shines. However, this matter is when they are in the place of prophecy, which is Netzach and Hod, "the two prophets of truth," where the nourishment of the prophets is; that is, in the secret of their union, as we spoke at length on this in the Gate of Names, chapter 12. And elsewhere in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, fol. 63, and in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 129) he explained that Malkhut, when Tiferet is united with her, is called the mirror that shines, and when Tiferet withdraws from her she is called the mirror that does not shine. And this does not disagree with what he explained, that the principal clearness and shining is from the side of Tiferet. And all of it is in the secret of their union in Netzach and Hod, by means of Yesod: YHVH in Netzach, Adonai in Hod, and in Yesod both as one,  Y A H D V N H Y:

Bind [אסר, asar]: there are three matters in it. The matter of a vow, as "and binds herself by a bond" (Num. 30:4): it is in Binah, the place of the vow. And the sense of being bound, as in the matter of "a king held captive [asur] in the tresses" (Song 7:6): that is, the binding of Tiferet with Malkhut, and it is their prison house; and the explanation of "who releases the bound" is that both of them are bound.
And the matter of forbidden [asur] and permitted: the forbidden is from the side of Gevurah, for there is the standing of the forbidden; and we spoke at length in the book Or Yakar:

Anger [אף, af]: this word is attributed to Malkhut, as it is said, "And yet for all that [ve-af gam zot]" (Lev. 26:44). But she is so called specifically in receiving strong judgment from Gevurah, which is "the heat of great anger." However, among the Substitutes there is Af; and this is "and many a time He turned His anger [appo] away" (Ps. 78:38). And it is possible that when she receives from Gevurah and acts by means of the Substitutes, which are called Af, then she is called af:

Ephod [אפוד, efod]: there are two aspects in it. The first is from the side of the back parts, adorned from the side of Gevurah; and this is the language of adornment, as in the matter of "and gird him [ve-afadta] with the band of the ephod" (Exod. 29:5). And there is [an ephod] from the side of the husks, as in the matter of "the ephod and the teraphim" (Judg. 18:20). This one from the side of the wine that gladdens, and that one from the side of the wine that intoxicates, which is poured out for idolatry:

The ceasing of thought [אפיסת הרעיון, afisat ha-ra'ayon]: the supernal Keter is so called. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason: because thought adds nothing in it at all. And it seems to me that the reason is that there thought ceases; for from there upward it is not grasped in reflection and thought; and of it it is said in Sefer Yetzirah, "If your heart runs, return to the place":

Channels of water [אפיקי מים, afikei mayim] are Netzach and Hod. And the matter is that for the most part their titles are the two of them together, which is not so with the other sefirot. And he said in the Zohar and the Ra'aya Meheimna that they are twins, two halves, both of them together one; and therefore most of their titles are alike. And they are called "channels of water" when both of them together draw the waters of the upper river from Binah by means of Tiferet; for he is the one who gives them drink together, equally. And when they encamp upon Yesod, then they are called "channels of water," for their bestowal is upon it, as explained in the Gate of Channels; and all this is explained in the Zohar (Acharei, fol. 68):

Thick darkness [אפלה, afelah] is Gevurah; and this is their saying, of blessed memory, "the water conceived and bore thick darkness." And it is a title for judgment close to compassion, like thick darkness, which is the thin cloud close to the waters. And this is their saying, "conceived and bore thick darkness": that is to say, the judgment that goes out from compassion; and it is the side of compassion that draws near to Gevurah and begins to thicken, and it is closer to judgment than to compassion because of its darkness. Therefore Gevurah is called afelah:

The ends of the earth [אפסי ארץ, afsei aretz]: the explanation, Malkhut from the side of her last aspects; and they are the aspects of Netzach and Hod that are in her. And the witness to this is "waters to the ankles [afsayim]" (Ezek. 47:3), which are the lowest part of the legs:

Fledgling [אפרוח, efroach]: in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Naso, fol. 121b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the fledgling is Tiferet, included of [six] extremities, which are six wings, flying [pore'ach] upward and downward. However, in the Tikkunim, at the beginning of the book, in the tale of Rabbah bar bar Chanah, he explains that the fledglings are from the side of the Righteous One, in the secret of the returning light, from below to above. And the explanation: the fledglings are like blossoms [perachim], which are not the completion of fruit; and they are the sefirot from the side of the tree that turns its face from below to above, from the side of Yesod, which is a more praiseworthy aspect than its return from the side of Malkhut, as we explained in the Gate From Below to Above. And it is possible that Tiferet too is so called from the side of the Righteous One, as we explained this matter in the aforementioned gate:
Cry out [אפעה, ef'eh]: the matter of crying out, as "like a woman in travail will I cry out" (Isa. 42:14).
And the matter of "and that which is crushed breaks out into a viper [ef'eh]" (Isa. 59:5) is the matter of the power of the husk that is harder than the serpent, as its matter is known:

Palanquin [אפריון, appiryon] (Song 3:9): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 127), that appiryon is Malkhut when she is included of ten sefirot, and each one of them included of ten, until they come to a hundred; and this is Yod; and she receives them by means of the Righteous One, Yod, the sign of the covenant. And appiryon is a palace, and the language of beauty. And Malkhut is so called when she is somewhat like Binah, as will be explained in the entry afarsemon, with the help of the Name. And the root of the word is apiryin. And this name is also related to Binah; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Bereshit (fol. 29); and it is when Binah too is included of ten by means of Chokhmah, which is Yod:

Balsam [אפרסמון, afarsemon]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Terumah there that it is Binah when she is included of six extremities, and each one of the extremities included of ten, which come to sixty, and this is Samekh [60]; and when she surrounds four extremities, and each one of the extremities is included of ten, it comes to forty [Mem]. And the root of the word is apiryon, with Mem and Samekh to hint at the secret expounded: that she is called afarsemon when she wishes to surround the children. For before, when she withdraws from over them, she is hinted at by the closed Mem; and when she surrounds them she is called the open Mem. And when she had withdrawn and is returning, and has not yet truly returned but wishes to return, she is hinted at by afarsemon:
Fingers [אצבעות, etzba'ot] are in two ways. The first: ten fingers hint at the ten sefirot, as we explained their matter in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 1.

And there is a further manifestation, as expounded in the book of the Zohar (Parashat Balak, fol. 186): that the five bars [of the Tabernacle] are five fingers; and the middle bar is the middle line, Tiferet; it is the middle finger, the highest of them all, for its head passes "from end to end" (Exod. 26:28). And the five fingers are Gedulah [and] Gevurah, on one side, two bars, or Gedulah [and] Netzach; and the two that remain are on the other side. And the self of the totality of the right hand is in Chesed, and of the left hand in Gevurah. The fingers are in the hands, for each one is included of ten, as is known. And on the words "the finger of God" Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in Sefer ha-Shem, these are his words: "For the finger is one of five in the hand, and it is the finger that acts by the power of Elohim"; accordingly they explained it as Malkhut:

Purple [ארגמן, argaman]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 139): "Purple: this is the gathering of all the colors," as we explained in the Gate of Colors. And by way of acronym, argaman is Uriel, Raphael, Gabriel, Michael, Nuriel. And the explanation: Alef-Resh-Gimel-Mem is Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet and Malkhut. And Uriel and Nuriel are all one thing, according to its receiving, whether from the right or from the left, whether or [light] or nur [fire]; and we explained it in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 6:

Long [ארוך, arokh] is Tiferet; and it is called "the long world," for it is the long Vav. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in many places in the Tikkunim and in the Ra'aya Meheimna; and he explained there that "in another length" is from its side; and likewise every place in the Torah where length is found is from its side. And likewise he explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 232) that it is called erekh appayim [long-suffering]: Alef, erekh; the Vavs, appayim, the thirteen attributes of compassion. And they are twelve boundaries, six in Tiferet and six in the Righteous One, this one to the right and that one to the left: they are twelve; and one in the middle unites them, for body and covenant are counted as one. And he explained this in another way in the entry Arikh Anpin. Further, he explained there that what is written, "and you shall prolong your days" (Deut. 22:7), "for the world that is wholly long," is in Tiferet (and it is in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 252):

Ark [ארון, aron] is the Shekhinah; and she is called "ark" because she is the ark [coffer] of Tiferet, and he is stored away within his ark; and this is the covenant, and she is the one called "the ark of the covenant." However, when she is called "the ark of the covenant," the Righteous One is in union with her within and without; and so he expounded by way of hint on the verse (Exod. 25:11), "within and without you shall overlay it." And so he explained in Parashat Noach (fol. 59), these are his words: "'And you shall come into the ark [tevah]' (Gen. 6:18): and then it is tevah, the ark of the covenant." And the explanation: before Noah, who is called "covenant," entered, Malkhut was called only tevah; but when Noah entered her, that is, was united with her, then she is called "the ark of the covenant." And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel (fol. 214a): "This ark is the secret for the Written Torah to enter into it and be stored away in it. And they are six boards surrounding [it], and this is called aron. When these six surround [it] to be as one, then it is one body, for the secret of the Torah to enter into it in six sides. And these boards are five, and five books enter into it; and these five are six in one level that enters into it in storing away, which is called the secret of all; and this is the secret of the covenant. When this enters within these five boards, then the ark and the Torah stand in the secret of nine levels, which are two names, YHVH Elohim. And afterward one board stands, one secret, a supernal secret, which covers all; and that is the secret of that firmament that surrounds and covers all, and all stand in storing away." Thus far his words.

And the intent in brief is that Malkhut is the ark in which Tiferet, which is the Torah, is stored away. And behold, just as Tiferet is included of six extremities, so Malkhut is included of six extremities; and the six are a palace for the six; and likewise the ark certainly had six sides. Afterward he said that the ark is of five, for Malkhut is called Heh, which comes to five; and they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod. And likewise Tiferet, which is the Torah, has in it five books, which are the five sefirot mentioned above. And the Shekhinah is completed to six in the secret of the middle groomsman, which is Yesod, who enters into her in concealment, in the secret of the union of male and female; and in him both of them are completed in the secret of six [and] six. And therefore she is called "the ark of the covenant," that is, the master of the Torah. And the cover [kapporet] that covers over the whole is Binah. And by this the saying and the matter of the title are explained:

The cedars of Lebanon [ארזי לבנון, arzei levanon] are the sefirot in their subtle manifestation, of which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (in the Zohar, Bereshit, fol. 35, "we have learned"): "they were like the horns of locusts," etc. And that is Lebanon, the place of whiteness [loven]; and this is "the cedars of Lebanon, which He planted" (Ps. 104:16). And in Parashat Balak (fol. 203) he explained "the cedars of Lebanon" as the three Patriarchs, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; and possibly because, being near, they draw nourishment from Lebanon:

Cedar [ארז, erez] without qualification: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra, that it is Tiferet in the secret of Da'at, which rises to draw nourishment from Lebanon, the supernal Keter. And so he explained in Parashat Metzora (fol. 53):

Lion [אריה, aryeh] is Chesed, in the secret of "and the face of a lion on the right side, the four of them" (Ezek. 1:10), in the secret of the upper Chariot. And likewise the hint to the letters of the name of seventy-two, which come to 216 [the number of aryeh]:
Long-suffering [ארך אפים, erekh appayim] is Tiferet; and in the Tikkunim he explained that it is long-suffering from the side of Chesed.
And the matter of erekh appayim we explained in the entry "long" and in the entry "great faces":

Palace [ארמן, armon] is certainly Malkhut, as it is written (Jer. 30:18), "and the palace shall be inhabited upon its own plan [al mishpato]"; and there is no doubt that she is so called when she is above, as in the matter of "upon its mishpat": that is, upon Tiferet, which is called mishpat [justice]; that is, when she is in Binah:

Palaces [ארמנות, armenot]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 5), on the verse "God in her palaces" (Ps. 48:4), that Netzach and Hod are the palaces of Malkhut, for the reason that at the time of the coupling the effluence is gathered in them, in the likeness of the testicles in the male, in which the seed is gathered, and by means of the covenant it is bestowed into the womb of the female. So the effluence is gathered in Netzach and Hod, "which are the two testicles of the male, and it goes out by means of the Righteous One." And when they are full and ready for this they are called palaces full of effluence:

Earth [ארץ, eretz] without qualification is the Shekhinah, who is earth from the side of all the sefirot. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 51, fol. 84): "'Et ha-shamayim' (Gen. 1:1): Tiferet and Malkhut; 've-et': Yesod and Malkhut; 'ha-aretz': this is the vessel of them all": the explanation, the vessel that receives all that is above, like the earth, which receives all that is bestowed from the upper ones. And we explained this saying at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance. Further, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 243b): "Old man, old man, the Shekhinah is called the earth of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, 'and the earth is My footstool' (Isa. 66:1); from the side of Chesed she is called," etc., "from the side of Gevurah," etc.; "and she is earth, the ground for all of them." Thus far. And it is that lower side in her, which is the last aspect in her selfhood, which receives from all of them together; and therefore she is "the vessel of them all." However, she is called eretz from the language of will [ratzon], for she has already been made content [nitratztah] by the good effluence that she received. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 12), on the verse "And God called the dry land earth" (Gen. 1:10), and these are his words: "And what was dry land was made earth," etc., "ar'a, a complete desire [ra'ava] as is fitting." Thus far his words.

And when eretz is joined to another word, there are these explanations of them. The upper earth is Binah; and she is called "earth" because she is, with respect to the first three, as Malkhut is with respect to what is above her. Or because, just as the earth brings forth all kinds of growth and offspring, so Binah brought forth all the beings and brought them into actuality; and this reason is related to Malkhut too. And she is called "upper" to distinguish between the upper, which is Binah, and the lower, which is Malkhut. And there is the land of the living [eretz ha-chayyim], and this is related to both of them. And of Malkhut it is written in Sefer ha-Orah that when this attribute draws from the upper pools and kinds of effluence and emanation from the Tree of Life, by means of the attribute called El Chai, she is called "the land of the living." Thus far his words.

And this is not related to Binah. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason in Binah: because Chokhmah dwells within her, and Chokhmah is called life, for from there life is drawn, as it is written (Eccl. 7:12), "wisdom gives life to those who have it." And it seems to me that because the life of the sefirot, their food and their effluence, depends on Binah, and likewise the life of the lower ones on Malkhut, therefore they are called "the land of the living": the explanation, their aspect that bestows life on all who draw their life from it. And we found support for this explanation in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 1b), these are its words: "'The land of the living,' which is the world to come." Thus far his words. Behold, it is explicit that the aspect of the world to come, that is, the bestowing side, is called "the land of the living." And in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that because Malkhut is included of seven, all of them in her are called "the lands of the living":

Further, each one of them is called the land of delight [eretz chefetz] (Mal. 3:12). And the correct reason is that the sefirot delight in Binah, to receive from her; and the upper ones [delight in] her, to bestow into her; and all of them, to bestow into Malkhut, for the reason that "the Shekhinah among the lower ones is a need on high," as explained in the preceding gates. And chefetz [delight] is the language of bestowal:

Further, Malkhut is called the pleasant land [eretz chemdah] (Jer. 3:19); and that is when she is included of what is above. For so chemdah means included: "and God finished [va-yekhal]" (Gen. 2:2), the Jerusalem Targum, "and He desired [ve-chamid]." The reason: when she is included in all her adornments she is desired by the upper ones and the lower ones:

Further, she is called a good land [eretz tovah]; and this is when she draws the light from the side of the good, that is, Chesed. And the explanation is "shining," as in "when he dresses [be-heitivo] the lamps" (Exod. 30:7). And "good" will be explained in its entry:

Further, she is called a broad land [eretz rechavah] (Exod. 3:8) when she draws nourishment from Binah, from the lower aspect in her, which is called "the broad places [rechovot] of the river," "she utters her voice in the broad places" (Prov. 1:20), as will be explained in its entry, with the help of the Name:

Further, in the husk there is a land cut off [eretz gezerah]; and it is "and the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities to a land cut off" (Lev. 16:22); so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 50b). And it is possible that it is also "a salt land and not inhabited" (Jer. 17:6). And the word eretz is difficult for us, for its explanation is the language of will. But we may say that here the explanation is the language of running [ratz], as "for their feet run [yarutzu] to evil" (Isa. 59:7):

Fire [אש, esh]: in every place where "fire" is found without qualification, it is in Gevurah; and it is a name that shows judgment, like fire in its strength. However, there are many fires [ishim], and they are five; and this is what he said, "and wholly for the fire-offerings [ishim]": which are the five fires from the side of Gevurah. And she is called "a devouring fire," which blazes and consumes all:

And there is a weak fire [esh chalushah], and it is Binah; and she is so called because from her judgment began, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Tzav, fol. 34) he called Binah "a fire that descends, compassion," and Malkhut "a fire that ascends, judgment"; for from the side of her drawing nourishment from Gevurah she is fire. And likewise Gevurah is called the great fire, to exclude Malkhut, which is small. And likewise Gedulah, Chesed, is called white fire, to hint at the judgment close to compassion, in the secret of whiteness. And some attribute this name to Tiferet, which is fire from the side of Gevurah, white from the side of Chesed. And Gevurah is called fire from water, for it is emanated from Chesed, which is water, in the way that we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And Tiferet is called fire [and] water, as we shall explain in the entry shamayim.
And further there is glowing fire [esh nogah]; and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 282a; and also in the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 6,
he called her glowing fire) that the Shekhinah is called "glowing fire" from the side of Netzach and Hod: fire from the side of Hod, glowing [nogah] from the side of Netzach:

Woman [אשה, ishah]: Malkhut is called ishah. And there is one who explained the reason: that the fires [ishim] that are below receive from her. And this is strained, for all that is beneath her, of the world of the separate ones, is fed from her. Rather, she is called ishah because she is the power of the female, which receives bestowal from the whole Emanation and bestows on the chariots; and further, that she is wife [ishah] to her husband, the bridegroom, as is known in the gates: Tiferet is her husband. And there is no doubt that the derivation of this word is esh [fire] drawing nourishment from the side of Gevurah, and Heh, in the secret of the female; which is not so of ish [man], which is esh [with] Yod, in the secret of the male; and the two of them together are esh [and] Yod-Heh. And there is no doubt that one fire is from the side of the right, white fire, and one fire from the side of the left, red fire; and that is Yod-Heh, Yod on the right, Heh on the left:

Fire-offering [אשה, isheh] is Malkhut from the side of the lower aspect that is in her, for there all the powers of judgment are united with compassion; and when all of them are united and gathered to her, that aspect is called isheh. So Rashbi explained on the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 73), on the verse "Draw me, we will run after you" (Song 1:4), etc.:

Flagons [אשישות, ashishot]: he explained in the Tikkunim (19, fol. 38) that ashishot are two fires: fire [with] Yod and fire [with] Heh. And he explained that the coupling is through the two colors, which are red fire and white fire, in the secret of the embrace through north and south, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And when Abba and Imma, that is, Yod-Heh, encamp upon these two fires, Yod, Abba, to the south, to the right, Heh, Imma, to the north, to the left; and this is ish and ishah. And of this he said, "Sustain me with flagons [ashishot]" (Song 2:5): with two fires; and it hints at the embrace, in the secret of "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me" (Song 2:6); and it is the saying of the Shekhinah. But in the Zohar, Parashat Shemini (fol. 40), he explained, and these are his words: "Ashishot: these are the Patriarchs, for these are filled first from that good wine that is preserved." Thus far his words.

It means that the three Patriarchs are called ashishot when they are full of the preserved wine, that is, the effluence of Binah. And as [we explained above], it is possible to say that that is ish and ishah, which are so called in the secret of their standing in Gedulah and Gevurah, which are clothed in fire, that is, the preserved wine, which gladdens and arouses the craving of love:

Clusters [אשכלות, eshkolot] are Netzach and Hod, which are clusters for the Righteous One, in which the secret of the preserved wine in its grapes is drawn; and he is the one who treads it in the winepress through the union. They are Netzach and Hod; and they are so called when they are full of new wine and wine, to draw them to the Righteous One in the secret of the union. And over against these holy ones there are two outside, and they are called "clusters of bitterness [they have]" (Deut. 32:32); and they are the language of "bereaved [shekhulah] and solitary" (Isa. 49:21), for they are drawn from "a land that bereaves" [meshakkelet] (Num. 13:32; Ezek. 36:13), "and the earth shall wear out like a garment" (Isa. 51:6): Lilith the wicked:

Watch [אשמורת, ashmoret]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Beshalach (fol. 54), on the verse "Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning [rosh] of the watches" (Lam. 2:19), that "the head" is Yesod, and "the watches" are Netzach and Hod, for Yesod is head to both of them, as explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And Rabbi Abba explained there that ashmoret is [written] defectively, for it is one watch; and so it is Yesod, the Life of the Worlds [the head of the watch]. And it is possible that Netzach, Hod and Yesod are called by the language of ashmoret because they are the language of guarding [shemirah], for the night is divided among them, for she draws nourishment from the three of them, sometimes from this one and sometimes from that one:

Tamarisk [אשל, eshel]: the verse (Gen. 21:33) "And he planted a tamarisk," etc., is explained as Malkhut. And to me it seems to be Tiferet; and that is in Malkhut, where its planting is, as it is written, "And he planted a tamarisk in Beersheba." And so they explained the word: a great tree. And it is called eshel from the side of Binah, for these three letters hint at her, as explained in many places:

Asher [אשר, asher]: on the word asher, Rashbi, peace be upon him, gave two explanations in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 39, fol. 77b). One is Binah, as it is said (Gen. 30:13), "Happy am I [be-oshri], for the daughters will call me happy [ishsheruni]"; and this Leah said. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 246), these are his words: "Come and see: 'Out of Asher' (Gen. 49:20): this is the place that all call happy [me'ashrin]. And what is it? The world to come, which the upper ones and the lower ones call happy and long for." Thus far his words.

And behold, he explained the law and its reason. And afterward in the Tikkunim there he gave another explanation, close to this: that asher is in Keter, but from the side of the Mother; and these are his words: "Asher is certainly the asher of 'Ehyeh asher Ehyeh'; and this supernal Keter, from the side of the female, is called asher," etc.:

And on the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 73b), on the verse "which is Solomon's [asher li-Shelomo]" (Song 1:1), he explained asher as Tiferet, and explained that it is "running and returning" (Ezek. 1:14): it rises to Binah and descends to Malkhut; and this is asher, meaning "it stands here and here." And elsewhere in the Tikkunim he explained that asher is in Chokhmah, and these are his words: "From the side of the supernal Keter three sefirot are called Ehyeh asher Ehyeh." Behold, accordingly, asher is in three places: in Binah, in Chokhmah, in Tiferet. And likewise further in the Tikkunim: "Asher is hinted in the word bereshit: asher is the Mother, which is Ehyeh asher Ehyeh." And to set this matter right we say that asher is in the secret of the bestowal of Chokhmah into Binah, in the secret of the union, in the secret of Da'at. And by this it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei Mot (fol. 65), these are its words: "We found in the book of King Solomon: asher: in the binding of bliss, the supernal citadel [kastira], companionship is found; as it is said, 'Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy.'" Thus far his words. And the explanation of the word kastira is palace; and so the Jerusalem Targum (Gen. 25:16), "and these are their names, by their villages [and by their encampments]," [renders] "and by their citadels [kastrohon]."

And behold, accordingly, kastira means palace, and kitura means binding and union. And the explanation of his words: "in the binding of bliss" means in the union and binding of Eden, which is Chokhmah, with Binah, which is the upper palace, that is, "the supernal citadel"; "companionship is found" means in complete union is found, that is, the word asher is found. And its matter is that the aspect of Chokhmah that is united with Binah is called asher; and so asher is found to be the last aspect of Chokhmah and the first of Binah. And this is what Leah said, "Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy": the explanation, the effluence bestowed on her from Chokhmah, by which she is made happy among the daughters, that is, the other sefirot. Thus far the explanation of the saying. And we find ourselves taught that Chokhmah in the aspect of its union with Binah, and likewise Binah in the aspect of its union with Chokhmah, is called asher. And by this it will not be far from us that asher is also in Tiferet, for it is what unites them and couples them, in the secret of Da'at, as explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 8, and likewise in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 17. And because happiness [osher] is bestowed through it from Chokhmah to Binah, therefore it is called asher. And in the Zohar Chadash on the Song of Songs mentioned above, it appears that it is called asher from the language of walking, as "none of his steps [ashurav] shall slide" (Ps. 37:31); and this is what he said, "it stands here and here": the explanation, it stands in Binah and it stands in Malkhut, as is proved there. And it is possible to say that it rises to Binah in the secret of Da'at, to be united. And so, along with the one, two are found: the language of walking and the language of happiness itself; that is, it rises and unites Abba and Imma, and descends and is united with Malkhut, and all at once. Further, asher is found in Yesod; and so Rashbi explained in Parashat Bereshit (fol. 47b) on the verse "Out of Asher, his bread shall be fat" (Gen. 49:20). And it is possible that it is so called when it draws nourishment from Tiferet at the time of the concealed union; and all the more so by what we explained, that it rises and unites Abba and Imma, and descends and is united with Malkhut by means of Yesod; and through the effluence bestowed from Chokhmah to Binah, and from there it bestows on Yesod, and from there on Malkhut. And therefore she is called asherah, as we shall explain with the help of the Rock and His salvation:

Asherah [אשרה, asherah]: he explained in the Zohar, Bereshit (fol. 49a), that Malkhut is called asherah when she draws nourishment from Tiferet, who is her husband, when he is called in the aspect of asher: he is asher and she is asherah. For such is the way of most of their titles, in the pattern of tzaddik, tzedek, ofer, afar:

Et [את, et]: all the commentators agreed that this word is in Malkhut, for she is female. However, Rashbi (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 77) explained: "Alef, male; Tav, female." And he said that Malkhut is so called when the power of the male, which she has already received upon her, is drawn within her. And we have already explained the saying itself in the Gate of Names, chapter 6. And likewise he explained elsewhere: "The Torah is included from Alef to Tav"; for through receiving the male the letters were engraved in her, as will be explained in the Gate of Letters. Further, they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 247a), that when the thirty-two paths are bestowed on Tiferet from the upper Torah, "the Torah is the unripe fruit of the wisdom above"; and Tiferet bestows on Malkhut the thirty-two mentioned; then Malkhut is called et, because et shows that she is included in the twenty-two letters; and the thirty-two paths are twenty-two letters and ten utterances. Accordingly it is found that et is in Malkhut and shows the inclusion of the thirty-two by means of Tiferet; that is, the union of Alef, male, with Tav, female, by means of Chokhmah, which bestows the thirty-two paths into Tiferet, as we explained. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Yesod is called et, and explained it from the language of ot [sign], that is, "sign," as we explained above in its entry:

At [את, at, you, feminine] is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 81b), on the verse "Behold now, I know that you [at] are a woman fair to look upon" (Gen. 12:11): that this word is the hint at Malkhut. And though she is called attah, as we shall explain, it will be in the way of leil, laylah, na'ar, na'arah, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2:

Attah [אתה, attah, You]: in Sefer ha-Orah he explained that Tiferet is called Attah, and brought a proof: "You, You are awesome" (Ps. 76:8); "awesome" is certainly in Tiferet, as will be explained in its entry. And the reason that he is called Attah is that he is the secret of the middle line, Tiferet, from which spread out all the branches and the boughs and the chariots, in the secret of their creation; and through the alphabets they were all created, in the secret of Sefer Yetzirah; and therefore the Alef and the Tav come in this name. And the Heh hints at the five places of articulation of the mouth, which go out from Binah; and therefore he is called Attah. This is the gist of his intent in the utmost brevity. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] added to him and said that because he was emanated from Binah, it says (Ps. 93:2), "You are from everlasting [me-olam]." And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, agreed in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 38a) that Attah is in Tiferet. But we found Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Commandments, the commandment to bless (in Parashat Ekev, fol. 271), [saying] the reverse of this; and these are his words: "Attah is the beginning of being revealed outward; and therefore it is called Attah. And which is it? This is the secret of the right."

Behold, he explained that Chesed is called Attah, in the second person, to show the beginning of the revealing and the appearing; which is not so in the first three, which are concealed, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance; and likewise there we copied from the Zohar what he explained on this verse, "YHVH, my God, are You [attah]." And we can set this right by what he further explained in the Commandments (there, fol. 271b): "Even the light that does not shine, at the time that it cleaves to the right, is called Attah."

Behold, accordingly, Tiferet, because he inclines to the right, for from there he is called the Written Torah, as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name, is therefore then called Attah; and likewise Malkhut, because she inclines to the right, as in the matter of the cup of blessing, which is in the right hand, is therefore called Attah. And in the Sava (of Mishpatim, fol. 104) he explained the reverse: that Attah is principally Malkhut, and because Chesed is united with her, Chesed is called Attah; and he disagrees explicitly with what Rashbi, peace be upon him, said. And these are his words: "For 'You [attah] are a priest for ever,' etc. (Ps. 110:4): here the cup of blessing is bound to the right, as is fitting." Thus far his words.

And there he says explicitly that he disagrees somewhat with Rabbi Shimon. And in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 193b), on the verse "YHVH, my God, are You" (Ps. 104:1), he explained Attah as Chesed, and proved the matter from the verse "You are a priest for ever." However, he said: "And we have established that there are three places, each one of which is called Attah." And the intent is that Tiferet is called Attah; and likewise Malkhut is called Attah; and so he explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Vayetze (fol. 154), that she is the revealed world, and therefore she is called Attah. And some explained the reason: et [with] Heh. And to me it seems that since she is called et, that is, "the Torah," etc., as we explained in its entry, so when she adds good to her good she is called attah, in the secret of na'ar, na'arah, leil, laylah; and all of it is in the secret of the right, for from there is the beginning of the revealing of the letters, and from there Tiferet is called the Written Torah. And in Parashat Pekudei (fol. 221), these are his words: "Attah is the secret of the mirror that does not shine, which shows in it all those images." Thus far. And some say that Chokhmah too is called Attah. And some explained that Binah is called Attah, and the secret is the language of "and He came [ve-atah] from the myriads of holiness" (Deut. 33:2), for so the world to come is called. And we have found no revealing of this in the Zohar:

Etanim [אתנים, eitanim]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 42a) that Netzach, Hod and Yesod are called etanim, which means, by permutation, tanna'im; and on the matter of the Tanna'im and Amora'im he explained in the entry Amora'im. Further, there is eitan, which Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained as the permutation tanya [it was taught]; and we shall explain it in its entry, with the help of the Name:
Itkafta [אתקפתא, itkafta, strengthening]: it is explained in the entry itkafta [spelled with Heh]; see there:

Etrog [אתרוג, etrog] is Malkhut, and it hints at the heart, which is the Shekhinah. And indeed the word etrog means, from the language of "and the tree was desirable to make one wise" (Gen. 3:6), whose Targum is u-meragag [desirable]. And the intent is that she is desirable, as expounded above; and therefore it must be without blemish, as in the matter of "My dove, my undefiled, is but one; she is the choice one of her that bore her" (Song 6:9). However, she is called etrog when she grows over all waters, for she is close to Chokhmah; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 121). Further, he explained there what we learned (Bikkurim, chapter 2): "The etrog is like a tree in three ways"; for she receives from three sides, which are Chesed, judgment and compassion, like the tree, Tiferet. Thus far our faltering and feeble strength has reached in the explanation of the entry Alef, with the help of God; and behold, we are entering to explain the entry Bet, with the help of the Name, may He be blessed:
The letter Bet itself we shall explain in the Gate of Letters; and so we have done for all the letters:

Well [באר, be'er] is Malkhut; and the reason is that she is a well springing with living waters, from the side of the spring and the source that is within her. However, sometimes this attribute is called bor [pit] and sometimes be'er [well]. And the pit is at the time that she has no spring and source within her, but only what she has received, gathered waters, and she is in poverty. And when she is called "well" she springs with water by means of the spring and the source that is within her. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 60); and we copied it and explained it in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 19. And there it was explained that what springs from within her is the souls of the righteous. And in the Zohar, Parashat Beha'alotekha (fol. 150), on the verse "The well, which the princes dug" (Num. 21:18), it is understood that she is called "well" only at the time that she receives from Binah by means of Gevurah. And it is possible that the source within her is the bestowal of Binah, bestowed by means of the souls of the righteous; and this needs study there in its place, for the matter is evenly balanced. And sometimes the well is called be'erah; and he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Chukkat (fol. 183), and these are his words: "'And from there to Be'er, that is the well' (Num. 21:16). Why is it here be'erah and afterward be'er? Rather, be'erah after the waters are gathered into the sea and go down below; be'er at the time that Isaac fills it." Thus far his words. And he said explicitly that she is called be'er in her receiving from the side of Gevurah, while she does not yet bestow but receives the effluence within her; and she is called be'erah when she bestows on the lower ones after she has been filled from the upper ones. And behold, accordingly be'erah is found to be Malkhut alone, after the male who bestows has withdrawn from her; and therefore she bestows. For this principle is in our hands: that an attribute does not bestow while it is receiving, but after the completion of its receiving it bestows, as we explained in the preceding gates. And there is no wonder from the matter of "the river that does not cease"; for that is in Binah above, and there is the source of the blessings, in the secret of her union with Eden, and it never ceases. But the sefirot in general do not bestow while they receive. And therefore she is called by the masculine be'er, for in the presence of the male the female does not rise in name.
