But after her receiving, when the effluence has withdrawn, she bestows and is called be'erah alone. And by this will be explained what is written there afterward: "Why first be'erah and now be'er? Rather, at first the female alone; and now that it says it, it is the totality of male and female, [and] it is called be'er. And in the place where the male is found, even a feminine word, we call all of it masculine." Thus far his words. And he proved that be'er is when she is with the male, who fills the well. And at first sight this appears to disagree with what we copied above; but by what we explained, the words of Rashbi are found to be all one matter, and all of them go up on one stalk. And sometimes she is called a well of living waters (Gen. 26:19) when it draws abundantly from the upper waters, or in the way that we explained in Elohim chayyim. And she is called Be'er-lahai-roi [the well of the Living One who sees me] (Gen. 16:14) when she keeps watch and looks to Yesod, which is called Chai [Living], to receive from it in her way. And she is called Beersheba [be'er sheva, the well of seven] when she is included of seven upper sefirot. And Binah is sometimes called Beersheba because she bestows into seven, and she is the one from whom all draw their effluence. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze. And in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 135b), it appears that Malkhut from the side of Gevurah is called "a well of living waters"; and the reason is that from there are the mighty acts [gevurot] of the rains. And there are a pit and a well among the Substitutes; and of this pit it is said (Gen. 37:24), "and the pit was empty, there was no water in it"; and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat 22a): "there was no water in it, but there were snakes and scorpions in it." And of it it is said (Exod. 21:33), "And if a man digs a pit, and [an ox] falls into it," etc.; "and He brought me up out of the pit of roaring" (Ps. 40:3). And likewise it is called "a narrow well, the alien woman" (Prov. 23:27); and of it it is said (Ps. 69:16), "and let not the well shut its mouth upon me." And the male among the husks is called bor; and from there "the boor [bor] does not fear sin" (Avot 2:5). And his female is called borah; and of her it is said (Gen. 37:24), "and they cast him into the pit [ha-borah]"; may the Compassionate One save us:
Garment [בגד, beged] is the Shekhinah, and she is the garment of the King of the world, as we explained in the entry imrato. And likewise it comes to nine, for she is included of nine points:

Void [בהו, bohu] is Gedulah; and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Hagigah 12a): "slimy stones," etc., "from which water goes out." And it is a hint at the going out of the letters from Binah, which are included in Chesed and bestow water, in the secret of "light, water, firmament," which he explained as the letters. And bohu is a thing that has substance, and it clothes the tohu [formlessness], which is Binah, a thing that has no substance, for it is not grasped; as in the matter of "you shall surely let the mother go" (Deut. 22:7). And the things go out from Binah, which is called ko'ach [power]: from potential [ko'ach] to actuality, Chesed (see Tikkun 19, fol. 39):

Boaz [בועז, bo'az] is Hod; and corresponding to this attribute was the left pillar that was in the Temple. And it is explained as bo oz, "in it is strength" and might, because of its principal nourishment from Gevurah. And it is called by this name when it strengthens the power of craving for the coupling:

Morning [בוקר, boker]: there are two mornings, besides dawn [shachar], which will be explained in its place with the help of the Name. The first is the morning of Abraham. And the reason may be that, just as the morning is the beginning of light in the world, so Chesed is the beginning of the light that is revealed. And further, the morning is under the rule of Abraham, the attribute of Chesed; and therefore it is written (Gen. 19:27; 22:3), "And Abraham rose early in the morning." And the second morning is the Righteous One, the attribute of Joseph; and of it it is said (Gen. 44:3), "The morning was light," etc. And it is possible that it is so called from the side of Chesed. And these two mornings are explained in the Zohar, Parashat Balak (fol. 204a):

Womb [בטן, beten] is Binah, as it is said (Job 38:29), "Out of whose [mi] womb came the ice?" And Mi [Who] is Binah, as will be explained in its entry, with the help of the Name. However, it is not the self of Binah but the womb of Binah; and her womb is Malkhut when she is above, and she is called beten. And of her it is said (Song 7:3), "Your belly is a heap of wheat." And there is no belly without a body, for the belly is united with the body, which is Tiferet; and all of it by means of Binah, in the secret of their concealment there. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it as Tiferet, and that is not the principal [view]:

Binah [בינה, binah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 103), and these are his words: "For she is called Binah above when she is with her husband." And elsewhere he wrote (there, fol. 108), and these are his words: "Binah: there are Yod-Heh, Abba and Imma, and the son [ben] within them, the pillar that supports them," etc. Thus far his words. From all this it will be seen that when Chokhmah is united with Binah by means of Tiferet, in the secret of Da'at, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, then she is called Binah, to hint at the three of them; and its permutation is ben Yah [son of Yod-Heh]:

Egg [ביצה, beitzah]: in the matter of "Hamotzi" over the measure of an olive and an egg, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 244b) that the egg is the Yod of the four-letter name, which is in Chokhmah. However, in the Tikkunim he explained that all the sefirot are called eggs from the side of Malkhut, and these are his words (in the Introduction, fol. 2b): "For the eggs are from the side of the lower Mother, who is an egg." Thus far his words. And the sefirot are called eggs from her side, in the secret of the returning light, from below to above. And it is possible that the Yod for Hamotzi, the Yod of the Name, is the lower Yod [the Yod of Adonai], from the side of the returning light that was in Malkhut; and she is certainly an egg (see there in the Ra'aya Meheimna mentioned above):

House [בית, bayit] is related to Malkhut and to Binah. And the reason is that both of them are houses: Binah is a house for Chokhmah, which is her husband, as is known; and they are father and mother [to all] the lower ones. And further, in another aspect, she is called "house" because Binah is a house for the whole Emanation below her; for in her they were, and from her they went out, and into her they return. And Malkhut is a house for Tiferet [her husband, and she is also a house for the whole Emanation; see the entry "ten"], with respect to the fact that to her they return to go, as is known, for all of them bestow into her and all of them enter into her. And a third reason in Malkhut: just as the house includes many things, and vessels of different kinds, so Malkhut too includes many things and many aspects and powers without end. And this is also related somewhat to Binah.

And the matter of the two reasons in these houses is two different aspects in each one of them. Binah has an aspect with respect to Chokhmah, for she is a palace for it, or with respect to the whole Emanation stored away within her. And likewise Malkhut has these two aspects: an aspect with respect to the whole upper Emanation, which is hidden in her, or with respect to Tiferet alone. And she has other houses besides these, with respect to her powers, with respect to the lower ones that are created, formed and made through her; and this is the third reason that we explained in her. And sometimes a name is joined to the houses, such as Beth-el [the house of El]; and Malkhut is so called when she is bestowed upon from the side of the right, which is called El. And therefore Abraham, the master of the right, made all his journeys "from the east [mi-kedem]" (Gen. 12:8), in the secret of Keter and Chokhmah, both of which are primordial [kedumim], as will be explained with the help of the Name; "toward Beth-el," in the secret of Malkhut; and likewise "Beth-el on the west [mi-yam]," in the secret of the south. And likewise all his matters were to bestow on this attribute and set it right, in the secret of the thread of Chesed. And likewise Isaac bestowed to the left and called her the house of Elohim. And when Jacob saw this he said, "This is none other than the house of Elohim" (Gen. 28:17), from the side of Isaac, in the secret of "His left hand is under my head" (Song 2:6); so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 151a). Further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained there that she is so called from the side of Binah, which is also called Elohim, as is known. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayishlach (fol. 173), it appears that Binah is called Beth-el; and it is possible to say the reason: that from there is the drawing of food and effluence to Chesed, which is called El; and this is Beth-el, meaning the house and treasury from which El, which is Chesed, is sustained; and in this aspect she is so called:

Further, Malkhut is called the house of assembly [beit ha-keneset, the synagogue] when she gathers in and collects blessings and effluence from all the upper attributes that are above her. And these are the words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 44, fol. 72a): "The house of assembly is the gathering of all blessings." Thus far his words:

Further, she is called the house of the Sanctuary [beit ha-mikdash, the Temple]; and the reason is that she is a house for the Sanctuary, which is Tiferet. And this Temple that will be built, speedily in our days, will be in the measures of the Temple above, which is Malkhut, who dwells in it. However, the title "the house of the Sanctuary" is more particular than Jerusalem; and it includes courts and chambers, etc., as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations:

And she is further called the house of the King; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason: for she is a house for the supernal King, Binah. And this is not compelling, for it is only "the house of the King," Tiferet; for he too is called King, and she is his house:

Further, there is the house of the world [beit ha-olam]; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is Chokhmah, for it is a house for all that is emanated and created; and "He is the place of the world, and the world is not His place":

Further, Malkhut is called a house of habitation [beit zevul] (1 Kings 8:13); and he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Beha'alotekha (fol. 150), these are his words: "When all the treasures of the King are deposited in her hands and she rules over them, then she is called beit zevul." And the reason is that beit zevul means a house in which there is a habitation for the Shekhinah and all the household above:

Further, there is a court [beit din] without qualification: it is Malkhut. And she is called a court of three; and so Rashbi explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 117), these are his words: "A court: the Shekhinah with three, the three living creatures of her Chariot." And the intent is that she includes three faces, the face of a lion, the face of an ox, the face of an eagle; for the man is the rider, and she too is herself a man, as we explained in the entry adam. And then, when she is included in three faces, she is called a court of three; that is, she receives from the right and from the left and from the middle. Further, there are the court of habitation, the upper court and the lower court; and they are the soft attribute of judgment and the harsh attribute of judgment. And likewise the great court and the small court. However, she is called the great court when Gevurah is full of merits from the side of Gedulah; and this is when Binah goes down to Gevurah and fills it from the side of Gedulah; then she is called the great court. And so it is explained in the words of Rashbi:
And so [בכן, u-vekhen] is Chesed; and likewise it comes to it in number [72]. And he explained in the Tikkunim that every use of u-vekhen is in Chesed:

Firstborn [בכור, bekhor]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] wrote that the firstborn is Keter, for it is the firstborn of the whole Emanation, as is known. And some explained it as Chokhmah. However, in the Commandments (in Parashat Bo, fol. 43b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote that the firstborn is Tiferet, for he is the firstborn son, including six extremities. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (there, fol. 42a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the firstborn as Tiferet from the side of Chesed; and therefore the redemption of the firstborn is with five sela'im of silver. And indeed the number five corresponds to the Heh that was added to Abraham, that is, the Heh of Binah. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] also explained "firstborn" as Chokhmah and Malkhut. And the matter is reconciled by what he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 14, fol. 28b): that of Chokhmah it is said, "Sanctify to Me every firstborn" (Exod. 13:2), and therefore all the firstborn are from the side of Chokhmah. And Malkhut is called bekhorah [birthright]. And the first fruits [bikkurim] from the side of Chokhmah are called first fruits for Malkhut, as it is written (Exod. 23:19; 34:26), "The first fruits of your land you shall bring," etc. And from the side of Chokhmah they are also called first fruits for Yesod; and of them it is said (Ezek. 44:30), "and the first of all the first fruits of all." And therefore we say that the principal firstborn is Chokhmah, but when it is in the masculine. And Tiferet, if he is called firstborn, is so from the side of Chokhmah, which makes him firstborn; and Malkhut, if she is called by the word bekhorah, is so called because of the manifestation of the Yod that she has from its side. And their saying in the Ra'aya Meheimna, "from the side of Chesed," is with respect to the silver; but with respect to the firstborn itself, it is from the side of Chokhmah. And the reason is that it is the firstborn of all that comes within the definition of emanated. And though Keter is before Chokhmah, there is a reason for this, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter:

High places [במות, bamot] are the Patriarchs; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkun (52, fol. 84a), and these are his words: "'And He makes me tread upon my high places' (Hab. 3:19): these are the Patriarchs." And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained "the high places of the earth" as Binah, which is higher than all the lands. And this does not settle, for bamotei is plural. Rather, Binah is called "upon the high places of the earth"; and this is "and I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth" (Isa. 58:14): for the earth is Malkhut, and the high places are the Patriarchs, and "upon the high places" is Binah:
And there are strange high places; and of them it is said (Deut. 33:29), "and you shall tread upon their high places": they are the husks, which are below holiness:
Son [בן, ben] without qualification is in Tiferet; and so it is explained in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim in places too many to count:

Further, he is called the son of Jesse [ben Yishai]; and it is explained as ben yesh Yod [the son of Something, Yod]: for Chokhmah is called Yesh [Something], and it is also Yod, as is known; and Tiferet is its son, and it is his father, as we explained:

Further, he is called a son of free men [ben chorin] (Eccl. 10:17); and the reason is explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Lekh (fol. 96): that he draws nourishment from two free ones [chorin], Binah and Chokhmah, when they are together. And he is called a son of freedom [ben cherut], which is singular, when he draws nourishment from Binah alone, in the secret of the Jubilee:

Further, it explained there that he is called a son of oil [ben shemen] (Isa. 5:1); and it is like "son of free men," for he draws nourishment from the upper oil, which is the effluence bestowed from the right when Chokhmah prevails over Binah. And this is the difference between "son of free men" and "son of oil": the "free men" is when Binah prevails, and therefore all of it is in the secret of the compassion of Binah, which is freedom; and "oil" is when Chokhmah prevails over Binah, for from the right is the secret of the oil:

Further, he is called a son of the house [ben bayit] to Binah, which is a house for Chokhmah. And there Moses was a chariot, and from her side he is called "son of the house"; and this is the aspect of Da'at:

Further, there is children [banim], in the plural, and there are two explanations of it: either the six days of the Work, six sons and one daughter; or Tiferet and Malkhut, son and daughter, are called banim. And it is explained in the entry "mother"; see there. And some explained banim as Netzach and Hod, for two reasons: either because whoever needs children should pray and ask from there first, and from there it rises to mazal, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance; or because it is the language of building [binyan], for they build the lower ones and emanate the hosts above and below:

Further, Netzach and Hod are called (in Tikkun 48, fol. 82b) the children of Israel, for they are children of Tiferet, and from there is their nourishment. And we can say that for this reason they are called "children," and they are so called at the time of their nourishment from there:

The daughters of Jerusalem [בנות ירושלים, benot Yerushalayim]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 242a). One explanation: that they are the souls of the righteous; and they are so called because they are bestowed from the upper Jerusalem, which is Malkhut. And the second explanation is that they are the twelve oxen on which the sea is set (1 Kings 7:25), and they are her twelve lower boundaries, and she crouches upon them; and they are called "the daughters of Jerusalem." And it is difficult for me why he did not explain that they are "the seven maidens fit to be given to her" (Esth. 2:9); and this needs study (see the book Me'orei Or):

Son [בר, bar]: in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 44) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verse "Kiss the son [bar]" (Ps. 2:12): that the Righteous One, when he is exiled and goes down from his place, is called bar, the language of baraita, which is outside, exiled from its place, etc. And it is baraita, outerness; for "the righteous one has perished" (Isa. 57:1), "and the river shall be wasted and dried up" (Isa. 19:5), and she has gone into exile:

Hail [ברד, barad]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that hail is in Chesed, and its principal nature is water, and it is the opposite of fire. However, it is explained in the Zohar (Vayetze, fol. 161) that by means of Gevurah the waters of the effluence are frozen and are not bestowed below. And likewise it is found that the nature of the north wind is to cool and to freeze; and by this it is proved that the power of Gedulah that draws near to Gevurah is hail. And this is "and fire flashing in the midst of the hail" (Exod. 9:24); and this is "hail and coals of fire" (Ps. 18:13), close to one another:

Blessed [ברוך, barukh]: explanations of it are many, even in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And there is a difference between the blessings of enjoyment and the other blessings, and this is not its place. However, in brief, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that barukh includes ten sefirot; and these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 116b): "Barukh: Bet shows two, the upper and the lower Shekhinah; Resh, reshit [beginning], Chokhmah; Vav shows six sefirot; Kaf shows the supernal Keter." Further, he explained there that the initials of barukh are rosh u-mekor kol berakhot [head and source of all blessings]: "For this is head and source of all the blessings; and therefore Bet is Chokhmah, and it shows Keter, which is the head and the spring of all blessings." Thus far his words. Behold, in his explanation he meant barukh as Chokhmah, showing Keter. And in the Commandments (in Parashat Ekev, fol. 271a) he said that barukh is in Binah, and these are his words: "Barukh: this is the secret of the source higher than all, to water and to draw out and to light all the lamps; and it is ever blessed, for its waters do not cease. And from there is the beginning of what is called the world to come." Behold, he said explicitly that barukh is in Binah. And elsewhere he said, "whoever bows, bows at barukh," etc. Behold, he said explicitly that it is in Malkhut; and for this reason one bows at barukh. And in the Tikkun (Tikkun 18, fol. 35, and Tikkun 70, fol. 119) he explained barukh as Yesod; and likewise "whoever bows, bows at barukh," etc., for there the sefirot go down to bestow. And we have already appointed this matter for the commentary on the Tikkunim, if the Name decrees life:

Iron [ברזל, barzel]: in the Zohar (Va'era, fol. 24) he explained that it is in Malkhut. And elsewhere it appears that it is in Tiferet. And it is possible that of both of them it is said (Prov. 27:17), "Iron sharpens iron together." And nevertheless it is from the side of judgment and war, and it is plain in the matter. And likewise "nor any tool of iron was heard in the house" (1 Kings 6:7), because the outer ones hold on to it. And so he explained in the Zohar on the Song of Songs:

Bars [בריחים, berichim]: we have already explained somewhat, in the entry "fingers," the matter of the five bars and the middle bar, which is a hint at the middle line. And behold, the bars were five on the right and five on the left; and we explained there that they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod. And according to what appears from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim, the five sefirot mentioned are called bars on account of the middle bar, which is Tiferet, which passes from end to end; that is, "from one end of heaven," the upper Heh, "to the other end of heaven" (Deut. 4:32), the lower Heh:

Baraita [ברייתא, baraita, the outer]: Malkhut, at the time that she wanders and is exiled from her place because of the exile, is called baraita, that is, the outer one, for she is outside her place. And elsewhere he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 44b) that she is so called from the side of Gevurah, for through the strength of judgment she is exiled and wanders:

Covenant [ברית, berit]: this word, when it is without qualification, is related to three places: to Malkhut, to Yesod and to Tiferet; and all three are found often in the words of the Zohar. However, when it is joined to another word it changes, as we shall explain. And there is the covenant of the tongue, and it is in Binah; but the principal is in Tiferet, as we explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine." And in Sefer ha-Orah he explained that Binah is called the covenant of the tongue, and the covenant of the mouth, and the covenant of the lips; and in Yesod it is the covenant of the member, the covenant of the Sabbath, the covenant of the rainbow; and Malkhut, when she is bound between Yesod and Binah, is also called covenant. And this is the secret of the uncovering [peri'ah]: for circumcision hints at Yesod, and uncovering at Malkhut. And of this it is said, "one who circumcised and did not uncover, it is as though he did not circumcise," because he lacks the gate of entry, which is Malkhut, which is the uncovering. Lo, these are some of the ways of Sefer ha-Orah, though they are not literally his words. Further, Yesod is called the covenant of peace (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 132a). And now all the covenants that we mentioned have been explained. The covenant of the tongue was explained above; and by the reason that we explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine" it is also settled. And it will be explained that the covenant of the mouth, the covenant of the lips, the covenant of the member, the covenant of the flesh and the covenant of circumcision are all one thing. And "the covenant of peace," to hint that it makes peace [mashlim] between Tiferet and Malkhut, in the way of "for all that is in heaven and on earth" (1 Chron. 29:11), and its Targum: "which holds on to heaven and to earth." And "the covenant of circumcision" means that which cuts off the foreskin and abolishes it from the world:

Pool [בריכה, berekhah] is Malkhut, for she is the pool that gathers all the effluence from all the upper sources. And sometimes Binah too is called a pool. And the source of the lower pool is Tiferet, by means of the spring, which is Yesod; and the source of the upper pool is Keter, by means of the spring, which is Chokhmah:

Blessing [ברכה, berakhah] is also in Malkhut, but at the time that she draws nourishment from the side of the right. And so it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna and in other places. And Binah too is called "blessing"; and so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 55, fol. 86a). And they gave a sign: "The blessing of YHVH, it makes rich" (Prov. 10:22), in the secret of "whoever wishes to become rich, let him turn northward." And there is a difference between berekhah and berakhah: the pool is from the side of her being a receptacle for the effluence that is bestowed, and the blessing is her bestowing the blessing below:

Lightnings [ברקים, berakim]: in the book of the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the lightnings that were at the giving of the Torah are from the side of Yesod, for it is what is called lightning. And these are his words: "Lightnings, from the side of the Righteous One, of whom it is said, 'and His arrow shall go forth as the lightning' (Zech. 9:14)." And he explained that the Righteous One is an arrow, and he is the bow that shoots the seed, which shoots like an arrow:
Spices [בשמים, besamim] are seven sefirot; and the three Patriarchs are called "chief spices" (Exod. 30:23), and Tiferet, in the secret of Da'at, is called "the chief spice":

Flesh [בשר, basar] is for the most part in Malkhut; and this is "and flesh of my flesh" (Gen. 2:23): they are two fleshes (flesh in Tiferet, and in the lesser [sense]) "and He closed up the flesh in its place" (Gen. 2:21); and that is her manifestation in him (and flesh is her manifestation below; and this is "and they shall be one flesh" (Gen. 2:24)). And likewise Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, with respect to his chariot: "for that he also is flesh" (Gen. 6:3): be-shagam [for that also] comes to [the number of] Moses. And all this is hinted at in the Tikkunim. And there is flesh from the side of judgment; and this is "the flesh was yet between their teeth" (Num. 11:33). And this is because reversed, basar comes to shever [breaking]; for the Shekhinah from the side of judgment is called flesh, and she is red; but she blazes with flames from the side of her love for her husband, from the side of the north, to couple. And when there is no completion of blessing and the coupling is not found, because of the iniquity of the generation, then she is shever. And in the time of famine, when there is no coupling, it is said (Gen. 42:19), "and carry grain [shever] for the famine," etc.; and likewise "there was grain in Egypt" (Gen. 42:1). And this is the iniquity of those who craved, who asked for flesh and pushed away the bread from heaven, which is the coupling: bread, the Shekhinah; heaven, Tiferet; and they wanted flesh. And this is "and the anger of YHVH was kindled against the people" (Num. 11:33). And the flesh in man is from the side of the left, and it rots, as is known; and we shall speak at length in the entry etzem [bone]:

Daughter [בת, bat] without qualification is Malkhut, but in her aspect that is called Yod, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And this aspect is also called the pupil of the eye [bat ayin, the daughter of the eye]; and when she is called bat ayin it means that around her are three colors, which are the Patriarchs, as is known in the matter of the eye, as explained in the aforementioned gate and in the Gate of the Soul. And the Yod is called daughter in relation to Chokhmah; but in relation to Binah, the manifestation of the Heh is called bat ayin; and that is "a woman and her daughter," who are the two Hehs: the woman, Binah, and her daughter, Malkhut. And sometimes [a word] is joined, and she is called bat kol [a heavenly voice, the daughter of a voice]; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason: for Binah is the voice and Malkhut the daughter. And though his words are right, nevertheless Rashbi, peace be upon him, did not explain it so (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 133b), and these are his words: "And she is bat kol from the side of the central pillar, which is called 'the voice of the shofar,' 'the voice is the voice of Jacob' (Gen. 27:22)," etc. Thus far his words. Behold, it is explicit that she is called bat kol on account of Tiferet; but specifically when Tiferet is close to Binah and goes out from her, for then he is called "the voice of the shofar," and she is called daughter to him; in the way our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Megillah 13a): "'and she was to him as a daughter' (2 Sam. 12:3): do not read 'as a daughter' [le-vat] but 'as a house' [le-vayit]"; and every woman is daughter to her husband. And she is called a king's daughter; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason: for she is the daughter of the supernal King, Binah. And it is possible to explain it as Chokhmah, which is also called King, as will be explained in its entry; and the manifestation of the Yod from the side of Chokhmah is called "the king's daughter is all glorious within" (Ps. 45:14), for she is concealed in the manifestation of the building, which is the Heh, like this , as was explained in the Gate of Manifestations (chapter 3). And she is called mate [bat zug]; and the reason is that she is the mate of Tiferet; and it is possible that she is so called when she is coupling with her husband. And she is called daughter of waves [bat gallim] (Isa. 10:30); and he explained in the Tikkunim that she is the daughter of ten wheels [galgallim], which are the ten sefirot included in her; this name shows the inclusion. And there is another explanation, explained in the entry gallim. And she is called Bath-sheba [bat sheva, daughter of seven] when she is included of seven. And the intent is not "included" in that she receives from seven, for then she is called Beersheba; but she is called Bath-sheba when seven sefirot shine in her selfhood. And in the Zohar, Parashat Shemini (fol. 38), he explained that she is called Bath-sheba from the side of Gevurah; and it is explained in the entry Elisheva. And it is already possible that Binah too is called Beersheba, as we explained in its entry. And she is sometimes called prince's daughter [bat nadiv] (Song 7:2), in the secret of "Abraham our father, peace be upon him, had a daughter"; for when she is united with him and receives from him the thread of Chesed drawn over her, then she is called bat nadiv, for Abraham, Chesed, is called nadiv [generous]. And she is further called daughter of many [bat rabbim] (Song 7:5); and so he explained in Parashat Pinchas (fol. 202b). And the reason may be that she receives from the three Patriarchs, who are called "many," as we shall explain in its entry. And she is called "daughter of waves" when she draws nourishment from Binah or from Chesed, and "waves" according to the explanation that he explained:

Inner houses or outer [בתי גוואי או בראי, batei gavvai o barai]: the inner are the first three sefirot, the concealed ones; and the outer are the seven sefirot, which are the seven days of the Structure. And the matter of "sadness in the inner houses and not in the outer houses" is explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 12. Thus far our poor strength has reached in the explanation of the Bet, with the divine help that is bestowed upon us; and behold, we are entering into the explanation of the entry Gimel, with the help of the Name:

Redemption [גאולה, ge'ulah] is Binah; for the principal redemption is in the secret of "it may be redeemed, and in the Jubilee it shall go out" (Lev. 25:31). For there, that is, in the redemption, is freedom, as is known; for the judgments of the accusers rise only up to Binah, and not up to and including it. And from it Yesod draws the redemption; and it is called "redeemer" from the side of Binah, and it bestows the redemption on Malkhut. And this is "if he will redeem you, good [tov]" (Ruth 3:13), as it is said (Isa. 3:10), "Say of the righteous one that it shall be good [tov]"; "and if not" [that is,] if he is not able, "then I [anokhi] will redeem you": Binah, as we explained in its entry. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. And in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 95b), he explained that Malkhut is called "redeemer" by means of Yesod, which bestows in her by means of Netzach and Hod, which assist the coupling, as it is known that they are the two testicles of the male. And he said there that therefore the four of them together, Netzach, Hod, Yesod and Malkhut, are called "four redemptions":

Pride [גאון, ga'on]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it as Tiferet; and these are his words: "the pride of Jacob" (Amos 6:8; Nah. 2:3; Ps. 47:5); "I will sing to YHVH, for He is highly exalted [ga'oh ga'ah]" (Exod. 15:1). And they are not a full proof. And it is possible that the matter of pride is according to the manifestation of effluence through which the sefirah is exalted and clothed in exaltation and elevation through it; and there are faint glimmerings of proof for this in the Zohar:

The swelling of the sea [גאות הים, ge'ut ha-yam] (Ps. 89:10): he explained [in the Zohar], in Parashat Noach (fol. 69b), that the thread of Chesed drawn down to Malkhut is called "the swelling of the sea"; and the reason is that through it the sea [which is Malkhut] is raised up, and it lifts her upward to be united with her husband, as in the matter of "and his right hand embraces me" (Song 2:6):

High [גבוה, gavoha] without qualification: "high" is the hint at the Ein Sof, for it is higher than all, without end. However, sometimes, incidentally, it is related to other attributes too, as it is said (Eccl. 5:7), "for one higher than the high watches, and there are higher ones over them":

Boundary [גבול, gevul]: he explained in the Tikkunim that Malkhut is called gevul for the reason that she is the boundary of the four-letter name; for up to her the Emanation reaches, and no further. And she is the last Heh, and she is the end and limit of the Emanation. And she is so called from the side of Binah and Chokhmah; for from the side of the Emanator she rises without limit, and the Emanator is concealed and united in Keter:

Gevurah [גבורה, gevurah]: the attribute of Isaac, the harsh attribute of judgment, is so called. And in the book Sha'arei Tzedek it is explained [as] the strength of judgment and the power of might; besides [the sense of] "the mighty in strength" who tremble [before God] and conquer their inclination, as it is said (Avot 4:1), "Who is mighty? He who conquers his inclination." And he explained that the mighty one is a chariot for Gevurah, and fit to enter its palace. And the rains, for the reason that they come down by the power of judgment, are called "the might [gevurot] of the rains," as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit 8b): "a day of rain is as hard as a day of judgment." And in Sefer ha-Shem Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is called Gevurah for the reason that it prevails and grows mighty to do judgment and vengeance, as is fitting for the upper ones and the lower ones. And in Sefer ha-Orah (Gate 6) he wrote fine words on this matter, and this is the summary of his words: "This attribute grows mighty to do judgment on the transgressors, and it is the one that takes vengeance on those who rise up; and it is the court above; and through the power of Gevurah all the judgments are completed; and it is the one that repays all who are fit for repayment. And when Israel sinned, the power of Gevurah is weakened; and this is what the prophet said (Isa. 63:15), 'Where are Your zeal and Your mighty acts [gevurotekha]?' And above this Gevurah there is a bestowing power, and it is Binah; [many powers of might spring from her,] and they are called gevurot, as it is written (Ps. 106:2), 'Who [mi] can utter the mighty acts of YHVH?'; and Mi is Binah, as will be explained. And when Israel are good and meritorious, those mighty acts are bestowed on Gevurah, and it takes the vengeance of YHVH; and then Israel prevail over the nations of the world." Thus far from Sefer ha-Orah. And in the book Sha'arei Tzedek, on the matter of the gevurot, he explained that Binah is called gevurot because her mighty acts annul the power of Gevurah, as it is said (Isa. 14:27), "and His hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?" Thus far his words. And of Gevurah Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that Fear [Pachad] is called gibbor [mighty], in the masculine, and Malkhut gevurah, in the feminine, as we shall explain in the entry gedulah, with the help of the Name. And Tiferet, from the side of Gevurah, is called gibbor. And likewise the angel Gabriel, from the side of his nourishment from there, is called "the doer of mighty acts." And he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (fol. 83), and these are his words: "'Who can utter [yemallel],' etc. 'Who can utter'? It should have said 'Who can speak [yedabber]'! Rabbi Chiyya said: As it is said (Deut. 23:26), 'then you may pluck the ears [melilot] with your hand.' 'The mighty acts of YHVH,' for they are many, and from one Gevurah they go out. And one taught: the supernal Gevurah, the diadem of diadems [itra de-itrin], is crowned [mit'atra], and from it go out fifty gates, some of them right and some of them left; and each and every one is called Gevurah, and each and every one is crowned with engraved, shining crowns [kardetei]; and all of them are called 'the mighty acts of YHVH.' Rabbi Chiyya said: gevurot is written defectively, for all of them are included in this one." Thus far his words. And the explanation: it was difficult for him that it should have said yedabber, which is the language of speech; for yemallel is the language of the Targum and has no place in the holy tongue. And to this Rabbi Chiyya answered that yemallel is not the language of speech but the language of gathering and collecting, from the language of "then you may pluck the ears," which is the matter of binding sheaves and gathering the ears. And the measure of the verse: Mi, which is Binah, as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name, is the one that gathers and includes all the mighty acts. And this is what he meant in saying "for the mighty acts are many, and from one Gevurah," which is Mi, "they go out" and are emanated; and his intent in this is that Binah too is called Gevurah. And for this he brought a proof: "one taught: the supernal Gevurah," which is Binah; and he called it "the diadem of diadems" because there is another Gevurah, and it is the attribute of Gevurah without qualification, and it too is called the supernal Gevurah, because there is a lower Gevurah, which is Malkhut; therefore he called it "the diadem of diadems," which is Binah, which is a diadem on the head of the Emanation, which are diadems over all. "Is crowned, and from it go out," etc.: the explanation, it is crowned in the secret of the inclusion of the sefirot in it, so that fifty gates may be included in it, which are five sefirot, each one included of ten, as we explained in the Gate of Gates. "Some of them right and some of them left": as we explained there. "And each and every one is called Gevurah": for since they are the offspring of the great supernal Gevurah, which is Binah, mother of them all, they are called gevurot by her name. "And each and every one is crowned with engraved, shining crowns": the explanation, each and every Gevurah of them has powers beneath it without number, into which it spreads; and their gathering together, all of them are called "the mighty acts of YHVH." And therefore of them it is said, Mi, which is Binah, "gathers" and collects "the mighty acts of YHVH," for it includes them. "Rabbi Chiyya said," etc., "all of them are included in this one": the explanation, for in the Tosefta it was not mentioned that it itself is called Gevurah, but it is called Mi and includes all the sefirot. And Rabbi Chiyya says that the word gevurot is written defectively, to show that all of them are included in one Gevurah, which is Binah itself; and of it is written "the might of YHVH" defectively. Behold, we have learned from this the matter that Binah too is called "the might of YHVH," and five gevurot are included in it, and each one spreads out into many gevurot. And one must not explain in this saying that yemallel is the language of mal [circumcising] and cutting, for the saying does not settle with this at all; and it is proved as we explained:

Mistress [גבירה, gevirah]: Malkhut is called so, for she is the mistress. And there is a handmaid, as it is said (Prov. 30:23), "and a handmaid when she is heir to her mistress"; and this is explained in the Gate of Substitutes, with the help of the Name:

Hills [גבעות, geva'ot]: Binah and Malkhut, each one of them is called giv'ah [hill]; and so it is explained in the Zohar (Va'era, fol. 52a). However, "hills" are "the virgins her companions that follow her" (Ps. 45:15); and so it is explained in the Zohar (Tissa, fol. 189b), on the verse "and shall be exalted above the hills" (Isa. 2:2): that the hills are "the virgins her companions that follow her," and she is above them. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 237b), he explained that Binah and Malkhut are called geva'ot, in the plural; and this is the principal explanation of geva'ot, because they are hills and high over what is beneath them: Malkhut is high over all her lower hosts, and Binah is high over the whole Structure. And what he explained there, that the hills are "the virgins her companions that follow her," was compelled by the matter; for since "the house of YHVH" is Malkhut, and it says "and shall be exalted above the hills," it is impossible to explain "hills" in its usual way, which is Binah and Malkhut. Therefore he explained "hills" as "the virgins her companions that follow her," which are her seven palaces; and the principal [sense] of "hills" is always Binah and Malkhut. Further, Malkhut is called the hill of frankincense [giv'at ha-levonah] (Song 4:6), in the secret of the moon [levanah], as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name:

The roof of the canopy [גג החופה, gag ha-chuppah]: the supernal Keter is so called; and it is so called because it is high over the whole Emanation like a roof, and it covers over it, in the likeness of a palanquin and a canopy, as we shall explain in the entry chuppah:

Gad [גד, gad] is the Shekhinah; and she is called Gad, which is from the side of the right; and so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 39b). Further there: "Why is she called Gad? Because she is included of seven sefirot, which come to the number of gad [7]." Thus far his words. Behold, it is explicit that Malkhut, when she is included of seven from the side of Chesed, is called Gad. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 244), he explained that Gad means Gimel-Dalet: Gimel is Binah, which gives drink to the Dalet, which is Malkhut, who is poor [dalah], as is known. And it is possible that the hint of the word is that the Gimel hints at the three Patriarchs, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, and the Dalet beneath them, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut; for by way of these the effluence comes. And the reason that she is called Gad from the side of Chesed is that Binah is called "the one who bestows kindness [gomelet chesed]," and this is the explanation of Gimel [gimel, gomel]; and this is its point [stretching] downward toward the right side. And in the Tikkunim elsewhere (Tikkun 21, fol. 52b): "Gad is right and left: gomel dallim [who bestows on the poor]." Thus far his words. And that is: the right is gomel, Binah, who bestows, and her inclining is toward the right; and the poor is Malkhut, the place of the poor, and her inclining is toward the left, in the secret of poverty:

Gedulah [גדולה, gedulah, Greatness]: Chesed is so called; and the reason is explained by the commentators, and these are their words: "It is called Gedulah because all the sefirot and the powers grow great [mitgaddelim] from this sefirah, even the accusers. And this is what the verse says (Ps. 104:21): 'The young lions roar after their prey and seek their food from El.' The young lions are the accusers; 'roar' means to bring out slander and to accuse the lowly world; and although they are emanated from the side of the left, they 'seek their food from El,' for El is the attribute of Chesed, and they seek bestowal. And therefore it is called Gedulah." Thus far his words; and his words are clear. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 118a) it appears that Chesed is called gadol [great], and Malkhut from its side is called gedulah; and likewise Gevurah, Fear, is called gibbor, and Malkhut from its side gevurah, etc. And these are the words there: "And from the side of the three Patriarchs, who are called El, Elohim, YHVH, who are 'the great, the mighty and the awesome God' (Deut. 10:17), she is called Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet." Thus far his words. And behold, he explained that Malkhut is called Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet from the side of the three Patriarchs; and the Patriarchs themselves are called great, mighty and awesome. And the word gedulah is in Malkhut: that is, gadol [with] Heh; and the explanation: the Heh clothed in the garment of the great one, which is Chesed. And after this manner it appears in Tiferet, which is [glorious, mefo'ar], and the Heh is called tiferet in the feminine; and it will be explained, with the help of the Name, in the entry tiferet:

Body [גויה, geviyyah]: the commentators wrote, and in particular Rabbi Moshe [de León], that it is in Yesod; and it is far-fetched. And it is true that Yesod, the covenant of circumcision, is called "the head of the body" [rosh ha-geviyyah] in the language of the Mishnah. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Tiferet is called geviyyah, and these are his words: "'And two covered their bodies' (Ezek. 1:11): this is the central pillar, which is the body." Thus far his words. And the matter is clear:

Skull [גלגלת, gulgolet] is a title for the first three in general. However, in particular, in the skull there are three airs and three brains; and they are Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Yod, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Yod: three Yods in Keter; and Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Alef: three Alefs in Chokhmah. The Alefs are female, and airs in which the Yods, which are the concealed drops of the brains, are concealed. And just as the drops are concealed in the airs that are in them, as mentioned, so Keter is concealed in Chokhmah; and all of it is a title for the head. However, Keter is called karkafta [the cranium]: for just as that bone is over the brain and over everything, so Keter is over all the sefirot and crowns them:
Wheel [גלגל, galgal] is a title for the Shekhinah, through whom the souls are cycled [in reincarnation]; and see the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 216b):

The bowls of the capitals [גולת הכותרות, gullot ha-koteret] (1 Kings 7:41): it is already known that they are on the heads of the pillars that Solomon made in the Temple; and he called them Jachin and Boaz, and they correspond to Netzach and Hod. And on their heads are the bowls of the capitals, and they correspond to Gedulah [and] Gevurah, this one to the right and that one to the left. And therefore Gedulah is called the right bowl, and Gevurah the left bowl. However, Yesod is called the bowl of gold (Zech. 4:2–3), which empties the good oil into the head of the lampstand; and the pure gold is from the side of judgment, as expounded in the Gate of Particulars of Names, on the name Elohim:

Body [גוף, guf]: Tiferet is so called. And the reason is that, just as from the body the hands and the feet spread out to four sides, so Tiferet has two arms, which are Gedulah and Gevurah, this one to the right and that one to the left, and two thighs, Netzach and Hod; and it is the extension of the body in the middle. And just as from the body the organ is drawn between the thighs, so from Tiferet Yesod is drawn. And just as the body has the head above it, so Tiferet has the first three above it. And just as the body has a belly, so the Shekhinah is a belly to Tiferet. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 18, fol. 35a): "The Shekhinah is the belly, and her body is the central pillar." The intent is her manifestation in the house of her husband before the diminishment. And by this will be understood what Rabbi Moshe [de León] wrote in Sefer ha-Shem, that Tiferet is called "the body of the Shekhinah," although in the reason he goes another way; and these are his words: "The body of the Shekhinah: know that the whole Structure together is called Shekhinah, and Malkhut too is called Shekhinah; and in the matter of the Emanation together, Tiferet is the body and the first three are the head," etc., "and with the helpmate corresponding to him it is a complete man, as it is said, 'male and female He created them,'" etc. Thus far his words. And what I wrote seems to me the principal [explanation], for they are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him:

Gezerah shavah [גזרה שוה, gezerah shavah, an equal cut]: he explained in the Tikkunim that Tiferet is so called for the reason that it cuts [gozer] and divides between the husks, so that they are not joined and do not couple, but are kept apart. And it is also called shavah [equal] because it makes equal between the two (extremities) [arms] that are in holiness, in the secret of the arbitration:

Coal [גחלת, gachelet]: Chokhmah is called "coal" when it is clothed in the secret of Gevurah; and likewise Malkhut is called "coal" in her receiving from there, to show that they are divided in the great fire. And likewise Chokhmah by itself is called "coal"; and this is the matter of "like the flame bound to the coal" [Sefer Yetzirah 1:7]. And the explanation: just as the coal brought out from its potential the flame, and it is not a new thing in it, for the flame was in its potential from the first, and nothing was added to it except bringing the flame out from concealment to revealing; so it is already known that the Yod emanated the letters Heh-Vav-Heh, as is known. And behold, the Yod is the coal and the Vav the flame; and the first Heh is the five lights that shine in the five colors of the last Heh, as is known (from Tikkun 21, fol. 43b), and it is explained in the Gate of Colors. And we have already explained in the Gate From Below to Above that, just as the Yod, Chokhmah, from above to below is coal and flame, so the Yod from below to above is coal and flame, in the secret of "I am the first and I am the last" (Isa. 44:6); and the form of Alef will prove it, as we explained in the preceding gates:

The sinew of the thigh-vein [גיד הנשה, gid ha-nasheh]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 19, fol. 39, and fol. 52b) that the sinew of the thigh-vein is the Shekhinah with the Righteous One: for the Shekhinah is called Gad, as we explained in its entry, and with the Yod of the Righteous One it becomes gid [Gimel-Yod-Dalet]. And we have already explained the matter of Gad above. And indeed the matter of "and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was put out of joint" (Gen. 32:26) does not belong here, but in the Gate of the Thigh of Jacob:

Gehinnom [גיהנם, gehinnom]: all the commentators agreed that it is in Gevurah. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason: "for it is from the side of the accusers, within and without; and it is a fire not blown, and it is a parable for the power of the harsh judgment." Thus far his words. And he explained it well. For this title is for the black color, as we explained in the Gate of Colors. And it is called gei, the language of depth, for "the mouth of strange women is a deep pit" (Prov. 22:14):

The valley of vision [גי חזיון, gei chizzayon] (Isa. 22:1): Malkhut is so called; and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 203a): for she is a mirror into which all the prophets look; and she is so called at the time of her nourishment from the seers, the prophets, Netzach and Hod. And she is called gei, the language of depth, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, "he went down to the Chariot," which is the depth of the matters in their hiddenness; and therefore Malkhut is the depth of prophecy:

A spring shut up [גל נעול, gal na'ul] (Song 4:12): the Shekhinah is so called because she is a virgin, "and no man had known her" (Gen. 24:16), in the secret of the rib, her concealed manifestation; and then "no man had known her" yet, as we explained in the Gate of the Diminishment [of the Moon], chapter 10; and so they explained in the Tikkunim:

The wheels of the Chariot [גלגלי המרכבה, galgalei ha-merkavah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that they are Netzach and Hod. And the matter is that the Chariot itself is: the face of a lion, Chesed; the face of an ox, Gevurah; the face of a man or of an eagle, Tiferet; the face of an eagle or of a man, Malkhut. And the wheels of the Chariot are Netzach and Hod (see above in the entry ofan):

Waves [גלים, gallim]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 63a), on the verse "Cry aloud with your voice, O daughter of Gallim" (Isa. 10:30): "The daughter of Gallim: the daughter of Abraham our father; so they established. Daughter of gallim, as it is said, 'a spring [gal] shut up.' Gallim are rivers that gather and go and enter into her and fill her; as it is said, 'Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates' (Song 4:13)." And the explanation: the daughter of Gallim is Malkhut; and she is called daughter of Abraham our father; and the reason is that through him she draws the thread of Chesed drawn over her. And this is the explanation of gallim: they are the sefirot, when they are all united to bestow on Malkhut; and they are called gallim by her name, when they enter there; for she is called gal, and they are gallim by her name. And when she is full of them she reveals [megallah] their manifestation; for she is the one full of the waters, "and its waves [gallav] roar" (Jer. 31:35). And he brought a proof of what he said, "and enter into her and fill her," from the verse "Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates": the explanation, "your shoots" [shelachayikh], the rivers sent [sheluchim] to you, make you "an orchard of pomegranates," for you are full, like an orchard of pomegranates; as they said, of blessed memory, "full of commandments like pomegranates." And accordingly it is found that the seven sefirot, the seven rivers, are called gallim when they are in the gal, which is Malkhut. And in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 249) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Binah is called gallim, and these are his words: "The world to come is called gallim, because everything stands in it and is included in it, heaps upon heaps [tillei tillim], and it goes out from it to all." Thus far his words. And behold, he explained that Binah is called gallim for the reason that the effluence fit for all the sefirot, as what is fit for Gevurah for Gevurah and what is fit for Malkhut for Malkhut, and likewise for the other sefirot, all of it stands there in heaps upon heaps, and from there it is bestowed on all of them. And behold, accordingly, just as Malkhut is called gallim, so Binah is called gallim: this one from the side of her bestowing and that one from the side of her receiving.

And further he gave there another explanation: that Binah is called gallim, and the waves are the seven sefirot, which go out from Binah and come to Malkhut, like the waves of the sea that are never quiet. And on all the explanations, both Binah and Malkhut are called gallim on account of the sefirot, which are called gallim, as we explained. And in Parashat Noach (fol. 69b) he explained that the waves of the sea are powers that are in Malkhut; they roar and demand to tear prey, and they are the ones that swell in the strength of judgment; and of them it is said (Ps. 104:21), "The young lions roar after their prey." And it is possible to say that they are the waves that are revealed in her from the upper waves; and it is all one matter:

Camel [גמל, gamal]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 236a), and these are his words: "The end of harsh agitation is a camel below; and this is the secret of death," etc. "Come and see: this camel is the secret of what is written, 'and his recompense [gemulo] shall be repaid to him' (Prov. 19:17); this is the recompense of the wicked," etc. "And this is the camel that stands to devour all and to destroy all." Thus far his words; see there:

The bestowing of kindnesses [גמילות חסדים, gemilut chasadim]: Malkhut is so called from the side of Chesed; so it is explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 114b, these are his words: "For the Shekhinah from the side of Chesed is called the bestowing of kindnesses"):

Garden [גן, gan]: Binah and Malkhut are so called; and the reason is clear. For Binah is a garden for the plantings that were "like the horns of locusts," as we explained above in the preceding gates. And Malkhut is called "garden" because she is a garden for the lower plantings: for all that is the delight and will of the Emanator to emanate there, all comes to the lower garden. And in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 4), he explained, and these are his words: "For Rabbi Eleazar said: Just as this garden needs to be hoed, to be guarded and to be watered," etc.; see there. Thus far his words. And he explained the matter of guarding as "I have set watchmen upon your walls, O Jerusalem" (Isa. 62:6), and likewise "every man has his sword upon his thigh," etc. (Song 3:8). And in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that she is called gan because she is included of the fifty-three [gan] portions of the Written Torah, to show that she draws nourishment and emanates the plantings of the garden that belong to her husband, as is known; and he is the one who waters them, to make her plantings grow, as is known. Further, there are gardens, and they are the five sefirot; for each one of them brings out fruit after its kind; and likewise they have a spring that waters them, and it is the garden, Binah. And after the garden is made a spring, it waters the gardens. And likewise the lower garden, Malkhut, from a garden becomes a spring and waters the gardens that are beneath her, "the virgins her companions that follow her" (Ps. 45:15); and so Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair explained in the Zohar (Parashat Balak, fol. 201b). And likewise Binah and Malkhut, each one of them is called the Garden of Eden. And in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 141b), he explained that Malkhut is called a watered garden (Isa. 58:11) when Yesod is within her and fills her and waters her with the upper waters, in its good custom. Further, she is called the garden of nuts (Song 6:11), for she is a garden sown from the nut that is in Yesod:

Vine [גפן, gefen]: the Shekhinah is so called, for she is "a fruitful vine" (Ps. 128:3); and she is "a vine You brought out of Egypt" (Ps. 80:9), when they went out of the exile. And of her it is said, "Look down from heaven, and behold, and remember this vine" (Ps. 80:15): a vine which is certainly zot [this]. And the reason she is called vine is that just as the vine does not receive grafting from another kind, so Malkhut receives only from her husband; so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 238a). And in her are three branches, which are the clusters that we explained in their entry; and she draws from the wine preserved in its grapes; they are grapes good to dream of, the effluence bestowed from Binah, as we shall explain in the entry yayin:

And there is a vine called "the degenerate plant of a strange vine" (Jer. 2:21), "their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter" (Deut. 32:32); and they are the husks. And there is an intermediate vine, and it is the vine and the grapes that are not good to dream of, which are from the side of judgment:

Stranger [גר, ger]: sometimes Tiferet is outside his place, and he is exiled because of the iniquities, as is known: "As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man that wanders," etc. (Prov. 27:8). And, as it were, he bestows on the outer ones; and then he is called ger. And of this Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, whose level is Tiferet, said, "for I have been a stranger in a strange land" (Exod. 18:3). And for this reason the one who converts is called ger: for until now he was standing in the place of the husk, in a strange land, drinking "the wine of their drink offerings" (Deut. 32:38), the bestowal of the degenerate plant of the strange vine, may the Compassionate One save us. Thus far the poverty of our knowledge has reached in the explanation of the letter Gimel; and behold, we have entered into the explanation of the letter Dalet, with the help of Binah, which bestows understanding [binah] on His creatures:

Speech [דבור, dibbur] is the Shekhinah, Malkhut; and she is so called for the reason that Tiferet is called voice and Malkhut speech. Just as speech is the dividing of the voices, the movements of the articulation, so Malkhut is the revealing of Tiferet, and shows him in his movements. And she is so called from the side of Gevurah, for every dibbur is a language of harshness. And not on this account do we deny that it is found in the other levels, as he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 86b), and these are his words: "Rabbi Eleazar said: We have been roused [to note that] va-yagged [and he told], va-yedabber [and he spoke] and va-yomer [and he said] are each explained according to its reason. Va-yedabber is in the revealing of the outer level, which is not the inner level like those upper levels; and this is 'I speak righteousness' (Isa. 45:19). Va-yagged is a hint at the inner, upper level, which rules over speech; and this is 'I declare [maggid] things that are right [meisharim]' (there). What is meisharim? This is the upper level, in which Jacob dwells, as it is written, 'You have established equity [meisharim]' (Ps. 99:4). And therefore maggid is written and not dover. Rabbi Isaac said: But it is written, 'And He declared [va-yagged] to you His covenant' (Deut. 4:13)! He said to him: It is certainly so: it is a level that rules over the lower one, which is 'I speak righteousness'; and in all of it there is [something] to look into. Come and see: although speech is lower, do not say that it is not upper; rather it is certainly full of everything, and it is an upper level. And your sign: 'For it is not an empty thing [davar] for you' (Deut. 32:47)." Thus far his words. And the intent is that Rabbi Eleazar explained that the words va-yagged, va-yedabber and va-yomer are different levels: for va-yagged is from the side of Chokhmah, as will be explained in the entry haggadah; va-yomer is Malkhut from the side of Tiferet, as we explained in its entry; and va-yedabber is in Malkhut herself. And for this reason the verse did not say "I speak righteousness and equity," [or] "I declare righteousness and equity," but "I speak righteousness, I declare equity": for with tzedek [righteousness], which is Malkhut, it used the language of speech, which is right for her; and with meisharim, which is Tiferet, it used the language of haggadah, which is a language right for the one who emanates the meisharim. And by this the words of Rabbi Eleazar are explained. And because Rabbi Eleazar said that maggid is found only with meisharim, and it was not possible to say "I declare righteousness and equity," for the language of haggadah is not right for Malkhut, therefore [Rabbi Isaac] objected to him from the verse "And He declared to you His covenant." And there is no doubt that it was not hidden from him that "covenant" may be in Yesod, as we explained in its entry; and nevertheless it was difficult [for him], for there is no haggadah in the place that Rabbi Eleazar assigned to us. And Rabbi Eleazar answered that since it is above Malkhut, it is possible that it is related to Yesod; and this covenant is an upper level relative to tzedek, and therefore maggid can properly be said of it; but in tzedek it is not found in any way, and therefore it did not say "I declare righteousness and equity." And in order to guard against objection, he said that although we assign these places to them, not on this account do we deny that, in a remote way, they are found outside their places. And this is what he said, "and in all of it there is [something] to look into": the explanation, they need looking into, for sometimes it is found outside their places for known reasons, in the matter of the aspects and the manifestations. And this is what he said, "Come and see: although speech is lower, do not say," etc.: for sometimes it too is found related to upper levels. And the reason is that it always means Malkhut, but [sometimes the intent is] the upper level that is revealed in Malkhut. And this is what he said, "rather it is certainly full of everything": for this attribute that is related to speech is an attribute in which all the attributes are seen; and therefore through her it is related also to the upper attributes. "And your sign: 'For it is not an empty thing'": the explanation, the word dibbur is only from the attribute hu [He], which is Tiferet. Thus far the explanation of the saying. And from it it is explained that the principal [place] of speech is in Malkhut, and it is related also to the upper attributes, remotely and by means of Malkhut:

Word [דבר, davar] is Malkhut; and this is "mighty in strength, that fulfil His word [devaro]" (Ps. 103:20); and it is explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 191): "who set right this davar," etc. And likewise "after the order [al divrati] of Melchizedek" (Ps. 110:4), which is the Shekhinah; and he called her divrati because she was the attribute of David. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that she is also called dever [pestilence], as "Before Him goes the pestilence," etc. (Hab. 3:5); for she is certainly "the hand of YHVH [that] is" (Exod. 9:3). And he said that some say that pestilence comes from Yesod, for pestilence is a mixing of the air, and likewise Yesod is not simple in its compassion, for it is the gathering of all the sefirot, as is known (and God forbid to say so; so it is written in the book Kehillat Ya'akov, entry dever):

Things [דברים, devarim]: he explained in the Zohar (Vayera, fol. 149) that Malkhut is also called devarim. And it is possible that she is so called with the joining to her of her seven maidens; for each one of them is called davar, and their union is devarim. And as proof from there, he called the husk "after the things" [achar ha-devarim], which is behind the devarim; and that is certainly behind all the maidens, as explained in the Gate of the Substitute Palaces and the Gate of Substitutes:

Honey [דבש, devash] is from the left side, in the power of Gevurah; and therefore its color is red. And though it is sweet, nevertheless of it it is said (Prov. 25:16), "Have you found honey? Eat as much as is enough for you." And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 39b), and these are his words: "'And its taste was like wafers with honey' (Exod. 16:31): from the side of the left." Thus far his words. And therefore it is said (Lev. 2:11), "for any leaven and any honey"; for honey is close to leaven, except that leaven is on the left altogether, in the secret of the husk, and honey in the secret of the strength of judgment. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 240), he explained that Malkhut, the Oral Torah, is called honey; and it is all one matter, for from the side of the left she is called honey:
Two-faced [ד"ו פרצופין, du partzufin]: they are in Tiferet and Malkhut, for both of them were emanated as one, as in the matter of Adam and Eve, who were two-faced.

And this matter I wrote at length in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon. However, they are so called when she is in that concealed manifestation that they had before the sawing apart, as will be explained there:

The faithful beloved [דוד נאמן, dod ne'eman]: he explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 189) that the Righteous One is called the faithful beloved; and so he explained there on the words "that goes down sweetly for my beloved [le-dodi]" (Song 7:10). And it is possible that he is so called for the reason that he is the beloved of Malkhut, for he is the secret of joining Redemption to Prayer. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 4), he said that Tiferet and Malkhut are called dodim [lovers]; and we explained it at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And accordingly Yesod is called dod, for it unites the two lovers, for through it is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, as is known. And in Parashat Shemini (fol. 39b) he explained that dod without qualification is Gevurah; and so he explained on the Song of Songs. And the reason may be that affection and love are aroused by the fire of Gevurah, and for this reason Gevurah is called dod. And accordingly it is found that they are three matters: the faithful beloved in Yesod; dodim, Tiferet and Malkhut; and dod, Gevurah. And it is possible that it is in Yesod from the side of Gevurah:

David [דוד, david]: Malkhut is so called for the reason that David, from the side of Malkhut, was made a chariot for this attribute. And likewise it is found that he set her right, when he sought her with his songs and his psalms; for all his praises depend on her, as is known. And indeed it was his attribute from the side of Hod; and therefore [David, with the word counted as one,] comes to the number of hod [15]. And so it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Vayikra, fol. 4a) that the attribute of David is the attribute of Hod; and there are the straits of the husks; and therefore he contended with those who rose up. And from the side of Hod she is called David:

Generation [דור, dor]: the explanation, Tiferet and Yesod. From the side of Yesod they are six extremities; and in Tiferet, which is included more because of its great light, they come to sixty. And this is "All the souls that came with Jacob [into Egypt] ... were sixty-six" (Gen. 46:26): for sixty is from the side of Tiferet, and six from the side of Yesod. And when it rises to the Alef it will be sixty thousand; and when it rises further to the supernal Keter it will be sixty myriads. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 37a). And all these generations cycle in Malkhut, for she is the cycle of all. And this is "A generation goes and a generation comes, and the earth stands for ever" (Eccl. 1:4). You learn that Tiferet and Yesod are each called dor. And this is "Generation to generation shall praise Your works" (Ps. 145:4): for "work" is Malkhut, and "from generation to generation" they bestow into her; for this is the intent of "praise" everywhere, as will be explained with the help of the Name. However, there is one who explained dor as Binah, in the secret of the Jubilee, which is "liberty [deror] to all its inhabitants" (Lev. 25:10), for she is the place of freedom; and the second dor is Malkhut, in the secret of the two Hehs, for both of them are equal:

Ink [דיו, deyo] is Binah. And the explanation: just as the ink is black and concealed, so the world to come, Binah, is concealed; and the world to come is attained only by one who blackens himself in this world. And it is one of the permutations of the Yod [Yod-Vav-Dalet], which is in Chokhmah. And these things Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna [in Parashat Terumah, fol. 159]:

Judge [דיין, dayyan]: all the commentators explained that dayyan is a title for Gevurah. But in the Ra'aya Meheimna, in various places, he explained that Tiferet from the side of Malkhut is called dayyan; and this is "the true Judge," for he is called truth. And who is as expert for us in the titles as Rashbi, peace be upon him? And the reason is that Malkhut is judgment [din], as they said, of blessed memory, "the law of the kingdom [malkhuta] is law [dina]"; and likewise a permutation of Adonai is dina; and from that side Tiferet is called dayyan:

The judgment of Torah and the judgment of truth [דין תורה ודין אמת, din torah ve-din emet] is the Shekhinah; and she is called din for the reason that we explained. And she is called truth and Torah from the side of Tiferet, in whom are truth and Torah, as was explained; and each one will be explained in its entry. And this matter is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 117):

Crushed [דך, dakh]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 13) that Yesod is called dakh, for it includes the twenty-four [Kaf-Dalet] letters of "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and ever." And when there is effluence and water of blessing in it, it is called kad [pitcher], for it is a pitcher full of water. And when "the river is wasted and dried up" (Isa. 19:5), it is called dakh; and of it it is said (Ps. 74:21), "Let not the crushed one [dakh] turn back ashamed." And Malkhut is called dakkah in the secret of the lack, as she is called kaddah [her pitcher] in the secret of the fullness, as we shall explain in its entry:

Dokhyam [דכים, dokhyam, their pounding] (Ps. 93:3): he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 46) that Malkhut from the side of Yesod is called dokhyam; and the explanation is dakh yam [the sea is crushed]: her sea, which has no effluence. And the reason is that it is below her, and it is not in its hand to bestow plenty of blessings. And further, because she is included of the twenty-four letters of "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and ever," which are in Yesod. And their hint I explained in the Gate of the Fifty Gates:

Poor [דל, dal]: the Righteous One is so called. And the reason is that he is poor in relation to Tiferet, who is rich. Further, he is called dal for the reason that "it has nothing of its own [de-leit leih]." And so it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Tissa, fol. 188). And then Malkhut is called dallah, as is known, and it will be explained there, with the help of the Name:

Blood [דם, dam]: this is explained in the Zohar Chadash on the Song of Songs (fol. 86b): that the final Mem hints at Binah when she is closed in the closed Mem, so as not to bestow; and then Malkhut is in the form of Dalet. And for this reason dam shows judgment, for these two are the causes of judgment, as is known; see there:

The twilight of the sun [דמדומי חמה, dimdumei chammah] is explained as Malkhut; and the reason is that she is taken from the sun, which is Tiferet. And it is possible to explain other reasons: that there the sun is concealed and silent [domem] and is not heard; or it is possible that it is the coupling of the sun, that is, a coming-in in silence:

Likeness [דמיון, dimyon] is Malkhut; and she is so called when she sits on the Throne of Glory, as was explained in the Gate of ABYA. And then, when she is included of all the visions and faces of the prophets, she is called dimyon. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 30a), and these are his words: "Because all the faces of the prophets are inscribed in her, she is called dimyon." And the intent is that all the matters that are likened [mitdammim] in the true prophets, Netzach and Hod, are revealed in her. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained this word as Netzach; and the matter is as we explained:

The likeness of a man [דמות אדם, demut adam] (Ezek. 1:26) is Malkhut. So he explained (in Tikkun 10, fol. 24a), and these are his words: "The small Heh is the likeness of a man; in it YHVH is completed":

Tears [דמעות, dema'ot]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 19a), on the matter that the Holy One, blessed be He, sheds two tears into the Great Sea, etc. And these are his words: "We have learned: among the ten crowns of the King, the Holy One, blessed be He, has two tears; and they are two attributes of judgment, for judgment comes from the two of them, as it is said, 'These two things have befallen you' (Isa. 51:19). And when the Holy One, blessed be He, remembers His children, He brings them down into the Great Sea, which is the sea of wisdom, to sweeten them; and He turns the attribute of judgment into the attribute of compassion, and has compassion on them. Rabbi Judah said: two tears from which judgment comes, from which the tears come." Thus far his words. And the explanation is clear: there are two attributes of judgment among the ten sefirot. And it is possible that they are Gevurah [and] Hod, both of which are judgment, as we explained in the preceding gates; or Gevurah and Malkhut; and the first is the principal. And when they are clothed in judgment, "the Holy One, blessed be He, remembers His children": the explanation, the suffering that Israel bear for the Torah in exile. "He brings them down into the sea of wisdom": the explanation, He raises them up; as "so-and-so went down to the Chariot" (brought in the Sha'ar, fol. 15b), where, from their subtlety to their depth, the going up to them is called going down. And likewise "the one who goes down before the ark," and likewise "so-and-so went down to the depth of the mind," etc., where the intent is going up; and many like them. "Into the Great Sea, the sea of wisdom": the sea of wisdom, the explanation, Binah is so called, as is known. And she is called "the Great Sea" when she bestows in Gedulah [Greatness]; and she is called "the sea of wisdom" when she is united with Chokhmah and Chokhmah bestows great compassion into her. And then she is filled with milk, in the secret of the upper whiteness; she bestows and suckles these two attributes from that compassion. And then "the blazing eyes are bathed in milk" (Song 5:12), as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 10. And when the eyes of Gevurah are bathed in the milk of the Mother, it turns to compassion, and the judgment is annulled, as we explained there:

Da'at [דעת, da'at, Knowledge] without qualification is Tiferet. And the Righteous One too is called Da'at; and this is "For YHVH is a God of knowledges [de'ot]" (1 Sam. 2:3): de'ot, two. And in permutation, edut [testimony]; and there is no testimony of fewer than two. And it is called da'at from the language of "And the man knew [yada] Eve his wife" (Gen. 4:1), "who know [yod'ei] the joyful shout" (Ps. 89:16), whose explanation is the language of joining. And this is also the reason: for Tiferet unites Chokhmah and Binah in the secret of Da'at, as explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter; and likewise Yesod unites and couples Tiferet and Malkhut. And we have already spoken at length on this in the preceding gates. However, each one of them is called Da'at, "each according to his work that they do." And close to this are the words of Rabbi Moshe [de León] and the words of the author of Sha'arei Tzedek:
