Dar [דר, dar]: all the commentators agreed that it is Malkhut. And in the book Sha'arei Tzedek he explained the reason: that she is a dwelling [dirah] for the four-letter name, which is Tiferet, as is known; and further, that she dwells [darah] among us, as it is said (Lev. 16:16), "that dwells with them in the midst of their uncleanness." And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that dar is the name of a precious stone; and also from the language of "thorns and thistles [dardar]" (Gen. 3:18); and likewise this attribute, for from her are good and evil. And he said that every dar is the language of liberty [deror]; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] himself explained dar as Binah; and it will be in Malkhut too, from her side:

South [דרום, darom] is Chesed; and so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra 25b): "Whoever wishes to become wise, let him turn southward"; and the explanation of "turn southward" is to direct [his intention] to the south, which is Chesed, for there is the drawing of Chokhmah to Chesed, as is known. And others explained the south as Tiferet, and the reasoning compelled this; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] likewise gave these two explanations. And its principal [place] is in Chesed. But why the south is parched and dry, and it should have been the reverse, we shall explain in the entry negbah, with the help of the Name:

Swallow [דרור, deror]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6, fol. 19b), on the verse "and the swallow [deror] a nest for herself" (Ps. 84:4), that Binah is called deror, in the secret of the Jubilee, which is called deror [liberty]:

Ways [דרכים, derakhim]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 197b), that the ways are channels through which Gedulah, Gevurah and Tiferet bestow on Malkhut when they receive from Binah. And they are called ways with respect to their being revealed and apprehended by all, like this way, which is an entrance for all; which is not so with the paths, which are concealed, as explained in its place. And in the Tikkunim he explained that "way" without qualification is Tiferet, and proved the matter from the verse (Num. 24:17), "a star shall tread forth [darakh] out of Jacob," and likewise "the way of the eagle in the heavens" (Prov. 30:19). And though there are many times that derekh is feminine, as "the way of women is upon me" (Gen. 31:35), and likewise those that he explained at the beginning of tractate Kiddushin, that there is a derekh that is feminine, the intent is that it is drawn from the males to the females; and that is "the way of a man with a maiden" (Prov. 30:19). Thus far the poverty of our knowledge has reached in the explanation of this entry; and behold, we are entering into the explanation of the entry of the letter Heh, with the help of the One who helps the poor and needy in Torah:

On the letter Heh: the letter itself is explained in the Gate of Letters. However, there is a difference between its coming at the head of the word and its coming at the end of the word, as in shim'ah [hear], selichah [forgive], hakshivah [hearken] (Dan. 9:19), where it is a hint at the last attribute; and so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Chayyei (perhaps he means fol. 132a). And a Heh at the head of the word is a hint at Binah, and at the end of the word at Malkhut. And nevertheless this rule does not always hold. And these are the words of the Zohar in Parashat Terumah (fol. 168): "Ha-motzi [who brings forth]: why ha-motzi and not motzi? For it is written, 'who creates [bore] the heavens' (Isa. 42:5), and not 'ha-bore the heavens'; 'who made [oseh] the earth' (Isa. 45:18), and not 'ha-oseh the earth.' Why here ha-motzi? Rather, all the words that are from the secret of the upper, hidden world, the Heh is hidden from there, to show that it is from the stored-away and hidden world. And all the words that are from the lower world, which is more revealed, are written with Heh, as it is written, 'ha-motzi their host by number' (Isa. 40:26), 'ha-kore [who calls] to the waters of the sea' (Amos 5:8): all of them are from the secret of the lower world. And if it is written in a name, it is with Heh, as 'ha-El the great.' And here, where it is in an enclosed way, it is from the secret of the lower world." Thus far his words.

And at first sight this saying appears to oppose what we explained above in the name of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And when we look into it closely, we find it disagreeing with itself in part. For first he said that the Heh of knowledge [the definite article] shows the revealed world, which is Malkhut; and at the end he says, "and here, where it is in a closed way, it is from the secret of the lower world," as though because it is the lower world it must be in a closed way. And besides its disagreeing with itself, the thing itself is contrary to reason. For granted what he said at the beginning, that because it is a revealed world it comes in revealing, and because Binah is a hidden world it comes in concealment and hiddenness, that is well. But on what he says, "and if it is written in a name," it is difficult: is it because she is Binah that it comes with the Heh of knowledge? Therefore we say that the kinds of revealing are two, and the kinds of concealment likewise two. There are two kinds of revealing. The first is the Heh of the revealing of the action: that is, that the action shows what is known, the revealing of an action, as ha-kore, ha-omer [who says], where the Heh of knowledge in the action shows a prior knowledge of the action; and this shows revealing. And there is a second revealing, and it is the revealing of the name itself with the Heh of knowledge, as ha-El ha-gadol; for the Heh shows the revealing of El, as is known, and ha-gadol, as is known. And therefore in the first revealing, which is the revealing of the action, there is concealment there, for it does not mention the name of the doer at all, as ha-kore, ha-omer, ha-oseh: for there is no revealing there of who said, who did, who called. And this matter comes for the title of Malkhut: because she is the revealed world, her action comes in revealing, which shows revealing; and because it is not fitting for the female to rise in name, for "the king's daughter is all glorious within" (Ps. 45:14), therefore she is concealed in the aspect of her name, even if the action is in revealing; because revealing and concealment are both related to her: revealing because she is revealed, concealment because it is not fitting to raise her in name, as we explained. And the correct and true reason for the matter is as we shall further explain with the help of the Name. However, Binah, the upper world: when they mention her action, they mention it with a name of concealment, without the Heh of knowledge, to show that she is a concealed world; and therefore it said bore, oseh. For Binah created the heavens, which are Tiferet, and likewise made the earth, which is Malkhut. And therefore, because she is a concealed world, her actions come in concealment, without the Heh of knowledge. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayera, on the verse (Isa. 38:5), "Behold, I will add [yosif] to your days": for it said yosif [He will add] and did not say "Behold, I will add [osif]," as would be fitting; because the adding of years is from Binah, and Binah is concealed, and therefore it said yosif.

Behold, her actions are fit to be in concealment, in the way that she is concealed. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 235b), and these are his words: "For it is written, 'was reared up [hukam]' (Exod. 40:17), and it did not explain by whose hand; rather, that it was reared up only from the secret of the upper world, which is enclosed and stored away." Thus far. However, in the name itself, on the contrary, this is her eminence: that she rises in name, not in the way of Malkhut. And therefore when the name has the Heh of knowledge it shows Binah, for the Heh hints at her; and not Malkhut, for it is not fitting that she rise in name, and all the more so with the Heh of knowledge in the name, which shows her greatness and her eminence. And with this premise the words of the saying are settled. For he objected: why did it say ha-motzi, as though without the Heh it would not suffice? And it is not so, for we find a matter of present action without Heh, as "who made [oseh] the earth by His power, who established the world by His wisdom" (Jer. 10:12); and there certainly the principal thing is the present making, which is the sustaining of the world at every hour and every moment. And likewise "who creates the heavens": the principal thing is the matter of their constant existence. If so, why did it say ha-motzi, with a superfluous Heh, without need? And he answered, "Rather, all the words," etc.; and he was precise in saying "all the words," meaning matters of actions, and he did not say "all the names and titles," or "words" [teivin]: because the intent is the actions that come with the Heh of knowledge or without Heh, as motzi, oseh or ha-oseh, and the like. But in names, such as ha-harah [to the mountain], ha-yom [the day], and the like, it is a category of its own, as will be explained. And he said "in the world that is more revealed," because, although it is the revealed world, it is in truth also concealed, as we shall explain in the entry mah with the help of the Name. "And if it is written in a name," etc.: the explanation, and if the Heh of knowledge is written in the name of the title itself and not in the action, then the rule is the reverse, that it shows Binah, as we explained. "However, here, where it is in an enclosed way": that it said ha-motzi and did not say who is the one who brings forth, and likewise ha-kore, etc.: all of it is in Malkhut, as "and he called to Moses" (Lev. 1:1), where it does not say who, and it is Malkhut, as is explained in the Zohar in many places; and we shall explain it in the entry "And YHVH: He and His court," in chapter 6. And by this the words of the saying are explained. And the reason for this matter, that Malkhut does not rise in name, is that it is not fitting for the woman to rise in name in the presence of her husband; and therefore she is not so well known. And if so, the Heh of knowledge does not properly apply to her, for she is not known; and likewise it is written of the woman of valor, "Her husband is known in the gates" (Prov. 31:23); but she does not rise in name. But her actions, for her good and for the merit of her matters, are fit to rise in knowledge, with a known name; for her deeds are famous in all the ends of the earth. Or possibly because Binah needs no covering and concealment from the husks; for she is called eagle, for she is like the eagle, which fears none of the birds in the world; and therefore her names are with the Heh of knowledge, to show that she does not fear the husks. However, Malkhut is called dove, and needs covering, as it is written (Ps. 68:14), "the wings of a dove covered with silver." And therefore it is not fitting that her names be with the Heh of knowledge, so as to cover her and conceal her, that the husks may not rule; for she is the dove that fears the pursuing birds. And this premise is explained at length in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 121), and for love of brevity we have not copied his language here. And the principle: a Heh at the end of a word is always in Malkhut; and a Heh at the head of a word, when it is a hint at the known action, as ha-motzi, is then in Malkhut; and when the action is unqualified, as oseh, bore, they are in Binah. And every Heh of knowledge that is at the head of a name, a literal name that is not an action, is then in Binah and not in Malkhut:

And on the matter of the large Heh and the small Heh, he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 93), these are his words: that the large Heh is in Binah and the small Heh in Malkhut. And further, he gave there another explanation: that the large Heh is a hint at Malkhut when she draws nourishment from Yesod; and therefore it is large, to show her completeness in her fullness, being filled from the sun. And when she is a small Heh, it hints at her being in the diminishment and lack of the moon, and drawing nourishment from judgment; but not so much as when she is called by the name Dalet, for she is poor [dalah] altogether. And they said there that the last explanation is the principal:

Breath [הבל, hevel]: there are seven breaths, and they are those mentioned in the verse "Vanity [hevel] of vanities," etc. (Eccl. 1:2). And they are: hevel, one; havalim, two: that makes three; hevel havalim, three more: that makes six; "all is hevel": that makes seven. And they are seven sefirot. And it is explained from the language of the breath of the mouth, which means breath of life [neshamah], as it is said, "and all their host by the breath of His mouth" (Ps. 33:6). And likewise there is a breath that rises and a breath that descends, and they are Binah and Malkhut: Binah rises to cleave to Chokhmah, and Malkhut descends to cleave to Tiferet, in the secret of  Y H H V, as we explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapter 15. And in the matter of hevel there is a permutation, lahav [flame], from the language of "hews out flames [lahavot] of fire" (Ps. 29:7); and it is so called from the side of Binah by means of Gevurah:

Telling [הגדה, haggadah]: its principal [place] is in Chokhmah; and every term such as va-yagged, va-tagged, and the like, is in Chokhmah. And so it is expounded on the Song of Songs [in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 84a], on the verse "Tell me [haggidah li]" (Song 1:7) (and in the Zohar, Vayechi, fol. 234b), and in many places of the Zohar. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a) he explained that the lower Chokhmah, from the side of the upper Chokhmah, is called haggadah; and likewise every feminine term in haggadah, and likewise the Midrash of the Haggadah. And elsewhere (Tikkun 21, fol. 44) he explained that Malkhut is called haggadah when YHVH, who is her husband, dwells in her. And the reason may be that the union is impossible except when she receives from Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance:

Footstool [הדום, hadom]: these are the words of Rabbi Moshe [de León] on this title: "Footstool: there are some of the Kabbalists who called Hod 'My footstool'; and it seems more right to give this name to the attribute of Malkhut." Thus far his words. And his last words certainly seem so, for it is written (Isa. 66:1), "and the earth is My footstool"; and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained it in the Tikkunim as Malkhut. And he explained there that she is called "My footstool" when she is included of ten; and then she is a footstool and a seat for all of them. And the explanation of raglai [My feet] is settled as in the matter of "I will pass through on my feet [be-raglai]" (Num. 20:19), ["the people that follow me [be-raglai]" (1 Kings 20:10)], whose explanation is the language of a company:

Myrtle [הדס, hadas]: in all the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim and in the Zohar, it is proved that the three myrtles are the three Patriarchs; and Malkhut from their side is called Hadassah, for it is explained as hadas [with] Heh. And it is possible that from this side Esther was greenish [Megillah 13a]. And the myrtle is green and bitter, from the side of judgment, from the side of the crowning of Binah, the green line, as explained in the Gate of Colors:

Majesty [הדר, hadar]: according to what appears, hadar is in Hod. But in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 112b) he explained that hadar is in Tiferet, and these are his words: "'The voice of YHVH is in majesty [be-hadar]' (Ps. 29:4): honor [hiddur] for Israel the Elder; as it is written, 'and you shall honor [ve-hadarta] the face of the old man' (Lev. 19:32)." Thus far his words. Behold, it is explicit that hadar is in Tiferet. And in the book Or Yakar we explained it as Netzach, and spoke at length with proofs from the verses; and so they explained in the Zohar (in the Sava of Mishpatim, fol. 98a), on the verse "You are clothed with glory [hod] and majesty [hadar]" (Ps. 104:1), that hadar is in Netzach. And possibly this is what he says, "and honor for Israel the Elder": for Netzach is a throne and a base for Tiferet (see the Zohar, Tetzaveh, fol. 186, that Yesod too is sometimes called hadar):

He [הוא, hu] is a title for Keter. And the intent is that this sefirah is hidden and concealed from every eye, and therefore they title it in the language of the hidden and the concealed [the third person]. However, in the Zohar, in Parashat Vayera, on the verse "and he [hu] was sitting at the door of the tent" (Gen. 18:1), he explained hu as Binah. And likewise in Parashat Vayetze (fol. 154b), and these are his words: "And the upper world, which is the Jubilee, we call hu, for all its matters are in covering." And likewise above in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 3, in the saying that we copied on the verse "And it shall come to pass in that day." And the reason may be that she is sometimes concealed, in the secret of her withdrawal to the manifestation of the Yod that is in Chokhmah. And when ha-hu has the Heh of knowledge, it is in Malkhut, hinting at her two manifestations: the first, the manifestation of the Yod, hu, and concealed; and the second, the manifestation of the Heh, and it is a revealed manifestation, and comes with the Heh of knowledge in the name, the reverse of what we explained at the beginning of the chapter; because hu is a concealed name, a concealed aspect, for the manifestation of the Yod. And sometimes Rashbi, peace be upon him, is found relating hu to Tiferet; and it is no wonder, for hu always shows the concealed, and Tiferet is concealed in relation to what is below. And sometimes Malkhut too is called hu when she is concealed, as we explained. And in the places where hu is written and hi [she] is read, he explained in the Zohar that it is the inclusion of the male with the female. And these are his words in Parashat Chukkat (fol. 183b): "Rabbi Abba said: Everywhere hu is written and we read hi: male and female as one. And the upper inclusion: Heh, female; Vav, male; Alef, the inclusion of all; for Alef dwells in completeness." Thus far his words. And the intent is that in the places where hu is written and hi is read, it is to hint at the King in His palace; and likewise the matter in this verse, hu is written and hi is read. And in hu itself there is also an inclusion, in which a great matter is included: that Malkhut is Heh, Tiferet Vav, and Alef above in Keter. For Keter dwells only in a complete place, that is, male and female as one; for this is a complete adam, as they said, "male and female He created them, and called their name adam" (Gen. 5:2), both of them together. And he said this matter because it was difficult: granted the four-letter name, which is written with Yod-Heh and pronounced with Alef-Dalet, the reason is that in the four-letter name too Malkhut is included, in the secret of the last Heh, and therefore we mention the Heh [Adonai], and there the rest of the Name is included. But in hu and hi, the female is not mentioned in hu; and therefore it should have been written only hi; and where hu is written, it should be read hu and not hi. And to this he answered that in hu too the female is mentioned; and this is what he said, "and the upper inclusion," etc. And we find ourselves taught the explanation of the word hu: that it includes Malkhut, Tiferet and Keter. And a further reason why hu is written and hi is read: for it hints at both of them together, the King within His canopy and His palace:

Hod [הוד, hod, Splendor]: in the book Sha'arei Tzedek [he gave] the reason that it is called Hod: when it is clothed in the attribute of Gevurah, to humble enemies, to win battles and to rescue the lovers of the Most High; and the secret is "and my splendor [hodi] was turned in me to destruction" (Dan. 10:8), etc. "And all the kinds of thanksgivings [hoda'ot] that David said in the book of Psalms are this attribute," etc. Thus far his words. And so he explained in the Orah. And in the Shem, Rabbi Moshe [de León] also explained that it is called Hod when it is clothed from Gevurah, and brought a proof from the verse (Ps. 45:4), "Gird your sword upon your thigh, O mighty one, your splendor [hodkha] and your majesty." Thus far. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, fol. 27) Rashbi too explained that every hodu [give thanks] is in Hod:

Be [הוה, heveh]: on the verse "Be [heveh] lord over your brothers" (Gen. 27:29), he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 143b), these are his words: "For these letters are the secrets of faith: Heh above, Vav in the middle, Heh afterward; and therefore he said, 'Heveh lord over your brothers,'" etc. Thus far his words. And the intent is that in the word heveh the secret of Binah and Tiferet and Malkhut is included; and the reason is to make holiness prevail over the husk, to destroy it, as we explained there:

Hoy [הוי, hoy, Woe]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Acharei Mot (fol. 74b) that when Tiferet withdraws, that is, Vav, with the extension of the Vav, that is, the head of the small Vav that is in Yesod, which is a Yod, it becomes vay [Vav-Yod]. And when it withdraws further to Binah, and no effluence is bestowed from her below, and the blessings are held back there, and the channel, which is Tiferet, which bestows on the whole Emanation, withdraws there, then hoy is said. And there is a difference between oy and hoy: for in the place where oy is said, the decree is not annulled by repentance, for there is no Heh there, which is Repentance; and when hoy is said, the matter still depends on repentance, and repentance annuls. And we spoke at length in the entry oy:

She [היא, hi] is a title for Malkhut, but in her hidden manifestation, which is level with Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations (chapters 3 and 4); and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 257a).
And the matter of "hu is written and hi is read" is explained above in the entry hu:

Palace [היכל, heikhal]: Malkhut is called so, for she is a palace for Tiferet, who is stored away within her; and likewise the name Adonai comes to the number of heikhal [65]. And the name Adonai is a palace for the four-letter name, in the manifestation of the sefirot and in the pronunciation of the mentioning, as is known. And Binah is a palace for Chokhmah and for Tiferet, which is stored away within her and goes out from the palace to the tower, which is the ark, which is Malkhut, as we shall explain in its entry with the help of the Name; so he explained in the Zohar (Shelach, fol. 164b). And in Parashat Lekh (fol. 94b) he explained that heikhal is Keter, and explained heikhal [as hei kol]: the intent is the place in which all is included, that is, Keter, which includes the whole Emanation. And in any case "palace" hints at the sefirah in which things are stored away; and therefore this title is related to all the sefirot. And to Keter it is also related, because in it all is stored away, in the secret of the Tzachtzachot, as we explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot (see the entry "ten"):

Halakhah [הלכה, halakhah] is the Shekhinah; and she is so called in her subtle manifestation, which is called the pupil of the eye. And this is "a halakhah to Moses from Sinai": for the intent is that she is the bride of Moses, in the secret of the manifestation of the Yod that she has, as explained in the Gate of Manifestations; so he explained in the Tikkunim. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna he explained that from the side of Gevurah she is called halakhah; for there is the Heh-Yod of Elohim, the Heh from Abraham, the Yod from Isaac. And she is called "the halakhah is according to the many" when she receives from the three Patriarchs, who are called "many," as we shall explain in its entry. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 45a) he explained that she is called halakhah when she is between Netzach and Hod, going [holekhet] to be united with her husband. And it is possible to distinguish between halakhah without qualification and "a halakhah to Moses from Sinai":

Complete Hallel and incomplete [הלל גמור ושאינו גמור, hallel gamur ve-she-eino gamur]: some explained that the complete is in the secret of Binah, and the incomplete in the secret of Malkhut. And the correct [view] is that the complete is in the secret of the moon in its fullness, and the incomplete in the secret of its defect. (And see Tikkun 13, fol. 27, that the complete Hallel shows a whole matzah and the incomplete a broken matzah; and therefore on Passover both are said):

Halleluyah [הללויה, halleluyah] is one of the ten tikkunim that Malkhut has from the ten sefirot; and from the side of Tiferet she has Halleluyah and every matter of praise [hillul]; so they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, fol. 27). And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayishlach (fol. 178), he explained that Halleluyah is a praise with which the Shekhinah praises Tiferet; and both of them come in this word, and it is hallel  Y H V. Hallel is the Shekhinah, Malkhut; and she is called hallel because she ever praises the Holy One, blessed be He.  Y H V  is Tiferet. And the matter of the order of these letters is Vav, Yod-Heh; and its explanation is that she praises Tiferet, which is Vav, which is included of Chokhmah and Binah and receives from them; and that is Yod-Heh:

Here I am [הנני, hineni] is Malkhut, her aspect alone, without the joining to her of any other aspect of the aspects of the sefirot at all; and it shows judgment, and shows her revealing and her readiness. So they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 65b); and the commentators explained it in another way:

Mountain [הר, har]: the mountains are many. However, "mountain" without qualification some explained as Yesod; and they are the author of Sefer ha-Orah; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] in Sefer ha-Shem also explained "mountain" as Yesod. However, in the Zohar (Tissa, fol. 190a), on the verse "the mountain of the house of YHVH shall be established" (Isa. 2:2), Rabbi Chiyya explained, and these are his words: "'The mountain of the house of YHVH': this is good without evil. 'The mountain of the house of YHVH,' certainly, for there is no portion there for the Other Side," etc. Thus far his words. And there the subject is Malkhut, as is proved there. Further, Malkhut is called Mount Moriah, and likewise the mountain of myrrh, as it is written (Song 4:6), "I will get me to the mountain of myrrh." And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that in Moriah there is the name Yah [Yod-Heh], toward the thirty-two paths.
And further, there is in it the language of teaching [hora'ah].
And further, the language of myrrh [mor], which is the matter of incense.

And behold, Jerusalem is Malkhut, and there are mountains round about her (Ps. 125:2); and among them Mount Seir, and among them the mount of Esau, and among them the mountains of twilight (Jer. 13:16); and they are a title for the husks. And some explained, on Mount Zion, [that] the mountain is Jerusalem and Zion is Yesod. And likewise it is called the goodly mountain (Deut. 3:25), because it is good and does good to all, in the way of "Say of the righteous one that it shall be good" (Isa. 3:10). And likewise it is called the holy mountain. And likewise there are the mountains of Zion (Ps. 133:3); and he explained that they are Netzach and Hod, for they are mountains round about the aforementioned Mount Zion, which bestow on Yesod, as is known. And what appears to us in the matter of the mountain is that "mountain" without qualification is in Malkhut; and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (fol. 69), these are his words: "'To the mountain of YHVH' (Isa. 2:3): this is Abraham, as it is written, 'as it is said to this day, In the mount of YHVH it shall be seen' (Gen. 22:14); for Abraham called it 'mountain.' Just as a mountain is ownerless for anyone in the world who wishes, so too this holy place is ownerless, to receive anyone in the world who wishes." And he explained that Malkhut from the side of Chesed is called "mountain," which is ownerless, from the side in which the proselytes take hold when they enter under the wings of the Shekhinah. And therefore in the days of Abraham she received many souls, as it is written (Gen. 12:5), "and the souls that they had made in Haran." And so he further explained there (fol. 70a), these are his words: "A mountain for the other peoples, when they come to enter under His wings." And he explained there that therefore the proselyte is called "a righteous proselyte" [ger tzedek], for he enters under the wings of the Shekhinah, who is called Tzedek; and he is called ger because he leaves his place and comes to take refuge. And in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 80a), he explained on the verse "And he removed from there to the mountain" (Gen. 12:8), these are his words: "From there he knew the mountain of YHVH, and all the levels that are planted in this place." It appears from his words that Malkhut, with respect to her including all her lower powers, is called "mountain," like the mountain on which there are many plantings. And so it shows in many places.

Behold, from all this, Malkhut is called "mountain." And indeed all the sefirot are called "mountains," as he explained in the Tikkun (21, fol. 42): "'Hear, O mountains' (Micah 6:2): these are the Patriarchs." For Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet are called mountains; and they are so called by her name, for she is the root of the mountains, as we explained above. And the word "mountain" shows the matter of height, for they are high and supernal:

All the six upper extremities are called the mountains of spices (Song 8:14), for the reason that they are perfumed [mitbasmim] each from its fellow. And "the virgins her companions that follow her" are called the mountains of separation [harei vater] (Song 2:17), for the reason that from there downward it is parted [yippared] (Gen. 2:10), and they are the mountain of separation; so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 158a). And she is called Mount Moriah from the side of Chesed; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verse (Song 5:1), "I have gathered my myrrh [mori]"; for the myrrh is in Abraham, and we shall explain it in its entry with the help of the Name. And she is called Moriah in the secret of Chesed being united with the first three, which are included in Yod-Heh, as is known. And likewise Keter is called myrrh; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verse (Song 4:6), "I will get me to the mountain of myrrh"; and it is possible that from its side Gedulah is so called. And the four of them together, when they pour out blessing and effluence on this mountain through that deed, that he bound Isaac his son, she is called by their name Mount Moriah. And she is called the holy mountain when she draws nourishment from the place of holiness, which is in Chokhmah, as we shall explain in its entry with the help of the Name. And she is called Mount Zion in her manifestation when (Yesod) is united with her at the point of Zion, which is the manifestation of the Yod that is in her, a dwelling for Yesod, as we shall explain in the entry Zion with the help of the Name. And by this everything is set right: for in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained Mount Zion as Yesod, and elsewhere he explained that Malkhut is called Mount Zion and proved it from the verse. And how is this? Rather, as we explained. And she is called Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal: from the right side, where the blessing is, Mount Gerizim; and from the left side, Mount Ebal, where the strength of judgment is. And she is called the goodly mountain in her receiving from Chesed, from the side of the aspect called good, as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name; and the explanation of "good" is shining, in the secret of the light of Chesed. And there is the mountain of Abarim (Num. 27:12) (as is written in the Zohar, Chukkat, fol. 183a): "which holds on to two sides [avarim]." Thus far. And for this reason too it may be in Yesod. Further, Malkhut is called "mountain" without qualification from the side of her selfhood, as we explained; and the mountain of YHVH from the side of her selfhood alone, without the joining of strange mountains with her. And there are called mountains round about her from the side of the mountains, some of them good and some of them evil. The good are called "the virgins her companions that follow her," as we explained above, and they will be called "the mountains of Zion." And the evil: some of them are called "the mountains of twilight" and "mountains of darkness," the reverse of "the morning was light"; and Mount Seir and the mount of Esau: all these are from the side of the husk, from the left side. And in the Tikkunim (Zohar Chadash, fol. 131), these are his words: "'And the ark rested' (Gen. 8:4): it dwells on the accursed mountains, to do judgment on them; for they are the mountains of Kardu, the dark mountains in exile, accursed in exile," etc. It will be seen from there explicitly that the husks are called "the mountains of Ararat," the language of curse [arur]:

Hatkafta [התקפתא, hatkafta, strength]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 44) that Malkhut from the side of Chesed is called hatkafta; and he proved it from the verse "Your right hand, O YHVH, glorious in power" (Exod. 15:6), whose Targum is "in strength" [be-tukfa]. And the truth is that she is from the side of the Gevurah that is in Gedulah; for so he proved in the Zohar, that the left is included in the right, from this verse. And there is no doubt that ko'ach [power] is from the side of Binah, in the secret of judgment toward the left; and from there Chesed is included in Gevurah. Thus far the study of our intellect has reached in the explanation of the entry of the letter Heh; and behold, we are entering into the explanation of the letter Vav, with the help of Heaven:

The letter Vav we shall explain in the Gate of Letters, with the help of the Name. However, a Vav at the head of a word shows Tiferet; and even though the word itself hints at Malkhut, as ve-attah [and now], ve-attah [and You], va-ani [and I], ve-zot [and this], the hint is at Tiferet and Malkhut united. And this is a great principle for everything like it, in the word va-YHVH, which we shall explain with the help of the Name:

And YHVH: He and His court [ויהו"ה הוא ובית דינו, va-YHVH hu u-veit dino]: it has already been explained that the four-letter name is Tiferet, and the court of the Name is Malkhut. And one may ask: for there is no hint here at His court at all, for the Name is in Tiferet and the Vav is a hint at Tiferet. And one may explain that the name of Malkhut is mentioned in completeness because in every place that says "and YHVH," it is He and His court; and there is judgment only in the prevailing of Malkhut, who is the attribute of judgment, over Tiferet, who is the attribute of compassion. And therefore her hand prevailed and her name was mentioned in completeness, and her husband is hinted over her with the Vav, to show the help of his agreement to the judgment. And the reason is that it is judgment mixed with compassion; and in every place where the four-letter name is mentioned in judgment, compassion is certainly mixed with it. And therefore this Name agrees; and this is what they said, "And YHVH: He": for the Vav, which is Tiferet, is called hu [He], as we explained in the preceding chapter. "And His court": for when it says an added Vav, the intent is that it adds to the first matter; and that is the female, concealed, to come in concealment, as we explained. And in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 138), on the verse "A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day" (Ps. 92:1), these are his words: "We find in many places that the lower world does not rise in name and comes closed, as in this one, and as 'And to Moses He said, Come up to YHVH' (Exod. 24:1), 'And He called to Moses' (Lev. 1:1). All of them close the name, and it does not rise in it; but because there is an upper level in it, and in relation to the upper level she does not rise in name." Thus far his words.

Behold, it is explicit that when Malkhut is united with Tiferet, only the male rises in name. And therefore here, where the principal is Tiferet, which is the Name, Malkhut comes in concealment, in the addition of the Vav, which shows that it is as though the male is added to the concealed female. And this they hinted in saying "He and His court": for a man cannot mention the four-letter name except in his court, and a judge does not judge the judgment except in the house [bayit]; and the name "His court" is compelled of itself. And the revealing came in the addition of the Vav, as one who adds, as though the female had already been mentioned, as we explained:

Vahu [וה"ו, vahu]: it is explained in the secret of Ani va-Hu [I and He], which are Tiferet and the Shekhinah of His strength, in the secret of what is called Tiferet, hu, as we explained in its entry. And there is no doubt that the name Vahu, without the Alef, is not as important as the complete name hu; for the name hu shows the complete union and the glory that covers over, and that is Keter, hinted at in the Alef. And in the name Vahu the Alef is lacking, as we explained in the entry hu. And there is no wonder that this is a name of the names of the seventy-two and that is a word; and if so, how did it rise higher than the name? For the like of this Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verses ve-et Shaddai, ve-El Shaddai (in the Zohar, Vayechi, fol. 247a) (see above in the entry El Shaddai):

Vay [וי, vai, Alas]: Rashbi explained that when the small Vav that is in Yesod, that is, the Yod, withdraws to Tiferet, and the effluence is gathered there in Tiferet, and the extension of the Vav of Tiferet, that is, the head of the Vav, which is Yesod, does not bestow, then vay is said. And we spoke at length in the entries oy and hoy:

And it came to pass [ויהי, va-yehi] is the attribute of judgment; it is Gevurah. And so our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Megillah 10b): va-yehi is the language of sorrow. And the reason is clear, for it is vay, as explained above. And hi too is the language of sorrow, as "lamentations, and mourning, and woe [hi]" (Ezek. 2:10), as we explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names. And all this shows that it is in the power of judgment, Gevurah. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 167a), these are his words: "And from the secret of the right the left goes out; and therefore 'and there was [va-yehi] light' (Gen. 1:3): this is the left. From here, the first va-yehi of the Torah was on the side of the left; and therefore it is not a sign of blessing. What is the reason? Because that darkness went out, which darkened the face of the world. And this is the sign: when the secret of Esau and his deeds was revealed, it was in this va-yehi, as it is written, 'and Esau was [va-yehi] a cunning hunter' (Gen. 25:27): it was fulfilled in va-yehi, 'Esau was a cunning hunter,' to entice the world, that they should not go in the straight way." Thus far his words.
Behold, it is explicit that va-yehi is from the side of Gevurah, in the aspect of darkness and blackness, as we explained in the Gate of Colors:

Vilon [וילון, vilon, Curtain] is Malkhut; for she is the first firmament, which serves for nothing except according to what is bestowed on her from above. "And it goes in in the morning and goes out in the evening, and renews every day the Work of Creation"; so our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in Hagigah (fol. 12b). And it is known that she is the attribute of night; and it is known that she said, "A lamp at noon, what use is it?" therefore her service is at night. "And renews every day": the explanation, she bestows on all the Work of Creation, for all of them are bestowed upon through her, as it is said (Prov. 31:15), "She rises also while it is yet night, and gives food to her household and a portion to her maidens." And this is what they said in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 236): "The lower Shekhinah is the Vilon, in which He brings in the evening and brings out the morning." Thus far. And it is difficult, for it is the reverse of the reading of the Gemara, which said, "goes in in the morning and goes out in the evening." And to explain it according to what we shall explain in the Gemara: if we explain according to the explanation of the Tosafot, "goes in in the morning" into this world to give light, "and goes out in the evening" from the world, and the world darkens; we shall explain accordingly what he said in the Ra'aya Meheimna: "brings in the evening": the explanation, it brings the light into its sheath, and the darkness spreads; "and brings out the morning," the light, and lights up the world; and they do not disagree. And according to the hidden [sense], it means the reverse of what we explained above: for at night, when she draws nourishment from judgment, her compassion is stored away and darkened, and the side of the left spreads in the world; and in the morning she brings out compassion, "and the darknesses have gone to the mountains of twilight." This is according to the language of the Ra'aya Meheimna. And the language of the Gemara: it goes in in the morning into the world to remove the darknesses and the idols from the earth, and it goes out in the evening from the world, and the compassion is stored away, so as "not to muzzle the ox when it treads" (Deut. 25:4). This is the explanation in the way of the Tosafot. And in the way of Rashi's explanation, of blessed memory, who explained "goes in in the morning" into its sheath, and explained that the Vilon is the cause of the darkness that darkens, we can also set the languages right, so that they do not disagree. And it is explained thus: the Gemara said it goes into the sheath in the morning, and the light spreads in the world, and it goes out in the evening and darkens the world, and the light is gathered in. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna it is explained: it brings in in the evening the darkness into this world and darkens it, and brings out in the morning the darkness from the world, and the light spreads. And by way of the secret, its explanation is as we explained at first above: that she is the attribute of night, and she delights in "the stone and the rock of stumbling" to reward and to punish. And this is "and they put the stone back upon the mouth [al pi] of the well" (Gen. 29:3), as he explained in the book of the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze: for al pi means by the mouth of the well, which is the Shekhinah, as "at the mouth [al pi] of YHVH they encamped, and at the mouth of YHVH they journeyed" (Num. 9:23). And it means that by her will and by her word they would put back the stone of stumbling, as explained there. And by her cause the husks spread at the beginning of the night, when she draws the strength of judgment. And she is the one who brings them in [in the morning] to their sheath, to the hole of the deep, where their sheath is, as explained in the Gate of the Substitute Palaces. And she is the one who gives them permission to spread [in the evening]; for "He has made everything beautiful in its time" (Eccl. 3:11), "and even the wicked for the day of evil" (Prov. 16:4), "and in the day of prosperity be joyful" (Eccl. 7:14):

Va'ed [ועד, va-ed, and ever]: they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 34), on the verse (Exod. 15:18), "YHVH shall reign for ever and ever [va-ed]," that the word va'ed is in Binah, "for there is the appointing [yi'uda] and the sustaining and the completion of all." And he explained that in Binah is the gathering of all the extremities, to receive effluence. And the word va'ed is the language of a house of meeting [beit ha-va'ad]; and the reason that they gather in her is that there is their sustaining and their completeness. And accordingly Binah is called va'ed only in the aspect of the gathering of the sefirot in her to be sustained, as we explained:

Gullet [ושט, veshet] is a hint at those powers that are called "the fire-offerings of YHVH," as it is said, "and wholly for the fires [ishim]." For they were the eaters of the flesh and the fats; and only the scent rises higher and higher. And this is "a fire-offering [isheh] of a pleasing scent to YHVH" (Lev. 1:9): the fire-offering is the gullet, and the scent is pleasing to YHVH. And this isheh is the totality of the lower powers that are beneath all the chariots. For in the matter of the offerings they draw near to YHVH, to stand to serve Him and to bless in His name. And so Rashbi explained (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 78) on the Song of Songs, on the verse "Draw me," etc. (Song 1:4). And to this he intended in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 235), these are his words: "And in the first composition: the gullet, which swallows the food, and from there it enters all the limbs; for it is in the level of the fires. The fires are the near ones; at once they swallow and take [it] wholly from within the upper fire, which is wholly for the fires. And this is the secret: 'They shall eat the fire-offerings of YHVH and His inheritance' (Deut. 18:1)," etc. Thus far our faltering knowledge has reached, by the power of His great effluence, in the explanation of the Vav.
And behold, we are entering into the explanation of the entry Zayin:

This [זאת, zot] is Malkhut. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 11b): "And because there is no apprehension for a prophet, a seer or a sage below her, the prophet said, 'Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom,' etc., 'but in this [be-zot],' etc. (Jer. 9:22–23). And therefore Jacob taught his sons and gave them a tradition from her, as it is written, 'and this [ve-zot] is what their father spoke to them' (Gen. 49:28). And David, who had a tradition from her, said toward her, 'Though a host should encamp against me,' etc., 'in this [be-zot] I trust' (Ps. 27:3); he hinted at her with that crown, and his thought rose toward her, and he said, 'my heart shall not fear,' etc. And Aaron, who had a tradition from her, did not enter the innermost [Holy of Holies] without her, as it is written, 'With this [be-zot] shall Aaron come into the holy place' (Lev. 16:3); for he knew that she is the root of all, for she is an offering to YHVH, a burnt offering to YHVH, a fire-offering to YHVH. And Israel, who had a tradition from her, did not ask of the Holy One, blessed be He, another pledge, that He would redeem them for its sake from the exile, but zot; as it is written, 'And yet for all this [ve-af gam zot], when they are in the land of their enemies,' etc. (Lev. 26:44). And the prophet, when he saw the strong distress of Israel in the exile, said for her sake, 'This [zot] I recall to my mind,' etc. (Lam. 3:21). 'And this [ve-zot] for Judah, and he said,' etc. (Deut. 33:7)." Thus far his words. And behold, this saying is clear for our intent. And the reason [that she is called] zot is because she is called et, for the reason that we explained in its entry; and when she is doubly good, receiving an addition of good from the seven lamps of the pure lampstand that is on her head, then she is called zot [Zayin, 7, with et]:

Zevul [זבול, zevul, habitation]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it in Sefer ha-Shem as the attribute of Binah, and these are his words: "Zevul, from the language of companionship, dwelling and joining. And the verse said (Gen. 30:20), 'Now will my husband dwell with me [yizbeleni], because I have borne him six sons'; and afterward she bore a daughter. And 'my husband' is the very wise one." Thus far his words. And his intent is that Leah is the hint at Binah, and she bore six sons, which are from Chesed to Yesod, and the daughter is Malkhut. And she said, "Now will my husband dwell with me": the intent is the union of Chokhmah and Binah, and "my husband" is Chokhmah. And if so, accordingly Binah is called zevul through the union of Chokhmah with her. Further, he wrote on the attribute of Tiferet, and these are his words: "Zevul, from the language of 'Now will my husband dwell with me'; and it is the one that joins and dwells with the whole Structure, a man and his house, and they are six. And Solomon said (1 Kings 8:13), 'I have surely built You a house of habitation [zevul].' And it is one of the seven firmaments. And this zevul is not like the zevul of Binah." Thus far his words. And the principle that emerges from his words is that Tiferet is called zevul when it is joined with the six extremities, for zevul is the language of joining, as we explained:

This [זה, zeh] is Tiferet; and he is called zeh because he comes to the twelve havayot, the twelve boundaries [Zayin-Heh = 12]. And zeh is joined and coupled with zot: zeh for the male and zot for the female. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bo (fol. 37b), and these are his words: "Thus we have learned: this crown that is called zot is called ishah [woman], as it is said, 'she [zot] shall be called woman' (Gen. 2:23). Why? Because it is written, 'for out of man [ish] was she [zot] taken.' Who is ish? That one which is called zeh; and this is the male man, as it is said, 'for this [zeh] man,' 'the man zeh,' etc. And zot was taken from zeh." Thus far his words. And he was precise: for from zeh, that is, ish, zot was taken; and that is the matter of the taking of the rib, which is the bride of Moses. And accordingly it is found that Tiferet is called zeh in the secret of the level of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, which is within, in the secret of Da'at, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And likewise Yesod too is called zeh: all that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph. And so they said in the Zohar, Parashat Beshalach (fol. 61a), and these are his words: "Rabbi Judah said: Israel did not draw near to Mount Sinai until they entered the portion of the Righteous One and merited it. From where do we know? For it is written, 'On this [ha-zeh] day they came,' etc. (Exod. 19:1): 'on this day' exactly; and it is written, 'And it shall be said in that day, Lo, this [zeh] is our God,' etc. (Isa. 25:9)." Thus far his words. And in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 236b), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained how holiness is called zeh and zot: because it is found with a man always, in the secret of the covenant. And these are his words: "And the holy spirit is called zot, for it is the secret of the covenant, the holy impress, which is found always with a man; and likewise zeh: 'this is YHVH, we have waited for Him' (Isa. 25:9), 'this is my God, and I will glorify Him' (Exod. 15:2)." Thus far his words. And it is clear. And there is no wonder that zot is in Malkhut and zeh in Yesod and zeh in Tiferet, as we explained; for all three are called covenant, as we explained in its entry. And the truth is that all three are held in it, in the secret of circumcision and uncovering. And likewise the covenant is called "the head of the body," for "body and covenant are counted as one." And all three are found ready with a man always, in the secret of the covenant; and therefore they are called by the language of readiness [the demonstrative], as one who points with a finger: "this":

Gold [זהב, zahav] is a hint at the attribute of Gevurah, as it is said (Job 37:22), "Out of the north comes gold." And sometimes it is related to Binah; and we spoke at length in the Gate of Colors, chapter 3; see there:

Olive [זית, zayit] is Malkhut. And it is already known that the breaking of bread is [with the measure of] the size of an olive and [of] the size of an egg; and he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 244b) that "the size of an egg" is the first Yod, and "the size of an olive" the second Yod, of the name  Y A H D V N H Y:

Remember [זכור, zakhor], as in the matter of "Remember" (Exod. 20:8) and "Keep" (Deut. 5:12): "they are the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah. Happy is he who unites them on the Sabbath day, which is Yesod," etc. Thus far his words. Behold, he said explicitly that "Remember" and "Keep" are Tiferet and Malkhut; and so it is agreed in the mouth of the Kabbalists, who say "Remember" [zakhor] for the male [zakhar] and "Keep" for the female. And some explained "Remember" as Yesod, and it is not the principal [view]. Further, he explained in the Zohar Chadash, Parashat Yitro (fol. 49b), on the verse "I [Anokhi] am YHVH your God" (Exod. 20:2): "Anokhi is the totality of male and female as one; and all of it is called zakhor. What is the reason? Because he takes the female and includes her within him; and therefore only he alone is mentioned. And when she [draws] her husband with her and comes toward him, as it is said, 'until I had brought him into my mother's house' (Song 3:4), then she takes the name, and all of it is called shamor. What is the reason? Because she draws him to her and takes him; then the whole house stands in her authority, and only she alone is mentioned. And they are never parted from one another." Thus far his words.

And to understand this saying clearly, one must raise against it a second saying of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 118b), these are his words: "And the Holy One, blessed be He, is zakhor from the right, shamor from the left; and the Shekhinah is remembering [zekhirah] from the right, keeping [shemirah] from the left. They are the tefillin of a man's head and his tefillin (another version: of the hand). And so the Shekhinah is 'the Torah of YHVH is perfect' (Ps. 19:8), and His commandment. And this, from the side of the central pillar, which includes judgment and compassion, is called zakhor and shamor; she is remembering and keeping. And in all the commandments she is equal to him in level. But from the side of Chesed and Gevurah, the Holy One, blessed be He, is zakhor and the Shekhinah shamor, as the masters of the Mishnah established: zakhor for the male and shamor for the bride; because on the right and the left the branches are parted, like the lobes of the lung, which are parted above; and corresponding to them are the living creatures," etc. Thus far his words.

And our intent here is not to explain the body of the sayings, for the inquiry would be drawn out on what is not our matter; but to explain the matter of zakhor and shamor in such a way that these two sayings settle in their measure, in this entry alone. It has already been explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance that the arousal of the female toward the upper coupling is from the side of the left, and the arousal of the male from the side of the right. And the matter is that the female's root is in the left and the male's in the right. And when the male couples toward the side of the female, then the male is secondary to the female, and the female is the principal, and the male does not rise in name. And when their coupling is so, it is right to say that both of them are shamor, from the side of the left that prevails. And even though it is impossible that the aspect zakhor not be mixed with her, from the side of the arousal of the right too toward the coupling, for "this without that does not suffice," nevertheless the male does not rise in name, nor the right, because they are secondary to the left, shamor, which is the female. And therefore her hand prevailed, and the principal name is related to her, certainly shamor; and both of them together are shamor. And when the female couples toward the male, that is, toward the side of the male, then the female is secondary to the male, and the male is the principal, and the female does not rise in name; and when their coupling is so, it is right to say of it that both of them are zakhor, from the side of the right that prevails. And even though it is impossible that the power of shamor not be mixed with them, from the side of the arousal of the left too toward the coupling, for "this without that does not suffice," nevertheless the female does not rise in name, nor the left, because they are secondary to the right, zakhor, which is the male. And therefore his hand prevailed, and the principal name is certainly related to him; both of them are related together as zakhor. And this matter will be well understood by what we explained in the aforementioned gate, chapter 23, on the matter of the branches parted to the right and to the left: for in Chesed and Gevurah they are YHVH to the right and Adonai to the left, and  Y A H D V N H Y  in Tiferet, for there the coupling is equal, as we explained there. And by this will also be understood "if the woman emits seed first, she bears a male" (Berakhot 60a): the explanation, when she draws near to go to the place of her husband, then she bears a male, for he rises in name and not she; and it is zakhor, compassion. But when he draws near to go to her place, then she bears a female, for she rises in name and not he; and it is shamor, judgment and female. And by this the sayings are explained, and the matter of zakhor [and] shamor in substance:

Remembrance [זכירה, zekhirah]: all the commentators agreed that remembrance is in Yesod; for it is what makes all things remembered above, in the place of life. And this is "Remember us for life" on Rosh Hashanah; and likewise "a remembrance of shofar-blowing" when it falls on the Sabbath day, Yesod. And likewise it is from the language of "its memorial portion [azkaratah] to YHVH" (Lev. 6:8), and as "May He remember all your meal-offerings" (Ps. 20:4). For the intent is Yesod, which binds all the attributes, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 56, fol. 87), and these are his words: "And all the branches are united there and bound and intertwined and receive from one another; and all of it through the Righteous One. And without the Righteous One there is no nearness and union, but brotherhood," etc. Behold, it is explicit that there is no binding and union for the sefirot at all except through Yesod. And the language of remembrance is the language of incense [binding], as in the matter of "its memorial portion to YHVH." And this is the intent of David in saying "A psalm of David, to make remembrance [le-hazkir]" (Ps. 38:1), which means to bind and to tie Malkhut with the other sefirot through Yesod. And it is already possible that the explanation of zekhirah is literally the language of zakhar [male]; for through the maleness, which is Yesod, is the union of all the sefirot, as we explained. And it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 160a), that just as there is remembrance from the side of the male in holiness, so there is remembrance for ill from the side of the husk, the left, as it is written (Ps. 78:39), "And He remembered that they were but flesh"; and many like them:

Merit [זכות, zekhut]: the author of Sefer ha-Orah wrote that zekhut is Gevurah; and the reason, because in it all the merits and all the sins are remembered. And the truth is that so many explained in the matter of "children, life and sustenance," etc. [do not depend on merit but on mazal]: the intent is that they do not depend on the harsh attribute of judgment. However, the reason that he said it is so called does not settle; for on the contrary, in Gevurah is the scale-pan of liability; there the liabilities of men are remembered; true, for all is in uprightness and justice; and nevertheless liability and judgment have their place in Gevurah; and if so, how is it called merit? And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 10, fol. 24) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Chesed is called zekhut, and these are his words: "And on Keter depend children, life and sustenance, for it is the mazal of all, and it does not depend on mazal. And therefore they established: children, life and sustenance, the matter does not depend on merit, but the matter depends on mazal; for Chesed is merit." Thus far his words. And one must investigate, for in the Palaces Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote that the palace of Gevurah is called the Palace of Merit, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 4; and he explained the reason: "for in this place the merit of all the children of the world is turned over." And at first sight it leans to the words of the author of Sefer ha-Orah, and his words contradict each other. However, they explained the reason in the Zohar, in Parashat Shemot (fol. 6a), these are his words: "And that palace is called the Palace of Merit, because when they judge judgment they turn [first] toward the merit [of a man]," as with the Sanhedrin; see there. And merit is always Chesed, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. In the book Me'irat Einayim, Parashat Vayera, in the explanation of the saying "the matter does not depend on merit," he said that Tiferet is called zekhut, and these are his words: "Zekhuta is Tiferet, which is compassion. And Rabbi Abner said that therefore zekhuta hints at Tiferet: for tzedakah hints at it, and the Targum of tzedakah is zekhuta." Thus far his words:

Ze'ir Anpin [זעיר אנפין, ze'ir anpin, the Small Face]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it as Tiferet, and these are his words: "Ze'ir Anpin in the language of the Zohar, in the secret of the great faces and the small faces. Know that Keter is head of the whole Emanation, and therefore it is called head; and with Chokhmah and Binah, the great faces and the closed brain. And Tiferet is head of the Structure, and it too is called head, in the likeness of the form of the spiritual man; and it is called the small faces; and they are the face of Jacob engraved on the Throne of Glory. And whoever knows the secret of the matter of 'Let us make man' will understand this well. And they are the face of Moses, the face of the sun." Thus far his words. And behold, his intent is that Ze'ir Anpin is Tiferet. And at first sight this thing is utterly strange, for he is called "the long world"; and how is it possible that Ze'ir Anpin be related to him? Rather it would have seemed that Ze'ir Anpin is Malkhut, for she is the likeness of all that is above her, and she is small; and there is proof for this in some places of the Zohar. However, it is difficult for us, for in the Zohar, Parashat Naso (fol. 129a), our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: "And from that path it is parted into six hundred and thirteen paths of the Torah, which are divided in Ze'ir Anpin, of which it is written, 'All the paths of YHVH are loving-kindness and truth' (Ps. 25:10)," etc.; see there. Thus far his words. Behold, in Ze'ir Anpin are the paths of loving-kindness and truth; and it is understood as Tiferet. And still "yes and no" are uncertain in our hands, until we reach the explanation of the Idra in the book Or Yakar; and there we shall explain this matter, with the help of Heaven:

Outcry [זעקה, ze'akah] is in Binah; and likewise we have some faint glimmerings of proof from the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 20a), which wrote, and these are his words: "For crying out [tze'akah] is in the heart, as it is written, 'Their heart cried out to YHVH' (Lam. 2:18); tze'akah and ze'akah are one thing." Thus far his words. And the heart is none other than Binah, as it is said, "the heart understands [mevin]"; and therefore the outcry [avails] in this world and in the world to come, as explained there. And we shall speak at length in the entry tze'akah, with the help of the Name:

Raising up [זקיפה, zekifah]: every raising up, as "who raises up the bowed down" (Ps. 146:8), and all of them, is in Tiferet. And so they said in the Gemara (Berakhot 12a): "whoever raises himself up, raises himself up at the Name," that is, Tiferet. And so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim on this matter many times:

Old [זקן, zaken] is Keter; and likewise it is very usual in the Zohar. However, zekenim [elders], in the plural, shows the sefirot; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Zohar, Balak, fol. 197b), on the verse (Deut. 21:19), "and they shall lay hold of him," etc.: "'the elders of his city': these are the first days, the ancient days of all." Thus far his words:

Zerach [זרח, zerach, shining]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it of Tiferet, whose sun shines and rises [zore'ach] over the breached city of David, in the secret of Peretz [breach], the moon that is renewed each and every month. And this remark is enough for the thoughtful one; and he aimed well:

The everlasting arms [זרועות עולם, zero'ot olam] (Deut. 33:27): Gedulah [and] Gevurah; and they are arms to the body, which is Tiferet. And it is a name that shows power and might, as it is said (Ps. 118:15), "the right hand of YHVH does valiantly," etc.; and further (Exod. 15:6), "Your right hand, O YHVH, glorious in power," etc. And the proof of this is "with an outstretched arm": for it is a name that shows length and power. And further, they are so called [after] the structure of the body of the emanated man:

Span [זרת, zeret]: in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 19, fol. 36b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and these are his words: "'And meted out the heavens with the span' (Isa. 40:12): what is zeret? This is Gevurah." Thus far his words. He taught explicitly that zeret is Gevurah. And Rabbi Chiyya explained in the book of the Zohar (Tissa, fol. 189b), and these are his words: "The cup of blessing needs to be set right in the right hand. 'And shall be exalted above the hills' (Isa. 2:2): it needs to be raised from the table the measure called a span, to bless the Holy One, blessed be He. And this is 'and shall be exalted above the hills.' What is 'above the hills'? Rather, between her and the virgins her companions that follow her, it is the measure of a span." Thus far his words. It is found accordingly that zeret is Malkhut with the virgins her companions that follow her. And we can say that he did not say "between her and the virgins," etc., "is a span," but "the measure of a span"; it appears that zeret is a matter by itself, but that these [have] its measure, a span. Therefore we say that the principal [sense] of zeret is Gevurah, as he explained in the Tikkunim:

Olives [זיתים, zeitim] are the upper organs that are above Yesod, from which Yesod brings out "pure olive oil," etc. (Exod. 27:20); for it bestows the upper effluence from the upper organs on Malkhut. For just as through the pounding of the organ, the covenant of the member, the organs are pressed and shaken to bestow into its female, so is the matter above in Yesod with the other organs, to bestow on Malkhut. For the effluence is oil, and the upper organs are olives. So Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim and in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 247a). [And this is what the verse says,] "and two olive trees by it," etc. (Zech. 4:3). And he explained that the lampstand is Malkhut, as is known; "and a bowl on the top of it" is Yesod, for it is a bowl of the upper waters; "and two olive trees by it" are Netzach and Hod, "the two testicles of the male"; for there is the drawing of the seed, and there it is ripened, in the likeness of the oil in the olives; and from there it is bestowed through Yesod. However, the sefirot are called olives in the secret of the right, where the oil is, as will be explained in its entry. But from the side of the left they are grapes and clusters [that draw wine from Binah], as we explained in its entry, and it will be explained with the help of the Name. Thus far has reached what we saw fit to speak in the entry Zayin. And behold, we hope for the compassion of God, that He help us in the explanation of the entry Chet:

Bound [חבוש, chavush]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6, fol. 20) that it is Tiferet, bound and imprisoned with Malkhut, from the side of Binah, which binds him with Malkhut within the exile. And of him it is said, "a prisoner cannot free himself from prison" (Berakhot 5b):

Hiding [חביון, chevyon]: Rabbi Moshe [de León], of blessed memory, explained: "Chevyon is the language of a hiding place [machavo]; and it is a parable for the greatness of hiddenness and concealment, of whose essence no other has any knowledge; and it is as though it were hidden, by way of parable." Thus far his words.

And "the hiding of His strength" (Hab. 3:4) he explained as Tiferet, and did not explain why. And the principal is in Keter, and it shows concealment. And it can already properly be said of the first three; and of Binah it says "His strength," as will be explained in its entry:

Rope [חבל, chevel]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Shofetim, fol. 274b) that the Vav of the Name is called chevel. And these are his words: "Samael and his mate, the world of the separate ones, are held by the rope with which he is strangled: Heh, Heh, by the five fingers of the right hand and the five of the left hand; Vav, the rope; Yod, their strangling. The name YHVH is death to Samael," etc. Thus far his words.

Behold, he explained that chevel is the Vav; and so it appears that the verse said (Deut. 32:9), "Jacob is the lot [chevel] of His inheritance." However, sometimes it receives from the side of judgment, and the language of chevel is the language of ruin [chavalah] and destruction; and this settles better in Malkhut, for she is the one who spoils the accusers. And sometimes it receives from the side of compassion, and then "Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" [in the secret of the Vav, which is the lot of His inheritance]:

Ruin [חבלה, chavalah]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 52) that the female husk is called chavalah and the male chovel [spoiler]; and from there are the angels of ruin, as there are angels of the Shekhinah:

Cask [חבית, chavit] is Binah; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 245b), and these are his words, concerning the ten things that they said of the cup of blessing, one of which is "living" [chai]: "'Living': they established, living from the cask. And by way of the secret, the upper Shekhinah is the eighth of the ten sefirot from below to above; and therefore she is called Chet [8]. And it is said of her, 'Through wisdom a house [bayit] is built' (Prov. 24:3); and that is chavit: Chet, bayit." Thus far his words.

And behold, accordingly she is called chavit when she is included of the eight sefirot that are beneath her, as we explained; for this is what is meant by Chet. And she will be a house and a base for Chokhmah, which dwells within her; then she is called chavit, for then she is the mistress of life, for she receives and bestows: she receives life from Chokhmah and bestows below in the Structure; and then the wine is chai [living]:

Rose [חבצלת, chavatzelet] is in the Shekhinah, as she said (Song 2:1), "I am the rose of Sharon," etc. And the reason is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 107a): just as the rose grows by the waters and gives off a good scent, so Malkhut is so called at the time of her nourishment from Binah, when she gives off a good scent.

And further, he said there: "At the time that she wishes to couple with the King, she is called chavatzelet; after she has cleaved to the King in those kisses, she is called shoshanah [lily]; because it is written, 'his lips are lilies' (Song 5:13)":

Festival [חג, chag]: all the festivals are in Malkhut; but it changes according to the place where her face is toward the face of her beloved. For example, when it is the festival of Passover, then she is joined with Tiferet in the attribute of Chesed; and when it is the giving of the Torah, then she is united with her beloved in his place fitting for him, in Tiferet; Rosh Hashanah, the day of judgment, then she is united with her beloved on the side of Gevurah (see Tikkun 21, fol. 44a). And in this way all the festivals and appointed times are in Malkhut. And this is explained in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim in places beyond searching and beyond number. However, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 225b), on the verse "And you shall keep it [ve-chagotem oto] a feast," etc. (Lev. 23:41), and these are his words: "'And you shall keep it [oto]': this is the letter [ot] Vav, the central pillar; chag: Chesed, Gevurah," etc. And we can settle it by what has already come before us on the matter of the embrace toward the coupling, which is the secret of "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me" (Song 2:6): for although she is united with her husband in whichever of the sefirot, as we explained, nevertheless she receives first from the right and from the left, that is, the embrace; and this is Chet-Gimel, which is explained as Chesed [and] Gevurah. And the principal festival is always in Malkhut, according to her union with her husband, as we explained before. And the verse is explained thus: "And you shall keep it": the explanation, join and unite Tiferet with Malkhut, and he draws nourishment first from Chesed and Gevurah; and that is chag. And by this everything is set right:

Chambers [חדרים, chadarim] are in Binah. And we explained them in the preceding gates: that they are the manifestation of the six extremities concealed in Binah. And what the verse says (Prov. 24:4), "And by knowledge [da'at] are the chambers filled": the explanation, by Da'at, which is the secret of the concealed Da'at, it fills those chambers and is clothed in them and concealed in them. For as is the way of Tiferet among the sefirot in their place, so is the way of Da'at in the concealed chambers. And likewise they are called the chambers of the Garden of Eden, for Binah is called the Garden of Eden. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained "the chambers of the souls" as Yesod, and these are his words: "The chambers of the souls: for from there they go out into the world; and they are the souls in the body, [of which it is said] that the son of David will not come until they are exhausted. And he said chadrei, in the plural, to show the multitude of the kinds after their kinds, as we wrote. And some call this attribute 'the chambers of Gedulah,' from the side of Chesed." Thus far his words.

And it is not in our view to explain "chambers" except in Binah; for so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the Song of Songs, on the verse "The King has brought me into his chambers" (Song 1:4). And therefore we say that the chambers of the souls are in Binah, for from there the souls are emanated after their kinds: some from the chamber of Tiferet, and some from the chamber of Gevurah, and the like, as will be explained in the Gate of the Soul, with the help of the Name. And likewise the chambers of Gedulah: the intent is the Gedulah concealed there. And they are called chadrei, in the plural, for each chamber is included of its fellow. This is our view on the matter of the chambers, in general and in particular:

New [חדש, chadash]: every new thing and renewal is in the moon; for she is the one renewed, in the secret of the moon in its renewal, in the secret of "the two luminaries," etc., which we explained in the Gate of the Diminishment. And this is the secret of "your youth is renewed like the eagle" (Ps. 103:5), "it shall bring forth new fruit every month [le-chodashav]" (Ezek. 47:12). And everything depends on the renewal of the moon, which is Malkhut, as we explained:

Eve [חוה, Chavvah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Malkhut is so called because she was "the mother of all living" (Gen. 3:20). In truth, she is the wife of Adam, the first man, in the secret of mah [45], [the number of] adam; and it is Chokhmah, ko'ach mah, as will be explained with the help of the Name:

Seer [חוזה, chozeh] is Tiferet; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, as will be explained in the entry chazon with the help of the Name. And it is possible that he is so called because he bestows the vision and the prophecy in Malkhut [by way of Netzach and Hod], and through her on the prophets, as we explained in the entry "the mirror that shines." And chozeh comes to twenty-six, the number of the Name:

The spinal cord [חוט השדרה, chut ha-shedrah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that they are Netzach and Hod, and these are his words: "Netzach and Hod are the spinal cords that hold up the sides of the body, here and there, and the whole Structure and the attributes that are beneath them." Thus far his words. And it does not settle. And the correct [view] is that the spinal cord is the secret of the middle line, Tiferet; and likewise it is drawn from the brain, and it bestows effluence on all the sides, as is known. Further, there is the scarlet thread [chut ha-shani]: it is the effluence of Gevurah, bestowed on Malkhut in the secret of the arousal of the north toward the union; and it arouses the kiss; and that is "Your lips are like a thread of scarlet" (Song 4:3). Further, there is the thread of Chesed: it is the effluence bestowed from Chesed on Malkhut. And from the side of Gevurah it is further called the thread of gold. And there is a great difference between the scarlet thread and the thread of gold, what is between red and gold, as we explained in the Gate of Colors. And from the side of Tiferet it is called the green line. And there is a difference between the spinal cord and the green thread: for green is composed of judgment and compassion, red and white, and the spinal cord is white as silver.
And the matter of the thread of Chesed, the thread of gold and the green line are found in the matter of the three colors of the eye; and she is Malkhut, the pupil of the eye, in the middle:

Nose [חוטם, chotem]: according to what appears from the words of Rabbi Moshe [de León], the nose is in Gevurah; "and the master of the nose is the one who knows how to prolong the anger [af, nose], so that her messengers do not go out from her before the plague begins. And therefore he is her husband, and he masters her, for the lord is husband." Thus far his words.

And behold, it is understood from his language that the nose is Gevurah and her husband is Gedulah, which holds her back from acting in judgment. However, what appears to us from the language of the Zohar is that the nose itself includes many sefirot, and it is a particular matter included in Chokhmah; and therefore Chokhmah is called the master of the nose. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 165b): "Scent to the south: 'a pleasing scent to YHVH.' And the nose has two nostrils, included of judgment and compassion, and they are Yod, Yod. The nose, Vav in the middle; two channels are its own. And it is said of it, 'the camp of Reuben to the south' (Num. 2:10): re'u ven [see, a son]. The two nostrils of the nose correspond to Leah and Rachel. The nose in a straight way between them: this is Jacob." Thus far his words.

And the explanation: the scent is in Chokhmah, as is proved in many places, and as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name. And he says "to the south," for there is Chokhmah, as they said, "whoever wishes to become wise, let him turn southward." And this is what he said, "a fire-offering, a pleasing scent to YHVH," for this name is in Chokhmah; and likewise it is proved there from the beginning of the matter. "And it has two nostrils": the explanation, the two holes of the nose through which the scent is drawn, as is known.
