"Included of judgment and compassion": for each one is included of judgment and compassion; and in the right there is also judgment, and in the left there is also compassion.

And the matter of Yod, Yod: they are Binah and Malkhut, except that Binah inclines to the right and Malkhut to Gevurah. And their being called Yods we explained in the Gate of Manifestations; and since the manifestation of both of them is in Chokhmah, which is the master of the nose, as we explained, if so their true manifestation is two Yods, as we explained in the aforementioned gate. "Vav in the middle" is Tiferet, the middle line, which is level between Gedulah and Gevurah; and this is in the secret of Da'at, which is concealed in Chokhmah. "And it is said of it, 'the camp of Reuben'": the explanation, re'u ven, Tiferet; and it is to the south, Chokhmah. "Two nostrils," etc.: explained above.

Behold, the nose is, in its totality, Tiferet and Binah and Malkhut with Chesed and Gevurah; and all this matter is in Chokhmah, for there is the principal scent, as he explained. Thus far what seems to me true in this matter. [However,] from the language of the Tikkunim in other places it appears that the nose is Tiferet, and the two nostrils of the nose are Gedulah [and] Gevurah; therefore "from one goes out smoke and fire" (cf. Ps. 18:9); and all of it settles by what we explained above:

Strand [חוליא, chulya]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (in the Addenda to the Zohar, part 3, fol. 308b): "A strand has no fewer than three windings; and this is the Shekhinah, who is the only daughter, bound in the Shin of Shabbat; for she is the sign of the tefillin, bound in the Shin of the tefillin, which is three branches of the Patriarchs; and this is the Shin-Yod of Shaddai."
And this matter will be explained by what was explained in the Gate of Manifestations on the matter of the three colors of the eye and the pupil of the eye:

The heat of the day [חום היום, chom ha-yom]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 14, and Parashat Vayera, fol. 98a): "'In the heat of the day' (Gen. 18:1): it is the shining of Chesed." It appears that "the heat of the day" is the light of Chesed. And it is possible that the light of Chesed is called "the heat of the day" in the secret of the little fire that stands at the gate on the side of Gedulah, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance:
Wall [חומה, chomah]: one verse says, "and the waters were a wall to them" (Exod. 14:22); and one verse says, "For I will be to her a wall of fire round about" (Zech. 2:9).

And behold, the wall is Malkhut. And when she draws nourishment from Chesed, "the waters were a wall to them"; and from the side of her nourishment from Gevurah she is called "a wall of fire." And she is called "wall" because she surrounds Israel, and she is a wall for them:

Stringency [חומרא, chumra]: in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Malkhut is called chumra from the side of the left; for from there is the severity of the matter, in the secret of the husk. And therefore one must be stringent and multiply fences, lest the serpent breach the fence. And there he explained that some say chumra is from the side of Chesed, which is over against the husks of the ass [chamor], as in the matter of "the ass from the right" (mentioned in the Zohar, Balak, fol. 207a; see there); and likewise "the heap [chomer] of great waters" (Hab. 3:15):

Strength [חוסן, chosen]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 5a) that it is a hint at Tiferet. And the proof is from the verse (Isa. 33:6), "And He shall be the faithfulness of your times, a strength [chosen]," and it is the order of Nashim, in Tiferet.
And behold, accordingly he is called chosen in his union with Malkhut. And from the sense of the word, he is called chosen, the language of strength and might:

Canopy [חופה, chuppah]: the masters of the Kabbalah pictured the whole Emanation as a canopy. And this is its order: Keter is the roof of the canopy, meaning that the drawing out of its effluence over everything is like the roof of the canopy over everything; Chokhmah is the walls of the canopy; Binah is the entrance of the canopy; and Chesed, Gevurah, Netzach and Hod are like arms standing at the entrance of the canopy; and Tiferet and Malkhut are the bridegroom and bride within their canopy, by means of Yesod, which is the groomsman:

The lawgivers of Israel [חוקקי ישראל, chokekei Yisra'el] (Judg. 5:9): he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 26a): "Who are chokekei Yisra'el? It is not written chakukei [the engraved ones of] Israel, but chokekei [the engravers]: these are Abba and Imma, who engrave holy Israel, which flows from between them." Thus far his words. And the explanation is clear: if [it had been written chakukei], the explanation would have been Netzach and Hod, which are engraved from Israel the Elder; for the explanation of chakukei is about the engraving, that is, the revealing in substance. And now that it said chokekei, its explanation is: those who reveal Tiferet and bring him into being as a being in substance; and they are Chokhmah and Binah, through both of which it is drawn; and that is "which flows from between them." And we find ourselves taught three things from this saying. First, that Chokhmah and Binah are called chokekei Yisra'el with respect to their bringing Tiferet into being. Second, that from here we may infer to the other sefirot: as in "with the lawgiver [bi-mechokek], with their staves" (Num. 21:18), where the explanation would be the one that emanates Yesod; for the staff is Yesod, and the one that engraves it is Tiferet. And all this is an example, so that we may judge for the other places according to the context. Third, as the relation of chokekei is from Emanator to emanated, so the relation of chakukei is from emanated to Emanator: for just as chokekei are emanators, so chakukei are emanated:

Seal [חותם, chotam]: on the matter of sealing there are in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 55, fol. 86b) words that contradict one another, and likewise on the matter of writing. And we shall not lengthen in copying his words here, for the matter would be long for us and this is not its place. However, we shall write what emerges for us, after going over all his words, in our view. And it is that to the matter of sealing there are four divisions: first, the ring; second, the seal set in the ring; third, the one who seals; fourth, the thing sealed, which receives the sealing.

And behold, the ring is Chokhmah; and the seal set in the ring is Tiferet; and the one who seals with it is Binah, which is called the fourteen letters of "YHVH our God YHVH," which are twenty-eight letters, fourteen [and] fourteen, these a garment for those, as explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapter 4; and she is the hand [yad, 14] that seals. And the one who receives the sealing is Malkhut, in whom the sealing settles; and she is the receptacle. And this whole matter is from the left to the right, that is, it is drawn from the left to the right. For the principal is Chokhmah, and Binah and Tiferet are drawn after it to the right to seal. However, Malkhut, who is on the left, on the left side, receives the sealing by means of Yesod. And this is "He seals up the hand of every man" (Job 37:7): and the intent is the seal that seals, which is held in the hand; and this matter is through Yesod, which is called kol [all]; and it is called kol from the side of Binah, as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name. This is the sum of the sealing:

And the matter of writing is also divided into parts. First, the writer, and they are the five fingers that hold the pen; and the pen itself; and the hand that writes; and the place in which the writing is written, which is the material that bears the written letters.

And behold, the pen is Tiferet, and it is called kaneh [reed] everywhere, as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name. And the fingers are the three that hold the pen, and they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; and the two that support below, which are a seat and base for the three fingers holding the pen, are Netzach and Hod. And the one that receives the writing, that is, the parchment, which bears the writing, is Malkhut. So the writing is found to be through six sefirot. And in some respect it is more praiseworthy than the sealing, for the writing is through Tiferet, which is the principal, but the sealing is through Yesod. And when we look at their source above, the sealing is superior, for it is through Chokhmah, and the writing not so much, for it is only through Tiferet, as we explained. However, the writing is the reverse of the sealing, for the writing is from the right to the left; for the principal of the writing is from Binah: katav [writing] is the initials of Keter, Torah, Berakhah [crown, Torah, blessing], and all three are in Binah; and the right is drawn to her through Tiferet. And now it is right [to say] that the writing is right and the sealing left, or the reverse; and likewise it is right [to say] that the writing is superior to the sealing, or the reverse, as explained above. This is what emerges, to the poverty of our knowledge, from the reconciling of the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him; for this matter came in great confusion in the Tikkunim:

The vision of the night [חזוא די ליליא, chezva di leilya] (Dan. 2:19): he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 196a), that the angel Gabriel is called "the vision of the night": the explanation, a mirror in which the matter of Malkhut, who is called leilya [night], appears; as it is written (Dan. 8:16), "Gabriel, make this man understand the vision" (see Parashat Vayetze, fol. 149b):

Vision [חזון, chazon]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (at the end of Tikkun 39) that it is the union of Tiferet with Malkhut; and these are his words: "She is chazon, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is chozeh [seer], who is YHVH Adonai. For so chazon, without the Vav, comes to sixty-five, the number of Adonai," etc. "And by what is she chazon? By the letter Vav; by it she is made the mirror that shines, her Lord [adon]." Thus far his words.

He taught explicitly that the Shekhinah, when Tiferet is joined to her, is called chazon, as explained. And by this will be understood why they called the beadle of the synagogue chazzan: for so it comes to [the number of] Adonai; and it is the attendant, for she attends all the sefirot:

Chazchaziyot [חזחזיות, chazchaziyot, glimpses]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it as Tiferet, and these are his words: "Chazchaziyot: the explanation, the vision of the seers. For all the seers find their vision, each according to the level of his place, coming to him from above to below it; for there are many levels and degrees to this prophecy, one above the other, and in the end all is from here." Thus far his words.
And this title seems more [fitting] for Malkhut, for the same reason:

Wheat [חטה, chittah] is in Malkhut. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason, and these are his words: "And some called her wheat; and the truth is that it is split, like a female. And also chittah from the language of sin [chet], 'sin crouches at the door' (Gen. 4:7)" (see Berakhot 61a). And in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 188b) he explained: "Wheat [chittah]: a daughter who coaxes [mitchatta] before her father, and he does her desire [re'uta]. And what is chittah? The totality of the twenty-two letters [Chet-Tet-Heh = 22]." Thus far his words. And behold, it is explicit that when she is included of twenty-two letters she is called chittah.

And further, from the language of longing, for she is a beloved king's daughter. And there he explained that chittah is from the language of mechittah [terror], with a Tav, as "and from terror, for it shall not come near you" (Isa. 54:14), the language of breaking, because she breaks all the side of the left, in the secret of "until a stone was cut out without hands," etc. (Dan. 2:34). And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 17, fol. 29,

and Tikkun 70, fol. 125b) he explained that chittah is a hint at the Shekhinah within the husks; and this is the matter of chet Heh: Malkhut is called Heh, and the husks in which she is clothed are called chet, which is from the language of "and in sin [chet] did my mother conceive me" (Ps. 51:7).
And behold, when she is clothed in the husks she subdues them, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA:

Sin-offering [חטאת, chatat]: there is the language of cleansing and there is the language of sin. However, chet [sin] is the male, the primordial serpent; and chatat is the female, the wicked Lilith. But there is chatat, the language of cleansing, and it is in Malkhut, when she was diminished and went down to the footstool of his feet, in the secret of "and he came down from offering the sin-offering" (Lev. 9:22), the language of going down; so he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 247b). Living [חי, chai] is Yesod; and so it is well known in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 245b). However, it is also called the Life of the Worlds [chei ha-olamim]; and in this word there is a difference between chai and chei. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] wrote that chai, with a patach, is a title for Binah, and chei, with a tzeirei, is a title for Yesod; and in the book Sha'arei Tzedek he spoke at length on this. However, in the Zohar no difference is found in it. And all the commentators wrote that it is called chai when it draws life from Binah to Malkhut. (And in the Zohar Chadash on the Song of Songs, fol. 73b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that when it takes and receives from the upper ones alone, it is called chai, for it receives life from above; and when it bestows the life and the effluence below, it is called chei ha-olamim, because it bestows life on the worlds that are below it. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Tiferet too is called chei ha-olamim, because it is the life of Malkhut, or of Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut, for all of them are called world. Thus far his words.

And he said in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 164a), that Tiferet is sometimes called chai; and on the contrary, the Righteous One draws life from it. And this is some support for the words of Rabbi Moshe [de León]. Further, Rabbi Moshe [de León] wrote that Malkhut too is called chei ha-olamim, for she gives life to all the worlds emanated from her. Thus far:

Riddle [חידה, chidah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that chidah is in Netzach, for there is the place of prophecy; and it is already known that prophecy comes to the prophet in a riddle, as it is said of Moses (Num. 12:8), "and plainly, and not in riddles":

Living creature [חיה, chayyah]: there is an upper living creature and a lower living creature. The upper one is Chokhmah, which is the living creature above the firmament; that is, the Yod that is over the Alef, like this [figure not reproduced]. And there is a lower living creature, which is Malkhut; and she is called "the living creature that was under the God of Israel" (Ezek. 10:20); that is, the Yod under the Vav, like this: א. All this is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 5, fol. 18a). And it is possible that she is so called from the language of life [chayyim]; for Chokhmah is the source of life for all the sefirot, as will be explained; and Malkhut too is life from the side of her manifestation, which is called the second Yod. And in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, further explained that Malkhut is called chayyah from the side of the holy living creatures. And it is possible that he means the upper living creatures, and that is because she receives from the upper living creatures; and it is possible that he means the lower living creatures, and that is when she causes her Shekhinah to dwell upon them:
The life of the King [חיי המלך, chayyei ha-melekh]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Yitro, fol. 91,

and Mishpatim, fol. 115b) that the King is Tiferet, and his life is Chokhmah and Binah; for they are called life, and from there life is bestowed, as it is said (Eccl. 7:12), "wisdom gives life to those who have it"; and Binah bestows the life that she receives from Chokhmah on Tiferet. And by this is settled what is found, that sometimes he says "the life of the King" is Chokhmah and Binah, and sometimes Chokhmah alone; and the reason is as we explained: that the principal and the source is Chokhmah, and from there it comes to Binah, and from there to Tiferet; and for this both are right together. Further, he explained that Chokhmah is called "the life of the world to come," for it is the life of Binah, which is called the world to come, as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name. Further, Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Binah is called "the life of the world"; and the reason is that she is the sustaining of all the worlds that are below her. And it is fitting to know that all these are called by these names only when they bestow to the place particular to each one, to bestow this effluence on it, which is the vitality of the sefirot, to bestow on what is other than it. The example of this: "the life of the King": the King is Tiferet, and the life bestowed on him is effluence, which is his vitality; and therefore it is titled by the name "life." The first three are called "life," for each and every one of them is life for what is below it, down to the last level; and from them life is drawn. And therefore the name "life" can properly be said of each and every one. And so they wrote in the Tikkunim that Tiferet is called the Tree of Life because it is a tree that draws nourishment from the life, which is Chokhmah and Binah; and we shall speak at length in the entry etz with the help of the Name. And in the book Sha'arei Tzedek there is a fine matter on this, and these are his words: "And how poor, lacking in heart, are those who think that there is good life or bad life in all the verses of the Torah. Know that in every place where it is called life, there is no evil there, neither little nor much. For the thing that is called life is the root and the substance of all the goods and all the pleasures and all the kinds of reward that are to come for the righteous and the pious. And the place called death is the reverse of life. And therefore the Torah said (Deut. 30:15), 'See, I have set before you this day life and good, and death and evil': with life comes good, and with death comes evil. For life itself is the substance of a thing that is so called, and it is the secret of the upper sefirot, the source for all kinds of emanation and effluence of blessings and goods and successes and health and life. And death itself is the substance of a thing, and it is the outer powers of impurity, the strange woman and the harlot, and the narrow well of the alien woman. And those who know this secret will understand the secret of expiring and being gathered in (and death) said of the righteous, and the secret of death said of the wicked." Thus far his words:

Palate [חיך, chekh] is in Chokhmah; so Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained. And it is possible that it will be so in the secret of its lower aspect, which is the end. And the proof is that the palate is literally below the brain, which is the substance of Chokhmah, as we shall explain in its entry. And the palate is devoid of all taste; and likewise in Chokhmah there is no knowledge at all to apprehend it:

My strength [חילי, cheili] (Hab. 3:19): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 52, fol. 84) that cheili is the Ein Sof, which is power and strength for all that is below it; and it is cheil Yod, which is the power of Chokhmah: "and this is Abba; its strength, its spring, is the Ein Sof." Thus far his words.
And we explained it in the Gate of Channels, chapter 2 (see there, and in his reading):

Freedom [חירות, cherut] is in Binah, for from there goes out liberty and freedom. And likewise the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned in the Torah fifty times, through her; and we explained it in the Gate of the Fifty Gates, chapters 1 and 2. And likewise of her it is said (Lev. 25:31), "and in the Jubilee it shall go out." And in Parashat Lekh (fol. 96b) he explained that chorin is Chokhmah and Binah together, in Binah, and cherut Binah alone; and we spoke at length in the entry ben:

The beasts of the field [חיתו שדי, chayto sadai] (Ps. 104:11): he explained in the Zohar (Beshalach, fol. 48b, and Parashat Pekudei, fol. 220a) that it hints at the lower powers that are under Malkhut; and they are called chayto sadai, for they are the lower, holy living creatures of the field:

Chokhmah [חכמה, chokhmah, Wisdom] is the second sefirah; and it is so called because it is the wisdom of the necessarily existent One, as explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapters 4 and 5. And of it it is said (Job 28:12), "And wisdom, from where [me-ayin] shall it be found?" And chokhmah is explained to mean ko'ach mah: mah [45] comes to the number of adam; and in it is the face of a man; and it is Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Alef, which comes to mah. And the hint of this name is in Chokhmah; and the ko'ach [28] hints at Binah, for in her twenty-eight letters are hinted, as we explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names.

And behold, it is called Chokhmah in the aspect that draws near to Binah, as we explained. And it is called primordial Chokhmah, to hint at the primordiality of the aspect that draws near to Keter, which is called primordial, as will be explained in its entry. Further, it is called the wisdom of God [chokhmat Elohim]; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason: "for it is wisdom given to the attributes called Elohim, and it makes them wise with its thirty-two paths, to Binah and to the Diadem." Thus far his words.

And his intent is that it is so called when it bestows on Binah and on Malkhut, when they are called Elohim. And it is also called the wisdom of all the children of the east [bnei kedem] (1 Kings 5:10); and the reason is that it bestows on all the primordial years [kadmoniyyot]; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. And there is another wisdom, and it is called the wisdom of Solomon; and the reason is that it is the wisdom that was given to Solomon; and of it the verse said (1 Kings 5:26), "And YHVH gave Solomon wisdom"; and further, because it is the mate of the King to whom peace [shalom] belongs, as we shall explain in its entry with the help of the Name. And it is also called the small wisdom [chokhmah ze'ira], because it is not like the wisdom of God. And this, that the second wisdom, which is Malkhut, is called by the name [Chokhmah], is in the secret of the manifestation of the Yod that is in her, in which she is level with Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And of these two wisdoms it is said (Isa. 44:6), "I am the first and I am the last": in the secret of wisdom at the head and wisdom at the end, as we explained there (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 117a). And therefore Malkhut is called the last Chokhmah. Further, the commentators explained that the upper Chokhmah is called ko'ach mah, [meaning] "wait and do not ask about what is before": the explanation, wait and understand, for there is no comprehension here to apprehend it. Thus far:

Milk [חלב, chalav]: Rabbi Moshe [de León], of blessed memory, explained: "It is known that it is white; and it is because the beginning of all things is like milk; and this will be seen in the seeds when they sprout in the earth, at the time of sprouting and growth. And by the power of the offspring of Gevurah the white turns into blood or into red wine. And Chesed is the beginning of the Structure. And the verse said (Isa. 55:1), 'and without price, wine and milk,' mixed in the man in between." Thus far his words.
And his intent is that it is in Chesed; and his reason is clear.

And behold, on the verse "bathed in milk" (Song 5:12), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Parashat Mishpatim, fol. 122a) that it is the effluence from the supernal Keter by means of Chokhmah to Binah; and there in Binah, the supernal Mother, it becomes milk and nurses the Structure. And we explained it in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 6:

Challah [חלה, challah] is the Shekhinah. And so he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Shelach, fol. 174a) that she is called challah when she is with the three Patriarchs. And the reason is that she is the measure of the dough, forty-three [mag] eggs and a fifth, which is MaGaN: Michael, Gabriel, Nuriel, who correspond to the three Patriarchs; and in the place where these are, there is the Shekhinah; see there.

Behold, challah is the Shekhinah with the three Patriarchs; and this is in the secret of Yod and Heh, which we have explained many times. And he further explained there that every term of chalah hints at her, whether it is the language of prayer, as "And Moses besought [va-yechal]" (Exod. 32:11), or the language of beginning, as "You have begun [hachillota]," etc. (Deut. 3:24). And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 16, fol. 29b) he explained that the Shekhinah is called challah, included of the seven species with which the land of Israel was praised. And therefore it is possible that these seven species are the seven days of the Structure:

Dream [חלום, chalom]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 280b) that the Shekhinah is called "a vision while awake" when she receives from five upper sefirot, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach and Hod. And the reason is that she is the pupil of the eye; and the three colors of the eye are the three Patriarchs, and the two eyebrows are Netzach and Hod. And when these bestow and shine in the Shekhinah, she is called "a vision while awake," in the opening of the eyes to bestow. And when their bestowal withdraws from her, then she is called "a vision in a dream"; and from there the prophet is bestowed upon, and there is his looking when he prophesies in a dream. Thus far:

Window [חלון, chalon]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 6, fol. 20b) that it is Tiferet; and he said that it is a window for Binah. And of it it is said (Gen. 8:6), "And Noah opened the window of the ark." And he explained that the ark is in Binah, and its window, which is in it, through which she receives, is Tiferet, in the secret of Da'at, which shines in Binah in the secret of her union through it with Chokhmah; and that is the window through which the light enters her. Or it is possible that it is Tiferet itself, and it is a window through which Binah is revealed. However, its manifestation is called window, which is called "and the Torah is light," as we explained in the entry "light"; and it is from the side of the right, for from there, by means of Chesed, is its rising to Binah. And in this aspect Binah is revealed through it; and that is the window that illumines below the matters of Binah. And the first is the principal for us:

Flint [חלמיש, challamish]: there is one who explained it as Chokhmah; and it seems to me in Malkhut. And the verse proves that she is flint from the side of Gevurah; and this is (Ps. 114:8), "who turns the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a fountain of waters": "flint," which is hard from the side of Gevurah; "into a fountain of waters," from the side of Chesed:

Loins [חלצים, chalatzayim]: it is the joining of Tiferet with the Shekhinah, and the union with which he is united between Netzach and Hod; for it is the cleaving of Tiferet, which is the body, with Netzach and Hod, which are the thighs; they are called chalatzayim; and it is the side of compassion. However, motnayim [loins] is said of [the place] higher up, in the secret of Gevurah and strength; and all is in one place, but this one is above, in the secret of judgment, and that one below, in the secret of compassion. And the matter is according to the prevailing: if [Hod] prevails over Netzach it will be judgment, or Netzach will prevail over Hod and it will be compassion. And we shall speak at length in the entry motnayim (see the Zohar, Balak, fol. 198b):

Hot [חם, cham] is the side of Gevurah; and it is hot in the secret of the fire of Gevurah. However, Ham is the father of Canaan, which is the secret of the blackness and darkness that is in Gevurah, as we explained in the Gate of Colors. And there are two kinds of heat. The first is the heat of transgression; and it is the heat of the fire of Gehinnom, the blackness of Gevurah. And the second is heat from the side of Gevurah, as with David, "that my lord the king may get heat" (1 Kings 1:2); and he was "ruddy, with fair eyes" (1 Sam. 16:12). And there is heat whose explanation is shining and sparkling, in the likeness of the sun, which, the more it shines, the more it heats. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat (Vayera, fol. 98a), and these are his words: "'In the heat of the day' (Gen. 18:1): for the right was shining." And the explanation: "in the heat of the day," in the shining of the day from Chesed, for from its side it is hot (and see above in the entry chom):

The delight of days [חמדת ימים, chemdat yamim] is the Shekhinah, Malkhut. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason: "that she is desirable to all the days that shine in her, and all of them desire her and love her." Thus far his words.

And the correct [view] is that she is included and desirable from all the upper days, as we explained in the entry "the pleasant land." And there is a great difference between "the pleasant land" and "the delight of days." And the matter is that she is called "the pleasant land" after she has become desirable, when she is a land that bestows below; and this the word eretz hints, as it is said (Isa. 66:1), "and the earth is My footstool." However, she is called "the delight of days" while she is receiving, when she is above, receiving from the days, and the name of the days is still upon her:

Sun [חמה, chammah] is Tiferet; and he is so called in the secret of "For YHVH of hosts is a sun [shemesh] and a shield" (Ps. 84:12). And it appears to us that from the side of the right he is called "the sun [shemesh] of righteousness, with healing in its wings" (Mal. 3:20); and from the side of the left he is called chammah, in the secret of the heat of the fire of Gevurah. And this is "He brings the sun [chammah] out of its sheath." For the sheath of Tiferet is Malkhut; and when he is within the sheath, in union, then he is compassion, and he is "the sun of righteousness," Tiferet and Malkhut. And when he goes out of his place, then he is chammah, in the secret of fire and judgment:

Five [חמשה, chamishah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 102), that every place where "five" and the like is said, the hint is at Tiferet, which is fifth. And likewise in every place where "on the fifteenth" is said, it is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut: Tiferet five, and Malkhut ten, as we shall explain in its entry. And in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 3b) he explained that "five" is Malkhut, which is Heh. And what appears from his language there is that she is called "five" when she is above, beside her husband, in the secret of "And the light of the moon shall be," etc. (Isa. 30:26):

Gracious [חנון, channun]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is in Chesed, and these are his words: "He gives grace freely [chinam], even though they are not worthy at all from the side of judgment; and it is said (Exod. 33:19), 'and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious.'" Thus far his words.
And it appears to us that the place in which a free gift is given is above, in the place where there is no judgment at all; and it is beyond the line of judgment altogether:

Chesed [חסד, chesed, Loving-kindness]: this is the attribute of Gedulah. And the word chesed is explained in Sefer ha-Orah, these are his words: "Know that the word chesed is whoever does a thing that he is not compelled to do from the side of judgment, but does it by his own delight and will, without anything compelling, and does that thing in his goodness: this is called chesed. For just as the attribute of Chesed is the reverse of the attribute of judgment, so the word chesed is the reverse of a thing done by compulsion." Thus far his words.

And his principal intent is that it is called Chesed for the reason that the action of this attribute is the reverse of judgment: even though by judgment one is guilty, it acquits him. And others explained that chesed comes to seventy-two, and it is a hint at the seventy-two bridges, etc.; and the intent is that it is called Chesed when it acts in its seventy-two bridges. And according to the truth, so the hint comes in chesed to seventy-two, as we explained. And likewise it is called Chesed in the secret that it does good to the bad and to the good. And Keter too is called supernal Chesed; so he explained in the Zohar, in the Idra; and the reason is that it bestows on Chokhmah, where the nourishment of Chesed is. And for this reason the side of Keter that bestows on Chokhmah is called supernal Chesed. And some say that Gedulah is called "Your former kindnesses" (Ps. 89:50); and the reason is that there are other kindnesses, as we shall explain. And to me it seems that the hint is at Keter; and likewise he was precise with the word ayyeh [where are] "Your kindnesses," which is in the first three, as we explained in its entry. Further, there is everlasting Chesed [chesed olam] (Isa. 54:8), the hint at Chesed when it draws nourishment from Binah; and this is Chesed that draws from olam, which is Binah, as is known. And there is the lower Chesed, and the commentators explained that it is Yesod. And likewise they explained that it is "the sure mercies [chasdei] of David" (Isa. 55:3), for it bestows on the attribute of David, which is Malkhut. And it is more fitting to say that the mercies of David are Netzach and Hod; and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 169a), and these are his words: "And on the Sabbath, when judgment is not found, so that Netzach and Hod are included in chasadim, we say, 'Be pleased [retzeh] and strengthen us,' so that both of them are 'the sure mercies of David.' And therefore, 'let there be no distress and sorrow on the day of our rest,' for Retzeh and Modim are the mercies of David." Thus far his words.

And the intent is that on weekdays they are not in substance the mercies of David, because there is some judgment in them. However, on the Sabbath, when there is no judgment, and Netzach, the branch of Chesed, is revealed, so that Netzach and Hod are included in the name chasadim, we say, "Be pleased and strengthen us"; for by this prayer we mention Netzach, which is the will [ratzon], the branch of compassion that is revealed; and both of them are included in the secret of the right and the left, for on the Sabbath both are compassion. "And therefore," etc.: the explanation, and for the reason that Hod is judgment in its place, without compassion, on weekdays; and on the Sabbath, when the will is revealed, we say, "and let there be no distress and sorrow on the day of our rest"; for distress and sorrow are from the side of judgment, and on the Sabbath there is no judgment, and the will is revealed, which is the right; and therefore "let there be no distress and sorrow"; and on the Sabbath both of them are called "the mercies of David."

Behold, from this saying it is explicit that Netzach is "the mercies of David" when it is revealed and includes Hod with it; and this is chasdei, in the plural. And Gedulah too is called good kindnesses [chasadim tovim]; and the explanation of tovim is shining, as "when he dresses [be-heitivo] the lamps" (Exod. 30:7). And it is the secret of Chesed before the spreading out, as will be explained in the entry tov; and the explanation, kindnesses that were good before; and this is compelled, as will be explained there; and we explained it in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 1:

Pious [חסיד, chasid]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 222b) that Chesed, when Chokhmah is within it, is so called; and to this the Yod in chasid hints: chesed [with] Yod. And for this they said (Avot 2:5), "nor is the ignorant man pious"; for wisdom is needed in Chesed, in order to be pious:

Stork [חסידה, chasidah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 163a), on the verse (Ps. 104:17), "as for the stork, the fir trees are her house," that Binah is so called; and the reason is that Chesed goes out from her, and then she is called chasidah. And it seems to me that when the three of them, Chokhmah, Binah, Chesed, are united, Binah is called chasidah: for there is chesed, which draws; and Yod, which is Chokhmah, which bestows; and Heh, which is Binah, which bestows; and this joining is in Binah. And in the Zohar, Parashat Pinchas (fol. 217b), he explained, and these are his words: "Chasidah: and this is the daughter of Abraham our father, who is called Chesed and does kindness with all the children of the world; and therefore she is called chasidah."

And behold, he explained two reasons why Malkhut is called chasidah. The first, with respect to what she receives; and this is "the daughter of Abraham our father," which is the secret of her nourishment from the side of Chesed. And the second, with respect to what she bestows; and this is "who does kindness with the children of the world." And this does not disagree with what he explained in Parashat Vayetze, for both of them are called chasidah, this one according to its law and that one according to its law:

Delight [חפץ, chefetz]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it as Chokhmah; and the reason, and these are his words: "Delight, and not by compulsion; and one must not reflect after it. And so they said of Thought: 'marvel not at the matter [ha-chefetz], for one higher than the high watches' (Eccl. 5:7)." Thus far his words.

And the correct [view] is that it is so called when it draws nourishment from the supernal will; and then it is called chefetz, a term of will. And their saying, "marvel not at the chefetz": the intent is, do not be astonished to say that there is the ceasing of thought; for still "one higher than the high watches, and there are higher ones," etc.: and they are Chokhmah and Binah, "high," and "higher ones over them," Keter and the Ein Sof. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 124a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Malkhut is called chefetz; and this is "but his delight [chefetzo] is in the Torah of YHVH" (Ps. 1:2): the explanation, the Shekhinah, which is united within it, is certainly called chefetz, in the secret of the union and the joining; for Tiferet bestows the delight and the will into her from the side of Chokhmah and Keter:

Free [חפשי, chofshi] is Binah, where the levels of freedom are, as we explained in its entry. And it appears to us that one should distinguish between cherut and chofshi: for cherut is from the side of the Jubilee, and chofshi from the side of the Sabbatical year, in the secret of its receiving the freedom from the Jubilee. And this is (Exod. 21:2), "and in the seventh he shall go out free [la-chofshi]"; and if [the seventh] does not suffice, then "he shall serve him for ever" (Exod. 21:6), the olam of the Jubilee:

Midnight [חצות לילה, chatzot laylah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 92b), that Malkhut is called chatzot [halving] for the reason that she draws nourishment from two sides. From the side of judgment and Gevurah she is called "night," for then judgments are aroused; and she is called "midnight" at the time of her nourishment from compassion, that is, from midnight onward, for then she draws nourishment from Chesed; and this is "midnight": her half that draws nourishment from the side of Chesed. And above the matter he gave there another explanation. And some wish to infer from there that Tiferet is called midnight; and it does not appear compelling to us; and whoever wishes to explain so needs proof from another place, for the title is strange and the language is evenly balanced, for it may be explained this way and that way:

Half [חצי, chatzi]: everything broken into halves is from the side of Malkhut, in the aspect of the diminishment of the moon. And there is a half [whose matter is the middle, as "half a hin"; see the entry "ten"]; and it is Tiferet, which is the middle between the two Hehs, which are Binah and Malkhut, in the secret of Heh-Vav-Heh. And likewise "the half shekel" is Tiferet. The reason: "the shekel is twenty gerahs" (Exod. 30:13); and that is Yod in its filling [Yod-Vav-Dalet], which is twenty; and it divides them into two, a Yod above and a Yod below, and the Vav in the middle, in the secret of Alef, as we have hinted in many places. All this is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna, and we copied its language in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 6, and there we explained it in a long explanation. Further, there is "the half cubit," and it is the Yod that is in Malkhut; and the measure of the Vav is two Yods, as we explained in the preceding gates; and we spoke at length in the entry ammah:

Arrows [חצים, chitzim]: he explained in the Tikkunim that the arrows are from the side of Yesod, which is what is called the bow, as we shall explain in its entry with the help of the Name. And the arrows are the three Vavs that are in Yesod, va-yissa, va-yavo, va-yet [Exod. 14:19–21], which are three Vavs, which are the three Patriarchs; or else their three branches, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod; and they are the arrows in the bow, and it shoots them toward Malkhut. And that is the secret of receiving the blessings from the right and from the left and from the middle, and bestowing them in Malkhut. And this is the secret of the seed that shoots like an arrow, in the secret of the coupling toward one of these three aspects, [according to] her union with her husband in the secret of the three festivals, Passover, Shavuot, Sukkot, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, as is known:

Trumpets of silver [חצוצרות כסף, chatzotzerot kesef] (Num. 10:2): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna that Netzach and Hod are so called when they receive from the side of Chesed, for there is the source of the silver. And they are called trumpets in the secret of the blasts, which are in Chesed and Gevurah; and these are their branches, for "the deeds of the fathers the children do":

The courts of YHVH [חצרות ה', chatzrot YHVH]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 248b), that the outer houses, which are the seven days of the Structure, are called "the courts of YHVH." And the reason is that, just as the court is a gatehouse for the house, and the house is concealed from the court and hidden, so the seven days of the Structure are revealed, and they are a gatehouse for the three upper sefirot, which are concealed from all:

Statute [חק, chok]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it in two ways. The first, Tiferet; and he said that it is a great term; and it is not the principal [view]. And the second is what all the commentators agreed upon: that Yesod is called chok; and they explained the reason, that it limits all the things that come within limit, and gives them a statute [chok], as we bless, "and set a statute in his flesh," for there is the commandment of the covenant:

Ordinance [חקה, chukkah] is in Malkhut; and for the same reason: for Yesod and Malkhut are the ones that limit and engrave for all the limited ones, and engrave for all the limited [things]. And chukkot and chukkim show the coupling of the two of them. And the difference between chukkot and chukkim is that in chukkot the principal is Malkhut and Yesod is included in her inclusion, and in chukkim the principal is Yesod and Malkhut is included; and likewise it is found that this is masculine and that feminine. However, some of the commentators wrote that the engraving of the letters is in Binah, and said that there is the hint of the engraving mentioned in Sefer Yetzirah. And in the Gate of ABYA we explained the matter of engraving well. And in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 73b), [he wrote], these are his words: "All those laws from the place called Tzedek are called 'My statutes' [chukkotai]." Thus far. The explanation: all the commandments that are called in the Torah "My statutes" depend on Malkhut, in her aspect that is called Tzedek, which shows judgment; and one may not alter, as will be explained in its entry. And in the Zohar, Parashat Kedoshim (fol. 86b), he explained that the powers of Malkhut, when they receive the portion [chok] of their food, then it is written (Prov. 31:15), "and gives food to her household and a portion [chok] to her maidens": they are their powers appointed over the matters of the world. And he said there that they are called "the ordinances of heaven" (Jer. 33:25), for the portion given to them through Malkhut is bestowed from heaven, that is, Tiferet; and this is "the ordinances of heaven":

Searching [חקר, chekker]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 19, fol. 37b), on the verse (Job 11:7), "Can you find out the searching [chekker] of Eloah?", that chekker is Malkhut, when she is under Tiferet, the footstool of his feet. And the reason appears to be that there are the searchings of Tiferet and his revealing; for there is none who attains him except in Malkhut. And this is "the searching of Eloah," which is Tiferet, etc.:

Sword [חרב, cherev]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is Gevurah, and said that David, peace be upon him, intended this in saying (Ps. 22:21), "Deliver my soul from the sword." And what seems to me is that the sword that David spoke of is the sword of the children of Ammon, which are the husks; and therefore he said, "Deliver my soul from the sword." For if it were in Gevurah, he had already said (Ps. 54:3), "and judge me by Your might [gevurah]," etc. And it is possible that the sage Rabbi Moshe [de León] also intended this, and said that "a two-edged [pifiyyot] sword" (Ps. 149:6) has an inner and an outer edge; and it seems to me that the inner is the side of holiness, and the outer is the side of evil. And in the Zohar (Parashat Shofetim, fol. 274, and in Tikkun 21, fol. 43) he explained that the two-edged sword is the four-letter name when it is outside its sheath, which is Adonai; and then it is judgment. And these are his words: "Yod, the head of the sword; Vav, the body of the sword; Heh, Heh, the two edges," etc. Thus far his words.

And we have already spoken at length on this. And likewise Malkhut is certainly called "sword" without qualification, and "a sword that executes the vengeance of the covenant" (Lev. 26:25). And the reason is that she exacts [punishment] for the forbidden unions, which separate between her and the chief of her youth. So it is found that "sword" hints at three places: one in Gevurah, one in Malkhut, and one in the husks:

Darkness [חשך, choshekh]: there are three kinds of darkness: one in Keter, besides two others, which are one in Gevurah and one in the husks. And these darknesses we explained in the Gate of Colors. And some called Malkhut mixed darkness; and the reason is that she has light, but it is mixed with darkness. And Rav Chamai Gaon in Sefer ha-Yichud explained that Malkhut is called mixed darkness "because all the flaming powers are mixed in her and change within her." Thus far his words.
And accordingly the reason that she is called mixed darkness is that she darkens the colors of the light and changes them, so that the lower ones can bear [them]:
Chashmal [חשמל, chashmal] (Ezek. 1:4): our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (in Hagigah 13b) that they are "living creatures of fire, speaking."

And further they said: "sometimes silent [chashot], sometimes speaking [memallelot]." And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that they are the six extremities; and they are at times silent, when they receive effluence from above, and at times speaking, when they bestow. And he said that chashmalah is Malkhut, in her aspect that is united with the six extremities in union; and the chashmal hints at Binah, which bestows on the six extremities. Thus far his words.
And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 223b

and fol. 228a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that chashmal is chash mal: chash [silent], Netzach; mal [speaking], Hod. And they are living creatures of fire, speaking; as it is known that they are the lips that speak in prophecy to the prophets. And by this will be explained what is explained in the Gemara (and in the Ra'aya Meheimna there; see there): "at the time that speech goes out from the mouth of the Almighty [ha-Gevurah], they are silent; and at the time that speech does not go out from the mouth of the Almighty, they speak": in the secret of prophecy to the prophets. And its matter is the two names, YHVH Adonai; and they are living creatures, etc.: for the four faces are the name YHVH, and the four wings are the name Adonai; and they are living creatures, sometimes silent, in the secret of the coupling, and in silence. For above, in the four-letter name, there is no speech but silence, for they are inner keys, and brevity in them is the principal. However, in the name Adonai, there is speech, for it is the revealer, and there it is fitting to explain and clarify the matters; and they are outer keys. And therefore it is found that chash is in Netzach, for the reason that from the side of Netzach, which is the right, is the four-letter name; and in Hod, which is the left, is Adonai; and therefore there is mal, which is speech. And therefore it is found that Yesod is called chashmal, for it includes the union of these two names. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 112a), these are its words: "The third vision: 'as the appearance of fire round about within it' (Ezek. 1:27); and this is the Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds, which holds between the Holy One, blessed be He, who is YHVH, and the Shekhinah, who is Adonai. And the Righteous One is chashmal, the totality of these two names, which are  Y A H D V N H Y; and he saw it from within the Prince of the Countenance." Thus far his words.

And behold, he explained that the matter of "as the appearance of fire round about within it" is Yesod, which Ezekiel saw. And the reason that it is called "as the appearance of fire," etc., is that it is the chashmal that surrounds the Shekhinah, to unite her with Tiferet. And therefore this name is particular to it; and it is chashmal, that is, "living creatures of fire, speaking"; that is, six sefirot, which are the six letters between the two Yods, and they are the six extremities; and that is  Y A H D V N H Y. And they speak after the union, to bestow, and are silent at the time of the coupling, as we explained above. And the rest of the saying is explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 6.
And the matter of chashmalah is the union of the two names in their manifestation below, as will be explained in the entry Kiriath-arba, with the help of the Name.
And we shall speak further on the matter of chashmal in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 6:

Their fillets [חשוקיהם, chashukeihem] (Exod. 27:10): he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 11b) that Netzach and Hod are called chashukeihem. And it is possible that they are so called because they long [choshkim] for one another, until they are reckoned as one; and all of it in the secret of the coupling, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. Or it is possible because they are the fillets of the house, for the house is established upon them, for they are Jachin and Boaz; and it is the language of support and stay [as he explained there]. Or it is possible that they are [so called] with respect to Tiferet and Malkhut, who are united between the two of them, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance:

Bridegroom [חתן, chatan]: Tiferet is called so; and the sign is "as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland" (Isa. 61:10). And in the entry chuppah we explained how he is a bridegroom within his canopy. And indeed he is called bridegroom when he is united with his bride, Malkhut; and they are crowned [mit'atrim] in the secret of the diadems [atarot] of bridegrooms, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. Thus far our weak strength has reached in the explanation of the letter Chet, with the help of God, who bestows upon us. And now we shall come to the explanation of the entry of the letter Tet:

Navel [טבור, tabbur] is the Shekhinah; and the hint in it is at her concealed manifestation, hinted at in the letter Yod. And indeed the body is Tiferet; and the belly is Malkhut from the side of Binah, that is, the manifestation of the Heh, which is the belly that she has from the side of Binah, as is known in the secret of the Heh. And the navel is the manifestation of the Yod, when it is in the belly and in Tiferet; and it is the point from which the world was founded; and it is the navel of the earth, and that is the point of Zion. And there is [room for] study in this, for it is possible that the point of the navel is Yesod; and we shall explain as much as is needed in the entry Zion. And all this is explained in the Tikkunim, one here and one there, scattered and dispersed in many places:

Ring [טבעת, taba'at] is in Chokhmah, and not Chokhmah itself in substance; rather it is the manifestation of Malkhut that is above in Chokhmah, [in the aspect] in which she is equal to Chokhmah, as was explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And at this the ring of betrothal hints, and at this the signet ring hints. And by way of transfer, Chokhmah is called ring. All this is explained in the Tikkunim:

Purity [טהרה, taharah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, stated a rule in the Tikkunim and in the Ra'aya Meheimna and in the Zohar in many places: that purity is from the side of Chesed, for from there is purity; and holiness from the side of the Levite. And we have heard some slight reason for it: that the purifying of the side of the left and its being cut off is as explained in the Gate of Names. And in the Zohar, Parashat Korach (fol. 176b), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the reverse, and these are his words: "There are two levels, holy and pure: the priest holy, the Levite pure." And there it is compelled from the matter itself that purity is from the side of the Levite and holiness from the side of the priest. And likewise in Parashat Chukkat (fol. 180b), on the verse "And you shall give it to Eleazar" (Num. 19:3), it is found: "Why to him and not to Aaron?" And he says there: "Aaron does not come from the side of the pure but from the side of the holy; and because this comes for purifying, it was not given to him." Thus far his words.

Further there: "'And a man that is pure shall gather' (Num. 19:9), and not 'holy'; 'and lay them up outside the camp in a pure place': for one is called pure only from the side of having been impure first," etc. And in this way he resolved the whole matter there. Therefore it seems to me to resolve it for the present: the principal holiness is in Chesed, for over it is Chokhmah, which is called kodesh [holy]; and from there, the secret of the right, is the drawing out of holiness over all. And purity is principally in the secret of Gevurah; for in the fire of Gevurah all are refined and whitened. And it is the secret of the red heifer, wholly red, for the strength of judgment, and not white even a little, that is, two hairs, so that there should be no compassion at all; and not black, so that the husks should not cleave to it, and in the place of their removal there would be their sustaining; but red.

And further, it is burned with the strength of fire. And so Rabbi Judah said (Pesachim 21a): "the removal of leaven is only by burning." And the Sages disagree with him and say: "he may also crumble it and scatter it to the wind," in the secret of the line of compassion, "or throw it into the sea," in the secret of the line of Chesed. And concerning fire, which is the strength of judgment, all agree. And even if purity is found from the side of Chesed, that is the little fire included in the right, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And likewise if a little holiness is found from the side of the Levite, that is in the secret of the little water on the side of Gevurah, as we explained in the aforementioned gate. And by this all the disagreeing languages on this matter are resolved for the present, until YHVH has compassion from heaven:

Good [טוב, tov]: every term of doing good is from the side of Chesed; and it is explained from the language of "when he dresses [be-heitivo] the lamps" (Exod. 30:7), and it is the language of shining. And of Tiferet from the side of Chesed "good" is said; and likewise of the Righteous One; and Malkhut from its side is called good. And likewise of David, "and goodly to look upon" (1 Sam. 16:12), for he drew nourishment from the Righteous One from the side of Chesed; the explanation, when the Righteous One draws nourishment from Chesed. And these are the words in the Zohar Chadash on the Song of Songs (fol. 76a): "'For good [are your loves]' (Song 1:2), toward the first light." And he was precise in his language, calling Chesed "the first light," to tell us that the aspect called good is its aspect higher than the aspect of Chesed; and it is called "the first light," the language of primordiality. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 168b), these are his words: "Why is it called good and why is it called Chesed? It is good when it includes all within it and has not spread out to come down below; Chesed when it comes down below and does good to all creatures." Thus far his words.

And we copied it in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 1. And likewise they explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 189) that the good is from the side of Chesed, on the verse (Song 7:10), "And your palate like the best [ha-tov] wine": in which water is put. And the explanation: that the wine is from the side of judgment, and good from the side of Chesed. And behold, when the sefirot shine from the side of the inwardness of that aspect that was concealed before there was Chesed, they are called tovim [good]: all of them good and shining, in the secret of the concealed inner subtlety. And Tiferet from there is called good, as it is said (Ps. 145:9), "YHVH is good to all." And likewise the Righteous One is called good, as it is said (Isa. 3:10), "Say of the righteous one that it shall be good." And Malkhut, good, as it is said (Esth. 8:5), "and I be good in his eyes," in the saying of Esther. And all of it is from the side of Chesed, as we explained. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 21a), on the verse (Ps. 52:11), "I will give You thanks for ever, because You have done it," he explained that the Righteous One is called good from the side of the sure mercies of David; and these are his words: "And when these mercies of David are filled from that goodness, then Yesod is called good." Thus far his words.

And the intent is that when Netzach and Hod are full of good, which is from the side of Chesed, then Yesod receives from them and is called good. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Keter too is called good, for it is what dresses [meitiv] all the lamps. And the words of the Zohar do not incline so, for it said "good is not," etc., in the language of negation. And we can say, with a strained reading, that when Keter bestows on Gedulah it is called good, because it bestows in good:

The good of Jerusalem [טוב ירושלים, tuv Yerushalayim] (Ps. 128:5): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 13), that it is the effluence bestowed on Malkhut from the side of Tiferet by means of Yesod; and these are his words: "What is the good of Jerusalem? Those blessings that go out to her from the holy King by means of that holy level of the Righteous One; and therefore 'YHVH bless you out of Zion,'" etc. Thus far his words.

And the explanation: the effluence bestowed on Malkhut from Tiferet by means of Yesod is called "the good of Jerusalem." And it is possible that it is so called only when both of them are called good, as we explained above:

Spleen [טחול, techol]: our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Berakhot 61b): "the spleen laughs"; and it is the laughter of the fool. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 244a), these are his words: "Me'erat [curse] (Prov. 3:33), written without Vav: this is Lilith, who is appointed over that oppression; and she is called the spleen; and she goes and laughs with the children, and afterward she makes agitation with them and tears to weep over them. The spleen goes to the kind of the liver; this one was created on the second [day] and that one on the fourth." Thus far his words; and his intent is clear:

Grinders [טוחנות, tochanot]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, gave two explanations in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 235). The first, that they are powers from the side of the angels called ishim; and these are his words: "From these ishim go out levels that go first and take from the liver first; and who are they? These grinders," etc. Thus far his words.

And afterward (on fol. 236a) he explained that they are Netzach and Hod, which are called shechakim [skies, "millstones"]; and the reason is that they grind manna for the righteous. And we explained this matter in the name Tzeva'ot in the Gate of Names. And he explained that they are called grinders [tochanot] from the side of the right, and shechakim from the side of the left. And the reason is that grinding is finer and better than pounding [shechikah]. And when the side of Netzach prevails over Hod, and there is an effluence of compassion, then they are called tochanot, which is a fine grinding of manna for the attribute of the Righteous One. And when the side of Hod prevails over Netzach, and judgment prevails, then they are called shechakim, which is from the language of pounding, which is not so good, for it is coarse, and the manna is not so well prepared as is fitting:

Dew [טל, tal] is the totality of Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, which comes to tal [39]; and it is effluence that comes from the supernal Keter by way of the sefirot and these letters, down to Malkhut, which is the [final] Heh-Alef. And the dew is for the head of Tiferet, as in the matter of "for my head is filled with dew" (Song 5:2), meaning from the aforementioned supernal effluence; and then it is (the dew of) the resurrection of the dead. And over against the dew of Malkhut there are the thirty-nine [Tet-Lamed, the reverse of tal] labors and the thirty-nine lashes that come from the evil strap, which is the husk, as we shall explain in the entry "thirty-nine":

The white tallit [טלית לבנה, tallit levanah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is Chokhmah; and the reason is that it is white, in the secret of compassion; and it is fringed in the secret of the thirty-two threads, in the secret of the thirty-two paths. And it is possible that it would be Binah too. For so he explained "who wraps Himself in light as with a garment" (Ps. 104:2): the light is in Binah, and the one who wraps is Chokhmah; and that is the Yod, Chokhmah, wrapped in the light of Binah, and it becomes avir [air], as we explained in its entry from the language of the Zohar.

And further, Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the white tallit as Chesed. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 228a) he explained that Tiferet from the side of Chesed is called the white tallit; and these are his words there: "When he is occupied with Tiferet, for the white tallit is to the right, from the side of Chesed, of which it is said, 'God, King, who sits on the throne of compassion,'" etc. Thus far his words.

And his intent is Tiferet; and so it is explained there explicitly. And by what we explained on the matter of light, all the explanations are explained. For the principal of the white tallit is light; therefore it is right for Tiferet, as it is written (Prov. 6:23), "and the Torah is light"; and it is right for Binah, and it is right for Chesed:

Basket [טנא, tene]: Rabbenu Bachya explained in Parashat Ki Tavo that Malkhut, the last Heh, is called tene (Deut. 26:2); and in it are placed the first fruits, which are three letters, which are  Y H V, which are first fruits and the beginning for the whole world:

Drop [טפה, tippah]: it is explained in the Tikkunim in many places (Tikkun 19, fol. 37a; Tikkun 21, fol. 43, and fol. 52b) that Malkhut is called tippah in the aspect of the Yod that is in her, which is one drop; and from her side Chokhmah and Binah are called two drops, from below to above and from above to below. And so it is explained there (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 115a, these are his words: "Abba and Imma, from the side of the King's daughter, are called drops," etc.; see there). And the intent is that they are two Yods, in the secret of va-yitzer [with two Yods] (Gen. 2:7), explained in the Tikkunim many times. And the husk is called "a putrid drop" (Avot 3:1); so they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 52a):

Handbreadth [טפח, tefach]: we have already explained somewhat of this word in the entry ammah; and there we copied the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim; and there it is explained that the Yod is half a cubit, which is three handbreadths. However, we found in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 245b) that he explained that a handbreadth is the measure of the Yod; and these are his words: "And one raises it from the ground a handbreadth, because the letter Heh is a cup; one must raise it with the letter Yod, which is a handbreadth, by which the Heh is opened with five fingers." Thus far his words. And behold, it appears from his words explicitly that the measure of the Yod is one handbreadth alone; and the two teachings contradict each other. And it appears to us, in reconciling these sayings, that the principal measure of the Yod is a handbreadth, which is the closing of the hand; and likewise the Yod is called "a clenched fist," as is seen in many places in the Tikkunim. And when it is opened it becomes a span, which is three handbreadths. And likewise when it is opened and becomes Heh, which is the opening of the Yod, as is known, then its measure is three handbreadths, which are three Vavs, which are in the Heh of the upper Yod. And they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, which are the totality of the Emanation, in the secret of AMeSh, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And likewise the small Yod below, when it is opened, is opened into a Heh, which is Netzach and Hod and Yesod, which are in truth three; and they are three handbreadths. And that is the Heh, which is five; for the five bars are included there in the span. And its measure is three handbreadths, that is, after its opening into five fingers, that is, five, a span, certainly. And when they said that it is a handbreadth, it is when the hand is closed, before it opens into the span. And this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, hinted in the saying of the Ra'aya Meheimna, in saying "which is a handbreadth, by which [the Heh] is opened": which is to hint that sometimes its measure is a span, which is three handbreadths, as we explained. And also in the manifestation of the Yod itself three handbreadths are included, though it is a Yod. And it is that the Yod has a tip above and a tip below and a body in the middle: they are three Yods included in the Yod. And that is: sometimes it is one Yod, and it is one handbreadth; and sometimes three Yods, three handbreadths. Thus far our poor intellect has reached in the explanation of the letter Tet, with the help of the One who is gracious to the poor. And now we shall come to explain the entry of the letter Yod:

River [יאור, ye'or]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 194a), that Yesod is called ye'or, and it itself is called nahar [river]. And it is already possible to say that all the places that are called nahar are called ye'or, and ye'or and nahar are all one matter; and its explanation is the language of light [or] and shining [nehiru]. And there is a difference between ye'or and nahar: for nahar is when it bestows great effluence and in a rush; and that is also what is explained from the language of "and all the nations shall flow [ve-naharu] to it" (Isa. 2:2), the language of rushing; and it is a parable for the abundance of effluence. And ye'or is when it bestows, but not so much; for the ye'or is a part of the nahar, and it is plain. And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 115a) he explained that Tiferet is called ye'or, and the reason: "for it is the light [nehora] of the Torah." We learn from it two things. First, that Tiferet too is called ye'or, as the name nahar certainly applies to it. Second, that its language is from the root or, as we explained:

Jabbok [יבק, Yabbok]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on this name (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Ekev, fol. 272b, and in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Mishpatim, fol. 116a) that it is the initials of Yichud [union], Berakhah [blessing], Kedushah [holiness]; and the intent is the three Patriarchs, hinted at in these three things: Tiferet for union, Gedulah for blessing, and Gevurah for holiness. And the reason is that the principal union is in Tiferet, for it is the one that is united; and from Gedulah effluence and blessing come to the world through it, as it is said (Gen. 12:2), "and be a blessing"; and from Gevurah holiness, as will be explained in its entry with the help of the Name. And this is Jabbok. And these three levels, all of them, are through Yesod. And likewise Amen, in the letters that follow [each letter] in the alphabet, comes to Jabbok: how so? Alef exchanged for Bet, Mem exchanged for Nun, Nun exchanged for Samekh: it comes to [the number of] Jabbok [112]. And Amen comes to ninety-one, the number of the name  Y A H D V N H Y, which hints at the union; and Jabbok comes to these two names with the name Ehyeh, which is also the union. And this is "and he passed over the ford of the Jabbok" (Gen. 32:23), in the secret of va-ya'avor [and he passed over], ibbur [intercalation]: seventy-two [and] two hundred and sixteen, which are the three Patriarchs, whose secret is ibbur; and the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, which are YHVH Adonai; and the canopy that covers over, Ehyeh; and of this union Jabbok is said. And of this it is said (Ps. 20:10), "May He answer us [ya'anenu] on the day [ve-yom] we call [kor'enu]" [whose final letters are Vav-Mem-Vav]. And this is "a sage expert [baki] in the law"; and this is the secret of the union of AMeSh: the line of Chesed, the line of compassion and the line of judgment. These are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Ra'aya Meheimna and in the Tikkunim, in many places, as one gleaning ears of grain. However, in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 78a), he explained, and these are his words: "'And I will make of you a great nation' (Gen. 12:2): from the side of the right; 'and I will bless you': from the side of the left; 'and make your name great': from the side of the middle; 'and be a blessing': from the side of the land of Israel. Behold here a throne of four legs," etc. Thus far his words. And it appears from his words that blessing is from the side of Gevurah. And likewise in the Tikkunim he explained holiness from the side of Chokhmah and blessing from the side of Binah, and we copied his language in the entry berakhah. And behold, we have reconciled this in the entry taharah, and we shall further explain in the entry kedushah:

Dry land [יבשה, yabbashah] is Malkhut. And when sin caused it, and the channels were broken and spoiled, and the effluence does not come down, and the heat burns with power, and judgment prevails, then she is called yabbashah; for the moisture of the waters of the effluence has dried up, and all the moisture of the waters of the effluence dries up and is parched; until Tiferet bestows into her, and through him the dry is moistened, and the effluence that has congealed in her is thawed. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 29b):

Hand [יד, yad]: we need to consider that in the hand there are five fingers, and they are five sefirot, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod. And they are included in two hands, which are the two Hehs, the upper Heh and the lower Heh, this one left and that one right. And the right is most times Binah, and the left is Malkhut. And the reason is that this one's inclining is to the right and that one's inclining is to the left, as in the matter of chasidah, which is what Binah is called. And there is no wonder at our saying that Binah is right, although her root is in the left line, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing; for in relation to Malkhut she is compassion.

And further, we were precise in our language in saying "her inclining": that she inclines, though she is judgment at root. And there are three hands, and they are six; that is to say, to each one of these three hands are joined the names great, strong, high. And the matter is that sometimes Binah bestows in Gedulah and is opened in the sources of Gedulah; and therefore she is called the great hand (Exod. 14:31). And when her bestowal is in Gevurah, judgment and strength, she is called the strong hand. And when her bestowal is in Tiferet, and through him her raising, she is called the high hand (Exod. 14:8). And as the relation of these three names to Binah from the side of her bestowal, so is the relation of Malkhut from the side of her receiving; and she is called by these three names, great, strong, high. And these three hands are hinted at and included in the name of forty-two. And the five lights mentioned in the passage "Let there be light" are the five fingers that are in the great hand; and the five firmaments that are in the passage "Let there be a firmament" are the five fingers that are in the high hand; and the five times "water" in that same passage are the five fingers that are in the strong hand, as we shall explain. And they are the particulars of the sefirot, that is to say, the branches of Gedulah and Gevurah. But the five fingers that are in the high hand are the substance of the five sefirot; and therefore it is "an inheritance without bounds," for there the husks have no power at all. However, in the particulars of the sefirot, Gedulah [and] Gevurah, there is power, in the way that we shall explain in the Gate of Substitutes. And there is a great difference between hand and arm: for in the hand the power of the accusers reaches, and therefore the washing of hands is needed; and therefore the nails are at the tips of the fingers, for there is their hold. However, the arm does not need washing, for it is the inwardness of the sefirot and their interior; and this is the reason for the washing of hands and not the arms. Further, there is the hand of YHVH [that] is [hoyah] (Exod. 9:3), and it is from the side of the judgment of Gevurah; however, it is the striking of judgment and its tipping toward compassion; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 8a). Further, there is a dim hand [yad kehah], and it is the power of strong judgment in Malkhut, from the side of the great fire, close to darkness, until "his eyes were dim" (Gen. 27:1) from the weight of judgment. And according to what appears from the language of the Tikkunim, Binah herself is "the hand of YHVH [that] is," and Malkhut herself is "the hand of Koh" [yad koh]. Further, Malkhut is called the writing hand from the side of Tiferet, and the sealing hand from the side of Yesod; and we spoke at length in the entry chotam. Further, there are the hands of a man (Ezek. 1:8), and Chesed and Gevurah are so called from the side that they go out from Tiferet, which is called man. And it is found accordingly that they are the Chesed and Gevurah that are in Tiferet, and his aspect from them, for he is included of both of them:

Knowing [ידיעה, yedi'ah] is the language of joining. And it is in one of two places: either in Tiferet, which joins and unites Chokhmah and Binah; or in Yesod, which joins and unites Tiferet and Malkhut, as we explained in the preceding gates:

Let there be [יהי, yehi] is in Tiferet; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 44, fol. 80a) [and these are his words: "Bereshit: there is Torah, there is fire; and of them it is said], 'Let there be lights [me'orot],' etc. (Gen. 1:14). Me'orot is written defectively without Vav. Yehi: this is the Written Torah, in which there is fire; me'orot: this is the Oral Torah. And although they established that me'orot, defective, is Lilith, the Torah has seventy faces." Thus far his words. And in their saying "the Written Torah, in which there is fire," he intended to explain the matter of yehi, which is from the root of va-yehi, the language of sorrow, which is in Gevurah, as we explained in its entry. And for this he said that yehi is in Tiferet, for there too is the fire of Gevurah, for "a fiery law for them." And there is no doubt that in this name the secret of the left and the secret of the right are hinted. The left is Heh over Yod, that is, the Heh-Yod of Elohim, which is certainly female; and the right is Yod over Heh, and this is Yod-Heh, which is male, compassion. And when the right and the left are included, it is the secret of  Y H Y:

Jubilee [יובל, yovel] is Binah. And she is so called because she is included of fifty years, in the secret of the fifty gates; and it is the fiftieth year, which is the gate hidden from Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, as it is said (Ps. 8:6), "for You have made him a little less [me'at] than God": do not read me'at but forty-nine, etc. And this attribute is called by this name when it shines in the fifty gates and bestows abundant effluence and good. And this is the sense of yovel, as "and spreads out its roots by the stream [yuval]" (Jer. 17:8). And when it cycles until it reaches the fiftieth gate, then in it it cleaves to Chokhmah. And of it it was said to Moses, "Be silent; so it arose in Thought": kakh [so] in numerical value is fifty [Kaf-Kaf]. For silence is in Chokhmah, which is Yod; and "it arose in Thought," which is Chokhmah. And for this reason he did not attain the matter of the death of Rabbi Akiva; for his death was by way of judgment, in the secret of the ascent, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 5. And we return to our matter: for when this gate cleaves to Chokhmah, then it is the Jubilee, and then the whole world is compassion and abundant effluence and freedom and redemption; and then this attribute is called Jubilee:

Day [יום, yom]: everywhere, "day" without qualification is Tiferet, on that side in which it cleaves to Gedulah. And this is what the verse says, "And there was evening and there was morning, one day" (Gen. 1:5); and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained: "evening of Isaac and morning of Abraham," etc.; and it was explained above in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," chapter 2. And likewise it is called everywhere the attribute of day.
