However, in Parashat Beshalach (fol. 49a), on the verse "This very day [ha-yom] he shall halt at Nob" (Isa. 10:32), they explained that "the day" is Malkhut. And it is possible to say that ha-yom, with the Heh of knowledge, is Malkhut, which is a revealed and known matter, as we shall explain in the entry "that day." And in the Zohar, Parashat Chayyei Sarah (fol. 132b), on the verse "for the day has turned away" (Jer. 6:4), he explained that Chesed is called "day," and it is called "day" only until midday, and from midday onward it is called evening. And likewise in Parashat Vayera (fol. 98a) he explained that "the day" is in Chesed; and these are his words: "'In the heat of the day': for the right was shining, the level of Abraham cleaved to it"; and it is explained in the entry chom.

And further, it explained there [that it is] in Tiferet; and Rabbi Abba explained there (fol. 98b) [that it is] in Yesod. And it is possible that they were compelled to these explanations because of the word chom [heat], as is proved there. And on all the explanations, the principal "day" is in Tiferet, of which it is said, "And there was evening and there was morning," etc., as we explained. And because its one side is day, and it is the side of Chesed, therefore "day" was related to Malkhut. And there is no doubt that she is so called only when she is a diadem on the head of the man; for then it is said (Isa. 30:26), "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun," etc.; and then she too draws nourishment from the right, and from its side she is called day. And [Yesod too] is called day, for "body and covenant are counted as one," as is known. And Malkhut is called that day [yom ha-hu] in the concealed manifestation that is united in her manifestation, as we spoke at length in the Gate of Manifestations, chapter 3. Further, there is the Day of Atonement [yom ha-kippurim]; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained, these are his words: "Day: the sefirah of Binah, called kippurim [atonements]; for [Malkhut] is below her, and she illumines her in the secret of 'the streams of Arnon'; and both are called Yod-Heh, in the secret of this union." And in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 100), he explained that Yod-Heh, the supernal Mother, shines in the Lady, and the Ancient One is revealed; and that is yom ha-kippurim, in the plural. And therefore there is no eating or drinking in it; for the world to come, Binah, has no eating in it, etc.:

By day [יומם, yomam]: he explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 191b) that yomam is the hint at Chesed when it is included of all the days that are beneath it and shines for all of them. And these are his words, on the verse (Exod. 13:21), "And YHVH went before them by day [yomam]": "But the one who went before them was the supernal Elder, the master of the house, the one to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, swore. And who is he? Abraham; as it is written, 'By day [yomam] YHVH will command His loving-kindness' (Ps. 42:9). And it is written, 'If My covenant be not day and night' (Jer. 33:25): the day in which all the days are included, the day of all the other days, certainly. And therefore it is called yomam and not yom." Thus far his words. And the explanation of his saying "the supernal Elder" is to show that it is head of all the days; and therefore it is fitting that it be called yomam, as he goes on to explain. "The master of the house," etc.: the intent is that in this verse the matter of the redemption of the Shekhinah is explained, as he explained there, that because of her [it says] "with a high hand" (Exod. 14:8), which is the hint at the Shekhinah, who went out with upright stature. And because the root of Malkhut is in the secret of Chesed, as it is said (Gen. 24:1), "and YHVH blessed Abraham with all [ba-kol]," and as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Bava Batra 16b), "Abraham had a daughter," etc., therefore it is fitting that the one who illumines be Chesed, which is the root. "The master of the house, the one to whom He swore": in the vision between the pieces. "As it is written, 'By day YHVH will command His loving-kindness'": for it appears from there that His loving-kindness is yomam. And because it is not so much of a proof, for the verse did not say "yomam, His loving-kindness," but "yomam He will command," therefore he brought a second proof from the verse "If My covenant be not day [yomam]"; and this covenant is the Torah, and the Torah was given from Chesed, as it is said (Prov. 31:26), "and the Torah of loving-kindness is on her tongue." "The day in which all the days," etc.: he gave a reason why it is called yomam and not yom: because it is included of all of them; because they all went out from it, and it is included of them because their manifestation remained there. "The day of all the other days": the explanation, the day that illumines and gives light to all the other days, for it is their day and light. "Of all the other days, certainly": the explanation, since there are two causes, the first with respect to their emanation and the second with respect to their nourishment, as we explained, if so it certainly settles in it that it is a day equal to all the days; and that is yomam, which means a great day, pregnant and filled, in the secret of all the days. Thus far. And from it the matter of yomam in Chesed is explained, for two causes: either because it is included of the manifestation of the other days, or because all of them draw light from it. And according to the truth, this is cause of that: for from the side of the sources, they are the manifestations that we said; from that side they draw nourishment from it:

Dove [יונה, yonah]: there is one who wishes to explain it from the language of "you shall not wrong [tonu]" (Lev. 25:17); and may the Compassionate One save us from this opinion. For on the contrary, the word yonah is in Malkhut when she is united with Tiferet. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 102): "'My dove' [yonati], on the third day, in which there is Vav." And it is explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2. And in many places Rashbi, peace be upon him, says that from the side of the birds she is called dove; and his intent is not that from the side of corporeal birds the Shekhinah is called dove; rather these birds are Metatron and the Righteous One, the foundation of the world. For of them it is said (Eccl. 10:20), "for a bird of the air shall carry the voice"; and through them is the union, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA. And therefore, when she is in Tiferet, she is called dove. And there is "a silly dove" (Hos. 7:11), and it is "the oppressing sword [cherev ha-yonah]" (Jer. 46:16), from the language of "you shall not wrong"; and it is the evil husk:

Joseph [יוסף, Yosef] is Yesod; and they called it by the name Joseph because he is a chariot for it. And therefore the hint at this attribute is in all his matters: both in that he sustained all his father's house, for so this attribute feeds the world, as we explained; and likewise in that he circumcised the Egyptians, as is known; and further in other matters, and this is not the place to lengthen:

Counselor [יועץ, yo'etz] (Isa. 9:5): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Tzav (fol. 31a), these are his words: "Counselor: this is the upper river, which flows and goes out and does not cease; and this counsels all and gives drink to all." Thus far his words. It appears from his words explicitly that Binah, with respect to her aspect of giving drink to all the sefirot, is called yo'etz; and Binah gives drink to all of them and governs them:

The Former of Bereshit [יוצר בראשית, yotzer bereshit]: it is written in the book Sha'arei Tzedek that the Righteous One, Yesod, is called yotzer bereshit; and the reason is that it forms all the forms that are formed in Malkhut, who is called reshit [beginning]. And accordingly the Bet of bereshit would be a serving letter, and it is explained: in which place does it form? Be-reshit, that is, in the place called reshit. And this is strained. And according to his explanation Yesod is so called specifically when it is united with Malkhut and gives her power to form the forms. And other commentators explained that Keter is called yotzer bereshit, for it formed Chokhmah; and yotzer would mean emanator. And it is not strained, for the language of creation has already come in place of emanation; and it is "Bereshit bara [In the beginning He created]" (Gen. 1:1), which is explained as "emanated," in the view of all the commentators. And accordingly Keter is called yotzer bereshit in that aspect from which Chokhmah was emanated:

The lobe of the liver [יותרת הכבד, yoteret ha-kaved]: this name is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 231b) at length, and we shall copy its language here; these are his words: "And in the first composition it is written, 'the lobe [ha-yoteret] from the liver' (Lev. 3:4), and it is written, 'and the lobe above the liver' (Lev. 9:10). After she has committed adultery, she rises over it. 'The lobe from the liver,' etc.: to lead astray the children of the world and to lead [them] astray over them; and she leaves the male to commit harlotries; and therefore 'the lobe from the liver.' 'The lobe above the liver': after she has committed adultery she rises over it; 'a harlot's forehead' (Jer. 3:3); she prevails over her husband," etc., "for he is the liver, in the irritation of the gall; 'a contentious woman' (Prov. 21:19)," etc. "And irritation," etc.

"And further, she is called yoteret [the remainder] from the Other Side: after she goes out to commit adultery with all, she gives the leftovers to her husband; and this is 'the lobe from the liver.' From within the liver and its lobe the gall goes out; and it is the sword of the Angel of Death, from which bitter drops go out to kill human beings; as it is written, 'but her end is bitter as wormwood' (Prov. 5:4). And it hangs on the liver, and all diseases and death hang on it." Thus far his words. And his words are clear. And just as there are in holiness male and female, so on the side of impurity; and they are the liver, male, and the lobe, female. And this matter will be explained in the Gate of Substitutes:

Union [יחוד, yichud]: the union depends on Tiferet. And the reason is that the principal union is Tiferet with Malkhut, and through them all the sefirot are united. And therefore "union" without qualification hints at Tiferet with Malkhut alone, and along with them all are united:

Wine [יין, yayin]: "wine" without qualification is in Gevurah; but the white is when it inclines toward Chesed, and the red is the power of Gevurah. And indeed it is called good when it is mixed with water, from the side of the waters of Chesed, where the good is, as we explained in the entry tov:

And there is the wine preserved in its grapes from the six days of Creation. And its explanation is that in Binah there is wine; and when that wine is bestowed on the six days of the Structure, then it is called "the wine preserved [meshummar] in its grapes." And there are two explanations of meshummar. The first is the language of lees [shemarim], and the explanation is "settled on its lees" (Jer. 48:11); for the lees of the wine are the dross of the gold, which is the side of the darkness of Gehinnom. And when this wine is above in Binah it is not yet settled; for it may be bestowed by way of Gevurah, and then it is harsh and needs fine mixing. However, when it has already been bestowed below in its grapes, then it is fine of itself, for it is settled. Or meshummar is explained from the language of keeping [shemirah], for it is kept there without the admixture of harsh judgment. And both these explanations Rashbi, peace be upon him, gave in the Zohar Chadash on the Song of Songs (fol. 76a), and these are his words: "Come and see: Israel take their portion and rejoice with the joy of good wine, which shines and is pure and settled and stands on its lees." Behold, he explained the word meshummar from the language of lees. And at the end of his words he said: "And therefore Israel's joy is in that wine that is kept, which goes out from the world to come and is kept in its grapes." Behold, he explained it from the language of keeping. And he was precise in the language "which goes out from the world to come," to show what he explained above: that as for wine, it is better after it has spread out, because it has already been mixed and sweetened. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that the wine preserved in its grapes is in Chokhmah; these are his words: "The wine preserved in its grapes is the secret of the effluence of Ehyeh, which stands in potential to go out by way of the thirty-two paths of knowledge, for the ear to hear in true tradition, for those who know them. And some of the Kabbalists call Malkhut the wine preserved in its grapes; and if so, the wine is red; and the verse said (Deut. 32:14), 'and of the blood of the grape you drank wine'; and it is kept in Yesod, and it is not so red." Thus far his words. And these explanations have no root at all; rather, as we explained, and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained:

Further, there is living wine [yayin chai, undiluted wine], and it is from the side of Binah when she is joined with Chokhmah, as we explained in the entry chavit. Further, another explanation: "living" from the side of Yesod, which is Chai. And both these explanations Rashbi, peace be upon him, gave in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 245): "wisdom gives life to those who have it"; and Yesod, El Chai, when it draws nourishment from Binah in the joining of Chokhmah; for through the three of them they are drawn below, to "the living creature that was under the God of Israel" (Ezek. 10:20):

Jachin [יכין, Yakhin]: this is the name of the right pillar that King Solomon, peace be upon him, made in the Temple (1 Kings 7:21); and it corresponds to Netzach. And Netzach is called Jachin for the reason that through it Malkhut is established [mitkonenet]; so all the commentators explained. And it is possible that their intent is that through it the thread of Chesed is drawn over Malkhut, and through it the bride is adorned, to be comely and graceful in the eyes of her husband. And it is difficult for us: for it should have been called mekhin [establishing], in the present, not yakhin [he will establish], in the future, to establish, and has not yet established. And it is possible to resolve, with a strained reading, that the intent of yakhin is: he will add to his establishing another establishing; as if to say, although he is establishing, he will yet establish, and add strength further. This is what appears to us in the way of the commentators' method. And what seems to me is that the intent is the redemption: for the beginning of its establishing and its coming into being is from Netzach. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the beginning of the redemption is from the dawn [shachar], and afterward morning; and he explained dawn as Netzach, as we shall explain in its entry. Thus far. And likewise the beginning of the redemption is from Netzach. And because Solomon, peace be upon him, knew that the house was destined to be destroyed, he set this pillar in the house and called it Jachin, meaning: it is destined to establish the house and to support it in the redemption; "when I sit in darkness, YHVH is a light to me" (Micah 7:8). Children [ילדים, yeladim]: Netzach and Hod are called yeladim; so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayishlach (fol. 172a). And they are called children in the secret of the cherubim, whose faces were like the faces of children:

Wailing [יללה, yelalah] is in Malkhut, from the side of the powers of judgment and the outer ones, which arouse weeping. And from this are derived the words Lilith and lilin [night demons]; and all of them are derived from the word yelalah, which is judgment and its rule, as is known:

Sea [ים, yam]: two attributes are called sea. The first is Binah; and she is called sea, for she shines in the fifty gates and below; and the great sea monsters go and return in her, and they are Tiferet and the Righteous One, for both of them are counted as one; and its name is Leviathan, which crouches in this sea, as will be explained in its entry. And there is a great difference between Jubilee and sea, although both of them hint at Binah and her fifty gates. For in yam, the Yod is Chokhmah and the Mem is Binah; and when Binah is called yam, it shows the revealing of Chokhmah too, through her fifty gates. And there is a difference between yam and mi [Who], although both of them hint at one matter: for mi is concealment, and therefore Binah precedes Chokhmah, to show that she is concealed in Chokhmah and does not bestow; and yam is the reverse, to show that Chokhmah is in Binah to bestow. And Malkhut is called sea, to show that she is broad, full of the waters that she has received. However, she is called sea when she receives from Chokhmah. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Beha'alotekha (fol. 106b); these are his words: "Sea: when she is lit up from the shining of Abba, then she is called sea." And although when she receives from Chokhmah she is called sea, nevertheless she is called sea only in her lower level. And so he explained in the Zohar (Shelach, fol. 163a, according to his reading): her lower holy levels are those called sea. And she is called the Sea of Reeds [yam suf, the sea of the end], because she is the end [sof] of all the levels; and it is an aspect further below "sea," as is known. And sometimes she is called the Salt Sea, in the secret of judgment, which is near the lower aspect. And when we look closely at the word "throne," it will be seen that it is the aspect of Beriah, beneath which are "the depths of the sea" (Micah 7:19), which is the evil strap to lash the wicked, as will be explained in its entry. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 241), he explained the reverse of this: that Malkhut is called the Salt Sea when Malkhut draws nourishment from Yesod, which is called "the covenant of salt" (Num. 18:19); and through it the judgment is quieted, for salt seasons the bitter and the insipid. And certainly these explanations contradict each other. And it is possible to say that the matter of salt is: a little of it is good, and much of it is harsh. And therefore, when the salt meant in the words "Salt Sea" is a little salt, it will show the quieting of the judgment and its sweetening through the covenant of salt, which is the Righteous One, in the manner of salt, whose way is to season the bitter and the insipid. But when the salt meant in "Salt Sea" is much salt, then it will show judgment and its strength, in the manner of much salt, which burns the dish. And behold, what compels one of the two explanations of the words "Salt Sea" will be according to the context. Or we can say that "Salt Sea" always intends the secret of judgment: for if the waters were not bitter they would not have needed salt; and even if the waters were seasoned, nevertheless the power of judgment still remains in them, for it is impossible to dismiss it with nothing. And so it is proved from the language of the Zohar on Vayechi mentioned above, which says: "And why salt? Because it sweetens and perfumes the bitterness to taste. And if there were no salt, the world could not bear the bitterness; as it is written, 'for when Your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness' (Isa. 26:9)." Thus far his words. And behold, he taught explicitly that the intent of the salt is not to annul the taste of the bitterness of judgment altogether, but so that the children of the world can bear it. And therefore, even though there is salt in it, nevertheless its taste remains in it; it is always judgment; and therefore it is right that we said "throne of judgment." Further, she is called the last sea [ha-yam ha-acharon], which is beside the former sea [ha-yam ha-kadmoni] (Zech. 14:8); for the former sea is Binah; and it is called kadmoni to show the union of Keter with Chokhmah and Binah, which are hinted at in yam, as we explained. And then Malkhut is called "the last sea," for the sefirot that are above her are seas; for then she is the last sea, implying that there are others that are not last; and they are seven seas, seven sefirot; and then there is effluence and blessing in the world. And likewise Malkhut is called the Sea of Kinneret, in the secret of the blue [tekhelet], which is the judgment that goes out from her; and she is so called in the secret of judgment, the color blue. And Malkhut herself is called seas [yamim], in the plural, because she is included of seven seas; so he explained in the Tikkun (21, fol. 42), these are his words: "Seas: seven in seven"; and we shall copy it in the Gate of Palaces. And in Parashat Vayechi (there) he explained that the aspects of Malkhut are many, according to the changing of the actions: there are sweet waters and there are salt waters and there are bitter waters; and all of them are seas, aspects in Malkhut:

The days of the world, the days of old [ימי עולם ימי קדם, yemei olam yemei kedem] (Micah 7:14; Isa. 63:9): he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Naso (fol. 134b): "the days of old, of the holy Ancient One, closed of all the closed; and the days of the world, of Ze'ir Anpin":

And there are the days of evil; and he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz, that just as there are days on the right in holiness, so there are days on the left, which are called the days of famine, the days of evil, "the days in which there is no delight [chefetz]" (Eccl. 12:1):

Days [ימים, yamim]: we saw fit to set out in this entry the matter of the days, that is, the days of the week and their order above, according to the views found among the commentators. Some counted the days in their order: day one Gedulah, day two Gevurah, day three Tiferet, day four Netzach, day five Hod, day six Yesod, the seventh day, the Sabbath, Malkhut. This is the general, simple view, as most of the Kabbalists explain. And in the book Me'irat Einayim there is another view, and it is also the view of Rabbi Shem Tov; and he says that it is also the view of Nachmanides; and it is this: day one Tiferet, day two Malkhut, day three Gedulah, day four Gevurah, day five Netzach, day six Hod, the Sabbath day Yesod. And this view does not settle, for several reasons. First, the fifth day is a day of judgment and justice, as is known; and according to their view the fifth day is Netzach, and Netzach is not judgment but, on the contrary, compassion. Further, according to this view the second day is Malkhut; and we hold that on the second day the luminaries were created; and this is impossible on this view, for Tiferet, which is the sun, is the first day, and the sun was created on the second day. And for this reason too it is impossible that Malkhut be the second day: for since the luminaries were created on the second day, the second day already preceded the creation of the luminaries; if so, the second day is not one of the luminaries.

And further, the first day is agreed in the Zohar to be Chesed. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 102) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that day one is Chesed, day two Gevurah, day three Tiferet, day four Yesod, day five and day six Netzach and Hod; night is the Shekhinah, and she is the night of the Sabbath. And we copied the saying itself and explained it in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2; see there. And we were precise there in his language, that he said "the two thighs are day five and day six," and did not wish to specify, because the fifth day is not related to Netzach, for the fifth day is judgment and Netzach compassion, as we said above. But it is difficult for us in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that he said that day four is the Righteous One; and this is impossible, for on it the luminaries were smitten, and on it croup falls on children. And if we said that Gevurah is day four, as the commentators explained, it would be well. And this would also be difficult for the first view, which said that Netzach is day four; for this is impossible for the reason that we said. Therefore it seems right to explain: it has already been explained that Tiferet and Malkhut were created two-faced; and they were day three, Tiferet, and day four, Malkhut; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar in many places. And by this this inquiry is right on all its sides: for on day one, Chesed; and on day two, Gevurah, and therefore Gehinnom was created on it; and day three, Tiferet, and therefore "good" is said on it twice, one of Gevurah and one its own; and day four was in Malkhut, and in the middle of her use she accused and was diminished and was given [to be] the footstool of his feet; and in her place Yesod served, for "body and covenant are counted as one"; for this is the first manifestation of Yesod; or, according to the second manifestation, Netzach and Hod are fourth and fifth, and the sixth is Yesod, and Malkhut is included with it; and that is the Heh of yom ha-shishi [the sixth day], as he explained in the Tikkunim; and she remained the footstool of his feet, the attribute of night; and the Sabbath day is divided between Yesod and Malkhut, as we shall lengthen the explanation in the entry Shabbat with the help of the Name. And on the matter of the two manifestations of Yesod, we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2, with the help of the Name:

Right [ימין, yamin] without qualification is particular to Chesed. And there are three rights, as we explained in the preceding gates; and they are Chokhmah, Chesed, Netzach. And the intent is not that there is right and left there, God forbid; but (the things) [the good things], set right in goodness in their order, are called right ones. And likewise our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded (Midrash Rabbah, Song of Songs 1, on the verse "to my mare," etc.): "they go to the right to acquit, they go to the left to condemn." Behold, all matters of guilt and the like are called left, and all matters of merit and the like are called right; and the whole matter is for judgment or for compassion, that is, guilt and merit:

Yesod [יסוד, yesod, Foundation]: all the commentators explained that it is called Yesod because it is the foundation of Malkhut. For the spiritual is the reverse of the corporeal: for the corporeal has its foundation below, and the spiritual has its foundation above. And Malkhut, in her longing to rise to it, is sustained, and through it is provided for. And it is possible that it is called Yesod at the time that it sits and feeds [all] "from the horns of the wild oxen to the eggs of lice"; and then it is the foundation of all the worlds, and all of them are fed from it, down to the last point. And there is revealing of this in the Zohar in Parashat Noach; we copied it and explained it in the Gate of Channels, chapter 3: that it is called Yesod in its aspect in which Malkhut has effluence and life only from it. And if, God forbid, it should enter the mind that that aspect should withdraw, the standing of Malkhut would be prevented, God forbid. And there we spoke at length:

Jacob [יעקב, Ya'akov] is Tiferet; but there is a great difference between Jacob and Israel. For Israel is the hint at Tiferet, as will be explained in its entry; but Jacob is from the language of akev [heel], and the hint is in Malkhut. And so it is hinted in the Zohar, Parashat Balak (fol. 210b), on the verse "Who has counted the dust of Jacob?" (Num. 23:10); and likewise in Parashat Vayigash (fol. 210b), on the verse "and the spirit of Jacob their father revived" (Gen. 45:27). However, when it is written full, with Vav, the hint is in Tiferet, which is the attribute of Jacob our father; and it is the Vav of the Name, which includes the six extremities. And there is a difference between akev itself and Ya'akov: for akev hints at her lower manifestation alone; but with the Yod it hints also at her concealed manifestation, at the point that shines at the circle, as we explained in the preceding gates and the preceding chapters:

Fair in its branches [יפה נוף, yefeh nof] (Ps. 48:3): in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 5), he explained that Tiferet is called yefeh nof; and the reason is that it is beautiful through the branches; and therefore it is called Tiferet, and therefore it is called yefeh nof. And in Parashat Vayigash (fol. 206b) he explained that Yesod is called yefeh nof; and the proof: "And Joseph was fair of form," etc. (Gen. 39:6). And the reason may be that "all that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph": for Yesod too is glorified in the six extremities, in the secret that it too is called Vav, as is known. And in the Tikkunim too he explained that Yesod is called yefeh nof:

Fair of eyes [יפה עינים, yefeh einayim] (1 Sam. 16:12): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it as Netzach, and these are his words: "Fair of eyes, from the side of Chesed, but not in the Chesed of Abraham, which is above it." Thus far his words.

And to me it seems that the eyes are Netzach and Hod, as we shall explain. And of Malkhut, the attribute of David, it is said (1 Sam. 16:12), "ruddy," from the side of judgment; "with fair eyes": the explanation, but he draws nourishment from Yesod, when it draws from the eyes when they are bathed in milk. Or we may say that the eyes are in the power of Gevurah, and she is called "fair of eyes" when she is bathed in the milk of the Mother, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 6; and Malkhut received through David in that aspect:

Isaac [יצחק, Yitzchak]: from the side of Gevurah she is called Isaac; and the reason is that Isaac our father is a chariot for it, as we explained in the Gate of Titles. However, it is called Isaac in that aspect for which Isaac is a chariot, and by its name he is called Isaac. And it is from the language of joy and laughter [tzechok]. And it is already known that joy and laughter are on the side of Gevurah; and a great proof is the Levites in the song. And this is specifically in the aspect of the wine that gladdens, not that which intoxicates. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayera (fol. 118); and he explained there that Isaac is joy, in the secret of the exchange of fire into water and water into fire. And it is possible that for this reason he is called Yitzchak, in the future tense [he will laugh]: the intent is judgment that will be turned into compassion and into laughter:

Precious [יקר, yakar]: it will be seen in Yesod in most places; and it will also be seen sometimes in Tiferet. And its root is the language of light, as it is written, "and the moon walking in brightness [yakar]" (Job 31:26):

Fear [יראה, yir'ah]: "fear" without qualification is in Gevurah, for from there is the root of fear; and likewise fear is called "the fear of God [Elohim]." And the Shekhinah, from the side of Gevurah, is called fear. And there is further a third fear, and it is upper; and it is the treasury of wisdom, and that is Binah; and the reason that she is so called is from the side of Gevurah, when she bestows on it. And what the verse says (Ps. 111:10), "The beginning of wisdom [is the fear of YHVH]": for the beginning of thought is fear, Malkhut, though she is last in deed. And this is what he said (Prov. 1:7), "The fear of YHVH is the beginning of knowledge." Or the explanation will be ("the beginning of wisdom is fear": Malkhut [and] Binah; and with this you will understand "the heel [ekev] of humility is the fear of YHVH" (Prov. 22:4)); for humility is the upper Chokhmah; and the wisdom that made fear a crown is the lower Chokhmah, and it made for the fear, which is Binah, a diadem and crown on her head. And the wisdom which is humility, or [the Da'at that rises up to] Keter, as will be explained in its entry, made for the fear a heel, although it is with Binah:

Shall be exalted [ירום, yarum]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 198), that it is in Binah; and so he explained in Parashat Vayeshev (fol. 181a), on the verse (Isa. 52:13), "He shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high": "'He shall be exalted,' from the side of the supernal light of all lights." Thus far his words. And he explained the reason that Binah is called yarum: because she is supernal, above all the sefirot of the Structure. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory (in the Tanchuma, at the end of Parashat Toledot), explained "He shall be exalted" [as] above Abraham. And they do not disagree; for so it is, for Abraham, which is Chesed, is below Binah. And we spoke at length in the entry ram:

Jerusalem [ירושלים, Yerushalayim] is Malkhut; and she is called Jerusalem in the secret of the outer aspect that is in her. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 171a), these are his words: "Rather, Jerusalem: all her holy levels, when they surround, are called Jerusalem." Thus far his words. And he explained there that she has more inner levels, and they are courts; and there are more inner, and they are the Sanctuary [heikhal]; and in them are levels within levels; and those levels that surround them are called Jerusalem. And there is a lower Jerusalem, and it is the last Heh; and we have already explained this in the Gate of Essence and Governance:

Moon [ירח, yare'ach] is the Shekhinah; and she is sometimes breached, sometimes full, in the secret of the accusation, as we explained in the Gate of the Diminishment. However, she is called yare'ach to hint at the addition and the subtraction; and that part and manifestation is called yare'ach. And there is a difference between yare'ach and levanah: for levanah shows her fullness, in the secret of "pure frankincense [levonah]" (Lev. 24:7); and she is levanah [white] from the side of her receiving from the white light of the sun. However, yare'ach shows her being breached at times. And six sefirot are called months [yerachim] from her side; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 253a):

Curtain [יריעה, yeri'ah] is Tiferet; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim; and the sign is "who stretches out the heavens like a curtain" (Ps. 104:2). And it is so called when it is stretched from Binah, where its beginning is, in the secret of the six extremities, down to Malkhut. For it passes from end to end: from the end, Binah, to the end, Malkhut; and it is united with the bride. And in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 164), these are his words: "And come and see: light and darkness, etc.: light from the side of the right and darkness from the side of the left. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He joined them as one and created from them heaven [shamayim]. What is shamayim? Esh [fire] and mayim [water]. He joined them as one and made peace between them. And when they were included as one, He stretched them out; like a curtain He stretched them out, and made from them the letter Vav; and this is called a curtain. Curtains: for from this letter a shining spread out, and curtains were made," etc.:

The recesses of the north [ירכתי צפון, yarketei tzafon] (Ps. 48:3): he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 46a) that Netzach and Hod are called "the recesses of the north"; and they are so called in their lower aspect, and because of their nourishment from Gevurah, which is called north. And they have aspects higher than yarketei, which are thighs [yerekhayim]; and they are the aspects of the loins and the hips and the kidneys and the testicles of the male, and the like:

Something [יש, Yesh]: its root is in Chokhmah, and Binah is included with it. And the hint: Yod, Chokhmah; Shin, Binah, "the root of the tree," as we explained in the entry ish. And the hint is that both of them were emanated from Keter, which is called Ayin [Nothing]; and it is something from nothing. Further, they are called yesh on account of the yesh [310] worlds that are included in both of them, and from them are drawn to Gedulah and Gevurah; and they are those that we explained in the entry or; and this is "to cause those who love me to inherit substance [yesh]" (Prov. 8:21):

Salvation [ישועה, yeshu'ah]: every term of salvation, hoshi'ah, va-yosha, etc., all of them are from the side of Chesed. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 169a), these are his words: "What are yeshu'ot? This is the right, which saves from all the accusers of the world; as it is written (Ps. 98:1), 'His right hand has wrought salvation for Him'; and it is written, 'Save with Your right hand,' etc. (Ps. 60:7)." Thus far his words. And accordingly the verse is explained: "Save, You the right," for You are the right of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to You belongs the craving for salvation; and therefore the verse lengthened its language and said "and answer me," which compels what he explained, that the intent is "and You, the right, answer me." And it is possible that, because at first sight it appears to oppose the language of the verse, he brought it to his explanation, to show that, on the contrary, from there is a proof, as we explained:

Jeshurun [ישורון, Yeshurun]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayishlach (fol. 177b), that Tiferet is called Jeshurun with respect to its receiving the right and the left, which are two rows [shurot], the row of the right and the row of the left, without the turning of the arbitration and the blending toward one of the extremes; but they are still two rows, as it received them. And it is called Israel after it turns the two rows to the nature of its effluence; and possibly toward Chesed; and that is the El [Alef-Lamed] that is in it:

Upright [ישר, yashar]: the explanation, yashar is in the Shekhinah, joined with the upright one, which is Tiferet. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the commandment of tefillin (Parashat Bo, fol. 43), these are his words: "'And you shall do that which is upright [ha-yashar]' (Exod. 15:26): this is the hand tefillin, to rest it against the head tefillin." Thus far his words. Behold, in his explanation, ha-yashar means Malkhut when she is made upright and included in all that is above, like the hand tefillin, which has four passages, four letters of YHVH. And in Sefer ha-Bahir it appears that yashar is in Tiferet, these are its words: "Jacob merited the attribute of truth, which is the attribute of peace; and the Holy One, blessed be He, measured to him according to his measure, as it is said, 'And Jacob was a whole [tam] man'; and tam is none other than peace, as it is said, 'The Torah of YHVH is perfect [temimah], restoring the soul.' And likewise truth is peace, as it is said, 'peace and truth shall be in my days'; and truth is none other than Torah, as it is said, 'The Torah of truth was in his mouth,' etc. What is written after it? 'He walked with Me in peace and in uprightness [u-ve-mishor]' (Mal. 2:6); and mishor is none other than peace, as it is said, 'whole and upright [tam ve-yashar]' (Job 1:1)." Thus far its words. Behold, it is explicit that yashar and every term of uprightness are in Tiferet, which is the attribute of Jacob. And this is according to his method, that tam is in Tiferet. And in the Zohar (Shelach, fol. 163b) he explained that tam is in Malkhut, as we shall explain in its entry. And therefore yashar too is in Malkhut. And it is possible that Malkhut is called by the language of uprightness only from the side of Tiferet; for it is what makes upright [meyasher] between the two extremes, as is known:

The Academy on high [ישיבה של מעלה, yeshivah shel ma'alah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna that Binah is the Academy on high. And it is possible that she is so called in the secret that all the extremities sit [yoshvin] in her, in the secret that she is the second array of the Emanation, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation:

Those who sleep in the dust [ישיני עפר, yeshenei afar] (Dan. 12:2): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the Patriarchs are those who sleep in the dust, and gave no reason for it. And we found [some] saying the reason: that they sleep between two dusts: the upper dust, Binah, and the lower dust, Malkhut. And this is "for dust you are, and to dust you shall return" (Gen. 3:19): Repentance [Teshuvah]. And the Patriarchs go out from this dust and enter into that dust and stand between the two of them. And it is possible that they are so called in the secret of their receiving from Binah and their bestowing on Malkhut:

Israel [ישראל, Yisra'el] is Tiferet. However, it is called Israel when it arbitrates between Chokhmah and Binah and tips the pan of Binah toward the side of Chokhmah, in its good way, when it inclines toward Chesed. And this is the explanation of the word Yisra'el: El from the side of Chokhmah, in the secret of Chesed; and yashar, meaning shir [song], from the side of Binah, in the secret of the song of the Levites; and song is tipped toward the word El. The intent is as we explained of shamayim in the Gate of Arbiters, that the intent is fire inclining toward water; and so here, song inclining toward El. And for this reason the word was turned from shir to yashar. And because this arbitration is not in Tiferet itself but in the secret of the concealed Da'at, therefore they said, "Israel arose in Thought": which hints that it is called Israel in the secret of its rising to the Thought, which is Chokhmah. And likewise it is called Israel the Elder [Yisra'el Sava], for the word sava has its root in Chokhmah. And there is the little Israel [Yisra'el Zuta], either in Yesod or in Malkhut. And in the Tikkunim they explained that Metatron is called the little Israel. And all of it comes to one place: for all is in Kol [All], and all is in Tiferet, and Metatron corresponds to Tiferet. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna he explained that Chokhmah is called Israel, and it rose in Binah, which is called Thought; and in the entry machashavah we copied his language. Thus far our poor and weak intellect has reached in the explanation of the entry Yod, with the help of God. And now we shall enter into the explanation of the entry Kaf:

Liver [כבד, kaved] is the male of Lilith. For on the side of the left there are male and female, as there are in holiness. And we have already hinted at this matter in the entry yoteret and in the entry techol: for all these organs are left ones; and in particular the liver, for it is what sends the choice and good part of the blood to all the organs and takes in the lees; and beside it is the gall, the wormwood, "whose heart is snares and nets" (Eccl. 7:26):

Glory [כבוד, kavod]: the commentators explained that all the sefirot are called glory, for each one is glory for what is below it; and they called Chokhmah "the first glory," because it is the beginning of the Emanation; and likewise Binah "the supernal glory," and the like. And all these things are without reason. However, the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is that the Shekhinah is called glory when she is joined to her beloved, and her defect is filled, and the moon is in its fullness; then she is called kavod. And the reason is that her husband has given her the power of the thirty-two upper paths; for so kavod comes to [32]. And in Chokhmah is the root of the glory. And not in every union in which she is united is she called glory, but specifically when she is adorned and whitened in a delightful palace that is called glory. And this is "and in His palace everything says, Glory" (Ps. 29:9); and then "the whole earth is full of His glory" (Isa. 6:3). And these things need great length, and it is not fitting to lengthen here. And in the book of the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 249a) this matter is explained at length, beside "Rabbi Abba opened: 'As the hart pants'"; it is somewhat close to it. And close to this matter he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 8a), on the verse "The heavens declare the glory of God [El]" (Ps. 19:2); these are his words: "On all the days of the year she is called El; and now that she has entered the canopy she is called kavod, and she is called El." Thus far his words. Behold, it is explicit that because of her entering the canopy she is called by the language of glory; and it is possible that then she is adorned with the thirty-two upper paths that shine from the side of Chokhmah, as we explained. Further, Binah is called glory, for the reason that Chokhmah arouses her paths in her; and likewise she is called the house of paths. And "my glory" [u-khevodi] hints at Binah, in the secret of the thirty-two paths [and] Yod, ten sayings; and when she shines in all this, then she is called u-khevodi, as we explained. And there is a difference between kavod and lev [heart], although both of them hint at the thirty-two paths: for kavod is said of the thirty-two upper paths that are in Chokhmah by means of Binah, and lev of the thirty-two paths that are in Malkhut. And so it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 256b), and we shall explain it in the entry lev. And Malkhut is called glory when she receives those upper paths in the secret of the union. And it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 197b), that the paths are bestowed in Malkhut by means of Yesod, with respect to its aspect called peace:

Held [כבוש, kavush]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 8b) that Tiferet is held with Malkhut, in the secret of her union with him even in exile, from the side of Chokhmah; and from its side she is called kavush:

Mighty [כביר, kabbir] is one of the titles of Gevurah, and it shows strength. And when it is called "mighty in power" [kabbir ko'ach] (Job 36:5), it shows Gevurah drawing nourishment from ko'ach, which is Binah, in the aspect that we shall explain in its entry:

Already [כבר, kevar]: this word includes the three upper sefirot: Kaf, Keter; Bet, Binah; Resh, reshit, Chokhmah. And the reason for this reversal, its hints and its matters, we spoke at length on in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 5. And the explanation of kevar: its matter is rakhav [rider] for the Cause of causes, blessed be He:

Lambs [כבשים, kevasim]: in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 248a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the seven lambs are like "seven complete weeks [shabbatot]" (Lev. 23:15), which are the totality of the seven sefirot, when each one shines in their seven days. And we can say that they are so from the side of Binah; and they are called kevasim because they subdue [kovshot] the judgment, in the secret of the days of whitening; for it is the removal of the idols from the earth. And in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Tiferet from the side of Chesed is called keves. And it is possible that from its side too all of them are called kevasim, in the secret that they are white:

Furnace [כבשן, kivshan]: Malkhut is called kivshan from the side of Gevurah, which burns her like a furnace and kindles her with the power of judgment. However, she is called by the language of kivshan and not by the language of darkness or blue, because she is subdued [kevushah] under her husband, and her judgment is subdued under the compassion. And it is the place of the baking and cooking of the effluence sent to her from her husband, for the food of the hosts; as it is known that the female, by the power of heat, cooks the seed to bring forth its like. And it is found accordingly that when Malkhut draws judgment, and that judgment is subdued under her husband, and by the power of that judgment she cooks the effluence for the lower ones, and she bakes and cooks, then she is called kivshan. And all this is explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 252b):

Pitcher [כד, kad]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 45b) that Yesod is called kad, which is the twenty-four [Kaf-Dalet] books of the Torah and the twenty-four letters of "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and ever." And the Shekhinah is called kaddah, which is explained as twenty-four [with] Heh. And of both of them it is said (Isa. 54:12), "And I will make your pinnacles of rubies [kadkod]," which are two pitchers [kad kad]. And they are called pitchers when they are full of the waters of the effluence of blessing from the river (see the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 13a):

Koh [כה, koh, thus]: the attribute of Malkhut is called koh. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 90b), on the verse (Gen. 15:5), "So [koh] shall your seed be": "from the side of Gevurah she is called koh," etc. It appears that koh hints at Malkhut from the side of judgment. And likewise in Parashat Naso (fol. 145b), on the verse (Num. 6:23), "Thus [koh] shall you bless," he explained that Malkhut is called koh from the side of judgment, and brought there many proofs for this matter. However, in the Zohar (Va'etchanan, fol. 269) it is found that there is a koh on the right side and a koh on the left side; and this is what the verse said, "Thus shall you bless," from the language of blessing, from the side of Abraham. And elsewhere it is for judgment; and this is "we will go yonder [ad koh]" (Gen. 22:5), and it is at the time of the binding; and further, "Is not My word like fire, thus [koh]?" (Jer. 23:29), which is toward the side of Gevurah. And he further explained (in the Tikkunim) that these are two times twenty-five [Kaf-Heh] letters of the reading of the Shema of the morning and the reading of the Shema of the evening: these correspond to the morning of Abraham, and those correspond to the evening of Isaac. Therefore it appears to us to say that Malkhut is called koh from the side of twenty-five gates that she receives through the right, and likewise she is called koh from the side of twenty-five gates that she receives through the left. How so? The ten of Gedulah and the ten that are in Netzach and the five of Tiferet toward the right are twenty-five gates on the right. And likewise twenty-five on the left: how so? Ten in Gevurah and ten in Hod and the five of Tiferet that are on the left side are twenty-five on the left side. And Malkhut receives them through Yesod; for "Binah spreads down to Hod," as we spoke at length in the Gate of the Fifty Gates; and from within it the inquirer will enter into these words of ours. And although we said that they are twenty-five to the right and twenty-five to the left, nevertheless, because on the side of the left are the gates where Binah is, as in the matter of their saying, of blessed memory, "whoever wishes to become rich, let him turn northward"; and the principal revealing of Binah is in Gevurah; it is found that even those that are on the side of Chesed are in Gevurah. And in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 11a, and Tikkun 21, fol. 45a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Binah is called koh; and it is no wonder, since she is included of twenty-five and twenty-five, which are fifty gates:

High Priest [כהן גדול, kohen gadol] is in Chesed. And it is called gadol [great] for the reason that it is greater than all the days of Creation, and it is the head. And it is called kohen, for the priests are from the side of Chesed, as it is written (Deut. 33:8), "Your Thummim and Your Urim are with Your pious one [chasidekha]": from the side of Chesed. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Naso, fol. 121b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Michael is an ordinary priest. And it is fitting that when he serves at the head of the whole circuit he is called great:

The helmet of salvation [כובע ישועה, kova yeshu'ah] (Isa. 59:17): some explained it as the Ein Sof, and some explained it as Tiferet, and some explained it as Malkhut. And this is the principal [view]: that she is a helmet and a diadem on the head; and she is salvation from the side of the redemption, which is in partnership with Chesed:

The cup of blessing [כוס של ברכה, kos shel berakhah]: this cup is a hint at Malkhut, but not in her selfhood, but in her aspect toward the outer side; and therefore it needs rinsing and washing, to purify her from the husks. And this place is called throne [kisse]; and when this throne is not complete it is called kes (Exod. 17:16). However, when she is called kos of blessing, it hints at a great matter. First, it hints at the matter of the Vav that is in her, and how the master of the throne sits on her, "according to the beauty [tiferet] of a man, to sit in the house" (Isa. 44:13), on the throne; therefore it is a cup full of the blessing of YHVH. And before his sitting there, the cup is purified by rinsing and washing, as it is in the Grace after Meals. And further, that she is held in the right, supported and sustained by Chesed. And when she has all this honor, then she is called the cup of blessing; for all these qualities belong to the cup of blessing. And there is the cup of salvations (Ps. 116:13); and she is so called when she is held and united with five salvations, which are five fingers, which are the five bars of the Tabernacle that are on the right side. And therefore the cup of blessing is in the right hand. So he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 1a, and in Terumah, fol. 169a):

Wall [כותל, kotel]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 116a) that the hint in it is at Tiferet, when it is united with Malkhut by means of the Righteous One. And this is the explanation: kav [Kaf-Vav] is in number [26] the four-letter name, which hints at Tiferet; and tel [mound] is the mound to which all turn, which is Malkhut, with the Righteous One, through whom both of them are united. And certainly she [too] is called kotel specifically when she has all this honor:

The laver and its base [כיור וכנו, kiyyor ve-khanno]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 12b) that the laver and its base are Netzach and Hod. And therefore it is compelled that the laver is Netzach and its base is Hod; for Hod is certainly a base and seat for Netzach, as he explained elsewhere (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 112a): "from the appearance of his loins and upward," Netzach; "and from the appearance of his loins and downward," Hod (Ezek. 1:27). And what is doubtful for us in this matter is that the laver and its base were of bronze; and it would have been fitting that the laver be of silver, which shows Netzach, whose root is in the line of Chesed. And similarly we are in doubt about the pillars Jachin and Boaz, which hint at them: why were both of them bronze, and why was not Jachin, which corresponds to Netzach, of silver? And it is possible that the reason in all this is that the hint at them is when they incline toward judgment; just as both are silver in the trumpets, when they incline toward Chesed. But it is difficult, for in the laver there was water, which appears to be in Chesed; unless we say that these waters were from the side of the rainwaters, which come down in Gevurah. And therefore they were disqualified by remaining overnight, because the strong judgment ruled over them:

Power [כח, ko'ach]: in the explanation of this word we spoke at length in the Gate of Particulars of Names, on the matter of the twenty-eight [Kaf-Chet] letters, and "whoever answers Amen with all his power [kocho]." However, the principle that emerges from there is that ko'ach is in Binah, in the joining of Chokhmah, ko'ach mah. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] called Tiferet "the power of Adonai" and explained the reason: that it is what gives power to Malkhut. And if according to his words, we need to say that it gives her specifically the power of Binah, and then it is called "the power of Adonai." And in the Zohar, Parashat Shelach (fol. 161b), he explained that the effluence bestowed on Malkhut from above, by way of the levels, from Keter to Chokhmah and from Chokhmah to Binah and from them to Malkhut, is then called "the power of Adonai" (Num. 14:17), etc. Thus far the gist of his words. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Netzach is called "the power of Chesed," because it is a branch of it; and Hod is called "the power of Gevurah," also for this reason. And he said that Netzach is called "the power that makes grow," because it makes the vegetative soul grow by the power of Chesed and compassion; and Hod is called "the power that weakens," because it weakens the power of the vegetative soul by the power of Gevurah. And further he called Netzach "the power of the bone of the body" and Hod "the power of the flesh." And possibly because [the flesh], which is red, comes from the power of Hod, and the bone, which is white, comes from the power of Netzach. And he called Yesod "the power of the sinew"; and the reason is that it is the upper sinew, to bring forth its like. And he called it "the power to draw out a thing and its opposite"; and the reason is that it receives the exchanges and the reversals from right and left that come down into it by way of the channels, guilt and merit. Thus far. And some title all the sefirot by the language of powers, and there is no need to lengthen:

For all [כי כל, ki khol] is explained as Yesod; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 227a) on the verse (1 Chron. 29:11), "for all that is in heaven and on earth," and said that it is Yesod. And to this Jonathan intended when he said, "which holds on to heaven and to earth"; and the intent is that it unites Tiferet and Malkhut:

All, bride [כל כלה, kol, kallah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 221b, and Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 111a) that Yesod is called Kol [All] from the side of the supernal Mother, in whom are fifty gates; and when it draws nourishment from her and is included in the fifty gates, the number of kol [50], then it is called Kol. And when Malkhut receives the fifty from the side of Yesod, then she is called kallah [bride]; the explanation, when she receives seven blessings, then she is called bride. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 169a), these are his words: "In every canopy there needs to be beautiful tikkunin for the canopy, for the honor of the bride, simply; for this one stands in the likeness of that one," etc., "in the likeness of the upper. Those seven blessings the bride inherits from the supernal spirit, the place from which all blessings flow." Thus far his words.

And his intent is clear: that one must set right the canopy with every kind of beauty; and the reason is because of the honor of the Shekhinah, who is there. And he said that just as the bride is called bride only when she receives seven blessings, so Malkhut is a bride only when she receives seven blessings. And he explained that she receives the seven blessings from Binah, which is "the supernal spirit, the place from which all blessings flow"; and she is Binah, for from there is the bestowal of all the blessings, as is known. And this explanation is compelled from its place there. And there he explained that the blessing over the wine is a blessing that she receives from Binah. And by this their saying is explained further: kallah is kol [with] Heh, which is fifty gates. For it is known that Kol is Yesod, as we explained, and the Heh is the secret of Malkhut; and the kol is the secret of the fifty gates, which are five sefirot, as we explained in the Gate of the Fifty Gates: that makes six sefirot; and the blessing over the wine, where the principal hint of the Heh is: that makes seven. So the words of the Zohar and the words of the Tikkunim (and the Ra'aya Meheimna) are found to be right together. And kallah hints at all, as we explained: for Kol is Yesod, through which Malkhut receives from Binah, as is known; and kol is fifty gates, which are five sefirot; and the fifty themselves have their hint in Binah: that makes six; and the Heh hints at Malkhut, who receives them. And in the Zohar (Shemot, fol. 2) he explained: "A complete bride, like this moon that is completed from the sun in all light and sparkling." Thus far. And it is close to what we explained: that she is called bride only when she is complete in every kind of completeness, receiving them from Yesod; and not that they are Yesod's, but the root is certainly from the sun, her husband; and through him is the principal receiving from Binah. And this is the language of kallah, meaning complete. And in Parashat Bo (fol. 43b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, these are his words: "Kol: the secret of Chesed in every place, whether above or below." It appears from there that every place where we title the name kol, the intent is from the side of Chesed. And this is (their saying, of blessed memory, Bava Batra 16b): "Abraham our father had a daughter, and Ba-kol was her name." And the intent is that she is called kol from the side of Chesed; and from its side, certainly, the fifty gates are included. And in the Tikkunim he explained that when the Righteous One is included of the three Patriarchs, it is called ba-kol, mi-kol, kol [Gen. 24:1; 27:33; 33:11], which are the three Patriarchs, through the Righteous One. And for all this, every term kol is through Chesed. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, proved (in Tikkun 47, fol. 81). Further, Yesod is called va-yekhullu [and were finished] (Gen. 2:1), which comes to seventy-two; and it is not fitting to lengthen further:

Kidneys [כליות, kelayot] are Netzach and Hod. And it seems to me that on account of their concealed manifestation, which counsels, they are called kidneys. And so they said, of blessed memory (Berakhot 61a), "the kidneys counsel." And there is no doubt that they are so called in the secret of their receiving from Chokhmah by means of Binah. And likewise it is said (Job 38:36), "Who has put wisdom in the inward parts [tuchot]?" The explanation: Mi, which is Binah, draws and bestows from Chokhmah to the inward parts, which are the kidneys. And for this reason they are called kelayot, the language of kol, because they are from the side of Binah, as we explained. And it would have been fitting that they be called kelot; and they added a Yod and they are called kelayot, to show that they receive from Chokhmah by means of Binah, as we explained. And there is a difference between tuchot and kelayot: for tuchot is derived from the language of tach [plaster], the language of hiddenness and concealment, while they receive; but kelayot is after their bestowal. And we were precise of ourselves, for all that is expounded in this title has no revealing, neither from the commentators nor from others:

Harp [כנור, kinnor] is Malkhut; and it has ten strings, because she is included of ten. And the north wind that blows on it is the arousal of Gevurah, which comes to her from there, in the secret of: northern, Gevurah; western, Malkhut, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, in the secret of the embrace. And it plays of itself through the effluence that comes from the north; and the melody and the song are from the left; so he explained in the Zohar. And we have heard on this the acronym kav ner: and the intent is the joining of Tiferet, which is kav [26], the number of the four-letter name; and ner [lamp] is Malkhut, as it is written (Prov. 6:23), "For the commandment is a lamp"; and the intent is the coupling:

The Assembly of Israel [כנסת ישראל, Knesset Yisra'el]: the Shekhinah, Malkhut, is called the Assembly of Israel. And the reason: he gave two explanations in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 197a), in another place. The first explanation is the language of gathering, for the intent is the assembly of a people; and she is so called because she gathers all the upper camps within her. The second explanation: knesset because the effluence is gathered [kanus] within her, and she gives only little by little. And the reason is that because of her great beauty all cleave to her; and because of the fewness of the merits that are below, she bestows only little by little, and all of it is gathered within her:

Wings [כנפים, kenafayim]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in many places that the four wings are the name Adonai, and the four faces the name YHVH. And the intent is that, just as the wings are to cover the faces, so the name Adonai covers and hides the four-letter name, as is known. And this one is called face and that one wing at the time of the joining, to hint at the entering of this one within that one, like this:  Y A H D V N H Y. And for this reason the wings of the eye are Netzach and Hod; because the eye is the matter of the three Patriarchs, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet; and Malkhut is the fourth leg of the Chariot above, in their place. And Netzach and Hod are called the wings of the eye because they screen and cover over the sefirot mentioned:

Throne [כסא, kisse]: there is a throne of judgment and a throne of compassion. Malkhut is called the throne of judgment, and Tiferet the throne of compassion; and the reason is that they go, this one to the right and that one to the left. However, sometimes you will find that Binah is called the throne of compassion; and the reason is that it too is a throne for the upper compassion. And Tiferet is called the Throne of Glory; and it is so called when it is a throne for the glory [kavod], which is the thirty-two paths; and when the thirty-two are bestowed in it, then it is called the Throne of Glory. And some explained that the Shekhinah is called the Throne of Glory, because she is a throne for Tiferet, which is called YHVH. And in every place where "throne" is found, it hints either at the throne or at the one who sits on the throne, each according to the place fitting for it. However, "throne" without qualification is in Malkhut; and not in Malkhut [herself], but in the place of her throne, which is called the world of Beriah, the Throne of Glory, in the secret of the Chariot, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA:

Kesseh [כסה, keseh, the covered moon] (Ps. 81:4) is the Shekhinah when she rises to Keter, which is covered [mekhusseh]. For when she rises to the covered place, which is Keter, of which it is said, "what is covered from you, do not investigate," she is called kesseh, for she is covered there (see Tikkun 55, fol. 86a):

Silver [כסף, kesef] is from the side of Gedulah; and likewise silver is white, in the secret of compassion. And he said in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 277a) that Binah from the side of Gedulah is called "fifty [shekels of] silver" (Deut. 22:29): for they are fifty, in the secret of the fifty gates, and silver in the secret of the redemption; see there:

The pan of merit and the pan of liability [כף זכות וכף חובה, kaf zekhut ve-khaf chovah]: the pan of merit is Chesed, the pan of liability Gevurah. And the reason is that this one teaches merit and has compassion on the creatures, and that one is the pan of liability, to judge the whole world. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] said that the pan is Chesed and the merit Tiferet:

Atonements [כפורים, kippurim]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is Binah; "and she is so called because she whitens the iniquities of Israel." Thus far his words. And likewise on the Day of Atonement washing, anointing, eating, drinking, wearing sandals and marital relations are forbidden: five afflictions, corresponding to the upper Heh. And of this they said, "the world to come has in it neither eating nor drinking," etc. And indeed it is possible that kippurim is plural, for they are the upper Heh bestowing and shining on the lower Heh; and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 102):

The ark cover [כפורת, kapporet] is Yesod; and it stands on the ark, which is Malkhut; and so he explained in the Tikkunim. And it is possible that it is so called specifically when it is over Malkhut and covers over her, as in the matter of "Joseph is a fruitful bough [ben porat]" (Gen. 49:22), which is expounded in the Zohar (Vayishlach, fol. 175a):

Branches of palm trees [כפות תמרים, kappot temarim] (Lev. 23:40): the Righteous One is so called when it holds on to heaven and to earth. And this is the language of kappot, for kappot is explained as the language of bound [kafut]: it holds above and holds below; as you say, "for all that is in heaven and on earth," and it is rendered, "which holds on to heaven and to earth." So they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 24a):

Cherubim [כרובים, keruvim]: this word serves many places. First, and it is according to its plain sense, they hint at two cherubim that are under Malkhut; and possibly they are Metatron and Sandalfon. This is the cherubim in their plain sense. However, in the Emanation, for the most part, Netzach and Hod are called [cherubim] (see the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 236a); and they are on the ark cover, which is Yesod, as we explained; and they are gold, from the side of Gevurah, as is known. And some explained the cherubim as Tiferet and Malkhut; and some explained them as Gedulah and Gevurah, incidentally. And sometimes the cherubim are related to Chokhmah and Binah (in Tikkun 70, fol. 131b). And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 112b) we found a thing by which all is settled, these are its words: "And of the central pillar and the Shekhinah it is said, 'And the cherubim spread out their wings on high' (Exod. 25:20). What are their wings on high? Right and left. 'Covering with their wings': the two supports of truth. 'Over the ark cover': this is the Righteous One, which needs to be covered. 'And their faces one to another': these are Chokhmah and Binah, which are the faces of the cherubim. And toward whom did they spread their wings and look one to another? Toward that one which enters into the supernal Keter, which is covered," etc. Thus far his words. And behold, it is explicit that the principal cherubim are Tiferet and Malkhut; and their wings, spread on high, are Gedulah and Gevurah; and the side of the wings with which they screen over the ark cover are Netzach and Hod; and their faces are Chokhmah and Binah. And since all these attributes are included in the cherubim, therefore the name cherubim was related to them, remotely. And the principal is Tiferet and Malkhut, which are truly the substance of the cherubim. And his saying, "this is the Righteous One, which needs to be covered": the explanation, the wings need to cover the Righteous One, because it is the upper covenant, and its way is to be concealed, in the way of the world, for it is a hidden place. And the reason for the covering above is so that the outer ones should not be aroused to draw nourishment from the left channel that is in it, as we explained in the Gate of Channels. And their saying "toward that one which enters," etc., is a great proof that the Ein Sof is not the Keter, as we explained there:

Vineyard [כרם, kerem] is Malkhut; and the verse cries out (Isa. 5:7): "For the vineyard of YHVH of hosts is the house of Israel"; and the house of Israel is Malkhut, as is known. And it is possible that she is so called when the hint is at the effluence sown for the Righteous One in rows and rows, like a vineyard, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance:

Bowing [כריעה, keri'ah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is in Netzach and Hod. And in the book of the Zohar (Pinchas, fol. 229a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that bowing is in the Righteous One; and this is "whoever bows, bows at barukh," which is the Righteous One; "and whoever raises himself up, raises himself up at the Name," which is Tiferet:
Writing [כתב, ketav]: we have already spoken at length on the matter of writing in the entry chotam:

Writings [כתובים, Ketuvim] without qualification are in Malkhut. For it is known that all the Writings were said by the holy spirit, and it is below the known Prophets; and both of them are below the known Torah. However, the word Ketuvim in particular shows Chesed and Gevurah, which are the Writings; and that is: Malkhut reveals them. And so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 47b, these are his words: "And from Malkhut, the Writings; and they are Chesed and Gevurah"). Beaten [כתית, katit] (Exod. 27:20): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that the manifestation of Yesod that is united with Malkhut, in the secret of the union of the male with the female, through the holy organ that is concealed in her, is called katit; that is the small Vav that is in the manifestation of the Heh. And that is what he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 247) on the matter of katit, "which is pounded with poundings": for in the secret of the movement the seed is uprooted from its place and is bestowed; and this is the matter of "beaten oil," for the seed and the oil are all one matter. And for all this: "and from my flesh I shall behold God" (Job 19:26):
The walls of the canopy [כתלי החופה, kotlei ha-chuppah]: we explained the matter of the canopy in its entry, and there were explained the walls, which hint at Chokhmah and at the rest; see there:
Garments of skin [כתנות עור, kotnot or] (Gen. 3:21): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 59, fol. 90a):

Shoulder [כתף, katef]: there is a right shoulder and there is a left shoulder; and they are the two Hehs, the upper on the right and the lower on the left; and the manifestation of both of them is in the two arms, right and left. And it is known that Binah is toward the right and Malkhut toward the left; so they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 39b):

Keter [כתר, keter, Crown]: many reasons have been given for this name. Some explained it from the language of waiting, as "Wait for me [katar li] a little" (Job 36:2; and see Tikkun 70, fol. 130). And the intent is: do not think about this place at all; rather wait until it spreads out, and then you can understand. So the Geonim explained. And some explained Keter according to its sense: and the reason is that, just as the crown is the head of all the garments of the body, so this attribute is the head of the whole Emanation. And some explained Keter from the language of surrounding [makhtir], which is the language of encircling, for it surrounds the whole Emanation within it, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing. And it is so called to hint at the six hundred and twenty [Kaf-Tav-Resh] pillars of light that shine from it and in its selfhood; and they are concealed powers that bestow the concealed light on the lower emanated ones. However, it is fitting to know that keter is a feminine term, to hint at the side in it that receives from itself, in the secret of the returning [light], as we spoke at length in the Gate From Below to Above, chapter 5; see there. And we found a hint of this in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 256b), these are his words: "And it is called Keter from the side of the supernal Mother." Thus far his words. And it is clear that from the side of Binah, the female, it is called Keter. And he was precise in saying "Mother" and not "Binah," to hint at the female itself.

And further, he explained in the Zohar (Chadash), Parashat Yitro (fol. 49), on the word Anokhi, these are his words: "And in every place, this is the female, which is called Keter," etc. (see there). Thus far his words. And the matter is that Keter itself, when it is called Keter, shows the receiving side in it; and it is female in relation to the bestowing side, for part of it receives from part of it, as we explained in the aforementioned gate. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Malkhut is called Keter; and she is the crown of Torah and the crown of priesthood and the crown of kingship, when she is over the three Patriarchs, in the secret of "a woman of valor is the diadem of her husband" (Prov. 12:4), which we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And the secret of the diadem is the Yod; and when it comes from the King her father, it is divided into three Yods over the three Patriarchs, three Vavs, three crowns, three Zayins, in the secret of the Shin. Thus far our weak strength has reached, with the divine help that is bestowed upon us, in the explanation of the letter Kaf; and we are entering into the explanation of the Lamed, with the help of Heaven:

Leah [לאה, le'ah]: the hint is at Binah. And so it is found that Leah bore six sons and a daughter; and likewise from Binah went out six sons and a daughter, and her name is Dinah. And it is possible that she is so called when she bestows on the six sons and the daughter that go out from her:

Heart [לב, lev]: the heart is Malkhut. However, she is called heart when she is on the left, in the secret of judgment, a dwelling for Binah, which is toward the left; and of this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot 61a), "the heart understands [mevin]." And through Binah she receives thirty-two [Lamed-Bet] paths of wisdom, until she is called lev, to hint at these aspects in her. And the difference between kavod, which hints at the thirty-two paths, and lev, which also hints at the thirty-two paths, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 256b): that the thirty-two upper paths that are in Chokhmah are called kavod. And when Malkhut is called kavod it hints at this: that through her having entered the palace of glory, and been purified for her husband, and united with him, she has received from the thirty-two upper paths. And when she is called lev, it hints at the thirty-two paths that are in her, simple, without any addition of light at all. And we explained it in the entry kavod. And likewise Binah too is called kavod and lev, in the way that we explained in Malkhut:

Frankincense [לבונה, levonah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 117), on the verse (Song 3:6), "perfumed with myrrh and frankincense," that the frankincense is Chokhmah; and possibly the name causes it [levonah, whiteness]. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 44) he explained that it is in Hod; and possibly this is in the secret of its color, and that in the secret of its taste:

Brick [לבינה, levenah] is the side of impurity. And this is (what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Avodah Zarah 46a): "he set up a brick and bowed down to it," etc. And this is "and they had brick for stone" (Gen. 11:3): the explanation, they brought brick in place of the tried stone; "and a handmaid when she is heir to her mistress" (Prov. 30:23):

The sapphire pavement [לבנת הספיר, livnat ha-sappir] (Exod. 24:10): besides its being a palace, as will be explained in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 1, further, Malkhut is called "as it were a work of the sapphire pavement," and not the sapphire pavement itself; so he explained in the Tikkunim. And the reason will be understood by looking closely at what we shall write there:

Moon [לבנה, levanah]: Malkhut is called so, for it is a hint at her. And the reason is that just as the moon has no light of its own but only what it receives from the sun, so Malkhut has no light of her own but only what she receives from Tiferet. And there is a great difference between yare'ach and levanah: for yare'ach shows [her] sometimes breached, sometimes whole; and levanah shows her whole, in the secret of compassion, certainly white [levanah]:

Lebanon [לבנון, Levanon] is the supernal Keter; and it is so called to hint at its great whiteness, which is the hint at simple compassion.
