And it is so called in the bringing down of the effluence, as it is written (Song 4:15), "and flowing streams from Lebanon"; and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 26):

Flame [להב, lahav]: Malkhut is called so when she is clothed in the flame of Gevurah; and this is the flame of the altar. And the effluence of the sefirot included in Gevurah is called flames. And there are flames from the side of the fire of Gehinnom, and of them it is said (Isa. 13:8), "their faces shall be faces of flames"; and this is the flame that set the Temple ablaze, because of our iniquities:

The flame of the sword that turns [להט החרב המתהפכת, lahat ha-cherev ha-mithapekhet] (Gen. 3:24): on this name many thought that Malkhut herself is called "the flame of the sword that turns." However, in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 19b), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and these are his words: "'And women rule over them' (Isa. 3:12), certainly; and these are called 'the flame of the sword that turns'; not that they are the sword that turns, but a flame from that sword which is called 'a sword that executes the vengeance of the covenant' (Lev. 26:25)." Thus far his words. And this is what the verse says (Isa. 3:12), "As for My people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them": for they are these women, which are the outer powers of judgment of Malkhut; and they are called lahat, the explanation, a spark that flames and sparkles from the sword, which is Malkhut. And this flame turns, sometimes men, sometimes women, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Palaces of Impurity, chapter 2. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Malkhut herself is called "the flame of the sword," for she turns, sometimes to judgment, sometimes to compassion. And it appears there (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 124a) that the flame is the six orders of the Mishnah, which are sometimes permitted, fit, pure and holy, exempt and innocent, in the secret of compassion; and sometimes forbidden, unfit, impure, piggul, liable to death, liable to pay, in the secret of judgment. And it is possible to say that these six orders are in her lower powers, in the secret of the Tree of Knowledge: good, this is Metatron, and evil, this is Samael. For there, from this side, are forty-nine aspects of pure, and that is Metatron [for the Nun is exchanged for Heh, in AT-BaCh, and it is the letters of forty-nine (Mem-Tet) pure], and forty-nine aspects of impure, Samael. And so the two explanations are found to be close to one agreement. And we found elsewhere (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 128a) that he explained: "The flame of the sword, what is it? Metatron, which is turned from a staff to a serpent and from a serpent to a staff." Thus far his words. And there he explained that the Oral Torah is "the flame of the sword": "if he merits, a drug of life; if he does not merit, a drug of death"; for Malkhut is sometimes judgment, sometimes compassion. And it is all one matter; for in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 12) he explained that the six orders of the Mishnah are in Metatron; the explanation, in the secret of the light revealed in Yetzirah; and from its side are impure and pure, unfit and fit, and the rest:

Tablets [לוחות, luchot]: the two tablets of stone on which the Torah was given are Netzach and Hod; and so it is in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 10b). And they are placed in the ark, which is Malkhut with Tiferet. From the side of the Torah written on them they are from the side of Tiferet; and from the side of the tablets, which is a feminine word, and their being stone and placed in the ark, they are from the side of Malkhut; and all this is clear. However, further there (in Tikkun 55, fol. 86a) [he explained] that the two tablets are the Vav-Heh of the four-letter name; and that is ve-ha-luchot [Vav-Heh-tablets]: that is, Tiferet in Netzach, Malkhut in Hod, as we explained. And it is possible that the writing is in Netzach, from the side of Tiferet, and the substance that receives the writing from the side of Hod, in Malkhut:
To him [לו, lo] everywhere hints at Tiferet, which is Vav, in partnership with Binah, which is Lamed, "a tower flying in the air":

Levi [לוי, Levi]: just as the priest is from the side of Chesed, so the Levite is from the side of Gevurah. And therefore "for every man against his son and against his brother" (Exod. 32:29): because they hint at the strength of judgment. And in the Zohar, Parashat Shelach (fol. 274), he explained that Levi is from the language of union and joining [yilaveh], that is, the union of Binah and Chokhmah; and that is "the house of Levi," the explanation, the union of these two attributes. And there is no doubt that this is in the secret of Da'at. And in the Zohar (Vayetze, fol. 154b), and in other places, on the matters of the tribes: Reuben in Chesed, Simeon in Gevurah, Levi in Tiferet, in the secret of the union of the two extremes. And therefore she said, "Now this time will my husband be joined [yilaveh] to me, because I have borne him three sons" (Gen. 29:34); for the matter of the arbitration was complete, and peace between the two extremes. And it is possible that they do not disagree; for the arousal of the heat of union is from Gevurah, as is known, and as he explained in the Zohar: "the evil inclination in the upper world, what is it? Gevurah." And also the name Elohim, which is in Gevurah, is [the number of] milah [circumcision] [86], that is, body and covenant; and so he explained in the Zohar Chadash on the Song of Songs (fol. 79):

Leviathan [לויתן, Livyatan]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 42) and the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 279) that Tiferet and the Righteous One, both together, are Leviathan. And the sum of his words is that it is Tiferet; and it has eyes, which are Binah and Chokhmah, and of it it is said (Eccl. 2:14), "the wise man's eyes are in his head"; and its body is the Righteous One; and its scales are Gedulah [and] Gevurah; and its fins Netzach and Hod. And it multiplies in seven seas, from the Great Sea, Binah, which is at its shore, down to the lower sea. And this will show the inclusion of the six extremities in the abundance of bestowal, like fish in the abundance of water. And by this will be understood what is explained in the Gemara (Chullin 66b): "whatever has scales has fins": for when it is included of Gedulah and Gevurah, all the more so it will be of Netzach and Hod, for "two hundred includes a hundred," and whoever has the root has the branch. However, when it has fins, which are Netzach and Hod, it is not compelled that it have scales, which are Gedulah [and] Gevurah. And this is what Rabbi Judah said (there, 59a): "two scales," to hint at the two. Therefore he said "under its jaws," that is, under its head, where Gedulah [and] Gevurah are, as we explained. All this is according to this method, that the fins are Netzach and Hod and the scales are Gedulah [and] Gevurah. But in the Tikkunim, elsewhere, he explained the reverse: that the two scales are Netzach and Hod, the two fins Gedulah [and] Gevurah. And for all this it is possible to say that "under its jaws" is its head, which is Tiferet, and under its head is Netzach and Hod; and that is its scales under its head. "And whatever has scales has fins": for Netzach and Hod are in Gedulah [and] Gevurah, where their bestowal is; for Gedulah bestows in Netzach, Gevurah bestows in Hod; and it is found that in Netzach and Hod Gedulah [and] Gevurah are included; but in Gedulah and Gevurah above there is no effluence of Netzach and Hod, which are below; and therefore whatever has fins has scales. And the explanation of livyatan is the language of union and joining; so he explained in the Zohar (Shemot, fol. 11b), on Levi and Leviathan. But Levi is one union, that is, Da'at, which unites Chokhmah and Binah; but livyatan means two unions, which are Da'at above and Yesod below; and that is Leviathan, which are Tiferet and the Righteous One, as we explained above:

Lulav [לולב, lulav]: most places in Rashbi, peace be upon him, decide and prove that Yesod is the lulav; and your sign: "The righteous one shall flourish like the palm tree" (Ps. 92:13). And possibly because its head reaches to heaven. And some explained it as Tiferet, and its head reaches to the supernal Keter. And it is all one matter, for the intent is by way of the middle line:

Bread [לחם, lechem]: what is usual in the explanation of the Kabbalists on this word is that it is Malkhut; and there is a proof of this: "Call him, that he may eat bread" (Exod. 2:20). However, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 244b) he explained the reverse of this, and these are his words: "Meanwhile, behold the Elder of elders came down to him and said: Faithful Shepherd, retract; for bread is Vav," etc. Thus far his words. And though the saying in its place is long, nevertheless his principal intent is to make known to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, that bread is Vav, in Tiferet, and not as was the opinion of the Faithful Shepherd at first. And here certainly, at first sight, they disagree with one another. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 37b) we found a thing by which we can set it right, somewhat by a strained reading: for there Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Malkhut has three manifestations, and they are cholam, shurek, chirik; and she is called cholam [over] the Vav when she is the diadem of Tiferet from the side of Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And he said there: "And reverse chelem and you will find lechem; and this is 'Man did eat the bread of the mighty' (Ps. 78:25)," etc. And the intent is that Tiferet was united with Malkhut in the secret of "And YHVH God built the rib ... and brought her" (Gen. 2:22), as we explained in the aforementioned gate. And behold, accordingly Malkhut is always bread, and there are in her two manifestations. The first, "the bread of affliction" (Deut. 16:3), to hint at her poverty and her breach; and the second, when she rises above to be cholam over the Vav. And this is what he said in the Ra'aya Meheimna, "bread is Vav," and he explained that her manifestation is the secret of the cholam. And in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 154a), [there is] a third view, and these are his words: "'And you shall make,' etc., 'a table' (Exod. 25:23): this is below, to put on it baked bread. Which is preferable, this or that, bread or table? If you say it is all one, for the table is arranged for that bread; and further, the table is below and the bread on it. It is not so; rather the table is the principal in its arrangement, to receive blessings from above and food for the world; and from the secret of this table food goes out to the world, as it is given into it from above. And that bread is the fruit and the food that goes out from that table, to show that from this table go out fruits and produce and food to the world. If there were no vineyard, the grapes, which are the fruit that go out from it, would not be found; if there were no tree, fruit would not be found in the world. Therefore the table is the principal, and the food that goes out from it is that bread." Thus far his words. And behold, from it it is explained explicitly that the bread is the effluence bestowed on Malkhut, and Malkhut is the vessel that receives it; and from this effluence all the children of the world are fed, and therefore it is called bread. And behold, this is neither according to the one who said that it is Tiferet nor according to the one who said that it is Malkhut. And we can say, with a strained reading, to set this right: that Malkhut, when she is full of effluence and all good, then is called bread, to show that "she went up empty, and YHVH brought her back full." And this is cholam, lechem: the explanation, then, in her receiving above, in the secret of her being the diadem of her husband, she receives the nourishing effluence from Tiferet. And then the bread is male bread, which means the prevailing of the male over the female; and the moon is filled from the light of Chokhmah; and the bread is male bread, the showbread [lechem panim], when she is in bliss from the side of her nourishment from above by means of Yesod; and this effluence is called "royal dainties" (Gen. 49:20); and so it is explained in Parashat Bereshit (fol. 47b). And in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 246a) he explained that this is when Malkhut receives from Binah by means of Yesod; see there. And they explained it further in Parashat Vayetze (fol. 164b), these are his words: "My bread: this is food that comes from above through the arousal from below." Thus far his words. And the intent is that the effluence bestowed on Malkhut from above, from Binah, in the secret of the coupling of Tiferet, through the union of Yesod, in the arousal of Malkhut, is called bread. And now, accordingly, since bread is the title for the effluence bestowed from the attribute, it is not far-fetched that the attribute itself should sometimes be called by the name of that effluence, which it receives or which it bestows; and this is "bread is Vav," etc., and the like found in the Zohar on Vayechi. And when the arousal and the coupling are in the secret of the filling of the moon, the effluence is bestowed in the secret of its fullness, and it is bread of honey [pannag]. And when the female prevails, and Tiferet hastens to come to her place because of the paucity of the arousal of the lower ones, and the union is in the secret of the diminishment of the moon, then the effluence will be "the bread of affliction" from the side of Malkhut. And by this everything is set right. And the Zohar spoke further at length on this matter in Parashat Vayechi mentioned above; and there he explained that of these two kinds of bread it is said (Exod. 16:22), "twice as much bread" [lechem mishneh]. And there is great confusion there on this matter; and by what we have set out, everything is set right:

The showbread [לחם הפנים, lechem ha-panim] is explained as Yesod. And possibly that is the effluence of the two faces, upper and lower, in the secret of the Prince of the Countenance [sar ha-panim], that is, the name  Y A H D V N H Y. And "bread" as we explained above:

Lat [לט, lat, thirty-nine] is an evil husk, the evil strap, with which they lash thirty-nine lashes; and they are forty less one, in the secret of the lack. And from there is Lot, the evil inclination; and they are from the side of "cursed be Canaan" (Gen. 9:25), with whom curses went out; for this is the explanation of lat: letuta [curse]. And this is [the punishment of] one who transgresses on the Sabbath over forty labors less one. And over against them in holiness there are tal [39] lights, dews of blessing; and we explained it in the entry tal:

To Me [לי, li]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the commandment of tefillin (in Parashat Bo, fol. 43b), these are his words: "Li: this is Binah, the secret of the upper world, the inner palace." Thus far his words. And he explained li as "to Myself": that it is not apprehended by the lower ones, that is to say, even by those emanated from it, [which are] the sefirot that are below it. And that is the aspect of Binah that is concealed, united with Chokhmah. And this he intended in the length of his language, "the upper world," which means on the side of the upper world. And he said again, "the inner palace," that is, in the secret of her being an inner palace for the concealed Chokhmah; and this is li, the explanation, "a palace for Me." And for this he called her palace: because Chokhmah is stored away within her. And behold, accordingly, Binah is called li when she is concealed, when she is not apprehended, for she is a palace for Chokhmah, and Chokhmah is concealed within her. And it is possible to say that Lamed is Binah, as is known, and Yod is Chokhmah; and the Yod is concealed within the Lamed, in the secret that the Yod is the brain, and it includes three Yods, as is known; and the three of them are concealed in the Lamed, like this [figure not reproduced]:

Night [ליל לילה, leil, laylah] is Malkhut; and she is so called in the secret of darkness, in the secret of judgment. However, sometimes she is called laylah and sometimes she is called leil. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bo, fol. 38b): "Before she has received the male upon her, she is called leil; when she has received the male upon her, she is called laylah." And the intent is that while she is not yet united with her husband, Tiferet, she is called by the word leil, without Heh, to hint at the strength of her judgment; and she has not yet received compassion, and her husband has not been united with her, and she has not been made a vessel. And when she has received the male, in the secret of compassion, then she is called laylah, with Heh. And so he explained in the Tikkunim, these are his words: "Laylah: this is the lower Shekhinah, included of Heh," etc. And we explained this matter at length in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2. And the verse cries out, "and the night shines as the day" (Ps. 139:12), to hint at "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" (Isa. 30:26). And the commentators explained "and night to night declares knowledge" (Ps. 19:3) [as] two nights, which are Binah and Malkhut; and it is not to the point. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that the left sefirot are called nights; and there is some support for this from the Zohar (Shemot, fol. 11b), and we copied it in the Gate of Palaces, on the matter of Gabriel:

Laish [לישה, laishah]: layish [lion] is in the way of ofer, afrah, asher, asherah: for this one is for the male and that one for the female. And he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 63a), that layish or laishah is in the secret of her nourishment from Gevurah. And sometimes the intent of this title will be the paucity of effluence and her nourishment from judgment; and sometimes that they have no effluence at all, as in the matter of "the old lion [layish] perishes for lack of prey" (Job 4:11), or in the matter of "the lion, which is mightiest among beasts" (Prov. 30:30): for this is mighty, drawing nourishment from the side of Gevurah alone; and this is "perishes," for it has nothing on which to lean. And the judging between these two explanations will be judged according to the context, or by the word that accompanies it. And this explanation is compelled in the saying; and this we arrived at after study and diligence in that saying. And let the inquirer not hasten to object, for the saying there is not according to its plain sense:

To you [לך, lekha]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 79b), that the word lekha is Malkhut, the first level of the Emanation from below to above; and therefore she is revealed and is called lekha, in the second person. And it is possible that she is also so called when she includes the fifty upper gates in her selfhood; and this is the number of lekha [50]. And this matter is compelled from the side that she is so called when she draws nourishment from Binah. And some of the commentators explained that Binah too is called lekha; and our view inclines so; and she is so called in the secret of the fifty gates of Binah; and she is called lekha in the secret of her revealing and her lower aspect, which bestows in the Structure:

The disciples of YHVH [למודי ה', limmudei YHVH] (Isa. 54:13): Netzach and Hod are so called. The reason is that both of them are taught, and are bestowed the learning and the prophecy from Tiferet, which is called YHVH. And it is possible that they are so called when the prophecy is bestowed from Tiferet on the prophets by way of the levels of prophecy, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces:

To the chief musician [למנצח, la-menatze'ach] is in Netzach, according to its sense. And the intent is: the one who makes Netzach prevail over the attribute mentioned after it; as "to the chief musician upon the Sheminith" (Ps. 12:1), which means the one who makes Netzach prevail over the eighth [sheminit], which is Hod; and likewise "to the chief musician upon Ayeleth" (Ps. 22:1), which is Malkhut:

Torches [לפידים, lappidim]: we have already explained in the entry berakim that the lightnings are from the side of Yesod. And in the Zohar, Parashat Va-yishma Yitro (fol. 81b), he wrote, these are his words: "'And the torches' (Exod. 20:15): first lightnings and now torches; all is one. But since they were set right in their tikkunim to be seen, they are so called." Thus far his words. The intent is that the lightnings are their selfhood in their spirituality, when they are in Yesod. However, when they become thick and are revealed below in Malkhut, or in the manifestation of Yesod itself, to be revealed and to be seen, then they are called torches:

Before Me [לפני, lefanai], and likewise lefanai: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 170b), that it is the Shekhinah, who is before the Holy One, blessed be He. And these are his words: "Lefanai: that which stands before, before the Holy One, blessed be He, and serves before Him." Thus far his words. And he explained the Shekhinah, and his intent is clear. And the reason: for lefanai means what is before Tiferet, from below to above, and stands before him; and that is Malkhut. And there he explained that milifnei is in Binah, above Tiferet; and we shall explain it in its entry:

Tongue [לשון, lashon]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is Binah. And she is so called because, just as the tongue brings out the thought of the heart and reveals it outward, so Binah reveals all the inner matters concealed in the first three. And so it is agreed in the mouth of all the Kabbalists. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 250a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Yesod is called "the tongue of the learned" (Isa. 50:4). And when it draws nourishment from Netzach and Hod, when they are "the disciples of YHVH," as we explained in its entry, Yesod is called "the tongue of the learned," because it draws nourishment from the learned ones, which are the lips; and the tongue is in the middle. And Yesod is called "seventy tongues" when it bestows on Malkhut, who is the attribute of seventy; for she is included of seven, and each one of the seven is included of ten: they are seventy; and Yesod, the tongue: they are seventy tongues. And it is possible to say that there are two mouths: the upper mouth and the lower mouth. The upper mouth: Gedulah [and] Gevurah are the lips, and the tongue, Binah, is in the middle, and the voice that goes out from between the two of them is Tiferet, as we explained above in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine." And likewise the lower mouth: Netzach and Hod are the lips, and the tongue Yesod, and the speech Malkhut. And from the upper mouth goes out voice alone, mere sound, without the articulation of words and letters, because of their great subtlety and spirituality; and from the lower mouth speech is revealed in the articulation of the letters. And we have, for these two mouths, faint glimmerings of proof from what we wrote in the entry "a two-edged sword" [cherev pifiyyot]: they are two mouths [piyyot], the two Hehs. And we have further clear proofs, and we shall explain them in the entry peh with the help of the Name. And in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 61a), he explained that Malkhut is called the holy tongue [leshon ha-kodesh] "when the secrets of the Torah go out and are aroused from her." And the principal [point] is that she also receives from the upper holiness, which is Chokhmah; and so they explained there:

The Chamber of Hewn Stone [לשכת הגזית, lishkat ha-gazit]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that "Gevurah is called the Chamber of Hewn Stone because the judgment is cut [chotkhin] in it." Thus far his words. And it seems to me that Malkhut is called so when the upper seventy of the Sanhedrin are gathered into her to cut judgments; she is called gazit [hewn].

And it is further possible to explain that Malkhut is called so because she was hewn from her place, and it was said to her, "Go and diminish yourself." And this is a reason for the judges to judge a judgment of truth in its truth, which is Tiferet, "to join the tent together, that it may be one" (Exod. 26:11). Thus far our poor intellect has reached in the explanation of the entry Lamed. And behold, we are entering, with the divine help, into the explanation of the entry of the letter Mem:

Very [מאד, me'od]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 83), on the verse (Gen. 13:2), "And Abram was very [me'od] rich": "me'od, from the side of the east"; the explanation, from the side of Tiferet, which is what is called east, as is known. And in the Zohar, Parashat Va-yishma Yitro (fol. 68b), he explained that me'od is the side of judgment, the explanation, in Gevurah; and he proved the matter from what they expounded, "me'od: this is Gehinnom." And it is possible to say that Tiferet from the side of Gevurah is called me'od, and its permutation is adam:

Luminary [מאור, ma'or]: there are two luminaries, the great luminary and the small luminary. The great luminary is Tiferet, and it is the sun; and the small luminary is Malkhut, and it is the moon. And the matter of these two luminaries needs explanation, and it is explained in the Gate of the Diminishment, with the help of the Name. However, we found a matter opposed to this in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 138b), these are his words: "The great luminary: this is the inner altar, which is the altar of gold." And it is known that the altar of gold is Binah. And likewise we found in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 8, fol. 22b) words like these, and these are his words: "And at that time, when the building is built through the Holy One, blessed be He, above and below, it is said of the upper and lower Shekhinah, 'And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun' (Isa. 30:26)." Thus far. And at first sight it appears that he said "sun" of Binah. However, when we look well into the language of the Tikkunim, light emerges for us on this matter. And the matter is that the sun is Tiferet, and the moon is Malkhut; and the light of the sun is Binah, and the light of the moon is also from Binah; for the light of the moon and the light of the sun are all one light; but this one draws from Binah herself without an intermediary, and Malkhut draws from her by means of an intermediary, which is the sun, between the moon and the light that comes to her. And in this the verse said that when the union is true and complete, and the diadem returns to its former state, to be the diadem of her husband, then the bestowal of Malkhut from Binah will be equal to Tiferet. And so the moon, which is Malkhut, and her light, bestowed on her from Binah, will be bestowed on her not by means of the intermediary, like the sun, which is Tiferet, which receives its light and its bestowal from Binah herself, not by means of the intermediary. And this is the intent of Rashbi in the Tikkunim, where he said "of the upper Shekhinah," etc.: for the intent is the lights, which are the bestowals that are drawn from Binah. And this is also the intent of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Terumah, in saying "the great luminary: this is the inner altar": the explanation, the luminary, that is, a title for the light that shines in Tiferet itself; and this luminary is bestowed from Binah. And so the verse was precise, that it did not say "and the moon shall be as the sun," but "the light of the moon as the light of the sun." This is what appears to us in setting right these sayings and settling them with the preceding premise, agreed in many places of the Zohar, that the great luminary is Tiferet, which is certainly called the sun, as we explained above:

Food [מאכל, ma'akhal]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 240a), that the effluence that Yesod bestows on Malkhut is called ma'akhal. And this matter is explained in the verse (Judg. 14:14), "Out of the eater came forth food": for the eater is Yesod, as we explained in its entry, and the food is the effluence that is bestowed:

Me'erat [מארת, me'erat, lights, written defectively] without Vav: Rashbi, peace be upon him, gave two explanations in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 44, fol. 80a), and these are his words: "What is me'orot? This is the Oral Torah. Although they established that me'orot, defective, is Lilith, the Torah has seventy faces." Thus far his words. The intent is that Malkhut is female, and therefore she is called me'orot, the language of light, and the Tav is a title for the female. And she is so called when she shines, but "the man is not at home" (Prov. 7:19), for she lacks the Vav. And when we explain it of Lilith, its explanation is from the language of me'erah [curse], as "the curse of YHVH is in the house of the wicked" (Prov. 3:33); and she is the wicked Lilith, the side of the left. And it is already known that this depends on that; and it will be explained in the Gate of Substitutes, with the help of the Name:

The spring of uprightness [מבוע היושר, mabbu'a ha-yosher]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Keter is so called "because it makes straight the paths of Chokhmah on the middle line, in a straight way." Thus far his words. And it seems to me that it is possible that it is so called when it bestows on Tiferet, which is called yashar, as we explained in its entry. And it is possible that both this and that are so:

Tower [מגדל, migdal]: this name is in two places: the first in Malkhut, and the second in Binah. And the reason is that she is like the tower built in a place higher than the whole building. And sometimes she is called a tower flying in the air; and the explanation is that she flies and screens with her wings over Tiferet, which is called avir [air], as we explained in its entry. And when she watches over the air in particular and is raised in this, then she is called "a tower flying in the air." And when her seat is on the high mountains, then she is called "tower" without qualification. And Malkhut is called "tower" for the same reason: for she is head of all that is from her downward, as is known; for she is the end of the Emanation and the head of all the created ones; not that she is created, God forbid, but she is head of them all, and all of them were created by her power. And Malkhut is called a tower of strength [migdal oz] (Prov. 18:10) when the strength is within the tower, as is known (from the Zohar, Shelach, fol. 164b). And it is already known that the name "tower" is a title showing also the keeping of the things that are within it, as in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory: "a chest, a box and a tower [cupboard]." And likewise she is called the tower of David (Song 4:4); and they explained it in the Zohar, in Parashat Vayigash (fol. 209b). And sometimes Keter is called "a tower flying in the air," for the reason that it flies and covers over Chokhmah and Binah, both of which together are called avir, which is explained as or [with] Yod, as we spoke at length in the entry avir, with the help of Heaven:

Shield [מגן, magen] is Malkhut; and she is so called when she draws nourishment from the three Patriarchs and bestows on the three camps whose heads are Michael, Gabriel, Nuriel, the initials MaGaN. This is what appears at first sight, and so the commentators explained. However, in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 3), it appears that the shield is the covenant; and he proved the matter from the verse (Ps. 84:12), "For YHVH God is a sun and a shield":

Strife [מדון, madon]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 16), on the verse (Prov. 16:28), "A man of perversity sows strife," that it is the bestowal of judgment sent into all the sefirot by the power of the man of perversity; for he is the one who arouses the power of judgment:

Midian [מדין, Midyan] [as in "the priest of Midian"] is the side of the left, as "a contentious [midyanim] woman" (Prov. 27:15); so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (fol. 68a). And there he explained that "the priest of On" and "the priest of Midian" are both equal, and all is one thing:

Understanding [מדע, madda] is Binah; and she is so called in her aspect in which she is the source of Da'at. And this is their saying, of blessed memory: "if there is no Binah, there is no Da'at." And the madda is the substance in act; for Da'at reveals what is in the madda; and for this reason, "if there is no Da'at, there is no Binah":

The attribute of day and the attribute of night [מדת יום ומדת לילה, middat yom u-middat lailah]: they are Tiferet, day, and Malkhut, the attribute of night. And the day and the night each have twelve seasonal hours, and their hours depend on the twelve boundaries, as we explained at length in the Gate of the Fifty Gates. And some explained that Netzach is the attribute of day and Hod the attribute of night. And possibly it is all one, for Malkhut is toward the left and Tiferet toward the right, as we explained in the Gate of Names:

The harsh and the soft attribute of judgment [מדת הדין הקשה והרפה, middat ha-din ha-kashah ve-ha-rafah]: they are Gevurah, harsh, and Malkhut, soft. And both of them are attributes of judgment, for they are two courts in which the world is judged. And these incline toward the side of judgment: Gevurah by its nature; and Malkhut soft, when she draws nourishment from the strength of Gevurah. And some divided the attributes into two parts: Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah, to govern the upper spiritual ones; and therefore it is the harsh Gevurah, according to the measure of the upper ones. And five natural ones, to govern the lower ones; and they are Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And Malkhut is the last Gevurah, soft judgment, to govern the lower ones; just as Gevurah is the last of the five upper ones. And this does not settle for us; for all seven sefirot are to govern the upper ones and the lower ones, each according to its measure, as we explained in the preceding gates:

What is his name, and what is his son's name [מה שמו ומה שם בנו, mah shemo u-mah shem beno] (Prov. 30:4): the intent is that Chokhmah is called mah, and Tiferet too is called mah. And the reason is that the four-letter name in its filling, Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Alef, comes to mah [45]. And the hint at this name is in Chokhmah, when ten sefirot shine in it; and therefore its name is included in ten letters and is called mah; and that is the mah that is in Chokhmah; and that is "what [mah] is his name." And likewise when Tiferet includes ten sefirot, the number of its ten letters, then it is called mah like Chokhmah itself; and this is "and what is his son's name." And that is: mah, which is Chokhmah, is called father, and his son is Tiferet. And there is, at first sight, something opposed to this in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 69, fol. 106a), and these are his words: "And the secret of the matter here: 'What is his name,' etc. 'What is his name': in the supernal Mother, where Chokhmah is; 'and what is his son's name': in the lower Mother it is known." Thus far his words. And when we look closely we find it according to these words of ours. For he intended to explain the word shemo [his name] and the word shem [name]. And the intent is that mah is in Chokhmah and is revealed in Binah; and this is his saying, "where Chokhmah is"; and if so, "his name" is Binah, for she is a name for Chokhmah, as we explained in the preceding gates. And likewise Tiferet is revealed by means of Malkhut; and this is "and what is his son's name, if you know": that is to say, the knowledge of these two things, which are Chokhmah and Tiferet, is in Binah and Malkhut. And this is what he said, "in the lower Mother it is known": the explanation, the knowledge of Tiferet in Malkhut. And in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 127a), Rabbi Judah explained, these are his words: "The lower level, which is the secret of the lower world, is called mah. And we have learned: do not read mah but me'ah [a hundred]; because all the lower levels in their completeness are here," etc. Thus far. The explanation: mah is a title for Malkhut in her lower aspect; and this is what he meant in saying "the lower level," which is Malkhut and her lower aspect, "which is the secret of the lower world," the explanation, in the secret of her lower aspect. And he needed all this because mah is explained, "do not read mah but me'ah," which is the secret of ten times ten; and if it were not in her lower aspect, there would be only nine times ten, which are ninety. However, now that we say that it is in her lower aspect, Malkhut in her upper aspect is found to complete the number too. Further, he said there: "Further, why is it called mah? Rather, although the upper drawing is drawn, it is not revealed until it is completed here, which is the place of the end of all the levels, the end of the drawing out of all; and it stands in revealing. And although it is revealed more than all, it stands to be asked: What [mah] have you seen? What have you known? As it is said, 'for you saw no manner of form' (Deut. 4:15)." Thus far his words. He added to give a reason why they did not come in the completeness of the hundred, since the intent in mah is a hundred, as he said, "do not read mah but me'ah"; to this he said, "Further," etc.: the explanation, an addition of explanation to what was expounded: for this level is the end of all the levels; and not only the end, but the end of the end, which is the end of the upper drawing, which is her lower aspect, as we explained above. And this he intended in saying "the end of all the levels"; and afterward he said, "the end of the drawing out of all," to hint at the last aspect, as we explained. And before this he said, "although the upper drawing," etc.: the explanation, although the drawing and the effluence are drawn included from above, it is not completed to the number of the hundred until the lower level, as we explained above. And because it is not completed, it is not revealed, to be seen in her aspect, until this aspect. And he gave the reason for this, "for it is the end," etc., as we explained above. And then, in the last aspect, it stands to be revealed, because it is completed in the number of the hundred. And although it is revealed, it stands in question, to show that there is no understanding there even in the aspect of revealing. And this is why this matter came in the name mah and not me'ah, as he said, "What have you seen?" etc. And by this is settled the intent of mah, which is a hundred lacking an Alef: to show that even in the aspect of a hundred the question "what?" still belongs. Thus far the explanation of the saying. And by this good sense and knowledge emerge for us why Malkhut is called me'ah: it is her revealed aspect, and she is included of ten days, as we explained. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 28a) he explained that Malkhut is called mah from the side of Chokhmah, to show the concealment of the concealed Emanator. And at first sight it is understood that he disagrees with this. And according to what we explained in the Gate of Names, they do not disagree; for there are two kinds of mah: either mah as we explained in Malkhut above, that is, me'ah; or mah as we explained in Chokhmah, which is explained as the filling of the Name, the face of a man. And that mah that is in Chokhmah is many and many times more praiseworthy. And the mah that is in Malkhut is called mah from the side of Chokhmah: that is, mah in that mah that is in Chokhmah, which is explained as the four-letter name in its filling, as we explained above of the mah in Chokhmah. And this resolution is proved there in the Tikkunim, for there we are dealing with the name mah, Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Alef, in Malkhut:

Brain [מוח, mo'ach] is in Chokhmah; and the covering of the brain, which is the cranium, is Keter, which is over the head; and therefore the hairs hint at worlds emanated from Keter. And the brain, which is Chokhmah in general, is divided into three parts, which are Chokhmah, Binah, Da'at, which are three powers in the brain; and that is three Yods. And the brain is cold, from the side of the waters of compassion; for Chokhmah bestows compassion on Binah. And therefore the brain is sometimes a title for Chesed. And it has already been explained that from Chokhmah the thirty-two paths are bestowed; and likewise from the brain thirty-two nerves are drawn, according to the view of the anatomists. And the principle that emerges is that when Chokhmah includes within it these three powers, it is called brain, and they are simple compassion. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 127a) he explained that the brain is Chokhmah when it is in Keter, which is the head; and these are his words: "And what is the brain? This is the supernal Chokhmah, enclosed in the Keter of the head, which is the supernal Keter." Thus far his words. And when these three powers are bestowed in the head of Ze'ir Anpin, they become a brain there too, in its likeness; and with Malkhut, their totality is the four-letter name; for Da'at is the Vav, and the rest are well known. And all this Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. However, the later Kabbalists called Keter "the enclosed brain." And likewise Rashbi, peace be upon him, titles all of them by the name brain, in saying, "this one is husk to that one, and that one brain [kernel] to this one." And the reason is that, just as the brain is covered in the head, so each one is concealed in its fellow; and likewise the lower is husk to the upper, to cover it and to conceal it. And there is one who explained that the brain is the fifty gates of Binah, one of the three parts of the brain; and it settles somewhat:

Pole [מוט, mot]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that Tiferet with Yesod is called mot. And it is already known that the forty-nine [Mem-Tet] letters that are in the reading of the Shema and in "Blessed be the name," etc., are Tiferet and Yesod; and it is explained in the Gate of the Fifty Gates. And they are six words in each verse, which are Vav-Vav; and that is the Vav, in its filling, that is between the Mem and the Tet. All this is hinted at in mot. And the principle that emerges is that it is a hint at Tiferet and Yesod when they are included of fifty gates and six extremities, each and every one (and see the Zohar, Mishpatim, fol. 115a):

The foundations of the earth [מוסדי ארץ, mosdei aretz] (Micah 6:2): he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 45a): "the foundations of the earth: Tzaddik and Tzedek." And possibly mosdei is the language of yesod, and aretz Malkhut:

Additional [מוסף, musaf]: Yesod is called so; so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 32, and Tikkun 21, fol. 44b). And the reason is that on it all addition depends: as the additional offering, an addition; and the receiving of the addition of the Sabbath; and the additional soul. And all these matters are called musaf in the secret of the holiness that is added in it; that is, the matter of the union, in which Tiferet and Malkhut are united; and then it rises through it above, and she is called holiness; and then it adds an addition of holiness:

Appointed time [מועד, mo'ed]: in Parashat Vayetze (fol. 164b) he explained that the union of Chesed and Gevurah, which are two appointed times, the appointed time of the morning and the appointed time of the evening, the morning of Abraham and the evening of Isaac, when they are included, fire in water and water in fire, both together are called mo'ed, in the singular. And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 111a) he explained that the six extremities are called mo'adim. But the first three, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, are called "the appointed times of YHVH"; and the second three are called "these are My appointed times," as it is written (Lev. 23:2), "these are [hem] My appointed times," which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, the appointed times of Malkhut. And reverse hem and mah is found, which is Malkhut. And elsewhere he explained that "their appointed time" is Binah; and this is "which you shall proclaim in their appointed time" (Lev. 23:4). Wondrous [מופלא, mufla] is Keter; and it is called mufla from the language of concealment, for it is exalted and wondrous beyond every thought. And every term of wonder depends on this:

Myrrh [מור, mor]: on this word Rashbi, peace be upon him, gave two explanations. In the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 117), on the verse (Song 3:6), "perfumed with myrrh and frankincense," he explained that it is Keter. And on the verse (Song 5:1), "I have gathered my myrrh [mori]," he explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Vayikra, fol. 3b) that it is Chesed. And it seems to me to distinguish: that in "perfumed with myrrh," mor is [written] defectively, without Vav, and it is explained as Keter, from the language of mar [lord], for it is lord over the whole Emanation; and the word mori, and all the others that are full, are in Chesed. And the intent is that, just as myrrh is the head of all the spices, so Chesed is the head of the whole Structure. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 44) he explained myrrh as in Chesed or in Netzach (and in the Zohar Chadash, Parashat Chukkat, he explained: myrrh, this is Abraham):

Savior [מושיע, moshi'a]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 279a) that Tiferet is called savior, for the reason that it is what saves the Shekhinah from the exile, speedily in our days; and therefore it is called savior. And it is possible that it is called savior from the side of Chesed, where salvation is, by the power of Binah; for from there is the drawing of salvation and freedom. Ruler [מושל, moshel]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Tiferet from the side of Yesod is called ruler. And likewise it is said of Joseph the righteous (Gen. 45:26), "and he is ruler," from the side of Yesod:

Death [מות, mavet]: Rashbi explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (in the Midrash ha-Ne'lam, fol. 148a), that it is the female husk, which receives from the male; she is called "the strange woman," and she is called death:

Altar [מזבח, mizbe'ach]: there are two altars, inner and outer. The inner is Binah, where the gold is and where the incense is; for she binds all the sefirot and joins them. And the outer, of bronze, is Malkhut. And the reason is found in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 139), and these are his words: "In the book of Solomon, peace be upon him: within this altar of bronze that we spoke of there are supernal secrets; for 'an altar of earth' is written, 'An altar of earth you shall make for Me' (Exod. 20:21); and this is the secret as is fitting. Bronze [nechoshet]: when other mountains rule, and she needs to feed them, she is colored with this color to feed them; and they are called mountains of bronze. And from those mountains of bronze one spirit is drawn out from within this altar. And when this altar withdraws in another withdrawal, then the letter Nun withdraws, which is the holy altar; and the spirit of those mountains of bronze remains. And when that spirit withdraws in its existence, it is called tachash, for the letter Nun has withdrawn from it [nechoshet less Nun]. And this is divided into many other spirits, and they too are called tachash. And therefore that (one) people is called Tahash, as it is said, 'and Tahash, and Maacah' (Gen. 22:24)." Thus far his words; and it is clear. And what he said, "and she needs to feed them": the intent is that she gives food and life to all, to the right of holiness and to the side of the left. And because it is not fitting to give them the holy food, she gives them from the lees of the wine and from the turbid, as they are in their impure bread. And therefore she is then called bronze, to show the matter of the tachash that is near her; and the Nun hints at Malkhut herself. And it is known that the altar that hints at Malkhut was "hollow with boards" (Exod. 27:8), and they filled it with earth [adamah]; and adamah is derived from adam, who is her husband; and around her is the husk of bronze. And until King Solomon, peace be upon him, came, it was an altar of bronze, for the reason that the moon was in her lack, and there was not a true coupling, as is known. And when the Temple below was built, the Temple above was built, and the moon was in her fullness; and the altar was entirely of earth, to show her whiteness; and the husk of tachash had already separated from her. And it was whitened, in the secret of the whiteness, to show that the days of whitening had already passed, and she had been purified of the blood, and stands white in whiteness. And this is the difference between the altar of earth and the altar of bronze. And the altar is sometimes called the altar of God [Elohim], in the secret of the nourishment of Malkhut from Gevurah. And when she draws nourishment from the middle line, her husband, she is called the altar of YHVH; so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 24b). And when Malkhut is called altar, it hints at her sitting on twelve oxen, twelve tribes, which are the tikkunim of the altar; and the altar of Elijah (1 Kings 18:31) will prove it. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Beha'alotekha (fol. 151b, the matter of the two altars):
Mezuzah [מזוזה, mezuzah]: he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 257), these are his words: "The Shekhinah is called mezuzah from the side of the central pillar, of the letters of YHVH":

Doorposts [מזוזות, mezuzot]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, fol. 64b) that they are Netzach and Hod, which are doorposts for Malkhut, who is called house; and that is "the doorposts of your house" (Deut. 6:9):

Food [מזון, mazon]: they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 168b), that Chesed is called mazon. And these are his words: "'For the land and for the food': this is the cleaving in Chesed. 'For the land': this is the land of the living; 'and for the food': this is Chesed; included this in that in one cleaving." Thus far his words. And he explained "the land of the living" in this [place] as Malkhut, for so he explained explicitly above the matter. And the intent is that through the Grace after Meals [birkat ha-mazon] Malkhut is united with Chesed; for so the cup is in the right; and so he explained there explicitly. And it is possible that Chesed is called mazon from the side that food depends on it, as we explained in the entry tov. And Chesed is called mazon when it bestows food below, in the way of tov and Chesed that we explained in the entry tov:

Mazal [מזל, mazal]: Keter is called mazal. And the reason is that it is what bestows and makes flow [mazil] and pours down showers on all the sefirot; and as the mazal is above the whole Emanation. However, it is called mazal from the side of its aspect that is revealed and bestows on all of them:

Psalm [מזמור, mizmor]: on this word Rashbi, peace be upon him, gave two explanations: the one of Malkhut and the second of Chesed. And it is possible that Malkhut is so called from the side of Chesed, for the thread of Chesed is drawn over her; and so he explained elsewhere. And in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 140a): "Mizmor: this is the holy spirit. Why is it so called? Because she ever praises the supernal King of all." Thus far his words. And the explanation: mizmor is Malkhut, who is called the holy spirit; and she ever praises Binah, to rise to her and to be equal to her, as is proved in the Zohar on the Song of Songs, on the first verse. And it is possible that this praise is by means of Chesed:

East [מזרח, mizrach]: the explanations of it are many. There is one who explained it as Chokhmah, and so he explained in the Zohar. And in Parashat Vayetze he explained that Binah is so called. And there are places in the Zohar where he explained that it is in Tiferet. And all this is one matter, as we shall explain with the help of the Name. And what is agreed in the Zohar, in Parashat Bemidbar (fol. 120a), is that the east is in Chokhmah. And we have already explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 4, that the east is in Chokhmah and in Tiferet; for Tiferet shines by the power of the east, which is Chokhmah; and there we spoke at length. And likewise the east in Binah will settle. And the reason is that the rising [zerichah] of the sun, which is Tiferet, its light is from the side of Chokhmah and Binah; and therefore, in the secret of the rising, which is the shining light of the sun, "east" can properly be said of Chokhmah and Binah, since they are the light and the rising of the sun:

Vision [מחזה, machazeh]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 91a), that Malkhut alone, without the joining of any sefirah to the prophecy, is called "in a vision" (Gen. 15:1). And we spoke at length in the entry chozeh:

The half shekel [מחצית השקל, machatzit ha-shekel]: it is known that "the shekel is twenty gerahs," which is the measure of two Yods, with the Vav, Tiferet, in the middle. And therefore it is called "the half shekel," to show that it is in the middle of the two Yods, which are a shekel. And your sign: Alef, a Yod at the head, a Yod at the end, a Vav in the middle. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained; and we copied his language and explained it in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine." And in the Ra'aya Meheimna, elsewhere (Terumah, fol. 158a), he explained that Malkhut too, when she rises to Tiferet in the secret of Vav-shurek, is called the half shekel:

Thought [מחשבה, machashavah]: the word machashavah is explained in many places. The Ein Sof is called Thought; and the supernal Keter, and Chokhmah and Binah; and Malkhut is also called Thought; and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained all of them. And these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 40a): "Rabbi Eleazar said to him: Father, but how many thoughts are there? The lower Shekhinah is called Thought, and the supernal Chokhmah is called Thought," etc., "and above all of them is a Thought above which there is none, and it is the closed of all the closed, the supernal of all the supernal." Thus far his words. He taught explicitly that Malkhut is called Thought, and likewise Chokhmah, and likewise the supernal Keter, and likewise the Ein Sof. And of Binah it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 229b), these are his words: "'Israel arose in Thought': reflection [hirhur] is Chokhmah, for the wise one, by hint; Chokhmah arose in Thought, which is Binah. Thought and reflection are all one: Chokhmah, which is known only in Binah, and Binah in the heart [lev, 32]. And therefore thought in the heart, reflection in the heart." Thus far his words. Behold, he said explicitly that reflection, which is not so much as thought, is hinted at in Chokhmah; and thought is hinted at in Binah, which is more revealed than reflection. And now we shall explain the reason for these titles. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in Sefer ha-Shem that Thought is in the supernal Keter and in Chokhmah, and these are his words: "In the supernal Keter, thought, but no apprehension at all from its side; and thought necessarily precedes all wisdom and understanding, and one must not think about it at all. And Chokhmah too is called Thought, for it is apprehended only in thought. Therefore in Keter and in Chokhmah is thought, in which is the beginning of thought and contemplation, but in small measure. And of both of them it is said (Ps. 92:6), 'Your thoughts are very deep': for through thinking on Chokhmah one comes to think on the supernal Keter, by estimation." Thus far his words. And what seems to me: we have already explained in the Gate of ABYA the matter of the levels, one above the other; so is the matter of thought. For Malkhut, with respect to the lower ones that are below her, is called thought, for she is subtle in the utmost subtlety, like the subtle thought. And accordingly, all the more so is "thought" right for the whole Emanation in its totality; as the commentators called the whole Emanation "a point of thought," to show the subtlety; and there is nothing in the corporeal more than thought with which to compare it; besides that they related it [to] "a point of thought" because it has no extremes at all. And therefore our saying "thought" of Binah is right; that is to say, she is thought with respect to the seven sefirot below her; and the lower sefirot are an act revealed with respect to her, who is the subtle thought; and the Structure is the Structure revealed in substance with respect to the concealed Binah. And likewise Binah is what reveals Chokhmah; therefore she is called coarse thought and Chokhmah subtle thought; and the supernal Keter is subtler than both of them; for this one is subtler than that one, and that one subtler than this one. And the whole Emanation is called an act in substance relative to the spiritual Thought, the Emanator, the King of the kings of kings. And to understand well the content of this matter one must look into the Gate of ABYA. And besides this I explained a great matter in the Gate of Names:

Laying bare the white [מחשוף הלבן, machsof ha-lavan] (Gen. 30:37): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that the supernal Keter is so called for the reason that from it the white is revealed and makes all the faces shine. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 161b), he explained that Tiferet, when it makes the side of Chesed prevail over judgment, is called machsof ha-lavan: the explanation, it reveals the whiteness and makes it prevail over judgment:

Bed [מטה, mittah] is Malkhut; and she is called mittah in her manifestation below, in her place. And she is so called because on her is the intimacy of a man and his wife, Tiferet and Malkhut, in the manifestation that is united with her husband; and the bed is the manifestation that remains in her place. And of her our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot 5b): "one who places his bed between north and south": which are Chesed and Gevurah, through which is the coupling, as we explained in the preceding gates. And behold, this bed, which is Solomon's, "the King to whom peace belongs," has "sixty mighty men" (Song 3:7), which are "sixty lashes of fire," which are from the power of Gevurah; and they are to guard the bed, that nothing unfit draw near to it, God forbid. "And they are of the mighty men of Israel": they are there by the power of Israel, Tiferet; Solomon from the side of Gevurah (see Acharei, fol. 60a):

Inclining toward Chesed [מטה כלפי חסד, matteh kelappei chesed]: Tiferet is called so, for the reason that it is Vav, included of six extremities; and then it is called matteh [staff]. And because its way is to tip toward compassion and Chesed, it is called "inclining [matteh] toward Chesed." And sometimes it is called "inclining toward judgment," according to the deeds of human beings, whether good or, God forbid, bad. And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 112b) he explained that Binah is called "the staff of God [Elohim]" (Exod. 4:20) from the side of Gevurah; and he explained matteh: Mem-Tet is forty-nine gates, and the Heh is the first Heh of the Name, which is the gate of compassion; and she is called Elohim from the side of her inclining toward judgment. We find ourselves saying that when she is included of fifty days and inclines toward judgment, she is called "the staff of God":

Target [מטרה, mattarah]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, fol. 28a) that Malkhut is called mattarah, for she is ready like a target for the arrow, that is, Yesod, the seed that shoots like an arrow. And he further explained there that she is called mattarah in the secret of the pupil of the eye, which is the manifestation of the Yod. And it is possible that it is also the language of netorah, the language of guarding, because she is shut and enclosed in the secret of the Yod within the Heh:

The Lady [מטרוניתא, Matronita]: Beriah, which is the Throne explained in the Gate of ABYA, is called the Lady, for she guards the garden. And sometimes Malkhut of Atzilut too is called the Lady, which means mistress; and Beriah is the handmaid, the maidservant. And we spoke at length in the Gate of ABYA:

Metatron [מטטרון, metatron]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in Sefer ha-Shem that Malkhut is called Metatron; and in the mouth of most commentators it is so. And it seems to me that the Shekhinah is called Mitatron, with Yod, specifically; and then it shows the concealment of the Shekhinah in the bird's nest, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA. And Metatron without Yod is the angel, the messenger of the Shekhinah, as he is also called Youth [na'ar]. And what they said, that his name is like the name of his Master: the intent is that it comes to [the number of] Shaddai [314]. And further they explained that he has seventy names, as the Holy One, blessed be He, has seventy names; and they come explained in the practical Kabbalah in many places; and we do not wish to copy them, for there is no benefit in knowing them for the [present] studies. And what the verse said (Exod. 23:21), "for My name is in him": the intent is the Shekhinah concealed within him, as in the matter of Mitatron:

Mi [מי, mi, Who]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Bereshit, fol. 1b) that this name is in Binah, and it shows that she is concealed, for the language of question, "Who is she?" etc., is right of her. And she is called Mi when she is included of seven Sabbatical cycles in the totality of the Jubilee year, which comes to the number of mi [50]. And the rest of this title we explained in the Gate of Names. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that the word mi is derived from the language of mayim [water]; and possibly his intent is mei [waters of], with tzeirei, although the beginning of his word is mi with chirik:

Waters [מים, mayim]: according to the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him, the waters are in Chesed; but it is the side that draws near to Gevurah that is water. And they explained this matter in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 167a), on the matter of "light, water, firmament." And for this it is found that the waters are mentioned on the second day. And on the matter of the upper waters and the lower waters, the explanations are many. There is one who explained that Chesed is the lower waters and Chokhmah the upper waters, and the firmament that divides between them is Binah. So Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in the entry Mi, on the sefirah of Binah, and these are his words: "From Binah are the issues of the lower waters; and the upper ones are the upper waters that depend on the Utterance. And she is the firmament that divides between water and water, Chokhmah and Chesed; and the verse shows this, in the manner of the Utterances: she is the drop that congealed; and they are the waters that are above the heavens. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: the upper waters are male, the lower waters female. And most of the Kabbalists said that the first five sefirot are the upper waters and the five lower ones are the lower waters, in this way: Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And it does not settle well for several reasons; and whoever is precise in the depth of the Kabbalah will understand of himself; and behold, they are seven of the totality of the Structure. And the clouds of glory are the lower waters, which swell and open their mouths to receive the upper waters; and they are perforated like a sieve, to pour out on the earth. And there is one who says that Malkhut alone is the lower waters; and it does not appear so; for he said that four parts are male and the fifth female; and the totality of the waters is seven in the passage of Bereshit, and five times 'water' in the passage 'Let there be a firmament.'" Thus far the words of Rabbi Moshe [de León] in the place mentioned. And to bring the matter mentioned out to light, we wish to explain all these things. The five times "water" are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, five faces of Gedulah; and therefore they are called water by its name. And in five the whole Structure is included, for Yesod and Malkhut are included with Tiferet. And some say seven times "water," two more times mentioned afterward in the passage; and it is the spreading out of Tiferet, which is Yesod and Malkhut; and they complete the number. However, "the waters that are above the firmament" and "the waters that are under the firmament" are another matter; and that is the words of Rabbi Akiva to his disciples, "When you reach the stones of pure marble," etc. And this saying Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 40, fol. 78), these are his words: "The Elder of elders, the Ancient of ancients, rose and said: Rabbi, Rabbi, what is it that Rabbi Akiva said to his disciples, 'When you reach the stones of pure marble, do not say, Water, water, lest you endanger yourselves; as it is written, He who speaks falsehood shall not be established before My eyes' (Ps. 101:7)? But it is written, 'Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between water and water' (Gen. 1:6).

"And further, there are upper waters and lower waters there; why did he say, 'do not say, Water, water'? The holy Lamp said to him: Elder of elders, it is fitting for you to reveal this secret, for the companions cannot stand on it in its clarity. The Elder of elders said to him: Rabbi, Rabbi, holy Lamp: certainly the stones of pure marble are Yod, Yod, which are one: the upper Yod of Alef and the second, the lower Yod of Alef. And here there is no impurity, but stones of pure marble; and there is no separation between water and water, for all is one union; for these are from the side of the Tree of Life, which is the Vav in the middle, of which it is said, 'and take also of the Tree of Life,' etc. (Gen. 3:22). But the tree of the Tree of Knowledge," etc. Thus far his words, as relevant to our matter. And the explanation: the explanation of the words of Rabbi Akiva is that they should not say there are two kinds of water, which is not true, and they would be found separating. And this is "do not say, Water, water": its matter is that they should not say two kinds of water, lest they endanger [themselves] because of the iniquity of separation. And to this the Elder asked two questions, which are true. "But it is written, 'Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide,'" etc.: so they are two kinds of water, and there is division between them; it appears that it is permitted to say two kinds of water; for harder than this the Torah said, "and let it divide between water and water," a literal division. Further, the Elder objected that, according to the truth, there are two kinds: waters above the heavens and waters under the heavens; and if so, why did he say "do not say, Water, water, lest you endanger," etc.? On the contrary, it is permitted to say two kinds of water, for it is no worse than the language of the verse.

And further, the manifestations themselves, as we explained. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, did not wish to explain the matter, so that the companions should hear the things from the mouth of the concealed Elder. And the Elder explained: "The stones of marble are Yod, Yod": its matter is as he explained in the Gate of Manifestations, on the matter of a Yod at the head and a Yod at the end, in the secret of "I am the first and I am the last." For the first Yod is in Chokhmah, and the second Yod is in Malkhut, in the aspect of Chokhmah, in the secret of the light that reverses from below to above. And the upper Yod is the Yod of the four-letter name, and the lower Yod is the Yod of Adonai, coming from below to above. And these are the female waters, and those are the male waters. And they are called female, for she receives from below, from the doing of the commandments; and through it she bestows upward and makes the light shine, and clothes the light that comes, as in the matter of a palace; and the light that comes is a king in his palace. And these are the inner keys and the outer keys: for the inner is the light that comes, certainly YHVH, which is the light that comes by way of the direct line; and the outer is a garment, in the secret of the returning light. And this is the matter that is said of the sefirot, from below to above and from above to below, as we explained in the Gate From Below to Above. And this is a Yod above the Alef and a Yod below. And this is the secret of  Y A H D V N H Y, which is a Yod at the head and a Yod at the end, as explained at length in the aforementioned gate. And these are the two Yods that are called stones of pure marble. And they are called stones: the explanation, every Yod is called stone for the reason that it is rounded like a stone. And it is called marble [shayish], because marble is white, and the white shows compassion, like the water. And because these two Yods are compassion, as they are water, in the secret of the waters of Chesed, he titled them by the name marble, since he was compelled to call them by the name stone, as we explained. Further, we can say by way of permutation that Chokhmah is called yesh [Something], and the lower Chokhmah, in reverse, is called shai [Shin-Yod]; the composition of both of them is shayish: that is to say, Yod, Chokhmah, is the source; and Shin is the Emanation in its branches, that is, the three Patriarchs and the three of Netzach [Netzach, Hod, Yesod], and Malkhut, which is the totality; and the totality is Binah; and the Yod at the head is the source from which these two were emanated. And Malkhut is called shai, in the secret of the light that reverses. And when these two words, which show the two lights, are composed, it will be called shai yesh; and the two Yods are united, and it is shayish. And the reason for saying "pure" is that there are many kinds of water, and one of them is the water of the menstruant; and therefore division and separation is said of them, as we shall explain with the help of the Name. And these waters of the three marbles are pure, all of them purity and Emanation. "Yod, Yod, which are one: the upper Yod of Alef," etc.: we have already explained above that in the name  Y A H D V N H Y  are included Chokhmah at the head and Chokhmah at the end, and six letters in the middle, a hint at the Vav, Tiferet, in its six extremities. And by its being placed in the middle of the two of them, they are united; the explanation, through it the daughter can rise to her father's house as in her youth. And for this reason he said: do not say that these two stones are separate and divided one from another, God forbid, which is not true; but on the contrary, the firmament placed between the two of them, which is Tiferet, is what unites them, and through it they are joined; for there is division only in the place of impurity, as it is written, "to divide between the impure and the pure" (Lev. 11:47). However, in the place of the pure, which is the stones of pure marble, "do not say, Water, water." And this is the saying of the Elder: "And here there is no impurity," etc., "for these are from the side of life," etc. These waters are in the Emanation, and therefore there is no division in them; and of them it is said, "the waters above the heavens" and "the waters under the heavens"; and the heavens is the Vav placed between them; and on the contrary, the firmament, which is the Vav, unites them. And by this one question that he objected is resolved. And the second question, which is that the verse said "and let it divide": this is said on the side of Gevurah, between the side of the pure and the side of the impure, between the pure gold and the dross of the gold; and there division is mentioned between pure, clear and limpid waters and impure, turbid waters, "the bitter waters that cause the curse" (Num. 5:18). And this he intended in saying "but the tree of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil": which is the place in which good is holiness and evil is impurity; as they said, of blessed memory, elsewhere, "good, this is Metatron; and evil, this is Samael": there is division between water and water. Thus far the explanation of the saying; and from within it the matter of the upper waters and the lower waters is explained:

The upper waters [מים העליונים, ha-mayim ha-elyonim]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Chesed is the upper waters, although there are ones higher than they, and they are the waters of Chokhmah; and we have already explained above on this. Further, he said that Chesed is called water from spirit, and he said that so it is written in Sefer Yetzirah; however, I explained that mishnah in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter. Further, he said that Chesed is called holy waters; and they are pure waters from the side of Chesed; and they are living waters. And on the outer side, in the husk, are impure waters, proud waters, evil waters, "the bitter waters that cause the curse," the waters of the Flood; and that is the division that is said of the waters, "and let it divide between water and water"; and they are the blood of purity and the blood of the menstruant, as we explained above. Further, he said that Chesed is called clear waters, because they are over against turbid waters, in the way that we explained. Further, Chesed is called many waters, because there are few waters, and they are the waters of Netzach, which is a small Chesed in relation to Chesed. And likewise the waters of Chesed are many waters, and the waters of Netzach are few waters. And we can also say that the lower kindnesses, which are called "the mercies of David," as we explained in its entry, are called few waters. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that few waters are in Gevurah, and possibly on the side of Chesed that is in it. And in the Zohar, Parashat Tahara of Metzora (fol. 54b), he explained that Binah too is called many waters; and the reason is that she is a river whose waters do not cease. And these are his words: "Another explanation: many waters: this is the upper river, from which rivers go out to every side, and all of them flow and are drawn from it." Thus far his words. Behold, explicitly, Binah is called many waters, in the secret of her aspect in which she bestows the waters of compassion on all the sources. Further, he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 171a), that still waters (Ps. 23:2) is the effluence bestowed from Binah. Further, Rabbi Moshe [de León] said that Chesed is called the waters of the laver; and the reason: waters that come from the upper laver, with which Aaron and his sons, the priests of YHVH, sanctify their hands and their feet, for the sustaining of the worlds. And the intent is that they are waters drawn from the upper waters, the root of Chesed, which is Chokhmah. And this is not the laver as we explained in its entry; and nevertheless the waters of the laver will be according to his explanation. Further, he said that Binah is called faithful waters (Isa. 33:16), and did not explain a reason for it. And it is possible that she is so called for the reason that she is "a river whose waters do not cease"; and therefore she is a faithful source that does not cease:

Circumcision [מילה, milah]: Yesod is called milah, and so it is agreed in the mouth of all the commentators. However, it is called milah only in its receiving from the strength of Gevurah, in the arousal of the wine that gladdens. And likewise the name Elohim is [the number of] milah with the addition of one, as we explained this matter in the Gate of Names, chapter 4. And there is no wonder at this matter, for the principal arousal to destroy the husks is from the side of Gevurah. And this is what we pray: "Let them be ashamed and dismayed in their might": for although the power of the husks and their nourishment is from Gevurah, nevertheless "let them be ashamed and dismayed," and the destruction will be from the side of their might, which is Gevurah, which bestows in them; in which is the removal of the husks. And this is "the removal of leaven is only by burning"; and although the view of the Sages is "he may also crumble it and scatter it to the wind," that is, by the power of Tiferet, "or throw it into the sea," by the power of Chesed; nevertheless, according to all, burning is preferable, for it is utter destruction, "and the idols shall be utterly cut off" (Isa. 2:18). And therefore circumcision, which is the removal of the husks, is through Gevurah:

Base [מכון, makhon]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] gave two explanations of this word. The first, in Binah, and these are his words: "A base for all the worlds; for all the worlds are a base and a throne for His dwelling, and He sits upon all of them; and He is their base and their sustaining and their joining." Thus far his words. And these words are not the principal for us. And it seems to me that Malkhut is called makhon because she is a base for the whole Emanation, and she causes it to dwell below. And likewise Binah is a base for the first three and causes them to dwell below upon her seven sons, as we shall explain in the entry Shekhinah:

Covered [מכוסה, mekhusseh]: the supernal Keter is so called, for the reason that it is wondrous and covered, and there is no grasping in it at all, because it is Ayin [Nothing]. And we can say that it is called covered when it is concealed in the utmost concealment, while it has not yet spread out below:

Machpelah [מכפלה, makhpelah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Chayyei (fol. 129a), that Malkhut is called Machpelah with respect to her being double [kefulah]: her aspect with the sefirot and her aspect with the chariots and the worlds that are beneath her; she is found double. Further, he explained there that she is double, for there is no letter doubled in the Name except her, who is the letter, the last Heh. And accordingly she is called Machpelah in the manifestation of the Heh that is united with the upper Heh, so as to be doubled. And it seems to me that Binah too is called Machpelah, for she too is doubled, for all is one:

The first and the second arbiter [מכריע ראשון ושני, makhri'a rishon ve-sheni]: the commentators called Tiferet and the Righteous One so; and we have already spoken at length on this, as much as needed, in the Gate of Arbiters:

Mikhtam [מכתם, mikhtam] (Ps. 16:1): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 223b) that this word is divided into two, makh [humble] and tam [whole]: makh is the Righteous One, and likewise it is called poor; and tam is Tiferet; and when they are united they are called mikhtam; and "body and covenant are counted as one":

Fullness [מלא, melo]: on the verse "The earth is YHVH's, and its fullness" (Ps. 24:1), he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 67): the Shekhinah, who is the upper earth; and her fullness is the souls of the righteous. And everywhere the fullness of the Shekhinah is the effluence and the upper light that comes from Tiferet to Malkhut; and they themselves are the souls of the righteous:

Angel [מלאך, mal'akh]: Malkhut is called angel [messenger] when she does two errands; and for this reason she is called angel: the explanation, that she does her errand through Metatron or Sandalfon.
