And sometimes she is called by an accompanying name, the angel of YHVH; and the reason is when she does the errand of her husband in particular; and this is YHVH, her husband, Tiferet; or it means when her husband too is with her in that assistance; and it is all one. And she is called the redeeming angel (Gen. 48:16) when her errand is to redeem from distress; and therefore Jacob called her "the angel who redeemed," because she always redeemed him from all distress. And she is called the angel of the covenant (Mal. 3:1) when she rewards for the covenant, or when she is "a sword that executes the vengeance of the covenant." And she is called the angel of His presence (Isa. 63:9) when she serves the presence of the One who sends; for sometimes her errand is in the hiding of the upper face, and sometimes when the upper face, which shines, makes her face shine. And sometimes she is called the angel of God [Elohim], when she watches for judgment; and this is at the Exodus from Egypt, "and the angel of God ... moved" (Exod. 14:19), because her action was the destruction of the Egyptians by the power of judgment. And she is not called angel at the time of the action [but before she acts, as is found in the Zohar, Balak (fol. 187a), these are his words: "Rather, when she is sent] from above and receives radiance from the upper mirror; for then Abba and Imma bless her, and say to her: My daughter, go, keep your house, attend to your house; do thus for your house; go and feed them; go, for that world below is waiting for you; the members of your household are waiting for food from you; here you have all that you need to give them. Then she is an angel. And if you say: but in many places she is called angel, and does not come to feed the worlds; and further, by this name she does not feed the worlds, but by the name YHVH: it is certainly so. When she is sent from within Abba and Imma she is called angel; and once she dwells in her place, on the two cherubim, YHVH is her name." Thus far his words. And behold, it is explained that she is called by the name angel only at the time of her coming, before the beginning of the action, that is, before her sitting on the cherubim to act:

Work [מלאכה, melakhah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayishlach (fol. 172a), that Malkhut is called melakhah because through her all the work of this world is done; and she is so called in her aspect that acts in the world. And so he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 42a [12a]), on the verse "And I have filled him," etc., "and in all manner of workmanship [melakhah]" (Exod. 31:3): "this is Heh." Thus far his words:

And he further explained (there, fol. 13a) that she is called melakhah from the language of "Thus was finished [va-tekhel] all the work of the Tabernacle," etc. (Exod. 39:32), which is the language of completeness. And likewise through Malkhut all the upper ones are complete, for she completes the Structure. And the Heh that completes is the fourth Heh of the letters YHVH; it is the completeness of all:

Kingship [מלוכה, melukhah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 7b), these are his words: "'And the kingship [melukhah] shall be YHVH's' (Obad. 1:21). What is melukhah? This is the Assembly of Israel, for the King is bound to her." Thus far his words. And it is clear that the Shekhinah is called melukhah when she is united with the King, who is Tiferet, as is explained:

Lodging [מלון, malon] is the Shekhinah; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 1b). And she is so called because she is a lodging and an inn for the Holy One, blessed be He, Tiferet. And she is so called at the time that she is not united with him in substance, but an inn; and that is malon, a lodging for one night. And elsewhere (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 118a) he explained that she is called a lodging place of wayfarers (Jer. 9:1), in the secret of Yesod, the wayfarer who lodges with her; see there:

Salt [מלח, melach]: according to what appears from the words of the Zohar in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 241b), salt is Yesod; for it is what gives taste to the dish; and if not for its effluence and its salt, a man could not stand before the bitterness of the judgment that is in Malkhut. And by its name Malkhut is called the Salt Sea, for she draws nourishment from the covenant [of salt, as we explained in the entry "the Salt Sea"]:

King [מלך, melekh]: on this name the explanations are many. And from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in most places, it appears that "king" without qualification is Tiferet. However, it is called king only when it stands upon Malkhut; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 276), these are his words: "He is not called king there until he rides upon his horse, the Assembly of Israel. The Holy One, blessed be He, when He is outside His place, is not king; and when He returns to His place, 'And YHVH shall be king,' etc. (Zech. 14:9). And so of Israel it is said, 'all Israel are kings' sons'; in the likeness of the Father are His sons: they are not kings' sons until they return to the land of Israel." Thus far his words. Behold, it is clear that he is called king only when he is upon Malkhut. And this is specifically in the attribute "king" without qualification. However, when another word is joined to it, then it will be in another way, according to the accompaniment. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained elsewhere, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Behar, fol. 109a), these are his words: "And everywhere 'the King' without qualification is the Holy One, blessed be He"; and he explained Tiferet, as is proved there. And in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 127b), on the verse "King Solomon made himself a palanquin" (Song 3:9), etc., he explained that "king" without qualification is Malkhut, who is the King Messiah, as we shall explain. Certainly this disagrees with that; unless we say that, just as he is called "king" without qualification, so she, by his name, is called "king" without qualification; and this is strained. And there is King Solomon, and there are three explanations in it. One, in Tiferet; and it is called "king to whom peace [shalom] belongs," for peace, which is Yesod, is his, as is known; so he explained in Parashat Terumah there.

And further, he explained on the Song of Songs that King Solomon is in Binah, for peace, which is Tiferet, is hers, as is known. And in the Sava (of Mishpatim, fol. 100a) he explained that King Solomon is Chokhmah, and peace, which is Tiferet, is its, in the secret that it is called "the son of Jesse," ben yesh Yod, which is Chokhmah, as we explained in its entry; and "the Torah has seventy faces." And on all the explanations, she is called King Solomon only in the secret of her bestowal in completeness; and when Tiferet or Yesod is with her, she is related to the name Shelomoh, which is the arbitration, as is explained in the entry shelamim. And there is the great King, and it is Binah, when she bestows in Chesed. And sometimes Binah is called the holy King; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that she is so called from the side of Tiferet, which is called holy. And it is possible that she is called holy from the side of Gevurah, for from its side too is holiness, as we shall explain in its entry and as we explained in the entry Jabbok. And likewise this matter in the secret of judgment: she is called the holy King. And it is already possible that Tiferet is called the holy King and the pure King: one from the side of Gedulah and one from the side of Gevurah, for from its side are holiness and purity, as we explained in the entry taharah; and the great King from the side of Gedulah. And in order that we may be able to distinguish when the king will be in Tiferet or in Binah: it will be that when the Heh of knowledge is joined at the head of the word and at the head of the name, as ha-melekh ha-kadosh, ha-melekh ha-mishpat, both of them are in Binah, when she dwells in Tiferet; then the Heh of knowledge is a faithful witness that this title is in Binah, as we explained in the entry Heh. But without Heh, then it will be in Tiferet. And this rule appears to us the principal. Further, we shall judge the accompaniment according to its matter by itself. And the word melekh according to its judging, with the Heh of knowledge, is in one of the two places mentioned. (And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 151), [he explained] that Binah is called the great Alef, and Binah is "the city of the great King" (Ps. 48:3); this compelled the first explanation. And it is possible that it is so called from the side of Chokhmah, where the matter of greatness [rabbot] is; for Gedulah is great in Chokhmah, rav; and possibly from the side of Gedulah.) And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 127), Chokhmah is called the great King, and Binah "the city of the great King"; he decided according to the first explanation on the matter of rav. Further, the King of the world [melekh ha-olam]: and this hint is certainly in Binah. And the reason is that she is the King of the olam, which is a hint at the circuit; and this is related only to Binah; and when she is king over the whole world, which is a hint at the six days of Creation, for then she bestows in them, as the king feeds and provides for all his servants. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it as Tiferet, and it does not settle, and it is the reverse of the view of the Zohar. Further, there is the King of the kings of kings [melekh malkhei ha-melakhim]; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained: King, Binah; malkhei, which are the three Patriarchs, who are kings over the kings, which are the three branches drawn from them. This is his intent in brief. And what settles more for us: that "King" is the supernal Keter, and it is the King who reigns over malkhei, who are two kings, Chokhmah and Binah, which are kings who reign over seven kings, which are the seven days of the Structure. And so in these three words all ten are included. And according to our way in this composition, when we mention the Ein Sof we say afterward "the King of the kings of kings," to unify Him in His ten sefirot and to make Him King over them. Further, there is the awesome King, it is Tiferet; and it itself is called awesome, as will be explained in its entry. Further, there is the King of Salem [melekh shalem], and it is Binah; so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 87a). And it is possible that she is so called at the time that she rules over Tiferet, which is shalem [whole]. Further, he explained there that Malkhut is called melekh shalem when she is united with Tiferet, for then she is whole. Further, he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 238a), that Malkhut, with respect to her aspect in which she has only what she receives from Tiferet, is called the King Messiah. And it is possible to explain: a king who has nothing but the anointing [meshichat] of the upper oil:

Malkhut [מלכות, malkhut, Kingship]: the tenth attribute is called Malkhut. And the reason is that it is the kingship of the King. And the name Malkhut includes the whole household above; for how many faces within faces are awesome, and how many backs behind backs that are not seen; and when all is included, it is called Malkhut; for this name includes all the kingdom, small and great. However, when this attribute and "the virgins her companions that follow her" are united with the King, Tiferet, then she is called the kingdom of heaven; and heaven is Tiferet, as is explained in its entry. And when she is included in the union of her husband with all that is above, then she is called the complete kingdom of heaven, which shows her completeness and not her breach: for she is a whole matzah, not broken. And sometimes she is called the kingdom of the house of David; and the reason is that all the kingdom of the house of David depends on her; and likewise she has twenty-eight times, the number of the kings of the house of David. And just as there is the kingdom of heaven, so there is "the kingdom of arrogance" [malkhut zadon], the wicked, which will be uprooted speedily in our days; and this is Lilith the wicked and her household, as we shall explain in the Gate of Substitutes and the Gate of the Substitute Palaces:

Melchizedek [מלכי צדק, Malki-tzedek]: they explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 193b) that it is Malkhut, these are his words: "'You are a priest for ever,' etc. (Ps. 110:4). Who is 'after the order [divrati] of Melchizedek'? Rather, the supernal Priest, this is the one that stands over the word [davar]; because that word stands only in the right. And that word, what is it? Melchizedek is its name." Thus far his words:

From before YHVH [מלפני ה', millifnei YHVH]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 171a), that millifnei is Binah, which is over Tiferet. And there he also explained it as Netzach and Hod; and it needs study there (and see there, "another explanation"):

A kingdom of priests [ממלכת כהנים, mamlekhet kohanim] (Exod. 19:6): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Tzav (fol. 34b), that when Malkhut is united with Tiferet and is raised by means of Chesed, which bestows through the priests, she is called "a kingdom of priests":

Rest [מנוחה, menuchah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Yesod is menuchah, for the reason that it is the language of repose and rest, for it rests in its house; or from the language of going down, for the Targum of "and he went down" is u-nechat, for it goes down to Malkhut. And it seems to me that Binah is called menuchah for the reason of "and He rested" (Gen. 2:2), whose Targum is ve-nach: the rest of things in the secret of the great Jubilee; and there is the rest of the cycle in all the Sabbatical cycles. And she is called the Great Sabbath, as will be explained in its entry:

Lampstand [מנורה, menorah] is the Shekhinah, when she shines [menaheret] in the secret of the seven lamps; when the seven upper sefirot pour into the seven lamps that are in her. And there is an upper lampstand, and they are the seven sefirot themselves. And the usual [sense] is the Shekhinah; and she is so called in her receiving from Chokhmah by means of Chesed; and that is the explanation of "the lampstand in the south," and "whoever wishes to become wise, let him turn southward"; so he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 12b). Further there, elsewhere (on fol. 13b), [he explained] that Metatron is the lampstand, meaning the vessel of the lampstand; the wick is the Shekhinah; the oil is the effluence of Yesod; the light is Tiferet:

Offering [מנחה, minchah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 247) that it is Malkhut; when she is between the two arms, then she is called "a new meal-offering" (Lev. 23:16). However, the afternoon prayer [tefillat ha-minchah] is from the side of Gevurah, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained: "Isaac instituted the afternoon prayer":

Border [מסגרת, misgeret]: "Close by the border shall the rings be," etc. (Exod. 25:27): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Bereshit (fol. 31a), that it is Binah, the world to come; see there:

The number of the days [מספר הימים, mispar ha-yamim]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 49, fol. 83b) that Malkhut is called "the number of the days"; and the reason is that she is the reckoning and number for the upper days. And he explained that the upper days are revealed by means of this attribute, and she is what reveals them; like the reckoning, which is the limiting of the thing that is counted, and from the side of the limit and the reckoning it is revealed:

Dwelling [מעון, ma'on]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Chesed is called ma'on, because it is emanated from the supernal Chokhmah, which is called me'onah, as it is said (Deut. 33:27), "The eternal God [Elohei kedem] is a dwelling place [me'onah]"; and the word kedem shows Chokhmah. And he said that sometimes Chokhmah too is called ma'on. And he said that Malkhut too is called ma'on, for she is a dwelling for the upper ones and the lower ones. And some explained it as Keter:

Spring [מעיין, ma'ayan]: on this word the explanations are many, both in the words of the commentators and in the words of Rashbi. And this is the settling of the matters in their measure. Binah is called a spring of gardens (Song 4:15); and the gardens are the sefirot that are beneath her. And within the spring is a source from which the waters go out; and it is Chokhmah, from which waters go out to Binah, and Binah bestows below. And Keter is called a spring sealed (Song 4:12), because it is the inner point from which onward is the outlet of the waters; the explanation, it is the coming-into-being of the waters. And it is found accordingly that "spring" is right of the three first sefirot. And in truth the three of them together are the spring. How so? The outlet from which the waters come into being is the point from which onward is the coming-into-being of the waters: it is Keter. And the spring through which the water is bestowed, that is, the pipe of the spring that pours the water, is Chokhmah. And the spring itself, that is, the pouring of the water outward, is Binah. And it is found accordingly that when we say "spring," the intent is the way of this bestowal from Keter to Chokhmah, and Chokhmah to Binah, and Binah bestows and gives drink to the gardens. And afterward, when [Malkhut] receives the effluence and is filled from it, she becomes a spring for the lower gardens; and in them too are these three levels; and there is no need to lengthen, for from the first three we infer to these three. And now, when we say "spring" in Malkhut, it will be in the abundance of the effluence that Tiferet bestows in her; for it is the point of the outlet of the waters, and Yesod is the pipe of the waters, and Malkhut the spring. For Yesod is the pipe that pours the waters into the spring, as we explained above:

The wells of salvation [מעייני הישועה, ma'aynei ha-yeshu'ah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Balak (fol. 212), that Chokhmah and Binah are so called, for the reason that from them salvation and freedom are bestowed. And he also explained that Netzach and Hod are so called. And it is possible that they are so called when they draw salvation from Chesed, in which is the root of salvation, as we explained in its entry; and Chesed receives salvation from Binah; and they bestow the salvation on joy [sasson], which is Yesod. And this is "Therefore with joy shall you draw water out of the wells of salvation" (Isa. 12:3); so he explained there:

Above the heavens [מעל שמים, me-al shamayim]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 16a), these are his words: "'Over the heavens' [al shamayim] would mean that place which stands over the heavens and no more. Since it says 'above the heavens' [me-al shamayim] (Ps. 108:5), it means that place which stands over the heavens, higher and higher. And what is it? It is the Mother." Thus far his words. And the explanation: if it had said al shamayim, the explanation would be Gedulah and Gevurah, which are over Tiferet, which is called heaven. But now that it said me-al shamayim, the explanation is the one higher than those that are over the heavens; that is, Binah, which is above Gedulah and Gevurah, which are above heaven, which is Tiferet, as we explained:

Depths [מעמקים, ma'amakim]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Chokhmah and Keter are called depths, and of them it is said (Ps. 130:1), "Out of the depths I have called You, O YHVH." And in the Zohar (Beshalach, fol. 63b) and in many places it appears that Chokhmah is called depths:

West [מערב, ma'arav]: Malkhut is called west for several reasons. The first, because in it the sun sets [ma'ariv], for there is its house. And further, for the east is Tiferet, and over against the east is the west, which is the woman, who is a helpmate over against him.

And further, she is called ma'arav because in her all the upper effluence is mixed [mit'arev] and blended, and there a fine blending is made in it. And for this reason (the Gaon, in the Tzachtzachot, chapter 4) called her me'urav [mixed], with a Vav. And further, for there the sun sets and the darkness [comes], as it is known that there is the absence of the light:

Array [מערכה, ma'arakhah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna that Binah is called ma'arakhah. And the reason may be that in her all the beings that come into being are arrayed, as we shall explain in the Gate of Gates; and she is the female who conceives from the subtle beings and brings them forth and makes them grow. And according to this reason the name ma'arakhah is already right also in Malkhut, who is also a female who reveals and thickens the beings that go out from Tiferet:

Deed [מעשה, ma'aseh]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, constantly calls Binah "deed" and Chokhmah "thought." And the reason is that, just as the deed is the revealing of the thought, and through the deed is the completion of the thought, so through Binah is the completion of the beings that come into being through Chokhmah, as we explained in the entry ma'arakhah. And in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 236a), he explained on the verse (Exod. 36:4), "And all the wise men that wrought came": right and left; that is, wisdom is right and deed left; and that is, that Malkhut is called wisdom and deed Binah, as we explained in the entry chokhmah, and as we shall explain:

The Work of the Chariot [מעשה מרכבה, ma'aseh merkavah]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 13b) that Metatron is called the Work of the Chariot, for it is rekhev mah: the explanation, a chariot for Mah, which is Malkhut, who is called Mah; and Metatron is a chariot for her:
The Work of Creation [מעשה בראשית, ma'aseh bereshit] is Malkhut. And the reason may be because she performs all the actions of Creation, or that she is a chariot for Chokhmah, which is called reshit:

Tithe [מעשר, ma'aser]: Malkhut is so called; and so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 87b), on the verse (Gen. 14:20), "And he gave him a tithe of all." And he explained the reason: that she is the tithe of the upper Emanation, and she is literally the tenth, a tithe. And so they said in the Tikkunim. And there is the tithe of the tithe; and he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 17, fol. 31a) that "tithe" is called the secret of her union with the Levite, Gevurah; and "the tithe of the tithe" is her union with the Priest, in the secret of the right. And there is a secret in this matter, as we explained in the entry Alef-Yod-Kof: for the Alef is the secret of the tithe of the tithe, and it is the middle point, and it is Chesed; and it spreads out into Gevurah; for it is known that Chesed is kernel with respect to Gevurah, and Gevurah husk. And Gevurah spreads out in Tiferet, and Tiferet is husk to Gevurah, in the secret of its manifestation below Gevurah. And therefore Tiferet is in a hundred branches that spread out [as] a tithe from Gevurah, which is the Levite; and Gevurah is ten branches that spread out from Chesed, which is one point; and that is one, the tithe of the tithe:

The outer keys [מפתחות החצוניות, ha-mafte'chot ha-chitzoniyot] are in Malkhut, in the secret of the name Adonai, as Rashbi explained (in the Introduction, fol. 4b, and fol. 10b); and the reason is that there is the entrance [petach] to the other sefirot (see the entry "ten"):

Pillar [מצבה, matzevah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 72b), that Malkhut, when she is united with Tiferet, is called matzevah. And these are his words: "'And this stone, which I have set up as a pillar' (Gen. 28:22). What is matzevah? That she was fallen, and he raised her up." Thus far his words:

A broken matzah [מצה פרוסה, matzah perusah] is in the secret of Malkhut. And she is called matzah, which has no admixture of leaven, for she has already been purified for her husband. And she is called broken, for she has not yet coupled so that her breach be completed. And to her the broken matzah on Passover hints. And even where it does not say "broken" but "matzah" without qualification, presumably it is "the bread of affliction." And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 157a). And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, fol. 28b) he explained that matzah is Heh, and its being broken is Dalet. And it is possible that matzah is also in Binah, where there is also a Heh; and there is some proof of this from the language; see there. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 15, fol. 29b) he explained that the mate of the Righteous One is "guarded matzah," in relation to "whole" [and] "rich" matzah. Therefore it appears that she is called rich and whole and guarded, all according to the aspects: rich from the side of wealth; and therefore one does not fulfill [the obligation] on Passover with rich matzah, because her principal commandment is from the side of Chesed, which is from the side of the south, and not with wealth, which is from the north, as they said, "whoever wishes to become rich, let him turn northward"; whole, when her breach has been completed; guarded, that is to say, adorned and waiting for her husband, the language of "waiting [shomeret] for the levir":

Commandment [מצוה, mitzvah] is Malkhut; and she is called mitzvah (as is written in Parashat Vayetze, fol. 157a), for he added a Vav to the matzah, to hint that she has been united with her husband. And therefore her principal is the commandment in the Torah to unite her with her husband, and not to separate her.

And further, in mitzvah the four-letter name is revealed in completeness; for Mem-Tzadi is Yod-Heh in AT-BaSh. And likewise she is called the commandment of the King, the commandment of the King of the world, who is Tiferet, as is known:

Commander [מצווה, metzavveh]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30, fol. 72b, these are his words: "And further, metzavveh): this is the central pillar, which is metzavveh from the side of Abba, who is rosh [head], and from the side of Imma, who is asher. And so the Righteous One commands and does from both of them. And therefore it is said of both of them, 'asher has sanctified us with His commandments': Imma has sanctified us, and Abba has commanded us. Concerning whom? Concerning the lower Shekhinah, who is 'whatever opens the womb' (Exod. 13:2), the opening of the womb [rechem], which is two hundred and forty-eight [Resh-Chet-Mem] commandments; she is the commandment of YHVH," etc. Thus far his words, as relevant to our matter. And we say in explanation that his intent in this is to explain the blessing "who [asher] has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us." And he said that the language of mitzvah is explained from the union of the commandment, that is, its union with Malkhut, who is called mitzvah, as is explained. "This is the central pillar," etc.: he called it here "pillar," etc., to hint at its rising by way of the middle line up to between Chokhmah and Binah; and by their power, for they strengthen it, it is united with Malkhut, who is called mitzvah, by means of Chokhmah, which is called Abba. And he called Chokhmah and Binah Abba and Imma to show that, just as the father and the mother give power and arrangement to the son to marry a wife, by means of their wealth, so is the matter with the upper Father and Mother. And he said rosh and asher: the intent is to explain the word asher that is in the blessing; and he explained that in the word asher Chokhmah and Binah are hinted. For Chokhmah is called rosh, and it is a permutation of the word asher; and asher according to its sense is Binah. "And so the Righteous One, from the side of both of them," etc.: for the union of Malkhut is with both of them, as is known; for it is the holy organ for the union. And he was compelled to this in order to set right the language kiddeshanu and tzivvanu [He sanctified us, He commanded us], which is [read as] plural; and if Tiferet alone were the commander, it would have been fitting to say "sanctified us and commanded me" in the singular. Therefore he said that they are Tiferet and Yesod, body and covenant. And Yesod too is metzavveh, united with Malkhut from the side of both of them, Chokhmah and Binah. And this is what he said, "And therefore it is said of both of them," etc., in the plural: the intent is that both of them were sanctified and commanded. "Imma has sanctified us and Abba has commanded us": the intent is that the holiness is a preparation for the union; and likewise from the side of Binah they prepare themselves for the union, as in the matter of the betrothal, which precedes the coupling; and likewise the arousal in the north, in the secret of "His left hand is under my head" (Song 2:6); and the union is in the right, "and his right hand embraces me." And likewise the union, which is the commanding, as we explained, is through Abba; that is, "and commanded us": Abba commanded us. And so it is proved that there is no union of Malkhut with Tiferet except in the secret of their receiving from Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. "Concerning whom? Concerning the Shekhinah," etc.: all this the intent is to explain that the Shekhinah, with respect to the coupling, is called mitzvah. And he brought a proof: for rechem [womb], which is the sustaining of the coupling, comes to two hundred and forty-eight; and "the opening of the womb" means the opening of the commandments. And therefore, when she opens, the gate that is shut all the six days of work, through the coupling, it is fitting that she be titled by the name mitzvah, that is, rechem. And this is what he said, "she is the commandment of YHVH": whose explanation is, when she is united with YHVH, then she is called "the commandment of YHVH," that is, YHVH Adonai united, like this,  Y A H D V N H Y, which shows the union. And now we have learned from the words of this saying that Tiferet and Yesod are each called metzavveh, in the secret of their union with the mitzvah, which is Malkhut. And along the way we have gained the explanation of the saying:

The depths of the sea [מצולות ים, metzulot yam] (Micah 7:19): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim and in the Zohar (Shelach, fol. 163b) that Samael and his mate are called the depths of the sea, for they are under the upper sea, under Malkhut. And the totality of all the husks, when they are beneath her, are called the depths of the sea:

Sanctuary [מקדש, mikdash]: it is possible that Tiferet is so called. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 137a), on the verse (Lev. 19:30; 26:2), "and you shall reverence My sanctuary." And likewise of Yesod:

Gathering of waters [מקוה, mikveh]: this name is related to Malkhut, because in her all the waters of the upper effluence are gathered and collected; and she is called mikveh when she is full of effluence. And Tiferet too is sometimes called mikveh; for of it it is said (Jer. 17:13), "O YHVH, the hope [mikveh] of Israel": behold, explicitly, the name YHVH, which is in Tiferet, is mikveh. And in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 33a), Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Yose disagreed: one said in Tiferet and one said in Yesod; and there is one who says there in Malkhut (that is, Rabbi Isaac):

Place [מקום, makom]: Tiferet is so called. And the reason is that the four-letter name comes to makom in the squared reckoning. How so? Ten times ten are a hundred; five times five comes to twenty-five; six times six comes to thirty-six; five times five comes to twenty-five: the total sum is 186, the number of makom; and Tiferet is called Makom. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 26, fol. 70a) explicitly. And the intent is that "He is the place of the world": the explanation, it bears the whole world, that is, the six extremities; and it is cause to all of them, for all of them branch out from it. "And the world is not His place": the explanation, the six extremities are not cause to it, as we explained; for it bestows, and it is in the middle, like a king among his princes; and in this aspect it is called Makom. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained Makom as Keter, for it is the place of the world:

Source [מקור, makor]: Keter is called source. And sometimes it is called the source of living waters (Jer. 2:13), which is the effluence bestowed from the upper life; and the source of the blessings, for from there all the blessings are bestowed. And sometimes it is called the source of life (Ps. 36:10), for from it the upper life springs. And these names, just as they are related to Keter, are sometimes also related to Chokhmah, and sometimes to Binah; for the matter of the source is related to all three of them, in the way of the spring that we explained in its entry. And likewise Yesod is sometimes called by these titles, also for this reason; for in it all these things that we explained are right. And in the Zohar, Parashat Tzav (fol. 34a), he calls Binah "the source of life," for she is the source for the life of Chokhmah, which is bestowed through Chokhmah. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Malkhut from the side of Keter is called "the source of living waters." And the reason may be that Keter is in substance the source of living waters, as we explained; and therefore, when she draws nourishment from it and bestows that life, she is called the source of living waters:

A rod of white poplar [מקל לבנה, makel livneh] (Gen. 30:37): Tiferet is so called from the side of Chesed; so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 161b). And the reason is that it is a rod, in the form of a Vav; and it is livneh [white] from the side of the whiteness of Chesed, and not from the side of the waters of Chesed. And it is possible to say that it is so called with respect to the aspects of the manifestation of Chesed concealed in Chokhmah, which is called white, which is white light, in which water has no place; and from the side of the revealed manifestation of Chesed, which is called water, from there it is moist [lach] (Gen. 30:37):

Rods [מקלות, makkelot]: he explained in the Zohar (there, fol. 161a): "What are the rods? These are levels, which are a court"; see there. And the matter is that the powers of judgment are called rods; and the reason is that they are to chastise man toward the straight way:

Cattle [מקנה, mikneh]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 83b), on the verse (Gen. 13:2), "And Abram was very rich in cattle": "in cattle, from the side of the west"; the explanation, from the side of Malkhut. And the reason may be that there are "creeping things innumerable, small creatures with great" (Ps. 104:25):

Holy convocations [מקראי קדש, mikra'ei kodesh]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 111a) that only Chesed and Gevurah and Tiferet are called holy convocations. And in Parashat Emor in the Zohar (fol. 93b) he explained that they are called holy convocations from the side that they are bestowed from Chokhmah, where the root of holiness [kodesh] is:

Mirror [מראה, mar'ah]: in this word there are different matters, and each one needs explanation. Malkhut is called mirror, and Binah is called mirror. And the reason is that, just as the mirror shows all things, so Binah shows outward all the sefirot that are concealed above her, and she shows them below. And Malkhut too is called mirror, for all the sefirot are seen in her too; but the appearing in which they appear in Binah is not like the appearing that is in Malkhut. For in Binah they are seen subtle in the utmost subtlety, more than their measure in their place, especially the seven last ones; but below, in Malkhut, they appear in revealing and more thickly. And what is not apprehended in its place is apprehended in Malkhut; for through her the concealed things are apprehended. And the example of this: as one who sees himself in a mirror, according to the measure of the mirror so will be the measure of what is seen. And therefore in Binah, which is a subtle mirror, the sefirot are seen in subtlety, in concealment; and in Malkhut, which is a coarse and thick mirror, they are seen in her in thickness and in revealing.

And further, it is fitting to know that all the sefirot are called mirrors [mar'ot, visions]. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Introduction, fol. 6a, and in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 112) on the visions of Ezekiel: that what is mentioned there ten times, the language of mar'eh, ha-mar'eh, ba-mar'eh, etc., are the ten sefirot. And they are called mar'ot only when they appear in one of the mirrors; and on account of this they are titled by the name mar'eh. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 280b) on this matter, these are his words: "This mar'eh sometimes is with the letter Heh, 'this great sight' [ha-mar'eh] (Exod. 3:3); sometimes with the letter Bet, 'I make Myself known to him in a vision' [ba-mar'ah] (Num. 12:6)," etc. "This mar'eh is included of ten sefirot, and each letter shows its sefirah: as ke-mar'eh, with the letter Kaf, shows Keter; and so the other letters show their sefirah. And there is no need to lengthen here; and for the wise, by a hint." Thus far his words.

And what he objected, that there should not have been any added letter at all, is because he explained above that the mirror, Binah, inclines to the side of Chesed, and he proved the matter from ba-mar'ah, which comes to two hundred and forty-eight, the number of Abraham. And because of this he objected that it was not fitting that mar'eh come with the addition of another letter, but only with the letter Bet, which shows the numerical value which is Abraham. Therefore he answered that the addition always shows the sefirot that are added in their appearing in the mirror, as he goes on to explain. Further, there are a vision in a dream and a vision while awake. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna there) and in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 30a): "In the closing of the eyes she is called a vision in a dream, and in the opening of the eyes she is a vision while awake." And the intent is that we explained the eyes and their colors in the preceding gates: for the pupil of the eye is Malkhut, in the manifestation of the Yod; and the three colors of the eye, which are around the pupil, white and red and green, are the three Patriarchs; and the two eyelids are Netzach and Hod. And when Malkhut is united with Tiferet, then these colors shine in her, and she is called a vision while awake, in the opening of the eyes. And when the union is not complete, then she is called a vision in a dream, in the closing of the eyes, for the colors do not shine; and Netzach and Hod are screens dividing, closing the eyes, dividing between her and her husband. And this is what is found in one place: "from the side of Tiferet, a vision while awake, and from the side of the Righteous One, a vision in a dream," as we copied above in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 5. Further, there is the closed vision, which is Binah, which is concealed, in which there is no likeness; and the revealed vision, which is Malkhut, in which there is revealing and likeness.

And behold, this closedness is the reverse of the closing of the eyes. For the closing of the eyes means that the lights are not revealed in Malkhut, and she is dark; but "the closed vision" means the concealment of the vision, in the paucity of the apprehension of it, because of the great brightness. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it also in Yesod; and it is not to the point. And Binah, from the side of Chesed, is called the vision of brightness [mar'eh ha-nogah], for every term of nogah is on the right; so he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 112b), and we shall explain it in its entry. And Malkhut, from the side of Netzach and Hod, is called the vision of prophecy, the mirror that receives the prophecy from the prophets. And there are the mirrors of the serving women [mar'ot ha-tzove'ot] (Exod. 38:8); and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained Netzach and Hod, and these are his words: "And the explanation: mirrors for everyone who comes to the host, the host to reach the hosts of prophecy, except for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him; and nevertheless it is the beginning of his prophecy." Thus far his words.

And to me it seems that they are so called when they bestow in Yesod, the Life of the Worlds, whose hosts are called tzeva'ot. Further, we can explain that Tiferet and Malkhut are called mirrors in the secret of the mirror that shines and the mirror that does not shine; and when they are in the hosts [tzeva'ot], which are Netzach and Hod, they are called "the mirrors of the serving women." And we spoke at length on this matter in the Gate of Names, with the help of the Name:

Gall [מרה, marah] is Gehinnom; and it is from the evil side, "the sword of the Angel of Death, the death of the great ones," which was created on the second day and hangs on the liver; "the starling beside the raven, because it is of its kind" (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 234a–b):

Chariot [מרכבה, merkavah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 247b) that Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet are called the upper Chariot, and Netzach and Hod and Yesod are called the second chariot [mirkevet ha-mishneh]. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Chokhmah and Binah and Gedulah and Gevurah are the upper Chariot. How so? Gedulah, lion; and Gevurah, ox; Binah, eagle; Chokhmah, the face of a man; and it is the upper Man. And the great eagle with the wings: they are six wings, six sefirot; and the upper Man rides upon the faces of the eagle and the lion and the ox. And the lower Chariot is Netzach, Hod, Yesod: lion, ox, eagle; and Tiferet, the face of a man, rides upon them from above. And Malkhut includes all the faces. And there is another way: that Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Malkhut are called the upper Chariot, which are the face of a lion, etc.; and beneath them, in the secret of Beriah, the throne on four legs, they are called the second chariot, for they are second to the upper sefirot. Further, there is in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 118b) that Malkhut is called chariot when she is clothed in the chariot and acts through the living creatures; and likewise in this way she is then called the face of an eagle, and likewise the face of a lion, the face of an ox, the face of a man, according to the action; see there. And this is a secret concerning the angels, which we shall widen the explanation of, with the help of the Name, in the Gate of Palaces:

Moses [משה, Moshe]: just as Jacob is a chariot for Tiferet, so Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is a chariot for Tiferet. And there is a great difference between them. For Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is a chariot for Tiferet in the secret of the concealed Da'at, the aspect of Tiferet from the side of Chokhmah. And behold, this Da'at is a subtle manifestation that Tiferet has, and it includes the six extremities in subtlety; and it is the soul for the manifestation of Tiferet, which is revealed, and it is concealed within it. And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is a chariot for this concealed Da'at, and Jacob for Tiferet. And this is what is found in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 98): "this one in the body and that one in the soul": the explanation, Jacob in the body, which is Tiferet, and Moses in the soul, which is Da'at. And this is what he also said elsewhere (Tikkun 13, fol. 27): "this one within and that one without": the explanation, Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, within, in the secret of the concealed Da'at, and Jacob without, in the secret of Tiferet. And because the concealed Da'at is the totality of the six extremities, it is said in the Tikkunim of Moses: "in him alone was what was in Adam and the three Patriarchs":

Settings of gold [משבצות זהב, mishbetzot zahav] (Exod. 28:13): he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24, fol. 68a) that Netzach and Hod are called settings; and they are called gold from the side of Gevurah:

The joy of the whole earth [משוש כל הארץ, mesos kol ha-aretz] (Ps. 48:3): in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 127a) he explained that Tiferet is called "the joy of the whole earth," because it is the joy for Kol, which is Yesod, and for the earth, which is Malkhut. And the language of the Zohar in Parashat Vayikra (fol. 5a) inclines somewhat to this:
Destroyer [משחית, mashchit] is one power of the four powers of the husk mentioned in the verse "And He, being full of compassion" (Ps. 78:38); and they are Destroyer, and Iniquity, Anger and Fury:

Pledge [משכון, mashkon]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 54a) that Malkhut is called mashkon, which is the pledge that Israel has, through which Tiferet dwells among them. And likewise mishkan [Tabernacle] is the language of mashkon:

Maskil [משכיל, maskil, instruction]: there is a maskil and there is a maskil. The one maskil is Yesod; for it makes understand and translates and makes known and explains to David, who is Malkhut, who reveals the upper things; and it makes known the upper effluence and the upper forms in Malkhut. And this is "Of David, a maskil" or "a maskil of David," from below to above or from above to below. And there is a maskil, that is, "maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite" (Ps. 89:1); and it is Binah, which rises above into the brain and cleaves to Chokhmah, and makes understand and explains and translates for ezrach Yod [the Ezrahite], who is Abraham, who shines from the upper world by the power of Chokhmah. And every maskil is by the power of Chokhmah, which is called sekhel [intellect] and haskel. And Yesod is called maskil only when it draws the extension of Binah, where Chokhmah is. And there is no wonder from the verse "And David was successful [maskil] in all his ways" (1 Sam. 18:14), for it is through Yesod, in its drawing from Binah. And to stand on the content of the things, look into the saying of the Sava (Mishpatim, fol. 110a) on the verse "Hear, O mountains," etc.:

Tabernacle [משכן, mishkan]: there are two tabernacles, the upper tabernacle and the lower tabernacle: Binah, the upper tabernacle; Malkhut, the lower tabernacle. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim. And of them it is said (Ps. 132:5), "tabernacles for the Mighty One of Jacob"; for Tiferet is between these two tabernacles; and the witness is the matter of Leah and Rachel. And Malkhut is called the Tabernacle of the Testimony, because in her is the matter of testifying, as it is written (Lam. 2:13), "What shall I testify to you?" And the reason is that there is the place of the testimony, which is the union of Tiferet and Yesod, as is explained. And he explained elsewhere that Malkhut is called mishkan only when she is a dwelling for Tiferet, which is within her:

Who repays recompense [משלם גמול, meshallem gemul]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained this word as Fear [Pachad]. And the reason seems to me because Gevurah repays the recompense equally, measure for measure, without passing over. And further, some of the commentators called her "who repays good reward to those who fear Him," specifically. And further, the language of payment shows the equality of the measure, measure for measure. And according to this she is called by this name in the middle aspect that is in Gevurah: for in the first aspect there is Chesed in it, and in the last there is the power of the evil fire, and in the middle it is in equal measure [for each according to his deeds]:

Second [משנה, mishneh] is Malkhut. However, she is called mishneh as "second to the king" (Esth. 10:3): the explanation, she is the aspect of the handmaid of the queen, in the secret of the throne of Beriah, explained in the Gate of ABYA; and she is second to her mistress, that is, the Lady. Or it will be in the manifestation of the Heh, which is second to the Yod. And both are right in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And elsewhere he explained that she is so called from the side of Chesed; and the reason is that through it is the manifestation of the Heh, as we explained in the Gate of the Diminishment. And elsewhere he explained that she is called mishneh in the secret that she is second to the King, who is Tiferet; and always in the secret of the Heh: for he is Vav and she is Heh, second to him:

Justice [משפט, mishpat]: what is well known on this word, in most of the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and the other commentators, is that Tiferet is called mishpat. However, they said that it is so called when it draws nourishment from judgment, from the side of Gevurah. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 130b), these are his words: "In measure, in weight and in quantity (Lev. 19:35): in measure, in the five tikkunim of the upper Heh; in weight, this is Vav; and in quantity, this is Heh. The justice of all: this is Yod. As it is written, 'But YHVH of hosts is exalted in justice' (Isa. 5:16)." Thus far his words. For the intent is that YHVH, which is Tiferet, is exalted to the justice, which is Yod, higher than the high. And it appears to us to settle the matter: that mishpat means judgment with some compassion; but it conducts itself on the line of the middle. And the explanation of mishpat means a measured, contracted base. And therefore he said that Chokhmah is what measures and contracts the attributes and settles them, so that they should not widen more than their measure. And the intent of mishpat is contraction; close to "who repays recompense" that we explained above. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna he explained that Tiferet is called judge [shofet] from the side of Binah; it will be explained in its entry. And in the Zohar, Parashat Kedoshim (fol. 85b), he explained that mishpat is judgment in an admixture of compassion; and by this everything is settled: for its root, from the side of Binah, is judgment, and it draws compassion from the side of Chokhmah. And these are his words: "When justice is aroused, there is compassion in it"; and the explanation, that there is judgment in it and there is compassion in it. And the reason is that it receives the compassion of Chokhmah by means of Binah. And in Parashat Acharei (fol. 73b) it is understood that it is compassion; and the reason is that its source, which is its root, is compassion; and that is Chokhmah:

Lintel [משקוף, mashkof]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it as Yesod, and these are his words: "When Yesod rises above Netzach and Hod, then they are two doorposts, and it is a lintel over them; and it is the secret of the Passover of Egypt." Thus far his words. And the proof of his words is from the blood of the covenant that was on the lintel in Egypt. And because it has a manifestation over them and a manifestation beneath them, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, therefore sometimes it says "on the lintel and on the two doorposts" (Exod. 12:7), and sometimes it says "on the two doorposts and on the lintel" (Exod. 12:22) (and see the book Kehillat Ya'akov):

Sweet [מתוק, matok]: Malkhut is called so from the side of Gevurah, in the secret of honey, as is written in the Zohar, Vayechi (fol. 240a). And it is possible to say that she is so called in the secret of "His left hand is under my head," which is sweetness from the side of judgment, as is explained in the preceding gates:

The giving of the Torah [מתן תורה, mattan Torah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Binah is so called, because in her the Torah was given, in the secret of the fiftieth day mentioned; and it does not settle. And according to the way of Rashbi, peace be upon him, the Torah was given on the seventh, and it is Yesod; and it is what is called "the day of the giving of the Torah," for through it is the giving of the Torah and its union with the Assembly of Israel. And what Rabbi Moshe [de León] proved from the fiftieth day is not a proof, for there is no number of days above, as we explained in the preceding gates. And elsewhere it appears that the giving of the Torah is Tiferet:

A good gift [מתנה טובה, mattanah tovah]: Malkhut is called so; and she is so called when she is above, in the secret of the Yod in Chokhmah. However, when she is clothed in three colors, which are the Heh, three Vavs, which is her being united with the three Patriarchs, which are the three colors of the eye, and the pupil of the eye in the middle; and that is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Betzah 16a): "I have a good gift in My treasure house": which is Chokhmah, in the secret of the rib. And she is called "a good gift," meaning shining, in the secret of "when he dresses [be-heitivo] the lamps." However, when she is clothed [in them] she is called Sabbath; and this is "and Sabbath is its name" [the end of that saying]. And every term of shem [name] is a garment and a palace, as explained in the preceding gates, and we shall explain it in the entry shem:

Loins [מתנים, motnayim] are above, in the secret of the union of Tiferet with Malkhut, who is the girdle that is united with the loins of a man. And their union above, in the secret of Gevurah and strength, is called motnayim; and the chalatzayim below, in the secret of the chalatzayim, as we explained in its entry. And our intent is not that the motnayim are in Gevurah; rather, the motnayim are Netzach and Hod; but the principal is according to the prevailing of its nourishment, whether from the side of Gevurah or from the side of Chesed. And the motnayim below are Hod, and the motnayim above Netzach. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verse (Ezek. 1:27), "from the appearance of his loins and upward."
Behold, the explanation of the entry of the letter Mem is concluded, with the help of the Rock who dwells on high. And we shall come to explain the entry of the letter Nun, with the help of the Name:

Faithful [נאמן, ne'eman]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, and the other commentators agreed that this name is a title of Yesod. And it may be so called when it bestows the effluence of truth from Tiferet to Malkhut, who is called emunah [faith]; and it is faithful between him and her, not to withhold the seed from its subtle manifestation, which is bestowed from above. Then it is called faithful, in the secret of truth and faith:

Comely [נאה, na'eh]: it is explained in the Gate of Titles, chapter 4, that na'eh is in Malkhut, from the side of her adornments, which are drawn to her from the male: that is, Nun, Malkhut; Alef-Heh, Tiferet, for it comes to six. And they are her adornments, included in her, in her form:

Prophecy [נבואה, nevu'ah]: Malkhut is so called from the side of the aspect of the bestowal of the prophets that is in her, which are Netzach and Hod: they are the prophets, and she is the prophecy. And through them the prophet prophesies from within Malkhut; and from this aspect she is called prophecy:

The prophets of truth [נביאי האמת, nevi'ei ha-emet] are Netzach and Hod. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, calls them nevi'ei keshot [prophets of truth], and it is all one. And when they prophesy, that is, bestow prophecy alone, then they are called simply prophets; but when they receive upon themselves the truth, which is Tiferet, then they are called the prophets of truth. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 236a) and in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 10b). And they are also called simply prophets from the side that they reveal the will of the Shekhinah below; and so he explained in the Tikkunim:

Negev [נגב, negev] is the south, the attribute of Chesed, the attribute of Abraham. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 44a [read 84a?]), on the verse (Gen. 12:9), "going on still toward the Negev." And what is difficult about this is that negev is the language of nagov [dried], and it is the language of dryness; and on the contrary, we see that in Chesed is the principal of the waters and their moisture, as is known. And Rabbi Menachem Recanati answered in this parashah that the reason it is called Negev is that it moistens the dryness of the judgment that is bestowed from Gevurah; and the dried thing is what it moistens. And it is far-fetched that it should be called by the language of drying because it moistens it. And what is correct, in our view, is explained by the reason why the south is dry and the north moist, when it would have been fitting to be the reverse: that the south should be moist from the side of the waters of Chesed that are in the south, and the north dry from the side of Gevurah. Rather, the sefirot are bound to one another with a strong bond; and behold, Gevurah acts toward the side of Chesed with the hard fire, and strikes with its judgment and bestows upon it, in order to bring it back to its own nature, until the heat of Chesed is greatly strengthened through this cause. And Gevurah is the reverse: for it is cooled and moistened by the power of the waters that are in Chesed, which prevail in it to bring it back to the nature of the waters. And it is found according to this that the face of Chesed that is over against the face of Gevurah (is compassion) [another version: is hot] exceedingly; and therefore the south, which is over against the north, is dried and dry. And Gevurah, the face that it has over against Chesed, is exceedingly moist; and therefore the north, which is over against the south, is moist. And according to this, Chesed will be called Negev on the side that draws near to Gevurah, which is from the language of nagov. And there is no wonder in this; for Abraham did not merit the attribute of Chesed in substance until he bound Isaac his son; and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat ha-Akedah. And therefore he pursued the Negev, to subdue it to Isaac and to bind him, so that the fire should be beneath the water. And now negbah [toward the Negev], with a Heh, is right; for it is the last Heh, the soft attribute of judgment, in which his pursuit was until he bound him, as we explained:

Melody [נגון, niggun]: every melody is from the side of Gevurah. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 13, fol. 26a), when he came to explain the ten kinds of praise that are in the book of Psalms: he said, "the fifth, with melody"; and there he counts the sefirot from above to below, and there it is explained that melody is from the side of Gevurah. And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 52, fol. 84b), on the verse (Hab. 3:19), "For the leader [la-menatze'ach], on my stringed instruments [bi-neginotai]," he said: "the cubit and two thighs." And necessarily the two thighs are la-menatze'ach, as we explained in its entry; and bi-neginotai is Binah. It appears that melody is in Binah. And we can say that it is all one matter; for so is the way of the Levite: from the side of Gevurah he would play the melody, and it is from the side of Binah, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance:

Plague [נגע, nega] is what the husk called evil is called; and the evil is Lilith, and nega is above her. And there is a nega which is "the plagues of the children of men" (2 Sam. 7:14), which are the demons that Adam begot in the hundred and thirty years that he separated from his wife; and they pursue the children of men, to lead them astray and to make them go whoring at night in nocturnal emission; and they appear to them in the likeness of women, and they have no hair. And it is the reverse of oneg [delight]; and of this it is said, "There is nothing above oneg and nothing below nega"; for "God has made the one over against the other" (Eccl. 7:14). And oneg we shall explain in its entry, with the help of the Rock and His salvation:

Nobles [נדיבים, nedivim]: the Patriarchs are so called, for they are generous to the poor man and the poor woman, Tzaddik and Tzedek, and give them abundant effluence with a good eye. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 3a) on the verse (Ps. 47:10), "The nobles of the peoples are gathered together." And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. It is found that Gedulah, Gevurah and Tiferet, when they bestow upon these in the time of their poverty, are called nobles:

Vow [נדר, neder]: what is agreed in all places is that the vow is in Binah. And he said (Rashbi, in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Mishpatim, fols. 115–116a) that for this reason they instituted "All Vows" [Kol Nidrei] on Yom Kippur, which is Binah. And therefore they said, "An oath does not take effect except on a thing that has substance"; because the oath is in Malkhut, and the oath itself is [supported] on Yesod, as it is written (Ruth 3:13), "As YHVH lives; lie down until the morning": that is, Yesod.

And behold, it takes effect on a thing that has substance, that is, Yesod, on which Malkhut is supported. And from its side she is called shevu'ah [oath], for all the attributes are called sevens in it, as we shall explain in the entry shevu'ah. And let us return to our matter: for the vow takes effect on a thing that does not depend on substance; but on the contrary, all the days of the circuit are nourished from her. And therefore they said, "vows take effect upon oaths"; for so she rises over all seven sefirot, and she crouches over them and hovers over them like a mother over the children. And so they said, "The release of vows flies in the air" (Chagigah 10a); and we explained in its entry that Tiferet is also called avir [air], and Binah flies over it. All this Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained.

And further, Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that for this reason the vow is in the language "behold, it is upon me," to hint that she hovers over seven days. And so Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that the language of neder is from the language of dirah [dwelling], for she dwells upon the circuit; and likewise also the language of deror [liberty] and freedom. And because she covers over the children, he said, "as though he vowed by the life of the King": the explanation, King, Tiferet; life, Binah, which covers over it and gives it life. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 255a) there is another explanation of all this inquiry; and it appears from there, according to his method, that the vow is in Chokhmah; and it needs explanation. And this is what is agreed by the mouth of all: that the vow is in Binah:

River [נהר, nahar]: on the verse (Gen. 2:10), "And a river went out of Eden," Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 55, fol. 85) different explanations of the word nahar: an explanation of the river in Chokhmah, an explanation of the river in Binah, an explanation of the river in Tiferet, and an explanation of the river in Yesod. And some of these explanations we explained in the preceding gates; and now we shall explain this matter clearly, without stammering. Sometimes Binah is called river; and then she is called "the river whose waters do not cease," to hint that it always flows and always goes out and never ceases; therefore she is called "that flows and goes out." However, Binah is so called when she bestows, in her aspect, upon the building. And sometimes Yesod too is called "the river that flows and goes out"; and one must judge according to the matter. However, "river" without qualification is sometimes what Yesod is called; and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 193b), on the verse (Gen. 41:1), "and behold, he stood by the river." And sometimes Tiferet too is called the river of fire [nehar dinur] (Dan. 7:10), from the side of its drawing nourishment from the side of Gevurah; and the river of its streams [nehar pelagav], from the side of Chesed, which hints at the abundance of the waters, as "streams of water" (Ps. 1:3). And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in one place. And elsewhere (in the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 4a) he explained that Yesod has two names, after the manner of Tiferet: the river of fire and the river of its streams. And he added further (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 247a) that from the side of the three first ones, through Tiferet, which draws them down upon its head, it is called the river Chebar [nehar kevar] (Ezek. 1:3); and the explanation of kevar: Kaf, Keter; Bet, Binah; Resh, Reshit, Chokhmah. And we explained a comely saying on this matter in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 5. Further, he explained there that these three names are in Metatron: the river of its streams, the river of fire and the river Chebar. And he said that Tiferet, from the two extremes, is called "the rivers, the brooks of honey and butter" (Job 20:17); and the intent is that the honey is from the side of Gevurah, in its redness, and the butter from the side of the right, in its whiteness; and it is included of both of them, and from their aspect it is so called. Further, his intent there is to explain that the seven sefirot, from the side of Chesed, are called seven rivers. And elsewhere he explained that Chokhmah and Binah are called rivers from the direction of Tiferet; and of them it is said (Ps. 93:3), "The rivers have lifted up their voice":

Brightness [נוגה, nogah]: we explained in the entry esh [fire] that Malkhut, from the side of Netzach and Hod, is called esh nogah [bright fire]: fire from the side of Hod, which inclines to Gevurah and its judgment; and nogah from the side of Netzach, which inclines to Chesed and its whiteness; and the brightness is a fire white as clean wool. And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 112b) he explained that Binah is called nogah from the side of Chesed. It is found that nogah is always on the right, from the side of Chesed; and from this direction Netzach is so called:

Habitation [נוה, naveh]: Malkhut is called naveh because she is the house and habitation of Tiferet. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Acharei (fol. 74b), on the verse (Jer. 25:30), "He shall mightily roar upon His habitation." And so it is said (Isa. 33:20), "Jerusalem, a quiet habitation." And it is possible to say that the letter Nun and the letter Heh are hinted in Malkhut, and the letter Vav in Tiferet, which dwells within the habitation:
Flowing streams [נוזלים, nozelim]: he explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 201b–

202a) on the verse (Song 4:15), "and flowing streams from Lebanon," that the five sefirot, that is, Gevurah, Hod and Netzach and Chesed, and body and covenant counted as one, are five. And when these five receive from the three first ones, which are all called by the name Lebanon, and bestow below, they are called nozelim: the explanation, that they make flow the pure waters that are bestowed from above to Malkhut:

The pleasantness of YHVH [נועם ה', no'am YHVH] (Ps. 27:4): the effluence that is bestowed to Malkhut from Keter by way of Chokhmah, and from Chokhmah to Binah, and from Binah to Malkhut by way of the rungs of the ladder, is so called. So they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shelach (fol. 161a

and Beshalach, fol. 56). And it is known that the principal of the pleasantness is in Binah, and nevertheless it comes from above, that is, from Keter; and in Binah the name no'am is given to it; and from Binah the pleasantness is bestowed to Malkhut, as we explained. And in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 142b), he said that the pleasantness of YHVH is the beauty of Jacob; and the explanation, the upper effluence that is bestowed upon Tiferet. And it is possible that it is the very same effluence that is also bestowed upon Malkhut, and all from within Binah, through Keter, which bestows in her, as we explained. And so it is explained in Parashat Miketz (fol. 197b): that the pleasantness is the effluence of the freedom of Binah, which shines for all the sefirot, and is bestowed to Malkhut through the Patriarchs:

Keeping mercy for thousands [נוצר חסד לאלפים, notzer chesed la-alafim] (Exod. 34:7): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is in Tiferet; and we have no proof for this matter, and he too did not write a reason for it. And there is one who explained that Binah is called notzer chesed, for the reason that she keeps mercy from the Sabbatical cycle that has passed for this Sabbatical cycle, and from this one to another; and so she does always. These are his words; and it does not settle (see the book Me'orei Or):

Awesome [נורא, nora] is Tiferet, and so all agreed. And there is a proof from the language of the Tikkunim that it is so called from the side of Gevurah. And the sense of the language shows this; for its explanation is from the language of fear and dread; and there is no fear except from the side of Fear [Pachad]:

Who bears iniquity [נושא עון, nose avon] (Exod. 34:7): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it in Tiferet, and did not give a reason for it. And there is one who explained it in Gevurah. And in the Zohar it is proved that it is in Yesod; and the reason is that the iniquity blemishes up to Yesod; and therefore it must be borne [the iniquity] from there:

Noah [נח, Noach]: Yesod is so called. And the reason is that Noah is a chariot for it; therefore he entered the ark, because he was united with her in a complete union. And of him it is said (Gen. 6:9), "a righteous man, perfect"; and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained that he was born circumcised. And he is called Noah, the language of menuchah [rest], for through it Malkhut finds rest, as we spoke at length in the Gate of Channels, chapter 4.

And further, for through it the effluence descends, as the Targum renders "and he went down," ve-nechat. And it is found according to these explanations that it is so called when it is united with Malkhut in the secret of Tiferet; and then the world is in rest and comfort, as it is written (Gen. 5:29), "Noah, saying, This one shall comfort us":

Sweet savour [ניחוח, nicho'ach]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 224a) that the effluence that descends from Chokhmah to Chesed, and from Chesed is drawn to Gevurah to quench the smoky fire that burns, is called nicho'ach. And he said that this is the re'ach nicho'ach; and it is explained in its entry:

Stream [נחל, nachal]: the commentators explained that Chesed is called the first stream, and Gevurah the second stream, and so all of them to the end of the Emanation. And the reason is that Binah is the great sea; of her it is written (Isa. 11:15), "and shall smite it into seven streams." However, the streams are what the seven branches are called that are drawn from Chesed, the foundation of the waters, as we explained. And the language of nachal and nahar is only from the side of Tiferet, which is called Vav, drawn out like a stream. And Tiferet is called the ancient stream [nachal kedumim] (Judg. 5:21); and Rashbi explained (in the Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55, fol. 85a) that from the side of Binah and Chokhmah it is called the ancient stream. And the reason is that there it is called kedem, as will be explained in its entry, with the help of the Name. And from the side of Keter, in the union of Chokhmah and Binah, it is called the stream of Your delights [nachal adanekha] (Ps. 36:9), a stream from the upper delights; however, the principal of the Eden is Keter, as we explained and as we shall explain in its entry. And there is a difference between nahar and nachal: for nachal is called what flows with water at times, even if they are far apart; but nahar is called what flows always and does not cease. And because the drawing of nourishment of Tiferet from the three first ones is not so constant, it is called nachal, for it appears that it has a cessation; but its drawing of nourishment from the right and from the left is never lacking; therefore it is called nahar from their side, as we explained in its entry, with the help of the Name. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 60b) he explained that nachal without qualification is Yesod, on the verse (1 Sam. 17:40), "and David took five smooth stones out of the stream"; see there. An inheritance without boundaries [nachalah beli metzarim]: Binah is so called; and the reason is that up to there reaches the cry of the dogs, in their crying "Hav, hav!" [Give, give!], as we shall explain in the Gate of Substitutes; but in Binah the cry and accusation of the oppressing adversaries [tzarim] does not reach there. So all the commentators explained. And to me it appears that metzarim is from the language of metzar [boundary]; and the thing that is apprehended has boundaries, which is the fence of the border; but in Binah, and from Binah upward, there is no apprehension at all, and she is not bounded; and therefore she is called "an inheritance without boundaries," for she has no border. And Tiferet is sometimes called an inheritance, etc.; and the reason is when it rises above into Binah; and then this inheritance is called "the inheritance of Jacob your father" (Isa. 58:14), which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat 118a) as an inheritance without boundaries. And in the Zohar, Parashat Chukkat (fol. 182a), on the verse (Eccl. 7:11), "Wisdom is good with an inheritance," he explained that the inheritance is the Righteous One, the Foundation of the World. And it is called inheritance because it is the effluence that descends from Tiferet to Malkhut, that is, the inheritance of Malkhut. And it is understood there that this title is borrowed for it, and is not the principal of its titles:

Strand [נימא, nima]: Yesod is called nima, just as it is called "the hair's thread"; and of it it is said, "between the upper waters and the lower waters there is only as much as the full of a strand" (see Tikkun 19, fols. 36–37a). And it is called nima because it is Vav, and on it hang the strings of the harp: for the harp is Malkhut, and the strings are the threads, which are five sefirot that hang on Yesod, after the likeness of Tiferet. And by them is the melody of the harp, through the bestowal of a number of strings like the number of the sefirot and branches that are in Yesod, according to the whole of the harp: sometimes in seven, sometimes in eight, sometimes in ten (as is found in Arakhin 13b and Tanchuma, Parashat Beha'alotekha; see there):
Banner [נס, nes]: in the Tikkunim it is understood that Yesod, when it is above Netzach and Hod, is called nes, for it stands over them as a banner:
Shoe [נעל, na'al]: Metatron, when he is a covering and garment for the Shekhinah, is called shoe. And we explained this matter at length in the Gate of ABYA:

Youth [נער, na'ar]: Metatron is called na'ar. And the reason is that he serves the service of a youth before the Shekhinah; for through him she distributes food to all the companies of the angels and to the lower world. And of the verse (Ps. 37:25), "I have been young [na'ar], and now am old," they said in the Gemara (Yevamot 16b): "The Prince of the World said this verse." And he is called na'ar specifically when he serves the service of a youth. However, sometimes he serves the service of an elder; and that is when Malkhut is locked [ne'ulah] within him. And therefore Eliezer, when he went to make the match of Rebecca, was called "his servant, the elder of his house" (Gen. 24:2). And the Shekhinah too is called na'ar, in the secret of na'ar [written for] na'arah [maiden]; and she is called na'ar while she has not yet received the male, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And sometimes Yesod too is called na'ar after her name; for just as the female is sometimes called by the name of the male, so the male is sometimes called by the name of the female; so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayeshev (fol. 182b). And sometimes two are called youths: the two lower cherubim, Metatron and Sandalfon; and sometimes the upper cherubim, Netzach and Hod. For these are over against those: when the Shekhinah rises above, the Netzachs are called youths serving beneath the Shekhinah; and when she is below, the youths are Metatron and Sandalfon:

Soul [נפש, nefesh] without qualification is Malkhut; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 87). And sometimes she is called living soul [nefesh chayyah], and so he explained in the Tikkunim. And the reason she is called living soul may be that from her is the quarry of the souls; and she is called living because she draws the effluence of the upper life of Chokhmah, on which the life depends; and she is called nefesh in the secret that she receives upon herself the ru'ach and the neshamah, which are Tiferet and Binah. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained living soul in Yesod, and it is not to the point. And sometimes Malkhut is called the additional soul [nefesh yeterah], when it is the Sabbath day, and she is included of ten and is included to rise above in the secret of the Sabbath of Sabbaths [Shabbat Shabbaton]; then she is called additional, for she is additional in ascent, additional in illumination. And likewise Malkhut is called the soul of David, because she is his attribute; so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 171a) (see Asis Rimmonim):

Standing [נצב, nitzav]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 150a), that the union and bond of the sefirot that are united with Tiferet, from Yesod and upward, Yesod not included, is called nitzav: that is, as ["a deputy (nitzav) was king"] (1 Kings 22:48). And it is possible that Tiferet itself is called nitzav for this reason, as he says (Gen. 28:13), "And behold, YHVH," that is, Tiferet, "stood [nitzav]." And somewhat this is understood from the language of the Zohar there:

Netzach [נצח, netzach, Eternity, Victory]: it is already known that the seventh attribute from above to below is called Netzach; and the reason is that it is the attribute of the victory [nitzachon] of the world, and on account of this it is called Netzach. And sometimes they call this attribute eternity of eternities [netzach netzachim]. And the reason is that each and every attribute also has aspects: an aspect that receives, and the aspect of itself, and an aspect that bestows. And these three aspects we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof Is Keter.

And behold, the middle aspect is the principal of Netzach, and the two extreme ones are called Netzachs; and likewise in Hod, Hods. And therefore it is said in the Zohar of these two, "his legs are pillars of marble [shesh]" (Song 5:15): for they are six [shesh] joints that are in the legs, these six aspects, as we explained. And sometimes this attribute is called the Eternal One of Israel [Netzach Yisra'el] (1 Sam. 15:29): when it cleaves to the body, then it is called Netzach Yisra'el:

Blossoms [נצנים, nitzanim] (Song 2:12): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Bereshit (fol. 1) that Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, at the beginning of their rising in the Thought, are called nitzanim. And the reason is that there is the beginning of their sprouting; and this is nitzanim, which is the beginning of the sprouting:

The vengeance of the covenant [נקם ברית, nekam berit] (Lev. 26:25): Malkhut is so called because she takes the vengeance of the one who profanes his covenant; because he separates the Chief [Aluf] from her, for they are united through the upper covenant, as is known. And therefore the vengeance of the covenant depends on her:

The lamp of YHVH [נר ה', ner YHVH]: the Shekhinah is called ner [lamp] for the reason that she is the lamp that receives the upper light.
