And she is so called when she is a vessel prepared to receive the upper light; and when she has already received the light and been kindled, she is called the lamp of YHVH, whose explanation is that she has already received upon herself the light of Tiferet. And she is called the lamp of the commandment [ner mitzvah] (Prov. 6:23); and it is all one, near to one another; for mitzvah is YHVH [in AT-BaSh], as we explained in its entry. And the flame of the lamp: there are in the Tikkunim two explanations. One, from Gevurah, which is fire; and one from the side of Chesed, which is light. And the third explanation: that it is included of three lights, as they explained [in the words of] the House of Hillel (Berakhot, chapter 8) on "the lights of the fire" [me'orei ha-esh]; and they are the three Patriarchs, white and red and green. And there is no doubt that the three lights of the lamp are from the side of Gevurah, for they are "the lights of the fire"; and so he explained in the Tikkunim. And he explained there (in Tikkun 21, fol. 54) that the Shekhinah is a lamp burning before Tiferet from the side of Gevurah:

Spikenard [נרד, nerd], and likewise nirdi (Song 1:12): he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 61), that it is in Yesod. And we copied his language in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 17:

Lofty [נשא, nissa]: the explanation, "high and lofty" (Isa. 57:15): there are those who explained Tiferet, and there are those who explained Keter. And according to what appears from the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory (in Tanchuma, end of Parashat Toledot), in their saying, "He shall be exalted more than Abraham, and lofty more than Isaac" (on Isa. 52:13); and he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayeshev (fol. 181b), that it is Binah, as we explained in the entry yarum: if so, it will be in Binah, which is over Gevurah. And see the entry ram, for there we spoke at length:

Kiss [נשיקה, neshikah]: the matter of kisses is in the arousal of the love between Tiferet and Malkhut; and there are no kisses except in their union; but in the union of Chokhmah and Binah there are no kisses. And the kisses are the cleaving of spirit to spirit, as is explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance:

Additional soul [נשמה יתירה, neshamah yeterah]: in every place neshamah without qualification is Binah, for from there is the quarry of the souls, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 243a) he explained that the additional soul is Keter. And we have nothing to explain except that we say that when Binah is called the additional soul, it is when she is united with Chokhmah and Keter; and she is called the additional soul from the side of Keter, for it is the surplus over the soul (see Tikkun 24, fol. 67, and these are his words: "for the additional soul, which is the upper Shekhinah," etc.):

Eagle [נשר, nesher]: all the commentators, and some of the sayings of the Zohar, agree that the face of the eagle is in Malkhut. However, in the Tikkunim, in many places, he explained the reverse of this: that the eagle is in Tiferet. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (fol. 80b), and proved it from the verse (Prov. 30:19), "the way of an eagle in the heavens." And therefore it appears to us that the eagle is always in Malkhut; however, Malkhut is called eagle when she stands above in her place, before the accusation. And there is "the way of an eagle in the heavens": the explanation, the place of the eagle, even though she is below on the earth, yet her place is in the heavens. And by this they explained in the Tikkunim that from the side of Tiferet Malkhut is called eagle, and proved it from the verse "the way of an eagle in the heavens." And elsewhere he said that she is called eagle from the side of the Throne, which is Beriah, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA. And the reason may be that on Sabbaths and festivals she and Yesod are clothed in Beriah, as we explained there; and then she is called eagle from the side of Tiferet. And elsewhere (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 111b) he explained that Binah is called "the great eagle with the wings" (Ezek. 17:3); and of her it is said (Deut. 32:11), "As an eagle that stirs up her nest," etc.; and the wings are six wings, six sefirot:

Paths [נתיבות, netivot]: it has already been explained in the Gate of Paths that the paths are thirty-two and they are in Chokhmah. And they are called wondrous paths [netivot pela'ot] because they are concealed, from the language of "wondrous" and "covered"; and we have already spoken at length in the gate mentioned. And the paths are a title for concealed channels. And the substance of Chokhmah he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 256b): that it is the highest path of all, which includes them all; and of it it is said (Job 28:7), "the path that no bird of prey knows"; and all the paths draw from it, and it is the first of the thirty-two, as we explained there. Thus far is concluded the entry of the Nun, with the help of God who bestows upon us from His good effluence. And now we shall come to the explanation of the entry of the letter Samekh, with the help of Heaven.

The Elder of Elders [סבא דסבין, Saba de-Savin]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 3a) that it is in Chokhmah; and in the Zohar he explained that Keter is so called. And all of it points to concealment; for it shows that Chokhmah is concealed in Keter, where the principal of old age is, as we explained in the entry zaken. And Binah is called the Grandmother of Grandmothers [Savta de-Savtin]; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 72b). And the matter is that she is so called in the secret of her manifestation and her source, which is concealed in Keter and Chokhmah; for there her manifestation is concealed. And just as Chokhmah is called the Elder of Elders in the secret of Keter, as we explained, so Binah, in the secret of her concealed manifestation, is called the Grandmother of Grandmothers; for she is female with respect to Chokhmah:

The Cause of Causes [סבת הסבות, sibbat ha-sibbot]: Keter too is called the Cause of Causes. And there is a difference between the Cause of Causes and the Cause of all Causes; and we explained it in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof Is Keter, and there we spoke at length:

Treasure [סגולה, segullah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 127a), that Malkhut is called the treasure of Tiferet. And the reason may be that in her he treasures up and stores away all his good effluence. And it is possible that she is so called in the secret of her drawing nourishment, through Tiferet, from the segol, which is the three Patriarchs, or according to the explanation that we explained in the Gate of Vowels; or in the secret of drawing nourishment from the segolta, which is the three first ones, or according to the explanation that we explained in the Gate of Cantillation Marks on the matter of the segolta:

The order of times [סדר זמנים, seder zemanim] are Tiferet and Malkhut, which are the attribute of day and the attribute of night; and in them the whole circuit is included. And because they preceded in the Thought, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 3): "This teaches that there was an order of times before this":

Secret [סוד, sod]: the Righteous One is called sod. And the reason is that sod is the gathering; and so the Righteous One is the gathering of all the effluence, and from there it is bestowed to Malkhut. And because the effluence is gathered and closed up in it, it is called sod, which comes to [the value of] yayin [wine]: the wine kept in its grapes, in which there is keeping:

Booth [סוכה, sukkah]: on the sukkah the explanations of Rashbi, peace be upon him, are many. In one place (in the Zohar, Vayishlach, fol. 172b) he explained that sukkah is Malkhut, and she is also called sukkatah. And elsewhere (in Tikkun 21, fol. 55a) he explained: Kaf-Vav, Heh-Samekh; the explanation, Kaf-Vav [26] is the name YHVH, and Heh-Samekh [65] the name Adonai; and both together come to sukkah. And although sukkah is written defective, nevertheless there is authority for the reading and there is authority for the written tradition. And elsewhere (Pinchas, fol. 255b) he said that sukkah is Binah, which covers [mesakekhet] over her children. And it seems to me to make a compromise in the matter: for sukkah is the joining of Tiferet with Malkhut, and its principal is Malkhut. That is to say: even though sometimes the joining of Tiferet and Malkhut is through the arousal of the male, and the male is the principal and the female is concealed in the male, in the sukkah the matter is the reverse; for the principal of the union is in the female, and the female is revealed and the male concealed. And therefore their joining is mentioned by the name of the female. And this is sukkah, Kaf-Vav Heh-Samekh, which is  Y A H D V N H Y, which shows their joining. And because when they join they enter the bridal canopy, and they enter and are raised into Binah in the secret of the six concealed extremities in her; and that is their manifestation, the sukkah: east, west, north and south, above and below. And they are a sukkah below in their place, and they are concealed and are a sukkah above. We are found to learn that the principal of the sukkah is in Binah, that is, the six extremities concealed in her. And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 6, fol. 21a, and Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 127a) he explained that Binah is called the tabernacle of peace [sukkat shalom], for she covers over peace, which is Tiferet, as will be explained in its entry:

End [סוף, sof]: he explained in the Tikkunim that the Righteous One is sof; and every place where sof and ketz come, it is in the Righteous One. And the reason is that Malkhut is not truly the end of the Emanation, even though she is below; for because of her diminishment she descended. However, the end and limit of the Emanation is the Righteous One. And even though in the entry yam suf we wrote that Malkhut is so called because she is the end of all the rungs, it is not difficult at all; for she can already be called sof with respect to her being the end after the diminishment. And therefore there are those who called her the end of the building, for she is the end of all six extremities:

Merchant [סחרת, socheret]: Chokhmah, when she is revealed in Binah, is called socheret. And the explanation is from the language of sechorah [merchandise]: for in her all the creatures in the world were created; therefore she is socheret, for from her the merchandise goes out, as it is written (Ps. 104:24), "In wisdom You have made them all." And it is also from the language of going round, for she goes round all the circuit that is in Binah. And we have already explained this matter at length in the Gate of Titles, with the help of Heaven:
Moon [סיהרא, sihara], meaning yare'ach: the Shekhinah is so called while she is sometimes full, sometimes lacking, as we explained in the entry yare'ach:

Clinging [סירכא, sirkha]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Tzav, fol. 28b, and in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Ki Tetze, fol. 282a) that the husk, when it takes hold of the Shekhinah and does not let her go up before the King, YHVH of hosts, because it claims judgment for the iniquities of Israel, then that husk is called sirkha; for it clings [mesarekhet] and takes hold of "the face of the throne" (Job 26:9), so that she does not go up to heaven. And then, through the iniquity of the generation, it becomes her mistress, as in "and a handmaid that is heir to her mistress" (Prov. 30:23). And this is the language of sirkha, from the language of "three presidents [sarekhin]" (Dan. 6:3). The help of Heaven [סיעתא דשמיא, siyata di-shemaya]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a) that every term of siyu'a [help] is Malkhut from the side of Tiferet, which receives from Gedulah when Chokhmah is in it. And he explained there that of them it is said (1 Kings 8; 2 Chron. 6), "then hear You in heaven":

Basket [סל, sal]: many of the commentators explained it in Malkhut in most places; and so she is a basket and a receptacle for all the Emanation. And likewise she is called the basket of unleavened bread (Lev. 8:2; Num. 6:17), for ten unleavened loaves are placed within her:

Selah [סלה, selah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it in Malkhut, and did not give it a reason. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 20), he explained on the verse (Ps. 32:5), "and You forgave the iniquity of my sin, Selah": "This is above, above, the place where the Holy Ancient One dwells." Thus far his words.

And according to the beginning of his words there, it is understood that the Holy Ancient One that he speaks of is Chokhmah, and the place of the Ancient One is Binah; and the explanation of selah is the hint to Binah when she is united with Chokhmah:

Forgiveness [סליחה, selichah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that the forgiveness is in Tiferet, and it forgives in the secret of the compassion that is in it. And some explain the forgiveness in the Supreme Crown; therefore Yom Kippur is a day of forgiveness, by the power of Keter, which flows upon her. And it is possible that for this reason too the matter of forgiveness will be in Tiferet.

And the matter of forgiveness is that the sin blemishes and darkens the light of the sefirah; and when the one who forgives strengthens his light and mends and illuminates that place, then that is the matter of forgiveness, and it is forgiven him:

Ladder [סלם, sullam]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 149a), that the Righteous One is so called; and it is "set up on the earth" (Gen. 28:12), Malkhut, "and its top reached to heaven," Tiferet. However, in the Ra'aya Meheimna he explained that the ladder is Tiferet; and the reason is that through it is the ascent of Malkhut and the extremities up to the Ein Sof. And likewise it is "set up on the earth," Malkhut, "and its top reached heavenward [ha-shamaymah]," which is Binah, for she is called more "heavenward." And it is all one matter; for Tiferet and the Righteous One, body and covenant, are counted as one. And both of them are a ladder, for by way of them is her ascent above, for there is no ascent apart from them; and therefore "ladder" is right for both of them:

Rock [סלע, sela]: in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 279b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that there are two kinds of sela. The first is the sela, the King's daughter; it is the rib [tzela], the bride of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. And therefore it is said (Num. 20:8), "and speak to the rock": with speech and appeasement, as to a King's daughter. However, there is another sela, and it is the manifestation of Beriah, which is called handmaid and is called mishneh, as we explained in its entry; and it is the throne that we explained in the Gate of ABYA:

Fine flour [סלת, solet]: Malkhut is so called when she is clean of all the depths that are beneath her, as fine flour is clean of bran, which are the husks that surround the brain. And she is so called when she wishes to rise to be united above, between the arms of the world; and then she is called "mingled with oil" (Lev. 2:5), the good oil, through the Righteous One; and then she is adorned and a good savour rises, to be united. So it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 247a); and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 248), on the verse (Gen. 49:27), "in the morning he shall devour the prey." And she is called "the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour" (Lev. 5:11), because she is the tenth, as we shall explain in its entry:

Sandal [סנדל, sandal]: the sandal is Sandalfon, who is a sandal for Tiferet when Malkhut is locked in the shoe, which is Metatron. For then necessarily Tiferet is clothed in the sandal, and the union is not complete; for he is in his garment and she in her garment; and the law is that they compel him to divorce:

The Great and Small Sanhedrin [סנהדרי גדולה וקטנה, sanhedrei gedolah u-ketanah]: the Great is in Binah, revealed in Tiferet. And the reason is that the seventy of the Sanhedrin are seventy branches that are in Tiferet; for they are seven sefirot, each one included of ten, behold seventy; and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is the secret of Da'at, behold seventy-one; and the whole that includes the seventy, they are seventy-two. And the Small Sanhedrin is in Malkhut, for there is the Chamber of Hewn Stone, as we explained in its entry. And there are times when they relate the Great Sanhedrin and the Small Sanhedrin as being in Malkhut, for there is their chamber, as we explained in its entry. And there are times when they relate the Great to Chesed and the Small to Gevurah; and it is no wonder, for it is known that Binah is toward the right, in Gedulah, and Malkhut toward the left, in Gevurah:

The great and the small meal [סעודה גדולה וקטנה, se'udah gedolah u-ketanah]: the great meal is from the side of Binah, the great Heh; and the small meal is from the side of Malkhut, the small Heh. And therefore, concerning Shavu'ot, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said that the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "I and you shall make a small meal":

Storm [סער, sa'ar] shows the force of judgment: sometimes the inner, sometimes the outer. The inner, such as se'arah [tempest], which is one of the attributes of Malkhut and shows judgment; and of this it is said (Job 38:1), "Then YHVH answered Job out of the tempest" [min ha-se'arah, read as] with a bent Nun, which is hinted to her. And the outer: "For He breaks me with a tempest," etc. (Job 9:17). And all of it shows the force of judgment; and likewise "the sea grew more and more tempestuous" (Jonah 1:11):

The counting of the Omer [ספירת העומר, sefirat ha-omer]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 16, fol. 37a) that Malkhut is called the counting of the Omer; for in her one counts seven days, which are "seven Sabbaths," etc., which are forty-nine days. And it appears according to this that she is called menorah when her seven lamps shine, each and every lamp included of seven other lamps:

Book [ספר, sefer]: sefer, sefar, sippur (another version: sippur): the principal of these things has already been explained in the Gate of Paths, chapter 1. And we would already have spoken at length on other explanations besides the one we explained there; but that explanation is fine flour, and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained it in the Zohar, as we explained there:

And there is the Book of Life [sefer ha-chayyim]; and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 31a) that the Righteous One, from the side of Binah, is called the Book of Life. And he explained that Binah bestows the life that is bestowed to her from Chokhmah, from above, from the source of life; and they bestow to the Righteous One; and there they come into being, a revealed being, in a thing that is bounded in a book by means of writing. And therefore the Righteous One, in its receiving the life from Binah, is called the Book of Life.

And further there is the Torah scroll [sefer Torah], and it is Tiferet; and it is called the Torah scroll when it is included of all six hundred and thirteen commandments: two hundred and forty-eight positive commandments from the side of Gedulah, and three hundred and sixty-five from the side of Gevurah; and it bounds them and includes them in itself, and is called the Torah scroll. However, its palace is in Binah; and so it is explained in the Zohar (Shelach, fol. 164a) in the explanation of the verse (Prov. 18:10), "The name of YHVH is a tower of strength." And from within this inner palace it goes out and is united within her (that is, in the Assembly of Israel), as it is written (Gen. 2:24), "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave to his wife." And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Hod is called the Book of the Wars of YHVH (Num. 21:14), because from it the wars go out, from the side of Gevurah. And the entry of the letter Samekh is completed, with the help of the Rock of Israel; and now we shall begin the explanation of the entry of the letter Ayin, with the help of Heaven:

Cloud [עב, av] is Chesed; and so chesed comes in numerical value to av, seventy-two. And to this hints "Behold, I come to you in the thick cloud [be-av he-anan]" (Exod. 19:9); and it is the power and emanation of the Name of Seventy-Two. And of it it is said (Isa. 19:1), "Behold, YHVH rides upon a swift cloud [av kal]." It is found that av is Chesed, when it is in the seventy-two bridges, as is known:

Servant [עבד, eved]: Malkhut is so called. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Kedoshim (fol. 86a), that the upper David is called servant, on the verse (Isa. 43:10), "and My servant whom I have chosen." And in the Tikkunim he explained that every term of servitude and service is a hint at the servant, who is Metatron, who is the one who serves and the servant; and from his side a man must make himself as a servant:

The service of the Levites [עבודת הלוים, avodat ha-levi'im]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 221b), that Binah is called the service of the Levites, in the secret of the song, as it is said (Num. 18:23), "and the Levite shall do the service," as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And he explained there a further explanation: that Malkhut is called the service of the Levites, in the secret that they would carry the Tabernacle on the shoulder from place to place (see the Zohar Chadash, Chukkat, fol. 60: it is explained that Malkhut is called service):

Round [עגולה, agullah]: Binah is so called, for she is like a circle, in which there is no grasping at all; which is not so below in the building, in which there is grasping, as it were. And even when she sits upon her children she is square [meruba'at], that is, crouching [rovetzet], as the Targum renders it revi'a. And so we explained above in the entry afarsemon, that she is round, a closed Samekh, when she rises above; but below, upon her children, a square Mem, which shows the bestowal, and that the mother crouches on the nest, hovering over her children:

Calf [עגל, egel]: it seems to me that it is from the side of Gevurah, like the matter of the ox. And eglah [heifer] is Malkhut from the side of judgment. However, they will hint at the powers of judgment close to these:

Until / Witness [עד, ad]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 247b), that Malkhut is called ad, whether she is united with Tiferet or whether she is below in her place. And the reason may be that up to her [adeha] the Emanation reached, and no further; and she is the end of the rungs; and when she rises above in union with her husband she is also called ad. And this is what he said there: "And this ad, so too above, so it is called." And the reason is that then ad is in the language of edah [congregation]; and therefore she is always called ad. And somewhat it is understood there that ad is also in Binah. And it is possible that it is also in Malkhut when she is with Tiferet; and that is "return unto [ad]" (Deut. 30:2; Hos. 14:2). And in Parashat Bereshit he explained that Yesod too is called ad; and it is possible for two reasons that he explained: that it is the place up to which the Emanation reached at first, before the diminishment; or because up to it reached the emanation of the world of the male, and from it downward is the world of the female. For Binah is the world of the male, as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 246a); and from Yesod upward all is male. Or because through it is the union, that is, ad [witness], as we explained:

Congregation [עדה, edah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 155b), that edah is Malkhut. And the reason is that south and north and east, which are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, gather and assemble [mitva'adim] in the secret of the union. And so he explained there, "and My testimony [edoti] that I shall teach them" (Ps. 132:12): that the word edoti is from the language of edah:

Testimony [עדות, edut] is the matter of the union. And do not read edut but de'ot [knowledges]; and they are Tiferet and the Righteous One, for both of them are de'ot, from the language of joining. The Righteous One is testimony between Tiferet and Malkhut, and Tiferet is between Chokhmah and Binah; and we have already spoken at length on this in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof Is Keter. And in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 221b), he explained that the letters Yod-Heh are testimony, and on them is the sustaining of all the worlds, as in the matter of "for in Yah YHVH is an everlasting rock" (Isa. 26:4). And it is possible that through them is the coming into being of the testimony, which is Da'at, which is Vav: Abba and Imma, Yod-Heh, Yod-Heh-Vav:

Eden [עדן, Eden]: there are many Edens, and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained them in the Tikkunim. However, he explained explicitly that the principal Eden, and the one that settles best, is the Supreme Crown; and the other places are by way of borrowing. And these are his words in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 11a): "And there is no Eden but the Supreme Crown, which is wondrous and covered; and because of this it is said of it, 'Eye has not seen, O God, beside You' (Isa. 64:3)." Thus far. Behold, he spoke in the language of negation, "and there is no Eden," etc. And one cannot say that "and there is no Eden" mentioned here is like "there is no …" as we say in the Talmud [that is, a statement of emphasis rather than of exclusion]; from the fact that he lengthened on the matter to decide that Eden is right only of Keter: for of Eden it is said, "Eye has not seen, O God, beside You"; and since that is so, the name Eden is right only of the Supreme Crown, which is wondrous and covered, and in which there is no apprehension at all. And the explanation of "Eye has not seen, O God": the intent is that Elohim is Binah, and there is none who can look with the eye except Binah. And by way of borrowing, Chokhmah and Binah are called Eden; and it is more right of Chokhmah than of Binah. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 55, fol. 85a): "'And a river went out of Eden' (Gen. 2:10): there is an Eden and there is an Eden. As it is written, 'and You make them drink of the stream of Your delights [adanekha]' (Ps. 36:9). Adanekha: certainly the upper Eden, the Supreme Crown. The lower Eden: this is Yod. And there is an Eden below, and this is the upper Mother; she is Eden with respect to the river below her; as it is written, 'And a river went out of Eden to water.'" Thus far his words, as relevant to our matter. And he was precise in his language in saying "there is an Eden and there is an Eden": because the verse says "the stream of Your delights," in the plural; and according to what is agreed, there is no Eden except in the Supreme Crown, as we explained above; therefore he said, "there is an Eden and there is an Eden," that is to say, there are Edens, and they are not all equal. And he was precise in this, in saying "as it is written" [ha-da hu di-khetiv], and not saying "for it is written" [di-khetiv], as is his custom; rather the intent is to say ha-da hu: the explanation, with this introduction, "the stream of Your delights" in the plural is settled. "Certainly the upper Eden," etc.: the explanation, in the Supreme Crown, which is Eden, there is no doubt that this is the true Eden. And he intended to call it the Supreme Crown: the explanation, certainly Keter is not called simply Eden, since we see that it is called the Supreme Crown; and since that is so, it is fitting that it be called the upper Eden. And if so, according to this there is an Eden below it which is not called upper. And this is what he said, "The lower Eden: this is Yod": the explanation, since there is an upper Eden, the lower Eden will be Chokhmah. And because it was difficult for him that Eden shows its being concealed, as is proved from the verse "Eye has not seen, O God, beside You," therefore he said "and this is Yod"; as if to say, Chokhmah too is concealed, for the letter hinted in it is not apprehended but concealed, that is, Yod. "And there is an Eden": the explanation, there is a third Eden, and this is not Eden in substance, even in its own self; however, it is Eden with respect to the river that takes delight and goes out from it. And this is what he said, "And there is an Eden below, and this is the upper Mother": and she is not Eden with respect to herself, but she is Eden with respect to the river that takes delight and goes out from her. And the explanation of "And a river went out of Eden" will be, according to this: Tiferet is the river that goes out from Binah. And even though the language of Eden is not precise, nevertheless the language "a river went out" is precise, that is, "that goes out from Binah"; for it goes out only from Binah. The rule that emerges from these sayings is that the principal Eden is in the Supreme Crown; and in Chokhmah it is related somewhat; and Binah, after great strain; and she is called Eden with respect to the river taking delight in her. And in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 247b), on the verse "The blessings of your father," etc. (Gen. 49:26), he explained Eden in another sense, and these are his words: "What is 'from Eden'? Rather, at every time that all the limbs sit in one bond, and they are in the delight of desire from the head, above and below, and all of them, from their delight and their desire, empty into it, and it becomes a river that flows and goes out from Eden, certainly." Thus far his words. And it is all one matter; for Eden is always above. And if we say Eden below, there is no sefirah below that is called Eden, except when all the sefirot are united, one with another, from the upper head, that is, Binah, down to below; then this matter is called Eden. And the intent is that they are not [so called] with respect to their being Eden, but with respect to their taking delight of themselves, through their drawing nourishment from the head, which is Binah. And on the contrary, from the language it is understood so:

Delight [עדנה, ednah] is Malkhut, when she is filled with effluence and will from the upper Eden; and the explanation, Eden [plus] Heh. And Sarah, for the reason that ednah was drawn upon her from the Eden of the Heh, said, "After I am waxed old, shall I have delight [ednah]?" (Gen. 18:12). And he was precise in the language hayetah, a feminine form. And so he was precise in the Zohar (Shelach, fol. 170b; see there). And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Chukkat (fol. 182b), on the verse (Eccl. 4:2), "Wherefore I praised," etc., "which are yet alive [chayyim adenah]": that it is Malkhut, Eden-Heh, female:

Who passes by transgression [עובר על פשע, over al pesha] (Micah 7:18): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is in Tiferet; and he explained the reason: that it passes by transgression by the power of the compassion, like a compassionate father toward the children:

And there is who passes among them that are numbered [over al ha-pekudim] (Exod. 30:13); and he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 111a) that Netzach and Hod are called pekudim, and Yesod passes over them, as is explained in the Gate of the Emanation, chapter 4. It is found that Yesod is so called in its aspect in which it is above them:

Burnt offering [עולה, olah]: Malkhut is so called when she receives from her place by way of the rungs of the ladder, rung after rung, until she rises up to Tiferet to be with her husband; and from there both of them rise to Binah, for there is their house. And when they make these journeys she is called olah [rising]. And therefore the burnt offering is wholly given to YHVH, and others have no portion in it at all. And therefore it is said of the morning burnt offering, which is the continual burnt offering, "it is the burnt offering" (Lev. 6:2): since it has risen, it will not descend in any way in the world; which is not so with the sin offering, in which there is a descent, as it is said (Lev. 9:22), "and he came down from offering the sin offering"; and the olah always rises. These are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 247 and fol. 256b). And in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 70a), it appears that the olah is in Tiferet; for so he says there: "The olah, a male goes up, and a female does not go up, as it is written, 'he shall offer it a male without blemish' (Lev. 1:3). Why is it written isheh [offering made by fire, a feminine-looking form]? For esh [fire] must be found there. Rather, even though the olah is offered as a male, and is offered to its place, the female must not be separated from him; rather, in her it is called, in order to join this one with that one; for the female goes up to the male, to be joined as one," etc. Thus far his words. This is no difficulty at all; for there too he says that the olah is Malkhut, as we explained above from the Ra'aya Meheimna. And thus is the explanation: and if it occurs to you that the olah is hinted in Tiferet and not in Malkhut, from what is written, "he shall offer it a male without blemish," it is difficult: why is it written isheh, which is a feminine form? Let it say esh, which is a masculine form. Rather, certainly the olah is offered as a male, certainly offered to its place, that is, Tiferet; and nevertheless the principal hint is to Malkhut, who rises into the place of the male; and the explanation of olah is Malkhut, who rises to the male. And therefore the male comes to show Malkhut, who rises to the male; and it is mentioned by name only as male, for he is the principal. And now his words are right together:

World [עולם, olam]: how many worlds there are, and they are divided according to their number! Malkhut is called olam; and he explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 242a) that the explanation of the word olam means youth. And the reason: either she serves the service of a youth, or the explanation is from the language of almah, meaning maiden; because she is a beautiful maiden, a virgin, hoping to be espoused by her husband after the redemption. And in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 58), he wrote that olam written defective, without Vav, is in Malkhut; and possibly as we explained. And there is olam in Yesod; but it is not called simply olam, rather the world of the souls. And the reason is that it is the tree from which the souls blossom forth; for through it the souls blossom forth to the Shekhinah, that is, through the union. And there are those who called it the middle world; and the reason is that it is the middle and intermediate world between Tiferet and Malkhut; and it is not to the point. And Tiferet: there are those who called it the world of the building; and the reason is that the circuit, which is what is defined by the name olam, as we shall explain, Tiferet includes, as is known; for it is the master of six extremities; therefore it is fitting that it be called by the name olam. And now, there are two worlds: this world and the world to come, and it is Binah. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Kiddushin 15a): "'And he shall serve him forever [le-olam]' (Exod. 21:6): this is the world of the Jubilee"; and that is Binah. And Binah is not called olam except in the secret of the aspect of the six extremities concealed in her:

And she is called the world to come [olam ha-ba]: the explanation, that it always comes, for its effluence is never held back but comes; and therefore he said ha-ba [that comes], and did not say she-yavo [that will come]. And Malkhut too is called olam, including seven lamps, seven sefirot, in the secret of her including all the circuit. And of these two worlds it is said, "from everlasting to everlasting" [min ha-olam ve-ad ha-olam] (Ps. 106:48). And between these two worlds a middle world takes hold, and it is the secret of the six extremities themselves; however, they did not relate it by the name olam. And Malkhut is called this world because sometimes the effluence ceases from her, through our iniquities; and because of the cessation we cannot say of her "the world to come"; for "the world to come" shows the negation of cessation; and Malkhut is subject to cessation; therefore she is called "this world," whose explanation is that there is in her only what is before us alone, until YHVH has compassion and further effluence is bestowed upon her. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, fol. 62a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Tiferet is called the world to come; and these are his words: "Vav-Heh are two children, and they are this world and the world to come: Vav, the world to come, which is a long world; Heh, this world, which is not long." Thus far his words. And we can say that the principal of the world to come is Binah; and she is called the world to come from the side of her aspect of drawing the river to water the plantings that are in the garden.

And the river is Vav, and that is the long world; and it is with respect to its aspect with Binah, and going out from her. And there are those who called Binah the world of life, because she receives the upper life that is in Chokhmah and bestows it below by way of the Life [Chai, Yesod]. And according to this she is called by this name only when she bestows the power of life from Chokhmah. And others called it the world of intellect; for she is called the world of intellect in her receiving the power of the intellect from the upper intellect, which is Chokhmah, near to Keter, as we shall explain. And others called Chokhmah the world of concealment, because in it the extremities are exceedingly subtle beings; therefore they called it the world of concealment. And according to this Chokhmah is called the world of concealment only in the revealing of those subtle beings that are in it in concealment. And nevertheless it is called the world of concealment:
Depth [עומק, omek]: the author of the Sefer Yetzirah called all the sefirot depths, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof Is Keter, and there we explained the reason:

Omer [עומר, omer]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, called Binah omer in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 37a); and these are his words: "'And they measured it with an omer' (Exod. 16:18): this is the upper Shekhinah, which is an omer for the skull [gulgolet] (Exod. 16:16), which is the skull of the head." Thus far his words.

And the explanation of the word omer is from the language of immur [binding sheaves], whose explanation is the matter of gathering and binding. And behold, Binah is what sheaves and binds the three first ones within her; and that is gulgolet, for the three first ones are called gulgolet. And it is found according to this that Binah is called omer when she sheaves the three first ones:

Bird [עוף, of]: he explained in the Tikkunim that Yesod is called "the bird of the heavens," for it is a bird for Tiferet (which is called heavens); and the intent is a bird that flies and serves Tiferet. And Metatron is a bird for Malkhut, serving beneath her: as the relation of Malkhut to Tiferet, so is the relation of Metatron to Malkhut:

Young hart [עופר, ofer]: Tiferet is so called; so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 49a). And it appears that it is called ofer when it draws nourishment from the two upper harts, which are Gedulah and Gevurah, and strengthens the power of judgment; for so Malkhut is called afar [dust] from its side, as is explained there, that she is called afar in the secret of [her lower aspect], as we shall explain in its entry:

Wonder-worker [עושה פלא, oseh fele] (Exod. 15:11): Tiferet is so called from the side of Keter, which is called Pele, Alef, as is explained in their entries; so he explained in the Tikkunim. And every working of wonder is through it:

Strong [עז, az]: Gevurah is so called, the strong attribute of judgment; so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 240a), on the verse (Judg. 14:14), "and out of the strong came forth sweetness":

Strength [עוז, oz] is Tiferet. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Zevachim 116a): "and there is no oz but Torah"; it is the Written Torah, Tiferet. And it appears that it is called oz [Ayin-Zayin, 77] when it is included of seventy branches and seven sefirot. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 119a) he explained that uzzo [His strength] is the Shekhinah, the upper Mother, Binah; and of her it is said (Isa. 62:8), "and by the arm of His strength"; for Gevurah is her arm; and she is called "and the Shekhinah of His strength in the heights of the heavens"; see there:

Diadem [עטרה, atarah]: Malkhut is called diadem; and she is not so called except when she rises up to Keter; and there she is "a diadem on her husband's head" (Prov. 12:4), the diadem of Tiferet; and likewise she is a diadem on the head of every righteous one; and likewise she is the crown [taga] of the Torah scroll. And we shall speak at length on its explanation in the Gate of Letters, in the explanation of the letter Zayin (see the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 10b). Eye [עין, ayin] is the totality of some of the sefirot together (see all this in Tikkun 4, fol. 18b). How so? The eyelids, which open and close, are Netzach and Hod; and the eye itself, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, are the three colors that go round the pupil, white and red and green; and the pupil is Malkhut; and the great pupil is Binah; the light of the pupil, this is Yod, from Chokhmah, through the Supreme Crown. However, this gathering here will be from the sefirot. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 256b) he explained that she is called eye from the side of the right. And it is possible to say that she includes these aspects from the side of Gedulah; and the reason is that there is the seeing, as will be explained. And therefore of Malkhut it is said (Jer. 2:2), "the love of your espousals [kelulotayikh]"; which is this inclusion [kelalut] from the right, and from its side the love is aroused. And therefore it is said (Song 4:9), "You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes." And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that "eye to eye" (Isa. 52:8) are Tiferet and Malkhut; both of them are called eye. And it may be so through the inclusion of these attributes in them. And from the Zohar, in Parashat Mishpatim (fol. 122b), it is understood that the eyes are in Gevurah; for he said, "for when Gevurah spreads out, and the eyes blaze," etc., as we copied it in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And there are those who explained that the eyes are Chokhmah and Binah; and there are those who explained in Gedulah and Gevurah. And there are some places in the Zohar from which it appears that they are Netzach and Hod; and we have nothing to explain. And over all the eyes there is one eye that has no eyebrows, for it is never closed; and it is Keter, and it is called in the Idra "the providence of all"; and it bestows the compassion on all the lower eyes. And in the Tikkunim, Malkhut, when she is included of the colors mentioned, is called the spring of water [ein ha-mayim], in which there is no cessation:

Weary [עיפתה, efatah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Malkhut is sometimes called "a land of thick darkness [eretz efatah]" (Job 10:22), from the side of Gevurah; and the matter itself shows this:

City [עיר, ir]: there are two cities. The upper city, and it is Binah, the upper Jerusalem; and there is the lower city, and it is the city of David, the lower Jerusalem, Malkhut. And it appears that she is called city in all her manifestations that she has in her walls, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations: for there is a middle point, and it is the point of the Temple; and around this point several chambers, courts, houses and walls, as we explained there:

Eruv [עירוב, eruv, the joining of domains]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24, fol. 67a) that Tiferet is called eruv, because through it one makes the eruv and carries from house to house, which are the upper house, Binah, and the lower house, Malkhut. And Tiferet mixes them and unites them together; and this is eruv:

Upon YHVH [על יהוה, al YHVH]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 79b), that the three first ones are called "upon YHVH," because they are above Tiferet. And therefore Hannah, who knew that children depend on mazal, prayed "upon YHVH"; and this is what the verse says (1 Sam. 1:10), "and she prayed upon YHVH"; and afterward she gave praise to the Place from which a son was bestowed upon her:

Above the heavens [על שמים, al shamayim] are Gedulah and Gevurah, which are above the heavens, which are Tiferet. So it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 7a?); and we copied his language in the entry "above the heavens" [me-al shamayim] and explained it:

Upon all waters [על כל מים, al kol mayim] is Binah. So he explained in the Zohar, Shemot (fol. 6a). And she is so called because she is "upon all waters" (Isa. 32:20); for she stands above the whole building, and even above Chesed:
The Cause of Causes [עלת העלות, illat ha-illot]: we explained it in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof Is Keter. And there is a difference between the Cause of Causes and the Cause over all Causes:

The pillar of fire and the cloud [עמוד האש והענן, ammud ha-esh ve-he-anan] is the Shekhinah. And when she draws nourishment from Chesed, in the secret of the attribute of day, then she is called the pillar of the cloud, for the cloud is from the side of Chesed. And when she draws nourishment from Gevurah, which is called the attribute of night, then she is called the pillar of fire. And Netzach and Hod are called pillars of marble [ammudei shesh]; and the reason is that in them six [shesh] are included: Netzach of Netzachs, Hod of Hods, as we explained in the entry Netzach. And likewise they were the pillars that Solomon, peace be upon him, made in the Temple; and both of them, Jachin and Boaz, are Netzach and Hod. And likewise they are also called simply pillars:
Clean wool [עמר נקי, amar neki] (Dan. 7:9): Chesed is so called, in the secret of the whiteness:

Grapes [ענבים, anavim]: the grapes are six sefirot and six extremities; and in them is the wine kept from the six days of Creation; and they are the six days. However, there are white grapes, and there are red grapes, and there are black grapes. When they draw nourishment from Chesed, then they are white; and they are good for a dream, showing Chesed. And when they draw nourishment from Gevurah they are red; and if he ate them, it is good for him, for he subdued the judgment and conquered it and annulled it. And the black ones show the force of judgment, in the secret of the blackness that is in Gevurah. So he explained in the Zohar Chadash, Song of Songs. And in Parashat Naso (fol. 127a) he explained that the grapes are in Malkhut. And it is possible to explain the matter: that anavim, in the plural, are the six extremities that are in Malkhut, and in them she receives the upper wine that is bestowed to her. And there is a beautiful judgment and a strong judgment; and that is the difference that there is between red and white (as is written in the Zohar, Terumah, fol. 144a):

Pleasure [ענג, oneg]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 55, fol. 85b) that it is the totality of three Sabbaths, which are Binah, Tiferet and Malkhut. And this word is an acronym of Eden, Nahar [river], Gan [garden]. The explanation: Eden, Binah with Chokhmah, and Keter included in them; river, Tiferet, which is the river that goes out of Eden and waters the garden, which is Malkhut. And all this is hinted in the word oneg. And in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 94a), he explained that the oneg and the ta'anug [pleasure] are in Binah; and this is "Take pleasure also upon [al] YHVH" (Ps. 37:4), precisely, that is, Binah. And it is possible to say that Binah is called oneg when Tiferet and Malkhut are concealed within her:

Humility [ענוה, anavah]: the explanation, Tiferet, in the secret of the concealed Da'at, which is the chariot of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him; and of it it is said (Num. 12:3), "Now the man Moses was very humble." And as for what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (in Song of Songs Rabbah, ch. 1): "What wisdom made a crown for her head, humility made a heel for her sole," etc.: the explanation is that Malkhut is called fear from the side of the left, and is called wisdom from the side of the right; and because she strengthens the left over the right, from her side; therefore "the fear of YHVH is the beginning of wisdom" (Ps. 111:10); for the fear always prevails from the side of this attribute. And nevertheless she is a heel and a throne for her husband, who is called humble in the secret of Da'at. And because she is sometimes her husband's diadem, therefore they said that in the aspect of humility she is always a crown over it; and that is in the secret of Da'at, which rises up to Keter (see Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 137, and these are his words: "and because of this, the heel of humility is the fear of YHVH," etc.; see there, and in the Introduction, fol. 8a):

Poor [עני, ani]: there is a poor man and a poor woman. The poor man is Yesod, and the poor woman Malkhut. And of the Righteous One Rashbi, peace be upon him, said that it has nothing of its own; and both of them are called poor. And there are those who wonder at the matter that she has nothing of herself. And I, a man, see the objection; I do not see [its force]. For just as the moon is a polished body that has no light at all except what it receives from the sun, so Malkhut has no light of herself except what she receives from Tiferet; and she borrows the light from it and bestows below. And if the objector objects: if so, that she has no light, she has no action; and if so, how are the other sefirot included of ten? Since Malkhut has no light, they are only nine. To this we answer: just as in the absence of the light of the moon we do not say that the planet Moon has been annulled from the world, which is certainly not so; rather, when it is in its fullness its actions are in strength, and in the days of its lack it has action, but not so much as before, when the light was flowing from it; so is the matter in Malkhut: for the sefirah is not annulled because of the diminishment of her light and her effluence; rather her light is absent and diminishes, and she remains like the sapphire stone, which, when the spark of the sun strikes it, shines a strong light in substance; and in the absence of the light and the spark of the sun that strikes it, it is not for this reason annulled and darkened entirely. And if we say "darkness" of it, it will be about the absence of that great light, not because she has no light at all. And even if we say that she has nothing of herself at all, the explanation is that she has no light at all of that light that was bestowed to her before, through whose cause she shone that strong light. And nevertheless her actions are not annulled, like the moon, of which we explained that it is not annulled entirely; however, her light diminishes and increases according to the place and according to the time. And just as we explained of Malkhut, that she is the poor woman who has nothing of herself, so we shall explain of Yesod, of which he said, "poor, for it has nothing of its own":

Cloud [ענן, anan] is Chesed. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Zohar, Emor, fol. 103a, and in Tikkun 30, fol. 72b) that Malkhut, from the side of Chesed, is called anan. And the seven clouds of glory were seven sefirot that are in the Shekhinah; and therefore they are called clouds of glory; and kavod [glory] is Malkhut, as we explained in its entry:

The branch of a thick tree [ענף עץ אבות, anaf etz avot] (Lev. 23:40): the three Patriarchs, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, are called "the branch of a thick [avot, read as 'Patriarchs'] tree." And therefore the myrtle is threefold, to hint at the three of them. And it is fitting to know that when they are called "the branch of a thick tree," each is included in its fellow, until all three of them are in each one; and therefore three branches of myrtle are required, and three [leaves] to each stem, to hint at the even unity and at the precious blending. And the principal of the branch is in Tiferet, which includes them and is thickened [me'ubbeh] by them; and so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 24a); and so it is understood from the language of "tree" and "branch":

Dust [עפר, afar] is the attribute of Malkhut; and she is called dust, for so she is the secret of the element of dust among the four upper elements, as we explained in the preceding gates; and likewise she makes fruits, as the dust makes fruits. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat (Vayishlach, fol. 170b). And there is one who explained dust also in Binah. And in the Zohar, Parashat Naso, fol. 125, and in Parashat Balak (fol. 210b), he explained that dust is the powers of judgment that are in Malkhut, in the secret of the judgment, which is the lower aspect that she has, in the secret of the blue [tekhelet]; and this is dust, which is lower; and likewise those powers of judgment are below, in the lower aspect; so it is explained there. And if so, in the secret of this aspect Malkhut is called dust. And in Parashat Bereshit (fol. 49a) he explained that Malkhut is called afar at the time of her drawing nourishment from Tiferet when it is called ofer [young hart]; as appears, specifically at the time of the prevailing of the side of Gevurah:

Tree [עץ, etz]: there are many trees, as we shall explain. However, "tree" without qualification is Tiferet; "for man is the tree of the field" (Deut. 20:19). However, sometimes it is called the Tree of Life. And the reason is that this tree, which is the tree of the Emanation as a whole, draws the life from Chokhmah. And so he explained in the Zohar in many places (see the Zohar, Shemini, fol. 40a, and fol. 41a), and especially in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 117a), and these are his words: "The Tree of Life, Tiferet; its life, Chokhmah and Binah," etc. And so he explained in the Tikkunim. And of it it is said that it is a walk of five hundred years: which are five sefirot, each one included of ten, and ten of ten; they are five hundred. And Yesod is called the pleasant tree [etz nechmad] (Gen. 2:9), because in it is the beauty of the sights; and likewise Tiferet is so called, the language of beauty [pe'er]. And according to these explanations they are called "pleasant to the sight" only in the aspect of their being included of the colors of the sefirot, and their being revealed in them and seen in them, whether in Yesod or in Tiferet. And there is the fruit tree, and it is Malkhut; and she is called the fruit tree because she is the tree where the fruits and souls are, which are bestowed within her from above; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 238a). And there is the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil; and sometimes Rashbi, peace be upon him, in his books calls Malkhut the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil. And one must not be seduced into saying that in Malkhut there is evil, God forbid; for this name is borrowed for her because beneath her are the good and evil. However, the Tree of Knowledge is Malkhut, for she is the tree united with the upper Da'at, and beneath her are good and evil: good, that is Metatron; and evil, this is Samael. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 53, fol. 85a, and in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 124a). Further, he explained there (in the Zohar Chadash mentioned) that Beriah too is called the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil; and there is no doubt that there is no evil in it at all, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA; and it is related to it in the way that it is related to Malkhut. And sometimes this name is borrowed for Malkhut for another cause: that she draws nourishment from the depth of good and the depth of evil, which are Gedulah and Gevurah; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 35a). And there is a transplanted tree [etz shatul] and a planted tree [etz natu'a]. Transplanted is from the side of Metatron, in whom there is uprooting and setting down: sometimes separated and uprooted from holiness, sometimes set down and united in holiness. The intent: sometimes he has light from above, sometimes he has no light from above; at times united with the Shekhinah, and sometimes not, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA. But the planted tree is Tiferet, in the secret of the constancy of the union, in the matter of "I am YHVH, and My glory will I not give to another" (Isa. 42:8); and therefore it is always planted, and it has no transplanting, like Metatron:

Sorrow [עצב ועצבון, etzev ve-itzavon]: they explained it in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 71), and these are his words: "Itzavon: sadness and agitation without the shining of the face, when the moon is darkened and blessings are not found. Be-itzavon: the side of the Other Spirit, which withholds blessings from the world." Thus far his words. And the intent is that when the upper light and effluence are lacking, and judgment is present, and the husks draw nourishment, then it is called itzavon:

Counsel [עצה, etzah]: our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Berakhot 61a): "the kidneys counsel." And the intent is that Netzach and Hod, which are the kidneys, as we explained in their entry, are what bestow counsel to Malkhut. And so they explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 193b) that Netzach and Hod are called "counsels from afar" (Isa. 25:1). And the reason is that they counsel the prophets, and prophecy comes only [through] Malkhut. Therefore we say that just as these are called prophets and the prophecy is Malkhut, so they are called counsels, counsellors, and Malkhut counsel:

Acacia wood [עצי שטים, atzei shittim]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Netzach and Hod are called acacia wood, for they stand and sustain the building and hold up the Tabernacle. And it is not compelling:

Bone [עצם, etzem]: the bone has an aspect that hints at compassion and an aspect that hints at judgment; and likewise the flesh. The bone, its whiteness hints at compassion, and its hardness hints at judgment; and the flesh, the redness hints at judgment, and soft to the touch hints at compassion. And therefore sometimes Rashbi, peace be upon him, relates this to judgment, sometimes its fellow. And these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 105a): "'Bone of my bones' (Gen. 2:23): this is Yod with Heh; 'and flesh of my flesh': Vav with Heh." Thus far his words. Behold, explicitly, that Chokhmah and Binah, which are Yod with Heh, are certainly called "bone of my bones," to hint that both of them are more compassion than Tiferet and Malkhut; and therefore he related them to the bone in its whiteness. And Tiferet with Malkhut, which are Vav-Heh, are "flesh of my flesh," which are judgment, like the redness of the flesh. And it is also possible to say that just as it is the way of the flesh to cover the bone, and the bone is clothed in the flesh, so Chokhmah and Binah are clothed in Tiferet and Malkhut, and Tiferet and Malkhut reveal the secret of Chokhmah and Binah. And elsewhere in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 65, fol. 93a), these are his words: "One of the good inclination and one of the evil inclination: one from the side of the bone, strong, hard judgment; and one from the side of the flesh; from there are the soft of heart. And those of the bone are the stiff-necked. And of a woman who was taken from the bone, Ben Sira said: 'A bone that fell to your lot,' etc., 'drag it.'" Thus far his words. Behold, explicitly, that he reversed the attributes; for he said that from the side of the bone there is strong judgment, and from the side of the flesh compassion. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 281a), these are his words: "He is ach [brother], asur and chavush [bound and imprisoned, Alef-Chet], who has no power to redeem himself, which is Dalet, atzmo de-ach [the bone of echad]. 'Bone of my bones' He called her with respect to Himself, in the skull of the head tefillin; and 'flesh of my flesh' He called her from the side of the heart." Thus far his words. And the explanation is clear: that from the side of the skull of the tefillin, which is Keter of the brain, he called her bone; and from the side of the heart, which is Binah, she is called flesh. And elsewhere (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 255b) he said that Malkhut from the side of Chesed is called "bone of my bones," and from the side of Gevurah "flesh of my flesh." And the matter is as we explained: that they are aspects that interchange in the thing signified; and we have no middle compromise in this for the present:

The very heavens [עצם השמים, etzem ha-shamayim] (Exod. 24:10): in the Ra'aya Meheimna there, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Malkhut is called etzem ha-shamayim for the reason that she is taken from Tiferet, which is called heavens; and that is "a bone from the heavens." And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Netzach and Hod are called etzem ha-shamayim on account of the might [otzmah] that comes to them from the heavens, until they give substance to every substance beneath them. And the principal is as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. And in the Palaces, the second palace is called etzem ha-shamayim, as we shall explain in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 2:

Assembly [עצרת, atzeret]: Malkhut is called atzeret; and he explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 197a) that she is so called because, through her beauty and her pleasantness before her husband, abundant effluence is bestowed upon her without any exactness, because she is worthy of him; and after the effluence comes to her, she holds it back because of the evil of the deeds of men, who are not worthy of that good. And when the effluence is held back there, then she is called atzeret: the explanation, that she restrains [otzeret] the effluence in her hand and does not send it below [except little by little], as we explained in the entry "Assembly of Israel":

Heel [עקב, akev]: Malkhut is so called; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (in the Tosefta to the Zohar, fol. 306b, and it is also brought in the Omissions to Bereshit, fol. 16). And the reason is that just as the heel is the end of the body, so the Shekhinah is the end of the rungs that are in the Emanation. And likewise Jacob [Ya'akov] is the Shekhinah, and we explained it in its entry. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained akev in Chokhmah, and the reason, that she is a heel to Keter; and it is not to the point, neither in akev nor in humility, as we explained (in the entries fear and humility):

Binding [עקדה, akedah]: in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Malkhut, from the side of Gevurah, is called akedah. And it is possible that this is in the secret of the bond of judgment and its binding. And Gevurah is called akud [bound], and she is the akedah:

Root [עיקר, ikkar] is Yesod. And the reason is that it is foundation and root and stock for the world, as it is written (Prov. 10:25), "but the righteous is an everlasting foundation"; and the explanation, a foundation for Malkhut. So it is explained in the Tikkunim:

Barren [עקרה, akarah]: Malkhut is so called; and the reason is that she is Rachel, barren, "till YHVH look down and behold from heaven" (Lam. 3:50). Or it may mean akeret ha-bayit [the mainstay of the house] (Ps. 113:9); and this explanation is explained in the Zohar, in different places, many times:

Evening [ערב, erev]: there is a great evening and there is a small evening, in the secret of the great minchah and the small minchah. The great evening [erev rav] is from six hours onward; and then the power of judgment prevails; and it is from the side of the soft judgment, Hod. And from her side the husks rule, in the mixed multitude [erev rav], hard husks. And in the small evening, a hard husk, not like the first. And in this there is no wonder, that there is an erev in holiness and an erev in the husk; for all is right, and this is held in that, as we explained (see the Zohar, Tisa, fol. 191a, and in Kehillat Ya'akov, the entry erev):

Aravot [ערבות, aravot, the heavens] in Tiferet. On this name they disagreed in the Zohar (Terumah, fol. 165a). And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that the firmament Aravot is in Yesod; and so it is explained in the Zohar too, elsewhere. And the reason may be that just as Tiferet is called Aravot because in it the powers mix [mit'arvim], which are Gedulah and Gevurah, so in Yesod Netzach and Hod mix, which are the power of Gedulah and Gevurah. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 121b) he explained that Tiferet itself is called Aravot, and Yesod the ground of Aravot; for it is the extension of the Vav, and it is the end of the arbiter; therefore Aravot is right of it:

Willows of the brook [ערבי נחל, arvei nachal] (Lev. 23:40) are Netzach and Hod, when they sit on the bank of the brook (Yesod and lips), over all the waters that come by way of the brook. And in the Zohar he explained that the brook is the sides of Gevurah. And it is possible to say that he speaks of Netzach and Hod when they draw nourishment from Gevurah; and it is possible to say that he speaks of the five gevurot that spread out from Gevurah; and it is a teaching in Parashat Emor (printed in Parashat Vayechi, fol. 220b), and it is written with us. And our inclination is toward the second explanation, by the force of the teaching there:

The evening prayer [ערבית, arvit] is Malkhut. And therefore they said, "The evening prayer is optional [reshut]"; because the authority [reshut] of her husband is upon her. And this is "and he lodged there, because the sun was set" (Gen. 28:11); and she is an authority kept for her husband:

Garden bed [ערוגה, arugah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that Malkhut is called arugah, for she is a garden and garden bed for the Torah, for in her are planted the fifty-three [gan] portions of the Torah. And it is possible that part of the garden is called arugah; for she is the one who includes all the garden beds:

Thick darkness [ערפל, arafel]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30, fol. 72b) that the Shekhinah, from the side of Gevurah, is called arafel; and he gave a sign: "And Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God [Elohim] was" (Exod. 20:21); for Elohim is from the side of Gevurah. And in the Tikkunim, elsewhere, he explained that arafel is from the side of Tiferet; and possibly when it draws nourishment from Gevurah (and see the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 225a, that Chokhmah and Binah are called "clouds and thick darkness are round about Him" [Ps. 97:2]):

Couch [ערש, eres]: the explanation, Malkhut, who is the Shekhinah. And in permutation, eser [ten], for she is included of ten. And of her it is said (Ps. 41:4), "YHVH will support him upon the couch of languishing"; that is, the Shekhinah, who is above the head of the sick:

Herb [עשב, esev]: on this word Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 61b), these are his words: "What is esev? Ayin-Bet [seventy-two], Shin: and they are seventy-two names, which are garments of the upper seventy-two names, like the herb, which is the garment of the wheat." Thus far his words; and his intent is clear. And elsewhere (in Tikkun 51, fol. 84a) he explained: "Esev, Ayin-Bet Shin: this is Jacob, who includes three Patriarchs, which are the branches of the tree, and they come to seventy-two names: Vav-Heh-Vav, Yod-Lamed-Yod, Samekh-Yod-Tet; for by this name were created the herbs and the trees, which are the souls of the righteous." Thus far his words. And these two expressions together shall be whole, and each one reveals its fellow. For the seventy-two names which are garments: it is already known that "one higher than the high watches" (Eccl. 5:7); and the seventy-two names have seventy-two beings, which are sources for the Name of Seventy-Two, as we explained in the Gate of the Particulars of the Names. And the intent is that these seventy-two are a garment for the seventy-two concealed names, whose root is Adonai, as is mentioned there. And that is the herb, the garment of the wheat, which is the Shekhinah. However, the seventy-two themselves are in Tiferet; for there is the seventy-two, which is the totality of two hundred and sixteen letters, which are three times seventy-two, for the three Patriarchs. And by the Name of Seventy-Two the souls were created, which blossom forth from the Righteous One. And the souls themselves are garments of the Shekhinah, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Introduction, fol. 6b) on the verse "like the appearance of fire," etc. (and these are his words: "and this is the Shekhinah; for so the Rabbis established, that the souls are like, before the Shekhinah, candles before the torch"): which are the souls of the righteous that surround her and become a garment for her, to adorn herself with them, to appear before her husband, as is known. And likewise she is clothed in them in this world, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 4. All this we pressed to settle these two expressions into one matter. And the intent of the word esev is in Tiferet, when it is included of the three Patriarchs:

Fruit-maker [עושה פרי, oseh peri] (Gen. 1:11): Tiferet is so called. And the reason is that it is the one that makes and emanates the fruits and the souls to Malkhut; and the principal of the making depends on the male. So he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 238a):

Smoke [עשן, ashan]: there is a smoke that is not good, as in "for then the anger of YHVH and His jealousy shall smoke," etc. (Deut. 29:19); and it is the smoke that goes out from above to below; and it is by the power of Gevurah, which is aroused in several powers that it has, of harsh judgment and an evil strap, to destroy, God forbid. And there is a good smoke, and it is the smoke of the array [of the altar]; and it is Tiferet, which rises by the power of the arousal of Binah toward Chokhmah, and rises to Chokhmah; and there Chokhmah and Binah are united through it, in the secret of Da'at; and then effluence and blessing descend. And the principal of its arousal is from the side of Binah, the female; and therefore it is a smoke of judgment.
And further, we spoke at length on the two smokes in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 12:

Rich [עשיר, ashir]: Tiferet is so called. And it is so called with respect to Tzaddik and Tzedek, which are poor, for they have nothing; and this one "shall delight itself in the abundance of peace" (Ps. 37:11); therefore it is called rich. And it is possible that it is called rich only when it is included of all the tens [asiriyyot]; and this is truly wealth [osher]; for one who has ten is not like one who has a hundred or a thousand. And so we explained in the Gate of Ten and Not Nine, chapter 6. And it is possible that it is called rich from the side of its drawing nourishment from Binah, in the secret of "whoever wishes to become rich, let him turn northward":

Ten and tenth [עשר ועשור, eser ve-asor]: the Shekhinah is so called; and the reason is because she is included of ten sefirot. And there is no wonder how all the sefirot are included of ten; for we have already explained this matter in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 2. And the intent is their being revealed in her, and she is truly adorned in ten. And Malkhut is called eser or asor only in this aspect, in the secret of this inclusion. And in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 102), he explained that every word asor is hinted in her; and the reason is that from above to below they are ten, down to Malkhut; and the explanation of asor is the tenth rung, as one says "the tenth" (see the Zohar, Tetzaveh, fol. 185b). And in the Tikkunim he explained that all the sefirot in her are called eser, because through her they come to ten tens, which are a hundred:

Tenth measure [עשרון, issaron]: all the sefirot are called issaronim in Malkhut. And the reason is that through her they all become included of ten; for she completes the count, as we explained above from the Tikkunim on eser. And the three Patriarchs are "three tenth parts" (Num. 28:12) through her; and "a several tenth part" [issaron issaron] (Num. 28:13) are Netzach and Hod, which are two tenths. So he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 17, fol. 31):

Time [עת, et]: Malkhut is called et; and of her it is said (Ps. 119:126), "It is time for YHVH to work." And because she is included of twenty-eight times [ittim]: fourteen when she is full, united with the sun, and they are good; and fourteen evil, when she is lacking and waning. And of this it is said (Lev. 16:2), "that he come not at all times [be-khol et]." And there is an evil time, and it is the husk. And by this the matter of the greeting is understood, that they are accustomed to offer greeting first and to say "a good hour": that is, Malkhut when she is in her fullness. And God forbid, "an evil hour" is her lack and the dominion of the husks. And therefore one must be careful not to say, "May it be in an evil hour," God forbid; for it looks as though he curses himself, the Compassionate One save us. And it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayera (fol. 116), that "an acceptable time" [et ratzon], and attah [now], as in "I will hasten it in its time [be-ittah]" (Isa. 60:22), are all one thing; and the explanation is et-Heh. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Binah is called et from the side of Gevurah; and therefore "that he come not at all times," because sometimes she bestows judgment. And just as these twenty-eight times are in Malkhut, so in Binah; for there is no judgment below unless it is from above:

The Ancient One [עתיקא, Attika]: Rashbi sometimes calls Keter so in the Zohar; and sometimes [he calls] "the Ancient of Ancients, the Concealed," etc., [and sometimes] the Ein Sof. And in this matter the principal discernment and judgment is according to its place. And nevertheless, when he calls Keter "the Ancient of Ancients," it shows greater concealment; and when he titles it by the name Attika, it shows concealment, and not so much. And when he calls Chokhmah Attika, it shows that she is concealed. All according to the aspects. However, the explanation of the words, in his saying "the Ancient of Ancients," etc., is explained in the Gate of Names:

Entreaty [עתר, atar]: the explanation, from the language of "And Isaac entreated [va-ye'tar]," etc. (Gen. 25:21). And it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 137a), that the prayer reached up to the Supreme Crown. And the matter of va-ye'tar is from the language of chatirah [digging through], as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (there, and in Sanhedrin 103a). And the intent is the digging through the sefirot until the prayer reached the upper mazal; for there the matter of children depends, as they, of blessed memory, said: "Children, life and sustenance do not depend on merit," etc. And it is possible that every place where it says va-ye'tar it is the ascent of the prayer up to Keter. Thus far the explanation of the entry of the letter Ayin has reached, with the help of Heaven, who bestows upon us in compassion. And now we enter into the explanation of the letter Peh, with the help of the Rock and His salvation:

Glory [פאר, pe'er]: it is already known what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Mo'ed Katan 15a), that the tefillin are called pe'er. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 8a) that the tefillin on the head of the Holy One, blessed be He, are Binah upon Tiferet; and, hovering over it, she is called pe'er, on account of her glorifying [mefa'er] Tiferet. And further, for then it includes six branches through her; and therefore she is called pe'er, from the language of "the goodly turbans [pa'arei ha-migba'ot]" (Exod. 39:28); the explanation, that she makes it branch out and glorifies it. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained close to this:
Mouth [פה, peh]: on the matter of the mouth we explained in the entry lashon [tongue]. And nevertheless we shall widen the explanation.

Behold, the mouths are two. The one mouth is Malkhut; and she is called mouth from the side of the circumcision, Yesod; and the numerical value of this is as the numerical value of that [peh and milah, 85]. And the principal is this: when we say that Malkhut is mouth, the intent is not that she is the whole mouth; rather the intent is that the opening of the mouth alone is Malkhut. As if we said: when a man opens his lips, that air and opening that comes into being between the lips is the mouth; however, the lips are Netzach and Hod; and the tongue, which goes round between the lips, drawn toward the inside, is Yesod; and therefore it is called lashon. And in the actions of speech the mouth is united with the throat by means of the tongue, whose one end, between the lips, reaches the mouth itself, and whose other end reaches the throat, in which is the windpipe [kaneh], which is Tiferet, as will be explained in its entry, with the help of the Name. And above the whole of this mouth there is another mouth: and it is Gedulah and Gevurah, they are the lips; and within them the tongue is Binah, which is called lashon; and not Binah herself, but Tiferet concealed in Binah, in the secret of Da'at. And the opening of the mouth itself is Binah, for she is the upper female. And the throat, from which the speech goes out, is Chokhmah:

And now we shall explain what these mouths serve. And the matter is that speech is the parable for the beings in the upper worlds. And just as in the lower world the speech comes into being through the union of these organs, which are mouth, lips, tongue, throat, so in the emanated world the beings come into being and are emanated through these vessels. And behold, the beings are concealed in Chokhmah to the utmost concealment, so that one does not judge the manifestation of beings there, but only in Binah. And behold, that concealment that is in Chokhmah goes out into Binah, and there a manifestation is revealed, subtle and exceedingly concealed; and we called it revealed, even though it is concealed, with respect to the great concealment and hiddenness that is in Chokhmah, until there is between them and the nothing and the naught only as much as a strand, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And when they are revealed in Binah they come into being in the manifestation of yesh [something], so that they are judged as something and not as naught. And it is explained that as the relation of Chokhmah to Binah, so is the relation of Tiferet to Malkhut; for Tiferet and Malkhut are called son and daughter, and Chokhmah and Binah father and mother. And behold, father and mother are united as the son and the daughter are united, as is well known. And behold, the union of the father and the mother is through the pleasant tongue that is called Da'at, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance; and through Da'at the beings go out into Binah. And in the matter of the speech of this Da'at, they are Gedulah and Gevurah.
