And that is: Da'at the tongue, and Gedulah and Gevurah the lips, and Binah the mouth, which brings out the letters and the speech from the chosen potential to the revealed actual. And there is no [wonder] in Binah's being the mouth above the lips, Gedulah and Gevurah; for so is the way of Malkhut, who through the coupling rises above Netzach and Hod; and whoever has eyes of intellect can prove this thing "from the holy flesh that is upon him" (cf. Hag. 2:12) at the time of his coupling. And when the beings were revealed in Binah, they were not revealed in speech and the cutting of the lips and the particulars of the letters, but in voice; and this shows the great concealment, for they are still like the light of the letters in Binah, as will be explained in the Gate of Letters, chapter 2. And through the voice, which in Binah is "a voice that is not heard," the beings were revealed; and there they are planted, a planting only, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And they were compelled to a transplanting, so that the beings be revealed well; and they needed a mouth; and it is the mouth of Malkhut, which is through the lips and the tongue.

And behold, Tiferet is united with Malkhut through Yesod, which is the tongue; and the letters and the beings go out from Binah through light, water, firmament, like the seed itself. And from there they are bestowed upon Tiferet, the firmament certainly, as will be explained in its entry. And when they are there, it bestows them through Yesod into Malkhut; and Malkhut conceives from them and gives birth to them and makes them grow and brings them out to the power of speech, which is the cutting of the words, through the complete union.

And behold, according to this, the mouths are two, an upper mouth and a lower mouth; and the tongues are two, an upper tongue and a lower tongue. And lashon is right in Binah, and its principal is in the secret of Da'at concealed in her, within her chambers, as is explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof Is Keter. And the speech goes out through both of them. And the lips are two upper and two lower. And "With him do I speak mouth to mouth" (Num. 12:8): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is Tiferet and Malkhut; and according to our way there is no need for this. Rather, the prophecy of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was through the two mouths, as we explained; and therefore it was clear and clarified. However, the other prophets' was through one mouth; for their prophecy was from below, and therefore it was thick with images. However, the prophecy of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was from above, and came to him from within two mouths; and therefore the things were in the cutting of speech, clear and beautiful. And it is already known that the Written Torah is bestowed from Chokhmah, as we shall explain in its entry in the chapter; and because it was from Chokhmah, the prophecy was compelled to be through two mouths, as we explained. And the Shekhinah is called the mouth of YHVH when she is joined with her beloved in the joining of coupling, not by way of speech; and then she is called the mouth of YHVH. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained in another sense: that she is called the mouth of YHVH to hint at compassion; and she is called the mouth of Gevurah to hint at her drawing nourishment from the side of Gevurah, and then she bestows the power of judgment. And this is pi [mouth], whose explanation is the place of the gatehouse, for entering and going out. And the word poh [here], with a cholam, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Tisa, fol. 190a), that it too is in Malkhut. And elsewhere it appears from his words that it is in Yesod; and it is all one, for Malkhut [through it] is called peh. (And in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 256b) we found, apparently, the reverse of what was expounded above in his name; and when we examine his language there we find that it is no difficulty. And these are his words: "And she is called ear from the side of the left: 'Incline Your ear, O YHVH, and hear' (Isa. 37:17); and she is called smell [re'ach] from the side of the central pillar; and she is called mouth of herself," etc. Thus far his words.

And behold, with respect to those (words) [aspects], which are ear and smell, which are from the side of Tiferet and from the side of Gevurah, he said that the mouth is from her own side, that it is not from their side; but not that it is not from the side of any attribute whatever. Or we may say that both are right: when she is in all her vessels, which are the tongue and the lips, then she is called mouth only from the side of Yesod, for through it she is united with these vessels; but when the mouth is related with respect to the mouth alone, without one of these vessels being joined to her, then she is called mouth from her own side:

Visiting iniquity [פקד עון, poked avon] (Exod. 34:7): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Gevurah is called poked avon, and he did not explain a reason for it at all. And it seems to me that it is so called only when it acts through Malkhut, in whom is the visiting [pekidah] for all the aspects, as we shall explain:

Fear [פחד, Pachad]: the explanation, Gevurah is called Fear because, from the power of the judgment, all the creatures, upper and lower, fear it. And it is so called when it is clothed in the power of the strong judgment. And it is called the Fear of Isaac because Isaac is a chariot for it; and the proof: "And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac" (Gen. 31:53):

That which opens the womb [פטר רחם, peter rechem]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30, fol. 72b) that the Shekhinah is called peter rechem because she is the opening of the two hundred and forty-eight [rechem] positive commandments. And it appears that she is so called when she is below, in her lower aspect, in which she bestows the commandments and their matter and their reward; and in this aspect she includes two hundred and forty-eight:

Wonder [פלא, pele] is from the language of "Is anything too wonderful [ha-yippale] for YHVH?" (Gen. 18:14), whose explanation in Targum Onkelos is "Is anything covered?" And its principal is in Keter, to hint at the great concealment. And Chokhmah too is sometimes so called; and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Tzav (fol. 31a): "Pele, this is the upper Wisdom, which is wondrous and covered from all." Thus far his words. And the reason is that she cleaves to Keter and is concealed with it; and this is what he said, "which is wondrous": the explanation, concealed in Keter. And the paths that are in Chokhmah are called pela'ot [wondrous]. And there is one who explained it from the language of "when a man shall clearly utter [yafli]" (Lev. 27:2; Num. 6:2), whose explanation is the matter of distinguishing and separating; and the paths are so called because they are separated from one another and distinguished from one another. And the principal, in our view, is that they are so called because they are concealed. And in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 193b) he explained: "Pele, this is 'the path that no bird of prey knows,'" etc.; see there. Behold, because of its concealment it is called pele. And according to this there is no wonder if one be found who calls Malkhut pele. And there are those who call Tiferet pele, because it rises up to Keter in the secret of Da'at. And the rule in these matters is that there is no pele except from the side of Keter, which is called Alef:

Channel [פלג, peleg]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Binah is so called because she is "the channel of God, full of water" (Ps. 65:10). And it seems to me that Malkhut is so called because she is a pool full of water; and she is called by the language of peleg because "the earth was divided [niflegah]" (Gen. 10:25) and was driven out below:

Shining faces [פנים המאירים, panim ha-me'irim]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is Tiferet, for they shine for Malkhut. And it is possible to say that the shining faces are the faces of the sun, which are the faces of Tiferet or Binah; and those that do not shine are in Malkhut. And even though we say that the shining are Tiferet or Binah, and those that do not shine Malkhut, it is already possible to say that the shining faces are Netzach, those that do not shine Hod, after the manner of the mirror that shines and the one that does not shine, which we explained in its entry. And there is face to face, and they are the face of Tiferet and the face of Malkhut. And likewise the face of Jacob is the moon; even though the commentators explained it in another sense, this is the principal; for the form of Jacob is engraved in the moon. And sometimes there is a face of indignation, as "the face of YHVH has divided them" (Lam. 4:16); and there is a face of favour, as "Make Your face to shine upon Your servant" (Ps. 31:17). And all according to the drawing of nourishment: when she draws nourishment from Chesed, then the face of favour and compassion; and when she draws nourishment from Gevurah, then, God forbid, a face of indignation. And in this way Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 282a): the faces of the sun, which are Gedulah and Gevurah; the faces of the moon, Netzach and Hod; the right ones of compassion, and the left ones of indignation; all according to the drawing of nourishment, to the sun or to the moon:

Ruling [פסק, pesek]: Malkhut is so called from the side of Tiferet, and when it inclines to judgment; for the reason that on her depend all the rulings of law and rulings of judgment. And this is the end [sof pasuk, verse-end] and the cutting-off [pesek] for all the holy rungs. And when Tiferet, which is Vav, is united with her, she is called pasuk [verse]: which is Tiferet with Malkhut united, and Tiferet rises in the name of Malkhut. We are found saying that Malkhut, from the side of Tiferet, is called pesek, and Tiferet pasuk. And so they explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a):

Visitation [פקודה, pekudah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pinchas (fol. 222b), on the verse (Job 10:12), "and Your visitation has preserved my spirit," that Malkhut is called pekudah. And the reason is that Tiferet, at its new moons, visits her, to prepare her and to sustain her; and therefore she is visited by it with its good effluence:

The numbered ones [פקודים, pekudim]: Netzach and Hod are so called; and likewise "These are the accounts [pekudei]" (Exod. 38:21): they are two pekudin; so it is explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 111a). Further, they explained there that the language of "I have surely visited [pakod pakadti]" (Exod. 3:16) is the same two pekudin, Netzach and Hod. And it is difficult for what is explained, that pekudah is Malkhut. However, she is aroused from the side of the Netzachs that are over her to visit. And in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 220a), he explained that all the lower holy powers that are in Malkhut below are called "the accounts of the Tabernacle," which are "the beasts of the field," as we explained in its entry:

Remembrance [פקידה, pekidah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that pekidah is in Yesod. And in the Zohar (Vayetze, fol. 159b) he explained that it is in Malkhut; and the proof: "God will surely remember [pakod yifkod] you," etc. (Gen. 50:24): Elohim, in Malkhut. And so they also explained in Parashat Vayera (fol. 115): pekidah for the female, zekhirah for the male. And in the Zohar (Parashat Vayetze, fol. 160b) he explained that just as there is zekhirah and pekidah on the side of holiness, so there is zekhirah and pekidah on the side of Samael and Lilith:

The red heifer [פרה אדומה, parah adumah]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 47a) that Binah, from the side of Gevurah, is called red, and from the side of Chesed, Abraham, is called temimah [without blemish]. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 243b) he explained that Malkhut too is called the red heifer, from the side of Gevurah, and without blemish from the side of Chesed. And it is all one: Binah from the side of her bestowal in them, and Malkhut from the side of her drawing nourishment:

Particular [פרט, perat]: at first sight it appears that Malkhut is called perat. But in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 123b) he explained: Keter, general; and Tiferet, particular; and Malkhut, general. And according to this way, that is to say, that in Keter Chesed, Judgment and Compassion are included; and they are particularized in Tiferet, in Chesed and Gevurah and Tiferet; and they are included in Malkhut, as is known. And we explained it in the Gate of Essence and Governance:

The fruit of a tree [פרי עץ, peri etz] is the Shekhinah, which is the etrog. And she is called "the fruit of a goodly tree [peri etz hadar]" (Lev. 23:40) when she is in the land of the living from year to year, "from the beginning of the year even to the end of the year" (Deut. 11:12). And it is a fruit taken from a goodly tree, in the secret of "And YHVH God built the rib" (Gen. 2:22); for they were created with two faces. And Tiferet is hadar [goodly], glorious. So they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 24a):

Uncovering [פריעה, peri'ah]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is in Yesod; and many of the commentators explained it in Malkhut. And the matter is that milah [circumcision] and peri'ah are two rungs. Milah is the cutting off of the foreskin and its removal from the world; and the explanation in the preceding chapters: "there is no removal of leaven except burning," etc. However, peri'ah is the bringing near of the foreskin to holiness; and we [tear] the husk in such a way that the holiness is revealed over them. And it is like the bullocks of the Festival, which are seventy princes, which are offered upon the altar; and in their being brought near to holiness they return to holiness; and we do not remove it entirely, as in the likeness of the milah. However, this peri'ah is from the side of Chesed, which brings everything near; like "Let the left hand always push away and the right hand bring near." And we spoke at length on this inquiry in the Gate of ABYA:

Veil [פרכת, parokhet]: Malkhut is called parokhet, for she is a veil and a screen between the Emanation and all the things that are beneath her. And her lower aspect is called parokhet, which is what divides between the holy place and the Holy of Holies:

Provider [פרנס, parnas]: Binah is so called because she nourishes and provides for all the upper hosts, which are the seven extremities of the building beneath her. And likewise Malkhut is called parnas because she nourishes and provides for all the lower hosts that are beneath her, as it is written (Prov. 31:15), "She rises also while it is yet night, and gives food to her household," etc. And they are so called when they provide for the lower ones that are beneath them:

Outstretched [פשוטה, peshutah]: Chesed is so called; and so he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a), and proved it from the verse "for Your right hand is stretched out"; and so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: "a plain [peshutah] note before it and a plain note after it," and it is the teki'ah; and that is Chesed:

Opening [פתח, petach]: Malkhut is called petach, for she is the entrance to the Emanation. And she is so called only in her lower aspect, in which she is the entrance to the Emanation. And she is also called the opening of the eyes [petach einayim] (Gen. 38:14), because she is an opening for the eyes, Netzach and Hod, which stand over her; and there is none who can prophesy and gaze at these eyes except from this opening. And in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fols. 71b–72b), he explained that she is called petach einayim "because all the eyes of the world look to this opening." Thus far. And so it is also explained in Parashat Bereshit (fol. 1b). And she is also called the door of the tent; so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayera. And it is possible that she is so called in the lower aspect, which is an opening to the rest of the tent, which is her very inwardness. And there are the everlasting doors [pitchei olam] (Ps. 24:7): the explanation, Yesod is called pitchei olam because it is an opening to the world, the circuit. And it is called pitchei in the plural because through it is the way of the right, Chesed, and the way of the left, Gevurah. And there is one who explained pitchei olam as Gevurah and Chesed, and they are the doors of Binah, which is called olam. And there are the doors of the bridal canopy, and it is Binah; and we explained it in the entry chuppah. Thus far the letter Peh is completed; and behold, we begin to explain the letter Tzadi, with the help of the Helper who bestows upon us:

Host [צבא, tzava]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that of Netzach and Hod it is said, "And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host" (Gen. 2:1); and likewise every term of tzava. And likewise they are what is hinted in the name Tzeva'ot [Hosts], as we explained in the Gate of Names. And it appears from the language of the Tikkunim that they are called tzeva'ot from the side of Yesod; and likewise the Patriarchs, Gedulah and Gevurah, Tiferet, are called tzivyonot from its side. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, fol. 66, and so in Tikkun 47, fol. 81, and see there the commentary Kisse Melekh), when he speaks of Yesod, these are his words: "And of it it is said, 'and all their host.' What is 'their host'? Two pillars of truth; and in it the three Patriarchs are called tzivyonot, as it is said, 'And on the seventh day God finished … and He rested on the seventh day … and God blessed the seventh day' (Gen. 2:2–3)." Thus far his words. And all of it is over against Yesod, and it is proved there. And close to this matter he explained in many places (in Tikkun 51, fol. 84), in his saying: "Tzeva'ot: He is a sign [ot] in His host [tzava]." And the matter is that the word ot in Tzeva'ot hints at Yesod, which is called ot [sign]; and tzava is Netzach and Hod; and of it it is said, "He is a sign in His host." As it appears, they are called host from the side of Yesod:

Gazelle [צבי, tzevi]: Yesod is so called; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Acharei (fol. 68), on the verse "As the hart pants" (Ps. 42:2); and its hint is from the verse "glory [tzevi] to the righteous" (Isa. 24:16). And it is understood there that it is called tzevi when it is beside Malkhut, when Malkhut is called ayyal [hart]. And in Parashat Bereshit (fol. 49a) he explained that Malkhut is called tzeviyah [doe]; and Tiferet is called tzevi, and she is tzeviyah. And it is all one; for "all that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph":

Righteous One [צדיק, Tzaddik]: Yesod is called Tzaddik. And it is so called only when it does tzedakah with Tzedek, which is Malkhut; and the Yod that is within the Tzaddik is Yesod: behold, Tzaddik. And in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 91), he explained that Yesod and Malkhut are called tzaddikim in the plural; and these are his words: "Who are the tzaddikim? This is Tzaddik and the Assembly of Israel." And it may be that they are so called because both of them are the sign of the covenant: this one circumcision, and that one uncovering; both of them are the sign of the covenant, tzaddikim. And the Righteous One is called Yesod [Foundation] only in the aspect in which Malkhut has no existence apart from its effluence, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters:

Righteousness [צדק, Tzedek] is Malkhut; and she is so called when she draws nourishment from the side of Gevurah. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 198b), and proved it from the verse (Isa. 26:9), "For when Your judgments are in the earth … righteousness," etc.: that is, righteousness and uprightness in the line of strict judgment. And in Parashat Bereshit (fol. 49) he explained that Tiferet is called Tzaddik and she is called Tzedek. And there is an upper Tzedek, and it is Binah; and she is so called after the manner of Malkhut:

Charity [צדקה, tzedakah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 70, fol. 127a) that tzedakah is compassion, and the tzedakah is the upper Binah. And it is possible that Malkhut too is called tzedakah when she is compassion, just as Binah too is called tzedek. And in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 72a), he explained on the verse (Gen. 38:26), "She is more righteous than I [tzadkah mimmeni]": that this is the saying of Tiferet concerning Malkhut; for she is tzedek, and she becomes tzedakah through it. And this is what he said: "from me." And the reason is that it makes her a vessel; and this is tzedakah with Heh, which shows the feminine, as we explained in na'ar, na'arah, in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 89a), he explained that tzedakah is Tiferet, when it is included in Gedulah, Gevurah, and shines in them. And so he explained in Parashat Miketz, that Tiferet is called tzedakah; and it may be so called because then it does tzedakah with Malkhut:

Neck [צואר, tzavvar]: Tiferet, in its manifestation that rises to cleave to the three first ones, above Gevurah and Gedulah, is called neck. Nevertheless the neck will also be in Binah; and so we have found in the Zohar:

Rock [צור, tzur]: this word bears three explanations. The first, the language of yetzirah [forming], as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Berakhot 10a): "'Neither is there any rock like our God' (1 Sam. 2:2): there is no artist [tzayyar]," etc. And when we explain it in this way, it will be explained in Binah; for Binah is what portrayed and brought into being all the beings. And the second explanation, tzur the language of sela [crag], which is flint, and for the reason that she is the rock that "He opened … and the waters gushed out" (Ps. 105:41); and it is Malkhut. And according to their aspect mentioned, each one is called by the name tzur. And on the verse (2 Sam. 22:47; Ps. 18:47), "YHVH lives, and blessed be my Rock," he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 193b), that it is Tiferet; and the reason may be on account of the word "blessed"; and it is strained. And the third explanation, tzur the language of strength; and this is in Gevurah, which is strong in the force of judgment:

The need of the world [צורך העולם, tzorekh ha-olam]: Malkhut is so called for several reasons: whether that she is the need of the upper world, as we explained in the preceding gates, that "the Shekhinah among the lower ones is a need on high"; and also because the principal of the emanation of this attribute was for the need of the lower world, as we explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation:

The form of a male [צורת זכר, tzurat zakhar]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Tiferet is called the form of a male; and the reason is that Tiferet and Malkhut are male and female: the male, Tiferet, and Malkhut female:

Drought [צחצחות, tzachtzachot]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 141a), and these are his words: "'And satisfy your soul in drought [be-tzachtzachot]' (Isa. 58:11): this is the shining mirror, which all the souls enjoy gazing at and taking pleasure within." Thus far his words. And the intent is certainly Binah, toward whom are the yearnings of all the souls. And they are called tzachtzachot because many sparks go out from her, according to the measure of the souls: for each soul one clear [tzach] spark:

Zion [ציון, Tziyyon]: on this name we have found two explanations of Rashbi, peace be upon him. The one is in Malkhut, which is sometimes called the point of Zion; the second is Yesod. And it appears to us to say that, just as in the union of male and female in the human species there is a place specific to the body, which is the spine, bestowing and receiving; and a place specific to the arms and the legs, bestowing and receiving, upper and lower; and a place specific to the covenant, "according to the space of each, with wreaths" (1 Kings 7:36); so in Malkhut, since Yesod is the organ of the union, there is in her a place specific to the particular Yesod, on which the principal of the union and coupling depends, and a specific place, etc., as we explained at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And now that point in which is the union of Yesod and Malkhut is called the point of Zion: this Zion and that Zion, point over against point, Yod over against Yod: this the Yod that is in Yesod, and that the Yod that is in Malkhut. This seems to me the settling of the sayings. However, it is somewhat difficult for us from the Zohar, Parashat Tzav (fol. 31), and these are his words: "Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Yose were going from Usha to Tiberias. Rabbi Chiyya said: It is written, 'For YHVH has chosen Zion,' etc.; 'This is My resting place,' etc. (Ps. 132:13–14). At times all the companions call this male, because Zion is compassion; and this verse calls it female. Rabbi Yose said: So have we heard from the upper Lamp: but at the time of coupling, when they couple as one, to show that the female is included in him in one inclusion, the female is called by the name (of the male); for then the blessings of the Lady are found, and there is no separation in him at all. And therefore 'He has desired it for His habitation' is written; and it is written, 'For YHVH has chosen Zion' [be-Tziyyon]: 'be-Tziyyon' precisely, in that which is within it, which dwells in it; and it is not written 'le-Tziyyon.' And all is one, whether one calls this by the name of the male or one calls this by the name of the female; all is one, and they stand in one rung." Thus far his words.

And behold, he objected that Zion is always male, in Yesod, and so it is agreed among the companions; if so, how did the verse call it [female], in what it said, "This is My resting place"? As it appears, Zion is female and not male. And Rabbi Yose answered that the reason that it comes in this verse in the feminine is not because Zion is female, but that Malkhut, the female, is included with him; and because she is included with him, the feminine language is right of him; and not of him himself, but of Malkhut, who is included with him. And he was precise in this from what the verse said, "For YHVH has chosen be-Tziyyon," and did not say "For YHVH has chosen le-Tziyyon," which would appear that the choice is that He chose Zion itself; but be-Tziyyon, whose explanation is: that which is included in Zion, that is, Malkhut.

And behold, from this saying it appears that Yesod is called Zion and Malkhut is not called Zion; and even according to this view, Yesod is called Zion only when it is united with Malkhut. And so Rabbi Yose himself explained there, and these are his words: "'And of Zion it shall be said,' etc. (Ps. 87:5): when they couple as one in one coupling, then it is called Zion; and Zion in Jerusalem is made known and found, and this depends on that." Thus far his words. And according to what appears, this language is understood somewhat as we explained at first. And nevertheless, the matter is not firm in our hands; for even the language in the previous saying can be set right; but it is not our intent to lengthen:

Plate [ציץ, tzitz]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the commandment of the fringes [tzitzit] (in Parashat Shelach, fol. 174b) that the tzitz is Binah. And therefore the High Priest is crowned with the tzitz, the crown of Binah; and it atones for brazenness of face; and there is found only the face of truth, the face included in Tiferet. And it seems to me that therefore there was written on it "Holy to YHVH": for "holy" is in the three first ones, as will be explained in its entry; and "to YHVH" is Tiferet; and the explanation, Binah, which hovers over Tiferet by means of the High Priest, the man of Chesed:

Fringes [ציצית, tzitzit]: it is the Shekhinah, in her lower manifestation, which draws near to the depths of the sea. And therefore it is blue [tekhelet]; for the blue in Malkhut is her lower aspect, in the secret of the sea beneath which are the depths, in the secret of the judgment that is in her. And therefore they said, "blue resembles the sea." So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (there in the Ra'aya Meheimna):

The drippings of the pot [ציקי קדירה, tzikei kedeirah]: Malkhut is like a pot, in which all the beings are cooked and come into being, beings fit for them. However, this pot needs spices to sweeten the smoky power. And therefore "she smelled the drippings of the pot" (Pesachim 56a): the intent, she craved the union of the male, which are spices for the pot; and "her servants brought it to her in silence." And therefore we unite her in "Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom" [said silently]. And the commentators explained it in another sense, and it is not the principal:

The shadows of evening [צללי ערב, tzilelei erev] (Jer. 6:4): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Chayyei (fol. 132b), and these are his words: "The shadows of evening, which are the rung of harsh judgment; and then the Temple was destroyed and the palace burned." It appears that the force of judgment with its outer wings is all included in the language "the shadows of evening":

The shadow of death [צלמות, tzalmavet]: he explained in the Zohar, Vayetze (fol. 160b), that the husk that rides upon the female is called tzalmavet; and the reason is that the male rider is called tzel [shadow], and his female mavet [death]; the explanation, a shadow and power for death:

Rib [צלע, tzela] is Malkhut in her concealed manifestation, taken from the upper Man, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And there is the side of the Tabernacle [tzela ha-mishkan]; and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 12a) that Metatron is called the side of the Tabernacle: the explanation, a side to Malkhut and a servant to her:

White wool [צמר לבן, tzemer lavan]: in Chesed; and so we explained in "clean wool" in its entry; and so Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained. And to us it appears that it is the whiteness of Keter, as he says (Dan. 7:9), "and the hair of His head like clean wool." And it is known that the hair of the head is in Keter, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Souls, chapter 8:

Pipes [צנתרות, tzanterot] (Zech. 4:12): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Chokhmah and Binah are so called, for they are upon the pure menorah, emptying the oil, and upon the seven lamps. And he aimed well, for so it is proved from the verse. However, they are both gold, even though the one is toward the right, in the secret of silver, and the one toward the left, gold; because it is Chokhmah within Binah, in the secret of Heh over Yod, as we explained in many places:

Outcry [צעקה, tze'akah] is in Binah; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 20a), and these are his words: "Rabbi Judah said: Therefore outcry is greater than all of them, for outcry is in the heart; as it is written, 'Their heart cried unto YHVH' (Lam. 2:18)," etc. And the explanation: outcry is greater than sighing and crying out [shav'ah], which we explained and shall explain in their entries: that the crying out is in Malkhut, and the sighing is in Tiferet, and the outcry is in Binah, and it is greater than all of them; and it is the heart, and the heart is in Binah, as we explained, "the heart understands." And so he said there: "Rabbi Isaac said: Great is outcry, for it rules over the attribute of judgment above"; and it is in Binah, which rules over Gevurah. And so it is said there: "Rabbi Judah said: Great is outcry, for it tears up the decree of a man's judgment from all his days": the explanation, the outcry is in Binah, and it overturns and tears up the judgment into compassion, from all the seven days that are beneath her.

And further, he said there: "Rabbi Yose says: Great is outcry, for it rules in this world and in the world to come"; and it is Binah, that is, the world to come. And there is a difference between these three Tannaim. For Rabbi Judah said first that the outcry is in the heart, that is, Binah. And afterward Rabbi Isaac added that it is Binah when she is possessed of compassion, and there is in her power to turn the attribute of judgment to compassion; that is "which rules" that he said, as we explained above. And Rabbi Judah added to it and said that not only does she overturn the attribute of Gevurah alone, but she overturns all of them: even if the attribute of judgment has already spread out in all seven days of the building, there is in the outcry a clothing of compassion to turn all of them to compassion. And Rabbi Yose added to it and said that the outcry is in Binah in her aspect above, which cleaves to Chokhmah; that is, "which rules in the world to come"; for the world to come is Binah with respect to the bestowing aspect, as we explained in its entry. And behold, we have learned that outcry is in Binah, in one of three aspects, according to the explanations of the Tannaim. And ze'akah and tze'akah are all one thing; and we explained it in its entry:

North [צפון, tzafon] is Gevurah in every place. And therefore "Out of the north the evil shall break forth" (Jer. 1:14); for from there is drawn the attribute of evil in the world, a strap to lash the guilty. And there is good recompense for the righteous, as it is written (Ps. 31:20), "Oh how great is Your goodness, which You have laid up [tzafanta] for them that fear You." And therefore sometimes this name is for evil, sometimes for good. And in the Zohar, Parashat Bamidbar (fol. 120), it is understood that it is in Binah; and it is all one thing:

Bird [צפור, tzippor]: the Shekhinah, Malkhut, is so called for the reason that, just as the bird wanders from its nest, so she wanders from her nest, from the aspect of her union. And her husband is called of [fowl], and she is tzippor from his side. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 46). And elsewhere they explained that Malkhut is called tzippor from the direction of Metatron, who is also called tzippor. And it is possible to explain it by what is known, that Tiferet nests in Metatron; and we explained it in the Gate of ABYA. And elsewhere he explained that from the side of the ofannim [wheels] she is called tzippor; and the ofannim are Asiyah, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA. And it will mean that she is in the ofannim and her husband in Metatron, tzippor; and she, then, in the ofannim, is called tzippor from the side of her husband, who is in Metatron; and that is that she is called tzippor from the side of the ofannim. And it is all one:

The bundle of life [צרור החיים, tzeror ha-chayyim] (1 Sam. 25:29): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained this word in three places: in Binah, and in Tiferet, and in Malkhut. And it seems to me that the law is according to him, but not for his reasons. Rather, the bundle of life is Malkhut; and there is no bundle of fewer than three; that is, Binah and Tiferet, which are revealed in her and shine and bestow in her. And from within Malkhut the righteous enjoy the upper radiance. And that is that she is called the bundle of the life that is bestowed from Binah by means of Tiferet. This seems to me according to the method of Rabbi Moshe [de León]; and there is some revealing of this from the Zohar. However, we have found in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 25b), these are his words: "Rabbi Isaac said, etc.: When the Assembly of Israel is crowned with the Holy King, she is crowned and called the bundle of life, because in her all is bound. Rabbi Eleazar said: The Shekhinah, when she journeys, journeys with the Patriarchs; as it is written, 'And the angel of God, who went,' etc. (Exod. 14:19). Rabbi Abba said: All is made one diadem [itra], so that they be crowned [de-yit'atar] as one, and the holy Name is seen in its colors; at that time she is called 'As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons' (Song 2:3)," etc. Thus far his words.

And behold, these three Tannaim, Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba, agree that these three verses are three Patriarchs; however, in the manner of her bond with them they disagree. Rabbi Isaac said, "When she is crowned," etc.: the explanation, the principal union of the Shekhinah is only with her husband, Tiferet; and this is her true crowning; and when she is united with him, then she is called the bundle of life. And the reason is that all is united with her; however, her principal intent is only to be united with Tiferet, and of themselves the rest of the Emanation are united with her. And because of this she is called the bundle of life; for she is a bundle and gathering for all the upper living beings, that is, all the Emanation. And Rabbi Eleazar said: I agree with you in one thing, that is, that there is no bundle of fewer than three; and I disagree with you in two. One, that you said that the Shekhinah is united only in Tiferet alone.

And further, you said that the bundle is on account of the union of all the Emanation. In these two I disagree with you. "The Shekhinah, when she journeys, journeys with the Patriarchs," etc.: he was precise not to say "when she is crowned," for crowning is the union in the matter of coupling; but "journeys": the explanation, a journey; when she journeys, it is only in the company of the Patriarchs. And even the union: if she does not receive from the Patriarchs, she will have no coupling at all; for the principal of the arousal is from Chesed and Gevurah, in the secret of the embrace. And he proved the matter from the verse "And the angel of God journeyed," etc.; and the matter is that "the angel of God" is in Malkhut.

And behold, there are mentioned three verses one after the other, that is, "and it journeyed," "and it came," "and he stretched out" (Exod. 14:19–21), in the journeying of the Shekhinah, to hint that when she journeys she does not journey with fewer than three Patriarchs with her; and that is that she is called the bundle of life. And Rabbi Abba agrees with Rabbi Eleazar in part and disagrees with him in part. For he said that Malkhut receives from the three Patriarchs, through each one in its place, from each one by itself; and for this he was compelled to bring a proof from "and it journeyed," and it is not so much of a proof. To this Rabbi Abba said, "All is made one diadem": the explanation, Tiferet is united in all of them and is released [mitpater] in all of them, "so that they be crowned as one": the explanation, he proved the thing and said, all is made one union in Tiferet. And the reason, "so that they be crowned as one": the explanation, so that all be united; and if not through Tiferet, the Emanation would not be included, as is known in one explanation: that it is the inclusion of the Emanation and is included in one, that is, ach Dalet [echad]. And therefore, in order that the Emanation be united, all is made in Tiferet one diadem and one union. And he proved the matter: "at that time she is called 'As the apple tree among the trees of the wood,'" etc.; and it is already known that in the apple there are three colors, white, red and green, that is, her union with the three Patriarchs. And now, in her being united with her husband Tiferet alone, she is united of herself with the three Patriarchs; and then she is called the bundle of life. Thus far his words.

And behold, from it three explanations of the bundle of life are made clear. Further, Tiferet is called the bundle of myrrh [tzeror ha-mor] (Song 1:13), for it is a bundle in which is gathered the effluence that is bestowed from myrrh, which is Chesed; and therefore it is called a staff toward Chesed:

Needful [צריכא, tzerikha]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a) that every term of need is in Malkhut; and she is so called from the side of Tiferet when it draws nourishment from the side of Gevurah; as if we said that she is so called from the side of Tiferet, from the side of the Gevurah that is in it. And he explained there: "in her [He] supplied our need in the wilderness." And the reason that she is then called tzerikha is because she then needs bestowal; for Tiferet draws nourishment from judgment and does not bestow in her according to all the need, but with contraction. But on the side of Tiferet itself she is called "she does not need," and that is la tzerikha: the explanation, that since she draws compassion from Tiferet, then she does not need; for the Vav bestows effluence to her from the side of its effluence, its aspect in itself. Thus far the strength of our poor and weak power has reached in the explanation of the entry of the letter Tzadi. And now we enter into the explanation of the letter Kof, with the help of Heaven:

Receiving [קבלה, kabbalah]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a) that Malkhut is called kabbalah from the side of Yesod, because she receives souls from above through it. And elsewhere (in Tikkun 21, fol. 45a) he explained that she is called kabbalah when her husband receives her between the two arms, between Gedulah and Gevurah. And it is all one; for then she receives souls in the secret of the coupling:

Holy [קדוש, kadosh] is in Keter, and in Tiferet, and in Yesod. And it is fitting to know that there is no kadosh except in the secret of Vav. Keter is kodesh without Vav; and when Tiferet rises in the form of a Vav into Keter, in the secret of Da'at, then it becomes kadosh with a Vav; so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim. And in the drawing of the holiness from above, it will afterward be kadosh in Tiferet, and afterward kadosh in Yesod, and afterward kedushah in Malkhut. It is found according to this that Keter is called kadosh only when Da'at rises within it; and Tiferet is called kadosh only in its descending from Keter, in the secret of the drawing of the holiness from above; and Yesod is called kadosh only in the drawing of the holiness from the head of Keter down to Yesod, and then it becomes kadosh. And when the kadosh enters Malkhut she is called kedushah:

Holiness [קדושה, kedushah]: Malkhut is called kedushah. The explanation: Tiferet is called kadosh; and when it joins and bestows its holiness in Malkhut, she becomes kedushah; the explanation, kadosh-Heh. And on the matter of holiness, whether it is from the right or from the left, there are sayings in the Zohar that disagree with one another: in places he says that holiness is from the right and purity in the left, and in places he says that holiness is in the left and purity in the right. And we have already set this matter right in the entry taharah [purity]:

Before [קדם, kedem]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Keter is called kedem because it preceded all the sefirot. And in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that kedem is Chokhmah. And the reason appears to be that it precedes all the revealing, as we explained in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof Is Keter; and so the Targum renders bereshit as be-kadmin. And it is found according to this that there are two firsts: kedem to the beginning of the Emanation, and kedem to the revealing. And elsewhere it appears to Rashbi, peace be upon him, that Binah too is called kedem. And the reason may be that she is kedem to the question; for in Binah is the beginning of the question; and so she is called Mi [Who]:

Holy [קדש, kodesh] is in Binah, and from Binah upward; for from Chokhmah upward it is called kodesh kodashim [Holy of Holies]. And it is possible to say that kodesh is Keter and kodashim are Chokhmah and Binah. And there is a great difference between kodesh and kadosh: for kodesh is in the three first ones; kadosh in Tiferet and from it downward, as we explained above. And the principal of kodesh without qualification is in Chokhmah. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 13a), and these are his words: "What is kodesh? The upper place, from which the spring of the deep stream goes out; as it is written, 'And a river went out of Eden to water' (Gen. 2:10); and Eden is what is called the upper kodesh." Thus far his words. And he intended to say [this] because Binah too is called kodesh; and for this he lengthened, "the upper place, from which the spring," etc.: the explanation, Chokhmah, which is the Eden from which goes out the river, which is Binah; and since it goes out from the kodesh, it is fitting that she too be called kodesh. And so it is explained in many places, in Parashat Mishpatim (fol. 121) and in Parashat Acharei (fol. 61a):

The middle line [קו האמצעי, kav ha-emtza'i]: Tiferet is so called because it is in the middle, rising and descending from the beginning of the Emanation to its end; rising up to above, and piercing and descending to below, in the secret of the extension before its taking hold of the extremities, as we explained in the preceding gates. And it is called the line of measure [kav ha-middah], in the secret of the inner spirituality, which is what gives measure to all the Emanation, as we explained in the Gate of Essences and Vessels. And it is called the green line that surrounds the world, which is the six extremities, in the secret of Da'at that spreads out within the circuit. And it is called green in the secret of its color, which is green, as we explained in the Gate of Colors. And others explained that Binah is called the green line; and her color we explained in the Gate of Colors, that it is not like the green of Tiferet. And elsewhere in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Tiferet is the green line from the side of Binah; and on this matter we explained in the entry chut [thread]. And elsewhere in the Zohar (in the Zohar Chadash, Parashat Balak, fol. 65b, and brought in the Tosefta to the Zohar) he explained that the outer husk is called the green line, and it surrounds the whole world, as we explained in the Gate of Substitutes:

Voice [קול, kol]: there is no voice except from the side of Tiferet, and it is what is called kol in every place. And there is an inner voice, which is not heard, and it is in Binah; and nevertheless the intent is the Da'at concealed in her; for there is no voice that is not in Tiferet, Vav. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that kol without qualification is in Tiferet. And all seven sefirot are called voices; and they are the seven voices that are in the psalm "Give unto YHVH" (Ps. 29); and all of them are from the side of Tiferet, which is called voice, as we shall explain. And even at the giving of the Torah, all of them are called voices from the side of Tiferet; and they are six voices, and it is the seventh voice, which includes them all, in the secret of its rising to Binah, as we shall explain. And there is kolot written defective, which is in Malkhut; and so he explained in the Zohar, "And all the people saw the voices [ha-kolot]" (Exod. 20:15), defective. And likewise every kol written defective is the Shekhinah. And so they explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Vayigash (fol. 210a), on the verse (Gen. 45:16), "And the report [ha-kol] was heard in Pharaoh's house"; and he explained there that she is so called, kol without Vav, when she lacks the Vav, which is her husband, and lacks the upper light. And the sign, "And the report was heard in Pharaoh's house": the explanation, a house that is peru'ah [unruly] and lacking entirely. And therefore it is said (Jer. 31:15), "A voice is heard in Ramah," at the time of the destruction. And there is kolah without Vav, and it is with Heh; and it is in Binah. However, kol without qualification is in Tiferet. And sometimes it is called the voice of the shofar; and the explanation, the voice that goes out from Binah; and she is the great shofar, as will be explained in its entry. And the voice goes out included of fire and water and air; and likewise the human voice is hot, and it is moist, and it is air, to hint at Tiferet, which is included of the three Patriarchs; and therefore it is called voice. For this voice of the shofar is more subtle than the manifestation of Tiferet itself, as he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemini (fol. 38b), and these are his words: "Rabbi Simeon said: What we have learned, that it is written 'the voice of the shofar,' is well; and this is Jacob, who rose up in the Thought of the Patriarchs, and they went out as one from within the shofar; for the shofar brings out water and fire and air as one, and from them a voice is made. So the upper Mother brought out the Patriarchs in one voice, and from within the Thought they rose up as one in one voice; and that voice is called the voice of the shofar; and this is Jacob, who includes the Patriarchs as one, and is called voice," etc. Thus far his words. And his intent is clear: that Jacob is called the voice of the shofar only when he rises in the inclusion of the Patriarchs, and the Patriarchs are included with him, and he rises up to the Thought, which is Chokhmah; and from there they go out through Binah and are included in Tiferet; and this is the voice of the shofar. Further, there is in Binah a voice that is heard outside and a voice that is not heard; and this is in the secret of two aspects. One, with Chokhmah, and she is called Mi; and this is the voice that is not heard, for she is concealed. And the second aspect is her aspect with the sefirot below; and it is what is called the voice that is heard outside, for she is revealed. Further, there is the still small voice [kol demamah dakkah] (1 Kings 19:12), which is in Malkhut; and the explanation, voice, which is Tiferet, united in the still small [silence], which is Malkhut, which is the standing [prayer] in silence. All this is explained on the matter of the voice. And there is the voice of the turtledove [kol ha-tor] (Song 2:12); and the explanation, the voice of Tiferet, which is the voice of the tor, which is Malkhut (see Parashat Vayikra, fol. 4b):

Leniency [קולא, kula]: Malkhut is called kula from the side of Chesed; for the lightness of the matter is from her side, through Chesed. And there he explained: "there is one who says the reverse," that kula is from the side of Gevurah; and he spoke at length in the Tikkunim (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 116b):

Stature [קומה, komah]: the stature is the extension of the spine from the neck, hinted in Binah as we explained in its entry, down to the end of the thighs, with the whole extension of Yesod. And Tiferet and the Righteous One are called stature in their being bound above in Binah, and their descending below down to Malkhut, "from the one end of heaven to the other" (Deut. 4:32):

Handful [קומץ, kometz]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 4a): the kometz is Yod, which is Chokhmah; and it opens to five fingers, which is Binah, Heh, the fifty gates of Binah. It is found that Chokhmah is called kometz, in the secret of the closing of the hand and its concealment above, before its revealing and spreading out to Binah:

Thorn [קוץ, kotz]: in every place the thorns of the letters are hinted in Yesod; for it is called the thorn that holds between heaven and earth, as it is written (1 Chron. 29:11), "for all that is in the heaven and in the earth," and we render it "which holds in heaven and in earth"; and all the thorns of the letters are hinted in it. And there is no wonder from the thorn of the Yod, which is in Keter (for there is the single Lord, wondrous and covered, etc.):

Cold and heat, summer and winter [קור וחום קיץ וחורף, kor va-chom kayitz va-choref] (Gen. 8:22): these four words are the four parts of the year, three months to each part of them. Certainly, according to their matter, they are the four parts of the diagonal boundaries that we explained in the Gate of the Particulars of the Names. And three are Chesed, and that is summer; and they are the three boundaries of the south, which are the Yod of the Name. And three are heat, Gevurah; and they are strong judgment; and these are the three boundaries of the north, which are the Heh of the Name. And the three boundaries of the east are from the side of Tiferet; and they are winter, which is water; and from the side of their being from the side of Gevurah it is called "the might of the rains," and from the side of Chesed they are water. And three are the boundaries of the west, from the side of Malkhut; and they are cold, which is the element of earth, cold and dry; "for He says to the snow, Be on the earth" (Job 37:6). And winter and cold may also be in Netzach and Hod; for Tiferet's inclination is in Netzach and Malkhut's in Hod; and they are the letters Vav-Heh in the Name:

Difficulty [קושיא, kushya]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a) that Malkhut is so called, in the secret of the hard attribute of judgment; for then there is difficulty and dispute:

The destruction that wastes at noonday [קטב ישוד צהרים, ketev yashud tzohorayim] (Ps. 91:6): and these are his words in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (fol. 236a): "For from the side of the gold the dross goes out when the gold is refined; and from there spread out all those sides of the left, which are the smelting of that dross; and they separate into several sides. And all those that have a red appearance, the color of gold, stand in the mountains when the sun is in its strength; because the strength of the sun shows the gold and begets it in the earth. And the one who is appointed over that strength of the sun, his appearance is like a calf; and he is called ketev yashud tzohorayim." Thus far his words. And behold, ketev yashud tzohorayim was the power of the golden calf with which Israel sinned. And he is called ketev; and he and his power are drawn from the side of Tiferet, in the secret of the inclination to Gevurah; and not from Tiferet itself, but by way of the chain of descent of the other outer rungs. And so it appears that he is ketev meriri [bitter destruction] (Deut. 32:24), whose explanation is that he is between the color of the sun, which is Tiferet, and the shadow, that is, the power of Gevurah, darkness:

Incense [קטורת, ketoret]: we have already explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance the matter of the incense: that it enters into the nose, which calms the power of judgment. And we explained in the entry ashan [smoke] that it is Tiferet, which rises to bind the worlds, Binah and Chokhmah, together; at the time of its rising it is called smoke. However, after it reaches within Chokhmah, that manifestation is called ketoret. And the reason is that when it has reached the haven of the union and the bond, and Chokhmah and Binah have been united through it, it is called ketoret, from the language of kesher [bond], whose explanation is that it binds the sefirot together. For in the light of these two faces, Chokhmah and Binah, all of them will see light and be united in a complete union. And therefore it is fitting that it be called ketoret, the language of bond. So it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 224a). And it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 54a) that Malkhut is the incense of Tiferet, because she is bound to her husband, as mentioned:

Stomach [קיבה, keivah]: he explained in the Zohar (Pinchas, fol. 234b) that it is one-sixtieth of death; and he said that it is one rung of the rungs of the husk. And there is in the stomach a good aspect, and it is what causes a dream of prophecy for the righteous; see there. And nevertheless the principal of the stomach is the husk:

Enduring [קיים, kayyam]: Rashbi explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 282a) that Tiferet is called kayyam; and these are his words: "Living [chai], Tzaddik; and enduring [kayyam], the central pillar." And we can say that from the side of its rising to Binah it is called kayyam; for she is what gives it endurance, just as it gives life to Yesod:
Pen [קולמוס, kulmus] is Tiferet; and it is called pen, in the form of a Vav, from the side of the hand that writes, as we explained in the entry chatimah [sealing]:

Sling [קלע, kela]: there is an upper sling and there is a lower sling, and they are the two Hehs. And of the upper sling it is said (1 Sam. 25:29), "and the souls of your enemies, them shall He sling out"; and it is the abolishing of the husk; so they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 115b and fol. 128b). And the sling stones are five, of which it is said (1 Sam. 17:40), "and he chose him five smooth stones out of the brook"; and they are five bars, five sefirot, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, body and covenant counted as one, and Netzach and Hod: they are five. And when they are united in Binah or in Malkhut they are called sling; and their union is the sling stone, the manifestation of the Heh that is concealed and becomes Yod, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 40a; see there in the Kisse Melekh):

Nest [קן, ken]: Malkhut is called nest. And the fledglings are the six children that crouch upon her, by means of Tiferet her husband, who lies in her bosom between her breasts. And the bird that hovers over the children is Binah, "a joyful mother of children" (Ps. 113:9). And as is the case of Binah, so is the case of Malkhut: and the fledglings are her six maidens, and her nest is Metatron. And of this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Avot, ch. 4): "Look not at the flask [kankan] but at what is in it"; for Malkhut is within it, as he said (Exod. 23:21), "for My name is in him." And sometimes the whole building is called nest, because they are the children that are in the nest; and the principal of the nest is only the eggs or the children. And elsewhere (in Tikkun 6, fol. 19) Metatron is called "the bird's nest," for the reason that on weekdays he is a nest for Malkhut, who is called bird:

Windpipe [קנה, kaneh]: in the windpipe there are six rings, and they are over against six sefirot; and they are the six steps to the upper throne. Binah is the heart that understands; and she rises by way of Tiferet to the brain, to be united with it, and through it, in the secret of Da'at. And the matter is in the secret of the permutation [of the Name] that is  Y V H H: and the Vav is found between the Yod and the first Heh; and the Heh rises by way of it to be united with her husband, Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And the matter is that the Thought that acts in Chokhmah has within it six extremities, and from it they went out to Binah; and they are subtle spiritual beings in the secret of Da'at. And it is so that in the rising of Tiferet to Binah it enters by way of her into Chokhmah, as we explained in the preceding gates. And from within this windpipe goes out the voice that includes the fire and the water and the air, and the inner Tiferet in the secret of Da'at, as we explained above. And the voice is like a soul to the windpipe. And the windpipe is the union between Binah and Chokhmah, in the secret of "Get [keneh] wisdom, get understanding" (Prov. 4:5). And there is a reed [kaneh] on the side of the husk; and that is the matter of "he stuck a reed in the sea, and on it was built the great city of Rome" (Shabbat 56b). And this is "Rebuke the beast of the reeds" (Ps. 68:31). "God has made even the one over against the other" (Eccl. 7:14):

The end of all flesh [קץ כל בשר, ketz kol basar] (Gen. 6:13): the husk, Samael, is so called, for the reason that it pursues the destruction of the creatures; that is, ketz from the language of cutting off. So he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit and Parashat Noach: that the husks are so called for the reason that they are the end and cutting off of all flesh. And there is the end of the right [ketz ha-yamin] (Dan. 12:13), from the side of the right; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 54a) and in Parashat Noach (fol. 63a). And the language of ketz in every place is Yesod; and we explained it at length in the entry sof; see there:

The leaping of the earth [קפיצת הארץ, kefitzat ha-aretz]: he explained in the Tikkunim that Malkhut is so called, in the secret that she leaps to couple with her husband. And likewise she is called the leaping of the way [kefitzat ha-derekh], for she is the leaping of the derekh, which is Tiferet, as we explained in its entry:

Inward parts [קרבים, kerabim]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 87a), on the verse (Ps. 103:1), "Bless YHVH, O my soul, and all that is within me [kol kerabai]," etc.; and these are his words: "Who are kerabai? These are the other outer living creatures, which are called kerabim, as it is said, 'and my bowels were moved for him' (Song 5:4)." Thus far his words. It appears that he explains this matter of the holy living creatures; and he called them outer living creatures because they are outside the Emanation; and they are called kerabim on account of their being near [kerovim] to the Emanation. And he brought a proof from the verse (Song 5:4), "and my bowels were moved for him"; for bowels and inward parts are all one thing. And the matter of "were moved [hamu] for him" is to their question, "Where is the place of His glory?" etc.; and this is hamu, the explanation, murmuring and singing; "for him," the explanation, for his sake; after the manner of the living creatures that sing to the Shekhinah (and see Tikkun 6, fol. 19b, the matter of "my bowels are moved for him"). Offering [קרבן, korban]: the Shekhinah is so called for several reasons. One, because in her all the sefirot draw near [mitkarvim] and are bound and united; and because of this she is called agudah [bundle], as we explained in its entry. And further, because she is an offering that draws near to Tiferet; and therefore she is called "an offering to YHVH" (Lev. 1:2), which shows the union of both of them together, Tiferet and Malkhut. And in Malkhut's drawing near to Tiferet, all the sefirot are united through her in a complete union and drawing near; and therefore she is called by the language of korban, on account of the drawing near: the explanation, the manifestation of the drawing near and union of the letters YHVH, which are the union of all the sefirot. So he explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Vayikra (fol. 5a, and in Parashat Tzav, fol. 31a):

Near [קרוב, karov]: Yesod is called karov for the reason that it is "a neighbour that is near" to the Shekhinah, and it is "better … than a brother far off" (Prov. 27:10), which is Tiferet at the time of its distance. It is found that Yesod is called near at the time of the distance of Tiferet, and the nearness of Yesod to her (see the Ra'aya Meheimna, Mishpatim, fol. 115b, and Tikkun 21, fol. 42b):

The terrible ice [קרח הנורא, kerach ha-nora] (Ezek. 1:22): the Shekhinah is called kerach, from that terrible one, the central pillar; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 19, fol. 38a). And kerach and chirek are all one; and she is called kerach in the secret of her lower manifestation. And there is a difference between kerach and chirek: for chirek is judgment, from the language of "they gnash [va-yachreku] the teeth" (Lam. 2:16), as we shall explain in the Gate of Vowels; and kerach is turned from judgment to compassion; and that is kerach, in the secret of the whiteness; and it is her lower manifestation, which is stretched over the heads of the living creatures. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained "the terrible ice" as Tiferet; and it is not to the point; for he confused kerach with nora:

Kiryat Arba [קרית ארבע, kiryat arba, the City of Four]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 33a) that the Shekhinah is called Kiryat Arba, because in her is the joining of the four passages that are in the tefillin; and they are the four-letter name, four letters. And further, he explained there: because in her four names are united, which are YHVH, EHYH, male and female, behold two; and YHVH, Adonai, male and female, behold another two: these in Chokhmah and Binah, and these in Tiferet and Malkhut. And we explained them in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 151), that she is also called the city of the great King (Ps. 48:3) when she receives from Binah, which is called the great King. And Binah is a city to Chokhmah, which is the great King over her:

Horn [קרן, keren]: on the matter of keren and chomesh [principal and fifth], Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Vayikra, fol. 24) that Tiferet is keren, and the Shekhinah chomesh. And he said that what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, that the ox that the first Adam offered had one horn on its forehead, was said of this horn. And likewise he said there that it is called the horn of the Jubilee: the explanation, the horn that goes out from Binah, which is the Jubilee. And it is possible that this keren is from the language of light, as "that the skin of Moses' face shone [karan]" (Exod. 34:35); and therefore it is in Tiferet. However, corner [keren zavit], and likewise "he went up on the ramp," etc., "and came to the corner [keren]," the explanation, Malkhut; and she is called keren because she is a corner and turning for all the Emanation. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 19b), on the verse (1 Sam. 2:10), "and exalt the horn of His anointed": "This is the Assembly of Israel, which is called keren (of the Jubilee)." Thus far his words. And in Parashat Lekh (fol. 96a) he explained that she is called keren when she draws the good oil that kindles and illuminates the sefirot, which is bestowed from the source of the oil, as is explained in its entry. And in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 9b) he explained that the two horns are Netzach and Hod, and they are the horns of the Shekhinah, in the secret of the two straps of the head; and one horn is Yesod, the horn of Malkhut, like this, הי, or like this, ה. And they said: "with two horns, and the one higher than the other" (Dan. 8:3); for so Netzach is higher than Hod. Thus far:

Ankles [קרסולים, karsullayim]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 2b) that they are Netzach and Hod. And the reason may be that they themselves are the thighs: with respect to Tiferet, which is the body, they are called thighs; and with respect to Yesod, which is truly below, they are called ankles; for with respect to it they are not united to it except in the aspect of ankles, which is below the thighs:
Gizzard [קרקבן, kurkevan]: the gizzard and the stomach [istomkha] are all one thing, and they have one explanation; and as we explained in the entry istomkha, so is the rule of the gizzard:

Ground [קרקע, karka]: the Shekhinah is so called (in Tikkun 19, fol. 37b, and in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 243b), because she is "the ground of the world" for all the nine upper sefirot; and of her they said (in Sanhedrin 74b), "Esther was the ground of the world." And in her they are planted, each in his place; and in this manifestation she is called ground. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 121b) he explained that Yesod is called the ground of Aravot, for Aravot is Tiferet; and this is the ground of Aravot. And the reason may be because it is ground to Tiferet; for it is the extension of the Vav; and that is the ground of Aravot:

Knot [קשר, kesher]: every knot is a bundle, and there is no bundle of fewer than three; and they are teki'ah, shevarim, teru'ah, that is, KeSheR [an acronym]; that is, the three Patriarchs, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. And Tiferet, which binds the three Patriarchs in the secret of the arbitration, is called kesher. And likewise Yesod, in the secret of its arbitration, is called the knot of three others like these, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod: three Patriarchs and three sons; and "the deeds of the fathers the sons will do." It is found a knot within a knot, Tiferet within Yesod; and that is a seal within a seal. And likewise the Shekhinah is called kesher, because she binds these three aspects, in the secret of Heh, three Vavs; and likewise Shabbat, Shin, bat: three Vavs [and a daughter]. And therefore she is called the knot of the tefillin. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Binah is called the knot of the sefirot, because she binds the seven sefirot with the three first ones, as we shall explain in the entry Shekhinah:

Bow [קשת, keshet]: he explained in the Tikkunim that Yesod is called keshet because it is the covenant of the bow, through which is the union; and of Joseph it is said (Gen. 49:24), "But his bow abode in strength." And keshet and kesher are all one thing; for KeSheR is teki'ah, shevarim, teru'ah, and that is KeSheT [teru'ah]. And the union is impossible without the strong knot, which are the covenant and the two testicles of the male. And then it is called keshet, and it shoots arrows, in the secret of the seed that shoots like an arrow, as we explained in the entry chitzim. And the letter Kof is completed, with the help of the One who makes every crooked thing straight. And now we shall come to the explanation of the entry of the letter Resh:

Seeing [ראייה, re'iyah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar that seeing depends on Binah; and the sign: "the heart sees." And so it appears from some of the places that the principal of seeing depends on Binah and Gevurah; and every place where you find the language of seeing, its principal depends on the left. And in other places, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 230a) and in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that seeing is the face of the lion [aryeh], and it is in Chesed. And likewise Reuben, or ben [light, son], and it is seeing and light, which is in Chesed and Chokhmah. And likewise the explanation of re'iyah is aryeh; for in re'iyah he added a Yod to the word aryeh; and the hint is to Chokhmah, which is Yod. And this explanation is the principal and more compelling. And their saying "the heart sees" is that in Binah too there is the power of seeing; nevertheless its principal is in Chokhmah and Chesed, and it is found in Binah through Chokhmah. And there is seeing for good and seeing for evil; and he proved the matter from the verses in the Zohar, Parashat Vayera (fol. 105b). And the reason is that sometimes Chesed inclines to judgment; and therefore seeing for judgment:

Head [ראש, rosh]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 39, fol. 77; see there) that the Supreme Crown, from the side of Chokhmah, is called rosh. For Chokhmah too is rosh, as we explained in the entry mitzvah; and Keter, over Chokhmah, is called the true rosh, for it is head to all heads. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that sometimes it is also called the white head, because in it is the true whiteness; and it is so called when it whitens the iniquities of Israel:

And Chesed is called the top of the mountains [rosh harim], because it is head to three mountains, which are the Patriarchs. "Hear, O mountains, the controversy of YHVH" (Micah 6:2): and who are the mountains? That is, the three Patriarchs; so he explained in the Zohar (Tisa, fol. 189b). And in the Tikkunim, on the verse (Gen. 8:5), "were the tops of the mountains seen," he explained that they are the three Patriarchs, which are called the tops of the mountains. And the reason may be because they are heads to all the other extremities, which are all called mountains, as we explained:

And the head of the righteous [rosh tzaddik] (Prov. 10:6): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze, two explanations. The first, that Tiferet is called rosh tzaddik for the reason that it dwells upon its head. And so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 7, fol. 82a [?]): "Who is rosh tzaddik? This is the central pillar." And the second explanation: the place from which the blessings of the Righteous One go out to Malkhut. The explanation: the place of the outpouring of the blessings, through whose watercourse the blessings are bestowed to Malkhut, is called rosh tzaddik; certainly it is the lower aspect of Yesod, with respect to its being united with Malkhut:

The head of the word [ראש דבר, rosh davar]: there are those who explained it in Chesed, and there are those who explained it in Tiferet. And this seems to me the principal; for it is head to Malkhut, who is called davar. And it is possible that for this reason it is said (Ps. 119:160), "The head of Your word is truth"; as it is written (Micah 7:20), "You will give truth to Jacob." And nevertheless it is somewhat right of Yesod:

The heads of the living creature [ראשי החיה, rashei ha-chayyah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 5, fol. 18b) that the living creature is Malkhut, and her heads are Netzach and Hod; and of them it is written (Ezek. 1:22), "And over the heads of the living creature there was the likeness of a firmament." And on the heads of the upper living creature there are many explanations in the Tikkunim:

Beginning [ראשית, reshit]: Chokhmah is called reshit because it is the beginning of the revealing, as we spoke at length in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof Is Keter. And Malkhut, in her manifestation of the Yod, which is likened to it, is also called reshit. And he said in the Tikkunim that she too is the beginning of all the creatures, just as the upper Wisdom is the beginning of all that is revealed in the Emanation. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] said that Chokhmah is called the first of the heave offering [reshit terumah], because it is the beginning, etc. Thus far. And because of this, one grain of wheat exempts the whole heap; and it has no measure, for the paucity of the apprehension of it. And likewise it is called the chief of the ointments [reshit shemanim] (Amos 6:6), because it is the beginning of the effluence of Keter:

Abundance [רב, rav]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 129a), on the verse (Gen. 48:16), "and let them grow into a multitude [la-rov]": wisdom, of which it is said (1 Kings 5:10), "and Solomon's wisdom excelled [va-terev]," etc. It appears that the language of rav is from the side of Chokhmah; and there is some support for the matter; for the Targum of "the anointing oil," which is in Chokhmah, is meshach revut kudsha:

Abundant in mercy [רב חסד, rav chesed] (Exod. 34:6): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Chesed is called rav chesed. And he was not precise well; for Tiferet is called rav chesed, because most of it [rubbo] is Chesed, even though there is judgment in it. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Rosh Hashanah 17a): "Rav chesed: He inclines toward Chesed"; and that is Tiferet, which inclines itself, and Gevurah with it, toward Chesed. And it is so called in its arbitration to the side of the right. And there is great goodness [rav tuv] (Isa. 63:7); and he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 7b), that it is "the pleasure of life that flows from the world to come to the Life of the Worlds." Thus far his words. And the intent is that the effluence bestowed from Binah, which makes Yesod grow, is called rav tuv; and its explanation is the effluence that increases and makes Yesod grow. Further, he explained there another explanation: that rav without qualification is Tiferet; and it is called rav because it is "a great [rav] and mighty tree, because there is a small tree from it." And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 52b) he explained that in the husk the male is called rav ha-chovel [the shipmaster, read as the chief spoiler], as we explained in the entry chavalah:

Square [רבוע, ribbu'a]: it appears from the language of the Zohar that the square and the four-square are all in Binah; and Binah is called four-square only when she crouches [rova'at] over the children, and especially when she crouches over the four sides of the world. And there is some revealing of this from the Zohar (Terumah, fol. 127a):

Many [רבים, rabbim]: it is agreed in the Zohar and in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 117a) and in many places that rabbim are the three Patriarchs, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; and together they are called rabbim; and likewise "there is no 'many' fewer than three" (in the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 1). And so it is proved from several places. And they are called rabbim because they are many; for before the union and the agreement in the secret of the arbitration they are called many: that is to say, three divided; for they are called many only when they are divided against one another; however, in their union they are called agudah [bundle], the language of union. And "they are many that fight against me" (Ps. 56:3): the explanation, rabbim from the language of riv [strife], or as "and he became an archer [roveh kashat]" (Gen. 21:20):

Fourth part [רובע, rova] is Yesod, which is so called from the language of revi'a [lying with], for through it the Chief lies with the wife of his youth. And he explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 204a) that it is called rova because the measure of the body is four covenants; and that is that it is called "the fourth part of Israel" (Num. 23:10). And in the Zohar (there, fol. 210b) he explained it in Malkhut, for two reasons: whether because she is fourth to the Chariot, or because she is "the bed which is Solomon's" (Song 3:7), that is, the language of revi'a:

Fourth [רביעית, revi'it]: Malkhut is called "the fourth part of a hin" (Exod. 29:40). And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 247b) the reason: that she is fourth to Yod-Heh-Vav, which are three letters, and Heh the fourth; and that is "the fourth part of a hin" [ha-hin, read as the Hehs]. And he explained further another explanation: "the fourth part of a hin," the fourth leg to the throne of four legs: Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, and Malkhut fourth to them. And according to all the explanations she is called "the fourth part of a hin" only when she is united with the three Patriarchs or with the three letters:

Rebecca [רבקה, Rivkah]: Malkhut is so called. However, she is so called only in her aspect from the side of the force of judgment, and when she is united with her husband from the side of Gevurah (see the Zohar, Toledot, fol. 137a):

Feet [רגלים, raglayim], and likewise regalim [festivals]: all of it is in Malkhut. And she is called feet in the secret of the lower aspect, which is clothed within the husk, in the secret of "I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?" (Song 5:3); and it is the stretching of the sparks that are clothed in the husks. And in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 86a), he explained that the angels are called feet; and these are his words: "Who are His feet? These are angels, which are beneath the Holy One, blessed be He; as it is said, 'And His feet shall stand in that day' (Zech. 14:4)," etc. Thus far his words. And it is somewhat right with what we explained above, that is, the feet of the Shekhinah, her aspect with [her] powers. However, raglayim is the one clothed in the pleasant shoes and sandals, as we explained in their entries; and this is "How beautiful are your steps in sandals, O prince's daughter" (Song 7:2). So it seems to me from the Introduction to the Zohar (and see Tikkun 18, fol. 34a):

Gutters [רהטים, rehatim]: according to what appears from the language of the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 37b), it will mean that Netzach and Hod are called "the gutters, in the watering troughs" (Gen. 30:38).
