And elsewhere (in Tikkun 6, fol. 138) he explained that rehatim is Binah; for he speaks of "the four channels [rehitei] of the brain":

Plenty [רוב, rov]: in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 143), it is understood somewhat that rov is in Yesod, when it is between Tiferet and Malkhut. And these are his words: "'And plenty of corn and wine' (Gen. 27:28): behold, they established it," etc. "'Yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken,' etc. (Ps. 37:25). Come and see: 'I have been young,' etc.; and they established that the Prince of the World said this verse," etc. "And therefore he said 'and plenty of corn and wine.'" Thus far his words. And the explanation: that it is called "plenty of corn and wine" because the abundance of the effluence never lacks from it, when it bestows to the Shekhinah and receives from above; that is, "Yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken" from above, from Tiferet. "Nor his seed begging bread": the explanation, seeking in whom to bestow; for "bread" is nothing but a wife. And therefore the abundance of the effluence is all the more obligatory; and this is the reason for "plenty of corn and wine." And in the Tikkunim: "the greatness of might [rov onim] (Isa. 40:26): this is the Supreme Crown"; and we explained it in the entry ish (see the book Kehillat Ya'akov):

Spirit [רוח, ru'ach]: ru'ach without qualification is Tiferet; and likewise it is the element of air, as is known. And it is called ru'ach in the secret of the aspect that arbitrates between Gedulah and Gevurah. And sometimes it is called the north wind, when it draws nourishment from Gevurah, where the north is; and this is the north wind that would blow on the harp of David. And when it draws nourishment from Chesed it is called the south wind, where the south is. And it is called a hot wind, in the secret of the heat of Gevurah, and a cold wind, in the secret of the cold waters of Chesed. And Malkhut is called the holy spirit [ru'ach ha-kodesh] when she draws nourishment from the side of Hod; for from there is the drawing of nourishment of those who speak by the holy spirit, who are below the prophets, who are from Netzach. So he explained in the Zohar, elsewhere. And in Parashat Acharei (fol. 61a) he explained that Malkhut is called the holy spirit when she receives from Chokhmah, which is called kodesh. And it is possible that both are so; for Chokhmah bestows to Hod, and Hod to Malkhut. And Malkhut is called a great wind when she draws nourishment from the south wind, and she is called a strong wind when she draws nourishment from the north wind: great from the side of Chesed, and strong from the side of Gevurah. And she is called the wind of the day (Gen. 3:8) from the side of Tiferet. And the reasons for these titles are clear. And on the word "the spirit of God [ru'ach Elohim] is in him" (Gen. 41:38), which [the commentators] explained in Chokhmah, the reason may be that it is spirit and soul to Binah, which is called Elohim. And also in this matter it is right of Tiferet, which is spirit to Malkhut, who is called Elohim; and also that it goes out from within the upper mouth, which is called Binah:

Breadth [רוחב, rochav]: it appears from the language of the Zohar in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Terumah, fol. 158a) that the breadth is from the side of Malkhut. And so he explained there: "five cubits the length, from the side of the upper Heh; and five the breadth, from the side of the lower Heh." It appears that the breadth is from the side of Malkhut:

Who rides the heavens [רוכב שמים, rokhev shamayim] (Deut. 33:26): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Binah is called rokhev shamayim; and the reason is that she rides upon shamayim, which are esh and mayim [fire and water] and their inclusion, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. And it seems to me that Binah is called rokhev shamayim in the aspect of the Heh, which is three Vavs, which are the three Patriarchs:

Merchant [רוכל, rokhel]: he explained in the Tikkunim that it is Yesod, as I explained in the entry avkat [powders]. And the reason is that in it all the kinds of effluence are mixed, and it is their merchant:

Height [רום, rom] or rum: the commentators explained that with a cholam it is in Keter, and with a shuruk [in Tiferet]. The height of heaven [rom shamayim]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, fol. 66) that Chokhmah is called the height of heaven; and of it it is said, "To whom do they lift the hands? To the height of heaven":

Spear [רומח, romach]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 10a) that at the time of the inclining of Tiferet to Chesed, which is Abraham, the two hundred and forty-eight [RaMaCh] positive commandments, with the Vav of Tiferet, are RoMaCh [spear]; and the hand that holds it is Malkhut, in the secret of the union:

Who feeds among the lilies [רועה בשושנים, ro'eh ba-shoshanim] (Song 2:16): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 25, fol. 69) that it is Tiferet, which feeds among two lilies, which are the two Hehs, in the matter of "the middle bar … from end to end" (Exod. 36:33):

Broad places [רחובות, rechovot]: Binah is called rechovot for the reason that in her is the breadth of everything; for she is "an inheritance without boundaries," as we explained in its entry. And it seems to me: rechovot on the side that spreads out below upon the children; and this is "rivers of water in the broad places" (Prov. 5:16), that is, the spreading out of the sefirot. And there is a proof of this from the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 141b; see there):

Compassionate [רחום, rachum]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Chesed is called rachum, because it has compassion on the creatures even though they are not worthy of themselves; and Tiferet is called rachaman. And to us it appears that Tiferet is called rachaman by the power of the compassion that is in it; and Chesed is called rachum by the power of the compassion of Tiferet; for Tiferet is the master of compassion, and Chesed the master of mercies [chasadim]. And it is found that RaChUM hints at RaMaCh [248] and Vav, which is Tiferet toward the side of Chesed, after the manner that we explained in the entry romach:

Far [רחוק, rachok]: the distance is always in Chokhmah; and because of the paucity of the apprehension of it, it is called far. And Tiferet is called "a brother far off" to Malkhut, as we explained in the entry karov; and the reason is because it is raised to Chokhmah. And of this it is said (Ps. 10:1), "Why do You stand afar off, O YHVH?": the explanation, Tiferet, which is raised to Chokhmah, and Malkhut remains desolate, God forbid. And so it is understood in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 20b), on the verse (Jer. 30:10; 46:27), "Behold, I will save you from afar." And it is somewhat understood there that Binah too is called far:

Rachel [רחל, Rachel]: Malkhut is so called in the secret of the aspect that is united by the power of the compassion [rachamim] of Tiferet, Jacob; and by the power of the compassion that is in her, of her it is said (Jer. 31:15), "Rachel weeping for her children":

Compassion [רחמים, rachamim]: Tiferet is so called, because it is the line of compassion, as we explained in the preceding gates. And Keter, because it is the root of the middle line, is called complete compassion, for there is no hold of judgment in it:

The controversy of YHVH [ריב ה', riv YHVH] (Micah 6:2): the Shekhinah is so called because she complains and contends with her husband over the destruction of her Temple and her exile and the exile of her children, "till YHVH look down and behold" (Lam. 3:50). And likewise Binah too makes a controversy over the dried-up Yesod, as it is said (Isa. 19:5; Job 14:11), "and the river shall be wasted and dried up." And both of them are called controversies, the upper and lower Shekhinah, as we explained (in Tikkun 21, fol. 42b; see there). Savour [ריח, re'ach]: its matter is that Malkhut, when she rises above for favour, in the secret of the smoke of the array, which we explained in its entry; for her rising is through Tiferet; and in their rising, united, to their concealed source that is in Chokhmah, then Malkhut, rising up to the Ein Sof, is called [re'ach]; and in their descending she descends by way of the nicho'ach [sweetness] that we explained in its entry.

And the matter of re'ach is this: when the fire and the power of Gevurah, which is what goes out from the nose, spreads out to burn the world and is bestowed to Malkhut, then, in the rising of Malkhut by way of the judgment, and her cleaving to the smoke, which is the powers of Gevurah that are bestowed from the upper Gevurah and cleave to their root, which is the ascent of the smoke of the fire; and it rises by way of the nose, which is Gevurah, and cleaves to Binah, where the source of the fire of Gevurah is, as is known: then love is aroused in the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, and they cleave in the union of Binah and Chokhmah, in the secret of Da'at, as is explained above. Then the effluence of Chokhmah is aroused in the sources of compassion that are in Binah; and those sources are opened (and bestowed), and Binah is clothed in the secret of compassion; and then the world is at rest [nachat]; and this is re'ach nicho'ach. This is what emerges for us by agreement, after study in the book of the Zohar on the inquiry. And we explained this in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 12, and there we copied some of the language of the Zohar. And by this the words of the commentators too are right, that re'ach without qualification is in Chokhmah; and likewise the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim:

Empty [ריקם, reikam]: in places in the Zohar it appears that every term of rek is in the husk, as "and the pit was empty [rek], there was no water in it" (Gen. 37:24); and they explained (our Rabbis, of blessed memory, Shabbat 22a): "There was no water in it, but there were snakes and scorpions in it." And likewise the language "that we shall not labour in vain [la-rik], nor bring forth for terror" (Isa. 65:23) proves it. And in the Tikkunim he explained that reikam is in the name Elohim: when it is empty of Heh-Yod, there remains illem [mute]. And the matter is that illem is the aspect of Tiferet when Malkhut, who is Heh-Yod, is not with it; and that is that it is empty of the Shekhinah; and Tiferet [remains, as it were,] mute, when the speech, which is the Shekhinah, is not with it (see the book Kehillat Ya'akov, the entry reikam):

High [רם, ram]: there are those who explained it in Keter, and there are those who explained it in Tiferet. And what appears more to us is that it is in Binah, as we explained in the entry yarum; see there. And what the verse said (Isa. 6:1), "sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up," the intent is Malkhut, who rises above Chesed and Gevurah; for ram will mean that "he shall be exalted more than Abraham, and lifted up more than Isaac." And therefore every "lifted up" and "high" without qualification is said of Binah, from the side of Chesed or from the side of Gevurah. However, when it is related to another matter, it will be explained in this way that we explained. And see the entry yarum and the entry nissa:
Pomegranates [רמונים, rimmonim]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 26, fol. 69b) that Netzach and Hod are called two pomegranates:

Joyful song [רנה, rinnah]: the joyful song is from the side of the Righteous One, as it is written, "Rejoice [rannenu], O you righteous," etc. (Ps. 33:1). And the Righteous One is so called when it draws nourishment from the side of the left, according to its custom. So he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, fol. 28a; see there):
Evil [רעה, ra'ah] is in the husk upon which the nega [plague] rides, as we explained in its entry:

Companions [ריעים, re'im]: Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim that Netzach and Hod are called two companions. And the reason is that they are companions in their action; and therefore most of their titles in man are found for both of them together. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained elsewhere: "Netzach and Hod are two halves of the body." And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 4a), he said that Chokhmah and Binah are called companions. And it is possible to say that when Netzach and Hod draw nourishment from Chokhmah and Binah by way of Chesed and Gevurah, they [too] are called companions, after the manner in which the roots of the roots are called companions:

Thunders [רעמים, re'amim] are from the side of Gevurah, as it is written (Job 26:14), "but the thunder of His mighty deeds [gevurotav]," etc.; and so he explained in the Tikkunim. And it may be that therefore we bless over them, "whose power and might [gevurato] fill the world":

Quaking [רעש, ra'ash]: there is a quaking and there is a quaking. There is a quaking of holiness, and it is that by which the Holy One, blessed be He, will in the future revive the dead; and of it it is said (Ezek. 3:12), "And I heard behind me the voice of a great quaking." And Malkhut is called ra'ash, and in the reversal of the letters eser [ten]; for she is included of ten, and is clothed in the force of Gevurah, and makes the kingdom of wickedness, the kingdom of insolence, quake, and destroys it (from the world). And this aspect is called ra'ash. And there is another ra'ash, and it is in the reversal of the letters resha [wickedness], which does wickedly and shakes the face of the world, to destroy the righteous in a moment, God forbid, the Compassionate One save us:

Will [רצון, ratzon]: the effluence that descends from the Supreme Crown placates and gives delight and good will to all the sefirot. And therefore they are called ratzon: as a man who is clothed in contentment at the time of his eating, so the sefirot are made content with the upper Will at the time of their drawing nourishment from it. And therefore the principal of the will is in Keter. And the passive form that is found in this [word] is the sefirah mentioned in the verse, according to the matter, which is made content by the upper Will. And the example of this: "YHVH, You have been favourable [ratzita] to Your land" (Ps. 85:2); and the intent [is the sefirah Malkhut, which is called land], upon which the effluence of the will is bestowed. And from this we may infer to everything like it:

Firmament [רקיע, raki'a]: the firmaments are many. First, all the sefirot together are called firmaments, as we explained in the preceding gates. Further, the five sefirot are called firmaments from the side of Gevurah; and that is the five firmaments mentioned on the second day, as we explained in the preceding chapters in this gate. And they were called firmaments because they spread out and are stretched in their action; and their likeness, from cause to effect, in the firmaments, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing. And the principal of the firmament is Tiferet; and through it they are five sefirot, five firmaments. And Yesod too is called the firmament that is over the heads of the living creatures that are in Malkhut. And Malkhut is sometimes called firmament, which is the firmament that is over the heads of the lower living creatures. And Binah is called firmament because she is the firmament over the heads of the upper living creatures, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet and Malkhut, which are the four living creatures of Atzilut that are in Atzilut. All these they explained in the Zohar (Vayigash, fol. 211a; Vayakhel, fol. 213a):

Domain [רשות, reshut]: Malkhut, when she is united to her husband, is called the private domain [reshut ha-yachid, the domain of the One], for she is the domain of the Only One of the world, Tiferet. And likewise the four-letter name: its breadth is four, which is YHVH, and its height ten, which is Yod-Vav-Dalet Heh-Alef Vav-Alef-Vav Heh-Alef. And therefore Malkhut, united with Tiferet her husband, is called the private domain; and when the man is not in his house she is called a domain by itself: the explanation, a domain alone, which is not with the union. Thus far the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 11a, and in Tikkun 5, fol. 18).

And further, he explained elsewhere (in Tikkun 24, fol. 67) that the public domain [reshut ha-rabbim, the domain of the many] is the serpent, the harlot, Samael. And it is called the domain of the many because they are many, seventy nations, and through it they all draw nourishment. However, the Only One of the world is one, single and unique. Thus far the explanation of the entry of the letter Resh has reached, with the divine help that flows upon us. And now we shall come to the explanation of the entry of the letter Shin:

Request [שאלה, she'elah]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a) that Malkhut, from the side of Chesed with Chokhmah, is called she'elah; and therefore the name El, which is Chesed, is sealed in the word she'elah. And therefore in her it was said to Solomon (1 Kings 3:5), "Ask what I shall give you"; and he asked wisdom, which is over Chesed. And they added the explanation there:

Roar [שאגה, she'agah]: the explanation, the roar of a lion is in Chesed, from the side of the judgment that is in it; and the matter shows this; for it roars from the side of judgment, and it is a lion, which is Chesed; and it is plain. And therefore it is said (Amos 3:8), "The lion has roared; who will not fear?" since all are clothed in judgment, and even Chesed:

Flesh [שאר, she'er]: we have already explained in the entry Moses the difference between Jacob our father and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. And Malkhut is called she'er from the side of her aspect with Tiferet in its concealed manifestation, where the chariot of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. And the language of she'er is as "the flesh of his flesh" [she'er besaro], as it is said (Gen. 2:23), "and flesh of my flesh":

Leaven [שאור, se'or]: there are those who explained it in Gevurah. And it is right only in the husk; unless we say that because it is bestowed from there it is called by its name; and this is strained:

Oath [שבועה, shevu'ah] is in Malkhut; and so it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 255). And elsewhere (Mishpatim, fol. 116) he explained that the oath is in Yesod; and elsewhere he explained that it is in Binah. And the matter is that the language of shevu'ah is explained from the language of shevi'iyot [sevens]; and the intent is that this one is included of seven branches; and no sefirah is called seventh, meaning included of seven, except through Yesod, as we shall explain in the entry shevi'it. And we are found to learn that the oath is in Malkhut in her rising to Yesod. And therefore the oath is "As YHVH lives [chai]," which is Yesod, which is called Chai, as is known. And all of it is through Binah; for the principal of the sevenness and the life of Yesod is through the effluence of Binah. And therefore the oath is right of Binah, and of Yesod, and of Malkhut; and its principal is in Malkhut, in her rising to Yesod and being included there of the seven branches of the menorah, through Binah:

Sevens [שביעיות, shevi'iyot]: every term of shevi'it, shevi'i and the like is all from the side of the Righteous One, even if it be in another sefirah. And these are the words of Rashbi in the Tikkunim: "All the sefirot are called sevens from the side of the Righteous One." However, the sefirot are not so titled from the side of the Righteous One except in its receiving from Binah; and so he explained in the Tikkunim:
Seven years [שבע שנים, sheva shanim] is Binah:

Seven Sabbaths [שבע שבתות, sheva shabbatot]: each sefirah of the seven days of the building is called one Sabbath, in the secret of one Sabbatical cycle. However, Binah, because she is the Jubilee and is included of seven Sabbaths, is also called seven Sabbaths. And the intent is that she is so called when Binah is included of seven sefirot, and seven sefirot, each one included of seven; there are found to be seen in her forty-nine sefirot, in the secret of the forty-nine gates and in the secret of the forty-nine years of the Jubilee. And the rest of the matter in this inquiry we spoke of at length in the Gate of Gates:

Seven [שבעה, shiv'ah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 102), that it is the hint to Tiferet in the union of Chesed and Gevurah; for Tiferet is five, and the two of them with it, behold seven; see there:

Seven days [שבעת ימים, shiv'at yamim]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 89b), and in Emor (fol. 92), that Binah is called seven days, because she includes within her the six days that are beneath her. And in Parashat Miketz (fol. 204) he explained that above there are seven upper days and below seven; and they are "seven days and seven days, fourteen days" (1 Kings 8:65):

Networks [שבכות, sevakhot]: the explanation, the networks that are upon the capitals that are on the tops of the pillars Jachin and Boaz (1 Kings 7:17); and they are Netzach and Hod; and the capitals that are on their tops are Gedulah and Gevurah, which are capitals on the tops of Netzach and Hod; and on the tops of these capitals are Binah and Chokhmah, networks over them:

Sabbath [שבת, Shabbat]: on the matter of the Sabbath there are divided opinions; and we shall explain it in a way that everything is set right, as we wrote in the entry yamim [days]. It emerged in our agreement that the Sabbath remains, according to the reckoning of the days, between Yesod and Malkhut. And the principal of the Sabbath is Malkhut; and your sign: Shin, bat [daughter]. And the intent: bat is Malkhut, in the manifestation of the Yod, in the manifestation of the Heh; Shin is three Patriarchs, included in the manifestation of the Heh, as we spoke at length in the Gate of the Emanation. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 254a) he explained that the Shin is three crowns: Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. And all of it comes to one place; for the heads of the Vavs are a segolta, that is, three Yods. And since the Sabbath is Malkhut, we know that she is the attribute of night. It is found that the eve of the Sabbath is she alone; and therefore we say in the prayer of the eve of the Sabbath, "and may they rest on her [vah]," to hint at the female. However, in the day, which is the male, as we shall explain, we say "and may they rest on him [vo]," to hint at the male. And the Sabbath, which is Malkhut, is called Sabbath only through Yesod, the seventh, as we explained above in its entry.

And behold, the Sabbath, which is Malkhut, is included with Yesod. And therefore we say Vayekhullu on the eve of the Sabbath; for vayekhullu is in Yesod; and therefore it comes to seventy [Ayin]; for Ayin is in Yesod, which is seventh, as we explained above. It is found according to this that there is no Sabbath except in the inclusion of Yesod with Malkhut. And likewise the word YeSoD is the inclusion of Yesod with Malkhut: for the Yod is in the Shekhinah, and SoD is "the secret [sod] of YHVH is with them that fear Him" (Ps. 25:14). And when it is morning, which is the attribute of day, behold, Malkhut, who is the Sabbath, rises to be united with the second Sabbath, which is Tiferet; for they are two Sabbaths as one, in a complete union. And this is "Moses rejoiced in the gift of his portion," in the secret of Tiferet, as is known. And when both of them are united, they rise to be crowned in the attribute of Binah; and she is the Great Sabbath. And of her we say Nishmat kol chai [The soul of every living thing], for she is the soul from which the souls are emanated, as is known. Therefore Shabbat Shabbaton is found. How so? Malkhut is called Shabbat, as we explained; Binah is called Shabbaton. How so? Shabbat, Malkhut; Vav, Tiferet; Nun, Binah. It is found that Shabbaton includes three Sabbaths in Binah. And when this union of these three attributes is, behold, they are united through Binah and Chokhmah, and through Tiferet, six extremities, and Malkhut herself. And for this all of them together are called many Sabbaths. This is our agreement on the matter of the Sabbath, compelled from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him:

Field [שדה, sadeh] without qualification is Malkhut; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Chayyei Sarah (fol. 122a; see there). And she is called sadeh: "and flesh that is torn of beasts in the field" (Exod. 22:30); and likewise "for he found her in the field," etc. (Deut. 22:27). And on the field of apples there are explanations; and what appears is that the principal of this word is in Tiferet; and it is so called because it is included of three colors, red and white and green, and they are the colors of the apple; and so Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 232) Tiferet is called long-suffering [erekh appayim], as we explained in its entry; and the reason is that it has two faces: the face of Chesed in the secret of the whiteness, and the face of judgment in the secret of the redness. The faces are like two apples, this on one side and that on the other side. And for this reason Tiferet is called a field of apples, in which there are two apples. And in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 142b), he explained that Malkhut is called the field of apples; and the reason is that she is called field, and all the apples, which are the Patriarchs, bestow to her. And likewise in Parashat Vayechi (fol. 249), these are his words: "Come and see: when the moon rules, she is called the field of apples." Thus far his words.
And Malkhut is also called the field of Anathoth (Jer. 32:7) when she is poor [aniyah]; so he explained in the Zohar there:

The spine of the lulav [שדרת הלולב, shidrat ha-lulav]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Yesod is called the spine of the lulav. And the lulav is Yesod and Tiferet together, as we explained in its entry; and it is so called in the secret of the leaves that rise on the stem, right and left; and they hint at the extremities included in both of them. And when we say "the spine of the lulav," the intent will be Yesod and Tiferet, included in the whole, and the hint is to their particularity alone:

Lamb [שה, seh]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna that it is the secret of Chesed; that is, "a lamb without blemish, a male" (Exod. 12:5); and as in the matter of "a plain man" [ish tam], "walk before Me and be perfect [tamim]" (Gen. 17:1) (see the Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Tzav, fol. 28a):

Officer [שוטר, shoter]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 117b) that Tiferet, from the side of Malkhut, is called shoter. And the reason is that the officer is the agent of the judge: for the judge decides the judgment, and the officer carries out the judgment against the will of the litigants; and if they need to be lashed, the officer lashes them. And for the reason that Malkhut is the pure strap to lash the wicked, therefore Tiferet, when it lashes through her, is called shoter from the side of Malkhut (and see the book Kehillat Ya'akov):

Who inhabits eternity [שוכן עד, shokhen ad] (Isa. 57:15): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Tiferet is called shokhen ad. And the reason is that Yesod is called ad, as we explained in its entry; and when Tiferet flows upon Yesod, when it is called ad, Tiferet is called shokhen ad. Or it is possible to say that it dwells in Binah, which is called ad, or in Malkhut, who is called ad, as we explained in its entry:

Table [שולחן, shulchan]: Malkhut is so called in the secret of her receiving from Gevurah, and Gevurah dwells upon it; and this is "the table in the north." So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Tikkunim, in Tikkun 24, fol. 68a, and in Tikkun 47, fol. 81b). Ruler [שולט, sholet]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna there that Tiferet, from the side of Yesod, is called sholet. And the reason is that a ruler is not so much as a king; and therefore the ruler is beneath the king. And when Tiferet is at the rung of ruler, it is from the side of the aspect of Yesod, where it is the ruler; as it is written (Gen. 42:6), "And Joseph was the governor":

Crying out [שועה, shav'ah]: the explanation, in Malkhut. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 19b), these are his words: "Rabbi Isaac said: There is no crying out except in prayer, as it is said, 'Hear my prayer, O YHVH, and give ear unto my cry' (Ps. 39:13)," etc. Behold, the crying out is in prayer, which is Malkhut:

Judge [שופט, shofet]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Mishpatim, fol. 117b) that the sefirot are all called judges from the side of Binah, and especially Tiferet, which is called judge. And the reason is that Binah is called Gevurah, because from her judgment is bestowed below. And therefore, when she spreads out in the power of judgment, all the sefirot are called judges from her side; and when this prevailing is upon Tiferet, then it is called judge:

Shofar [שופר, shofar]: there is the great shofar and the shofar without qualification. The shofar without qualification is Tiferet, which is also called keren [horn], as we explained in its entry. However, the great shofar is Binah; and therefore it is called great, because on her depends the freedom, in the secret of the Jubilee; and therefore she is called the horn of the Jubilee. And it is possible that she is called great from the side of Gedulah; and this shows her greatness, that she is apprehended only in Gedulah alone; and in the aspect of her concealment to this measure she is called the great shofar:

Legs [שוקים, shokayim]: Netzach and Hod are called legs, in the secret that Tiferet, which is the body, leans upon them. And it appears that they are called legs only when they are included of Netzach of Netzachs, Hod of Hods, as we explained in the entry Netzach; for so it is written (Song 5:15), "His legs are pillars of marble [shesh]":

Ox [שור, shor]: what is agreed in the words of the commentators is that the ox is in Gevurah. However, in this ox there is the innocuous ox [shor tam] and the forewarned ox [shor mu'ad]. The innocuous ox is from the side of holiness, at the rung of holiness; and the forewarned ox is from the side of impurity, for it is forewarned to do evil. And because this ox is from the side of the force of judgment, one keeps fifty cubits away from an innocuous ox. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Tiferet, from the side of Gevurah, is called ox. And in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 8b) it appears further that what is expounded, "the ox that the first Adam offered had one horn on its forehead," is Malkhut; and the horn on its forehead is Yesod, as we explained in the entry keren:

Lily [שושן, shushan]: there is a red lily and a white lily. Sometimes the red rules over the white and prevails over it; and it is Hod prevailing over Netzach, which is white inclining to red. And the white lily prevails over the red; and it is Netzach prevailing over Hod, and it is redness inclining to whiteness. And these are shushan in the masculine. However, there is shoshanah, feminine, and it will be explained in its entry, with the help of the Name:

Rose [שושנה, shoshanah] is Malkhut; and she too is included of two colors, red and white, which is the color of the arousal of the right and the left. And likewise in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 107a), he explained that she is called shoshanah: "At the time that she wishes to couple with the King [she is called chavatzelet (lily of the valley). After she has cleaved to the King] in those kisses, she is called shoshanah." Thus far his words.

And it is already known that before the kisses is the embrace, that is, through Gedulah and Gevurah, redness and whiteness; and they are the colors of the rose. And in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 1), he explained that in the rose there are thirteen leaves; and likewise Malkhut has thirteen attributes of compassion. If so, the rose hints at her when she shines from the thirteen upper attributes. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 38, fol. 78b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the matter of the rose in its particulars, and these are his words: "'In the beginning Elohim created': he opened and said, 'As a rose among thorns,' etc. (Song 2:2). The rose has five leaves within and five without; and they are Heh, Heh. Its stem, Vav; its apple [hip], Yod. And all of it is Elohim: its five letters; Heh, five leaves without; Heh, five leaves within; Yod, the apple; Vav, full, the stem," etc. Thus far his words.

And the explanation: since he intended to explain the name Elohim that is in "In the beginning Elohim created," therefore he opened with the verse "As a rose among thorns." And the intent is the Shekhinah, who is in exile among the thorns, among the husks of impurity, which are thorns and briars and brambles. And his intent in beginning with this verse is to explain the name Elohim, in which the Heh is over the Yod; and this is not the order of the letters in the four-letter name, but Yod over Heh. And to explain this matter he said that the name Elohim is in the Shekhinah, and the rose is in the Shekhinah, and the four-letter name is in the rose and in the Shekhinah.

And behold, this name is reversed; for Heh, Heh are the five leaves within and without. And the intent of the truth in the parable of the rose: for in the rose there are five inner leaves, and they are the principal of the rose; and five outer leaves are a garment for the five inner ones that are within. And likewise Malkhut is Heh, and Binah is Heh; and the intent is that in Malkhut there are five sefirot, which are the five bars of the Tabernacle, which are Gedulah and Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod; and Yesod is included with Tiferet. And these five are in Binah; and Binah shines these five into the lower five that are in Malkhut, and shines these in those. And it is found according to this that the upper five are a soul to the lower five, and the lower ones a garment for the upper ones; and this is what is signified by the leaves of the rose. "Its stem, Vav": the explanation, the stem by which the rose is held is Vav, which is Tiferet. And the apple, which is the apple of the rose, is Yod. We are found to learn that in the rose the Name is not in its proper order and line; for the Hehs are over Vav, Yod; and likewise in the name Elohim. And this is what he said, "And all of it is Elohim": the explanation, all this manifestation is in the name Elohim. For the five letters themselves are the five leaves without; and the Heh by itself is the five leaves within; and the Yod is the apple; and the rest of the name, which is the letters MaLA, hints at the Vav in its fullness, which is the stem. And behold, in this there is no wonder at the Heh being over the Yod. And he intended to say MaLA and not ILeM, as is his way in other places, for the reason that the word male hints at Tiferet, that is, Vav; but illem hints at Malkhut, as is proved in the Tikkunim many times. Thus far the explanation of the saying. And from it the matter of the rose is made clear: that in it YHVH is hinted with the letters reversed, and in it the name Elohim is hinted. And likewise the matter of the hint of the manifestation of the rose is explained. Further, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 25, fol. 69b): roses [shoshanim] are two, and they are the upper Shekhinah and the lower Shekhinah, etc.; and of them it is said shoshanim, in the plural. And in them there are thirteen leaves, which are six and six, in the secret of judgment and compassion, from above to below and from below to above; and likewise for each and every one; see there:

Skies [שחקים, shechakim]: Netzach and Hod are so called. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained: when they grind [shochakim] manna for the righteous; that is, the bestowal that comes through them to the Righteous One. For just as the two testicles of the male ripen the seed, for otherwise it could not come to the covenant, so is the matter in these two sefirot: for they bestow the effluence of Tiferet and ripen it and bring it into a being fit for Yesod. And they are called shechakim when they grind effluence from the side of the left, Gevurah; however, from the side of the right they are called millstones. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 235a), and we explained it in its entry:

Dawn [שחר, shachar]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 119b, and in Pinchas, fol. 243a) that there are two rungs, morning and dawn: the morning of Abraham, and dawn in Netzach. For the morning is after the complete illumination and the rising of the light in substance; and dawn is before the light of day, which is the beginning of the column of dawn [ammud ha-shachar]; and its language is from the language of the column of dawn. And in truth, the explanation of ammud ha-shachar is the language of blackness [shacharut]; for even though it is white, with respect to Chesed it is black. And Netzach is called shachar when it is in Chesed, like Chesed itself; and it precedes it, from below to above:

Sitnah [שטנה, sitnah, enmity]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that it is in Gevurah; and it does not settle with us. Rather, it is in the husks that accuse [mastinot] the world; and it is the well over which they strove (Gen. 26:21): "a broken cistern, that can hold no water" (Jer. 2:13). However, the well, the source of living water, they did not strive over. And in truth it is correct that sitnah is in the husks and not in holiness:

Hoary head [שיבה, seivah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Kedoshim (fol. 87), on the verse (Lev. 19:32), "You shall rise up before the hoary head," that seivah is in Keter; and the reason may be because of the whiteness that is in it. Shrub [שיח, si'ach]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 51, fol. 84a), on the verse (Gen. 2:5), "And every shrub of the field was not yet," and these are his words: "Rabbi Eleazar said to him: Father, si'ach, from where do we know that it is the Righteous One? He said to him: My son, in it you will find Chai [Chet-Yod]; Shin is a totality that includes three flocks of sheep, which are the root of the tree," etc. Thus far his words. Behold, the Righteous One is called si'ach when it is Chai from the side of the life of Binah, and when, from her side, it is included of three colors, which are Chesed, Judgment, Compassion. And he was precise in calling them "three flocks of sheep," to prove that these colors are in Yesod. And the reason is that three flocks of sheep crouch upon her; and the verse said (Gen. 29:2), "And behold a well in the field": it is Malkhut; "and three flocks of sheep lying by" the well itself: that is, three colors. And he called them "the root of the tree" to hint that it is included of them from the side of Binah, which is the root of the tree; because in her are sunk the roots of the tree, which is the Emanation:

Acacia [שיטה, shittah]: he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a) that Malkhut is called shittah from the side of the extension [peshitah] of Chesed; for it is [from the language of] peshutah [plain]; the explanation, as the teki'ah, which is plain, and it is the secret of Chesed:

Song [שיר, shir]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that shir is in Chokhmah; and your sign, shar Yod [the Yod sings]. And elsewhere he explained that Malkhut is called shirah, the explanation, shir-Heh. And sometimes he explains shir in Malkhut; and especially in the Song of Songs there is no doubt. And the reason is that Chokhmah and Malkhut have one manifestation, in the secret of the Yod that is in Malkhut, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations; and in that aspect shir, shar Yod, is right. However, in the manifestation of the Yod and the Heh both together she is called shirah, which is explained shar Yod, shar Heh. And elsewhere (in the Introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar, fol. 3a) he said: "The song of the Levites is from the left." It is possible to say, in YiSRa'EL, that he said there: shir El; and he explained "the song of the Levites"; see there. But elsewhere, where he said shir, the explanation shir Yod, there is no doubt that it has a share in Binah, in the secret of the song:

Forgetfulness [שכחה, shikhechah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 193b), that forgetfulness is from the side of the husk, for there is no remembrance there. And even though there is remembrance there on the side of the husk, as we explained in its entry, nevertheless their remembrance is for evil, and it is worse than forgetfulness. And this is (as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, Avot, ch. 4): "Blessed be He, before whom there is neither iniquity nor forgetfulness," etc.; as "evil shall not sojourn with You" (Ps. 5:5):

Shekhinah [שכינה, shekhinah]: there is the upper Shekhinah and the lower Shekhinah; and they are Binah and Malkhut, the upper Heh and the lower Heh. And the reason that Malkhut is called Shekhinah is because she causes all the upper Emanation to dwell [meshakkenet] in the lower world. And Binah too is called Shekhinah because she causes the three first ones to dwell upon the seven sefirot of the building. Or it is possible to say that they are the place in which the six extremities dwell, whether in the upper female, in the secret of their rising, or in Malkhut, in the secret of their descending; and there they make their dwelling. And Binah is called the Shekhinah of His might [shekhinat uzzo]: the explanation, the Shekhinah that gives might to Gevurah; so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 119a):

Good understanding [שכל טוב, sekhel tov]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Yesod is called sekhel tov. However, our opinion is that every place of the language of understanding [haskalah] is from the side of Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate of Paths; and tov we explained in its entry. Further, he said that Keter is called the primordial intellect, which shows its primordiality; and likewise the fixed intellect, which shows its fixedness in compassion; and they are not to the point. And there are those who called Malkhut the active intellect; the reason, that she is the lower Wisdom, which performs the actions in the lower world. And there are those who called the upper Wisdom the separate intellect, because there is a separation between it and Binah, and between it and Keter, like the separation between something and naught, as is known:

Neighbour [שכן, shakhen]: in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 115a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Yesod is called "a neighbour that is near" (Prov. 27:10), when it is a neighbour to Malkhut and it dwells upon her. And see the entry karov:

Snow [שלג, sheleg]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Tiferet is so called; and he proved the thing from their saying, of blessed memory, "the snow that is beneath the Throne of Glory"; and he explained that the Throne of Glory is Binah, which is a throne for Chokhmah, which is glory. And he aimed well. However, he wished also to prove the matter from "the terrible ice"; and the matter is not as he thought, as we explained in its entry. And it is possible to say that it will be in Chesed; and the language of the saying will be precise, "beneath the Throne of Glory" itself; and it is Chesed, in the secret of the whiteness. All this is according to reasoning. But in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 6), he explained that the snow is strong judgment; and so they explained there on the verse (Prov. 31:21), "She is not afraid of the snow for her household." And according to this explanation we can settle the saying "the snow that is beneath the Throne of Glory": that is, Gevurah, which is beneath Binah, as is known:

Flame [שלהבת, shalhevet]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that the coal is Yod, that is, Chokhmah; and the flame that spreads out from it is Vav, that is, Tiferet with the totality of the six extremities. And Chokhmah is called coal and Tiferet flame when they are clothed in judgment; and we have already spoken at length on it, all that is needed, in the entry gachelet. And on the flame of Yah [shalhevetyah] (Song 8:6) he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Metzora (fol. 54b), these are his words: "And what is shalhevetyah? This is a fire that goes out from within the shofar, included with air and water; and from within that flame, when it blazes in the Assembly of Israel, it burns the world with its flames, in the jealousy of the Holy One, blessed be He." Thus far his words. And it is clear that it is called flame with respect to Gevurah; and it is called Yah because it goes out from within the shofar, which is from within Binah, through Chokhmah; and therefore it is called shalhevetyah. And for the reason that what goes out from within the shofar is the voice that is included in water and fire and air, therefore he said, "included with air and water." And there is a great difference between flame and voice: for in the voice the principal is the air, and the water and the fire are secondary to it; and in the flame the principal is the [fire], and the water and the air are secondary to it. And the flame is to arouse the love, in the secret of "His left hand is under my head" (Song 2:6):

Peace [שלום, shalom]: Keter is so called, in the secret of the three aspects that are in it, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, ChaDaR [Chesed, Din, Rachamim]; and on account of the peace that mediates between these extremes it is called shalom. And this name is also related to Yesod; and they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 193b), the reason: that when the covenant receives the thirty-two upper paths that are bestowed from above to Malkhut, as is known, and when Malkhut is blazing in the power of judgment, then it receives those paths and bestows them to Malkhut and calms the power of her judgment; then it is called shalom, for it completes [mashlim] the judgment. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 44b) he explained that they are two peaces: peace from the side of Binah, the upper Heh, and it is Tiferet; and peace from the side of Malkhut, the lower Heh, and it is Yesod. Both of them are found, Yesod and Tiferet, to be called shalom. And it is possible that Tiferet is called shalom for the reason that we explained in Yesod: for as the way of Yesod toward Malkhut, so is the way of Tiferet toward Binah, in the secret of Da'at (see Asis Rimmonim):

Salem [שלם, Shalem]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 90b): the Assembly of Israel is called Shalem, for she camps and dwells only in a whole [shalem] place; and therefore she is called Shalem. And your sign: "And Melchizedek king of Salem" (Gen. 14:18); "In Salem also is His tabernacle" (Ps. 76:3):

Peace offerings [שלמים, shelamim]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 256) that Malkhut is called shelamim for the reason that she completes the count of ten sefirot, and she completes the count of the four letters that are in the Name, and she completes Tiferet so that it is called shalom; as it is written (Gen. 5:2), "Male and female He created them … and called their name Adam": a woman is half of the body. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 12b), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and these are his words: "And the peace offerings are held in the positive commandments and in the negative commandments, on this side and on that side; and therefore they are called shelamim. And the secret of the matter: 'and Jacob was a plain man [ish tam]' (Gen. 25:27), as the Targum renders it, gevar shelim, whole above, whole below." Thus far his words. And according to what appears from his words, Tiferet is called shelamim because it makes peace between Chesed and Gevurah. However, let us examine the language of the saying, which said tam, as its Targum, shelim; and shelim means shalem [whole]. And shalem is right only of what is whole from all sides: whether from the side that its female is not lacking, or from the side that it must be the master of the extremities; for otherwise it is not called whole, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters, chapter 7. And it is found that in the language of shelamim is included its including the arbitration and also its union with the Shekhinah, who is its half, as we explained. And further, the principal of the arbitration is through its union with Malkhut. For the reason that Chesed is water, cold and moist; and the fire, Gevurah, hot and dry; and Tiferet, air, hot and moist, unites Chesed and Gevurah from the side of the one contrary, for it equalizes the heat from the side of Gevurah and the moisture from the side of Chesed. However, the dryness and the coldness are not united except through Malkhut, which is the earth, cold and dry; and through her the coldness that is from the side of the element of water, Chesed, and the dryness that is from the side of the element of fire, Gevurah, are equalized, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters. And by this it is proved that Tiferet does not arbitrate in substance except through Malkhut, when she is united with it. And now Tiferet alone is not called shelamim, nor Malkhut alone, but when they are united. And by this the plural is understood, two peaces: whole from the side of the air, whole from the side of the earth. And by this we know the difference between shalom, singular, which is Tiferet alone, and shelamim, plural, Tiferet and Malkhut:

There [שם, sham]: the explanation, Malkhut is called sham. And it is possible that it comes to seven in the small reckoning; for she is included of the seven when they are included in a great inclusion: that is, Shin, three hundred, three Patriarchs, as is known; and Mem, forty, that is, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And also if it be found in Binah, according to the opinion of some of the commentators, it will mean: Shin, three Patriarchs, and the closed Mem, Binah, over them. And nevertheless it is more right in Malkhut; and she is so called because one cannot point with the finger and say "there" except of her, for she is the pointing of all. And from the language of shimah [placing], it is possible that it is in Malkhut, who is the one that encamps over the world, and she is called Shekhinah. And it is already possible to explain it for this reason also in Binah, for she too is called Shekhinah:

Name [שם, shem]: the explanation, according to the truth, garment. For just as the four-letter name is a garment to the sefirot, so all the sefirot are a garment to the Ein Sof, as is written in the preceding gates. And according to this the language of shem is already right of each one of the attributes; for "this is a husk to that, and that a brain to this"; and likewise this one is a name for its fellow, and its fellow for its fellow. And according to what is customary, Malkhut is called shem for the reason that she is the name of all the upper Emanation, which is all clothed in her. And the world of Beriah is called shem because it is a name and garment to the Emanation, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 129b) that Binah is called shem, on the verse (Gen. 48:16), "and let my name be named on them": this is the upper Shekhinah. And the reason may be because he said shemi [my name], which is explained shem-Yod: the garment and palace to the Yod is the Heh, as is known. And Malkhut is called the name of YHVH because she is a name and palace to YHVH, which is Tiferet. And elsewhere Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim that Binah is called the name of YHVH; and possibly because she is a garment to the YHVH that is in Chokhmah. However, the explicit name and the unique name and the proper name [shem ha-etzem] are explained in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, chapter 1:

Left [שמאל, smol]: in Gevurah. And sometimes Binah and Hod too are so called; and we explained the reason and the matter in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing and in the Gate of Essence and Governance. However, there is an impure left, and it is the husks. And sometimes in the Zohar he calls the impure "the side of the left," and sometimes the pure; and one must discern from the matter:

Keep [שמור, shamor]: our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Shevu'ot 20b): "'Remember' and 'Keep' were said in one utterance." And the intent is the two faces, which are Tiferet and Malkhut; and they are "Remember" for the male and "Keep" for the female. And the reason that this is called zakhor, the language of remembering, and that shamor, the language of keeping, is because to positive commandments remembering belongs, as it is written (Num. 15:40), "that you may remember and do"; and to negative commandments keeping belongs, as "Take heed [hishamer] lest," and "Do not" is nothing but a negative commandment. And likewise "to work it and to keep it" (Gen. 2:15); and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (end of Tikkun 21): "to work it," these are the positive commandments; "and to keep it," the negative commandments. And the positive commandments are two hundred and forty-eight, from the side of Chesed; and the male inclines to Chesed; and the three hundred and sixty-five negative commandments are in Gevurah; and therefore the female inclines to the left. And for this, "Remember" for the male and "Keep" for the female. And according to this she is called shamor only from the side of Gevurah, and he is called zakhor only from the side of Chesed. And sometimes both together are called shamor, and sometimes both zakhor; and so he explained in the Zohar (Chadash, Parashat Yitro, fol. 49a). And we spoke at length in the entry zakhor:

Joy [שמחה, simchah] is Binah; and all the joys are bestowed from her; and she is an attribute that requires joy, as is explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar on the Song of Songs, which we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 10. And likewise in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 15b) (and these are his words): "For the Mother sits in complete joy; as it is written, 'a joyful mother of children' (Ps. 113:9)." Thus far his words. And there are those who explained it in Malkhut; and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 8b), and these are his words: "And there are those who teach thus: joy, this is the Assembly of Israel." Thus far his words. And it is possible to say that when she receives the joy from above, that is, from Binah, she is called joy (and see the Zohar, Bamidbar, fol. 118a, when Malkhut is called joy):

Sabbatical year [שמטה, shemittah] is Malkhut; and she is called shemittah when the seven lamps that are in her, seven Sabbatical cycles, shine in the secret of the shemittah, which are seven years. And there is a great difference between shemittah and Jubilee: for the Jubilee is Binah, and she is included of seven, and each one of the seven is included of seven others; however, in the shemittah, which is Malkhut, the illumination in her is seven simple sefirot:

Heavens [שמים, shamayim]: Tiferet is called shamayim because it is included of esh and mayim [fire and water]. And the reason why it said shamayim and did not say mi-esh, after the way of the order, for the water precedes the fire, we explained in the Gate of Arbiters (in chapter 2). And Tiferet is called shamayim only in the manifestation of the arbitration, which includes the extremes together and completes them. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayigash (fol. 207a), and we explained it in the gate mentioned. And the reason that it is called shamayim in the plural is because, when Tiferet is included in this pleasant inclusion, then they are seen through five colors, which are the five sefirot Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod; and on account of all of them it is called shamayim. And it is already known that Chesed includes Netzach, which is a branch of it, and Gevurah includes Hod, which is a branch of it; and just as Tiferet includes Gedulah and Gevurah, so it includes also Netzach and Hod:

Heavenward [שמימה, shamaymah]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 118b, and in Tikkun 69, fol. 113b) that Malkhut, from the side of Tiferet, which is called shamayim, is called shamaymah:

The Eighth Day of Assembly [שמיני חג העצרת, Shemini Chag ha-Atzeret] is Malkhut. And she is called eighth because she is eighth to Chokhmah; and she is called chag because she is included in Chesed, Gevurah [ChaG], as we explained in its entry; and she is called atzeret on account of the fact that at the time of her rising above into Chokhmah, then she is atzeret [restraint], for she does not bestow at all until the time of her coming to her place. And in this matter the opinion of those who say that Shemini Chag Atzeret is in Chokhmah, or in Binah, or in Keter, is right; for all of it is in Malkhut, however specifically at the time of her rising, to be eighth there. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] spoke at length on the matter with different explanations:

The eighth [שמינית, sheminit]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 223b) that Hod is eighth, and it is called sheminit; and this is "For the leader [la-menatze'ach], upon the sheminit" (Ps. 12:1): Netzach upon Hod. And elsewhere he explained that Binah is eighth. And possibly they do not disagree; for Binah spreads out down to Hod, as we explained in the Gate of Gates. And further, for in two ways: from above to below, Hod is eighth; and from below to above, Binah is eighth; as we explained in the Gate of From Below to Above, that Binah is in Hod and Hod in Binah:

Hearing [שמיעה, shemi'ah] depends on Gevurah, from the side of Binah. And likewise Simeon [Shim'on] is in Gevurah, and it is the language of [hearing]; and likewise in Binah, as it is said, "the heart hears." And as for what is found, hearing for judgment and hearing for compassion: it is because sometimes Gevurah inclines to the side of Chesed through Binah. And sometimes the hearing is in Chokhmah; and this is not so far-fetched; for all five senses are in the brain, and it is called the common sense, in which the five senses share, in the way of the world; and likewise these there. And the matter is that Gevurah is hearing, the explanation, the sense of hearing; Gedulah seeing, the explanation, the sense of sight; and both of them are found in Binah, for so is their manifestation there; and the three of them in Chokhmah, for so is their manifestation there, concealed; and that is the common sense; and on account of their all being in Chokhmah and all in Binah. Nevertheless the principal of the seeing is in Chokhmah, as the principal of Gedulah is in Chokhmah; and the principal of the hearing is in Binah, as the principal of Gevurah is in Binah. And this, in our view, is the principal for answering several sayings of the Zohar that disagree on this matter:

One keeping [שמירה אחת, shemirah achat]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 11a) that Malkhut is called "one keeping," because it is already known that the language of shamor is in Malkhut, as we explained above. And she is "one keeping for many Sabbaths"; for in her all the sefirot are kept. The intent is that she is the keeping of the negative commandments that depend on all the sefirot. And likewise he explained that Malkhut is also called the keeping of the Sabbath, as we explained. And she needs keeping, for around her is the husk, in the matter of "The wicked walk on every side" (Ps. 12:9). And therefore one must not profane her with profanation of the Sabbath:

Oil [שמן, shemen]: there are many oils; and they are the anointing oil; and it is the effluence that is called oil, as we shall explain. And when Malkhut receives the oil from the side of Chesed she is called the anointing oil; and the reason is that its Targum is meshach revuta, and it is the language of greatness [gedulah], which is Chesed. And when she receives from the side of Tiferet she is called oil for the light, for the reason that Tiferet is the great luminary, and from its side the Shekhinah shines. And she is called the oil of holy anointing from the side of Gevurah, where the holiness is, as it is written, "and you shall sanctify the Levites." And because, when she draws the effluence from the side of Gevurah, Chesed is included with it, therefore she is called shemen mishchat kodesh: shemen, which is the effluence, which is from two united rungs; mishchat, which is Chesed; kodesh, which is Gevurah; that is, on the side of Gevurah, and not Gevurah itself, as we explained in the entry tahor. And she is called beaten oil [shemen katit] from the side of Yesod; and the reason is that Yesod beats the olives and crushes them and presses their oil, which is the effluence, and brings it down to Malkhut. And the matter of human coupling is already known: that it is through beating; and that crushing is a cause that the effluence, which is the seed, is aroused from all the limbs of the body. So is the matter above: that through crushing (the effluence is aroused, the seed drawn from the brain, which is Chokhmah, the manifestation of Yod, a drop of seed, in the aspect of the olive, the upper Yod), an upper crushing, the oil is aroused from the upper olives, and Yesod beats them and crushes them. And likewise from the side of Yesod she is called pure olive oil beaten; for Yesod is called "a green olive tree" (Ps. 52:10). And it may be so called in the aspect of the effluence of itself, which is one olive, in the singular.

And the matter of the effluence itself that is called oil: it is the effluence that is bestowed from Binah, and its principal is in Chokhmah; and it is an effluence in the secret of the right, and it is found in the right, as we shall explain. And it comes through Binah; and likewise Binah is called EHYH, and that is the second name EHYH that is in the verse (Exod. 3:14). And EHYH and  Y H V  are all one thing; and likewise  Y H V  is in Binah; for so the word BiNaH hints: its permutation is ben Yah; and ben is Vav with Yah, that is,  Y H V. And  Sh M N  in AT-BaSh comes out  B Y Ṭ  [Bet-Yod-Tet]; and it is a holy name; and this name comes to [the value of] EHYH and  Y H V; so I have heard. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] said that Yesod is called good oil, and he said that Keter too is so called; and it does not settle. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 7b), these are his words: "'Like the good oil upon the head' (Ps. 133:2): what is the good oil? This is the oil of holy greatness, which flows and goes out from the Holy Ancient One, to be found in that upper river that suckles the children, to kindle the lamps. And that oil of greatness flows upon the head of the King, and from His head to the glory of the holy beard; and from there it flows to all those garments of glory that the King is clothed in; as it is written, 'that came down upon the skirt of his garments.'" Thus far his words.

And behold, he explained explicitly that the good oil is the effluence that comes from Chokhmah to Binah; and there it is gathered to bestow below, to dress [le-heitiv] the lamps that are in the menorah. And he was precise in the length of his language, in saying "which flows and goes out from the Holy Ancient One, to be found in that river"; because the oil is always bestowed from Binah; for through her are bestowed whether Chesed, whether judgment, whether compassion; and therefore through her the oil is bestowed, as we explained. And the verse said, "Like the good oil upon the head": and the head is in Chokhmah, and there is the oil; and from there it descends and is gathered in Binah, and is prepared there to bestow to the other sefirot. And he said "to kindle the lamps," for the reason that the language of tov [good] in every place is the language of illumination, as "when he dresses [be-heitivo] the lamps" (Exod. 30:7), as we explained in the entry tov. And for this he said that what the verse said, "like the good oil," is from the language of illumination, because it is in Binah, to illuminate the lamps, the lamps of the menorah. And this is what he said, "to kindle the lamps." He intended to explain that the two aspects that he spoke of, from Chokhmah to Binah and from Binah to the other sefirot, are explained in the verse, in what it said: "like the good oil upon the head," that is, in Chokhmah; "that came down upon the beard," that is, in Binah. And Binah is called "the beard of Aaron" because from her Chesed draws the good oil, for it is the first of the building. "And from there, upon the skirt of his garments [middotav, read as his attributes]": that is, all the other sefirot; and this is what he said, "to all those garments of glory," etc. And even though the passage is by way of Binah, and there it is gathered, nevertheless its principal is in the secret of the right. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemini (fol. 39a), and these are his words: "Oil, which is in secret, in a whisper, always comes from the side of the Thought, which is always in a whisper and is not heard; and it is in secret; and therefore it is from the right." Thus far his words. And it is explained explicitly that the oil is from the side of the right and from the side of Chokhmah. And by this the language "the beard of Aaron" is precise; for it is Binah in the aspect of Chesed, the right. And this is enough of a notice on the matter of the oil:

Hear [שמע, Shema]: Malkhut is called Shema; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verse "Hear [Shema], O Israel" (Deut. 6:4). And he explained Shema from the language of gathering; for in her all the upper effluence is gathered. And she is so called in her lower aspect, which is the gathering of the effluence. And one must examine this matter; for in the Zohar, Parashat Chayyei (fol. 132a), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that shim'ah with Heh is the hint to Malkhut, and shema without Heh is the hint to Tiferet; and he proved the matter there from the verses. And it may be said that the intent of the hearing is to the male, even if the word is female; as if it says "Hear, O Israel": behold, Israel is Tiferet; behold, the hearing is said to Tiferet. And if our intent is to say that it should receive Malkhut to itself, nevertheless Tiferet is the receiver. But when it says shim'ah, the receiving and the speech are to Malkhut. This seems to me to answer the different places:

Tradition [שמעתא, shema'ta]: Malkhut is so called from the side of Gevurah, in the union of Binah, where the hearing is, as is explained above; and it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a):

Sun and moon [שמש וירח, shemesh ve-yare'ach]: Tiferet and Malkhut are so called. And it is already known that the moon accused the sun, as is explained in the Gate of the Diminishment; and of both of them it is said (Isa. 30:26), "Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun," etc. And Tiferet is called sun in the secret of the aspect that receives from Binah, from where is its rising, and bestows in Malkhut, as the sun shines on the moon. And in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 3b), it is understood that Yesod is called sun; and these are his words: "As the sun rises and shines on the world, so too the holy covenant rises and shines on the body of a man." And there are another sun and moon, and they are Samael and Lilith; and of them it is said (Isa. 24:23), "Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed":

Year [שנה, shanah]: a year without qualification is twelve months. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Commandments, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 277b), that Malkhut is called shanah for the reason that there are twelve months, and they are twelve maidens; the explanation, twelve stones upon which the house is established, as it is written (1 Kings 7:25), "It stood upon twelve oxen." And elsewhere (in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 248a, according to his version there) he explained that Tiferet is called shanah from the side of Binah, for it includes three hundred and sixty-five days from her side, which are the three hundred and sixty-five negative commandments. And it is possible that from there too Malkhut is called shanah; for in Malkhut is the principal of the three hundred and sixty-five negative commandments. And so he also explained elsewhere that all of them, from the side of Tiferet, are called years. And he explained that the principal year is Tiferet, which includes twelve boundaries; and from its side, that is, from the side of the aspect of ben Yah, all of them are called former years [shanim kadmoniyyot] (Mal. 3:4); for the three first ones are the preceding ones. And in the Zohar, Parashat Kedoshim (fol. 87b), he explained that Malkhut, when she is united with Tiferet, is called the fourth year (Lev. 19:24), for she is the fourth leg to the throne and to the Chariot. And in the Tikkunim he explained that Binah is called the fiftieth year:

Change [שנוי, shinnuy] of place, name and deed: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 21, fol. 55b) and in many places that there is no change except in Malkhut, which is this world; and specifically when Malkhut is hidden and concealed in Metatron, as is written in the Gate of ABYA. And there is the change of place; for there is no place there except in Malkhut. And the change of name is clear; for from her side are the substitutions, the explanation, the alphabets, and the matter of permutation and substitution, as is written in the Gate of Permutation, with the help of the Name. And the change of deed there is clear; for the principal of the deed of Malkhut is there, in the deeds in her place:

The measure of the stature [שעור קומה, shi'ur komah]: according to what appears from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, the soul that is united within the sefirah is called shi'ur, because it gives measure to the whole stature; and it is what says to the sefirot "Enough!" or makes them grow, as we explained in the Gate of Essences and Vessels. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it in Tiferet; and it is not correct:

Barley [שעורה, se'orah]: Malkhut is called barley in the aspect in which there is in her food for cattle and beasts; and for human beings, who take their sustenance from her, she is called wheat. And there is a side from which the faces of the living creatures, which are lion, ox, eagle, take sustenance from her; and this face is called barley, the food of the cattle and the holy beasts. And she is called barley on the outer side that is in her, which draws near to the depths of the sea. And she is called se'orah because there is a measure [shi'ur] to that place, up to the husk; and there the Shekhinah contracts and measures herself (see the book Sefat Emet):

Foxes [שועלים, shu'alim]: the explanation of "Take us the foxes" (Song 2:15): the intent is the powers of the husks that take hold of the wings of the Tabernacle; and this is "that spoil the vineyards":

Gate [שער, sha'ar]: he explained in the Tikkunim that Malkhut is called sha'ar, which is the reversal of the letters of eser [ten], to show that she is included of ten. And further, the Targum of sha'ar is tar'a [671]; and the filling of the name Adonai, Alef-Lamed-Peh Dalet-Lamed-Tav Nun-Vav-Nun Yod-Vav-Dalet, comes to the number six hundred and seventy-one. And of this it is said (Ps. 118:20), "This is the gate of YHVH":

Gates [שערים, she'arim]: gates without qualification are in Malkhut, for she is a gate to all the upper. However, "gates" without qualification he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 160b), that the six sides are called gates; the explanation, the six sefirot are called gates. And according to this it is found that there are gates in Malkhut and gates above her. And in the husk there are the gates of death and the gates of the shadow of death, as we explained in their entries. And there are the gates of tears, and they are in her from the side of the Chesed that is in her; for in her is the tear, in the secret of the water libation, for there is no water libation greater than this. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 11, fol. 25a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the tear is from the pupil [bat ayin], which is the daughter (of) the eye, which is the manifestation of Malkhut, the Assembly of Israel, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And the gates of righteousness are when they are the gates through which righteousness and uprightness are bestowed in the force of judgment, as is explained in the entry tzedek. And the gates of prayer are in her from her own side, which is called prayer; and it is the language of union; for in those gates Tiferet is united with Malkhut. And nevertheless we may infer to all the gates according to their titles. And she is further called the gate of Bath-rabbim (Song 7:5); and so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pinchas (fol. 220b). And we have already explained the matter of Bath-rabbim, that she is so called in the lower place, which is a gatehouse for Malkhut herself; and this is "the gate of Bath-rabbim," a gate to Bath-rabbim. Or it is possible to explain "the gate" as the gate itself being Bath-rabbim; and it is strained:

The gate of heaven [שער השמים, sha'ar ha-shamayim] (Gen. 28:17): at a glance it appears that it is Malkhut. And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 150b), he explained that Yesod is a gate to the heavens, which is Tiferet; for all the effluence that is bestowed from the heavens, Tiferet, comes through Yesod. And just as there are in holiness gates of life, and they are powers in holiness, so there are in the husks powers of impurity that are called gates of death, and likewise gates of the shadow of death, as mentioned above. And the difference between the shadow of death and death we explained in their entries:
Sha'atnez [שעטנז, sha'atnez, a mixture of wool and linen]: it is the evil handmaid, included of ox and ass, a strap to lash; and it is the husk. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained:

Lip [שפה, safah]: in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ekev, fol. 272) Rashbi explained that it is Malkhut; and so he explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 60b), that she is called safah. And he explained that so it comes to the number of Shekhinah [385]. And safah is the opening of the mouth round about, that is, mouth; for the lips themselves are Netzach and Hod; and we spoke at length on their matter in the entry peh. And in the Tikkunim he further explained that Malkhut is called the brink of the river [sefat ha-ye'or]: that is, because she is a brink to Tiferet, which is called ye'or, as we explained in its entry:

A lying lip [שפת שקר, sefat sheker] (Prov. 12:19): he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Toledot (fol. 143a), that the serpent is called the lying lip; for so is its evil custom; and the proof is from the first Adam, for the serpent with its lies brought curses upon the whole world:

Sackcloth [שק, sak] is the husk; and of it it is said (Esth. 4:2), "for none might enter into the king's gate clothed with sackcloth." SaK is an acronym of Sone Kedoshim [hater of the holy ones]. And we shall speak at length on this matter in the Gate of Substitutes, chapter 6:

Watching [שקד, shaked]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 15b), that every term of shekidah [watchfulness] is judgment, and likewise the language of shekedim [almonds]. And the proof: "Therefore has YHVH watched [va-yishkod]," etc. (Dan. 9:14); "for I watch [shoked]," etc. (Jer. 1:12):
The shekel of the sanctuary [שקל הקדש, shekel ha-kodesh]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Tiferet is called the shekel of the sanctuary:

The watering troughs [שקתות המים, shiktot ha-mayim] (Gen. 30:38) are Netzach and Hod; so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, fol. 38b). And the channel by which these troughs are filled is Tiferet; and they are filled with water from the side of Chesed; and they are so called when they water Malkhut below. And elsewhere in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 129a) he explained that the troughs are Gedulah and Gevurah, from the side of the waters of Binah, from where is the principal of their receiving:

Prince [שר, sar]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Malkhut is called the Prince of the World. And even though the truth is so, only Metatron the angel is so called; and of him they said in the Gemara (Yevamot 16b): "'I have been young, and now am old': the Prince of the World said this verse." And likewise he is called the Prince of the Face, because he has two faces, which are two unique names,  Y A H D V N H Y, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 6:

Sarah [שרה, Sarah]: Malkhut is called Sarah; and she is so called on the side in which she is united with her husband in Chesed. And the matter of Abraham, the husband of Sarah, is already known. And the explanation of SaRaH: shar Heh [the Heh sings], as we explained in the entry shir:

Sharon [שרון, sharon]: Binah is so called; so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 107). And the reason is that the Sharon is a place of the stream, which turns into a pool of water; like Binah, which is the source of all the effluence that waters the garden:

Princes [שרים, sarim]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Beha'alotekha (fol. 150), on the verse (Num. 21:18), "The well, which the princes dug": "These are Abba and Imma." For Chokhmah and Binah are called princes; and the reason may be because they are the princes of all the Emanation:
Seraph [שרף, saraf]: he explained in the Tikkunim that Malkhut is called saraf when she acts through the lower seraphim; just as she is also called, in this way, angel, as we explained in its entry:

Seraphim [שרפים, serafim] are Netzach and Hod, when they draw nourishment from the side of the fire of Gevurah: six wings, when they are included one in its fellow, in the matter of "pillars of marble [shesh]," as we explained in the entry Netzach and in the entry Hod. So Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 236):

Navel [שררך, shorrekh] (Song 7:3): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that shorrekh is the navel, the point of Zion; and it is the Yod that is in her, as is written in the entry tabbur and in the entry Zion:

Fine twined linen [שש משזר, shesh moshzar]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 12a), these are his words: "Fine twined linen [shesh, six]: which are the six days of Creation, included of ten utterances and thirty-two paths, which are thirty-two times Elohim in the work of Creation." Thus far his words. And it is possible to say that he explained that just as the twined yarn is doubled and redoubled, so shesh moshzar is explained as the six sefirot, each one included of seven, which are forty-two; and that is twined, doubled and redoubled, and twisted. Further, he explained in the Tikkunim there that Malkhut is called shesh moshzar when she is included of the six upper extremities:

Gladness [ששון, sason]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Balak (fol. 212b), that the Righteous One is called sason; and there is one who explained there that Tiferet is called sason. But what is more agreed there is that the Righteous One is called sason; and the reason is that the gladness of Malkhut depends on it.
