And it is called sason when it draws the effluence from Binah, that is, joy, as we explained in the entry simchah and in the entry "the wells of salvation." And the commentators explained that it is called sason with respect to its drawing nourishment from six [shesh]. And it is found according to this that it is called sason only when it is included of the six:

Six days [ששת ימים, sheshet yamim]: Tiferet is so called; and the reason is that it is included of six days, which are the six extremities. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 257a) Rashbi explained that Tiferet is called six days because over it are six days, from Keter to Tiferet; and it is somewhat strained; "and who can come after the king?" (Eccl. 2:12). However, in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 191a) he explained that Chesed is called six days, for the whole building is within it, as we explained in the entry yomam; see there. And it may be so called when Tiferet is within it. Thus far the letter Shin is completed, with the help of Heaven. And now we enter into the explanation of the letter Tav, with the help of the Name:

Craving [תאוה, ta'avah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (fol. 202b), that Malkhut is called ta'avah; and it is in the aspect of the receiving of the prayers; and she brings them in above and gives to each one his craving:

Twins [תאומים, te'omim]: Netzach and Hod are like two twins; for "Netzach and Hod are two halves of the body." And there is another explanation of this by Rashbi, peace be upon him (in the Zohar, Yitro, fol. 78b): that te'omim is Tiferet; and it is called te'omim because it matches [mat'im] the two extremes to the mean. And almost all of it comes to one place; for Netzach and Hod too are matched through the arbiter (which is Yesod):

Produce [תבואה, tevu'ah]: he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 226b), that Malkhut is so called; and it is with respect to her first aspect, with respect to the rung of holiness; and so it is proved there:

Discernment [תבונה, Tevunah]: Binah herself is called Tevunah. And there is a difference between Binah and Tevunah: for she is called Binah in the secret of ben Yah, through Tiferet, in the secret of Da'at, which unites above and joins Chokhmah and Binah; and it is ben Yah: Yah is Chokhmah and Binah, as is known, and ben is Tiferet in the secret of Da'at, the son who lies in the bosom of his father and his mother; and this is the explanation of Binah. However, she is called by the name Binah when she is in union with Chokhmah; and because the principal of this union is in Binah and not in Chokhmah, therefore she rises in the name, and not Chokhmah; as in the matter of "Remember" and "Keep," which we explained in their entries; see there. And Tevunah is explained: Heh, which is Binah alone, and ben and bat [son and daughter], which are Tiferet and Malkhut. And when Binah flows and lies over them like a mother over the children, she is called Tevunah; and this is why the Yod is lacking from the name, which is the father, Chokhmah; because that union has departed. All this is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 103a) and in the Zohar and in the Idra (Ha'azinu, fol. 207), letter by letter. And he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 10b) that Malkhut, from the side of Binah, is also called Tevunah:

Formlessness [תהו, tohu]: Binah is called tohu. And the reason is that he explained in the Sefer ha-Bahir: "What is bohu? A thing that clothes the tohu. And what is tohu? A thing that bewilders [matheh] human beings." So it is explained there, in interchanged places. And he explained that bohu is a thing that has substance [bo hu, "it is in it"]. And Binah is a thing in which there is no hold; and therefore she is called Mi [Who], the language of question. And it is like the hyle, which is a thing that has no form, and it precedes the manifestation of form and receives all the forms. And this is Binah, which precedes the manifestation of the revealing and receives every manifestation, according to her spreading out, whether judgment, whether compassion, whether Chesed; and there is no understanding in her except through the building. And because she is a question without an answer, he said in the Sefer ha-Bahir, "a thing that bewilders": the intent, a thing that astonishes human beings, for there is no answer to the question, as we explained:

Praise [תהלה, tehillah]: on this name many explanations are given in the book of the Zohar. And in the Ra'aya Meheimna Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that tehillah is in Keter; and in other places tehillah is in Binah. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Chokhmah and Binah are each called tehillah, and both together tehillot. And Malkhut too is called tehillah; and so it is proved in the Sefer ha-Bahir and in the Zohar, Bereshit (fol. 36a), on the verse "And the woman saw," etc. And Rabbi Moshe [de León] proved the matter from the verse (Deut. 10:21), "He is your praise, and He is your God." And what seems to me for the settling of the matter is that the true tehillah is Keter; and from there it is bestowed to Chokhmah and to Binah; and both of them together are tehillot, because they are bestowed from the great tehillah. And Malkhut is tehillah in the secret of Ani and Ayin, "its end is fixed in its beginning." And they are called tehillot only from the side of Malkhut, where the praises are, in the secret of the ten kinds of psalms, which are in the ten sefirot, in the secret of Malkhut, which are the book of Psalms [Tehillim]:

Midst [תוך, tokh]: it is explicit in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 60a), on the verse (Prov. 5:15), "and running waters out of the midst of your own well," that the word tokh is in Tiferet. And the reason is that it is in the midst, in the middle of Gedulah and Gevurah. And there he explained two explanations: that it is in Tiferet in the secret of Da'at, which is the middle within the middle, as is explained in many places in the preceding gates; or that it is Tiferet itself, which is the middle between Gedulah and Gevurah. And we explained the saying in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 19. And it seems to me that the language "deceit [tokh] and guile" (Ps. 55:12) is a husk among the husks; and it is the middle one, over against Tiferet; for "God has made even the one over against the other":

Worm [תולעת, tola'at] is certainly the husk, as it is written (Deut. 28:39), "for the worm shall eat them"; and likewise "maggot and worm." However, there is a tola'at on the side of holiness; and that is scarlet [tola'at shani]; and it is in Malkhut, as it is written (Prov. 31:21), "for all her household are clothed with scarlet." And possibly tola'at is in Tiferet, as it is written (Isa. 41:14), "you worm Jacob." And nevertheless this too is right in Malkhut, as we explained in the entry Jacob. And therefore David said (Ps. 22:7), "But I am a worm, and no man [ish]"; which is the upper aspect in Tiferet, as we explained in the entry ish:

Addition [תוספתא, tosefta]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116b) that Malkhut, from the side of Yesod, is called tosefta. And the reason is that Yesod is called musaf [additional], as is explained in its entry; and just as it is called musaf on the Sabbath day and on the other festivals, so she is then called tosefta:

Turtledove [תור, tor]: in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 4), on the verse (Song 2:12), "and the voice of the turtledove," he explained that it is the Oral Torah. For the Written Torah is called simply Torah, and the Oral Torah he calls tor, as we say va-yikar and va-yikra. And the intent is understood from what I wrote in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 2, in the name of the Zohar, on the matter of na'arah and na'ar: when she has received the male upon her, she is called na'arah. And therefore the Written Torah is called Torah, to hint at Tiferet and Malkhut together; and the principal is Tiferet; for so is the way that we explained in the entry "Keep" and in the entry "Remember." And therefore she is called tor while she has not received the male. And likewise va-yikar is Malkhut, and it is without Alef, to hint that the Alef has not yet been united with her. And even though va-yikra is also in Malkhut, they have already answered this there in the Zohar:

Torah [תורה, torah]: there are many Torahs. There is Torah in Chokhmah; and from Chokhmah the Torah was emanated, that is, Tiferet, as is known; and this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: "The Torah is the unripe fruit of the Wisdom above." And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Kedoshim (fol. 81a), and these are his words: "There is no Torah without Wisdom, and no Wisdom without Torah; and all is in one rung, and all is one. But the Torah is found in the upper Wisdom, and stands in it, and in it its roots were planted on all sides." Thus far his words. Behold, it is explained that the Torah was emanated from Chokhmah, and its principal depends on Chokhmah, and they are never separated. And even though it is below in its place, in Tiferet, nevertheless its roots are rooted above, within the depths of Chokhmah. And this is what he said, "There is no Torah without Wisdom," etc. And therefore it is called the Primordial Torah, as bereshit, whose Targum is be-kadmin. And there is the Written Torah and the Oral Torah; and on this matter there are many differences in the Zohar. In one place he said: the Written Torah, Chesed; and your sign, "and the Torah of Chesed is on her tongue" (Prov. 31:26); and the Oral Torah, Gevurah; and this is what we say, "from the mouth of the Gevurah." And in another place he said: the Written Torah, Tiferet; and the Oral Torah, Malkhut. And the matter is that Tiferet and Malkhut are male and female; and the male is the secret of compassion, inclining toward Chesed; and the female the secret of judgment, as we explained in "Remember" and "Keep"; and we explained it in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon, chapter 10. And at the time of her rising to be united, this one inclines to the right, in the secret of Chesed, male; and the female to the left, judgment. And Chesed and Tiferet are found to the right, the Written Torah; and Gevurah and Malkhut to the left, the Oral Torah; and this is "from the mouth of the Gevurah": "from the mouth," which is Malkhut; and Gevurah as its sense; both of them united, as we explained. And so he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 6b) that Malkhut, from the side of Chesed, is called the Written Torah, and from the side of Gevurah is called the Oral Torah, through Gedulah and Gevurah, as we explained. If so, Malkhut too is called the Written Torah from the side of Chesed. And the Written Torah was given through the left and the right; for so Tiferet is included of both of them. And with this introduction the verse is understood (Deut. 33:2), "from His right hand went a fiery law [esh dat] for them": the explanation, "from His right hand," Chesed; "fire," Gevurah; "law," Tiferet. And he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 9b) that Malkhut is called the Torah of YHVH from the side of the central pillar; and the reason is in the secret of the union of Tiferet and Malkhut. And then she is temimah [perfect]; for "a woman is half of the body," and "a King without a Lady is not a king." And elsewhere (in the Introduction, fol. 4b) he explained that Malkhut is called "the Torah of YHVH is perfect" (Ps. 19:8) from the side of the central pillar. And elsewhere he explained that she is called the Oral [be-al peh] Torah in the secret that she is mouth to mouth [al peh] with her husband, in the secret of the kiss; as it is written (Song 1:2), "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth," in the masculine. And in the Tikkunim, elsewhere, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Malkhut is called the Torah of the wise (Prov. 13:14) in her place below, in the secret of the lower Wisdom, as we explained in its entry. And on the matter of why Tiferet is called Torah, Rabbi Judah explained in the Zohar, Parashat Metzora (fol. 53b), these are his words: "Why is it called Torah? Because it teaches [orei] and reveals what was enclosed and not known." And the intent is that Tiferet is called Torah from the language of hora'ah [teaching]; and it is so called when it reveals the concealed things; for there must be revealing after revealing: from Chokhmah to Binah, and from Binah to Tiferet, and from Tiferet to Malkhut; and Malkhut reveals it below. And there is a matter related to this in Parashat (Vayakhel, fol. 200), for it is proved there that Binah is the Written Torah: Binah is the Torah, and Tiferet the writing that reveals it; and it is concealed in the Torah. And that is, that Chokhmah is Torah, that is to say, it reveals the concealed matters in the secret of the first array; and Binah is Torah, revealing the concealed things that are in Chokhmah; and it is Torah; and of her it is said (Prov. 1:8; 6:20), "and forsake not the Torah of your mother"; "if you call to Binah" (Prov. 2:3); and so he explained in the Tikkunim. And Tiferet is Torah [revealing] the concealed things that are in Binah; and Malkhut is Torah revealing the concealed things that are in Tiferet. And there he explained that Malkhut is called the Oral Torah, for she is over all the rungs that are beneath her; for she is called al peh because they are called peh, because they reveal all the Emanation:

The Sabbath limit [תחום שבת, techum Shabbat]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 11a) that the Sabbath limit is the limit of Malkhut, which is her boundary round about; for it is not fitting to profane her and to make her void [chalal], God forbid; but that one should keep her limit from profanation, lest the point depart, God forbid. And elsewhere he explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 2a, and in Tikkun 21, fol. 53a) that the Sabbath limit is eight thousand [cubits], and they are the eight days of circumcision and the eight passages that are in the tefillin. And the matter is that the union is in the secret of the name  Y A H D V N H Y, which is eight letters. And they are the two Yods that are in this name, which are the secret of the middle point, for the male and for the female; and around them are six letters, their limit. And the total of the letters is eight, when we say that the two Yods, which are Yod in its filling, twenty, are one: Yod at the head and Yod at the end is the middle point; Vav in the middle is the line of the circle that surrounds the point of the center, which is Yod.

And behold, on the matter of six letters and eight they disagreed in the Gemara (Eruvin 49b) concerning the Sabbath limit: this one says circular, and that one says square. For so it is: when the square is eight, the circle is six. And the one who says circular, because he holds that the Yods are not included in the eight letters, for they are the point of the center; and there remain six letters, which are  A H D V N H, around the two Yods, which are the middle. And the one who says square, because so is its way and the way of the Emanation, that they are counted here and here, as the twelve boundaries; and the point, which is the name that bears them, they are thirteen, as we explained in the entry Alef-Yod-Kof. And therefore he said there, "so that he gains the corners"; for every corner is a Yod in its form and in its matter and in its hint. And two Yods in their filling, Yod-Vav-Dalet Yod-Vav-Dalet, are four Yods for four corners. And in the secret of the Yods with the corners they become square; and this is "so that he gains the corners." And therefore the void of the point is six days, and the middle is the Sabbath, as we explained in the Gate of Gates, chapter 10:

Supplication [תחנה, techinnah]: in Malkhut. And apart from this, the language of prayer is Malkhut; and she is called techinnah from the side of Binah, that is, from the language of chanun [gracious]. And one asks even though one is not worthy, as it is written (Prov. 18:23), "The poor uses supplications"; and it is written (Exod. 33:19), "and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious," even though he is not worthy; that is, from the side of Binah, where there is a free gift:

Ark [תיבה, tevah]: what is agreed in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, fol. 59, and in the Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas, fol. 256) is that the ark is in Malkhut; and therefore Noah was joined to her, in the secret of "a righteous man, perfect he was." However, in the Tikkunim he said that Noah's ark is in Binah. And the tevah of the synagogue, on which the prayer leader stands to read in the Torah: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Zohar, Shelach, fol. 164a) that it is Malkhut; and the Torah scroll is united with her through the groomsman, Yesod, that is, the prayer leader who reads and prays:

The central spine of the lulav [תיומת הלולב, tiyyomet ha-lulav]: Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained that Tiferet is called the tiyyomet of the lulav; and he explained the reason by it: if the tiyyomet is split it is invalid. And it is a foundation established with us that the lulav is the middle line, as is explained in its entry; and the tiyyomet is above, in the secret of Da'at, which unites Chokhmah and Binah; and therefore, if its tiyyomet is split, it is invalid. And this reason is fine, even though the commentators disagreed about it. And this is more agreed: that the tiyyomet is the two upper leaves:

Let it stand [תיקו, teiku]: he explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116b) that Malkhut is called teiku from the side of Keter, for the reason that it is the place of silence, for one must not ponder; and of such it is said, "Be silent; so it arose in the Thought." And elsewhere he explained that Malkhut is so called in the secret that her husband has departed to Keter, in the secret of "Why do You stand afar off, O YHVH?" (Ps. 10:1). And silence is always from the side of Keter:

Blue [תכלת, tekhelet] is Malkhut in her lower manifestation, in the secret of the sea that draws near to the depths of the sea, which are the lower husks. And therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Menachot 43b): "Blue resembles the sea." And the color blue, in the secret of the force of judgment in her, draws near to the husk. And therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: "All colors are good for a dream except for blue." And we spoke at length on this in the Gate of Colors:

Mound [תל, tel]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim, fol. 116a) that Yesod is called tel, "to which all turn"; and the reason is that the effluence and the sustenance are from Yesod downward, and the principal is in Yesod:

White as snow [תלג חוור, telag chivvar] (Dan. 7:9): Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained it in Keter. And it is difficult for us; it is well with "the hair of His head," that is, in Keter; however, His garment is not Keter. Therefore it appears to us to say that it is the white tallit in which the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself, as we explained in its entry:

Plain [תם, tam]: he explained in the Zohar (Balak, fol. 163b [?]) that tam is the Shekhinah with the totality of the upper holy rungs that are in her; she is called tam. And this is "and Jacob was a plain man [ish tam]" (Gen. 25:27): the explanation, the husband [ish] of the Lady:

Likeness [תמונה, temunah]: in Malkhut. And the verses contradict one another; for in one place it says (Deut. 4:15), "for you saw no manner of likeness," and in another place (Num. 12:8), "and the likeness of YHVH does he behold." "The likeness of YHVH," of which it says "does he behold," is Binah, which is also called temunah, as we wrote. And the reason they are called likenesses is because they are the likenesses in which the upper and the lower ones are seen; as it is known that in Malkhut the beings are revealed, and in Binah they are concealed; and therefore they are called likenesses. And we have already spoken at length on this in the preceding gates and in this gate, in the entry peh:

Substitution [תמורה, temurah]: we shall explain in the Gate of Permutation that the substitutions and the permutations are in Metatron. And the Shekhinah is called temurah when she is in Metatron, as is explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 4:

Perfect [תמים, tamim]: Malkhut is so called. And he added yam [sea] to tam: for tam is Malkhut in the secret of the upper holy rungs that are in her; and yam is the totality of the lower holy rungs, with those that are not holy, foreskin and uncovering together, as it is known that beneath her are the depths of the sea. And when "small creatures with great" (Ps. 104:25) are included together, all of it is called tamim. So it is explained (in the Zohar, Balak, fol. 163a [?]). And because these aspects are united through the union, therefore Yesod is called tamim and Malkhut temimah: this male and this female. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi. And Malkhut is called temimah from the side of Chesed; and the intent is whole; so it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 243); and we explained it in the entry parah:

Timnah [תמנתה, Timnatah] (Gen. 38:12): Rabbi Abba explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 72), these are his words: "What is Timnatah? As it is said, 'and the likeness [temunat] of YHVH does he behold.'" Thus far his words. And the intent is clear: for Timnatah and temunat are all one; and it is explained in its entry:

Palm [תמר, tamar]: there is a male palm and a female palm. And therefore Tiferet and the Diadem are each called tamar. And therefore a palm tree does not make fruit unless there is a male opposite her. And both of them are explained in the verse: "The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree" (Ps. 92:13); "and she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah" (Judg. 4:5): behold, male and female. And likewise Tamar, the mother of Perez and Zerah, has a secret in her; for Perez and Zerah are [the aspects of] Tiferet and Malkhut. And if so, according to this, Tamar would be compelled to be in Binah; and this is greatly strained. And we can say that Perez and Zerah were before the husbands of Tamar; and when they did not merit, they descended below in the secret of the transmigration; and from a wife He made a mother. And they descended from their rung in the secret of the letters Vav-Heh: "his wife, his mother; her brother, her father," which is expounded in the Sava (of Mishpatim, fol. 100b) in the secret of the transmigration. And therefore Tamar is always in Malkhut.

And the matter of Perez and Zerah is the manifestation of the ascent itself, above. And close to this matter it is explained in the Sava (there, fol. 101a) on the matter of Er and Onan, who were uprooted from the world of the male, from being above the female, Tamar, and descended from their rung. And because Er was at an upper rung, in Tiferet, Onan, who is in Yesod, came to fill the place of his brother; and he did not wish to be sustained in that place; and they descended to the secret of the world of the female, and were changed like the female tree, which turns its face to rise by way of from below to above. Therefore Perez preceded Zerah, in the secret of Heh over Vav (see the book Sefat Emet by Rabbi Menachem Azariah of Fano, of blessed memory):
Tannaim [תנאים, tanna'im]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 21, fol. 42b) that they are in Netzach, Hod, Yesod; and their matter we explained in the entry Amora'im:

Infant [תנוק, tinok] is Tiferet; and it is so called when it sucks [yonek] from Binah. And this is "an infant sucking from the breasts of its mother," who is Binah. And the breasts are Gedulah and Gevurah, in the secret of honey and milk, this white and this red. And this infant puts on tefillin; and this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: "the place where the brain of an infant is soft"; and that is the place that is united in the upper tefillin; it is Binah, the tefillin on the head of the central pillar:

The great sea monster [תנין הגדול, ha-tannin ha-gadol] (Ezek. 29:3): Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 21, fol. 42a) that Tiferet, which is the middle bar within the boards, is called the great sea monster:

The great sea monsters [תנינים הגדולים, ha-tanninim ha-gedolim] (Gen. 1:21): he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemini (fol. 39b), these are his words: "'The great sea monsters': these are the Patriarchs, who are watered first and are rooted over all." The explanation: they are called great because they are the first to receive the effluence from the upper river, Binah:

Testimony [תעודה, te'udah]: Binah is called te'udah; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetze, fol. 281a) and in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 59); and she is so called when she bestows in Metatron. And in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 90b), he explained that Malkhut is called te'udah; and these are his words: "'Bind up the testimony' (Isa. 8:16): this is the Oral Torah; because there the bundle of life is bound up; and in the testimony is tied the knot of life that is above, so that all be one." Thus far his words.

And the explanation: that she is called te'udah because in her the life is united to Binah; and because she receives from Binah she is called like her. And what he said, "is bound up," etc., is the explanation of tzor te'udah, the language of tzeror [bundle]; and what he said, "is tied the knot," etc., is the explanation of te'udah:

Tiferet [תפארת, tiferet, Beauty]: the Chariot of which Jacob is a chariot is called Tiferet. And the explanation is from the language of porot [boughs] (Ezek. 17:6), and as "the goodly turbans [pa'arei ha-migba'ot]" (Exod. 39:28); and the explanation, branches and boughs. And it is so called when it is clothed in all the sefirot and in all the colors. And it is also called by the language of pe'er; for when it is clothed in the colors it is glorious [mefo'ar], and then it is called Tiferet. And the language of tif'eret shows the feminine. And he explained in the Tikkunim that Malkhut, in her receiving from this attribute, it is called mefo'ar, and Malkhut from its side tif'eret. And we spoke at length in the entry gedulah:

Apples [תפוחים, tappuchim]: Netzach and Hod are called apples. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (in Tikkun 19, fol. 38): "'Comfort me with apples' (Song 2:5): they are the two pillars of truth, which are white and red." And they are called apples because there is the fragrance of the covenant in the coupling. And they are called apples only in the secret of their inclining to Chesed, to whiten the red and to dilute the intoxicating wine. And so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemini (fol. 40a); except that it appears from there that the three Patriarchs too are called apples. And it is all one; for "the deeds of the fathers the sons will do." And in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 74a), he explained that Tiferet is called tappu'ach, as he says (Song 2:3), "As the apple tree among the trees of the wood"; and these are his words: "In everything she praises Him: in colors, in fragrance and in taste. As the apple is healing for all, so too the Holy One, blessed be He, is healing for all. As the apple is found in colors, as we have established, so too the Holy One, blessed be He, is found in upper colors. As the apple has a fine fragrance, more than all the other trees, so too of the Holy One, blessed be He, it is written, 'and his fragrance as Lebanon' (Hos. 14:7). As the apple, its taste is sweet, so too of the Holy One, blessed be He, it is written, 'His mouth is most sweet' (Song 5:16)." Thus far his words.

And his intent is that when Tiferet bestows to the world it is called tappu'ach. And this is what he said, "As the apple is healing," etc.: and the intent is on the showing of the bestowal to all, as he says (Ps. 145:9), "YHVH is good to all [la-kol]"; or to Malkhut; and that too is kol. And it is called tappu'ach when it is included of three things, which are color and fragrance and taste. And the colors: when it is included in the three Patriarchs, three colors, as is known; and this is "As the apple is found in its colors," etc., "so too the Holy One, blessed be He." "As the apple has a fine fragrance": a fine fragrance, that is, the effluence that is bestowed upon it by way of the middle line from the Supreme Crown, which is called Lebanon; and this is "and his fragrance as Lebanon." "As the apple, its taste," etc.: it is the effluence of Chokhmah and Binah, where the union is, as we explained in its entry; and that is "His mouth is most sweet [mamtakkim]," two kinds of sweetness. And when it bestows, when it is included in these matters, it is called tappu'ach. And there is a difference between tappu'ach, singular, and tappuchim, plural, as we explained (and see the Zohar, Ha'azinu, fol. 286, and in the saying of Rabbi Abba there, fol. 287):

Prayer [תפלה, tefillah]: Malkhut is called tefillah because in her all the sefirot are gathered; and that is the hand tefillah, in which is the gathering of the passages that hint at the four-letter name. And likewise every prayer of all the prayers hints at her; except that there is a difference among them. For the evening prayer is the union of Malkhut with the Tiferet that is in Tiferet; and in the morning prayer, her union with the Tiferet that is in Chesed; and in the afternoon prayer, in the Tiferet that is in Gevurah. And always she is hinted in Malkhut, "leaning upon her beloved" (Song 8:5). And in the Zohar, Parashat Vayishlach (fol. 168), he explained that Tiferet is the head tefillah, and it is called "a prayer of Moses" (Ps. 90:1), and Malkhut "a prayer of the afflicted" (Ps. 102:1); see there:

The line of scarlet thread [תקות חוט השני, tikvat chut ha-shani] (Josh. 2:18): Malkhut is so called; and your sign: "Your lips are like a thread of scarlet" (Song 4:3); so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 241b). And it may be so called in the secret of the judgment that arouses the kiss, that is, in the secret of Gevurah; and that is, that the scarlet thread is in the lips that kiss, in the secret of the north:

Teki'ah, teru'ah, shevarim [תקיעה תרועה שברים, teki'ah teru'ah shevarim]: we explained in the entry keshet and in the entry kesher that they are three Patriarchs. And in the Zohar he explained that the teru'ah is in Malkhut and the second teki'ah in Tiferet. And it is possible to say that the teki'ot are always all in Chesed and Fear [Pachad], which is in Tiferet; that is, in the secret that it inclines toward Chesed, to incline Gevurah to compassion, between Gedulah and Tiferet; that is, two teki'ot. And the teru'ah is always in Malkhut; and it is related also to Tiferet in its place before the diminishment. And in the Tikkunim, Malkhut is called teru'ah from the side of the judgment, the force of the drawing of Gevurah from the upper Gevurah:

Mighty [תקיף, takif]: he explained in the Tikkunim that it is in Chesed, and they proved this from the verse (Exod. 15:6), "Your right hand, O YHVH, glorious in power," and its Targum is be-tukfa. And we explained it in the entry hitkafta:

Heave offering [תרומה, terumah]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, said that Malkhut is called the great heave offering from the side of Chesed; and she is called the heave offering of the tithe from the side of Gevurah; and that is, that the Levite would separate it and give it to the priest, so that the Israelite be included in the right. And in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 17, fol. 29b) he explained that she is called terumah, the explanation, terei mi-me'ah [two from a hundred], which are Tiferet and Malkhut, two to the hundred; for the sefirot come, ten times ten, to a hundred. And he further explained that it is a hint to the two tablets of the Torah that were given at forty days; and that is terumah: Torah, Mem [forty]:

Beryl [תרשיש, tarshish] (Song 5:14): he explained in the Zohar: terei shesh [two sixes], that is, the three joints that are in the right arm and the three that are in the left arm; and that is Chesed of Chasadim, Gevurah of Gevurot. And we spoke at length in the entry "Netzach of Netzachs":

Return [תשובה, teshuvah]: Binah is called teshuvah. And the reason is that there is the return of the things and the beings, all of them, in the secret of the Jubilee; and from there the beings return and spread out, and the Sabbatical cycles roll on, and return and complete their circuit, and return and are swallowed up in their place, in the secret of the Jubilee. So the commentators explained. However, in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 16a), he explained, and these are his words: "Rabbi Judah said: When is it called teshuvah? When the Mother is covered and stands in joy over the children, as it is written, 'a joyful mother of children' (Ps. 113:9); and she returns in her existence; and what was closed returns to its place; and all of them return one to another, and each and every one is blessed; and then it is called complete teshuvah. Teshuvah without qualification, to include all." Thus far his words.

And the intent is clear: for when judgment comes into being in the world, Binah departs and judgment is claimed, and the world is judged. And when she returns over the children and bestows compassion, she is called teshuvah without qualification. However, when she returns and sets right the other rungs within her, to receive from their upper place, then she is called complete teshuvah; for she returns and the rungs return one to another; and then she is complete in substance, all the rungs. And this return is through the Supreme Crown being revealed from the head of the Emanation, and piercing and descending down to Malkhut; and this is teshuvah; and so it is explained there explicitly. And in Parashat Naso (fol. 122b) he explained that Malkhut too is called teshuvah; and these are his words: "Rather, this is called teshuvah when compassion turns toward her, and she returns over all those hosts and suckles them." Thus far his words.

And the matter is that when she draws nourishment from judgment, then she bestows to all the sides of impurity and the husks, and then the world is judged. And when the compassion is bestowed upon them, then she returns to suckle all her holy hosts; and at that time she is called teshuvah: the explanation, tashuv Heh [the Heh returns]; for the Heh has returned to her place, over her hosts. And likewise, in the language of the answer [teshuvah] to a question, Malkhut is called so from the side of Binah; and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a). And the reason is that there is no answer unless Binah precedes, that the man understand; and by this he answers the one who asks. And so he explained there that Malkhut is called teshuvah from the side of Binah. And so it is fitting: that she not return to water her hosts unless she receives from Binah. Thus far.

Behold, the entry of the Tav is completed, with the help of the One who "gives power to the faint, and to them that have no might He increases strength" (Isa. 40:29). And this glorious gate is concluded; praise to God, Creator of the world. And now we shall begin the Gate of Palaces, with the help of Heaven:
Gate Twenty-Four is the Gate of Palaces:

After we have hoed, measured and completed all our intent in the matter of the sefirot, our wish is to write the matter of the palaces, as is wanted in this book. And in the matter of these palaces there is no new matter from the part of speculation at all, apart from copying the language of the book of the Zohar in extreme brevity, as far as is possible within our ability:
Chapter One:

The first palace, from below to above, is the one called the Palace of the Pavement of Sapphire [היכל לבנת הספיר, heikhal livnat ha-sappir] (Exod. 24:10). And in this palace there is one appointed one, Tahariel by name. And he stands at the entrance of this palace with several appointed angels who are with him; and all of them are blazing fire, and rods of fire are in their hands, and all of them are full of eyes. And when the soul rises above, if it has merited and is fit to enter, they open an entrance for it and it enters; and if it is defiled, they push it away. And outside this palace there is one appointed one and several angels of ruin; and they push it away until they bring it down to Gehinnom, and it is judged there twelve months. And in this way in the matter of prayer: if it is a congregational prayer, after it has split the air and reached the entrance of the palace, they receive it at once, as it is written (Ps. 102:18), "and has not despised their prayer"; and they are handed over in this firmament, which is called Bazak, as we shall explain; and there they are held back under the hand of this appointed one until all Israel complete their prayer; and then they are all handed over together into the hand of Sandalfon, the angel who ties crowns for his Master; and from there they are handed over and become diadems for the head of the Righteous One, the Foundation of the World, as is known. And if it is the prayer of an individual, they look into it, as it is written (there), "He has regarded the prayer of the destitute": if it is fit, they bring it in; and if not, they push it away. And from there it descends to the lower firmament and is handed over into the hand of the angel Sahadiel, to do with it as we shall explain in the Gate of Intention, with the help of the Name.

And behold, this angel Tahariel is commanded and appointed at this entrance to push away or to receive the soul or the prayer; and it is possible that he is called Tahariel because he purifies [metaher] it or disqualifies it according to its deeds. Above this entrance there is another entrance; and they are gates that the Holy One, blessed be He, dug for the masters of return [ba'alei teshuvah], who shed tears in their prayer; and they are called the gates of tears; and they have never been locked, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bava Metzi'a 59a): "All the gates are locked, but the gates of tears are not locked." And when the prayer of tears rises to enter by this entrance, an ofan [wheel] is present there, Rachmiel by name; and he stands over six hundred great living creatures, and he takes the prayer of the tears and brings them in above. In the air of the inwardness of this palace there is one spirit, and it is called (Sastoria) [another version: Statoria]; and this is the sapphire mentioned above. And its color is like the color of the sapphire, sparkling; and it is divided into two lights. The first light is white, sparkling to every direction, above and below and the four directions. And the second light is concealed and revealed; and from this light four lights are separated, to the four directions, and all of them are one light. And these sparks shine like burnished red, as it is written (Ezek. 1:7), "and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass." All this is to the right of this palace; and it is called sapphire when the upper firmament, Binah, emanates the souls within the seventh palace, which is called the Holy of Holies, as we shall explain; for there they are emanated. And when an arousal descends from Binah to the seventh palace, then the souls are males, for the reason that the male prevails over the female; and then a male is born; for "whoever is stronger prevails." For the upper arousal arouses the female, and then she emits seed first; and when the soul descends, the upper power prevails, and it is male. And then this spirit, the right sapphire, which is the male, as we explained, gathers them below, until they are included in their females, to scatter them in this world among human beings. And this matter we spoke of at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 17, with the help of Heaven. And to the left of the palace, the air of its inwardness is one spirit, and it is called Livnat, and its name is Adiria Senunia; and this light is white and red included together, because their origin and emanation is from the right light, which is white and its sparks red, as we explained. And when the sparkling of this left light reaches the sparks of the right, this left one is concealed within it and included in it, and is not seen at all; after the way of the female, to be concealed beneath the male. And this light, which is called Livnat, is female; and when the arousal is from below, from this palace to Binah, then the souls that are bestowed there are females. Afterward they descend from this palace, and this light receives them; and the two lights are united with one another, male with female; and the souls are united, male with female; and both of them descend, united, to the lower Garden of Eden; and there they are separated. And this is that the Holy One, blessed be He, couples couples, as he explained in the Zohar, and we copied it in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 22. And these two lights together are called livnat ha-sappir; and they are Statoria Adiria Senunia [another version: Senigia]. And in the union and coupling of these two spirits, the right and the left, the souls of the male and the female are included, as we explained. And when these two spirits have been included and come to be united in their meeting, to be included in one another, then they sparkle, and sparks are created and spread out to every side; and from the left light sparks sparkle; and those sparks are the ofannim, of which the verse said (Ezek. 1:16), "The appearance of the wheels and their work," etc.; for they are not like the kind of the living creatures. And these ofannim are blazing with fire and stand in a row.

And the matter of the coming into being of these sparks is like the sparks that burst forth from beneath the hammer when it strikes the burning iron, which throws off sparks. And likewise is the matter in the meeting of the right light with the left. And when these two spirits and lights, which are livnat ha-sappir, are joined, a light goes out from them, which is one living creature, rising and descending, and it settles upon four ofannim, as we shall explain here. And the likeness of this living creature is like a lion; and it rules over thirteen hundred myriad other ofannim, apart from these four ofannim; and they are arranged in these four rows; their wings are like the wings of the eagle. And this living creature is called Bazak [flash of lightning] (Ezek. 1:14). And from this Bazak one firmament spreads out; and this firmament stands upon two pillars, one on this side and one on that side, and the firmament over them; and these two pillars are two cherubim. And of this firmament it is written (Ezek. 10:1), "Then I looked, and behold, in the firmament that was above the head of the cherubim." And this is not the firmament that is over the heads of the living creatures. And over this firmament the Bazak is appointed, and it is what covers over all. And in this firmament the prayers are set in order, until they are all gathered, until Sandalfon comes to receive them, as we explained above. And likewise all those who occupy themselves with Torah at night and pray: this Bazak receives them until the rising of the dawn. And after the rising of the dawn and the shining of the day, those prayers and the Torah rise and ascend to the firmament that is called the Book of Remembrance. The Bazak mentioned stands upon four ofannim; they are the wheels [galgallim]; and their names are Ahaniel, Kedumiel, Malkhiel,  Y A H D V N H Y. And each one of them stands upon four pillars: they are sixteen pillars for four wheels. And each one of these four ofannim has four faces, which are sixteen faces for four ofannim; and these faces look to the four directions of the Bazak, which stands upon them. And in these four ofannim four letters are included, which are Adonai, which Sandalfon, the master of the chariots, uses. And these four ofannim fly in the pure air; and that air is included in four letters,  Y H V D  [YHVH]; and the letters YHVH are included in the letters Adonai; and they are interlaced, "one to another," "the loops held one to another" (Exod. 26:5),  A A A  [an abbreviation, probably ish el achiv, "each to his brother"]; and they are included in the manifestation of the included light, which is  Y A H D V N H Y, which is the totality of this whole palace. And when it is wholly included in this name to ascend, then it sparkles with a sparkling like the color of the sun sparkling in water. And of this manifestation it is said of the ofannim (Ezek. 1:20), "Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went," etc. And from the middle of this palace is one pillar; and it is fixed from this first palace to the second palace; and the name of this pillar is Aharhaniel [Adarhaniel]. And when what is in this palace is included one with another, and all of it in the spirit of judgment, then, through the prayers, [the palace] is united, from the including spirit that is in this palace, with the spirit of the upper palace that is in the second palace, through this pillar. And the manifestation of this palace is supported on two pillars toward the east. And their names: the first, Kar'iel, and he is appointed over twelve thousand angels; and the second, Shema'iel, and he is appointed over twelve thousand other angels; and the two of them, this to the right and this to the left; and they are called the pegs of the Tabernacle. And toward the south two other pillars, and their names are Sa'adiel, Satriel; each one is appointed over twelve thousand other appointed ones. And they are appointed over the sustaining of the world; and these are called balances, for they stand to weigh every male and female who are fit to be united with one another. And even though sometimes the scale-pan of the man outweighs the woman, or the reverse, nevertheless they are the ones who unite; and therefore they are called "balances, to go up" (Ps. 62:10), for they go up together even though they are not equal; and they are not the ones that are called "just balances." Toward the north two others, and their names are Petachiel, Atariel; and each one is appointed over twelve thousand other appointed ones; and they too are pegs. Toward the west two others, and their names are Pedatiel, Tumiha'el; and they are appointed, each one, over twelve thousand other appointed ones; and they shed tears over those who divorce the wives of their youth, on account of the seven blessings with which they were blessed and which were not sustained when they were divorced. And this thing shows the departure of the seven blessings with which the upper female was blessed; and then a heavenly voice goes out and says, "Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement," etc. (Isa. 50:1). And all these are pegs like the first ones that we spoke of. And these are the eight pegs; and then eight cords, which are lights, are held by the pegs; and all of them are outside the palace, and this palace is supported upon them. And all of them are uprooted from the place when the spirit that is in the palace wishes to be included in the second palace, as we explained. And this is what we have gathered from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Pekudei (fol. 246 and fol. 255) and in Parashat Bereshit, fol. 42:

The second palace is called the Very Heaven [עצם שמים, etzem shamayim]. Within this palace one spirit is appointed, of pure light, which is called etzem, "and as it were the very heaven for clearness" (Exod. 24:10); and it is called Orpaniel. And in this palace there are three entrances: one toward the south, and one toward the north, and one to the east, in the middle. And the entrances of the south and the north are locked; and over them are two appointed ones, who are under the hand of this appointed one whose name is Orpaniel; and he is appointed over the middle entrance of the east; and he rules over three directions of the world, south and east and north. And all the souls that are those killed by the court, or those killed by the other nations, are all under the hands of these appointed ones. And the appointed one who is over them engraves their likeness on his garments, which are burning fire, and rises above and shows them to the Holy One, blessed be He. And the Holy One, blessed be He, engraves the form of those killed by the nations on His garment, on His purple robe, "garments of vengeance for clothing" (Isa. 59:17), as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained. And those killed by the court he brings down and brings in by the two closed entrances; and the two other appointed ones stand over them; and from there they go out and see the rungs of the righteous who keep the Torah, and are ashamed and are burned by the canopy of the righteous; until this appointed one, whose name is Orpaniel, opens for them the gate of the east, and shines for them, and gives them life from the side of the east; for on the side of this appointed one is a light of life, which is full of lights. And this light is called the cup of consolations, the cup of life; for because of the bitter cup that they drank they merited this cup. And there is the cup of staggering, and it will be explained in the explanation of the Palaces of the Substitutes. And this light, which is called Orpaniel, is a white color that does not change; and of it it is said, "and as it were the very heaven for clearness." And it is hard for it to sparkle, because it is concealed; but when the lights and the spirit that are in the first palace, which is called the Pavement of Sapphire, sparkle and strike against it, then it revolves and shines like the color of the eye, which shines only in its revolving. And this light, which is called Orpaniel, shines for this palace and for the first palace; and while it does not sparkle it is called the Palace of Radiance [zohar], because it is a simple radiance. However, when the lower palace revolves to sparkle, then it sparkles and is included with one light that is on the left side, which is called Hadarniel. And when the two of them are included together, and the left color, which is called Hadarniel, is included with the left red color that is in the lower palace, which we mentioned in the previous chapter, then the three colors are mixed together: the white that is on the right, which is called Orpaniel, and the blue with the red; and the three of them together make it like the color of the heavens; and this is "and as it were the very heaven [shamayim]": fire and water [esh u-mayim], white and red and blue. And the whole lower palace is included in this second palace; for it does not sparkle unless it is included. And then it is called etzem ha-shamayim, as we explained; and of it it is said (Ezek. 1:28), "As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain," etc. And of the first light alone, which is called Orpaniel, it is said, "as the colour of the chashmal" (Ezek. 1:27); and sometimes it is the chashmal, because from it go out seraphim, living creatures of speaking fire, concealed living creatures, seen and not seen. And likewise you will find Or Paniel equal in number to chashmal.

And the matter of Orpaniel of which we spoke is the power of life and compassion; and by it the power of the husk is subdued, as we shall write with the help of the Name. And when the power of the husk rules and the world is in judgment, this light is stored away and darkened, and the world is judged. And in this spirit stand the garments of the righteous who rise to see the face of the Lord, YHVH of hosts. And when they rise there to appear, on reaching this palace, an appointed one is present for it, Tzadkiel by name; and the angel takes this garment; it is its garment, which it merited by doing the commandments; for according to the effort a man makes, so he merits the garment. And it goes with it until it reaches the river of fire [nehar dinur]; there the soul is whitened and washed. And sometimes that soul is sunk within the river and is burned there and does not rise all the day; except that every day in the morning, when a wind is aroused from the side of the south, which is the side of Chesed (and so the morning is related to Abraham), and from the side of Chesed they are renewed and stand and say song, like the other angels who pass from their dominion, who are burned there and renewed every day. If the soul has merited, and is not burned and not sunk in the river of fire, then the angel Tzadkiel mentioned clothes it with the garment of which we spoke; and from there it rises to be offered upon the altar through Michael, the great prince who is in the fourth palace, so that it stand before its Owner "to be enlightened with the light of the living" (Job 33:30). And when these three lights, which are the secret of etzem ha-shamayim, come to be united, before their union, in their beating one against another, sparks sparkle in them, as one who strikes with the hammer on the anvil, which throws sparks to every side. So there sparkle [and are created] from between these lights and spirits several angels appointed over the matters of this world, and several seraphim with six wings; and they sanctify YHVH of hosts three times every day. And they are masters of the force of judgment, who are exacting with the righteous as a hair's breadth; and they are those who stand to punish in this world and in the world to come those who make light of those from whose mouth they learn Torah and do not treat them with honour as is fitting; and likewise those who make use of those who learn the six orders of the Mishnah. And when the lights have already been united and settled together, then one living creature goes out from between them, whose name is Yofiel; and it rules over four living creatures, and those four rule over the other seraphim that we mentioned above, because they are included within it; and the faces of the four living creatures are the faces of an eagle. And the living creature whose name is Yofiel is the Prince of the Torah, and all the keys of wisdom are in his hand; and he was the teacher of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, according to the opinion of some kabbalists. And this living creature demands of the Holy One, blessed be He, to give good reward to all those who pursue the sages to learn Torah from them, and even from any man, as it is said (Ps. 119:99), "I have more understanding than all my teachers," and who learn for the sake of Heaven. And the reward that he pays to those who pursued the Torah is to guard them from the side of impurity: for when the soul rises above, this living creature goes out upon four flying seraphim, and they go before it, and it does not let any one of the angels of ruin draw near to it; and several angels of peace go round about it. And the seraphim that we spoke of above, when they are within the four living creatures that we mentioned, when they journey, all those serpents, the seraphim that go out from the primordial serpent, are all subdued when these go out, journeying and seen. And when the soul rises and reaches this living creature, then it asks it concerning the wisdom of the Torah that it learned; and according to how it laboured in the Torah and pursued it, at that rung it rewards it. And if it was able to occupy itself [and attain] more in the Torah and did not occupy itself, it pushes it down beneath that palace in shame and in disgrace. And when the seraphim that are beneath the living creature lift their wings and strike them one against another, they burn that soul; and it is burned and not burned, scorched and not scorched; and so it is judged every day, even though it has good deeds, since it did not occupy itself in the Torah as is fitting. And all the lights and the living creatures and the ofannim are all included beneath this living creature; and all of them hide beneath their wings, to rise through it above. And this living creature, when it takes hold of four other living creatures that are below it, as we said: each one of the four living creatures has four ofannim: one ofan turns toward the east, and its name is Chaniel; and one ofan turns toward the north, and its name is Karshiel; and one ofan turns toward the south, and its name is Azriel; and one ofan turns toward the west, and its name is Aniel. And each ofan and wheel has three pillars on which it stands; three pillars are found for each ofan; they are twelve pillars for each living creature (and four living creatures come to forty-eight pillars). And all the pillars turn toward the middle; for the cause of their going is from the middle; and all of them, "at its commandment they journey and at its commandment they encamp" (Num. 9:20). And in the journeying of the ofannim the sound of their pleasantness is heard up to the heights of the firmaments; and all the living creatures and the ofannim sing to the Holy One, blessed be He: the right ones say "Holy," and the left ones say "Blessed," and the middle ones say "Holy" and "Blessed." And the reason is that holiness is from the side of Gevurah and blessing from the side of Chesed, and the middle is composed of both of them; for the middle line is of fire and of water, as is known. And here the right ones say "Holy" and the left ones say "Blessed," to show the greatness of the union: right included in left and left in right. And when the pillars are united in the ofannim, and the ofannim in the living creatures, and the living creatures in the four great ofannim that belong to the great middle living creature, Yofiel, and they are joined and interlaced one to another, to be united above in the spirit of the upper palace, then they are called chamudot [precious things]. And for this reason it was said to Daniel (Dan. 9:23), "for you are (a man) greatly beloved [chamudot]." And the reason is that the second palace is the palace of the vision and the dream; that is to say, the palace of those who speak by the holy spirit. And the third palace is the palace of prophecy, the place of the drawing of the prophets:

And now it is fitting to know that the place of the drawing of the prophets is not in the sefirot themselves; for the sefirot are not a revealed thing in any way in the world, even to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. However, the difference between Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and the other prophets is that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, would prophesy from within the Palace of Will, which is the sixth palace, as we shall explain; and the other prophets from the Palace of Brightness [Nogah], which is the third palace; and Daniel and his companions, who speak by the holy spirit in vision and dream, look into this second palace in which we are.

And further, apart from this: when Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, prophesied from the Palace of Will, through the joining of Tiferet and Malkhut, which are revealed in that palace, his prophecy was from a refined mirror; for he did not need an intermediary between him and the palace to look into the matters of the prophecies; and therefore it was (not) in a vision and not in riddles (Num. 12:8). But the other prophets unite these sefirot in the third palace; and those who speak by the holy spirit would unite these sefirot in the second. And the matter is that the sixth palace points to the upper union, in the aspect that is the shining mirror, Tiferet. And in the third palace, which is the Palace of Brightness, as we shall explain, the light of the union is revealed, which is the union of two sefirot in the prevailing of Tiferet over Malkhut; and the mirror that does not shine is seen within Malkhut. And those who speak by the holy spirit, in the revealing of the light of the union in this palace, which is the Palace of the Very Heaven, in the prevailing of Malkhut over Tiferet; and it is more the one that does not shine than (the other) [than for the other] prophets. And that is, that the union of Tiferet and Malkhut is in Netzach and Hod, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance and in the preceding gates. And apart from this there is a third aspect: for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, understood his prophecy without intermediaries between him and his palace and its sefirot; and the other prophets had many screens between the sefirot and the palaces and themselves; and that is, that they needed an explanation for their prophecies, as he says (Dan. 8:16), "Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision"; and likewise in Jeremiah 1, "What do you see?" etc.; and likewise in the other prophets.

And behold, when the prophecy is bestowed through intermediaries, the more the intermediaries multiply, the more the riddles and visions multiply; and the witness is from Daniel. And because the prophecy of Daniel was from this palace, with its parts united, as we explained, he was called "a man greatly beloved [ish chamudot]":

And through the prayers of which we spoke, all the powers mentioned are united: the seraphim in the pillars, and the pillars in the ofannim, and the ofannim in the living creatures, and the living creatures in the ofannim of the great living creature, and these ofannim in the living creature itself; and they rise and are united by way of the pillar that is in the middle of the palace, and are united within the third palace. For this is the principal of their desire: that the palaces, that is to say the lights and the spirits that are within them, be one within another, after the manner of the embryo in its mother's womb. And this palace too is supported upon eight pegs, like the first palace of which we spoke: two of them toward the east, and their names are Yehadniel, Gezuriah; and each one of them is appointed over twelve thousand other appointed ones. And these are appointed over the voices and cries of the woman sitting on the birthstool; and they take them and bring them in to the appointed one who is over the entrance; and impurity has no power to accuse. And sometimes the side of the left gets ahead to accuse first and can do harm, God forbid. And two toward the north, Salsaliel, Karspiha'el their names; and they are appointed, each one appointed over twelve thousand other appointed ones; and these are appointed over the blood of the covenant of children circumcised at eight days. And when, God forbid, agitation is found in the world, the Holy One, blessed be He, looks at that blood and does not give the Satan permission to accuse. And the way of these pegs is like the pegs of which we spoke in the first palace; and likewise for the other palaces:

The third palace is called the Palace of Brightness [היכל נוגה, heikhal nogah]. This palace is more exalted and praiseworthy than the two preceding palaces. And in this palace there are four entrances, to the four directions of the world. One entrance toward the south; and in it there is one appointed one, and his name is Malkhiel; and he rules over all the rulings of judgment that have been decreed upon human beings, to judge them: when they go out from the upper court they come under the hands of this appointed one. And under his hand are two scribes, and their name is Shamshiel; and they set in order all the notes that go out concerning human beings, to judge them. And meanwhile he holds them back, so that they are not handed over into the hand of Sangadiel, the angel appointed in the first palace that is on the left side, in the substitutes, who stand to accuse human beings and sometimes to judge them; may YHVH save us. And we shall speak at length in the Gate of the Palaces of the Substitutes, with the help of the Name. And therefore this appointed angel sets them in order and further turns over their merit, to see whether perhaps there is over them "an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand" (Job 33:23), and to soften the strong judgment upon him. And after all the notes and decrees of judgment have been set in order at this entrance, Gezariel takes them and brings them to the second entrance, which is on the side of the east; and there is an appointed one there whose name is Azriel. And the name of each and every entrance is after the appointed one who is over it. And the appointed one who is at this entrance is to seal the rulings for life or for death, God forbid. And under his hand are two attendants, whose names are Sitriah, Adiel: one stands at his right and one stands at his left. The one who stands at the right, in his hand life depends, and the seal of life; and the one who stands at the left, in his hand death depends, and the seal of death is in his hand. And this gate is closed all the six days of work; and on the Sabbath and the New Moon it is opened, to show the life in the seal of life that is there. And on Yom Kippur this gate is closed until the passing of the time of the afternoon prayer of Yom Kippur; after the afternoon prayer a spirit is aroused and goes out from the Palace of Merit, which is the fourth palace, as will be explained with the help of the Name; and this gate is opened; and the appointed angel and two attendants stand, one at his right and one at his left, and the seal of life and death is in their hand; and all the decrees of judgment are sealed, whether for death or for life. At the third entrance, toward the north: at this entrance it is made known when they decree upon a man kinds of sufferings, whether sicknesses or poverty, any decree of judgment that is not for death. And over this entrance there is one appointed one, Kaftziel by name; and he is appointed there to close the entrance upon the decree of the man who is decreed against, so that his return is not received in any way unless it be complete and strong. And of this it is said (Job 12:14), "He shuts up a man, and there can be no opening." And when judgment is decreed upon small children for the iniquities of their father, under the hand of this appointed one there is one angel whose name is Iriel; and he goes out and proclaims to the side of the left; then a power is aroused on the side of impurity, Askarah [croup] by name, and it rules over that child, God forbid, and is given permission; as the matter is written at length in the Gate of the Palaces of the Substitutes. The fourth entrance stands toward the west; and this gate is the gate of healing. And over this gate there is one appointed one, Pedael by name; and he is the angel of healing; and he brings in all the prayer of those afflicted with sickness and pains and sorrow, to be an interpreter for them. And this angel raises their merit and their prayer and brings them in before the King, YHVH of hosts. And of this it is said (Job 33:23), "If there be over him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand"; and it is written there (33:24), "and he says, Deliver [pede'ehu] him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom." Within this palace there is one light called Nogah [Brightness]. And this spirit and light is praiseworthy and concealed beyond (the gate) [the other] lights that are in the palaces of which we spoke; and there is no revealed color in it at all; and therefore it is called tohar [clearness], to show its purity. And it is revealed only when the other lights are raised within it; and then, through it, the light of a color different from the other colors of the lights is revealed. And this light is called Zohariel. And this light was created from the oil of holy anointing that descends and flows from Binah, the world to come; and of this it is said (Ps. 132:17), "I have ordained a lamp for My anointed." And through the entering of the other lights of the lower palaces within this palace, and when they are included in it, they are anointed and kindled with the good oil. And this light is for all those who have a portion in the world to come; and it crowns them with radiance and brightness, so that they enter the other palaces without permission, and none protests against them. And when this palace is set in order with the other lower palaces that are within it, then it brings out one praiseworthy light, Ahadiel by name; and this light stands beneath the light of which we spoke, to anoint with the oil of holy anointing all those souls that rise above. For in their rising by way of the other palaces that we mentioned, they are inscribed with the twenty-two letters of the Torah; and when they reach this palace, this angel anoints them; and they rise and enter the river of fire, and from there they rise to be offered upon the altar. And this light, Ahadiel, is included of three lights, because the anointing oil is included of three colors. And when this light sparkles, twenty-two lights sparkle from it, corresponding to the twenty-two letters inscribed in the soul; and the twenty-two lights are all appointed ones and attendants before it; and all of them are called by its name, and all of them are included in it. And this light, with the twenty-two lights, are all included within the great light, Zohariel, of which we spoke. And when the lights of the palaces and the light Ahadiel, in the twenty-two letters, come to be joined together within the great light Zohariel, one living creature goes out from among them all, whose name is Ahiel; and it is included in two colors, lion and eagle, all included in one form. And when the great light shines in it, there go out from between the sparkling four ofannim, included in all the colors; and their names are Hadriel, Yehadriel, Ahaduria, Asimon; and they are for the four directions of the world. And each one of these has eight wings, and four wings and four faces; and the two faces look within their middle, toward the great living creature that is over them; and the two outer faces are covered with their wings, for they cannot look at the great lights that are in the palace, because of the great sparkling and the radiance and the brightness. And these ofannim show war, or the uprooting of a king; for there is no war in this world that is not first above, in the host of heaven; and first they uproot the prince, and afterward the nation. And when these ofannim journey to show war, according to what is bestowed to them from above, from the Palace of Merit, where the place of judgment is, from their sweat there are made beneath them several kinds of hosts, camps without number. And of them some are masters of song, to praise their Creator; of them some are messengers appointed in the world to guard the disciples of the sages from those impure bands that go out from the husks, as is written in the Gate of Substitutes, with the help of the Name. And of this it is said (Ps. 91:11–12), "For He shall give His angels charge over you … They shall bear you up in their hands, lest you dash your foot against a stone," etc.; for "God has made even the one over against the other": just as there is "a tried stone, a precious corner stone" (Isa. 28:16), the Rock of Israel, so there is "a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence" (Isa. 8:14); and it will be explained in the Gate of Substitutes. And likewise they stand to guard those who go on the way of a commandment, that they not be harmed by these bands that go out from the third palace that is in the husk, as we shall explain there. In the middle of the palace, within the light Ahadiel of which we spoke, which is in its middle, "as it were a wheel within a wheel" (Ezek. 1:16), stands one palace; and it has four entrances to the four directions of the world; and at each and every entrance ten appointed ones, which are forty in all. These forty take and receive judgment from the Palace of Merit, which is the palace of judgment, as we wrote; and they chastise the soul that needs to be chastised; and it stands there rebuked until the days of its rebuke are fulfilled. And likewise these forty excommunicate everyone from whose mouth goes out obscene speech; and for forty days his prayer does not enter above. And likewise they excommunicate everyone who commits a transgression for which he is liable to excommunication. And ten heralds go out every day in all the firmaments and proclaim and say: "Beware of So-and-so, for he is excommunicated for such-and-such an iniquity"; and all the days of his excommunication his prayer does not enter above, nor his soul at night; and the angels that accompany the man keep apart from him until he returns in teshuvah. And after his return those forty gather and release him, and proclaim concerning him: "So-and-so, the rebuke is released." And in this palace there is one place whose color of light is like the light of burnished gold, and sparkles to the light of the eyes. And in that place are stored away several hosts and camps of angels; and at the four directions of this palace stand several shields, rows upon rows, round about; and the color of their light is like the color of gold. And this place is called the guard chamber of the runners [ta ha-ratzim] (1 Kings 14:28). And the reason is that the angels within this place, the shields, are called chashmalim; and they stand to protect everyone who needs a shield; shields over Israel; and they run to fight with the evil runners that are in the third palace of the husks; for they are runners over against runners: these go out to do good, and those go out to do evil. Of those it is said (Esth. 3:15), "and the city of Shushan was perplexed"; and of these it is said (Esth. 8:15), "and the city of Shushan shouted and was glad"; and this is "the runners went out, being hastened by the king's commandment" (Esth. 8:14). And on account of this the place is called the guard chamber of the runners, because they run to protect Israel with several spears, with several swords full of judgment, by the power of the fourth palace, the Palace of Merit. And when the ofan that stands over the four appointed ones that we mentioned above wishes to enter this place, they enter before the four appointed over the four entrances; and all the shields rise and are all united in one spirit and an upper light; and all of them are called one shield; and the sign: "I am your shield" (Gen. 15:1). Within this palace are twelve ofannim, and their arrangement is within this palace; and they are seraphim in two colors, white, red, compassion and judgment. And these are called windows, because they are appointed to watch over those in sorrow who are made to suffer by human beings; and this is what the verse says (Song 2:9), "he looks forth at the windows." And they stand to watch over those who pray, who come early to be counted among the first ten; and they rise and write them above, and become companions to them; and this is "the companions hearken to your voice; cause me to hear it" (Song 8:13). And they raise the prayer above, up to the entrance of the fourth palace. From these twelve ofannim go out four pillars to the four directions of the world; and their names are Aniel, Azariah, Azriel, Yitriel; and they are called lattices; and of them it is said, "he peers through the lattices" (Song 2:9); because the principal watching is the complete looking forth, and these four are called lattices, which is with a slight watching; and this is the language of "peers." And these four lattices stand to watch over those who occupy themselves with good deeds, and likewise over those who thought thoughts of a commandment, even though it did not come to their hand because they were not able. Aniel stands toward the east. Azariah stands toward the south, to watch over those who comfort the poor, or who grieve over them even though it is not in their power to give them anything; and over all those who go to a matter of a commandment, and those who do kindness with the dead; and this one raises them above and engraves their form there, to make them merit the life of the world to come. Azriel stands toward the north; and he stands to watch over all those who think to do evil or a transgression, and conquered their inclination and did not do it. Yehariel stands toward the west; and he stands to watch over all who occupy themselves with Torah and bring their sons to the study of Torah, and over all those who visit the sick and watch over them, to bring them back in teshuvah before their Owner, so that they be healed. And all these four together stand to watch over all those who give evil counsel; and they raise the thing above and annul that counsel. And under each one of these four angels there are several angels without number. And this palace, when it is united, branch in root and root in source, and when it is united with the lower palaces, it is united and concealed through one pillar that stands in the middle of the palace and rises up to the fourth palace; and this is its longing and its craving and its delight and its completeness. And this palace too is supported on eight pegs, like the preceding palaces. And there are two appointed ones toward the east, and their names are Yehudiah, Azriel; and each one of them is appointed over twelve thousand other appointed ones. And toward the south two others, and their names are Shekhaniel, Azuziah; and each one is appointed over twelve thousand other appointed ones. And these are appointed over the breath of the mouths of the children of the house of their teacher; and from each and every breath he makes one spirit, and it rises to be crowned above; and from it one guardian is made for the sustaining of the world. And toward the north two others, and their names are Azpiel, Katatriha'el; and each one is appointed over twelve thousand other appointed ones. And two appointed ones toward the west, and their names are Asasniah, Ahadiriah; and each one of them is appointed over twelve thousand other appointed ones. And these are appointed to proclaim in all the firmaments concerning all those who take their sons away from study and keep them from their learning; and they proclaim concerning him and say: "Woe to So-and-so, who took his son away from the Torah; woe to him, for he has lost his portion of the world to come." May YHVH the Compassionate save us:

The fourth palace is called the Palace of Merit [היכל זכות, heikhal zekhut]. And this palace stands to guard the ways of the Torah; and in it are judged all the merits and the debts, and all reward and punishment, for all who keep the Torah or who transgress it, God forbid. Within this palace there are four palaces, each different from the other, and all of them together one palace. In this palace there is one light, which is called Zekhuta'el; and after its name it is called the Palace of Merit; and it is what is called El; and here all the judgments of the people of the world are judged; and this is "and El has indignation every day" (Ps. 7:12). And the four palaces mentioned have four entrances, and in them four appointed ones, as we shall explain:

And at the entrance of this palace that includes the four, which is called the Palace of Merit, there is one appointed one, and his name is Sansinia [another version: Sansaniah]. And over this appointed one there is one appointed one on the left side, who takes from him the matters of judgment, to pass it on in the world; and because he takes from him he is called by his name, Sansiniel [another version: Sansaniah]. And when the judgment is concluded within the Palace of Merit, this appointed one who is at the gate stands and proclaims the judgment to those twelve appointed ones who are appointed over twelve gates; and they stand and proclaim all the judgments that are judged in this palace.
