This light of which we spoke, which includes all, which is called Zekhuta'el: from it go out seventy lights; and all of them stand like a round threshing floor, so that they be included with one another, that none be hidden from its fellow; after the manner of the Sanhedrin, who stand like half a round threshing floor, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained. And from these, in their middle, go out two lights, standing to bear witness continually. And the secret of the matter: the seven eyes of YHVH that run to and fro through the whole earth (Zech. 4:10), to which the Geonim related these names: Orpaniel, Tagriel, Danriel, Palmiel, Asimon, Safiel, Boel; and they are those that watch over the matters of human beings. And in them and in their very self every likeness and image and form of all the things that are done in this world is portrayed, whether evil or good. And when they rise above, these two lights look at them and see what is portrayed, and bear witness before the seventy; and they judge the innocent and the guilty, for good or for evil, for merit or for debt. And the two mentioned are the scribes of the judges. These seventy-two lights stand in the middle of the palace; and this is "Your navel is like a round goblet" (Song 7:3). And over against these, on the right side, seventy-two other lights; and on the left side, seventy-two other lights: all of them are found to be two hundred and sixteen lights. And all of them are included in the great light that is called Zekhut-El. And even though there are seventy-two on the right and seventy-two on the left, the principal of the judgments is only through the middle seventy-two; for the matter is known: the seventy-two of the right is a hint in Gedulah, and the seventy-two of the left in Gevurah, and the middle seventy-two, the most inner, in Tiferet, which is the arbiter and decides the judgment; and therefore the principal of the judgment is through the middle ones, and they are the most inner of all. And in the Zohar, Parashat Beshalach (fol. 51b), on the verse "and it journeyed, and it came, and he stretched out" (Exod. 14:19–21), these are his words: "And we have learned: from the side of Chesed seventy-two witnesses; from the side of Gevurah seventy-two scribes; from the side of Tiferet seventy-two colors, to be glorified." Thus far his words.

And we have another way. For behold, in Parashat Pekudei (fol. 251a) he explained that two lights are witnesses, as we explained. In this light, which is called Zekhuta'el, three letters of the name  Y H V  are inscribed; and when these three letters are joined in this palace, then these three letters are portrayed in it. And of them David, peace be upon him, said (Ps. 94:22), "and my God [ve-Elohai] is the rock of my refuge": in this word is hinted El, the name of the palace, and the three letters portrayed within it, which are  Y H V. Afterward another light went out, shining and sparkling to four directions, which are four palaces. And this light brought out three kinds of lights, which are three courts that are divided below to judge the matters of the world: in wealth, in poverty, in sicknesses and in healing, and the like. And the four palaces: two of them for the two kinds of lights that we mentioned above, which are to the right and the left; and the third palace for all those full of eyes, who reckon the matters of the world; and the fourth palace for other scribes, who are under those first, inner ones. These four palaces are included in this palace, which is called the Palace of Merit, after the name of the great light Zekhut-El, as we explained. At each and every entrance of these palaces there is one appointed one. At the first entrance there is one appointed one, and his name is Gezariel; and he is appointed to make known the judgments that have been decreed to the angel appointed in the first palace on the side of impurity. And through this angel the judgments are revealed; and heralds go out and proclaim in all the firmaments, in purity and in impurity. And the manner of the descent of the proclamation is from mouth to mouth and from firmament to firmament, until that decree comes down even into the hand of the birds; and they proclaim it below into the hand of human beings; and this is the wisdom of the chirping of the birds. At the second entrance there is one appointed one, and his name is Dahariel; and he is appointed to bring in the merit of human beings within, so that they be judged on the pan of merit. And when the man is "upon the couch of languishing" (Ps. 41:4), and this angel brings in his merits, and they are found more than his iniquities, and the pan of merit has prevailed, he makes it known to the appointed one who is at the entrance of the third palace, whose name is Pedael; and he proclaims and says, "Deliver him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom" (Job 33:24). And from there the decree descends from rung to rung, down to this world, as we explained above. At the third entrance there is one appointed one, Gadiel by name; and he is toward the left side, appointed over all the debts of human beings and their iniquities; and he brings them to the balance that is at the fourth entrance, as we shall explain. And there they are weighed, these against those, merit against debt. And under the hand of the right appointed one who is at the fourth entrance, as we shall explain, several angels are ready to save the man from the side of the left, if the merits prevail. And if the debts prevail, then several angels under this left appointed one make the things known to several angels of ruin; and they come and take the soul. The fourth entrance: at this entrance there is one appointed one, and his name is Yazniah; and he is the balance in which they weigh debt and merit, as we explained. And under his hand are two appointed ones, one to the right and one to the left: the one on the right, Hariel by name; and the one on the left, Gadovel [another version: Gedudiel] by name. And when debt and merit have been weighed, this one tips to merit and that one tips to debt. And all these powers and lights are included in the great light that is called Zekhut-El. And when they are included in it, one blazing living creature goes out, and its name is Kumiel [another version: Tumiel]. And this living creature stands to watch over the matters of human beings in this world in general. And there are several thousand thousands and myriad myriads full of eyes; and all of them are called "the eyes of YHVH that run to and fro through the whole earth"; and they watch over all the deeds that are done in secret; and likewise they watch over those deeds that are done with a good heart and with good intention, even though they are not in deed as is fitting. And likewise this living creature stands over every request of human beings that they ask, and over all the prayers. For every request is held back in this palace forty days; and every day this living creature goes out and takes that request and sets it before the seventy-two lights; and they judge it. And then that light which is called Zekhut-El examines it as is fitting, whether it is fit to fulfil the request or not. If that prayer has merited in its request, twelve appointed ones go out with it, and each one establishes the fulfilment of the request. Under this living creature are four blazing seraphim, and their names are Harpiel, Barki, Kodshi, Kruma; and these four stand under this living creature to the four directions of the world. And they are appointed to examine those who keep the Sabbath and delight in it as is fitting, as we shall explain with the help of the Name. And these four, when they journey, sparks of fire go out in knop and flower; and from these sparks were made seventy-two ofannim blazing with fire. And when these ofannim journey, the river of fire is made beneath them: "thousand thousands ministered unto" that [river of] fire, "and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him" (Dan. 7:10), from within that fire; and from there go out several thousands of hosts and ofannim. And these four seraphim that we mentioned are those from which the river of fire goes out. Within that river they burn several hosts, several angels, several spirits, several rulers, all the weekdays. And when the Sabbath enters, a herald goes out and calms the fire and its tumults, and the whole world is at rest. And this living creature goes and is raised upon the four seraphim mentioned, and enters within the middle of this palace; and it is called oneg [delight]. And the reason is that on the Sabbath, in this place, all the tables of the children of Israel who keep the Sabbath are arranged; and they are called the children of the King's palace. And thousand thousands stand appointed over these tables; and when this living creature enters with the four seraphim and sees all the tables, all those who stand over them stand and bless them, and all those thousand thousands of thousands answer Amen; and likewise all the seventy lights mentioned bless them. The rule of the matter: all the judgments and all the decrees are judged in this palace, except for three, which are children, life and sustenance; for these do not depend on this palace, which is called Merit, but depend above, on mazal. And even though they do not depend on this palace, nevertheless they judge it in this palace; and if he has merited, they give it to him from above; and the explanation of "they give" is: they command to give; for the giving is only below, as we explained in the preceding gates. And this palace stands under more guard than the other preceding palaces; and it has thirty-two upper pegs, and beneath them five hundred thousand other appointed ones; and over all of them four appointed ones who are over the thirty-two; and the names of the four: Chasdiel, Kesiriah, Kedumiah, Dahariel. And these four are appointed over all the judgments that have been judged and were not given to be written; and all come to ask of the mouth of these appointed ones. And the thirty-two appointed ones are appointed over all those who fix times for Torah; and all of them are appointed to punish all those who were able to occupy themselves in the Torah and did not occupy themselves:

The fifth palace is called the Palace of Love [היכל אהבה, heikhal ahavah]. And it is the palace on which depend the sustenance and the life of the other palaces that are beneath it. And in this palace there is one entrance, and in it one appointed one, and his name is Sanegoriah; and he stands to plead in defence [sanegoria] of Israel, so that the side of the left should not rule over them. In this palace stands one light included of four lights of four colors: white, black, green and red. And this spirit, which is included of all of them, is called Suriah, the prince of all the hosts that are beneath it; and all the upper keys are handed over into his hand; and he closes and opens; and all the secrets of his Master are handed over into his hand. And in it all the lights that are beneath it are included three times every day, and are nourished from it. And because in it are stored away all the treasures and secrets of the Master of the worlds, therefore it is called Love, as it is written (Song 7:13), "there will I give you my love"; which is the secret of the cleaving of every one who cleaves. And therefore in it is all the upper guarding; and therefore it is called the Guardian of Israel, the Guardian of the covenant; because here all the upper secrets are guarded and stored away; and from here go out paths and ways to all those below it, to shine with its light. And these four colors of lights of which we spoke: when white is united with red, black with green, afterward black with white, one living creature is made from them, its likeness embroidered in the form of a man, which includes all the forms; and it is called Zohar [Radiance]. And of it it is said (Ezek. 10:20), "This is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel." And from it go out four pillars, which are great living creatures over those that are below. The first is called ofan; and they are two; for within the ofan another ofan is made within it; and when it sparkles, the other sparkles within it; and of this it is said (Ezek. 1:16; 10:10), "as it were a wheel within a wheel." And afterward two others, also one within the other, included together like the first ones; and the four sparkle together to the four directions of the world, and all of them are one; and of them it is said, "as it were a wheel within a wheel." The light of which we spoke above, which is included in four colors, includes two spirits, lights: the one to the right, and it is this one that brought out the living creature of which we spoke; and one to the left (it includes); and it sparkles two lights, which are four; and they turn about in colors; and this is "the flame of the sword that turned every way" (Gen. 3:24), as we shall explain. And from between these two lights seraphim go out; and it holds them and makes them blaze. By the power of this flame that turns about it brought out one living creature, standing on four pillars, as the right one brought out; and the four, two on the right and two on the left. And when the great light enters within these and sparkles in them, two lights go out from them and sparkle outside this palace, and turn about into several matters: sometimes males and sometimes females, sometimes spirits, sometimes angels; and they are the messengers of judgment in the world; and so they are on the left side of this palace. And from this palace go out all the souls that are destined to enter bodies in this world. And this palace has never stood empty since the day the world was created; and it receives all the souls that are bestowed from Binah; and it is called guf [body]. And of this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yevamot 62a): "The son of David does not come until all the souls in the guf are finished." And when the King Messiah comes, this palace will be aroused above, and another palace below this palace; and of them it is said (Song 4:5; 7:4), "Your two breasts are like two fawns." For the great light and the first living creature of which we spoke bring out two lights included together, bound to one another; and they are called El Shaddai. And the reason that it is called Shaddai is because it goes out from between these breasts [shadayim]. And further, for this El receives from this place all that compassion which is fit for the sustenance and life of those lower ones that are in the Palace of Merit, which are from the side of the right; and likewise for all those lower ones that are called the pegs of the Tabernacle. And for the reason that it suffices [maspik] sustenance for them it is called El Shaddai: El its name, as we explained in the fourth palace; and Shaddai because of the upper breasts; and the reason is that it suffices milk from the breasts for all those lower ones. And also from this great light goes out one right living creature; and it is over the left one, which turns into a male; and it is appointed over the world at a time when there is famine and destruction, to guard the righteous and the good, so that they not die of famine; and it sustains their heart, so that the food not be spoiled in their bowels by the two powers of impurity that are called Destruction [Shod] and Famine [Kafan], as their matter is written in the Gate of the Palaces of the Substitutes, with the help of the Name. And this is "At destruction and famine you shall laugh" (Job 5:22). In this palace there are two lights; each one stands over thousand thousands of thousands and myriad myriads, which are called vines; and thousand and myriad myriads [which are called pomegranates]; and all of them stand in love. And these are the ones who bring love between Israel and their Father in heaven; and it is by their mentioning the piety that Israel does below. And when they arouse the love from below, then this palace is filled with several good things, with several mercies, with several compassions. And these stand in attendance over those who give over their souls in love for the unification of their Owner; and the kindness that human beings do, all of it rises here, and from there they rise and are crowned before the Holy One, blessed be He. And this palace has three hundred and sixty-five pegs, as the number of the days of the solar year; and above them all four pegs, the highest of all; and their names are Karshiha'el, Sartiha'el, Asiriah, Kadmiel. And these are appointed to gladden the world on the eve of the Sabbath: when the [additional] soul is added in Israel, these go out with it and remove from all Israel all agitation and all worry and all sadness, and gladden them with joy; and these are the gladdeners of the world. And those that are under the four appointed ones [are appointed] to remove the judgment from those who sit in Gehinnom. And therefore all the pegs that are in the [fifth] palace are masters of joy. Thus far:

The sixth palace is called the Palace of Will [היכל רצון, heikhal ratzon], for the reason that on it depends the time of favour [et ratzon] and good heart for every thing and for every request and for every prayer. And the reason is that in it is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, as we shall write with the help of the Rock and His salvation. And therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, departed in it at a time of favour; for he died by a kiss, which is the kiss of a wife with her husband. And in this palace there are six entrances, for the six extremities: four for the four directions of the world, and above and below. And one great appointed one is appointed over all of them, and his name is Raziel; and all the mysteries of the secrets of the Torah are under his hand. And these entrances stand to be revealed; for when they are revealed, all the palaces are revealed, and all the lights and all the spirits are revealed, when the gates of will are opened. In this palace were handed over the souls of Rabbi Akiva and his companions, and all those killed for the love of their Owner, who do not enter the river of fire; which is not so with the other souls, as we explained. And this palace brings out twelve lights, for the reason that it is included of six lower palaces and of six upper ones. And when the twelve lights rise and sparkle they bring out four living creatures; and all of them are included in the twelve, after the manner of the standards of the wilderness, which are four and are divided into twelve, each one into three. The four mentioned are all included as one, like this nut, which is divided into four heads and they are included as one. And for this reason this palace is called the Garden of Nuts; and this is "I went down into the garden of nuts" (Song 6:11): that the Holy One, blessed be He, delights with the righteous in the union of Tiferet and Malkhut. The four that are for the four directions: the first, toward the south, is the right; and it is called Michael. This prince is the guardian of Israel, who pleads in their defence, that they be saved from the accusation of the husks. And when the Temple was destroyed and the hand of the evildoers prevailed, it is said of this light, "He has drawn back His right hand" (Lam. 2:3); and it draws nourishment from the side of Chesed. On the side of the north stands the second light; and it stands to take judgment from the side of the fourth palace, the Palace of Merit, and gives the judgment to the angel appointed over the entrance, so that he give it to the angels that stand on the side of impurity; for it draws nourishment from the side of Gevurah, and therefore it is called Gabriel. And sometimes he himself judges the man, and he is not handed over to the husks; for this are the sufferings of love. And the reason is that it is included from the side of Chesed, and therefore it is called El. And therefore every blow that comes from this side is near to being healed; for blow and healing are held in one another. And this angel too is appointed over conception: that is to say, he takes the drop and raises it above, and the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees upon it, wise or foolish, etc. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 11a), and these are his words: "For we have learned: at the hour when the body of a righteous one is born in this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, calls Gabriel; and he takes that soul that is in the Garden and brings it down to this body of the righteous one that is born in this world; and he is appointed over it and guards it. And if you say: that angel who is appointed over the spirits of the righteous, his name is Lailah [Night], and you say that he is Gabriel? So it is certainly, because he comes from the side of the left; and everyone who comes from the side of the left is so called." Thus far his words.

And the explanation: everything that is bestowed from judgment is called night; and the reason is that the attribute of night is the attribute of judgment. And Lailah in the small reckoning comes to [the same as] Gavri'el:

And on the side of the east stands the third light; and it draws nourishment from the side of Tiferet; and it takes hold of and includes these two lights, after the manner of the sefirah. And it is the prince of healing; and it brings to remembrance for healing all those sick who have been forgotten in their sicknesses; and it raises their remembrance above; and on account of this it is called Raphael. And this healing is healings of judgment, with constraint; for it draws healing from the side of the right and constraint from the side of the left; and therefore the healing from this side comes to the sick with great constraint. And even though sometimes the name Raphael is related to Malkhut and to the west, there is no wonder; for it is also there, in the secret of Tiferet in Malkhut and Malkhut in Tiferet. And nevertheless most of the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the holy book agree that this name is in Tiferet, in the east, as we explained. On the side of the west there is one light, and its name is Nuriel; and he himself is Uriel. And he is the messenger of the three lights that we mentioned; for he is over against Malkhut, which is included of the three upper ones. And when she draws nourishment from the side of the right, Chesed, he is called Uriel, which is from the language of or [light]; for the language of light is toward the right, as we explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And when she draws nourishment from the left, Gevurah, he is called Nuriel, from the language of nur, burning. And the matter of this angel is expounded in the Zohar, Parashat Yitro (fol. 78a), and these are his words: "In the third month, over which Uriel the great appointed one rules, and three hundred and sixty-five myriad camps with him, as the reckoning of the days of the year. And all of them have three hundred and sixty-five keys of lights from that light that goes out from within the upper, inner chashmal, stored away and closed, on which the mysteries of the upper holy letters of the holy Name depend. And it is the secret of 'a plain man,' the master of the house, 'the man of God.' Tam [plain]: for there is the end and the knot of the tefillin; and Jacob was 'a plain man.' And in his likeness stands the secret of the inner, upper chashmal, concealed and stored away; and it takes all the upper closed lights, and they go out from it. And all these camps take those keys of that light that goes out from within the chashmal. And that light is included in two lights, and they are one. The first light is a white light, over which the eye has no power; and this is the light that is stored away for the righteous, as it is written, 'Light is sown for the righteous,' etc. (Ps. 97:11). The second light is a light that sparkles and blazes in a red colour. And the two lights are included as one and became one. And this Uriel, the great appointed one, and all those camps take that light; and because it is included of two, it is called Twins [Te'omim]. And therefore that constellation rules in it which is called, in its secret, Twins; and in it the Torah was given. And from here rungs are drawn below, until they rise in names to conduct the world." Thus far his words.

And see in Parashat Tzav (fol. 32b), and these are his words: "Come and see: it is written, 'And there came forth fire from before YHVH and consumed upon the altar the burnt offering,' etc. (Lev. 9:24): this is Uriel, who descends in the appearance of fire, in a flame, until he descends to the altar to receive the gift; and he is seen as a great lion crouching upon the offering." Thus far his words.

And in Parashat (Beha'alotekha, fol. 154) great matters are expounded in the Zohar concerning these four angels; and from there it appears that the four living creatures that are in Ezekiel are also in them; and because of the length of the matter we shall not copy them. And let us return to his words in Parashat Pekudei. And the four lights that we mentioned are over against the four elements; and from these the elements were separated: of them angels of fire, from the side of Gabriel; of them angels of air, from the side of Raphael; of them angels of earth, from the side of Uriel; of them angels of water, from the side of Michael. And these four are united, and beneath them eight, which are twelve, as we explained. This palace is included of all the lower ones, and all of them are included in it. And this palace has a hundred pegs toward the right side, and over them two upper appointed ones, and their names are Malkhiel, Shema'iha'el; and toward the left a hundred, and over them two other appointed ones, and their names are Masasraniah, Tzaftzaniah. And they are appointed, at the time that the time of the righteous one arrives to depart from the world, to be present there, so that his soul go out by a kiss, and that it not be "like a hair from the mouth of the gullet," as is explained in Tractate Berakhot (fol. 8a). And all the lower palaces crave this palace; and they are united one within another, [within] the Pavement of Sapphire, within the Very Heaven, within the Palace of Brightness, and so all of them. And this is all their delight and all their cravings and their completeness; for by this they are united in their root. And the matter of this union is through the prayer, when it is as is fitting, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains there:

The seventh palace is called the Holy of Holies [קדש הקדשים, kodesh ha-kodashim]. In this palace there is no image and nothing grasped; but it is a thing concealed and exalted; and it is what draws near to the Emanation. And within this palace a veil is spread out, to divide between the holy place and the Holy of Holies; and there, within the veil, are two cherubim. And on the matter of the heavenly curtain [pargod] that is spread out it is said in Parashat Beshalach (fol. 58a), and these are his words: "For we have learned: Sandalfon is higher than all his other companions by five hundred years; and he stands behind the heavenly curtain of his Master and ties crowns for Him from the requests of the prayer of Israel. And at the hour that that crown reaches the head of the Holy King, He receives the prayers of Israel; and all the hosts and multitudes tremble and roar and say, 'Blessed be the glory of YHVH from the place of the house of His Shekhinah.'" Thus far his words.

And at first sight it is understood that Sandalfon is in the palace that is called the Holy of Holies, and the heavenly curtain mentioned here is the veil of which we spoke; and so it appears from the words of the Geonim. And within the veil, there, within the Holy of Holies, there is the encampment of the Shekhinah and the beginning of the receiving of the effluence from the upper Throne, which is Beriah, as we wrote. And this palace receives the holy souls from Binah: those new souls that are destined to be renewed in the world in the time of the Messiah, with the help of the Name. Thus far the copying of the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, from Parashat Pekudei on the matter of the palaces has reached:

And we have found other words on the matter of the palaces by the Geonim, Rav Natronai Gaon and Rav Nachshon, etc., and these are their words: "We have received that there are seven palaces in the firmament of Vilon [Curtain]. In the first palace, Kenesiel; and his palace is called the Assembly of the Houses; and there the holy angels pray three times every day. In the second palace, Kavtziel, who is destined to gather the congregation of Israel from exile. In the third palace, Yofiel: for the souls of the children who died from six years old to seven years old learn and complete [their study] before him; and the Shekhinah embraces them; and their souls rise in the coupling of the lower Shekhinah up to the place of the High Priest, and are offered as an offering upon the altar of the upper Shekhinah. In the fourth palace, Tahariel: he purifies and makes radiant the souls that were defiled in the bodies of the wicked; and they wash and immerse in the waters of the stones of pure marble of Rabbi Akiva and his companions, which are the radiances of the four holy living creatures at the hour that they embrace and draw near to one another for the service of the upper Master; and this is 'that touched one another' (Ezek. 3:13). In the fifth palace, Nuriel: the river of fire goes out from before him, from the fire and from the light of the angels; for there sparks of light are renewed, which say praise for that for which they were created, and are concealed. And this is the mystery of mysteries: that they draw near, afterward they separate (a word is missing) times, which are thirty; and they chirp from radiance to radiance and air, until they reach the radiance of their Master, the crown of the upper Kingdom; and they are the souls of the holy prophets. And far be it from us and from our companions to sum up in the words of the God of heaven, and to reveal what is not possible, and what the masters, our predecessors, of blessed memory, did not permit us. In the sixth palace, Enoch, who was clothed in a garment of the radiance of light, and changed his name and his body; and his name is Metatron, like the name of his Master, and his seal and his body. And he is the great one in the sixth palace; and he purifies all the souls that rise from the earth to the height of the firmament; and they are refined and clothed and stripped of every kind of defilement of the bodies, and clothed in the radiances of bodies of horns [of light], which are stored away and portrayed in the radiance of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is the Life of the Worlds; from where the souls fly from world to world, up to the great world; it is the world whose radiance shines for six worlds; where the souls of the bodies are pampered and in bliss, as they were decreed from there at that hour when they were created. And we have no permission to reveal words and mysteries that are the hidden things of the world. In the seventh palace, Sandalfon, the firm binding, the word of the work of His might in the heavens to the earth; and between two great men, rulers, in the form of embryos in their mothers' wombs. And he it is who gives to all of them the spirit of life; and he it is who kills the creatures of the earth with a drawn sword of fire that is not blown; and all the creatures of the earth, and all who rule in the air of the firmament, are under his dominion. And in his hands is the garment of light of the King, which clothes the prophets at the time that they prophesy; and their spirits are from the radiance of his spirit, and their bodies are conducted in his body. And he is the mouth, and speaks to the spirit in their lips; and his mouth and his tongue Gabriel, the master of prophecy, arranges, as he was commanded (by the Master) [from the Master] of the world and the Shekhinah of Israel." Thus far the words of the order of the Shimmusha Rabba, the order of the palaces. Thus far.

And there is no doubt that these palaces are the very palaces that we explained in the preceding chapters. And even though in some things, or most of them, it is understood that they disagree with Rashbi, peace be upon him, nevertheless all of them said one thing; except that Rashbi, peace be upon him, told of the matter of the lights, which are like a soul to the palaces, and they explained the matter of the palaces themselves. And close to this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, and especially in Parashat Terumah, as we shall write in a chapter by itself, with the help of the Name:

Further, Rashbi told us on the matter of these palaces in general, and he related to them the name medorin [dwellings]; and it is all one matter, palace and dwelling. And these are his words in Parashat Terumah: "There are seven dwellings above, rung over rung; and in all the dwellings there are upper angels, these over those. So too below. And all is held one in another, so that all be one. There are seven dwellings above, and this upper Land holds them, and all of them stand in it. And in all of them stands the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He: rungs separated from one another, and places separated from one another."

"The first dwelling is a place of darkness, without light; and it is prepared for the dwellings of spirits and storms and strong whirlwinds, which are not seen; and there is in them neither light nor darkness nor likeness at all. And there they have no knowledge of it at all; for there is no form in it at all, within the whole of the Throne. And over that place one angel is appointed, Tahariel by name; and with him seventy appointed ones, flying, and they are wiped out by the flashes of sparks that are over them, and do not endure, and are not seen and not found. And when morning comes, all of them are renewed and do not endure; when they reach this place they are lost and not found, and enter into one hollow of the abyss and are not seen. When night falls they are wiped out by those sparks, until morning comes."

"The second dwelling is a place that is more lit, and it is dark, but not dark like that first one. And it is prepared for the dwellings of angels who are appointed over the deeds of human beings, and to lead them astray in that evil way in which they go. And that place is seen more than the first; and these angels have nearness to human beings, and take pleasure in the savour and the spice from below, to rise with benefit and to shine more. And over them is one appointed one, Kedumiel by name. And these open song and are silenced and go away and are not seen, until Israel below open and say song; then they stand in their places and are seen and shine more. And three times a day they sanctify the sanctification. And when Israel occupy themselves in the Torah, all of them fly and bear witness above, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has pity on them."

"The third dwelling is a place of sparks and smoke. And there is the flowing of the river of fire that flows and goes out, which is the place of burning of the souls of the wicked; from there fire descends upon the heads of the wicked; and there are the angels of ruin that drive them. And from there is found the accuser against Israel at times, to lead them astray, except at the time when they take a remedy to push him away. And one appointed one is over them, from the side of the left; all of them from the side of darkness, as it is said, 'and darkness was upon the face of the deep' (Gen. 1:2). And the guilty Samael is found there."

"The fourth dwelling is a place that is lit; and there is light for the upper angels that are on the side of the right; and they open song and conclude. And they do not go to be removed like those first ones, who open song and are burned and removed in burning fire, and return and are renewed as before. And these stand in their places and are not removed; and these are the angels of compassion, who never change. And of them it is written (Ps. 104:4), 'Who makes His angels spirits,' etc. And these do missions in the world, and are not seen by human beings except in a vision, or on another side, with great understanding. And one angel is appointed over them, Pedael by name; and in him are opened the keys of compassion for those who stand toward their Master; and they open gates to pass through their prayers and their requests."

"The fifth dwelling is a dwelling that shines with a light more than all the first ones. And there are angels in it: of them fire and of them water; at times they are found in compassion and at times they are found in judgment; these on this side and those on that side; at times these shine and those are dark. These are appointed to sing to their Master: these at midnight, and those when the light rises. And one appointed one is over them, Kedushiel by name. When the night is divided and the north wind is aroused, and the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to delight with the righteous in the Garden of Eden, then the north wind strikes and reaches those who are appointed at midnight to sing; and all of them sing and open song. And when morning comes and the blackness of morning is joined with the light, then all the others say song; and all the stars of the firmament and all the other angels below help them; as it is said (Job 38:7), 'When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy'; until Israel take up the song and the praise after them."

"The sixth dwelling is an upper dwelling, near to the Kingdom of Heaven. And in it are ships and rivers and streams that divide from the sea, and several fishes that swarm to the four sides of the world. And over them, appointed presidents; and one appointed one over them, and Uriel is his name; and he is appointed over all these lower ones. And all of them journey at hours and moments, when the ships journey to this side and to that side. When the ships journey toward the south, the appointed one who stands on that side is Michael, who comes from the right. And when the ships journey toward the north, the appointed one who stands over them on that side is Gabriel, who comes from the side of the left. And when the ships journey toward the east, behold, there the appointed one who stands over them on this side, Raphael [another version: Uriel] is his name; and he is to the right. And when the ships journey toward the west, the appointed one who stands over them on this side, Uriel [another version: Raphael] is his name; and that one is behind."

"The seventh dwelling is the dwelling above all. And there are found only the souls of the righteous, who there are in bliss in the upper radiance and in bliss amid upper luxuries and blisses. And there are found only those righteous ones, and the treasuries of peace and blessing and free gift. All of it is after the upper pattern, and behold, the companions have said it."

"So it is for the land below, in seven dwellings; and all of them after the upper pattern. And in all of them there are kinds in the appearance of human beings; and all of them thank and praise the Holy One, blessed be He. And there is none who knows to serve Him as is fitting like those in the upper dwelling; and they see His glory, to serve Him as is fitting and to praise Him and to make His glory known. And this upper world, which is Tevel, does not stand in its existence except for the sake of the righteous, who are holy bodies. As above that seventh dwelling stands only for the souls of the righteous, so too this seventh dwelling below stands only for the bodies of the righteous, so that all be one, this after the pattern of that." Thus far his words:

And behold, we have already said above that there is no wonder that these palaces are not like those. For the palaces mentioned above are the inwardness of the palace and the inner spirit; and this is the palace itself. And as for his counting the first three palaces as where the outer ones are, so it is; for we have already explained in chapters 3 and 4 that the angels stand and proclaim to the outer ones and make it known to human beings; and this is because of their nearness; for "round about the Tabernacle they shall encamp" (Num. 1:50), and "the wicked walk on every side" (Ps. 12:9); and therefore these are near to them, intermediaries between holiness and impurity, crushed [between them]. And as for his saying that Samael is in the third palace, this is no wonder; for they have already told us that before the sin of the first Adam, Samael was one of the seraphim with six wings, and he rebelled against his Master, until his day comes, the day of his visitation; "for it will surely come, it will not delay" (Hab. 2:3). And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 21, fol. 42a) that the palaces are seven in seven, these a brain to those, as we shall explain with the help of Heaven:

And after we have already written all that is inscribed in the writing of truth, behold, it is fitting for us to inquire into the matter of these palaces: what their matter is, whether Atzilut or Beriah or Yetzirah or Asiyah; and what their matter is; and why their matter comes to seven and not ten, as the number of the sefirot; for all the things that are beneath the sefirot are from ten to ten. And after the inquiry into this matter we say that it is impossible that they be Atzilut, for several reasons. First, because it is not fitting that in Atzilut the matter of the angels be related; and behold, in the palaces there are angels themselves, as is proved from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that we copied in the preceding chapters. And for this reason too it is not related to Beriah, which is the established Throne, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 2, with the help of Heaven. Second, because Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Pekudei (fol. 245a) explained on the matter of the palaces that the husk round about is near to the first palace; and these are his words: "The first palace is the beginning within the faith; this is the beginning of the secret of the faith, and in the rungs of the vision of the faith. The prophets of truth would see from within this, the mirror that does not shine. And because this is the beginning of the faith, it is written (Hos. 1:2), 'The beginning of the word of YHVH by Hosea'; for he saw from within the rung that is the beginning of all the rungs, to rise above, and the end of all the rungs, to descend below. And because Hosea saw from within this beginning, the end of all the rungs, he needed to take this wife of harlotry; because Israel had taken hold and been drawn from there downward, to that place which is called the wife of harlotry; because they left and did not cleave to that woman of valour. And he saw from there all those palaces that are on the side of impurity. For they have palaces that are impure; all of them defile whoever cleaves to them. And therefore it is written, 'Take to yourself a wife of harlotry and children of harlotry.' And did a true prophet need this? Rather, because it is forbidden for a man to enter those palaces, lest he be drawn after them, as Noah did, as it is written (Gen. 9:21), 'And he drank of the wine and was drunken, and he was uncovered within his tent.' And Hosea feared to look into those palaces in which Israel were defiled and to which they cleaved, until He said to him, 'Take to yourself a wife of harlotry and children of harlotry'; and it is written, 'So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim'; to know in what they had cleaved and been defiled, and had left the secret of the faith for the sake of a strange god. And therefore he saw from within this palace, the beginning of all the rungs. This palace is the beginning of all, to rise in the rungs." Thus far his words.

Behold, it is understood from this saying explicitly that this palace is the head and beginning of holiness [from below to above] and the end of holiness from above to below; and from it downward is the husk. And therefore Hosea descended to this place, to look at what place Israel were defiled in; and there is no other end to holiness, so that he could descend to it to look in it at the rungs of impurity. And it is known that the husk is round about the world of Metatron; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained explicitly, and as is written in the Gate of Substitutes, with the help of Heaven. And when we say that impure ones entered the palace, it is specifically in the world of the angels, the world of Metatron, as is written there, with the help of the Name. And apart from this, we have a saying that shows explicitly that the palaces are beneath the Throne; and these are his words (in Tikkun 21, fol. 43b): "Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: Father, behold, there are seven seas, and the upper sea is over all of them; and of them it is said, 'for they shall suck the abundance of the seas' (Deut. 33:19). From whom do they suck? He said to him: My son, they are seven in seven, poured out [mutzakot]. And so there are seven firmaments, etc. And so there are seven lands, seven in seven; and their heads are two; and the secret of the matter: 'two and two, seven and seven' (Gen. 7:2–3); and all of them male and female; and above, one, concealed and stored away. And so there are seven thrones, seven in seven; seven palaces, seven in seven; and so the appointed ones are seven in seven." Thus far his words.

And behold, Rabbi Eleazar craved to know the order of the manifestation of the world from its beginning to its end, in brief. And for this he asked: for it is known that the sefirot are called seas, and they are seven; and the upper sea, which is Binah, which is also related by the name sea; but from her upward it is related only as source and spring, which is subtle and concealed; but "sea," which shows spreading out, is not related. And the verse says, "for they shall suck the abundance of the seas": the intent, that the seas suck effluence; and from whom do they suck? For they themselves are the sources of the effluence, and the language of sucking does not belong to them. And for this Rashbi, peace be upon him, answered that there are seven upper seas and seven lower seas, and the lower ones suck from the upper ones. And there is no doubt that the upper ones are the very self of Binah, which is the upper sea, included of seven; and seven lower seas suck from her. Or we may explain that the sefirot themselves are the seven upper seas, and the seven sefirot that are in Malkhut are the seven lower seas; and the upper ones are poured out into the lower ones. And he said the language "seven in seven, poured out," the language of the verse, to prove it from the verse (Zech. 4:2) that said, "seven and seven pipes to the lamps, which are upon the top thereof." And likewise they are related by the name firmaments from the side of Tiferet, and likewise they are related by the name lands from the side of Malkhut; and all of them are seven in seven, as he goes on to explain. And afterward he said that as is the order of the sefirot, so is the order of Beriah, which is the Throne of Glory, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 3, with the help of Heaven; and they are seven thrones poured out into seven; and all of them are included in the name Throne of Glory. And so is the way of Yetzirah; and this is "seven palaces, seven in seven"; and their matter is that they are seven within seven, as we explained, for these are spirits to those, these suck from those, as is explained in the previous chapter. And he says further that so is the way of Asiyah; and this is "the appointed ones are seven in seven," as we explained in the Gate of ABYA. Further, Rashbi explicitly explained (in the Zohar, Bereshit, fol. 41b), on the matter of the palaces, that from them is the drawing of the seven planets. And these are his words, speaking of the Palace of the Pavement of Sapphire, which is the first palace: "Beneath this palace hosts spread out outside, to several sides of the lower firmaments, until they reach the star of Saturn [Shabbetai]; all of them look to this palace; from there are nourished all those that are in this palace; all of them look to that spirit," etc. And of the Palace of the Very Heaven (there, fol. 42b) he said, and these are his words: "And so several hosts and camps that descend below and are mixed with the lower ones, until they reach the star of Jupiter [Tzedek]; and there are several appointed over the world." And of the Palace of Brightness (there, fol. 43a) he said, these are his words: "In this place there hang on four sides six hundred thousand myriads of shields of gold, for each and every side. And likewise below them, rows surrounding; and those rows and all these shields are all makers of war, swords and spears, outside, in all those messengers of judgment of the world, until they reach, rung by rung, the star of Mars [Ma'adim]," etc. And of the Palace of Merit (there, fol. 44a) he said, and these are his words: "And from within these heralds all the winged ones take up the word, until the word is made known to the firmament of the sun [Chamah]." And of the Palace of Love (there, fol. 44b) he said: "of them pomegranates; until several hosts reach outside, up to that star which is called Venus [Nogah]." And of the Palace of Will and of the Palace of the Holy of Holies he revealed nothing; and it is possible that they are drawn from them to the star of Mercury [Kokhav] and the Moon [Levanah]; and he was brief in the matter. And as for his speaking of them from below to above, it is because they are like a seal that is reversed from Yetzirah to Asiyah. Or it is possible that Saturn is "the black dross," over against the husk that prevails in it, as he explained in the Tikkunim; and therefore its drawing is from the first palace, where the cleaving of the husk is, as we explained. However it may be, behold, he taught that the seven planets, ShTzaM ChaNKaL [Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon], draw from the palaces according to the order of the rungs that descend one from another, down to the stars in their spheres. He taught explicitly that there is nothing between these and those except that this is Yetzirah and that is Asiyah; and he wished to reveal the order of the drawing of Asiyah from Yetzirah. And as for what he wrote in Parashat Pekudei and in Parashat Bereshit, that this is the completeness of the [prayer of] receiving, to unite these palaces, and they are "the seven maidens, who were meet to be given her" (Esth. 2:9): there is no wonder from this at all; for on the contrary, from there is a proof, to the credit of the inquirer, of what we explained on the matter of Yetzirah in the Gate of ABYA. And there we said that Yetzirah is nothing but ten rungs of the angels that are included in the name Metatron in the six weekdays. However, the ten sefirot of Yetzirah are the branches of the sefirot that spread out with the Shekhinah, which are called by the name Yetzirah; and therefore there is need of the union, to unite the branches to their sources. And therefore it is not the whole substance of the palaces that is united, but the pure light that is within each and every one of them. And because they are branches spreading out in Metatron, who is called na'ar [youth], therefore these branches are called maidens [ne'arot]; and these are "the seven maidens, who were meet to be given her, out of the king's house"; for they spread out from the upper sefirot with the Shekhinah into the na'ar, and are clothed there. And then the Shekhinah too is called na'arah; and sometimes she is called lacking the Heh, in the secret of na'ar. And of this it is said (Ps. 103:5), "your youth [ne'urayekhi] is renewed like the eagle's"; as these matters are explained in the Zohar in many places. And because the branches that spread out are included in the six weekdays, as is proved in the Tikkunim; therefore on the Sabbath day, which is Malkhut, she has no palace at all. For the Palace of the Pavement of Sapphire is in Yesod; and nevertheless Yesod is not found without the Shekhinah, so as not to separate; and that is the Heh of "the sixth day" (Gen. 1:31), which is Yesod and Malkhut united. And therefore in the Palace of the Pavement of Sapphire male and female are included: sapphire male, pavement female, as is explained in chapter 1. And the Palace of the Very Heaven is over against Hod; and the Palace of Brightness over against Netzach; and the Palace of Merit over against Gevurah; and the Palace of Love over against Chesed; and the Palace of Will over against Tiferet; for so it is above them all, certainly seventh, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation. And the Palace of the Holy of Holies is concealed, over against the three first ones. And all of them are ten branches spreading out above; the explanation, the rungs of the angels that are included in the seven palaces mentioned. And this is the matter of the order and the relation that the palaces have to the sefirot. However, from the preceding sayings it is understood that the rung of the souls of the righteous is more praiseworthy than the rung of the angels, especially from the saying that we copied in chapter 8. And to understand the matter well we shall devote a chapter to it by itself:

What is intended in this chapter is to consider the matter of the angels well, and the reason for the rising of the soul above them. And the matter is that all the things in the heavens above and on the earth beneath were all emanated from a high place; and therefore the pious were careful not to speak in disparagement of any one of the creatures. And the matter is that the four upper elements are: Gedulah, the element of water; Gevurah, the element of fire; Tiferet, the element of air; Malkhut, the element of earth. And they are united in a true and strong union, as is written in the preceding gates.

And behold, through these four upper, emanated, subtle elements, the four elements that are in the order of Atzilut and Beriah and Yetzirah and Asiyah came into being, rung after rung, from cause to effect: from Atzilut to Beriah, and from Beriah to Yetzirah, and from Yetzirah to Asiyah.

And behold, all these four rungs are in each and every one of the rungs themselves: for in Atzilut itself there are ABYA, and all of them are Atzilut; and in Beriah itself there are ABYA, and all of them are Beriah; and so for all the rungs. And this matter is likened to the refiner of silver, who separates each and every kind by itself into four kinds. The first is clean silver, in which there is no dross at all; and the second, silver that descends one rung below the clean silver; and the third, silver in which there is about half dross; and the fourth, silver that is mostly dross. And it is impossible for the clean silver to be entirely silver, with no dross in it at all (equally); rather, necessarily there are also in it four parts, related to the measure of the purity of the silver, as the measure of the first four parts themselves. The example: clean silver that cannot be cleaned further, and this is a small part of the part of the silver; and a second part, and it is clean silver, but not like the first part; for because of the cleanness of the preceding silver the name "clean" is not related to it entirely; and so one makes a further third part, and it is clean without qualification, and not like the second; the fourth, the silver in which there is a little admixture of dross, so that it is not reckoned as anything. And likewise we can divide four divisions in the second, and likewise in the third, and likewise in the fourth. It is found likewise in ABYA: for the Asiyah that is in Atzilut is head to the Atzilut that is in Beriah; and the Asiyah that is in Beriah is head to the Atzilut that is in Yetzirah; and the Asiyah that is in Yetzirah is head to the Atzilut that is in Asiyah. And from the four chains of descent of these rungs all the worlds descended: from Atzilut to Beriah, from Beriah to the palaces, from the palaces to the husks, from the husks to the manifestation of the firmaments, which are the constellations, and from them to these thick and composite elements, as they are before our eyes.

And behold, it is found that Atzilut is root to Beriah, and Beriah root to Yetzirah, and Yetzirah root to Asiyah. And likewise it is found that this world draws from the side of the husk; they are the princes and their impure attendants; for the seventy princes are not so pure. And the princes are from Yetzirah; they are the angels; and the seventy princes are intermediaries between the constellations and the chariots. And the thrones are from the sefirot, and the sefirot from the Self of the Ein Sof that spreads out and gives them life, as we explained. It is found according to this that the four elements of the firmaments are themselves those of Yetzirah, and so up to the upper ones. However, because of the chain of descent they became thick and revealed; for according to their distance from their source, so they became thick and revealed. And according to this there is nothing in the world upon which effluence and light are not bestowed from above; except that that effluence, according to its descending from the back parts, which are the front to the other lower rungs, so it becomes thick and revealed and corporeal, from rung to rung, as is fitting to that turbid matter; until you will not find in this world anything in which there is not some spirituality and life, according to the measure of its body and its matter, according to the rungs that it is distant from the source and quarry of all things.

And behold, when the thick matter is raised to the manifestation of nearness to the subtle matter that is above it, behold, the measure of the light of that superior matter shines in it. The example is a great lamp burning in the middle of the palace hall; and because of the greatness of the hall it does not shine to the corners of the hall at the far ends, except a little light, so that a man does not see his fellow. And the more a man draws near to the lamp, it shines a fairer and stronger light, until one who reaches within its four cubits, his eyes are dimmed by the greatness of its light. So is the matter here: for when the things are distant from their partition and their source, they become thick and corporeal, and are found turbid, coarse to the utmost coarseness, like this earth; that is to say, the element of earth, which does not move, and from its place does not depart. Which is not so with water; because earth is last in rung, and the water over it is a higher rung, drawing nearer earlier. And likewise over them the element of air, in which there is somewhat more movement and disposition than in the element of water. And all the more the element of fire, in which there is more and more life; and we learn from the little element of fire that we have, that it does not rest and is not still until it rises to its element.

Behold, even the elements, which are dead lumps, as it appears, have a superiority each over its fellow, according to the measure of the light of the upper life that flows upon it. And likewise the order of the rising of the composites one over another: over the inanimate is the vegetative, and over the vegetative the animal, and over the animal the speaking. And from this we can understand the matter of the soul of the beast and the other living creatures. For when that matter is gathered, composed of the four elements, and the beast or that creature comes into being from it, behold, because the elements have been formed into a respected form, they have risen in rung and drawn near to the living light that flows; and that light that flows in it is a soul to them. And in truth there is a living soul; and in greater truth there is no soul in it at all. For when the beast dies and is separated, it returns to its elements, to be distant from the light; for it has no soul, nor spirit and neshamah, that should rise or descend; and it was only like the fly that flies in the air: behold, when it draws near to the [burning] lamp, the light shines on it, and this is called its life; and when it is distant at the far ends of the hall, the light goes out from upon it because of its distance; and this is its death; and it has nothing by which to return to its source, and nothing by which to descend. And there is no objection from the choicest of the sages, Solomon, peace be upon him, in saying (Eccl. 3:21), "Who knows the spirit of man," etc., "and the spirit of the beast that goes downward to the earth?" For on the contrary, it is a support to this matter; for in the secret of transmigration it rises above. However, when it does not have that matter, it goes downward in separation, and its return to the element of earth; and from this, that it goes downward to the earth in being distant from the quarry and the source, and returns to its elements; and that living spirit returns, each one to its element: the fire to its element, and the air to its element. And by this is understood what is written in Tractate Sanhedrin (fol. 65b): "Rava created a man and sent him before Rabbi Zeira. He spoke with him, and he did not answer him. He said to him: You are from the companions; return to your dust." And Rashi explained there that Rava did this by his occupation with the Sefer Yetzirah. And this thing is difficult: could it enter the mind that there is power to bring down a neshamah and nefesh and ru'ach into that body? And behold, this thing is among the wondrous: that there should be power in the hand of man to bring down a neshamah from above upon a new creation, even if its creation is by the power of the alphabets, as we explained in the Gate of the Particulars of the Names, chapter 10. "But if YHVH make a new thing" (Num. 16:30), what would be its superiority, its advantage over that creation? I wonder!

And further, how would that poor one not cry out "Violence!" before its Owner, for they compelled it to descend here, where it would not be completed; and nothing would come to the hand of that soul but the toil and heavy burden of this world?

And further, in the saying of Rabbi Zeira, "You are from the companions; return to your dust," he would be found, God forbid, like one who sheds blood, for the return of that soul in shame of face, oppressed and crushed, before its Owner [without any completion]. Rather, with this introduction of ours everything is understood. For when those sages gather that gathering of dust, and through their wisdom, in their occupation with the Sefer Yetzirah, create a new creature, behold, that creature, which is in the form of a man, its parts are gathered and raised above in their drawing near to their quarry and their source; and the light that is fitting for them shines over against those elements, like the gathering of the parts of the beast; and not that there is in it a neshamah or a nefesh or a ru'ach, but mere life; even though it is superior to the life of the beast, because of the disposition of its form and its nature, which is more praiseworthy than the form of the beast, and it has drawn nearer to the source of the light than the beast.

And behold, in the return of that body to its elements it has only like the death of the beast: that the parts are separated and return to the dust itself, as it was; "for dust it is, and unto dust it shall return" (Gen. 3:19). And therefore he did not set his eyes upon it to put it to death; for it has no death in substance, even like a beast; but its return to the dust in a moment, and the elements are scattered and separated. And that is what he said to it, "Return to your dust." And therefore there is no punishment at all in its death and its killing, just as there is no punishment in the killing of a beast, as is explained. And now, because the elements are gathered through purity and holiness, the light that shines in them is the holiness and the purity; therefore the Torah permitted us the eating of some of the permitted beasts, wild animals and birds. And because some of them, the gathering of their parts is through the husks, as is known, and what shines in them is the impurity of the husks, therefore the Torah forbade [the forbidden beasts, wild animals and birds]. And with this we understand that all things in this world rise from rung to rung. The water descends on the earth, and that seed draws the thickness and fatness of the earth and their growths, whose foundation is from these thick ones, to the part of the limb of that seed. And the seed grows and becomes a herb; a light shines in it more praiseworthy than the light of the elements, because of their gathering and their nearness to the source. And then what was under the angel appointed over the element of earth goes out of his domain; for its light that flows in it is only the light that is bestowed from the angel appointed over the herbs, and especially the one appointed over that herb. And this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bereshit Rabbah, Parashah 10): "There is no herb below that does not have an angel above, who strikes it and says to it, Grow!"

And the matter of the striking: its matter is the striking of the light and its shining in that herb through the angel; and it is the channel of the concealed light in the secret of the formation [yetzirah] of the world of the angels. And for this the angel shines in the herb through the star, as is known; for the stars that are in Asiyah are attendants and servants to Yetzirah. And for this it is found in the Zohar that sometimes he relates this matter to the angels and sometimes to the stars; and it is all one matter, and there is no doubt about them. And let us return to our matter: for the simple elements rise in rung and become part of a limb of the herb, and draw nearer to the source. And afterward the beast eats that herb, and it becomes part of a limb of it, and becomes like its form, and draws nearer to its source; and according to its nearness to its source, so the light draws near to it, and the illumination grows in it, as is known. And what was under that angel appointed over the herbs goes out of his domain and enters under the angel appointed over the beasts, and especially of that kind; for the angel appointed over the herbs does not flow in it, but the light of the angel appointed over those beasts. And when the man eats that flesh, the flesh rises to a praiseworthy and superior rung, in its nearness to the manifestation of the man, upon whom flows the light of the King of the kings of kings, which is the upper neshamah, as we shall explain, with the help of the Name. And for this cause the ignorant man [am ha-aretz] is forbidden to eat meat; because he has no nearness to his source, on account of the evil of his deeds; and the beast is better than he, for it is on the side of holiness, and this one is on the side of the husk in his wickedness. And by this is understood what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 108b [?]): "Whoever is able to eat barley bread," etc.; for a man who is able by his nature to raise small things to the rung of man, it is not fitting that he strive to raise great things. And the example: a skilled and wise refiner who knows how to make clean silver from tin, and knows also how to refine silver and clean it: behold, according to the truth it is fitting for this craftsman to strive only to refine the tin into silver; for it is a praiseworthy degree and its benefit is greater. And let us return to our matter: for to this the choicest of the sages intended in saying (Eccl. 3:19; see there in the Targum and Rashi), "so that a man has no pre-eminence above a beast," etc.: for man, from the side of the gathering of his parts alone, has no advantage or superiority over the beast. And the men of the Great Assembly explained, in saying "except the pure neshamah," etc., and likewise "the neshamah that You have given in me is pure," etc., "You breathed it," etc.: for man has, over the gathering of the parts, a pure neshamah, hewn from a holy place. And of this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: "Israel are not under constellation" and angel and seraph; because they are superior, and their neshamah is above the angels, as is proved in the saying that we copied in chapter 8. Rather, the light that is bestowed upon them is the light of the Lord, may He be blessed, which shines for all the worlds. And on the contrary, the angels draw effluence from the righteous; and therefore, when there is a righteous man in this world, even the angels receive good through him. And this is the reason that Israel, while Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was alive, their bestowal was through the Shekhinah herself; and when they sinned it was said (Exod. 23:20), "Behold, I send an angel," etc.; because they descended from their rung and their degree to beneath what is caused from them. And therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not want it, and answered, "If Your presence go not, carry us not up hence" (Exod. 33:15). And apart from all this, even in his elements there is a preparation, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (in Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 14): "The first Adam was created from the place of his atonement," which is the dust of the altar; for the reason that there is the point of the world, and there is the force of the illumination of the light of the King of the kings of kings, may He be blessed, as is known. And this is "The words of the wise are … as nails well fastened" (Eccl. 12:11): the explanation, as this nail, of which only its head is seen, and through a man it enters to its depth, within its fastening, by its fineness and its point; so the sayings of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, have an inside and a depth, and there is no end to their depth.

And behold, through this chapter it is explained that the angels are pure and clear in the secret of the gathering of their parts and their nearness to the upper elements; and in this aspect man is certainly distant from it; for the degree of the gathering of the parts of man is not like the degree of the gathering of the parts of the angel. But the angel has in its inwardness only plain light, after the manner of the other passages of the light that flows. And man is not so; for there is within him a neshamah, clean and clear, so that when he makes the neshamah prevail over the parts of his matter, there shines in him the light that illuminates his neshamah, an upper light, more praiseworthy than the light that flows upon the angel; because his neshamah is from Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah; and he does not need to receive through any one of the rungs, but through himself; for it shines and receives the effluence from the place of the source of his neshamah, as the matter will be lengthened in this inquiry in the Gate of the Soul, with the help of the Name.
And further, we shall add teaching on the matter of the angels and their matter in this chapter, so that its matter be well explained:

What is intended in this chapter is to explain the matter of the angels, and especially what we mentioned in chapters 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 on the matter of the judgments with which they judge human beings, and the matter of the witnesses who testify against him, and all these matters, which are somewhat strange to the mind. And for this we say that it has already been explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation that the whole substance of the Emanation is only so that the very Self of the Godhead be clothed in it. And it is explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels that the matter of the changes is not in Him, may He be blessed; for He is simple and does not change, God forbid; and all is through the sefirot. And we said that because of the nearness of the sefirot to the source, it is still not fitting to relate the matter of the changes to the sefirot at all; but the Emanation was clothed in Beriah; and as the relation of the Emanator to the Emanation, so is the relation of the Emanation to Beriah. And because the changes multiply without end, Beriah is still near to the emanated ones and does not receive the changes at all; however, it is clothed in Yetzirah. And the relation of Beriah to Yetzirah is as the relation of Atzilut to Beriah. And Yetzirah is clothed in Asiyah, in the matter of the actions of ruin, and the defilements of the soul, to purify and to whiten, and the injuries of human beings, to injure them, to punish them, to bring them near to the service; Asiyah was needed, which is called the evil strap, a strap to lash. And therefore the matters of Yetzirah in their changes are near to the deeds of human beings: this one weighs and this one counts, this one a witness and this one an advocate; these judges of decrees and these judges of robberies, and these judges of injuries and these judges of monetary cases and these judges of capital cases; near to the changes to the utmost nearness. And these, the masters of Asiyah, are appointed to punish by confiscation, by uprooting, to put to death, to imprison, to injure: as the judges instruct, so the officers of the judges do. And now, when the righteous man is raised in the rungs of his soul, the light of his neshamah of Atzilut or of Beriah flows upon him; for these are held one in another; for the garment of the ten sefirot [of Atzilut is] Beriah, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA.

Behold, the righteous man is found to go out from under the hand of these judges, and it is not in their power to judge him, neither in much nor in little. And on the contrary, he is the source of the effluence upon them, and all of them draw from him; and he bestows to the ministers, and annuls their service for whom he wishes; in the matter of "Sun, stand still upon Gibeon" (Josh. 10:12); and likewise "He who said to the oil that it should burn will say to the vinegar that it should burn"; and likewise many, many annulments of nature in Yetzirah and in Asiyah; and possibly in Atzilut somewhat, as in the matter (explained in the Zohar, Pinchas, fol. 242a, on the verse) "Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones shout for joy" (Ps. 132:9). All this shows the force of the providence over the righteous man, until he changes and annuls the powers of Yetzirah entirely, and they do not judge him, and his judgment is bestowed from above. And this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: "Be silent; so it arose in the Thought"; to show that his judgment is in the place of silence, in a high place. However, when he sins, and the neshamah of Atzilut and of Beriah departs from him, and he remains in Yetzirah, then the masters of Yetzirah judge him. And this is "and I will hide My face from them, and they shall be devoured," etc. (Deut. 31:17); for he remains in the hand of Yetzirah and in the hand of Asiyah; and then they judge him according to his deeds and according to his aspects. And this is the matter of the one who weighs and the matter of the scribe and the matter of the advocates, because of their nearness to the changes, as we explained. However it may be, the whole manifestation of the world, from the upper point to the lower point, is found to be like the parable of the ray of the sun that passes by way of the window, which has four panes: the first bright, and the second bright but not so much, and the third somewhat turbid, and the fourth turbid entirely.
And behold, the light of the ray passes by way of the panes.

And behold, these four panes are four rungs, which are ABYA; and the light that flows is the light of the Ein Sof, the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, the very root that spreads out and shines down to the last point.

And behold, the light has not changed except with respect to the receivers. And those who have regard for the honour of their Owner know that it is not fitting to pass that light by way of the turbid pane, which is Asiyah. And this is the reason "how the firmament dwells in vain in the Land of Israel," as is written in the Gate of Substitutes (in chapter 2, on this saying of the Zohar), with the help of the Name. And it is like the pure air, the north wind, a healing for the soul, that passes by way of a stinking dunghill; for then it is certainly harmful. And who caused this thing? Those who caused the passing of (the light) [the air] by way of the dunghill. And that smell is not truly acquired by that wind; for whoever breathes it before it comes by way of the dunghill, its smell is like the smell of spices. And likewise exactly the parable of the light: who caused the turbidity of the light? Its passing by way of the turbid pane. And whoever looked at the light before it came, behold, it is a sweet light. And how much more will the honour of the light grow for whoever looks at it before it comes to the third pane, which is also somewhat turbid; for then he will recognize its degree. And to say that he will look at it before its passing by way of the second pane is impossible; for it is a light so bright that it darkens the eye of the beholder. And by this is understood the matter of the angels: that they have some revealing of the glory of the King of the world, by way of the light that is clothed in them; and this is their benefit and their matter, and this is the matter of their power. And all the more the maggidim, who say many times the precious names, in the verse "My commandments, My statutes and My laws" (Gen. 26:5), and in matters like these, which show strangeness at first sight. And it is plain: for they say so through the effluence that is bestowed, that is, the light that is clothed in them. And they are called limbs, because the light spreads out into sparks, clothed in each and every angel; that angel is found to be a limb of the limbs of the Chariot, since it is a clothed light. And the example of this is a great lamp burning within the hall, and in it fine windows and openings; and the light passes between the windows and is clothed in those channels and shines outward. And there is no doubt that the sparks are all one matter; and if they are divided into many sparks, the reason is that the openings are many; and according to their measure the lights multiply, though they are all united in the source; and that multiplicity is not truly acquired by the light; for if the openings were united, the light would be united. And this is the reason for the union of the palaces, in the secret of the union, in the secret of the prayer: so that the sparks clothed in them, which are the upper light, be united. And the matter is not with respect to the palaces, that is to say, the angels themselves, but with respect to the light clothed in them. And this is the power of the multiplicity of the light: that the openings are united one to another through it. And this is the power of the greatness of the Creator: that the corporeal limbs are united through the soul that spreads out in them. And "from our flesh we behold" (cf. Job 19:26) this matter: for the soul is not a substance divided into parts at all; rather it is one substance, in which parts are not judged at all. However, it is divided into parts with respect to the body, which is divided into parts; and nevertheless our saying "the limbs of the soul" is related with respect to the spreading out of the soul in the limbs.
