And so too limbs are related to what spreads out, with respect to its spreading out in limbs; which are the angels, upper limbs, to the light that spreads out in them. And after we have stood upon this, in the secret of the angels and their matter, from this we know the degree of the soul over the angel. For the angel is a body of four simple elements, drawing near to the source, and the light that flows upon them is the principal.

And behold, the soul of the righteous man is the principal of the light that spreads out within the angel, clothed in the angel; and the relation of the angel to the soul is found to be as the relation of the body to the soul; except that this is Asiyah and that Yetzirah. And certainly this is a great matter and a great key in the matter of the angels. And in this secret is understood his saying (Num. 23:4), "And God happened upon [va-yikkar] Balaam"; and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (in Vayikra Rabbah, Parashah 1) that the language va-yikkar is the language of nocturnal emission [keri] and impurity. For God forbid to think, in their saying, that there is impurity and keri above. And the matter is about those blessings that spread out and are bestowed from within the holiness to the husk; and that is the secret of the light that spreads out within the turbid pane and defiles the light, God forbid, so that Balaam should look and prophesy those blessings. And therefore the verse said (Num. 24:4), "which sees the vision of the Almighty [machazeh Shaddai]"; and he explained in the Zohar: "the vision of the Almighty," and not "the Almighty"; that is to say, a mirror in which the Shekhinah is seen, in the secret of her being ruling [shoreret] to subdue the husks, in the secret of "and His kingdom rules over all" (Ps. 103:19), explained in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 4.

And behold, the holy light spread out and was clothed within the husk, so that Balaam should know those blessings and prophesy; and as it were, the light of holiness was clothed in him. And the verse revealed this secret: "And YHVH put a word in Balaam's mouth," etc., "and thus you shall speak" (Num. 23:5). And our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Bamidbar Rabbah, Balak, ch. 20), concealed the secret and said that He put a nail in his mouth, to show that it was to subdue him; and like a nail, which does not let him speak as he wishes; and it is a subduing to him, in the secret of "and His kingdom rules over all"; "a time wherein one man rules over another to his hurt" (Eccl. 8:9): and this "to his hurt" is for the man of Belial, as we explained in the chapter mentioned.

And further, they hinted by saying "nail," as we explained above in the previous chapter, in the secret of "and as nails well fastened": to show the light whose spark spreads out from the source to the desired place. And this is enough of a notice on this matter. And when the Holy One, blessed be He, came to dispute with Israel, He said, "O My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him; from Shittim unto Gilgal; that you may know the righteous acts of YHVH" (Micah 6:5). And this is certainly the righteousness of YHVH: a great righteousness He did with Israel in this, as mentioned:

After it has emerged in our agreement that man in his righteousness is more praiseworthy than the angels, and this is proved from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him: if so, what is the degree of Elijah and Enoch, who, being righteous above all the people of their generation, merited only the degree of the angels? And so they explained explicitly in the Book of Palaces [Sefer ha-Heikhalot]: "Rabbi Ishmael said: I asked Metatron: Why are you called by the name of your Owner, in seventy names; and you are greater than all the princes, and higher than all the angels, and more beloved than all the ministers, and more honoured than all the hosts, and greater than all the mighty ones in greatness and in kingship and in glory? He answered and said to me: Because I am Enoch the son of Jared. And when the generation of the Flood went astray and were corrupt in their deeds, and said to God, 'Depart from us' (Job 21:14), what did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He took me from among them, to be a witness against them in the heavens on high, for all who come into the world. And since the Holy One, blessed be He, took me to serve the Throne of Glory and the wheel of the Chariot and all the needs of the Shekhinah, at once my flesh was turned to flame, and my sinews and my bones to coals of juniper, and the light of my eyelids to the radiance of lightnings, and the balls of my eyes to a torch of fire, and the hairs of my head to blaze and flame, and all my limbs to wings of burning fire, and the body of my stature to blazing fire; and at my right hewers of flames of fire, and at my left burners of torches of fire; and round about me there blow wind, storm and tempest, and the sound of quaking and thunder before me and behind me." Thus far his words.

He taught in this explicitly that he is Enoch the son of Jared, the righteous one, of whom it is said (Gen. 5:24), "And Enoch walked," etc. And so is the matter with Elijah, that he is an angel. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (fol. 151b), and these are his words: "And Rabbi Judah said: All of them met at this well. And David, why did he not meet at it? Rather, David's enemy was opposite it at that time, and therefore he did not meet at it. Jacob and Moses this well received with joy, and wished to draw near to them; and therefore, as soon as this well saw them, the waters rose toward them, like a woman who rejoices with her husband. And if you say: behold, Elijah fled and did not meet at it; why? Rather, Elijah is below the well, and not above it, as Moses and Jacob were; and therefore he is an angel and does a mission. And because Jacob and Moses are above the well, the well rejoiced toward them and rose to receive them, like a woman who rejoices toward her husband and receives him." Thus far his words.

And from it it certainly appears that Elijah is an angel of the angels who do missions. And if so, it is found that they have no benefit at all in this degree; for they descended from their degree; for if they had been in the degree of the righteous they would have been above, above; and now they are found within the bound of Yetzirah and within the bound of the angels. And to understand and comprehend the matter of Enoch and Elijah we need to copy here one saying from the Zohar on the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 82); and even if the matter is long, the benefit will be great. And these are his words: "'I am black, but comely' (Song 1:5). It is written, 'Train up [chanokh] a child in the way he should go,' etc. (Prov. 22:6). When the Holy One, blessed be He, created Adam, He created him in the upper likeness, his limbs and organs all in the upper secret. He brought him down to the earth, within the Garden of Eden that the Holy One, blessed be He, created on the earth, in a place concealed and stored away, which is in the likeness and form of above; as it is written, 'And YHVH God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to keep it' (Gen. 2:15). 'And put him in the Garden of Eden' without qualification, for all is in one secret. And if you say: in the upper Garden of Eden several boundaries and several walls are bounded round about it, of several upper camps and holy spirits; and here, in this Garden of Eden below on the earth, it is not so bounded. For if you say, since it is in the upper likeness, it is set in order with several spirits and souls of the righteous; if so, before there were righteous in the world, this lower Garden of Eden was not in the upper likeness. Rather, certainly it is in the upper pattern and likeness from the day the world was created. And before Adam was created there were several walls, boundaries of upper angels, surrounding it; for it was not without guarding; because in all those palaces that are there, there are rulers guarding it, until those spirits are included to come into this world. All the spirits and souls that were destined to enter this world were all there before Adam was created; and before those spirits and souls come into this world they are all ready to be given there. And these spirits and souls rise and go out from the upper Garden and descend into the lower Garden of Eden, and are clothed there in garments like the body of this world; and they occupy themselves in the Torah, to know and to gaze in that garment at the glory of their Master, each and every one as he is destined to be in this world. And the one whose tikkun is fine and fitting in that garment, and whose endeavour was as is fitting, they raise him above, before the Holy King, in that garment like this world; and he stands before Him, and the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices in him. As it is written, 'As YHVH lives, before whom I stand' (1 Kings 17:1): 'before whom I stood,' before I went out to this world. There are garments in which the spirits are clothed, like the body of this world; and this body is destined to leave the holy spirit and to stray after the evil spirit. That holy spirit flies from within that garment, and that garment is drawn outside the Garden of Eden; because on every second day and every fourth day the evil spirit of the wife of harlotry goes round about the Garden of Eden; and there are garments that are drawn after that evil spirit, and that evil spirit comes and dwells in them. And since the holy spirit descends and is clothed in it, it does not settle within it, and flies from it and rises above; and that garment is drawn after that evil spirit, and they bring it outside; and it sits there until that man comes and is clothed in it, and brings it down to Gehinnom, and it is judged in it every day. And that holy spirit that flew from that garment rises above and enters one treasury, until there goes out from that wicked one a son or a seed in whom that holy spirit will descend and be completed in it as is fitting. And that wicked one, who has rest afterward, chirps and rises and is clothed in another garment, and stands at the entrance of the Garden of Eden, and sees that holy spirit that he [left] there, in how much glory, in how much light; he is ashamed of it. And likewise he gazes at the glory of the other righteous, and weeps and is ashamed of his deeds. And when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the first Adam, He brought him into the Garden of Eden in one precious garment of the light of the Garden of Eden; and he was completed in it, and a holy spirit and soul, to be complete in all. He and his wife would stroll in the Garden of Eden, and upper angels round about them, giving them pleasure with several blisses and pleasures. He opened for him one treasury and showed him all those later generations, each and every generation; and he would see upper and lower likenesses in the light of the mirror that shone upon them. The wife of harlotry descended, and the one who rides and rules over her, that one lacking heart, who led all astray. And she saw that upper glory that was in Adam and his wife. The wife of harlotry was strengthened in the power and the strength of the one who rules over her, and drew near to Eve, and began to seduce her with several seductions, with several sweetnesses of the tongue, so that she was seduced; then Adam too was seduced afterward. And those garments flew from him, and the soul, the radiance of the mirror above, rose from him; and he remained naked of everything, he and his wife. When he did teshuvah, after he was driven out of the Garden of Eden and was sustained outside, the Holy One, blessed be He, had pity on him and made for him other garments, as was needed to make use of in this world. And afterward he lived outside and begot children. And that radiance of the upper soul that flew from him rose above and was stored away in one treasury, which is the guf, until he begot children and Enoch went out into the world. And when Enoch came, that upper radiance, the holy soul, descended in him; and Enoch was in that upper greatness that Adam had left; as it is written, 'And Enoch walked with God,' etc. And afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, needed to take him from this world, and for the holy spirit to be included from below and from above; and all was included in that holy spirit; and he was included from below and from above, so that the whole world be drawn, kind after its kind. When he was included, he was made appointed one in this world and in the upper world: in this world from the side of that inclusion in which he was included from this world, and in the upper world from the side of that inclusion in which he was included from above. And at each and every time that there are righteous and pious in the world, that inclusion with which he was included from below, from the side of Enoch, is renewed; then he is a youth [na'ar] in the secret of the renewal of the moon. And this secret is 'Train up [Chanokh] a youth in the way he should go,' etc.: what [is it]? That Enoch should go in that way of truth, in a straight and complete path. 'Even when he is old': that likeness of Enoch, from that time that he was included in that holiness. Do not say that he has aged from many days and has departed from that place. It is not so; but at every time that there are pious and righteous in the world, that inclusion of that side is renewed, and that likeness will be seen as literally a youth, and will not depart from there. And because of that inclusion, the lower ones inherit from the dew of the upper watering; and the inheritance of the greatness of holiness descends to the world." Thus far his words.
And because of the length of the matter we shall explain from this saying only those that come to our matter.

Behold, he told at the beginning of his words that it is possible for the soul, before its coming to this world, after it has descended to the lower Garden of Eden, to be clothed in a garment like his garment that he will be clothed in in this world. And when his ways are good, and he does not incline after the husk that surrounds, then it rises before its Owner in the likeness of that garment. And this was the matter of Elijah, who said, "As YHVH lives, before whom I stood," as we explained. And afterward he said that in the first Adam there were three things. One, the soul, that is to say, a soul or spirit without qualification; for this was not lost from him even after his sin. And the second, the garment in which he was clothed, which is (literally) [the garment of] the man whom the Holy One, blessed be He, created, which inclined after the husk. Third, the radiance of the upper soul, which is an honoured degree. And to the three of them he intended in saying, "in one precious garment of the light of the Garden of Eden," etc.: this is the garment that became corporeal, mentioned above, which sometimes inclines after the husk; second, a spirit, which is clothed in that garment; third, the soul, the upper radiance. Afterward he said, "then he was seduced, and those garments flew from him": they are not the garments that inclined after the husk; for those themselves were Adam and Eve, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, created; but over them there was a further garment of light; and that is the garments that flew from him; and likewise the soul, which is the upper radiance, etc.

And behold, those matters and degrees that the first Adam lost, the upright Enoch merited, according to the law of the souls, as we explained above. And he said, "afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, needed to take him," etc. It is known that the Holy One, blessed be He, when He created the first Adam in those upper garments and that praiseworthy soul, the principal intent was that the first Adam should be a source of all the effluence for the upper and the lower ones. Therefore all of them bowed down to him, as they, of blessed memory, explained on the verse "O come, let us bow down and bend the knee" (Ps. 95:6). And the intent is that the bowing down is the drawing of bestowal, as is written in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And the creatures, seeing that they received from him, all their intent was that it be bestowed from him to them alone. And he said to them that one must not do so, but that they be bestowed from the source of the effluence; that is, "let us kneel before YHVH our Maker." But afterward, when he sinned, and all saw "that Adam bowed down to this place and cleaved to it, they were drawn after him, and he caused death to himself and to all the world," as he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 107b; see there). And now, when Enoch merited his degree, his glory was somewhat lacking, because his garment and his disposition were like the people of this world; and according to this it was not in his power to bestow except to corporeal beings alone. And therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, wished that his corporeal body should turn to torches of fire, as he himself explained in the Book of Palaces. And this is what he said: "And since the Holy One, blessed be He, took me to serve the Throne of Glory." Because the Throne of Glory is Beriah; and he (the explanation, Metatron) is Yetzirah; and he serves the Throne; for the Throne is clothed in him, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA; and he receives the effluence from the Throne and bestows to all that is from him downward. And this is in the secret of his flesh that turns to torches of fire, etc. And that is "that he was included from above and from below," mentioned in this saying: for because he was a son of man, and in his very form like human beings, the likeness of a youth, therefore he is included from the lower ones; and because his body returned to spiritual, he is included from the upper ones. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, was precise in his language, in saying "and for the holy spirit [ru'ach] to be included"; and likewise in all his language he mentions ru'ach, not neshamah. For the neshamah rose to the place of the souls, the secret of the Garden of Eden above; but the ru'ach, which stands in the Garden of Eden below and does not rise further, as is explained in the Zohar in many places, is what merited to be included in two inclusions, from the upper ones and from the lower ones. And this is what he added over the righteous: for the righteous do not serve in the body in this world, but in the Garden of Eden below; but from there upward they do not rise except in the secret of the neshamah, which is clothed in spirituality. But Enoch merited to rise to the degree that he turned into torches of fire; and the other righteous are not so; rather they are stripped of the body and the corporeality, and the body is consumed in the dust and rots, and they are clothed in another garment. And this angel, his very body endures; and it is what turned into torches of fire, etc., as is proved from his words in the Book of Palaces that we copied at the head of the chapter. And his soul is always in the secret of the souls of the righteous and the pious, in the place fitting for it:

After we explained the matter of Enoch in the previous chapter, we shall come to explain in this chapter the matter of Elijah. And we say that as is the case of Enoch, so is the case of Elijah; even though one has a superiority over his fellow; for into this we shall not now enter in inquiry, until the end of the gate, with the help of the Name.

And behold, the matter of Elijah is that he is corporeal like other human beings; and because he merited in the Garden of Eden that degree, that he did not incline after the husk, and from the greatness of his piety and the completeness of his soul, his body merited to be turned into torches of fire; and not exactly like Enoch; for Enoch was literally turned into a torch of fire, but for Elijah another body was prepared. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Vayakhel (fol. 197a): "Another explanation: 'Who has ascended up into heaven, and descended?' (Prov. 30:4). This is Elijah, of whom it is written, 'And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven' (2 Kings 2:11). And how could Elijah go up to heaven? For all the heavens cannot bear even a grain like a mustard seed of the body of this world; and you say, 'And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven'? Rather, as it is said, 'And YHVH came down upon Mount Sinai' (Exod. 19:20); and it is written, 'And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud, and went up into the mount' (Exod. 24:18). And the Holy One, blessed be He, who was on Mount Sinai, as it is written, 'And the sight of the glory of YHVH was like devouring fire on the top of the mount' (Exod. 24:17): how could Moses go up to Him? Rather, of Moses it is written, 'And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud, and went up into the mount': for he entered into the cloud as one who is clothed in a garment. So too he was clothed in the cloud and entered within it; and in the cloud he drew near to the fire and was able to draw near. So too Elijah, of whom it is written, 'And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven': for he entered into that whirlwind and was clothed in that whirlwind and went up above. And a secret I have found in the book of the first Adam, who said, of those generations of the world: one spirit there will be that will descend to the world, on the earth, and be clothed in a body; and Elijah is his name. And in that body he will ascend, and be stripped of his body, and it will remain in the whirlwind; and another body, of light, will be prepared for him, to be among the angels. And when he descends, he will be clothed in that body that remained in that world; and in that body he will be seen below, and in the other body he will be seen above. And this is the secret of 'Who has ascended up into heaven, and descended?' There was no man whose spirit went up to heaven and afterward came down below, except Elijah, who went up above and came down below." Thus far his words.

And from it it is made clear that he has a soul like other men of the righteous of Israel; and because of his merit he merited two degrees. First, to be clothed in the garment of that angel, and to be an upper minister, even though his neshamah is bound in the place of the other souls; and the ru'ach alone is what is clothed, as is proved from the language of the saying, which mentioned only ru'ach; as it appears, the neshamah is raised in the degree of the souls. And now it is fitting that we ask why Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and Moses did not attain this degree, who are greater than Elijah; as the Zohar wrote, Parashat Vayetze, on the matter of the well, that it did not rise toward Elijah when he fled; and it answered, "he is an angel," etc., as we copied in the previous chapter. And we say that if they had had so, they would have been lacking from their degrees; because the degree of the Patriarchs is that they are a chariot to the very sefirot, in the way that we explained in the Gate of Titles, chapter 3. And if so, if they had been clothed in the degrees of any angel whatever of the degrees of the angels, behold, they would have descended from their degrees; for in their lifetime they were channels for the effluence bestowed from the Shekhinah herself through the sefirot, and the whole substance of the effluence was bestowed through them, even to the upper ones; as in the matter of "And God went up from Abraham" (Gen. 17:22). And it is a choicer degree than the degree of Metatron, the head of the princes; for explicitly it is explained in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim that when there is no righteous man in this world, then the Shekhinah is clothed in Metatron, as is written in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 4, with the help of Heaven. And if so, it is found that the degree of the righteous, when they are a chariot, is greater than the degree of the angels; and therefore, if they rose in their lifetime to the degree of the angels, they would be found to lose their degrees. And if you say: after their death their body has no degree at all in the matter of the chariot; and if so, it would have been fitting that their body rise to the degree of the angels: this is no difficulty at all; for even after their death, in their burial, they are in their degree. And the proof is from David, peace be upon him, who reigned in Hebron seven years; and he explained in the Zohar (Va'era, fol. 31a) the reason: that David joined [them], so that his kingdom be established in the attribute of Malkhut with the Patriarchs, who are in Hebron. It is found that even after their death they stand in their degree. But Elijah and Enoch are not in the degree of the chariot itself; for they never rose except in the rung of this degree mentioned alone. And this is what [the Zohar above] answered, "Rather, Elijah is an angel": the explanation, he is at the rung of an angel, not at the rung of a chariot; and the proof is that his end proves his beginning. And at all events, both the soul of Elijah and the soul of Enoch are bound up in the bundle of life like the other souls of the righteous; except that they added that they merited that their ru'ach be clothed in the degree of the angels; which is not so with the other righteous, whose ru'ach does not rise from the lower Garden of Eden, for there it is clothed.

And further, they merited that they are limbs of the Godhead in the secret of the palaces that I explained; and it is a degree added beyond the others: that they are limbs of the Godhead in the secret of the chashmal that spreads out.

And the matter of the Patriarchs is a degree greater than theirs: for they are not limbs, but they are the whole substance of the Godhead that spreads out to the lower ones. And now there are found in this matter four aspects. The first aspect, the smallest of all, is the aspect of the angels; and they are channels and openings in which the upper light is clothed, and through them shines a dark light; and they are called the limbs of the Chariot. The second aspect, greater than the first, is the aspect of the righteous, who are channels and openings in which the upper light, the very Tiferet, spreads out. And this secret was revealed in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi (fol. 245), and these are his words: "Rabbi Simeon said: Every place needs silence, except the silence of the Torah. I have one treasure stored away, and I do not want it to be lost from you; and it is an upper word, and I found it in the book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder. Come and see: in every place the male pursues the female and arouses love toward her. And here we find love that she arouses and pursues him; and the way of the world is that it is no praise for the female to pursue the male. Rather, it is a closed word and an upper word, of the house of the King's treasures. Come and see: there are three souls," etc. "Another soul is the soul of the righteous; they come from those upper souls, from the soul of the male and from the soul of the female. And therefore the souls of the righteous are above all those hosts and camps above. And if you say: behold, they are upper from every side; why do they descend to this world, and why do they depart from it? To a king to whom a son was born," etc. "Come and see: if all the righteous knew this, they would rejoice on that day that comes to them to depart from this world. And is it not an upper honour, that the Lady comes for their sake, and to bring them to the King's palace, and that the King rejoice in them every day? For the Holy One, blessed be He, delights only in the souls of the righteous. Come and see: the upper arousal, the love of the Assembly of Israel toward the Holy One, blessed be He: the souls of the righteous below arouse it, because they come from the side of the King, from the side of the male. And this arousal reaches the female from the side of the male, and the love is aroused. It is found that the male arouses affection and love for the female," etc. Thus far his words, as relevant to our matter; and we skipped what is not needed by us, so as not to lengthen.

And behold, he said explicitly that the souls are the very self of the male, Tiferet. And by this the principal of his question is answered: how is it possible to say that the female goes round after the male, the reverse of the conduct of this world; and that is, that the Shekhinah demands the union. And therefore he answered that the souls are the very self of the male. And since the arousal is through the souls, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 17, therefore the principal that precedes the arousal is the souls, which are the very Tiferet that spreads out in them. And therefore they are above all the other creatures, even above the angels, as we explained. The third aspect is the aspect of the composition of the angels and the righteous; and that is the aspect of Metatron and Elijah, whose souls are bound up in the bundle of life above, and their spirits are clothed in the secret of the angels; and this is certainly a service doubled and redoubled, as we explained. The fourth aspect is the aspect of the Patriarchs and all those who are a chariot to the sefirot; which are the aspect of the righteous in their souls, and they were raised above them, for they are a channel to the very self of that sefirah even in their body, as we explained above. And now there remains for us to explain somewhat more on the matter of Elijah; and we shall devote a chapter to it by itself:

On the matter of Elijah's lineage our Rabbis, of blessed memory, disagreed (in Bereshit Rabbah, Parashah 71) as to which tribe he was from: some of them said he was from the tribe of Gad, and some of them said from the tribe of Benjamin, and some of them said, "Phinehas, this is Elijah." And for each of these opinions they have support from the verses. And there are some of them who said that he is from the seed of Rachel, and he himself was related sometimes to this one and sometimes to that one. And there are kabbalists who wished to explain everything in the secret of impregnation [ibbur]. And we have found on this matter, from the commentators, of blessed memory, who said that Elijah was sent forth [from above]; because we do not find in any place the name of Elijah's father, but "Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead" (1 Kings 17:1); and understand.

"And further, it is said of Elijah (1 Kings 18:15), 'As YHVH lives, before whom I stand [amadti]': that is to say, when he had already stood. And therefore they said that that place which is Enoch is Metatron, and the place which is Elijah is Sandalfon. And when Elijah went up by a whirlwind heavenward, his flesh was turned into torches of fire, and his body remained in the world of the spheres or in the world of the angels, and his spirit rose to its place. And when the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to send him on a mission, he descends and is clothed, and descends to the earth and does his mission. And therefore he was revealed to sages and to the perfect and to prophets, and they would speak with him, because there was in him a side of matter; and it is the body mentioned. And when he departs, he leaves that body in its place and rises." Thus far his words.

Further, we have found in the name of Rabbi Moshe de León, of blessed memory: "And as to what you asked on the matter of Elijah, who went up on high, which no other man went up: know that in the secrets of the Torah I have seen an exceedingly wondrous secret. Elijah: you will not find for him in the whole Torah father and mother, nor that it is written of him 'son of So-and-so,' but 'Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead.' And they said that before this he descended from heaven, and his name is known in the secrets of wisdom. And further, afterward he was seen by the sages in many places, in many likenesses: at times in the likeness of an Arab, at times like a horseman, at times like one of the great ones of the generation; in many matters his likeness and his form. Therefore do not wonder at this matter, that Elijah is at a rung higher than all other human beings. And if you say: how was his likeness and his form, all those years and all that time, the likeness of a man? For an angel, if he is seen, it is for an hour or a day, and no more. They said that at the hour that the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to create man, He said to the angels, 'Let us make man.' They said before Him: Master of the world, 'What is man, that You are mindful of him?' (Ps. 8:5). He stretched out His finger against them and burned them. He called a second band likewise, until He called So-and-so and his company. He said to him, 'Let us make man.' He said before Him: Master of the world, if it is good before You, before me all the more so; and if it is good in Your eyes, I will descend and be an attendant before him. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: From here onward your name will no longer be called So-and-so, but So-and-so. And even so he did not descend at that time; but he descended after a time, and established the faith in the world that YHVH is God, in the matter of Ahab. And after a few days that he established this in the world, the Place raised him to the heavens on high. And the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: You are a good guardian for human beings; by your life, you shall descend and establish My faith in the world. And of this it is written (1 Kings 18:36–37), 'Hear me, O YHVH,' etc., 'and that I have done all these things at Your word,' etc.: 'at Your word,' before I descended to the world. And this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: 'Michael in one, Gabriel in two, Elijah in three'; for the cause is his being at their rung. And if you say: behold, it is written, 'for I am not better than my fathers' (1 Kings 19:4); and if the thing is so, why did he say these words? Rather, certainly what he asked concerning this, being drawn after human beings for several years: and indeed his good was not from the side of father and mother, merit in the world; for his good and his standing in the world were not from them; and therefore he said that this is not the way for one who is like me to tarry in the world." Thus far his words.

And this opinion is void of itself from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, whose opinion is that Elijah was a human being; and so is the opinion of all the sages of the Gemara; for they disagree only on which tribe he was from; but to say that he was an angel who became corporeal, there is none who agrees to this. And the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, on this matter are in Parashat Vayigash (fol. 209), and these are his words: "For Rabbi Simeon said: All the souls of the world all go out from that place that flows and goes out; and the bundle of life takes all of them. And when the female conceives from the male, all of them are in the craving of the female toward the male. And when the craving of the male goes out with desire [re'uta], then those souls are in greater endurance, because all is in the craving and desire of the Tree of Life. And Elijah, because he was from that desire more than any other man, endured. And therefore it is written (1 Kings 19:4), 'for himself [el nafsho],' and it is not written 'et nafsho'; for et nafsho, this is the female. And if you say, 'unto the woman He said' (Gen. 3:16): the inclusion of male and female, when it is within the male, then 'unto [el] the woman He said'; 'et the woman,' the female alone, without the inclusion of the male. In this way, el nafsho, male alone; et nafsho, female alone, without the inclusion of the male. And because he is on the side of the male more than all the people of the world, he endured in his existence more, and did not die like the other people of the world; because all of him is from the Tree of Life, and not from within the dust. And therefore he ascended above, and did not die after the way of all the people of the world, as it is written (2 Kings 2:11), 'And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.' Come and see what is written: 'And behold a chariot of fire, and horses of fire,' etc.; for then the body was stripped from the spirit, and he ascended, not like the other way of the people of the world; and he remained a holy angel like the other upper holy ones, and does missions in the world. And behold, they have established that the miracles that the Holy One, blessed be He, does in the world are done through him." Thus far his words.

And behold, it appears from it explicitly that his soul was like the other souls of the righteous; except that because of his added holiness at the time of the upper coupling he rose to that degree. And so he also proved in the saying that we copied in chapter 12, on the matter of "As YHVH lives, before whom I stood," which we explained. And nevertheless it may already be possible that he is Sandalfon, in the way that we explained of Metatron, that he was Enoch before, and was literally a man, as is explained in the preceding chapters:

Maimonides, peace be upon him, believed that the matter of the appearance of the angels to Abraham our father, peace be upon him, and the like, was in the vision of prophecy. And this is because he believed that they are subtle to the utmost subtlety, spiritual, not becoming corporeal; and because of this their multiplicity was difficult for him. And he answered that they multiply by way of cause and effect, as we explained, with the help of Heaven, in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, chapter 6. And for this, those who came after him objected to his opinion: that if so, it would be required that the angels be only ten, emanated from one to one, since the procession is only from cause to effect. And their rungs are ten: chayyot, ofannim, er'elim, chashmalim, serafim, mal'akhim, elohim, benei elohim, keruvim, ishim.

And behold, it is known that they are more and more. And they strained themselves in several matters to settle this matter, and did not succeed. And we have only the tradition of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who explained that it is possible for the angels to become thick and to take on body in the air; and these are his words in Parashat Vayera (fol. 101a): "Come and see: (at the hour) [after] Abraham was circumcised, he was sitting and in pain; and the Holy One, blessed be He, sent to him three angels openly," etc. "And who can see angels? For it is written, 'Who makes His angels spirits,' etc. (Ps. 104:4). Rather, certainly he saw them descending to the earth like human beings. And let this not be difficult for you; for certainly they are holy spirits; and at the hour that they descend to the world they are clothed in airs and in the elements of bodily forms, and are seen by human beings exactly in the appearance of their likeness. And come and see: Abraham saw them like the appearance of human beings; and even though he was in pain from the circumcision, he ran after them, so as not to diminish what he used to do before this." Thus far his words.

And behold, he said explicitly that it is possible for the angels to take on body and to be seen by the pure of attributes and the righteous, the pure of sight. Further, we have learned there on the matter of the angels that they do not know about this world and its matters, but each one about his service and about his watch; and apart from this they have no knowledge in the world. And these are his words (there, fol. 101b [?]): "'Where is Sarah your wife?' (Gen. 18:9). And did the upper angels not know that Sarah was there in the tent? Why is it written 'Where'? Rather, they do not know in this world except what is handed over to them to know; and what is not handed over to them to know they do not know. Come and see: it is written, 'For I will pass through the land of Egypt … I am YHVH' (Exod. 12:12). And how many angels and messengers does the Holy One, blessed be He, have! Rather, because they do not know between a drop of a firstborn and one that is not firstborn, except the Holy One, blessed be He, alone. Likewise (Ezek. 9:4), 'and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men': and why did they need it? Rather, because they do not know except what is handed over to them to know they know; such as all those things that the Holy One, blessed be He, is going to bring upon the world. And what is the reason? Because the Holy One, blessed be He, passes a herald through all the firmaments concerning that thing that He is going to bring upon the world, and they hear the thing and it is known. Likewise, at the hour that the spoiler is found in the world, a man must hide in his house and not be seen outside in the market, so that he not come to ruin; as it is said, 'and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning' (Exod. 12:22). From them, one who is able to hide, yes; but from before the Holy One, blessed be He, one cannot hide. What is written? 'Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? says YHVH' (Jer. 23:24)." Thus far his words; and it is clear. Further, we have learned from there a third teaching on the matter of the angels: that their principal sustenance is from the side of Chesed. And these are his words (there, fol. 104): "Come and see: 'And the men rose up from thence' (Gen. 18:16): from that meal that Abraham prepared for them, and he merited by them. And even though they were angels, he merited by them; and of all that food nothing remained of it, for the sake of Abraham, and to give him merit by it; for it is written, 'and they did eat' (Gen. 18:8): it was eaten in their fire. And if you say: behold, they were three angels: this one fire, and this one water, and this one air. Rather, each and every one was included in its fellow; and therefore 'they did eat.' Likewise, 'they beheld God, and did eat and drink' (Exod. 24:11): eating, certainly, they ate; for they were nourished from the Shekhinah. So too 'they did eat': they caused themselves to be nourished from that side to which Abraham cleaved; and therefore nothing remained of what Abraham gave them. Likewise a man must drink from the cup of blessing, so that he merit that blessing above. So too they ate from what Abraham prepared for them, so that they merit to be nourished from the side of Abraham; for from that side goes out the sustenance for all the upper angels." Thus far his words.

He taught explicitly that the sustenance of the angels is all from the side of Chesed. Further, I have found in the Tikkunim on this matter that the angels: some of them draw nourishment from the side of Gevurah, and some of them from the side of Chesed, and some of them draw nourishment from the side of Tiferet, and so from all the sefirot. And nevertheless they do not disagree; for, as regards their sustenance, it is from the side of Chesed for all of them equally. Further, the commentators explained that every angel whose name ends in El, as Michael, his drawing is from the side of the sefirah of Chesed; and every name that ends in Yah, his drawing is from the side of Tiferet; and every name that ends in a final Nun, his drawing is from the side of Gevurah. "And one need not search after them, for all of them go out from the verses; however, they have a support in the verse by way of the number and the like. And the other names that have no sign from these three go out from the verses." Thus far his words.

Further, we have learned in the Tikkunim that the drawing of the angels is from known sefirot, and their action is like the actions of the sefirot, and their name is after the name of the sefirah: as Gabriel, after the name of Gevurah; and likewise Chasdiel, after the name of Chesed; and likewise Ahaviel, after the name of Chesed, which is called Love; and likewise after the name of all the other actions. And the reason is that ten lights spread out from Beriah to Yetzirah, and through the lights the actions are performed, as is explained in the Gate of ABYA.
And behold, from these ten lights the creation of the angels spreads out. Therefore they are titled after the name of the sefirot and after the name of the action of the sefirot:
Gate Twenty-Five is the Gate of Substitutes:

What is intended in this gate is to explain the matter of the husks: what they are, and from what side they were emanated, and how their emanation was, and what their benefit and their matter are, as we shall explain with the help of the Rock and His salvation:
Chapter One:

After we have spoken in the preceding chapters of all that is inscribed on the matter of the holy angels, it is fitting for us to know that "God has made even the one over against the other" (Eccl. 7:14). For just as there is the side of holiness and purity and righteousness and uprightness and the good disposition of the governance, as we explained, so there is the side of the husk, which is the crushed impurity, which is the accusation; and from its side is the one who accuses and perverts man from the straight way to a way that is not good; and they rise and accuse him and defile him; for "he is unclean, and Unclean shall he cry" (Lev. 13:45), and impurity they pursue. And there are those who ask: since the holiness and the purity and the subtlety are in the Emanation without end, and it is separated from these attributes with the utmost separation, if so, from where did the husks and the impurities go out, and where were they before their formation? And at first sight it is a mighty question, and the intelligent man will be astonished at it. And we have received on this from our teacher a fine answer; and it is the parable of the grain, cleaned of all refuse to the utmost cleanness and purity: behold, at any rate, when a man eats it and that food is digested in his bowels, much refuse and excrement remains there.

And behold, shall we say that at the time of his eating he ate that filth and excrement? No. Rather, according to the manifestation of the food before its eating, that thing eaten was cleaner than it could be in manifestation, separated from all excrement and from all filth. However, after the eating and the separation of the choice thing from it, that excrement remains, which was not until now. And so is the thing in the Emanation. The truth is that above, in the place of the Emanation, "no evil thing descends from heaven"; for above, the things are subtle to the utmost subtlety. However, in the thickening of the things and their descent in the order of the emanated rungs, it was necessary that the thing be separated, "food from within food," and refuse came into being there. A further fine parable, which settles better: the parable of the seed of man, which is of the choicest that comes into being in the body of man; and it goes out from the brain by way of the testicles to the organ; and from that drop, in the full womb, the child comes into being from it, and other filthy things apart from the child. And could it enter the mind that in the brain of man, which is the choicest of the body, the manifestation of that filth comes into being? No; certainly, if so, he would perish at once. But that filth comes into being in the drawing of the seminal drop from place to place and from rung to rung: the filths come into being in the separation of the choice part from which the child comes into being, and from the rest the filth comes into being. And so are the things in the Emanation: above, in its place, there is no evil thing; however, in its being drawn below, there comes into being from it, in the separation of the purity and the holiness, an impure thing, which is the refuse and the dross of the gold. And after we pursued the inquiry of the inquiries of wisdom, we found support on this matter in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 167a), and these are his words, on the passage "Let there be light": "And because these are five rungs that separated and were drawn from this first light, 'light' is written five times; and all of them were from the side of the right and were included in it. And when they were included in the side of the left, they were included in the secret of the waters, which takes from the right; and therefore 'waters' is written five times. And when they were completed in the secret of the middle, 'firmament' is written five times. And therefore three they are, light, waters, firmament, corresponding to these three rungs in which all five rungs are included; and therefore in all of them five times is written, in each and every one. Here is the secret of secrets: in these three the secret of the likeness of Adam was portrayed and engraved in an engraving. For they are light at first, afterward waters, afterward the firmament spread out within them, which is the engraving that engraved the likeness of Adam; like the engraving of the form of the likeness of Adam in his begetting. For in the begetting of Adam, at first seed, which is light; for the light of all the limbs of the body is that seed, and therefore it is light; and that light is called seed, as it is written, 'Light is sown,' etc. (Ps. 97:11): it is literal seed. Afterward that seed, which is light, spread out and became waters in its moisture. It engraved more and spread out a spreading within those waters, the spreading of the body to every side. When the form and likeness of the body had been portrayed and engraved, that spreading congealed and is called firmament; and this is the 'firmament in the midst of the waters' (Gen. 1:6). And after it congealed it is written, 'And God called the firmament Heaven' (Gen. 1:8); for that moisture that flowed congealed, and that refuse remained in the body, which was within those waters. When the body was clarified and cleaned with cleanness, that moisture that flowed and remained (was) refuse, which was made within the smelting; and they are the evil, turbid waters; and from them was made the refuse, the accuser of all the world, male and female. Afterward, when those turbid waters descended and were smelted below, on the side of the left, they went out to accuse all the world. Happy is he who is saved from them. When the accuser went out, then it is written, 'Let there be lights [me'orot, defective]' (Gen. 1:14), defective, and croup was drawn out among children, and the light of the moon was lacking," etc. Thus far his words.

And his words are clear, and his intent is to what we said concerning the parable of the seed; and this is what he wished in saying "like the engraving of the form of the likeness of Adam." And from it it is explained that the principal of the portraying is in Gevurah, and there the turbid waters remained, as I explained. However, it remains for us to explain, since it is so that the matter of the husk came into being from the matter of the spreading out of the Emanation up to Gevurah: how is the husk bestowed from there by way of rungs, since there are still five rungs of holiness to complete to ten; and all the more since Beriah and Yetzirah still remain, according to what we explained above? And for this it appears that it is explained by what we explained above in the Gate of Channels, chapter 4, on the matter of the second channel that is in Yesod, from whose side is the drawing of the husks: all the surplus of the upper effluence; for all surpluses are fitting for the husks, which are the surplus. And nevertheless the name of impurity did not take effect on it until it went outside. And so they were precise in this in the language of the saying, which said "that moisture that flowed and remained," etc., "and from them was made the refuse, the accuser," etc.

Behold, explicitly: the surplus became refuse, and it had no power to accuse or to defile until its descending below. And this is what he was further precise in his language afterward, and said, "Afterward, when those turbid waters descended and were smelted below, on the side of the left, they went out to accuse all the world." And it appears that above, in the place of their first smelting and their surplus, in the holy place, there was not yet the name of impurity on the surplus in substance, even though those waters were fit for that impurity. And from this we may infer concerning the effluence that is bestowed upon them and their sustenance that is given them from the King's table: that while they are before the King, even though it is fit for the husk, the name of impurity does not take effect on them until they descend below from the place of the channel through which it is bestowed to them. And this is no wonder; for behold, excrement (in a man): the ruling of the law is that if he is sitting and it is not seen, it does not prevent the recitation of the Shema, even though the name of excrement has already taken effect on it; and the reason is that the spirit of impurity has not ruled over it until it goes out from the body of the man entirely. And likewise the law with semen: even though it has been uprooted from its place to go out, while it has not gone out no impurity has taken effect on it, and the man is still pure; and it does not defile until it goes out from the mouth of the organ outward; for then that evil power takes effect on it. And for this that channel was needed above from the beginning; because before it goes out to the air it is already fit for them, from the place of the surplus; and from there it is separated to the left side by way of that channel, until it goes outside, where "sin crouches" (Gen. 4:7), and they receive it; and then "he is unclean," and unclean is the one who eats it; "Nabal is his name, and folly is with him" (1 Sam. 25:25):

It remains an obligation upon us to explain a great doubt on the matter of the husks. Since all the rungs of existence, one above another down to the point of the earth, descend in a chain from cause to effect, and every effect is surrounded by its cause, if so, it is fitting to infer according to this that every good and every effluence that is bestowed in this world comes by way of the husk and the impurity, God forbid. And likewise the soul at the time of its rising, even if he was pious, would be compelled to be clothed first in impurity and to be defiled there before its rising above, God forbid. And this is certainly a thing outside the truth and outside the subject.

And further, the manna that descended to Israel: how shall we say that it passed by way of there? And likewise the Torah, and the ascent of Moses on high, and the ascent of Elijah. And there is an answer, to say that they went up in a whirlwind [se'arah]; for God forbid that this whirlwind be a whirling storm; rather, it is the barley [se'orah] through which they would offer the offering (of the Omer), which is Malkhut from the side of judgment, as there were horses of fire and a chariot of fire; but not that we say that they went up by way of the husks, God forbid; and this is strained. And likewise the clothing of the angels and their descent into this world is difficult, and several other matters. And on this matter we were confused in resolving the doubt, until YHVH enlightened the eyes of our intellect with a saying from the book of the Zohar in Parashat Vayakhel (fol. 209a), and these are his words: "And in each and every firmament there is an appointed one, and he is commanded over the world and over [the earth, to conduct all; except] the Land of Israel, which no firmament and no other power conducts, but the Holy One, blessed be He, alone; and behold, they have established it. And if you say: how does the firmament rest in vain over the Land of Israel? For behold, rain and dew descend upon it from the firmament, as upon every other land. Rather, in every firmament there are appointed ones ruling over the world; and that appointed one who rules over that firmament gives of the power that he has in that firmament, in order to give below; and that firmament takes from that appointed one and gives below to the earth. And that appointed one takes only from the residue of above. But over the Holy Land no other appointed one and no other power rules over that firmament that is over it, but the Holy One, blessed be He, alone; and He commands the Holy Land in that firmament. In each and every firmament there are known entrances; and the dominion of every appointed one is marked from entrance to entrance; and from that entrance onward he does not rule even as much as a hair; and this one does not enter into the boundary of the entrance of his fellow, except when permission is given to him to rule one over his fellow; then the kings of the earth rule one over his fellow. In the middle of all the firmaments there is one entrance, which is called Gevilon. And beneath this entrance there are seventy other entrances below, and seventy appointed ones guarding, at a distance of two thousand cubits, so that they do not draw near to it. And from that entrance a way rises above, above, until it reaches within the upper Throne; and from that entrance to every side of the firmament, up to the gate of the entrance that is called Megidon, where is the end of the firmament of the boundary of the Land of Israel. And all those seventy entrances that are marked within that entrance which is called Gevilon are all marked in the holy Throne; and all of them we call 'the gates of righteousness' (Ps. 118:19), for no other rules over them. And the Holy One, blessed be He, commands the Land of Israel in that firmament from entrance to entrance, with command, as much as is needed. And from the residue of that command those seventy appointed ones take, and give to all the other appointed ones." Thus far his words.

And his words are clear; and from it it is seen, as we explained, that over the Land of Israel there is no thing surrounding, even a cubit, except the firmament that rises above to receive from beneath the Throne of Glory. And in this thing no doubt remains for us: that all the upper ones who descend from heaven or rise, all of them rise and descend by way of the Land of Israel. And this is what the verse said (Gen. 28:17), "and this is the gate of heaven"; and the intent is a gate to enter; which is not so in other places, where there are husks dividing, and partitions: "You have covered Yourself with a cloud," etc. (Lam. 3:44), God forbid. And "the air of the land of the nations defiles," and the air of the Land of Israel purifies; and "the air of the Land of Israel makes wise"; for the husks do not rule in it at all. And so they further explained this matter in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 141a), and these are his words: "In the Holy Land all is set in order in another fashion; for the strong husk is broken from that place, so that no husk rules in it at all. The strong husk is broken from that place always, and opened from this side and from that side; and that opening was in the Holy Land at all the time that they served the service as is fitting. When sins caused it, they drew that opening to this side and to that side, until the husk drew near, all as one. When the husk closed over the brain, then that husk ruled over them and pushed them outside that place. And with all this, even though it pushed them outside, that husk could not rule in that holy place, which is not its place. And if you say: if so, since that strong husk cannot rule in that holy place, why does it stand destroyed? For destruction is not in the world except from the side of that strong husk. Rather, certainly when it was destroyed, it was destroyed only from that side, at the hour that it closed over the brain. And the Holy One, blessed be He, made it so that that strong husk should not rule over that place. And when He pushed Israel from it, that husk returned and was opened as before. And because the holy people were not there, a holy covering, a thin veil, covers over that opening, to guard that place, so that that strong husk not close it; and it holds on all its sides. For the greatness of holiness to be upon the land as before, it cannot; for that thin covering holds, so that it does not descend below; for the holy people are not there; and therefore the ruin has not been built since the day they were destroyed. For that strong husk to rule, it cannot; for that thin covering holds it on all its sides, in that opening, so that it does not rule there and does not close over the brain. That covering, the thin veil, is from within the drawing of the holy veil above, which guards that place. And because of this, all the souls of the other peoples who dwell in the land, when they go out from this world, it does not receive them, and pushes them outside; and they go and wander and roll in several rollings, until they go out from all the Holy Land and go round to their side in their impurity. And all those souls of Israel that go out there rise, and that thin covering receives them, and they enter the upper holiness; because every kind goes to its kind. And the souls of Israel that go out outside the Holy Land, in the domain of that strong husk, go and go round and roll until it returns to its place and enters the place that is fitting for it. Happy," etc. Thus far his words.

And all his words are clear and pure; and they are a mighty proof and a broad explanation for our matter: that in the Land of Israel there is no husk at all, so that they would not need to pass by way of the husks, God forbid. And likewise the souls of the wicked, that is to say, the wicked of the nations, are rolled outside, as it is written (1 Sam. 25:29), "and the souls of your enemies, them shall He sling out, as from the hollow of a sling." For the gate of heaven to enter into holiness is the Land of Israel; and because of this prophecy dwells only in the Land of Israel. And there is no objection from the prophecy of Ezekiel, which was outside the Land; for our Rabbis, of blessed memory, have already answered it. And there is no objection from the matter of the generation of the wilderness; for the air of the Land of Israel went with them. For if you do not say so, how did they eat holy things outside the Land? Rather, the air and the firmaments and the heavens and the windows and the princes all journeyed with the Shekhinah, who journeyed with them. And this is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 140b), and these are his words: "As it is written, 'And it came to pass on the day that Moses had finished [kallot]' (Num. 7:1): that the bride [kallat] of Moses descended to the earth. And if you say: in every place va-yehi is nothing but the language of sorrow, and here it is written va-yehi be-yom. Rather, on that day that the Shekhinah descended to the earth, an accuser was found toward her, and that darkness and gloom covered toward her, so that she should not descend," etc. "And at that time all the assemblies of the upper angels were found before the Holy One, blessed be He; they said before Him: Master of the world, all our radiance and all our light is in the Shekhinah of Your glory; and now she will descend to the lower ones? At that hour the Shekhinah was strengthened and broke that darkness and gloom, as one who breaks strong bars, and descended to the earth. When all of them saw so, they opened and said, 'O YHVH our Lord, how mighty is Your name in all the earth' (Ps. 8:2): mighty, certainly; for she broke several bars and strong hosts and descended to the earth and ruled over all. And therefore it is written va-yehi be-yom: the sorrow that several hosts and camps received on the day that the bride of Moses descended to the earth." Thus far his words.

And the matter of the darkness and the gloom is known. And besides these there was an accuser, and he did not give place to open a gate to descend in any way, except by way of breaking. And besides the accuser, the holy hosts were saying, "all our radiance and all our light," etc. And when she descended, she did not need the breaking of the accuser and the holy hosts; rather she needed the darkness and the gloom, to annul it, which is the shield so that she not descend. And that gate and air went with them until the entering into the Land of Israel, to her place fitting for her; and there is the rest of the holiness; for there is the gate of heaven, as we explained:

Now we are obliged to explain the benefit of this husk and its matter in the world; for to say that it is to punish, etc., does not suffice. For we will ask: the whole substance of the punishment, is not its cause the evil inclination and the husk? Let there be no husk, and there will be no evil inclination. And we say that the reason for their creation by the will of the Creator is that the world and the creatures needed to receive their sustenance and their livelihood by the power of judgment and righteousness and uprightness. And if they were all angels, without choice in their deeds, the world would not be rewarded for their action, because they are compelled in their action like angels. And for this it was necessary that man be a master of choice, and that he be composed of the evil inclination and the good inclination; so that if he wishes by his nature to incline to the good, the evil inclination will be at his left to oppose him, to incline him to evil; and when he wishes to incline after evil, the good inclination will be at his right to chastise him and to remind him of the words of his Creator; in such a way that he receives reward for the inclining to one of the extremes, whether good or whether evil. And "to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings" (Jer. 17:10), it was necessary that there be the impure side, the servant who rebels against his master, to chastise the wicked according to his wickedness, by number, and to seek out his wickedness, and that he cleave to the fitting side, and there receive his punishment. And this matter is well explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 163a), and these are his words: "All that the Holy One, blessed be He, made above and below, all of it is to show His glory, and all of it is for His service. And who has seen a servant who rebels, that he should be an accuser of his master, and in all that is the desire [re'uta] of his master he becomes an accuser? The desire of the Holy One, blessed be He, is that human beings be always in His service in this world and go in the way of truth, in order to give them merit with several good things. Since the desire of the Holy One, blessed be He, is in this, how does an evil servant come and is found an accuser against the desire of his master, and leads human beings astray to an evil way, distances them from the good way, and makes them not do the desire of their Master? Rather, certainly he does the desire of his Master. [It is like] a king who had an only son, and he loved him greatly, and commanded him in love not to draw himself near to an evil woman; because whoever draws near to her is not worthy to enter within the palace of the king. That son agreed to do the desire of his father in love. In the king's house, outside, there was a harlot, fair of appearance and beautiful of form. After some days the king said: I wish to see the desire of my son toward me. He called that harlot and said to her: Go and seduce my son, to see the desire of my son toward me. That harlot, what did she do? She went after the king's son and began to embrace him, to kiss him, and to seduce him with several seductions. If that son is fitting and obeys and listens to the command of his father, he rebukes her and does not obey her and pushes her away from him. Then his father rejoices in his son and brings him within the curtain of his palace and gives him gifts and presents and great honour. Who caused all this honour to that son? Say, that harlot. And does that harlot have praise in this, or not? Certainly she has praise from every side: one, that she did the command of the king; and one, that she caused to that son all this honour, all this goodness, all this love of the king toward him. And therefore it is written (Gen. 1:31), 'and behold, it was good [tov]': this is the angel of life; 'very' [me'od]: this is the angel of death; who is certainly very good for whoever obeys the command of his master. And come and see: if this accuser were not, the righteous would not inherit those upper treasures that they are destined to inherit in the world to come. Happy are those who have met him, this accuser, and happy are those who have not met him. Happy are those who have met him and been saved from him; for because of him they inherit all those good things and all that bliss and all those longings of the world to come; of which it is written (Isa. 64:3), 'Eye has not seen, O God, beside You, what He will do for him that waits for Him.' And happy are those who have not met him; for because of him they would inherit Gehinnom and be driven from the land of the living: those who do not obey their Master and are drawn after him. And therefore the righteous should hold him a good [turn]; for because of him they inherit all those good things and bliss and longings in the world to come. The benefit of this accuser, when the wicked obey him, what is it? Rather, even though he has no benefit, he does the command of his Master. And further, he is strengthened by this: since he is evil, he is strengthened when he does evil. The wicked man is not strengthened until he kills human beings; when he kills human beings, then he is strengthened and prevails in his power and has rest. So that accuser, who is called the angel of death, does not prevail in his power until he leads human beings astray and accuses them and kills them; then he has rest and is strengthened and prevails in his power, when the wicked obey him and he rules over them. May the Compassionate One save us. And happy are those who merit to overcome him and to subdue him, to merit because of him the world to come; and a man is strengthened in the Holy King always. Of this it is said (Ps. 84:6), 'Happy is the man whose strength is in You; in whose heart are the highways.' Happy are they in this world and in the world to come." Thus far his words.

And his words are clear and refined as silver is refined; and it is a clear reason that the husk is a need on high, fitting for the world, fitting for the righteous. And we have a further fine reason on the matter of the evil inclination. And it is that it is known that the action of the upper roots is handed over into the hand of man, in the matter of his saying (Deut. 32:18), "Of the Rock that begot you you are unmindful [teshi, read as weaken]"; and likewise the matter of "who rides upon the heavens in your help" (Deut. 33:26); and likewise the matter that they turn the attribute of judgment to the attribute of compassion and the attribute of compassion to the attribute of judgment, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance; and we shall explain the matters of its reason in the Gate of the Soul, with the help of Heaven. And now it was necessary that man be composed of judgment and of compassion, so that through these two branches he act above on the concealed roots.

And behold, the evil inclination is from the side of Gevurah, and the good inclination from the side of Chesed; even though the evil inclination is in the secret of the husk and the good inclination in the secret of holiness. And when the upright man's inclination prevails over him and seeks to incline him from the straight way to a way that is not good, it points to the husk prevailing to act by the power of Gevurah that flows upon it, from which is its drawing; and then judgment prevails over compassion. And when the upright man, by the power of his intellect, makes the good inclination prevail over the evil inclination, then it points to subduing the power of the husk; and the judgment is sweetened, and the power of compassion prevails, and the attribute of judgment is turned to the attribute of compassion. And all this is in the secret of the branches that are in the hand of the upright man, to arbitrate them and to incline them to one of the sides. And when, God forbid, the wicked man makes the evil inclination prevail over the good inclination, it points to the power of Gevurah ruling over the power of compassion; and judgment is present, and the husk prevails. And this is what they, of blessed memory, said: "Cursed are the wicked, who turn the attribute of compassion to the attribute of judgment." For through the lower actions, in the secret of the branches, the roots act. And this is the reason that the Holy One, blessed be He, created the evil inclination: so that it can be subdued beneath the hand of the good inclination; and then the attribute of judgment is turned to the attribute of compassion, and the upper roots draw from the radiance of the upper light and are united in a complete union. And this is a complete reason on the matter of the evil inclination. And there is a further, finer reason, supported by the words of Rashbi in the Zohar. And it is that the matter of the husk: its cause was because of the spreading out, as we explained in the first chapter. (And behold, the spreading out, its cause is the first Adam), as we explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation, chapter 6, in general.

And behold, he is found to be the one who perverted, and he was the cause of the corruption; therefore he needed to be the one who sets right what he corrupted. And by what? He subdues the power of the husk when he makes the good inclination prevail over the evil inclination; and the husk is subdued and broken; and then he sets right what was corrupted because of him. And apart from this, he purifies the impure: for when he subdues it and brings it into the fulfilment of the commandment, he returns it to holiness, and it is purified through him; and then he brings it into holiness as it was before; and the husk is included in holiness, and all is pure, as we explained in the first chapter. And certainly the evil inclination is purified and becomes the good inclination. And so Rashbi explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Bo, fol. 43a), and these are his words: "This commandment: to redeem the firstling of an ass, and to break the neck of the firstling of an ass if one does not redeem it; as it is written, 'And every firstling of an ass you shall redeem with a lamb; and if you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck' (Exod. 13:13). And this secret: the evil inclination can return in repentance, and it becomes the good inclination; as they established, 'If he merits, a help; if he does not merit, against him' (cf. Gen. 2:18). Because they are one likeness, one of a lamb and one of an ass; and if he merits to return in repentance, even though he is an ass, an ignorant man, 'you shall redeem' from exile 'with a lamb,'" etc. Thus far his words, as relevant to our matter. And from it it is explained that the evil inclination is purified and becomes the good inclination; and this is "you shall redeem with a lamb," etc. And the matter is in the way that we explained: that he performs the action of commandments, and behold, the evil inclination becomes the good inclination, and the like. And likewise it is expounded elsewhere in the Zohar, that he said: "The evil inclination above, who is it? Gevurah." He taught that the evil inclination can be from the side of Gevurah, from the side of the wine that gladdens, not from the side of the wine that intoxicates. And likewise now the husk and the intoxicating wine are set right in the secret of the tefillin, which are the Torah: he sets it right and sweetens it, and it becomes the wine that gladdens; for he returns it to its source, and it is purified. And by this is understood the matter expounded in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 61a), these are his words: "Come and see: if Adam had brought out offspring from the Garden of Eden, they would not have been destroyed for generations of generations, and the light of the moon would never have been darkened; for all of them would have endured forever. And even the upper angels would not stand before them in light and radiance and wisdom; as it is said, 'in the image of God He created him' (Gen. 1:27). But since he caused sin, and went out from the Garden, and made offspring outside, they did not endure in the world and were not as is fitting. Rabbi Hezekiah said: And how could they make offspring there? For if he had not drawn upon himself the evil inclination and sinned, he would have endured in the world alone, and would not make offspring. Likewise, if Israel had not sinned with the calf and drawn upon themselves the evil inclination, they would never have made offspring, and later generations would never have come. He said to him: If Adam had not sinned, he would not have made offspring in this fashion [from the side of the evil inclination; but he would have made offspring from the side of the holy spirit]; for now he makes offspring only from the side of the evil inclination. And because all the offspring of human beings are all from the side of the evil inclination, therefore they have no endurance; for it is impossible for them to endure, because the Other Side is mixed in them. But if Adam had not sinned and had not been driven from the Garden of Eden, he would have made offspring from the side of the holy spirit, holy like the upper angels, enduring for generations of generations, after the pattern of above. Since he sinned and begot children outside the Garden, and did not merit to bring them out from the Garden, they did not endure, even to take root in this world, until Noah came," etc. Thus far his words.

And behold, explicitly: while he was in the Garden of Eden there was in him power to beget from the side of the holy spirit; for this was the beginning of the intent. And he drew upon himself the evil inclination, in that he made the power of the husk prevail over him, and its power prevailed over him. And through this man is compelled to set right and to sweeten the evil inclination, and to return it in its root to the wine that gladdens, as we explained:

What is intended now is to explain, on the matter of the husks, that they have ten sefirot and seven palaces, like the matter of holiness; for they are over against holiness "as an ape before a man." And just as the side of holiness draws effluence and sustenance for all its pure creatures, so the husk draws and bestows sustenance and effluence for many creatures that are on its side. And this is the reason for the forbidden and the permitted, the impure and the pure, the unfit and the fit. For just as the side of whiteness and purity comes from the side of Chesed, which is the likeness of the elder, "You shall rise up before the hoary head" (Lev. 19:32), so there is whiteness in impurity and husk; and it is "the guilty elder" [zaken ashmai], who is desolate, and the root of desolation and "destruction decreed" (Isa. 10:22). And just as there is permitted redness and blood of purity on the side of Gevurah, which is the side that returns to the pure arbitration, and this is the one who conquers his inclination, as we explained above, so there is impure and forbidden redness and blood. And just as there is green on the side of compassion, the middle line, from the side of Tiferet, where fitness and goodness are, so there is the green gall, which kills by a drop from which "his face turns green" [cf. Avodah Zarah 20b], and the unfitness and the evil; for these are over against those.
