And just as these three, which are Chesed, Judgment, Compassion, are included in ten sefirot, as we explained at the end of the Gate of Essence and Governance, so these three have ten sefirot in the accusing husks, as we shall explain. However, on these names the explanations are many, and we shall abbreviate the much into the little that suffices:

The first is called Te'omiel. The explanation: it is from the language of te'omim [twins], in the attribute that rebelled against the Lord, blessed be He, and makes itself as a twin to Him; like "for a servant when he reigns … and a handmaid that is heir to her mistress" (Prov. 30:22–23). And there is no wonder at the name El being found in the likeness of the husks; for just as there is the name El on the side of holiness, so there is another el; and this is what the verse says (Num. 24:4), "He says, who hears the words of El"; and he explained in the Zohar: "this is another el." And there are those who received the name of this husk as Tumiel, without Alef; and the explanation is that their whole intent is to make an end and to finish [le-hatem] the holiness, God forbid, and to diminish it from watching over. And these two names Rashbi related, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 105a; see there), to the husks that are over against Netzach and Hod. And to the first husk he related there the name Katriel, to show that it is a crown [keter] to the other husks; and from this husk is the karet [cutting off]; for it is sometimes called Kartiel, and through it the wicked are cut off. And there are those who received the name of this husk as Kamtiel; and possibly as we explained in Kartiel; and its matter is kamat, from the language of "who were cut down [kummetu] before their time" (Job 22:16). And now this matter is precise: "who were cut down before their time," that is, the nine hundred and seventy-four generations that were cut down and cut off before their time, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (in Chagigah 13b):

The second is called Ogiel. And he explained the reason: that it is a hindrance [ugah] to its fellow; so Nachmanides, of blessed memory, explained. And it is possible to explain it from the language of "would you therefore shut yourselves off [te'agenah]?" (Ruth 1:13); and the intent is that it holds back the effluence and prevents the providence, like a screen that divides between Israel and their Father in heaven. And there are those who read Go'iel, and explain it from the language of "or does the ox low [yig'eh] over his fodder [belilo]?" (Job 6:5); and the intent is that it lows to confuse [levalel] the Emanation and to tear down the building. And possibly from the language of gevi'ah [expiring]; for the aim of its face is to make expire and to destroy all the holy things. And there are those who read without Vav, Ga'iel, or Aga'el; and possibly one can explain it in the way that I explained it with Vav. And in the Tikkunim (there) Rashbi called this sefirah "the man of Belial": for the holy Chokhmah is called Adam, as is explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles; and this, which is over against it, is called the man [adam] of Belial. And these names, Ogiel, etc., he related to over against Tiferet. And there are those who called this husk Beli'el; and the intent is clear: for it denies the existence of God; and this is beli El [without God]:

The third is called Sitriel; for it hides [mastir] the face of compassion, in the matter of "You have covered Yourself with a cloud," etc. (Lam. 3:44). And others call it Harsiel; and the explanation is the language of harisah [tearing down], that it tears down. And the intent is that it is the reverse of Binah: for Binah causes the Godhead to dwell and reveals it, and likewise she builds the building of holiness; and this one conceals the Godhead and tears down the building. And in this way we can explain Sitriel from the language of setirah [demolition]. And in the Tikkunim (there) Rashbi called it Se'iriel; and from there is Esau, "a hairy [sa'ir] man" (Gen. 27:11); and from there "the hair of a woman is nakedness." And there are those who called it Itiel; and possibly one can explain it from the language of "a man in readiness [itti]" (Lev. 16:21); and the intent is that it is ready to make itself a god, like the matter of the calf that came into being of itself. And the commentators wrote that these three husks were annihilated in a moment; and these are the matter of "He built worlds and destroyed them." And according to their opinion these three kinds of impurity are not in existence, and there are only seven husks. And this thing is not right with the explanation of the Zohar; for explicitly Rashbi explains (there in the Tikkunim) that they are ten kinds of husks; and he calls them ten lower crowns, and over against them ten he-asses and ten she-asses. And possibly their intent in the matter of the annihilation is that its providence is absent from the world; and this too is not right; for behold, Se'iriel is the third husk, and behold, from it is Esau, "a hairy man," and likewise "the hair of a woman is nakedness":

The fourth is called Ga'ash Kalah. And Nachmanides explained that it is appointed over bands of hosts, bands of the jealous; and in its jealousy, in which it is jealous of the purity, it storms [go'esh] and quakes and destroys [mekhaleh] several souls; and then even "the angels of peace weep bitterly" (Isa. 33:7). Thus far. And in the Tikkunim (there) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that this husk is called Uziel; and from there are Uza and Azael, who are two powers of impurity. And likewise he called it Chazriel: "The boar [chazir] out of the wood ravages it" (Ps. 80:14). And others said that it is called Samael; and others related Samael to another place, as we shall explain:

The fifth is called Golahav. And the explanation is as "they are driven forth from among [gev] men" (Job 30:5); and the intent is that it is a body [guf] of flame [lahav]; for from this is the beginning of the bodies that are covered over from human beings, etc.; and its throne is surrounded by flames of fire; and if not for the delight of the Name, may He be blessed, in His creatures, the bands of its hosts would destroy all the lower creatures in a moment. And others explained that gu is from the language of "within," the Aramaic language; and its matter is that it is within the flame, etc. And others explained that it is called Za'afiel; and the intent is from the language of za'af [rage]; for it is the prince of rage; and YHVH save us. And in the Tikkunim (there) he called it Agagiel, and said that from there is Agag king of Amalek:

The sixth is called Tagrinon. And the intent is that it is ready to put strife [tigra] between the kings with a loud voice of crying, which confounds. And others wrote that it is called Za'amiel; and possibly it is the prince of indignation [za'am]. And in the Tikkunim (there) he called it Ogiel, over against the central pillar; and from there is Og king of Bashan. And the word Ogiel was explained above:

The seventh is called Arvazrak. And the intent is that it is like a cruel raven [orev] and intends to throw away [lizrok] its young. Further explanation: at the time of its receiving from holiness it is sweet [arev] to it, and after it receives from the husk it hates that effluence and throws it away. And it is possible for us to explain that at first it is sweet to a man in its speech, and "smoother than oil is its palate" (Prov. 5:3); and afterward it throws to him a deadly poison, and he finds "the gall of asps" in its honey (cf. Job 20:14). And others wrote that it is called Katzpiel, the prince of the outburst [ketzef]:

The eighth is Samael the wicked. And there is no need for length on its matter; for it is well known that he is the accuser of Israel. And in the Tikkunim there he explained that husks seven and eight are Te'omiel and Tumiel; and he said that from there is "the depths [tehomot] cover them" (Exod. 15:5). And others wrote that it is called Rogziel; and possibly it is the prince of agitation [rogez]:

The ninth is Gamliel. And the Geonim say concerning this husk: "There is an accuser in the multitude on high, Gamliel by name. And when he draws nourishment from the (perhaps one should read: from the gazers of the) heavens, all his hosts are hosts of peace; and when they are seen by human beings, they have permission to be seen by them in the form of a man, and they tell them future things. And when he draws nourishment from the accuser who is over him, at known times, his name is turned and he is called Nachashiel; and all his hosts are hosts of terror, in the likeness of serpents, terrifying human beings." Thus far the explanation of the Geonim. And it is possible that when it draws nourishment from the side of purity it is called Gamliel, for the reason that it too [gam] has a drawing from the side of purity; and when it draws nourishment from the husk it is called Nachashiel, to say that the serpent [nachash] is its god and its power. And others called this husk Avriel; and possibly it is the prince of rage [evrah]. And in the Tikkunim (there) he called it "Samael the uncircumcised"; for over against the circumcision is the foreskin:

The tenth is called Lilith. And she receives from all the husks, like the purity; and she is called the wife of harlotry. And in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 70a), he explained that the tenth rung in the husks is called "one who inquires of the dead" (Deut. 18:11). And the other names of the husks are explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles:

The ancients explained that there are two Liliths, one small and one great. The great one is the mate of Samael, and she is the wife of harlotry; and the small one is the mate of Ashmedai, as will be explained in the Gate of the Palaces of the Substitutes, with the help of the Name. And concerning this Lilith, the bride of Samael, the Geonim explained: "There are under her hand four hundred and eighty hosts, as the reckoning of her name; and they go out on Yom Kippur to the deserts; she goes and howls, for she is the prince of howling. And Machalat the daughter of Ishmael is also the concubine of Samael; and they go out with four hundred and seventy-eight hosts; she goes and sings in the holy tongue song and praise. And when they meet one another they quarrel, on Yom Kippur, there in the desert; they strive with one another until their voice rises to heaven, and the earth quakes at their voice. And all this the Holy One, blessed be He, does, so that they not plead accusation against Israel in their prayer." And others wrote that this husk is called Meshulchael; and the reason is that it sends [meshallachat] evil angels; may the Compassionate One save us. And we have found written: "Samael the wicked and Lilith the foolish are like one coupling, by means of a groomsman who receives the emanation of wickedness and insolence from this one and bestows it to that one. And of this secret it is said (Isa. 27:1), 'In that day YHVH with His sore sword,' etc., 'shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, and leviathan the crooked serpent; and He shall slay the dragon [tannin] that is in the sea.' Leviathan [livyatan]: the explanation, the joining and coupling [levayah] of the two of them, who are like serpents; therefore he doubled: 'the piercing serpent,' over against Samael; 'the crooked serpent,' over against Lilith. 'And He shall slay the dragon that is in the sea': just as there is a pure leviathan in the sea, according to its plain sense, and it is called tannin, so there is a great impure tannin in the sea, according to its plain sense; and likewise above, by way of the concealed. And the tannin above is a blind prince, who is like a middle groomsman between Samael and Lilith; and his name is Taniniver; and it is as tannin iver [blind dragon]. And the masters of the Kabbalah said that that tannin that is in the sea is without eyes; and likewise the tannin above is like a spiritual form without colors, which are the eyes; therefore his name is Taniniver. And he is the one who joins the accompaniment and the coupling between Samael and Lilith. If he had been created whole, in the completeness of his emanation, he would destroy the world in one moment. And when the will comes, and the emanation that comes from the side of Samael and Lilith by means of the blind prince is diminished and lacking, in complete destruction, then the saying of the prophet will be fulfilled: 'In that day YHVH will punish,' etc." Thus far his words.

And it appears that the truth is with them; for in many places (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 138, and in Tikkun 31, fol. 74a) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that Samael and Lilith are over against Tiferet and Malkhut; and they are called heaven and earth; and of them it is said (Isa. 51:6), "for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment." But of Tiferet and Malkhut it is said, "Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice" (Ps. 96:11); and likewise it is said of Tiferet and Malkhut, "Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" (Isa. 30:26). And of Samael and Lilith it is said (Isa. 24:23), "Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed," etc. And there is no doubt that, just as there is a pure and holy leviathan, from the coupling of Tiferet and Malkhut, and it is Yesod, so there is on the side of impurity a power that joins these powers together; and it is blind. For if it had eyes, the impure coupling would be complete, God forbid, and they would destroy the world. But in holiness it has eyes; and of it it is said (Eccl. 2:14), "The wise man's eyes are in his head," as we explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, in the entry livyatan. However, of this leviathan it is said (Job 11:20), "But the eyes of the wicked shall fail." And the Geonim explained that Samael too has twelve powers, just as Tiferet has twelve powers, as we explained on the matter of the boundaries. And the names of the powers are these; and this is the copy of their language: "Samael is the fourth emanated, after the three destroying powers that were wiped out from the world, which are Kamtiel, Beliel, Itiel; and Samael is fourth to them. And from him were emanated twelve spoiling, cursed powers, accusing the twelve tribes of Yah, upper and lower; each prince of them evil, evil. And these are their names:

"The first prince, Ba'ariron; and he is so called on account of his being fourth, and also full of evil. The second prince, Adamiron; his colors are like blood mixed in water. The third, Tzelel Damiron; his colors are like the appearance of clear blood. The fourth, Shichrinon; his colors are all black. The fifth, Shalhaviron; his colors are like the likeness of a flame of fire. The sixth, Afriron; his colors are the likeness of dust. The seventh, Avireron; his colors are the likeness of the clouds that cause in the world all kinds of injuries. The eighth, Nechushtiron, another version Nechashikhon; his colors are like the colour of brass. The ninth, Nechashiron; (his colors are like the colour of serpents, he and all his camp. The tenth, Dagdagiron; his colors) are the likeness of great fishes, and the colors are like the likeness of the signs of the impure. The eleventh, Behemiron; he and all his camp, colors the likeness of beasts or wild animals; and he is a prince ruling over a thousand strong princes in the mountains; and each and every prince of them, a thousand is his camp; and this is the secret of 'the cattle upon a thousand hills' (Ps. 50:10). The twelfth, Neshimiron; he and all his camp, the form of evil women, and more harmful than all the harmful bands. And the masters of this wisdom, who are expert in use, say, by way of tradition and practice, that his name is also Chatulariron; and sometimes he and all his camp are seen like the likeness of great cats." Thus far. Thus far what we have found on the matter of the impure sefirot and the husks in the words of the Geonim, peace be upon them, and the commentators and the Zohar. And we have abbreviated much in them, because these things are not our intent, but only a notice to the inquirer, so that he succeed in the explanation of the Torah and its secrets; and apart from this we have in it neither portion nor knowledge:

What is intended in this chapter is to save those lacking knowledge from error: let not the thinker think that the husks enter within the pure and holy Emanation, God forbid, far be it, far be it; for whoever thinks this forfeits his head to his Owner. And what is found in some places that would show that the husks enter beneath the holiness is neither in the world of Atzilut nor in the world of Beriah, but it is in the world of Yetzirah; it is the world of Metatron; for "the wicked walk on every side" of it (Ps. 12:9). And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the book of the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 227), and these are his words: "Above, in the Tree of Life, there are no husks; 'for none might enter into the king's gate clothed with sackcloth' (Esth. 4:2). Below there are husks, in Metatron, who is in the likeness of the central pillar. For at the time that the Holy One, blessed be He, is apart from His Kingdom, He is covered with the wings and faces of His servant Metatron; as it is written (2 Sam. 22:11), 'And He rode upon a cherub, and did fly.' And those husks that surround the four living creatures of Metatron are: tohu [formlessness]: 'and behold, a great and strong wind rent the mountains and broke in pieces the rocks … but YHVH was not in the wind' (1 Kings 19:11). Bohu [void]: 'and after the wind an earthquake; but YHVH was not in the earthquake.' Behold two husks, green and white. For the husks of the nut: one, tohu, the green line; the second, bohu, slimy stones, a hard husk like slimy stone. Corresponding to these two husks, the chaff and the straw of the wheat. The third husk is thin, corresponding to the bran of the wheat; for so it cleaves to the wheat and cannot be separated from there until they grind it with millstones, which correspond to the molars of the mouth of a man, who must grind with them the words of Torah until they are like flour of clean fine flour; and in the sieve, which is the lip, the refuse, which is bran, is sorted out, until the law is found clean fine flour. At that time the heart and the brain and all the limbs of the body, in which the soul spreads out, take it; and the soul is sustained by it, just as the body is sustained by the things of the world; for 'God has made the one over against the other': the bread of the body and the bread of the Torah; as it is written (Prov. 9:5), 'Come, eat of my bread.' And this husk is like the husk that cleaves to the kernel of the nut. And at the time that the nut is soft, that husk separates from the kernel of the nut without difficulty; and at the time that the nut is dry, it is hard for a man to remove it from there; for still 'the difficulty stands in its place.' And therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded man to return in repentance in his youth, before the evil inclination grows old in him; as it is written (Lev. 19:32), 'You shall rise up before the hoary head': before your hoary head. And this husk is fire, and it is aroused in it: 'and after the earthquake a fire; but YHVH was not in the fire.' The fourth, the abyss [tehom], the hollow of the nut; in it is 'a still small voice'; there the King comes; 'and out of the midst thereof as the colour of chashmal, out of the midst of the fire' (Ezek. 1:4)," etc. Thus far his words.

And we shall not withhold our hands from explaining this saying, because of its great benefit. He said "above, in the Tree of Life," because there is the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil. And the Tree of Life is Tiferet in particular, and in general all the Emanation; for there is life, and there is no death except in the place of the husks, which are round about the world of Metatron, which is the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil; as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 51, fol. 85), these are his words: "And the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil is below: the Tree of Knowledge, good, this is Metatron; and evil, this is Samael." Thus far his words, in brief, because of the great length. And from here is a demolition of the one who says that the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil is in Malkhut; for it is an error in their hand. And what is found in Rashbi, peace be upon him, that sometimes he calls Malkhut the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, is by way of borrowing; for all that is below Malkhut is related to her; and its principal is in Metatron; and it was borrowed for Malkhut because "her feet," which are Metatron, "go down to death" (Prov. 5:5), which are the husks. And he related the husks to the name Samael, because he is their messenger for every quarrel and for every plague, for every iniquity and for every sin, as is well known in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in several places, and in several midrashim and aggadot in the Talmud. And let us return to the saying, which said that in the Tree of Life there are no husks; for it is a kernel without a husk. And he proved this from the verse "for none might enter into the king's gate clothed with sackcloth [sak]," as we wrote in the entry sak; and sak is the husk. And for this reason those who return wear sackcloth, to show that they take upon themselves the pain and the affliction of the sackcloth in this world, because they hated the knowledge of the holy ones and made the sackcloth king over them. And it is possible to say concerning it that sak is an acronym of sone kedoshim [hater of the holy ones]; and in permutation it is kash [stubble]; and they are the stubble and the straw that are in the grain; and they are hard as sinews. "Below there are husks, in Metatron": he is the Tree of Knowledge, good, and evil round about him, like the likeness of the husk and the fruit. "Who is in the likeness," etc.: he intended to explain to us that all that we say, that the husks enter within the holiness and rule over it, and the like, the matter is in Metatron, who is over against Tiferet and the sefirot; and Tiferet is covered and concealed sometimes within him, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA. And for this reason we say that they enter the sefirot; for one who touches the garment of the king is as one who touches the king himself. And we know that according to this it will be difficult for the inquirer from many sayings of the Zohar, and especially in Parashat Acharei (fol. 79), these are his words: "For we have learned: at the hour that the strong serpent is aroused because of the sins of the world, it begins and joins with the female and casts filth into her; the male separates from her, because she is defiled and is called impure, and it is not fitting for the male to draw near to her," etc., "at the time that she is defiled." Thus far his words.

And the inquirer will imagine that what he said, that it cast filth into her, is that it had intercourse with her, God forbid, and cast filth into her; as they wrote that the serpent came upon Eve, according to its plain sense, God forbid, far be it, far be it; for who has put forth his hand to this and been guiltless? And the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, are "deep waters," etc., "but a man of understanding will draw it out" (Prov. 20:5). We have already written in the Gate of Channels (chapter 4) on the matter of the two channels that are in Yesod, one to the right and one to the left; for "from my flesh I shall see God" (Job 19:26). And just as in man there are two passages, one for the holy seed and one for the impure surplus, so above the surplus comes into being in Gevurah; for there is the refining of the silver and the gold, as we explained in the first chapter.

And behold, when merit and uprightness and happiness and righteousness and fitness multiply in this world, then Malkhut is aroused from the side of the souls of the righteous, which are the female waters, and they are the cause of arousal, as is explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance; and then she draws from the side of the good oil; "and iniquity stops her mouth" (Ps. 107:42), and "all wickedness shall vanish like smoke." And when the people of this world are the reverse, then Malkhut draws from the side of the surplus, from the channel that bestows the dross of the silver and the dross of the gold, which is the impure effluence fitting for the husk. And the matter is that since Malkhut has nothing by which to be aroused and to claim the effluence, and there is no merit on which to depend, then the serpent is aroused and pleads accusation with the iniquities and transgressions done in the world, and begins to provoke and to accuse, and says: Master of the world, what have You seen to bestow blessings and good upon Israel? Behold my children, who are the seventy nations, whose souls are emanated from the husk, uncover nakedness, and Israel uncover nakedness; these worship idols, and these worship idols. And since it is so, give me the portion of my children. And then, God forbid, the power of strong judgment is aroused upon the enemies of Israel. And so they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 50), these are his words: "And they are to distance the Satan from them, so that he not draw near to the Throne, which is the heart, to claim judgment against the holy limbs, which are Israel; and the heart is the Shekhinah among them." Thus far his words.

That is to say, "to distance the Satan from them, so that he not draw near to the Throne": that is, the Throne of Glory, the world of Beriah. And when the husk enters into the world of Metatron, as we explained, it certainly draws near to the Throne, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA; for the world of Beriah is the Throne. And he was precise in saying that his nearness there is "to claim judgment": that is, that he says, these uncover nakedness and these uncover nakedness, etc.; and then the judgment is bestowed to the Shekhinah upon the enemies of Israel; and that is "the heart and the limbs" that he spoke of. And because of his crying, Malkhut does not draw from the side of the holy channel, but draws from the side of the left channel, in which the surplus and the dross are bestowed; and then the serpent is wound about her heel to receive this bitter effluence; for this is his power, his god. And then the Shekhinah tastes the bitternesses of that evil effluence. And this is the matter of "and casts filth into her": not that the intent is that he rises above, God forbid; but the intent is that through his arousal there is bestowed upon her what is more bitter than death.

And behold, this bitter effluence is the blood of menstruation; and these are the stains that defile; and then the woman defiles the one who has intercourse with her, like the menstruant herself. And it is already known that "the portion of Jacob is not like these" (Jer. 10:16); for his inheritance is an inheritance without boundaries, and "in his joy a stranger does not intermeddle" (Prov. 14:10). And therefore she does not come to the King; for she is defiled, God forbid; and then the King does not come to her until after she is purified and reveals the light of her face, which was hidden, and whose lights were darkened. And she counts days, a number sevenfold, so that "the light of the moon be as the light of the sun"; and then she immerses in the waters of a ritual pool of forty se'ahs, which is a known palace in which Malkhut receives her purity and her adornments; and it is explained in the Tikkunim and in the Ra'aya Meheimna at length. And afterward she is united with her husband. And therefore you will find that after the great agitation, its end is compassion and favour.
And behold, the husks never enter within holiness, God forbid. And this is enough of a notice to the inquirer, and a warning, that he not stumble forever and ever:

Let us return to the explanation of the saying we were in: "And those husks," etc. Our principal intent in this chapter, in the explanation of the rest of this saying, is on the matter of a mighty question that falls in this inquiry. For what is understood from this saying and from many other sayings appears to be that the husks are three, apart from that thin one, which is "the still small voice," as we shall explain. And above, in chapter 4, we explained explicitly in the name of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and the other commentators, that the husks are ten, corresponding to ten sefirot, specified and known by name. And there is a difficulty, his words against his words: for in one place he said that they are ten, and in one place he said that they are three or four. And in the answer to this question we need to know that the husks are before the holiness "as an ape before human beings." And just as the ape before the man does every deed of the man by way of mockery, wishing to resemble and not resembling, so the impurity and the husk do as the deed of holiness, whether in the matter of the souls, whether in the matter of the actions, whether in the matter of the colors. And just as the Emanation is included in three lines, the line of Chesed, the line of compassion and the line of judgment, as we spoke at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance at its end, so the impurity is included in Chesed, Judgment and Compassion. Not that the chesed is literal Chesed; rather chesed is as the Targum of "reproach," which is chisuda. And the compassion: "the compassion of the wicked is cruel" (Prov. 12:10). And the judgment needs no explanation; for it is an evil strap to lash the wicked; and further, it is the perversion of judgment, as he explained in the Zohar (Chadash, fol. 110b), in the Midrash of Lamentations, on the verse (Eccl. 12:3), "and the strong men shall bow themselves"; and the matter of their judgment will be further explained in the Palaces. And likewise in the matter of the colors: white, from there Laban [Lavan, white] the Aramean, and from there "an old and foolish king" (Eccl. 4:13), "the guilty elder." And likewise green, a sign of transgression: dropsy [hidrokan]. And likewise red: "from the red, this red [pottage]" (Gen. 25:30). And these three colors are over against the three holy colors that are in the bow. And this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 37, fol. 78a), these are his words: "Three husks there are in the foreskin, corresponding to three husks of the nut; and of them it is said, 'And the earth was formlessness and void, and darkness' (Gen. 1:2). Tohu, the green line, the first husk; bohu, the second husk; darkness, the third husk. And these three, one over another, correspond to three colors of the eye, of which it is said, 'and that you go not about after your own heart and your own eyes,' etc. (Num. 15:39). Corresponding to them, three colors of the bow, in which shines the pupil of the eye, which is a point, the sign of the covenant; of it it is said, 'and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant' (Gen. 9:16), etc. When? After the three evil husks are removed from it. And at the time that she is clothed in these husks, she says, 'Look not upon me, because I am black,' etc. (Song 1:6)." Thus far his words.

Behold, explicitly: these three husks are over against the three colors of the eye. And we have already explained above, in the Gate of Manifestations, in the name of Rashbi, that the three colors of the eye are the three Patriarchs; and so we explained in the entry Sabbath in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And likewise he said that they are the three colors of the bow; and the three colors of the bow are over against the three Patriarchs, which are fathers to Chesed, Judgment and Compassion: red, white, green. And for the reason that they are over against ChaDaR [Chesed, Din, Rachamim], therefore their annulment and their cutting down is through them. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, fol. 34b), these are his words: "And my son, until these husks of the nut are removed and broken, by teki'ah and shevarim and teru'ah: shevarim, in which is 'you shall break in pieces [shabber teshabber] their pillars' (Exod. 23:24), which are husks of the nut; and with teru'ah, 'you shall break [tero'em] them with a rod of iron' (Ps. 2:9); and with teki'ah, 'and hang them up [ve-hoka] unto YHVH against the sun' (Num. 25:4)." Thus far his words.

And it has already been explained in the Gate of Names and in the preceding gates that teki'ah, teru'ah, shevarim are over against the three Patriarchs, Chesed, Judgment and Compassion; and we explained it also in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And by this our question is answered: that they are ten and are included in three, as we explained. However, one must examine: since they are included in three, which are over against the three Patriarchs, why are they the reverse of the order of holiness? For in holiness they are white, Chesed, first; and afterward green in the middle, over against Tiferet; and the red to the left, over against Gevurah. And in the foreskin they are the reverse: for first is the green husk, and after it white, and after it darkness and fire, which are all one. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this order in the Tikkunim (there, above this), these are his words: "'And I looked, and behold, a whirlwind came out of the north' (Ezek. 1:4): this is the line of tohu, the green husk of the nut, which is the green line. 'A great cloud': the second husk, the white of the nut, and this is bohu. 'And a fire infolding itself': the third husk of the nut [and this is darkness. 'And a brightness was about it': this is the fourth husk of the nut, which] is joined to the kernel. 'And out of the midst thereof as the colour of chashmal': this is the kernel." Thus far his words.

And behold, he explained explicitly that the first is green, and the second white, and the third is darkness and fire. And it appears to answer by what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained on the verse "and God divided between the light and the darkness" (Gen. 1:4), and on the verse "Separate yourselves from among this congregation" (Num. 16:21): that the impurity and the husk do not want the arbitration; and therefore Korah and his congregation were separated, for they did not want the arbitration of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him; and they fell into Gehinnom. And we hinted at this matter in the preceding gates. And for this reason the green line, the arbiter, which is the middle line, is not in the middle between the white husk and the red, to show that they are the root of strife and quarrel, and there is no peace between them at all. And the green came first; for since it was pushed out from between the two extremes, it inclined toward the chasadim and the reproaches [cherpot], after the way of holiness; except that it inclined entirely and did not arbitrate between them. For the white is the utmost hardness, and the red, its manifestation is soft; and even if it is hard in separation and division, it cleaves to it with the utmost cleaving, as we shall explain, with the help of the Name. And the two extremes are found together, and the middle pushed outside, as we explained. And let us return to the matter of the saying: because three husks are over against the three Patriarchs, which are three living creatures of the Chariot, therefore they are husks to the living creatures that are in Metatron. And he said that they are three husks, specified by names. The first, tohu, the green line; the whirlwind in Ezekiel, and the strong wind in Elijah. And it is already known that the wind [ru'ach] is the arbiter between the fire and the water on the side of holiness; and in impurity they pushed it outside, and it inclined to the side of chesed and the reproaches, as we explained. The second, bohu, slimy stones; and the explanation of mefullamot is strong; so he explained in the Arukh, in the entry mefullam: "slimy stones, sound, moist and strong." And so it is the hardest husk of all; for the husks are the reverse of holiness; and they are moist, flowing with water: they are "the bitter waters that cause the curse" (Num. 5:18). And likewise it is called earthquake, and "a great cloud," etc.; for the cloud is from the side of the waters, in Chesed; and so this cloud is impure, in the place of the pure. And the third, fire and darkness; for it is already well known that the fire that is on the side of impurity is dark; for the black is red that has been smitten, as we explained in the Gate of Colors. And beneath these three husks is the husk that draws near to the kernel, which draws near to holiness, which is in the air [and it is the husk of Nogah]; and it is almost holiness, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Palaces of the Husks. And it is the fourth division; and it is what is between pure and impure; for it is intermediate, and it is clear. However, one may wonder: for there is no air in the nut between the thin husk and the kernel; but it is before the thin husk. And this is no doubt: for the air that we speak of is the air that there is somewhat when they are separated from one another, that is, the thin husk from the kernel. Or we may say that when it is moist, so that it is easy to be removed, as the saying explained, then there is some separation between this and that. Or we may also say that in the nut the thin husk cleaves to the kernel because of its nearness also to holiness. However it may be, the air, which is the abyss, is the husk nearer to holiness than the three preceding ones. And of the three it is said, "YHVH was not in the wind," "not in the earthquake," "not in the fire"; however, of "the still small voice" it is said, in it is YHVH. And this is "and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of chashmal"; for this fourth husk draws near to holiness most; therefore Rashbi, peace be upon him, sometimes does not mention it with the three, and it is not included in the ten impurities at all. And for this, concerning the planting of the tree, the verse said (Lev. 19:23–24), "three years shall it be as uncircumcised unto you"; for the husk always precedes the fruit; however, "in the fourth year all the fruit thereof shall be holy, for giving praise unto YHVH." For just as the firstling of an ass is holy, for it is forbidden to make use of it, and it needs redemption; and this is for the reason that, being a firstborn, it has drawn near to holiness; and if he does not redeem it, it needs its neck broken, so that the power of the husk not prevail over it and it be found separated from the place of holiness; so the fruit of the fourth year is holy and needs redemption.

And behold, the firstling of an ass, even though the owner gives it to the priest, the priest cannot make use of it unless he redeems it with a lamb. But the fruit of the fourth year, if he wishes, he may eat the fruit himself in Jerusalem, or redeem it and eat its value in Jerusalem, like the law of all second tithe. And the reason is that the ass is the portion of impurity itself, and its portion is strong; therefore it needs redemption; and even though it is in the hand of a priest, there is still a doubt lest it go out to evil ways; and even in the hand of a priest, who is the right, it needs redemption. But the fruit of the fourth year, when he eats it in Jerusalem, where there is no husk at all, neither thin nor coarse, it is enough; and in this it is clear to us that it will not go out of its holiness. But if he wishes to eat it in the outlying districts it needs redemption; for the power of holiness is not so strengthened in the outlying districts as in Jerusalem, where the place of the chashmal is; and therefore "brightness shall be about it," and it will not go outside. Thus far.
And behold, this chapter is completed, and this gate is concluded, with the help of Heaven:
The Gate of the Palaces of the Husks, which is Gate Twenty-Six:

We have already hinted above that these husks resemble the Emanation in their matter "as an ape before human beings." And therefore, just as in holiness there are seven palaces, which are a dwelling and garment for ten sefirot, so in impurity there are seven palaces, which are a garment for ten rungs. And not that they resemble exactly; for above the seventh palace in the husks there is no impurity at all; and it is not so in holiness; for above the sixth palace there are many, many rungs of the Throne, as we explained:
Chapter One

The first palace is the one called Pit [בור, bor]; "and the pit was empty" (Gen. 37:24). And whoever comes to enter it has no supporter to take hold of his hand so that he not fall; rather all of them push him so that he falls within it. In this palace there is one appointed one, and his name is Dumah; and he stands here in this palace, and stands at the entrance of the first palace of holiness, outside, with several angels of ruin, to take hold of the souls that the holy angel Tahariel pushes away, as we explained in the Gate of the Palaces of Holiness, chapter 1. And under this appointed one, Dumah, there is another appointed one, and his name is Petut [Seducer]; and under his hand several thousand and myriad angels of ruin. And he stands to seduce human beings from the good way, to look upon adultery and harlotry; as his name, so is his action. And all the angels of ruin that are with him go before human beings, so that their eyes be on the transgression. And this appointed one is also called Sarsarim [another version: Sarsuria]; for he is the go-between [sarsur] of the transgression. And this appointed one stands over the grave at the time that the body is judged, and breaks his eyes, because he inclined after his counsel. For so is the way of the husk: to accuse below, and to rise and accuse above, and to descend and take his soul; and whoever is drawn after it, it itself takes its vengeance on him. Within this palace there are several serpents and scorpions that bite the soul when it enters there. And over this whole palace there is one appointed one, and his name is Gamgima [another version: Gamguma]; and he is red as a rose. And he stands to accuse, when the prayer of a man is pushed away from the first palace of holiness, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 1. And when this one receives that prayer that is pushed away, he rises with it up to the seventh palace of the husk; and from there he pleads guilt against him and mentions his iniquities. And this is what the verse says (Job 1:6), "and the Satan also [gam] came among them": gam is the name of the Satan, which is Gamgima [another version: Gamguma]. [There are] appointed ones to take hold of every kind of obscene speech or blemished thing that a man brings out with his lips, and they keep it; and when the man afterward brings out of his mouth words of holiness, such as words of Torah or prayer, then they defile [another version: they are defiled] those holy words with that impurity that he brought out of his mouth before; and then, as it were, the power of holiness is weakened; and then woe to him, woe to the soul of that sinner. Further, in this palace, over all these appointed ones, there is one appointed one, and his name is (Tafsarinia), another version Safsirita; and under his hand several angels of ruin. And they are appointed over all those things that a man throws from his hand in irritation; and they take that thing and raise it above, and say: "This is the offering of So-and-so, which he offered to us"; and they proclaim: "Woe to So-and-so, who went whoring after a strange god." And a heavenly voice goes out a second time and says: "Woe unto them, for they have fled from Me" (Hos. 7:13). And this palace is called the Pit of the Satan:

The second palace is the one called Corruption [שחת, shachat]; and it is impure and it is darkness. In this palace there are three entrances to three sides. At one entrance stands one appointed one, and his name is Astiria; and under his hand several thousands and myriads, appointed over those who emit seed in vain, who do not see the face of the Shekhinah. And these come and defile them in this world; and afterward, when his soul goes out, these take hold of him and bring him in to be judged among them. And these are called boiling semen; and these take the heat of the transgression and the seed and raise it above, and it causes, God forbid, the holy covenant to be subdued [another version: to enter] beneath the husks. At the second entrance there is one appointed one, and his name is Taskifa; and he is appointed over all those who come upon beasts, or upon the severe forbidden unions in the Torah; and under his hand several thousands and myriads of angels of ruin; and their way with this man is like the way of those of whom we spoke above. In this palace there is one appointed one, and in his hand the cup [another version: whose name is Kos (Cup)] of staggering. And all those killed by the court, who were killed and drank the cup of staggering in this world, are saved from the cup of staggering of the world to come. And what is the cup of staggering? When the soul goes out from the body, this appointed one [in whose hand is] the cup of staggering takes hold of him and makes him drink the cup of staggering. And in the cup are three drops: one gravel, and one more bitter than death, and one dregs. And in this palace stands one appointed one, and his name is Ni'atziriel; and from him go out the three drops of which we spoke, and they enter the cup of staggering; and from there they make him drink it on the day of death. And they are the three drops that are on the sword of the angel of death, of which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, spoke (in Tractate Avodah Zarah, fol. 20b). At the third entrance there is one appointed one, and his name is Sangadiel; and he is appointed over all those who bring in and defile the holy covenant in the daughter of a strange god. And all those who defile themselves with foreign women: here the forms of the women with whom they defiled themselves are portrayed, in this appointed one and in several thousand appointed ones that are under his hand. And when his soul goes out they defile it in that form, and it binds itself in this palace. And this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (in Tractate Sotah, fol. 3b): "'And he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her' (Gen. 39:10): to lie by her in this world, to be with her in the world to come." Within this palace there is one impure spirit, and on it depend all the sorceries and all kinds of divinations; and all of them depend on the impurity of boiling seed. And this was the wisdom of Balaam the wicked, who would defile himself with his she-ass, and then he would succeed in his sorceries. And on account of this this palace is called impure Corruption; for "he is unclean, and Unclean shall he cry." Beneath this upper impure spirit there is in this palace a further impure spirit, and its name is Sartia; and several thousands and myriads of angels of ruin beneath it. And they are ready, at the hour that the dream descends from the side of holiness: this spirit and all the angels of ruin that are with it descend with that dream and mix with it, and make known to that man words of falsehood, words of mockery, with the true dream. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot 55a): "Just as it is impossible for grain without straw, so it is impossible for a dream without idle things." And from the side of this palace go out two spirits that turn about, sometimes men, sometimes women. And when the upper impure spirits journey, from the side of their journeying the two come into being as flames and blazes, and go and spread out in the world, and appear to human beings in a dream in the likeness of beautiful women, and defile them with nocturnal emission. And all this is for one who is drawn after their words and draws their spirit upon himself by his deeds. And this is what the Torah warned: "then you shall keep yourself from every evil thing" (Deut. 23:10), as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (in Tractate Ketubbot, fol. 46a): that a man should not think by day and come to emission at night, God forbid. And on this matter he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 130a), and these are his words: "One appointed one stands on that side, over that hollow of the north, with all those bands of demons; Sanugiria is his name. And at the hour that that smoke bends its way and rises, this appointed one and sixty thousand myriad other camps all stand ready to receive it and to be nourished from it; and they stand in that hollow and enter by one entrance that is called Keri. And this is the secret of what is written (Lev. 26:21), 'And if you walk contrary [keri] unto Me,' etc.; and it is written, 'then I will walk contrary unto you in fury' (Lev. 26:28): in that agitation that goes out from the entrance of Keri. And these are those who roam at night. And at the hour that the souls go out to rise to be seen above, these go out and accuse them, so that they cannot rise and be seen above, except those holy pious ones who split firmaments and airs and rise. And these bands of demons go out and make known lying words to human beings, and appear to them in other likenesses, and laugh with them until they emit seed; and they are called masters of keri, because those who go out from the entrance of Keri caused it to them. And at the hour that the limbs and the fats were consumed, that smoke would sate them and nourish them; as is their honour, so is their sustenance, what is fitting for them; and by this they did not go out and did not roam in the Holy Land." Thus far his words.

And what he said, "that smoke bends," he explained above in the matter, and explained that in the morning continual offering and in the afternoon continual offering the wind did not overcome the column of smoke; but at night the smoke would bend of itself to the side of the north, so that these masters of keri be nourished from it, so that they not roam in the Land of Israel. And on the matter of the masters of keri it is further explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 55a), that Naamah is the mother of the demons; and she is of the seed of Cain; and after her the sons of God, Uza and Azael, went astray. And the children of her children are those who lead human beings astray in the matter of heat; and sometimes also the women are heated and conceive from them and bear demons and evil spirits. And it is possible that all the spirits come into being from this palace, to lead human beings astray, and are clothed in the form of human beings through Naamah. Further, it is explicit there that the first Adam, in the hundred and thirty years that he separated from his wife before he begot Seth, would beget spirits and demons whose work is to lead human beings astray in the matter of keri; and their form is like the form of human beings, and they do not change from form to form, after the way of the other demons; except that they have no hair on their head. And possibly the reason is to show that they have no root above; for the hairs point to the secret of the upper roots, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul. And it is possible that they are powers from this palace that were clothed and came into being through Adam in those years. And he explained there (fol. 47b) that these are called "the plagues of the children of men" (2 Sam. 7:14):

The third palace is called the Palace of Gloom [Ofil]; and it is darker and gloomier than the first ones; and it is called Silence [Dumah]. For even though we said that he descends into the first palace, his principal is in this palace. And over against this the evil inclination is called Enemy. In this palace there are four entrances, and over them four appointed ones, as we shall explain. At the first entrance, one appointed one, and his name is (Katritia) [another version: Skafortia]; and he stands in the power of agitation, when judgment is stretched out in the world; and he is the stumbling of the wicked. Of this it is said (Prov. 4:19), "The way of the wicked is as darkness; they know not at what they stumble." This appointed one stands at the parting of the ways, to make stumble with his plague those who go alone on the roads and in the markets; and he can injure them if he meets them; and this is when he rules in the world in the force of the stretched-out judgment, God forbid. At the second entrance, one appointed one, Negadiel [another version: Sangadiel] is his name; and under his hand several thousands and myriads of angels of ruin; and all of them stand to receive the notes of judgment from outside the third palace, the palace [another version: from the palaces] of holiness. And when he receives the notes of the judgments he descends to the two preceding palaces, which are Corruption and Pit; and there he has several thousands and myriads of angels of ruin; and all of them roam in the world to complete that judgment. At the third entrance, one appointed one, and his name is Angirihon [another version: Angaryon]; and he is appointed over the fever that burns within the bones, and all kinds of evil sicknesses that inflame and burn the body; and from him go out several thousands and myriads appointed over this matter, like him. At the fourth entrance, one appointed one, and his name is Askarah [Croup]; and this one is appointed over the killing and death of children (up to thirteen years old); and he appears as a woman who rears and nurses them and plays with them, and strangles them; and their soul [is handed over] into the hand of Azriel, the angel who is in the third palace of holiness, as we explained there. In the middle of this palace stands one spirit, and it is called Agirusion [Agirison]; and this one is appointed over the death of the young men from thirteen years old to twenty years old, of whom it is said (Prov. 13:23), "but there is that is destroyed by want of judgment"; for since they do not guard themselves from sin when they are small, because of the evil of their upbringing, and he sees in them a sign that they will sin and be corrupted, he kills them before they come to sin. And of this it is said, "and behold, it was very good": this is the angel of death. From this palace two spirits spread out, and their names are Anger [Af] and Fury [Cheimah]. These Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, saw in his descending from the mountain, and said (Deut. 9:19), "For I was afraid of the anger and the fury." And under their hand several thousands and myriads of angels of ruin; and all of them are appointed over all those who hear a ban or excommunication from the mouth of a master of Torah and do not lay it to heart; and likewise over all those who mock the words of Torah or the words of the sages. And likewise all of them encamp and go to provoke all those who occupy themselves with Torah, and likewise in doing a commandment, so that they not rejoice in it and be saddened with it. Beneath these spirits there is one spirit, and its name is Sikhsikha; and when a man informs on his fellow or stirs up strife [mesakhsekh] against him, this one is aroused with that informing, to record the matter and to kill by that informing. Come and see: even though the Holy One, blessed be He, fixed for all the wild animals and serpents a time for the shedding of their skin, nevertheless [all] depends on evil speech and on informing. When a man informs on his fellow, the lower serpents shed their skin and give voices; and those voices rise above, into the palace that is called Pit, where there are several serpents and scorpions, as we explained above; and all of them plead accusation, to arouse the primordial serpent, the great serpent; and he sheds his skin; and all his scales, that is to say, his camps and his hosts, separate from him, and he brings them down below into the palaces; and he rises to plead provocation with that informing. And if not for the shedding of his skin, no man could stand before him; may the Compassionate One save us. And all this is because of the force of informing and evil speech; and not for nothing our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Arakhin 15b) that it is a most severe transgression, like idolatry and forbidden unions and bloodshed:

The fourth palace is called Guilt [Chovah], and it is called the miry clay [tit ha-yaven] (Ps. 40:3); and over against this the evil inclination is called the stone of stumbling. This palace is called Guilt for the reason that it is over against the Palace of Merit. And all the debts of human beings and their iniquities are in this palace; and several angels of ruin gather them and bring them into this palace. And on the day of judgment, on Rosh Hashanah, when they weigh debt and merit: if the scale-pan of merit (prevails, from the powers of the side of holiness they take hold of him) [of the side of holiness prevails, he is holy], and they judge him for life; and if the pan of liability prevails, several of the masters of debt take hold of him and say, "He is ours, he is ours," and rejoice in him, and they judge him for death. Come and see: as a man conducts himself in this world, so it is drawn and bestowed upon him from above. If he pursues the impure inclination and the transgressions, the spirit of impurity pursues him and helps him to be defiled more, and causes him to come to more severe transgressions and more crushed impurities than the first. And if a man purifies himself and pursues holiness and sanctifies himself, the spirit of holiness is drawn after him and bestowed upon him, and purifies him and sanctifies him and clothes him with humility and fear, and brings him to greater purity; as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Tractate Avodah Zarah (fol. 20b): "Watchfulness brings to alacrity," etc. In this palace is the place of all those that are called other gods; and they are those who seduce human beings with the pleasures of this world, and with adulteries and harlotry. And over all these [that are called] other gods there is a spirit that rules over all of them; and it is called El Nekhar [a strange god]. And it is what seduces those who learn Torah in the house of study with evil, strange thoughts and with defilements; and they say to him: Why do you stand here and waste the days of your youth in the occupation of learning, and weaken your strength? Is it not better for you to rejoice in your youth in adulteries and harlotry? And when a man is seduced after it, several masters of impurity go after him to defile him in this world; and all these are called boiling excrement, who stand to soil the man, as we explained. In the middle of this palace there is one spirit, and its name is Plague [Nega]; and from it spreads out one spirit, and it is called the plague of leprosy. And they stand to defile all those masters of evil speech, more than all those who defile it. And the upper Plague of which he spoke is appointed to curse all those tables that were not arranged on the Sabbath as is fitting; and all of them are set out before him, and he curses them with grievous curses, which there is no need to lengthen upon; may the Compassionate One save us. And as the way of holiness is for good, so the way of impurity is for evil. In this palace all things depend for evil, except for children, life and sustenance, which depend above, in the other palaces, and descend to this palace; and from there accusers go out for evil: whether to diminish the children of a man, (or) to kill them, or to diminish their sustenance; may the Compassionate One save us. From this palace goes out one impure spirit, and it is called Aririya; and under its hand several thousands and myriads of angels of ruin; and all of them are called "they that curse the day" (Job 3:8). And they are appointed over one who curses himself in irritation, and over oaths of imprecation (and the curses); and they take that curse and raise it above, and arouse with it the primordial serpent, "leviathan the crooked serpent," so that it rise and arouse grievous curses, God forbid. And this is what Job intended (Job 3:8) in saying, "Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan": who are those destined to arouse leviathan, which is the crooked serpent; may the Compassionate One save us:

The fifth palace is called Sheol; over against this the evil inclination is called Uncircumcised [Arel]; and this is the principal of the foreskin. In this palace there is one entrance, and over it one appointed one, and his name is Enmity [Eivah]; and he arouses strifes and enmities in the world; and after his name this palace is called Enmity. In this palace there is one impure spirit that rules over all, and its name is Shoded [Despoiler]; and it arouses destruction and breaking; and it crouches in the high mountains, among rocks and crags and forests. From this palace draw all those despoilers; and from there go out all those murderers and killers, and go after "the flame of the sword which turned every way" (Gen. 3:24), to kill everything. [From there goes out one spirit, and it is called Shod (Destruction).] And when there is famine in the world, God forbid, this spirit that is called Shod couples with another spirit that is called Kafan [Famine]: this one to despoil the people of the world and to kill them, and this is what is called Shod; and that one to curse the food in their bowels, so that they are not sated; and it is what is called Kafan. And when there are among Israel doers of kindness at the time of famine, they cause these not to rule in the world over Israel; and they rule over the nations of the world; and the side of impurity is subdued, and Israel are blessed. And when, God forbid, there is none among Israel who does kindness, and the nations of the world do kindness, then, God forbid, the husk prevails; and one of these bestows to the nations and draws all the holy effluence. And of this it is said (Song 1:6), "they made me keeper of the vineyards" [these are the nations of the world]; "but my own vineyard have I not kept": these are Israel; for all the effluence descends from holiness to the other side, God forbid. Beneath these of which we spoke there are impure spirits, and they are called Foreskin [Orlah]; and they are the branches of the foreskin and the boughs of the foreskin. And over all of them is one appointed one, and he is called Gezar Dinia; and he is appointed over all those who do not keep the years of orlah, and over those who delay the circumcision. And this is the reason for "a bridegroom of blood, because of the circumcision" (Exod. 4:26), which Zipporah said. And he is appointed over the man when he defiles his covenant, to bring him into Sheol and Abaddon to judge him there. In the middle of this palace there is one spirit that lies in wait on the roads and in the places, to see those who transgress the Torah, to inform on them above, to bring enmity between the upper ones and the lower ones. And likewise all of them stand to seduce the man from the good way to the evil way; and afterward it rises and accuses him and kills him; and it is found that they bring him out of this world and out of the world to come. And there is no enmity greater than this; and therefore it is called the Palace of Enmity. And this spirit is called Afrira; and the intent is the dust of ashes, which does not make fruits and does not grow plants; the reverse of the holy dust (which is Malkhut), which makes fruits. And the reason is that it has already been explained that every spirit of impurity is castrated. And this is from the dust of the burning of the sin offering; for it is held in the sin, which is the crooked serpent. And further, for when a man sins this dust prevails through the serpent; and this is included in "the bitter waters that cause the curse"; and this is the dust of the Tabernacle from which the priest would make the sotah drink, because she played the harlot and inclined after the serpent, the harlot. For this they make her drink of the dust of the floor of the Tabernacle, which is the dust, in the bitter waters; and this spirit rules over her and destroys her. And these are "the last waters are obligatory." May the Name save us:

The sixth palace: this palace is higher than all the palaces, like the side of holiness; for "God has made even the one over against the other," as we explained. In this palace there are four entrances, and in it four impure powers: one Death [Mavet], and one Evil [Ra], and one Shadow of Death [Tzalmavet], and one Gloom [Ofel]. These stand always to do evil and to accuse. And the four of them are united as one, like the four of the side of holiness; and on account of the union mentioned it is called the House of Association [beit chaver], as it is written (Prov. 21:9; 25:24), "than with a contentious woman in a wide house [beit chaver]"; and this is "or a charmer [chover chaver]" (Deut. 18:11). Of this palace it is said (Prov. 27:6), "but the kisses of an enemy are profuse." Here stand all those kisses and seductions and bodily cravings of harlotry and adultery, through which a man is driven out from this world and the world to come. And all those that are written in Proverbs (chapter 7), in the passage "For at the window of my house I looked forth through my lattice," etc., all those seductions are from the side of the spirit of this palace. And of it it is said, "her feet abide not in her house" (Prov. 7:11); for she goes to seduce human beings; and after she has seduced him she makes him taste "the cruel venom of asps" (Deut. 32:33). And she brings out his soul with her sword, and on it are three drops. With the first his soul is confused and finds no place to rest; and with the second his soul is uprooted and goes out; with the third his face turns green, and his soul goes out "like a hair," etc. All this because he was drawn after her; and this is what the verse said (Prov. 5:4), "But her end is bitter as wormwood," etc. In this palace stand all those accusers who seduce a man in his clothes and in his garments, and make him curl and finger his hair, and wash his body, and adorn his appearance, so that the women will look at him. And over this matter one appointed one, Sktupa is his name. Within this palace [another version: And beneath this appointed one] stands another appointed one (and his name is Mirror), in which and through which the man sees himself, and beautifies himself and curls; and afterward he looks in the mirror and is clothed in it with pride and arrogance and haughtiness. And then another power that is in the palace is aroused, and its name is Asirta, which is appointed over all the dreams, to show a man a likeness that he will be drawn after, to lose his soul. And this appointed one arouses another appointed one that is under his hands, and descends and arouses in the lower palace in which is Askarah; and there he arouses a female [one]; and she is Lilith, the mother of the demons. And when a man in his haughtiness arouses the appointed one Asirta, then Lilith is bound with him; and then on every new moon that mirror of which we spoke is aroused with her, of Lilith; and sometimes the man is injured by them; and he falls to the ground and has a fit and is injured. And all this the mirror caused him; and according to the greatness of his pride with which he was proud, so is the greatness of his evil and his injury and his impurity, "till a dart strike through his liver," etc. (Prov. 7:23). May the Compassionate One save us:

The seventh palace: this palace is the palace of the dregs of the wine, to be drunk from it, as it is written (Gen. 9:21), "and he was drunken, and he was uncovered within his tent." And they are the grapes that Eve pressed, through which she caused death to her husband and to all those who come after him: "their grapes are grapes of gall" (Deut. 32:32), etc. In this palace stand all those impure souls, to bestow them on all those who defile themselves with a menstruant and a married woman, and on the son that goes out from them, who is a mamzer. And he is called mamzer because he is me-el zar [from a strange god]. And according to the transgression and the matter of the evil inclination, so he draws upon himself the soul from this palace; and "all that see them shall acknowledge them," that they are an unfit seed, a mamzer, from a strange god; and all his deeds testify about him that he is unfit, as he called to a strange god, and they recognized him, that he is from a strange god. From this palace goes out one spirit that is appointed over all those souls, and its name is Tzefoni [the Northern one]; and the sign: "But I will remove far off from you the northern one" (Joel 2:20). And over against this palace Gehinnom is called the Nethermost Land [eretz tachtit]. In this palace there is a thin point, near to the sefirot of the husks; and from it go out (like those) [another version: all those] thin spirits that roam in the world, which see and are not seen. And these stand to do miracles for human beings; for these do not stand in the husks so filthy as the others. And over these is one appointed one, Nesira is his name; and it is an Aramaic word, and its explanation is cut off; for the intent is that it is most separated from the impure husks; and we explained this matter at length above in the previous gate. And these fly in the air and refine to the side [another version: and do harm from the side] of their impurity, for doing [another version: from doing] miracles in the world for those who stand on the side of holiness. From this palace go out strong fire and snow and a strengthening wind, to judge the wicked; and this is what the verse says (Ps. 68:15), "it snowed in Zalmon." In this palace stand four entrances, open to four directions; and these take hold of the side of holiness; and there the light of holiness shines; and it is a sweet place for the pious of the nations of the world, who did not do evil to Israel. At the entrance of the palace, in the middle, outside, are six entrances, and they are directed over against the holiness; and there are places set in order for the kings of the nations of the world who did not do evil to Israel and did not oppress them, and protected them; and they have honour there for this; and the light of holiness shines for them within that darkness. And of this it is said (Isa. 14:18), "All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in glory." And if they oppressed Israel, several angels of ruin take hold of them and judge them three times every day with several strange judgments; and each and every day they testify concerning Israel and concerning their good faith. Thus far, in general, the matter of these palaces. However, I copied it from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Pekudei, fol. 263. And at first sight it would appear that they are palaces for the sefirot of the husks of which we spoke in the previous gate; however, what is reasonable is that the sefirot are included in the palaces; and the palaces and the husks are all one thing and one matter. And over against these seven are seven kinds of evil inclination, which receives power from these seven; and therefore the evil inclination is called by seven names; and these are they: Evil, Impure, Abomination, Enemy, Stone of Stumbling, the Northern One; and over against these seven dwellings in Gehinnom, in which the sinner is judged in these seven kinds; and these are they: Pit, Corruption, Silence, Miry Clay, Sheol, Shadow of Death, Nethermost Land. And they are this over against that: over against purity, impurity; over against fitness, unfitness; over against permitted, forbidden; over against merit, guilt. For "God has made even the one over against the other," as we explained in the previous chapter:
The commentators wrote in the name of the Geonim that from the power of impurity three divisions are drawn:

"The first division is Ashmedai, the great king of the demons; and he has no permission to accuse or to spoil except on the second day of the week." And it seems to me that the reason is that on it the luminaries were smitten; and for this cause the husk prevailed from the side of the diminishment, as is explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in many places. "And Ashmedai is under the dominion of Samael. And know that Samael makes use of Lilith the Elder, his bride, as we explained in the previous gate; and Ashmedai makes use of Lilith the Younger. And these two powers with their mates: each one of them was born with his mate, two-faced, like Adam and Eve. And Lilith the Maiden, the bride of Ashmedai, is the daughter of the king whose name is Kafkefoni, whom we shall explain further on. And the ancient sages said that jealousy was born between Samael, the great prince, and Ashmedai, the king of the demons, over Lilith, whom they call Lilith the Maiden, who is in the form of a beautiful woman from her head to her navel, and from the navel downward blazing fire; for like mother, like daughter: she is the daughter of Mehetabel, the wife of Kafkefoni, the mother of Lilith the Maiden. And both of them, daughter and mother, are occupied in their war with Lilith the Great, the Elder, the wife of Samael. And from the offspring of Ashmedai and Lilith his wife a great prince was formed in heaven, ruling over eighty thousand destroyers and spoilers; and they call him the Sword of King Ashmedai; and his name is Alpafonias; and his face blazes like a flaming fire.

"And further they call him the Whelp of Judah [Gur Yehudah]; and the explanation, he accuses and contends with the princes of Judah, who are three princes who plead merit for Judah: Malkhiel, Aturiel, Nashriel." And we explained them above in the Gate of ABYA, chapter 3. "And at the hour that that destroyer was born, there was also born in heaven a prince, the root of the Kingdom, who is called the Sword of King Messiah; and he has two names, and these are they: Meshichiel, Kokhaviel. And when the will comes and arrives, then the sword will go out from its sheath, and the verses of the prophecies will be fulfilled: 'For My sword has drunk its fill in heaven' (Isa. 34:5); 'there shall step forth a star out of Jacob' (Num. 24:17)."

"The second division: Kafkefoni and his wife Tzar'ita. They used her half the year, and half the year they used another woman, and her name is Sagrit. And the offspring that go out from them are forms different from one another; they have bodies, and the recognition of their faces is in two likenesses: the children of Tzar'ita are like the likeness of lepers;" and there are those who say that the lepers are children of menstruation, who become leprous at ten, at twenty, at thirty, at forty, at fifty, at sixty, at seventy [years], as explained in Midrash Tanchuma, Parashat Metzora; "they are born from the power of this ugly offspring. And the children of Sagrit have no recognition of face, but are like the likeness of those afflicted with plague. And there is a long war between them; evil spirits spread out in the air; and all the injuries and the earthquakes go out from the power of these mixtures. And the dominion of Ashmedai and his terror is laid upon them; and of what is renewed for them they make known to those below them."

"The third division: they are the harmful spirits, created and clothed in several kinds of forms, different from one another. There are of them whose form is the form of dogs; and if the iniquity of the man causes it, the dog formed from this evil offspring happens upon the man and bites him; and his healing is exceedingly hard to be healed. And sometimes his form is changed, in his iniquity, to the form of the dog, and he is changed into that form; and he barks and cries out and bites, and that dog bites again; and he has no healing forever until he dies; and he is again clothed in the mixture of that air by the power of that form; and this is his punishment and his annihilation. And concerning this secret the sweet singer of Israel prayed and said (Ps. 22:21), 'Deliver my soul from the sword, my only one from the power of the dog.' And there are of them whose form is the form of goat-demons, the form of goats; and of these was the chariot of Uza and Azael. And the two of them alone have literally the form of man; and when they fell from the holy place they were clothed in the power of this air that is over us, and were made corporeal in the corporeality of human beings; and the upper power was weakened, and they received a lower power. But the offspring that went out from them were tall in exceeding stature and in strong might beyond all human beings. And there are of them the form of women, seen by human beings; and there is among them only falsehood and lie; and they have jealousy of human beings, and their intent is to deceive them and to make them stumble; and they would almost consume and destroy all that is seen by them, were it not for the attribute of Malkhut, which makes rule, from her emanation, a prince beloved and dear before the Shekhinah, whose name is Yofiel, the Prince of the Face. And were it not for his providence and his terror over them, they would leave no creature in the world. And this prince subdues them and humbles them," as we explained in the Gate of the Palaces of Holiness, in the third palace, chapter 3. "And the prince over this third division, his name is Kafkefoni; and the name of his wife, Mehetabel the daughter of Matred. And the offspring that go out from the two of them leap [kofetzim] with one leap from the end of the air to the end of the air. And permission is given them sometimes to do good and to drive away the injuries from human beings; and they make known future things to human beings when they are seen by them in the forms of human beings; and they have no dominion in falsehoods nor in lies. And whoever asks of them will find his question according to his will, if the asker is worthy to be answered; and if not, they answer him, by the power of the adjuration, that permission has not been given them to answer his question. And sometimes, according to the power and the dominion given to this prince Kafkefoni, he joins and cleaves with one daughter that he has, and her name is Lilith; she is the wife of Ashmedai, as we explained above; and his cause is his cleaving to this Lilith." Thus far the words of the Geonim, peace be upon them. Further, we have found in the words of the commentators: "Three bands of angels of ruin were created in the world, and these are they. One band of them was created when the serpent came upon Eve on the eve of the Sabbath. And the second band was created from 'the plagues of the children of men,' from the emissions that the first Adam saw all those hundred and thirty years that he separated from Eve; and likewise they come into being from the emissions of other human beings. And the third band is created from them; for they are fruitful and multiply, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (in Tractate Chagigah, fol. 16a): 'Six things were said of demons: three like the ministering angels, and three like human beings'; and one of them, they are fruitful and multiply like human beings." Thus far his words.
