And in the Zohar (see the Introduction to the Zohar, fol. 17), in different places (see the Zohar, Bereshit, fol. 48), it appears that the demons are the powers of the impurities and the husk that spread out on the eve of the Sabbath; and it wished to be strengthened in a body, and bestowed and brought out those powers, which are the demons; and because the day was sanctified, impure souls remained without a body at all; as is expounded on the verse "which God created to make" (Gen. 2:3). And they stood and were clothed and took on body through Cain, the nest of impurity; and they took on body only for a time. And of them the verse said (Gen. 36:24), "this was that Anah that found the yemim [mules] in the wilderness," etc. And behold, Anah pursued these impurities, and found them in the wilderness; for there is their dwelling place, as is fitting for them, "in a land of drought and of the shadow of death" (Jer. 2:6), a place where there is no settlement at all. And it is called yemim, written defective; and the reason is because they are neither from the sixth day nor from the Sabbath day; for they were created at twilight; and therefore yemim is written, for they are not, not from one day and not from two days. And Anah, in pursuing them, found them. And the reason is that Zibeon came upon his mother and begot a mamzer son like this, who is Anah; and because of his impurity he pursued the mamzerut; and "God delivered into his hand" a find like this: he met one like himself; and they taught him to bring out mamzerim like themselves; and they would teach him several kinds of divinations and sorceries, to bring forth impurities and husks in the world. And behold, in the earth [Arka] are the children of the children of Cain; and over them in the earth are two appointed ones, princes of impurity; and of the matter of those demons and their deeds it is expounded there at length. Thus far the copying of these things has reached, to be of benefit for the understanding of the Torah and the comprehension of its secrets. And of God we ask help, to save us from all impurity and defilement, so that we may cleave to His holiness, to serve Him with a whole heart. Amen, so may it be His will.
And behold, this chapter is completed, and this gate is concluded:
The Gate of Letters, which is Gate Twenty-Seven [the Hebrew reads "Twenty-Six"]:

What is intended in this gate is to explain the hint of the letters, which are twenty-two things, and their dependence on the upper roots, as is expounded in the words of the commentators, and especially the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him; for they rise higher and higher. And the reason for this is that they are an entrance to this wisdom, as will be explained with the help of the Name:
Chapter One:

Before we enter into the explanation of each and every letter, as our Owner shall be gracious to us, our wish is to set first a fine introduction to the matter of the letters. Many thought that these letters are conventional; that is to say, the sages agreed to make signs for the outputs of speech. How so? They agreed that the movement divided at the lips, which are  B V M P, should be expressed in the form of Bet and in the form of Vav and in the form of Mem and in the form of Peh; and likewise for the other movements that they agreed upon. And likewise the other languages of the nations have signs for everything they wish; and as the masters of number did, who invented for themselves ten signs, in which they included all number, according to the change of the places and according to the measure of their multiplications, as is well known to the masters of number. And according to this it is found that there is no difference between these letters and the other signs of the nations for their language in their lands, by their nations; except that these are conventional for the nation of Israel by the counsel of Moses, from the mouth of a prophetic spirit, and those are the convention of a foolish intellect that invented so for them. And according to this convention it would follow that there is no principal in that inscribed writing, but only the revealing of the intent of the speaker; like the wise physician who writes his wisdom in a book of medicine, where the intent is not that that book be healing at all, but his intent in his book is to reveal his opinion, or what he wishes, on the matter of healing; and when a man understands the principal of the wisdom written in the book, there remains no benefit at all in that book. And similar to this the philosopher said to his disciples: "My sons, do not trust in the skins of dead carcasses." And according to this the law would be that if a man studies in that book years without number, if he does not understand the learning of the wisdom it will not profit him anything, and he will not complete the soul by his learning at all, since he does not understand the inquiries of the wisdom; but on the contrary he has lost his time on what will harm him and not profit him: for the loss of his time and the exhaustion of his strength will harm him, and it will not profit him, since he learned no learning from it. And likewise their opinion on the matters of the Torah: that the intent is the revealing of the inwardness and the governance for the completeness of the soul; and whoever does not know the matters of its inquiries, no benefit reaches him in its study, God forbid. And this is impossible; for certainly the words of the Torah are "restoring the soul" (Ps. 19:8). And the proof is from what we are obliged in the completion of the Torah, "twice the Scripture and once the Targum," and even "Ataroth and Dibon" (Num. 32:3); and this points to the completeness of the Torah, and that it has an inwardness and concealment and spirituality and life. And so Rabbi Simeon explained in Parashat Beha'alotekha (fol. 152), and these are his words: "Rabbi Simeon said: Woe to that man who says that the Torah came to show mere stories and the words of a commoner. For if so, even at this time we could make a Torah from the words of commoners, and more praiseworthy than all of them. If to show the things of the world, even the rulers of the world have among them higher things; if so, let us go after them and make a Torah from them in this fashion. Rather, all the words of the Torah are upper words and upper secrets. Come and see: the upper world and the lower world are weighed in one balance: Israel below, upper angels above. Of the upper angels it is written (Ps. 104:4), 'Who makes His angels spirits' (this in the upper place). At the hour that they descend below they are clothed in the garment of this world; and if not, they cannot stand in this world, and the world cannot bear them. And if with angels it is so, the Torah, which created them and created all the worlds, and they stand for its sake, how much more so: since it descended to this world, if it were not clothed in these garments of this world, the world could not bear it. And therefore this story of the Torah is the garment of the Torah. Whoever thinks that that garment is the Torah itself, and not another thing, may his spirit expire, and he will have no portion in the world to come. Because of this David said (Ps. 119:18), 'Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Your Torah': what is beneath the garment of the Torah. Come and see: there is a garment that is seen by all; and those fools, when they see a man in a garment that appears fine to them, do not look further. They think that that garment is the body; the importance of the body is the soul. In this fashion the Torah has a body; and the words of the Torah, which are called the bodies of Torah, this body is clothed in a garment, which are the stories of this world. The fools of the world look only at that garment, which is the story of the Torah, etc. And those who know more do not look at the garment, but at the body that is beneath that garment. The wise, the servants of the upper King, those who stood at Mount Sinai, look only at that soul, which is the principal of all, the Torah itself. And in the world to come they are destined to look at the soul of the soul of the Torah. Come and see: so too above there is a garment and a body and a soul and a soul to the soul. The heavens and their hosts are the garment; and the Assembly of Israel, this is the body that receives the soul, etc. The soul that we spoke of, this is the Beauty [Tiferet] of Israel, which is the Torah itself. And the soul to the soul, this is the Holy Ancient One; and all is held one in another. Woe to those wicked of the world who say that the Torah is nothing but a mere story; and they look at the garment and no further. Happy are the righteous who look at the Torah as is fitting. Wine sits only in a jar; so the Torah sits only in this garment. And therefore one should look in the Torah only at what is beneath the garment; and therefore all these words and all those stories are garments." Thus far his words.

And behold, from this saying it appears explicitly that the divisions of the Torah are four, and under each one of these four are a thousand thousands of thousands of aspects. The first division is the one he titles by the name of the upper garment, which is the story of things, which was made corporeal so that it be understood by us. And one who learns in the Torah to know [only this], as one who learns in a book of chronicles, this certainly will not profit in learning, and no benefit will reach him from it; and would that he not lose. But when a man comes to learn in the Torah, his intent must be that he is learning that matter as being divine words whose great inwardness is concealed from him. And by this thing the breath of Torah that goes out of his mouth will please before the Holy One, blessed be He, "better than an ox or a bullock" (Ps. 69:32), even though he understands in it only the plainness of the story. And needless to say this; but even one who does not understand at all, because he is not expert in the language in its explanation, but occupies himself in the Scripture alone, he too has a good reward in his toil. And of these and the like it is said (Ps. 1:2), "and in his Torah does he meditate day and night"; and our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded (Avodah Zarah 19a): it does not say "and in the Torah," but "and in his Torah": the explanation, according to the measure of his knowledge. For even one who does not know how to join the words, he too, if he occupies himself in it day and night, "his reward is with him and his recompense before him" (Isa. 40:10); on condition that he always add; for if you do not say so, behold, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Mishnah (Avot, ch. 1), "And he who does not add, diminishes; and he who does not learn," etc. And the second division is those who occupy themselves in the understanding of the plain sense; that is to say, the laws and the midrashim, and the explanation of the commandments, and the explanations of the decisors, such as the six orders of the Mishnah, in their answers and their use, which they titled by the language of Talmud and the attendance on the disciples of the sages; and likewise the midrashim of aggadah of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, in their plain sense. For they gladden the heart and enlighten the eyes; may our Creator make us merit that our portion be in them and our lot with them; for they are those who sustain the world; and the length of the matter would not be sufficed by writing. And this division Rashbi, peace be upon him, titled by the name body. And to this the masters of the Mishnah intended in saying (Avot, ch. 3): "Bird offerings and the beginnings of menstruation, these, these are the bodies of the laws." The third division is those who occupy themselves in the pleasant Kabbalah, such as the secrets expounded in the Zohar, that a man enter into them, and through it add further like them and like them; for they have left us room. And on condition that the inquirer continue constantly the occupation with the inquiries of this book; for "then shall he walk in his way securely" (Prov. 3:23). And they are soul and inwardness certainly for the whole Torah; for all the midrashim and the mishnayot and all the laws and all the doing of the commandments have an inwardness and a pleasant secret. The fourth division is the spirituality of the letters and their manifestation, and their joining with one another, and their relationship; for whoever goes down to the depth of this matter can create worlds. And this is called the soul to the soul, which depends on Binah, which is called the world to come; and this is the joy that we hope for after the resurrection. And under each division of these four divisions there are many, many aspects, which a man can judge of himself. And it is found according to this that the matter of the Torah is the very self of the sefirot, as he explains: in the body, which is Malkhut; and the soul, which is Tiferet; and the soul to the soul, which is Binah. And the Torah itself is found to be a garment to the very Self of God, just as the sefirot are a garment to the very Self of the root that spreads out, as is expounded in the preceding gates. And for this cause the occupation with the Torah is above all, as is known, apart from other reasons.

And behold, the three preceding divisions Rashbi, peace be upon him, titled by the name masters of Scripture, masters of Mishnah, masters of Kabbalah. The first division is called masters of Scripture, and the second division is called masters of Mishnah, and the third division is called masters of Kabbalah. And the fourth division is hardly found, and therefore it did not come by name. And under it stand the Names and their action and their permutation from within the verses, with the joining to them of the knowledge of their drawing and their order in the upper Chariot, which is hardly found. And in the book Berit Menuchah it occupied itself in this matter somewhat. And the entrance to it is these three gates that we shall explain one after another; and they are the Gate of Letters, and the Gate of Vowels, and the Gate of Cantillation Marks, as will be explained with the help of the Name:

Before we enter into the explanation of the letters, our wish is to set first one introduction, with which was the opening of our speech in this gate in the previous chapter. And it is that the letters of the Torah are not conventional; rather they are spiritual, related in their form to the inwardness of their soul. And this is why our Rabbis, of blessed memory, were precise in the explanation of the manifestation of the form of the letters and their thorns and their crowns and their decorations: because they hint at a known spirituality of the upper sefirot. And each and every letter has a spiritual form and an honoured light, emanated from the very self of the sefirah, descending in a chain from rung to rung, after the manner of the chain of descent of the sefirot.

And behold, the letter is a palace and a base for that spirituality. And when a man mentions and moves a letter of the letters, necessarily that spirituality is aroused; and from the breath of the mouth holy forms come into being from it; they rise and are bound in their root, which is the root of the Emanation. And not this alone, but also in their manifestation, that is to say in their writing, they have a spirituality that rests on those letters. And this is the reason for the holiness of a Torah scroll. And this is the reason that the Mem and the Samekh in the tablets stood by a miracle: because the spirituality held up that pure body. And this is the reason in the matter of the breaking of the tablets, which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained, that the letters flew off. And these are the words in the Midrash: "He looked at the tablets and saw that the writing in them had flown off; and they became heavy on Moses, and fell from his hands and were broken." Thus far.

Further, in the Jerusalem Talmud (Ta'anit, ch. 4) Rabbi Azariah explained the matter in the name of Rabbi Judah: "The tablets, their weight was forty se'ahs, and the writing bore them. When the writing flew off they became heavy on the hands of Moses, and they fell and were broken. So everything from which the Holy One, blessed be He, removes His Shekhinah no longer endures." And in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah, ch. 2): "'And his banner [ve-diglo] over me was love' (Song 2:4). [At first, whoever pointed at the image of the king with the finger would be killed; and the children go to the house of the book and point at the Name with the finger. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'And his banner over me was love': do not read ve-diglo] but ve-dilugo [and his skipping]." Thus far.

All this showed the spirituality of the letters. And this is the reason for the matter of a Torah scroll that was burned, God forbid, which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Mo'ed Katan 26a) that one tears two tears; and they proved it from the verse "after that the king had burned the roll and the words" (Jer. 36:27): that he tears one for the parchment and one for the writing; that is, the spirituality of the letters. And many like these show the matter of the spirituality of the letters even in their writing alone; all the more in their reading; all the more in their intention. And the matter is that the written letters are a body and palace for the letters fixed in the mouth. The example of this: the written letters are corporeal, and those read by mouth are spiritual. And this is the reason for the Written Torah and the Oral Torah: for the Written Torah is spirituality in a high place, and needs a case, so that its light be clothed in corporeal letters; but the Oral Torah is itself a case, and does not need the garment of the case at all.

And behold, the written letters are a body and palace for what is mentioned in the mouth; and those mentioned in the mouth are corporeal with respect to those of thought, which are in the heart; and those that are in the heart are the Emanation, known in the heart of the wise among the people of the children of Israel.

And behold, the matter in this is with respect to the simple letters, each one alone. However, when the letters are joined and gathered and words are made from them, according to the measure of the word in the number of its letters, so is the measure of its spirituality. The example of this: Mem alone is Binah, and Yod alone is Chokhmah; and each one alone points to a matter of spirituality and power emanated from these two attributes. And when they are composed, there comes into being from them a more important spirituality. And not that the two preceding powers were included in the word Mi and there is there only the spirituality of Mi; rather it is a root, and rides upon two emanated powers, which are Mem by itself and Yod by itself; and that is Mi. Afterward there rides upon it a spirituality that includes them; and it is Mi, which points to Binah concealed in Chokhmah, in the secret of the aspects.

And behold, not because of this did the power of Binah lack from its place, nor did the power of Chokhmah lack; however, between the two of them there comes into being a fine manifestation, choicer than each letter alone; and it is Mi. And the example of this is two branches that spread out from the root; for not because of the spreading out did the root lack the power of the two of them, God forbid. And that is Mi, the root to Yod by itself and to Mem by itself; even though it is not a root in substance; but on the contrary, Mem and Yod are two branches to another great branch. And likewise the law for a word composed of three letters, like emet [truth]: for certainly Alef by itself is in Keter, and the Mem in Binah, and Tav in Malkhut; and they are thin branches. And when the three of them are joined, a high branch is made, emet, which hints at Tiferet. And we do not say because of this that the Alef and the Mem descended from their degree, for until now they were in Keter and Binah and now they are in Tiferet; for now they draw near to the root and the principal. And Alef may be the Keter that is in Tiferet or the Keter that is in Malkhut; and likewise in Mem; for each one is included of ten, and ten of ten. And there is a difference between the branches distant from the root, even if they hint at a high place, and the branches near to the root, even if they hint at a low place. And from this matter we may infer to a word of four and of five and the like. And this is the reason for the permutation: that the more the letters multiply, the more the permutation and the powers multiply, as we shall come to in the Gate of Permutation, with the help of Heaven.

And behold, when a man mentions that word that hints at the letters, by the cause of the movement of those powers and their striking against one another by the hammer of the soul, apart from their being aroused in their upper root to do that action, there further comes into being from it, from the breath of his mouth, a spirituality and manifestation, which will be like an angel, which will rise and be bound in its root, so that it hasten to effect its action with alacrity and speed. And this is the secret of the mentioning of the Names and the intention of prayer. And after the fixing of this introduction in the heart of the inquirer, this too is needed by him: that even though the letters are equal in their form and their movement, they are not equal in their spirituality and their emanation. And likewise the words, even though they are equal words; and we have already explained this in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. And the proof is from the four-letter name in the thirteen attributes, "YHVH, YHVH, God compassionate," etc. (Exod. 34:6): and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Idra that the first hints at the Supreme Crown and the second at Malkhut, even though the letters are equal. And the reason is that the principal is the spirituality and emanation and soul of the word or the Name. And so is the matter in EHYH three times (Exod. 3:14): each one points to a matter by itself, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and we copied it in the Gate of Names, chapter 2.

And the matter of their division, even though they are equal, is caused according to the order of the words, whether it is second or first; and likewise in the letters, whether it is second in the word or first, such as the two Hehs in the Name; and likewise according to the letter adjacent to it. And the explanation of these matters Moses received from the mouth of the Gevurah. And this is why Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, tarried on the mountain forty days and forty nights for the second tablets: it was in the learning of the secrets, more and more than what he learned the first time. For the matter of the secrets of our holy Torah, imagination and thought cannot contain them. And this and the like is the fourth division of which we spoke in chapter 1, which we are destined to attain at the time of the resurrection of the dead. And near to this, in the world to come: for the righteous in the Garden of Eden sit and occupy themselves in the learning of the secrets; and this is their joy, when new insights of Torah and its secrets are renewed among them. And let us return to our matter: for the letters are palaces and castles for the spirituality, and they are vessels that draw the Emanation, after the manner of the body, which draws the soul within it. And according to this it is found that even if a man knows only the reading of the Torah, that is to say, the verse alone, necessarily he will receive reward for that reading, and his reward will be great. And one may not say that because of this the reward of reading the Written Torah will be greater than the reward of reading the Oral Torah; for this is nothing; for one who reads in the Torah is like one who reads everything without understanding. And in the reading of the words the principal is that he must intend to their soul and their source and their spirituality, which are their explanation. And if he occupies himself in the Torah without this, he is like one who reads in a body without a soul. For this, necessarily, he must occupy himself in the Oral Torah, which is the explanation of the Torah; and it is the soul of the Torah; that is to say, it reveals its spirituality, which is its explanations and its secrets. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote (in the Zohar, Terumah, fol. 176), and these are his words: "What is the Book of Concealment [Sifra di-Tzeni'uta]? Rabbi Simeon said: Five chapters there are, which are included in a great palace and fill the whole earth. Rabbi Judah said: If these are included, they are better than all. Rabbi Simeon said: So it is for one who entered and went out; and for one who did not enter and go out, not so. A parable of a man whose dwelling was among the rocks, and he did not know the dwellings of the city. He sowed wheat and ate wheat in its raw state. One day he entered the city; they brought him good bread. That man said: This, what is it for? They said to him: It is bread, to eat," etc. "He said: And from what is this made? They said: From wheat. Afterward they brought him cakes kneaded with oil; he tasted of them and said: And these, from what are they made? They said: From wheat. Afterward they brought before him royal pastries kneaded with honey and oil. He said: And these, from what are they made? They said: From wheat. He said: I am master of all these; for I eat the principal of all these, which is wheat. And because of that opinion he did not know the delicacies [ma'adanei] of the king, and they were lost to him. So is one who takes hold of the general principle and does not know all the enjoyable delicacies that go out from that general principle." Thus far his words.

And behold, Rabbi Simeon began to praise the Book of Concealment, which is five chapters, and in them he included all the wisdom of the Kabbalah. And therefore Rabbi Judah said: if so, it is found that a man needs only the learning of that book alone. And Rabbi Simeon answered him that so it is for one who entered the Idra and went out. And he said "and went out" because ten entered and only seven went out; for three departed, as is written in the Idra at its end. But one who did not enter, and did not know the introductions that were revealed there, cannot benefit from the secrets of that concealed book. And he gave the parable of the villager, etc. And likewise certainly it will overtake one who learns in the Written Torah and says that in it all is included: for he will remain empty of everything; the case of the villager will happen to him too. And therefore the principal of completeness in the understanding of the Written Torah is the Oral Torah, as was explained. And after we have explained the matter of the letters in the manifestation of their spirituality, we shall come to relate them in general to the roots, and afterward we shall relate them in particular, with the help of the Name:

And concerning the letters in general the commentators said that some of them are judgment and some of them compassion and some of them intermediate. "A rule in the divine Torah: that Alef-Bet, Gimel-Dalet, Heh-Vav are complete compassion; Zayin, Chet, Tet, Yod, compassion without qualification; Kaf-Lamed, Mem-Nun, Samekh-Ayin are mixed of judgment and compassion; Peh-Tzadi, Kof-Resh, Shin-Tav are complete judgment. And when you wish to join names and prayers and words according to the action that you wish, you will make a composition in the matter of the names that point to the action, whether for compassion or for judgment: for compassion, let most of them be from the compassion; and if judgment, let most of them be from the judgment; and so with the rest." Thus far their words.

And their words are concealed; for we do not see that the things are right according to the manifestation of the letters. For letters that are compassion he counts in the secret of judgment; and especially Shin, which is in Binah, as we shall explain, and it is compassion according to what appears; and he counts it with the letters of complete judgment. And likewise Dalet, which is poor [dalah] and afflicted, and he said that it is compassion. And it is possible to say that their manifestation will be compassion even if they hint in the secret of judgment; and likewise we say that their manifestation is judgment even if they hint in the secret of compassion. And at all events their words are words of tradition. Further, we have found on this matter in the Sefer Yetzirah: it said that there are three Mothers, Alef-Mem-Shin; and we explained them in the entry Alef-Mem-Shin, that they are: Alef, Keter; Mem, Chokhmah; Shin, Binah. And it called them Mothers because they are mothers to the Emanation, as we explained in the Gate of Arbiters. And seven doubles, which are  B G D   K P R T; and they are the seven days of the building: Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And they are called doubles because they receive judgment and compassion, dagesh and rafeh; and likewise they are among the masters of judgment and compassion, which is not so in the three first ones, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And in this way Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained them in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 124) and in the Ra'aya Meheimna. And twelve simples, which are  H V   Z Ch   Ṭ Y   L N S   Ā Tz Q: they are twelve, corresponding to twelve boundaries. And even though we divide them in this way, not because of this will it be difficult that they are in specific places in such-and-such a sefirah; for they will be particulars in a branch of such-and-such a sefirah. As the example: the Mem of Alef-Mem-Shin, he said here that it is in Chokhmah; and not because of this will it be difficult that it is in Binah; for it will be the branch of Binah that is in Chokhmah, or the reverse. And likewise the letters  H V  etc. hint at twelve boundaries, which are in Tiferet, as we explained in the Gate of the Particulars of the Names; not because of this will Heh not hint at Binah or at Malkhut, and likewise Yod at Chokhmah. And in these things there is further to explain according to what we explained in a saying of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Gate of Names, chapter 6: that the order of the letters is: the Alef includes all the letters, and it is a source for them, and all of them draw from it. And afterward they are divided into seven sevens, which are twenty-one. How so?  B G D   H V   Z Ch  are the secret of the line of Chesed;  Ṭ Y   K L   M N S  are the secret of the line of compassion;  Ā P   Tz Q   R Sh T  are the line of judgment. How so?  B G D  are literally in Chesed;  H V Z  are in Netzach; Ch in Malkhut from the side of Chesed.  Ṭ Y K  are in Tiferet;  L M N  are in Yesod; S is Malkhut from the side of the middle line.  Ā P Tz  are in Gevurah;  Q R Sh  are in Hod; T in Malkhut from the side of the line of judgment. And behold, three in Malkhut, from the side of three lines; just as there are three in each and every sefirah, from the side of three lines. How so? Alef: Yod at its head, Chesed; Yod at its end, Gevurah; and Vav in the middle, Tiferet. And the Alef is a source for all the letters, in the secret that it includes all three lines, as we explained. Afterward  B G D  are bestowed to Chesed in the secret of three lines. From the side of Chesed it is Bet, that is to say, a house [bayit] for all the effluence to bestow. Afterward, from the side of judgment, Gimel, which is to say Gevurah; and nevertheless it does kindness [gomelet chesed]. And afterward Dalet, from the side of Tiferet; for it is the door [delet] of all the effluence that is bestowed. Or the reverse: Gimel in Tiferet, for it is third to them, and it does good kindnesses; and Dalet in Gevurah, for from there is the poverty [dalut] of the effluence and its diminishment.  H V Z  in Netzach: Heh from the side of Chesed, that is, the union of a man and his wife; and what was poor [Dalet] from the side of judgment was set right and became Heh in the secret of Chesed. Vav from the side of Tiferet, as its sense. Zayin from the side of judgment, that is, in the secret of lamp and fire, which is from the side of Gevurah; and likewise Yod over Vav is a lamp above, at the head of the shaft of the menorah. Chet, Malkhut from the side of Chesed; that is, literally Chesed or chayyim [life], for it is all one.  Ṭ Y K  in Tiferet; for so it comes in reckoning to tal [dew, 39], which is  Y H V, which is in Tiferet; and it brings down the dew. Tet from the side of Chesed; that is, "YHVH is good [tov] to all" (Ps. 145:9); and it is compassion and life, as is proved in the Zohar in the explanation of the letter Tet. Yod from the side of Tiferet; for so it is compassion; Tiferet is glorified in ten sefirot, that is, Yod. And likewise Malkhut with respect to Tiferet is called Yod, the diadem of her husband. Kaf is from the side of Gevurah; for so it is said (Ezek. 21:19), "smite hand [kaf] to hand"; and likewise it is called the scale [kaf] of guilt; except that through Tiferet it becomes the scale of merit.  L M N  in Yesod: its permutation is namal [haven], and it is Yesod; and Malkhut is a ship to the haven.

And further, Malkhut is called nemalah [ant], and of her it is said (Prov. 6:6), "consider her ways, and be wise." And Yesod is namal without the foreskin [orlah], which is circumcision [milah]; and likewise the Shekhinah is called pure, fine flour without bran; she is called nemalah. Lamed from the side of Chesed; for so Lamed is in Binah, in the secret of the tower that flies in the air; and it is bestowed from the side of Chesed. Mem in the secret of Tiferet, for through it the waters [mayim] of Chesed are bestowed to it. Nun from the side of Gevurah; in it is falling [nefilah]. Samekh is Malkhut, which is supported [semukhah] from the side of the line of compassion; and in it "YHVH upholds [somekh] all that fall" (Ps. 145:14).  Ā P Tz  in Gevurah. Ayin from the side of Chesed; for in it are springs [einot] of water; and the arousal of love is in the eyes; and this is the right eye; and of it it is said (Ps. 33:18), "Behold, the eye of YHVH is upon them that fear Him"; and likewise the eye sees, and seeing is in Chesed. Peh [mouth] from the side of Tiferet, which comes to milah [word/circumcision, 85]; and likewise "Who has made man's mouth," etc., "is it not I, YHVH?" (Exod. 4:11): Binah through Tiferet; and likewise the voice goes out from the mouth, which is Tiferet. Tzadi from the side of Gevurah; for even though it is judgment, "the place of judgment, that wickedness was there" (Eccl. 3:16), there righteousness [tzedek], judgment, the Righteous One [Tzaddik].  Q R Sh  in Hod; and when it is turned to the attribute of judgment, the letters are turned to sheker [falsehood]; for it prevails in the secret of the husk that prevails through judgment. Kof from the side of Chesed: there "YHVH is near [karov] unto all them that call upon Him" (Ps. 145:18); and there is the kometz [handful]; and with all this it is a serpent because of the left, as we shall explain. Resh from the side of Tiferet, which is head [rosh] to the Patriarchs, binding the three of them. And so he explained in the Sefer ha-Bahir why it is called heavens: that it is round like a head; and I explained it in the Gate of Arbiters. Shin from the side of Gevurah; for there is Binah, the root [shoresh] of the tree. Tav in Malkhut from the side of Gevurah, of which it is said (Ezek. 9:4), "and set a mark [ve-hitvita tav]." Sometimes Tav is "you shall die" [tamut], and sometimes Tav is "you shall live" [tichyeh]; all according to the receiving. This is the order of the letters according to what we hold, following Rashbi, peace be upon him. Therefore we shall portray the letters in general after the manner of the menorah, like this:

And now we shall come to the explanation of each and every letter by itself, according to what is found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and the other commentators, with the help of YHVH and His salvation:

The letter Alef: the author of the Sefer ha-Temunah explained that its principal is in Keter, with the joining of the two attributes, which are Chokhmah and Binah; and this is the Vav in the middle, it is Keter. And it is above them all; and especially when we set it upright like this, א, and two Yods on its two sides are the two attributes. For to this hint the Yod that is in it on the right side is found looking upward, like this, א, hinting at Chokhmah, which looks upward to receive. The second Yod, which is Binah, looks downward, like this, א, to bestow to the lower ones; for she is the mother crouching upon the children to nurse them; and therefore she is called Shekhinah, for she causes to dwell and binds the two first ones with the seven days of the building. And he said further that the Alef is hinted, that it is Vav with two Yods, which comes to twenty-six. And the intent is to say that the Alef is the three first ones, and the principal is in Keter. And it is known that Keter bestows in Tiferet; for it is raised up to it by way of the middle line. And therefore the revealing of this letter is through Keter. And if so, it is found that the spirituality of this letter is a hint of its being included of the manifestation of the three first ones, Keter being principal and prevailing; and the portraying [of the Alef] is by way of Tiferet. And he said there that the dominion of this form and spirituality is at the hour of Venus [Nogah]. And there is one who explained that Tiferet is hinted in the Vav, and the two Yods are its two arms, and they are open to receive Malkhut and to embrace her. Or it may mean that the Vav is the arms stretched out to receive Malkhut, as we explained; and the first Yod is a hint to Chokhmah, from where it was emanated; and the second Yod a hint to Malkhut, the last Heh. And according to this the whole four-letter name is found in the form of Alef. And there is one who explained that Alef hints at the Supreme Crown, which is called Alef; and it is pele [wonder], from the language of "if there arise a matter too hard [yippale]" (Deut. 17:8); for it is concealed and hidden from the eye of all. And there is one who explained in another sense, and these are his words: "Alef has three sides: head and middle and end. The head is from the upper side, to which it is attached; and it points to the substance of wisdom and the memory of the power from which it is emanated. And the middle points to the substance of the intellect that multiplies from the wisdom; and the end points to the knowledge that multiplies from the intellect. And this is its form, ready to understand the work of the upper ones; and it is a beginning to found the lower ones. Therefore it is made one thing; and they are like the firstborn of knowledge, these three sides, an absolute effluence; and they draw power from this part that is before it, from the side of their equalization. And by their merit and their radiance they bore a receptacle for the emanated power, and the one lacking from them; which is the Gedulah seen in the ten sefirot, which is the totality of the branches of Chokhmah, which are in the upper roots beside Keter, in order to draw the power of strengthening in all the sefirot." And there is one who explained: the Supreme Crown is a great Alef, and it is a spirituality in the secret of the upper alphabet; the spirituality is head to every alphabet; and it is called Alef because it is true and first; and on it everything depends, in the secret of the form of Alef and "the middle bar," which bears the upper and the lower ones. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 117a), these are his words: "Alef: Yod above, Yod below; wisdom at the head and wisdom at the end; Vav, the binding of the two of them." Thus far his words.

And its matter is that in the form of the Alef is the inclusion of three sefirot, which are Chokhmah and Malkhut, and they are two Yods (for Malkhut too is called Yod, as is explained in the Gate of Manifestations), and the Vav that is in the middle of the two of them is Tiferet, which unites them together; for through Tiferet Malkhut rises to Chokhmah. And elsewhere he said: "the second, Binah, as they established: at all events Alef is Binah," etc. And it appears that in Keter Alef is from the language of pele, which points to the utmost concealment.

And further, just as Alef is first to the letters, so the Supreme Crown is the beginning of the Emanation. And in Binah, the language of alef is the language of teaching, from the language of "and I shall teach you [a'allefkha] wisdom" (Job 33:33); and likewise she is called Binah, the language of understanding.
And further, in the Supreme Crown it is the large Alef specifically.

And further, in the Supreme Crown it is from the language of alluf [chief], that is to say, great; for the Supreme Crown is chief to all the Emanation. And by all the explanations it points in it to the concealment. And in Tiferet it is also the large Alef, when it is concealed in Keter, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations.

And further, there is a small Alef, and it is hinted in Malkhut, to hint that she is first from below to above. And others explained: to hint that she is concealed from the lower ones, from the language of pele. And it is already possible to explain it in the language of alluf: for as the relation of Keter to the Emanation, so is the relation of Malkhut to all that is beneath her. And it is possible that it is the language of teaching, as "and I shall teach you wisdom"; for she is what makes the prophets wise and shows them the upper Emanation. Further, Alef hints at Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; and likewise it hints at three in the manifestation of Chesed, and all is Chesed. And likewise it hints: Binah, the upper Yod; Malkhut, the lower Yod; Vav in the middle, Tiferet, which holds the two of them in the secret of the union. And these three explanations Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, and we wrote them in the Gate of Names, with the help of Heaven. And in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 73a), these are his words: "And come and see: the first word of the Torah that they give to children, Alef-Bet: this is a word that the people of the world cannot cleave to with understanding and cannot raise with desire; and all the more to speak with their mouth. And even upper angels, and the upper ones of the upper ones, cannot cleave to it, because they are the closed things of the holy Name. And a thousand and four hundred and five myriad worlds all hang on the thorn of the Alef. And seventy-two holy names engraved in inscribed letters, on which the upper and the lower ones stand, the heavens and the earth and the Throne of glory of the King, hang from one side to one side. For the extension of the Alef is the sustaining of all the worlds, and the supports of the upper and lower ones, in the secret of wisdom. And enclosed tracks and deep rivers and ten utterances all go out from that lower thorn that is beneath the Alef. From here onward the Alef begins to spread out into the Bet. And there is no reckoning to the wisdom that is engraved here." Thus far his words, as relevant to our matter. And the reason for the concealment of these worlds in the Alef is because the Alef is a hint at Keter. And it is already known that in Keter all the worlds and all the Emanation were included before the spreading out, as we explained in the preceding gates. And therefore all the things mentioned in the saying were included in it: the letter Alef, which is Keter, pele, alef. Or it is possible, as we explained above, that Alef is in Chesed, the head of the revealing in seven days; and it is a letter that includes all the letters, as we explained above in the previous chapter. Further, he explained (in the Zohar Chadash, Song of Songs, fol. 77) that Alef is a Yod at the head, Chokhmah; Vav, Tiferet; and a Yod below, Malkhut; and the thorn of the lower Yod is a hint at all the camps that are beneath her, small and great, outer and inner, included in Malkhut, who is the very self of the Yod:

On the letter Bet we shall copy the language of the Sefer ha-Temunah and what appears to us in its explanation: "Bet: from its form they make Dalet-Vav; and this is its form: . And it is two paths, to the upper and the lower Wisdom; and its portraying points to two attributes; for it includes Tiferet, that is to say, the court of the Holy One, blessed be He," etc. Thus far his words.

And his intent is to say that the Bet hints at Chokhmah. However, the hint in it is that it is Dalet-Vav [du, two]; and they are the two faces [du partzufin], which are Tiferet and Malkhut, of which it is said, "they were created with two faces." And they are two together when they are in Chokhmah; for then she rises in the degree of the rib, which was in Chokhmah, a rib to Tiferet. For one should not think that the diminishment of the moon and the matter of "and He took one of his ribs" (Gen. 2:21) are all one matter. Rather, "and He took one of his ribs" is in their emanation in Chokhmah, where they were included as one, united, like Adam, who was with his wife two-faced. And there, from Chokhmah, they were divided into two, and he entered Binah and she brought her to him; and there they were "two great lights" (Gen. 1:16). And afterward was the diminishment of the moon; for it is a matter by itself. And because they are du in Chokhmah, therefore the filling of the Yod is Dalet-Vav; for the filling and the impregnation of the Yod is Chokhmah, and its paths are the two faces. And it has already been explained that the Bet that is in Chokhmah is the hint to the paths, as it is written (Prov. 8:2), "in the house [beit] of the paths she stands." And therefore the portraying of the Bet is a hint to the two faces, which are two sefirot below. And this is what he said, "and its portraying, two attributes." And we explained this matter at length in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon, chapter 4. And what he said, that it is a house for Tiferet: the intent is that the thirty-two paths are also in Tiferet, as is explained in the preceding gates; and likewise thirty-two [LaV] and lulav are hinted in it; for the four-letter name comes to twenty-six, and six extremities, they are thirty-two. And therefore Malkhut too is a house, for she is a house for Tiferet, to conduct the world, whether for judgment or for compassion. The rule that emerges: the spirituality of the Bet hints at Chokhmah with its thirty-two paths that are in the two faces; and it includes Malkhut, who draws from Gevurah; for the force of judgment is the cause of her blemish and her fullness, as is known; therefore its dominion is at the hour of the moon. Thus far. And there is one who explained that the Bet is Malkhut; and because she was united with her husband, his two arms with which he embraced her were portrayed in her, and he is in the middle, like this: . And this is in the secret of "Set me as a seal" (Song 8:6): that his form remain engraved in her. And the thorn of the Bet is a Yod, to hint that she was emanated from Chokhmah. And close to this matter is found in the Tikkunim: that the Bet is three Vavs, three pillars, which are  V H V,  Y L Y,  S Y Ṭ, the Patriarchs supporting the Shekhinah, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations, in the manifestation of the Heh that is in Malkhut. And most of the commentators agreed that the Bet is in Chokhmah; and Rabbi Moshe [de León] explained the reason: that it is second; and its thorn is to show that there is above a manifestation subtler than all subtle. And there is one who explained close to this matter in another sense, and these are his words: "Bet has two sides in its substance, going out on the side; two sides, behind it and before it; and it is open, in order to receive the addition of the holy spirit from the side of the Alef, like words in the mouth of a disciple; and it is the house; and its form is ready to contain the principal of the unity. And this is the explanation of its matters and the understanding of its proofs, in the discernment of wisdom and the precision of intellect." And Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas, fol. 256b), explained, these are his words: "Anokhi [I] (Exod. 20:2): in it Kaf, Keter; and in it Ayin. And it is called Keter from the side of the upper Mother; for the going out from Egypt is mentioned toward her fifty times in the Torah. And she is the Bet of Bereshit, which includes ten utterances from the side of Chokhmah, the daughter of Yod," etc. Thus far his words.

And its explanation: he comes to explain "I am YHVH your God"; and he said that in the word Anokhi is the hint to Keter; and in Anokhi are the letters Ayin, which is Keter; and there is Kaf, which is Keter. And he explained to us that it is called Keter from the side of Binah, as we explained in the Glossary of Titles; and for this reason the going out from Egypt is mentioned there; as it is known that fifty times the going out from Egypt is mentioned in the Torah, to hint at the fifty gates of Binah, as we explained in the Gate of Fifty Gates. And he said that Binah is the Bet of Bereshit. The intent of this length is to explain how the ten Commandments were divided, five in the first and five in the last; it is from the side of the ten Commandments that are in Chokhmah, which are bestowed to Binah. And for this reason he said of her "Yod": "Through wisdom is a house built" (Prov. 24:3).
And behold, according to this saying, Bet is Binah.

And further, in the Song of Songs of Rashbi, peace be upon him: "Alef, male; Bet, female." And behold, the female is not in Chokhmah, as is known. And in truth all this is the reverse of his words in other places, where he explained that Bet is always in Chokhmah. And to answer this it seems to me to say that by what he said, "Through wisdom is a house built," and likewise in other places, that Yod is the spring to the garden, which is Binah, everything is answered. For since the Yod builds the house, if so it is required that the root of the house and its subtle manifestation be concealed in its source; and if so they are two houses: a house concealed in Chokhmah, and a house in Binah. Further, there is a small house; it is Malkhut; and its source is Tiferet, and the spring Yesod, as this is explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him:

The letter Gimel. What is explained from the words of the author of the Sefer ha-Temunah is that the power of this letter is in Binah; and therefore it is third. And it is called Gimel from the language of gomel [bestowing], for it bestows on all through the completion of the extremes to the mean; that is to say, judgment and compassion are changed, and through it the actions go out to act with speed; for it is also from the language of "and bore [va-yigmol] almonds" (Num. 17:23). And these two things are clear: for from her Gevurah receives compassion and is washed in the milk of the mother, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 6. And therefore, when she (receives) [sweetens] the judgment, peace is found between judgment and Chesed. And likewise all seven sefirot of the building receive from her, and through her act with speed. And in their form, Vav and Zayin; for the Zayin is a hint in Netzach, and the Vav a hint in Tiferet, as will be explained. Therefore this spiritual form hints that its principal drawing is from Binah, and it is portrayed in its form through Tiferet and Netzach; and therefore its dominion is through the sun, which is in Tiferet, as is known. And there are those who explained: the head of the Gimel is a Yod that has four thorns, which are Keter above, and Chokhmah to the right, and Binah to the left, and Chesed beneath the three of them; this is the form of the head of the Gimel. And the Vav, which is upright, is Tiferet; and the leg, which is stretched out, is the right hand stretched out to receive those who return; and the thorn is a hint to Malkhut; and it is the recompense [gemul] of the righteous, who sit with their diadems on their heads. And there is one who explained that Gimel hints at Chesed, because it does good [gomel tov] to the guilty and purifies them. And there is one who explained in another sense, these are his words: "Gimel has two sides: a staff, and the wood of the staff is held in its middle, after the pattern of radiance, made to receive the effluence of the letters from above to below; and it is open in front, in order to bestow of that power in the letters that are below it. And it has a window after its pattern; because all the letters are forms standing in the equalization of the windows that were created within them; and they are like shining mirrors, like glass dyed in kinds of colors, ready to complete a work with them." And there are those who explained as an acronym of  B G D: Binah gomel dallim [Binah bestows on the poor]. And the poor are Yesod and Malkhut, and they were called poor, as is explained in the Glossary of Titles; and they receive from Binah. And likewise she also does kindnesses, in the secret of her bestowal by way of Chesed; and that is its thorn toward the right, the channel of the effluence:

The letter Dalet: he said in the Sefer ha-Temunah that it is hinted in Chesed; and so it is fourth in the simple number. And he said that it is a simple form, which has no joining with another; and it looks to Tiferet, which is the Vav. And he did not say that it looks to the Heh, because in the Heh too there is the Dalet; and through this it looks to the Vav. And it is found according to this that the spirituality of the letter receives from Chesed and from compassion, which is Tiferet. And he said that it is called Dalet from the language of "and the hair [dallat] of your head like purple" (Song 7:6), whose explanation is the matter of separation, from the language of singleness; as the part of the head that is separated from its fellow. And likewise this letter is single in its form, for it does not join in another form. And he said that its dominion is at the hour of Mercury [Kokhav]. And there is one who explained that the Dalet is the explanation of the Gimel; that is, as he explained above concerning the Gimel, that at its head it has four thorns, etc.; except that this one is reversed, to hint at the wicked, who overturn the upper things and confound "their father's couch" (Gen. 49:4); and therefore death is turned for them from life, God forbid. But the Gimel, which is the recompense of the righteous, they sit with their crowns on their heads, as we explained above in the letter Gimel. And there is one who explained that Dalet hints at the Diadem, who stands at the door [delet] of the King like a poor woman. And there is one who explained in another sense, and these are his words: "Dalet has two sides, a stretched side and a supported side; and it is a mould to complete the matter of the elements, attached in the middle of the Gimel; and its window has substance in it, to contain from all its sides, from below and not from above; and nevertheless it is called the essence of formation." And therefore, according to the Zohar, the Shekhinah is called delet; and she is so called when she is poor [dalah] in poverty; and the thorn of the Dalet hints at Yesod, which joins her with Tiferet, in the secret of "for all [kol] that is in the heaven and in the earth" (1 Chron. 29:11). And this is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna and in many places. Also it hints at Binah; for so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Zohar, Mishpatim, fol. 123b), these are his words: "Heh was Dalet; when the male joined with her, she conceived one son and was called Heh." Thus far his words; and we copied it in the Gate of Names, chapter 1.

And behold, he said that Binah, which is Heh, its principal is Dalet; and the manifestation of the Dalet is its thorn, which is Chokhmah; and "the river spreads out from here and from here": that is, the spreading out of Binah from the right, which is Chesed, and from the left, which is Gevurah. You are found to say that the manifestation of the Dalet is also in Binah, in the secret of her spreading out in Chesed and Gevurah; and we have already spoken at length on this, all that is needed, in the gate mentioned. And the language of dalet in Binah will not be the language of poverty, but the language of "my eyes are lifted [dallu] upward" (Isa. 38:14); and likewise the language of the Mishnah (Pe'ah, ch. 4), "on a trellis [dalit] and on a palm," which is the language of height:

The letter Heh: he explained in the Sefer ha-Temunah that its principal is in Gevurah. However, it is also in Malkhut, as is known in the matter of the four-letter name. And he said that it is a hint that the attribute of judgment can act harshly and softly; and he said that all this is by the power of Binah. And it is true that through her the judgment is softened or strengthened, as we explained above; and therefore it hints also at Binah. And its form is yad [hand, Yod-Dalet]; and we have found yad for good, as "with a high hand," "the great hand" (Exod. 14:8, 31), "Is YHVH's hand waxed short?" (Num. 11:23); and yad for judgment: "For indeed the hand of YHVH was against them" (Deut. 2:15). And likewise there are many hands, as we explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. In brief: the spiritual form of this letter receives its principal from Gevurah, but receives also from Binah; and through her the judgment is softened, and it becomes soft below in its receiving from her. And its dominion is at the hour of the moon; for therefore it is hinted in Malkhut, the power of the moon. And there is one who explained that the letter Heh is Malkhut; and its Dalet points to half a round threshing floor; and in the middle of the half threshing floor, which are the seventy of the Sanhedrin, the father of the court stands, and he is the small Vav that is beneath the Dalet. And all is hinted in Malkhut; for she is the source of judgment; and she is the moon that stands like half a threshing floor, like the moon; and the point in the middle is its fullness. Further, he explained in another manner: that the Dalet is a hint to Malkhut, and the small Vav a hint to Metatron, the son of the Shekhinah; and he sucks from between the breasts of his mother. And this is somewhat right according to what we wrote on the matter of the explanation of the Heh in the Gate of Names, in the four-letter name. Further, he said a correct matter: that the Heh is the Shekhinah standing upon the four living creatures of the Chariot, and they are  A B   G D; and it is fine. And there is one who explained in another sense, these are his words: "Heh stands in its pattern, open, in order to receive effluence from every side; and open opposite it, before it; for all the letters draw from it, after the manner of the effluence that it draws. And it is closed from above, so that the effluence not spread out to go outside it." And likewise we have already explained in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name and in the Gate of Gates that the manifestation of the Heh is in two places, which are Binah and Malkhut; and in both of them in one way; for the manifestation of the form of the Heh is three Yesods [three Vavs]; and they are in Binah because they were emanated through her, and in Malkhut because they bestow in her, and she is adorned through them in the secret of the coupling, as we explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation.

And behold, Malkhut is poor [Dalet] when she draws from the two extremes, from the right and from the left; and then the serpent seeks to suck; until she receives from the middle and her husband is portrayed in her, that is, Vav, whether it be the Vav of Tiferet itself or the Vav of Yesod; then she is full of all good; and that is Heh, made a vessel:

The letter Vav: he said in the Sefer ha-Temunah that it is in Tiferet; and it is well known. And he said that it is simple, to hint that it is a pillar for the world. And it is possible to say the reason: that at first the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world in judgment; and when He saw that the world would not endure, He associated compassion with it; behold, the compassion is the cause of the endurance of the world; and therefore the compassion is a pillar supporting the world. And he said that its face is turned away from the Heh, to hint that the Heh is judgment in which there is no compassion. And it is possible to say the reason is that it inclines toward Chesed and turns its face from judgment. Or it is possible that it looks to the Zayin that is before it, for it bestows in it, as we shall explain. And he said that it watches above, toward Keter, to receive, and watches below, to bestow to Malkhut, as is known. And he said that its dominion is at the hour of the sun; for so it is titled, as it is said (Ps. 84:12), "For YHVH God is a sun and shield."

And there is one who explained in another sense, these are his words: "Vav stands in this form, to inscribe in it the form of nature, and to find in it a hidden pattern; and what is recognized in this form is called the primordial matter." And therefore it is true that the place specific to it is Tiferet; however, the hint to it is when it is bound and included of six extremities, which are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod. And to hint at its beauty in this inclusion, it is called Vav, which comes to six. And it is long; for it is the river that waters, by way of concealment, in the secret of Da'at, all the other plantings of the garden, as is explained in the preceding gates; and almost then it is called the soul of Tiferet, as we hinted there. And when the Vav is in Tiferet, it is called the upper Vav, or Vav without qualification; however, sometimes Yesod is called the small Vav or the lower Vav; because it too is included of six extremities, like Tiferet itself; for "all that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph," for "body and covenant are counted as one," as is explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in many places. However, there is another Vav, and it is at the head of Keter; we explained it in the Gate of Arbiters at its end. And sometimes the Vavs also go round on Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, three Vavs; and that is  V H V,  Y L Y,  S Y Ṭ, three Vavs; and likewise Netzach, Hod, Yesod, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And these are the words of Rabbi Moshe de León, of blessed memory, in the Sefer ha-Shem, on "the hooks [vavei] of the pillars" (Exod. 27:10): "The hooks of the pillars, in the secret of the Vav of 'in Yah is His name' (Ps. 68:5), which is the staff of Moses, six sefirot," etc. "And there is no Vav without two Vavs" [Vav-Alef-Vav]; "and it is a hint to Yesod, which takes hold of it":

The letter Zayin: he explained in the Sefer ha-Temunah that its form is in Netzach; and it is a hint to a weapon [klei zayin], to be victorious [lenatze'ach] in judgment. And likewise it is the attribute of Moses, and by it he was victorious in the war of Amalek; for he would raise his hand, and then Israel prevailed; and it is the raising of the right hand, which is Netzach, over the left, which is Hod; and then the power of compassion prevails. And likewise in the lifting of the hands [of the priests] one must raise the right over the left. And when a man raises his hand it will be seen like a Zayin in the stretching of his fingers; and it is hinted in Netzach, where the victory is, through the Zayin. And he said that its dominion is at the hour of the sun, for the reason that the power of compassion prevails over it through Tiferet; and therefore it rules at the hour of the dominion of the sun, which is the planet of Tiferet. In brief: the spirituality of this letter hints at the side of Netzach alone.

And there is one who explained that the Zayin is Yesod; and it is the secret of the covenant; and it is the secret of the Sabbath. And just as the Sabbath is a diadem over the six days of work, so in the Zayin there is a diadem over the Vav; and this diadem is the diadem that is in the covenant. And just as the Sabbath gives sustenance to all the other days of the week, so this letter is called Zayin on account of the sustenance [mazon] bestowed from it. And it is the covenant drawn from Tiferet, which is the body hinted in the Vav; and the Zayin, the covenant; and the Chet, the female, standing to receive, and opening her legs to receive the effluence of the male.

And there are those who explained in another sense: "Zayin stands in this form in order to set right the equalization and division for the emanated golem and what is made from matter." And there is one who explained that Zayin hints at the attribute of Gevurah, which takes weapons to fight against the wicked; and therefore Zayin. What is well known in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim on the matter of this letter is that its form is a hint to Vav and Yod. And behold, it is explained in two things. For Malkhut, in her rising to her first place, "unto her father's house, as in her youth" (Lev. 22:13), does she not rise by way of the rungs of the ladder? And in her rising to the head of the Righteous One, then she is a diadem on the head of every righteous one. And the intent is that the garment of the righteous in the world to come is from the side of Malkhut; and this is "and Esther put on royalty [malkhut]" (Esth. 5:1); for she saw her world in her lifetime. However, this is from the side of Malkhut, when she is below, reigning in this world; but in her rising above, from the side of Binah, for through her being the mother she rises to her father's house, she is a diadem on the head of the Righteous One, the Foundation of the World. And this is "In the world to come there is neither eating," etc., "but the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads"; for the world to come is Binah, as is explained in its entry. And this is "And Mordecai went forth from the presence of the king" (Esth. 8:15), which is Binah, "in royal apparel," from the side of Malkhut, as is explained, "and with a great crown of gold," from the side of the diadem on the head of each and every righteous one. And this is that he saw his world in his lifetime. And by this is understood why a diadem [atarah] was not given to Esther, but a royal crown [keter malkhut]. And because the diadem is on the head of the Righteous One, there is found Yod over Vav, and it is Zayin; therefore it is the seventh day; and this is not the place for its explanation. And this is the small Zayin, for its name was not made well known.

And further, there is a diadem on the head of the Torah scroll; and it is called, in the language of Rashbi, peace be upon him (in Tikkun 10, fol. 23a), "the crown [taga] of the Torah scroll"; and this is in her rising by way of the rungs up to Chokhmah above; and this is the diadem of her husband; and then she is Yod over Vav, and she is Zayin. And to these Zayins is the hint of the crowns [tagin]; and this is that Tiferet too is the seventh day. And sometimes this Yod settles on the head of the three Patriarchs, and they make three Zayins, like the matter of Shin; and likewise in Netzach, Hod, Yesod. And all this is ears of gleaning from the field of Rashbi, peace be upon him:

The letter Chet: he explained in the Sefer ha-Temunah that it is in Hod, which is eighth from above to below; and he said that it also hints at Binah from below to above; and both of them are judgment, as is known. And he said that because it is in Hod, the attribute of Aaron the priest, he had eight garments, as is known. And likewise Aaron was a man of Chesed, as he says (Deut. 33:8), "Your Thummim and Your Urim be with Your pious one," to hint that it too receives from Binah, which is over Chesed; but its principal is in Hod. And he said that the form of this letter includes [two letters], which are Dalet-Vav, to hint that it receives effluence also from Chesed, which is Dalet, as we explained; and all is ten [Dalet-Vav, 4+6], to hint that all is included in Malkhut, which is tenth. And he said that the language of Chet is from the language of "And your mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed [ve-chattu]" (Obad. 1:9), to hint at the judgment of Hod; for it is the principal. And he said that its dominion is at the hour of the moon, for the reason that the moon is (the crown) [the power] in Malkhut; and this, all is included in ten, as we explained. And his words are supported in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, as we explained in the Gate of Fifty Gates: that Hod comes to the number fifty, which is five times Vav-Dalet [ten]; all comes to fifty; for up to Hod fifty gates spread out, and all of them are revealed through Malkhut, as we explained there. And the rule of his words is that the spiritual form of this letter receives from Binah and Chesed, and from Tiferet, and from Hod.

And there is one who explained that the Chet is a hint to the Shekhinah, open below, after the way of the woman, who is closed on three sides and open on a fourth side to receive the effluence of her husband. And further, it is a portico in which is the dwelling of the souls. And it has two sides: the right side corresponding to the congregation that saves, and the left side corresponding to the congregation that judges; and the body of the Shekhinah over the two of them; and the fourth side open to receive: whoever wishes to plead merit, let him come and plead; and the Righteous One is placed between the two bands, to declare righteous and to declare guilty. And further, three sides are a hint to the three Patriarchs: the right arm to the right side, and the left arm to the left side, and the body, which is Tiferet, over them; and that is three Vavs,  V H V,  Y L Y,  S Y Ṭ, as we explained. …
And there is one who explained in another sense, and these are his words: that Chet hints at Gevurah, from the language of "and the terror [chittat] of God was" (Gen. 35:5), which is fear.

And there is one who explained in another sense, and these are his words: "Chet is so called on account of its being a mould for the cause of the golem, a spiritual golem and a bodily golem; the likeness of the Chet is a form for all things that are natural living beings; and therefore it is called in the language of chayyim [life]." And the hint of this letter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in the Zohar, Pinchas, fol. 257a) in the word echad [one]: that the Chet is hinted in eight sefirot, from Chokhmah downward to Yesod. And these are his words: "Echad: ach [Alef-Chet] includes nine sefirot: for Alef is Ayin, Keter; Chet, eight sefirot from Chokhmah to Yesod; Dalet, Malkhut," etc. And in other places he explained that Binah is called Chet because she is eighth from below to above; and these are his words: "Binah, which is eighth of ten sefirot from below to above." Thus far. And it is possible to settle and say that when Binah includes the eight from below to above, then she is called Chet. And possibly Chet because she is the bestowal of the life [chiyyut] to all the sefirot from Chokhmah, which is the source of the life that flows in her. And by this the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, are settled and reconciled.

The letter Tet: the author of the Sefer ha-Temunah explained that this letter is in Yesod, which is ninth. And he said that this attribute is seventh in the number of the days, even if it is ninth in the number of the sefirot; and the reason is as we explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles, in the entry yamim. And he said that it is called Sabbath, the language of rest, and the language of ceasing and annulment and destruction; and it is called Kol, the language of desire and the language of destruction. And therefore for the good, tovah [good]; and for the wicked, Tet from the language of "and I will sweep it [ve-te'teti'ha] with the besom of destruction" (Isa. 14:23). And for this reason the dominion of this spiritual letter is in the planet Saturn.

And there is one who explained that the Tet shows in its portraying that when Tiferet embraces Malkhut with its holy arms, Malkhut remains pregnant with several souls and several angels and other matters. And behold, its form points to the embrace of the arms; and its inner thorn points to the embryo sitting in its mother's womb, as we explained. And therefore the pregnant woman gives birth at nine months, as the number of Tet. And at the head, on the left side, a Yod, to show that from there, from the Yod, the river and the effluence are drawn round about. And he said further that this letter is a hint to the attribute of Chokhmah, ninth from below to above, and receives from Keter; for Chokhmah is second to it. And therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (in Menachot 34b): "Tat in Katpi is two." And by it the whole world was conceived, and from it it went out, as it is written (Ps. 104:24), "In wisdom You have made them all." Therefore it is in the form of a Yod at its head, and pregnant with the beings of the world that came into being from it, as we explained. And there is one who explained that Tet hints at Gevurah, from the language of "and I will sweep it with the besom of destruction," which is the language of destruction; for it destroys all in judgment.

And there is one who explained in another sense, and this is what he said: "Tet is bent in front and upright on all its sides; and from it are emanated all the things that are the garment of the intellect and the knowledgeable; that is to say, the hidden, which are hidden within it." And on the matter of this letter they explained in the Zohar (Terumah, fol. 151) a great matter: that it is the source of life. And this is the cause that there is a known place in the world in which people do not die, as is explained also from the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Sotah 46b). And the reason is that on its air depends the letter Tet, of the permutation of the letters by which the world was created. And in the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 83a–b) Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the verse (Eccl. 9:14) "a little city" in the manifestation of the Yod; for then there is none who understands it, for it is concealed and small for the apprehension of human beings; and therefore "and few men within it"; and therefore she says (Song 1:6), "Look not upon me, because I am black"; the explanation, do not think that you will apprehend me, for I am concealed. "And there came a great king against it … and built great bulwarks against it": that is the manifestation of the building of the rib, the building of a wall surrounding round about the city. And this is that Binah, her manifestation is Lamed, as was explained; and when she surrounds Malkhut round about, from the Lamed a Tet is made, like this. And I have found those who say that Tet is in Malkhut, in the secret of the manifestation of the light of Binah, which adorns her. And there is no doubt that the manifestation of the Tet is choicer than the manifestation of the Heh; and it is the secret of "For I, says YHVH, will be unto her a wall of fire round about" (Zech. 2:9):

The letter Yod: he explained in the Sefer ha-Temunah that it is Malkhut, the tenth attribute; and it is directed over against Chokhmah, which is called Yod like her. And he explained that the reason for the Yod is that even in her there is no likeness and form, but like a small Yod, a point simple of form and likeness, as it is written (Isa. 40:18), "To whom then will you liken God?" And it is the sign of the covenant, as is known. And the language of Yod is from the language of "Let them give thanks [yodu] to YHVH for His mercy" (Ps. 107:8); for she is the place of thanksgiving and praise, as is well known from David. And its dominion is at the hour of the moon, for it is her attribute, as is known. And he said that up to here [from Alef to Yod they hint at ten sefirot] in their order; and from here onward, as we shall explain, they are not in order.

And there is one who explained: in the Yod four sefirot are hinted, Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Chesed; and I explained them above. And he said that its upper thorn, which is Keter, bestows effluence to two extremes, which are to two sides, this to the right and this to the left, which are Chokhmah and Binah; and below them Chesed, which bestows to the whole spinal cord, which is the Vav; and from there the whole body of the Emanation is (silenced) [watered]. And he said that this is the explanation of Yod in its filling: that Yod is the head that bestows; and the Vav, the body, Tiferet, and the holy covenant; and the Dalet, two legs and two arms; and all is included in the word Yod.
And further he explained: ten sefirot, Yod; six extremities, Vav; four legs of the Chariot, Dalet, "whose troops are without number." Thus far.
And there is one who explained: Yod hints at Chokhmah, which is called Yod, which is a golem without form.

And there is one who explained in another sense, and these are his words: "Yod is a spiritual form that receives effluence and blessing, and becomes an equalization for all of them; and all of them draw from it; and it gathers all of them, and becomes like the likeness of an upright form, silent, and sits at the head, and becomes head to all of them; and it is with all of them and outside all of them. And the other letters are hidden in the reversal of their purpose, up to the Shin, which is the knot of the tefillin. For so he said: that twenty-two letters, and their equalization and their preparation, and the reversed letters that change in them, all of them are Vav, bound to one another, to complete an action and to prepare a work; and this is the knot of the tefillin; that is to say, that all of them cleave to the power of the Shin and from the power of the Tav; and Alef becomes head to all of them, and the Yod the inclusion of all of them. And all points to the stature of the Holy One, blessed be He; and this is what it says (Exod. 33:23), 'and you shall see My back; but My face shall not be seen'; its Targum: 'and you shall see what is after Me': that is to say, you shall apprehend what cleaves to Me and is joined to Me, all a completed creature. (But what was before the cause of My existence you cannot apprehend; so that you not say of Me as (of) all the others, until it be said: So-and-so went out from such-and-such a place, and So-and-so was from such-and-such a place; and My unity would be found profane. And the place of holiness is swallowed, like the sword that is swallowed within its sheath.)" Thus far his words. And for us it has already been explained in what preceded that the Yod is in Chokhmah; and likewise according to the manifestation, sometimes in Malkhut; and in strangeness, sometimes it is in Binah. Further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that in the Yod there are three thorns; and these are his words in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 5, fol. 18a): "Yod in every place: its thorn above, and its inside in the middle, and its end below: the totality of the letters, a body for the two of them; and its thorn below, in the secret of the vowels." Thus far his words.
