And because all the Emanation, that is to say the beings, are included in Tiferet and Malkhut; and when Tiferet and Malkhut are united, then it is the union of the upper ones; and then all four letters that are in the Name are united, which are Tiferet and Malkhut and Chokhmah with Binah; and the lower Vav-Heh are concealed with the upper Yod-Heh, until all the sefirot ask, "Where [ayyeh] is the place of His glory," etc. AYeH: they are Alef, Keter; Yod, Chokhmah; Heh, Binah. Mekom: it is the place, which is Tiferet. Kevodo: Malkhut. Le-ha'aritzo: the explanation, to strengthen it with the strength of the bestowal and the coupling and the union in which they are united. And then they are closed and concealed, and there is no bestowal to the worlds, because of the greatness of the concealment. And then it is said chashmal, that is, "at times silent [chashot]"; for there is no flowing to them, until the time of "You open Your hand [yadekha]" (Ps. 145:16), which are the two Yods that are in the name  Y A H D V N H Y: the one in Tiferet and the second in Malkhut, which are the name YHVH and the name Adonai. And when they separate one from another, they bestow to the worlds abundant effluence and blessing from what they received. If so, it is fitting that they be related to kamatz, since in their union they are closed above, and in their union all is closed, and through them the treasured kamatz is revealed. Therefore the principal of the form of the kamatz is Vav, Yod: Tiferet and Malkhut. And Chesed is the beginning of the revealing from Keter, Chokhmah and Binah. And all is one matter, united, a strong and firm bond. And in this there is no wonder at the words of the kabbalists who say that the kamatz is judgment, because it shows closing and concealment, as we explained. And, as it were, meanwhile there is some hiddenness, even though through that hiddenness there is drawn afterward abundant effluence and blessing:

And the servant of the kamatz is the patach; for the reason that it is Tiferet alone, and shows the revealing and the opening [petichah] of the things. And it is that Malkhut, in her coming from before the King, tells her maidens of every kind of food that he eats, which she received from her husband, and the precious things that her husband gave her; and then she shows the King's seal engraved with her, in the matter of "Set me as a seal" (Song 8:6), which we explained in the preceding gates. And for this reason in some places he explained that the patach is in Gevurah; because through it she separates from leaning upon her beloved, in order to divide and to give food to her household and a portion to her maidens. And sometimes the patach is related to Chokhmah, because it too reveals and opens Keter and bestows its matter below, in the secret of the thirty-two paths, which reveal their root, which are the six hundred and twenty pillars of light, the branches of Keter, that we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And there is one who explained concerning the patach that it is the Shekhinah; and she is the opening [petach] to all the upper Emanation; and he said that it is over against the firmament created on the second day. Further, he explained that the patach is a hint to the firmament, which is a veil that serves beneath the Shekhinah; and possibly he intended Sandalfon, who is a veil in the seventh palace, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces. And concerning the kamatz he explained that the firmament is the firmament mentioned above, and the point is Metatron, who is beneath the firmament mentioned. And in the sefirot, the kamatz is Hod and Yesod; and Yesod is called kamatz because it gathers the effluence and closes it within it. And the vowel sheva: Rashbi explained that it is called the servant of servants, for it serves all the vowels. And the sheva, its pronunciation is in tzeirei; and it is the reverse of the tzeirei: for the tzeirei is a hint to the two great lights, and the sheva a great light and a small light. And this certainly shows that after their union the bundle was separated, and she descended below to bestow; and therefore she is below, revealing the matter of the union in their separating one from another. And sometimes it is with the patach, for the reason that Gevurah, which is (the patach) [the sheva], in the force of its judgment required the diminishment and her being a small light and a great light; and therefore [the patach] comes with it, to show what is said. Or it is possible to hint that, even though they are a small light and a great light, which shows the diminishment, nevertheless the eye of her husband is upon her, which is patach, which is Vav, "and His glory He will not give to another" (Isa. 42:8), God forbid. And there is one who explained the matter of the sheva, that it is Yesod and Malkhut; and therefore it is hurried [mitchatef] more than the other vowels, because the fire of Malkhut is swallowed in the fire of Yesod. And in the angels he explained that they are Metatron and Gabriel, who are one above the other. And therefore the reason for the chataf: so as not to mention the matter of the diminishment, but on the contrary to conceal it, for the sake of "It is the glory of God to hide a thing" (Prov. 25:2). And further, so as not to arouse the judgment; for the sheva in its pronunciation arouses the power of judgment; and because it arouses the judgment, therefore when it is with a ga'ya, which is Vav, which is her husband, then it is turned to compassion entirely. And the divisions of the ga'ya will be explained in the Gate of Cantillation Marks, with the help of Heaven. And likewise sheva is judgment, and it needs no proof. And we did not wish to lengthen in the explanation of words and Names and vowels; for the principal of this matter is in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him:
After we explained in the preceding chapters the matter of the vowels in particular, we shall come in this chapter to clarify them in general.

And behold, the vowels in general are subtle branches, emanated and branching out in the letters. And the source of their emanation is from Chokhmah; and from there is their coming into being and their revealing, and from there their manifestation. And this Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkun 70, fol. 123b), these are his words: "'And their rings': this is the upper Mother, who is over the sefirot that are beneath her, from whom are all the letters. 'And as for their height': this is Chokhmah, from where are the vowel points." Thus far his words.

Behold, explicitly: as is the relation of the source of the letters from Binah, so is the relation of the source of the vocalization from Chokhmah. And even though we said that their source and their coming into being are from Chokhmah, nevertheless it is through Keter; for by the power of Keter Chokhmah emanated them. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 83): "The vowel points go out from the secret of the brain, to sustain the letters in their tikkunin; and by one point a word is changed, and it passes that word from existence (in existence) [another version: into another fashion]. The Lamp of Darkness [Botzina de-Kardinuta], when it struck that air in the brain, struck and did not strike, reached toward that brain and departed from it, reached and did not reach; then that striking went out toward the letters from within the brain, and the letters were vocalized." Thus far his words.

And its explanation: "The vowel points," etc.: the explanation, they go out from the secret of Chokhmah; and not from Chokhmah from the side of her outer aspects that spread out, but from the side of her inner aspects; that is, "the secret of the brain." And he did not say "from the brain," but "from its secret" and its inwardness; that is, her aspect that cleaves to Keter; for by the power of Keter they were emanated, as he goes on to explain. And he called Chokhmah "brain" and did not call her by her known name, for two reasons. The first, to show the concealment of the aspect of the source of the vocalization; that is, the aspect of her being brain; that is, from her side that draws near to the membrane of the brain, to the skull, which are titles related to Keter, as is explained in the Glossary of Titles. The second, because the brain is a dwelling for knowledge and intellect; and the intellect of a man is titled by the name brain; and likewise the intellect of the words, which are the vowels, as he goes on to explain, it is fitting that they be related by the name brain to the letters, and their knowledge and their understanding. "To sustain the letters," etc.: the example of this: the word  Y T N  has no sense and no tikkun [until we say] yiten [he will give] or yutan [it will be put], with a shuruk; and there is a great difference in their meaning, as they explained in the Gemara (Bava Metzi'a 22b): "yutan is like yiten."

Behold, the change of the understanding of the words is through the vowels; and therefore their tikkun and their knowledge and their intellect are the vowels, as we explained. "The Lamp of Darkness," etc.: the explanation, Keter; and I explained it in the preceding gates many times. "When it struck that air in the brain," etc.: the explanation, Keter is called "pure air" and is called "the Lamp of Darkness." And there is a great difference between them: for it is called the Lamp of Darkness on account of its concealed inwardness, which is united in its cause, the Cause of all causes, the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He; and therefore it is called the Lamp of Darkness, as we explained in the preceding gates. And it is called "pure air" in its aspect that is united in Chokhmah, which is the outer aspect that is in it.

And behold, the aspect of the Lamp of Darkness struck in the third aspect, which is the air in which it is united in Chokhmah. And the measure of the composition of the language of the saying is thus: "the Lamp of Darkness," which is the first aspect, "when it struck," that is to say, hit or beat, and the explanation, revealed the last aspect that is in it, "that pure air."

And behold, the revealer was "the Lamp," etc., and the revealed was "the air"; and the matter in which it was revealed is "this brain." And the language of striking is not literally according to its sense; but his intent is like the light that is emanated from the eye and strikes the thing seen, and the sight draws it in; and we have no fitting parable in the corporeal world but this, which is the subtlest in us, to give as a parable. "Struck and did not strike": the intent is to show the subtlety of the emanation, which is revealed and not revealed: revealed with respect to its concealment, and not revealed, for it is not attained even through this revealing.

And the matter of the bestowal of Keter in Chokhmah was not the manifestation of the vowels, but the effluence fitting for them, as we explained in the previous gate concerning the matter of the power of Chokhmah in the letters; and the principal of the coming into being of the vowels was from Chokhmah, which is called brain. And this is what he said, "went out toward the letters from within the brain; then," etc.; for from there are the vowels; and therefore "the letters were vocalized."

And behold, like the matter that Chokhmah is nefesh and ru'ach to Binah, and Binah is a body with respect to Chokhmah, so are the vowels, which branch out from Chokhmah, to the letters, which are branches that branch out from Binah. And one may not ask and say: if so, how is it possible that the concealed be explained by what is more closed than it, the reverse of the upper matters? For the lower ones reveal and make known the upper ones, and here the upper ones make known the lower ones. This is no wonder; for it is like the panes of glass, each one of a known color; and behold, when one looks at them they do not reveal their color and do not shine; and through the ray of the sun, simple of color, which shines in them, their color is seen in them. And likewise the matter of the letters: for Binah in her branches is like the pane of glass that has no color except through the ray of the sun that shines. And as is the relation of the vocalization to the letters, so is the relation of the cantillation marks to the vowels; and it will be explained in the Gate of Cantillation Marks, with the help of the Name. And just as the spirituality of the letters changes to different aspects, as we explained in the previous gate, so is the matter exactly in the vowels; for according to the rung of the nefesh will be the rung of the ru'ach, and according to the rung of the ru'ach will be the rung of the nefesh. For certainly the vocalization of the titles is not equal to the vocalization of the Names, and the vocalization of the Names is not equal to the vocalization of the beings; for according to the degree and holiness of the Names, so will be the degree of their vocalization, in the height and depth of their emanation. And the proof of this is from what we wrote in the first chapter in the name of the book Berit Menuchah. And we know that it will be difficult for the inquirer: if so, according to this it would have been fitting that the vocalization of the Names be forbidden to erase, like the Names themselves, and more so, because the vowels are more spiritual, as we explained; and we have not found anyone who forbade this; and also that they forbade the letters in the explanation of the zarka. This is no question at all; for it happened to the vocalization and to the cantillation marks as it happened to the name EHYH and the four-letter name, as we explained in the Gate of Names (chapter 5): that because of the concealment of Keter, the four-letter name was not revealed in it, because of its great subtlety and its concealment; however, the garment of its garment was revealed, as we spoke at length there, with the help of Heaven. And so it happened to the vowels and to the cantillation marks: that because of their great concealment only the garment of their garments was revealed, like the relation of the titles that may be erased to the Names that may not be erased. And it is possible that this too is a reason why the vocalization is not written in the Torah scroll, apart from other sufficient reasons that there are in the matter.
And behold, with this the chapter is completed and this gate is concluded, with the help of Heaven, with the help of the Name:
The Gate of Cantillation Marks, which is Gate Twenty-Nine:

After we explained in the previous gate according to what is found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim, we shall now come to explain the cantillation marks, according to what is also found in his words. And the cantillation marks in their names and their form are these:

Zarka, makaf, shofar holekh, segolta, pazer gadol, yerach ben yomo, karnei farah, ga'ya, telisha, azla, geresh, pasek, revia, shofar mehupakh, kadma, zakef katan, zakef gadol, shalshelet, shnei gerishin, trei ta'amei, darga, tevir, ma'arikh, tircha, etnach, rafeh, dagesh, yetiv, tirtza, shibbolet, sibbolet, mappik in Heh, sheva ga'ya, ga'ya sheva, sof pasuk:

These are the cantillation marks, by their names and their form, and their source in their language. And now we enter into the explanation of each and every one of these cantillation marks, as is found in Rashbi, peace be upon him:
Chapter One:

On the explanation of zarka, makaf, shofar holekh, segolta. First, zarka is Malkhut; and it is called zarka when she is thrown [nizreket] toward her concealed source, and rises and is united in the secret of Chokhmah up to Keter, as we explained in the previous gate, chapter 1, on the cholam. And for this it is found that it returns from the end of the word to its head, to show that she is below, at the end of the rungs, and sometimes returns "unto her father's house, as in her youth," and "shall eat of her father's bread" (Lev. 22:13), and receives abundant effluence and "great goodness toward the house of Israel" (Isa. 63:7): they are her camps and her hosts, who wait for the time of her coming, "to give food to her household and a portion to her maidens" (Prov. 31:15). And it is the point of the head that is at the head of that thread; and the thread is hinted in Tiferet; for by way of Tiferet is her ascent; by way of the six steps she rises; and there she becomes a diadem of glory, "a woman of valour, the diadem of her husband" (Prov. 12:4). And this the form of the zarka shows in its portraying and its hint. And because of her it is said (Dan. 2:34), "You saw till a stone was cut out without hands, and smote the image"; so she then is aroused in the power and strength of her ascent and annuls all the images and graven images of other gods. And she is what gives strangling to those who cleave to the gates of death that are beneath her; and it is a scarf, with which the Sanhedrin would strangle. And because before her ascent she is the form of a chirik, somewhat below, like this, ב֮, for it is her lower manifestation; and she rises from the left to the right, for so every ascent is from the left to the right, and the descent from the right to the left, for the right is always over the left; and afterward it spreads out straight upward, to look toward Keter; for there is the principal intent of her ascent, in the secret of "I am the first, and I am the last" (Isa. 44:6), Ayin at the head and Ayin at the end, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. It is found that zarka in the cantillation marks and Alef in the letters are all one matter and one hint: Yod at the head and Yod at the end, Vav in the middle; and that is the form; and likewise the zarka: Yod at the head and Yod at the end, Vav in the middle:

Makaf: it seems to me that this mark is in Chokhmah, like the patach, which is hinted in Chokhmah; and indeed it is in the secret of Da'at, which stands and joins [makif] and connects and unites the two attributes, which are Chokhmah and Binah, as we spoke at length in the preceding gates. And the language of makaf is the language of joining, as ["one may not join (makifin) two casks"] (Betzah 32b), whose matter is the language of joining and union. And it is found according to this that the explanation of these cantillation marks is thus: zarka is the ascent of Malkhut higher and higher; and the beginning of her return, she returns according to her attributes; and first she returns to Chokhmah; and there is the makaf, after her standing in Keter; for there is the hint of the zarka, as we explained. And for this the zarka is found above, at its head, bent toward the left side, to show her return. And likewise in its melody there is, after the ascent in the melody, some lowering. And afterward the makaf, which joins the two second attributes together, in a melody of speed; and the makaf returns with the shofar, which is Binah, as we shall explain:

Shofar holekh, mehupakh: shofar is Binah; and likewise she is the shofar of which we say, "Sound the great shofar for our freedom"; for in her is the freedom, as we explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And the language of shefer [beauty]: for she is the midwife [Shifrah] who beautifies the child; for she nurses milk to Tiferet and beautifies it with her bestowal. And therefore the wide side is found in the shofar, to show the broad places of the river; and she bestows below. And there is no wonder from the matter of the blowing, which is from the narrow side to the wide; for it is to arouse the upper power; and it is in the secret of the returning light. And when merit and commandments shine in the world and illuminate, then it is shofar holekh [going], which always returns and bestows, like the matter of "the river that flows and goes out." And when, God forbid, the iniquities cause it, the upper Shekhinah departs; and then it is shofar mehupakh [reversed]; that is to say, good reversed; like the matter of the wicked, who turn the attribute of compassion to the attribute of judgment, God forbid; and the world is in sorrow, until the mother returns and looks down upon the children:

Segolta: it is known that from the shofar go out fire and water and air; for the voice is included of the three of them, which are three elements, fire, water and air; and they are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; and they are segolta, which are three points. And there is no wonder at Tiferet being above Gedulah and Gevurah; for we have already explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation that it too has a relation above the two of them, because it is emanated from Keter and rises up to Keter. And all the more now, in the matter of the segolta, in which we are occupied, in the secret of the ascent in which Malkhut rose, and now the beginning of her descent to her place; and therefore it is above, in the secret of Da'at, in the secret of the makaf, to unite it with the shofar, as we explained. And even though this mark is sometimes found related by Rashbi, peace be upon him, to the three first ones, the principal is in the Patriarchs; and for the reason that the three first ones are bestowed here in these three, they are called by their name. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 127b), these are his words: "Segolta, in the secret of the three Patriarchs who stand within the shofar." Thus far his words. And above this he said: "And three knots stand in its place. And even though they stand in another secret, all is in one secret; for these three knots that stand in its place, beneath the wings of that shofar." Thus far his words. Behold, the very difficulty was difficult for Rashbi, peace be upon him; and he answered that even though in other places he said that the segolta is in Chokhmah [in Keter, Chokhmah, Binah], nevertheless the principal is in the three Patriarchs; except that, because they stand beneath Binah, after the manner in which they are called segolta, the upper ones are so called; and the principal is in the three Patriarchs, as we explained. And elsewhere in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that segol is male, the manifestation of Tiferet; and segolta is from the side of Malkhut, "a woman of valour, the diadem of her husband." And the reason is that Tiferet, from the side of its standing, is below two Patriarchs, and they are segol; and Malkhut above Netzach and Hod, and they are segolta. And likewise, in the secret of their ascent, her husband will be in the secret of segolta, prevailing, from the side of their ascent, over Gedulah and Gevurah, as we explained:

On the explanation of pazer gadol, yerach ben yomo, karnei farah, ga'ya, telisha. Pazer gadol: this mark is principally in Tiferet, with the totality of the six extremities that are in it. And it is called pazer gadol from the language of "He has dispersed [pizzar], he has given to the needy" (Ps. 112:9); for it is what nourishes and provides for two needy ones, which are Yesod, the poor man, and Malkhut, the poor woman; and both of them are needy and long for all that it bestows. And its movement is somewhat in wonder, to show its life, high over the whole building, and somewhat wondering. And the form of this mark is like the form of three points breadth and three length, like this:

And three are seen from here and three from here, and they are five. So the sefirot are five and they are six: they are five, for Yesod is from the very self of Tiferet and beside it, as in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, "body and covenant are counted as one"; and they are six, for it is a sefirah by itself in truth. And likewise these points are seen six and they are five. These are the copy of the words of Rashbi in one place. And elsewhere he explained that the pazer is in Yesod. And it is possible to say that "all that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph"; for since it bestows in Yesod, Yesod becomes one who "scatters, and yet increases" (Prov. 11:24). Also it shoots the seed that shoots like an arrow, and it throws it into Malkhut, as is known:

Yerach ben yomo [moon one day old]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that it is Malkhut, which is the moon. However, it has already been explained in the Gate of Manifestations, on the matter of the Heh and the Yod that are in Malkhut; and it is known that the manifestation of the Yod never has lack and diminishment; however, the fullness and the lack are in the manifestation of the Heh, the three colors of the eye, which are over against the three Patriarchs, as we explained there. And the pupil of the eye is the source that bestows light to all the sides that are around it; and from it they draw effluence and blessing; and it is the point of Zion, from which the whole world was founded; and it is what illuminates its surroundings, which is the moon. And it seems to me that the reason that it is called yerach ben yomo is because it is illuminated from Tiferet, which is a complete day; and this is "the son of its day." And it is possible to say that it is the son of its day only, which is the beginning of the receiving of the light; and then this mark is hinted to her. Further, it is possible to say that it is a moon shining of itself, from its own day; that is, the middle point, which shines from it, as we explained; and in that aspect it is called a day shining [of itself]:

Karnei farah [the horns of the cow]: they are Netzach and Hod, which are two horns, this to the right and this to the left. And they are called the horns of the cow: it is Malkhut, who is called the red cow when she receives from Gevurah. And likewise Binah is called the red cow when she bestows in Gevurah; and these are her horns with which she gores downward and bestows. And likewise Malkhut: her head is Yesod, and on her head are these horns, with which she gores westward and northward and southward and eastward. And therefore they are in wonder, at the secret of their receiving from judgment, and to show strength and exaltation:

Ga'ya: this mark shows Tiferet, which is the secret of Vav; however, it shows its drawing from judgment, that it lows [go'eh] in it; and it is strong judgment, which separates and descends to seek after its palace, and behold, it is burned; after its house, and behold, it is destroyed; and after its Shekhinah, and behold, she is falling in exile. And this is ga'ya alone; and in its joining to the sheva it will be explained, with the help of Heaven:

Telisha, tirtza: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the telisha is to the left, and he explained in it tal esh [a mound of fire]; and tirtza to the right. And we can say that the hint in both of them is to Yesod. And it is known that Yesod receives from two lines, from Chesed to the right and from Gevurah to the left. And therefore, when it receives from the right, it is tirtza, the language of will [ratzon]; and its melodies are three melodies, to hint at its receiving from three sources that are on the right, Chokhmah, Chesed, Netzach. And when it receives from the left it is called telisha, tal esh; and its melody is in three melodies, which are over against three sefirot that are on the left, and they are Binah, Gevurah, Hod. And the form shows the receiving of Yesod through Tiferet; and Malkhut and her ascent above: this is that it is a clear point, like the round goblet, on the middle line; and it inclines with her to the two sides:

On the explanation of azla, geresh, pasek, revia, kadma, zakef katan, zakef gadol. Azla, geresh: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that they are two arms. And what appears in these marks is that they are the arms at the time of their being united in Tiferet, to the middle line. And this is that the one is from the right side and the one from the left side; and both of them are matched from above to the one ring, which is Tiferet; and it is what unites them in the line of the mean. And therefore the one is called azla [going], because it is the right, the power of Chesed and compassion, which are bestowed of themselves, after their way; and they go in the way of their going. But the left is called gerish, for it is the power of judgment, which drives itself [megaresh] from its place to the side of compassion:

Pasek is Yesod, which cuts off [posek] and divides between the upper world and the lower world; for it is between Tiferet and Malkhut. And the witness is the pasek that is between the first four-letter name in the thirteen attributes and the second name; for the one is above, in Keter, and the second below, in Malkhut; and the pasek unites them by way of the middle line. And this is "there is between the upper waters," males, "and the lower waters," females, Malkhut, "only as much as a strand"; and the fullness of a strand is the hair's thread; and it is Yesod. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Tikkun 19, fols. 36–37) that concerning this pasek that is between name and name, they said that the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous as a hair's thread. And the reason is that the righteous is very bristling [nis'ar], from the side of its attribute, which is the hair's thread:

Revia: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the revia, the hint in it is to Binah, which is a concealed point; and she is so called because she is like a mother crouching [revi'a] over the children. And its movement is in ascent, which hints at Tiferet, which rises to be concealed in the mother. It is found that the revia, the hint in it is to Tiferet concealed in Binah, when Binah crouches over the children:

Kadma is Tiferet, which receives from judgment to lash the guilty; and for this it is a staff that inclines to the left side, Gevurah, and bestows judgment even to Netzach, which stands at the side of Chesed. And for this its melody is like a blow with the voice:

Zakef katan is Chesed and judgment alone. And even though the line of the mean is not between them, nevertheless Chesed prevails over Gevurah. And it is called small with respect to the prevailing of Chesed over Gevurah not being like the relation in which the line of Chesed arbitrated the line of judgment to the right side; but they are one over the other, after the way of their emanation, Chesed over Gevurah:

Zakef gadol: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the two points are Chesed and Gevurah; and therefore the one is above its fellow, to show the prevailing of Chesed over Gevurah; and therefore it is called gadol, from the language of Gedulah. And all this through Tiferet, which inclines Gevurah to the right side; and therefore it is to the left side, to show that it passed Gevurah to the side "beyond the river," Chesed, the power of compassion. And what was like this, ⁝ [one], Tiferet between the two lines [points], became like this, :l, that is, the two lines [points] to the right side:

Shalshelet: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that it is in Tiferet; and he said that teru'ah too is in Tiferet. And even though it is in Malkhut, nevertheless it settles also in Tiferet; for from there is the principal of Malkhut, and from there she came, and to it she will return; for the two of them are together. And the reason that it is in Tiferet is because it is the chain [shalshelet] that binds the two extremes, the side of compassion and the side of judgment. And we can say, in order to distinguish between shalshelet and azla geresh: that the shalshelet is hinted in Tiferet at the time that it binds between Chokhmah and Binah, and between Gedulah and Gevurah, and between Netzach and Hod (for "body and covenant are counted as one"). And for this reason there are in the shalshelet three humps, like this, ב֓, to show the bond of these three places in the secret of the arbitration; and it bestows their bestowal down below, in the secret of the lower point that is in it, which is the secret of the bestowal that is gathered in Malkhut, in which is the principal of the teru'ah:

On the explanation of all the other cantillation marks. Shnei gerishin [two gerashim]: Rashbi explained that they are two arms. And we can say that they are the two arms included in Tiferet, which is the arbiter between the fire and the water. And on this, shnei gerishin are like the two Vavs that are in Vav in its filling [Vav-Alef-Vav], to show that Tiferet is long-suffering [erekh appayim]: and the explanation, two faces: the face of judgment from the side of Gevurah, and the face of compassion from the side of Chesed; and it is included of them and unites them and makes all of them one. And this is Vav uniting the two Vavs, which are two faces; and it inclines them, united, toward Chesed. And therefore the shnei gerishin are the two arms, equal, inclining to the right side; and they are raised in their melody, for Tiferet to receive from Keter, so that the power of compassion prevail over it, to tip the left to the right. And there is no wonder at there being two Vavs in Gedulah and Gevurah; for we have already explained in the preceding gates the matter of the three Vavs, which are  V H V,  Y L Y,  S Y Ṭ, which are the three Patriarchs. And they are called shnei gerishin because from their side two expulsions [gerushin] were obligated: the expulsion of the First Temple and the expulsion of the Second Temple; because Israel transgressed the Written Torah and the Oral Torah; and likewise the two hundred and forty-eight positive commandments and three hundred and sixty-five negative commandments, which are in Chesed and Gevurah; so Rashbi explained. And according to reason they are called expulsions because Tiferet drives them from their place and brings them to the line of the mean and inclines them to the side of Chesed:

Trei ta'amei [two accents]: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that they are Netzach and Hod, inclining to the right to draw the Chesed; and they show the male who opens his thighs to be united with the female, who is etnach, as was explained. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (in Parashat Balak, fol. 189) that for this reason it is said (Gen. 27:25), "and he brought him wine, and he drank" with two accents: to strengthen Tiferet, which is the attribute of Jacob, to settle it in its arrangement; and Netzach and Hod, to incline Gevurah to the side of compassion. And it seems to me that they are called trei ta'amei [two tastes], for the taste of the manna that Netzach grinds from the side of Chesed is not like the taste of the manna that Hod grinds:

Darga: it seems to me that the darga is the union of Netzach and Hod with Yesod, which unites them and blends them; and it is a third of the shalshelet, as we explained in the previous chapter. And it is possible that the darga is in Malkhut; for it is one rung [darga]; and it is called darga when this union comes through Yesod:

Tevir: this mark Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained: that in tevir is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, to break [le-shabber] and to subdue the husks. And therefore the point comes to the left side, to show the force of the judgment, whose drawing is from the left; and it inclines to the right side, to show that this judgment is for good and for compassion:

Ma'arikh, tircha: it seems to me in this mark that the ma'arikh is from the side of Chesed, which is long-suffering [ma'arikh af] even to the wicked, so that they return; and the tircha is Gevurah, for the deeds of the wicked, and His compassion upon them, are a burden [torach] to it; and it burdens human beings with its sufferings on account of their corrupted deeds. Or it is possible that the ma'arikh and the tircha are the extension of Chesed and the arousal of judgment toward Malkhut, to arouse her to the coupling, like etnach; and the arousal in the secret of "he went up on the ramp," etc., which we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 21:

Etnach: this mark Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Malkhut; and the hint is that she opens her legs to receive the seed of the male, her husband, in joy and good heart; for the matter of the coupling is in calm and in silence. Therefore it is called etnach, the language of rest; and likewise its melody is in silence, that is to say, the standing of the word. And it is called etnach in her receiving from Tiferet through Netzach and Hod; and therefore their portraying is found in her, "like the form of the children of a king" (Judg. 8:18), and a point over them, to show Tiferet. And all this is in the secret of "Set me as a seal," which we explained above:

Rafeh, dagesh: we have already explained in the preceding gates the manifestation of the rafeh, which is the secret of compassion, and the manifestation of the dagesh, which is the secret of judgment; but not literally the compassion of Chesed; rather, the rafeh is the secret of Tiferet, which is the male, and its inclining to Chesed and compassion; and the dagesh is the secret of Malkhut, who is the female, whose inclining is to judgment. And therefore the letters of the throat do not receive dagesh, because they are in Chesed, as we explained in the Gate of Letters, with the help of Heaven. And behold, the rafeh is the secret of Vav, and it is a firmament stretched over their heads above; and dagesh is Malkhut, of whom it is said (Ezek. 1:13), "it went up and down among the living creatures"; and therefore the dagesh is within the letter:

Yetiv is the secret of the holding back of the effluence in Chokhmah, in the secret of "Why do You stand afar off, O YHVH?"; and it is the firmament, Vav, Tiferet, which was stretched out to bestow, like this, ו, and was folded upward and departed, like this, yetiv: the standing of the effluence and its holding back, in the secret of "YHVH sat [yashav] at the flood" (Ps. 29:10), which he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 64b): "He sat alone, for He did not come with judgment." And likewise, when the judgment spreads out and the world is judged, it turns its face from the left to the right; and the sword takes "the vengeance of the covenant," and it sits [yetiv] alone; and that is yetiv, it turned its end somewhat to the right, because of the force of the judgment. And all is one matter:
Tirtza: you will find it explained in chapter 2:

Shibbolet, sibbolet: what appears from this point is that this letter, its hint is in Binah; and it is a hint to the three lines that are drawn from her, which are the three Patriarchs. And behold, the right is Chesed and the left Gevurah. And when this point is on the right, it shows Chokhmah, which is in Chesed, flowing upon it; and it is soft [rafeh], in the secret of compassion. And when the point is on the left one, it shows Binah, "from whom judgments are aroused," as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And therefore this one takes dagesh and that one does not take dagesh; for Chokhmah is concealed and Binah is revealed; apart from the reason of judgment that we explained:

Mappik in Heh: in this mark the secret of Heh-Yod of Elohim is revealed, which is in Binah; and it is in the lower Wisdom, Malkhut; for both of them are called Elohim, as we explained in the Gate of Names. And the matter is revealed in the Name in the filling of Yods, Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Yod, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Yod: behold, in that which is in Binah and in that which is in Malkhut the Hehs came upon Yods, females upon males; and it is judgment, as is explained in the Gate of From Below to Above. And the principal secret is that in Malkhut is the manifestation of Yod, and likewise Binah; however, they built the secret of the building that covers over the Yods; and that is Heh, which is the secret of three Vavs, in which the Yod is clothed, as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations. And therefore the principal in the Hehs is like this. And therefore, when the Heh comes to hint at the name of the female and her titles, the Heh comes at her end with mappik, like this, to show the judgment, like the name Elohim, in which is Heh-Yod. And therefore the mappik is more than the dagesh, as we explained:

Sheva ga'ya is exactly in the way of the zakef gadol that we explained in the previous chapter; except that these are below, in the secret of the vowel, to show that both of them returned to the secret of the right, in the secret of compassion. And therefore the movement of the sheva, which is judgment, returned to the movement of patach, which is compassion; which is the order of the male who unites, which is the ga'ya. And when it is adjacent to the letters of the throat, which are the letters of Chesed, its movement is in them, because of the prevailing of Chesed over them. And when it is adjacent to the letter Yod, then it is always chirik, showing the judgment, in the secret of the concealment and the departure of the bestowal from her; and that she is "black, as the tents of Kedar" (Song 1:5), which is the letter Yod, as is expounded in the Song of Songs from the Zohar. Further, it is possible to say that the sheva ga'ya below shows Yesod, which inclines Netzach and Hod to the right side, as we explained above in zakef gadol. And this is reversed to ga'ya sheva at times, which is that it inclines Netzach and Hod to the left side, in the secret that it too sometimes inclines to the side of judgment; which is not so in Tiferet, which is always in zakef gadol; because Tiferet does not incline to the side of judgment, but departs from among them, and the judgment is present, in the secret of yetiv, as we explained above:

Sof pasuk [end of verse]: it seems to me that it is Yesod, like the pasek itself; except that there is a great difference between them: for after the pasek there is Malkhut, the tenth rung, in the secret of her manifestation below, after the diminishment, and Yesod ninth to the Emanation; but sof pasuk shows that it is tenth, and Malkhut is in the secret of "the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" (Isa. 30:26), and Yesod tenth, the end of the Emanation, and it cuts it off; and there is nothing below it but the secret of the cherubim upon which the Throne is established, which are Metatron, Sandalfon; and they do not depend on the writing, but they are two points one above the other. Thus far the explanation of the cantillation marks and their secret has reached, with the help of Heaven:

After the cantillation marks have been explained in the preceding chapters, according to what is found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, with much addition on what is not found explained in the books of the Zohar, we shall now come to explain the cantillation marks in general.

And behold, their source and their emanation are from Keter itself; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, fol. 123b), and these are his words: "'And their rings': this is the upper Mother, who is over the sefirot that are beneath her, from whom are all the letters. 'And as for their height': this is Chokhmah, from where are the vowel points. 'And they were dreadful [ve-yir'ah]': this is Keter, where the cantillation marks are." Thus far his words.

And we have already written and repeated this saying in the preceding gates; and what is necessary is not to be despised. Further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 87a), and these are his words: "Since that striking was settled in the brain, from within the pure air that is grasped; for there is a pure air that is not grasped at all; and this one that is grasped, when that upper striking was settled in that brain, then all the movements of the cantillation marks went out." And it is the end of the saying that we copied in the Gate of Vowel-Points, chapter 6; and there we explained that the vowels are from Chokhmah through Keter; and not that the vowels came into being from Keter, but by the effluence and power of Keter they came into being in Chokhmah; and for this he said "reached and did not reach, struck and did not strike"; for it was only the subtlety of the effluence, as we explained there. And now he said: since that striking, which is the emanation of Keter, was settled and came into being in a being of substance, even from Keter itself; for it did not need Chokhmah to complete, but they are settled in themselves, and were emanated from within Keter. "For there is a pure air," etc.: the aspect of Keter itself, which is not attained by another, for it is concealed, as is explained in the Gate of Tzachtzachot. And "the pure air that is grasped" is the aspect of Keter [that is united] with the aspect of Chokhmah. And now, since the cantillation marks are branches spreading out from it, it is required that they be from the aspect of Keter that is grasped.

And further, it is explained from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that the letters are nefesh, and the vowels the ru'ach for the nefesh, which are the letters; and the cantillation marks are neshamah to the ru'ach that is in the nefesh. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (in the Introduction, fol. 7a): "And the cantillation marks are souls [neshamot], and the vowels spirits, and the letters nefashot. These are conducted after those, and those after those: and the letters are conducted after the vowels, and the vowels after the cantillation marks; 'for one higher than the high watches, and there are higher than they' (Eccl. 5:7)." Thus far his words.

And it is fitting that we say that, just as the spirituality of the letters and the spirituality of the vowels are not equal even though they are equal, as is explained in the preceding gates, so the spirituality of the cantillation marks is not equal [even though they are equal; for they change because of their place and their matter, etc.]; and it is clear, and there is no need to lengthen. And further, just as the rung of the letters is like the nefesh to the vowels, and the vowels ru'ach to them, and the cantillation marks neshamah to the ru'ach, so is their matter in the corporeal. For the letters fixed in the mouth in five outlets are explained well in these corporeal vessels; and the vowels ride upon the letters like a rider on the horse; and because of their great subtlety, more than the letters, they do not encamp in substance in the corporeality of the letter, but in their pronunciation, which is after the mentioning of the letter, such as the letters of extension that come into being from the vowels; and in the letter it only touches and does not touch, as a hair's thread, after the manner of the subtle spirit itself, which is not well united with this nefesh because of its great subtlety. And the cantillation mark, we find that it does not touch the letter at all, but rides upon the vowel, which is a concealed pronunciation; and a man must examine this closely of himself; for there is no way in writing to explain it, but from mouth to mouth. And with this this chapter is completed and this gate is concluded. Blessed be YHVH forever, Amen and Amen:
Gate Thirty is called the Gate of Permutation:

The knowledge of the secrets of our holy Torah is through the permutations and the gematriot and the substitutions, and initial letters and final letters and middle letters of words, and the beginnings of verses and the ends of verses, and the skipping of letters and the permutation of letters. And these matters are exalted and concealed, and their secret is too high, and there is no power in us to attain them because of their great concealment; for they change according to these ways without end and without limit. And of this it is said, "The measure thereof is longer than the earth," etc. (Job 11:9). And these matters we hope will be revealed after the resurrection, after the consuming of the turbid matter, and after the smitten body is refined and the form remains in the delight of its Creator. And behold, we have found the parts of this inquiry to be three; and they are the part of permutation, and the part of substitution, and the part of gematria. And we shall come to their explanation in these chapters:
Chapter One:

On permutation. We have learned in the Sefer Yetzirah: "Two stones build two houses; three build six houses; four build twenty-four houses; five build a hundred and twenty houses; six build seven hundred and twenty houses; seven build five thousand and forty houses. From here onward go out and reckon what the mouth cannot speak and the ear cannot hear." Thus far. We have already explained in the Gate of Letters that the letters are the hewn stones of Binah, which are concealed spiritual powers. And one stone will not build a house at all; however, two stones build two houses; for in the joining of two letters two words come into being, each word one house. And the explanation: when two letters are joined together they make two words, like this, א"ב ב"א; for the word rolls from its head to its end and from its end to its head. And when three stones are joined together, six houses are built from them, like this: אב"ג אג"ב, behold two houses, at the head of each one Alef; בא"ג בג"א, behold two houses, at the head of each one Bet; גא"ב גב"א, behold two houses, at the head of each one Gimel; and their total is six houses. "And four build twenty-four houses": how so? אבג"ד אבד"ג אגב"ד אגד"ב אדב"ג אדג"ב, behold six houses, and their beginning Alef; באג"ד באד"ג בגא"ד בגד"א בדא"ג בדג"א, behold six houses, and their beginning Bet; גאב"ד גאד"ב גבא"ד גבד"א גדא"ב גדב"א, behold six houses, and their beginning Gimel; דבג"א דג"אב דא"גב דבא"ג דאב"ג דג"בא, behold six houses, and their beginning Dalet. Their total comes to twenty-four. And when we examine these permutations and look at them and consider them, they are found arranged: for in each one of the four parts there is the permutation of the three stones that preceded; and the end of the twenty-four is the reverse, in all its matters, of the first of them. And we shall look at their order and find them: that when a word of four or five or six comes into our hand, we must first raise in our mind that the two last stones are a word alone, and permute them alone. The example of this: Shelomoh [שלמה]. We raise in our mind that the word is מ"ה alone, and we permute from it two houses, מ"ה ה"ם; (and afterward ה"ל, and there will come up ל"ה ה"ל) (and afterward מ"ל, and two will come up in our hand, which are ל"ם מ"ל). And afterward we put at the head of each one of these words the third letter, and there will be six words of three letters. How so? The word ל"מ or מ"ל: we put Heh at the head, and it becomes הל"ם or המ"ל; and likewise for all three permutations that we made. And in this way we can permute easily, without error, even a word of ten letters, if we keep this order that we have arranged. And now we shall arrange Shelomoh in four letters; and it will be found that the two letters are permuted together and the three are permuted together. And this is its order, arranged in four arrays, six [to] the array, "pure frankincense" (Lev. 24:7). שלמה שלהם שמלה שמהל שהלמ שהמל: behold six permutations, and they are the permutation of three letters, for Shin is at the head of all of them. And now we put Lamed, the second letter, at the head of six second words, like this: לשמה לשהם למשה למהש להשם להמש: behold six permutations, and they are the permutation of three letters, for Lamed is at the head of all of them. And now we put Mem, the third letter, at the head of six third words, like this: משלה משהל מלשה מלהש מהשל מהלש: behold six permutations, and they are the permutation of three letters, for Mem is at the head of all of them. And now we put Heh, the fourth letter, at the head of six fourth words, like this: השלמ השמל הלשם הלמש המשל המלש: behold six permutations, and they are the permutation of three letters, for Heh is at the head of all of them. And now, when we consider the initial letters of all the second words standing in a row, we find their initial letters Shelomoh, Shelomoh, six times, and "there is nothing froward or perverse in them" (Prov. 8:8). And when we go deep into these permutations, they are found [thus]: when they are two stones, they build only two; but when it rises to three, it makes three times the two preceding; for the reason that the third stone rolls the two; and when the third is exchanged in three letters, once it makes this one prevail and once it makes its fellow prevail, and it comes up to the initial letters; it is found twice three, which are six. And in this way four make four times six, which are twenty-four. And in this way it will come out that when it is of five letters, five times twenty-four, whose number is a hundred and twenty houses; and six stones build six times a hundred and twenty, which are seven hundred and twenty; and seven stones build seven times seven hundred and twenty, which are five thousand and forty houses. And from here onward in this way we reckon, up to a place where there is no number and reckoning; according to the multitude of the stones the houses are multiplied, how much more and more, as we explained. And after we have explained in this chapter the permutation of the simple words, that is to say, the letters in which there is no doubling, we shall explain the permutation of the doubled words:

All the matters of permutation that we explained in the previous chapter are on condition that there be no doubled letter at all in the permutation; and then the permutation comes up in the number of the rungs of the ladder of which we spoke. However, if a doubled letter is found, then immediately half the permutation that should come according to the number of the stones is subtracted, whether many or few. And for this reason the four-letter name and the name EHYH come up in their permutation only to twelve permutations; half the permutation that should be in it is found lacking; for four stones build twenty-four houses, and these four stones build only twelve, half of what is fitting. And likewise, if it is of three letters, whose law is six words, if one letter is doubled it is permuted three times alone. And likewise, if there are three doubled letters equal in the word of the doubling: the first subtracts half the permutation, as we explained; and the second doubling, which is a third letter, subtracts two thirds of the remaining permutation that the first doubling left; and from twelve they return to four. How so? אגג"ג: it should have had twenty-four permutations, and because of the three equal letters only four remained. And if it is a word of five letters, whose simple permutation is a hundred and twenty permutations, if one letter is doubled, as אבדג"ד, only sixty permutations remain; for half the permutation is subtracted because of the one doubling. And if another letter is doubled, as אבד"דד, then because of the third letter the doubling subtracts two thirds of the remaining permutation, and only twenty permutations come into being from it, which are a third. And if a fourth letter is doubled, then a quarter of the permutation that the second doubling, which is a third letter, left remains. The example: אדד"דד: no man can permute it except five times, which is a quarter of the twenty remaining, as we explained. And if another, fifth, letter is also doubled, then a fifth of the remaining permutation remains, and it is permuted only one permutation, which is a fifth of the five. The example of this: דדדד [דדדדד]: there is no permutation in it except once. The rule that emerges: according to the count of the doubling letter, so is the measure of the remainder of the permutation. If two, which is the first doubling, that is to say, that there are only two doubled there, then half the permutation remains; and if they are three, then a third of the permutation remains of what would have been fitting if there were only two doubled; and likewise a quarter, only a quarter of the remainder remains; and likewise a fifth, and likewise a sixth, and likewise a seventh; and in this way we may infer, as we explained. All this rule is when the doubling is of the kind of the first doubling; the example: that the matter of the second doubling is of the kind of the first doubling. However, if it is of the kind of a second doubling, as the example א"א ב"ב, then it has another law. For in the first doubling half the permutation is subtracted, as we set first: for a word of four letters should have had twenty-four permutations; and the Alef was doubled; half the permutation was subtracted, and twelve permutations remained. And because of the second doubling only six remain; for it subtracted half of the remaining permutation that the first doubling left. The example: א"א ב"ב: there is no ability to permute it except six times, which is half of the twelve remaining, as we explained. And if the word is of five letters, whose law would be to roll a hundred and twenty times, and two doublings were doubled in it, א"א ב'ב'ג', then its law will be thus: in the first doubling half the permutation, which is a hundred and twenty, is subtracted, and sixty of them remain; and in the second doubling half of the sixty is subtracted, and thirty remain. And if the word is of six letters and all of them are pairs, which, if not for the doubling, its law would be to roll seven hundred and twenty times: and because of the first doubling half the measure is subtracted, and of the seven hundred and twenty, three hundred and sixty remain; and in the second doubling half the remaining permutation is subtracted from three hundred and sixty; a hundred and eighty remain; and in the third doubling [two thirds] of the permutation that remained from the second doubling are subtracted, and from a hundred and eighty sixty remain, which is a third of the hundred and eighty. And if a word is of four pairs, its law will be thus: for the first doubling subtracted the half, and the second doubling subtracted the half from the remaining permutation, and the third doubling subtracted two thirds of the remaining permutation, and only one third alone remained, as we explained above; and the fourth doubling will subtract three quarters from the third that the third doubling left, and only a quarter of it remains. And in this way we may infer for all the doublings, according as they multiply or diminish. And this is the way of the permutation of the doubled ones, according to what the commentators wrote and according to what appears by the power of experiment. And after we have explained the manifestation of the permutation in the matter of the letters, we shall explain the reason for their permutation in spirituality in a chapter by itself; for these things need short chapters, so that the intellect be able to encompass them and not be confused by them:

It has already been explained in the Gate of Letters what the spirituality of the letters is and their manifestation. And therefore, when we come to permute three letters, since these letters are spiritualities, simple forms, they must necessarily be compounded and included each one of its fellow; for such is the way of spiritual things. For this matter did not happen only to the sefirot; but this matter happened also to the branches and the emanations that branch out from them, since they are emanated forms. And the proof of this is from what we said in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 4, on the matter of the seventy of the Sanhedrin who sit in "the round goblet" (Song 7:3), who are all included together in each one of them. And since this matter is so, let us say: the letters אי"ן [Ayin], which hint at Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, as is explained in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles: behold, certainly Keter is included of Chokhmah and Binah, and Chokhmah of Keter and Binah, and Binah of Keter and Chokhmah. But it is included in them in two ways: either that Chokhmah receives from Keter and bestows in Binah. And for this the order of the letters was obligated thus: the Yod of Ayin, which is Chokhmah, prevails, because all three letters are in the very self of Chokhmah; and therefore its aspect prevails always; and behold, therefore Yod is at the head of the permutation. And afterward Alef, because the hint in it is Keter, and it receives from Keter and bestows in Binah; and therefore Alef prevails over Nun; and this is יא"ן, and it is the first permutation. Further, it is permuted in another way, that Binah prevails over Chokhmah, in the secret of the returning light; and therefore it receives light from Binah and bestows in Keter; and therefore the Nun of Binah prevails over the Alef that is in Keter; and this is the second permutation, which is ינ"א, to Chokhmah; for Chokhmah always prevails. And likewise to Keter two, for these causes. How so? The letter of Keter is Alef, and therefore it always prevails; and because sometimes there is bestowal from Chokhmah to Binah, according to the order of the light, therefore its permutation is אי"ן; and because also sometimes, in the secret of the returning light, Binah prevails over Chokhmah, therefore its permutation is אנ"י; and they are two permutations to Keter. And likewise two to Binah, for these causes. How so? The letter of Binah is Nun, and therefore it always prevails; and because sometimes it receives from Keter through Chokhmah, in the order of the light, therefore Alef prevails over Yod, and its permutation is נא"י; and because sometimes Chokhmah prevails over Keter, in the secret of the returning light, therefore the letter Yod prevails over Alef, and its permutation is ני"א.

Behold, in the word אנ"י there are six permutations explained, which are: אנ"י אין in the secret of the Alef; יא"ן ינ"א in the secret of the Yod; נא"י ני"א in the secret of the Nun. And this will be the secret of the permutation for four letters or for five. However, when the letters are doubled, even though in the corporeal permutation they are not permuted, it is possible for them to be permuted in the spiritual permutation, for their spirituality is not equal, as we explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names, on the matter of the twenty-four permutations that are in the four-letter name, which is explained in the Sefer ha-Bahir; let it be looked at there. However, these doubled ones are, these males and these females, as is explained there. And brevity is good. And because of the matter of the inclusion of the lights and their illuminating these in these, it is found that some of the ancients explained that, in the permutation and the rolling of the name of seventy-two or the other names, after great seclusion, there will be revealed to the deserving righteous one who has understanding in their matter something of the part of the bat kol; that is to say, "the spirit of YHVH spoke by me, and His word was upon my tongue" (2 Sam. 23:2); for the reason that he joins the powers and unites them and makes them long for one another, "according to the space of each, with wreaths" (1 Kgs. 7:36), until much effluence is bestowed upon him; and on condition that the one who occupies himself with this be a vessel prepared to receive the spirituality and worthy of it; for if not, it will turn into a cruel one, and he will be turned into "the degenerate plant of a strange vine" (Jer. 2:21), "and offer strange fire, which He had not commanded" (Lev. 10:1). And after we have occupied ourselves in the preceding chapters with understanding the permutation of the letters, we shall come now to explain the matter of the permutation of the vowel-points:

On the permutation of the vowels. However, the vowels by way of permutation: most of the commentators agreed to permute only in five vowels, according as their mnemonic is "engravings of a signet" (Exod. 28:11). And some wrote that they are with the sheva. And all this seems strained to us; for the vowels are twelve, and their powers and their form differ one from another, as we explained in the Gate of Vowel-Points. If so, it is fitting to permute and roll the words by all of them. However, so as not to breach the fence and border that our first ancients set, we shall write only the permutation of the five, which are נוֹטָרֶיִקֻוּן [notarikon]; and from this the student may infer to the rest; and if it does not suffice the student, let him look in the Gate of Particulars of Names; for there we spoke at length on these differences that are between the commentators and us. And first, the number rises to the words and these permutations in the way that the number of the permutation is multiplied and rises in the letters, as is explained in the first chapter. How so? The letter Alef builds five houses, and these are they: אֹ אִ אֻ אֵ אָ, behold five; and if six, six come up; and if twelve, twelve. And when we add a second letter they come up to five times five; and likewise when they are six vowels they come up to six times six, which are thirty-six; and likewise, if they are twelve, they come up to twelve times twelve, which are a hundred and forty-four, as we permuted in the aforementioned gate. And this is the permutation of two letters in five vowels:

Behold, we have set out the way: how two stones build five times five, which are twenty-five. And when we permute a word of three letters, it comes up to five times twenty-five, which are a hundred and twenty-five. How so? Each letter is five, and falls upon the twenty-five five times; a hundred and twenty-five are found. And this is its form. Behold, we have arranged five forms of twenty-five words each one; for in the reigning of the kamatz, twenty-five. And a man will understand the matters of himself, by his understanding of the forms, more than he would understand by his study of the matters by word of mouth.

And behold, if the letters are four, the permutation comes up to six hundred and twenty-five; and if the letters are five, the permutation comes up to three thousand one hundred and twenty-five. For in three letters they are a hundred and twenty-five; for with the doubling of the letter it prevails five times a hundred and twenty-five, which are six hundred and twenty-five; and if we add another letter it makes five times six hundred and twenty-five; and in this way its number rises; for what was the total of the permutation becomes one portion of five portions of the permutation, as is drawn before you. And this is enough of a note on the matter of the permutation of the vowels, with the help of Heaven. And behold, what came up in our mind to compose on the matter of the part of permutation is completed; and now we shall come to the part of substitution, with the help of Heaven:

The matter of substitution is to illuminate letter by letter in the two hundred and thirty-one gates, as we shall explain. And there is a difference between permutation and substitution as high as the heavens above the earth. And the reason is that in permutation "the hallowed stones are poured out" (Lam. 4:1) and are not changed from these letters to those letters, except that they are at the head of the permutation; and those that are at the head of the permutation are those at the end of the permutation; but it is like a wheel that rolls from its head to its end and from its end to its head, and head becomes end and end head, head middle and middle head, end middle and middle end; and the letters never change, even if they change in their order. But substitution is the exchange of the letters in the twenty-two alphabets, as we shall explain; as the example: the name ידו"ד אלד"ינו ידו"ד, which is exchanged in Avgad into כוז"ו במוכס"ו כו"זו; and in Atbash into מצפ"ץ תכצ"מטפ מצפ"ץ; and likewise in the other alphabets, up to twenty-two. And this way is more praiseworthy than gematria, as we shall explain; for in gematria the letters are exchanged, even though the number of these is not as the number of the one; for sometimes from three they make four, and from four three, as we shall explain:

These are the twenty-two alphabets in which the letters are exchanged, as they came in the Sefer Yetzirah; and he called them the two hundred and thirty-one gates, because they are two hundred and thirty-one pairs:
אל בת גש דר הק וץ זף חע טס ין כמ:
אב גת דש הר וק זץ חף חע יס כן למ:
אג דת הש ור זק חץ טף יע כס לן במ:
אד בג הת וש זר חק טץ יף כע לס מן:
אה בר ות זש חר טק ין כף לע מס גן:
או בה גד זת חש טג יק כץ לף מע נס:
אז בו גה חת טש יד כק לץ חף נע דס:
אח בז גו דה טת יש כר לק מץ נף סע:
אט בח גז דו ית כש לר מק נץ סף הע:
אי בט גח דז הו כת לש מר נק סץ עף:
אב בי גט דח הז לת מש נר סק עץ יף:
אל בך גי דט הח וז מת נש סר עק פץ:
אמ בל גס די הט זה צת סש ער פק זן:
אג בם גך דק הי וט זח סת עש פר צק:
אס בג גמ דל הס וי זט עת פש צר חק:
אע בס גנ דמ הל וכ זי חט פת צש קר:
אף בע גס דנ המ ול זכ חי צת קש טר:
אץ בף גע דס הג ומ זל חס טי קת רש:
אק בץ גף דע הס וג זם חל טב רת יש:
אר בק גץ דף הע וס זג חמ טל יב שת:
אש בר גק דן הף וע זס חג טמ יל כת:
את בש גר דק הץ וף זע חס טן ימ כל:
Thus far the two hundred and thirty-one gates that are in the Sefer Yetzirah are completed; and in them the letters are exchanged, all that is needed for the exchange of the names and the powers:
Further, there are other alphabets that we found scattered among the words of the old books; and these are they. The first is the straight alphabet, and it is this:
אב גד הו זח טי כל מג סע פצ קר שת מנצפך:
אחס בטע גיף דכץ הלק ומר [פנים ואחור ואלו הן] זנשת:
איק בנר גלש דמת הנך וסס זען חפף טצץ:
אל בם גן דס הע וף זץ חק טר יש כת:
אט בח גז דו הג סס על פך צי קת רש:
תשרק צפעם נמלך יטחז והדגבא:
And besides these two hundred and thirty-one, we found further in the mouths of the masters of wisdom two hundred and thirty-one gates written front and back; these are they:

And these gates and alphabets are found in this way: when we write one alphabet reversed and one straight, then Atbash comes out. And by rolling the circles there comes out further a second alphabet, which is א"ש ב"ר, etc.; and likewise all of them, some of it from the front side and some of it from the back. And so that this matter be understood according to its pattern, we have drawn here the circles, as needed.

Behold, we have set out these four circles one inside another: three alphabets straight, אבג"ד, and the fourth תשרק. From the first two we can produce the two hundred and thirty-one gates, front and back, as they are written in the previous chapter; and from the three circles that are straight we can produce from them alphabets of Achas Beta and the like, compounded of three letters; and from the last two, which are the one straight and the second תשרק, we can produce the twenty-two alphabets that are in the Sefer Yetzirah, which we also copied in the previous chapter. And after the manifestation of the alphabets and their rolling have been explained, we wish to explain the matter of substitution and its cause. And the matter is that the letters are in Tiferet; for there is the principal of their coming into being, in the very self of being, which is the firmament, as we explained in the Gate of Letters. In Tiferet they are the order of the alphabet straight, אבג"ד, etc.; and in Malkhut they are reversed, תשר"ק. And the reason is because they are male and female: male in אמ"ש, female in אש"ם. For such is the way of the seal: the form engraved in the seal from above to below is reversed [in the sealed impression, from below to above]. And likewise male,  Y H V H, straight; female,  H V H Y, reversed; as we explained in the Gate of From Below to Above. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, revealed this matter in the Song of Songs (in the Zohar Chadash, fol. 79), and these are his words: "Upper large letters go in a straight way toward the male; lower small letters go in reverse, backward, toward the female. Upper large letters go in a straight way toward the male: אבג"ד, and so all of them, as is fitting for the letters to go in a straight way toward the male. Small lower letters go in reverse, backward, within the female: תשרק, and so all of them, as is fitting toward the female, who was behind, the knot of the tefillin, which is called 'behind', as you say, 'You have formed me behind and before' (Ps. 139:5): behind toward the female, and before toward the male. And this is what is written, 'And you shall see My back' (Exod. 33:23): this is the female, who was behind." Thus far his words.

And in the Tikkunim Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the letters אבג"ד straight are in Chesed, and the letters תשר"ק are in Gevurah. And they do not disagree; for it is known that the matter of תשר"ק is in the name  H V H Y, which is from the side of the female and from the side of Gevurah, from the side of the prevailing of the left side over the right, as we explained in the Gate of From Above to Below, and we shall explain it here further. And the letters אבג"ד are in the matter of the name  Y H V H  straight, from the side of the male, from the side of Chesed, and from the side of the prevailing of the right over the left. And the matter is that the way of the male is to incline to the right, and the way of the female is to incline to the left. And when the power of the male prevails over the female, that is, the power of compassion prevails over judgment; and when the power of the female prevails over the male, that is, the power of judgment prevails over compassion. And all is one matter and one way.
Behold, it is found now that the letters אבג"ד are in Tiferet and the letters תשר"ק in Malkhut.

And behold, the letters that are in the male are three alphabets, which are light, water, firmament, which are three rungs, Chesed and Gevurah, Tiferet, as is explained in the Gate of Letters; and all of them straight; for the alphabet of תשר"ק is only from the side of the female, in the joining of the judgment; but from the side of Gevurah itself it will be straight. And because they are three rungs straight, therefore there comes into being from them the alphabet of Achas Beta and the like, all of them of three letters; because they are wheels rolling and bestowed one within another, as we shall explain. And Tiferet, which is the firmament: beneath it Malkhut rolls. And it is already known that the courses of the moon are swifter than the courses of the sun; and therefore, when Malkhut rolls and receives from Tiferet, sometimes the Tav that is in Malkhut receives from the Alef that is in Tiferet; and in this way the whole alphabet of Atbash. And when the moon hastens its rolling and the sun is still in its standing, the Shin that is in Malkhut receives from the Alef that is in Tiferet; and likewise the whole alphabet of א"ש ב"ר; and in this way all of them. And there is no wonder that a letter receives from its fellow even though it is not its partner; because all the letters are included of the ten sefirot; for all the things that are bestowed and emanated from the very self of the sefirot are possessed of ten, because there was no separation in it. And if so, when the upper letter illuminates opposite it to bestow, the lower letter stands to receive according to the measure of the upper, and the upper according to the measure of the lower. And the example of this: when the upper is the aspect of Tiferet, it prepares and illuminates in the lower the side that it has from Malkhut, to receive; and when the lower is Tiferet, it prepares in the upper the side that it has from Keter, to bestow. And in this way all the letters, in a manner that "the loops are opposite" (Exod. 26:5), and they receive one from another, and there is not one whose eye, God forbid, is evil toward that of its fellow:

And since we are with this introduction "between the porch and the altar" (Joel 2:17), let us further enter with it from the porch inward. For according to this way the letters will be each one included of the twenty-two; for such is the way of spiritual things, each one included of its fellow, as we explained above in the Gate of Particulars of Names, on the matter of Teli, Galgal, Lev, and likewise in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 4, on the matter of the seventy luminaries that are included, etc. And it is a clear thing that, since each one is included of ten, so that there be no separation, God forbid, so also all the particular branches are included. And as it is said of the sefirot all together, so also it is said of each and every sefirah and of each branch. And the difference between them is after the way of the difference between the sefirot that we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance: that the principal is what prevails. So in the branches: each branch is included of its fellow, except that here this branch is revealed more than its fellow, etc. And let us return to our matter: since each one of the letters is included of the twenty-two, if so it is no wonder that each one of them is exchanged with whichever it may be, since in it too there is a part of that letter that is exchanged with it; except that, with all this, the principal is the letter written in the principal of the name, and the one exchanged for it is a branch of it. And the example of this: the name  Y H V  is exchanged in Atbash into מצ"ף.

And behold, these letters are branches from it; not that the whole very self of the name that is in  Y H V  is in מצ"ף. And because of this the power of substitution is not praised like permutation; for in permutation the whole very self of the letters is the name that was permuted, and nothing is lacking, except that it was reversed with respect to the aspects, as we explained in chapter 3. But in substitution the power of the aforementioned name is diminished, after the way that we explained. And in this way we may infer for all the substitutions and for all the names. And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21, fol. 59 and fol. 70) it is proved that the matter of these substitutions is from the side of Metatron: "And the Holy One, blessed be He, strips Himself of all titles and of all chariots of Metatron, which are כוז"ו במוכס"ז כוז"ו, מצפ"ץ," etc. And he said that the substitutions of YHVH Eloheinu YHVH in כוז"ו במוכס"ז כוז"ו, and likewise YHVH in מצפ"ץ, are chariots of YHVH in Metatron, and they are the garments of the Name, which are in the time of the exile. And it is expounded there that in the time of the redemption the Holy One, blessed be He, strips Himself of all the titles, etc., as he concludes. The example of this: when the four-letter name is clothed in the letters מצפ"ץ, it shows that the Name was clothed in Metatron, in the garment so called; and likewise for all the other names and for all the substitutions:

And what we need to know is that not all the alphabets are equal. For the alphabet that always rises in its reckoning shows its excellence, that it rises by way of the ladder and does not descend. The example of this: the alphabet of Achas Beta, etc., always rises and does not descend; that is to say, the reckoning of the first letter of the first word is one, and the first of the second word is Bet; it always rises. And likewise all the other words, and likewise all the other letters, always rise and do not descend. And this shows the cleaving of this alphabet to its upper source; and therefore it rises toward above in the reckoning of its letters. And there is an alphabet that rises and descends, the example Atbash; for it rises in its half and descends in its half; it shows that it is not so great in its excellence. For the one that rises, rises and is united in its source and does not descend, which shows the strength of its ascent, so that it does not descend. And the other, it is true that it rose, but it did not rise so much as to be united in its source; rather, it returned to descend by way of the steps by which it rose.
