Sometimes it rises a little and descends more than those steps by which it rose: this shows that it does not rise in excellence and rung as the alphabets that are equal in their ascent and their descent; and all the more that they are not equal with the one that rises more than its descent. The end of the matter: according to the matter of the ascent and the descent will be the rung of the alphabet. And not only the alphabet; but even the name that is permuted from the rising alphabet, its excellence will be more praiseworthy than the name that is permuted from the descending alphabet, which is תשר"ק, etc. And likewise the one permuted by means of the alphabet that rises and descends is more praiseworthy than the one that always descends. And therefore the name that is permuted by means of Avgad is more praiseworthy than the name that is permuted by means of Atbash, such as מצפ"ץ; because Avgad rises and does not descend, and Atbash rises in its half and descends in its half. And the name of forty-two, whose principal permutation is by means of alphabets that rise and do not descend, which are Albam, Ayak Bekhar, Achas Beta, and Avgad, and the rest, as is explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names according to the tradition of the Geonim; see there:

behold, its excellence and its rung are more than all of them, in that it rises and does not descend. And by this introduction the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Terumah (fol. 132b) will be understood, and these are his words: "The name of forty-two letters: its secret is the Patriarchs, who are crowned in the upper world, and the upper world in what is above. And therefore it rises and does not descend; it is crowned within the upper Thought. Happy is the portion of the one who knows it and is careful with it. The name of seventy-two letters is David, who is crowned in the Patriarchs; and its secret rises and descends. In the same way, מצפ"ץ, the name of the thirteen measures of compassion: they are twelve, the secret of the holy chariot that goes out from one that dwells upon them. And therefore it rises and descends. And all of them rise and descend, except this [name of forty-two], which rises and does not descend. And therefore the name of seventy-two rises and descends: it rises from this side and descends from this side. [The name of the thirteen measures rises from this side and descends from this side.] And that which descends, [in order] to draw goodness below. And therefore א"ת ב"ש ג"ר ד"ק ה"ץ ו"ף ז"ע ח"ס ט"ן י"מ כ"ל: the first letters rise in reckoning, and the other letters descend in reckoning, in order to draw goodness from above to below. The name of forty-two crowns the upper chariot; the name of seventy-two crowns the lower chariot. Happy is the portion of the one who strives to know his Master; happy is he in this world and in the world to come." Thus far his words.

And his intention is clear. For he said that the name of forty-two rises and does not descend, as we explained above; because of this it shows a high place; for its letters hint at the Patriarchs, who are united in Binah, and Binah in Chokhmah and Keter; it is found that it rises above and does not descend. And this he intended in saying, "The name of forty-two: its secret is the Patriarchs," which are Gedulah and Gevurah, Tiferet. And it is already known that they are held in their three branches that branch out from them; and therefore six of its names hint at them. However, the seventh name is hinted in Binah; for Tiferet and Malkhut and Binah are all one, and they are the secret of Shabbat. And likewise these seven names are the secret of seven days, as we explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapter 13. And therefore its principal is in the Patriarchs, which are fathers to Netzach, Hod, Yesod; and they rise and are crowned in the secret of the Shabbat day, which is the seventh, in Binah itself; and Binah is united with what is above her. We are found to learn that it rises and does not descend; for it rises "within the upper Thought": it is the secret of Keter Elyon, which is called the upper Thought, as is known. However, the name of seventy-two is "David, who is crowned in the Patriarchs"; for three verses, which are Va-yisa, Va-yavo, Va-yet (Exod. 14:19–21), are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet; and in their particulars and their totality, seventy-two, two hundred and sixteen, that is, ויעב"ר [va-ya'avor], the secret of the gestation [ibbur]; for ibbur and va-ya'avor, the letters of this one are as the letters of that one. And it descends below in the secret of the coupling of husband and wife, in the secret of Tiferet and Malkhut; for there is the gestation of the souls. And therefore it rises in the secret of the reversed verse, which shows the ascent and the withdrawal upward; for it turns its face to rise to its source. And there is no wonder at the ascent being by means of Gevurah, which is the left, the verse Va-yavo; for there is no ascent by way of the steps of the ladder except in the secret of the left, and the descent in the right; and it is well known. And therefore the thrusting away is always with the left, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 107b): "Always let the left thrust away and the right draw near." And therefore the withdrawal by the left shows the thrusting away; which is not so with the names of compassion; for the principal is the drawing downward, in the secret of the bestowal that is bestowed. And this he intended in saying, "In the same way, מצפ"ץ, the name of the thirteen measures of compassion," etc.: they are the exchange of the thirteen attributes in Atbash, as is well known; and from the side of the alphabet in which it is exchanged, in this respect it is called rising and descending. And he said, "they are twelve, the secret of the chariot," etc.: the explanation is that they are twelve borders, and the including power, the source that bestows them and emanates them; they are thirteen. And the twelve are twelve stones, which are a chariot to Tiferet, as we explained on the matter of the twelve borders in the Gate of Particulars of Names, chapter 6. And the thirteenth is the source that emanates them, which surrounds them and encompasses them; it is "the one that dwells upon them" and hovers over them. "And therefore it rises and descends," etc.: the explanation is that, for the reason of its being compassion, it needed to descend and bestow. "And all of them rise," etc.: the explanation is that, since the ascent is a need for receiving and the descent a need for bestowing, all the names, all of them, rise and descend; rise to receive and descend to bestow, after the way of the powers and the names; except the name of forty-two, which rises to be crowned above and does not descend, to show the might of its power and its strength, and that it is united in its root. And therefore it is true of it that it is judgment; even though the principal of its ascent is only for praise, to be exalted, with all this it rises to be crowned and does not descend to bestow; and there is in this matter judgment, since it withdraws and does not bestow. And the name of seventy-two is not so; for it is compassion and bestows; it rises and descends. And this he meant in saying, "And therefore the name of seventy-two rises and descends," etc., "the name of thirteen," etc.: for the thirteen attributes are of compassion, and the secret of compassion is to bestow; and therefore it rises and descends. And seventy-two and thirteen are all one thing; for the name of seventy-two depends on the twelve borders, which are thirteen, as is explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, brought the thirteen attributes there only to establish the name of seventy-two, that it is compassion and bestows; and therefore after its ascent it descends. And with this the whole rest of the saying is explained. And there has come out for us the matter of the secret of the rising and descending alphabets. We are also found to learn that the rising ones are in the secret of the ascent, and therefore they rise in their number. And it is difficult: for according to this it would have been fitting that the alphabet of Avgad, which shows the ascent, be in the secret of Malkhut, in the secret of the returning light, in the secret of receiving; and the alphabet of תשר"ק be in the secret of Tiferet, in the secret of the direct light, in the secret of bestowal and compassion. And the words of Rashbi in the Song of Songs are not so, as we explained in the previous chapter, where he says that תשר"ק is in Malkhut and Avgad in Tiferet. And to this we shall answer: when we examine closely the words of Rashbi there, where he says that the matter of תשר"ק is in Malkhut and Avgad in Tiferet, it is in the secret of "You have formed me behind and before" (Ps. 139:5); the explanation, before the sawing apart of Eve, which we explained in the Gate of the Diminishment, chapter 2. And therefore they were back to back, cleaving; the male facing upward, to his roots, and the female downward. It is found according to this that the order of the letters is thus: Avgad, etc., is the front, and the back is Atbash, etc.; and the male faces upward, in the secret of the back, and the female faces downward, the reverse of their descent. And after the sawing apart, when their joining was face to face, the male bestows, looking downward toward the female, and the female upward toward the male, to receive from him; and therefore Avgad rises in the male and תשר"ק in the female, and as we explained.
Behold, the part of permutation is concluded in all that is needed. And now we shall come to explain the part of gematriot:

On the part of gematria; and it is the matter of the number of the letters being equal to equal. And to this part there are other divisions; and they are, first, the part of the weight [mishkal]; and it is the most praiseworthy of all the gematria. And its explanation: as רזיא"ל [Raziel], which comes up to the reckoning of אברהם [Abraham], and their letters are equal, this one five letters and that one five letters; and likewise בי"ט comes up to יה"ו, for in this one three letters and in that one three letters; and they are weighed together, this as that and that as this. And this is the most praiseworthy of all the gematriot, because the whole matter of the branches and the powers that are in this name are in that name, except that the letters were exchanged, and the powers into other powers. And this is possible after the way that we wrote above; and this way is near, in some respect, to substitution. And under this part there is another part, and it is the part of joining and separation.

And the matter of the joining is if there are in it three letters that are joined into two. How so? הו"ה, when the two Hehs are joined into Yod, and it becomes י"ו; and likewise אהי"ה, when Alef and Heh are joined into Vav, and it comes up יה"ו; and likewise חיים [chayyim], when the two Yods are joined into Kaf, and it becomes חכם [chakham]. And this is a somewhat praiseworthy part; for the letters do not change entirely by way of the reckoning, as we shall explain; but they stand in their place, except that two of them were joined or separated; and from the union and the joining the separation is known, and from the separation the union is known; and therefore there is no need to lengthen on it. However, the matter is that each and every letter, according to its number, so will be its powers; for the number is not for nothing. For the Tav will have four hundred branches branching out from it, all of them "a knob and a flower" (Exod. 25:33); and likewise for all the branches going out from the pure candelabrum, in which twenty-two things are fixed, as we explained in the Gate of Letters. And even though it is found that Alef is in Keter, its reckoning one, showing one branch, and Tav is in Malkhut, or in whatever place it may be, showing four hundred; and certainly Alef is in a greater excellence than Tav: this is no question. For there is a branch which, even though it is single, includes many branches hidden and concealed in it; like the Alef, which includes all the branches, that is to say, all the letters, as we explained in the Gate of Letters; and all of them are united in Alef. And with this the matter of gematria will now be understood: that it is one matter with the thing counted in it. The example: אמ"ן [amen], which comes up to יאדהונה"י, as is well known in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. For when Tiferet and Malkhut are joined, there are united in the union the twenty-six branches that are in Tiferet, as the number of the four-letter name, and the sixty-five branches that are in Malkhut, as the number of Adonai. And when we wish to join them, we join them in the name סוכ"ה [sukkah], or in the name אמ"ן, or in the name מלאך [mal'akh]; for in all of them are hinted the ninety-one branches that are in their union. True, they are not equal in their matter; for סוכה is more united, for it is כ"ו ה"ס [26, 65], whose branches are revealed upon the matter that is hinted in the two names. And similarly, when we join two letters into one, and likewise two names into one, behold, that letter and that name will not be related in very self [one] to the first letter or to the first name that was principal in its spirituality. And from this we may infer to when the word is changed entirely. However, the order of the count of the gematria: they received concerning them that they are nine; and these are their names, as the ancients named them. 1. The general rounded number; and it is in the return of the wheel; that is to say, that the thousands are reckoned only as ones; as five times two hundred and sixteen, which come up to אנכ"י [Anokhi, 81]. And many named this number by the name "small number" [mispar katan]; and the reason is because it makes the number small; for from a hundred it makes one, and from three hundred three, and from four hundred four; and likewise in this way it makes the number of the thousands small, to the rung of the ones. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, names this number for Enoch; and likewise it is customary in many places, especially in the Tikkunim, "by the small reckoning of Enoch." And it seems to us that this matter is because Enoch is the youth Metatron; and this angel makes the attributes small because he is "a small mirror"; that is to say, that there are in him the branches of the sefirot spreading out and clothed in his light, and he does not merit them in their being included of ten or more. For this is the secret of the number that is in the letters: that the ones rise to the tens in the secret of one included of ten, and from the tens to the hundreds in the secret that each one is included of ten, and ten of ten; for each one of ten branches is further included of ten; and it is found that from one it rises to a hundred; and likewise in this way they rise to a thousand. And Metatron is the reverse of this attribute; for the light of the inclusion is dark for him, and he has no inclusion of the attributes, because he is in the world of separation (that is, the world of Yetzirah). And therefore, on the contrary, he makes the number of the letters small; and what shines above in the sefirah in a thousand shines below in Metatron in one. And this is the secret of the small number. And from this we can infer to the adding numbers: that they add the inclusion; and those that add in the letters themselves add the very self of the including branch; and likewise the one that adds the word, and the like; and likewise those that add the filling, in the secret of the fillings that we explained in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. And this is enough of a note for understanding the other numbers, so that we need not explain them; for in this gate all of them enter, above and below:

2. The antecedent number: as Gimel comes up to six, when we count from the beginning of the alphabet up to the Gimel; Dalet comes up to ten; and Heh comes up to fifteen, when we count from the head of the alphabet. And we have wished to complete here all the numbers, all of them, from the head of the alphabet to its end, so that it be easy for us to count when we need the number. And this is its form: אב comes up to ג; אבג comes up to ו; אבגד comes up to י; אבגדה comes up to טו; אבגדהו comes up to כא; אבגדהוז comes up to כח; אבגדהוזח comes up to לו; אבגדהוזחט comes up to מה; אבגדהוזחטי comes up to נה; אבגדהוזחטיכ comes up to עה; אבגדהוזחטיכל comes up to קה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמ comes up to קמה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנ comes up to קצה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנס comes up to רנה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנסע comes up to שכה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנסעפ comes up to תה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנסעפצ comes up to תצה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנסעפצק comes up to תרצה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנסעפצקר comes up to תשצה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנסעפצקרש comes up to אלף צה; אבגדהוזחטיכלמנסעפצקרשת comes up to אתצ"ה. And behold, with this table it will be easy for us to bring out the number for all that is needed, with the help of the Rock and His salvation:
3. The necessary number; and it is the number of the word according to what it is: as חסד [Chesed] comes up to seventy-two; גבורה [Gevurah] two hundred and sixteen, or ארי"ה [aryeh, lion]:

4. The additive number: it is that we add the letters of the word to the number, or the word itself, if all is needed, according to the need. And likewise the concealment of these has been explained above, and likewise their reason. And the reason for the antecedent: since it is its cause, after the way that I explained concerning the sefirot in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation:

5. The general square number: as דוד [David], which comes up to fourteen. One must permute the word according to the order of the letters, and we say: four times fourteen comes up to fifty-six; six times fourteen comes up to eighty-four; behold a hundred and forty. And four times fourteen comes up to fifty-six. The total of all of them is a hundred and ninety-six. And the reason of the matter is that, since they are fourteen branches in three powers, and certainly each one of the powers that are in the three powers is included of all the powers, therefore it will be fourteen times fourteen; for each one of the powers is included of all of them, as we explained; and therefore they rise to this great number:

6. The particular square number: as two times two come up to four; three times three, behold nine; and likewise four times four, behold sixteen. And this matter is that the letter is included in the totality of the powers that are in it alone, not in all the powers that are in the word, like the preceding inclusion in the general number:

7. The nominal number; that is to say, to put upon the word the filling of the letters: as YHVH in the filling of Alefs, like this, יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א, which comes up to forty-five, as the number of אדם [adam]. And this has already been explained above:

8. The numeral number; that is to say, Yod is "ten" [עשרה], and "ten" comes up to five hundred and seventy-five; Heh is "five" [חמשה], and "five" comes up to three hundred and fifty-three. And this matter is that those five powers are included in the count of their name; for there the name of their number testifies concerning them:

9. The great numeral number; that is to say, Yod in its filling is twenty, and "twenty" [עשרים] in gematria is כתר [Keter]. And its explanation is after the way that we explained in the eighth; "and its fellow tells of it" (Job 36:33).
Behold, the part of gematria is concluded:

There is further something near to this matter, and it is called notarikon; and it is the matter of initial letters, and final letters, and middle letters of words. The example: אל מלך נאמן [God, faithful King], whose initial letters are אמן, and final letters לכ"ן, and middle letters מל"א; and the like. And the rest of the names that go out from the initial letters of words, or from their end, or from their middle, or by skipping one letter and taking one letter, skipping its fellow, and things like these; like the name הס"ר תי"ו אה"ן, which goes out from "The hidden things belong to YHVH our God" (Deut. 29:28) by skipping a letter and taking a letter; and many like these things. And there is no need to lengthen; for this whole matter shows the honour of the Torah and its concealment: that it was made corporeal and received all the permutations that can be in the world, and was clothed in a strange garment, as I explained in the Gate of Letters, chapter 1. And all this so as to complete our souls; for "YHVH was pleased, for His righteousness' sake," etc. (Isa. 42:21). And in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (fol. 46b), it appears explicitly that reckonings and gematriot all depend on Malkhut; for in the sefirot above the branches are not revealed in reckonings and gematriot; and what reckoning and gematria is found there, with all this their principal is in Malkhut, and from there they hint above. And with this this chapter is completed and this gate concluded, with the help of Heaven. Blessed be YHVH forever, Amen and Amen. Blessed is He who "gives power to the faint, and to him that has no might He increases strength" (Isa. 40:29):
The Gate of the Soul, which is Gate Thirty-One:

After we have occupied ourselves in the preceding gates with all the parts of the concealed wisdom, whether much or little, our intention in this gate is to explain the matter of the human being, that is to say, his form, which is his soul and his spirit and his vital soul. And our occupation will be in three parts of this inquiry. The first: the place of the soul, and its matter in this world, and the benefit of its creation. Second: its joining in the smitten body, even though it is a subtle being, more spiritual than the ministering angels, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces. Third: the matter of its sin and its punishment, and its blemishing above in the honoured roots, and the blemishing of itself, and likewise its cutting of the plantings, God forbid:
Chapter One:

On the explanation of the first part, which is the place of the soul. What is well known in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is that the soul [neshamah], that is to say, the form of the human being, is divided into three parts; and they are vital soul [nefesh], spirit [ruach] and soul [neshamah]. And the vital soul is a chariot for the spirit, and the spirit a chariot for the soul. And the emanation of the three of them is from the upper sefirot, the roots of all the roots that belong to them. However, they are divided in their emanation: for the soul is emanated from Binah; and the sign: "and the soul of Shaddai gives them understanding [tevinem]" (Job 32:8). And the spirit is emanated from Tiferet; and as Tiferet is a throne and seat for Binah, therefore the spirit is a throne and seat for the soul. And the vital soul is emanated from Malkhut; and therefore the vital soul is a throne and seat for the spirit, as Malkhut is a seat and throne for Tiferet. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained their emanation in the Zohar, Parashat Va-yiggash (fol. 206), and these are his words: "Come and see: all of them are these rungs, these upon those: vital soul, spirit, soul, rung upon rung. The vital soul first, and it is the lowest rung, as we have said. The spirit afterward, which dwells upon the vital soul and stands over it. The soul is the rung that rises over all; and they have established it. The vital soul: this is the vital soul of David, and it is the one that stands to receive the vital soul from that river that flows and goes out. The spirit: this is the spirit that stands over the vital soul, and there is no existence for the vital soul except by the spirit; and this is the spirit that dwells between fire and water; and from here this vital soul is nourished. The spirit stands in the existence of another, upper rung, which is called soul; for from there go out vital soul and spirit; from there the spirit is nourished. And when the spirit takes, then the vital soul takes; and all is one, and they are brought near one to another: the vital soul is brought near to the spirit, and the spirit is brought near to the soul; and all is one." Thus far his words.

And explicitly he explained that they are: soul, Binah; spirit, Tiferet; vital soul, Malkhut. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 114a), and these are his words: "'The lamp [ner] of YHVH is the soul of man' (Prov. 20:27). Ner: nefesh, ruach; and they are the emanation of the Shekhinah and of the central pillar, which includes six sefirot. 'The soul of man': the emanation of the upper Mother." Thus far his words.

And behold, by His power, may He be blessed, these three powers are bound with a firm and strong bond, each one according to its rung and its matter, "each man to his service and to his burden" (Num. 4:19). And some ask: since the three parts are emanated from Binah, Tiferet and Malkhut, if so, how do we say that the soul of Abraham is from the side of Chesed, and likewise Isaac from the side of Gevurah, and Jacob from the side of Tiferet, and the like? And this question Rabbi Judah Chayyat asked of Rabbi al-Castili. And this is his answer to him: "What you asked concerning the matter of what our Sages, of blessed memory, said, that the vital soul of Abraham is related to the right and Isaac to the left, and likewise many, each and every one related to his attribute; and you objected: but every man is included of three rungs, vital soul, spirit and soul: vital soul from Malkhut, and spirit from Tiferet, and soul from Binah; if so, how is it possible that the words be settled? You already know, my brother, that all the rungs are included one in another, for 'their end is fixed in their beginning'; and therefore each and every one is found to include the whole Emanation. And since three forms are found from three rungs of the Emanation, from which the intellectual, the sensory and the natural suck, in the secret of vital soul, spirit and soul, they themselves are found in each and every sefirah." Thus far his words.

And the sum of his words is that the three rungs belong to Abraham from the Binah and the Tiferet and the Malkhut that are in Chesed; and likewise to Isaac from the side of Gevurah, and likewise to Jacob from the side of Tiferet. And some explained in another manner, after this way: that the soul of Abraham is from the side of the Chesed that is in Binah, and the soul of Isaac from the side of the Gevurah that is in Binah, and the soul of Jacob from the side of the Tiferet that is in Binah; and the spirit of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, from the side of the Chesed that is in Tiferet, and the spirit of Isaac from the side of the Gevurah that is in Tiferet, and the spirit of Jacob from the side of the Tiferet that is in Tiferet; and likewise for the vital soul, from the side of the Chesed that is in Malkhut, or from the side of the Gevurah that is in Malkhut, or from the side of the Tiferet that is in Malkhut. And we have in this another way: for each and every soul is included of ten; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained; and we copied his language in the Gate of Ten and Not Nine, chapter 5, in the saying "And there are others, masters of the Book of the Torah," etc.; see there.

And behold, since every soul is included of ten; and just as a man, by his fitting deeds, makes one of the attributes prevail to act, and all the other attributes are clothed in the matter of that attribute, from the side of the strength of the bestowal, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance; so also, if a man wishes, he makes prevail in his soul, by his actions, whatever part he wishes. For example, if he occupies himself with Torah, he makes the power of Tiferet prevail upon himself; and the part of Tiferet that is in his soul is found shining, until it is the principal and the other parts are secondary to it. And with this will be understood the matter of Abraham our father, which they expounded in the Sefer ha-Bahir (brought in the Omissions of the Zohar, part 1, fol. 13) on the verse (Ps. 118:22), "The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner": that Abraham our father rejected the attribute of Malkhut, and likewise Isaac, etc. And if their soul was emanated from her, how did they reject her? And likewise, if the soul of Abraham was emanated from the side of Chesed, if so he was of necessity a chariot to Chesed; and if so, how is it possible to reject, or how did he reject? And with what we have explained this matter is settled: for a man can make whatever part he wishes prevail in his soul, according to his deeds. And behold, the Patriarchs did not wish to cleave except to a high place, and they made prevail in their soul: Abraham the part of Chesed, Isaac the part of Gevurah, etc.; and likewise all men. And we have already explained this matter at length in the Gate of Titles, chapter 4, with the help of Heaven. And in this way it is possible for an Israelite to be reincarnated in a priest or a Levite, according to the prevailing of the part that he merited to make prevail by his deeds before his reincarnation.

And behold, apart from the soul being included of ten, as is explained, it is further included of four upper elements, like the body, which is included of four elements. And the elements of the soul are the spiritual waters, from the side of Chesed; and the spiritual fire, from the side of Gevurah; and the holy wind [ruach], from the side of Tiferet; and the fine dust, from the side of Malkhut. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Va-era (fol. 24b), and these are his words: "Rabbi Simeon said: That which Rabbi Chizkiyah said, that when the Holy One, blessed be He, created Adam, he was created from the dust of the lower Sanctuary; from the dust of the upper Sanctuary the soul was given in him. Just as when he was created from the lower dust, three sides of the elements of the world were joined in him, so also, when he was created from the upper dust, three sides of the elements of the world were joined in him; and Adam was completed." Thus far his words.

For the soul is always included of ten sefirot; and apart from this, the appearance of the four [aforementioned elements] prevails in it more, until the four faces are seen shining in it more and more than the rest of the ten. And like this matter in the sefirot themselves: for even though each one is included of ten, sometimes they are included in four, sometimes in five, sometimes in seven, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And the matter is that, apart from the inclusion of the ten, the seven attributes prevail in it until they shine more than all. And likewise with respect to Tiferet: for even though it is included of ten, like the other sefirot, with all this it is said of it that it includes six extremities. And this law holds for all the sefirot, as we explained in the aforementioned gate. And apart from these inclusions that are in the soul itself, there are in the manifestation of the soul many, many other particulars:

After we explained in the previous chapter the emanation of the three parts of the form of the human being from a high place, from Binah and Tiferet and Malkhut, one may ask: if so, it would have been fitting that, when a man departs from the world, all these three parts should depart to their source and their spiritual foundation. And the thing is not so; for Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained explicitly that the dwelling of the vital soul is in the grave, and the dwelling of the spirit in the lower Garden, and the dwelling of the soul in the upper Garden. And one may ask why. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar (Va-yechi, fol. 224b): "We have learned: one thousand five hundred fragrances rise every day from the Garden of Eden, with which are perfumed those precious garments of that world, which are crowned from the days of a man. Rabbi Judah said: How many garments are there? Rabbi Eliezer said: The mountains of the world disagreed on this. But there are three. One, in which the spirit that is in the Garden of Eden of the earth is clothed. And one, in which the soul is clothed within the bundle of life, among the purple of the King's house. And one outer garment, which stands and does not stand, is seen and is not seen. In this one the vital soul is clothed, and goes and roams in the world; and on every New Moon and Shabbat it goes and is bound with the spirit in the Garden of Eden on earth, which stands behind the precious heavenly curtain; and from it it learns and knows what it knows, and roams and makes it known in the world." Thus far his words.

And from it it becomes clear that the principal dwelling of the vital soul is in this world, and of the spirit in the lower Garden of Eden, and of the soul above. And so it is explained in Parashat Acharei (fol. 70b), and these are his words: "Three dwellings the Holy One, blessed be He, made for the righteous. One, that those righteous merited, who are not wiped out of this world. And when the people of the world need compassion, and they, the living, sit in distress, they pray a prayer for them, and go and make the matter known to those who sleep in Hebron; and they are aroused and enter the Garden of Eden of the earth, where the spirits of the righteous are clothed in diadems of light; and they take counsel with them and decree a decree, and the Holy One, blessed be He, does their desire [re'uta] and has pity on the world. And those vital souls of the righteous are found in this world to protect the living; and this is called nefesh. And this is not wiped out of this world, etc., to look and to know and to protect the generation. And this is what the companions said, that the dead know the distress of the world. And the punishment of the guilty who are in the earth is in this, as it is written, 'and that vital soul shall be cut off from its people' (Lev. 7:20). The second dwelling is the Garden of Eden that is on earth, in which the Holy One, blessed be He, made upper precious dwellings, in the likeness of this world and in the likeness of the upper world; and palaces of two kinds without number; and trees and grasses and fragrances that rise every day. And in this place dwells that which is called the spirit of those righteous; and the dwelling of that spirit dwells in it. And each and every spirit is clothed in a precious garment, in the likeness of this world and in the likeness of that upper world. The third dwelling is that upper holy dwelling which is called the bundle of life, where that upper holy rung, which is called soul, is in bliss; and this cleaves to take pleasure in the upper bliss. Of it it is written, 'Then you shall take pleasure in YHVH, and I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth' (Isa. 58:14)." Thus far his words. And the matter is further explained there, and likewise it is explained in many places of the Zohar. And now: why do the vital soul and the spirit not rise to their upper root, since they are emanated from above?

And to this we say: certainly no emanated soul is emanated below into the lower world unless it is created and formed and made; and these aspects are not separated; that is to say, there is no manifestation of Atzilut in the world unless the rungs are linked down in a chain; for the garment of Atzilut is Beriah, and the garment of Beriah is Yetzirah, and the garment of Yetzirah is Asiyah. And therefore it was necessary that there be for the soul of Atzilut one garment; and it is the soul of Beriah; and it is the one more commonly found; for who merits Atzilut? However, the one in whom there is the soul of Beriah is called a servant of YHVH; and the one in whom there will be the soul of Atzilut is called a son. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 6a), and these are his words: "From the side of the created Glory, Israel say toward the Master of the world, 'if as servants'; and from the side of the emanated Glory it is said of them, 'if as sons.'" Thus far his words. And so he explained in the book of the Ra'aya Meheimna. However, a soul of Yetzirah and Asiyah is not found at all; because the spirit is Yetzirah to the soul of Beriah, and the vital soul Asiyah to the formed spirit. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 132b), and these are his words: "'Let us make man' (Gen. 1:26): the wheel and the angel and the Throne were joined and said, 'Let us make man,' that he be in our partnership: the soul from the Throne, and the spirit from the angel, and the vital soul from the wheel, to be in our likeness," etc. Thus far his words.

And it is still more explained elsewhere in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6, fol. 21b): "'You shall not take the mother with the young' (Deut. 22:6). Eggs are from the side of the wheels; fledglings from the side of the youth Metatron; young from the side of the Throne, which is the tabernacle of peace, which is the nest of the Shekhinah. For the upper Mother nests in the Throne, in three upper sefirot; the central pillar, which includes six sefirot, nests in Metatron; the lower Mother nests in the wheel, of which it is said (Ezek. 1:15), 'and behold one wheel upon the earth.' And further, the Shekhinah, from the side of the Throne, is called eagle; from the side of the youth, dove; and from the side of the wheel, bird. And the Shekhinah is 'the likeness of a man to them' (Ezek. 1:5). 'You shall surely send away' (Deut. 22:7): come and see, there is an angel who is appointed over birds, which are the souls that are called birds, and Sandalfon is his name. And at the time that Israel fulfil this commandment, and the mother goes driven away and the young cry out, he pleads merit for his birds and says before the Holy One, blessed be He: 'It is written of You, "and His compassion is over all His works" (Ps. 145:9); why have You decreed upon this bird that it be driven from its nest?' And likewise Metatron pleads merit for his birds, which are spirits that fly in human beings. From the Throne, they are souls; and from this living creature, they are spirits; and from the wheel, vital souls; and they are in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. On Shabbat and festival there descend upon them souls and spirits and vital souls by way of Atzilut, which are the Holy Spirit." Thus far his words.

And though we have copied it in the Gate of ABYA, with all this we have lengthened in copying it, because it is needed by us. And the intention is that the Throne, that is, Beriah; and Metatron, that is, Yetzirah; and Sandalfon, who is the wheel, by whose means the Holy One, blessed be He, causes His Shekhinah to dwell in the world, and of whom it is said, "and behold one wheel upon the earth," is a garment to the Shekhinah, to be clothed in Asiyah, as is explained in the Gate of ABYA. And he said that the souls are from the side of the light that is revealed and clothed and spreads from the very self of the sefirot to Beriah; and the spirits are from the light that is clothed in Yetzirah; and the vital souls from the light that is clothed in Asiyah, that is, in the wheel. And because soul, spirit, vital soul, without qualification, are from Binah, Tiferet, Malkhut, for this he said that the light of Binah is revealed in Beriah, and the light of Tiferet in Yetzirah, and the light of Malkhut in Asiyah; that is, the Throne and Metatron and Sandalfon, who is the wheel. And it is found according to this that the soul of Beriah is clothed in the spirit of Yetzirah, and the spirit of Yetzirah is clothed in the vital soul of Asiyah.

And behold, Asiyah is this world in all its aspects, as is explained in the Zohar in many places. And the purple of which he spoke above, in the saying of Rabbi Eleazar, is Beriah, a precious garment to the King, as is explained in the aforementioned gate. And since these luminaries have their principal only from the luminary that spreads in these aspects, therefore, when a man departs from the world, each one of the rungs departs literally to their root, which are Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. And therefore the spirit is in the Garden, for there is Yetzirah, in the holy palaces; and the vital soul roams in this world in its length and its breadth, in the secret of the light that spreads in it, that is, Asiyah. However, these three powers, when they are from the side of Atzilut: on Shabbatot and festivals [there is added in it] the matter called the additional soul, like the addition of light that is added from the side of Keter, that is, what is above Beriah. For Binah is clothed in Beriah; and above her are Keter and Chokhmah; and according to the truth, that is, the ten sefirot emanated in the secret of their Atzilut: from there the additional soul is bestowed. And because these two are not clothed in Beriah, as we explained, therefore Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in some places that the additional soul is from the side of Keter. And when it is a soul from Atzilut, this is a soul that will rise up to its upper roots, in the secret of Atzilut. And therefore on the weekdays it is said (Exod. 20:9), "Six days you shall labour [ta'avod]", the language of servant [eved]; for a man is then in the aspect of a servant, for his soul is then from the side of the servant, from Beriah alone, even for the worthy. And with all this, sometimes the vital soul and the spirit and the soul rise, and are bound one with another, and rise up to the roots. Since they are sparks spreading from an upper light, therefore in the union of the worlds the branches are bound to the roots; just as the palaces are bound and united and rise to their upper root in the secret of prayer, as is explained in the Gate of Palaces, so is the law of the vital soul and the spirit and the soul. And so they explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Terumah (fol. 142b), and these are his words: "A vital soul that has rest: this one, when it goes and roams, meets with this appointed one, Yedumiel, and with those officers of his; and they take it and bring it in through all the gates of the Garden of Eden, and show it the honour of the righteous and the honour of that spirit of its own; and it cleaves to it in rest within that garment; and then it knows those things of the world, etc. And it is illuminated from it like the moon when it is illuminated from the sun. And the spirit is bound within that soul; and that soul is bound within the end of Thought, which is the secret of the upper vital soul; and that vital soul is bound within that upper spirit; and that spirit is bound within that upper soul; and that soul is bound in Ein Sof," etc. Thus far his words. And from it is explained the matter of the union and bond of the branches and their withdrawal into their source, as we explained: for Asiyah is united with Yetzirah, and Yetzirah with Beriah, and Beriah with Atzilut, and Atzilut with the upper point. And to stand on the depth of this inquiry one must consider what we explained in the Gate of ABYA in its entirety; and afterward these words of ours will be understood and comprehended according to their pattern, with the help of the Name:

Even though in the previous chapter we established that a soul of Beriah is not found unless it is clothed in a spirit of Yetzirah, and a spirit of Yetzirah is not found unless it is clothed in a vital soul of Asiyah, with all this it is possible that a vital soul of Asiyah be found without a spirit of Yetzirah, and likewise a spirit of Yetzirah without a soul of Beriah; because not all merit the spirit, and not all merit the soul. For according as a man draws near to his Maker, so his spirit is bestowed upon him; and when he is more refined, his soul is bestowed upon him; and when he adds strength in his service, the soul of Atzilut is bestowed upon him, so that he be called a member of the household of the Holy One, blessed be He. And with all this, all these rungs do not encamp upon him except at known times, according to the measure of his purity. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Va-yikra (fol. 24b), and these are his words: "A man sanctifies himself from below; they sanctify him from above. And when he is sanctified with the holiness of his Master, they clothe him with a holy soul, the inheritance of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Assembly of Israel. And then he inherits all; and these are called sons of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, 'You are sons to YHVH your God' (Deut. 14:1); and behold, they have established it." Thus far his words. And this thing is with respect to the emanated soul; and therefore he said, "the inheritance of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Assembly of Israel," that is, from the union of Tiferet and Malkhut; they are from the side of Atzilut, from where they are called sons, as we explained above in the previous chapter. And this is what he said: "and these are called sons," etc.

And Rashbi, peace be upon him, added further explanation in this parashah (there, fol. 25a), and these are his words: "Behold, we have learned: there is one who merits a soul, and there is one who merits the arousal of spirit, and there is one who merits only a vital soul." Thus far his words.

And so they explained in Parashat Acharei (fol. 70b), and these are his words: "For Rabbi Yose said: In all human beings there is a vital soul, and there is a vital soul higher than a vital soul. If a man merits this vital soul, they pour upon him one diadem, which is called spirit; this is what is written, 'until a spirit be poured upon us from on high' (Isa. 32:15). Then a man is aroused with another, upper arousal, to look into the laws of the holy King. If a man merits that spirit, they crown [me'atrin] him with the diadem [itra] of the upper holy crown, which includes all, and it is called soul, which is called 'the soul of God' (Job 27:3)," etc. Thus far his words.

And behold, Rabbi Yose in this saying added much further explanation: that he may not even merit the vital soul itself. And because on the face of it it implies that if a man has no vital soul he cannot live, for this he said, "there is a vital soul and there is a vital soul"; for there is the natural, animating vital soul, which is a chariot to the divine vital soul, as we shall explain. And even though the man be alive, it is possible that a vital soul is not emanated in him; but he lives from the side of the animating vital soul. And when he merits, the divine vital soul is bestowed upon him; and if he merits further, they bestow upon him spirit and soul, as he explains. They further explained this matter in the Zohar, in Parashat Va-yiggash (fol. 206a), and these are his words: "And these three rungs are included in human beings, in those who merit the service of their Master. For at first there is in him a vital soul; and it is a holy perfecting, for a man to be perfected in it. Once a man comes to be purified in this rung, he is perfected to be crowned with a spirit, which is a holy rung that dwells upon the vital soul, for that man who merits to be crowned in it. Once he has risen in them, in vital soul and spirit, and has entered and been perfected in the service of his Master as is fitting, then there dwells upon him the soul, an upper holy rung that rules over all, so as to be crowned with an upper holy rung. And then he is the perfection of all, perfect on all sides, to merit the world to come. And he is the beloved of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, 'that I may cause those who love Me to inherit substance [yesh]' (Prov. 8:21). Who are 'those who love Me'? These are they in whom there is a holy soul." Thus far his words. And from it our intention is explained in a fine light.

And so it is explained in the Zohar (Chadash, fol. 12b; see there, "and may it be pleasant for you") that Rashbi, peace be upon him, made a feast in honour of Rabbi Eleazar his son, when his soul was bestowed upon him. It is further explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 134), and these are his words: "Come and see: as soon as a man is born, they give him the vital soul of a beast, from the side of purity, from those that are called the holy wheels [ofanei kodesh]. If he merits more, they give him a spirit [from the side of the living creatures, which are] the holy living creatures [chayyot ha-kodesh]. If he merits more, they give him a soul from the side of the Throne. And these three are the maidservant and the servant and the handmaid of the King's daughter. If he merits more, they give him a vital soul by way of Atzilut, from the side of the only daughter; and she is called a king's daughter. If he merits more, they give him a spirit by way of Atzilut, from the side of the central pillar; and he is called a son of the Holy One, blessed be He; this is what is written, 'You are sons to YHVH your God.' If he merits more, they give him a soul from the side of Father and Mother," etc.; see there. Thus far his words, for our matter.

Behold, it is found that according to the measure of a man's occupation in this world, so his soul or his spirit or his vital soul is bestowed upon him, all according to the measure of his service. And the manner of its blemishing, even though it is not in this body, will be explained, with the help of Heaven. And there are times when the soul is bestowed upon a man at the time that he fulfils some commandment, or in some matter of occupation in Torah; then YHVH watches over him, and a soul is bestowed upon him according to what he is, so that he be perfected by it. And apart from these three parts there are further parts besides them, which are the angels that accompany a man to guard him, of whom it is said (Ps. 91:11), "For He shall give His angels charge over you." And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the book of the Zohar (in the Introduction, fol. 13a). And Rabbi Simeon and Rabbi Pinchas disagreed on their number: Rabbi Simeon said that they are two, for it is said, "For He shall give His angels charge over you"; and Rabbi Pinchas said three, for it is written (Job 33:23), "If there be over him an angel," behold one; "an interpreter," two; "one among a thousand," behold three. And elsewhere (in Mishpatim, fol. 106b) he explained that these angels are the ones that separate from a man at the time of his sin; and of them it is said (Isa. 57:18), "and I will restore comforts to him and to his mourners": these are these angels, who mourn over him and separate from him according to his evil deeds; for they are concealed through his deeds and they are revealed through his deeds. And the reason is because they are emanated in the emanation of his soul; for at the time that the soul is emanated from the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, these angels are emanated with it. And so Rashbi explained (in the Introduction, there, fol. 12), and these are his words: "'Let the waters swarm with the swarming of living souls' (Gen. 1:20): this is the holy covenant of existence, the river that flows and goes out; and its waters increased and swarm with a swarming and an increase of souls for that living creature. And in those souls that enter this living creature there go out many birds and great hosts that fly the whole world. And when the soul goes out to this world, that bird that flew and went out with this soul from that tree goes out with it. How many go out with each and every soul? Two: one from the right and one from the left. If he is worthy, they guard him, as it is written, 'For He shall give His angels charge over you'; and if not, they accuse him. Rabbi Pinchas said: There are three that stand as guardians over a man, as it is written, 'If there be over him an angel, an interpreter,' etc." And he concludes there that Rabbi Simeon agreed with Rabbi Pinchas. And one cannot say that these angels are not the ones that our Sages, of blessed memory, called the good inclination and the evil inclination; for explicitly they explained in the Zohar (Va-yishlach, fol. 165b) that they themselves are the good inclination and the evil inclination. And these are his words: "Rabbi Judah opened: 'For He shall give His angels charge.' This verse the companions have established: for at the hour that a man comes into the world, immediately the evil inclination is made ready with him, which always accuses a man, as it is said, 'sin crouches at the door' (Gen. 4:7). What is 'sin crouches'? This is the evil inclination. And David too called it so, sin, as it is written, 'and my sin is ever before me' (Ps. 51:5), because it makes a man sin before his Master. And this evil inclination does not depart from a man from the day that he is born and forever. And the good inclination comes with a man from the day that he comes to be purified. And when does he come to be purified as is fitting? When he is thirteen years old. Then a man is coupled with both of them, one from the right and one from the left, etc. And these are literally two appointed angels, and they are always found with him. When a man comes to be purified, that evil inclination is subdued before him, and the right rules over the left; and both of them are coupled to guard a man in all his ways that he does, as it is said, 'For He shall give His angels charge over you,'" etc. Thus far his words.

And from it it is explained that the matter expounded above concerning the two angels is the good inclination and the evil inclination. Further there (fol. 174b): "Rabbi Abba said: At the hour that a man goes in the ways of the Torah and all his ways are arranged as is fitting, many advocates stand over him to mention him for good. He opened and said: 'If there be over him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand,' etc., 'then He is gracious to him and says, Deliver him,' etc. (Job 33:23–24). And is it not revealed?" etc. "Come and see: in this verse you will find the clarity of the matter. It is written, 'If there be over him an angel': if more had not been written, it would be fitting. But it is written, 'an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand.' And who is he? This is the angel that is appointed with a man on the left side, as it is written, 'A thousand shall fall at your side' (Ps. 91:7); and this is the left side, for it is written after it, 'and ten thousand at your right hand.' But 'one among a thousand': this is the evil inclination, which is one of those thousand that are on the left side; because it rises above and takes permission. And therefore, if a man goes in the way of truth, that evil inclination becomes a servant to him, as it is written, 'Better is he that is lightly esteemed and has a servant' (Prov. 12:9). Then it rises and becomes an advocate, and says before the Holy One, blessed be He, merit concerning the man. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, says, 'Deliver him from going down to the pit,'" etc. Thus far his words, for our matter.

And behold, from it it is explained that the two angels are the evil inclination and the good inclination. And what was said above, that the evil inclination is emanated with the soul too, just as the good inclination is emanated with it: because the evil inclination is from the side of Gevurah, and it is a holy angel; however, its chariot is impure, and it is clothed in the power of impurity. For so there are many holy angels appointed over the strange powers. And its chariot is a power spreading from four impure husks, which are Iniquity [Avon], Destroyer [Mashchit], Anger [Af] and Fury [Cheimah]; and it rides upon the four of them and goes at the left side of a man. And likewise the good inclination rides in a holy chariot, which is the power of Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, Raphael; and it rides upon the four of them and goes at the right side of a man. And a man inclines himself to one of the sides; and it is in his hand, the ability to tip the scale-pan of liability to the side of merit, or the reverse; for so they explained this matter in the book of the Ra'aya Meheimna. And the other matters of the soul, concerning the matter of its emanation, are explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance; and likewise the evil inclination is explained in the Gate of the Palaces of Impurity:

On the clarification of the matter of the image [tzelem], which is expounded in the Zohar in many places. And what is well known is that this image is a fourth matter, which is neither vital soul nor spirit nor soul; however, it is revealed more than they, so that there are some of the pious who perceive its likeness in this world. And as for the matter of its essence and the manner of its formation, it is explained in Parashat Emor (fol. 104b), and these are his words: "In the book of King Solomon we found that at the hour that coupling is found below, the Holy One, blessed be He, sends one likeness in the visage of a man, marked and engraved in an image, and it stands over that coupling. And if permission were given to the eye to see, a man would see over his head one image marked like the visage of a man; and in that image a man is created. And until that image which his Master sent him stands over his head and is found there, a man is not created. This is what is written, 'And God created man in His image' (Gen. 1:27). That image is made ready opposite him until he goes out into the world. When he goes out, in that image he grows up; in that image he goes; this is what is written, 'Surely man walks in an image' (Ps. 39:7). And this image is from above. At the hour that those spirits go out from their place, each and every spirit is arranged before the holy King in precious tikkunin, in the visage in which it stands in this world. And from that likeness, that precious tikkun, this image goes out. And this is third to the spirit. And it goes before, in this world, at the hour that the coupling is found. And there is no coupling in the world in which an image is not found among them. But holy Israel: this holy image, and from a holy place, is found among them. And for the idolaters an image from those evil kinds, from the side of impurity, is found among them. And therefore a man ought not to mix his image with the image of idolaters, because this one is holy and that one impure." Thus far his words.

And his words are clear: for he said that the image is third to the pure and holy spirit; and it is second to the vital soul, and fourth to the soul. And as for the manner of the manifestation of its coming-to-be, he said, "At the hour that those spirits go out from their place," etc. He means that the manifestation of the soul is like the craftsman who refines the silver, and in his will is to portray a form, and he melts the silver.

And behold, to portray the form of the matter that he wishes, he must first portray the place in which that form will be portrayed; and the refined silver, prepared for the form, is moulded within the hollow of that form that portrays it. And behold, the souls are spiritual, whether the part of the spirit, or the part of the vital soul, or the part of the soul. And behold, since by means of the coupling the effluence fitting for these parts is arranged, a fourth aspect is needed, in which they are moulded to the form of a man, portrayed in the air of the Garden. And behold, it is the manifestation of the mould of the air in which the form of the aforementioned parts was portrayed; and therefore it is third to the spirit and fourth to the soul and second to the vital soul. And that is because the vital soul is portrayed in the mould of the image, and the spirit is portrayed by means of the vital soul, and the soul by means of the spirit. And of this portraying is what he said: "is arranged before the holy King," etc., "in the visage in which it stands," etc., "and from that likeness, that precious tikkun, this image goes out." For from the manifestation of the moulding of the aforementioned parts in their mould is the image. And therefore, when a man couples with his wife, this image goes before, so that by its means the child be moulded like the mould of the form of the visage, as we explained at the head of the saying:

Behold, this is the essence of the image. And it is called shadow [tzel] because it shades over the head of a man, as he goes on to explain. However, just as it precedes the formation, so it departs before the death, thirty days. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Va-yechi (fol. 217b), and these are his words: "Rabbi Yose said: When the days of that man draw near, thirty days they proclaim concerning him in the world, etc. And if he is righteous, thirty days they proclaim concerning him among the righteous in the Garden of Eden. It has been taught: all those thirty days his soul goes out of him every night, and rises and sees its place in that world; and that man does not know, and does not notice, and does not rule over his soul all those thirty days as he did at first; as it is written, 'There is no man that has power over the spirit to retain the spirit,' etc. (Eccl. 8:8). Rabbi Judah said: From when those thirty days begin, the image of a man is darkened, and the likeness that is seen on the earth is withheld." Thus far his words.

And he lengthened further on the matter there. And likewise he explained in another place in this parashah (fol. 227a), and these are his words: "Rabbi Chizkiyah opened: 'And it came to pass, when the sun was going down, that a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and lo, a dread, a great darkness, fell upon him' (Gen. 15:12), etc. This is the day of harsh judgment, when they bring a man out of this world. For it has been taught: that day on which a man goes out of the world, that day of great judgment, when the sun is darkened from the moon, etc.: this is the holy soul, which is withheld from a man thirty days before he goes out of the world; and he sees that the image is withheld from him and is not seen. What is the reason that it is withheld from him? Because the holy soul rises and passes from him and is not seen. For do not say that when a man dies and is weakened this soul passes from him; rather, when he is in his life, in his strength, the soul passes from him and does not shine to the spirit, and the spirit does not shine to the vital soul; then the image passes from him and does not shine for him. From that day all proclaim concerning him, even the birds of the heavens. What is the reason? Because the soul rises from him, and the spirit does not shine to the vital soul; then the vital soul is weakened, and food and every craving of the body rise from him and pass away." Thus far his words.

And from it also it is explained that the departure of the image, with the other parts, is thirty days before the passing. And the words of the Zohar (in this parashah, fol. 220a) are not so; rather, that on the night of Hoshana [Rabbah] the image departs. And these are his words: "Come and see: when judgment is aroused in the world, when the Holy One, blessed be He, sits on the throne of judgment to judge the world, a man must arouse repentance, that he return from his sins. For on that day writs are written, and all of them are found in Achmetha (Ezra 6:2); behold, they are written. If a man merits to return before his Master, they tear up the writs that are upon him. Afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares before a man the Day of Atonement, the day of repentance. If he returns from his sins, good; and if not, the King commands to seal the writs. Woe to him, for repentance seeks to depart from him. If he merits in repentance, but not complete as is fitting, they hang it for him until the last day of the Assembly, which is the eighth of the festival. And if he does complete repentance before his Master, the writs are torn up. And if he does not merit, those writs go out from the King's house and are delivered into the hands of the officer, and judgment is done, and the writs do not return any more to the King. Then the images pass from him and are not found with him. And since they pass from him, behold, certainly the King's sentence will pass upon him, and he will taste the cup of death. And on that night of the last festival the officers are ready and the writs are taken. After they have taken them, the images pass and are not found. And if a lack is found in them, either judgment passes upon him or evil sicknesses, in the measure of their lack. And behold, we have established this." Thus far his words.

And from it it is explained explicitly that the departure of the image is on the night of Hoshana [Rabbah]; and the deeds of every day [bear it out], etc. And it seems fitting to say that they certainly depart on the night of the sealing, as he explains here and in other places besides it. But the matter of this departure is only for its hour, to show a man the matters of the sealing; but afterward the shadow returns over his head, until near his death, thirty days, and then it departs and does not return again. And it is explained in the Zohar that from this image there comes into being yet another image, and the two of them are united. And these are his words, in the parashah (Va-yechi, fol. 220a): "Come and see: this holy image, when a man goes and grows up and his likeness is made from this visage, another image is made, and they are joined as one, and this one takes that one. At the hour that two images are found, that man is guarded, and his body is in guarding, and the spirit dwells within him. At the hour that his days draw near, they pass from him, and this one rises to that one, and the man remains without guarding. Then it is written, 'Until the day breathe, and the shadows flee away' (Song 2:17): two." And behold, from this saying it is explained that an image is made for the image:

It is found that the totality of a man in this world in his form is seven powers: three of them vital soul, spirit, soul; two of them the evil inclination and the good inclination, which are the aforementioned angels, and according to the opinion of Rabbi Pinchas they are three; and further, two shadows. Their total is seven, or eight according to the opinion of Rabbi Pinchas. And it is possible that Rabbi Pinchas does not disagree with Rabbi Simeon; and because of this Rabbi Simeon says there, "He has said well"; and not because Rashbi, peace be upon him, retracts what he said, two; but because they are two and they are three. For the left angel, which is the evil inclination, is turned into two hues: the one accuser, and sometimes it is advocate; and it is found that in it is the inclusion of two powers, and it is judged as two. And behold, it is found that the words of Rashbi and the words of Rabbi Pinchas, peace be upon them, are both right; for they are two and they are three, and all is one, as we explained. And after the manifestation of the form of a man in its general aspects and its particulars has been concluded in the preceding chapters, we shall come now to explain the benefit of its being in the lowly world, even though its dwelling is in the heights:

On the explanation of the benefit of the soul in this world. And the matter is that the principal of the soul is after its ascent from the world of deeds to the world of reward. For before its descent it is very lacking, even though it is in a high place, in the height of the world. And the matter is: the soul has no manifestation before the upper begetting; and even after the begetting it is as if naked. And after its descent it is clothed in the lower Garden of Eden in a pure garment from the air of the Garden of Eden; and likewise, by all the way of the rungs by which it will rise, then it descends and is clothed. And when it occupies itself in this world with the deed of the Torah, then it merits a beautiful garment, which is called the robe of the Rabbis [chaluka de-rabbanan]; and it is the garment of the Torah and the commandments with which it occupied itself in this world. And in this garment it merits to rise and to see the face of the King, YHVH of hosts, its Father. For before its coming into this world it was naked; and in its going out from this world it does not come to the King until it is clothed in the garments of the Torah and the commandments. Because the garment of the air of the Garden of Eden is a simple garment, pressed, without adornments; and it needs that "fine linen and purple be its clothing" (Prov. 31:22), the garments of adornments, which are the spirituality of the commandments; and they are subtle, spiritual; in them it is offered upon the altar by means of [Michael] the high priest. And the matters of these garments Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar, Parashat Va-yakhel (fol. 210a), and these are his words: "Then these two chariots enter within the concealed palace of the Garden, which is called Ahalot [aloes]; and there twelve kinds of spices are stored away, as it is written (Song 4:14), 'Nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon,' etc.; and they are the twelve kinds of spices that are below. And there are all those garments of the souls that are fit to be clothed in them, each and every one as is fit for it. In that garment are marked all those good deeds that he did in this world; and all of them are marked in it; and they proclaim: This is the garment of so-and-so. And they take that garment, and that soul of the righteous that is in the Garden is clothed in it, in the likeness of the likeness of this world," etc. "Happy is the portion of the one who merits these garments of which we have spoken, in which the righteous are clothed in the Garden of Eden. These are from the good deeds that a man does in this world, in the commandments of the Torah; and by them the soul stands in the Garden of Eden and is clothed in these precious garments. When the soul rises through that gate of the firmament above, other precious, upper garments are made ready for it, which are from the desire [re'uta] and the intention of the heart in Torah and in prayer. For when that desire rises above, the one who is crowned is crowned with it; and a portion remains for that man, and garments of light are made from it, in which the soul is clothed to rise above. And even though they have established that those garments depend on deeds, these depend only on the desire of the spirit, as has been said, to stand among the angels, holy spirits. And this is the clarity of the matter; and the holy Lamp learned so from Elijah: the garments below, in the Garden of the earth, by deeds; the garments above, by the spirit and the desire and the intention of the heart." Thus far his words.

And we wish to explain this matter in a way from which this saying will be explained. It is known that the manifestation of the soul and the vital soul and the spirit, at the time of their cleaving in their root before their emanation, are not bounded in the manifestation of being; but their being is from the side of their spreading and their bestowal in the female; after the way of light, water, firmament, which we explained in the Gate of Letters, chapter 27. That is to say, that it has no being at all; but like the way of the seed, which comes into being from the side of the subtle power that spreads from the brain; for there there is no manifestation of seed, but like the likeness of light, that is to say, a power fit for seed to come into being from it, until its bestowal into the place of ripening; and on the way of its descent it comes into being as blood; and in the place of ripening it is ripened and turned into the seed; and when it is in the full womb, that form comes into being from it. And likewise the way of the soul: for in Binah it is like the likeness of light; and likewise the effluence fitting for the spirit in Tiferet, and the effluence fitting for the vital soul in Malkhut; and by means of the union that effluence comes into being as the form of soul and spirit and vital soul. And the matter of the union is explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And by means of the holy and pure coupling it comes into being from no form to the manifestation of the form:

And now, with this introduction, the matter of the benefit of the soul in the manifestation of its bestowal from the roots will not be difficult in our eyes; because by this it comes into being in the form of a soul [and goes out from potential to actual; see Asis Rimmonim]. For the souls are sons to YHVH, and the father and the mother are Tiferet and Malkhut. And just as the question does not fall upon the manifestation of the son, on his coming-to-be from the power of the father and the mother, in his going out into the air of the world, because of his previous nonexistence, so the question does not fall in the matter of the soul; for this is like that; and from the corporeal we understand the spiritual, for the way is the same for both of them. And what remains now to doubt about this: this is well in the matter of the manifestation of their emanation and their coming-to-be from the roots until their emanation to the upper Garden; for there they go out to the manifestation of the soul. But their coming from the Garden of delights to the reproaches of this world, why? For it is better for them to be there than their manifestation in this world; for in this world they are near to loss and far from reward; for all the good with which YHVH does good to them is their ascent to the place from which they were hewn.

And behold, the souls did not gain by this at all; for before their descent they had this matter; and now, in their nearness to the turbid matter, in any case it is blemished; for "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not" (Eccl. 7:20).

And behold, this question will be explained by means of this saying that we have written: for when it is above, before its descent to the manifestation of this world, the world of Asiyah, it sits naked without any garment at all, and it does not appear before the King its Father at all until its descent into this world; and then it merits the coat of many colours: behold, these are the robes of the Rabbis that we explained above in the saying of the Zohar. And it is said of these vessels (2 Sam. 13:18), "for with such robes [me'ilim] were the king's daughters that were virgins apparelled": profitable [mo'ilim] for appearing before the King. And apart from this it needs two kinds of garments, a garment for the lower Garden of Eden and a garment for the upper Garden of Eden, because of its two manifestations in spirit and soul. The subtle manifestation that is in the upper Garden of Eden is the soul; and the manifestation that is in the lower Garden of Eden is the spirit, as is explained above. And therefore it needs two garments, one for the lower Garden of Eden and one for the upper Garden of Eden.
And we shall further "add learning" (Prov. 9:9) on the matter of these garments, with the help of Heaven:

We have already explained in the Gate of Letters the matter of the spirituality of the letters and their mention and their ascent and their union in their root. And therefore, in prayer, when a man prays without intention of the heart, the prayer is found to be like a deed without thought; and therefore, when it wishes to rise, it has no ability to rise from the lower Garden of Eden and above; because the cessation of the deed is there; and from there and above it must strip itself of the body and the corporeality, which is the deed, and rise in a spiritual being, which is the thought; and the intention is the soul of the deed. And therefore that prayer is pushed away from the Garden of Eden above, and it has no place to rise there. And there is prayer that rises somewhat to the Garden of Eden too, but does not merit to enter into the inner rungs. And we are found to say also in the matter of the soul: that according to its deeds so it rises. If its deeds are spiritual, subtle with the subtlety of the upper rung, certainly it will rise according to the measure of its garments, rung after rung, until the ending of those garments, when its merit has not reached to rise from there and above, because of his intention. And with this will be understood what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Palaces on the matter of prayer: that even though they received it in the first palace, they still examine it in the second palace. And it is difficult: since they judged it in the first palace and acquitted it in its judgment, and it merited to rise, why do they not receive it in the second palace, and likewise in the other palaces, and it would not need these judgments?

And further, sometimes they push it away in this palace after they received it in the preceding one, because they found it guilty from the side of judgment. And can we say that, God forbid, they perverted judgment in the preceding palace? This certainly not. But certainly as we have said: that even though it is fit in matters according to the measure of the subtlety of this palace, they still need to judge it in the second palace, lest it has not merited, in the matters of its actions, the spirituality of the second palace; and in this way for all the rungs. And with this introduction will be understood the seven reckonings that they reckon for a man from the time of his passing until the resurrection, as we explained in the Zohar (Va-yakhel, fol. 199b). And likewise with this will be explained the matter of the great Day of Judgment: why, after they have already judged them and rewarded them with the Garden of Eden, do they still need judgment and reckoning? And the matter is, to see whether they have power in subtlety to merit the true world to come, which is after the resurrection. And likewise there will be explained with this what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Menachot 29b) concerning Moses our teacher, peace be upon him: at the hour that he went up on high, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, sitting and binding crowns to the letters, etc. "And Akiva ben Joseph is his name, who is destined to expound on each and every thorn," etc. "He said before Him: Master of the world, show him to me," etc. "He said before Him: Master of the world, You have shown me his Torah; show me his reward," etc. "He saw that they were weighing his flesh in the meat-market," etc. "He said to him: Be silent; so it rose in thought before Me." And it is very difficult: did Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, ask about his death or his punishment, that they showed him that they were weighing his flesh? The Holy One, blessed be He, should have shown him his reward; and what business have we with his death, by what it would be? For this answer is not of the kind of his question. And the matter is that the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous as a hair's thread; because according to the measure of his good deeds, so his soul rises in the steps of the ladder. And even though he sinned the smallest sin in the world, if that small blemish prevents him from meriting the great and mighty rung where the might of the subtlety of his deeds is, behold, if they do not punish him and purify him of it, he loses a great loss; for he loses his good deeds and the merit of their spirituality, which rise higher and higher by way of the steps of the ladder, because of that sin; and this is not fitting. And therefore "YHVH was pleased, for His righteousness' sake" (Isa. 42:21), "and was pleased to crush him by disease" (Isa. 53:10), to acquit him and to cleanse him, to enter that rung, the rung of his deeds.
