And therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous. And this is the excellence of Rabbi Akiva: for his right deeds reached up to the upper Thought; and it was necessary that his punishment be great for an iniquity as fine as a hair's thread; for according to the excellence of the place to which the soul withdraws, so great is the sin and the punishment. And therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, that they were weighing his flesh: so that from this he would recognise the might of the excellence of his soul; that even though he was a completely righteous man, and the greatness of his Torah, by means of this he needed a great tikkun, to raise his soul to the excellence of his deeds, which prevailed upward to the head. And with all this Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, wondered a wonder, in saying, "This is Torah and this its reward?"; for it appeared in his eyes a great punishment. And He answered him, "Be silent; so it rose in thought": the explanation, that so Rabbi Akiva rose in the rungs of his good deeds to the rung of the Thought; and to rise above without any blemish he needed this punishment:

And let us return to our matter: that in the ascent of the prayer by way of the rungs, according to the measure of the rung of the cleaving and the intention that belong to the one who prays, or to the one occupied with that commandment, so it rises in its steps. For the deed does not rise from the lower Garden of Eden and above; for there is the standing of the excellence of the body; and from it and above the power of the excellence of the body is weakened and cut off, and it is not fit to rise; only the soul of the prayer, which is the intention and the spirituality. And likewise is the law for the commandments; for the intention of the prayer and the commandment is their soul, as they said, "Prayer without intention is like a body without a soul." And with all this, not all the souls are equal, just as not all the intentions are equal; according to the measure of the intention will be the greatness of the soul. And this is what he said in the saying [of the Zohar] before us: "other precious, upper garments are made ready for it, which are from the desire and the intention of the heart in Torah and in prayer; for when it rises," etc., "is crowned," etc. The explanation: when the prayer rises crowned with those known matters with which it is crowned, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces. "And a portion remains," etc.: the explanation, it is known that the principal of prayer is to draw blessings and effluence to the world; and he said that even though the prayer is a benefit for the whole world, with all this, of that effluence and light that descends by means of the prayer, his portion remains there, so that that light make for him a garment for his soul at the time of its ascent to its place. And with this introduction the matters of the garments will be understood. For the intention is not that the commandments make him a garment; for this matter the mind does not encompass. However, the intention is that that one who prays, or who fulfils that commandment, when he merits to raise his commandment or his prayer by way of the upper steps, and the palaces receive it, and from there Malkhut receives it, then by its power she arouses the male, and he bestows in her from the upper rungs; and behold, by his merit much effluence and blessing is bestowed upon her. And of that light that is bestowed they give him too his portion, and it is made for him a garment; and these are the robes of the Rabbis. And these are the commandments that stand before the King of the world to plead merit for him, and say, "I am from so-and-so, who made me," as we explained in the Zohar (Kedoshim, fol. 83b). And according to the power of his bestowal by means of his prayer, so he will merit to light in the light of his garment.

And behold, with this it is found that the garments too are from an upper light, the light of the sefirot; except that there is a great difference between them: that the soul comes into being by means of the union and the coupling, "according to the space of each, with wreaths" (1 Kgs. 7:36), after the way of the joining of husband and wife; however, the garments are from the matter of the union of Malkhut with Tiferet, as she receives much effluence, great goodness and great light. And with these introductions this saying will be well understood. And the rest of the language does not need explanation, for it is clear of itself (see Asis Rimmonim):

After we had written all that is "inscribed in the writing of truth" (Dan. 10:21), we found a saying that "stirs up to help" (cf. Ps. 35:23) from Parashat Pekudei (fol. 229b), and these are his words: "Come and see: the soul does not rise to appear before the holy King until it merits to be clothed in a garment [from above, to appear there. And likewise, in the same way, it does not descend below until it is clothed in the garment of this world. In the same way, the holy angels above, etc., do not descend below until they are clothed in the garment] of this world. And all is according to the likeness of that place to which it goes. And behold, we have established that the soul does not rise except in that garment which shines. And come and see: the first Adam, when he was in the Garden of Eden, was clothed in a garment like that of above; and it is a garment of upper light. When he was driven out of the Garden of Eden and needed the hues of this world, what is written? 'And YHVH Elohim made for Adam and for his wife coats of skin [or], and clothed them' (Gen. 3:21). At first they were coats of light [or], the light of that upper light in which he served in the Garden of Eden. For behold, the Garden of Eden: the upper light that shines serves in it. And therefore the first Adam, when he entered within the Garden, the Holy One, blessed be He, clothed him in the garment of that light and brought him in there; and if he had not been clothed at first in that light, he would not enter there. Once he was driven out from there, he needed another garment; then, 'And YHVH Elohim made,' etc. And all as was needed. And here likewise: 'they made the plaited garments, to minister in the holy place' (Exod. 39:1), to enter the holy place. And behold, they have established that the good deeds of a man, which he does in this world, those deeds draw from the light of the upper radiance a garment, to be arranged in it for that world, to appear before the holy King. And in that garment in which he is clothed he has enjoyment and sees within the mirror that shines, as it is said, 'to behold the pleasantness of YHVH, and to visit in His palace' (Ps. 27:4). And therefore the soul is clothed in two worlds, to have perfection in all, in this world below and in the world above. And of this it is written (Ps. 140:14), 'Surely the righteous shall give thanks to Your name': in this world; 'the upright shall dwell in Your presence': in that world." Thus far his words.

And behold, from this saying all the parts of the inquiry in which we are are explained, a complete explanation. First, in what he said, "the soul does not rise," etc.: and behold, since the soul is naked until it rises from this world in its honoured garments, and they are the garments of the deeds, as we explained with the help of Heaven; and this is what he said, "in a garment from above": the explanation, the garment that is made by means of the commandments that are done in this world; and it is impossible to attain them until it comes to be clothed in this world, which is the world of the fulfilment of the commandments and of the deed. He further explained that a man is clothed from the upper light that he draws upon himself by means of the deeds, as we explained in the previous chapter; and this is what he said, "those deeds draw from the light," etc.; and as we explained above, that by means of his prayer and his commandments the sefirot are united and bestow great light, and they receive one from another; and of that light a portion is kept for him, until his ascent, to be clothed in it. And now, with this introduction, the matter of the creation of the first Adam will be understood: for his service was in contemplation and in intention and in study and in the understanding of the hidden things of the secrets of the upper commandments alone; for the reason that he did not need the garment of the world of deeds, that is, the garment of the Garden of Eden below, as is explained in the previous chapter.

And this matter is necessary; and to it our Sages, of blessed memory, intended (in the Zohar, Bereshit, fol. 27, and in Tikkun 21, fols. 61 and 85): "to work it and to keep it" (Gen. 2:15): "to work it," these are the positive commandments; "and to keep it," these are the negative commandments. And it is fitting to investigate: did Adam need to plough in the Garden of Eden, so that he was commanded, "You shall not plough with an ox and an ass together" (Deut. 22:10), etc.? And was it not after his expulsion from the Garden of Eden that it was said to him, "In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread" (Gen. 3:19)? And from this we may infer to the rest: gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and the corner, and the poor man's tithe; for if there is no ploughing and harvest, gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and the corner, whence would they come?

And further, the poor man, the stranger, the orphan and the widow: how do they belong there? And lengthening on this is without need. However, the intention is to the contemplative commandments, that is to say, the understanding of their spirituality. "You shall not plough with an ox and an ass together": the explanation, you shall not unite these two husks together; and this, by his being drawn after them, he gives them power to be united, God forbid. And likewise the matter of wrapping in the fringes [tzitzit]: the explanation, that he bestow light on Malkhut and adorn her with those adornments, which are four fringes, four corners, etc., as is expounded in the Zohar; that they are the inwardness of the Torah. And this was the principal of his service; and he had no part at all there in deeds. But when he was driven out from the Garden of Eden, his book of remedies was driven out with him. And just as the soul was clothed in a bodily garment, so the Torah was clothed in a bodily garment. And at his return to its inwardness, when he will strip off the bodily garments, the Torah too will strip off its garments; and its general rules and its particulars and its fine points and the orders of its Mishnayot will be understood in their inwardness. And this is the occupation of the righteous in the Garden of Eden.

And the matter of the negative commandments is to save him, that he not be drawn after the husk that surrounds the Garden, as is explained in the Gate of Palaces. And would that the one who has understanding go deep into these things, and understand the excellence of the one who occupies himself with the inwardness in this world; for he has done in this world the commandments of the world to come. And what we have to ask in this is: since our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat 146a) that as soon as Israel stood at Mount Sinai their filth ceased, if so, why did He not bring them then into the lower Garden of Eden? And why did they still need the settlement of this world, and the Land of Israel, and the other things? And the Name has enlightened our eyes in this exalted inquiry that we have explained concerning the matter of the garments. For after Adam was driven out of Eden he lost his garment and remained naked, as it is written (Gen. 3:7), "and they knew that they were naked"; for the light departed from them, and their spirits remained naked without a garment, until the Holy One, blessed be He, clothed them in coats of skin and the air of this world. And he stood in this world a time, until, out of the deed and the fulfilment of the commandments, he was clothed in the Garden of Eden, as we explained. And therefore, even though when Israel stood at Mount Sinai their filth ceased, it is true that they refined their matter much; but with all this, had they entered the Garden of Eden they would have stood naked without a garment, because they had not yet fulfilled the commandments; and without the fulfilment of the commandments they have nothing in which to be clothed, as we explained. And to say that they would enter there in this garment in which they are clothed in this world, though their matter was refined: far be it to say so. And this thing is for a sign (and toil) [and symbol]: that one must not think that when a man is pure with the utmost purity he can therefore enter in his turbid matter into the Garden of Eden in his life, unless he strips off that garment, and it ends of itself, and he puts on the garments that are of the kind of that world, as we explained in the saying at the head of our chapter. For even Elijah: his ascent among the angels is not in the bodily garment in which he is clothed when he is in this world, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces. And likewise Rabbi Joshua ben Levi and his companions (in Tractate Ketubbot, fol. 77b), who live in the Garden of Eden: for they too are clothed in the garment of the Garden, and the turbid body ended of itself, and they remained clothed in the garment of their right deeds. And a great proof: for behold, he met Rashbi, peace be upon him, there; and would it enter the mind that a bridegroom would stand among the groomsmen, and a groomsman among the bridegrooms, in a foreign garment, God forbid? But certainly, he as they, all of them equal for good, clothed in the garment of their good deeds. And if you say: if so, what is the matter of their excellence, in our saying that they live in the Garden of Eden, since one happening is to them and to the righteous who are in the Garden? To this we answer that their excellence is very great. For the one who tastes the taste of death cleaves to the portion of death; and the husks, which are death, rule over him, like the matter of their rule over the whole world; "and dust he is, and to dust he shall return" (cf. Gen. 3:19), and dust wears away his body; and even if he be righteous, he will not merit to be clothed in the Eden of the Garden until his body ends; for so it is explained in the Zohar (Terumah, fol. 151a). And now certainly great is the excellence of the righteous man who did not taste the taste of death; and his body ended and was burned by the power of the pure and holy air, and he is clothed there in his garment without the taste of death; for there is no husk there, God forbid. And there is no wonder at the death of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and the death of the other righteous mentioned in the Torah; for that death is not death but being stored away, each one according to his measure. And there is no need to lengthen further.
And behold, it remains for us to explain a short matter in this part; and we shall explain it in a chapter by itself; and it is the matter of the garments of the righteous:

What is intended in this chapter is to explain this matter which is found in the Zohar, Parashat Emor (fol. 101a), and these are his words: "As we have learned, the good deeds that a man does in this world make for him in that world a precious, upper garment, to be clothed in them. And when a man prepares good deeds, and evil deeds prevail over him, and the Holy One, blessed be He, looks at him and his evil deeds are many, and he is a wicked man, found a sinner before his Master, and he regrets those good things that he did at first, behold, he is lost from all, from this world and from the world to come. What does the Holy One, blessed be He, do with those good things that this sinner did at first? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He: even though that wicked sinner is lost, those good things and merits are not lost. There is a righteous man who goes in the way of the upper King and prepares his garments from his deeds, [and before he completed his garments he departed]. The Holy One, blessed be He, completes it for him from those deeds that that wicked sinner did, and completes his garments, to be arranged in them in that world. This is what is written, 'he may prepare it, but the righteous shall put it on' (Job 27:17). That sinner prepared, and this righteous one is covered with what he prepared. This is what is written, 'the covering of the sinner,'" etc. Thus far his words.

And the intention of the saying itself is clear. And the intention is to explain the meaning of the verse, "the covering of the sinner", whose explanation is that there is a righteous man who wears the covering of the sinner. How so? Behold, one man did some commandments, and regrets them; he loses them, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Kiddushin 40b) on the verse, "The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him," etc. (Ezek. 33:12); and Resh Lakish said: when he regrets the former ones. And Rashbi said that those commandments that he did are not lost entirely. For granted that he, in his regretting, lost them; but they in themselves are not lost. But the Holy One, blessed be He, gives them to a righteous man who departed in his youth and did not fulfil all that was needed, and completes his garment by means of the action of that wicked man who regretted. This is the sum of the saying. And it is very difficult for me: how many regretters will there be, so that the righteous merit those garments? Shall it be said that the righteous who wear them are as the number of the regretters, equal to equal? And never has a righteous man died who needed this without there being opposite him a wicked man regretting his commandments, so that the righteous man may wear them?

And further, if two righteous men die and need two garments, and only one regretter is found, shall it be said that they cast lots for that garment, to whom it will fall by lot? Or "together they shall eat portion for portion" (cf. Deut. 18:8)?

And further, "Will God rob a man?" (inverting Mal. 3:8). Granted that that wicked man, by his evil inclination, regrets his righteous deeds that he did. But the pure, poor soul, which merited some of that garment: why, after it receives its punishment, should they strip it naked, as on the day it was born? For this is not the line of judgment. For such is the way of the souls: this one completes some, and that one completes some, until the soul of one man is completed in bodies. And this was the cause of the reincarnation, "that he that is banished be not an outcast from him" (2 Sam. 14:14). And this oppressed soul tasted the bitterness and the filth of that sinner, and saw no good; for "all his righteous deeds shall not be remembered" (Ezek. 33:13), and its strength and its labour are spent in vain. This is certainly outside the line of judgment:

Therefore we say that this matter is understood with the introduction of the secret of reincarnation, for one who has merited its secret. And it is known that the soul is completed by means of many bodies; and in those bodies a soul sparkles, like one who lights a lamp from a lamp, from the principal soul; and those bodies "spend their days in good" (Job 21:13) and inherit their world, which they merited in their lives.

Behold, the owner of the principal soul does not taste of its perfections or of its commandments which it did (before its coming into its body, or) after its going out from its body, if it comes into another body. For even though, from the side of its reincarnation, much benefit is drawn to it, with all this the reward of the commandments: none receives their reward except the one who did them. The example of this: if the soul of Reuben is reincarnated in the body of Judah, Reuben does not receive the reward of the commandments that Judah did, nor Judah the reward of the commandments that Reuben did; even though their soul is one, and spreads into two sparks. And even though much benefit is drawn to them, to each one from his fellow, because by means of the two of them the soul is completed, and both of them are found to merit souls complete, clean and pure; and of them it is said (Dan. 12:13), "But go you your way till the end be; and you shall rest, and shall stand," etc.; with all this, the principal of the commandments: each and every one shall eat portion for portion of his deeds, whether little or much. And after we have included the much in the little in this introduction, we say that the attribute of judgment has no power to destroy the soul of the regretter. For even though he was a regretter, with all this, against his will, the soul was completed by his good deeds which he did; and the smitten body, the regretter, is consumed in the dust and lost and cut off entirely. However, that soul is reincarnated; and when the poor soul is afterward in a second body, a righteous one, the Holy One, blessed be He, in His wisdom, shortens his years, so that he too not be thrust away from the land of the living, like the first body, the regretter, who was thrust away. And the second body, the righteous one, even though he did not do the good deeds and the commandments for his garment, the Holy One, blessed be He, completes his garment with the commandments that he did in the first body, the regretter; and by right he wears them, for they are his own: "he may prepare it, but the righteous shall put it on." For he was righteous and loved righteous deeds, and his years were cut short, and he saw no good, and tasted only "a little of that honeycomb" (cf. 1 Sam. 14:29). And in the nature of the matter, the righteous deeds that the first body regretted, he wears them; for behold, his soul merited this garment before its coming here; and all the more now, when he is righteous, except that he died in shortness of years; for then certainly "his rest shall be glorious" (Isa. 11:10).

And behold, in this chapter we have included the much in the little; and behold, one part of this gate is completed. And now we shall come to explain the joining of the soul in the smitten body, even though it is a subtle being, more spiritual than the ministering angels:

It is well known that according to the preparation of the lower things, so is the longing of the upper ones to cleave to them. And a great proof is from the making of the Tabernacle: because its limbs [one], their totality and their particulars, hint at the upper matters, I mean at the upper chariots, therefore those worlds and chariots were drawn and bestowed into those lifeless forms. And though they were dead forms, from the side of the hint of their action the upper life was drawn upon them; and therefore the Shekhinah dwelt in them, "and the glory of YHVH filled the Tabernacle" (Exod. 40:34). And likewise the matter: because the body resembles the spiritual, therefore it was necessary that, even though the thing be spiritual, it cleave to the corporeal because of its great yearning for it. And the reason is because the lower ones are a dwelling for the upper ones; and just as the longing of the caused is to rise to its cause, so the longing of the cause is that its caused be near to it; and as the longing of the effect for its cause, so the longing of the cause that its effect draw near to it. And these things are necessary of themselves; for by this is the bond of the worlds, since they are a candelabrum of joints. And if, God forbid, the delight of the cause were to rise and of the caused to descend, there would be no standing in the world for the manifestation of the beings, and the union and the bond would be broken into pieces. And to such a matter it is said in the Torah, "You shall be holy, for I am holy" (Lev. 19:2). And this is one of the reasons that the Ein Sof is united with His attributes, apart from what we wrote in the Gate of Self and Vessels.

And behold, according to these things the bond of the spiritual with the corporeal will not be far from us. And all the more, since the rungs in all matters are linked down in a chain from Atzilut to Beriah, and from Beriah to Yetzirah, and from Yetzirah to Asiyah; and all is bound with a firm bond. And likewise the matter in the soul: for it is linked down from cause to effect by means of the aforementioned rungs, as is explained in the explanation. "And how much more so" (cf. Mishnah Avot), a double good: for just as we have hinted in this gate and in the preceding gates concerning the soul, so the body, which is its chariot, which the Holy One, blessed be He, created for it, resembles it in all its matters:

And now we shall explain a little of the hint concerning the pattern of the body. It has already been explained that the whole of Atzilut is included in Chesed, Judgment and Compassion; and the hint to the three of them is Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. And to each one of these there are seventy-two branches, as we explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names; and their totality is two hundred and sixteen. And when we include with them the root of the seventy-two, which are the thirty-two paths that are in Chokhmah, it comes up to the number two hundred and forty-eight. And they are the two hundred and forty-eight limbs that are in a man; two hundred and forty-eight upper powers, which are the two hundred and forty-eight positive commandments, luminaries from the side of Chesed.

And further, there are in a man three hundred and sixty-five sinews, over against three hundred and sixty-five luminaries that are in Gevurah, over against which He gave us three hundred and sixty-five negative commandments. And their total is six hundred and thirteen; and they are the six hundred and thirteen commandments that depend on the name YHVH "like grapes in a cluster," as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. This is the totality of his limbs; and their particulars are many.

And behold, in his head the three first ones are hinted. How so? The membrane of the brain, and the bone that covers it, and the skin that is over it, are a hint to Keter Elyon. And therefore there are hairs on it, to hint at its upper root; and they are worlds and channels that spread out from the power of the Ein Sof that is concealed within it. And to show its excellence and its power, each one of the hairs of the head has a pit by itself and a sucking by itself, to show the might and strength of the upper bestowal, from which all the emanated beings draw effluence from the Source of sources, which is the Ein Sof, before whom there is no narrowness of eye at all. And therefore each and every one has a channel by itself, and does not need its fellow; for there is no poverty in a place of wealth. Which is not so with the other hairs of the body. And it is known that each and every hair is a world by itself, and has a concealed root that is united in its cause; like the hair, which, the more it enters into its source within the skin, draws near to the manifestation of the nature of the flesh. And the brain beneath the membrane is divided into three brains, to show three manifestations in Chokhmah; and they are wisdom, understanding and knowledge, as we explained in the preceding gates. And likewise the bone that covers the brain is hollowed with many hollows and many chambers, to show concealed worlds, like the matter of the six hundred and twenty pillars of light that are in Keter, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And likewise there hang from the brain the senses, and they are: Y, sight;  Y H, hearing;  Y H V, smell;  Y H V H, speech; as is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, fol. 116a). And the sages of anatomy said that thirty-two paths are drawn from the brain to the body, to hint at the thirty-two paths that are in Chokhmah, as we explained in the Gate of Paths. And likewise thirty-two sources are bestowed from the head to the thirty-two teeth that a man has in the mouth, to hint at the thirty-two paths; and thirty-two over against thirty-two. And the thirty-two teeth are divided in a spiritual form: four upper front teeth and four lower ones, and two upper canines and two lower ones; these are twelve. And five molars on the right side and five on the left side; these are ten above, in the upper jaws; and over against them, in the lower ones, ten. And they come to hint at a great matter: for they are five on this side and five on that side, and six in the middle, between canines and teeth; behold, two Hehs and Vav in the middle, to show the four-letter name; and the Yod is the brain over all, from which all the thirty-two are bestowed. And they are the secret of  H V H  above, in the upper teeth, and  H V H  below, in the lower teeth; that is, male and female, "seven and seven pipes" (Zech. 4:2), like this:  H V H  Y,  H V H. And they are the seven branches of the upper candelabrum, in the secret of the one who bestows, and the secret of the seven branches of the lower candelabrum, which receives; and they are Tiferet and Malkhut. And the spirit [ruach] that is between them is the middle line that unites them, which goes out in the power of speech. And with this will be understood the reason that "the remnant of Israel shall not speak lies" (Zeph. 3:13), and also the reason that the punishment for lying is very great: for the source of living waters is turned for him into a lying [akhzav] brook.

And further, the mouth hints at Binah, and the palate at Chokhmah. And because there is no attainment in Chokhmah, therefore the palate is devoid of any taste in the world; for it has no taste at all.
And further, in the windpipe there are six rings, to hint at the six sefirot that are in the middle line.

And further, the face has in it two apples, like the upper apples that are bestowed by means of Malkhut, which is called the field of apples; and their colour is red and white, in the secret of "My beloved is white and ruddy" (Song 5:10). And the beard is the beard of Aaron. And two eyes, which hint at two Yods; and the nose, a Vav in the middle, in the secret of the Alef, which we explained in the preceding gates. And the two nostrils, to hint at two bestowals that are bestowed from Tiferet: the right, Chesed, and the left, Gevurah. And they hint also at the two Hehs, each one of which is three Vavs, which are three Patriarchs. And the pupil, to hint at the Yod that is within the Heh. And the white that is in it hints at the manifestation of Malkhut, Yod, which is called sea. And seven coats of the eye (as the sages of anatomy also explained) are a hint to seven sefirot. The light that is in them hints at Keter. The inner pupil is Yod, with the joining of Binah, and its principal is in Chokhmah. Ten sefirot are found in the eye. And when we examine closely, there is found there the filling of Yods. Yod is the secret of the brain, which bestows the sense of sight; and sight is in Chokhmah; and the sight itself is Yod. And the two eyes are  H Y,  H Y: for the Yods are the inner pupil, and the three Vavs are three Patriarchs that are in the Heh, like this, ה. And the nose in the middle is the Vav between the Hehs; and it is Vav in its filling: two Vavs, the two sources of the nose; and the aspect that unites is Alef. And these matters have already been explained in the preceding gates. And the two cherubim [of the eyes, which are the eyebrows], which spread out wings, are Netzach and Hod; and the hairs that are in them hint at worlds spreading out. And from the power of judgment they are not large, for they are burned in their fire; for an eye, without qualification, is judgment; and that is "he set his eyes upon him," etc., and "every place where the sages set their eyes." And the sinew that surrounds the two cherubim, by whose means they are united, opening and closing, is the Foundation of the world, which is called sinew [gid]. And the manifestation of the eyes in general is hinted at Chokhmah and Binah; and the manifestation of the nose in general is hinted at Da'at, which mediates between the two of them. And the forehead that is over the three of them is the Forehead of the Will, Keter Elyon. And the beard, the beard of Aaron, is hinted in Chesed, to hint at the worlds drawn from Keter in the secret of the thirteen attributes of compassion that are in it; and they are the thirteen tikkunim of the beard, with the corners of the head, as is explained in the Idra.

And further, many lines in the face and in the forehead and in the other limbs, whose secret is concealed from us. And the neck is Binah; and of it it is said (Song 7:8), "This your stature is like to a palm tree"; and the stature of the body is hinted at her; and it is called קומ"ה [stature], מקו"ה [gathering] of waters. But the body is hinted in Tiferet in general. And the two arms, right and left, which are Gedulah and Gevurah. Because the totality of the three Patriarchs, which are three Vavs, comes to eighteen [chai], in the secret of Va-yisa, Va-yavo, Va-yet, therefore there are eighteen vertebrae in the spine. And the matter is that each one of the three Patriarchs is included of six extremities; and they are three times six, which are the aforementioned eighteen. And its drawing is from Chokhmah, in the secret of Da'at; and that is the white thread that is drawn from the brain; and its sheath is Tiferet itself, and Da'at is a soul to it, as is explained in the preceding gates.

And behold, the arms are drawn from the body; the four-letter name is hinted in them. How so? Heh in the shoulder, Vav in the arm, Yod the palm of the hand, Heh the five fingers; they are YHVH. And so Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim in many places. And it is difficult for us: for what reason is the Yod below, beside the last Heh? And if we say that the five fingers are the first Heh, in the end it is still difficult, for the Yod is below the Heh, or below the Vav, since it is between the Vav that is in the arm and the Heh that is in the fingers. Therefore it seems right to say that a hand, without qualification, is Malkhut; and the palm of the hand is the Yod that is in Malkhut, which is opened in Heh, which are five fingers. And the Yod that is in Chokhmah is the one held in the arm that spreads out in the shoulder, which is called in the vernacular pala.

And further, in the arm itself, in the manifestation of two bones beside the palm of the hand; and they are two twins; and they are the two Netzachs [Netzach and Hod] that bestow in Yesod, to water the Yod and Heh that are in Malkhut, that is, fourteen. And the upper bone is the manifestation of Tiferet, which bestows by their means to Yesod. And when a man folds his arm upward, the hand rises to the shoulder; that is, the ascent of Malkhut to Binah by means of the union of Tiferet, by means of Malkhut; and then she is a Zayin: Yod upon Vav, the palm of the hand upon a small Vav. And if they raise it upon her head, then it hints at her ascent in Keter; and then she is a great Zayin: Yod upon a great Vav; and she is "a woman of valour, the diadem of her husband" (Prov. 12:4). And like this for the two arms. And five fingers, the secret of the five bars of the Tabernacle; and the middle one "bars from end to end" (Exod. 26:28). And the total of ten fingers, ten sefirot. Fourteen joints in the fingers of the right and fourteen joints in the fingers of the left, to hint at the hands [yadot] that we explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names. And all this shows divisions and manifestations and aspects that are in each and every sefirah. And the entrails that spread within the body are an upper hint; and all the more, since a veil is a screen that divides between the holy place and the Holy of Holies, which is the heart. The heart is a hint to Binah; and it also hints at Tiferet, and also at Malkhut. And in the heart there are two hollows, which are the two Hehs; and within it two points: it is the right Yod, which is in Binah, and it bestows life to all the limbs; and the second, in which is the blood, a hint to the left Yod, judgment; certainly it is Malkhut. And in it are two rings upon the two hollows, a hint to "the round goblet, which lacks not mingled wine" (Song 7:3); and they are a hint to the two manifestations of Malkhut, which are in the navel, in a literal ring; and they are one from the side of Chokhmah and one from the side of Binah; and they are "housings for the staves" (Exod. 37:14), which are two Yods. And who can tell the height of the concealed wisdom that is in them? And the two lobes of the lung, in which there are five lobes, which are seven: they are seven sefirot that blow a vital wind from the side of Chokhmah, which is sight; right; ריא"ה [lung], ראי"ה [sight], all is one matter; and it blows a wind of compassion upon the heart, which is Binah, to quiet the judgment. And outside the veil, the gullet is the Vav, and its drawing is to the bowels; compassion: "and my bowels were moved for him" (Song 5:4). However, it is not the Holy of Holies, from the side of the residue that is bestowed from it to them, outward. Outside are the spleen and the liver and the gall and the lobe of the liver; they are four outer powers, so that it be included in all. Below, the kidneys; and they are those that show Netzach and Hod, "which counsel" and are springs of wisdom; and they bestow into the covenant, which is Yesod. And it is said that each one of the kidneys has twelve channels, springing from their source and bestowing into the covenant; to hint at the bestowal of the right, Netzach, which is Vav, behold six; and Chesed, Vav, behold six; they are twelve. And likewise the left: Hod, Vav, and Gevurah, Vav; behold twelve. For the Patriarchs are hinted in three Vavs, and likewise the Netzachs; and all is bestowed into Yesod, which is the covenant. And in it there are two openings, to hint at the two channels that are explained in the Gate of Channels, one to holiness and one to the husk. And the two testicles are Netzach and Hod; and they are two Yods, with Vav in the middle; and that is the manifestation of Alef.

And the matter of the thighs and the legs and the loins: they are Netzach and Hod, according to their aspects; and likewise they are called chalatzayim; and we have explained them in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And ten toes, to hint at the ten lower sefirot that are in Beriah, which are beneath Malkhut. And because of the smallness of their ability, for they are only a throne, therefore they scarcely move; "their good is not in their hand" (Job 21:16). And after we set our mind to all these matters, we shall understand what they expounded (our Sages, of blessed memory, in Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 12) on the verse (Deut. 32:6), "He made you and established you": the Holy One, blessed be He, and His court took counsel over each and every limb, and set it in its place. All this is to show that the whole upper court, all the concealed worlds, all of them are hinted in man. And one who is expert in the wisdom of anatomy in the way of truth will understand and comprehend many concealed matters, many kinds of wisdom and knowledge concerning the matter of the concealed worlds in their root, and the matter of the Account of Creation and the Account of the Chariot. For the body of man, even though it is turbid matter, includes all, upper and lower, as we explained:

And since this body is built a pleasant and important building such as was explained in the previous chapter, there is a further, double good: for in these pleasant limbs there is compounded a vital spirit, which spirit is not literally emanated from a high place; however, it comes into being within the body from the side of the refining of the materials to the rung of the form and of that creation, and from the side of the ascent of the matter and the dust to the state of the form of man, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces (chapter 10). And upon this vital spirit is the dwelling of the vital soul; and upon the vital soul the spirit; and upon the spirit the soul. And on this (the Tannaim) [the commentators] disagreed, as we shall explain. And before the explanation of this introduction it is fitting to refute the opinion of some of the commentators, who said that the bones are the dwelling of the spirit and the flesh the dwelling of the vital soul; and they wished to establish this matter from the verse that said (Job 14:22), "But his flesh upon him has pain, and his soul within him mourns." And they say: since the vital soul mourns from the pain of the flesh, behold, certainly the flesh is a chariot to the vital soul. And this opinion does not come out well, for several reasons. First: if it is so, that the flesh is a chariot to the vital soul and the bones the dwelling of the spirit, if so it would have been fitting that after the burial, when the flesh is consumed, the vital soul would depart and the spirit remain there while the bones endure. And the thing is not so; but on the contrary, "the spirit returns to God who gave it" (Eccl. 12:7), to the Garden of delights; and the vital soul in the grave delights the body, or the reverse, all according to the deed. And so they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 141b); and we have already written somewhat of this above in chapter 3; and likewise in Parashat Acharei (fol. 70b). And further: since the vital soul is below the rung of the spirit, certainly, if so, it would have been fitting that the spirit, whose life is great, have its dwelling in the flesh, whose life is greater than the bones, clearly; for in the flesh the pulsing and the non-pulsing veins spread, and it certainly feels with life more than the bones. And most difficult of all: for Rashbi, peace be upon him (in Parashat Lekh), explains, as we explained, that there is a vital spirit in which is the dwelling of the vital soul, as we shall explain. And now we shall come to the explanation of the linking down of this soul from its beginning to its end. It has already preceded for us in the preceding gates, concerning the matter of the letters and their spirituality, that "it is not a vain thing" (Deut. 32:47). And the matter is literally the same in the breath of the mouth: from the breath there come into being letters and spirituality and a soul, which withdraw from effect to cause, up to the place wanted for them, united in the roots of this soul. And this is the matter of "the new heavens and the new earth" (Isa. 66:22), which are made from new insights of Torah, as is expounded in the Zohar, Bereshit (in the Introduction, fols. 4 and 5), and in Parashat Kedoshim (fol. 85): for when a man brings forth new insights of Torah, those letters that come into being and are joined in his mouth, there comes into being from them a spirituality and a pleasant matter. And this is the matter of prayer, which Akhtariel receives and binds as crowns for his Master, as we explained in its entry. And this introduction is a key to many palaces of Torah. And for this our Sages, of blessed memory, said, "Commandments require intention" [that is, intention to fulfil the obligation]; and all of them agreed that if his intention was not to fulfil the obligation, certainly he has not fulfilled it (see Beit Yosef, section 589). And the matter is that when a man fulfils the bodily commandments, behold, they will be a body and a dwelling for the spirituality of his intention, which is drawn from his soul; and the intention is clothed in the deed of the commandment. And therefore, when the commandment has no intention, behold, according to the truth it is like a body without a soul. And from this we may infer that the more a man's intention grows in the deed of the commandments, behold, according to its measure its spirituality grows, and it rises higher and higher by way of the rungs, as we explained above in chapter 6.

And since this introduction is true and right, behold, when a man is united with his partner in good, and with complete intention for His service, may He be blessed, so as to unite the Bridegroom and the Bride, and to bring forth for himself thereby a soul from holiness, behold, then truly the Name, may He be blessed, will bring forth for him a soul from among the holy souls. And all the more if the known pleasant prayer preceded the coupling for him: behold, "how much more so," a double good, that there come into being from that deed a body and a drop prepared for a holy soul.

And behold, as in the union of the bodily male and female, so in the union of the pleasant souls, which also have male and female; and they act, in the goodness of their intention, in the spirituality of vital soul, spirit and soul, for the soul to be clothed in its upper steps. And this pleasant intention is the drop which the angel appointed over conception raises up; for one cannot say that he means a bodily drop.

And behold, so it is explained in the Zohar (Bereshit, fol. 54; see there, 54b) concerning the nocturnal emissions and afflictions of human beings: that the spirits conceive from an emission. And it was difficult for them: since a man is corporeal, how is it possible that the simple spirit conceive from him, even though it is impure? And they said that the conception is not from the drop, for the drop is drawn to waste; rather, it conceives from that craving with which a man is heated to sow seed. And we explained it in the Gate of the Palaces of Impurity, chapter 2. And so it is with regard to holiness, as I explained. And then, when that drop is raised, that is to say, his holy intention and the spirituality, before the Lord, YHVH of hosts, the Master of judgment, judgment is passed upon it. And according to its preparation, so is the decree of the Lord concerning the obligation of the soul that is bestowed and given into that drop. And now there will be revealed to us the matter of the commandment that a man marry the daughter of a Torah scholar, so that her soul be clean and pure and she direct her mind for the sake of Heaven. And likewise the matter of what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shevuot 18b): "One who sanctifies himself at the time of intercourse," etc. And likewise the matter of the permission of intercourse with a pregnant woman and a nursing woman, and it is not called seed in vain, God forbid; because, even though it is not for the matter of bodily begetting, it is for the matter of spiritual begetting; for in the goodness of their intention the upper Bridegroom and Bride are united, as from the other deeds of the commandments. And this is the secret of Abraham and Sarah, who begot souls for proselytes, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained: for by means of their intention the Bridegroom and the Bride were united and begot, in the secret of the upper begetting explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, holy souls for those proselytes; and that is (Gen. 12:5) "and the souls that they had made in Haran." And let us return to our matter: that then, when that drop is before the King, a soul is bestowed upon it. And it has already been explained in the Zohar, in the Sava (of Mishpatim, fol. 102), that when a man has relations with his partner he puts into her a spark of his spirit; and that spirit stands within her body, rattling in her, as this matter is explained there at length. And from this we may infer to the upper soul that is sent to the child: it is clothed in the spiritual drop within the soul of the female; and the female is found pregnant in herself and pregnant in her soul. And there is no wonder in this at all; for such is the way even with males, that they are impregnated [with the impregnation of another soul]; as the matter of Pinchas, who was impregnated with the soul of Nadab and Abihu, as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Acharei (fol. 57b) and Parashat Pinchas (fol. 217a); and like the matter of the first Adam, who was joined to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, as is expounded in the Zohar and the book of the Ra'aya Meheimna and in the Tikkunim.

And the matter of the aspect of impregnation [ibbur] is one of the secrets of the secrets of reincarnation. And therefore they said (our Sages, of blessed memory, Arakhin, fol. 7a), "The foetus is the thigh of its mother," and one does not wait for a woman, to punish her with death, until she gives birth. For just as the soul of the woman was defiled within the husk in that transgression, so the soul of the foetus was defiled; and both of them need purification; and therefore both of them die, and one does not wait for them until she gives birth. And this note is enough on the excellence of the drawing down of the soul; and from it many of the King's secrets will be opened to the one who understands:

Now we shall explain the matter of its dwelling within the smitten body. And it is that the principal dwelling of the vital soul is the vital power that is in a man; which power is a nature naturally implanted in him, like the likeness of the life in the beasts; and it is not a thing emanated upon him, like the matter of the seven parts of a man that we explained in chapter 4. And therefore some called it the animal soul, which is the power of life of the beasts; and it has no essential knowledge in the world; but it is a smoky vapour dwelling in the hollow of the heart, spreading in the whole body. And it is the life that comes into being out of the raising of this dust to the rung of the form of man; as those men who occupied themselves with the practice of the Sefer Yetzirah used to create them, as we explained in the Gate of Palaces (chapter 10). And since this vital power is a dwelling for the vital soul, it needed to be like the likeness of the emanated vital soul in its constitution and the pleasant inner limbs explained in the previous chapter. And this life needed to be spreading and branching out, like the matter of the likeness that belongs to the body. And because this vital soul is still most subtle, it needed to have a subtle matter in which to be clothed; and that is the fine blood that is in the veins of the heart; and they are the living veins that pulse. And for the reason that, if it were from this life that spreads in those veins without the joining of bones and sinews, it could not endure at all; for it would not stand, because of its weakness, and would be lost, and a light thing would damage it. For this it needed to arrange an array of bones, which are like bridges upon which these vessels spread. And because the bones are hard to the touch, with protruding places and sunken places, it needed to level them with flesh, in its chosen constitution, with the likening of the form to the upper form, as we explained. And because the flesh is without guarding, out of the softness of its nature, for it is slack and keeps dissolving, therefore it needed to coat it with the skin, which is a fence and a hedge, so that the flesh not be lost and not be spoiled. And for the reason that the flesh not be blemished and lost of itself, there needed to be channels watering it, the sinews; and they are the veins of the liver, which are dead, for there is in them only the watering of the flesh, that it grow and be refined and be moist, and be watered by them in exchange for what is melted away by the natural heat. This is the summary that we need from the wisdom of the nature of creation, for the soul.

And behold, upon that vital spirit will be the dwelling of the vital soul. And a proof of this vital power is: at the time of a man's sleep, when the vital soul departs to give account before its Maker, that vital spirit remains, sitting and feeding and sustaining the constitution of the man. And this is the matter of the vital spirit that blows in him the breathing and the powers of the body that belong to it, like the likeness of the power of digestion and the other powers of the vital soul, such as the attracting power and the expelling power, etc., which are explained in natural science. And this matter is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh Lekha (fol. 83), and these are his words: "Come and see: the vital soul of a man, when he goes up to his bed, goes out of him and rises above. And if you say that all of them rise: not each and every one sees the face of the King. But the vital soul goes out and rises, and there remains with the body only one impression, a measure of the life of the heart. And the vital soul goes and seeks to rise," etc. Thus far his words.

And the intention is clear: that at the time of a man's sleep his vital soul departs from him, and there remains in the body only a mere vital spirit; and it is, according to the truth, the natural life that is in the body; and it is what is made a chariot for the vital soul, and the vital soul for the spirit, and the spirit for the soul; and all this by means of the honoured image, as is explained above in the preceding chapters. And behold, now it will not be a wonder in our eyes that the soul is joined to the body, even though it is corporeal and the soul a subtle and spiritual being.
And behold, the second part is concluded. And now we shall come to the explanation of the third part; and it is the matter of its blemishing in itself and its blemishing in the honoured gates:

There are some of the kabbalists who said that there is no sin in the soul; rather, the sin is the vital soul's, which is the one blemished. And they established the matter from the fact that there is not found in the whole section of the offerings "a soul [neshamah] when it sins" or "a spirit when it sins", but "a vital soul [nefesh] when it sins" (Lev. 4:2); and likewise it is said (Ezek. 18:4), "the vital soul that sins, it shall die"; for there is no death except in the vital soul. And likewise it is written (Job 14:22), "and his vital soul within him mourns"; for the spirit too departs from him when a man comes to sin. And this opinion is not right in some respect. For it is true that the cutting off and the consumption and the loss are in the vital soul and not in the other parts; and so they explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Acharei (fol. 70b), in the saying "It has been taught: Rabbi Judah said: It is written, 'Let the earth bring forth the living vital soul' (Gen. 1:24)," etc.; and there they lengthened much on the matter of the vital soul; and among his words he said: "And the punishment of the guilty who are in the earth is in this, as it is written, 'and that vital soul shall be cut off from its people' (Lev. 7:20)." Thus far his words.

And what he said, "the punishment of the guilty is in this": the explanation, the punishment of cutting off [karet]. For the other rungs are not cut off entirely, God forbid; however, they are defiled, and they are purified from their filth by means of the river of fire [nehar dinur], as is explained in the Gate of Palaces. However, the vital soul is cut off entirely, and the soul is defiled. And so it is explained in the Zohar, in Parashat Tetzaveh (fol. 182), and these are his words: "For when the Holy One, blessed be He, created man, He made him in the likeness of the upper image, and breathed into him a holy spirit that includes three; and behold, they have established that there are in him vital soul, spirit and soul; and above them all, the soul, which is the upper power, to know and to keep the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He. And if he brings that holy soul into another service, he defiles it, and it goes out from the service of its Master; because these three powers are all one: vital soul, spirit, soul are partners together and are one." Thus far his words.
And the words of the saying do not need explanation, for they are clear; and from them we learn that the soul is defiled.

And further there, further on in the matter: "'in whose nostrils is breath [neshamah]' (Isa. 2:22): for he tears that holy soul and defiles it, because 'in whose nostrils is breath'; he exchanged it for his anger [appo]."

And behold, it is a complete necessity that the soul be blemished and defiled. However, the matter of its defilement, even though it departs from the body, will be as we explained in the Gate of Manifestations (in chapter 1; see there), concerning holiness, that it is multiplied. And likewise the soul: when it is emanated according to the ways that have been explained, so its manifestation remains present in the place from which it was hewn, a subtle and pleasant manifestation; and its rungs descend rung after rung, by way of the steps of the ladder, until its coming to the lowly world. And this is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, fol. 64), and these are his words: "'Set me as a seal' (Song 8:6): this is the soul, whose impression is engraved above; as they have established concerning Jacob, whose likeness is engraved on the Throne of Glory. All the souls that are hewn from there: their engraving is engraved above, and their impression [below. And that engraving above] is a seal; and the impression below is the impression of the seal. And since the impression of the engraving of the soul is above and its impression below, it is said of it, 'and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it' (Gen. 28:12): they rise above and look at the likeness of the soul that shines in that engraving, and tremble from it; they descend below and look at the impression of that likeness below, and see that it has not changed from the likeness above, and fear it." Thus far his words.

And from it it appears explicitly that there remains above, in the place of the hewing of the soul, a praiseworthy and subtle likeness, until it is more and more praiseworthy than the soul below; for concerning the upper likeness of Jacob he said, "and tremble from it," which is not so with the soul below, as he explained. And when that soul, by way of its rungs, is related to this body, even though it rises and departs from the body, behold, all the action of the body is drawn to the soul by way of the chain of its linking down, and it is necessarily blemished. And is it not so, that as there are rungs of the linking down of holiness, so there are rungs of impurity? And just as, when a man sins, he draws upon himself the power of impurity, so he draws and bestows it upon his soul; for in impurity itself there are divisions and there are manifestations: there is a subtle manifestation, like a concealed filth, an impure emanation; and there is a coarse manifestation. And therefore the one who defiles himself defiles his soul; for he draws upon it the power of impurity and makes it cleave to the husks, whether subtle or coarse. And a proof of this is from the pious man who cleaves to holiness by means of his deeds: he bestows upon his soul much effluence from the upper place by way of steps, and "it makes him understand knowledge and teaches him wisdom" (cf. Isa. 40:14), like the way of the prophets and those who speak by the Holy Spirit, who cleave to their Maker until they draw the light upon their soul, and their soul bestows in them the secrets that it received and the words of the concealed wisdom. And so is the thing in impurity: for when a man sins he makes the power of impurity rule over himself abundantly. According to the measure of the action in which he sinned, so will be the matter of the impurity. And a proof of this is from the Zohar, Parashat Kedoshim (fol. 86b), and these are his words: "And come and see: at the hour that a man shows a deed below in a straight way, as is needed, there flows and goes out and dwells upon him the upper Holy Spirit (as is needed). And at the hour that he shows a deed below in a crooked way, which is not the straight way, then there flows and goes out and dwells upon him another spirit, which is not needed, which turns a man aside to the evil side. Who draws that spirit upon him? Say: that deed which he showed on the other side." Thus far his words.

And behold, it is established that according to the rung of the pious man in his drawing the Holy Spirit upon himself, so is the rung of the wicked man in his drawing the spirit of impurity upon himself abundantly. And in Parashat Naso (fol. 122a) they also explained this matter, and these are his words: "For when a man goes in the ways of the Torah, he draws upon himself the upper Holy Spirit, as it is said, 'until a spirit be poured upon us from on high' (Isa. 32:15). And when a man turns aside his ways, he draws upon himself a spirit from the other side, which is the impure side; and the impure side is aroused from the side of the female of the great abyss, where are the dwellings of the evil spirits that harm human beings, and they are called the harmful spirits of the world." Thus far his words.

And behold, he taught explicitly that when a man turns from the straight way he bestows the power of impurity abundantly, until it is bestowed upon his soul; and from there it is bestowed to the body; for "one happening is to the righteous and to the wicked" (cf. Eccl. 9:2). And that impurity is the blemish that is in the soul; and it is the blemish that needs washing by repentance. For when he returns to his God and accepts upon himself his repentance as is fitting, according as he cleaved to the husk, so he will subdue himself, until he breaks those husks into which he entered by means of the iniquity; and then his soul returns to the place of holiness and attains a spiritual excellence. And in this way will be understood their saying, of blessed memory (Berakhot 34b): "In the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous do not stand," etc. For by his repentance he breaks the husks. The example: if he entered into the seventh husk, he breaks it, until its descent below; behold, he has subdued the husks and their powers and broken them. And this is certainly a great excellence: for apart from his having returned in complete repentance and the soul having returned to its place, there is further drawn from this a subduing and a breaking for the husks; which was not so for the completely righteous man who never sinned. For it is true that he repaired himself; but with all this he did not spoil others, for he did not break the husks, and their power is still in them to harm against their masters. And near to this matter they expounded in the Zohar, Parashat Va-yikra (fol. 5), and these are his words: "It is written, 'the sacrifices of Elohim' (Ps. 51:19), and not 'the sacrifices of YHVH.' He said to him: Certainly, etc. Rather, 'the sacrifices of Elohim'; and therefore their slaughtering is in the north; for the slaughtering is for the sake of Elohim, that side of Gevurah, that it be sweetened, and the spirit of judgment be broken, and the judgment be weakened, and compassion prevail over judgment. And therefore 'the sacrifices of Elohim': to break the power and the strength of harsh judgment, as it is written, 'a broken spirit': that that strong spirit be broken, and its spirit and its power and its strength not prevail. And a man must then stand upon the altar with a broken spirit, and be ashamed of his deeds, so that that strong spirit be broken; and all so that the judgment be sweetened and compassion prevail over judgment." Thus far his words.

And behold, it is explicit that in a man's subduing his evil inclination, and in his being ashamed of his iniquities, he subdues the power of Gevurah and judgment. And if so in holiness, how much more, and an a fortiori son of the son of an a fortiori, that he subdues the left side, which depends on the side of the strength of judgment. And this thing is not light; for it is the foundation and pillar of the world. For behold, Abraham our father, peace be upon him, needed to go down to Egypt to subdue the power of the husks, to enter into them and go out in peace; and had he not entered there, it would not have been possible for him to be a chariot to Chesed. And so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lekh (fol. 83a), concerning the descent of Abraham to Egypt, and these are his words: "Come and see the secret of the matter: if Abraham had not gone down to Egypt and been refined there first, he would not be the portion and lot of the Holy One, blessed be He. In the same way for his sons: when the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to make them one people, a perfect people, and to bring them near to Him, if they had not gone down first to Egypt and been refined there, they would not have been a people unique to Him. In the same way, if the holy land had not been given to Canaan first, and he ruled in it, it would not have been the land, the portion and the lot of the Holy One, blessed be He. And all is one secret." Thus far his words.

And it is a complete proof for our intention. And likewise Bathsheba, who was given to Uriah before David took her, because she was chosen for a seed fit for kingship, as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 73b). And brevity is good:

After we have explained in the previous chapter the blemishing of the soul in itself, now we shall explain the manifestation of its blemishing above, in what we set forth in the previous chapter concerning the soul, that it has a manifestation above, above manifestation.

And behold, by means of its actions all of them are blemished in this; except that there is a difference: that when a man blemishes his vital soul by a sin in which there is no judgment of death, such as the negative commandments of the Torah, he does not draw upon himself the power of impurity so much. However, he draws upon himself some; and that some will be one rung. For of the husks there are subtle ones, that is to say, slack, for they are below in rung; that is to say, little impurity or much impurity. And if a man sins lightly, he draws upon himself from the light one; and according to what he draws upon himself, so he blemishes above; for he makes the husk rule in the place of that iniquity on which the commandment depends. The example of this: if he sins in a light commandment, and it depends on one of the attributes, he makes the husk rule in that place, in some of the manifestation of his upper soul which is in that place; for according as he drew the husk upon himself below, so he drew the husk upon himself above. And one must not think that the husk enters into the place of holiness, God forbid; however, the matter is the claim of judgment, to say: this soul is of my portion; and it is necessary that that soul be driven out from that upper place, and the subtle husk rules over it. And if, God forbid, he sins a grave iniquity, in whatever sefirah its aspect may be, likewise he makes the husk rule over the subtle upper soul, and it is driven out from its place; and a blemish is found above, and "he cut the plantings"; because that place is found blemished, and the soul is found among the husks. And the intention in our saying that the upper soul is driven out from its place, and likewise that it enters into the husks: the intention is not literally that it enters into the husks, God forbid; however, it is concerning the matter of its sucking from within the bitter channel known in the upper covenant, which is the place of the food of the husks and the outlet of the residues. And therefore it was necessary that, just as before his sin it sucks from the right, and by its means the place of its holding, Malkhut, and all the rungs of holiness were bestowed from the holy effluence, so by means of its sin the holy rung in which it is held is bestowed from the bitterness of that left channel, and it bestows from the dross of the silver and the gold. And there is no blemish greater than this: that he forces his holy rung to bestow to the husk by means of the channel of his soul. And the explanation of this matter is: just as, when a man bestows effluence to the world by his good deeds, there remains of the light of that effluence his portion, to be clothed in it in the Garden of Eden, as we explained in chapter 5, and from it the clean garment comes into being for the soul; so is the matter of the filthy garments: that the soul is clothed from an unclean effluence, and he bestows to the husks, and his portion remains kept, to be clothed in it. And just as the upright man, by his good deeds, bestows to Malkhut a good and pleasant effluence, for by his means Malkhut is joined to Tiferet, and it illuminates opposite her, so the wicked man, by his corrupted deeds, bestows by means of his soul, as we explained above, an effluence bitter as death, by way of the evil channel, which is the channel of the residues; and then the Bride is separated as a menstruant, and says, "Like the likeness of a red rose I have seen," etc. And it is found that from his side she is separated from "the companion of her youth" (Prov. 2:17) and sucks from the left, the ugliness and the residues; and the soul of the wicked cleaves to the side of that channel, and gives power to the husks and arouses them to suck "the cruel venom of asps" (Deut. 32:33). And his portion is found kept for him, to clothe his soul from it at the time of its departure from the world. And these are the filthy garments, the garments of the iniquities. And this thing is hinted in the Zohar, Parashat Pinchas (fol. 214a), and these are his words: "'Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments' (Zech. 3:3); and they have established it. But filthy garments are certainly the garment in which the spirit is clothed in that world, etc. And this has been said: everyone who is to enter Gehinnom, those garments in which they clothe him, how are they? What is written here? 'Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel.' Who is the angel? This is the angel that is appointed over Gehinnom, and appointed over whoever is seen in those garments; until a voice answered and said, 'Take away the filthy garments from him' (Zech. 3:4). From here one should observe that the evil deeds of human beings make for him those filthy garments. 'And he said to him, See, I have caused your iniquity to pass from you, and I will clothe you with festive robes': He clothed him in other garments, prepared, in which a man rises in the radiance of the glory of his Master. And come and see: in the same way Pinchas did not depart from the world until other garments of the spirit were prepared before him, which he would enjoy in the world to come. In one hour he was stripped of these and clothed in those, to establish what is written, 'Behold, I give him My covenant of peace' (Num. 25:12)." Thus far his words.

And behold, in this saying he made the measures equal: for as is the happening of the righteous with his pleasant garments, so is the happening of the wicked with his filthy garments; and all from the deed of this world, and the matter depends on the deed. And from the garments you may infer to the blemish that is blemished above in the holy rungs; for the garment is "his portion from all his labour" (Eccl. 2:10) that he laboured, and from his effluence that he bestowed.

And behold, this is an opening to understand the matter of the blemish and the cutting. And brevity in this is good, to be concerned for the honour of one's Maker. And in this way it will be understood that when the soul sucks from the residue, the plantings are found cut from its side, and that channel is blemished; and this is the cutting. And by his repentance he will break that husk, and the soul will return to its first place, and the planting that is planted in the holy place will draw from a pure place. And with this will be understood the matter of the verse (Ps. 50:16), "But to the wicked God says: What have you to do to declare My statutes," etc. For since the wicked man is within the husks, when he blesses he necessarily bestows to the husks, as we explained; for by means of that blessing some effluence is bestowed upon him, and he is within the husk. And if so, it is necessary that the husks claim and say: Behold, the prayer and the blessing of so-and-so, who prayed, is ours; and then it is necessarily bestowed upon them. And this is (Prov. 30:23), "and a handmaid that is heir to her mistress." And for this reason they said in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 16b), that every nation among which Israel dwell in exile is exalted; because when Israel pray, they are bestowed upon against our will, because they rule over us. And likewise the husks, because they rule over the wicked man, take that effluence that is bestowed by means of the blessing. And because of this David our king, peace be upon him, said, "But to the wicked God says," etc. And according to these things they said, "In the place where penitents stand," etc.: and he subdues them and takes from them all his blessings. And this is (Eccl. 8:9), "a time when man rules over man to his hurt"; and it is to the hurt of the man of Belial, as we explained in the Gate of ABYA.

And behold, with this "he breaks the jaws of the unrighteous, and plucks the prey out of his teeth" (Job 29:17); "he has swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up" (Job 20:15). And this is the explanation of the verse (Job 8:6), "surely now He will awake for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous [ve-shillam]". And the intention: He will awake concerning those commandments, and receive them from the side of impurity. And then "ve-shillam": the explanation, the habitation of righteousness is perfected [mishtallemet]; which is the Shekhinah, as we wrote in the entry Naveh, that it is Malkhut, and the Throne, from which the souls are hewn, in the entry Tetzivah [hewing?], which is Yetzirah. And one must not think that those blessings or commandments that are sunk there are afterward loathsome in His eyes, may He be blessed, God forbid; for on the contrary, they are praiseworthy, after the way of "In the place where penitents stand," etc.; and so it is hinted in the Zohar. And with this this chapter is completed and this gate is concluded. Blessed be YHVH forever, Amen and Amen:
The Gate of Intention, which is Gate Thirty-Two:

What is intended in this gate is to explain what the benefit is in the doing of the commandments and in the matters of prayer, and the order in which one should direct his intention in his prayer, so that there be no stumbling in it, God forbid:
Chapter One:

Since it has already been explained in the previous gate that man is "a portion of God from above" (Job 31:2), "whether his work be pure, and whether it be right" (Prov. 20:11), and he is held "with cords of love" (Hos. 11:4) to the roots of holiness by his soul, which rises in all the worlds and in all the rungs, as we explained in the previous gate: behold, when he does righteousness and uprightness and directs his intention, in his right thought, by way of the steps, to unite the rungs, "the loops opposite" (Exod. 26:5), "each cleaving to his brother" (Job 41:9), and his soul is clothed in his soul, part in part, a candelabrum of joints: behold, it is necessary that by his means the sefirot be united and be bound with a firm bond; and he, in his soul, will be a channel through which the sefirot are bestowed, from the first to the last, by means of the firm rope that binds them. For when his soul is united in his soul by means of his study, it follows from this that the roots remain bound with a firm bond. And in this way will be understood the reason why what this one blemishes, all the other souls cannot repair his blemish, until he returns in repentance, now or in reincarnation, and the rope is bound literally by his own means. And let us give a fine parable. When we raise in our mind that there be here a fine, great spring, as thick as the beams of the olive press, and the root of this spring is sources upon sources, fine as the eyes of a needle; however, when all of them are united together, the whole makes a great river, "the waters of Shihor" (Isa. 23:3). And now, if one comes and closes one source of the fine, small sources, will not the spring in any case be diminished by the measure of that source? And by this we shall consider that the great spring is the strength of the bestowal that is bestowed in the world; and the fine channels are the manifestation of the souls, which are threads of flames rising and concealed within their source in all the sefirot; and by their means will be their union and their binding and their bestowal. And when the sinner sins and uproots his subtle manifestation from one of the rungs, according to the measure of the sin, if great, above, and if small, below, will he not diminish the good and the bestowal that is bestowed by way of the channel of his soul? For he closes that channel and cuts it, as we explained. And is there among all those fine channels that remain one who can repair what that broken channel perverted? It is a great thing that there is none who can repair it; but on the contrary, all of them received blemish and spoiling. For until now each one of the fine channels was included of six hundred thousand channels, as the number of the souls; and now there remain six hundred thousand less one, and all of them are included in six hundred thousand less one, and the one part is blemished. Behold, explicitly, he has blemished himself and others. And this is "All Israel are sureties one for another" (Shevuot 39a). And even though we said that they are channels, we do not say because of this that the channels are equal; but there are in this matter many differences. For when the upright man does one commandment, according to the measure of the commandment and its reward, so he bestows in it, and the bestowal of that channel grows, and it thickens, and its light and its bestowal grow. And when a man's Torah is his craft, the greatness of that bestowal never ceases. And for this it is found that in the time of Rashbi, peace be upon him, when their Torah was their craft, they were punished for the neglect of their Torah even for a moment, as rebels; as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemot (fol. 17b): "Rabbi Yose went out on the road, and Rabbi Acha bar Jacob was going with him. While they were going, Rabbi Yose was silent and thought about matters of the world, and Rabbi Acha thought about matters of Torah. While they were going, Rabbi Yose saw a snake running after him. Rabbi Yose said to Rabbi Acha: See that snake running after me. Rabbi Acha said to him: I do not see it. Rabbi Yose ran, and the snake after him. Rabbi Yose fell, and blood flowed and came down from his nostrils. He heard that they were saying, 'You only have I known of all the families of the earth' (Amos 3:2), etc. Rabbi Yose said: If for one hour it is so, the one who despairs of it, how much more!" Thus far his words.

And behold, from this saying we learn their praise: that they never ceased from their Torah even for a moment. And for this Rabbi Yose was punished. And the reason is as we explained: for when they were occupied with Torah and with commandments, the greatness of the bestowal was bestowed by their means, and the world was at ease; and as Rashbi, peace be upon him, said of himself and of his companion, "We are the seven eyes of YHVH, we": to hint that by their means the Shekhinah was united in the seven days. And for this reason, when they ceased for a moment, that effluence was lacking, God forbid, and a lack of bestowal was found above; and therefore they were punished in a moment. And this is that he saw the crooked serpent running after him, and Rabbi Acha did not see it: to hint that it came for the neglect of Rabbi Yose's Torah. And this is that he heard, "You only have I known," etc., "therefore I will visit upon you." And this is the reason that the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous as a hair's thread.
