And this inquiry is explained with extreme brevity in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, fol. 64b), and these are his words: "'Set me as a seal' (Song 8:6): this is the soul, which is engraved on the Throne. At the time that it is aroused in prayer below, the Throne is aroused above," etc. Thus far his words.

And behold, he explained that since the likeness and image of his soul is engraved on the Throne, it was necessary that by means of his prayers and his good deeds his soul be aroused and arouse the Throne itself. And this is certainly a great proof for our intention. And when the pious man sins, his punishment grows more and more than one of the empty ones; because he rose by his deeds in the roots to a great excellence, and did wonders in his bestowal, until most of the thickness of the channel depended on him. For according to the abundance of piety the thickness of the channel grows by means of the soul, as we explained; and when he sins and is guilty, God forbid, that bestowal is diminished in a moment, and the world remains dark because of him. And therefore the anger of YHVH burns against him, even to destroy, God forbid, until he returns in his repentance and repairs what he perverted:

And after this introduction has been explained, now it will be understood how much, how much the double good of the rung of the pious man in his prayer, according to the measure of his intention. For if he directs his intention to bestow from rung to rung, like the rungs of the ladder, and cleaves to his Maker in his knowledge, in the doing of his commandments, his soul rises and is exalted from rung to rung, and from cause to cause, and from effect to cause, until much effluence is bestowed upon him; and he will be the place of dwelling and the seat for the bestowal, and from him it is divided to the whole world; as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 169a), and these are his words: "The one who blesses the blessing of food takes blessings first of all, and is blessed in the totality of the blessing of food; and therefore he has length of life." Thus far his words. And his saying, "and is blessed in the totality of the blessing of food": the intention is that he is blessed in the totality of Malkhut, that is, the blessing of food. And for the reason that his manifestation is above, as we explained, therefore he "takes blessings first"; for he precedes the whole world, as we explained. And so it is further explained in Parashat Pekudei (fol. 238a), and these are his words: "And therefore everyone who prays a prayer and binds the union: they look at him, whether it is a prayer and a binding as is fitting. And if that prayer and that binding are as is fitting, then he is blessed first, from the place from which all blessings go out." Thus far his words.

And therefore, according to these things, he will be a seat for the Shekhinah. Since the effluence comes by his means, it is found that the righteous man is in the place of the great channel, the Foundation of the world; and therefore it is fitting that the Shekhinah cleave to him; and he is called the groomsman of the King. And happy is he, and happy is his portion; for he merited and caused others to merit, and the whole world is judged on the side of merit because of him. And in this way it is found that at the hour that there is a righteous and pious man in the world, the whole world is fed by his means, as they said, of blessed memory (Berakhot 17b): "The whole world is fed for the sake of Chanina my son," etc. And with this we will certainly know and attain how many excellences, and what an elixir of life the God will grant, to the one who knows how to direct his intention in the roots, more than to the one who knows how to direct his intention only in the plain meaning. And certainly this is the principal of this wisdom, even though its benefits are many apart from these. And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar, Parashat Chukkat (fol. 184): "Rabbi Simeon said: Here I wish to reveal a matter. Come and see: everyone who knows how to arrange the deed as is fitting and to arrange the words as is fitting, etc., behold, certainly he arouses the Holy One, blessed be He, to draw upper words, which are made fit, etc. If so, behold, the whole world knows how to arrange the deed and to arrange the words; what is the importance of the righteous, who know the root of the matter and the deed, and know how to direct the heart and the desire [re'uta], more than those others who do not know so much? Rather, those who do not know the root of the deed so much, but only the arrangement, and no more, draw upon themselves a drawing from behind the shoulders of the Holy One, blessed be He, which does not fly in the air that is called providence. And those who know and direct the heart and the desire bring out blessings from the place of Thought; and they go out in all the trunks and roots in a straight way as is fitting, until the upper ones and the lower ones are blessed, and the holy Name is blessed by their means. Happy is their portion; for the Holy One, blessed be He, is near to them and ready opposite them. At the hour that they call Him, He is ready for them; at the hour that they are in distress, He is with them. He honours them in this world and in the world to come, as it is written, 'Because he longs for Me, therefore will I deliver him,' etc. (Ps. 91:14)." Thus far his words.

And behold, from this saying is explicitly understood the excellence of the one who directs his intention over the one who does not, in different kinds. Either: that this one, who does not direct his intention but prays after the order of the world, takes "from behind His shoulders," etc.: the intention is that the King does not turn His face to answer him; however, he takes from outside; like a king who hears the cry of one of the common people from outside his palace, and commands that that man not enter inside with his cry; however, they answer him outside by means of one of the King's servants. And this is the matter of "from behind His shoulders," etc. And he gave a cause for this: that his prayer does not rise above, because it has no wings to fly in the pure and holy air and to cleave airs and firmaments and hosts. However, the excellence of the one who directs his intention in his prayer: he will surely make himself wings to fly to the heavens, and his prayer cleaves up, higher and higher, up to Keter; and from there, by way of the rungs, he bestows much effluence from before the face of the King, and he carries "a great portion" (cf. Gen. 43:34), "according to the good hand of the King upon him" (cf. Ezra 7:9; Neh. 2:8):

After we have spoken extensively in the previous chapter of the excellence of the one who directs his intention, it is fitting to consider that in the matter of intention in the sefirot there is some stammering. For it is found in the Sifrei: "'as YHVH our God is, whenever we call upon Him' (Deut. 4:7): upon Him, and not upon His attributes." And so it is fitting; for how is it possible that one should ask of the King's servant and not of the King? And it is fitting to pray only to the Master of the treasuries. And why should we relate all our prayer to the sefirot? And especially since all the words are like titles of them; and if he directs his intention to them, it is found that all his prayers hint in the sefirot, and no intention remains for him in the Source of sources. Second: how is it possible to direct the intention in the attributes? For when a man imagines in his mind one sefirah of the sefirot, he necessarily bounds it and makes it corporeal; for what can he imagine in the matter of spirituality? For all that a man thinks in his thought is corporeal, and the sight of his intellect cannot imagine the spiritual unless it makes it corporeal and bounds it. If so, it is found that intention in the sefirot is impossible. Further, third: when a man thinks of one of the attributes, he necessarily separates; for behold, he imagines in his intellect an attribute separated from the other attributes; and this is certainly not fitting, as we are obligated concerning their union, as is known:

And now we shall explain that, for the tikkun of these matters, one must first of all know that for the Ein Sof, the King of the kings of kings, blessed be He, there is no name and word that bounds Him, God forbid; and attributes are not true of His Self, because He is not subject to changes nor possessed of descriptions, and He does not change from will to will nor from action to action. And therefore it is not fitting for a man to direct his intention to Him, saying that He is called El or Eloah or Elohim, and the other names and the other titles. And these names are in the sefirot. And in our saying "in the sefirot," the intention is not in the sefirot themselves, God forbid; for the one who does so falls into a deep pit; and of such they said in the Sifrei, "upon Him, and not upon His attributes." However, our intention is as we explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels: for the intention is that He is called mighty in the attribute of Gevurah, for He is the one who gives power in Gevurah to act. And therefore the one who directs his intention must intend, when he says, "the great God," that it hints in Gedulah; and the word itself is in Gedulah; however, his intention is to the Self that spreads in Gedulah; and likewise Gevurah and the other sefirot. And it is found that the words name them in the sefirot, which are His descriptions; but his intention is to the Ein Sof, who makes use of them and is clothed in them. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 3a), and these are his words: "In every place and in every utterance one must direct the speech in Adonai and the voice in YHVH, and unite them as one in the union of that which is the One, concealed, who joins them and unites them as one. And in Him the intention is needed; for one cannot say of Him voice and speech, but thought." Thus far his words.

And behold, explicitly, the four-letter name is in Tiferet, and the whole prayer, without qualification, is in it; and therefore all the voice that goes out from his mouth, the hint is in it. And the speech is in Adonai, which is Malkhut. But the thought is in the Ein Sof, by whose means these two attributes are united. And there is nothing in the whole prayer that hints at Him, except the intention, that a man intend in Him, that He is all, and He is the one who unites the attributes and bestows upon them. And this is in the secret of the Self that spreads within the sefirot; and by this the sefirot have power to act; and by this the actions are related to Him, as is explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels. And as for the matter of the sefirot: the intention is not that a man direct his intention in the sefirot such that he imagine the matter of the sefirot; for this is impossible, as we explained. But the intention is that the sefirot have ten names of the four-letter name, as we explained in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name; and they are divided in their vowel-points; and these are they. Keter Elyon: YHVH, and its pointing is all kamatz; it shows Keter; and the four letters that are in it show the ten sefirot that are in it, so that there be no separation, God forbid. And the name of Chokhmah: YHVH, all of it patach; and it is the name in which Chokhmah is revealed. And Binah too has a name, YHVH, all of it tzeirei; and it is the name in which Binah is revealed. And Chesed too has a name, YHVH, all of it segol; and it is the name in which Chesed is revealed. And Gevurah too has a name, YHVH, all of it sheva; and it is the name in which Gevurah is revealed. And Tiferet too has a name, YHVH, all of it in cholam. And Netzach too has a name, YHVH, and it is pointed all chirik; and it is the name in which Netzach is revealed. And Hod too has a name, YHVH, and it is pointed with kibbutz sefatayim. And Yesod too has a name, YHVH, and it is all in shuruk. And Malkhut has a name, YHVH, and it is without any pointing at all, but simple; and according to her receiving, so is her pointing:

And now the one who directs his intention will intend in these names, and will raise in his mind that there is nothing that can hint at the attribute desired by him except in the havayah portrayed in his mind, which are four letters pointed according to their pointing, as we explained. And then "he shall walk in his way securely" (Prov. 3:23), and will not fear and will not dread. And he will also intend that in these four letters the ten sefirot are included, to hint that the ten sefirot agree with the actions of that attribute desired by him. And how good and how pleasant, if he wishes to portray these havayot in their colour; for then certainly his prayer is more and more effective; on condition that it be in his intention that there is nothing in this world that can represent the action of that attribute except a known colour, which is such-and-such. And because the colours have been set out at length by us in the Gate of Colors, we shall not explain the colours here; but when he wishes to direct his intention, behold, that gate is before the student. And with this we shall not fear error in any one of the three things that we said in this chapter.
And further, apart from this, there are conditions for intention; we shall explain them in a chapter by itself, with the help of the Name:

What is intended in this chapter is to explain the principal of intention. The one who directs his intention must draw spirituality from the upper rungs to the letters that he mentions, so that he can make those letters fly up to that upper rung, to hasten his request. And the intention: for the breath of a man's mouth "is not a vain thing" (Deut. 32:47), as we explained in the preceding gates; but it is a spirituality that comes into being from the breath of a man's mouth. And that spirituality needs power to make his requests fly and to raise the letters up to the rungs desired by him. And this is the principal of intention: to draw power, so that by that power the letters rise above and come into being in the place of the height of the world, and hasten his request. However, it is fitting to know that the mention of the titles is not equal to the mention of the four-letter name, even though it be in his intention always to the havayot, as we explained above. And the matter is that when a man mentions the four-letter name, then it is fitting that he direct his intention to the very self of the sefirot and to their inner spirituality, which is made a garment to the Self that spreads from the Ein Sof. And when he directs his intention in the titles, then he will portray in his mind a sefirah in a particular aspect that is in the sefirah; even though it is included of ten sefirot, which are hinted in the four letters of the Name, and they are the branches of that sefirah, as is explained above; even though it is united in all ten by means of the ten branches; for this is the bond and union of the sefirot, as we explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And even though Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the four-letter name in a known sefirah, with all this it hints at the ten roots in general, with a particular arousal for that sefirah:

And further, it is fitting to know that, in mentioning one of the titles, it is fitting that we know to which aspect, of the aspects that are in the sefirah, that title hints, as we explained in the Gate of Titles and in the Gate of the Glossary of Titles. And with this a doubling of words in one attribute will not be difficult; for what this title hints, that one does not hint. And it is fitting to direct the intention in each and every matter according to its way. "And the thing is very near to us, in our mouth and in our heart, to do it" (cf. Deut. 30:14). And now let us return to explain that when we mention one of the names that are not erased, we must direct our intention in the totality of that sefirah that is hinted in it, without turning to one of its aspects; even though they have an explanation, as we explained in the Gate of Names, how they include all the attributes, and many other aspects. However, they are palaces to the very self of the sefirot, which are the names mentioned above, which is the name of havayah that is in each and every sefirah. And therefore, when we mention the four-letter name itself, which sometimes hints in one of the sefirot, then certainly the intention will be [also] to the very self of the inwardness of the sefirot; and this is found only very rarely. And when we mention one of the names that are not erased, then the intention is that it is a palace to the very self [of the inner sefirot, which are the aforementioned havayot], but in the totality of the sefirah. And when we mention one of the titles, then certainly it is in the aspects that are distinguished in each and every sefirah, according to what the title will be. This is with respect to the particularity of the words. However, in the whole prayer one must direct the voice in Tiferet and the speech, which is the articulation of the words, in Malkhut, YHVH Adonai; and they are united together; for behold, he says voice and speech together. It is found that his mind is always to this name, יאהדונה"י, which is a hint to the union. And likewise at every time that he wishes to hint at the union, he will direct his intention to this name.

And further, he will intend that the voice and the speech are included of fire, water, air, which are Gedulah and Gevurah, Tiferet, by whose means is the union; as is known, that the voice goes out compounded of fire and water and air, as is explained in the Glossary of Titles. And since the intention of the union in prayer is to the name of the union, he will not come to iniquity. And it is fitting to direct the intention, in each name of the names of the four-letter name, to the name of twelve that we explained in the Gate of Particulars of Names. Further, it is fitting that he intend in his prayer in which attribute of the prayers he is at present, whether morning or afternoon or evening; and in that attribute all his intentions will be, according to its hour; that is to say, before his prayer. And there are further many, many particulars that are explained in the matters of prayer, which it is not fitting to bring up in writing here, because of their length; and further, because they do not belong here; and they will come in a book by itself, if the Name decrees life.
And behold, this chapter is completed, and this gate is concluded, and this book is perfected. Praise to God, may He be blessed, and thanksgiving to His great and holy name, blessed be He:
